'''Fernando José Torres Sanz''' ({{IPA|es|feɾˈnando ˈtores}}; born 20 March 1984) is a Spanish [[Association football|football]] [[Manager (association football)|manager]] and former [[Football player|player]] who played as a [[Striker (association football)|striker]]. He is the current manager of [[Atlético Madrid B]]. Due to his consistent goalscoring as a young player, Torres came to be nicknamed '''''El Niño''''' ('The Kid'), which stuck with him throughout his career.<ref name="www.sports-king.com">{{Cite web |title=El Nino Nickname - What does it mean and how did it come about? - Player Biography and Profile |url=https://www.sports-king.com/nicknames.php?q=el-nino |access-date=28 May 2022 |website=www.sports-king.com |archive-date=24 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220524075642/https://www.sports-king.com/nicknames.php?q=el-nino |url-status=live }}</ref> In his prime, he was regarded as one of the best strikers in the world and was known for his pace, prolific goalscoring, and technical abilities.

Torres started his career with [[Atlético Madrid]], progressing through their youth system to the first team. He made his debut in 2001 and left the club with 75 goals in 174 [[La Liga]] appearances. Torres joined [[Premier League]] club [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] in 2007 and became the fastest player in Liverpool history to score 50 league goals.<ref name="www.goal.com">{{Cite web |title=Counterattack: Is Torres The Best Striker In The World? {{!}} Goal.com |url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/1929/fifa-confederations-cup/2009/06/18/1332257/counterattack-is-torres-the-best-striker-in-the-world |access-date=27 May 2022 |website=www.goal.com |archive-date=27 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220527100851/https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/1929/fifa-confederations-cup/2009/06/18/1332257/counterattack-is-torres-the-best-striker-in-the-world |url-status=live }}</ref> In [[2008 Ballon d'Or|2008]], he finished third for both the [[Ballon d'Or]] and [[FIFA World Player of the Year]]. Striving to compete for trophies, Torres left Liverpool in January 2011 to join [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] for [[List of most expensive association football transfers|a Premier League record transfer fee of £50 million]], which made him the most expensive Spanish player in history. At Chelsea, he won the [[FA Cup]], the [[UEFA Champions League]], and the [[UEFA Europa League]]. Torres went on to have a brief stint at [[AC Milan]] before returning to Atlético Madrid, where he won the [[2017–18 UEFA Europa League|2017-18 UEFA Europa League]]. He signed for Japanese club [[Sagan Tosu]] in July 2018, before retiring from professional football after the [[2019 J1 League|2019 season]].

In 2003, Torres made his debut for Spain in a friendly against [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]]. He was [[List of men's footballers with 100 or more international caps|capped 110 times]] and is his country's [[Spain national football team#Top goalscorers|third-highest top goalscorer]] with 38 goals. With Spain, he participated in six major tournaments: [[UEFA Euro 2004]], the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]], [[UEFA Euro 2008|Euro 2008]], the [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010 World Cup]], [[UEFA Euro 2012|Euro 2012]], and the [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014 World Cup]]. Spain won the 2008, 2010, and 2012 tournaments and Torres scored in the finals of both [[UEFA Euro 2008 final|Euro 2008]] and [[UEFA Euro 2012 final|Euro 2012]]. He won the Golden Boot for scoring the most goals in the 2012 tournament.

==Early career==
Born in [[Fuenlabrada]], [[Community of Madrid]],<ref name=Fernando>{{cite news |title=Fernando Torres condecorado con la Medalla 'Ciudad de Fuenlabrada' |url=http://www.sermadridsur.com/noticias/fernando-torres-condecorado-con-la-medalla-ciudad-de-fuenlabrada_1499/ |website=SER Madrid Sur |date=6 February 2009 |access-date=13 March 2010 |language=es |archive-date=25 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201125155101/http://www.sermadridsur.com/noticias/fernando-torres-condecorado-con-la-medalla-ciudad-de-fuenlabrada_1499/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Torres loved [[association football|football]] as a child and joined his first youth team, Parque 84, at age five.<ref name=Infancia>{{cite web |title=Infancia |url=http://www.fernando9torres.com/index.php?s=biografia&ss=infancia |publisher=Fernando Torres |access-date=20 June 2010 |language=es |archive-date=19 January 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120119103337/http://www.fernando9torres.com/index.php?s=biografia |url-status=live }}</ref> His grandfather was an [[Atlético Madrid]] fan.<ref name=Infancia/>

Torres began playing football as a [[goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Torres asegura que habría sido "un gran portero" |url=http://archivo.marca.com/edicion/marca/futbol/internacional/es/desarrollo/1113428.html |newspaper=Marca |location=Madrid |date=17 April 2008 |access-date=18 May 2011 |language=es |archive-date=21 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110721051923/http://archivo.marca.com/edicion/marca/futbol/internacional/es/desarrollo/1113428.html |url-status=live }}</ref> At age seven, he began playing as a [[Striker (association football)|striker]] for Mario’s Holanda, the neighbourhood’s '[[Indoor soccer|indoor football]]' club,<ref>{{cite news |title= El Niño: an Oral History of Fernando Torres at Atlético de Madrid, Chapters 1 & 2|date=25 February 2017 |url=https://www.intothecalderon.com/2017/2/25/14656994/el-nino-an-oral-history-of-fernando-torres-at-atletico-de-madrid-chapters-1-2 |access-date=25 February 2017 |via=IntoTheCalderon.com}}</ref><ref name=Infancia/> using the characters from the [[anime]] ''[[Captain Tsubasa]]'' as inspiration.<ref>{{cite news |title=Japanese comic superhero drawn to Tokyo Olympic bid |url=http://www.thefreelibrary.com/Japanese+comic+superhero+drawn+to+Tokyo+Olympic+bid-a01611962772 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120917183559/http://www.thefreelibrary.com/Japanese+comic+superhero+drawn+to+Tokyo+Olympic+bid-a01611962772 |url-status=dead |archive-date=17 September 2012 |agency=Agence France-Presse |date=11 August 2009 |access-date=20 June 2010 |via=TheFreeLibrary.com}}</ref> At age 10, he joined Rayo 13 and scored 55 goals in his first season. He later joined Atlético’s youth system at age 11 in 1995.<ref name="Atlético de Madrid">{{cite web |title=Atlético de Madrid |url=http://www.fernando9torres.com/index.php?s=biografia&ss=atmadrid |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130501152102/http://fernando9torres.com/index.php?s=biografia |archive-date=1 May 2013 |access-date=17 November 2008 |publisher=Fernando Torres |language=es}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Atlético Madrid===
[[File:Atleti-lega2001FernandoTorres.png|thumb|left|Torres entering the pitch on his debut for [[Atlético Madrid]] on 27 May 2001]]
After progressing through the ranks, Torres won his first important youth title in 1998.<ref name="Atlético de Madrid"/> Atlético sent an under-15 team to compete in the Nike Cup, in Spain and Europe, to play against youth teams from other clubs; Atlético won the tournament.<ref name="Atlético de Madrid"/><ref name="Lowe-2007">{{cite news |first=Sid |last=Lowe |title=Will Torres be Kop's new God or just another Fernando? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2007/jul/04/newsstory.sport8 |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=4 July 2007 |access-date=5 August 2014 |archive-date=14 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220214234623/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2007/jul/04/newsstory.sport8 |url-status=live }}</ref> He was later voted the best player in Europe for the age group.<ref name="Lowe-2007"/> In 1999, at the age of 15, Torres signed his first professional contract with Atlético.<ref name="Atlético de Madrid"/> He spent his first year playing in the youth team and participated in the Honor Division when he was 16.<ref name="Primer equipo">{{cite web |title=Primer equipo |url=http://www.fernando9torres.com/index.php?s=biografia&ss=primerequipo |publisher=Fernando Torres |access-date=17 November 2008 |language=es |archive-date=1 May 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130501152102/http://fernando9torres.com/index.php?s=biografia |url-status=live }}</ref> The [[2000–01 Atlético Madrid season|2000–01 season]] had started poorly, as Torres suffered from a cracked shinbone which kept him out of play until December.<ref name="Primer equipo"/> Torres trained with the first team to get prepared for pre-season, but eventually made his debut on 27 May 2001, at the [[Vicente Calderón Stadium]], against [[CD Leganés|Leganés]].<ref name="Primer equipo"/> One week later, he scored his first goal for the club, against [[Albacete Balompié|Albacete]], and the season finished with Atlético narrowly missing out on [[Promotion and relegation|promotion]] to [[La Liga]].<ref name="Primer equipo"/>

Atlético were promoted to La Liga at the end of the [[2001–02 Atlético Madrid season|2001–02 season]], although Torres did not perform well in the season, as he netted only 6 times in 36 appearances in the [[Segunda División]].<ref name=Torres>{{cite web |url=http://www.footballdatabase.com/index.php?page=player&Id=555&b=true&pn=Fernando_Jos%C3%A9_Torres_Sanz |title=Torres |website=FootballDatabase |access-date=8 June 2008 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20090215042343/http://www.footballdatabase.com/index.php?page=player&Id=555&b=true&pn=Fernando_Jos%C3%A9_Torres_Sanz |archive-date=15 February 2009}}</ref> Torres's first season in La Liga, [[2002–03 Atlético Madrid season|2002–03]], was better, however, as he scored 13 goals in 29 appearances, with Atlético finishing in 11th place.<ref name="Primer equipo"/><ref name=Torres/> In July 2003, soon after his takeover of the club, [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] owner [[Roman Abramovich]] had a [[Pound sterling|£]]28 million bid for Torres rejected by Atlético's board of directors.<ref name="Chelsea sign Bridge">{{cite news |title=Chelsea sign Bridge |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/2408099/Chelsea-sign-Bridge.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220111/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/2408099/Chelsea-sign-Bridge.html |archive-date=11 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |date=21 July 2003 |access-date=30 January 2013}}{{cbignore}}</ref> In the [[2003–04 Atlético Madrid season|2003–04 season]], his second in La Liga, Torres made further strides, scoring 19 league goals in 35 appearances,<ref name=Torres/> meaning he finished as the joint third-highest scorer in the league.<ref name="Statistics: top scorers: 2003/2004">{{cite web |title=Statistics: top scorers: 2003/2004 |url=http://www.espnfc.com/spanish-primera-division/15/statistics/scorers?season=2003 |website=ESPN FC |access-date=5 August 2014 |archive-date=21 April 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200421045024/http://www.espnfc.com/spanish-primera-division/15/statistics/scorers?season=2003 |url-status=live }}</ref> At age 19, Torres was named Atlético's [[captain (association football)|captain]].<ref name="Lowe-2007"/> Atlético narrowly missed out on qualification for the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]], but by finishing in seventh place in the 2003–04 season, they qualified for the [[2004 UEFA Intertoto Cup]], giving Torres a first taste of a competition at the European level.<ref name="UEFA Intertoto Cup 2004">{{cite web |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesu/uic04.html |title=UEFA Intertoto Cup 2004 |website=[[RSSSF]] |access-date=9 June 2008 |archive-date=13 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220713102158/https://www.rsssf.org/tablesu/uic04.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He scored two goals in the two fourth round matches against [[OFK Beograd]], with one coming in each leg.<ref name="UEFA Intertoto Cup 2004"/> Atlético reached the final, but lost 3–1 on a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] to [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] following a 2–2 draw on aggregate.<ref name="UEFA Intertoto Cup 2004"/> [[Premier League|FA Premier League]] champions Chelsea were believed to be interested in signing Torres during the summer of 2005, but Atlético club president [[Enrique Cerezo]] said that they had "no chance" of signing him.<ref name="Atletico warn Chelsea off Torres">{{cite news |title=Atletico warn Chelsea off Torres |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/europe/4630265.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=28 June 2005 |access-date=18 May 2011 |archive-date=20 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210420152515/http://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/europe/4630265.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Cerezo later said in January 2006 that the club was willing to listen to offers for Torres, and Torres claimed [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] of the FA Premier League had made a bid to sign him in March.<ref name="Atletico prepared to sell Torres">{{cite news |title=Atletico prepared to sell Torres |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/europe/4644186.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=24 January 2006 |access-date=18 May 2011 |archive-date=17 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201017210512/http://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/europe/4644186.stm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Newcastle want me, claims Torres">{{cite news |title=Newcastle want me, claims Torres |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/4811932.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=16 March 2006 |access-date=27 July 2011 |archive-date=17 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201017220840/http://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/4811932.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[File:Fernando Torres Atlético Madrid.png|thumb|upright|Torres playing for Atlético Madrid in 2006]]

Torres stated after the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]] that he had turned down an offer to join Chelsea at the end of the [[2005–06 Atlético Madrid season|2005–06 season]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Tom |last=Adams |title='Flattered' Villa to stay with Che |url=https://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11667/2404638/flattered-villa-to-stay-with-che |website=Sky Sports |date=6 February 2007 |access-date=5 August 2014 |archive-date=25 January 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210125235825/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11667/2404638/flattered-villa-to-stay-with-che Premier League club [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]],<ref>{{cite news |first=David |last=Prentice |title=Torres is Reds' number one target |url=http://icliverpool.icnetwork.co.uk/0500liverpoolfc/0100news/tm_headline=torres-is-reds%2D-number-one-target%26method=full%26objectid=19326444%26siteid=50061-name_page.html |newspaper=Liverpool Echo |date=20 June 2007 |access-date=30 June 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130603224454/http://icliverpool.icnetwork.co.uk/0500liverpoolfc/0100news/tm_headline%3Dtorres-is-reds--number-one-target%26method%3Dfull%26objectid%3D19326444%26siteid%3D50061-name_page.html |archive-date=3 June 2013 |url-status=dead}}</ref> but Cerezo stated, "We've received no offer from Liverpool or any other club or player."<ref name="No Reds offer for Torres">{{cite news |title=No Reds offer for Torres |url=http://www.thedailystar.net/2007/06/27/d70627043553.htm |newspaper=The Daily Star |location=Dhaka |date=27 June 2007 |access-date=20 June 2010 Atlético had agreed a deal with Liverpool for Torres; the fee was rumoured to be £25 million with [[Luis García (footballer, born 1978)|Luis García]] moving to Atlético in a separate transfer deal.<ref>{{cite news |first=Oliver |last=Kay |title=Garcia the key as Liverpool step up pursuit of Torres |url=http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/sport/football/premier_league/liverpool/article1996591.ece |newspaper=[[The Times]] |location=London |date=28 June 2007 On 30 June, Atlético announced a deal to sign [[Diego Forlán]] from Villarreal, in what was seen as a move to replace Torres before his departure became official.<ref name="Liverpool complete Torres signing">{{cite news |title=Liverpool complete Torres signing |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/europe/6239286.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=4 July 2007 |access-date=18 May 2011 that Torres had cut short a vacation to fly back to Madrid to finalise the move to Liverpool.<ref name="Torres' £27m Liverpool deal">{{cite news |first=Charles |last=Carrick |title=Torres' £27m Liverpool deal |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2316106/Torres-27m-Liverpool-deal.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220111/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2316106/Torres-27m-Liverpool-deal.html |archive-date=11 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |date=30 June 2007 |access-date=18 May 2011 |location=London}}{{cbignore}}</ref> The following day, Torres passed a medical at Liverpool's [[Melwood]] bid farewell to the Atlético fans, before completing his move to Liverpool on a six-year contract.<ref name="Liverpool wrap up record Torres transfer"/> The transfer fee was the highest in Liverpool's history.<ref name="Liverpool complete Torres signing"/> In March 2008, [[manager (association football)|manager]] [[Rafael Benítez]] stated in an interview with ''[[The Times]]'' that Torres was acquired for around £20 million, although this figure takes into account García's move to Atlético.<ref>{{cite news |first=Guillem |last=Balague |title=Rafael Benitez opens up on transfers, treachery, ===Liverpool===
====2007–08 season====
Torres made his competitive debut for Liverpool against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] in a 2–1 win on 11 August 2007.<ref name="Aston Villa 1-2 Liverpool">{{cite news |first=John |last=Sinnott |title=Aston Villa 1–2 Liverpool |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/6931045.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=11 August 2007 |access-date=18 May 2011 |archive-date=20 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201020064918/http://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/6931045.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> He made his first appearance in the [[UEFA Champions League]] four days past his first performance in a 1–0 victory over [[Toulouse FC|Toulouse]], after coming on as a 79th minute [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]].<ref name="Toulouse 0-1 Liverpool">{{cite news |first=Mandeep |last=Sanghera |title=Toulouse 0–1 Liverpool |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/europe/6941921.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=15 August 2007 His first Premier League goal came on his [[Anfield]] debut on 19 August 2007, in the 16th minute in a 1–1 draw against Chelsea.<ref name="Liverpool 1-1 Chelsea">{{cite news |first=Saj |last=Chowdhury |title=Liverpool 1–1 Chelsea |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/6941876.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=19 August 2007 |access-date=18 May 2011 |archive-date=18 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201018111721/http://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/6941876.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> His first [[Hat-trick (association football)|hat-trick]] came in a 4–2 victory over [[Reading F.C.|Reading]] in the [[EFL Cup|League Cup]] on 25 September 2007, with all of his goals coming in the second half.<ref name="Reading 2-4 Liverpool">{{cite news |first=Andrew |last=McKenzie |title=Reading 2–4 Liverpool |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/league_cup/7008013.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=25 September 2007 }}</ref> His first goals in the Champions League came on his third appearance in the competition as Liverpool beat [[FC Porto|Porto]] 4–1 on 28 November 2007, as he scored twice.<ref name="Liverpool 4-1 FC Porto">{{cite news |first=John |last=Sinnott |title=Liverpool 4–1 FC Porto |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/europe/7110714.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=28 November 2011 Torres was named the [[Premier League Player of the Month]] for February 2008,<ref name="Moyes & Torres win monthly awards">{{cite news |title=Moyes & Torres win monthly awards |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/7284223.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=7 March 2008 |access-date=18 May 2011 |archive-date=18 October 2020 |title=Fernando Torres: My pride at Anfield hat-trick record |url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/fernando-torres-pride-anfield-hat-trick-3490568 |newspaper=Liverpool Echo On 4 May 2008, Torres scored a 57th-minute winner against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], which equalled the consecutive Anfield league goal record of eight games set by [[Roger Hunt]].<ref name=sb0708/><ref name="Torres equals Hunt record">{{cite news |title=Torres equals Hunt record |url=http://www.football.co.uk/liverpool/torres_equals_hunt_record_264224.shtml |website=football.co.uk |publisher=Digital Sports Group |date=5 May 2008 |access-date=5 August 2014 Torres faced his old rivals [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] on 10 March 2009 in the Champions League last 16 and due to an ankle injury, he had a painkilling injection before the game to enable him to play.<ref>{{cite news |first=David |last=Brown |title=Fernando Torres used powers of persuasion to play against Real Madrid |url=https://www.thetimes.com/article/fernando-torres-used-powers-of-persuasion-to-play-against-real-madrid-p3pf9l8vd0w |newspaper=[[The Times]] |location=London |date=11 March 2009 |access-date=13 April 2009}}</ref> He scored the first goal of the game, which ended as a 4–0 victory, meaning Liverpool progressed to the quarter-finals 5–0 on aggregate.<ref name="Liverpool 4-0 Real Madrid">{{cite news |title=Liverpool 4–0 Real Madrid (agg 5–0) |first=Phil |last=McNulty |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/europe/7899615.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=10 March 2009 |access-date=18 May 2011 |archive-date=18 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201018111717/http://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/europe/7899615.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Four days later, he lined up against Manchester United at [[Old Trafford]] and he scored the equaliser in a game that finished as a 4–1 victory.<ref name="Man Utd 1-4 Liverpool">{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Man Utd 1–4 Liverpool |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/7922069.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=14 March 2009 |access-date=18 May 2011 |archive-date=19 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201019041728/http://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/7922069.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> His [[goal celebration]] at Old Trafford endeared him to Liverpool fans when he held out his hand to United fans – making the "five times" gesture –

Torres was named in the FIFPro World XI for the second successive season in December 2009.<ref>{{cite news |first=Jimmy |last=Leach |title=FIFA/FIFPRO World XI announced |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/international/fifafifpro-world-xi-announced-1847812.html |newspaper=The Independent |location=London |date=22 December 2009 |access-date=31 August 2014 |archive-date=18 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201018230754/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/international/fifafifpro-world-xi-announced-1847812.html |url-status=live }}</ref> His stoppage-time winning goal against Aston Villa on 29 December 2009 made him the fastest Liverpool player ever to score 50 league goals.<ref name="Aston Villa 0-1 Liverpool">{{cite news |first=David |last=Ornstein |title=Aston Villa 0–1 Liverpool |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/8428990.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=29 December 2009 |access-date=18 May 2011 |archive-date=18 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201018182934/http://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/8428990.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> He was substituted on 65 minutes in a 1–1 draw with [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] on 4 April 2010, which Benítez justified by saying Torres was "exhausted".<ref>{{cite news |title=Rafa Benitez defends his decision to take off Torres |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/8602891.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=4 April 2010 |access-date=27 July 2011 |archive-date=9 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160109084648/http://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/8602891.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Torres made his last appearance of the season scoring twice in a 4–1 victory over [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] in the Europa League on 8 April 2010,<ref name=sb0910/> and it was announced on 18 April that he would miss the rest of the season to undergo knee surgery.<ref name="Liverpool's Fernando Torres out for rest of season">{{cite news |title=Liverpool's Fernando Torres out for rest of season |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/8628770.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=18 April 2010 |access-date=27 July 2011 |archive-date=23 August 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130823132414/http://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/8628770.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> This meant that Torres finished the season with 22 goals in 32 games in all competitions, finishing as Liverpool's top scorer for the second time.<ref name=sb0910/>

====2010–11 season====
[[File:Fernando Torres v Blackpool 2010.jpg|thumb|left|Torres playing for Liverpool in 2010]]
Following [[Roy Hodgson]]'s appointment as Liverpool manager, Hodgson stated that Torres would not be sold by the club, saying, "He is not for sale and we don't welcome any offers for him. We want to keep him."<ref>{{cite news |title=Gerrard and Torres staying at Liverpool – Hodgson |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/8829753.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=16 July 2010 |access-date=27 July 2011 |archive-date=17 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201017224301/http://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/8829753.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Hodgson dismissed reports Torres was set to leave Liverpool by saying, "He has told us that he is looking forward to Monday, to getting back to work and looking forward to playing for Liverpool next season. That is what I know so other reports, I would suggest, are erroneous."<ref>{{cite news |title=Hodgson expects Fernando Torres to stay at Liverpool |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/8853856.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=27 July 2010 |access-date=27 July 2011 |archive-date=17 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201017224249/http://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/8853856.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Torres stated his commitment to Liverpool on 3 August: "My commitment and loyalty to the club and to the fans is the same as it was on my first day when I signed."<ref>{{cite news |title=Striker Fernando Torres committed to Liverpool |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/8881776.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=3 August 2010 |access-date=27 July 2011 |archive-date=21 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201021211612/http://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/8881776.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

Torres made his first appearance of the [[2010–11 Liverpool F.C. season|2010–11 season]] in the opening match, a 1–1 draw with Arsenal on 14 August 2010, entering the game as a substitute in the 74th minute.<ref name="Liverpool 1-1 Arsenal">{{cite news |first=Mandeep |last=Sanghera |title=Liverpool 1–1 Arsenal |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/8909559.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=15 August 2010 |access-date=18 May 2011 |archive-date=18 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201018142005/http://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/8909559.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> He scored his first goal of the season with the winner in a 1–0 victory over West Brom on 29 August 2010,<ref name="Liverpool 1–0 West Brom">{{cite news |first=Mandeep |last=Sanghera |title=Liverpool 1–0 West Brom |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/8945965.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=29 August 2010 |access-date=18 May 2011 |archive-date=17 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201017205421/http://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/8945965.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> his 50th goal at Anfield in all competitions.<ref>{{cite news |title=Torres landmark nets WBA win |url=http://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/latest-news/torres-landmark-nets-wba-win |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |date=29 August 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141227231303/http://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/latest-news/torres-landmark-nets-wba-win |archive-date=27 December 2014}}</ref> Torres scored the winning goal in a 2–1 victory at home to [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] on 24 October 2010, his first goal since August.<ref name="Liverpool 2-1 Blackburn">{{cite news |first=Alistair |last=Magowan |title=Liverpool 2–1 Blackburn |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/9107874.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=24 October 2010 |access-date=18 May 2011 |archive-date=20 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201020064924/http://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/9107874.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> He scored his final goals for Liverpool in a 3–0 win |title=Chelsea's £40 million bid for Liverpool striker Fernando Torres is an act of desperation |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/liverpool/8287671/Chelseas-40-million-bid-for-Liverpool-striker-Fernando-Torres-is-an-act-of-desperation.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220111/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/liverpool/8287671/Chelseas-40-million-bid-for-Liverpool-striker-Fernando-Torres-is-an-act-of-desperation.html |archive-date=11 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |date=27 January 2011 |access-date=6 February 2011}}{{cbignore}}</ref> He handed Request', Wolfsburg Offer Volkswagens For Schulz And Adriano Galliani Is The New Moggi & More West Ham |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/9462715.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=23 April 2011 |access-date=24 April 2011 |archive-date=19 October 2020 ====2011–12 season====
[[File:MALAYSIA VS CHELSEA 2011 (5969056175).jpg|thumb|Torres playing for [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in 2011]]

Torres got the [[2011–12 Chelsea F.C. season|2011–12 season]] underway in Chelsea's 0–0 draw away against [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] on 14 August 2011, in which his "link-up play was sharp, plus he was willing to make intelligent runs into space to receive the ball".<ref>{{cite news |first=Alistair |last=Magowan |title=Stoke 0–0 Chelsea |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14435069 |website=BBC Sport |date=14 August 2011 |access-date=24 June 2017 |archive-date=10 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220210211742/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14435069 |url-status=live }}</ref> He scored his second goal at Chelsea, and his first of the season, on 18 September 2011, in a 3–1 away defeat to Manchester United. However, that was overshadowed by his miss at an open goal.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Manchester United 3–1 Chelsea |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14869914 |website=BBC Sport |date=18 September 2011 |access-date=24 June 2017 |archive-date=10 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220210211649/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14869914 |url-status=live }}</ref> He scored his second goal of the season at home to [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]] in a 4–1 victory.<ref name="Chelsea 4-1 Swansea">{{cite news |first=Aled |last=Williams |title=Chelsea 4–1 Swansea |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/14957961.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=24 September 2011 |access-date=25 September 2011 |archive-date=9 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160109084648/http://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/14957961.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Ten minutes after his goal, however, a two-footed challenge on [[Mark Gower]] resulted in his first [[Red card (association football)|red card]] in English football and a three-match domestic suspension.<ref>{{cite news |first=Pascal |last=Lemesre |title=Fernando Torres handed red card after scoring |url=http://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/chelsea/news/torres-handed-red-card-after-scoring_4229.html |website=Sportsmole |date=24 September 2011 |access-date=24 September 2011 |archive-date=12 May 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130512033648/http://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/chelsea/news/torres-handed-red-card-after-scoring_4229.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Fernando Torres: Chelsea start has been 'very, very difficult' |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2011/sep/26/fernando-torres-red-card-chelsea |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=26 September 2011 |access-date=12 April 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111206104603/http://www.guardian.co.uk/football/2011/sep/26/fernando-torres-red-card-chelsea |archive-date=6 December 2011}}</ref> On 19 October 2011, Torres scored two goals in a 5–0 victory against [[K.R.C. Genk|Genk]] in the Champions League, his first in Europe since the quarter-final of the [[2008–09 UEFA Champions League|2008–09 Champions League]] with his old club Liverpool, against Chelsea.<ref>{{cite news |first=Stephan |last=Shemilt |title=Chelsea 5–0 Genk |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/15269495 |website=BBC Sport |date=19 October 2011 |access-date=24 June 2017 |archive-date=27 April 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200427171034/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/15269495 |url-status=live }}</ref> His next Chelsea goals came after scoring twice and also assisting two others against [[EFL Championship|Championship]] team [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] in an FA Cup [[2011–12 FA Cup|quarter-final]] on 18 March 2012, ending a goal drought that stretched 24 games.<ref>{{cite news |first=Graham |last=Chase |title=Chelsea 5–2 Leicester |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17330279 |website=BBC Sport |date=18 March 2012 |access-date=24 June 2017 |archive-date=10 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220210094644/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17330279 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 31 March 2012, Torres scored his first Premier League goal since 24 September 2011, against Aston Villa in a 4–2 away win.<ref name=sb1112/>

Torres came on as a substitute for [[Didier Drogba]] on 24 April 2012 to score a last-minute goal against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in the Champions League semi-final, which gave Chelsea a 2–2 draw and sealed their place in the final.<ref name="Barcelona 2–2 Chelsea (agg 2–3)">{{cite news |first=Phil |last=Dawkes |title=Barcelona 2–2 Chelsea (agg 2–3) |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17817584 |website=BBC Sport |date=24 April 2012 |access-date=24 April 2012 |archive-date=24 April 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120424050333/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/17817584 |url-status=live }}</ref> He scored the first hat-trick of his Chelsea career in a 6–1 win against [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]] on 29 April 2012.<ref name="Chelsea 6-1 QPR">{{cite news |first=Marc |last=Higginson |title=Chelsea 6–1 QPR |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17803533 |website=BBC Sport |date=29 April 2012 |access-date=29 April 2012 |archive-date=26 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160126134512/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/17803533 |url-status=live }}</ref> Torres came on in the second half of the [[2012 UEFA Champions League Final]] on 19 May 2012, directly after [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]]'s opening goal, and following a 1–1 draw after [[Overtime (association football)|extra time]] Chelsea won the penalty shoot-out 4–3.<ref name="Bayern Munich 1-1 Chelsea">{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Bayern Munich 1–1 Chelsea |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/18044385 |website=BBC Sport |date=19 May 2012 |access-date=23 August 2012 |archive-date=16 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160116042658/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/18044385 |url-status=live }}</ref> His first full season at Chelsea finished with 11 goals in 49 appearances.<ref name=sb1112/>

====2012–13 season====

Torres started the [[2012–13 Chelsea F.C. season|2012–13 season]] in the [[2012 FA Community Shield]] against Manchester City at [[Villa Park]], where he scored the opening goal, as Chelsea lost 3–2.<ref name="Chelsea 2-3 Man City">{{cite news |first=Ben |last=Smith |title=Chelsea 2–3 Man City |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19133978 |website=BBC Sport |date=12 August 2012 F.C.|Norwich City]] as Chelsea topped the table in the early weeks of [[2012–13 Premier League|the season]].<ref name=sb1213/><ref name="English Premier League 2012-2013 : Table">{{cite web |title=English Premier League 2012–2013 : Table |url=http://www.statto.com/football/stats/england/premier-league/2012-2013/table/2012-10-06 |publisher=Statto Organisation |access-date=11 April 2013 Torres was sent off for receiving two [[Yellow card (association football)|yellow cards]] against Manchester United on 28 October 2012, the second for [[Diving (association football)|diving]], leaving Chelsea with nine men after teammate [[Branislav Ivanović]] was also sent off; the team went on to lose 3–2.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Chelsea 2–3 Man Utd |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160109084648/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/20020062 |url-status=live }}</ref> Torres scored his first goal in the Champions League [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League|for the season]] after deflecting [[FC Shakhtar Donetsk|Shakhtar Donetsk]] goalkeeper [[Andriy Pyatov]]'s clearance into goal, as Chelsea needed a 94th-minute winner from [[Victor Moses]] to secure a 3–2 victory on 7 November 2012.<ref name="Chelsea 3-2 Shakhtar Donetsk">{{cite news |title=Chelsea 3–2 Shakhtar Donetsk |url=http://espnfc.com/us/en/report/355690/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5901 |website=ESPN FC |date=7 November 2012 |access-date=8 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140226110609/http://espnfc.com/us/en/report/355690/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5901 |archive-date=26 February 2014}}</ref> On 21 November 2012, [[Roberto Torres ended a goal drought that stretched over 11 hours of game time with two goals in Chelsea's 6–1 defeat of [[FC Nordsjælland|Nordsjælland]] in the Champions League on 5 December 2012.<ref name="Torres: I need more time to perform">{{cite news |first=Kevin |last=Palmer |title=Torres: I need more time to perform |url=http://www.espnfc.com/story/1254141 |website=ESPN FC |date=7 December 2012 |access-date=5 August 2014 |archive-date=21 April 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200421045841/http://www.espnfc.com/story/1254141 |url-status=live }}</ref> Three days later, he scored another two goals, ending a run of eight Premier League games without a goal, as Chelsea defeated Sunderland 3–1.<ref>{{cite news |title=Fernando Torres nets brace as Chelsea see off Sunderland in Premier League |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/sland-vs-chelsea/report/261717 |website=Sky Sports |date=8 December 2012 |access-date=13 November 2015 |archive-date=10 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220210100155/https://www.skysports.com/football/sland-vs-chelsea/report/261717 |url-status=live }}</ref> He then scored in Chelsea's [[2012 FIFA Club World Cup]] semi-final 3–1 win against [[C.F. Monterrey|Monterrey]] of the Mexican [[Liga MX]] on 13 December 2012, before playing in the 1–0 defeat to Brazilian [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|Série A]] side [[Sport Club Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]] in the [[2012 FIFA Club World Cup Final|final]] three days later.<ref name=sb1213/>

On 14 March 2013, Torres scored the third goal as Chelsea defeated [[FC Steaua București|Steaua București]] 3–1 to advance 3–2 on aggregate to the quarter-final of the [[2012–13 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]].<ref name=sb1213/> With this goal, Torres became the first player to score in seven different competitions in one season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.givemesport.com/437823-30-truly-random-football-facts |title=30 truly random football facts |website=GiveMeSport |last=Peterson |first=Brad |date=3 March 2017 |access-date=16 November 2017 |archive-date=10 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190410201918/https://www.givemesport.com/437823-30-truly-random-football-facts |url-status=dead }}</ref> He scored twice against [[FC Rubin Kazan|Rubin Kazan]] in the 3–1 win in the first leg of the Europa League quarter-final on 4 April 2013, before scoring again in the second leg 3–2 defeat, with Chelsea progressing to the semi-final 5–4 on aggregate.<ref name=sb1213/> Torres scored the opening goal in Chelsea's 2–1 triumph over Benfica in the [[2013 UEFA Europa League Final]] on 15 May 2013.<ref name=sb1213/> During the final match of the season, a 2–1 home win over Everton, he scored his first league goal of 2013, and finished the season with 22 goals in 64 matches.<ref name=sb1213/><ref name="Goal total clarification"/>

===AC Milan===
Torres joined Italian [[Serie A]] club [[AC Milan]] on a two-year [[Loan (association football)|loan]] on 31 August 2014.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28991464 |title=Fernando Torres: AC Milan seal loan deal for Chelsea striker |website=BBC Sport |date=31 August 2014 |access-date=31 August 2014 |archive-date=19 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160119104826/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/28991464 |url-status=live }}</ref> He debuted on 20 September, replacing [[Andrea Poli]] for the last 14 minutes of a 1–0 home defeat against [[Juventus FC|Juventus]]<ref>{{cite news |title=Milan 0–1 Juventus |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29275757 |access-date=21 September 2014 |website=BBC Sport |date=20 September 2014 |archive-date=9 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160109084648/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/29275757 |url-status=live }}</ref> and scored his first Milan goal with a looping header in their 2–2 draw with [[Empoli FC|Empoli]] two days later.<ref>{{cite news |title=Empoli 2–2 Milan |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29311328 |access-date=4 January 2015 |website=BBC Sport |date=23 September 2014 |archive-date=9 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160109084648/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/29311328 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Return to Atlético Madrid===
[[File:Fernando Torres DEP-ATM 024 1200.jpg|thumb|upright|Torres warming up for [[Atlético Madrid]] in 2015]]

On 27 December 2014, it was announced that Torres's move to Milan would be made permanent on 5 January 2015,<ref>{{cite news |title=AC Milan sign Chelsea's Fernando Torres on permanent deal |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30612861 |website=BBC Sport |date=27 December 2014 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141228005942/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/30612861 |archive-date=28 December 2014}}</ref> but two days later, he agreed to rejoin La Liga club Atlético Madrid on loan until the end of the 2015–16 season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Fernando Torres: Atletico Madrid loan deal for AC Milan striker |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30612861 |website=BBC Sport |date=29 December 2014 |access-date=29 December 2014 |archive-date=28 December 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141228005942/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/30612861 |url-status=live }}</ref> The loan was agreed after [[Alessio Cerci]] went the opposite way from Atlético to Milan on the same day.<ref>{{cite news |title=Official: Cerci joins AC Milan on loan |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/11/transfer-zone/2015/01/05/7672632/official-cerci-joins-ac-milan-on-loan |publisher=AC Milan |date=5 January 2015 |access-date=5 January 2015 |archive-date=10 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220210094651/https://www.goal.com/en/news/11/transfer-zone/2015/01/05/7672632/official-cerci-joins-ac-milan-on-loan |url-status=live }}</ref> Torres's unveiling at the Vicente Calderón Stadium on 4 January drew a crowd of 45,000 persons.<ref>{{cite news |title=Fernando Torres: Atletico Madrid fans welcome striker on return |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30672923 |website=BBC Sport |date=4 January 2015 |access-date=4 January 2015 |archive-date=9 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160109084648/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/30672923 |url-status=live }}</ref> He played the first match of his second spell on 7 January, starting in the first leg of a [[2014–15 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey last 16 tie]] against Real Madrid. He had no shots on target and was replaced by [[Koke (footballer, born 1992)|Koke]] after 59 minutes, but Atlético won 2–0.<ref>{{cite news |title=Atl Madrid 2–0 Real Madrid |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30688019 |access-date=7 January 2015 |website=BBC Sport |date=7 January 2015 |archive-date=9 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160109084648/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/30688019 |url-status=live }}</ref> Eight days later in the second leg, he scored two goals – in the first minute of each half – as Atlético advanced, his first goals in an away [[Madrid derby]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Real Madrid 2–2 Atl Madrid |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30818662 |access-date=15 January 2015 |website=BBC Sport |date=15 January 2015 |archive-date=18 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160118195547/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/30818662 |url-status=live }}</ref> Torres scored in the first minute again in the quarter-finals, albeit in a 2–3 home defeat against Barcelona.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Reddy |first1=Luke |title=Atl Madrid 2–3 Barcelona |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30991020 |access-date=28 January 2015 |website=BBC Sport |date=28 January 2015 |archive-date=9 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160109084648/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/30991020 |url-status=live }}</ref>

[[File:Loko-AM2018 (3).jpg|thumb|upright|left|Torres playing for Atlético Madrid in 2018]]
Torres scored the winning kick in Atlético's 3–2 penalty shoot-out defeat of [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] in the second leg of the teams' [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League knockout stage#Round of 16|round of 16]] tie on 17 March 2015.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/mar/17/atletico-madrid-bayer-leverkusen-champions-league-match-report |title=Atlético Madrid through after penalty pressure sinks Bayer Leverkusen |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=18 March 2015 |access-date=11 December 2016 |archive-date=10 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220210094652/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/mar/17/atletico-madrid-bayer-leverkusen-champions-league-match-report |url-status=live }}</ref> Four days later, he scored his first La Liga goal since his return in the third minute of a 2–0 win against [[Getafe CF|Getafe]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/31991902 |title=Atl Madrid 2–0 Getafe |date=21 March 2015 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=11 February 2018 |archive-date=9 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160109084648/http://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/31991902 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 6 February 2016, Torres scored his 100th goal with Atlético Madrid in a 3–1 home league victory against [[SD Eibar|Eibar]] on his 295th appearance for the club.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.marca.com/futbol/atletico/2016/02/06/56b626e2ca4741e82b8b45b7.html |title=Torres marca su gol 100 con el Atlético de Madrid |trans-title=Torres scores his 100th goal with Atlético Madrid |newspaper=Marca |location=Madrid |date=6 February 2016 |access-date=26 January 2018 |language=es |archive-date=26 January 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180126014911/http://www.marca.com/futbol/atletico/2016/02/06/56b626e2ca4741e82b8b45b7.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The following month, he marked his 300th appearance for Atlético by scoring in a 3–1 victory over [[Valencia CF|Valencia]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2016/03/06/56dcad22e2704e495f8b4630.html |title=Torres marks 300th Atleti appearance in style |newspaper=Marca |location=Madrid |date=6 March 2016 |access-date=8 March 2016 |archive-date=26 January 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180126184927/http://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2016/03/06/56dcad22e2704e495f8b4630.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He scored the opening goal of Atlético's [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Quarter-finals|quarter-final]] with Barcelona at the [[Camp Nou]] on 5 April, before being sent off ten minutes later in an eventual 2–1 loss.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2016/apr/05/barcelona-atletico-madrid-champions-league-live |title=Barcelona 2–1 Atlético |date=5 April 2016 |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |access-date=11 December 2016 |archive-date=10 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220210095153/https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2016/apr/05/barcelona-atletico-madrid-champions-league-live |url-status=live }}</ref>

Torres signed for Atlético permanently on 5 July 2016, on a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/torres-signs-one-year-contract-atletico-madrid |title=Torres signs one-year contract with Atletico Madrid |website=FourFourTwo |date=4 July 2016 |access-date=24 June 2017 |archive-date=10 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220210100151/https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/torres-signs-one-year-contract-atletico-madrid |url-status=live }}</ref> In February 2017, he scored his 100th league goal in Spanish football when he netted a brace against Leganés.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espnfc.com/spanish-primera-division/story/3054242/fernando-torres-very-happy-after-scoring-100th-league-goal-for-atletico |title=Fernando Torres 'very happy' after scoring 100th league goal for Atletico |website=ESPN FC |last=Corrigan |first=Dermot |date=4 February 2017 |access-date=28 February 2017 |archive-date=19 October 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171019221650/http://www.espnfc.com/spanish-primera-division/story/3054242/fernando-torres-very-happy-after-scoring-100th-league-goal-for-atletico |url-status=live }}</ref> On 4 July 2017, Torres signed a new one-year contract with the ''Rojiblancos'' to stay with his boyhood club for one more year after they were banned from signing new players.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espn.co.uk/football/soccer-transfers/story/2907394/fernando-torres-signs-new-atletico-madrid-contract |title=Fernando Torres signs new one-year Atletico Madrid contract |website=ESPN FC |date=4 July 2017 |access-date=12 July 2017 |archive-date=10 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220210095026/https://www.espn.co.uk/football/soccer-transfers/story/2907394/fernando-torres-signs-new-atletico-madrid-contract |url-status=live }}</ref>

Torres came on as a 90th-minute substitute on 16 May 2018 as Atlético beat Marseille 3–0 at [[Parc Olympique Lyonnais]] in the [[2018 UEFA Europa League Final]].<ref name=2018UEL>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44113764 |title=Marseille 0–3 Atlético Madrid |first=Shamoon |last=Hafez |website=BBC Sport |date=16 May 2018 |access-date=23 October 2018 |archive-date=28 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328044625/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44113764 |url-status=live }}</ref> He scored two goals in his last match with Atlético in a 2–2 draw versus [[SD Eibar|Eibar]] in the final week of championship.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.the42.ie/fernando-torres-final-atletico-madrid-match-two-goals-4024710-May2018/ |title=Club legend Torres bows out with two goals in final game for Atletico Madrid |website=The42 |publisher=Journal Media |date=20 May 2018 |access-date=21 May 2018 |archive-date=10 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220210214839/https://www.the42.ie/fernando-torres-final-atletico-madrid-match-two-goals-4024710-May2018/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

==International career==
===2001–02: Success at youth level===
In February 2001, Torres won the Algarve Tournament with the [[Spain national under-16 football team|Spain national under-16 team]].<ref name="9. Fernando Torres">{{cite news |title=9. Fernando Torres |url=http://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/liverpool-fc/liverpool-players/2007/09/12/9-fernando-torres-50061-19780051/ |newspaper=Liverpool Echo |access-date=8 June 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121013054318/http://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/liverpool-fc/liverpool-players/2007/09/12/9-fernando-torres-50061-19780051/ |archive-date=13 October 2012}}</ref> The under-16s took part in the [[2001 UEFA European Under-16 Championship]] in May, which they also won, with Torres scoring the only goal in the final, as well as finishing as the tournament's leading scorer, and was also named the player of the tournament.<ref name="Lowe-2007"/><ref name=Torres/> In September 2001, Torres represented the [[Spain national under-17 football team|under-17 team]] at the [[2001 FIFA U-17 World Championship]], but the team failed to progress through the group stage.<ref name=Torres/> In July 2002, he won the [[2002 UEFA European Under-19 Championship]] with the [[Spain national under-19 football team|under-19]] team and was again the only goalscorer in the final.<ref name="Lowe-2007"/> Also, he finished as top scorer and was named player of the tournament.<ref name=Torres/>

===2003–06: Senior debut and early years===

Torres debuted for the [[Spain national football team|Spanish senior squad]] on 6 September 2003 in a [[Exhibition game#Association football|friendly]] against [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]],<ref>{{Cite news|title=Sólo coincidieron en dos partidos|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/2003/11/07/polideportivo/1068182167_850215.html|website=[[Diario AS]]|date=7 November 2003|access-date=19 June 2024|language=es|archive-date=19 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240619120615/https://as.com/masdeporte/2003/11/07/polideportivo/1068182167_850215.html|url-status=live}}</ref> scoring his first goal against [[Italy national football team|Italy]] on 28 April 2004.<ref>{{Cite news|first=Óscar|last=García|title=Valerón y Torres eclipsan a Baggio|url=https://as.com/futbol/2004/04/28/mas_futbol/1083103218_850215.html|newspaper=Diario AS|date=28 April 2024|access-date=19 June 2024|language=es|archive-date=19 June 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240619120617/https://as.com/futbol/2004/04/28/mas_futbol/1083103218_850215.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He was selected for the Spanish squad for [[UEFA Euro 2004]].<ref name=Torres/> After appearing as a late substitute in Spain's first two group games, he started for the deciding game against Portugal.<ref name=Torres/> Spain were losing 1–0 and, towards the end of the game, he hit the post.<ref name=Torres/>

[[File:Fernando Torres Spain.jpg|thumb|upright|Torres celebrating victory with [[Spain national football team|Spain]] at [[UEFA Euro 2008]]]]
Torres scored 7 goals in 11 appearances in [[2006 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|qualifying]] for the 2006 FIFA World Cup,<ref>{{cite web |title=Fernando Torres |url=https://www.fifa.com/fifa-tournaments/players-coaches/people=183864/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906191705/http://www.fifa.com/fifa-tournaments/players-coaches/people=183864/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=6 September 2015 |publisher=FIFA |access-date=13 November 2015}}</ref> making him Spain's top scorer for qualification, including a vital two goals against [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]] and his first international hat-trick against [[San Marino national football team|San Marino]].<ref name=Torres/> At his first ever appearance in a [[FIFA World Cup]] finals at the 2006 World Cup in Germany, Torres scored the final goal in a 4–0 victory over [[Ukraine national football team|Ukraine]] with a volley.<ref name="Spain 4-0 Ukraine">{{cite news|title=Spain 4–0 Ukraine|url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/world_cup_2006/4852902.stm|website=BBC Sport|date=14 June 2006|access-date=18 May 2011|archive-date=11 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220211090538/http://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/world_cup_2006/4852902.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> In the second group match, Torres scored twice against [[Tunisia national football team|Tunisia]], first in the 76th minute to take Spain 2–1 into the lead, and then again from a penalty kick in the 90th.<ref name="Spain - Tunisia">{{cite web |title=Spain – Tunisia|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/archive/germany2006/results/matches/match=97410031/report.html|publisher=FIFA|access-date=18 May 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131017150726/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/archive/germany2006/results/matches/match%3D97410031/report.html |archive-date=17 October 2013 |url-status=dead}}</ref> With three goals, he finished the tournament as Spain's top scorer alongside fellow striker [[David Villa]].<ref name="Top goals">{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/archive/germany2006/statistics/players/topgoals.html |title=Top goals|publisher=FIFA |access-date=11 June 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131213021026/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/archive/germany2006/statistics/players/topgoals.html |archive-date=13 December 2013}}</ref>

===2009–10: World Cup champions===
[[File:El autobús de los campeones - 1.jpg|thumb|left|Torres celebrating with Spain at [[Plaza de España (Madrid)|Plaza de España]] on 12 July 2010 after winning the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]]]]

Torres made his 60th appearance for Spain in a 2010 World Cup qualification victory over [[Turkey national football team|Turkey]] on 28 March 2009, becoming the youngest player to reach this milestone.<ref>{{cite news |title=España vence a una digna Turquía en el partido 60 de Torres con la Selección absoluta (1–0) |url=http://www.fernando9torres.com/index.php?p=3095 |publisher=Fernando Torres |language=es |date=28 March 2009 |access-date=31 March 2009 |archive-date=11 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220211070301/https://www.fernando9torres.com/index.php?p=3095 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Torres was named in Spain's team for the [[2009 FIFA Confederations Cup]] in June.<ref>{{cite news |title=Spain unveils Confederations Cup roster |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/spain-unveils-confederations-cup-roster-1.805052 |website=CBC Sports |date=1 June 2009 |access-date=5 August 2014 |archive-date=12 March 2022 Spain after 17 minutes into a Confederations Cup match against [[New Zealand men's national football team|New Zealand]] on 14 June,<ref name="Spain 5-0 New Zealand">{{cite news |first=Peter |last=Scrivener |title=Spain 5–0 New Zealand |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/internationals/8095578.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=14 June 2009 |access-date=18 May 2011 the fastest hat-trick by a player for Spain.<ref>{{cite news |first1=R. |last1=Mollina |first2=T. |last2=Campos |title=Torres logra el 'hat trick' más rápido de la historia de la selección |url=https://www.marca.com/2009/06/14/futbol/copa_confederaciones/espana/1245009872.html |newspaper=Marca |location=Madrid |date=14 June 2009 |access-date=14 June 2009 |language=es |archive-date=11 as they were defeated 2–0 by the [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]] in the semi-final,<ref name="Spain 0-2 United States">{{cite news |first=Saj |last=Chowdhury |title=Spain Having undergone knee surgery on 18 April 2010, and missing the end of the Premier League season, Torres's rehabilitation and fitness was closely monitored by Spain manager [[Vicente del Bosque]].<ref name="Liverpool's Fernando Torres out for rest of season"/> Although still out injured, Torres was selected for Spain's [[2010 FIFA World Cup]] squad in May.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/world_cup_2010/8695232.stm |title=Spain omit Marcos Senna from 2010 World Cup squad |website=BBC Sport |date=20 May 2010 |access-date=18 May 2011 |archive-date=11 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220211090525/http://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/world_cup_2010/8695232.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> On 8 June, Torres made his first appearance on the field in exactly two months, coming on as a substitute on 66 minutes against [[Poland national football team|Poland]] in a pre-World Cup friendly.<ref>{{cite news |title=World Cup 2010 – Torres helps Spain rout Poland |url=https://uk.sports.yahoo.com/09062010/58/world-cup-2010-torres-helps-spain-rout-poland.html |website=Yahoo! ==Style of play==
Torres was described as having "an eye for the spectacular" and being "capable of world-class skill", as well as being regarded as a "technically proficient, highly successful striker".<ref>{{cite web |title=Profile |url=http://espnfc.com/player/_/id/24257/fernando-jose-torres-sanz?cc=5739 |website=ESPN FC |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140104081852/http://espnfc.com/player/_/id/24257/fernando-jose-torres-sanz?cc=5739 |archive-date=4 January 2014}}</ref> He had the ability to find open spaces and capitalize on defensive errors.<ref>{{cite news |first=Ed |last=Wyman |title=The 25 Best Premier League Speedsters: Ashley Cole, Fernando Torres, Gareth Bale and More: Fernando Torres |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/530379-the-25-best-fast-premier-league-players-cole-torres-bale-and-more |website=Bleacher Report |publisher=Turner |date=6 December 2010 |access-date=13 November 2015 |archive-date=13 November 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151113162223/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/530379-the-25-best-fast-premier-league-players-cole-torres-bale-and-more/page/19 |url-status=live }}</ref> A hard-working striker, Torres was known for chasing down and putting pressure on opposing defenders. He was also capable of creating chances for other attackers; this also saw him being deployed in a deeper role as a [[second striker]] on occasion.<ref name="Smith-2010"/><ref>{{cite news |first=Ben |last=Welch |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/performance/training/torres-art-striking |title=Torres on the art of striking |website=FourFourTwo |access-date=24 June 2017 |archive-date=17 September 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170917214010/https://www.fourfourtwo.com/performance/training/torres-art-striking |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espnfc.us/blog/tactics-and-analysis/67/post/1839585/torres-on-evolutionary-path |title=Torres on evolutionary path |website=ESPN FC |first=Richard |last=Jolly |date=8 December 2012 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2015/apr/14/fernando-torres-atletico-madrid-real-champions-league-quarter-final-first-leg |title=Atlético's Fernando Torres happy with cameo role as Real |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/chelsea-2-bayer-leverkusen-0-fernando-torres-shows-unselfish-streak-in-creative-role-bkq0nt8f2q3 |url-status=live }}{{subscription required}}</ref>

Due to his consistent goalscoring as a young player, Torres was nicknamed ''El Niño'' ('The Kid').<ref name="www.sports-king.com" /> He could score with his head and both feet. In his prime (2007–2010), his prolific goalscoring earned him a reputation as the best striker in the world at that time.<ref>{{cite web |date=17 April 2009 |title=Torres sogna l'Italia: Inter, Juve e Milan alla finestra |url=http://sport.sky.it/calcio/2009/04/17/Torres_sogna_Italia.html |access-date=16 March 2017 |website=Sky Sport |language=it |archive-date=26 November 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201126020322/https://sport.sky.it/calcio/2009/04/17/Torres_sogna_Italia.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Wilson |first=Steve |date=1 October 2009 |title=Torres, Drogba or Rooney – who's the best? |website=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/blogs/stevewilson/2009/10/torres_drogba_or_rooney_who_wo.html |access-date=16 March 2017 |archive-date=8 April 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220408112430/https://www.bbc.co.uk/blogs/stevewilson/2009/10/torres_drogba_or_rooney_who_wo.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=25 May 2004 |title=Fernando Torres |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/euro_2004/spain/players_to_watch/3594045.stm |access-date=18 May 2020 |publisher=BBC Sport |archive-date=8 April 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220408112437/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/euro_2004/spain/players_to_watch/3594045.stm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="www.goal.com" /> Prior to the 2009 Confederations Cup, the ''[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation|CBC]]'' described him as: "The golden boy of Spanish soccer and one of the most dangerous forwards in the game. Nicknamed El Niño (The Kid), Torres is coming off a solid second season for Liverpool in which he scored 14 goals. Torres is lightning quick, a deadly finisher and a player of such high class with the ball at his feet that he routinely makes the spectacular look ordinary."<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/spain-group-a-1.841307 |title=SPAIN - GROUP A |work=CBC |date=1 June 2009 |access-date=17 May 2020 |archive-date=18 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200818233215/https://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/spain-group-a-1.841307 |url-status=live }}</ref> However, Torres lost most of his pace and form in later seasons due to injuries.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/9088027/what-went-wrong |title=What went wrong? |website=Sky Sports |first=Peter |last=Fraser |date=28 December 2013 |access-date=16 March 2017 |archive-date=14 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220214235945/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/9088027/what-went-wrong |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/blogs/philmcnulty/2011/09/can_50m_striker_torres_recaptu.html |title=Can £50m Striker Torres Recapture His Golden Form? |website=BBC Sport |first=Phil |last=McNulty |date=16 September 2011 |access-date=16 March 2017 |archive-date=11 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220211072233/https://www.bbc.co.uk/blogs/philmcnulty/2011/09/can_50m_striker_torres_recaptu.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.espnfc.us/club/atletico-madrid/1068/blog/post/2283469/should-torres-or-mandzukic-complete-simeones-atletico-strike-duo |title=Should Torres or Mandzukic complete Simeone's Atletico strike duo? |website=ESPN FC |first=Lee |last=Roden |date=6 February 2015 |access-date=17 March 2017 |archive-date=10 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190410201849/http://www.espnfc.us/club/atletico-madrid/1068/blog/post/2283469/should-torres-or-mandzukic-complete-simeones-atletico-strike-duo |url-status=live }}</ref>
