====2015–16 season====
[[File:De Gea (ManUtd).jpg|thumb|upright|De Gea playing for Manchester United in 2016]]

On 7 August 2015, Manchester United manager Louis van Gaal confirmed that De Gea would not be considered for selection for United's Premier League opener against Tottenham the following day, due to the uncertainty surrounding his future.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/33816902 |title=Man Utd: David De Gea not the same as last season – Van Gaal |website=BBC Sport |date=7 August 2015 |access-date=8 August 2015}}</ref> On 13 August, Van Gaal revealed that De Gea had requested to goalkeeping coach [[Frans Hoek]] that he be left out of the team.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Jolly|first1=Richard|title=Louis van Gaal says David De Gea agreed to be left out against Spurs|url=http://www.espnfc.com/barclays-premier-league/story/2562108/van-gaal-says-david-de-gea-agreed-to-sit-vs-tottenham|website=ESPN FC |access-date=14 August 2015|date=13 August 2015}}</ref> De Gea claimed he never expressed a desire not to play, but trained with the reserves soon after.<ref>{{cite web|last=Roan|first=Dan|title=Man Utd: David De Gea is surprised at being left out|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33935204|website=BBC Sport|access-date=14 August 2015|date=14 August 2015}}</ref> On 31 August, after a summer of speculation, an agreement for a transfer was reached between Manchester United and Real Madrid worth £29 million, including the part-exchange of fellow goalkeeper [[Keylor Navas]]. The deal, however, collapsed due to paperwork not being submitted before the transfer window in Spain closed.<ref>{{cite news |title=David De Gea: Man Utd deny blame for failed Real Madrid deal |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34117354 |website=BBC Sport |date=1 September 2015}}</ref> After the transfer window closed, Spanish head coach Vicente del Bosque admitted that it would be difficult for him to select De Gea in Spain's European Championship squad if Manchester United continued not to select him.<ref>{{cite news |title=Vicente del Bosque warns David de Gea over Euro 2016 spot |url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/9976084/vicente-del-bosque-david-de-gea-must-play-to-earn-place-in-spain-squad |website=Sky Sports |date=2 September 2015 |access-date=11 September 2015}}</ref>

On 11 September, De Gea signed a new four-year deal with Manchester United, with an option to extend it for a further year.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Football-News/2015/Sep/David-De-Gea-signs-new-contract-at-Manchester-United.aspx |title=De Gea signs new United contract |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=11 September 2015}}</ref> Twelve days later, in the third round of the League Cup, De Gea [[captain (association football)|captained]] Manchester United for the first time, wearing the armband for the final nine minutes of their win over [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Richard|last=Jolly|date=24 September 2015|title=David De Gea 'proud' to captain Man United after Real Madrid transfer saga|access-date=13 January 2016|url=http://www.espnfc.co.uk/manchester-united/story/2629446/david-de-gea-proud-to-captain-man-utd-after-real-madrid-saga|publisher=ESPN FC}}</ref> In April 2016, while leading the race for the Premier League Golden Glove with 14 clean sheets, De Gea was the sole Manchester United player named in the PFA Team of the Year.<ref>{{cite news|title=PFA awards: Leicester and Spurs dominate Premier League team|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36106596|access-date=21 April 2016|website=BBC Sport|date=21 April 2016}}</ref> On 23 April, in a 2–1 win over Everton in the FA Cup semi-finals, he saved a penalty from [[Romelu Lukaku]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Wilson|first1=Paul|title=Anthony Martial takes Manchester United past Everton to final at the last|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/apr/23/everton-manchester-united-fa-cup-match-report|access-date=23 April 2016|newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=23 April 2016}}</ref>

In May 2016, De Gea became the first player ever to win Manchester United's Player of the Year for a third consecutive season.<ref>{{cite news|title=David de Gea wins Manchester United Player of the Year for record third time|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11667/10267586/david-de-gea-wins-manchester-united-award-for-record-third-time|access-date=18 May 2016|website=Sky Sports|date=3 May 2016}}</ref> During the same month, he also won BBC ''Match of the Day'' Save of the Season for the third consecutive year, for his save against [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] on 21 November 2015.<ref>{{cite news|title=BBC MOTD Save of the Season|work=BBC Sport |date=8 May 2016 |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/live/football/36230500|access-date=18 May 2016}}</ref> In the last league match of the season, a 3–1 win over [[AFC Bournemouth]], De Gea was denied the chance to share the Premier League Golden Glove with Arsenal's [[Petr Čech]] due to a stoppage-time own goal by [[Chris Smalling]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Petr Cech wins Premier League Golden Glove award|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/10286338/petr-cech-wins-premier-league-golden-glove-award|access-date=18 May 2016|website=Sky Sports|date=18 May 2016}}</ref>

====2016–17 season====
Under new Manchester United manager [[José Mourinho]], De Gea made his first appearance of the season in the [[2016 FA Community Shield|FA Community Shield]] against Premier League winners [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]]. The match ended in a 2–1 victory for United.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/36934956|title=Jose Mourinho began his reign as Manchester United manager with a trophy |website=BBC Sport |date=7 August 2016}}</ref> De Gea started the Premier League season by keeping 2 clean sheets in his first 3 games against [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] and [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.premierleague.com/results?co=1&se=54&cl=12|title=Premier League Football Scores, Results & Season Archives|publisher=Premier League |access-date=14 August 2019}}</ref> De Gea was part of the Manchester United team which lost 4–0 to [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], their heaviest Premier League defeat since the 6–1 loss against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in October 2011.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/37670362|title=Chelsea 4-0 Manchester United|publisher=BBC Sport|date=23 October 2016|access-date=14 August 2019}}</ref> On 26 February 2017, he won his first [[EFL Cup]] title after a 3–2 victory over Southampton in the [[2017 EFL Cup final|final]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/feb/26/manchester-united-southampton-efl-cup-final-match-report|title=Ibrahimovic takes Manchester United to EFL Cup final win over Southampton|work=The Guardian|date=26 February 2017}}</ref>

On 20 April 2017, De Gea was selected as a goalkeeper in the PFA Team of the Year for the fourth time in his career.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/chelsea-tottenham-dominate-pfa-premier-league-team-year|title=Chelsea, Tottenham dominate PFA Premier League Team of the Year|date=20 April 2017|magazine=FourFourTwo}}</ref> On 24 May, he won his third trophy of the season, as Manchester United beat [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] 2–0 in the [[2017 UEFA Europa League final|Europa League final]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.manutd.com/en/videos/detail/highlights-of-2017-europa-league-final-man-utd-2-ajax-0|title=Highlights of 2017 Europa League final Man Utd 2 Ajax 0|publisher=Manchester United|date=May 2017}}</ref> despite being an unused substitute to [[Sergio Romero]] in that match.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://beinsports.com/en-us/soccer/premier-league/articles/david-de-gea-wont-play-europa-league-final-co|title=David De Gea Won't Play Europa League Final Confirms Jose Mourinho|publisher=beIN SPORTS|date=12 May 2017}}</ref>

====2017–18 season====
[[File:Manchester United v Leicester City, 26 August 2017 (09).JPG|thumb|De Gea (in black) playing for Manchester United in 2017]]

On 17 September 2017, at the fifth match of the Premier League against [[Everton F.C.|Everton]], De Gea made his fourth clean sheet of the season and 100th overall for Manchester United.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Features/2017/Sept/Video-David-De-Gea-reaches-century-of-clean-sheets-for-Manchester-United.aspx |title=David De Gea's Century of Clean Sheets |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=17 September 2017 |access-date=18 September 2017 |last=Higgins |first=Adam}}</ref>

On 2 December 2017, in a 3–1 win over [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], De Gea recorded 14 saves and equalled the mark that was shared by [[Tim Krul]] and [[Vito Mannone]] as the Premier League record for the greatest number of saves in a single game and he also won the Man of the Match award.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/de-gea-equals-record-for-most-saves-in-a-premier-league-game/a4e0puwgjqfa1r8jh881rzla6|title=De Gea equals record for most saves in a Premier League game|website=Goal.com|date= 2 December 2017|access-date=25 May 2018}}</ref>

On 18 April 2018, De Gea was selected as a goalkeeper in the PFA Team of the Year for the fifth time as the only Manchester United player.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/de-gea-equals-record-for-most-saves-in-a-premier-league-game/a4e0puwgjqfa1r8jh881rzla6|title=De Gea equals record for most saves in a Premier League game|website=Goal.com|date=2 December 2017|access-date=2 December 2017|last=Vertelney|first=Seth}}</ref>

On 11 May 2018, after a 0–0 draw against West Ham, De Gea earned his 18th clean sheet of the season and also secured his first [[Premier League Golden Glove]] since he joined Manchester United in 2011.<ref>{{cite news|title=Manchester United goalkeeper David De Gea dedicates Golden Glove award to teammates|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37553778/manchester-united-goalkeeper-david-de-gea-dedicates-golden-glove-award-teammates|work=ESPN|date=10 May 2018}}</ref>

====2018–19 season====
The 2018–19 season began with De Gea keeping just five clean sheets in his first 25 appearances. The start of 2019, however, saw him manage the same number in just eight appearances, including a 1–0 win over [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] on 13 January 2019, in which he made 11 saves to keep Spurs off the scoresheet, the second most by a goalkeeper in any one Premier League match, behind only his 14 saves against Arsenal a year earlier.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tottenham vs Manchester United: David de Gea puts his best foot forward to reach new heights |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/tottenham-hotspur-vs-manchester-united-result-final-score-david-de-gea-saves-video-epl-a8726441.html |newspaper=The Independent |date=14 January 2019 |access-date=25 February 2019}}</ref> His clean sheet against Liverpool on 24 February was his 100th for Manchester United in the Premier League, making him the seventh goalkeeper to reach that milestone for a single club in the competition and the second for Manchester United after Peter Schmeichel.<ref>{{cite news |first=Chris |last=Bevan |title=Liverpool held to goalless draw by injury-hit Man United |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47268878 |website=BBC Sport |date=24 February 2019 |access-date=25 February 2019}}</ref> In March and April, De Gea suffered a run of poor form; being criticised by fans and pundits for mistakes made in losses to [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/what-the-hell-was-flappy-hands-doing-de-gea-ridiculed-after/18cyu9crvu6311tsvztjiukx4p|title=David de Gea mistake vs Arsenal: 'What the hell was flappy hands doing?' - Man Utd goalkeeper ridiculed after howler from Granit Xhaka's shot | Goal.com|website=Goal.com}}</ref> [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://metro.co.uk/2019/04/17/barcelona-fans-mocked-david-de-gea-howler-camp-nou-9225866/|title=How Barcelona fans mocked David De Gea after howler at the Camp Nou|date=17 April 2019|newspaper=Metro|access-date=28 April 2019}}</ref> [[Everton F.C.|Everton]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://metro.co.uk/2019/04/21/paul-robinson-questions-david-de-gea-man-uniteds-4-0-thrashing-everton-9281538/|title=Paul Robinson questions David De Gea after Man United's 4-0 thrashing by Everton|date=21 April 2019|newspaper=Metro|access-date=28 April 2019}}</ref> [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/manchester-derby-player-ratings-bernardo-14576715|title=Manchester Derby player ratings from City victory at Old Trafford|last=McDonnell|first=David|date=24 April 2019|newspaper=Daily Mirror|access-date=28 April 2019}}</ref> and a 1–1 draw against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.express.co.uk/sport/football/1120129/Man-Utd-David-de-Gea-error-fans-Old-Trafford-Chelsea-top-four|title=What Man Utd fans did as David de Gea walked off Old Trafford pitch after Chelsea error|last=Powers|first=Adam|date=28 April 2019|newspaper=Daily Expres|access-date=28 April 2019}}</ref> De Gea ended the season with just 7 clean sheets in 38 Premier League appearances,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://footystats.org/players/spain/david-de-gea|title=David de Gea - Clean Sheets & Stats|website=footystats.org|access-date=13 August 2019}}</ref> his lowest tally during his time at Manchester United, and kept only 10 clean sheets all season for the club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.stretford-end.com/2019/06/2018-19-season-ending-player-review-david-de-gea/|title=2018-19 Season Ending Player Review: David De Gea|last=Aravena|first=Juan Pablo|date=25 June 2019|website=Stretty Rant|access-date=13 August 2019}}</ref>

====2019–20 season====
On 3 July 2019, ahead of the 2019–20 season, De Gea was offered a new contract.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48854483|title=David de Gea: Man Utd offer improved new deal to stay|date=3 July 2019|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> By 15 July 2019, the negotiations were ongoing.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48996919|title=David de Gea: Man Utd talks continue over goalkeeper's long-term future|date=15 July 2019|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 11 August 2019, De Gea started in Manchester United's opening Premier League match against Chelsea and kept his first clean sheet of the season, as United beat Chelsea 4–0.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/11782873/manchester-united-4-0-chelsea-frank-lampard-thrashed-on-pl-managerial-debut|title=Manchester United 4-0 Chelsea: Frank Lampard thrashed on PL managerial debut|website=Sky Sports|access-date=13 August 2019}}</ref> On 16 September 2019, Manchester United confirmed that De Gea had signed a four-year contract renewal, keeping him at the club until at least June 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/David-De-Gea-signs-new-contract-with-Manchester-United|title=David De Gea signs new long-term contract at Man Utd|publisher=Manchester United F.C.}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49719629|title=David de Gea: Manchester United goalkeeper signs new deal at Old Trafford|date=16 September 2019|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

In October 2019 he became an injury doubt for the [[Liverpool F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry|North-West derby]] after being injured in a game for [[Spain men's national football team|Spain]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50064128|title=David de Gea: Injured keeper a doubt for Man Utd v Liverpool|date=15 October 2019|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> Despite this, De Gea started the game which ended in a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |authorlink= Phil McNulty |title=Man Utd 1-1 Liverpool: Adam Lallana saves Reds' unbeaten start |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50030956 |website=BBC Sport |date=20 October 2019 |access-date=5 March 2021}}</ref>

In Manchester United's first game after the [[2019–20 Premier League#Effects of the COVID-19 pandemic|break in the season enforced by COVID-19]] against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]], De Gea made an error leading to a goal that cost United the win.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2020/06/19/tottenham-vs-man-united-premier-league-live-score-latest-goal/|title=Bruno Fernandes atones for David de Gea's error as Manchester United salvage point at Tottenham|first=Rob|last=Bagchi|date=19 June 2020|newspaper=The Daily Telegraph}}</ref> This came after a series of errors earlier in the season against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/11793173/manchester-united-1-2-crystal-palace-david-de-gea-error-costs-hosts|title=Manchester United 1-2 Crystal Palace: David de Gea error costs hosts|website=Sky Sports}}</ref> [[Watford F.C.|Watford]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://talksport.com/football/646641/david-de-gea-mistake-watford-goal-manchester-united-clean-sheet/|title=De Gea shows Christmas spirit by gifting Watford opening goal with howler |publisher=talkSPORT |date=22 December 2019}}</ref> and [[Everton F.C.|Everton]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://talksport.com/football/676979/david-de-gea-arrogant-man-united-goalkeeper-mistake-everton/|title='David de Gea is arrogant' - Man United keeper slammed after latest big blunder |publisher=talkSPORT |date=2 March 2020}}</ref> This error spell, like last season, resulted in calls from fans for [[Dean Henderson]] to be made Manchester United's first choice goalkeeper. Manager [[Ole Gunnar Solskjær]] backed De Gea saying, "one day [Henderson will] be England's and United's Number 1" but that De Gea was currently "the best goalkeeper in the world".<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.theguardian.com/football/2020/jun/23/solskjaer-de-gea-worlds-best-dean-henderson-future-manchester-united-england-no1|title=Manchester United 'not too far away' from title contention, says Solskjær|date=23 June 2020|newspaper=The Guardian}}</ref> However, de Gea continued his error-prone season in United's [[2019–20 FA Cup#Semi-finals|FA Cup Semi-final]] tie against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], where he was directly responsible for one of the goals in a 3–1 defeat.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.theguardian.com/football/2020/jul/19/de-geas-decline-continues-as-uniteds-fa-cup-chance-evades-his-grasp|title=De Gea's decline continues as United's FA Cup chance evades his grasp|first=Jonathan|last=Wilson|authorlink=Jonathan Wilson (writer)|date=19 July 2020|newspaper=The Guardian}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53467353|title='Solskjaer says De Gea is best in world - he's not even best in Manchester'|work=BBC Sport }}</ref> This came one week after reaching a number of landmarks and records for United including becoming the most capped non-British or Irish player to play for United, achieved on 9 July, and reaching 400 appearances for the club on 13 July.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/the-best-david-de-gea-stats-as-he-reaches-400-appearances|title=The best David De Gea stats as he reaches 400 appearances|publisher=Manchester United F.C.}}</ref> On 16 July 2020, he also kept his 112th PL clean sheet against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]], equalling [[Peter Schmeichel]]'s club record in the top flight.<ref>{{cite web |date=17 July 2020 |title=Manchester United goalkeeper David de Gea equals Peter Schmeichel's clean sheet record as Red Devils continue remarkable away form |url=https://talksport.com/football/733667/manchester-united-david-de-gea-peter-schmeichel-clean-sheet-record/ |access-date=17 July 2020 |publisher=talkSPORT}}</ref> On the last day of Premier League, De Gea kept his 113th PL clean sheet against [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] and surpassed Schmeichel's record.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Carney |first=Sam |date=26 July 2020 |title=The best stats from the King Power Stadium |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/the-best-stats-after-man-utd-beat-leicester-to-secure-top-four-spot |access-date=28 July 2020 |publisher=Manchester United F.C.}}</ref>

==== 2020–21 season ====
The return of [[Dean Henderson]] from an extended loan spell at [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] meant De Gea went into the [[2020–21 Manchester United F.C. season|2020–21 season]] with a true competitor for Manchester United's number 1 jersey for the first time since joining the club.<ref>{{cite news |first=Andy |last=Hunter |title=Dean Henderson aiming to oust David de Gea as Manchester United's keeper |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2020/sep/02/dean-henderson-oust-david-de-gea-manchester-united-keeper |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=2 September 2020 |access-date=10 May 2021}}</ref> De Gea began the season as first-choice, missing just two of the club's first 26 league matches: he was left out of the squad for the match against [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] on 5 December 2020 after aggravating an injury suffered in the club's previous league game against [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]],<ref>{{cite news |first=Lars Magnus |last=Igland Røys |title=Ole explains De Gea absence |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/ole-gunnar-solskjaer-explains-david-de-gea-injury-pre-west-ham-v-man-utd-5-december-2020 |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=5 December 2020 |access-date=10 May 2021}}</ref> while Henderson was preferred against Sheffield United on 17 December.<ref>{{cite news |first=Joe |last=Ganley |title=Ole: Why I selected Henderson over De Gea |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/ole-gunnar-solskjaer-explains-why-dean-henderson-was-selected-to-start-against-sheffield-united |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=17 December 2020 |access-date=10 May 2021}}</ref> On 2 February 2021, De Gea played the full 90 minutes and kept a clean sheet in Manchester United's Premier League record-equalling [[Manchester United F.C. 9–0 Southampton F.C.|9–0]] home win against [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]].<ref>{{Cite news|first=Simon|last=Stone|title=Man Utd beat nine-man Southampton 9-0|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55806211|website=BBC Sport|date=2 February 2021|access-date=3 February 2021}}</ref>

De Gea also started five of Manchester United's six Champions League group matches, but after the team finished third in their group and dropped down to the Europa League, Henderson was preferred in goal for the Europa League knockout phase. At the start of March 2021, De Gea returned to Spain for the birth of his first child, which meant Henderson was able to take over as first-choice goalkeeper in the league and De Gea started to be preferred in the Europa League; he kept clean sheets in the two matches against [[Granada CF|Granada]] in the quarter-finals, and on 6 May, he made nine saves in a 3–2 away defeat to [[AS Roma|Roma]] in the second leg of UEFA Europa league semi-final, as United progressed to the final with an 8–5 aggregate victory.<ref>{{Cite news|date=6 May 2021|title=Edinson Cavani sends Manchester United into final despite Roma scare|url=http://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/may/06/roma-manchester-united-europa-league-semi-final-second-leg-match-report|access-date=10 May 2021|newspaper=The Guardian}}</ref> On 26 May, in the [[2021 UEFA Europa League final]], De Gea missed his team's last penalty in an 11–10 [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] defeat after the match finished 1–1 after [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]] to hand Spanish side [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] their first ever European title.<ref name="2021 Europa League Final summary">{{cite web |title=Full Time Summary Final – Villarreal v Manchester United |url=https://www.uefa.com/newsfiles/uefacup/2021/2029909_fr.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210526220616/https://www.uefa.com/newsfiles/uefacup/2021/2029909_fr.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=26 May 2021 |publisher=UEFA |access-date=26 May 2021}}</ref>

====2021–22 season====
[[File:Manchester United v Everton, 7 August 2021 (27).jpg|thumb|left|De Gea playing for Manchester United in 2021|234x234px]]
De Gea started the league season against [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]], in which he conceded a goal in a 5–1 home win.<ref>{{cite news |first=Simon |last=Stone |title=Manchester United 5–1 Leeds United: Bruno Fernandes hat-trick earns hosts thumping win |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58124893 |website=BBC Sport |date=14 August 2021 |access-date=14 August 2021 }}</ref> He earned his first clean sheet of the season in a 1–0 win against [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Neil |last=Johnston |title=Wolverhampton Wanderers 0-1 Manchester United: Mason Greenwood hits winner |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58295875 |website=BBC Sport |date=29 August 2021 |access-date=29 August 2021 }}</ref> In the fifth gameweek of the season, De Gea saved his first penalty for Manchester United since a 2016 [[FA Cup]] tie against [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] as he denied [[Mark Noble]] of [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] from the spot in the last action of the game, ensuring a 2–1 victory for the Reds after a late goal from [[Jesse Lingard]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Rob |last=Smyth |title=West Ham v Manchester United: Premier League - Live! |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2021/sep/19/west-ham-united-v-manchester-united-premier-league-live |website=The Guardian |date=19 September 2021 |access-date=19 September 2021 }}</ref>

====2022–23 season====
[[File:De Gea Man United v Brighton (cropped).jpg|thumb|265x265px|De Gea playing for Manchester United in 2022]]
On 16 October 2022, he played his 500th match for Manchester United in all competitions, in a goalless draw against [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Cristiano Ronaldo and David De Gea to be honoured prior to Newcastle game |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/cristiano-ronaldo-and-david-de-gea-to-be-honoured-prior-to-newcastle-game |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=16 October 2022 |access-date=6 November 2022 }}</ref> On 12 February 2023, he played his 400th Premier League match for Manchester United, with no non-British player making more for one club.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Burton |first=Chris |date=12 February 2023 |title=Man Utd goalkeeper David de Gea makes history with 400th Premier League appearance |url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/man-utd-goalkeeper-david-de-gea-history-400-premier-league-appearance/blt7fe1c63d672573c3 |access-date=12 February 2023 |website=Goal}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=12 February 2023 |title=De Gea makes 400th Premier League appearance |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/david-de-gea-makes-400th-premier-league-appearance-in-leeds-game |access-date=12 February 2023 |publisher=Manchester United F.C.}}</ref> On 26 February, he broke [[Peter Schmeichel]]'s record for the most clean sheets in Manchester United's history, after a 2–0 win over Newcastle United in the [[2023 EFL Cup final]] marked his 181st.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/david-de-gea-breaks-peter-schmeichels-clean-sheet-record-26-february-2023|title=De Gea breaks record|publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=26 February 2023|access-date=26 February 2023|language=en}}</ref> On 20 May, he won the [[Premier League Golden Glove]] for the first time since the 2017–18 season.<ref>{{Cite web |author=The Athletic Staff |title=De Gea wins Premier League Golden Glove award |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4537460/2023/05/20/de-gea-premier-league-golden-glove/ |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=The Athletic |date=20 May 2023 |language=en}}</ref> On 3 June, he played his last match for Manchester United in a 2–1 defeat against Manchester City in the [[2023 FA Cup final|FA Cup final]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://talksport.com/football/fa-cup/1444860/david-de-gea-gundogan-goal-fa-cup-man-utd-fans/ |title=Manchester United fans blame David de Gea for goal which lost FA Cup in possible last appearance |publisher=talkSPORT |date=3 June 2023 }}</ref>

De Gea's contract at Manchester United expired on 1 July 2023 as negotiations over a new contract broke down, leaving him a free agent while discussions continued.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Man Utd keeper De Gea becomes free agent |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66053069 |access-date=2023-06-30}}</ref> His departure from the club was confirmed on 8 July 2023.<ref>{{cite news|title=De Gea departs Manchester United |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/david-de-gea-leaves-man-utd-after-12-years-as-number-one-goalkeeper-8-july-2023 |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=8 July 2023 |access-date=8 July 2023 }}</ref> De Gea left Manchester United as their seventh all-time appearance maker, having played in 545 games in all competitions for the club.<ref>{{cite news|title=De Gea confirms Man United departure after 12 years at club |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/story/_/id/37978521/de-gea-confirms-man-united-departure-12-years-club |publisher=ESPN |date=8 July 2023 |access-date=8 July 2023 }}</ref> At the time of his departure, he became the last player from the [[History of Manchester United F.C. (1986–2013)|Sir Alex Ferguson era]] to leave Manchester United.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/david-de-gea-manchester-united-ferguson-b2372488.html|title=David de Gea, Sir Alex Ferguson's last player, ends 88 years of Manchester United history|date=10 July 2023|work=[[The Independent]]}}</ref> However, the club would re-sign former defender and Premier League winner [[Jonny Evans]] that same summer, meaning this was no longer the case.

===Fiorentina===
After spending the entirety of the 2023–24 season as a free agent, on 9 August 2024, De Gea signed for [[Serie A]] club [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.acffiorentina.com/en/news/all/news-men-first-team/2024-08-09/de-gea-signs-for-fiorentina|title=De Gea signs for Fiorentina|website=ACF Fiorentina|date=9 August 2024|accessdate=9 August 2024}}</ref> On 22 August, he made his debut for the club in a 3–3 draw against [[Puskás Akadémia FC|Puskás Akadémia]] in the [[2024–25 UEFA Conference League qualifying phase and play-off round#Play-off round|2024–25 UEFA Conference League play-off round]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.acffiorentina.com/en/news/all/news-men-first-team/2024-08-22/full-time-fiorentina-3-3-puskas|title=FULL TIME: Fiorentina 3-3 Puskas|website=ACF Fiorentina|date=22 August 2024|accessdate=23 August 2024}}</ref> Later that year, on 6 October, he saved two penalty kicks, securing a 2–1 win over [[AC Milan]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-07 |title=Former United Goalkeeper David De Gea Shines At New Club Fiorentina - Simple Football |url=https://fotbalsimplu.com/former-united-goalkeeper-david-de-gea-shines-at-new-club-fiorentina/ |access-date=2024-10-07 |website=fotbalsimplu.com |language=en-US |archive-date=7 October 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241007110048/https://fotbalsimplu.com/former-united-goalkeeper-david-de-gea-shines-at-new-club-fiorentina/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> On 31 May 2025, De Gea signed a new contract with Fiorentina, keeping him at the club until 2028.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-31 |title= David de Gea agrees new long-term Fiorentina deal |url= https://www.tribalfootball.com/article/soccer-serie-a-david-de-gea-agrees-new-long-term-fiorentina-deal-08c5d3fb-86c1-4c6b-a948-89ffec2aacd1 |website=Tribal Football |language=en-US}}</ref>

==International career ==
===Youth===
[[File:David de Gea at the UEFA European Under-21 Football Championship - 20110622.jpg|thumb|right|De Gea with [[Spain national under-21 football team|Spain U21]] in 2011|190x190px]]
De Gea helped [[Spain national under-17 football team|Spain's under-17 team]] win the [[2007 UEFA European Under-17 Football Championship|2007 European Championship]],<ref>[http://archivo.marca.com/edicion/marca/futbol/seleccion/es/desarrollo/992385.html La selección española sub'17 se proclama campeona de Europa] [The Spain under-17 team is proclaimed European champion], Marca (in Spanish), 13 May 2007</ref><ref name="destiny">{{cite news |last=Bandini |first=Nicky |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2011/may/25/david-de-gea-manchester-united |title=The 'New van der Sar' fulfils his destiny |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |date=25 May 2011 |access-date=25 May 2011}}</ref> and finish second at the [[2007 FIFA U-17 World Cup|2007 World Cup]].<ref name="factfile"/> In early May 2010, courtesy of solid Atlético performances, he was named by senior squad manager [[Vicente del Bosque]] in a provisional 30-man squad for the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]];<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.marca.com/2010/05/10/futbol/seleccion/1273509662.html |title=Valdés, De Gea, Azpilicueta, Javi Martínez y Pedro entran en la preselección de 30 |trans-title=Valdés, De Gea, Azpilicueta, Javi Martinez and Pedro are short listed 30 |date=10 May 2010 |access-date=16 December 2014 |newspaper=Marca|location=Madrid |language=es}}</ref> however, he did not make the final cut.<ref name="factfile"/> In 2011, he was part of the [[Spain national under-21 football team|Spain under-21]] team that won the [[2011 UEFA European Under-21 Championship]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2011/6/29/united-hope-de-gea-will-add-to-keeping-legacy|title=United hope De Gea will add to keeping legacy|date=29 June 2011|access-date=9 April 2024|website=Al Jazeera}}</ref> and was named in UEFA's Squad of the Tournament.<ref name="tott">{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/under21/news/0283-1876f534fb25-e069a027749d-1000--2023-under-21-euro-team-of-the-tournament/|title=2023 Under-21 EURO Team of the Tournament|date=11 July 2023|access-date=9 April 2024|website=UEFA}}</ref>

On 15 May 2012, De Gea was called up to the [[Spanish national football team|Spanish senior team]] for two matches against [[Serbia national football team|Serbia]] and [[China national football team|China]].<ref name="factfile"/> He was in consideration for Del Bosque's [[UEFA Euro 2012|Euro 2012]] squad, but did not make the final 23-man group. He was selected, however, to play at the [[Football at the 2012 Summer Olympics|2012 Summer Olympics]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Euro 2012 trio Mata, Alba & Martinez in Spain Olympic squad |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/olympics/18693622 |website=BBC Sport |date=5 July 2012 |access-date=8 July 2012}}</ref> and played all three matches as the nation was eliminated in the group stage. De Gea was part of the Spain under-21 team that [[2013 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|retained their European title in 2013]] and was named in the Squad of the Tournament for the second time.<ref name="tott"/>

===Senior===
On 13 May 2014, De Gea was selected in Spain's 30-man provisional squad for the [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014 World Cup]], and later made the final squad. He made his first senior international appearance against [[El Salvador national football team|El Salvador]] in a 2–0 friendly victory on 8 June in preparation for the tournament, replacing [[Iker Casillas]] for the last seven minutes of the match at the [[FedExField]] in Washington D.C.<ref>{{cite news |title=El Salvador 0–2 Spain |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27383467|access-date=14 June 2014|website=BBC Sport |date=3 June 2014}}</ref> As third-choice goalkeeper behind Casillas and [[Pepe Reina]], De Gea was the only member of the squad not to feature at that World Cup, in which Spain were eliminated in the [[2014 FIFA World Cup Group B|group stage]].

On 4 September 2014, he made his first start for Spain, playing the whole 90 minutes against [[France national football team|France]] in a friendly match and conceding a goal from [[Loïc Rémy]] to lose 1–0.<ref>{{cite news |title=France beat Spain 1–0 in Paris courtesy of a Loic Remy goal |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/live/match/323819/report |date=4 September 2014 |access-date=12 October 2014|website=Sky Sports}}</ref> He played his first competitive international on his third cap on 12 October, keeping a [[shutout|clean sheet]] in a 4–0 win away to [[Luxembourg national football team|Luxembourg]] in [[UEFA Euro 2016 qualifying Group C|UEFA Euro 2016 qualifying]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=12 October 2014 |title=Luxembourg 0-4 Spain |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/29588735 |access-date=22 September 2023}}</ref>

Many tipped De Gea to succeed Casillas as the long-term number one goalkeeper,<ref name="Future"/><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.espnfc.com/spain/story/2080939/david-de-gea-should-replace-iker-casillas-as-spains-no-1-marca-poll |title=David De Gea should replace Iker Casillas as Spain's No. 1 - Marca poll |date=10 October 2014 |access-date=15 December 2014 |website=ESPN FC}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Balague |first=Guillem |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/12087/9515709/spain-guillem-balague-says-david-de-gea-has-toppled-iker-casillas-as-no-1 |title=David De Gea has toppled Iker Casillas as No. 1 |date=13 October 2014 |access-date=15 December 2014 |website=Sky Sports}}</ref> including Casillas himself.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/casillas-tips-de-gea-greatness |title=Casillas tips De Gea for greatness |date=2 June 2011 |access-date=15 December 2014 |magazine=FourFourTwo}}</ref> On 31 May 2016, he was named to Vicente del Bosque's final [[UEFA Euro 2016 squads#Spain|23-man Spanish squad]] for [[UEFA Euro 2016]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/36416575|title=Euro 2016: Arsenal's Hector Bellerin in Spain squad after injury forces out Dani Carvajal|website=BBC Sport|date=31 May 2016|access-date=1 June 2016}}</ref> He started their opening match against the [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic]] in [[Toulouse]], keeping a clean sheet in a 1–0 [[UEFA Euro 2016 Group D#Spain vs Czech Republic|victory]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Gerard Pique heads late winner as holders Spain edge past Czech Republic|url=http://sport.bt.com/football/euro-2016/gerard-pique-heads-late-winner-as-holders-spain-edge-past-czech-republic-S11364067719337|access-date=13 June 2016|website=BT Sport|date=13 June 2016|archive-date=16 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190416131127/http://sport.bt.com/football/euro-2016/gerard-pique-heads-late-winner-as-holders-spain-edge-past-czech-republic-S11364067719337|url-status=dead}}</ref> He followed up with another clean sheet against [[Turkey national football team|Turkey]] as Spain [[UEFA Euro 2016 Group D#Spain vs Turkey|won]] 3–0.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/live/football/36335617 |title=Spain 3-0 Turkey |website=BBC Sport |first=Tom |last=Rostance |date=17 June 2016 |access-date=9 July 2018}}</ref> The following match, however, he conceded twice to [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]] as his team [[UEFA Euro 2016 Group D#Croatia vs Spain|lost]] 2–1.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/36524210 |title=Croatia 2-1 Spain |website=BBC Sport |first=Mandeep |last=Sanghera |date=21 June 2016 |access-date=9 July 2018}}</ref> Spain was [[UEFA Euro 2016 knockout phase#Italy vs Spain|eliminated]] in the round of 16 on 27 June, with their opponent [[Italy national football team|Italy]] scoring the only two goals of the match.<ref>{{cite news |first=Jim |last=Foulerton |title=Dominant Italy brush aside champions Spain |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0253-0d81b24e0059-7534c6d3e771-1000--dominant-italy-brush-aside-holders-spain-in-euro-2016-first/ |publisher=UEFA |date=27 June 2016 |access-date=27 June 2016}}</ref>
[[File:ESP-RUS (13).jpg|thumb|De Gea with [[Spain men's national football team|Spain]] at the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]]|317x317px]]
On 21 May 2018, De Gea was called up to Spain's squad for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]] in Russia.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2777080-david-de-gea-isco-headline-spains-full-2018-world-cup-provisional-squad-roster|title=David De Gea, Isco Headline Spain's Full 2018 World Cup Provisional Squad Roster|website=Bleacher Report|first=Christopher |last=Simpson|date=21 May 2018|access-date=22 May 2018}}</ref> In Spain's first game of the tournament on 15 June, he was at fault for [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]]'s second goal, letting a [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] shot slip through his grasp; Ronaldo completed a hat-trick during the 3–3 draw, with his first goal coming from a penalty, and his third from a free-kick, which were Portugal's only other shots on target.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-india/news/105/main/2018/06/16/45555222/portugal-3-spain-3-brilliant-ronaldo-hat-trick-earns|title=World Cup report: Portugal 3 Spain 3|access-date=14 January 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/soccer/world-cup/news/spain-vs-portugal-final-score-crazy-draw-as-ronaldo-becomes-oldest-to-score-world-cup-hat-trick/amp/|title=Spain vs. Portugal final score: Crazy draw as Cristiano Ronaldo becomes oldest to score World Cup hat trick|website=cCBS Sports |access-date=16 June 2018}}</ref> In Spain's second group match against [[Iran national football team|Iran]] on 20 June, he kept a clean-sheet in a 1–0 victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/44439093 |title=Iran 0-1 Spain |website=BBC Sport |first=Luke |last=Reddy |date=20 June 2018 |access-date=9 July 2018}}</ref> De Gea continued to struggle in Spain's final group match against [[Morocco national football team|Morocco]] on 25 June, however, which ended in a 2–2 draw;<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/44439235 |title=Spain 2-2 Morocco |website=BBC Sport |first=Mike |last=Whalley |date=25 June 2018 |access-date=9 July 2018}}</ref> his unsteady performances in the group stage drew criticism in the media, who noted that he had only made one save in the tournament.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.marca.com/en/world-cup/2018/06/26/5b320cb0468aeb97738b4620.html |title=De Gea: One save and a thousand doubts |newspaper=Marca |first=Javier |last=Estepa |date=26 June 2018 |access-date=9 July 2018}}</ref> On 1 July, De Gea also failed to make a save during Spain's 4–3 penalty shootout loss to hosts [[Russia national football team|Russia]] in the Round of 16; the match had ended in a 1–1 draw after extra-time, with De Gea being beaten by an [[Artem Dzyuba]] penalty in the first half.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Coleman |first1=Joe |title=ABSOLUTE DISGRACE' Fans turn on Manchester United star David De Gea after shock World Cup exit for Spain |date=July 2018 |url=https://talksport.com/football/393451/spain-manchester-united-david-de-gea-world-cup/ |publisher=talkSPORT |access-date=1 July 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/live/football/43976553 |title=Catch-up: Fifa World Cup - Spain v Russia |website=BBC Sport |first=Stephan |last=Shemilt |date=1 July 2018 |access-date=9 July 2018}}</ref> De Gea ended the tournament having conceded six goals from seven shots on target, excluding the four goals he conceded in the penalty-shootout; with only one save, he recorded fewer saves than any other goalkeeper who had played at least three matches in a single edition of the tournament since [[1966 FIFA World Cup|1966]].<ref name="auto"/> De Gea criticised the [[Adidas Telstar 18]] official match ball, calling it "really strange" and claiming that "it could have been made a lot better."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/worldcup/fifa-world-cup-2018-ball-adidas-telstar-18-football-a-problem-for-goalkeepers-a3864336.html|title=Fifa World Cup 2018 ball: Adidas Telstar 18 football 'a problem for goalkeepers'|newspaper=Evening Standard|first=Jaime|last=Teather|date=15 June 2018|access-date=15 July 2018}}</ref>

On 24 May 2021, De Gea was included in [[Luis Enrique]]'s [[UEFA Euro 2020 squads#Spain|24-man squad]] for [[UEFA Euro 2020]],<ref>{{cite news|date=24 May 2021|title=Spain Euro 2020 squad: The complete line-up for Euro 2020|url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/spain-euro-2020-squad-the-complete-line-up-for-marchs-internationals|access-date=19 November 2021|website=FourFourTwo.com}}</ref> where he served as backup to [[Unai Simón]]. He was later excluded entirely from the Spain [[2022 FIFA World Cup squads#Spain|squad]] for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]], with Simón, [[David Raya]] and [[Robert Sánchez]] selected as the three goalkeepers.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ramos, Thiago, De Gea left out of Spain's World Cup 2022 squad |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2022/11/12/no-ramos-thiago-or-de-gea-as-spain-name-young-world-cup-squad |website=Al Jazeera|date=12 November 2022|access-date=5 February 2023}}</ref>

==Style of play==
[[File:Boutaib goal against De Gea.jpg|thumb|left|221x221px|De Gea making a save with his feet against [[Morocco national football team|Morocco]] at the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]]]]
De Gea was regarded as a promising goalkeeper in his youth.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/de-gea-makes-manchester-united-claim|title=De Gea makes Manchester United claim|website=FourFourTwo|date=10 December 2010|access-date=17 January 2018}}</ref> He later developed into one of the best professional goalkeepers in the world in his prime.<ref name="best in world">{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/manchester-united/11295641/Wayne-Rooney-Man-Utd-can-win-title-with-best-in-world-David-de-Gea.html |title=Wayne Rooney: Man Utd can win title with 'best in world' David de Gea|newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |last=Ogden |first=Mark|date=15 December 2014 |access-date=15 December 2014}}</ref><ref name="best goalkeeper">{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/manchester-united/11294620/David-de-Geas-performance-sparks-best-goalkeeper-in-the-world-debate-but-who-would-you-vote-for.html |title=David de Gea's performance sparks 'best goalkeeper in the world' debate|newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |date=15 December 2014|access-date=15 December 2014}}</ref> De Gea grew up playing futsal as an outfield player until the age of 14. He has incorporated futsal goalkeeping techniques into his playing style, including the use of his feet to make saves.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11667/11621314/david-de-gea8217s-futsal-technique-is-changing-goalkeeping|title=David de Gea's futsal technique is changing goalkeeping|website=Sky Sports|access-date=15 August 2019}}</ref>{{Tone inline|date=April 2026}}

De Gea has been complimented for his reflexes, agility, and is well known for making saves with his feet.<ref name="main man">{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/15115/9745310/the-stats-suggest-david-de-gea-is-manchester-uniteds-main-man-under-louis-van-gaal-this-season|title=The stats suggest David de Gea is Manchester United's main man under Louis van Gaal this season|website=Sky Sports|first=Adam |last=Bate|date=5 March 2015|access-date=17 January 2018}}</ref><ref name="eye">{{cite web|url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/de-geas-saves-may-well-catch-eye-theres-so-much-more-his-triumphant-rise|title=De Gea's saves may well catch the eye, but there's so much more to his triumphant rise|website=FourFourTwo|first=Seb|last=Stafford-Bloor|date=16 April 2015|access-date=17 January 2018}}</ref><ref name="legend">{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/manchester-united/12104579/Manchester-United-goalkeeper-David-de-Gea-well-on-his-way-to-club-legend-status.html|title=Manchester United goalkeeper David De Gea well on his way to club legend status|newspaper=The Daily Telegraph|first=Alan|last=Smith|date=17 January 2016|access-date=17 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2017/12/09/forget-great-attacking-players-david-de-gea-andederson-secrets/ |title=Forget the great attacking players, David De Gea and Ederson are the secrets behind Manchester clubs' success |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |first=Sam |last=Wallace |date=9 December 2017 |access-date=21 January 2019}}</ref> In 2018 [[Shay Given]] called De Gea the best shot-stopper in the world.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2018/04/06/ederson-vs-david-de-gea-shay-given-compares-premier-leagues/ |title=Ederson vs David De Gea: Shay Given compares the Premier League's two best goalkeepers |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |first=Shay |last=Given |date=6 April 2018 |access-date=21 January 2019}}</ref> <ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2017/dec/02/david-de-gea-manchester-united-arsenal-onslaught|title=David de Gea brings greatness to bear for United to repel Arsenal onslaught|newspaper=The Guardian|first=Barney|last=Ronay|date=3 December 2017|access-date=17 January 2018}}</ref>

Due to De Gea's slender frame, he initially struggled at defending high balls as a youngster, often punching balls away rather than holding on to them, and was at times reluctant to come off his line. He later showed improvements in his aerial prowess, handling, command of his area, decision making, and ability to come out and claim crosses, in particular after he developed physically and gained more experience, even being described as a "strong presence in the box" by Kyle Diller in 2012.<ref name="eye" /><ref name="legend" /><ref name="De Gea and Henderson">{{cite news |url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/manchester-united-de-gea-henderson-19896184 |title=Man United fans identify difference between David de Gea and Dean Henderson |newspaper=Manchester Evening News |last1=Jackson |first1=Elliott |date=23 February 2021 |access-date=4 April 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1082190-david-de-gea-did-criticism-actually-benefit-the-manchester-united-goalkeeper |title=David De Gea: Did Criticism Actually Benefit the Manchester United Goalkeeper? |website=Bleacher Report |last1=Diller |first1=Kyle |date=27 February 2012 |access-date=4 April 2021}}</ref> However, in his later seasons at Manchester United, his inability to come off his line and deal with crosses was once again cited as a weakness in his game, in particular in comparison to teammate Dean Henderson.<ref name="De Gea and Henderson" /><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/us/news/david-dea-and-dean-henderson-compared-as-battle-to-be-man-utd-number-one-hots-up-1617450243000 |title=David Dea and Dean Henderson compared as battle to be Man Utd number one hots up |website=FourFourTwo |date=3 April 2021 |access-date=4 April 2021}}</ref>
[[File:UEFA EURO qualifiers Sweden vs Spain 20191015 David de Gea 3.jpg|thumb|De Gea passing the ball whilst playing for Spain in 2019]]
De Gea is highly regarded for his speed when rushing off his line in one on one situations, which also enables him to function as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)#Sweeper-keeper|sweeper-keeper]].<ref name="United confirm signing"/><ref name="corsport"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/soccer/club/manchester-united/360/blog/post/2788922/manchester-united-gk-david-de-gea-superb-in-win-v-liverpool|title=David De Gea superb for Manchester United in triumph at Liverpool|publisher=ESPN |first=Musa|last=Okwonga|date=17 January 2016|access-date=17 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/soccer/club/name/360/blog/post/2201494/headline|title=How David De Gea has become one of the Premier League's best goalkeepers |publisher=ESPN |first=Michael|last=Cox|date=17 December 2014|access-date=17 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/peter-schmeichel-hails-mental-strength-of-manchester-united-goalkeeper-david-de-gea-8352571.html|title=Peter Schmeichel hails mental strength of Manchester United goalkeeper David de Gea|newspaper=The Independent|first=Simon|last=Stone|date=26 November 2012|access-date=17 January 2018}}</ref> In later seasons, however, Adam Bate of [[Sky Sports]] noted in 2019 that De Gea mainly stayed in his area and would come out to sweep up the ball less frequently than other leading keepers in the Premier League; his change in style also drew criticism from Mark Ogden of ''[[ESPN]]'' in 2020,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11667/11703131/david-de-geas-form-whats-up-with-manchester-uniteds-goalkeeper |title=David de Gea's form: What's up with Manchester United's goalkeeper? |website=Sky Sports |last1=Bate |first1=Adam |date=25 April 2019 |access-date=4 April 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://tribuna.com/en/news/manutd-2020-06-09-de-gea-hardly-leaves-his-penalty-area-espn-expert-mark-ogden-urges-united-star-to-take-in/ |title='De Gea hardly leaves his penalty area': ESPN expert Mark Ogden urges United star to take inspiration from Alisson |publisher=Tribuna.com |date=9 June 2020 |access-date=4 April 2021 }}</ref> while that same year, Mark Critchley of ''The Independent'' opined that De Gea "has never been especially comfortable playing behind a high line, regularly coming out second-best in one-on-ones with opposition strikers."<ref name="danger">{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/manchester-united-news-david-de-gea-everton-dean-henderson-a9367726.html |title=David de Gea in no danger of losing United place yet |newspaper=The Independent |last1=Critchley |first1=Mark |date=2 March 2020 |access-date=4 April 2021}}</ref> [[Jonathan Wilson (writer)|Jonathan Wilson]] in a 2020 article for the ''Irish Times'', also noted that sweeping was not a natural part of his game, and that his tendency to sit deeper with Manchester United in comparison to his position with Spain, who play with a higher line, was one of his reasons for his loss of form since his poor and error–prone performances at the 2018 World Cup.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/soccer/english-soccer/david-de-gea-s-decline-evident-since-2018-world-cup-1.4308638 |title=David de Gea's decline evident since 2018 World Cup |newspaper=The Irish Times |last1=Wilson |first1=Jonathan |authorlink=Jonathan Wilson (writer)|date=20 July 2020 |access-date=4 April 2021}}</ref>

In addition to his goalkeeping abilities, in his prime, De Gea possessed excellent ball control, vision, and distribution with either foot, which enabled him to start attacking plays from the '''David Olatukunbo Alaba''' ({{IPA|de-at|ˈdeɪvɪd ˈalaba, ˈdaːv-|lang|audio=David Alaba.wav}};<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 December 2022 |title=David Alaba: München oder Madrid? |trans-title=David Alaba: Munich or Madrid? |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V0K1zKT_aZQ&t=5s |access-date=18 May 2023 |website=[[YouTube]] |language=German |archive-date=18 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230518044931/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=V0K1zKT_aZQ&t=5s |url-status=live }}</ref> born 24 June 1992) is an Austrian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[centre-back]] for and [[Captain (association football)|captains]] the [[Austria national football team|Austria national team]]. He was previously deployed as a [[left-back]], and was widely considered one of the best in the world at this position.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.hitc.com/en-gb/2019/12/26/7-greatest-left-backs-of-the-decade// | title = 7 greatest left-backs of the decade | date = 26 December 2019 | publisher = HITC Sevens | access-date = 1 June 2020 | archive-date = 26 December 2019 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20191226210211/https://www.hitc.com/en-gb/2019/12/26/7-greatest-left-backs-of-the-decade/ | url-status = live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = https://footballiconic.com/top-25-best-left-backs-in-football-in-the-21st-century/ | title = Top 25 best left-backs in football in the 21st century | publisher = Football Iconic | access-date = 1 June 2020 | archive-date = 12 February 2021 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20210212171103/https://footballiconic.com/top-25-best-left-backs-in-football-in-the-21st-century/ | url-status = live }}</ref>

Alaba started out in Bayern's [[Bayern Munich Junior Team|youth system]] before being promoted to the [[FC Bayern Munich II|reserve team]] for the 2009–10 season.<ref name="Im 16'er" /> In January 2011, Alaba joined [[TSG 1899 Hoffenheim|TSG Hoffenheim]] on loan until the end of the [[2010–11 Bundesliga|2010–11 season]]. He returned to Bayern at the start of the [[2011–12 FC Bayern Munich season|2011–12 season]], where he went on to become a regular member of the first-team squad. Alaba made over 400 appearances for [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]], winning 27 honours including ten [[Bundesliga]] titles and two [[UEFA Champions League]] titles in 2013 and 2020, both as part of [[Treble (association football)|trebles]]. During his time in Germany, he was named in the [[UEFA Team of the Year]] three times. In 2021, Alaba joined [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] where he won the [[2021–22 La Liga]], [[2022 Supercopa de España|Supercopa]] and [[2021–22 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] title in his debut season. In 2024, he won [[2023–24 La Liga|La Liga]] and the [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] again, becoming the only player in history to win the Champions League twice with different teams.

Alaba is Austria's second youngest player to play for their senior national team, debuting for them in 2009 as a 17-year-old.<ref name="Standard">{{cite web |url=https://www.derstandard.at/story/2000116968781/alabas-rekord-als-juengster-teamfussballer-gehoert-ernst-joachim-jokl |title=Alabas Rekord als jüngster Teamfußballer gehört Ernst "Jokl" Joachim |language=de |publisher=Standard |date=20 April 2020 |access-date=20 April 2020 |archive-date=16 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200616054616/https://www.derstandard.at/story/2000116968781/alabas-rekord-als-juengster-teamfussballer-gehoert-ernst-joachim-jokl |url-status=live |trans-title=Alaba's record as the youngest national team player belongs to Ernst "Jokl" Joachim}}</ref><ref name="Im 16'er">{{cite web|url=http://16-er.de/deutschland/bundesliga/554-david-alaba-die-vita-eines-wunderknaben.html |title=David Alaba – Die Vita eines Wunderknaben |language=de |publisher=Im 16'er |date=7 May 2012 |access-date=15 February 2014 |first=Hermann |last=Holstein |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222152523/http://16-er.de/deutschland/bundesliga/554-david-alaba-die-vita-eines-wunderknaben.html |archive-date=22 February 2014 |url-status=dead|trans-title=David Alaba – The life story of a wunderkind}}</ref> He has earned over 110 caps and represented his country at [[UEFA Euro 2016]], [[UEFA Euro 2020|Euro 2020]] and the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]]. Widely regarded as one of the best Austrian players of all time, he was voted [[Austrian Footballer of the Year]] on ten occasions (including six consecutive times from 2011 to 2016).

==Club career==
===Early career===
Born in [[Vienna]],<ref name="da"/> Alaba began his career with SV Aspern, his local club in [[Aspern]], in the Vienna district [[Donaustadt]], before joining the youth setup of [[FK Austria Wien|Austria Wien]] at age ten. He rose through the ranks quickly; in April 2008, he was named on the first-team substitutes' bench for an [[Austrian Bundesliga]] match.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.planetlinz.tv/s132,1,1005,Jugend_TOTO_Cup_David_Alaba_im_Portraet.html |title=Jugend-TOTO-Cup: David Alaba im Porträt |trans-title=Jugend-TOTO-Cup: David Alaba portrayed |language=de |work=planetlinz.tv |access-date=10 February 2010 |date=29 August 2008 |archive-date=19 September 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100919025443/http://www.planetlinz.tv/s132%2C1%2C1005%2CJugend_TOTO_Cup_David_Alaba_im_Portraet.html |url-status=dead}}</ref> He also played five times for Austria Wien's [[Austria Vienna II|reserve team]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://derstandard.at/1246542124976/Talent-David-Alaba-Versprechen-und-Prophezeiung?sap=2&_pid=13508991 |title=David Alaba, Versprechen und Prophezeiung |trans-title=David Alaba, Promise and Prophecy |work=[[Der Standard]] |language=de |access-date=10 February 2010 |date=14 July 2009 |archive-date=10 August 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110810065405/http://derstandard.at/1246542124976/Talent-David-Alaba-Versprechen-und-Prophezeiung?sap=2&_pid=13508991 |url-status=dead }}</ref> before leaving in summer 2008 to join German side [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] of the [[Bundesliga]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fussballboom.de/david-alaba-supertalent-des-fc-bayern/ |title=David Alaba: Supertalent des FC Bayern |work=Fussballboom |language=de |access-date=10 February 2010 |date=21 April 2009 |archive-date=24 May 2012 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120524163723/http://www.fussballboom.de/david-alaba-supertalent-des-fc-bayern/ |url-status=dead|trans-title=David Alaba: FC Bayern's super talent}}</ref>

===Bayern Munich===
====Youth, reserves and Hoffenheim loan====
He started out in Bayern's [[Bayern Munich Junior Team|youth system]], playing for the under 17 and under 19 teams, before being promoted to the [[FC Bayern Munich II|reserve team]] for the 2009–10 season.<ref name="Im 16'er"/> He made his debut in a [[3. Liga]] match against [[Dynamo Dresden]] in August 2009<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.oefb.at/show_berichtdetail.php?ber_id=14415&fpid=284|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20110607044755/http://www.oefb.at/show_berichtdetail.php?ber_id=14415&fpid=284|url-status= dead|archive-date= 7 June 2011|title=David Alaba erstmals bei den Bayern-Profis|trans-title=David Alaba for the first time with the Bayern pros|work=oefb.at|language=de|access-date=10 February 2010}}</ref> and scored his first professional goal for FC Bayern Munich II on 29 August 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kicker.de/scholls-erster-sieg-513868/artikel |title=Scholls erster Sieg |trans-title=Scholl's first win |work=[[Kicker (sports magazine)|kicker.de]] |language=de |access-date=10 February 2010 |date=31 August 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100919025443/http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/3liga/startseite/513868/artikel_Scholls-erster-Sieg.html |archive-date=19 September 2010 |url-status=live}}</ref> He was named in [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]]'s squad for the [[2009–10 UEFA Champions League|2009–10]] [[UEFA Champions League]],<ref>{{cite web |publisher=[[UEFA]] |access-date=7 September 2009 |title=FC Bayern München |url=http://www.uefa.com/footballeurope/club=50037/competition=1/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090901082933/http://www.uefa.com/footballeurope/club%3D50037/competition%3D1/index.html |archive-date=1 September 2009}}</ref> where he was assigned the shirt number 27. In January 2010, it was announced that Alaba would train with the first team for the rest of the 2009–10 season,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/de/news/827/bundesliga/2010/01/02/1722024/%C3%B6sterreich-jungstar-alaba-trainiert-mit-bayern-profis |title=Österreich-Jungstar Alaba trainiert mit Bayern-Profis |trans-title=Austrian starlet Alaba trains with Bayern club pros |language=de |date=2 January 2010 |publisher=goal.com |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100303102437/http://www.goal.com/de/news/827/bundesliga/2010/01/02/1722024/%C3%B6sterreich-jungstar-alaba-trainiert-mit-bayern-profis |archive-date=3 March 2010 |access-date=15 February 2014 |url-status=dead}}</ref> along with reserve teammates [[Diego Contento]] and [[Mehmet Ekici]].<ref>{{cite web |date=9 January 2010 |url=http://www.fcbayern.t-home.de/en/news/news/2010/21929.php |access-date=10 January 2010 |title=Alaba, Ekici and Contento give it their best shot |work=[[FC Bayern Munich]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100112120212/http://www.fcbayern.t-home.de/en/news/news/2010/21929.php |archive-date=12 January 2010}}</ref>

The trio were named on the first-team substitutes' bench for the first time on 10 February 2010, for a [[DFB-Pokal]] game against [[SpVgg Greuther Fürth]], and Alaba came on in the 59th minute, replacing [[Christian Lell]].<ref>{{cite web|work=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |date=10 February 2010 |access-date=10 February 2010 |url=https://www.kicker.de/bayern-gegen-fuerth-2010-dfb-pokal-993584/analyse |title=Bayern München – SpVgg Greuther Fürth |language=de |archive-date=15 July 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100715201719/http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/dfbpokal/spielrunde/dfb-pokal/2009-10/4/993584/spielbericht_bayern-muenchen-14_spvgg-greuther-fuerth-82.html |url-status=live}}</ref> After one minute on the pitch, and with his second touch of the game, he set up [[Franck Ribéry]] to give Bayern a 3–2 lead, in a match they went on to win 6–2. He also became Bayern's youngest ever player in a competitive fixture, at 17 years, 7 months and 8 days old.<ref name=jung>{{cite web |date=11 February 2010 |access-date=12 February 2010 |work=[[Bayern Munich]] |url=http://www.fcbayern.t-home.de/en/news/news/2010/22311.php |title=Praise for new boys Contento and Alaba |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100214200406/http://www.fcbayern.t-home.de/en/news/news/2010/22311.php |archive-date=14 February 2010}}</ref>

In January 2011, Alaba joined [[TSG 1899 Hoffenheim|TSG Hoffenheim]] on loan until the end of the [[2010–11 Bundesliga|2010–11 season]]. Later that month, he scored his first-ever goal in the Bundesliga in a 2–2 draw with [[FC St. Pauli]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dfb.de/datencenter/bundesliga/2010-2011/19-spieltag/1899-hoffenheim-fc-st-pauli-191524 |title=1899 Hoffenheim 2–2 FC St. Pauli |website=dfb.de |language=German |date=23 January 2011 |access-date=23 February 2021 |archive-date=14 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210514195126/https://www.dfb.de/datencenter/bundesliga/2010-2011/19-spieltag/1899-hoffenheim-fc-st-pauli-191524 |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2011–2013====
Alaba returned to Bayern at the start of the [[2011–12 FC Bayern Munich season|2011–12 season]], where he became a regular member of the first-team squad. On 23 October 2011, Alaba scored his first league goal for Bayern in the 1–2 away loss against [[Hannover 96]]. On 20 December, Alaba was named [[Austrian Footballer of the Year]] for the first time.<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.goal.com/en/news/725/bundesliga/2011/12/20/2811491/bayern-munichs-david-alaba-named-austrian-footballer-of-the| title = Bayern Munich's David Alaba named Austrian Footballer of the Year| publisher = goal.com| access-date = 22 March 2019| archive-date = 22 March 2019| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190322101845/https://www.goal.com/en/news/725/bundesliga/2011/12/20/2811491/bayern-munichs-david-alaba-named-austrian-footballer-of-the| url-status = live}}</ref> During the second half of the [[2011–12 Bundesliga]] season, he established himself as a starter for Bayern. On 25 April 2012, he played in the [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League]] semi-final second leg against [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]], and scored Bayern's first kick of the [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|shootout]] as they won 3–1 on penalties. However, due to being [[Yellow card (sport)|booked]] in the semi-final, Alaba was unable to play in the [[2012 UEFA Champions League Final]] through suspension.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://blogs.independent.co.uk/2012/05/08/david-alabas-suspension-for-the-champions-league-final-is-the-most-regrettable-of-all/ |author=Kit Holden |title=David Alaba's suspension for the Champions League final is the most regrettable of all |date=8 May 2012 |work=[[The Independent]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120510060416/http://blogs.independent.co.uk/2012/05/08/david-alabas-suspension-for-the-champions-league-final-is-the-most-regrettable-of-all/ |archive-date=10 May 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:David Alaba - Österreiche Fußballnationalmannschaft (01).jpg|thumb|upright|right|Alaba with [[Austria national football team|Austria]] in 2009]]

Alaba played for Austria at [[Austria national under-17 football team|under-17]], [[Austria national under-19 football team|under-19]] and [[Austria national under-21 football team|under-21]] level. In October 2009, he was called up to the senior [[Austria national football team|Austria]] national team for a match against [[France national football team|France]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nachrichten.at/sport/fussball/art99,272293 |title=Frankreich-Match: um Alaba wird uns Europa beneiden |trans-title=Match against France: Europe will envy us for Alaba |work=nachrichten.at |language=de |date=7 October 2009 |access-date=10 February 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110706094150/http://www.nachrichten.at/sport/fussball/art99%2C272293 |archive-date=6 July 2011 |url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his debut in this game, making him the youngest player in the history of the Austria national team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sport.freenet.de/fussball/wm-2010-juengster-austrianationalspieler-aller-zeiten-bayerns-david-alaba-fuer-oesterreich-nominiert_1075016_489260.html |title=WM 2010: Jüngster Austria-Nationalspieler aller Zeiten?: Bayerns David Alaba für Österreich nominiert |trans-title=World Cup 2010: Youngest Austrian international ever? Bayern's David Alaba called up for Austria |work=sport.freenet.de |language=de |date=11 October 2009 |access-date=10 February 2010 |archive-date=24 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110724144712/http://sport.freenet.de/fussball/wm-2010-juengster-austrianationalspieler-aller-zeiten-bayerns-david-alaba-fuer-oesterreich-nominiert_1075016_489260.html |url-status=dead}}</ref> He scored his first goal for Austria on 16 October 2012 in a World Cup Qualifying game at home to [[Kazakhstan national football team|Kazakhstan]] where Austria were 4–0 winners.

At the age of just 19, Alaba won the prestigious vote for [[Austrian Footballer of the Year]] in 2011. In the poll organised by APA (Austrian press agency) among the coaches of the ten [[Austrian Bundesliga]] clubs, Alaba finished top on 21 points, just ahead of [[Austria Wien]]'s Dutch star [[Nacer Barazite]] (20 points) and [[VfB Stuttgart]]'s [[Martin Harnik]]. In December 2012, he received the award for the second consecutive year.<ref>{{cite news|date=18 December 2012 |access-date=12 April 2012 |url=http://www.kleinezeitung.at/sport/fussball/3194078/bayerns-david-alaba-wieder-fussballer-des-jahres.story |title=David Alaba ist "Fußballer des Jahres" |trans-title=David Alaba is "footballer of the year" |work=kleinezeitung.at |language=de |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121231165055/http://www.kleinezeitung.at/sport/fussball/3194078/bayerns-david-alaba-wieder-fussballer-des-jahres.story |archive-date=31 December 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref> On 10 September 2013, Alaba scored the only goal of the game against Ireland in the 84-minute to give Austria a 1–0. He scored the final goal in Austria's 3–0 win in the final qualification match against [[Faroe Islands national football team|Faroe Islands]].

Alaba ended the [[2014 FIFA World Cup qualification]] campaign as Austria's [[2014 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)#Goalscorers|top scorer]] with six goals.<ref>{{Cite web |last=FIFA.com |title=Top scorers |url=http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/preliminaries/europe/statistics/topscorers.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090305092436/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/preliminaries/europe/statistics/topscorers.html |archive-date=2009-03-05 |access-date=2026-03-16 |website=www.fifa.com |language=en}}</ref> He scored a ninth-minute [[Panenka (penalty kick)|Panenka-style]] penalty kick on 8 September 2015 to open a 4–1 away win over [[Sweden men's national football team|Sweden]] at the [[Friends Arena]] in [[Solna]]. The result qualified Austria for [[UEFA Euro 2016]], their first successful qualification campaign for the continental championship.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Dutt |first=Sujay |date=2015-09-08 |title=Sensational Austria qualify in Sweden |url=http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/qualifiers/season=2016/matches/round=2000446/match=2014021/postmatch/report/index.html#austria+qualify+sweden |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151113043401/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/qualifiers/season=2016/matches/round=2000446/match=2014021/postmatch/report/index.html#austria+qualify+sweden |archive-date=2015-11-13 |access-date=2026-03-16 |work=Uefa.com |language=en}}</ref> Alaba played in all three group matches as Austria finished last in their group with one point.<ref>{{Cite web |last=uefa.com |title=UEFA EURO 2016 - History - Austria – UEFA.com |url=http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/season=2016/teams/team=8/matches/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825150518/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/season=2016/teams/team=8/matches/index.html |archive-date=2017-08-25 |access-date=2026-03-16 |website=UEFA.com |language=en}}</ref> On 24 March 2017, he captained Austria for the first time in a [[World Cup 2018 qualification]] game against [[Moldova national football team|Moldova]] in a 2–0 victory, deputizing in the absence of suspended captain [[Julian Baumgartlinger]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2017-03-24 |title=Österreich ringt Moldawien nieder |trans-title=Austria wrestles Moldova down |url=http://sport.orf.at/stories/2270775/2270774/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170527124341/http://sport.orf.at/stories/2270775/2270774/ |archive-date=2017-05-27 |access-date=2026-03-16 |work=sport.ORF.at |language=de-DE}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Christopher |first=Trimmel |date=2021-09-26 |title=trực tiếp bóng đá |url=https://giovangtv.net/ |access-date=2026-03-16 |website=giovangtv.net |language=en-US}}</ref> Alaba played in eight matches as Austria failed to qualify for the [[2018 World Cup|2018 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=FIFA.com |title=2018 FIFA World Cup Russia™   - Qualifiers - Europe - All Matches - FIFA.com |url=http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/preliminaries/europe/all-matches.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150728235810/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/preliminaries/europe/all-matches.html |archive-date=2015-07-28 |access-date=2026-03-16 |website=FIFA.com |language=en-GB}}</ref> Alaba captained Austria during the [[UEFA Euro 2020]], in which they reached the knockout stages in that competition for the first time in their history.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro-2020/match/2024477--italy-vs-austria/postmatch/report/ |title=Italy 2–1 Austria: Mancini's subs squeeze Azzurri through |website=UEFA |date=26 June 2021 |access-date=27 June 2021 |archive-date=28 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210628200743/https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro-2020/match/2024477--italy-vs-austria/postmatch/report/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 17 June 2023, Alaba played his 100th match for Austria in a 1–1 away draw against [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]] during the [[UEFA Euro 2024 qualifying]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2023/06/17/alaba-reaches-100-caps-for-austria |title=Alaba reaches 100 caps for Austria |publisher=Real Madrid CF |date=17 June 2023 |access-date=25 June 2023 |archive-date=25 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230625171057/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2023/06/17/alaba-reaches-100-caps-for-austria |url-status=live }}</ref> However, he was unable to feature in the [[UEFA Euro 2024]] due to his long-term injury. Nonetheless, he was named as a "non-playing captain" for the team.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/40192662/euro-2024-david-alaba-austria-captain-real-madrid-injury |title=Euro 2024: Injured Alaba named Austria's 'non-playing captain' |publisher=ESPN |date=21 May 2024 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=21 May 2024 |title=Alaba named Austria's non-playing Euros captain |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/40192662/euro-2024-david-alaba-austria-captain-real-madrid-injury |access-date=22 June 2024 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

On 18 May 2026, Alaba was selected in [[Ralf Rangnick]]’s 26-man squad for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]], marking Austria’s first appearance in the tournament since 1998.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/austria-ralf-rangnick-world-cup-squad|title=Alaba, Arnautovic feature as Austria name World Cup squad|date=18 May 2026|access-date=17 June 2026|language=en}}</ref>

==Style of play==
A versatile defender, Alaba regularly plays as a left-back, and he has been deployed as a centre-back, central midfielder, and left midfielder. Although not known to have a fast pace, and his positioning has sometimes been questionable, Alaba possesses a powerful left foot; in which besides his defensive prowess, he is noted for his offensive capabilities and ability to read the game, where he has gained a reputation carrying the ball upfront in attacking plays and supplies his team with passes.
