'''Pierre-Emerick Emiliano François Aubameyang''' (born 18 June 1989) is a professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Striker (association football)|striker]] for {{Spanish football updater|Deportivo A Coruña}} club [[Deportivo de A Coruña|Deportivo A Coruña]]. Born in France, he played for the [[Gabon national football team|Gabon national team]]. He is considered as one of the best strikers in the world at his peak and in the Bundesliga. With over 400 goals in his career, he is the all-time top goalscorer in the [[UEFA Europa League]] (34) and has the most goals in Europe's top five leagues for an African player, with over 240 goals.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Most Goals By An African Player All Time |url=https://www.statmuse.com/fc/ask/most-goals-by-an-african-player-all-time?l=eu5 |access-date=2026-08-08 |website=StatMuse |language=en |archive-date=8 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260808223036/https://www.statmuse.com/fc/ask/most-goals-by-an-african-player-all-time%3Fl%3Deu5 |url-status=live }}</ref> He is also the highest-scoring African player in the history of the [[Bundesliga]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang: A world-class striker, made in the Bundesliga |url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-arsenal-striker-borussia-dortmund-made-in-germany-5731 |access-date=2026-08-08 |website=bundesliga.com - the official Bundesliga website |language=en |archive-date=8 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260808192741/https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-arsenal-striker-borussia-dortmund-made-in-germany-5731 |url-status=live }}</ref>   

Aubameyang began his senior club career after signing for [[AC Milan]] in Italy, but never made an appearance for the club, instead spending several loan spells in France. He transferred permanently to [[AS Saint-Étienne|Saint-Étienne]] in 2011, where he won the [[2012–13 Coupe de la Ligue]]. In summer 2013, he joined [[Borussia Dortmund]], scoring 141 goals in four and a half seasons.<ref>{{cite news |title=The 100 best footballers in the world 2016 – interactive |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/ng-interactive/2016/dec/20/the-100-best-footballers-in-the-world-2016-interactive |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=20 December 2016 |archive-date=2 August 2020 |access-date=25 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200802150024/https://www.theguardian.com/football/ng-interactive/2016/dec/20/the-100-best-footballers-in-the-world-2016-interactive |url-status=live }}</ref> He collected the [[Vereinigung der Vertragsfußballspieler#Awards|VDV Silver Boot]], the [[List of Bundesliga top scorers|Bundesliga']][[List of Bundesliga top scorers|s top goalscorer]] award, and won the [[2017 DFB-Pokal final|DFB-Pokal]]. His 31 goals in 32 matches in the [[2016–17 Bundesliga]]<ref name=":2" /> made him the first player in 40 years to score 30 goals in a Bundesliga season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-05-20 |title=Bundesliga: Aubameyang, meilleur buteur, entre dans l'histoire |url=https://rmcsport.bfmtv.com/football/bundesliga/bundesliga-aubameyang-meilleur-buteur-entre-dans-l-histoire_AN-201705200123.html |access-date=2026-08-08 |website=RMC Sport |language=fr |archive-date=9 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260809023108/https://rmcsport.bfmtv.com/football/bundesliga/bundesliga-aubameyang-meilleur-buteur-entre-dans-l-histoire_AN-201705200123.html |url-status=live }}</ref>  

In 2018, Aubameyang joined [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] for a then-club record fee of £56 million (€60 million).<ref name="completes £56m">{{cite news |title=Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang completes £56m Arsenal move |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/jan/31/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-joins-arsenal-deadline-day-transfer |newspaper=The Guardian |date=31 January 2018 |access-date=31 January 2018 |archive-date=15 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200615075720/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/jan/31/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-joins-arsenal-deadline-day-transfer |url-status=live }}</ref> He went on to captain the club,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Media |first=Arsenal |title=Club update: Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/club-update-pierre-emerick-aubameyang-aULxr6b7XUsp |access-date=2026-08-09 |website=Arsenal FC |language=en}}</ref> helping them reach the [[2019 UEFA Europa League final|2019 Europa League final]] and win the [[FA Cup]] in [[2020 FA Cup final|2020]]. Individually, he was awarded the [[Premier League Golden Boot]] in [[2018–19 Premier League|2018–19]] and was named in the 2020 [[PFA Team of the Year]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Aubameyang: Arsenal's talisman |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/53625368 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=1 August 2020 |archive-date=2 August 2020 |access-date=9 September 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200802065247/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/53625368 |url-status=live }}</ref> After leaving Arsenal in 2022, he had spells with [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] before joining [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] in 2023. He was named in the [[Ligue 1 Team of the Year]], while his performances in the [[2024–25 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] earned him the competition's [[UEFA Europa League#Awards|Player of the Season]] award. In 2024, he joined [[Saudi Pro League]] club [[Al Qadsiah FC|Al-Qadsiah]], spending one season there before returning to Marseille in 2025. After one season in France, he subsequently returned to Spain, joining Deportivo de La Coruña. 

After playing once for the [[France national under-21 football team|France under-21 team]], Aubameyang switched to represent [[Gabon national football team|Gabon]] at international level, making his senior debut in 2009 at the age of 19; with 40 goals, he is the nation's [[List of international goals scored by Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang|all-time top scorer]]. He represented Gabon at six [[Africa Cup of Nations]] tournaments and the [[Football at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Summer Olympics]]. In 2015, he was named [[African Footballer of the Year]]; the first Gabonese and second European-born player to win the award.<ref>{{cite news |title=Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang beats Yaya Toure to Caf award |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/35257500 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=7 January 2016 |access-date=8 January 2016 |archive-date=15 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190415041520/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/35257500 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Club career==

===AC Milan===
Aubameyang joined [[AC Milan]]'s youth academy in January 2007. In August, he was part of the squad that finished fourth in the [[2007 Champions Youth Cup|inaugural Champions Youth Cup]] held in [[Malaysia]], where he made a name for himself and attracted the attention of scouts internationally. He scored against every opponent Milan played, finishing with seven goals in six matches.<ref>{{cite news |title=CYC: Juventus battuta di misura |url=http://it.eurosport.yahoo.com/19082007/8/champions-youth-cup-juventus-battuta-misura.html |url-status=dead |publisher=Eurosport |date=19 August 2007 |access-date=9 August 2008 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120525220412/http://it.eurosport.yahoo.com/19082007/8/champions-youth-cup-juventus-battuta-misura.html |archive-date=25 May 2012 |language=it}}</ref>

====2008–09: Loan to Dijon====
For the [[2008–09 Ligue 1|2008–09 season]], Aubameyang was loaned out to [[Dijon FCO|Dijon]] of [[Ligue 2]] in France to gain first-team experience.<ref>{{cite news|title=AC Milan, Aubameyang to Dijon|url=http://www.transfermarketweb.com/?action=read&idsel=19005|publisher=TransferMarketWeb|date=21 June 2008|access-date=9 August 2008|archive-date=30 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180130204423/http://www.transfermarketweb.com/?action=read&idsel=19005|url-status=dead}}</ref> His performances there led him to appear in ''[[World Soccer (magazine)|World Soccer]]''{{'s}} Talent Scout section in the summer of 2009.<ref>{{cite news |title=Talent Scout: Tomorrow's Stars Today |first=Mark |last=Gleeson |magazine=World Soccer |date=Summer 2009 |page=75}}</ref> He finished with a total of ten goals and two assists in all competitions, including two goals in a [[Coupe de France]] tie against [[Is-Selongey Football|Selongey]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/match-direct/coupe-de-france/2008-2009/selongey-dijon-live/160405 |title=Résultat Selongey - Dijon, Coupe de France, 8e tour, Samedi 13 Décembre 2008|publisher=lequipe.fr|access-date=15 February 2021 }}</ref>

====2009–10: Loan to Lille====
On 24 June 2009, it was announced [[Ligue 1]] club [[Lille OSC|Lille]] had decided to sign Aubameyang on loan.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.losc.fr/?r=0,0,1,7041 |title=Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang rejoint le LOSC ! |date=24 June 2009 |access-date=25 June 2009 |publisher=losc.fr |language=fr |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090627021426/http://www.losc.fr/?r=0%2C0%2C1%2C7041 |archive-date=27 June 2009 }}</ref> Relative to his previous season, however, Aubameyang did not perform as well, scoring just two goals in 14 appearances, four as a starter.{{citation needed|date=January 2018}}

====2010–11: Loans to Monaco and Saint-Étienne====
For the [[2010–11 AS Monaco FC season|2010–11 season]], Aubameyang was loaned for the season to [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]]. On 21 August 2010, he scored his first goal for Monaco in an away match against [[RC Lens|Lens]], then scored again on 29 August at home to [[AJ Auxerre|Auxerre]], where Monaco won 2–0.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2010/08/29/france/ligue-1/association-sportive-monaco-fc/association-de-la-jeunesse-auxerroise/936383/ |title=Monaco vs. Auxerre – 29 August 2010 |publisher=Soccerway |date=29 August 2010 |access-date=10 August 2013 |archive-date=9 August 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130809082142/http://int.soccerway.com/matches/2010/08/29/france/ligue-1/association-sportive-monaco-fc/association-de-la-jeunesse-auxerroise/936383/? |url-status=live }}</ref> In January 2011, after six months with the club, Aubameyang was loaned to [[AS Saint-Étienne|Saint-Étienne]] until the end of the [[2010–11 Ligue 1|2010–11 season]], finishing the season with four goals and three assists. In July 2011, the loan was extended for the entire [[2011–12 Ligue 1|2011–12 season]].{{citation needed|date=January 2018}}

===Saint-Étienne===
[[File:Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang (03-08-2011).jpg|thumb|300x300px|Aubameyang during a training session in August 2011 ]]
On 22 December 2011, Aubameyang signed with Saint-Étienne on a permanent deal. He was quickly added to the starting lineup and was given the number 7 jersey. In February 2012, he scored his first [[hat-trick]] against [[FC Lorient|Lorient]]. He became an integral part of the squad, scoring half of the team's away goals during the season, and went on to be Ligue 1's 4th top scorer having scored 16 goals behind Montpellier's [[Olivier Giroud]] with 21, PSG's [[Nenê (footballer, born 1981)|Nenê]] with 21 too and Lille's [[Eden Hazard]] with 20.

On 20 April 2013, Aubameyang was in the starting line-up for Saint-Étienne in the [[2013 Coupe de la Ligue Final]]. ''Les Verts'' won the match 1–0 with a goal from [[Brandão (footballer, born 1980)|Brandão]] to give Aubameyang his first major trophy as a professional footballer. He finished the season with 18 goals and seven assists in all competitions.{{citation needed|date=January 2018}}

In the [[2012–13 Ligue 1|2012–13 season]], Aubameyang ended second in the competition's [[2012–13 Ligue 1#Top goalscorers|top-goalscorers list]], scoring 19 goals and finishing behind only [[Zlatan Ibrahimović]]. From his 37 appearances, he also provided eight [[2012–13 Ligue 1#Assists table|assists]]. The season was widely regarded as his breakout year—he appeared in the Ligue 1 team of the season and he won the Ligue 1 African Player of the Year award.<ref name=":5">{{cite web |title=Aubameyang wins best African player in France award |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/22523487.app |publisher=BBC Sport |date=14 May 2013 |access-date=20 May 2017 |archive-date=9 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230409053421/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/22523487.app |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Borussia Dortmund===

====2013–15: DFL Supercups====
[[File:Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang (BVB) (cropped).jpg|thumb|Aubameyang during a pre-season friendly match against [[Rot-Weiss Essen]] in August 2014]]
On 4 July 2013, Aubameyang joined [[2013 UEFA Champions League Final|2012–13 Champions League finalists]] [[Borussia Dortmund]] on a five-year contract.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/jul/04/borussia-dortmund-pierre-emerick-aubameyang |title=Borussia Dortmund sign Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang from St-Etienne |date=5 July 2013 |newspaper=The Guardian |access-date=21 July 2013 |archive-date=18 May 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190518121147/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/jul/04/borussia-dortmund-pierre-emerick-aubameyang |url-status=live }}</ref> He made his competitive debut for his new club on 27 July 2013 against [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] in the [[2013 DFL-Supercup|DFL-Supercup]], replacing [[Jakub Błaszczykowski]] for the last 18 minutes of Dortmund's 4–2 victory, assisting Dortmund's final goal, scored by [[Marco Reus]].{{citation needed|date=August 2020}} On 10 August, Aubameyang made his [[Bundesliga]] debut and scored a hat-trick against [[FC Augsburg]], including a goal from his first [[Shooting (association football)|shot]] in the league. In the process, Aubameyang also became the first Gabonese player to appear in the Bundesliga.<ref>{{cite web|title=Aubameyang hat-trick has Dortmund flying |url=http://www.bundesliga.com/en/liga/news/2013/0000264271.php |publisher=Bundesliga.de |access-date=10 August 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130813011953/http://www.bundesliga.com/en/liga/news/2013/0000264271.php |archive-date=13 August 2013}}</ref> On 27 November, he scored his first [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] goal in a 3–1 win against [[S.S.C. Napoli|Napoli]] in the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League group stage|group stage of the 2013–14 competition]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/nov/26/borussia-dortmund-napoli-champions-league |title=Borussia Dortmund gain lifeline after turning on the style against Napoli |date=27 November 2013 |access-date=19 December 2013 |newspaper=The Guardian |archive-date=19 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131219134843/http://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/nov/26/borussia-dortmund-napoli-champions-league |url-status=live }}</ref> He later took a [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty]] against [[TSV 1860 Munich|1860 Munich]] that propelled Dortmund into the next round of the [[2013–14 DFB-Pokal]], finishing the year with 13 league goals and 16 goals in all competitions.{{citation needed|date=January 2018}}

On 13 August 2014, Aubameyang assisted Borussia Dortmund's first goal and scored the second goal in a 2–0 victory over Bayern Munich in the [[2014 DFL-Supercup|DFL-Supercup]].<ref name="Spider-Man">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/28762490 |title=German Supercup: Borussia Dortmund 2–0 Bayern Munich |publisher=BBC Sport |date=13 August 2014 |access-date=5 October 2014 |archive-date=28 September 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140928101629/http://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/28762490 |url-status=live }}</ref> After scoring the goal, he celebrated by putting on a [[Spider-Man]] mask.<ref name="Spider-Man" /> In Dortmund's next match, a 4–1 win over [[Stuttgarter Kickers]] in the first round of the [[2014–15 DFB-Pokal|DFB-Pokal]], Aubameyang scored two second-half goals and provided the assist for [[Adrián Ramos]]' goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kicker.de/stg-kickers-gegen-dortmund-2014-dfb-pokal-2397926/spielbericht |title=Aubameyang packt auch ohne Spider-Man doppelt zu |magazine=Kicker |date=16 August 2014 |access-date=5 October 2014 |language=de }}</ref> On 13 September, Aubameyang scored his first [[2014–15 Bundesliga|Bundesliga]] goal of the season, netting Dortmund's final goal of their 3–1 win over [[SC Freiburg]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kicker.de/dortmund-gegen-freiburg-2014-bundesliga-2407246/analyse |title=Rückkehrer Kagawa schlägt voll ein |magazine=Kicker |date=13 September 2014 |access-date=5 October 2014 |language=de }}</ref> Three days later, Aubameyang scored Dortmund's second goal in a 2–0 win over future club [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] in the first group match of the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/29209551 |title=Arsenal's Champions League Group D campaign got off to a poor start as Borussia Dortmund scored either side of half-time to secure a deserved victory. |publisher=BBC Sport |date=16 September 2014 |access-date=5 October 2014 |archive-date=4 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141004161818/http://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/29209551 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Aubameyang ended his second season in Dortmund with 25 goals from 46 appearances, including one in the [[2015 DFB-Pokal Final]], where Dortmund were defeated 3–1 by [[VfL Wolfsburg]] at the [[Olympiastadion (Berlin)|Olympiastadion]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.espnfc.com.au/club/borussia-dortmund/124/blog/post/2544298/aubameyang-extension-dortmund-signals-intent-club-player |title=Aubameyang signing a coup for Dortmund this season and beyond |date=31 July 2015 |publisher=ESPN |archive-date=2 October 2015 |access-date=10 November 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151002070802/http://www.espnfc.com.au/club/borussia-dortmund/124/blog/post/2544298/aubameyang-extension-dortmund-signals-intent-club-player |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2015–16: League runner-up====
On 31 July 2015, Aubameyang signed a new contract to last until 2020, saying, "Every part of me wants to be here and I have never wanted to leave."<ref>{{cite news |title=Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang: Dortmund forward signs new deal |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33739240 |access-date=31 July 2015 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=31 July 2015}}</ref> On 20 August, he scored a brace as Dortmund came from 0–3 down to win 3–4 at [[Odds BK]] in the first leg of their Europa League [[2015–16 UEFA Europa League qualifying phase and play-off round#Play-off round|play-off]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Odd 3 Dortmund 4: Mkhitaryan seals remarkable comeback |url=http://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/odd-3-dortmund-4-mkhitaryan-seals-remarkable-comeback |access-date=26 August 2015 |magazine=FourFourTwo |date=20 August 2015 |archive-date=24 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924044714/http://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/odd-3-dortmund-4-mkhitaryan-seals-remarkable-comeback |url-status=live }}</ref> By scoring in Dortmund's 1–1 draw with [[TSG 1899 Hoffenheim|1899 Hoffenheim]] on 23 September, Aubameyang became the first player in Bundesliga history to score in each of his team's opening six matches of a season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/34341766|title=TSG 1899 Hoffenheim 1–1 Bor Dortmd|date=23 September 2015|website=BBC Sport|archive-date=24 January 2016|access-date=13 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160124174006/http://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/34341766|url-status=live}}</ref> He later extended this record to eight matches, scoring in the team's next two fixtures against [[SV Darmstadt 98|Darmstadt 98]] and Bayern Munich, before failing to score for the first time in the [[2015–16 Bundesliga|Bundesliga season]] in a 2–0 win at [[1. FSV Mainz 05|Mainz 05]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://soccer.nbcsports.com/2015/10/25/another-aubameyang-hat-trick-puts-dortmund-ace-at-13-goals/|title=Another Aubameyang hat-trick puts Dortmund ace at 13 goals|date=25 October 2015|publisher=NBC|archive-date=1 December 2017|access-date=27 October 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201032246/http://soccer.nbcsports.com/2015/10/25/another-aubameyang-hat-trick-puts-dortmund-ace-at-13-goals/|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 22 October, Aubameyang scored a hat-trick in a [[2015–16 UEFA Europa League|UEFA Europa League]] match against [[Gabala FK|Gabala]] of Azerbaijan.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.bvb.de/eng/content/view/full/110898|title=3–1 – Aubameyang hat-trick seals victory for BVB away at Gabala FK|date=22 October 2015|publisher=Borussia Dortmund|archive-date=1 December 2017|access-date=27 October 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201132133/https://www.bvb.de/eng/content/view/full/110898|url-status=live}}</ref> Three days later, he scored another hat-trick in a 5–1 defeat of Augsburg at the [[Westfalenstadion]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/bundesliga/borussia-dortmund/article148053594/Tor-Wetten-motivieren-BVB-Stuermer-Aubameyang.html|title=Tor-Wetten motivieren BVB-Stürmer Aubameyang|date=26 October 2015|newspaper=Die Welt|language=de|archive-date=31 January 2016|access-date=11 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160131142415/http://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/bundesliga/borussia-dortmund/article148053594/Tor-Wetten-motivieren-BVB-Stuermer-Aubameyang.html|url-status=live}}</ref> On 8 November, Aubameyang scored the winning goal for Dortmund in a 3–2 [[Revierderby]] victory over rivals [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/nov/08/borussia-dortmund-schalke-bundesliga-match-report |title=Borussia Dortmund beat Schalke in derby to keep Bayern Munich in sight |date=9 November 2015 |newspaper=The Guardian |archive-date=31 January 2018 |access-date=12 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180131023531/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/nov/08/borussia-dortmund-schalke-bundesliga-match-report |url-status=live }}</ref> At the halfway stage of the Bundesliga season, Aubameyang was the league's top scorer with 18 goals from 17 appearances.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/sport/pep-guardiola-exit-leaves-bayern-munich-in-suspense-bundesliga-half-time-talk-1.104196/ |title=Pep Guardiola exit leaves Bayern Munich in suspense – }}</ref>

On 30 January 2016, Aubameyang scored his 19th and 20th league goals of the season to give Dortmund a 2–0 home victory over [[FC Ingolstadt 04|Ingolstadt 04]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/jan/30/borussia-dortmund-ingolstadt-bundesliga-match-report |title=Borussia Dortmund's Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang ends Ingolstadt resistance |date=31 January 2016 |newspaper=The Guardian |archive-date=31 January 2018 |access-date=12 December 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180131080919/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/jan/30/borussia-dortmund-ingolstadt-bundesliga-match-report |url-status=live }}</ref> Aubameyang reached 30 goals in all competitions in a 3–1 victory over [[VfB Stuttgart]] in the quarter-final of the [[2015–16 DFB-Pokal]]. In addition to scoring himself, he assisted the side's other two goals scored by Marco Reus and [[Henrikh Mkhitaryan]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://worldsoccertalk.com/2016/02/09/aubameyang-nets-30th-goal-as-dortmund-reach-dfb-pokal-semis/|title=Aubameyang nets 30th goal as Dortmund reach DFB-Pokal semis|date=9 February 2016|agency=Agence France-Presse|archive-date=31 January 2018|access-date=8 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180131023506/http://worldsoccertalk.com/2016/02/09/aubameyang-nets-30th-goal-as-dortmund-reach-dfb-pokal-semis/|url-status=live}}</ref> On 10 March 2016, Aubameyang scored for Borussia in their 3–0 win over [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] in the [[2015–16 UEFA Europa League#Round of 16|UEFA Europa League Round of 16]] first-leg. A week later, he scored both goals in the 2–1 second-leg victory at [[White Hart Lane]], taking him to 35 goals for the season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/35815545|title=Tottenham Hotspur 1–2 Borussia Dortmund|date=17 March 2016|website=BBC Sport|archive-date=1 December 2017|access-date=13 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201071031/http://www.bbc.com/sport/football/35815545|url-status=live}}</ref> In scoring two goals in a 5–1 win against VfL Wolfsburg on 30 April, Aubameyang reached 25 goals in the Bundesliga season, thus ending as the league's second-top scorer behind [[Robert Lewandowski]] of Bayern Munich.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.kicker.de/bundesliga/scorer/2015-16|title=1. Bundesliga – Scorer 2015/16|access-date=20 May 2016|magazine=Kicker|archive-date=21 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211021210629/https://www.kicker.de/bundesliga/scorer/2015-16|url-status=live}}</ref>

====2016–17: Bundesliga top goalscorer and DFB-Pokal====
[[File:Aubameyang170727.jpg|thumb|upright|Aubameyang training in July 2017]]

Aubameyang began his [[2016–17 Bundesliga|2016–17 season]] in the Bundesliga with a double against Mainz 05 on 27 August in a 2–1 victory, while also scoring twice against [[VfL Wolfsburg]] on 20 September. Aubameyang scored three days later against recently promoted Freiburg, bringing his season total to five, into a tie atop the scoring charts with Lewandowski early in the season. Following an injury to [[Marcel Schmelzer]], Aubameyang wore the captain's armband for Dortmund for the first time on 22 October, also scoring a goal in the 3–3 draw at Ingolstadt.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/blmd9v-aubameyang-exclusive-interview-ahead-of-revierderby-with-schalke-418522.jsp |title=Aubameyang exclusive: 'We've got huge talent within the team' |publisher=Bundesliga |date=25 October 2016 |access-date=5 November 2016 |archive-date=17 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180617193304/https://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/blmd9v-aubameyang-exclusive-interview-ahead-of-revierderby-with-schalke-418522.jsp |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Aubameyang also got off to an excellent start in Dortmund's [[2016–17 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] group stage matches, scoring in each of their first leg matches as Dortmund were joint top of their group with [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]]. However, Aubameyang was left out of the squad by [[Thomas Tuchel]] for their return leg against [[Sporting CP]] on 2 November due to an "internal issue".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11899/10642293/borussia-dortmund-striker-pierre-emerick-aubameyang-dropped-for-internal-reasons |title=Borussia Dortmund striker Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang dropped for 'internal reasons' |publisher=Sky Sports |first=Mark |last=Ashenden |date=3 November 2016 |access-date=5 November 2016 |archive-date=5 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161105160730/http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11899/10642293/borussia-dortmund-striker-pierre-emerick-aubameyang-dropped-for-internal-reasons |url-status=live }}</ref> It turned out that he received a one-game suspension for breaking club rules, by traveling to [[Milan]] instead of staying in Dortmund.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/borussia-dortmund/story/2990033/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-admits-mistake-in-midweek-and-apologises-to-dortmund|title=Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang admits midweek 'mistake,' apologises to BVB|date=5 November 2016|publisher=ESPN|access-date=7 November 2016|archive-date=7 November 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161107183107/http://www.espnfc.com/borussia-dortmund/story/2990033/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-admits-mistake-in-midweek-and-apologises-to-dortmund|url-status=live}}</ref> Expected to return that weekend at [[Hamburger SV]], Aubameyang exploded with a four-goal performance in a 5–2 victory, their first in five tries in the Bundesliga, while also assisting [[Ousmane Dembélé]] for Dortmund's final goal.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-borussia-dortmund-9201774 |title=Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang hits FOUR on return after Borussia Dortmund suspension |newspaper=Daily Mirror |first=Jack |last=Rathborn |date=5 November 2016 |archive-date=30 July 2018 |access-date=5 April 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180730170822/https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-borussia-dortmund-9201774 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 19 November, Aubameyang scored the only goal of a 1–0 win over Bayern Munich at the Westfalenstadion. This was Dortmund's first Klassiker victory in the league since April 2014.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://theworldgame.sbs.com.au/article/2016/11/20/aubameyang-goal-helps-dortmund-down-bayern|title=Aubameyang goal helps Dortmund down Bayern|date=20 November 2016|publisher=SBS|archive-date=20 December 2016|access-date=17 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220165726/http://theworldgame.sbs.com.au/article/2016/11/20/aubameyang-goal-helps-dortmund-down-bayern|url-status=live}}</ref> On 7 December, Aubameyang scored Borussia's first goal in a 2–2 comeback draw with Real Madrid at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]] to secure qualification to the next stage as group winners.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com.au/blog/the-match/60/post/3009186/borussia-dortmund-overcome-two-goal-deficit-at-real-madrid-to-top-champions-league-group-with-draw|title=Dortmund overcome two-goal deficit at Real Madrid to top group with 2–2 draw|date=7 December 2016|publisher=ESPN}}</ref> On 16 December, Aubameyang scored his 100th goal for Borussia Dortmund in a 2–2 draw away to 1899 Hoffenheim.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://theworldgame.sbs.com.au/article/2016/12/17/aubameyang-goal-salvages-draw-after-reus-sees-red|title=Aubameyang goal salvage draw after Reus sees red|date=17 December 2016|publisher=SBS|archive-date=20 December 2016|access-date=17 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220045134/http://theworldgame.sbs.com.au/article/2016/12/17/aubameyang-goal-salvages-draw-after-reus-sees-red|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 4 March 2017, Aubameyang passed 20 Bundesliga goals for the second consecutive season with two goals in a 6–2 defeat of Bayer Leverkusen.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/blmd23n-aubameyang-moves-into-the-record-books-as-borussia-dortmund-down-leverkusen-435363.jsp|title=Aubameyang moves into the record books as Borussia Dortmund down Bayer Leverkusen|date=4 March 2017|publisher=Bundesliga|archive-date=9 November 2019|access-date=9 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191109002357/https://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/blmd23n-aubameyang-moves-into-the-record-books-as-borussia-dortmund-down-leverkusen-435363.jsp|url-status=dead}}</ref> Four days later, he scored a hat-trick in a 4–0 win over [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] to put Dortmund into the [[2016–17 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Quarter-final|quarter-finals]] of the Champions League.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2017/mar/08/borussia-dortmund-benfica-champions-league-last-16-live|title=Dortmund 4–0 Benfica|date=8 March 2017|newspaper=The Guardian}}</ref> On 20 May, Aubameyang scored twice in Borussia's final-day defeat of [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]] to end the season as the [[List of Bundesliga top scorers|Bundesliga's top scorer]] with 31 goals.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/borussia-dortmund-werder-bremen-live-blog-hoffenheim-augsburg-hamburg-wolfsburg-aubameyang-nagelsmann-bobby-wood-444540-blmd34v.jsp|title=Dortmund defend third place with thrilling home win over Bremen, Cologne into Europa League!|date=20 May 2017|publisher=Bundesliga|archive-date=9 November 2019|access-date=20 May 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191109002354/https://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/borussia-dortmund-werder-bremen-live-blog-hoffenheim-augsburg-hamburg-wolfsburg-aubameyang-nagelsmann-bobby-wood-444540-blmd34v.jsp|url-status=dead}}</ref> In the [[2017 DFB-Pokal Final|final]] of the [[2016–17 DFB-Pokal]] on 27 May 2017, he scored the winning goal, a penalty, as Dortmund beat [[Eintracht Frankfurt]] 2–1.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/eintracht-frankfurt-borussia-dortmund-dfb-cup-final-report-line-ups-statistics-aubameyang-reus-fabian-445473.jsp|title=Aubameyang on the spot as Dortmund win DFB Cup|publisher=bundesliga.com|date=27 May 2017|archive-date=22 April 2020|access-date=25 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200422032843/https://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/eintracht-frankfurt-borussia-dortmund-dfb-cup-final-report-line-ups-statistics-aubameyang-reus-fabian-445473.jsp|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Arsenal===
On 31 January 2018, Aubameyang signed for [[Premier League]] club, [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], for a then-club-record fee,<ref name="auto1">{{cite press release|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-signs-club|title=Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang signs for the club|date=31 January 2018|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|access-date=31 January 2018|archive-date=31 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180131112118/https://www.arsenal.com/news/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-signs-club|url-status=live}}</ref> reported to be £56 million.<ref name="completes £56m" />

====2018–2019: Debut season, Premier League Golden Boot====
[[File:24 Merci Arsène - Celebrating Aubameyang's goal (41910954172).jpg|thumb|250x250px|Aubameyang (left) celebrating a goal in the [[Premier League]] in May 2018]]
On 3 February, Aubameyang made his debut for Arsenal against [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] in the Premier League in a 5–1 home victory, scoring the team's fourth goal, chipping the ball over a grounded [[Jordan Pickford]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11670/11235986/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-impresses-on-his-arsenal-debut|title=Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang impresses on his Arsenal debut|work=Sky Sports|access-date=4 February 2018|archive-date=5 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180205000709/http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11670/11235986/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-impresses-on-his-arsenal-debut|url-status=live}}</ref> After missing the Europa League matches against [[Östersunds FK|Östersunds]] for the Gunners due to being [[cup-tied]], Aubameyang registered his first away goal for the club in the team's 2–1 away defeat to [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43186393|title=Brighton & Hove Albion 2–1 Arsenal|date=4 March 2018|website=BBC Sport|access-date=22 March 2018|archive-date=19 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180319104141/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43186393|url-status=live}}</ref> Aubameyang registered his first assist for the team, setting up Henrikh Mkhitaryan's goal in a 3–0 win over [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] in which he also scored.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43275529|title=Arsenal 3–0 Watford|date=11 March 2018|website=BBC Sport|access-date=22 March 2018|archive-date=19 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180319104436/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43275529|url-status=live}}</ref>

Aubameyang scored twice in a 3–0 home win against [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]], making him the first player to score five times in his first six games for the club.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43530417|title=Arsenal 3–0 Stoke City|date=1 April 2018|website=BBC Sport|access-date=6 April 2018|archive-date=25 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181025010912/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43530417|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://twitter.com/Arsenal/status/980490246495395841|title=Arsenal FC on Twitter|work=Twitter|access-date=6 April 2018|archive-date=14 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191214150427/https://twitter.com/Arsenal/status/980490246495395841|url-status=live}}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=December 2019}} He scored twice in manager [[Arsène Wenger]]'s final home game for the club, opening and closing the scoring, whilst also assisting [[Alex Iwobi]]'s goal, in a 5–0 win over [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43939015|title=Arsenal 5–0 Burnley|date=6 May 2018|website=BBC Sport|access-date=6 May 2018|archive-date=25 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190425131933/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43939015|url-status=live}}</ref> He ended the season with ten goals and four assists in thirteen Premier League games and was the last goalscorer for Arsenal under Arsène Wenger.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44020157|title=Huddersfield Town 0–1 Arsenal|date=13 May 2018|website=BBC Sport|access-date=13 May 2018|archive-date=29 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190529104908/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44020157|url-status=live}}</ref>
[[File:Chelsea vs. Arsenal, 29 May 2019 20 (cropped).jpg|left|thumb|220x220px|Aubameyang after the [[2019 UEFA Europa League final]] loss in May 2019]]
Aubameyang scored his first goal of the following season in a 3–2 away win over [[Cardiff City]] on 2 September 2018. His strike from outside the box ended his personal run of 76 consecutive goals from inside the box in club football and was also his 150th goal in league football.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Pearlman |first1=Michael |title=Cardiff City 2–3 Arsenal |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45312124 |access-date=3 September 2018 |archive-date=2 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180902203212/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45312124 |url-status=live }}</ref> Aubameyang made his European debut for Arsenal, in the 4–2 home win over [[FC Vorskla Poltava|Vorskla Poltava]], scoring two goals while playing for 57 minutes.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45577861|title=Arsenal 4–2 Vorskla Poltava: Gunners cruise to Europa League win|date=20 September 2018|access-date=29 September 2019|website=BBC Sport|archive-date=13 November 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251113020016/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45577861|url-status=live}}</ref> By October 2018, Aubameyang had tallied 16 goals in Premier League play since joining Arsenal in February. According to Opta statistics, that gave him a minutes-per-goal ratio of 104.6, which set the record for the best minutes-per-goal ratio in Premier League history (minimum 10 goals).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dailycannon.com/2018/10/aubameyang-sets-new-premier-league-record-for-goals-per-minute/|title=Aubameyang sets new Premier League record for goals per minute|first=Dan|last=Critchlow|website=Daily Cannon|date=27 October 2018|access-date=27 October 2018|archive-date=25 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200325073753/http://dailycannon.com/2018/10/aubameyang-sets-new-premier-league-record-for-goals-per-minute/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Aubameyang became the first player to reach 10 goals in the Premier League that season, following a brace in Arsenal's 4–2 victory over [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] in the [[North London derby]] on 2 December. He also assisted a goal as Arsenal rose above Tottenham in the Premier League on goal difference.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46333099|title=Arsenal 4–2 Tottenham Hotspur: Unai Emery praises 'special' comeback|date=2 December 2018|access-date=29 September 2019|website=BBC Sport|archive-date=31 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190331121748/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46333099|url-status=live}}</ref> He scored his first Arsenal hat-trick in a 4–2 win over [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] on 9 May 2019 as the club reached the [[2019 UEFA Europa League Final|Europa League final]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48171988|title=Valencia 2–4 Arsenal: Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang hat-trick helps Arsenal to Europa League final|date=9 May 2019|access-date=29 September 2019|website=BBC Sport|archive-date=13 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190513184656/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48171988|url-status=live}}</ref> He was the first Arsenal player to score a hat-trick in the semi-finals of a European competition.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.squawka.com/en/features/valencia-arsenal-winners-losers-aubameyang-history-spain|title=Valencia 2–4 Arsenal: Winners and losers as Aubameyang makes history in Spain|publisher=Squawka|last=Jennings|first=Steven|date=9 May 2019|access-date=10 May 2019|archive-date=10 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190510124348/https://www.squawka.com/en/features/valencia-arsenal-winners-losers-aubameyang-history-spain|url-status=live}}</ref>

Aubameyang finished the season with two goals in a 3–1 away win at Burnley, meaning he ended the season sharing the [[Premier League Golden Boot]] title with Liverpool's [[Mohamed Salah]] and [[Sadio Mané]], on 22 goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48243725|title=Premier League Golden Boot: Salah, Mane and Aubameyang share prize|date=12 May 2019|work=BBC Sport|access-date=27 August 2019|archive-date=14 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190514054713/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48243725|url-status=live}}</ref> He played the full 90 minutes in Arsenal's 4–1 defeat to [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in the Europa League, failing to make a significant impact as the result meant Arsenal missed out on Champions League qualification.<ref>{{cite web |last=Elvin |first=Gustav |title=Koscielny, Aubameyang both 3/10 as Arsenal wilt in Europa League final |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/club/arsenal/359/blog/post/3863912/koscielnyaubameyang-both-3-10-as-arsenal-wilt-in-europa-league-final |publisher=ESPN |date=29 May 2019 |access-date=19 July 2020 |archive-date=18 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200818143442/https://www.espn.com/soccer/club/arsenal/359/blog/post/3863912/koscielnyaubameyang-both-3-10-as-arsenal-wilt-in-europa-league-final |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2019–2022: FA Cup win and departure====
On 11 August 2019, Aubameyang scored his and Arsenal's first goal of the season in their 1–0 opening match victory over [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] at [[St James' Park]], in which he demonstrated perfect technique to cushion a cross from [[Ainsley Maitland-Niles]], to slot the ball past [[Martin Dúbravka]], with [[José Mourinho]] hailing the strike as "a moment of genius".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/aug/11/newcastle-arsenal-premier-league-match-report|title=Aubameyang's Arsenal winner gives Steve Bruce losing start at Newcastle|last=Taylor|first=Louise|date=11 August 2019|work=The Guardian|access-date=11 August 2019|issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://metro.co.uk/2019/08/11/jose-mourinho-hails-pierre-emerick-aubameyang-genius-finish-arsenals-win-newcastle-10553898/|title=Jose Mourinho hails Arsenal star for moment of 'genius' in win over Newcastle|website=Metro|date=11 August 2019|access-date=29 September 2019|archive-date=21 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190921090003/https://metro.co.uk/2019/08/11/jose-mourinho-hails-pierre-emerick-aubameyang-genius-finish-arsenals-win-newcastle-10553898/|url-status=live}}</ref> Aubameyang scored his first home goal of the campaign in Arsenal's next game, a 2–1 win over Burnley on 17 August.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49302581|title=Arsenal 2–1 Burnley: Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang scores winning goal for Gunners|last=Poole|first=Harry|date=17 August 2019|access-date=29 September 2019|website=BBC Sport|archive-date=14 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190914150535/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49302581|url-status=live}}</ref> He scored his first European goal of the season on 19 September against [[Eintracht Frankfurt]] in the [[2020–21 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]], as Arsenal won 3–0 away from home on matchday 1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49745913|title=Eintracht Frankfurt 0–3 Arsenal: Gunners begin Europa League with win in Germany|last=Henry|first=Matthew|date=19 September 2019|access-date=29 September 2019|website=BBC Sport|archive-date=9 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210309235533/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49745913|url-status=live}}</ref>

Aubameyang's five goals in September, including equalizers against Tottenham and [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] and the winner against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], saw him named the [[Premier League Player of the Month]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/auba-named-premier-league-player-month|title=Auba named Premier League Player of the Month|website=www.arsenal.com|date=11 October 2019|access-date=11 October 2019|archive-date=11 October 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191011100817/https://www.arsenal.com/news/auba-named-premier-league-player-month|url-status=live}}</ref> On 5 November 2019, after [[Granit Xhaka]] was stripped of the Arsenal captaincy following his angry reaction to getting booed by the Arsenal supporters during their [[Premier League]] game against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportbible.com/football|title=Granit Xhaka Tells Arsenal Fans To "F**k Off" As He's Substituted|last=Jabbar|first=Nasir|website=Sport Bible|date=27 October 2019|access-date=27 October 2019|archive-date=14 August 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250814164227/https://www.sportbible.com/football|url-status=live}}</ref> head coach [[Unai Emery]] confirmed that Aubameyang would take over as the new Arsenal captain.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/50309446|title=Granit Xhaka: Arsenal midfielder stripped of captaincy - Unai Emery|website=BBC Sport|date=5 November 2019|access-date=5 November 2019|archive-date=6 November 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191106103534/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/50309446|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 1 December, following the dismissal of Emery, Aubameyang scored both goals in Arsenal's 2–2 draw with [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] under interim head coach [[Freddie Ljungberg]]. Aubameyang's first goal (a penalty) had to be retaken, after [[Video assistant referee|VAR]] discovered there to be encroachment in the penalty area. Aubameyang's first effort was kept out by goalkeeper [[Tim Krul]], however, his second effort (the same side as his previous attempt), was successfully converted.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50534313|title=Norwich City 2–2 Arsenal: Freddie Ljungberg says Gunners can '100%' make the top four|last=Sutcliffe|first=Steve|website=BBC Sport|date=1 December 2019|access-date=1 December 2019|archive-date=30 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191230010711/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50534313|url-status=live}}</ref>

Aubameyang scored in Arsenal's 1–1 draw with Crystal Palace on 11 January 2020, but was also sent off for a late challenge on Palace midfielder [[Max Meyer (footballer)|Max Meyer]]. Aubameyang was originally given a yellow card for the tackle by referee [[Paul Tierney (referee)|Paul Tierney]], however, the card was eventually upgraded to a red card, by the [[Video Assistant Referee|VAR]], resulting in Aubameyang's first-ever red card for the Gunners and would mean that the striker would miss Arsenal's next three matches against [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]], [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], and Arsenal's [[FA Cup]] tie against [[A.F.C. Bournemouth|Bournemouth]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50990599|title=Crystal Palace 1–1 Arsenal: Jordan Ayew scores equaliser for hosts as Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang sent off|last=Falkingham|first=Katie|website=BBC Sport|date=11 January 2020|access-date=11 January 2020|archive-date=11 January 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200111144414/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50990599|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 27 February, in Arsenal's Europa League second leg round of 32 match against [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] and with the aggregate score tied at 1–1, Aubameyang's scissor kick goal in extra time allowed his side to equalize the match and lead the tie on aggregate. However, following a 119th-minute goal by Olympiacos that meant Arsenal would be heading out of the competition, Aubameyang missed an open shot from five yards out in the last seconds of the match that would have seen his side through.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/51623263|title=Arsenal 1–2 Olympiacos (Agg: 2–2 AET): Gunners knocked out by last-gasp away goal|last=Rostance|first=Tom|website=BBC Sport|date=27 February 2020|access-date=19 July 2020|archive-date=14 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201014170117/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/51623263|url-status=live}}</ref> Following Arsenal's elimination, Aubameyang apologized for and lamented his miss, stating, "I feel very, very bad. It can happen but I do not know how I missed this chance. I was tired, I had some cramps but it is not an excuse."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en/amp/news/aubameyang-rues-very-very-disappointing-result-as-arsenal/oani0iu7fdu719gcaei63ik05|title='I feel very bad' - Aubameyang unsure how he missed late chance as Arsenal crashes out of Europe|last=Shaw|first=Alex|website=goal.com|date=28 February 2020|access-date=19 July 2020|archive-date=19 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200719075958/https://www.goal.com/en/amp/news/aubameyang-rues-very-very-disappointing-result-as-arsenal/oani0iu7fdu719gcaei63ik05|url-status=live}}</ref>

Following the resumption of the league in the wake of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Aubameyang did not score or assist in the first three Premier League games after the restart for Arsenal, but eventually netted a brace on 1 July against Norwich City in a 4–0 rout. Aubameyang's first goal was his 50th in the league for Arsenal, making him the quickest player to reach 50 goals for the club in the Premier League era, having achieved the feat in just 79 league appearances, four games quicker than all-time club goalscorer [[Thierry Henry]], and also became the sixth fastest to 50 in the Premier League, behind [[Andy Cole]], [[Alan Shearer]], [[Ruud van Nistelrooy]], [[Fernando Torres]] and Mohamed Salah.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/arsenal-pierreemerick-aubameyang-50-premier-league-goals-a4486121.html|title=Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang becomes fastest Arsenal player to 50 Premier league goals with Norwich strike|last=Ouzia|first=Malik|website=Evening Standard|date=1 July 2020|access-date=1 July 2020|archive-date=3 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200703190440/https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/arsenal-pierreemerick-aubameyang-50-premier-league-goals-a4486121.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Aubameyang also assisted the Gunners' second goal, which was scored by Granit Xhaka.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52072989|title=Arsenal 4–0 Norwich City: Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang scores two|last=Johnston|first=Neil|website=BBC Sport|date=1 July 2020|access-date=1 July 2020|archive-date=9 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201009003050/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52072989|url-status=live}}</ref> He ended the season with 22 league goals, one behind [[Jamie Vardy]], the winner of the [[Premier League Golden Boot|Golden Boot]], and tied with [[Danny Ings]] for second place.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Premier League Top Scorers|url=https://www.premierleague.com/stats/top/players/goals|access-date=24 August 2020|website=Premier League|archive-date=1 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191201143457/https://www.premierleague.com/stats/top/players/goals|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 18 July, in their FA Cup semi-final against defending champions [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], Aubameyang scored both goals in a 2–0 win for Arsenal, sending them to the [[2020 FA Cup Final|final]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2020/jul/18/arsenal-manchester-city-fa-cup-semi-final-match-report|title=Aubameyang doubles up to send Arsenal past City and into FA Cup final|last=Ronay|first=Barney|work=The Guardian|date=18 July 2020|access-date=18 July 2020|archive-date=2 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200802083704/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2020/jul/18/arsenal-manchester-city-fa-cup-semi-final-match-report|url-status=live}}</ref> On 1 August, he converted a penalty and scored the winner in the final, as Arsenal defeated [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] 2–1 and Aubameyang lifted his first trophy with the club, becoming the first African to win the FA Cup as a captain.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Arsenal 2-1 Chelsea: Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang double settles FA Cup final|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-chelsea/report/426339|access-date=1 August 2020|website=Sky Sports,Sky Sports|archive-date=3 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200803032710/https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-chelsea/report/426339|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="bbc">{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53546100 |title=Arsenal 2–1 Chelsea |first=Phil |last=McNulty |website=BBC Sport |date=1 August 2020 |access-date=1 August 2020 |archive-date=1 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200801202716/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53546100 |url-status=live }}</ref>
[[File:Manchester United v Arsenal, 2 December 2021 (08).jpg|thumb|Aubameyang (left) ahead of a Premier League match against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] in December 2021]]
On 29 August 2020, Aubameyang scored a goal in normal time and the fifth and winning penalty in a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|shoot-out]] win against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] in the [[2020 FA Community Shield|Community Shield]], after the game ended 1–1.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2020/aug/29/arsenal-liverpool-mens-fa-community-shield-match-report-290820 |title=Arsenal defeated Liverpool 5-4 on penalties to win the FA Community Shield |website=FA |date=29 August 2020 |access-date=30 August 2020 |archive-date=10 March 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210310001454/https://www.thefa.com/news/2020/aug/29/arsenal-liverpool-mens-fa-community-shield-match-report-290820 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 12 September, he scored in the first league game of the new season the final goal of a 3–0 win away to [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Sportbible |title=Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang Scores Incredible Team Goal As Arsenal Beat Fulham 3-0 |url=https://www.sportbible.com/football/news-pierre-emerick-aubameyang-scores-incredible-team-goal-for-arsenal-20200912 |access-date=14 October 2020 |publisher=Nasir Jabbar |date=19 September 2020 |archive-date=13 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210513163943/https://www.sportbible.com/football/news-pierre-emerick-aubameyang-scores-incredible-team-goal-for-arsenal-20200912 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 15 September, Aubameyang signed a new three-year contract with Arsenal.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/auba-signs-new-long-term-contract|title=Auba signs a new long-term contract!|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=15 September 2020|access-date=15 September 2020|archive-date=21 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211021205557/https://www.arsenal.com/news/auba-signs-new-long-term-contract|url-status=live}}</ref> On 1 November, he scored a penalty in a 1–0 away win against Manchester United, to grant Arsenal their first Premier League win at [[Old Trafford]] since 2006.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/54679344 |title=Manchester United 0–1 Arsenal |website=BBC Sport |date=1 November 2020 |accessdate=1 November 2020 |archive-date=3 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220203101806/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/54679344 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Aubameyang scored two goals for Arsenal in their 3–0 victory over [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] on 18 January 2021.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/55613917 |title=Arsenal 3–0 Newcastle |website=BBC Sport |date=18 January 2021 |accessdate=18 January 2021 |archive-date=15 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210415052146/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/55613917 |url-status=live }}</ref> However, he did not play in the club's next three matches, in order to tend to his ill mother.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/arsenal/story/4300553/aubameyang-doubt-for-arsenal-clash-with-man-united-explains-absence-on-sick-mother |title=Aubameyang doubtful for Arsenal-Man United due to sick mother |publisher=ESPN |date=28 January 2021 |accessdate=14 February 2021 |archive-date=15 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211215160300/https://www.espn.com/soccer/arsenal/story/4300553/aubameyang-doubt-for-arsenal-clash-with-man-united-explains-absence-on-sick-mother |url-status=live }}</ref> On 14 February, Aubameyang scored his first [[List of Premier League hat-tricks|Premier League hat-trick]] in a 4–2 win over [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]]. This took him to 200 career goals across [[Big Five (association football)|Europe's top five leagues]].<ref>{{cite news|date=14 February 2021|title=Aubameyang scores first Premier League hat-trick as Arsenal captain passes 200 goals in Europe's top five leagues|url=https://www.goal.com/en-in/amp/news/aubameyang-scores-first-premier-league-hat-trick-arsenal-captain-/lpf8wwo347ja16t1gvgmk83yo|access-date=14 February 2021|website=Goal.com|archive-date=16 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211216031636/https://www.goal.com/en-in/amp/news/aubameyang-scores-first-premier-league-hat-trick-arsenal-captain-/lpf8wwo347ja16t1gvgmk83yo|url-status=live}}</ref> On 25 February, he scored two goals against Benfica in a 3–2 win to secure a place in the [[2020–21 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] round of 16.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56185885 |title=Arsenal 3–2 Benfica |website=BBC Sport |date=25 February 2021 |access-date=26 February 2021 |archive-date=16 December 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211216031626/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56185885 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 14 March, Aubameyang was left out of the starting lineup in the North London Derby against Tottenham, the manager citing disciplinary reasons.

On matchday 16 of the 2021–22 season, Aubameyang was omitted from the squad for Arsenal's match against Southampton, with manager [[Mikel Arteta]] yet again citing disciplinary reasons.<ref>{{cite web|url =https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4184252/2021/12/11/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-left-out-of-arsenal-squad-after-returning-late-from-trip-abroad/|title =Aubameyang left out of Arsenal squad after returning late from trip abroad|website =The Athletic|date =11 December 2021|access-date =13 June 2025|archive-date =13 June 2025|archive-url =https://web.archive.org/web/20250613100136/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4184252/2021/12/11/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-left-out-of-arsenal-squad-after-returning-late-from-trip-abroad/|url-status =live}}</ref> Three days later, Aubameyang was stripped of the captaincy.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Aubameyang decision tough - Arteta|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59653090|access-date=15 December 2021|archive-date=2 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220202190304/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59653090|url-status=live}}</ref> On 1 February 2022, Arsenal announced Aubameyang's departure from the club by mutual consent.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-leaves-arsenal|title=Aubameyang leaves club by mutual consent|publisher=Arsenal FC|date=1 February 2022|accessdate=1 February 2022|archive-date=15 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220215173841/https://www.arsenal.com/news/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-leaves-arsenal|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Barcelona===
On 2 February 2022, Barcelona reached an agreement for Aubameyang to join the club. Aubameyang signed a contract until 30 June 2025 with an option to agree departure on 30 June 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|title=FC Barcelona sign Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2467985/fc-barcelona-sign-pierre-emerick-aubameyang|access-date=2 February 2022|website=www.fcbarcelona.com|language=en|archive-date=22 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220222095446/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2467985/fc-barcelona-sign-pierre-emerick-aubameyang|url-status=live}}</ref> Aubameyang made his debut for Barcelona on 6 February 2022, coming on as a substitute in a 4–2 win over [[Atlético Madrid]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=7 February 2022|title=Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang makes Barcelona debut in clinical win over Atletico Madrid - European round-up|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12534815/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-makes-barcelona-debut-in-win-over-atletico-madrid-european-round-up|access-date=8 February 2022|website=Sky Sports|language=|archive-date=8 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220208085349/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12534815/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-makes-barcelona-debut-in-win-over-atletico-madrid-european-round-up|url-status=live}}</ref> On 20 February, he scored his first competitive goals in his fourth match for Barcelona, scoring a hat-trick in a 4–1 away win at the [[Mestalla Stadium|Mestalla]] over [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] in a man-of-the-match performance.<ref>{{cite web |title=Valencia - Barcelona en directo de 25a Jornada en Estadio de Mestalla – SPORT |url=https://www.sport.es/es/directo/laliga/valencia-barcelona-22358141/narracion |website=Sport |language=es |date=14 February 2022 |access-date=20 February 2022 |archive-date=20 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220220171425/https://www.sport.es/es/directo/laliga/valencia-barcelona-22358141/narracion |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang nets first Barcelona goals as Xavi Hernandez's side stick four past Valencia |url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/liga/2021-2022/liga-live_sto8804890/story.shtml |work=Eurosport |date=20 February 2022}}</ref> On 20 March, Aubameyang scored a brace and assisted [[Ferran Torres]] in his only [[El Clásico]] helping Barcelona to a 4–0 away victory against the league leaders.<ref>{{Cite news |date=19 March 2022 |title=La Liga: Barca take stunning 4-0 lead at Real Madrid in Clasico |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/live/football/60564705 |access-date=20 March 2022 |archive-date=20 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230720164628/https://www.bbc.com/sport/live/football/60564705 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 14 May 2023, Barcelona beat [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] in a 4–2 win to secure the [[2022–23 La Liga]] title, meaning Aubameyang claimed the first league title in his career, despite playing just nine minutes for Barcelona before joining [[Chelsea F.C|Chelsea]] in the summer of 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ikechukwu |first=Chukwu |date=16 May 2023 |title=Barcelona Stars Greeted by Thousands of Fans During La Liga Title Victory Parade |url=https://sportsbrief.com/football/40867-barcelona-stars-greeted-by-thousands-fans-la-liga-title-victory-parade/ |access-date=18 May 2023 |website=SportsBrief - Sport news. |language=en |archive-date=18 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230518135002/https://sportsbrief.com/football/40867-barcelona-stars-greeted-by-thousands-fans-la-liga-title-victory-parade/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Marseille===
On 21 July 2023, Aubameyang left Chelsea and signed a three-year deal with [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Aubameyang exits Chelsea |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/aubameyang-exits-chelsea |date=21 July 2023 |access-date=21 July 2023 |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |archive-date=21 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230721170426/https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/aubameyang-exits-chelsea |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Marseille complete signing of Aubameyang from Chelsea |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4710288/2023/07/21/aubameyang-chelsea-marseille-complete-signing/ |date=21 July 2023 |access-date=21 July 2023 |website=The Athletic |archive-date=8 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250108050405/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4710288/2023/07/21/aubameyang-chelsea-marseille-complete-signing/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On 12 August, he made his debut coming on as a substitute in the 67th minute in a 2–1 win against [[Stade de Reims|Reims]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/677191 |title=Marseille 2–1 Stade de Reims |work=ESPN |date=12 August 2023 |access-date=31 August 2023 |archive-date=31 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230831003310/https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/677191 |url-status=live }}</ref> Three days later, he scored a brace against [[Panathinaikos F.C.|Panathinaikos]] in the [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League qualifying phase and play-off round|Champions League third qualifying round]] which gave his team a 2–0 lead; however, Marseille conceded a penalty in the stoppage time which equaled the tie 2–2, before losing 3–5 on penalties to be eliminated from the competition.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://talksport.com/football/1534471/marseille-matteo-guendouzi-pierre-emerick-aubameyang-champions-league-arsenal/ |title=Matteo Guendouzi cancels out ex-Arsenal captain Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang's heroics with two blunders to cost Marseille Champions League |work=talkSPORT |date=16 August 2023 |access-date=31 August 2023 |archive-date=31 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230831003312/https://talksport.com/football/1534471/marseille-matteo-guendouzi-pierre-emerick-aubameyang-champions-league-arsenal/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Al-Qadsiah===
[[File:Paris Saint-Germain - Olympique de Marseille, 8 février 2026 (42) (cropped).jpg|thumb|Aubameyang (middle) warming up ahead of a [[Ligue 1]] match against [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] in February 2016]]
On 18 July 2024, newly promoted [[Saudi Pro League]] club [[Al Qadsiah FC|Al-Qadsiah]] confirmed the signing of Aubameyang on a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/40588893/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-joins-saudi-club-al-qadsiah |title=Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang joins Saudi club Al Qadsiah |work=ESPN |agency=Reuters |date=18 July 2024 |access-date=15 January 2025 |archive-date=19 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240719203332/https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/40588893/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-joins-saudi-club-al-qadsiah |url-status=live }}</ref> He left the club a year later on 17 July 2025, after spending a single season at the club and notably scoring 17 league goals.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/aubameyang-leaves-saudi-side-al-qadsiah-after-one-season-2025-07-17/ |title=Aubameyang leaves Saudi side Al-Qadsiah after one season |website=Reuters |date=17 July 2025 |access-date=19 July 2025}}</ref>
