Dépor and Elche share the points after stunning goals from Aubameyang and Aguado |publisher=Mundo Deportivo |date=18 August 2026 }}</ref>

==International career==
Aubameyang was invited to play for [[Italy national under-19 football team|Italy U19s]] after a good season with Dijon, but he debuted for the [[France national under-21 football team|France under-21]] team in February 2009 in a friendly match against [[Tunisia national football team|Tunisia U21]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fff.fr/selections/espoirs/actualite/527910.shtml |title=FFF : sélections, football, fiche, espoirs, féminines, masculines, UEFA, FIFA |publisher=Fff.fr |language=fr |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090223055850/http://www.fff.fr/selections/espoirs/actualite/527910.shtml |archive-date=23 February 2009 }}</ref>

Aubameyang was also eligible to play for [[Spain men's national football team|Spain]] because he has [[Spanish nationality law|Spanish nationality]]. He decided to represent Gabon because his father once captained the team, but he maintains a close relationship with Spain and expressed a desire to play in La Liga prior to signing for Barcelona.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/20151028/202477613914/aubameyang-descarta-la-premier-y-revela-que-su-sueno-es-jugar-en-espana.html?facet=amp|title=Aubameyang reitera su sueño de jugar en España|website=mundodeportivo.com|date=28 October 2015|access-date=6 April 2018|archive-date=20 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180120071300/http://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/20151028/202477613914/aubameyang-descarta-la-premier-y-revela-que-su-sueno-es-jugar-en-espana.html?facet=amp|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2016/03/10/primera/1457603194_834392.html|title=Aubameyang: nació en Francia, pero su madre es de Ávila|last=AS|first=Diario|access-date=22 March 2018|language=es|archive-date=6 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200806085156/https://as.com/futbol/2016/03/10/primera/1457603194_834392.amp.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 25 March 2009, Aubameyang was selected for the [[Gabon national football team|Gabon national team]]<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/archive/southafrica2010/news/newsid=1040520/index.html | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20121111123635/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/archive/southafrica2010/news/newsid=1040520/index.html | url-status = dead | archive-date = 11 November 2012 | title = Giresse turns to Aubameyang youngsters | publisher = FIFA | date = 24 March 2009 | access-date = 10 August 2013}}</ref> and made his debut for the squad. He scored his first goal in a 2–1 victory over [[Morocco national football team|Morocco]], then scored a goal each in friendly matches against [[Benin national football team|Benin]], [[Togo national football team|Togo]], [[Algeria national football team|Algeria]] and [[Senegal national football team|Senegal]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=2015 Africa Cup of Nations Qualifiers matches|url=https://africanfootball.com/tournament-matches/220/2015-Africa-Cup-of-Nations-Qualifiers/|website=African Football|access-date=26 May 2020|archive-date=6 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200806055518/https://africanfootball.com/tournament-matches/220/2015-Africa-Cup-of-Nations-Qualifiers/|url-status=dead}}</ref>[[File:Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang – Gabon national football team.jpg|thumb|250px|upright|Aubameyang playing for [[Gabon national under-23 football team|Gabon]] at the [[Football at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Summer Olympics]]]]

Aubameyang was a key member of the Gabon national side that reached the quarter-finals of the [[2012 Africa Cup of Nations]] as co-hosts of the competition. He netted three goals in total, finishing the tournament as one of the top scorers. On 5 February 2012, he set up the opening goal for his team and hit the post in the quarter-final against [[Mali national football team|Mali]]. However, the match ended 1–1 after [[extra time]] and Aubameyang had his penalty saved in the [[penalty shootout|shootout]] to decide the game.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16889291|title=Gabon 1–1 Mali|website=BBC Sport|date=5 February 2012|archive-date=29 July 2019|access-date=25 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190729104642/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16889291|url-status=live}}</ref>

In July 2012, Aubameyang represented [[Gabon national under-23 football team|Gabon]] at the [[Football at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Summer Olympics]] in London. He scored in the team's opening game against [[Switzerland national under-23 football team|Switzerland]], which was Gabon's first-ever Olympic goal, and would also prove to be Gabon's only goal of the tournament. They were eliminated in the group stage.<ref>{{cite web |title=London 2012 football men – Olympic Football |url=https://www.olympic.org/london-2012/football/football-men |publisher=International Olympic Committee |access-date=3 November 2019 |date=7 March 2019 |archive-date=1 August 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120801011711/http://www.london2012.com/football/event/men/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 15 June 2013, Aubameyang scored a hat-trick of penalty kicks in Gabon's 4–1 [[2014 FIFA World Cup]] [[2014 FIFA World Cup qualification – CAF second round|qualifying]] win over [[Niger national football team|Niger]]. He then scored a brace against [[Burkina Faso national football team|Burkina Faso]] in the 2015 Africa Cup of Nations Qualification.{{citation needed|date=January 2018}}

Aubameyang [[Captain (association football)|captained]] Gabon at the [[2015 Africa Cup of Nations]], scoring the team's opening goal of the tournament in their 2–0 win over Burkina Faso on 17 January 2015.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.france24.com/en/20150117-football-africa-cup-nations-gabon-defeat-burkina-faso-2-0/|title=Gabon defeat Burkina Faso 2–0 in Africa Cup of Nations|date=17 January 2015|publisher=France 24|access-date=18 January 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160829200130/http://www.france24.com/en/20150117-football-africa-cup-nations-gabon-defeat-burkina-faso-2-0|archive-date=29 August 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> He rejected a callup for a pivotal World Cup qualifier at home to the [[Ivory Coast national football team|Ivory Coast]] in August 2017, and they lost 3–0.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mg.co.za/article/2017-08-31-gabon-weeps-for-its-lost-dreams|title=Gabon weeps for its lost dreams|first=Thomas|last=Kwenaite|date=31 August 2017|work=Mail & Guardian|access-date=28 September 2017|archive-date=28 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170928060010/https://mg.co.za/article/2017-08-31-gabon-weeps-for-its-lost-dreams|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 25 March 2021, Aubameyang captained Gabon to a 3–0 win at home to [[DR Congo national football team|DR Congo]], scoring the third goal to ensure qualification to the [[2021 Africa Cup of Nations|African Cup of Nations]] to be staged in Cameroon.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/arsenals-aubameyang-powers-gabon-to-2022-africa-cup-of/1xt979qst5wj51wbv2xhyvo8rn|title=Arsenal's Aubameyang powers Gabon to 2022 Africa Cup of Nations | Goal.com|website=www.goal.com|access-date=25 March 2021|archive-date=25 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210325195443/https://www.goal.com/en/news/arsenals-aubameyang-powers-gabon-to-2022-africa-cup-of/1xt979qst5wj51wbv2xhyvo8rn|url-status=live}}</ref> At that time, he contracted [[malaria]], in which he got a fever and had to be hospitalized.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/57000901 |title=Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang lost four kilos and was 'really, really down' after malaria |website=BBC Sport |date=5 May 2021 |access-date=5 May 2021 |archive-date=5 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210505225222/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/57000901 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Aubameyang tested positive for [[COVID-19]] before Gabon's first game in the [[2022 Africa Cup of Nations|African Cup of Nations]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/africa/59894558 |title=Afcon 2021: Gabon's Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang tests positive for Covid-19 |website=BBC Sport |date=6 January 2022 |access-date=14 January 2022 |archive-date=11 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220111000644/https://www.bbc.com/sport/africa/59894558 |url-status=live }}</ref> He withdrew from the tournament a few days later to undergo further medical examinations in England after being diagnosed with heart lesions.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ramsey |first1=George |title=Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang returns to Arsenal from AFCON for 'in-depth exams' |date=17 January 2022 |url=https://www.cnn.com/2022/01/17/football/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-arsenal-gabon-afcon-spt-intl/index.html |publisher=CNN |access-date=18 January 2022 |archive-date=18 January 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220118035128/https://www.cnn.com/2022/01/17/football/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-arsenal-gabon-afcon-spt-intl/index.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 18 May 2022, Aubameyang announced his retirement from international football.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Husband |first1=Ben |title=Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang releases statement announcing international retirement |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-international-retirement-27003069 |website=[[Daily Mirror]] |access-date=18 May 2022 |date=18 May 2022 |archive-date=22 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220622080507/https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-international-retirement-27003069 |url-status=live }}</ref> He made a total of 72 appearances for the Gabon national team and scored 30 goals.<ref>{{cite news |date=20 May 2022 |title=Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang: Gabon captain retires from international football |url=https://citisportsonline.com/2022/05/20/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-gabon-captain-retires-from-international-football/ |access-date=21 May 2022 |website=Citi Sports Online}}</ref> However, a year later, he announced he had changed his mind and would return to the national side. He said his decision had been prompted by a meeting with President [[Ali Bongo]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Aubameyang announces Gabon retirement U-turn|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/africa/65623145|access-date=17 May 2023|archive-date=15 September 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230915102524/https://www.bbc.com/sport/africa/65623145|url-status=live}}</ref>

Following a group stage exit at the [[2025 Africa Cup of Nations]] where Gabon lost all three matches, the Gabonese government decided to suspend the national team. Additionally, Gabon's sports minister Simplice-Desire Mamboula sacked head coach [[Thierry Mouyouma]] and banned both Aubameyang and team captain [[Bruno Ecuele Manga]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Battison |first=Paul |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cn56z2ye7nro |title=Government suspends Gabon team and bans Aubameyang |publisher=BBC Sport |date=2 January 2026 |access-date=5 January 2026 |archive-date=5 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260105064442/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/cn56z2ye7nro |url-status=live }}</ref> However, the suspension was lifted shortly after by new sports minister Paul Ulrich Kessany.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c07xdzdlg4mo |title=Gabon's government lifts sanctions on team and Aubameyang |publisher=BBC Sport |date=13 January 2026 |access-date=14 January 2026 |archive-date=14 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260114120452/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c07xdzdlg4mo |url-status=live }}</ref> On September 2, 2026, Aubameyang announced his retirement from international football, citing the "humiliation" from the sports minister as a key reason for his decision.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Aubameyang ‘humiliated’ as ex-Arsenal striker quits Gabon national team|publisher=Al Jazeera|url=https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/9/2/aubameyang-humiliated-as-ex-arsenal-striker-quits-gabon-national-team|date=2 September 2026|language=en|archive-date=2 September 2026|access-date=2 September 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260902212225/https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/9/2/aubameyang-humiliated-as-ex-arsenal-striker-quits-gabon-national-team|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Style of play ==
[[File:Aubameyang170727-2 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Aubameyang striking the ball in a training session with Dortmund in 2017]]
Aubameyang is primarily a striker, although he has also played as a winger, particularly on the left.<ref name=":0" /> His main assets are his pace, movement, and finishing.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-06-22 |title=Premier League Transfer News: World class striker Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang is perfect for the Premier League {{!}} Goal.com |url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/world-class-striker-aubameyang-is-perfect-for-the-premier-league/1bsuqdrfk08vs1qpo3b5ryufgy |access-date=2026-08-08 |website=www.goal.com |language=en |archive-date=8 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260808213057/https://www.goal.com/en/news/world-class-striker-aubameyang-is-perfect-for-the-premier-league/1bsuqdrfk08vs1qpo3b5ryufgy |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite news |last=Wilson |first=Paul |date=2019-08-23 |title=Jürgen Klopp wary of threat from former pupil Aubameyang |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/aug/23/jurgen-klopp-wary-pierre-emerick-aubameyang-threat |access-date=2026-08-08 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> Initially deployed on the wing by [[Jürgen Klopp]] at Dortmund, a position he occupied at Saint-Étienne, Aubameyang gradually transitioned into a more central role following the departure of striker Lewandowski in 2014.<ref name=":0" /> Klopp later described him as a "really good central striker" who developed into a "goal machine", highlighting his combination of speed and finishing.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-08-24 |title=Aubameyang's only weakness is his fashion, says Klopp |url=https://www.sbs.com.au/sport/article/aubameyangs-only-weakness-is-his-fashion-says-klopp/rpzs80emh |access-date=2026-08-08 |website=SBS Sport |language=en}}</ref> 

Aubameyang was regarded as one of the best strikers in the world during his prime years at Dortmund and Arsenal.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Baker |first=Andy Kelly, Ian |title=Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang one of world’s best strikers, says Jürgen Klopp |url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-one-of-worlds-best-strikers-says-juergen-klopp-znslhfggm |access-date=2026-08-08 |language=en-GB |archive-date=9 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260809093321/https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-one-of-worlds-best-strikers-says-juergen-klopp-znslhfggm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=2017-06-22 |title=Premier League Transfer News: World class striker Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang is perfect for the Premier League {{!}} Goal.com |url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/world-class-striker-aubameyang-is-perfect-for-the-premier-league/1bsuqdrfk08vs1qpo3b5ryufgy |access-date=2026-08-08 |website=www.goal.com |language=en |archive-date=8 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260808213057/https://www.goal.com/en/news/world-class-striker-aubameyang-is-perfect-for-the-premier-league/1bsuqdrfk08vs1qpo3b5ryufgy |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Man City line up move for Dortmund striker Aubameyang - source |url=https://www.espn.com.sg/soccer/story/_/id/37474072/manchester-city-line-move-borussia-dortmund-striker-pierre-emerick-aubameyang-source |access-date=2026-08-08 |website=www.espn.com.sg |archive-date=8 August 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260808141756/https://www.espn.com.sg/soccer/story/_/id/37474072/manchester-city-line-move-borussia-dortmund-striker-pierre-emerick-aubameyang-source |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Gary Neville]] hailed Aubameyang as "world class" in February 2020.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Gary Neville: Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang is world class |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/30965/11942019/gary-neville-pierre-emerick-aubameyang-is-world-class |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250723130307/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/30965/11942019/gary-neville-pierre-emerick-aubameyang-is-world-class |archive-date=23 July 2025 |access-date=2026-08-08 |work=Sky Sports |language=en-GB |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Antoine Griezmann]] was of similar praise as well: "He is definitely a world class striker who has an incredible consistency in his game".<ref name=":3" /> According to Klopp, Aubameyang is "one of the best players for the counterattack because of the timing of the runs and his really outstanding finishing.”<ref name=":4">{{Cite news |last=Hytner |first=David |date=2018-11-02 |title=Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang: from ‘crazy kid’ to Arsenal’s cutting edge |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/nov/02/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-arsenal-cutting-edge-lacazette |access-date=2026-08-08 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> His former Dortmund teammate Reus said, "You can always find 'Auba' on the pitch. I rate his running highly. Maybe things don't always work out, but if we get it even a bit right, we create very dangerous situations."<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=UEFA.com |title=The official website for European football |url=https://www.uefa.com/errors/ |access-date=2026-08-08 |website=UEFA.com |language=en |archive-date=24 February 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110224231632/http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/clubs/player%3D58031/profile/index.html |url-status=live }}</ref> 

In November 2018, ''[[The Guardian]]'' was of high praise for him in light of his goalscoring rate since arriving at Arsenal:<blockquote>"Aubameyang did it in France with St-Étienne, when he was Ligue 1’s second-top scorer in 2012-13 with 19 [...] He did it in Germany with Dortmund, when he was the Bundesliga’s top scorer in 2016-17 with 31 [...] Now he is doing it in England. How many other strikers can say they have delivered in three of Europe’s major leagues?"<ref name=":4" /></blockquote>Aubameyang credits former African strikers [[Samuel Eto'o]] and [[Didier Drogba]] as his main influences.<ref name=":1" /> He also has a tattoo on his arm dedicated to former Argentina striker [[Hernán Crespo]] that reads 'Crespo for life'.<ref name=":1" /> 

==Media==
Aubameyang was involved in the [[List of Amazon Prime Video original programming|Amazon Original]] sports [[docuseries]] ''[[All or Nothing: Arsenal]]'', which documented Arsenal by spending time with the coaching staff and players behind the scenes both on and off the field throughout their [[2021–22 Arsenal F.C. season|2021–22 season]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/full-all-or-nothing-trailer-released |title=Full 'All Or Nothing' trailer released |date=19 July 2022 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=21 July 2022 |archive-date=19 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220719150527/https://www.arsenal.com/news/full-all-or-nothing-trailer-released |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite AV media |date=19 July 2022 |title=All or Nothing: Arsenal {{pipe}} Official Full Trailer 🎬 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ta3CLkX-bzk |access-date=21 July 2022 |publisher=[[Amazon Prime Video|Amazon Prime Video Sport]] |via=[[YouTube]] |archive-date=20 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220720213032/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ta3CLkX-bzk |url-status=live }}</ref>

Produced by [[Fulwell 73]], [[FIFA]] released ''Captains'' in 2022, an eight-part sports [[docuseries]] following six national team captains in their respective [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification]] campaigns.<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |date=12 April 2022 |title=FIFA launches FIFA+ to bring free football entertainment to fans everywhere |url=https://www.fifa.com/about-fifa/organisation/media-releases/fifa-launches-fifa-to-bring-free-football-entertainment-to-fans-everywhere |access-date=17 October 2022 |website=[[FIFA]] |archive-date=5 March 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240305134456/https://www.fifa.com/about-fifa/organisation/media-releases/fifa-launches-fifa-to-bring-free-football-entertainment-to-fans-everywhere |url-status=live }}</ref> Aubameyang, representing Gabon, starred alongside [[Thiago Silva]] ([[Brazil national football team|Brazil]]), [[Luka Modrić]] ([[Croatia national football team|Croatia]]), [[Andre Blake]] ([[Jamaica national football team|Jamaica]]), [[Hassan Maatouk]] ([[Lebanon national football team|Lebanon]]) and [[Brian Kaltak]] ([[Vanuatu national football team|Vanuatu]]).<ref name=":02" /> It was released by [[Netflix]] and also shown on FIFA's own streaming platform, [[FIFA+]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zaazaa |first=Bassam |date=14 October 2022 |title=Lebanon's captain Hassan Maatouk to star in Netflix football documentary |url=https://www.arabnews.com/node/2181136/sport |access-date=17 October 2022 |website=[[Arab News]] |archive-date=27 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221027143814/https://www.arabnews.com/node/2181136/sport |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Aubameyang was born in [[Laval, Mayenne]], France.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/FootballFicheJoueur29427.html |title=Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang |newspaper=L'Équipe |location=Paris |access-date=30 August 2020 |language=fr |archive-date=1 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200701180015/https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/FootballFicheJoueur29427.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He is the son of former Gabonese international footballer [[Pierre Aubameyang]] and younger half-brother of [[Catilina Aubameyang|Catilina]] and [[Willy Aubameyang|Willy]], who have both played for Milan's youth teams.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0251-0e965c455bf7-d3f19b3ce371-1000--europa-league-final-key-man-pierre-emerick-aubameyang/|title=How brilliant is Dortmund's Aubameyang?|date=29 May 2019|publisher=UEFA|access-date=21 March 2025|archive-date=18 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170118155353/http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/newsid=2435147.html|url-status=live}}</ref> His mother is Spanish.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/leditiondusoir/data/750/reader/reader.html?t=1464279262044#!preferred/1/package/750/pub/751/page/15|title=Aubameyang, une star 'made in Laval'|website=l'édition du soir|first1=Arnaud|last1=Bodin|first2=Guillaume|last2=André|date=26 May 2016|access-date=1 August 2020|archive-date=28 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200228235234/https://www.ouest-france.fr/leditiondusoir/data/750/reader/reader.html?t=1464279262044#!preferred/1/package/750/pub/751/page/15|url-status=live}}</ref>
He is married to Alysha Behague, the couple have two sons, Curtys and Pierre.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://futballnews.com/aubameyang-celebrates-sons-pierre-jr-curtys-with-a-harry-potter-themed-birthday-party-after-fa-cup-magic/ |title=Aubameyang celebrates sons Pierre Jr & Curtys Birthday with a "Harry Potter" themed birthday party after FA Cup magic |website=Futball News |date=4 August 2020 |access-date=31 August 2020 |archive-date=7 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220707014047/https://futballnews.com/aubameyang-celebrates-sons-pierre-jr-curtys-with-a-harry-potter-themed-birthday-party-after-fa-cup-magic/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Fowler|first=Kate|date=27 January 2021|title=Who is 's wife? Age and Instagram of Alysha Behague|url=https://www.hitc.com/en-gb/2021/01/27/aubameyang-wife/|access-date=15 February 2021|website=HITC|language=en-GB|archive-date=27 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210127172257/https://www.hitc.com/en-gb/2021/01/27/aubameyang-wife/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In August 2022, Aubameyang suffered a broken jaw during a violent robbery of his home in [[Barcelona]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kinsella |first1=Nizaar |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-broken-jaw-robbery-barcelona-b1022072.html |title=Chelsea transfer target suffers fractured jaw in terrifying home robbery ordeal |website=Evening Standard |date=31 August 2022 |access-date=1 September 2022 |archive-date=1 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220901113022/https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-broken-jaw-robbery-barcelona-b1022072.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

He is multilingual, speaking French, English, Spanish, Italian, and German.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-borussia-dortmund-interview-future-my-100-th-goal-467965.jsp |title=Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang: "I have something in mind for my 100th goal, but it's a surprise |website=bundesliga.com |access-date=9 September 2020 |archive-date=12 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220812040629/https://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-borussia-dortmund-interview-future-my-100-th-goal-467965.jsp |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He raced alongside [[Lando Norris]] for [[McLaren]] in 2020 Virtual [[F1]] Monaco Grand Prix.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/f1/news/12433/11991770/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-confirmed-for-f1s-virtual-monaco-gp |title=Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang confirmed for F1's Virtual Monaco GP |url-status=dead |access-date=2 April 2026 |archive-date=27 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200627201820/https://www.skysports.com/f1/news/12433/11991770/pierre-emerick-aubameyang-confirmed-for-f1s-virtual-monaco-gp }}</ref>

'''Ibrahim Afellay''' ({{langx|ar|إبراهيم أفيلاي}}; born 2 April 1986) is a Dutch former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as an [[attacking midfielder]] or [[winger (association football)|winger]]. He currently works for Dutch broadcaster [[Nederlandse Omroep Stichting|NOS]] as a football pundit.

He played youth football at [[USV Elinkwijk|Elinkwijk]] before joining the [[PSV Eindhoven]] youth academy at age 10. After debuting in 2004, he represented PSV for eight seasons, helping them to four [[Eredivisie]] titles before moving to [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] for €3 million in January 2011. Rarely used by Barcelona and marred by injury, he was loaned to [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]] and [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] before signing for [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] in 2015. Afellay spent three seasons with Stoke before ending his career back at PSV.

Making his [[Netherlands national football team|Netherlands national team]] debut in 2007, Afellay appeared at the [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010 World Cup]], contributing to the Dutch side finishing in second place in the tournament. He was also present at [[UEFA Euro 2008|Euro 2008]] and [[UEFA Euro 2012|Euro 2012]], making over 50 appearances in total.

==Early life==
Afellay is of [[Morocco|Moroccan]] [[Riffian people|Riffian]] descent; his parents left their hometown [[Al Hoceima]] in the 1960s to work in the Netherlands. He grew up in Overvecht, a neighbourhood in [[Utrecht]] with a large immigrant population.<ref name=guardian>{{cite web | title = Euro 2012: Barcelona's Ibrahim Afellay could be Holland's lucky charm | url = https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2012/jun/01/euro-2012-barcelona-ibrahim-afellay-holland | work = The Guardian | access-date = 23 September 2013 | first = Edwin | last = Winkels| date = June 2012 }}</ref> Afellay and his brother, Ali, were brought up by their mother, Habiba, after his father died when he was young.<ref>{{cite web|title=Euro 2012: Barcelona's Ibrahim Afellay could be Holland's lucky charm|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2012/jun/01/euro-2012-barcelona-ibrahim-afellay-holland|website=The Guardian|date=June 2012 |access-date=21 May 2016 |last1=Winkels |first1=Edwin |last2=Dagblad |first2=Algemeen }}</ref>

==Club career==
===Beginning of career===
Afellay started to play football at local side VSK, but joined [[USV Elinkwijk]] after one season.<ref name=nos>{{cite web | title = Ibrahim Afellay – Story of Life | date=5 October 2011 | url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TYLV2jF2o04 | publisher = NOS | access-date = 23 September 2013}}</ref>

Afellay scored twice and provided an assist in the match.<ref name=uefa/><ref>{{cite web | title = Ibrahim Afellay blinkt uit bij PSV-Feyenoord | url = http://www.vi.nl/nieuws/ibrahim-afellay-blinkt-uit-bij-psvfeyenoord.htm | publisher = Voetbal International | access-date = 23 September 2013 | language = nl | date = 15 May 2005}}</ref> He also won the [[KNVB Cup]] after appearing as a substitute in the [[2004–05 KNVB Cup|final]] against [[Willem II (football club)|Willem II]], which PSV won 4–0.<ref name=matches/>

In the [[2005–06 Eredivisie|2005–06 season]], Afellay established himself as a first-team regular at PSV.<ref name=barca/> He formed a midfield partnership with [[Timmy Simons]] and [[Phillip Cocu]].<ref>{{cite web | title = seizoen 2005–2006 | url = http://www.psvweb.nl/archief/seizoen/2005-2006.php | publisher = PSVweb | access-date = 23 September 2013 | language = nl | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140427045231/http://www.psvweb.nl/archief/seizoen/2005-2006.php | archive-date = 27 April 2014 | df = dmy-all }}</ref> In his first four matches (Johan Cruijff Shield and league), Afellay received four yellow cards, resulting in an immediate suspension.<ref>{{cite web | title = Vierde geel Afellay kost hem duel tegen FC Utrecht | url = http://psv.netwerk.to/nieuws/artikel/11066_Vierde%20geel%20Afellay%20kost%20hem%20duel%20tegen%20FC%20Utrecht.php | publisher = PSV Netwerk | access-date = 19 September 2013 | language = nl | date = 28 August 2005}}</ref> In September, Afellay made his [[2005–06 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] debut against [[Schalke 04]] (1–0 win).<ref name=matches/> Overall, he managed to play a total of 23 league matches during a season hit with a string of minor injuries. PSV won the Eredivisie in 2006; Afellay's second title in a row.<ref>{{cite web | title = Historie: seizoen 2005/2006 | url = http://psv.netwerk.to/historie/seizoen.php?seizoen=2006 | publisher = PSV Netwerk | access-date = 23 September 2013 | language = nl}}</ref> In the [[2006–07 Eredivisie|next season]], he played 27 league matches and scored six goals for PSV. The team won the Eredivisie on a single goal difference after defeating Vitesse (5–1) in the last league round. Afellay made the third goal of the match.<ref name=matches/> For his performances that year, Afellay was awarded the [[Dutch Footballer of the Year|Johan Cruijff Award]] for being the most promising youngster in The Netherlands.<ref name=uefa/>

Afellay started the [[2007–08 Eredivisie|2007–08 season]] well by scoring the first goal and assisted the second in the away match against [[Heracles Almelo]] (0–2).<ref>{{cite web | title = Afellay leidt PSV naar moeizame zege: 0–2 | url = http://psv.netwerk.to/nieuws/artikel/16050_Afellay%20leidt%20PSV%20naar%20moeizame%20zege%3A%200-2.php | publisher = PSV Netwerk | access-date = 23 September 2013 | language = nl | date = 19 August 2007}}</ref> A month later, a broken toe forced Afellay into a two-month recovery.<ref>{{cite web | title = Afellay vier tot zes weken uit de roulatie | url = http://psv.netwerk.to/nieuws/artikel/16279_Afellay%20vier%20tot%20zes%20weken%20uit%20de%20roulatie.php | publisher = PSV Netwerk | access-date = 23 September 2013 | language = nl | date = 21 September 2007}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title = Afellay en Culina pakken speeltijd | url = http://psv.netwerk.to/nieuws/artikel/16762_Afellay%20en%20Culina%20pakken%20speeltijd.php | publisher = PSV Netwerk | access-date = 23 September 2013 | language = nl | date = 24 November 2007}}</ref> He extended his contract until 2011 in December.<ref>{{cite web | title = Afellay reaffirms PSV commitment | url = https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01c8-0e6ecb587129-013c09fe0f3f-1000--afellay-reaffirms-psv-commitment/ | publisher = UEFA | access-date = 23 September 2013 | date = 4 December 2007}}</ref> Afellay played 24 Eredivisie matches in the 2007–08 season.<ref name=matches/> He missed second-to-final match against [[FC Twente]] in which PSV could seal the championship, but the team failed to do so.<ref>{{cite web | title = Afellay mist kampioenswedstrijd door schorsing | url = http://psv.netwerk.to/nieuws/artikel/17875_Afellay%20mist%20kampioenswedstrijd%20door%20schorsing.php | publisher = PSV Netwerk | access-date = 23 September 2013 | language = nl | date = 6 April 2008}}</ref> The league title was eventually won in the last match against Vitesse with Afellay in the team.<ref name=matches/> The start of the [[2008–09 Eredivisie|2008–09 season]] was troublesome for Afellay when he received less holiday then desired after [[UEFA Euro 2008|Euro 2008]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Onvrede Afellay over beslissingen PSV | url = http://psv.netwerk.to/nieuws/artikel/18424_Onvrede%20Afellay%20over%20beslissingen%20PSV.php | publisher = PSV Netwerk | access-date = 23 September 2013 | language = nl | date = 27 July 2008 }}</ref> His season started well though, with the [[2008 Johan Cruyff Shield|Johan Cruyff Shield]] victory against [[Feyenoord]] (0–2) and three goals in the opening two Eredivisie matches. Afellay scored 13 league goals in total, including the only goal in the home match against Feyenoord in December. The 2008–09 season, in which PSV finished fourth, ended prematurely after he suffered an injury in April.<ref name=matches/><ref>{{cite web | title = Historie: seizoen 2008/2009 | url = http://psv.netwerk.to/historie/seizoen.php?seizoen=2009 | publisher = PSV Netwerk | access-date = 23 September 2013 | language = nl}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title = Blessure voor Afellay | url = http://psv.netwerk.to/nieuws/artikel/20216_Blessure%20voor%20Afellay.php | publisher = PSV Netwerk | access-date = 23 September 2013 | language = nl | date = 25 April 2009}}</ref>

For the [[2009–10 Eredivisie|2009–10 season]], Afellay shifted to a more defensive midfield position under new coach [[Fred Rutten]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Ibrahim Afellay| url = http://www.goal.com/en/people/netherlands/9518/ibrahim-afellay/profile| publisher = Goal.com | access-date = 13 September 2013}}</ref> In February, Afellay was promoted to second captain of the team. But because first captain [[Timmy Simons]] was mostly on the bench that season, Afellay was effectively the new captain.<ref>{{cite web | title = Afellay nu reserve-aanvoerder achter Simons | url = http://psv.netwerk.to/nieuws/artikel/21860_Afellay%20nu%20reserve-aanvoerder%20achter%20Simons.php | publisher = PSV Netwerk | access-date = 23 September 2013 | language = nl | date = 3 February 2010}}</ref> In March, Afellay received a three-match ban after video evidence showed foul play against [[Eyong Enoh]] in the match against Ajax.<ref>{{cite web | title = PSV accepteert schorsing Afellay | url = http://psv.netwerk.to/nieuws/artikel/22187_PSV%20accepteert%20schorsing%20Afellay.php | publisher = PSV Netwerk | access-date = 23 September 2013 | language = nl | date = 16 March 2010}}</ref> PSV and Afellay ended the Eredivisie season in third.<ref>{{cite web | title = Historie: seizoen 2009/2010 | url = http://psv.netwerk.to/historie/seizoen.php?seizoen=2010 | publisher = PSV Netwerk | access-date = 23 September 2013 | language = nl}}</ref> In the summer, he was officially appointed as team captain.<ref>{{cite web | title = Afellay aanvoerder, Engelaar reserve | url = http://psv.netwerk.to/nieuws/artikel/22897_Afellay%20aanvoerder%2C%20Engelaar%20reserve.php | publisher = PSV Netwerk | access-date = 23 September 2013 | language = nl | date = 27 July 2010}}</ref> In October, Afellay announced he would not sign a new contract with PSV.<ref>{{cite web | title = Verklaring PSV en Ibrahim Afellay | url = https://www.psv.nl/Nieuws/Nieuwspagina/Verklaring-PSV-en-Ibrahim-Afellay.htm | publisher = PSV.nl | access-date = 23 September 2013 | language = nl | date = 22 October 2010 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140427051140/https://www.psv.nl/Nieuws/Nieuwspagina/Verklaring-PSV-en-Ibrahim-Afellay.htm | archive-date = 27 April 2014 | df = dmy-all }}</ref> With the contract nearing its end, PSV was willing to sell in the winter break.<ref name=dutch>{{cite web| title = Ibrahim Afellay| url = http://www.dutchplayers.nl/player.php?id=569_Ibrahim%20Afellay| publisher = Dutch Players| access-date = 13 September 2013| archive-date = 27 April 2014| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20140427054000/http://www.dutchplayers.nl/player.php?id=569_Ibrahim%20Afellay| url-status = dead}}</ref> On 15 November, it was [[FC Barcelona]] who agreed on a deal with PSV.<ref name=barca/> Afellay signed a contract for four and a half years.<ref name=dutch/> In his last PSV match against Roda JC, he was granted a farewell by the fans.<ref>{{cite web | title = Afellay: ik had het er best wel moeilijk mee | url = http://psv.netwerk.to/nieuws/artikel/24048_Afellay%3A%20ik%20had%20het%20er%20best%20wel%20moeilijk%20mee.php | publisher = PSV Netwerk | access-date = 19 September 2013 | language = nl | date = 19 December 2010}}</ref>

===Barcelona===
[[File:Ibrahim Afellay 2011.jpg|thumb|left|Afellay with Barcelona in 2011]]
After completing the €3 million transfer, Afellay signed a contract for four and a half years at FC Barcelona.<ref name="dutch"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01eb-0e763b92ccd4-43e0cb818596-1000--barcelona-and-psv-strike-deal-for-afellay/|title=Barcelona and PSV strike deal for Afellay|publisher=UEFA|date=16 November 2010|access-date=16 November 2010}}</ref><ref name="Agreement with PSV for Afellay signing">{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada10-11/11/15/n101115114035.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101118011034/http://www.fcbarcelona.com/web/english/noticies/futbol/temporada10-11/11/15/n101115114035.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=18 November 2010|title=Agreement with PSV for Afellay signing|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=15 November 2010|access-date=16 November 2010}}</ref> He made his Blaugrana debut on 5 January 2011 in the [[2010–11 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]] match against [[Athletic Bilbao]], replacing [[David Villa]] in injury time. He continued to play 28 Barcelona matches in his first season, of which 18 were as a substitute. Afellay was given his first start on 19 January 2011 against [[Real Betis]] in the Copa del Rey.<ref name=afellay2010>{{cite web | title = Afellay: Ibrahim Afellay (2010–11) | url = http://www.bdfutbol.com/en/p/j8549.html?temp=2010-11 | publisher = BDFutbol | access-date = 12 September 2013}}</ref> His first goal also occurred in the Copa del Rey against [[UD Almería]] in February.<ref name=blau>{{cite web | title = FC Barcelona: On Ibrahim Afellay's Future | url = http://www.barcablaugranes.com/fc-barcelona-transfer-rumours-news/2013/7/6/4498206/on-ibrahim-afellay-future | publisher = Barça Blaugranes | access-date = 12 September 2013 | date = 6 July 2013 | first = Arron | last = Duckling}}</ref> Afellay scored his first league goal in a 3–1 away win against [[Málaga CF]] on the last day of the season.<ref name=afellay2010/> The [[2010–11 La Liga|2010–11 season]] ended in the title win for Barcelona and the fifth league championship for Afellay overall.<ref>{{cite web | title = Season 2010–11 First Division | url = http://www.bdfutbol.com/en/t/t2010-11.html | publisher = BDFutbol | access-date = 12 September 2013}}</ref> He made his Champions League debut for Barcelona against [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] and also went on to appear in the quarter-finals against [[Shakhtar Donetsk]]. He then played a vital role in the first match of the semi-finals against archrivals [[Real Madrid]] by coming on as a late substitute, dribbling past [[Marcelo (footballer, born 1988)|Marcelo]] into the box and assisting [[Lionel Messi]] for Barcelona's crucial opening goal in their 2–0 away victory. Afellay and Barcelona eventually [[2011 UEFA Champions League Final|won the Champions League]] after beating [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] (3–1). Afellay came on in the 90th minute of the final.<ref name=afellay2010/><ref name=blau/>

Afellay had a minor hamstring injury in the [[2011–12 La Liga|2011–12]] pre-season, therefore missing out on the [[Supercopa de España]] matches against Real Madrid.<ref>{{cite web | title = Ibrahim Afellay moet tijdje toekijken bij Barcelona | url = http://www.vi.nl/nieuws/ibrahim-afellay-moet-tijdje-toekijken-bij-barcelona.htm | access-date =13 September 2013 | language = nl | date = 31 July 2011}}</ref> He returned in time for one Champions League and one La Liga match before suffering an [[anterior cruciate ligament injury]] during training in September.<ref name=afellay2011>{{cite web | title = Afellay: Ibrahim Afellay (2011–12) | url = http://www.bdfutbol.com/en/p/j8549.html?cat=-&temp=2011-12&equip=-&rival=- | publisher = BDFutbol | access-date = 12 September 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Affelay set for knee surgery|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=1514992.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110925090229/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=1514992.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=25 September 2011|publisher=FIFA | date = 22 September 2011 |access-date = 1 September 2012}}</ref> After undergoing surgery, Afellay went through a seven-month recovery period. On 29 April, he returned to the field as a substitute in the 71st minute replacing teammate [[Sergio Busquets]] against [[Rayo Vallecano]] on a 7–0 away trashing win for the Catalan side.<ref name=afellay2011/> Although he appeared in two more La Liga fixtures, manager [[Pep Guardiola]] did not call-up Afellay for the major matches against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] and Real Madrid.<ref name=guardian/><ref name=afellay2011/>

====Schalke 04 (loan)====
In the build-up for the [[2012–13 La Liga|2012–13 season]], Barcelona manager [[Tito Vilanova]] notified Afellay of his decreased playing time in the upcoming year. It prompted him to accept a loan offer from [[FC Schalke 04]] on 31 August. He was reunited with [[Jefferson Farfán]] and coach [[Huub Stevens]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Afellay op weg naar hereniging met Stevens bij Schalke | url = http://www.vi.nl/nieuws/afellay-op-weg-naar-hereniging-met-stevens-bij-schalke.htm | publisher = Voetbal International | access-date = 12 September 2013 | language = nl | date = 30 August 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title = A fresh start | url = http://www.bundesliga.com/en/liga/news/2011/0000221387.php | publisher = Bundesliga | access-date = 13 September 2013 | date = 4 September 2012 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20131203084706/http://www.bundesliga.com/en/liga/news/2011/0000221387.php | archive-date = 3 December 2013 | df = dmy-all }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title = Trainer und Manager zufrieden: Freuen uns, dass der Transfer geklappt hat | url = http://www.schalke04.de/content/news_archive/news/trainer-und-manager-zufrieden--freuen-uns-dass-der-transfer-geklappt-hat-31-08-2012.html | publisher = schalke04.de | access-date = 31 August 2012 | date = 27 April 2014 | language = de | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150924114918/http://www.schalke04.de/content/news_archive/news/trainer-und-manager-zufrieden--freuen-uns-dass-der-transfer-geklappt-hat-31-08-2012.html | archive-date = 24 September 2015 | df = dmy-all }}</ref> Afellay made his debut the next day against [[FC Augsburg]]. He scored four goals at Schalke, including the opening goal in the [[Revierderby]] against [[Borussia Dortmund]] (1–2) and a goal against Arsenal in the [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]]. Afellay played his last Schalke match on 10 November; he picked up a muscle injury in a [[Netherlands national football team|Dutch national team]] friendly against [[Germany national football team|Germany]] a few days later.<ref>{{cite web | title = Goals guaranteed in Leverkusen | url = http://www.bundesliga.com/en/liga/news/2012/0000230052.php | publisher = Bundesliga | access-date = 13 September 2013 | date = 16 November 2012 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20131204035211/http://www.bundesliga.com/en/liga/news/2012/0000230052.php | archive-date = 4 December 2013 | df = dmy-all }}</ref> The injury prevented Afellay from playing until January, when he suffered a similar muscle strain in a friendly against [[Al Sadd SC]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Afellay sidelined for two months | url = http://www.bundesliga.com/en/liga/news/2012/0000236152.php | publisher = Bundesliga | access-date = 13 September 2013 | date = 7 January 2013 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20131205015052/http://www.bundesliga.com/en/liga/news/2012/0000236152.php | archive-date = 5 December 2013 | df = dmy-all }}</ref> With the recovery this time taking the remainder of the season, Afellay returned to The Netherlands after expressing his discontent with the medical treatment at Schalke 04.<ref>{{cite web | title = Afellay lijkt laatste duel voor Schalke te hebben gespeeld | url = http://www.vi.nl/nieuws/afellay-lijkt-laatste-duel-voor-schalke-te-hebben-gespeeld.htm | publisher = Voetbal International | access-date = 13 September 2013 | language = nl | date = 12 February 2013}}</ref> Although both parties kept in contact, Afellay did not return to [[Gelsenkirchen]] anymore after the injury; a move that led to criticism from Schalke's general manager [[Horst Heldt]].<ref>{{cite web | title = Schalke 04 verbitterd dat Afellay zich niet meer laat zien | url = http://www.vi.nl/nieuws/schalke-04-verbitterd-dat-afellay-zich-niet-meer-laat-zien.htm| publisher = Voetbal International | access-date = 13 September 2013 | language = nl | date = 26 February 2013}}</ref>

Afellay returned to Spain in May to evaluate his problems with the FC Barcelona medical staff.<ref>{{cite web | title = Toekomst herstelde Afellay bij Barcelona uiterst onzeker | url = http://www.vi.nl/nieuws/toekomst-herstelde-afellay-bij-barcelona-uiterst-onzeker.htm| publisher = Voetbal International | access-date = 13 September 2013 | language = nl | date = 31 May 2013}}</ref> He decided to start training two weeks earlier than the rest of the squad in order to focus on his recovery.<ref>{{cite web | title = Afellay meldt zich vroegtijdig bij Barça voor extra arbeid | url = http://www.vi.nl/nieuws/afellay-meldt-zich-vroegtijdig-bij-barca-voor-extra-arbeid.htm | publisher = Voetbal International| access-date = 13 September 2013 | language = nl | date = 25 June 2013}}</ref> But in August, Afellay had to undergo another surgery on a thigh injury in Barcelona, sidelining him for another four months.<ref>{{cite web | title = Afellay out of action until 2014 | url = http://www.goal.com/en/news/12/spain/2013/08/23/4207030/afellay-out-of-action-until-2014?ICID=PP_9518 | publisher = Goal.com | access-date = 12 September 2013 | date = 23 August 2013 | first = Stefan | last = Coerts}}</ref> Although he was originally not given a squad number, Barcelona assigned Afellay the number 19 jersey after the transfer window deadline had passed.<ref>{{cite web | title = Cuenca and Afellay assigned shirt numbers 23 and 19 | url = http://www.totalbarca.com/2013/news/cuenca-and-afellay-assigned-shirt-numbers-23-and-19/ | publisher = Total Barça | access-date = 12 September 2013 | date = 3 September 2013 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20130906053825/http://www.totalbarca.com/2013/news/cuenca-and-afellay-assigned-shirt-numbers-23-and-19/ | archive-date = 6 September 2013 | df = dmy-all }}</ref>

====Olympiacos (loan)====
On 10 August 2014 [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] announced the acquisition of Afellay on a season long deal. He scored his first goal in the [[Super League Greece|Super League]] on his debut on 23 August, receiving the ball in the 32nd minute following a pass from [[Alejandro Domínguez (Argentine footballer)|Alejandro Domínguez]].<ref>{{cite news|title=The Legend kicks off the championship with a win!|url=http://www.olympiacos.org/en/article/39662/legend-kicks-championship-win|access-date=24 August 2014|agency=Olympiacos.org|date=23 August 2014}}</ref> Afellay enjoyed a successful [[2014–15 Olympiacos F.C. season|season]] in Greece with Olympiacos as they won the league and [[Greek Football Cup|cup]] double.<ref>{{cite web|title=Olympiakos win Greek league for the fifth straight year|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/international/olympiakos-win-greek-league-for-the-fifth-straight-year-10188335.html|website=The Independent|date=19 April 2015 |access-date=13 September 2016}}</ref> At the end of the 2014–15 season, he was released by Barcelona after his injury hit stay at the club.<ref>{{cite news|title=Stoke City transfer gossip: Barcelona target heading for Turkey|url=http://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/Stoke-City-transfer-gossip-Barcelona-target/story-26706329-detail/story.html#CEuL4SlyGr2eLT1i.99=|access-date=15 July 2015|agency=m.stokesentinel.co.uk|date=16 June 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150715133305/http://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/Stoke-City-transfer-gossip-Barcelona-target/story-26706329-detail/story.html#CEuL4SlyGr2eLT1i.99=|archive-date=15 July 2015}}</ref>

===Stoke City===
Afellay joined [[Premier League]] side [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] on a two-year contract on 27 July 2015.<ref>{{cite web|title=Stoke Swoop For Afellay|url=http://www.stokecityfc.com/news/article/club-confirm-ibrahim-afellay-signing-2575152.aspx|website=Stoke City|access-date=27 July 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Afellay signs for Stoke City|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/33676556|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=28 July 2015|date=27 July 2015}}</ref> He made his debut on 9 August, in a 1–0 defeat against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] at the [[Britannia Stadium]], playing 78 minutes before making way for [[Peter Odemwingie]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Stoke City 0–1 Liverpool |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33750574 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=9 August 2015}}</ref> He was sent-off against [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] on 29 August 2015, for slapping [[Craig Gardner]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Stoke 0–1 West Brom|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34025390|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=21 May 2016}}</ref> He scored his first goal for Stoke on 1 December 2015 in a 2–0 [[Football League Cup|League Cup]] victory against [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Stoke 2–0 Sheff Wed|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34907303|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=2 December 2015}}</ref> Afellay scored his first Premier League goal on 13 February 2016 in a 3–1 win against [[AFC Bournemouth]].<ref>{{cite news|title=A.F.C. Bournemouth 1–3 Stoke City|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35510252|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=13 February 2016}}</ref> He scored his second Premier League goal on his 30th birthday in a 2–2 draw with [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]] on 2 April 2016.<ref>{{cite news|title=Stoke City 2–2 Swansea City|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35902640|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=2 April 2016}}</ref> On 22 April 2016 Afellay suffered a serious knee injury in training, ruling him out for up to eight months.<ref>{{cite news|title=Ibrahim Afellay: Stoke City midfielder has long-term knee injury|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36120070|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=23 April 2016}}</ref> In total Afellay played 36 times for Stoke in [[2015–16 Stoke City F.C. season|2015–16]] scoring three goals as the side finished in ninth position.

Afellay made his return from injury against Liverpool on 27 December 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Many players don't come back from this injury – I've done it twice|url=http://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/ibrahim-afellay-many-players-don-8217-t-come-back-from-this-injury-8211-i-8217-ve-done-it-twice/story-30015566-detail/story.html|website=Stoke Sentinel|access-date=28 December 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161229151045/http://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/ibrahim-afellay-many-players-don-8217-t-come-back-from-this-injury-8211-i-8217-ve-done-it-twice/story-30015566-detail/story.html|archive-date=29 December 2016}}</ref> Afellay signed a two-year contract extension with Stoke on 2 March 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Playmaker commits to Stoke by signing new two-year extension|url=http://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/playmaker-commits-to-stoke-by-signing-new-two-year-extension/story-30173239-detail/story.html|website=Stoke Sentinel|access-date=2 March 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170302090659/http://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/playmaker-commits-to-stoke-by-signing-new-two-year-extension/story-30173239-detail/story.html|archive-date=2 March 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Ibrahim Afellay signs new Stoke deal through to 2019|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39142046|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=2 March 2017}}</ref> He suffered another injury in April 2017 and underwent knee surgery.<ref>{{cite web|title=Stoke playmaker Ibrahim Afellay targeting pre-season comeback from injury|url=http://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/stoke-playmaker-ibrahim-afellay-targeting-pre-season-comeback-from-injury/story-30344176-detail/story.html|website=Stoke Sentinel|access-date=22 May 2017}}{{dead link|date=December 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> Afellay managed to make 13 appearances in [[2016–17 Stoke City F.C. season|2016–17]], of which 3 were starts as Stoke finished in 13th position.<ref name="2016/17"/><ref>{{cite web|title=Stoke 2016/17 Premier League season review|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11701/10887143/stoke-201617-premier-league-season-review|website=Sky Sports|access-date=22 May 2017}}</ref> He returned from injury in September 2017 but was unable to establish himself in Mark Hughes' in [[2017–18 Stoke City F.C. season|2017–18]] team making just six appearances. Afellay then had a training ground bust up with new manager [[Paul Lambert]] in March 2018 and was told to stay away from the club.<ref>{{cite news|title=Exclusive: Ibrahim Afellay told to stay away from Stoke City by Paul Lambert|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2018/03/28/ibrahim-afellay-told-stay-away-stoke-city-paul-lambert/|website=The Telegraph|date=28 March 2018 |access-date=29 March 2018|last1=Percy |first1=John }}</ref><ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43584854 BBC Sport, 29 Mar 2018, Stoke: Ibrahim Afellay told to stay away....] retrieved 31 March 2018</ref> Afellay returned to the club for pre-season ahead of the [[2018–19 Stoke City F.C. season|2018–19]] season and scored in a friendly against [[Walsall F.C.|Walsall]] but suffered another long-term knee injury.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ibrahim Afellay expected to remain on Stoke City sidelines for foreseeable future |url=https://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/stoke-city-ibrahim-afellay-injury-2099435 |website=Stoke Sentinel |date=11 October 2018 |access-date=11 October 2018}}</ref> His contract with Stoke was terminated by mutual consent on 28 January 2019.<ref>{{cite web |title=AFELLAY DEPARTS |url=https://www.stokecityfc.com/news/afellay-departs |website=Stoke City |access-date=28 January 2019}}</ref>

===Return to PSV===
On 18 June 2019, PSV announced the return of Afellay after nine years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.psv.nl/english-psv/news/article/afellay-returns-to-psv.htm|access-date=18 June 2019|title=Afellay returns to PSV|date=18 June 2019|archive-date=18 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190618085541/https://www.psv.nl/english-psv/news/article/afellay-returns-to-psv.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 31 January 2021, Afellay announced his retirement from professional football.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Afellay (34) hakt knoop door en zet punt achter voetballoopbaan|url=https://nos.nl/l/2366848|access-date=1 February 2021|website=nos.nl|date=31 January 2021 |language=nl}}</ref> He stated: "What I wanted has not happened. But I am at peace with it. You know that this moment will come sooner or later. It's fine like this."<ref name=":0" />

==International career==
[[File:Ibrahim Afellay.jpg|thumb|Afellay with [[PSV Eindhoven|PSV]] in 2008]]
Afellay and his family are [[Moroccans in the Netherlands|Moroccan Dutch]]. After both the Moroccan and the Dutch national teams managers selected him for their squads, he was caught in the dilemma to either play for the Moroccan national team, because of his Moroccan descent, or to play for the Dutch team, the Netherlands being his place of birth and residence. He ultimately decided to play for the Dutch national team despite the heavy competition for places in midfield.<ref name=qantara>{{cite web|title=Little Big Man in a Team of Giants|url=http://en.qantara.de/Little-Big-Man-in-a-Team-of-Giants/8072c8141i1p164/index.html|publisher=qantara.de| date = 20 June 2008 |access-date=20 June 2008}}</ref> He made his international debut in a Euro 2008 qualifier against [[Slovenia national football team|Slovenia]] on 28 March 2007. He played in the [[UEFA Euro 2008|2008 European Championships]] as a substitute.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/euro_2008/7363339.stm | title = Netherlands 3-0 Italy | publisher = BBC | date = 9 June 2008 | access-date = 4 April 2018}}</ref> Just seconds after replacing [[Dirk Kuyt]] in the group match against [[Italy national football team|Italy]] he nearly scored a goal but his shot hit the top of the crossbar. In their last group match against [[Romania national football team|Romania]], he was given a place in the starting eleven alongside [[Arjen Robben]] in midfield. On 12 October 2010, Afellay scored his first international goals in a [[UEFA Euro 2012 qualification|Euro 2012 qualifier]] against [[Sweden men's national football team|Sweden]].

===2010 World Cup===
Afellay was part of the Dutch team for the [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010 World Cup]] managed by [[Bert van Marwijk]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2010/may/27/holland-world-cup-23-man-squad |title=Holland coach Bert van Marwijk finalises World Cup squad |work=The Guardian |date=27 May 2010 |agency=Press Association |access-date=27 May 2010}}</ref> The player came on as a substitute for their first and second matches in the competition, a 2–0 victory over [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]]<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.fifa.com/tournaments/archive/worldcup/southafrica2010/matches/round=249722/match=300061478/index.html | title = Netherlands 2:0 Denmark | publisher = FIFA | date = 14 June 2010 | access-date = 27 April 2014}}</ref> and 1–0 victory over [[Japan national football team|Japan]] respectively, as well as the round of 16 match against [[Slovakia national football team|Slovakia]].

===Euro 2012===
Despite being injured for most of the [[2011–12 La Liga|2011–12]] season, he was included in the Netherlands' [[UEFA Euro 2012|Euro 2012]] squad. On 2 June 2012, Afellay scored two goals in a 6–0 friendly win over [[Northern Ireland national football team|Northern Ireland]], which was the Netherlands' final match ahead of the tournament. In the first match of the tournament, his team suffered a [[UEFA Euro 2012 Group B|1–0]] loss to [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]]. He was part of the starting eleven against [[German national football team|Germany]] as well. After the second loss, the head coach [[Bert van Marwijk]] decided to replace him with [[Rafael van der Vaart]].

Marinos to help Kashima Antlers reach the Emperor's Cup Final.{{cite news|title=柴崎がコンディション不安一蹴の2アシスト!!鹿島19冠王手「次が大事」|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?206568-206568-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=29 December 2016|access-date=18 April 2020}} He helped the club beat [[Kawasaki Frontale]] 2–1 to win the [[2016 Emperor's Cup#Final|Emperor's Cup Final]].{{cite news|title=ゲキつよっ!!vol.5「際立った鹿島の完成度。憲剛はレジェンドの境地へ」|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?206691-206691-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=31 December 2016|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=鹿島Ｖ ベテラン若手が融合...黄金時代再来の予感|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/news/1759867.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=1 January 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}} At the end of the 2016 season, he went on to make forty–six appearances and scoring six times in all competitions. ===Tenerife=== Following the 2016 season, Shibasaki was linked a move away from Kashima Antlers, which the club's executives were willing to sell him at a right price.{{cite news|title=柴崎の海外移籍を鹿島容認 好条件なら「仕方ない」|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/news/1754118.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=20 December 2016|access-date=18 April 2020}} It was announced on 31 January 2017, Shibasaki signed a six-month contract with Spanish [[Segunda División]] side [[CD Tenerife]].{{cite web|url=http://www.clubdeportivotenerife.es/noticia/gaku-shibasaki-nuevo-jugador-del-cd-tenerife|title=Gaku Shibasaki, nuevo jugador del CD Tenerife|trans-title=Gaku Shibasaki, new player of CD Tenerife|publisher=CD Tenerife|language=es|date=31 January 2017|access-date=18 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190505032213/https://www.clubdeportivotenerife.es/noticia/gaku-shibasaki-nuevo-jugador-del-cd-tenerife|archive-date=5 May 2019|url-status=live}} His departure was confirmed by Kashima Antlers the next day.{{cite web|url=https://www.antlers.co.jp/news/release/58378|title=柴崎選手がCDテネリフェに移籍|publisher=Kashima Antlers|language=ja|date=1 February 2017|access-date=18 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200413152903/https://www.antlers.co.jp/news/release/58378|archive-date=13 April 2020|url-status=live}} He was linked with a move to [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]] but chose instead to join CD Tenerife.{{cite news|title= El plan B es Gaku Shibasaki|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/las-palmas/2017/01/20/58827696e5fdea2e638b469e.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=20 January 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=柴崎急転、破談ラスパルマスの隣島テネリフェと契約|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/world/news/1772777.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=1 February 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}} Having trained with the club shortly, Shibasaki's career at CD Tenerife, however, suffered a setback when he struggled to adapt to an unfamiliar environment, and at one point, wanted to leave the club.{{cite web|url=https://www.clubdeportivotenerife.es/noticia/primer-entrenamiento-de-gaku-shibasaki|title=Primer entrenamiento de Gaku Shibasaki|publisher=CD Tenerife|language=es|date=2 February 2017|access-date=18 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417154700/https://www.clubdeportivotenerife.es/noticia/primer-entrenamiento-de-gaku-shibasaki|archive-date=17 April 2020|url-status=live}}
{{cite news|title=¡Shibasaki quiere irse de Tenerife... 10 días después!|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/tenerife/2017/02/10/589de38aca47411a308b470e.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=10 February 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=柴崎が堪能した故郷の味。テネリフェ島の日本料理店で見せたピッチ外の素顔【現地取材】|url=https://www.footballchannel.jp/2017/03/06/post200779/|publisher=Football Channel|language=ja|date=6 March 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}} But Shibasaki managed to overcome the setback and resumed training with the side, with the club's manager [[José Luis Martí]] called on the media and supporters for patient on Shibasaki and give him more time in adapt in Spain.{{cite news|title=Martí pide paciencia con Shibasaki|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/tenerife/2017/02/22/58acb3fb22601da9618b458a.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=22 February 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=柴崎、テネリフェでトレーニング開始も指揮官は慎重な姿勢「全体練習に参加できるまでは...」|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?210258-210258-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=es|date=25 February 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=テネリフェ柴崎、全体練習合流でデビューへ前進! 今節メンバー入りの可能性も|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?210602-210602-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=2 March 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}} He made his debut for the club on 19 March 2017, replacing [[Aitor Sanz]] in a 1–0 home loss against [[CF Reus Deportiu]].{{cite web|url=https://www.clubdeportivotenerife.es/noticia/tropiezo-en-el-heliodoro-rodriguez-lopez|title=Tropiezo en el Heliodoro Rodríguez López|publisher=CD Tenerife|language=es|date=19 March 2017|access-date=18 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417155916/https://www.clubdeportivotenerife.es/noticia/tropiezo-en-el-heliodoro-rodriguez-lopez|archive-date=17 April 2020|url-status=live}} Since making his debut for CD Tenerife, Shibasaki said in an interview with Marca that his style of football fit well in Spain and acknowledged that the differences of "the pace of the game" in Spain compared to Japan.{{cite news|title=Shibasaki: "Creo que mi estilo puede encajar bien en España"|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/tenerife/2017/05/04/590b33b446163f2b748b45e9.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=4 May 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Shibasaki destaca la mayor intensidad del fútbol español|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/tenerife/2017/04/03/58e214b7e5fdea51248b45be.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=4 March 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}} Shibasaki then scored his first goal abroad on 28 May 2017 (as well as, his 25th birthday), netting his team's second in a 3–1 away win against [[AD Alcorcón]].{{cite web|url=https://www.clubdeportivotenerife.es/noticia/victoria-de-un-pletorico-cd-tenerife|title=Victoria de un pletórico CD Tenerife|publisher=CD Tenerife|language=es|date=28 May 2017|access-date=18 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417162132/https://www.clubdeportivotenerife.es/noticia/victoria-de-un-pletorico-cd-tenerife|archive-date=17 April 2020|url-status=live}}
{{cite news|title=Shibasaki se estrena como goleador en España ... ¡el día de su cumpleaños!|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/tenerife/2017/05/28/592acc29e2704e3c688b459b.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=28 May 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}} He became a regular starter for the side and impressed during [[2017 Segunda División play-offs|the play-offs]], scoring the winner in a 1–0 home success over [[Cádiz CF]]; his side, however, failed to achieve promotion.{{cite news|title=Shibasaki mete al Tenerife en la final doblegando a un gran Cádiz|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/segunda-division/2017/06/18/5946e2d5268e3ee64d8b4693.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=18 June 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=La tardía pero crucial importancia de contar con... Gaku Shibasaki|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/segunda-division/2017/06/21/594ae093e5fdea20128b4627.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=21 June 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}} Despite this, Shibasaki's performance earned him recognition among CD Tenerife supporters and the Manager, José Luis Martí, himself.{{cite web|url=https://www.clubdeportivotenerife.es/noticia/gaku-shibasaki-recibira-el-premio-al-jugador-cinco-estrellas|title=Gaku Shibasaki recibirá el premio al Jugador Cinco Estrellas|publisher=CD Tenerife|language=es|date=15 June 2017|access-date=18 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417160838/https://www.clubdeportivotenerife.es/noticia/gaku-shibasaki-recibira-el-premio-al-jugador-cinco-estrellas|archive-date=17 April 2020|url-status=live}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.clubdeportivotenerife.es/noticia/gaku-tenemos-un-corazon-muy-fuerte-y-jugamos-con-nuestra-aficion|title=Gaku: "Tenemos un corazón muy fuerte y jugamos con nuestra afición"|publisher=CD Tenerife|language=es|date=16 June 2017|access-date=18 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417160826/https://www.clubdeportivotenerife.es/noticia/gaku-tenemos-un-corazon-muy-fuerte-y-jugamos-con-nuestra-aficion|archive-date=17 April 2020|url-status=live}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.clubdeportivotenerife.es/noticia/premio-de-montesano-para-jorge-y-gaku|title=Premio de Montesano para Jorge y Gaku|publisher=CD Tenerife|language=es|date=22 June 2017|access-date=18 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200417160824/https://www.clubdeportivotenerife.es/noticia/premio-de-montesano-para-jorge-y-gaku|archive-date=17 April 2020|url-status=live}}
{{cite news|title=柴崎を称賛するテネリフェ監督「フットボールをよく理解している」|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?216759-216759-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=21 May 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}} At the end of the 2016–17 season, he went on to make sixteen appearances and scoring two times in all competitions. ===Getafe=== Despite CD Tenerife planned on extending his contract, it was announced on that 17 July 2017 Shibasaki signed a four-year contract with [[Getafe CF]], [[2016–17 Segunda División|recently promoted]] to [[La Liga]] instead.{{cite news|title=テネリフェ、半年後の柴崎との契約延長も視野に...ポジションはトップ下か|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?208785-208785-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=2 February 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=テネリフェ、柴崎岳との契約延長を希望とスペイン紙|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/world/news/1846673.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=27 June 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite web|url=http://getafecf.com/Noticia/tabid/137/Article/4551/Gaku-Shibasaki-azulon.aspx|title=Gaku Shibasaki azulón|publisher=Getafe CF|language=es|date=17 July 2017|access-date=18 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170802174118/http://getafecf.com/Noticia/tabid/137/Article/4551/Gaku-Shibasaki-azulon.aspx|archive-date=2 August 2017|url-status=live}} Upon joining the club, he said about the transfer move: "I had been wanting to reach the Spanish League for a long time. Since last season I was able to be in Spain and now I have been able to take the opportunity to be here."{{cite news|title=Gaku Shibasaki ya apunta al Real Madrid|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/getafe/2017/07/21/5971cde946163f20788b462c.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=21 July 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}} Shibasaki made his debut in the category on 20 August 2017, starting in a 0–0 away draw against [[Athletic Bilbao]].{{cite web|url=https://futbol.as.com/futbol/2017/08/20/primera/1503219846_950709.html|title=Premio a la resistencia del Geta|trans-title=Prize to ''Geta's'' resistance|publisher=[[Diario AS]]|language=es|date=20 August 2017|access-date=20 August 2017}}
{{cite news|title=ヘタフェ柴崎岳２トップの右で先発、決定機は作れず|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/world/news/1875395.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=21 August 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}} He scored his first goal for Getafe against [[FC Barcelona]] in a 1–2 loss at home.{{cite news|title= Así fue el misil tierra aire de Shibasaki que hizo soñar al Getafe|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/getafe/2017/09/16/59bd3d45ca47416b148b45da.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=16 September 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}} However, during the match, Shibasaki suffered a foot injury and was substituted in the 54th minute; as a result, he was sidelined for three months, with December was his expectant return date.{{cite news|title=Shibasaki estará mes y medio de baja|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/getafe/2017/09/19/59c0e10a46163f0f298b462b.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=19 September 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=ヘタフェ柴崎岳は12月復帰か、スペイン紙報じる|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/world/news/201710040000096.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=4 October 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}} It wasn't until on 9 December 2017 when he made his return, coming on as a 74th-minute substitute, in a 0–0 draw against [[SD Eibar]].{{cite news|title=Las paradas de Dmitrovic empiezan a dar puntos|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/eibar/2017/12/10/5a2d599ae5fdea43638b468f.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=10 December 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Getafe y Eibar, empate entre clones|url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2017/12/09/actualidad/1512819612_035866.html|publisher=El Pais|language=es|date=9 December 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}} Since returning to the first team, Shibasaki rotated in the starting line–up, mostly coming from the substitute bench.{{cite news|title=El Getafe gana a Las Palmas y se acerca a Europa|url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2017/12/20/actualidad/1513806151_552441.html|publisher=El Pais|language=es|date=20 December 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=El Getafe acelera la caída del Málaga|url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2018/01/12/actualidad/1515788463_438061.html|publisher=El Pais|language=es|date=12 January 2018|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=La lógica del Getafe para sobrevivir y pelear en Primera|url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2018/03/02/actualidad/1520010307_183388.html|publisher=El Pais|language=es|date=2 March 2018|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=柴崎、乾ともにベンチ 日本人対決実現せず|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/world/news/201804220000195.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=22 April 2018|access-date=18 April 2020}} At the end of the 2017–18 season, he went on to make twenty–appearances and scoring once in all competitions. Shibasaki made his first start of the 2018–19 season, starting the whole game, in a 2–0 loss against Real Madrid in the opening game of the season.{{cite news|title=Bale se hace con los mandos del Madrid|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/primera-division/2018/08/20/5b79eb14468aeba9668b45d5.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=20 August 2018|access-date=18 April 2020}} However, his first team opportunities at Getafe soon became limited and spent most of the season on the substitute bench.{{cite news|title=Rober Ibáñez vuelve a una lista tres jornadas después|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/getafe/2018/09/30/5bb0ee73268e3e47758b461d.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=30 September 2018|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=A Huesca con todo|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/getafe/2018/11/03/5bddc88ae5fdeaac6f8b4678.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=3 November 2018|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Flamini entra en la lista para Montilivi|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/getafe/2018/12/20/5c1ba01222601d65258b45de.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=20 December 2018|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=David Soria vuelve a la lista y Samu se queda fuera|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/getafe/2019/03/16/5c8ceed6e5fdea515b8b4600.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=16 March 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=ヘタフェで苦境の柴崎岳にチャンス?国王杯で開幕戦以来10試合ぶりに先発か|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?258008-258008-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=31 October 2018|access-date=18 April 2020}} After spending 127 days without playing for the side, Shibasaki made his return against [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] on 21 April 2019, where he started and played 61 minutes before being substituted, in a 3–0 win.{{cite news|title=El Getafe se postula para la Champions a golpe de VAR|url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2019/04/21/actualidad/1555834044_934556.html|publisher=El Pais|language=ja|date=21 April 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Gaku Shibasaki volvió a jugar 127 días después|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/getafe/2019/04/22/5cbd78de22601dbe3e8b45c3.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=21 April 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}} At the end of the 2018–19 season, Shibasaki went on to make nine appearances in all competitions. Reflecting on his second season at Getafe, he said: "I haven't played so much in the league for the last two years. After all, I want to prove my strength in a tournament of this level."{{cite news|title="導き手"柴崎岳の熱い思い「自分の力を証明したい」|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?277203-277203-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=17 June 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}} ===Deportivo La Coruña=== On 14 July 2019, Shibasaki signed a four-year contract with [[Deportivo de La Coruña]] in the second division, for a reported fee of around €2 million.{{cite web|url=https://www.rcdeportivo.es/noticia/gaku-shibasaki-nuevo-jugador-del-depor-2019-2020|title=Gaku Shibasaki, nuevo jugador del Dépor 2019–2020|trans-title=Gaku Shibasaki, new player of ''Dépor'' 2019–2020|publisher=Deportivo La Coruña|language=es|date=14 July 2019|access-date=10 August 2021|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20190714123332/https://www.rcdeportivo.es/noticia/gaku-shibasaki-nuevo-jugador-del-depor-2019-2020|archive-date=14 July 2019|url-status=live}} He was previously linked with a move to [[Club Universidad Nacional|UNAM]] and [[SD Huesca]].{{cite news|title=Michel piensa en el japonés Gaku Shibasaki para reforzar el centro del campo de Pumas|url=https://www.marca.com/claro-mx/futbol/mercado-de-fichajes/2019/06/12/5d011c4b46163f54568b45dd.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=12 June 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=El Huesca también quiere a Gaku Shibasaki|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/getafe/2019/01/02/5c2d152b22601d132b8b45e5.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=1 February 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}} Upon joining the club, Shibasaki said his objectives at Deportivo La Coruña is to get more playing time and helped the club get promoted to La Liga.{{cite web|url=https://www.rcdeportivo.es/noticia/gaku-en-su-presentacion-se-marca-como-meta-ayudar-al-equipo-a-conseguir-el-ascenso|title=Gaku, en su presentación, se marca como meta "ayudar al equipo a 2019|url-status=live}} In addition, he was given a number twenty–two shirt.{{cite web|url=https://www.rcdeportivo.es/noticia/dorsales-del-depor-para-la-temporada-2019-2020|title=Dorsales del #DÉPOR para la Temporada 2019-2020|website=Deportivo La Coruña|language=es|date=3 September 2019|access-date=10 August
