made his Deportivo La Coruña debut, starting the whole game, in a 3–2 win against [[Real Oviedo]] in the opening game of the season.{{cite news|title=Christian Santos rescata al Dépor|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/segunda-division/cronica/2019/08/18/5d596e84ca4741365e8b45f8.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=18 August 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}} After the match, his performance was praised by the Spanish newspaper.{{cite news|title=柴崎岳、開幕戦でフル出場デビュー...現地メディアからは称賛の嵐でチーム単独最高採点も|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?282689-282689-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=18 August 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}} In a follow–up match against SD Huesca, he set up a goal for [[Christian Santos]] to score the late consolation, in a 3–1 loss.{{cite news|title=El Huesca enamora y noquea al Deportivo La Coruña|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/segunda-division/cronica/2019/08/25/5d62e63a22601de8348b462a.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=25 August 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}} Since making his debut for the club, Shibasaki found himself in and out of the starting line–up, which saw him placed on the substitute bench.{{cite news|title=デポルティボ不調の要因に柴崎岳。現地メディアは「最高の状態からは程遠い」|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?286711-286711-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=2 October 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}}

{{cite web|url=https://www.cdleganes.com/noticia/previa-el-c-d-leganes-a-por-una-victoria-que-le-meta-en-el-play-off-de-ascenso|title= Previa: el C.D. Leganés, a por una victoria que le meta en el 'play-off' de ascenso|website=CD Leganés|language=es|date=23 May 2021|access-date=10 August 2021|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210810192520/https://www.cdleganes.com/noticia/previa-el-c-d-leganes-a-por-una-victoria-que-le-meta-en-el-play-off-de-ascenso|archive-date=10 August 2021|url-status=live}} ===Return to Kashima Antlers=== Following the expiration of his contract with Leganés, it was announced on 1 September 2023 that Shibasaki had re-joined Kashima Antlers. He joined the first team of the club on 4 September 2023 and was assigned squad number 20.{{Cite web|url=https://www.antlers.co.jp/news/team_info/95680 |title=柴崎 岳選手 加入合意のお知らせ |website=www.antlers.co.jp |language=Japanese |access-date=1 September 2023 |publisher=Kashima Antlers }} On 21 October 2023, he suffered a left hamstring injury that would keep him out for 8 weeks.{{cite web|url=https://www.antlers.co.jp/news/team_info/96600|title=柴崎 岳選手の負傷について|language=ja|website=www.antlers.co.jp}} Ahead of the 2024 season, Shibasaki was appointed captain and given the number 10 shirt.{{cite web |title=鹿島の新主将にＭＦ柴崎岳 １０番＆選手会長との"三刀流"主将と１０番兼任はクラブ史上初 |url=https://hochi.news/articles/20240121-OHT1T51138.html?page=1 |website=スポーツ報知 |access-date=15 January 2025 |language=ja |date=21 January 2024}} He made 26 appearances across all competitions. ==International career== ===Youth career=== Throughout 2007, Shibasaki represented the [[Japan national under-17 football team|Japan U-15]] side and appeared for the U-15 side in a number of matches.{{cite news|title=U-15代表、練習試合で京都ユースに敗戦|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?25943-6550-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=21 June 2007|access-date=13 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=[全日本ユース選手権]注目選手一覧(北海道、東北、関東編)|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?27791-8733-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=1 September 2007|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=U-15日本代表、宇佐美のゴールなどで快勝|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?29238-9804-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=18 October 2007|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=[AFC・U-16選手権予選]U-15日本代表が白星発進!!|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?29445-10023-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=25 October 2007|access-date=18 April 2020}} In 2008, Shibasaki was called up to the Japan U-16 squad for both the [[Montaigu Tournament]] and [[Viktor Bannikov Memorial Tournament]].{{cite news|title=U-16日本代表に宇佐美ら|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?37691-18435-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=24 May 2008|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=U-16代表、宇佐美が1点返すも同トルコ代表に6失点大敗|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?38317-19092-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=9 June 2008|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=U-16代表、杉本、高木弾でポーランドに終盤追いつきドロー|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?38318-19093-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=9 June 2008|access-date=18 April 2020}} Later in September 2008, he was called up to the Japan U-16 squad for the [[2008 AFC U-16 Championship|AFC U-16 Championship]] in [[Uzbekistan]].{{cite news|title=アジア選手権に挑むU-16日本代表メンバーを発表|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?42501-23230-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=16 September 2008|access-date=18 April 2020}} Shibasaki scored Japan's U16 first goal of the tournament, in a 4–0 win against [[Malaysia national under-16 football team|Malaysia U-16]] on 5 October 2008.{{cite news|title=[AFC U-16選手権]宇佐美2発!U-16日本代表白星発進! |url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?43443-24319-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=5 October 2008|access-date=18 April 2020}} He made two more appearances in the group stage and helped the national side progress to the quarter–finals of the tournament.{{cite news|title= [AFC U-16選手権]U-16代表、UAEに6発大勝(現地レポート) |url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?43535-24413-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=8 October 2008|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=[AFC U-16選手権]日本、ロスタイム被弾でイエメンに敗れる(現地レポート) |url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?43635-24513-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=10 October 2008|access-date=18 April 2020}} Shibasaki appeared in two more matches in the tournament by beating [[Saudi Arabia national under-17 football team|Saudi Arabia U-16]] 2–0 in the quarter–finals, but lost 2–1 to [[South Korea national under-17 football team|South Korea U-16]] in the semi–finals.{{cite news|title=[AFC U-16選手権]日本ベスト4進出でU-17W杯出場権獲得!(現地レポート) |url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?43762-24656-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=13 October 2008|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=[AFC U-16選手権]日本、準決勝で韓国に敗れる|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?43879-24771-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=16 October 2008|access-date=18 April 2020}} In January 2009, Shibasaki was elected [[Japan national under-17 football team|Japan U-17 national team]] for the first time.{{cite news|title=U-17代表メキシコ遠征メンバー発表|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?48239-29297-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=13 January 2009|access-date=18 April 2020}} He made his Japan U17 debut, starting a match before being substituted in the 55th minute, in a 2–2 draw against [[Brazil national under-17 football team|Brazil U17]] on 25 January 2009.{{cite news|title=U-17代表、宇佐美の2ゴールでブラジルとドロー|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?48813-29891-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=25 January 2009|access-date=18 April 2020}} Later in October 2009, Shibasaki was called up to Japan U-17 squad again for the [[2009 FIFA U-17 World Cup|2009 U-17 World Cup]] in [[Nigeria]] and wore the number 10 shirt for the U-17 side.{{FIFA player|307719}}{{cite news|title=U-17W杯メンバー21人が決定|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?60112-43685-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=5 October 2009|access-date=18 April 2020}} He played in all three matches, as Japan U-17 were eliminated in the group stage.{{cite news|title=[U-17W杯]プラチナ世代初陣。ブラジル戦は後半ロスタイムに...... |url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?60955-44844-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=25 October 2009|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=[U-17W杯]宮吉!小島!日本、強豪から3発も・・・・・・|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?61083-45004-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=28 October 2009|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=[U-17W杯]"プラチナ世代"は3連敗終戦・・・|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?61162-45130-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=31 October 2009|access-date=18 April 2020}} Six months later, Shibasaki was called up to the [[Japan national under-20 football team|Japan U19]] squad but never made an appearance for the U-19 side.{{cite news|title=U-19代表候補大阪合宿メンバーに宮吉、碓井、柴崎ら|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?67790-54568-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=20 April 2010|access-date=18 April 2020}} ===Senior career=== In February 2012, Shibasaki was called up to the [[Japan national football team|Japan]] for the first time ahead of a match against [[Iceland national football team|Iceland]] by Manager [[Alberto Zaccheroni]].{{cite news|title=アイスランド戦に臨む日本代表メンバー発表!!柴崎、金園、久保ら初選出|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?95801-94672-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=17 February 2012|access-date=18 April 2020}} However, he appeared as an unused substitute in a match, as Japan won 3–1 on 24 February 2012.{{cite news|title=ザック監督明言「若手３人は使わない」|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/p-sc-tp2-20120224-908115.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=24 February 2012|access-date=18 April 2020}} Shibasaki's hope of making his debut for the national team continued to be delayed until August 2014 when he was called up.{{cite news|title=ザックジャパン、W杯最終予選へ向け柴崎岳をリストアップ|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?99266-99911-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=11 May 2012|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=柴崎岳が体調不良のため東アジア杯代表メンバー辞退...徳永を追加招集|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?117502-122013-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=19 July 2013|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=柴崎２年ぶり日の丸に「期待に応えたい」|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/f-sc-tp2-20140407-1282006.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=7 April 2014|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=アギーレ初選考はW杯メンバー12人+初選出&復帰組11人|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?146012-146012-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=28 August 2014|access-date=18 April 2020}} On 9 September 2014, Shibasaki debuted and scored a goal for [[Japan national football team|Japan national team]] against [[Venezuela national football team|Venezuela]].{{cite news|title=武藤&柴崎が代表初ゴールも...ベネズエラと2-2ドローでアギーレJ初勝利ならず|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?146835-146835-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=9 September 2014|access-date=18 April 2020}} In a follow–up match against [[Jamaica national football team|Jamaica]], he played a role that led to [[Nyron Nosworthy]] scoring an own goal to give Japan a 1–0 win.{{cite news|title=柴崎シュートで相手オウンゴール誘発|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/f-sc-tp2-20141010-1380154.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=10 October 2014|access-date=18 April 2020}} After the match, Manager [[Javier Aguirre]] praised his performance.{{cite news|title=早くも中心選手の風格、アギーレ監督「柴崎はワールドクラス」|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?149080-149080-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=11 October 2014|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=日本の新たな可能性...柴崎岳が欧州組をコントロール|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?149063-149063-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=10 October 2014|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=ＯＧ呼んだ柴崎「ワールドクラス」と絶賛|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/p-sc-tp2-20141011-1380230.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=11 October 2014|access-date=18 April 2020}} He later made two more appearances by the end of 2014.{{cite news|title=世界との差を体感した柴崎「もっともっと自分を戒める」|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?149369-149369-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=15 October 2014|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=遠藤復帰弾などアギーレJが6発大勝!!乾、豊田も代表初ゴール|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?151576-151576-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=14 November 2014|access-date=18 April 2020}} In December 2014, Shibasaki was elected Japan for [[2015 AFC Asian Cup|2015 Asian Cup]] in Australia.{{cite news|title=アジア杯メンバー23人が決定!!清武がW杯以来の復帰でアギーレJ初招集|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?153584-153584-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=15 December 2014|access-date=15 April 2020}} After appearing in the first two matches of the tournament as an unused substitute, he made his first appearance, coming on as a late substitute, in a 2–0 win against [[Jordan national football team|Jordan]] on 20 January 2015, which saw Japan through to the next round.{{cite news|script-title=ja:本田3戦連発!香川9戦ぶりゴール!日本は3連勝で首位突破|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?155930-155930-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=20 January 2015|access-date=18 April 2020}} Shibasaki's next appearance came against [[United Arab Emirates national football team|United Arab Emirates]] in the quarter–finals of the Asian Cup and scored an equalising goal; and the match was played throughout 120 minutes; ultimately, they were eliminated after losing in penalty–shootout (despite Shibasaki, himself, successfully converted the shootout.{{cite news|title=川島、PKを止められず...「自分自身、力不足」|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?156102-156102-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=23 January 2015|access-date=18 April 2020}} Two months later on 31 March 2015, he scored his second Japan's goal of his career, in a 5–1 win against [[Uzbekistan national football team|Uzbekistan]].{{cite news|title=柴崎42メートル弾、ピッチ中央から冷静無人ゴールへ|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/1455026.html|publisher=Nik|language=ja|date=31 March 2015|access-date=18 April 2020}} Five months later, Shibasaki was called up to Japan for the [[2015 EAFF East Asian Cup|EAFF East Asian Cup]] in [[China]].{{cite web|url=http://www.jfa.jp/news/00006836/|title=EAFF東アジアカップ2015（8/2～9＠中国／武漢） SAMURAI BLUE（日本代表）メンバー・スケジュール|publisher=Japan Football Association|language=ja|date=23 July 2015|access-date=18 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200416200221/http://www.jfa.jp/news/00006836/ |archive-date=16 April 2020|url-status=live}} He was featured three times in the tournament, as they finished last place.{{cite news|title=武藤のデビュー弾で先制も...北朝鮮に逆転負けでハリルJ初黒星|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?168642-168642-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=2 August 2015|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=山口の初ゴールで追いつくも...日本は韓国と1-1ドローで連覇消滅|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?168958-168958-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=5 August 2015|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=武藤弾で追いつくも1勝もできず...日本は東アジア杯初の最下位|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?169302-169302-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=9 August 2015|access-date=18 April 2020}} [[File:Gaku Shibasaki 20180612.jpg|thumb|300px|Shibasaki pictured during a friendly match against [[Paraguay national football team|Paraguay]] on 8 June 2018.]] Two years later away from the national team, Shibasaki was called to Japan's squad and made his first appearance on 5 September 2017 against [[Saudi Arabia national football team|Saudi Arabia]] and helped the side win 1–0.{{cite news|title=柴崎、豪戦先発あるぞ移籍序盤苦闘もトップ下高評価|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/1877236.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=25 August 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=２年ぶり国際Ａマッチの柴崎「ものにできなかった」|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/1883484.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=6 September 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}} Six months later on 28 March 2018, Shibasaki played a role when he set up a goal for [[Tomoaki Makino]], in a 2–1 win against [[Ukraine national football team|Ukraine]].{{cite news|title=日本がＤＦ槙野同点ヘッドもウクライナに力負け|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/201803270000660.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=27 March 2018|access-date=18 April 2020}} Two months later, he was named in Japan's preliminary [[Japan national football team|squad]] for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]] in Russia.{{cite news|title=西野J始動へ...W杯最終候補27人に本田、香川らを選出!!青山がサプライズ|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?245043-245043-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=18 May 2018|access-date=18 April 2020}} Eventually, Shibasaki made it to the final cut of the 23 men squad.{{cite news|title=Gaku Shibasaki estará en Rusia|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/getafe/2018/05/31/5b0fb950e2704e667e8b4658.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=31 May 2018|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=西野監督の新戦術「３－４－３」長谷部がＣＢに|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/201805260000796.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=26 May 2018|access-date=18 April 2020}} Shibasaki made his World Cup debut against [[Colombia national football team|Colombia]] in Matchday 1 of the group stage, where he played 80 minutes in the match, in a 2–1 win.{{cite news|title=World Cup: Japan beat 10-man Colombia in Group H|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44439048|publisher=BBC Sport|date=19 June 2018|access-date=18 April 2020}} After the match, Manager [[Akira Nishino (footballer)|Akira Nishino]] praised Shibasaki's performance.{{cite news|title=国際試合の"奇跡"再び...西野朗監督「柴崎がよくゲームメイクしてくれた」|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?247585-247585-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=19 June 2018|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=指揮官も称賛の司令塔、大舞台で輝いた柴崎が意識したのは...|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?247600-247600-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=20 June 2018|access-date=18 April 2020}} He then made two more starts in the World Cup, as Japan progressed through the knockout stage in the tournament.{{cite news|title=光ったピッチでの分析力、柴崎「そこが狙い目と思って切り替えた」|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?248084-248084-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=25 June 2018|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=自身の成長を実感する柴崎「中盤の支配権を日本に」|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?248612-248612-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=30 June 2018|access-date=18 April 2020}} In a match against [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]] in the World Cup Round of 16, Shibasaki set up the opening goal of the game for [[Genki Haraguchi]], as the opposition team later made a comeback in the second half, resulting Japan losing 3–2 and was out of the tournament.{{cite news|title=伊メディア柴崎岳&乾貴士を絶賛「なんてクオリティだ」川島には酷評「2失点の責任」|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?248865-248865-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=3 July 2018|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=「それは言い訳にならない」全4試合先発の柴崎岳、4年後への課題|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?248844-248844-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=3 July 2018|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=またW杯のピッチに...今大会で組み立ての中心となった柴崎岳「ベスト16の壁を打ち破りたい」|url=https://www.goal.com/jp/%E3%83%8B%E3%83%A5%E3%83%BC%E3%82%B9/%E3%81%BE%E3%81%9Fw%E6%9D%AF%E3%81%AE%E3%83%94%E3%83%83%E3%83%81%E3%81%AB%E4%BB%8A%E5%A4%A7%E4%BC%9A%E3%81%A7%E7%B5%84%E3%81%BF%E7%AB%8B%E3%81%A6%E3%81%AE%E4%B8%AD%E5%BF%83%E3%81%A8%E3%81%AA%E3%81%A3%E3%81%9F%E6%9F%B4%E5%B4%8E%E5%B2%B3%E3%83%99%E3%82%B9%E3%83%8816%E3%81%AE%E5%A3%81%E3%82%92%E6%89%93%E3%81%A1%E7%A0%B4%E3%82%8A%E3%81%9F%E3%81%84/1v2s2csz6d4iw16f4d0zgqen3u|publisher=Goal.com|language=ja|date=3 July 2018|access-date=18 April 2020}} Shortly after, [[Fox Sports]] named Shibasaki in the Asian's Best Eleven of the tournament.{{cite news|title=「サムライブルーで最高のパフォーマンス」、海外メディアがW杯アジアベスト11を選出|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?249070-249070-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=6 July 2018|access-date=18 April 2020}} [[File:Iran - Japan, AFC Asian Cup 2019 17.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Shibasaki and [[Iran national football team|Iran]]'s [[Ashkan Dejagah]] clashed after clearing a ball away during the [[2019 AFC Asian Cup knockout stage#Iran vs Japan|semi-finals]] of the [[AFC Asian Cup]].]] In December 2018, Shibasaki was one of 23 Japanese players selected for the [[2019 AFC Asian Cup]].{{cite web|title=SAMURAI BLUE (Japan National Team) Squad, Schedule - AFC Asian Cup UAE 2019 (1/5-2/1)|url=http://www.jfa.jp/eng/news/00019975/|date=13 December 2018|website=jfa.jp|access-date=5 April 2020}} He started his first match of the tournament, starting the whole game and Japan win 3–2 against [[Turkmenistan national football team|Turkmenistan]].{{cite news|title=日本大迫２発、堂安弾でヒヤヒヤ勝利／アジア杯詳細|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/201901080001324.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=10 January 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}} In a match against Saudi Arabia in the Asian Cup Round of 16, Shibasaki set up a goal for [[Takehiro Tomiyasu]], who scored the only goal of the game, resulting in Japan winning 1–0 to progress to the quarter–finals.{{cite news|title=日本８強！冨安Ｖ弾サウジ下す／アジア杯決勝Ｔ詳細|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/201901210000391.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=21 January 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}} He later played two more matches of the tournament, which saw the national side reaching the final for the first time since 2011.{{cite news|title=日本代表、堂安の"VAR弾"でベスト4進出！ FIFAランク100位のベトナムに辛くも勝利|url=https://www.soccer-king.jp/news/japan/national/20190124/897439.html|publisher=Soccer King|language=ja|date=24 January 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=大迫２発だ！原口１発だ！日本３発決勝 イラン撃破|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/201901290000012.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=29 January 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}} Shibasaki started in the [[2019 AFC Asian Cup Final|AFC Asian Cup final]] against Qatar, as they lost 3–1, finishing as runner–up in the process.{{cite news|script-title=ja:苦しみ抜いた南野が一矢、小３から変わらぬ強い体幹|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/201902020000084.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=2 February 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}} Two months later on 22 March 2019, Shibasaki captained Japan for the first time in his career, as they lost 1–0 against Colombia.{{cite news|title=前半の好機生かせずPKに沈む...森保J、コロンビアに0-1敗戦|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?269432-269432-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=22 March 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}} Two months later, he was called up to the [[Japan national football team|squad]] ahead of the [[2019 Copa América|Copa América]] in Brazil.{{cite news|title=植田が昨年９月以来の招集 再びチャンス来る|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/201905240000109.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=24 May 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}} Ahead of the tournament, Shibasaki was appointed as captain for Japan and once captained the national side for the second time, in a 0–0 draw against [[Trinidad and Tobago national football team|Trinidad and Tobago]] on 6 June 2019.{{cite news|title=相手GKが好守連発...3バック初採用の森保Jは初のスコアレスドロー|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?276299-276299-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=5 June 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=森保ジャパン、コパ・アメリカメンバーの平均年齢は22.3歳。東京五輪強化を色濃く反映|url=https://www.goal.com/jp/%E3%83%8B%E3%83%A5%E3%83%BC%E3%82%B9/%E6%A3%AE%E4%BF%9D%E3%82%B8%E3%83%A3%E3%83%91%E3%83%B3%E3%82%B3%E3%83%91%E3%82%A2%E3%83%A1%E3%83%AA%E3%82%AB%E3%83%A1%E3%83%B3%E3%83%90%E3%83%BC%E3%81%AE%E5%B9%B3%E5%9D%87%E5%B9%B4%E9%BD%A2%E3%81%AF223%E6%AD%B3%E6%9D%B1%E4%BA%AC%E4%BA%94%E8%BC%AA%E5%BC%B7%E5%8C%96%E3%82%92%E8%89%B2%E6%BF%83%E3%81%8F%E5%8F%8D%E6%98%A0/2fa2gp4akwhk1oh0l58fd19xk|publisher=Goal.com|language=ja|date=10 June 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=【日本代表】柴崎岳が語った３バックとコパ・アメリカ、そして東北への思い|url=https://soccermagazine.jp/_ct/17279203|publisher=Soccer Magazine|language=ja|date=10 June 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}} He started and captained Japan in all three matches, playing in the centre–midfield position, as they were eliminated in the group stage.{{cite news|title=試合巧者チリに脱帽...MF柴崎岳「ウィークを徹底的に突いてきた」|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?277317-277317-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=18 June 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=若手への"嫉妬"も清々しく吐露...柴崎が感じた手応えと伸びしろ|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?277572-277572-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=21 June 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=日本、GL突破ならず...中島先制弾もエクアドルとドローで終戦|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?277893-277893-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=25 June 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}} After the national team side were eliminated, Shibasaki said: "It was not a bad experience to bring the team together. I personally wanted to prove my ability at these times, and I think it's one of the ways to be a professional when you can do it. Don't let yourself down mentally and spend those periods consciously. I was able to reconfirm that it would be connected to this kind of situation."{{cite news|title=「悪くない経験だった」 主将・柴崎岳が振り返るリーダーとしてのコパ・アメリカ参戦|url=https://www.football-zone.net/archives/199707|publisher=Football Zone|language=ja|date=26 June 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}} Following the tournament, Shibasaki started the remaining matches of 2019, including one when he was a captain against Venezuela on 19 November 2019.{{cite news|title=中島ゴラッソ&南野ヘッド!! 久保も39年ぶり大記録の森保J、カタールW杯へ白星発進|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?284702-284702-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=10 September 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=リズムもたらしたMF柴崎岳「突破は前提。どう突破していくか」|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?287452-287452-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=11 October 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=日本３発快勝！南野２発＆浅野弾／Ｗ杯２次予選詳細|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/201910150000027.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=15 October 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=変則キルギスに大苦戦も..."新ユニ"森保JがW杯予選無傷の4連勝、5戦連発南野は大記録樹立! |url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?290379-290379-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=14 November 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=65年ぶり大量失点劇に観衆ブーイング...南野ら不在の森保J、ベネズエラに1-4惨敗|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?290828-290828-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=19 November 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}} Almost a year later, Shibasaki was called up to the Japan squad for a match against [[Cameroon national football team|Cameroon]] and [[Ivory Coast national football team|Ivory Coast]].{{cite news|title=日本代表の背番号が決定。中島翔哉不在で南野拓実が10番、鎌田大地が9番に|url=https://www.footballchannel.jp/2020/10/06/post392001/|website=Football Channel|language=ja|date=6 October 2020|access-date=10 August 2021}} In a match against Ivory Coast, he played a role in a match by taking a free kick that led to [[Naomichi Ueda]] scoring a header, in a 1–0 win for the national team.{{cite news|title=植田直通が劇的ゴール！ 日本、コートジボワールを下して2020年初勝利|url=https://www.soccer-king.jp/news/japan/national/20201014/1130374.html|website=Soccer King|language=ja|date=14 October 2020|access-date=10 August 2021}} Shibasaki went on to make three starts for Japan by the end of the year.{{cite news|title=久保も南野も不発、森保日本はカメルーンとドロー|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/202010090001198.html|website=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=9 October 2020|access-date=10 August 2021}}
{{cite news|title=南野拓実がPKで決勝点! 3バック採用の森保J、3戦連続無失点でパナマに勝利|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?316212-316212-fl|website=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=14 November 2020|access-date=10 August 2021}}
{{cite news|title=森保J、2020年最終戦はメキシコに2失点完封負け…前半チャンス連発も決め切れず|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?316597-316597-fl|website=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=17 November 2020|access-date=10 August 2021}} ==Personal life== Shibasaki has two older brothers, whom one of them got him into football. Growing up, Shibasaki said in an interview that his ambition is to become a footballer, having no interests in anything but football.{{cite news|title=見据える先は『100年後』。柴崎岳が語った原点と、日本が目指すべき未来:独占インタビュー|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?277415-277415-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=19 June 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}} He also idolised [[Alessandro Del Piero]], [[Francesco Totti]] and [[Hidetoshi Nakata]].{{cite news|title=柴崎岳が明かす憧れの選手は?デポルティボ地元紙で語る「日本人で言うと...」|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?286428-286428-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=29 September 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=デポルティボ柴崎岳に現地紙インタビュー。「ア・コルーニャは青森に似ている」|url=https://www.footballchannel.jp/2019/09/28/post340277/|publisher=Football Channel|language=ja|date=28 September 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}}{{cite news|title=Gaku: "El Leganés me ha dado la oportunidad de volver a empezar"|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/leganes/2020/11/06/5fa433be46163fee128b460c.html|website=Marca|language=es|date=6 November 2020|access-date=10 August 2021}} When asked in an interview on how does his improve his concentration before the game, Shibasaki said: "First of all, I start by creating my own world. I create my own senses, spaces, and rhythms. At the same time, I become more focused by being aware of my surroundings. I'm doing something over there, I picked up something and I recognize the movement in the space."{{cite news|title=【インタビュー】類い稀なメンタリティで試合を操る柴崎岳、その集中力の高め方とは|url=https://www.soccer-king.jp/news/japan/jl/20160907/489347.html|publisher=Soccer King|language=ja|date=7 September 2016|access-date=18 April 2020}} He began a relationship with the actress and singer [[Erina Mano]] and their relationship wasn't made public until on 25 November 2017.{{cite news|title=真野恵里菜、ブログ更新も柴崎岳との交際には触れず|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/entertainment/news/201711250000717.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=25 November 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=真野恵里菜、柴崎岳と真剣交際 報道陣の質問に無言|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/entertainment/news/201711260000064.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=26 November 2017|access-date=18 April 2020}} They were married on 16 July 2018.{{cite news|title=真野恵里菜事務所、柴崎との結婚「報告受けてない」|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/world/news/201804190000045.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=19 April 2018|access-date=18 April 2020}}
{{cite news|title=柴崎岳が真野恵里菜との結婚「あらためてご報告」|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/201807230000499.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=23 July 2018|access-date=18 April 2020}} In September 2015, it was announced that Shibasaki was appointed as a support leader of the 94th National High School Soccer Championship.{{cite news|title=第94回全国高校サッカー選手権の応援リーダーに鹿島MF柴崎が就任|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?176063-176063-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=10 November 2015|access-date=18 April 2020}} In addition to speaking Japanese, he has been learning Galician and acknowledged at Deportivo La Coruña's press conference that his Spanish is not good.{{cite web|url=http://www.rcdeportivo.es/noticia/gaku-shibasaki-pienso-que-puedo-mejorar-y-quiero-mejorar-mas|title=Gaku Shibasaki: "Pienso que puedo mejorar y quiero mejorar más"|publisher=Deportivo de La Coruña|language=es|date=20 February 2020|access-date=10 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210809190455/https://www.rcdeportivo.es/noticia/gaku-shibasaki-pienso-que-puedo-mejorar-y-quiero-mejorar-mas|archive-date=9 August 2021|url-status=live}}{{cite news|title=Gaku Shibasaki golea al choque cultural|url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2017/06/20/actualidad/1497985522_533544.html|website=El Pais|language=es|date=20 June 2017|access-date=10 August 2021}} Shibasaki also spoke out about living in Spain.{{cite news|title=柴崎岳がアンブロのイベントに登場! スペイン生活、日本代表、スパイク選びを語る|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?275632-275632-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=30 May 2019|access-date=18 April 2020}} In the wake of [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Shibasaki posted a message on his social media account, urging people to stay at home.{{cite news|title=柴崎岳、感染拡大で心構え「他人ごとだと思わず」|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/world/news/202003280000661.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=28 March 2020|access-date=18 April 2020}} ==Career statistics== ===Club=== {{updated|15 January 2025}}Nippon Sports Kikaku Publishing inc./日本スポーツ企画出版社, [https://www.amazon.co.jp/2017-J1-J3%E9%81%B8%E6%89%8B%E5%90%8D%E9%91%91-NSK-MOOK/dp/4905411424/ref=pd_sim_14_1/356-9491148-0114816?_encoding=UTF8&psc=1&refRID=BA8BN4Y0F97GNWKQM78H "2017 J1&J2&J3選手名鑑 (NSK MOOK)"], 8 February 2017, Japan, {{ISBN|978-4905411420}} (p. 284 out of 289)[https://int.soccerway.com/players/gaku-shibasaki/102666/ Japan – Gaku Shibasaki – Profile with news, career statistics and history] Soccerway.{{cite web |title=2024 Gaku Shibasaki Players |url=https://soccer-db.net/player/index/5989/2024?la=e |website=Soccer D.B. {{Nihongo|'''Yoshinori Muto'''|武藤 嘉紀|Mutō Yoshinori|born 15 July 1992}} is a Japanese professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] or a [[Forward (association football)#Winger|winger]] for [[Vissel Kobe]].

Muto started his career with [[J1 League]] club [[FC Tokyo]] in 2013 who he played with for three seasons. In May 2015, he signed for German club [[1. FSV Mainz 05|Mainz 05]] where he amassed 72 appearances and scored 23 goals before moving to [[Premier League]] club Newcastle United in August 2018.

==Club career==
===FC Tokyo===
As a child, Muto joined FC Tokyo's youth system, where he kept developing until 2010. He then enrolled in the Faculty of Economics of [[Keio University]] but kept playing football, for Keio's team. Despite an injury which sidelined him, in his first season with Keio he won the "Rookie of the Year" title.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://keispo.org/wordpress/?p=5171 |title=【ソッカー男子】開幕前取材、第3弾 武藤嘉紀編 |publisher=Keio Sports Press |date=3 May 2011 |language=ja}}</ref>

In 2012 and 2013, FC Tokyo included him in their roster as a "Special Designated Player",<ref>{{cite news |title=武藤嘉紀選手（慶應義塾大学）「ＪＦＡ・Ｊリーグ特別指定選手」承認のお知らせ |url=http://www.fctokyo.co.jp/?p=148757 |language=ja |publisher=FC Tokyo |date=26 June 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140302075513/http://www.fctokyo.co.jp/?p=148757 |archive-date=2 March 2014}}</ref> an option that allows J-League clubs to field university players without a professional contract. However, he got on the pitch just once, at the end of a match in July 2013.

In 2014, he signed his first professional contract with FC Tokyo<ref>{{cite web |title=武藤嘉紀選手(慶應義塾大学)来季新加入内定のお知らせ |url=http://www.fctokyo.co.jp/?p=180838 |language=ja |date=12 December 2013 |publisher=FC Tokyo |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131222115444/http://www.fctokyo.co.jp/?p=180838 |archive-date=22 December 2013}}</ref>  and was given the shirt number 14. Coach Massimo Ficcadenti decided to use him from the first league round and, at the end of the season, Muto reached 33 appearances and scored 13 goals, matching the top debut record in the Japanese first division.<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea scout out Muto |url=http://www.marca.com/en/2015/04/09/en/football/international_football/1428615427.html |newspaper=Marca |date=9 April 2015}}</ref> At the end of the season, he was part of the J-League's Best XI.<ref>{{cite news |first=Dan |last=Orlowitz |title=Yasuhito Endo awarded 2014 J-League MVP; FC Tokyo and Gamba Osaka spearhead Best XI |url=http://footballchannel.asia/2014/12/09/post1086/ |publisher=Football Channel Asia}}</ref>

Muto graduated from Keio University in March 2015, and the following month was subject to a bid by [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Yoshinori Muto: Chelsea make bid for Japanese striker |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32230300 |access-date=9 April 2015 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=9 April 2015}}</ref> In April, he was elected as March's MVP (Player of the Month) in the J-League.<ref>{{cite news |title=Muto named Coca-Cola MVP winners in March |url=http://www.jleague.jp/en/news/20150411-03.html |access-date=11 April 2015 |work=JLeague Sport |date=11 April 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150419024121/http://www.jleague.jp/en/news/20150411-03.html |archive-date=19 April 2015}}</ref>

===Mainz 05===
On 30 May 2015, Muto joined [[Bundesliga]] club [[1. FSV Mainz 05|Mainz 05]] on a four-year contract until 2019.<ref>{{cite news |title=Mainz 05 sign Yoshinori Muto |url=http://www.mainz05.de/mainz05/en/aktuell/news/news-detail/article/mainz-05-verpflichtet-yoshinori-muto.html |access-date=30 May 2015 |publisher=Mainz 05 |date=30 May 2015 |archive-date=31 May 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150531054433/http://www.mainz05.de/mainz05/en/aktuell/news/news-detail/article/mainz-05-verpflichtet-yoshinori-muto.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> On 31 October 2015, he scored a [[hat-trick]] for the first time in his career and also became the second Japanese player after [[Naohiro Takahara]] to score a hat-trick in the Bundesliga, in his team's 3–3 draw against [[FC Augsburg]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2015/11/01/soccer/muto-hits-hat-trick-mainz-draw/#.VjhdKNLhBRB |title=Muto hits hat-trick in Mainz draw |newspaper=The Japan Times |date=1 November 2015 |access-date=3 November 2015 |archive-date=9 December 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151209114552/https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2015/11/01/soccer/muto-hits-hat-trick-mainz-draw/#.VjhdKNLhBRB |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Newcastle United===
[[Premier League]] club [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] announced on 27 July 2018 that they had reached a deal to sign Muto, pending him being granted a [[Work permit (United Kingdom)|UK work permit]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/newcastle-united-confirm-sealed-transfer-14962597.amp |title=Newcastle United confirm they have all but sealed the transfer of Yoshinori Muto |newspaper=Evening Chronicle |first=Lee |last=Ryder |date=27 July 2018 |access-date=27 July 2018}}</ref> He was granted the work permit on 2 August, officially becoming a Newcastle player on a four-year contract as part of a £9.5 million fee.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11678/11457570/yoshinori-muto-completes-newcastle-move-after-work-permit-granted |title=Yoshinori Muto signs for Newcastle after work permit granted |publisher=Sky Sports |first=James |last=Dale |date=2 August 2018 |access-date=3 August 2018}}</ref> Muto's first goal for Newcastle came in a 3–2 away loss to [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] at [[Old Trafford]].<ref>{{cite news|url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2018/oct/06/manchester-united-v-newcastle-united-premier-league-live|title= Manchester United 3-2 Newcastle United: Premier League – as it happened|newspaper= The Guardian|date= 6 October 2018|last1= Smyth|first1= Rob}}</ref>

====Eibar (loan)====
On 16 September 2020, Muto was loaned out to Spanish club [[SD Eibar|Eibar]] for the 2020–21 season.<ref name="Eibar loan">{{cite web |url=https://www.nufc.co.uk/news/latest-news/muto-loaned-to-eibar/ |title=Muto loaned out to Eibar. |publisher=nufc.co.uk |date=16 September 2020 |access-date=16 September 2020}}</ref>

===Vissel Kobe===
On 7 August 2021, [[Vissel Kobe]] announced that they signed Muto.<ref name="Kobe announcement">{{cite web |url=https://www.vissel-kobe.co.jp/news/article/19003.html/ |title=FW武藤嘉紀選手 完全移籍加入のお知らせ |publisher=Vissel Kobe |date=7 August 2021 |access-date=7 August 2021 |language=ja}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Yoshinori Muto.jpg|thumb|right|Muto playing for Japan during the 2018 FIFA World Cup]]

Muto made his debut for [[Japan national football team|Japan]] on 5 September 2014 in a 2–0 friendly defeat to [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]] at the [[Sapporo Dome]], replacing [[Yusuke Minagawa]] after 58 minutes.<ref>{{cite web |title=Japan 0–2 Uruguay: Cavani on target for Celeste |url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/japan-vs-uruguay/1837187/report |access-date=9 April 2015 |publisher=Goal.com |date=5 September 2014}}</ref> Four days later at [[Yokohama]]'s [[Nissan Stadium (Yokohama)|Nissan Stadium]] he scored his first international goal, coming on as a half-time substitute against [[Venezuela national football team|Venezuela]] and scoring the first goal of a 2–2 draw six minutes later.<ref>{{cite web |last=West |first=Harry |title=Japan 2–2 Venezuela: Kawashima mistake costs Aguirre maiden win |url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/match/japan-vs-venezuela/1837189/report |access-date=10 April 2015 |publisher=Goal.com |date=9 September 2014}}</ref>

As a substitute, Muto played all of Japan's matches at the [[2015 AFC Asian Cup]] in Australia, ending with defeat to the [[United Arab Emirates national football team|United Arab Emirates]] in the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite news |title=Asian Cup 2015: UAE complete shock win over Japan to reach semi-final after penalty shootout dramatics |url=http://www.abc.net.au/news/2015-01-23/uae-japan-asian-cup/6043964 |access-date=9 April 2015 |publisher=Australian Broadcasting Corporation |date=23 January 2015}}</ref>

On 31 May 2018, he was named in Japan's final 23-man squad for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]] in Russia.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-worldcup-jpn-squad/football-nishino-opts-for-experienced-japan-squad-for-world-cup-idUKKCN1IW101 |title=Football – Nishino opts for experienced Japan squad for World Cup |work=Reuters |language=en |date=31 May 2018 |access-date=3 August 2018}}</ref>

On 20 December 2018 he has been called up for the 2019 Asian Cup replacing the injured [[Takuma Asano]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Muto gets Asian Cup call|url=https://www.nufc.co.uk/news/latest-news/muto-gets-asian-cup-call/|access-date=16 September 2020|website=Newcastle United Football Club|date=18 December 2018 |language=en}}</ref>

'''Divock Okoth Origi''' (born 18 April 1995) is a Belgian former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Striker (association football)|striker]]. 

Origi began his career at [[Lille OSC|Lille]], and scored on his professional debut for them in 2013. A year and a half later, he was signed for £10 million by Premier League club [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], who loaned him back to Lille for the [[2014–15 Ligue 1]] season. After struggling at Liverpool due to injuries, and spending a year on loan at [[VfL Wolfsburg]], Origi made various crucial contributions to the club during the [[2018–19 Liverpool F.C. season|2018–19 season]]. Most notably, he scored two goals, including the winning goal, in the [[2018–19 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Liverpool v Barcelona|2019 Champions League semi-final]] comeback against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]]. He was also a part of the squad that won the [[2019–20 Premier League]] the following season, Liverpool's first league title for 30 years. In 2022, after winning a domestic double with Liverpool the [[2021–22 Liverpool F.C. season|previous season]], Origi signed for [[AC Milan]]. He spent the 2023–24 season on loan at [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]], and terminated his Milan contract in 2025.

Origi made his international debut for [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]] in 2014 and was part of their team which reached the quarter-finals of the [[2014 FIFA World Cup]], during which he became the youngest goalscorer in Belgian World Cup history as a 19 year old.

==Early and personal life==
Origi was born in [[Ostend]] and grew up in [[Houthalen-Helchteren|Houthalen-Oost]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.nieuwsblad.be/article/detail.aspx?articleid=BLBOZ_01167498 |title=Mike Origi: 'Natuurlijk zijn we fier op Divock' |date=4 July 2014 |newspaper=Het Nieuwsblad |access-date=22 July 2014 |language=nl |archive-date=27 July 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140727074127/http://www.nieuwsblad.be/article/detail.aspx?articleid=BLBOZ_01167498 |url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2882767-divock-origi-talks-2019-ucl-final-jurgen-klopps-hugs-lebron-more-in-br-ama |title=Divock Origi Talks 2019 UCL Final, Jurgen Klopp's Hugs, LeBron, More in B/R AMA |last=Wells |first=Adam |date=24 March 2020 |access-date=11 April 2020 |website=Bleacher Report |quote=It came from the name Vlade Divac. My parents watched him play and wanted to personalize the name a little bit.}}</ref> He was born into a family of footballers: his father, [[Mike Origi]], played for [[KV Oostende]] (at the time Divock was born) and Genk, among other Belgian clubs, as well as the Kenya national team. His uncle, Austin Oduor Origi, played for [[Gor Mahia F.C.|Gor Mahia]] in the [[Kenyan Premier League]] while his other uncles, Gerald and Anthony, played for [[Tusker F.C.|Tusker]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kenyafootball.com/|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20071006140034/http://kenyafootball.com/index.php?doc=story&id=1033&categ=1| title=Kenya Football – Kenya Football|archivedate=6 October 2007}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{cite web |url=http://www.liverpoolfc.com/team/first-team/player/divock-origi |title=Divock Origi |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160325010947/http://www.liverpoolfc.com/team/first-team/player/divock-origi |archive-date=25 March 2016}}</ref> His cousin, [[Arnold Origi]], is also a professional player who has been capped for the Kenyan national team as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]]. The Origi family is of [[Kenyans|Kenyan]] [[Luo people|Luo]] ethnicity.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.standardmedia.co.ke/worldcup/article/2000126369/divock-origi-proud-of-kenyan-heritage-speaks-kiswahili-and-four-luo-words |title=In footsteps of his father: Belgium star Divock Origi proud of Kenyan heritage, speaks Kiswahili and four Luo words |date=29 June 2014 |first=Robin |last=Toskin |newspaper=The Standard |location=Nairobi |access-date=5 July 2014}}</ref> Origi speaks four languages fluently: [[Swahili language|Swahili]], [[English language|English]], [[Dutch (language)|Dutch]] and [[French language|French]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/may/12/divock-origi-liverpool-psychology |title=Liverpool's Divock Origi: 'Maybe if I wasn't a footballer I'd be a psychologist' |date=12 May 2017 |first=Andy |last=Hunter |newspaper=The Guardian |access-date=5 December 2019}}</ref>

Origi is a [[Christianity|Christian]]. He has said, "My religion, being a Christian, has values of working hard, staying focused on the right things that helps you in life. Of course you're going to slip. I made mistakes. But those mistakes helped me and still help me these days."<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hughes |first1=Simon |title=Alisson, Roberto Firmino and religion's role at Liverpool and in the Premier League |website=[[The Athletic]] |date=16 January 2020 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1477023/2020/01/16/alisson-firmino-baptism-evangelicalism-liverpool-premier-league/ |access-date=20 May 2022}}</ref>

In 2021, the Divock Origi Scholarship was introduced when Origi partnered with the [[University of Liverpool]] to provide undergraduate courses to students with financial troubles.<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 June 2021 |title=Divock Origi partners with University of Liverpool to offer new scholarship |url=https://legacy.liverpoolfc.com/news/announcements/436231-divock-origi-partners-with-university-of-liverpool-to-offer-new-scholarship |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240511194426/https://legacy.liverpoolfc.com/news/announcements/436231-divock-origi-partners-with-university-of-liverpool-to-offer-new-scholarship |archive-date=11 May 2024 |access-date=11 May 2024 |website=Liverpool FC}}</ref> The [[scholarship]] covers tuition fees (£9,250 per year) as well as an annual payment of £3,000 towards living costs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Learn about the Divock Origi Scholarship {{!}} IDP Education |url=https://www.idp.com/scholarship/university-of-liverpool/divock-origi-scholarship/154240/ |access-date=11 May 2024 |website=www.idp.com}}</ref> Originally, in the 2021–22 academic year, the scholarship was offered to two students with the prospect to increase the enrolment in the future.<ref>{{Cite news |date=6 April 2022 |title=Liverpool footballer Divock Origi funds degree scholarships |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-merseyside-61010929 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220413104400/https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-merseyside-61010929 |archive-date=13 April 2022 |access-date=11 May 2024 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Early career===
Origi began his career playing football at [[K.R.C. Genk|Genk]]'s youth academy where he spent nine years before signing for [[Lille OSC|Lille]] in May 2010, aged 15, after turning down an approach by [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/origi-turning-down-manchester-united-10994105 |title=Origi: Why turning down United and ending up at Liverpool was best thing for me |date=5 March 2016 |last=Doyle |first=Ian |newspaper=Liverpool Echo |access-date=11 March 2016}}</ref>

===Lille===
[[File:Divock Origi (LOSC Lille).JPG|thumb|upright|left|Origi playing for [[Lille OSC|Lille]] in 2014]]

On 24 January 2013, Origi was an unused substitute in Lille's 3–1 away win over [[Stade Plabennecois|Plabennec]] in a [[2012–13 Coupe de France|2012–13]] [[Coupe de France]] match.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ligue1.com/ligue1/article/lacklustre-lille-held-at-home.htm |title=Lacklustre Lille held at home |date=2 February 2013 |publisher=Ligue de Football Professionnel |access-date=5 February 2013 |archive-date=17 May 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140517121120/http://www.ligue1.com/ligue1/article/lacklustre-lille-held-at-home.htm |url-status=live}}</ref> Nine days later, he scored on his competitive debut for the senior Lille side, coming on as a substitute in the 69th minute for [[Ronny Rodelin]] and scoring to bring his side level from 1–0 down against [[Troyes AC|Troyes]].<ref>{{cite web |language=fr |date=3 February 2013 |url=http://www.losc.fr/actualite-foot-lille/ligue-1/b-pedretti-origi-le-rayon-de-soleil-de-la-soiree |title=B. Pedretti : "Origi, le rayon de soleil de la soirée" |publisher=Lille OSC |access-date=5 February 2013 |archive-date=17 May 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140517154355/http://www.losc.fr/actualite-foot-lille/ligue-1/b-pedretti-origi-le-rayon-de-soleil-de-la-soiree}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |access-date=5 February 2013 |date=4 February 2013 |url=http://www.futaa.com/football/article/divock-origi-scores-on-ligue-1-debut-for-lille |title=Divock Origi scores on Ligue 1 debut for Lille |author=Patrick Korir |website=Futaa.com |archive-date=17 May 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140517121707/http://www.futaa.com/football/article/divock-origi-scores-on-ligue-1-debut-for-lille}}</ref>

===Liverpool===
On 29 July 2014, [[Premier League]] club [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] announced that they had completed a £10 million transfer for Origi, who signed a five-year contract, but was immediately [[Loan (association football)|loaned]] back to Lille for the [[2014–15 Ligue 1|2014–15 season]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/167369-reds-complete-origi-deal |title=Reds complete Origi deal |date=29 July 2014 |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |access-date=29 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/28551650 |title=Liverpool sign Belgium striker Divock Origi from Lille for £10m |date=29 July 2014 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=29 July 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140729230536/http://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/28551650 |archive-date=29 July 2014 |url-status=live}}</ref>

====Loan to Lille====
In his first match back in Lille, Origi scored his first goal of the new [[Ligue 1]] season through a penalty against [[Stade Malherbe Caen|Caen]] to secure a 1–0 win for his side. This was after he had been brought down in the box by defender [[Dennis Appiah]], who was sent off by the referee towards the 70th minute.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/live/match/321521/report |title=Ligue report: Lille let off the hook |date=15 August 2014 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=17 August 2014}}</ref>

On 11 December 2014, as Lille lost 0–3 at home to [[VfL Wolfsburg]] to be eliminated from the [[2014–15 UEFA Europa League group stage|UEFA Europa League group stage]], Origi had a penalty saved by [[Diego Benaglio]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Holyman |first1=Ian |title=LOSC left high and dry by Wolfsburg |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/025a-0ea6f085d031-338a700fbfed-1000--losc-left-high-and-dry-by-wolfsburg/ |access-date=11 December 2014 |publisher=UEFA |date=11 December 2014}}</ref> On 15 March 2015, Origi scored a [[Hat-trick (association football)|hat-trick]] for Lille in a 3–0 league win against [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espnfc.com/french-ligue-1/match/393429/lille-stade-rennes/report |title=Origi back with a bang in Lille win |website=ESPN FC |date=15 March 2015 |access-date=15 March 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ligue1.com/ligue1/feuille_match/79062 |title=Lille 3–0 Rennais Match Report |publisher=Ligue de Football Professionnel}}</ref>

====Return to Liverpool====
[[File:Divock Origi (25273591916).jpg|thumb|upright|Origi with [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] in 2016]]

On 11 July 2015, Origi was named in Liverpool's 30-man squad for their pre-season tour of Thailand, Australia and Malaysia. In his non-competitive debut for Liverpool, a pre-season friendly against [[Thai Premier League All-Star Football|Thai All-Stars]] on 14 July, Origi scored his first goal for the club in a 4–0 win.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/liverpool-fc-4-0-thai-stars-9656001 |title=Liverpool FC 4–0 Thai All Stars: Origi nets debut goal as monsoon fails to dampen Reds' pre-season stroll |date=14 July 2015 |newspaper=Liverpool Echo |access-date=15 July 2015}}</ref>

His first competitive game for the team was on 12 September, replacing [[Danny Ings]] for the final sixteen minutes of a 3–1 loss at [[Liverpool F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry|rivals]] Manchester United.<ref>{{cite news |last1=McNulty |first1=Phil |title=Man Utd 3–1 Liverpool |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34160795 |access-date=2 December 2015 |website=BBC Sport |date=12 September 2015}}</ref> Origi scored his first competitive Liverpool goals on 2 December, a hat-trick in a 6–1 away win over [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] in the quarter-finals of the [[Football League Cup|League Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Southampton 1–6 Liverpool |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34918281 |access-date=2 December 2015 |website=BBC Sport |date=2 December 2015}}</ref> Eleven days later, he scored his first Premier League goal, replacing the injured [[Dejan Lovren]] in the 79th minute and scoring an added-time equaliser from outside the penalty area for a 2–2 draw against [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] at [[Anfield]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Dawkes |first1=Phil |title=Liverpool 2–2 West Brom |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35018987 |access-date=13 December 2015 |website=BBC Sport |date=13 December 2015}}</ref> On 14 February, he scored his second league goal against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] in a 6–0 victory, only 27 seconds after replacing [[Daniel Sturridge]] in the second half; this was the fastest goal scored by a substitute that season.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35515112 |title=Aston Villa 0–6 Liverpool |date=14 February 2016 |website=BBC Sport |last1=Sanghera |first1=Mandeep |access-date=14 February 2016}}</ref>

On 7 April 2016, Liverpool manager [[Jürgen Klopp]] surprisingly started Origi ahead of Sturridge (the team's first-choice striker) during Liverpool's [[2015–16 UEFA Europa League knockout phase|Europa League quarter-final]] match against [[Borussia Dortmund]], Klopp's former side. Origi scored a vital away goal in a 1–1 draw. Three days later, he scored two goals in a 4–1 win over [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] after coming on as a substitute to replace [[Sheyi Ojo]] at half-time.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35953097 |title=Liverpool 4-1 Stoke City |work=BBC Sport |first=Mike |last=Henson |date=10 April 2016 |accessdate=6 September 2021}}</ref>

On 20 April 2016, Origi sustained a severe ankle ligament injury in a home game against [[Everton F.C.|Everton]]. This was caused by a foul tackle by Everton defender [[Ramiro Funes Mori]] who received a red card and subsequent three match ban.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/apr/21/ramiro-funes-mori-everton-apology-liverpool |title=Everton's Ramiro Funes Mori issues apology for red card against Liverpool | Everton |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |location=London |date=21 April 2016 |accessdate=9 March 2022}}</ref>

Origi was used predominantly as a substitute and cup player at the start of the [[2016–17 Liverpool F.C. season|2016–17 season]]. He scored his first goal of the season on 23 August 2016 in a 5–0 [[2016–17 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] win over [[Burton Albion F.C.|Burton Albion]].<ref>{{cite web|last=|first=|date=23 August 2016|title=Burton Albion 0–5 Liverpool|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37091102|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160822233913/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37091102 |archive-date=22 August 2016 |access-date=7 February 2021|website=BBC Sport}}</ref> He scored his first [[2016–17 Premier League]] goal on 26 November, coming off the bench for the injured [[Philippe Coutinho]] to score the opener in a 2–0 win over [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2016/11/26/premier-league-clockwatch-liverpool-vs-sunderland-rest-3pm-kick/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2016/11/26/premier-league-clockwatch-liverpool-vs-sunderland-rest-3pm-kick/ |archive-date=12 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |title=Liverpool 2 Sunderland 0: Divock Origi provides relief after Philippe Coutinho is stretchered off |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |last=Findon |first=Ben |date=26 November 2016 |access-date=30 November 2016}}{{cbignore}}</ref> On 1 April 2017, he scored Liverpool's third in a 3–1 win against rivals Everton.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39390276 |title=Liverpool 3–1 Everton |website=BBC Sport |date=1 April 2017 |access-date=6 December 2019}}</ref> On 14 May, he scored Liverpool's fourth in a 4–0 win against [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]], edging the team closer to [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League|Champions League qualification]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39833967 |title=West Ham United 0–4 Liverpool |website=BBC Sport |date=14 May 2017 |access-date=6 December 2019}}</ref>

====Loan to VfL Wolfsburg====
On 31 August 2017, [[Bundesliga]] club VfL Wolfsburg signed Origi on a season-long loan.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.vfl-wolfsburg.de/en/info/news/detailspage/artikel/welkom-divock-origi-47146.html |title=Welkom, Divock Origi! |publisher=VfL Wolfsburg |date=31 August 2017 |access-date=31 August 2017 |archive-date=13 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180613090827/https://www.vfl-wolfsburg.de/en/info/news/detailspage/artikel/welkom-divock-origi-47146.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/liverpools-divock-origi-joins-wolfsburg-in-6m-season-long/13zpa1prlvhfw1k7zy6spcfxkw |title=Liverpool's Divock Origi joins Wolfsburg in £6m season-long loan deal |website=Goal.com |access-date=13 June 2018}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club against [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]], on 19 September.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dfb.de/bundesliga/spieltagtabelle/?spieledb_path=%2Fmatches%2F2279266 |title=Spieltag/Tabelle |date=18 March 2014 |publisher=German Football Association |language=de |access-date=6 December 2019}}</ref> He scored six goals in total for the club during his loan spell.<ref name="Soccerway" />

====Return to Liverpool====
[[File:Liverpool vs. Chelsea, UEFA Super Cup 2019-08-14 37 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Origi playing for [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] in the [[2019 UEFA Super Cup]]]]

On 2 December 2018, Origi scored his first goal of the season in a [[Merseyside derby]] match against city rivals Everton, which Liverpool won 1–0. Origi came on as a substitute for [[Roberto Firmino]] in the 84th minute and scored with a header in the 96th minute, capitalising on an error from Everton goalkeeper [[Jordan Pickford]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/328060-match-report-liverpool-everton |title=Origi saves the day{{!}} |date=2 December 2018 |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |access-date=2 December 2018}}</ref> On 4 May 2019, he scored a last-minute goal against Newcastle in a 3–2 victory, keeping Liverpool's hunt for their first title since the introduction of the Premier League alive.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/48075158 |title=Newcastle 2–3 Liverpool: Divock Origi's late winner ensures title race goes to last day |date=4 May 2019 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

On 7 May 2019, Origi scored for the first time in the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]], netting a brace in the semi-final second leg against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], vitally scoring the final goal to complete Liverpool's comeback from a three-goal first leg defeat.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/48179167 |title=Liverpool 4–0 Barcelona (4–3 agg): Jurgen Klopp's side complete extraordinary comeback |date=7 May 2019 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 1 June 2019, he scored Liverpool's second goal in a 2–0 win over [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham]] in the [[2019 UEFA Champions League final]], as he won his first honour with the club.<ref name="Guardian-Summary">{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/jun/01/tottenham-liverpool-champions-league-final-match-report |title=Liverpool win Champions League after Salah and Origi sink Tottenham |newspaper=The Guardian |last=Taylor |first=Daniel |date=1 June 2019 |access-date=1 June 2019}}</ref> In doing so, he became only the second Belgian player to score in a Champions League final after [[Yannick Carrasco]] in 2016.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48368443 |title=Tottenham Hotspur 0–2 Liverpool |first=Phil |last=McNulty |website=BBC Sport |date=1 June 2019 |access-date=15 June 2019}}</ref>

On 10 July 2019, Origi signed a new long-term contract with Liverpool.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48943512 |title=Divock Origi: Liverpool striker signs long-term contract |date=10 July 2019 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 30 October, Origi scored twice, including a last minute [[bicycle kick]] in an [[2019–20 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] match against [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] which Liverpool eventually won on penalties following a 5–5 regular time finish.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/50148250 |title=Liverpool 5–5 (5–4) Arsenal: Shootout decides 10-goal thriller |website=BBC Sport |date=30 October 2019 |access-date=6 December 2019}}</ref> On 4 December, he scored two goals as Liverpool beat rival Everton 5–2 in the Merseyside derby to extend their unbeaten run in league football to 32 matches, which was a new club record.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2019/12/04/liverpool-vs-everton-premier-league-live-score-latest-updates/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2019/12/04/liverpool-vs-everton-premier-league-live-score-latest-updates/ |archive-date=12 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |title=Liverpool put five past Everton for new unbeaten club record as Marco Silva teeters on the brink after derby defeat |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |date=4 December 2019 |access-date=6 December 2019 |last=Bascombe |first=Chris}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

Origi featured seventeen times and scored only one goal for Liverpool over the course of the [[2020–21 Liverpool F.C. season|2020–21 season]]. His second goal in the [[2021–22 Liverpool F.C. season|2021–22 season]] was a [[Scorpion kick (association football)|scorpion kick]] inside the six-yard box in a 2–0 [[EFL Cup]] win over [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]] on 27 October.<ref>{{cite news |title=Origi's incredible scorpion kick goal! |url=https://www.skysports.com/watch/video/sports/football/12446387/origis-amazing-scorpion-kick-goal |access-date=28 October 2021 |agency=Sky Sports}}</ref> He scored Liverpool's winning goal in a 2–1 win away to [[AC Milan]] on 7 December 2021, as Liverpool became the first English club to [[2021–22 UEFA Champions League group stage#Group B|win all six Champions League group games]] in the competition's history.<ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool beat Milan for perfect group stage record |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/59553411 |access-date=7 December 2021 |agency=BBC}}</ref>

In June 2022, it was announced by Liverpool that Origi would leave the club at the end of the month when his contract expired.<ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool: Divock Origi and Loris Karius among seven to leave Reds |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61742711 |access-date=9 June 2022 |work=BBC Sport |date=9 June 2022}}</ref>

===AC Milan===
[[File:Divock Origi.jpg|thumb|upright|Origi playing for [[AC Milan]] in 2022]]

On 5 July 2022, Origi signed for [[Serie A]] club [[AC Milan]] on a four-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Divock Origi, joins AC Milan: official statement |url=http://www.acmilan.com/en/news/articles/media/2022-07-05/official-statement-divock-origi |access-date=5 July 2022 |website=AC Milan |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Origi joins AC Milan after leaving Liverpool |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/62054038 |access-date=5 July 2022}}</ref>

====Loan to Nottingham Forest====
On 1 September 2023, Origi joined Premier League club [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] on a season-long loan with an option to buy.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nottinghamforest.co.uk/news/2023/september/01/forest-sign-divock-origi-on-loan-from-ac-milan/ |title=Forest sign Divock Origi on loan from AC Milan |publisher=Nottingham Forest |date=1 September 2023 }}</ref> On 7 February 2024, he scored his first and only goal for Forest in a 1–1 draw against [[Bristol City F.C.|Bristol City]] in the [[2023–24 FA Cup]], which his team would go on to win on [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68235324 |title=Nottingham Forest v Bristol City |publisher=BBC Sport |date=7 February 2024 }}</ref>

====Return to AC Milan====
By July 2024, Origi returned to AC Milan but according to [[Zlatan Ibrahimović]], the striker would play only for their newly created reserve team [[Milan Futuro]].<ref>{{cite news |work=Liverpool Echo |date=8 July 2024 |last=Squires |first=Theo |access-date=8 December 2024 |title=Liverpool legend banished to youth team as exile confirmed |url=https://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/liverpool-legend-banished-youth-team-29498997 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.beinsports.com/en-us/soccer/serie-a/articles-video/the-bizarre-and-lucrative-situation-for-divock-origi-hero-of-liverpool-s-epic-barcelona-comeback-2024-11-14|title=The Bizarre and Lucrative Situation for Divock Origi, Hero of Liverpool's Epic Barcelona Comeback|website=beIN SPORTS}}</ref>

He terminated his contract with the club on 22 December 2025, more than 600 days after his last competitive appearance.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/serie-a/origi-non-e-piu-un-giocatore-del-milan-l-attaccante-ha-firmato-la-risoluzione-del-contratto-2182253 |title=Ufficiale: Origi non è più un giocatore del Milan: l'attaccante ha firmato la risoluzione del contratto|date=22 December 2025 |website=TuttoMercatoWeb |language=it |trans-title=Official: Origi is no longer a Milan player: he signed mutual contract ending}}</ref>

On 8 June 2026, Origi announced his retirement from professional football.<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 June 2026 |title=Thank You, God. Thank You, Football. |url=https://www.theplayerstribune.com/divock-origi-soccer-retirement-belgium-liverpool |access-date=8 June 2026 |website=The Players' Tribune}}</ref>

==International career==
Origi has represented Belgium at [[Belgium national youth football team|under-15]], [[Belgium national youth football team|under-16]], [[Belgium national under-17 football team|under-17]], [[Belgium national under-19 football team|under-19]] and [[Belgium national under-21 football team|under-21]] level. He scored ten goals while in the under-19 team, the first in a [[2013 UEFA European Under-19 Championship qualification]] match against [[Belarus national under-19 football team|Belarus]] on 12 October 2012.<ref>{{cite news |title=Belgium 1–0 Belarus |url=https://www.uefa.com/under19/match/2009273--belgium-vs-belarus/?referrer=%2funder19%2fseason%3d2013%2fmatches%2fround%3d2000318%2fmatch%3d2009273%2findex |access-date=8 December 2021 |agency=UEFA}}</ref>

The [[Football Kenya Federation]] expressed an interest in persuading Origi to play for the [[Kenya national football team|Kenya senior national team]] in the future.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.goal.com/en-ke/news/4522/kenya/2013/02/04/3726151/kenya-fa-reveal-they-will-lure-striker-divock-origi-to-play?ICID=HP_MR_2 |title=Kenya FA reveal they will lure striker Divock Origi to play for Harambee Stars |date=4 February 2013 |first=David |last=Kwalimwa |website=Goal.com |access-date=5 February 2013 |archive-date=8 February 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130208060847/http://www.goal.com/en-ke/news/4522/kenya/2013/02/04/3726151/kenya-fa-reveal-they-will-lure-striker-divock-origi-to-play?ICID=HP_MR_2 |url-status=live}}</ref> However, on 13 May 2014, [[Belgium national football team|Belgium senior national team]] manager [[Marc Wilmots]] announced Origi would be part of the 23-man squad representing Belgium at the [[2014 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/27395150 |title=Adnan Januzaj included in Belgium's World Cup squad |date=13 May 2014 |access-date=13 May 2014 |website=BBC Sport |archive-date=1 July 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140701141133/http://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/27395150 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Origi came on as a substitute for [[Romelu Lukaku]] in the 58th minute of the opening [[2014 FIFA World Cup Group H|Group H]] game against [[Algeria national football team|Algeria]] in [[Belo Horizonte]] on 17 June. In Belgium's second match, again after coming on as a substitute for Lukaku, he scored his first senior international goal in the 88th minute of a 1–0 win over [[Russia national football team|Russia]] to qualify the ''Red Devils'' for the [[2014 FIFA World Cup knockout stage|knockout stage]].<ref name="bbc">{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/25285242 |title=Belgium v Russia |first=Graham |last=Chase |date=22 June 2014 |access-date=22 June 2014 |website=BBC Sport |archive-date=8 July 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140708204715/http://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/25285242 |url-status=live}}</ref> In so doing, at 19 years, two months and four days, he became the youngest goalscorer of the tournament (until [[United States national men's soccer team|American]] winger [[Julian Green]] scored against Belgium during their [[2014 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Belgium vs United States|round of 16 match]]), the youngest goalscorer in Belgian World Cup history, and the first player of Kenyan origin to score at a [[FIFA World Cup|World Cup finals]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2105895-divock-origis-late-goal-for-belgium-defeats-russia |title=Divock Origi's Late Goal for Belgium Defeats Russia |website=Bleacher Report |first=Sean |last=Swaby |date=22 June 2014 |access-date=22 June 2014 |archive-date=10 July 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140710225439/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2105895-divock-origis-late-goal-for-belgium-defeats-Russia |url-status=dead}}</ref> For his performances, he was named the Young Talent of the 2014 [[Belgian Sportsman of the year]] awards.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.goal.com/en-ke/news/4522/kenya/2014/12/16/7122662/origi-scoops-belgiums-award-for-most-promising-youngster |title=Lille loanee Divock Origi has won Belgium's award for most Promising Youngster of the Year 2014 as Liverpool summer signing continues to impress |access-date=2 December 2015 |website=Goal.com |date=16 December 2014}}</ref>

Origi scored once in Belgium's successful [[UEFA Euro 2016 qualifying]] campaign, in a 6–0 home win over [[Andorra national football team|Andorra]] on 10 October 2014.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Chambers |first1=Miles |title=Belgium 6–0 Andorra: De Bruyne and Mertens bag doubles in record-equalling win |url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/match/belgium-vs-andorra/1653181/report |access-date=2 December 2015 |website=Goal.com |date=10 October 2014}}</ref> He was included in the squad for [[UEFA Euro 2016|the final tournament]], but missed out on the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/29908/11380541/radja-nainggolan-left-out-of-belgium-world-cup-squad |title=Radja Nainggolan left out of Belgium World Cup squad |website=Sky Sports |date=21 May 2018}}</ref>
==Style of play==
Liverpool manager [[Jürgen Klopp]] described Origi as "a legend on and off the pitch. Fantastic footballer, a world class striker and [he] is our best finisher".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/story/_/id/37627833/liverpool-merseyside-derby-hero-divock-origi-our-best-finisher-jurgen-klopp|title=Liverpool's Merseyside derby hero Divock Origi our 'best finisher' - Jurgen Klopp|website=ESPN |date=24 April 2022}}</ref>
