=== Economic policy ===
After winning the 2017 election, Weah promised a Pro-Poor Agenda for Development and Prosperity, saying that this will benefit not just the poor, but all Liberians.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Finding Economic Solution: President George Manneh Weah commits to implementation of National Dialogue Recommendations {{!}} United Nations in Liberia |url=https://liberia.un.org/en/21164-finding-economic-solution-president-george-manneh-weah-commits-implementation-national,%20https://liberia.un.org/en/21164-finding-economic-solution-president-george-manneh-weah-commits-implementation-national |access-date=18 July 2023 |publisher=United Nations }}{{dead link|date=May 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

In 2019 inflation went as high as 28%. It made many Liberians to worry which led protests called "Save the State" in Monrovia and in Washington, D.C.<ref>{{Cite web |date=28 May 2019 |title=Liberians are worried their country is sliding into economic uncertainty under president Weah |url=https://qz.com/africa/1629355/liberias-george-weah-is-struggling-with-a-sinking-economy |access-date=18 July 2023 |website=Quartz}}</ref>

In September 2019, Weah attended the National Economic Dialogue (NED), seeking solutions amidst Liberia's economic crisis. A host of organizations rallied to develop a comprehensive program aimed at bolstering Liberia's economy. Weah urged Liberians to use the Dialogue as a national platform to craft strategies and offer workable solutions for the crisis. The forum yielded several recommendations, some of which are listed below:<ref>{{Cite web |title=Finding Economic Solution: President George Manneh Weah commits to implementation of National Dialogue Recommendations |publisher=United Nations |url=https://liberia.un.org/en/21164-finding-economic-solution-president-george-manneh-weah-commits-implementation-national |access-date=16 August 2023}}</ref>

* Review of recommendations of the TRC including the establishment of economic and war crimes court
* Printing of new currency
* Broad-based review of the national custom code
* Recapitalization of the Central Bank of Liberia
* Review of domestic and external debts
* Practical agriculture programs, peace and national reconciliation

During his second year in office, Weah and his administration witnessed a deterioration in the economy, with inflation reaching 30%. This economic downturn, coupled with payment delays, triggered protests against which the police employed tear gas and water cannons.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rouse |first=Lucinda |title=Liberians grow wary of George Weah as economic woes deepen |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/1/28/liberians-grow-wary-of-george-weah-as-economic-woes-deepen |access-date=18 July 2023 |publisher=Al Jazeera}}</ref>

During his fourth State of the Nation address, President Weah presented a series of proposed economic policies and legislative reforms, aiming to address the worsening economic conditions.<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 January 2021 |title=Liberian economy front and centre of Weah's state of the nation speech |url=https://www.rfi.fr/en/africa/20210126-liberian-economy-front-and-centre-of-weah-s-state-of-the-nation-speech-africa-politics-growth-coronavirus |access-date=18 July 2023 |publisher=Radio France Internationale}}</ref>

After Weah came to power, Liberia's unemployment rate increased from 3% in 2017 to 4.1%. The Liberian economy grew 1–5% in the first five years of his administration (2018–2022).

=== Domestic policy ===
On 29 January 2018, in his first annual message to the national legislature, he reduced his salary and other benefits by 25% with immediate effect, stating, "With the assessment that I gave you earlier of the poor condition of our economy, I believe that it is appropriate that we should all make sacrifices in the interest of our country. According to Article 60 of the [[Constitution of Liberia]], the salaries of the president and the vice president are established by the [[Legislature of Liberia]] and cannot be increased or reduced during the period for which they are elected. However, in view of the very rapidly deteriorating situation of the economy, I am informing you today, with immediate effect, that I will reduce my salary and benefits by 25% and give the proceeds back to the Consolidated Fund for allocation and appropriation as they see fit."<ref>[http://www.emansion.gov.lr/2press.php?news_id=4347&related=7&pg=sp President Weah Delivers Maiden State of the Nation; Assures 25% Cut in Salary] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180811022706/http://www.emansion.gov.lr/2press.php?news_id=4347&related=7&pg=sp |date=11 August 2018 }}, ''Libgov''. Retrieved, 29 January 2018</ref>

On 29 January 2018, Weah announced he would seek constitutional changes to allow people of different ethnic descent to be citizens and allow foreigners to own land. He called the present situation "racist and inappropriate".<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-42871741 |title=Weah to scrap 'racist' citizenship law |year=2018 |website=BBC News |access-date=30 January 2018}}</ref>

[[File:2018 July 4 Celebration (2).jpg|thumb|Weah at a 4 July celebration in 2018.]]

On 12 September 2020, he declared a national emergency over sexual violence in the country, pledging to create a special prosecutor for rape, a national sex offender registry, and a national task force to tackle the issue.<ref>{{cite web |date=12 September 2020 |title=Liberia declares rape a national emergency after spike in cases |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/9/12/liberia-declares-rape-a-national-emergency-after-spike-in-cases |access-date=16 June 2022 |publisher=Al Jazeera}}</ref> He further announced a 2 million dollar emergency fund, part of which was used to purchase DNA-testing equipment for forensic identification of perpetrators.<ref>{{cite web |date=9 December 2021 |title=Liberia: One Year Since President Weah Declared Rape a National Emergency Activists Say Nothing Has Changed |url=https://frontpageafricaonline.com/front-slider/liberia-one-year-since-president-weah-declared-rape-a-national-emergency-activists-say-nothing-has-changed/ |first=Mae |last=Azango |access-date=16 June 2022 |work=FrontPage Africa}}</ref> However, as of March 2022, the DNA-testing equipment had yet to be made functional.<ref>{{cite web |date=11 March 2022 |title=Women Legislative Caucus Calls for functional DNA Machines amid Increase in Rape Case |url=https://frontpageafricaonline.com/gender-issues/women-legislative-caucus-calls-for-functional-dna-machines-amid-increase-in-rape-case/ |first=Gerald C. |last=Koinyeneh |access-date=16 June 2022 |work=FrontPage Africa}}</ref> As well, the special prosecutor had yet to be appointed, the sex offender registry had yet to be implemented, and specialized gender-based violence courts had only been implemented in three of the sixteen Liberian counties.<ref>{{cite web |date=7 June 2022 |title=Has Liberia's 'feminist' president forgotten his promise to tackle rape? |url=https://www.opendemocracy.net/en/5050/liberia-president-george-weah-rape-impunity/ |first=Bettie K. |last=Johnson-Mbayo |access-date=16 June 2022 |work=openDemocracy}}</ref>

Weah signed a drug bill into law which passed by the legislature after months. The law aimed to regulate, restrict, control, limit, or eradicate the illegal export and importation as well as the flagrant use, abuse, and proliferation of narcotics within the nation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=President Weah Signs Drugs Bill into Law {{!}} The Executive Mansion |url=https://www.emansion.gov.lr/media/press-release/president-weah-signs-drugs-bill-law |access-date=18 July 2023 |website=www.emansion.gov.lr}}</ref>

Months before the [[2023 Liberian general election|2023 election]], he accepted the endorsement of the [[Bassa people (Liberia)|Bassa people]] for re-election. They did this because "he has the competence and passion to develop Liberia."<ref>{{Cite web |title=President Weah Accepts Bassa People's Reelection Endorsement {{!}} The Executive Mansion |url=https://www.emansion.gov.lr/media/press-release/president-weah-accepts-bassa-peoples-reelection-endorsement |access-date=18 July 2023 |website=www.emansion.gov.lr}}</ref>

Under his presidency Liberia has made improvements to education by constructing and renovating schools to make sure children have better education and environment.<ref name="African Leadership Magazine 2023">{{Cite web |last=Admin |date=5 June 2023 |title=George Weah's Political leadership impact on Liberia |url=https://www.africanleadershipmagazine.co.uk/56331-2/ |access-date=18 July 2023 |website=African Leadership Magazine}}</ref>

=== Healthcare ===
Healthcare in Liberia improved since he became president in 2018. His administration invested into health infrastructure and medical equipment. He also deployed doctors to many  underserved areas of the country. Weah instituted health insurance programs. Liberia's first dialysis center was built under his administration.<ref>[https://www.afro.who.int/countries/liberia/news/president-weah-commissions-liberias-first-national-dialysis-center-and-names-it-honour-his President Weah commissions Liberia's first National Dialysis Center and names it in honour of his predecessor] [[World Health Organization]] 7 March 2022 {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220315125929/https://www.afro.who.int/countries/liberia/news/president-weah-commissions-liberias-first-national-dialysis-center-and-names-it-honour-his|date=15 March 2022}}</ref><ref name="African Leadership Magazine 2023" />

=== Foreign policy ===
{{See also|List of international presidential trips made by George Weah}}
Upon his election to office, Weah first made an official visit in Senegal to meet with President [[Macky Sall]], to "strengthen the bond between the two countries". On 21 February 2018, Weah made his first official visit outside Africa, to France, meeting French president [[Emmanuel Macron]]. The meeting focused on improving the relationship between France and Liberia and also sought French help for a sports development project in Africa. The meeting was also attended by Didier Drogba, [[Kylian Mbappé]] and [[FIFA]] president [[Gianni Infantino]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.parismatch.com/Actu/Politique/Macron-recoit-Weah-a-l-Elysee-en-presence-de-Drogba-et-Mbappe-1465295 |title=Macron reçoit Weah à l'Elysée en présence de Drogba et Mbappé |year=2018 |work=Paris Match |access-date=21 February 2018 |language=FR}}</ref>
On 25 May 2018, following a meeting with President Weah, the Liberian Football Association president [[Musa Bility]] announced that Liberia would vote for the [[Canada–Mexico–United States 2026 FIFA World Cup bid|Canada–Mexico–United States World Cup bid]], breaking ranks with the rest of Africa, who were voting for the [[Morocco 2026 FIFA World Cup bid|Moroccan bid]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Edwards |first1=Piers |title=Liberia to vote against Morocco's 2026 World Cup bid |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/44247560 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

He made a visit to China to congratulate [[Xi Jinping]] on his re-election of [[General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party]] as well as the [[Paramount leader|top leader]] of China. President Weah said he looked forward to further cementing the strong ties that exist between both countries since establishment between both nations.<ref>{{Cite web |date=11 June 2023 |title=Pres. Weah Congratulates Pres. Xi on His Reelection {{!}} The Executive Mansion |url=https://www.emansion.gov.lr/media/press-release/pres-weah-congratulates-pres-xi-his-reelection |access-date=18 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230611173518/https://www.emansion.gov.lr/media/press-release/pres-weah-congratulates-pres-xi-his-reelection |archive-date=11 June 2023 }}</ref>

[[File:Reuven Rivlin with George Mena Wah, February 2019 (8308).jpg|thumb|Weah with [[Reuven Rivlin]] in Israel, 2019.]]

In July 2023, he met with Israeli prime minister [[Benjamin Netanyahu]] to discuss topics of cementing ties, trade, cooperation on international affairs, peace, and security.<ref>{{Cite web |title=President Weah Holds Bilateral Meeting With Israeli Leaders {{!}} The Executive Mansion |url=https://www.emansion.gov.lr/media/press-release/president-weah-holds-bilateral-meeting-israeli-leaders |access-date=18 July 2023 |website=www.emansion.gov.lr}}</ref>

=== Song ===
On 25 March 2020, the Liberian president recorded his song with the local group The Rabbis, the text of which was written by himself. In this song "He invites the Liberian and African population to stand up by all means against this virus <nowiki>[</nowiki>[[SARS-CoV-2]]<nowiki>]</nowiki> which is causing damage around the world."<ref>{{cite web |last=Cochimau |first=Houngbadji |date=9 April 2020 |title=Liberia: l'émouvante chanson du président George Weah contre la Covid-19 (vidéo) |url=https://beninwebtv.com/2020/04/liberia-lemouvante-chanson-du-president-george-weah-contre-la-covid-19-video/ |access-date=10 April 2020 |website=BENIN WEB TV |language=fr-FR |archive-date=12 April 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200412171959/https://beninwebtv.com/2020/04/liberia-lemouvante-chanson-du-president-george-weah-contre-la-covid-19-video/ |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=La chanson de George Weah contre le Covid-19 |url=https://www.20min.ch/ro/sports/football/story/20002404 |access-date=10 April 2020 |website=20 Minutes |date=April 2020 |language=fr}}</ref><blockquote>"It could be your mother, it could be your dad, your brothers or your sisters. Let's all stand together to fight this dirty virus"-an extract from President Weah's song on a [[reggae]] rhythm. The majority of people in Liberia do not have internet or Facebook access, but radio is a popular and very accessible form of entertainment in the African country.. The song would be played on various stations across the country to properly broadcast the message, according to the president's spokesperson.<ref name="Franceinfo 2020">{{cite web |date=2020-03-26 |title=Liberia : le président George Weah chante contre le coronavirus |url=https://www.francetvinfo.fr/monde/afrique/societe-africaine/liberia-le-president-george-weah-chante-contre-le-coronavirus_3885653.html |access-date=2020-04-10 |website=Franceinfo |language=fr}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=George Weah chante contre le coronavirus – Foot – Coronavirus |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/George-weah-chante-contre-le-coronavirus/1123858 |access-date=2020-04-10 |website=L'Équipe |language=fr}}</ref></blockquote> Weah had already recorded a song against [[Ebola virus epidemic in Liberia|Ebola]].<ref name="Franceinfo 2020" />

== Personal life ==
Weah has four children; three with his Jamaican-born<ref>{{cite web |url=https://globeafrique.com/jamaican-first-lady-for-liberia-excites-jamaicans-worldwide |title=Jamaican 'First Lady' for Liberia Excites Jamaicans worldwide |access-date=29 December 2017 |work=Globe Afrique |date=4 October 2017 |first=Ben |last=Mabande |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171230060245/https://globeafrique.com/jamaican-first-lady-for-liberia-excites-jamaicans-worldwide/ |archive-date=30 December 2017 |url-status=dead}}</ref> wife [[Clar Weah]]: [[George Weah Jr.|George]], Tita, and [[Timothy Weah|Timothy]]; and a child from another relationship. In 2016, he was sued by the mother of his daughter for child support expenses.<ref>{{cite web |title=Weah child support expenses |url=https://frontpageafricaonline.com/diaspora/u-s-court-denies-weah-attorney-fees-in-child-support-case/ |work=Front Page Africa |date=October 2016}}</ref> George and Timothy became footballers and signed for Paris Saint-Germain,<ref>{{cite web |title=Weah's Son Signs For PSG |url=http://monroviainquirer.com/2015/09/15/weahs-son-signs-for-psg/ |website=The Inquirer Newspaper |publisher=The Inquirer |access-date=5 December 2015 |date=15 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208103909/http://monroviainquirer.com/2015/09/15/weahs-son-signs-for-psg/ |archive-date=8 December 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref> with Timothy going on to play for the first team.<ref>{{cite news |title=U.S.'s Timothy Weah, son of George, makes debut for PSG |url=http://www.espn.co.uk/football/paris-saint-germain/story/3404724/us-youth-international-timothy-weah-son-of-george-makes-debut-for-psg |access-date=10 April 2018 |publisher=ESPN |date=3 March 2018}}</ref> Both played as youth internationals for the United States,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ussoccer.com/players/2014/05/14/10/51/timothy-weah |title=Timothy Weah |publisher=U.S. Soccer |access-date=29 August 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140903074554/http://www.ussoccer.com/players/2014/05/14/10/51/timothy-weah |archive-date=3 September 2014}}</ref> and Timothy went on to play for the [[United States men's national soccer team|senior team]]. Weah has a cousin, Stephen Weah, who also played as a footballer for [[Preston Lions FC]] of [[Melbourne]], Australia.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.liberiansoccer.com/Weah's%20Cousin%20on%20football%20trial%20in%20Australia.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050308084523/http://www.liberiansoccer.com/Weah's%20Cousin%20on%20football%20trial%20in%20Australia.htm |archive-date=2005-03-08|title=Weah's Cousin on football trial in Australia | access-date=2023-10-01}}</ref> His nephew [[Jester Weah|Jester]] is a former [[gridiron football]] player in the [[National Football League|National]] and [[Canadian Football League]]s.<ref>{{cite news|last=Latham-Coyle|first=Harry|url=https://www.khou.com/article/sports/nfl/texans/texans-udfa-wide-receiver-jester-weahs-family-has-serious-sporting-pedigree/285-547195071|title=Texans UDFA wide receiver Jester Weah's family has serious sporting pedigree|publisher=[[KHOU]]|date=30 April 2018|access-date=10 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Gray|first=Britton|url=https://www.ckom.com/2022/05/31/student-of-the-game-weah-still-learning-as-he-tries-to-catch-on-at-riders-camp/|title=Student of the game: Weah still learning as he tries to catch on at Riders camp|publisher=[[CKOM]]|date=31 May 2022|access-date=10 June 2026}}</ref>

Weah practiced Islam for ten years before converting to Christianity.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/sports_talk/forum/1550731.stm |title=You quizzed George Weah |website=BBC Sport |date=18 September 2001 |access-date=5 November 2023}}</ref> In October 2017, he was spotted in the church of prominent Nigerian pastor [[T. B. Joshua]] alongside Liberian senator [[Prince Johnson]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Weah, Boakai Seek Nigerian Prophet T.B. Joshua's Blessing For Liberian Presidency |url=https://frontpageafricaonline.com/index.php/politics/5841-prince-johnson-george-weah-attend-same-service-in-nigeria |work=Front Page Africa (Liberia) |date=22 October 2017 |access-date=11 January 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171226170235/http://frontpageafricaonline.com/index.php/politics/5841-prince-johnson-george-weah-attend-same-service-in-nigeria |archive-date=26 December 2017 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Joshua was allegedly a key influence in Johnson's decision to endorse Weah's candidacy in the 2017 election.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Ex-Liberian Warlord Endorses Weah After Joint Visit To Nigerian Pastor |url=http://www.africanews.com/2017/10/27/ex-liberian-warlord-endorses-weah-after-joint-visit-to-nigerian-pastor/ |work=Africa News |date=27 October 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Liberian newspapers zoom on Prince Johnson, Weah in Nigeria for prayers, others |url=https://www.journalducameroun.com/en/liberian-newspapers-zoom-on-prince-johnson-weah-in-nigeria-for-prayers-others/ |work=Journal Du Cameroun |date=23 October 2017 |access-date=9 November 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171110124433/https://www.journalducameroun.com/en/liberian-newspapers-zoom-on-prince-johnson-weah-in-nigeria-for-prayers-others/ |archive-date=10 November 2017 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Weah holds French citizenship and speaks French fluently.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.lemonde.fr/afrique/article/2017/12/29/george-weah-l-enfant-du-ghetto-devenu-president_5235874_3212.html |title=George Weah, l'enfant du ghetto devenu président du Liberia |work=Le Monde Afrique |date=30 December 2017}}</ref>

'''Kepa Arrizabalaga Revuelta''' (born 3 October 1994), often referred to simply as '''Kepa''',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tribuna.com/en/blogs/arteta-made-the-right-decision-to-start-kepa/|title=Arteta made the right decision to start Kepa|date=26 March 2026|access-date=26 March 2026|website=Tribuna|author=Nathan Cartwright}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11670/13523213/arsenal-starting-kepa-backfired-big-time-after-carabao-cup-final-howler-helps-man-city-to-trophy-says-jamie-redknapp|title=Arsenal starting Kepa 'backfired big time' after Carabao Cup final howler helps Man City to trophy, says Jamie Redknapp|date=23 March 2026|access-date=26 March 2026|website=Sky Sports}}</ref> is a Spanish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for {{English football updater|Arsenal}} club [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]].

After progressing through [[Athletic Bilbao]]'s youth academy including their farm and reserve teams, he played for [[SD Ponferradina|Ponferradina]] and [[Real Valladolid]] on consecutive [[Loan (sports)|loan]]s between 2015 and 2016, after which he became a first-team regular at Athletic. In 2018, he moved to [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in a [[Transfer (association football)|transfer]] worth €80 million (£72 million), a record fee for a goalkeeper. There, he won the [[2018–19 UEFA Europa League|UEFA Europa League]], the [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] and the [[2021 UEFA Super Cup|UEFA Super Cup]]. After inconsistent performances, he joined [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] on loan in 2023, where he won [[La Liga]] and the Champions League. Following another loan stint, this time at fellow Premier League club [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]], he moved to rival Arsenal on a permanent deal.

Arrizabalaga won the [[2012 UEFA European Under-19 Championship|2012 European Under-19 Championship]] with [[Spain national under-19 football team|Spain's under-19 team]]. He made his senior debut in 2017, and was part of the national squad for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018 World Cup]], although he did not make an appearance at the tournament.

==Club career==
===Athletic Bilbao===
Born in [[Ondarroa]], [[Biscay]], [[Basque Country (autonomous community)|Basque Country]], Arrizabalaga joined [[Athletic Bilbao]]'s youth setup at [[Lezama Facilities|Lezama]] in 2004, aged ten. He made his senior debut with [[farm team]] [[CD Basconia|Basconia]] in January 2012, in [[Tercera División]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.europapress.es/deportes/futbol-00162/noticia-chelsea-ficha-kepa-portero-mas-caro-historia-20180808231338.html|title=El Chelsea ficha a Kepa, el portero más caro de la historia|trans-title=Chelsea sign Kepa, most expensive goalkeeper in history|publisher=Europa Press|language=es|date=8 August 2018|access-date=9 January 2019|archive-date=28 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190628195135/https://www.europapress.es/deportes/futbol-00162/noticia-chelsea-ficha-kepa-portero-mas-caro-historia-20180808231338.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 5 May 2012, Arrizabalaga was called up to the main squad for a [[La Liga]] match against [[Getafe CF|Getafe]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=12069&idi=2|title=Athletic Club-Getafe: Line-ups|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=5 May 2012|access-date=11 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131107090108/http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0|archive-date=7 November 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> but remained unused in the 0–0 draw at the [[San Mamés Stadium (1913)|San Mamés Stadium]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/marcador/futbol/2011_12/primera/jornada_37/ath_get/|title=Sin argumentos en la Catedral|trans-title=No arguments at the Cathedral|newspaper=Marca|location=Spain|first=Álvaro|last=Sánchez|language=es|date=5 May 2012|access-date=11 December 2014|archive-date=18 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170818044846/http://www.marca.com/marcador/futbol/2011_12/primera/jornada_37/ath_get/|url-status=live}}</ref> He was also called up to pre-season in July, and on 23 September was also a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] in another home game of the same outcome, against [[Málaga CF|Málaga]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2012_13/primera/jornada_5/ath_mga/|title=Europa les pesa|trans-title=Europe weighs on them|newspaper=Marca|location=Spain|first=Ángel|last=Liceras|language=es|date=23 September 2012|access-date=11 December 2014|archive-date=15 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180815091055/http://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2012_13/primera/jornada_5/ath_mga/|url-status=live}}</ref>

web|url=http://bizkaia.eldesmarque.com/athletic-club/33979-en-lezama-apuestan-fuerte-por-kepa-arrizabalaba|title=En Lezama apuestan fuerte por Kepa Arrizabalaga|trans-title=Lezama bets high on Kepa 3 March, he was one of two players [[Ejection (sports)|sent off]] towards the end of a 3–1 home win over [[SD Amorebieta|Amorebieta]], as well as teammate [[Jon García Herrero|Jon García]];<ref>{{cite web|url=http://bizkaia.eldesmarque.com/athletic-club/noticias/34732-el-bilbao-athletic-amenaza-el-liderato-del-alaves|title=El Bilbao Athletic amenaza el liderato del Alavés|trans-title=Bilbao Athletic threaten Alavés' lead|publisher=El Desmarque|language=es|date=4 March 2013|access-date=29 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208055810/http://bizkaia.eldesmarque.com/athletic-club/noticias/34732-el-bilbao-athletic-amenaza-el-liderato-del-alaves|archive-date=8 December 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> in April, he suffered a [[Athletic pubalgia|pubalgia]], only returning to the field in September.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://bizkaia.eldesmarque.com/athletic-club/37480-Kepa-Arrizabalaga-reaparece-casi-seis-meses-despu%C3%A9s-en-el-Bilbao-Athletic|title=Kepa Arrizabalaga reaparece casi seis meses después en 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150114082209/http://bizkaia.eldesmarque.com/athletic-club/37480-Kepa-Arrizabalaga-reaparece-casi-seis-meses-despu%C3%A9s-en-el-Bilbao-Athletic|archive-date=14 January 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Arrizabalaga appeared regularly for the B's after his return, but broke the first [[metacarpal]] of his right hand in January 2014,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=13915&idi=2|title=Kepa Arrizabalaga's injury|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=22 January 2014|access-date=11 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131107090108/http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0|archive-date=7 November 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> being sidelined for a month. On 11 March, Getafe submitted a loan request to the ''Lions'' for him, as a replacement to injured [[Miguel Ángel Moyá]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aupaathletic.com/noticias/noticias-ver.asp?id=11023|title=El Getafe pide la cesión de Kepa Arrizabalaga|trans-title=Getafe ask for Kepa Arrizabalaga's loan|publisher=Aupa Athletic|language=es|date=11 March 2014|access-date=11 December 2014|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304030026/http://www.aupaathletic.com/noticias/noticias-ver.asp?id=11023|url-status=live}}</ref> but it was rejected a day later.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://athletic.elcorreo.com/noticias/2014-03-12/athletic-rechaza-ceder-hasta-20140312.html|title=El Athletic rechaza ceder hasta final de Liga al portero Kepa al Getafe|trans-title=Athletic reject loaning goalkeeper Kepa to Getafe until the end of the League|newspaper=El Correo|first=Javier|last=Ortiz de Lazcano|language=es|date=12 March 2014|access-date=11 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150114081242/http://athletic.elcorreo.com/noticias/2014-03-12/athletic-rechaza-ceder-hasta-20140312.html|archive-date=14 January 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 5 January 2015, Arrizabalaga was loaned to [[Segunda División]] club [[SD Ponferradina|Ponferradina]] until June.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sdponferradina.com/-/mi|title=Kepa Arrizabalaga se incorpora a la Ponferradina|trans-title=Kepa Arrizabalaga added to Ponferradina|publisher=SD Ponferradina|language=es|date=5 January 2015|access-date=5 January 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150109172714/http://www.sdponferradina.com/-/mi|archive-date=9 January 2015}}</ref> He made his professional debut six days laer, starting in a 1–1 home draw against [[Racing de Santander|Racing Santander]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2015/01/11/futbol/2adivision/1421014655.html|title=El Racing encontró justo premio a su trabajo en el último minuto|trans-title=Racing's work paid off in the last minute|newspaper=Marca|location=Spain|language=es|date=11 January 2015|access-date=14 January 2015|archive-date=10 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180810072631/http://www.marca.com/2015/01/11/futbol/2adivision/1421014655.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 20 July 2015, Arrizabalaga moved to [[Real Valladolid]], also of the second tier, in a [[2015–16 Segunda División|season]]-long loan deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realvalladolid.es/noticias/actualidad/20072015/Kepa-cierra-la-porteria-del-Pucela/|title=Kepa cierra la portería del Pucela|trans-title=Kepa shuts down goal of Pucela|publisher=Real Valladolid|language=es|date=20 July 2015|access-date=20 July 2015|archive-date=28 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190628202959/http://www.realvalladolid.es/noticias/actualidad/20072015/Kepa-cierra-la-porteria-del-Pucela/|url-status=live}}</ref> He played his first competitive game on 22 August, in a 0–1 loss at [[Córdoba CF|Córdoba]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2015/08/23/futbol/equipos/cordoba/1440284201.html|title=Fidel resuelve en un gran partido del Córdoba|trans-title=Fidel the decider in a great Córdoba match|newspaper=Marca|location=Spain|first=Alberto|last=Laz|language=es|date=23 August 2015|access-date=7 September 2015|archive-date=15 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180815164116/http://www.marca.com/2015/08/23/futbol/equipos/cordoba/1440284201.html|url-status=live}}</ref> and missed only three matches as his team finished 16th.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.diariodevalladolid.es/noticias/deportes/kepa-traera-dinero-zorrilla_125966.html|title=Kepa traerá dinero a Zorrilla|trans-title=Kepa will bring money to Zorrilla|newspaper=Diario de Valladolid|language=es|date=8 August 2018|access-date=9 January 2019|archive-date=9 January 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190109205400/http://www.diariodevalladolid.es/noticias/deportes/kepa-traera-dinero-zorrilla_125966.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

After returning from loan, Arrizabalaga was included in the first team squad, initially as third-choice behind [[Gorka Iraizoz]] and [[Iago Herrerín]]. He made his debut in the top flight on 11 September 2016, starting in a 1–0 away win over [[Deportivo de La Coruña]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2016_17/la-liga/jornada_3/dep_ath/|title=Raúl García exhibe su pegada|trans-title=Raúl García shows his power|newspaper=Marca|location=Spain|first=Jaime|last=Rincón|language=es|date=11 September 2016|access-date=18 September 2016|archive-date=27 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190327023118/https://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2016_17/la-liga/jornada_3/dep_ath/|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 22 January 2018, amid heavy transfer speculation linking him to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], Arrizabalaga renewed his contract – due to expire that June – until 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11848/11218301/kepa-arrizabalaga-ends-real-madrid-speculation-by-signing-athletic-bilbao-deal|title=Kepa Arrizabalaga ends Real Madrid speculation by signing Athletic Bilbao deal|website=Sky Sports|date=22 January 2018|access-date=23 January 2018|archive-date=6 September 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180906095140/http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11848/11218301/kepa-arrizabalaga-ends-real-madrid-speculation-by-signing-athletic-bilbao-deal|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Chelsea===
====2018–19: Debut season, UEFA Europa League victory====
[[File:Liverpool vs. Chelsea, 14 August 2019 37 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Arrizabalaga playing for [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in the [[2019 UEFA Super Cup]]]]

On 8 August 2018, Athletic Bilbao announced on their website that Arrizabalaga had paid his required [[release clause]] (€80 million / £71.6 million),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.athletic-club.eus/en/noticias/19263/kepa-pays-termination-clause.html|title=Kepa pays termination clause|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=8 August 2018|access-date=8 August 2018|archive-date=8 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180808172052/https://www.athletic-club.eus/en/noticias/19263/kepa-pays-termination-clause.html|url-status=live}}</ref> making him the [[List of most expensive association football transfers|world's most expensive goalkeeper]] only weeks after the record was set by [[Alisson (footballer, born 1992)|Alisson]]'s transfer to [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/aug/07/chelsea-kepa-arrizabalaga-athletic-bilbao-record|title=Chelsea to pay £71.6m for Athletic Bilbao goalkeeper Kepa Arrizabalaga|newspaper=The Guardian|first=Dominic|last=Fifield|date=7 August 2018|access-date=14 August 2018|archive-date=13 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180813172123/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/aug/07/chelsea-kepa-arrizabalaga-athletic-bilbao-record|url-status=live}}</ref> Later that day, his move to [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] on a seven-year contract was confirmed,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2018/8/8/kepa-arrives-at-chelsea|title=Kepa arrives at Chelsea|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|date=8 August 2018|access-date=8 August 2018|archive-date=27 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190827101629/https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2018/8/8/kepa-arrives-at-chelsea|url-status=live}}</ref> replacing [[Thibaut Courtois]] who had departed for Real Madrid. He made his [[Premier League]] debut three days later in a 3–0 away win against [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/45067371|title=Huddersfield Town 0–3 Chelsea|website=BBC Sport|first=Michael|last=Emons|date=11 August 2018|access-date=14 August 2018|archive-date=26 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190326060755/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/45067371|url-status=live}}</ref> going on to keep six clean sheets<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/chelseas-kepa-relishing-being-worlds-most-expensive-keeper/ph9py6s9dsx616jcv411ad0jq|title=Chelsea's Kepa relishing being world's most expensive keeper|website=Goal (website)|publisher=Perform Group|date=10 October 2018|access-date=9 January 2019|archive-date=1 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190601212714/https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/chelseas-kepa-relishing-being-worlds-most-expensive-keeper/ph9py6s9dsx616jcv411ad0jq|url-status=live}}</ref> in the team's 12-match unbeaten run in the league, before a 3–1 defeat at the hands of [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/tottenham-vs-chelsea/390883|title=Tottenham 3–1 Chelsea: Maurizio Sarri's unbeaten start ended|website=Sky Sports|first=Ron|last=Walker|date=24 November 2018|access-date=25 November 2018|archive-date=3 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190703095843/https://www.skysports.com/football/tottenham-vs-chelsea/390883|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 24 January 2019, in the second leg of the [[EFL Cup]] semi-final, Arrizabalaga saved a [[Penalty (association football)|penalty]] from Tottenham's [[Lucas Moura]] in a 4–2 [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] win at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]], helping his team go through to the final.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sportinglife.com/football/news/chelsea-make-spurs-pay-the-penalty/157724|title=Carabao Cup semi-final: Chelsea beat Tottenham 4–2 on penalties to book final clash with Manchester City at Wembley|newspaper=Sporting Life|date=24 January 2019|access-date=24 January 2019|archive-date=20 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190420085431/https://www.sportinglife.com/football/news/chelsea-make-spurs-pay-the-penalty/157724|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 24 February 2019, during the [[2019 EFL Cup Final]] against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], with the match at 0–0 near the end of extra time, [[Maurizio Sarri]] called for Arrizabalaga to be substituted off for [[Willy Caballero]] for the upcoming penalty shootout. Arrizabalaga refused to be substituted, gesticulating and remaining on the field. During the shootout, he saved one penalty as Chelsea lost 4–3.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Burt |first1=Jason |last2=Tyers |first2=Mike |title=Manchester City take the honours after Kepa Arrizabalaga antics overshadow otherwise drab League Cup final |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2019/02/24/chelsea-vs-manchester-city-carabao-cup-final-2019-live-score/ |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |date=24 February 2019 |access-date=25 February 2019 |archive-date=30 May 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190530134323/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2019/02/24/chelsea-vs-manchester-city-carabao-cup-final-2019-live-score/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=WATCH: Kepa Arrizabalaga defies furious Chelsea boss Maurizio Sarri in Carabao Cup final |url=https://news.sky.com/story/watch-kepa-arrizabalaga-defies-furious-chelsea-boss-maurizio-sarri-in-carabao-cup-final-11647428 |publisher=Sky News |access-date=25 February 2019 |archive-date=25 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190225162305/https://news.sky.com/story/watch-kepa-arrizabalaga-defies-furious-chelsea-boss-maurizio-sarri-in-carabao-cup-final-11647428 |url-status=live }}</ref> After the game, both Arrizabalaga and Sarri said that the situation was a misunderstanding, with Sarri incorrectly believing that Arrizabalaga was too injured with cramp to continue.<ref>{{cite news |title=Maurizio Sarri: Kepa Arrizabalaga incident a 'misunderstanding', says Chelsea boss |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47352319 |access-date=25 February 2019 |archive-date=16 June 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190616151539/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47352319 |url-status=live }}</ref> Later on, Arrizabalaga met with Sarri and apologised to him and to the rest of the club. He was fined a week's worth of pay as a result of his actions, with Sarri leaving the decision of any further discipline up to the club.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/47365945 |title=Kepa Arrizabalaga: Chelsea goalkeeper fined & apologises for Wembley incident |date=25 February 2019 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=26 February 2019 |archive-date=28 June 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190628220731/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/47365945 |url-status=live }}</ref> Arrizabalaga was dropped from the starting lineup for Caballero in Chelsea's next match, a Premier League game against Tottenham.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/its-a-message-to-the-group-sarri-explains-reasoning-for-dropping-/fei9ryhrddhg13xh86pt31i0v|title='It's a message to the group' – Sarri explains reasoning for dropping Kepa|website=Goal (website)|publisher=Perform Group|date=28 February 2019|access-date=1 March 2019|archive-date=1 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190301214515/https://www.goal.com/en/news/its-a-message-to-the-group-sarri-explains-reasoning-for-dropping-/fei9ryhrddhg13xh86pt31i0v|url-status=live}}</ref> He returned to the lineup for the following match.

On 9 May 2019, Arrizabalaga saved two penalties in the shootout at the end of the second leg of the [[UEFA Europa League]] semi-final against [[Eintracht Frankfurt]] to take Chelsea to [[2019 UEFA Europa League Final|the final]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/48171995|title=Chelsea 1–1 Frankfurt|website=BBC Sport|date=10 May 2019|access-date=10 May 2019|archive-date=9 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190509224428/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/48171995|url-status=live}}</ref> which they won 4–1 over [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]].<ref name=uel19/>

====2019–21: Struggles, UEFA Champions League win====
Under the management of [[Frank Lampard]], Chelsea failed to win any trophies. Throughout the 2019–20 season, Arrizabalaga struggled to stay in form, eventually being benched in favour of Willy Caballero in late January 2020 in a cup match against [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]]. Arrizabalaga remained outside of the starting eleven during the next four league matches and a [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] match.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.football.london/chelsea-fc/news/kepa-arrizabalaga-chelsea-everton-lampard-17887905 |title=Chelsea fans hail Kepa's form since returning to first team |last=Ha |first=Andy |date=9 March 2020 |website=footballlondon |access-date=9 March 2020 |archive-date=28 March 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200328123024/https://www.football.london/chelsea-fc/news/kepa-arrizabalaga-chelsea-everton-lampard-17887905 |url-status=live }}</ref> He regained his starting spot on 4 March during the [[FA Cup]] fifth round against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] where he made a string of saves to deny the eventual Premier League champions;<ref name=kepareturn>{{Cite web |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/fa-league-cups/chelsea-liverpool-kepa-arrizabalaga-frank-lampard-fa-cup-result-highlights-a9373516.html |title=Kepa stands out on potentially pivotal night for Lampard's Chelsea |date=3 March 2020 |website=The Independent |access-date=9 March 2020 |archive-date=4 March 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200304185542/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/fa-league-cups/chelsea-liverpool-kepa-arrizabalaga-frank-lampard-fa-cup-result-highlights-a9373516.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Chelsea went on to win the match 2–0.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-liverpool/423678/|title=Chelsea 2–0 Liverpool: Willian and Ross Barkley fire Blues to FA Cup quarter-finals|website=Sky Sports|last=Gholam|first=Simeon|date=4 March 2020|access-date=6 May 2020|archive-date=19 May 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200519210205/https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-liverpool/423678|url-status=live}}</ref> But he would find himself benched to end the season, missing out on the team's run to the [[2020 FA Cup Final|final]] of the FA Cup.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/kepa-benched-again-fa-cup-161306506.html|title=Kepa benched again for FA Cup final as Chelsea tackle Arsenal|website=Yahoo|date=1 August 2020|access-date=11 September 2020|archive-date=4 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200804065220/https://sports.yahoo.com/kepa-benched-again-fa-cup-161306506.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> During the second half of the season, Arrizabalaga faced abuse from Chelsea fans which led to him turning off comments on social media.<ref>{{cite tweet|user=cfcdaily|number=1291055300942929921|title=Kepa has limited his comments on Instagram. #cfc}}</ref>

Arrizabalaga appeared for Chelsea in the opening game of the [[2020–21 Premier League]] season against [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]]. Chelsea won 3–1. Arrizabalaga was judged to have made a significant error in the next match against Liverpool, after his pass went straight to [[Sadio Mané]] who collected the ball and scored; Chelsea went on to lose 2–0. Lampard publicly criticized Arrizabalaga, stating that his mistake had cost a goal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54226825|title=Chelsea boss Frank Lampard says Kepa Arrizabalaga needs his support after latest mistake|date=20 September 2020|website=BBC Sport|access-date=21 September 2020|archive-date=28 September 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200928053352/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/54226825|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 24 September, Chelsea signed [[Édouard Mendy]] from [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]], and Arrizabalaga was relegated to the bench.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://talksport.com/football/770391/kepa-arrizabalaga-losing-place-chelsea-edouard-mendy/|title=Kepa Arrizabalaga breaks his silence on losing place in Chelsea team|date=6 October 2020|access-date=7 October 2020|website=talkSPORT|archive-date=10 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201010002822/https://talksport.com/football/770391/kepa-arrizabalaga-losing-place-chelsea-edouard-mendy/|url-status=live}}</ref> He did not feature again until 17 October against [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] where his performance received further criticism in the media as the side drew 3–3.<ref>{{Cite news|last=SNTV|first=Source|date=18 October 2020|title=Chelsea's Lampard defends Kepa after latest mistake against Southampton – video|newspaper=The Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/video/2020/oct/18/chelsea-frank-lampard-defends-kepa-arrizabalaga-mistake-southampton-video|access-date=19 October 2020|issn=0261-3077|archive-date=19 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201019014059/https://www.theguardian.com/football/video/2020/oct/18/chelsea-frank-lampard-defends-kepa-arrizabalaga-mistake-southampton-video|url-status=live}}</ref> On 10 January 2021, Arrizabalaga marked his 100th appearance for the club in a 4–0 home win against [[Morecambe F.C.|Morecambe]] in the fourth round of the FA Cup.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://twitter.com/ChelseaFC/status/1348249712227459078|title=Ready to make it a century of appearances in a Chelsea shirt Congratulations, @kepa_46|date=10 January 2021|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|via=Twitter|access-date=26 January 2021|archive-date=10 January 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210110124657/https://twitter.com/ChelseaFC/status/1348249712227459078|url-status=live}}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=August 2023}}

Arrizabalaga's fortunes turned under the coaching of [[Thomas Tuchel]]. He kept five clean sheets in eight games, all of which came in successive games. He had a save percentage of 89.4% under the German manager, significantly higher than under the previous manager.<ref>{{Cite web |url= https://fbref.com/en/players/28d596a0/matchlogs/2020-2021/keeper/Kepa-Arrizabalaga-Match-Logs |title= Kepa Arrizabalaga 2020–2021 Match Logs |access-date= 26 September 2021 |archive-date= 24 November 2021 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20211124042617/https://fbref.com/en/players/28d596a0/matchlogs/2020-2021/keeper/Kepa-Arrizabalaga-Match-Logs |url-status= live }}</ref> He was named as part of the 25-man squad for the [[2021 UEFA Champions League Final]] on 29 May, and was an unused substitute as Chelsea beat Manchester City 1–0 at the [[Estádio do Dragão]], lifting his second European trophy.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/chelsea-fc-champions-league-final-squad-confirmed-porto-b937637.html|title=Chelsea FC Champions League Final squad confirmed as Blues fly to Porto|date=28 May 2021|work=Evening Standard|access-date=1 June 2021|archive-date=2 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210602215743/https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/chelsea-fc-champions-league-final-squad-confirmed-porto-b937637.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0269-12650cedca55-37515f69768e-1000--report-chelsea-claim-second-title/ |title=Man. City 0–1 Chelsea: Havertz gives Blues second Champions League triumph |publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=29 May 2021 |accessdate=29 May 2021 |archive-date=3 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210603073706/https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0269-12650cedca55-37515f69768e-1000--report-chelsea-claim-second-title/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2021–22: Super Cup win and EFL Cup final defeat====
[[File:Group_photographs_of_Chelsea,_Al_Hilal_SFC_vs_Chelsea_F.C.,_9_February_2022_(Kepa_Arrizabalaga).jpg|thumb|Kepa Arrizabalaga playing for Chelsea in the [[2022 FIFA Club World Cup]].]]
In the [[2021 UEFA Super Cup]] against [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]], Arrizabalaga came on as a substitute in the 119th minute to replace first-choice goalkeeper Mendy. He saved two penalties, including the decisive attempt from Villarreal captain [[Raúl Albiol]], in the shootout as Chelsea won their second Super Cup title.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/58182206|title=Kepa goes from penalty villain to hero|work=BBC Sport|date=11 August 2021|access-date=12 August 2021|archive-date=12 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210812043050/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/58182206|url-status=live}}</ref> The Spaniard got a start against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]], keeping a clean sheet.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/soccer/news/tottenham-vs-chelsea-live-score-highlights-premier-league/eg69nw30bao51we1vz89ch2k9 | title=Tottenham vs. Chelsea result: Thiago Silva, N'Golo Kante and Antonio Rudiger score in London derby win | date=19 September 2021 | access-date=26 September 2021 | archive-date=26 September 2021 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210926050633/https://www.sportingnews.com/us/soccer/news/tottenham-vs-chelsea-live-score-highlights-premier-league/eg69nw30bao51we1vz89ch2k9 | url-status=live }}</ref> Later in the season, Arrizabalaga started only a few matches including an [[2021-22 EFL Cup#Third round|EFL Cup]] third round tie against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], which Chelsea would go on to win 4–3 on penalties after a 1–1 draw. Arrizabalaga made a decisive save against a spot kick from [[Marvelous Nakamba]], leading him to become Chelsea's most successful goalkeeper at saving penalties during shootouts, passing [[Petr Čech]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kepa breaks Chelsea penalty shoot-out record {{!}} Official Site {{!}} Chelsea Football Club|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2021/09/23/kepa-breaks-chelsea-penalty-shoot-out-record|access-date=25 September 2021|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|archive-date=25 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210925032452/https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2021/09/23/kepa-breaks-chelsea-penalty-shoot-out-record|url-status=live}}</ref>

During January 2022, following Mendy’s departure to the [[AFCON]], Arrizabalaga was reinstated to the first team. The Spaniard took his team to the final of the EFL Cup, notably thanks to his quick thinking to trap [[Harry Kane]] offside.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.chelsea-news.co/2022/01/video-big-brain-kepa-catches-kane-out-with-instinctive-offside-trap/ | title=(Video): Big brain Kepa catches Kane out with instinctive offside trap | date=13 January 2022 | access-date=17 February 2022 | archive-date=17 February 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220217001245/https://www.chelsea-news.co/2022/01/video-big-brain-kepa-catches-kane-out-with-instinctive-offside-trap/ | url-status=live }}</ref> He then went on to have another excellent performance in the [[2021 FIFA Club World Cup]] semi-final, as Chelsea went on to win the tournament.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chelsea win FIFA Club World Cup™|url=https://publications.fifa.com/en/annual-report-2022/2022-at-a-glance/fifa-club-world-cup-2021/|website=fifa.com|access-date=3 June 2026}}</ref> On 27 February, in the [[2022 EFL Cup Final|EFL Cup Final]], Arrizabalaga came on in the 120th minute, ready for the [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shootout]]. Despite this, he failed to save a single penalty and was the only player who failed to convert his penalty, blasting his kick over the crossbar as [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] won the shootout 11–10.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chelsea goalkeeper Kepa Arrizabalaga misses decisive penalty as Liverpool wins Carabao Cup after shootout drama |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2022/02/27/football/carabao-cup-final-liverpool-chelsea-spt-intl/index.html |publisher=CNN |date=28 February 2022 |access-date=26 August 2023 |archive-date=26 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230826235611/https://edition.cnn.com/2022/02/27/football/carabao-cup-final-liverpool-chelsea-spt-intl/index.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2022–23: Re-emergence====
In 2022, Chelsea replaced Tuchel with new manager [[Graham Potter]], and also brought in new goalkeeping coach [[Ben Roberts (footballer)|Ben Roberts]]. This coincided with Mendy, who was Tuchel's preferred goalkeeper, being injured and in poor form.<ref name="football.london">{{Cite web|title= Graham Potter facing crucial Chelsea selection decision in first Premier League game in charge|date= 30 September 2022|url= https://www.football.london/chelsea-fc/players/graham-potter-chelsea-premier-league-25146210|website= football.london|access-date= 23 October 2022|archive-date= 23 October 2022|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20221023054755/https://www.football.london/chelsea-fc/players/graham-potter-chelsea-premier-league-25146210|url-status= live}}</ref> Kepa contributed to a draw in Potter's first game with a save to deny [[Benjamin Šeško]], but this was followed by a game cancelation and an international break. Kepa continued in the team in the next game against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]], a 2–1 win. He kept his place in the squad with a run of five consecutive clean sheets, including impressive away displays at [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] and [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]], the latter of which being his 50th for Chelsea.<ref name="weaintgotnohistory.sbnation.com">{{Cite web|title=Kepa Arrizabalaga reaches Chelsea clean sheet milestone in frustrating draw|url=https://weaintgotnohistory.sbnation.com/2022/10/20/23414120/kepa-arrizabalaga-reaches-chelsea-clean-sheet-milestone-in-frustrating-draw|date=20 October 2022|website=weaintgotnohistory.sbnation.com|access-date=23 October 2022|archive-date=23 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221023054755/https://weaintgotnohistory.sbnation.com/platform/amp/2022/10/20/23414120/kepa-arrizabalaga-reaches-chelsea-clean-sheet-milestone-in-frustrating-draw|url-status=live}}</ref> After having gone 10 hours without conceding, Kepa conceded a last-minute header against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]].<ref>{{Cite tweet|user=NizaarKinsella|number=1583886164020596738|title=Good effort by Kepa, he finally concedes after over 10 hours. Ball is barely over the line.}}</ref> Following the turn of the year, he won three back-to-back Man of the Match awards, following clean sheets against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]], Liverpool, and [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Man Of The Match|url=https://www.premierleague.com/man-of-the-match|date=11 April 2023|publisher=Premier League|access-date=11 April 2023|archive-date=7 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230407020221/https://www.premierleague.com/man-of-the-match|url-status=live}}</ref>

Kepa finished the season with the third best save percentage in the league, having also kept out the third most shots based on the [[Expected Goals]] model.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Statistical Leaders – 2022|url=https://scores.nbcsports.com/epl/player_leaders.asp?category=107|accessdate=6 June 2023|website=nbcsports.com|archive-date=6 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606210857/https://scores.nbcsports.com/epl/player_leaders.asp?category=107|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=2022–2023 Premier League Advanced Goalkeeper Stats|url=https://fbref.com/en/comps/9/keepersadv/Premier-League-Stats#all_stats_keeper_adv|accessdate=6 June 2023|website=fbref.com|archive-date=6 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606210856/https://fbref.com/en/comps/9/keepersadv/Premier-League-Stats#all_stats_keeper_adv|url-status=live}}</ref> One of the saves he made in the aforementioned clean sheet at Aston Villa in October won the Premier League Save of the Season award.<ref name="auto">{{cite web|url=https://www.premierleague.com/video/single/3529269?FOOTBALL_CLUBS=4|title=Watch Kepa's 2022/23 Castrol Save of the Season|publisher=Premier League|date=4 June 2023|accessdate=4 June 2023|archive-date=4 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230604121234/https://www.premierleague.com/video/single/3529269?FOOTBALL_CLUBS=4|url-status=live}}</ref>

====2023–24: Loan to Real Madrid====
On 14 August 2023, Real Madrid announced the signing of Kepa from Chelsea on a one-year loan deal.<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 August 2023 |title=Official Announcement: Kepa |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2023/08/14/official-announcement-kepa |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230814094000/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2023/08/14/official-announcement-kepa |archive-date=14 August 2023 |access-date=14 August 2023 |website= |publisher=[[Real Madrid C.F.]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Kepa is a new Real Madrid player |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2023/08/14/kepa-is-a-new-real-madrid-player |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230814095321/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2023/08/14/kepa-is-a-new-real-madrid-player |archive-date=14 August 2023 |access-date=14 August 2023 |website= |publisher=Real Madrid C.F. |language=en}}</ref> The move was initiated in response to a long-term injury sustained by their primary goalkeeper, [[Thibaut Courtois]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 August 2023 |title=Kepa joins Madrid on loan to replace Courtois |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/story/_/id/38189464/chelsea-kepa-joins-real-madrid-loan-replace-courtois |access-date=14 August 2023 |publisher=ESPN |language=en |archive-date=14 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230814095814/https://www.espn.co.uk/football/story/_/id/38189464/chelsea-kepa-joins-real-madrid-loan-replace-courtois |url-status=live }}</ref> The following day, Kepa was unveiled by Real Madrid president [[Florentino Pérez]] at the [[Ciudad Real Madrid]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=15 August 2023 |title=Goalkeeper Kepa says Real Madrid was an easy choice despite offers from other clubs |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/soccer/2023/08/15/kepa-real-madrid-arrizabalaga/b80b4f86-3b6d-11ee-aefd-40c039a855ba_story.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231225173207/https://www.washingtonpost.com/ |archive-date=25 December 2023 |access-date=15 August 2023 |newspaper=[[Washington Post]] |language=en-US |issn=0190-8286}}</ref>

On 25 August 2023, Kepa made his debut for the club in a 1–0 away win over [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]], simultaneously keeping his first clean sheet for [[Carlo Ancelotti]]'s side.<ref>{{cite web |date=25 August 2023 |title=Celta Vigo 0–1 Real Madrid: Jude Bellingham scores late winner |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66623788 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230825233823/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66623788 |archive-date=25 August 2023 |access-date=26 August 2023 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=McGrath |first=Mike |date=2024-04-15 |title=What happened to David de Gea? The Golden Glove winner who cannot find a team |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2024/04/15/david-de-gea-next-club-golden-gloves-winner-man-utd/ |access-date=2024-08-22 |work=[[The Daily Telegraph|The Telegraph]] |language=en-GB |issn=0307-1235 |url-access=subscription}}</ref>

After starting thirteen consecutive matches for Real Madrid, Kepa suffered an adductor injury warming up for the [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League group stage|group]] match against [[SC Braga|Braga]] on 8 November.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/live-blogs/premier-league-news-injury-live-updates/Pqp1T9CT7IUx/|title=Premier League live news: Latest injury updates and build-up to weekend action|date=24 November 2023|website=The Athletic|access-date=16 February 2025}}</ref> After returning from injury against [[Union Berlin]] on 12 December, Kepa rotated with in-form Ukrainian goalkeeper [[Andriy Lunin]], with the latter being selected to start in the [[2024 Supercopa de España]] [[2024 Supercopa de España final|final]] against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] after an error from Kepa resulted in an [[Antonio Rüdiger]] own goal in the semi-final against [[Atlético de Madrid]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5207991/2024/01/17/real-madrid-arrizabalaga-lunin-ancelotti-goalkeepers/|title=Who is Real Madrid's No 1? Kepa Arrizabalaga or Andriy Lunin?|date=17 January 2024|website=The Athletic|access-date=16 February 2025}}</ref> Lunin remained coach [[Carlo Ancelotti]]'s first choice goalkeeper until the return to fitness of Courtois in April 2024.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/article/2024/may/29/the-wall-is-back-thibaut-courtois-champions-league-final-fitness-race-real-madrid-borussia-dortmund|title=The Wall is Back: Thibaut Courtois' Champions League Final Fitness Race|date=29 May 2024|website=The Guardian|access-date=16 February 2025}}</ref> Kepa's final appearance of his loan spell came as a substitute on the last day of the [[2023–24 La Liga|La Liga season]], playing 27 minutes against [[Real Betis]] at the [[Estadio Santiago Bernabéu|Santiago Bernabéu]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://en.as.com/soccer/why-was-thibaut-courtois-substituted-for-real-madrid-is-he-injured-n/|title=Why was Thibaut Courtois substituted for Real Madrid? Is he injured?|website=AS|date=25 May 2024 |access-date=16 February 2025}}</ref>

Kepa returned to Chelsea at the end of the season, having played twenty matches for Real Madrid and winning the [[List of Spanish football champions|La Liga]], [[Supercopa de España]] and [[2023–24 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] titles.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.afcb.co.uk/teams/First%20Team/kepa/|title=Kepa Arrizabalaga – First Team|website=AFC Bournemouth|access-date=16 February 2025}}</ref>

====2024–25: Loan to Bournemouth====
On 29 August 2024, Kepa was loaned out to fellow Premier League club [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]] until the end of the [[2024–25 AFC Bournemouth season|2024–25 season]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/kepa-completes-premier-league-loan-switch-bournemouth |title=Kepa completes Premier League loan switch |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=29 August 2024 |accessdate=29 August 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.afcb.co.uk/news/2024/august/29/kepa-arrizabalaga-joins-on-loan/ |title=Kepa Arrizabalaga joins on loan |publisher=AFC Bournemouth |date=29 August 2024 |accessdate=29 August 2024}}</ref> He replaced [[Neto (footballer, born 1989)|Neto]], who joined [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] on a season-long loan the following day.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c207jv6ej64o|title=Neto completes Gunners loan move|website=BBC Sport|date=30 August 2024|access-date=16 February 2025}}</ref>

He made his debut for Bournemouth in a 3–2 win at [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] on 31 August.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/4213040|title=Everton 2–3 Bournemouth: A timeline of this season's incredible match|date=4 January 2025|website=Premier League|access-date=16 February 2025}}</ref> His first clean sheet for the ''Cherries'' came on 19 October in a 2–0 home win over Arsenal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bournemouthecho.co.uk/sport/24670636.afc-bournemouths-kepa-arrizabalaga-win-arsenal/|title=AFC Bournemouth's Kepa Arrizabalaga stars in win over Arsenal|website=Bournemouth Echo|date=23 October 2024|access-date=16 February 2025}}</ref>

===Arsenal===
On 1 July 2025, Kepa signed for fellow [[Premier League]] club [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] after they reportedly met the £5 million release clause in his Chelsea contract.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/kepa-arrizabalaga-signs-arsenal|title=Kepa Arrizabalaga signs for Arsenal|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=1 July 2025|access-date=1 July 2025}}</ref> He reportedly signed a three-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13381253/kepa-arrizabalaga-transfer-news-arsenal-complete-5m-deal-to-sign-chelsea-goalkeeper|title=Kepa Arrizabalaga transfer news: Arsenal complete £5m deal to sign Chelsea goalkeeper|publisher=Sky Sports|date=1 July 2025|access-date=1 July 2025}}</ref>

Kepa made his competitive debut for Arsenal in an [[EFL Cup]] victory away at [[Port Vale F.C.|Port Vale]], keeping a clean sheet in the process.<ref name="Port Vale 0–2 Arsenal">{{cite web |title=Port Vale 0–2 Arsenal |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2025-Sep-24/port-vale-0-2-arsenal-match-report |website=Arsenal.com |access-date=25 September 2025}}</ref> Kepa made six saves in the following round against [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton]], and kept another clean sheet in the 2–0 win.<ref name="Port Vale 0–2 Arsenal"/>

On 28 January 2026, Kepa made his first [[UEFA Champions League]] appearance for Arsenal, as the ''Gunners'' beat [[FC Kairat]] 3–2 at [[Emirates Stadium]] to make it eight wins out of eight in the [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League#League phase|league phase]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Team news: Havertz starts against Kairat Almaty|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/team-news-havertz-starts-against-kairat-almaty|first=Charlie|last=Peat|website=arsenal.com|date=28 January 2026|access-date=3 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Arsenal 3-2 Kairat Almaty|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Jan-28/arsenal-3-2-kairat-match-report|first=Charlie|last=Peat|website=arsenal.com|date=28 January 2026|access-date=3 June 2026}}</ref>

Kepa started all of Arsenal’s domestic cup games in his first season, as the Gunners reached the quarter-finals of the [[2025–26 FA Cup|FA Cup]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Southampton 2-1 Arsenal|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Apr-04/southampton-arsenal-match-report|first=Charlie|last=Peat|website=arsenal.com|date=4 April 2026|access-date=3 June 2026}}</ref> and the final of the [[2025–26 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]]. In the [[2026 EFL Cup final|EFL Cup final]] on 22 March, Kepa made an error in the lead-up to the tie’s first goal, letting [[Rayan Cherki]]’s cross slip through his hands, which allowed [[Nico O'Reilly]] to head in to the empty goal from close range. Manchester City went on to win the final 2–0.<ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Arsenal 0-2 Manchester City|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-Mar-22/arsenal-0-2-manchester-city-match-report|first=Jonathon|last=Rogers|website=arsenal.com|date=22 March 2026|access-date=3 June 2026}}</ref>

On 24 May, Kepa made his first Premier League appearance for Arsenal in their 2–1 final day win against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] at [[Selhurst Park]], where Arsenal were presented the [[2025–26 Premier League|Premier League]] trophy after the game.<ref>{{cite web|title=Team news: First league starts for Kepa & Norgaard|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/team-news-first-league-starts-kepa-norgaard|first=Jonathon|last=Rogers|website=arsenal.com|date=24 May 2026|access-date=3 June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Report: Crystal Palace 1-2 Arsenal|url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2026-May-24/crystal-palace-1-2-arsenal-match-report|first=Josh|last=James|website=arsenal.com|date=24 May 2026|access-date=3 June 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Kepa Arrizabalaga (6) (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Arrizabalaga with [[Spain national under-19 football team|Spain U19]] in 2012]]

After appearing for [[Spain national under-18 football team|Spain's under-18s]], Arrizabalaga was called up to [[Spain national under-19 football team|the under-19 team]] for [[2012 UEFA European Under-19 Championship|that year]]'s [[UEFA European Under-19 Championship|UEFA European Championship]]. He was the starter during the tournament, as his side were crowned champions;<ref name="U19">{{cite web|title=Spain make it six of the best in Estonia|date=16 July 2012|url=https://www.uefa.com/under19/history/2012/|url-status=live|access-date=11 October 2021|publisher=UEFA|archive-date=30 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211030024215/https://www.uefa.com/under19/history/2012/}}</ref> highlights included a 3–3 semi-final success against [[France national under-19 football team|France]], where he saved two penalties in the shootout.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/under19/news/0250-0c50fbcad2a5-79cf400be761-1000--spain-finally-see-off-france-in-semi-final-shoot-out/|title=Spain finally see off France in semi-final shoot-out|publisher=UEFA|date=12 July 2012|access-date=11 December 2014|archive-date=23 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160123102058/http://www.uefa.com/news/newsid=1840396.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Arrizabalaga missed the [[2013 FIFA U-20 World Cup]] due to injury, being replaced in the [[2013 FIFA U-20 World Cup squads#Spain|tournament squad]] by [[Rubén Yáñez]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sefutbol.com/kepa-arrizabalaga-deja-concentracion-lesion-y-se-perdera-mundial-turquia|title=Kepa deja la concentración por lesión y se pierde el Mundial de Turquía|trans-title=Kepa leaves training camp due to injury and misses World Cup in Turkey|publisher=Royal Spanish Football Federation|language=es|date=7 June 2013|access-date=11 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130611001020/http://www.sefutbol.com/kepa-arrizabalaga-deja-concentracion-lesion-y-se-perdera-mundial-turquia|archive-date=11 June 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 8 November 2013, he was called up to the [[Spain national under-21 football team|under-21 team]], along with Athletic teammate [[Iker Muniain]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=13702&idi=2|title=Under21 Call-up|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=8 November 2013|access-date=11 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131107090108/http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0|archive-date=7 November 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Arrizabalaga was called up to the [[Spain national football team|senior side]] on 22 March 2017 ahead of a [[2018 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|2018 FIFA World Cup qualifier]] against [[Israel national football team|Israel]] and a [[Exhibition game|friendly]] with [[France national football team|France]], as a late replacement for the injured [[Pepe Reina]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.india.com/sports/kepa-arrizabalaga-gets-spain-call-as-pepe-reina-suffers-injury-1950330/|title=Kepa Arrizabalaga gets Spain call as Pepe Reina suffers injury|publisher=India.com|date=22 March 2017|access-date=23 March 2017|archive-date=27 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190327023111/https://www.india.com/sports/kepa-arrizabalaga-gets-spain-call-as-pepe-reina-suffers-injury-1950330/|url-status=live}}</ref> He earned his first [[Cap (sport)|cap]] on 11 November of that year, playing the full 90 minutes in a 5–0 friendly win over [[Costa Rica national football team|Costa Rica]] in [[Málaga]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/90minutes/ct-hoy-silva-nets-brace-spain-thrash-costa-rica-in-friendly-20171111-story.html|title=Silva nets brace, Spain thrash Costa Rica in friendly|newspaper=Chicago Tribune|date=11 November 2017|access-date=12 November 2017|archive-date=27 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190327023120/https://www.chicagotribune.com/90minutes/ct-hoy-silva-nets-brace-spain-thrash-costa-rica-in-friendly-20171111-story.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sefutbol.com/en/match-report-spain-thrash-costa-rica-malaga-5-0-0|title=Match report: Spain thrash Costa Rica in Málaga (5–0)|publisher=Royal Spanish Football Federation|date=11 November 2017|access-date=15 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171116130528/http://www.sefutbol.com/en/match-report-spain-thrash-costa-rica-malaga-5-0-0|archive-date=16 November 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Arrizabalaga was named in Spain's [[2018 FIFA World Cup squads#Spain|23-man squad]] for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]] in Russia,<ref>{{cite web|last=Maston|first=Tom|date=21 May 2018|title=Morata misses out on Spain's 23-man World Cup squad|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/morata-misses-out-on-spain-world-cup-squad/1ub1qz7jod09i1lfvdcy84ea2l|access-date=21 May 2018|website=Goal (website)|publisher=Perform Group|archive-date=9 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190709141140/https://www.goal.com/en/news/morata-misses-out-on-spain-world-cup-squad/1ub1qz7jod09i1lfvdcy84ea2l|url-status=live}}</ref> although he did not play in the tournament.

|url-status=live }}</ref> During his second season with Chelsea, he once again drew criticism over his shot-stopping ability and mistakes, which led to him being dropped by manager [[Frank Lampard]] |url-status=live }}</ref> Arrizabalaga regained his starting position during the FA Cup tie against Liverpool later in the season.<ref name=kepareturn /> However, following more goalkeeping mistakes he was once again dropped for the final league match of the season and the [[2020 FA Cup Final|FA Cup Final]]. He finished the season with the worst save percentage in [[Premier League]] history,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kepa Arrizabalaga Has The Worst Save Percentage In Premier League History|url=https://www.sportbible.com/football/stats-fails-kepa-has-the-worst-save-percentage-in-premier-league-history-20200729|access-date=19 October 2020|website=sportbible.com|archive-date=20 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201020113158/https://www.sportbible.com/football/stats-fails-kepa-has-the-worst-save-percentage-in-premier-league-history-20200729|url-status=live}}</ref> an unwanted record eventually broken by [[Gavin Bazunu]] of Southampton.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2022–2023 Premier League Goalkeeper Stats|url=https://fbref.com/en/comps/9/keepers/Premier-League-Stats#all_stats_keeper|access-date=6 June 2023|website=fbref.com|archive-date=6 June 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606023204/https://fbref.com/en/comps/9/keepers/Premier-League-Stats#all_stats_keeper|url-status=live}}</ref>

During his re-emergence in subsequent seasons under different managers, Arrizabalaga was noted for his good distribution, a skill that would come in handy for English manager [[Graham Potter]] in 2022.<ref name="football.london"/> He has also been praised for his good reflexes and decision making, particularly during a stretch of consecutive clean sheets for Potter.<ref name="weaintgotnohistory.sbnation.com"/>
