'''David Sergio Trezeguet''' ({{IPA|fr|david sɛʁʒjo tʁezəɡɛ|lang}}, {{IPA|es|daˈβið ˈseɾxjo tɾeseˈɣe(t)|lang}}; born 15 October 1977) is a French former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Striker (association football)|striker]]. Trezeguet played in teams like [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]], [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] and [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]], he also was part of the France national team who won the [[1998 FIFA World Cup]] and the [[UEFA Euro 2000|UEFA Euro 2000]], scoring the [[golden goal]] in the [[UEFA Euro 2000 final|final]].

Trezeguet began his career in Argentina with [[Club Atlético Platense]] at the age of eight, progressing through their [[youth system]] to their first team, where he made his debut in the [[Primera División Argentina|Primera División]] in 1994. After one season, he transferred to [[Ligue 1|Division 1]] side [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]], where he would form a striking partnership with international teammate [[Thierry Henry]], winning the league in the [[1996–97 French Division 1|1996–97 season]]. He left the club in 2000, having scored 52 goals in 93 Division 1 appearances and having claimed two [[List of French football champions|Division 1 championships]] and the [[Trophée des champions|1997 Trophée des champions]].

In 2000, Trezeguet signed for [[Serie A]] club [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] for a transfer fee of £20 million. With 24 goals, he was the joint recipient of the ''[[Capocannoniere]]'' award for top scorer as his team won the [[2001–02 Serie A]] title; Trezeguet also scored eight goals in 10 [[2001–02 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] appearances as Juventus reached the second round of the tournament. Despite struggling with injuries the following season, he won another [[2002–03 Serie A|league title]] with the club, and also scored four goals in 10 [[2002–03 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] appearances as Juventus reached the [[2003 UEFA Champions League Final|final]] of the tournament, eventually losing 2–3 on penalties to [[A.C. Milan|Milan]], as Trezeguet missed his spot kick in the resulting shoot-out. Overall, Trezeguet scored 138 goals in 245 league appearances for Juventus, making him the fourth-highest goalscorer in the club's history.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/world-match-centre/news/newsid/178/972/8/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140421050543/http://www.fifa.com/world-match-centre/news/newsid/178/972/8/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=21 April 2014|title=Trezeguet: I'm Argentinian at heart|date=22 October 2012|access-date=20 April 2014|work=FIFA}}</ref> Later in his career he had brief spells in Spain, the United Arab Emirates, Argentina and India.

Born in France where his Argentine father was playing football, Trezeguet grew up in Argentina. At international level, Trezeguet chose to represent the [[France national football team|France national team]]. He scored 34 goals in 71 appearances for France  between 1998 and 2008. He also played for France at [[France national under-18 football team|under–18]], [[France national under-20 football team|under–20]], and [[France national under-21 football team|under–21]] levels.<ref>{{cite web |title=Toutes les sélections françaises de Football depuis 1988<!-- Bot generated title --> |trans-title=All French national football teams since 1988 |url=http://www.rlfoot.fr/index.php?page=http://www.rlfoot.fr/Selections/95-96_18ans_joueurs.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180204000520/http://www.rlfoot.fr/index.php?page=http://www.rlfoot.fr/Selections/95-96_18ans_joueurs.htm |archive-date=4 February 2018 |access-date=15 July 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=1996-1997 : équipe de France 20 ans |trans-title=1996-1997: France U20 team |url=http://www.rlfoot.fr/index.php?page=http://www.rlfoot.fr/Selections/96-97_20ans_joueurs.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180617165301/http://www.rlfoot.fr/index.php?page=http://www.rlfoot.fr/Selections/96-97_20ans_joueurs.htm |archive-date=17 June 2018 |access-date=15 July 2012}}</ref> Trezeguet represented France at the [[1997 FIFA World Youth Championship]], the [[1998 FIFA World Cup]], [[UEFA Euro 2000]], the [[2002 FIFA World Cup|2002 World Cup]], [[UEFA Euro 2004|Euro 2004]] and the [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006 World Cup]] (where he missed his penalty in the [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|shoot-out]] against Italy in the [[2006 FIFA World Cup Final|final]]). Trezeguet is part of the [[FIFA 100]] list of ''125 Greatest living players''. In 2015, he was named one of the [[Golden Foot#Award legends|Golden Foot Award Legends]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.juventus.com/en/news/news/2015/trezeguet-honoured-at-golden-foot-awards.php|title=Trezeguet honoured at Golden Foot Awards|publisher=Juventus.com|date=21 September 2015|access-date=21 September 2015}}</ref>

==Early life==
David Sergio Trezeguet<ref>{{cite web |url=http://actas.rfef.es/actas/RFEF_CmpActa1?cod_primaria=1000144&CodActa=14296 |title=Acta del Partido celebrado el 21 de mayo de 2011, en Alicante |trans-title=Minutes of the Match held on 21 May 2011, in Alicante |publisher=Royal Spanish Football Federation |access-date=16 June 2019 |language=es}}{{dead link|date=May 2026}}</ref> was born on 15 October 1977 in [[Rouen]], Seine-Maritime, France,<ref name="lequipe">{{cite news |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/fiche/david-trezeguet/238654 |title=David Trezeguet |newspaper=L'Équipe |location=Paris |access-date=6 June 2026 |language=fr}}</ref> but grew up in [[Buenos Aires]], Argentina. His father [[Jorge Trezeguet]] was playing football for [[FC Rouen]]. He left the club in 1979 and returned to Argentina with his family.{{citation needed|date=June 2026}} In 1999, David Trezeguet married Beatriz, who is from [[Alicante]], Spain. They have two sons together, Aarón (born 2000) and Noraan (born 2008). They divorced in 2012.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bon anniversaire David Trezeguet ! |trans-title=Happy birthday David Trezeguet! |url=http://www.programme.tv/news/actu/146951-bon-anniversaire-david-trezeguet/ |access-date=21 July 2018 |publisher=Programme.tv |date=15 October 2012 |language=fr}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Platense===
Trezeguet began his career at [[Club Atlético Platense|Platense]] in the [[Argentine Primera División]], where he played his first professional game on 12 June 1994 as a 16-year-old in a 1–1 tie against [[Gimnasia y Esgrima de La Plata|Gimnasia]].<ref name="Trezeguet">{{cite news |title=La increíble historia de Trezeguet |trans-title=The incredible story of Trezeguet |url=http://www.lanacion.com.ar/86361-la-increible-historia-de-trezeguet |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141025215310/http://www.lanacion.com.ar/86361-la-increible-historia-de-trezeguet |archive-date=25 October 2014 |access-date=22 January 2015 |newspaper=La Nación |publisher=Lanacion}}</ref> After just five matches with the team, he moved to play for [[AS Monaco FC|AS Monaco]].<ref name="Trezeguet"/>

===Monaco===
In 1995, he was close to joining [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]], but the deal was cancelled after the two clubs failed to agree a deal. Shortly afterwards, he opted to join Monaco.<ref name="Trezeguet"/> Monaco coach [[Jean Tigana]] was "impressed" by Trezeguet, who scored five goals in trial, signing a deal which saw him earn 15,000 francs a month.<ref>{{cite web |title=Trezeguet est arrivé à Monaco les mains dans les poches |trans-title=Trezeguet arrived in Monaco empty-handed |url=https://www.humanite.fr/1997-12-11_Articles_-Trezeguet-est-arrive-a-Monaco-les-mains-dans-les-poches |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090608004150/http://www.humanite.fr/1997-12-11_Articles_-Trezeguet-est-arrive-a-Monaco-les-mains-dans-les-poches |archive-date=8 June 2009 |access-date=22 January 2015 |work=L'Humanité}}</ref> Trezeguet spent two seasons with Monaco B, having made just nine appearances in total for the club's first team during his first two seasons.<ref>{{NFT player|id=2422|name=David Trezeguet}}</ref> In 1998, Trezeguet scored the fastest ever goal in terms of velocity in [[UEFA Champions League]] history in a quarter-final match against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]. The shot that resulted in a goal was clocked at 97.6 mph (157.3 km/h).{{Citation needed|date=January 2012}} With Monaco, he won [[Ligue 1]] twice and was named [[Trophées UNFP du football#Young Player of the Year|Ligue 1 Young Player of the Year]] in 1998. He scored a total of 60 goals in 113 appearances for the Monégasque club and it was here that he made his name as a potent goalscoring [[Forward (association football)#Centre forward|poacher]].<ref name="Gli eroi in bianconero: David TRÉZÉGUET">{{cite web |author1=Stefano Bedeschi |date=15 October 2013 |title=Gli eroi in bianconero: David TRÉZÉGUET |trans-title=The heroes in black and white: David TREZEGUET |url=http://www.tuttojuve.com/gli-eroi-bianconeri/gli-eroi-in-bianconero-david-trazaguet-66189 |access-date=24 April 2015 |website=tuttojuve.com |language=it}}</ref>

===Juventus===
During his first season with [[Juventus FC|Juventus]], under manager [[Carlo Ancelotti]], Trezeguet managed 14 goals in Serie A, despite being predominantly utilised as a substitute striker, behind [[Filippo Inzaghi]], who started alongside [[Alessandro Del Piero]]. Juventus missed out on the [[2000–01 Serie A|2000–01 Serie A title]] that season, finishing in second place behind [[A.S. Roma|Roma]]. In his second season at the club, under manager [[Marcello Lippi]], he scored 24 league goals in 34 league matches to finish as the [[Capocannoniere|Serie A top goalscorer]], along with [[Dario Hübner]] of [[Piacenza Calcio|Piacenza]], as Juventus won the [[2001–02 Serie A]] title. That same season, he was named [[Serie A Footballer of the Year]] and [[Serie A Foreign Footballer of the Year]], also reaching the final of the [[2001–02 Coppa Italia]]; he also scored eight goals in ten [[2001–02 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] appearances, although the club were eliminated in the second round of the competition. In January 2002, a car carrying Trezeguet and teammates [[Mark Iuliano]], [[Gianluca Zambrotta]] and [[Enzo Maresca]] after a 3–1 win over [[Hellas Verona F.C.|Hellas Verona]], collided with two others; none of the four players were injured in the accident.<ref>{{cite news |title=Trezeguet unharmed after crash |url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/025e-0f905f2c17ca-3f86e290f828-1000--trezeguet-unharmed-after-crash/ |website=[[UEFA]] |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=28 January 2002 |access-date=27 May 2020 }}</ref> 

In his third season, his appearances were limited by injuries, although he still helped Juventus to defend the [[2002–03 Serie A|Serie A title]], also winning the [[2002 Supercoppa Italiana]] and scoring four goals in ten appearances as Juventus reached the [[2003 UEFA Champions League Final]]. In the final, Trezeguet was one of three Juventus players to have their penalty saved by [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] keeper [[Dida (footballer, born 1973)|Dida]], as Juventus lost 3–2 on penalty kicks after a 0–0 draw. This would be the closest Trezeguet ever got to winning the Champions League. During the 2003–04 season, Trezeguet helped the team to win a second consecutive [[2003 Supercoppa Italiana|Supercoppa Italiana]] title, scoring a goal during the match, also reaching another [[2004 Coppa Italia Final|Coppa Italia final]], although their [[2003–04 UEFA Champions League|European]] and [[2003–04 Serie A|domestic league campaigns]] would be less successful, despite his 16 goals in Serie A that season, as the club finished the league in third place. In 2004, [[Brazil national football team|Brazilian]] legend [[Pelé]] included Trezeguet in the [[FIFA 100]], his list of the 125 greatest living footballers.<ref name="Gli eroi in bianconero: David TRÉZÉGUET" /> 

[[File:David Trezeguet.jpg|thumb|180px|Trezeguet playing for Juventus in 2007.]]

Although Trezeguet won the [[2004–05 Serie A]] and [[2005–06 Serie A]] titles with Juventus, scoring 23 league goals in the 2005–06 season, Juventus were caught in the [[2006 Italian football scandal]] that rocked Italian football, and along with Milan, [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]], [[S.S. Lazio|Lazio]], and [[Reggina Calcio|Reggina]] were accused of [[match fixing]]. While the players had no part in the scandal, Juventus were subsequently stripped of their [[2004–05 Serie A|2004–05]] and [[2005–06 Serie A|2005–06]] titles, relegated to [[Serie B]], and were to start the [[2006–07 Serie B|2006–07 season]] with a deficit of 30 points, eventually reduced to nine points on appeal. Following the enforced relegation to Serie B, the club lost several of its star players, including [[Fabio Cannavaro]] to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], [[Gianluca Zambrotta]] to [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], [[Adrian Mutu]] to Fiorentina, and [[Zlatan Ibrahimović]] to [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]]. Trezeguet's compatriots [[Lilian Thuram]] and [[Patrick Vieira]] also left Juventus, for Barcelona and Inter, respectively. Manager [[Fabio Capello]] defected to Real Madrid and former Juventus legend and Trezeguet's former [[France national football team|France]] teammate and captain, [[Didier Deschamps]], was appointed the new manager of Juve. As one of the club's star players, Trezeguet was heavily linked to a move away from Juventus, but he ultimately stayed with the ''Bianconeri'' to help the club return to Italy's top flight.<ref name="Gli eroi in bianconero: David TRÉZÉGUET"/>

On 16 September 2006, before Juventus' [[2006–07 Serie B|Serie B]] match against [[Vicenza Calcio|Vicenza]], he was awarded a commemorative plate in recognition of his 125 career goals. On 19 May 2007, Juventus achieved promotion to Serie A after a 5–1 win over [[A.C. Arezzo|Arezzo]]. Trezeguet scored the fifth goal which made the promotion mathematically possible. Despite the successful return to Serie A, and an eventual Serie B title, the season was not without controversy. After scoring a goal in Juventus' final match of the [[2006–07 Serie B]] season against [[Spezia Calcio|Spezia]], Trezeguet made a gesture toward the club president, making a number 15 with his fingers – the number of goals he scored throughout the Serie B season – which was followed by a hand gesture which, in [[Italian language|Italian]], means "I'm out of here".{{Citation needed|date=November 2008}} Juventus, however, announced on 25 June 2007 that Trezeguet had renewed his contract until 2011.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://home.skysports.com/list.aspx?hlid=473852&CPID=21&clid=128&lid=8&title=Trez+extends+Juve+deal |title=Trez extends Juve deal |first=Peter |last=O'Rourke |author-link= |publisher=[[Sky Sports]] |date=26 June 2007 |access-date=28 June 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070701150114/http://home.skysports.com/list.aspx?hlid=473852&CPID=21&clid=128&lid=8&title=Trez+extends+Juve+deal |archive-date=1 July 2007 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=442024&cc=5901 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130103043243/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=442024&cc=5901 |url-status=dead |archive-date=3 January 2013 |title=Trezeguet claims he snubbed United and Liverpool |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=25 June 2007 |access-date=25 June 2007 }}</ref>

During the [[2007–08 Serie A]] season, Trezeguet scored 20 league goals and was second only to teammate and club captain Alessandro Del Piero for the ''Capocannoniere''. Juventus finished third in the league to qualify for the Champions League after missing out on the tournament for two consecutive seasons.<ref name="Gli eroi in bianconero: David TRÉZÉGUET"/> In the [[2008–09 Serie A|2008–09 season]], Trezeguet sustained a groin injury that kept him out for most of the season. Trezeguet finally made his return on 4 February 2009 against [[S.S.C. Napoli|Napoli]] in the [[Coppa Italia]] and had a goal controversially disallowed. Nevertheless, he was one of the players who scored in the penalty shootout, which Juventus won 4–3. Trezeguet would shortly get his first goal of 2009 in a 2–0 win against [[U.S. Città di Palermo|Palermo]] in late February – a match where he received the [[Captain (association football)|captaincy]] for the first time in his professional career. Juventus finished the season in second place in the league, also reaching the semi-finals of the [[2008–09 Coppa Italia|Coppa Italia]] and the round of 16 of the [[2008–09 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]].<ref name="Gli eroi in bianconero: David TRÉZÉGUET" /> On 9 December 2009, Trezeguet scored his 168th goal for Juventus in a 4–1 defeat to [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] in the [[2009–10 UEFA Champions League]], making him the club's highest-ever foreign goalscorer, surpassing [[Omar Sívori]]'s total of 167 goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/1716/champions-league/2009/12/08/1674979/juventus-1-4-bayern-munich-germans-record-sensational-victory-in-|title=Juventus 1-4 Bayern Munich: Germans Record Sensational Victory in Turin To Qualify For Last 16 - Goal.com|date=8 December 2009}}</ref> At the end of the [[2009–10 Serie A|2009–10 season]], Trezeguet ranked fourth among Juventus' all-time top goalscorers with 171 goals. In August 2010, he was released from the remaining 12 months of his contract by Juventus.<ref name="football.uk.reuters.com">[http://football.uk.reuters.com/leagues/seriea/news/2010/08/28/LDE67R091.php Trezeguet released by Juve and set to join Hercules] {{webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20120525083047/http://football.uk.reuters.com/leagues/seriea/news/2010/08/28/LDE67R091.php |date=25 May 2012 }} Reuters</ref>

===Hércules===
[[File:Trezeguet presentación Hércules 3.jpg|thumb|150px|left|Trezeguet during his presentation as a player of [[Hércules CF|Hércules]] in August 2010.]]

On 28 August 2010, Trezeguet completed his move to newly promoted [[La Liga]] team [[Hércules CF|Hércules]] on a two-year deal; the club is based in his then wife's hometown.<ref>{{cite news|title=Trezeguet joins Hercules|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/12961/6344748/trezeguet-joins-hercules|access-date=15 October 2017|publisher=Sky Sports|date=28 August 2010}}</ref> He made his debut on 11 September in a 2–0 surprise victory against defending champions Barcelona.<ref>{{cite news|title=FC Barcelona 0 - 3 Hércules|url=http://actas.rfef.es/actas/RFEF_CmpPartido?cod_primaria=1000144&CodActa=11582|publisher=rfef|date=11 September 2010|access-date=14 February 2012|archive-date=9 July 2012|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120709053619/http://actas.rfef.es/actas/RFEF_CmpPartido?cod_primaria=1000144&CodActa=11582|url-status=dead}}</ref> Eight days later, Trezeguet scored his first goal for the club, a conversion from the penalty spot in a 2–1 loss against [[Valencia CF|Valencia]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Hércules 1 - 2 Valencia CF|url=http://actas.rfef.es/actas/RFEF_CmpPartido?cod_primaria=1000144&CodActa=11643|publisher=rfef|date=19 September 2010|access-date=14 February 2012|archive-date=26 July 2012|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120726091553/http://actas.rfef.es/actas/RFEF_CmpPartido?cod_primaria=1000144&CodActa=11643|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was unable to prevent relegation for the side, however, and left the club at the start of the summer of 2011.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11800_7062111,00.html | publisher=Sky Sports | title=Trezeguet eyes France return – Sky Sports – Football – Ligue 1 – News}}</ref> Trezeguet made 31 league appearances and scored 12 goals, making him the club's top goalscorer for the season.{{citation needed|date=January 2021}}

===Baniyas===
On 30 August 2011, Trezeguet completed his move to [[UAE Pro-League]] side [[Baniyas SC|Baniyas]] on a one-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/950867/david-trezeguet-completes-move-to-uae%27s-bani-yas?cc=5901|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130102221756/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/950867/david-trezeguet-completes-move-to-uae's-bani-yas?cc=5901|url-status=dead|archive-date=2 January 2013|title=Trezeguet completes Bani Yas move}}</ref> On 21 November 2011, his contract was mutually terminated due to an injury which had kept him sidelined for most of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/994059/david-trezeguet-leaves-uae-side-bani-yas-after-two-games?cc=5739|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120717211051/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/994059/david-trezeguet-leaves-uae-side-bani-yas-after-two-games?cc=5739|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 July 2012|title=Trezeguet quits UAE after two games|date=8 December 2011|work=ESPN Soccernet|access-date=8 December 2011}}</ref> Trezeguet only appeared in the opening league match and a fixture in the [[Etisalat Emirates Cup]] for Baniyas.<ref>{{Cite web |last=AP |date=2011-11-20 |title=Trezeguet terminates contract with UAE's Baniyas - Sports - FootBall - Emirates24{{!}}7 |url=https://www.emirates247.com/sports/football/trezeguet-terminates-contract-with-uae-s-baniyas-2011-11-20-1.429188 |access-date=2025-06-22 |website=www.emirates247.com |language=en}}</ref>

===River Plate===
On 19 December 2011, Trezeguet moved to [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]] in Argentina on a three-year contract, shortly after the club was relegated to the [[Primera B Nacional|Argentine second division]] for the first time in its history.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Olé |title=Hay goleador por tres años |trans-title=There's a goal scorer for three years |url=https://www.ole.com.ar/river-plate/futbol/goleador-anos_0_613138772.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170814095752/https://www.ole.com.ar/river-plate/futbol/goleador-anos_0_613138772.html |archive-date=2017-08-14 |access-date=2025-06-22}}</ref> Trezeguet, a childhood fan of River, having grown up in [[Buenos Aires]],<ref>{{Cite web |author1=App |date=2011-12-15 |title=Trezeguet on verge of joining River Plate |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/trezeguet-verge-joining-river-plate |access-date=2025-06-22 |website=FourFourTwo |language=en}}</ref> spoke of it as his dream move, saying, "Being here is a unique feeling, motivated by everything that River represents."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Lawrence |first=Amy |date=2012-01-05 |title=David Trezeguet's move to River Plate shows money does not rule all |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2012/jan/05/david-trezeguet-river-plate |access-date=2025-06-22 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> On 19 January 2012, Trezeguet scored in his first appearance for River Plate in a friendly match against [[Racing Club de Avellaneda|Racing Club]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Still got it: David Trezeguet scores on River Plate debut |url=http://www.101greatgoals.com/still-got-it-david-trezeguet-scores-on-river-plate-debut/135814/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120123045642/http://www.101greatgoals.com/still-got-it-david-trezeguet-scores-on-river-plate-debut/135814/ |archive-date=2012-01-23 |access-date=2025-06-22 |language=en-US}}</ref> He made his official debut on 13 February 2012. He played his first match at [[Estadio Monumental Antonio Vespucio Liberti|Estadio Monumental]] the following week and scored his first official goal for River Plate after coming on as a substitute. On 26 February, he scored his second official goal, again after coming on as a substitute in the second half. 

Trezeguet scored his first double in River Plate on 10 March against [[Defensa y Justicia]], the first goal giving River Plate a 2–1 lead, while the second one tying the match 3–3. In the next match, he played for the first time in the starting XI and scored in the first half to maintain his excellent scoring form for River Plate. Trezeguet would later state that the adrenaline he gets while playing for River surpasses any other moment he experienced in his career, including winning the [[1998 FIFA World Cup]] with France and scoring the [[golden goal]] in the finals of [[UEFA Euro 2000]]: "I am feeling things that I have never felt before. Not with Juventus, nor with Monaco and not even at international level with France. Being a River fan and seeing the passion that exists in this team, all the people and all the pressure, I have more adrenaline than ever before."<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Week in Quotes |url=http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/news/newsid=1600593.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120319222747/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/news/newsid=1600593.html |archive-date=2012-03-19 |access-date=2025-06-22 |website=www.fifa.com |language=en}}</ref> In the final match of the championship against [[Almirante Brown Partido|Almirante Brown]] on 23 June, Trezeguet secured victory by scoring both of River's goals to seal promotion back to [[Argentine Primera División|the top flight]]; Trezeguet also missed a penalty during the match.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/columns/story/_/id/1116916/kelly:-david-trezeguet-helps-river-plate-wake-from-their-nightmare?cc=5901|title=River Plate wake from their nightmare|access-date=29 June 2012|archive-date=2 January 2013|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130102205214/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/columns/story/_/id/1116916/kelly:-david-trezeguet-helps-river-plate-wake-from-their-nightmare?cc=5901|url-status=dead}}</ref> Trezeguet finished his first season at River Plate with 13 goals in 18 matches, finishing sixth behind the team's top goalscorer, [[Fernando Cavenaghi]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://blogs.independent.co.uk/2012/06/27/david-trezeguets-return-to-river-plate-ranks-as-the-greatest-comeback-in-a-season-full-of-them/ |title=David Trezeguet's return to River Plate ranks as the Greatest Comeback in a Season full of them |location=London |work=The Independent |first=Charles |last=Reynolds |date=27 June 2012 |access-date=5 February 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150919041047/http://blogs.independent.co.uk/2012/06/27/david-trezeguets-return-to-river-plate-ranks-as-the-greatest-comeback-in-a-season-full-of-them/ |archive-date=19 September 2015}}</ref> On 9 September 2012, he scored his first goal in the [[Argentine Primera División|Primera División Argentina]] against [[Newell's Old Boys]] in a 3–3 draw. He would later score against [[Estudiantes de La Plata]] in a 1–0 win and also against [[Colón de Santa Fe|Colón]] in a 2–1 victory.{{citation needed|date=January 2021}} Despite being a key member of the River Plate squad which returned to the Primera División Argentina, it was decided in June by head coach and manager [[Ramón Díaz]] that he would no longer be a part of the team's squad, despite fan protests.{{citation needed|date=January 2021}}

=== Newell's Old Boys ===
On 22 July 2013, Trezeguet joined [[Newell's Old Boys]] on a one-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/sports/2013-07/23/c_132563982.htm|title=Trezeguet joins Argentina's Newell's Old Boys|access-date=15 February 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304125647/http://news.xinhuanet.com/english/sports/2013-07/23/c_132563982.htm|archive-date=4 March 2016}}</ref> He made his debut on 18 August coming on as a substitute for [[Víctor Aquino]] in the 73rd minute, his side drew 0–0 with [[Belgrano de Córdoba|Belgrano]]. In his second game for the NOB he scored his first goal in the 90th minute against [[Atlético Rafaela|Atletico Rafaela]], they won the game 2–0. On 1 November, Trezeguet scored his 300th career goal against [[Colón de Santa Fe|Colón]] and 11 minutes later followed up with his 301st career goal and subsequently the equaliser, drawing 2–2 on the night.{{citation needed|date=January 2021}}

=== Pune City ===
On 30 July 2014, Trezeguet signed for [[Indian Super League]] club [[FC Pune City|Pune City]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Indian Super League: Ex-Juventus and Monaco striker David Trezeguet joins FC Pune City|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11095/9400553/indian-super-league-ex-juventus-and-monaco-striker-david-trezeguet-joins-fc-pune-city|publisher=Sky Sports|access-date=31 July 2014}}</ref> Trezeguet scored his first goal for the club against [[FC Goa|Goa]], by the virtue of which, his franchise registered their first victory in the tournament.<ref>{{cite web|title=David Trezeguet on target as FC Pune City register maiden win.|url=http://indianexpress.com/article/sports/football/indian-super-league-david-trezeguet-on-target-as-fc-pune-city-register-maiden-win/|work=The Indian Express|date=26 October 2014|access-date=22 January 2015}}</ref> This was followed by his second and his last goal in ISL, which came in a defeat against [[Kerala Blasters FC|Kerala Blasters]].<ref>{{cite web|title=David James pleased to register first win for Kerala Blasters|url=http://www.goal.com/en-india/news/7083/isl/2014/10/31/5650631/david-james-pleased-to-register-first-win-for-kerala|publisher=Goal|access-date=22 January 2015}}</ref> On 20 January 2015, it was announced that Trezeguet had retired as a player and was set to join the Juventus management team. It was confirmed by Trezeguet's agent.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/frances-euro-2000-hero-trezeguet-retires-221730119--sow.html|title=France's Euro 2000 hero Trezeguet retires|date=20 January 2015|work=Yahoo Sports|access-date=15 February 2015|archive-date=21 January 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150121135817/http://sports.yahoo.com/news/frances-euro-2000-hero-trezeguet-retires-221730119--sow.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==International career==
As a French–Argentine, Trezeguet was eligible to play for France or [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/3277/la-liga/2011/03/05/2380313/david-trezeguet-chose-to-play-for-france-not-argentina|title=David Trezeguet chose to play for France not Argentina because he wanted to win - Thierry Henry|website=Goal.com|access-date=21 April 2021}}</ref> Trezeguet first competed internationally in the French youth squad alongside [[Thierry Henry]], [[Willy Sagnol]], and [[William Gallas]], and played in the [[1997 FIFA World Youth Championship]]. In the lead up to the [[1998 FIFA World Cup|1998 World Cup]] in France, [[Aimé Jacquet]] gave younger players such as David Trezeguet, Henry and [[Patrick Vieira]] the chance to display their talent, and all three were eventually selected for the World Cup ahead of experienced French players including [[David Ginola]]. Trezeguet scored one goal in the tournament, in the 4–0 win over [[Saudi Arabia national football team|Saudi Arabia]], as France went on to win the World Cup, defeating [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] 3–0 in the final at the [[Stade de France]]. Two years later France were crowned European champions after defeating [[Italy national football team|Italy]] 2–1 in the [[UEFA Euro 2000 Final|Euro 2000 final]], courtesy of Trezeguet's [[golden goal]] in [[Overtime (sports)#Association football|extra time]] from a [[Robert Pires]] assist.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Lacey |first=David |date=2000-07-03 |title=France add Europe to the world |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2000/jul/03/euro2000.sport4 |access-date=2025-06-22 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

Although ranked first in the world, France was not very successful in the [[2002 FIFA World Cup|2002 World Cup]], being eliminated in the group stage without scoring a single goal, despite David Trezeguet, Thierry Henry and [[Djibril Cissé]] being the top goalscorers respectively in [[2001–02 Serie A|Serie A]], the [[2001–02 FA Premier League|Premier League]] and [[2001–02 French Division 1|Ligue 1]] that season. The failure was then followed up by a quarter-final exit at [[UEFA Euro 2004|Euro 2004]] at the hands of unheralded [[Greece national football team|Greece]] with Trezeguet scoring just one goal in the tournament in a 2–2 draw against [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]]. However, with the return of [[Zinedine Zidane]] from brief international retirement, France would go on to reach the final of the [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006 World Cup]]. Throughout the tournament, Trezeguet found himself out of place in [[Raymond Domenech]]'s [[Formation (association football)#4.E2.80.932.E2.80.933.E2.80.931|4–2–3–1 formation]] which only used one striker – a position allocated to Thierry Henry. On 9 July 2006, Trezeguet took part in the final, coming on as a substitute. The match, against Italy, went to a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shootout]] and Trezeguet was the only player from either team to miss his penalty, his shot hitting the crossbar, as Italy won 5–3 on penalty kicks after a 1–1 draw.<ref name="Gli eroi in bianconero: David TRÉZÉGUET"/>

On 19 October 2007, Trezeguet threatened to quit France after being overlooked for two [[UEFA Euro 2008 qualifying|Euro 2008 qualifying]] matches by coach [[Raymond Domenech]].<ref name="retirementthreat">{{cite web|url=http://uk.eurosport.yahoo.com/19102007/58/euro-2008-trezeguet-threatens-quit-france.html|title=Yahoo UK & Ireland - Sports News - Live Scores - Results|website=Yahoo Sports}}</ref> On 26 March 2008, Trezeguet was selected for a friendly against [[England national football team|England]] to replace the injured [[Karim Benzema]], which would turn out to be his last appearance for France as he was subsequently not chosen for the squad that competed in [[UEFA Euro 2008|Euro 2008]].<ref>{{cite web|title=France drop Trezeguet from Euro 2008 squad |url=http://fourfourtwo.com/news/restofeurope/9438/default.aspx |publisher=FourFourTwo |access-date=19 May 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110711021556/http://fourfourtwo.com/news/restofeurope/9438/default.aspx |archive-date=11 July 2011}}</ref> On 9 July 2008, he announced his retirement from international football, finishing his France career ranked third among France's all-time top goalscorers with 34 goals from 71 caps.<ref>{{cite news| title= Trezeguet quits France scene|url =http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11854_3797840,00.html|publisher=Sky Sports|access-date=8 July 2008|date=9 July 2008}}</ref> He cited "the awful Euro 2008 and the reappointment of the coach" being the main reasons for this decision, and also added "I see football differently from how they see it in France. Euro 2008 was very negative, but what annoys me more is that Domenech is staying."<ref>{{cite web|title=Trezeguet retires from international football |url=http://fourfourtwo.com/news/restofeurope/12953/default.aspx |publisher=FourFourTwo |access-date=9 July 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110711021604/http://fourfourtwo.com/news/restofeurope/12953/default.aspx |archive-date=11 July 2011}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Trezeguet was a prolific, complete, and talented striker, who was gifted with pace, power, instinct, and an eye for goal.<ref name="Gli eroi in bianconero: David TRÉZÉGUET"/><ref name="BBC Profile">{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/euro2000/teams/france/squad/747335.stm|title=Euro 2000 Profile: David Trezeguet|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=12 September 2014}}</ref> A highly opportunistic player, he was excellent at taking advantage of chances and loose balls in the area, and was an accurate striker of the ball, known for his clinical finishing, as well as his ability to score with few touches, due to his ability to shoot first time and finish off chances from close range, even when off-balance or from awkward positions. He was capable of scoring with either foot, despite being naturally right footed, as well as with his head, and excelled in the air; he was also known for having a penchant for scoring acrobatic goals. Although he wasn't particularly known for his link-up play, he was highly regarded for his positional sense, anticipation, reactions, offensive movement, and his ability to lose his markers, as well as for his skill at playing with his back to goal, courtesy of his solid technique.<ref name="Gli eroi in bianconero: David TRÉZÉGUET"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://juventinologo.blogspot.ca/2009/05/david-trezeguet-scheda-tecnica.html|title=David Trezeguet – Scheda tecnica|access-date=12 September 2014}}</ref><ref name="Trezeguet's ruthless finishing">{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.us/blog/tactics-and-analysis/67/post/2259406/david-trezeguets-ruthless-and-clinical-finishing-made-him-a-memorable-striker|title=David Trezeguet's ruthless finishing made him a memorable striker|publisher=ESPN FC|author1=Michael Cox|date=22 January 2015|access-date=6 March 2017}}</ref> Considered to be one of the best strikers of his generation, due to the number of goals he scored for Juventus he gained the nicknames: ''Cobra'', ''Trezegol'', and ''Re David'' (King David, in Italian), during his time at the club. Despite his ability, his playing time throughout his career was often limited by injuries.<ref name="Gli eroi in bianconero: David TRÉZÉGUET"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.juveatrestelle.it/opinioni/david-trezeguet-mito/|title=Il mito di Re David|trans-title=The myth of King David|website=juveatrestelle.it|language=it|access-date=12 September 2014|archive-date=12 September 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140912192955/http://www.juveatrestelle.it/opinioni/david-trezeguet-mito/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=15 October 2016 |title=Auguri, Trezegol! |trans-title=Happy birthday, Trezegol! |url=http://www.juventus.com/it/news/news/2016/auguri--trezegol--.php |access-date=6 February 2017 |publisher=juventus.com |language=it}}</ref>

'''Ricardo Andrade Quaresma Bernardo''' {{post-nominals|post-noms=[[Order of Merit (Portugal)|ComM]]}} ({{IPA|pt|ʁiˈkaɾðu kwɐˈɾɛʒmɐ}}; born 26 September 1983) is a Portuguese former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Winger (association football)|winger]]. He began his career at [[Sporting CP]] and went on to play for [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], [[Inter Milan]], [[FC Porto|Porto]] (twice),{{cite web|url=http://www.fcporto.pt/pt/noticias/Pages/quaresma-antes-besiktas-fcp-201117.aspx?p_page=8|title=Quaresma: "Serei do FC Porto até morrer"|trans-title=Quaresma: "I will be FC Porto until I die"|publisher=FC Porto|language=pt|date=20 November 2017|access-date=6 August 2018}} [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], [[Beşiktaş J.K.|Beşiktaş]] (twice), [[Shabab Al-Ahli Club|Al-Ahli Dubai]], [[Kasımpaşa S.K.|Kasımpaşa]] and [[Vitória S.C.|Vitória de Guimarães]]. Regarded as a mercurial talent, his tricks, including the ''[[rabona]]'' and ''[[trivela]]'' (a bending shot with the outside of his right foot) made him a popular figure among fans around the world.{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2016/07/04/portugal-vs-wales-euro-2016-ricardo-quaresma-emerges-from-cristi/|title=Ricardo Quaresma emerges from Cristiano Ronaldo's shadow to help duo to brink of career-defining glory|newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|last=Liew|first=Jonathan|date=4 July 2016|access-date=10 August 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2016/07/04/portugal-vs-wales-euro-2016-ricardo-quaresma-emerges-from-cristi/|archive-date=12 January 2022|url-access=subscription}}{{cbignore}}{{cite web|url=https://backpagefootball.com/wonderkids-of-the-past-ricardo-quaresma-edition/126709/|title=Wonderkids of the past – Ricardo Quaresma edition|publisher=Back Page Football|last=Adade|first=Aaron|date=10 November 2020|access-date=4 July 2024}} A [[Portugal national football team|Portugal international]] for 15 years, Quaresma won 80 [[Cap (sport)|caps]] and played at three [[UEFA European Championship|European Championships]], including the victorious [[UEFA Euro 2016|Euro 2016]], and the [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018 World Cup]]. ==Club career== ===Sporting CP=== Quaresma was born in [[Lisbon]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com.br/futebol/artigo/_/id/4462314/rei-da-trivela-quaresma-fracassou-no-barcelona-e-sofreu-com-preconceito-por-ser-cigano|title=Rei da trivela, Quaresma fracassou no Barcelona e sofreu com preconceito por ser cigano|trans-title=King of ''trivela'', Quaresma failed at Barcelona and fought prejudice for being gypsy|publisher=[[ESPN (Brazil)|ESPN]]|last1=De Laurentiis|first1=Francisco|last2=Bianchini|first2=Vladimir|language=pt|date=25 June 2018|access-date=14 March 2022}} A trainee at [[Sporting CP]]'s famed [[Sporting CP Youth Academy|academy]], the 17-year-old was promoted to the first team by manager [[László Bölöni]] before the start of the [[2001–02 Primeira Liga|2001–02 season]], playing 28 [[Primeira Liga]] matches and scoring three goals as the team won [[Double (association football)|the double]].{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/019f-0ea6cc8cb753-8aea14778d26-1000--porto-seal-quaresma-deal/|title=Porto seal Quaresma deal|publisher=UEFA|date=6 July 2004|access-date=29 June 2018}}{{cite news|url=https://observador.pt/2016/06/13/quaresma-as-sete-vidas-de-um-desalinhado-com-pernas-tortas/|title=Quaresma. As sete (ou oito, ou nove) vidas de um desalinhado com pernas tortas|trans-title=Quaresma. The seven (or eight, or nine) lives of a misfit with crooked legs|newspaper=[[Observador]]|last=Palma|first=Tiago|language=pt|date=13 June 2016|access-date=6 August 2018}} Under the same coach, Quaresma scored five times in the league [[2002–03 Primeira Liga|the following campaign]], but the team could only finish in third place. ===Barcelona=== In 2003, Quaresma was sold to [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] for a reported €6 million fee and the loan of [[Fábio Rochemback]].{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11833_2271059,00.html|title=Barca seal Quaresma swoop|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|last=Higham|first=Paul|date=18 July 2003|access-date=3 February 2010}} In his [[2003–04 La Liga|first year]] in [[La Liga]] he made ten starts and 12 [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] appearances, scoring in the 5–0 home rout of [[Albacete Balompié|Albacete]].{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/diario/2004/02/02/deportes/1075676407_850215.html|title=Una goleada balsámica|trans-title=Therapeutic rout|newspaper=[[El País]]|last=Piñol|first=Àngels|language=es|date=2 February 2004|access-date=6 August 2018}} Quaresma injured his right foot in the final weeks of the season, forcing him to miss both the [[2004 UEFA European Under-21 Championship]] and [[UEFA Euro 2004]] tournaments.{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/page/LatestNews/0,,10268~1543209,00.html|title=Quaresma signs on loan|publisher=Chelsea F.C|date=2 February 2009|access-date=24 April 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090226105649/http://www.chelseafc.com/page/LatestNews/0,,10268~1543209,00.html|archive-date=26 February 2009}} Shortly after, he announced his refusal to play for the Spanish club as long as manager [[Frank Rijkaard]] was in charge.{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11833/2302511/Quaresma-in-Barca-quit-threat|title=Quaresma in Barca quit threat|publisher=Sky Sports|last=Acedo|first=Francisco|date=2004|access-date=24 April 2013}} ===Porto=== Quaresma signed for [[FC Porto|Porto]] in the summer of 2004 as [[Deco]] moved in the opposite direction for a fee of €15 million plus Quaresma, valued at €6 million.{{cite web|url=http://www.fcporto.pt/IncFCP/PDF/Investor_Relations/FactosRelevantes/VendaDeco060704.pdf|title=Facto relevante|trans-title=Relevant fact|publisher=FC Porto|language=pt|date=6 July 2004|access-date=17 April 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101205172904/http://www.fcporto.pt/IncFCP/PDF/Investor_Relations/FactosRelevantes/VendaDeco060704.pdf|archive-date=5 December 2010}} He started [[2004–05 Primeira Liga|the campaign]] on a high note by scoring the only goal in a [[2004 Supertaça Cândido de Oliveira|win]] against [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] in the [[Supertaça Cândido de Oliveira]],{{cite news|url=https://www.record.pt/futebol/futebol-nacional/liga-nos/fc-porto/detalhe/fc-porto-benfica-1-0-dragao-ganha-primeira-taca-de-futebol-de-praia.html|title=FC Porto-Benfica, 1–0: Dragão ganha primeira taça de futebol de praia|trans-title=FC Porto-Benfica, 1–0: Dragon wins first beach soccer cup|newspaper=[[Record (Portuguese newspaper)|Record]]|language=pt|date=21 August 2004|access-date=6 August 2018}} and also scored in the [[2004 UEFA Super Cup|2–1 loss]] to [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] in the [[UEFA Super Cup]].{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/uefasupercup/history/season=2004/|title=2004: Baraja brings joy to Valencia|publisher=UEFA|access-date=21 May 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140521214557/http://www.uefa.com/uefasupercup/history/season=2004/|archive-date=21 May 2014}} Quaresma scored five goals in his first year at the [[Estádio do Dragão]], and the club finished as runners-up. In the [[Penalty shootout (association football)|penalty shootout]] defeat of [[Once Caldas]] in the [[Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)|Intercontinental Cup]], he successfully converted his attempt in an [[2004 Intercontinental Cup|8–7 victory]] in [[Yokohama]].{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablest/toyota04.html|title=Intercontinental Club Cup 2004|publisher=[[RSSSF]]|last=Leme de Arruda|first=Marcelo|access-date=6 August 2018}} ===Inter Milan=== [[File:Ricardo Quaresma - Inter Mailand (1).jpg|thumb|upright|Quaresma with Inter in August 2009]] On 1 September 2008, Quaresma signed for Italian champions [[Inter Milan]] in a cash/player exchange fee of €18.6 million, with youngster [[Pelé (footballer, born 1987)|Pelé]] joining Porto.{{cite web|url=http://inter.it/aas/news/reader?N=29697&L=en|title=Quaresma completes Inter switch|publisher=Inter Milan|date=1 September 2008|access-date=1 September 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090108190631/http://inter.it/aas/news/reader?N=29697&L=en|archive-date=8 January 2009}} He scored in his first [[Serie A]] match against [[Catania FC|Catania]], with one of his trademark ''[[trivela]]s'' in a 2–1 home win.{{cite news|url=http://www.repubblica.it/2008/09/sezioni/sport/calcio/serie_a/giornata-2/inter-catania/inter-catania.html|title=Prima vittoria dell'Inter di {{sic|nolink=y|Muorinho}} – Sconfitto il Catania, ma che fatica|trans-title=First win for Mourinho's Inter – Catania beaten, but what an effort|newspaper=[[La Repubblica]]|language=it|date=13 September 2008|access-date=6 August 2018}} However, he found opportunities in the starting XI limited, as coach [[José Mourinho]] stated:
"He is a great talent, but the joy I have at seeing the way [[Zlatan Ibrahimović|Ibra]] works for and with the team I do not yet have with Quaresma. He will have to learn, otherwise he won't play, and I am sure he'll change and become more tactically disciplined. He likes kicking the ball with the outside of his foot, but if you ask me about him in a few months' time, we'll be talking about a different Quaresma."{{cite web|url=http://www.inter.it/aas/news/reader?N=30099&L=en|title=Mourinho: A deserved victory|publisher=Inter Milan|date=22 October 2008|access-date=23 October 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121012092450/http://www.inter.it/aas/news/reader?N=30099&L=en|archive-date=12 October 2012}}{{cite web|url=http://www.portugoal.net/index.php/more-inter-milan-news/335-mourinho-issues-quaresma-warning|title=Mourinho fires warning to Quaresma|publisher=PortuGOAL|date=20 October 2008|access-date=23 October 2008}}
At the end of [[2008–09 Serie A|the season]], Quaresma was given the [[Bidone d'oro]] award for the worst footballer in the Italian top division.{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/columns/story?id=601467&cc=3436|title=Rafa writes off Reds, Ronaldo a 'traitor'|publisher=[[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]]|last=Raynor|first=Dominic|date=12 December 2008|access-date=9 September 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120714052745/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/columns/story?id=601467&cc=3436|archive-date=14 July 2012}} On 2 February 2009, [[Transfer window|transfer deadline day]], he signed on loan for [[Premier League]] club [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] until 30 June, making his first appearance five days later in a 0–0 home draw with [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]].{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/7867071.stm|title=Chelsea 0–0 Hull|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|last=Hassan|first=Nabil|date=7 February 2009|access-date=24 April 2013}} On 7 March, he provided [[Assist (association football)|the cross]] for [[Alex (footballer, born June 1982)|Alex]] to score against [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]] in the [[2008–09 FA Cup|sixth round]] of the [[FA Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/fa_cup/7910378.stm|title=Coventry 0–2 Chelsea|publisher=BBC Sport|last=Bevan|first=Chris|date=7 March 2009|access-date=24 April 2013}} After a disappointing start at the [[San Siro]], he said his move had restored his confidence, and he further stated "When I was at Inter, I wasn't feeling very confident. I wasn't playing well and wasn't happy, I already feel more confident here at Chelsea. It has brought the joy back for me, which I didn't have at Inter."{{cite web|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/1603857|title=The Thursday Interview: Ricardo Quaresma|publisher=Chelsea F.C|date=26 March 2009|access-date=24 April 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130424154847/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/1603857|archive-date=24 April 2013}} Having returned to Inter{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2009/may/27/ricardo-quaresma-wants-internazionale-return|title=Ricardo Quaresma pledges future to Internazionale|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=27 May 2009|access-date=29 June 2018}} despite attempts made by the club to offload him,{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/10/italy/2009/09/07/1485677/ricardo-quaresma-vows-to-win-over-inter-fans|title=Ricardo Quaresma vows to win over Inter fans|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|last=Masiello|first=Vince|date=7 September 2009|access-date=20 October 2009}} Quaresma inherited the number 7 shirt following the retirement of his compatriot [[Luís Figo]].{{cite web|url=http://goal.com/en/news/10/italy/2009/07/10/1374872/jose-mourinho-to-give-ricardo-quaresma-second-inter-chance|title=Jose Mourinho to give Ricardo Quaresma second Inter 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140521223118/http://www.goal.com/en/news/10/italy/2009/07/10/1374872/jose-mourinho-to-give-ricardo-quaresma-second-inter-chance|archive-date=21 May 2014}} However, after the arrival of [[Goran Pandev]] he did not feature much in Mourinho's plans as the team went on to win [[Treble (association football)|the treble]], making 11 appearances in the league without scoring.{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=292116&cc=5739&league=ITA.COPPA_ITALIA|title=Inter claim first gong of the treble|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=6 May News]]|last=Abbasher|first=Yasir|date=29 May 2013|access-date=7 October 2013}} ===Return to Porto=== Quaresma returned to Porto on 1 January 2014, where over 10,000 fans greeted him in training.{{cite web|url=http://www.fcporto.pt/pt/noticias/Pages/Ricardo-Quaresma-%C3%89-nesta-casa-que-me-sinto-feliz.aspx?p_page=1|title=Quaresma: "É nesta casa que me sinto feliz"|trans-title=Quaresma: "This is the [[2013–14 UEFA Europa League knockout phase#Round of 32|Europa League's round of 32]] on 20 February (2–2 home draw),{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0212-0e88e2a821ed-cbc52955b647-1000--eintracht-stun-porto-with-dramatic-comeback/?iv=true|title=Eintracht stun Porto with dramatic '''Claudemir Jerônimo Barreto''' (born 27 March 1981),<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.spiegel.de/sport/fussball/0,1518,700034,00.html | title = Ich will einfach nur spielen | trans-title = I just want to play | language = de |work=Der Spiegel | date = 12 June 2010 | access-date =17 June 2010}}</ref> known as '''Cacau''' ({{IPA|pt|kaˈkaw}}, {{IPA|de|kaˈkaʊ|lang}};<ref>{{Cite web |date=21 November 2020 |title=Cacau über seine Jugend, sein Leben in Deutschland und Rassismus im Fußball {{!}} deep und deutlich |trans-title=Cacau about his youth, his life in Germany and racism in football {{!}} deep and clear |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oYs7xjfJaiY&t=19s |access-date=17 December 2024 |website=[[YouTube]] |publisher=[[ARD (broadcaster)|ARD]] |language=German}}</ref>), is a former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Striker (association football)|striker]]. Born in Brazil, he represented [[Germany]] at international level.

Cacau received [[German nationality law|German citizenship]] in February 2009 and made his international debut in May that year in a friendly match against [[China national football team|China]]. He was in the Germany national team at the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/players/player=312546/profile.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100610215419/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/players/player=312546/profile.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=10 June 2010|title=19 Cacau|work=[[FIFA]]|access-date=13 June 2010}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Early career===
Cacau's career in Germany started with fifth-division side [[SV Türkgücü-Ataspor München|Türkgücü München]] in the 1999–2000 season, after which he went on to join [[1. FC Nürnberg]]'s [[1. FC Nürnberg II|reserve team]]. Following his good performances with the reserves, he was given his [[Bundesliga]] debut against [[F.C. Hansa Rostock|Hansa Rostock]] on 18 November 2001. In only his second Bundesliga match, against [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] on 8 December 2001, he scored two goals in Nürnberg's 4–2 defeat. He finished his first Bundesliga season with 6 goals in 17 appearances, but failed to repeat the success the following season, when he only scored 2 goals in 27 appearances and Nürnberg were relegated.

===VfB Stuttgart===
[[file:Cacau 2011 VfB Stuttgart.jpg|thumb|Cacau with Stuttgart in 2011]]
Having already signed a contract with [[VfB Stuttgart]] in January 2003, Cacau joined the club for the 2003–04 season. In his first season with Stuttgart, he also made four appearances in the [[UEFA Champions League]] In the 2004–05 season, he scored 12 Bundesliga goals and was the club's second-best goalscorer. In the first part of the same season, he also had a successful [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]] campaign, netting three consecutive braces in Stuttgart's first three matches of the competition.

After an unsuccessful season in 2005–06, in which he only scored four Bundesliga goals for Stuttgart, he went on to be one of the key players in the club's run to the league title in 2007, once again becoming their second-best goalscorer with 13 goals, crucially netting both goals in their 2–0 win over [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] as well as the winning goal in a 3–2 away win over [[VfL Bochum]] in the final five rounds of the season. During the 2006–07 season, he also helped Stuttgart reach the final of the [[DFB-Pokal]], scoring five goals in six matches, including the opening goal in the final against his former team Nürnberg. However, he was sent off 11 minutes later and Stuttgart went on to lose the final 3–2 after extra time.

In the 2007–08 season, he made further five appearances for Stuttgart in the UEFA Champions League and also scored his first goal in the competition, netting the equaliser in a 3–2 win over [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]]. He also helped the club finish sixth in the Bundesliga, netting 9 goals in 27 appearances during the season.<ref>{{Cite web | url = https://www.rsssf.org/players/cacaudata.html | title = CACAU Claudemir Jerônimo Barreto - Matches and Goals in Bundesliga | first = Matthias | last = Arnhold | date = 1 December 2016 | access-date = 1 December 2016 | publisher = [[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|RSSSF]]}}</ref> In 2008–09, he scored 7 Bundesliga goals in 25 league matches, helping Stuttgart to finish third in the league.

On 20 February 2010, Cacau scored four goals in a 5–1 victory in an away game against [[1. FC Köln]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=273014&cc=5739|title=FC Cologne 1–5 VfB Stuttgart|date=20 February 2010|work=[[ESPN]]|access-date=23 February 2010|archive-date=21 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121021224113/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=273014&cc=5739|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 30 April, Cacau scored his final goal of the season in a 2–1 win away at [[TSG 1899 Hoffenheim|1899 Hoffenheim]]. This brought his tally to eight Bundesliga goals on the campaign. Following this, on 1 May 2010 Cacau extended his contract with VfB Stuttgart until the summer of 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://vfb.de/archiv/en/aktuell/news/2009/36415.php|title=Cacau staying at VfB|access-date=1 May 2010|date=1 May 2010|publisher=[[VfB Stuttgart]]|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110816155017/http://www.vfb.de/archiv/en/aktuell/news/2009/36415.php|archive-date=16 August 2011}}</ref>

Cacau started the 2011–12 Bundesliga campaign in good form, scoring on a header against [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]] on 6 August helping his side to a 3–0 win.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://soccernet.espn.go.com/gamecast?id=321039&cc=5901 | title = VfB Stuttgart 3–0 Schalke 04 | publisher = ESPN Soccernet | date = 6 August 2011 | access-date = 6 August 2011 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20121026130946/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/gamecast?id=321039&cc=5901 | archive-date = 26 October 2012 | df = dmy-all }}</ref> He was called up to the German squad for their game against his native [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] the following Wednesday.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.goal.com/en/news/15/germany/2011/08/04/2604630/real-madrids-mesut-ozil-sami-khedira-left-out-as-ilkay | title = Real Madrid's Mesut Ozil & Sami Khedira left out as Ilkay Gundogan included in Germany squad to face Brazil | date = 4 August 2011 | access-date = 6 August 2011 | publisher = goal.com}}</ref>

On 22 March 2013, Cacau took a contract option which extended his contract with Stuttgart until June 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vfb.de/en/aktuell/meldungen/news/2013/cacau-vertragsverlaengerung-option-vfb-stuttgart/page/2180-1-1-.html|title=Cacau signs on for a further year|access-date=22 March 2013|date=22 March 2013|publisher=[[VfB Stuttgart]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304002437/http://www.vfb.de/en/aktuell/meldungen/news/2013/cacau-vertragsverlaengerung-option-vfb-stuttgart/page/2180-1-1-.html|archive-date=4 March 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Cerezo Osaka===
On 11 August 2014, Cacau transferred to [[Cerezo Osaka]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.cerezo.co.jp/news_detail.asp?c_idx=10013972&contents_code=100100100 | archive-url = https://archive.today/20140811103204/http://www.cerezo.co.jp/news_detail.asp?c_idx=10013972&contents_code=100100100 | url-status = dead | archive-date = 11 August 2014 | script-title = ja:カカウ選手と契約合意のお知らせ | date = 11 August 2014 | access-date = 11 August 2014 | work = cerezo.co.jp | publisher = Cerezo Osaka | language = ja }}</ref> On 9 June 2015, he was released from his contract.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.cerezo.co.jp/news/2015-06-09-3/ | script-title=ja:カカウ選手との契約について | date = 9 June 2015 | access-date = 9 June 2015 | work = cerezo.co.jp | publisher = Cerezo Osaka | language= ja}}</ref>

===VfB Stuttgart II===
On 1 February 2016, Cacau returned to Stuttgart and joined [[VfB Stuttgart II]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vfb.de/de/aktuell/meldungen/news/2016/cacau/page/11087-1-3-.html|title=Cacau spielt für den VfB II|access-date=1 February 2016|date=1 February 2016|publisher=[[VfB Stuttgart]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160201171331/http://www.vfb.de/de/aktuell/meldungen/news/2016/cacau/page/11087-1-3-.html|archive-date=1 February 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Retirement===
Cacau announced his retirement from professional football on 11 October 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/news/detail/cacau-ein-neuer-lebensabschnitt-beginnt-155423/|title=Cacau: "Ein neuer Lebensabschnitt beginnt"|access-date=11 October 2016|date=11 October 2016|publisher=dfb.de}}</ref>

==International career==
[[file:Cacau 2011.jpg|thumb|Cacau with Germany in 2011]]
Although Cacau was born in Brazil, he was never called up by the [[Brazil national football team|Brazil national team]].

In February 2009, he became eligible to play for [[Germany national football team|Germany]] after he acquired a German passport<ref name="German citizen">{{cite web|url=http://vfb.de/archiv/en/aktuell/news/2008/29328.php|title=Dual-Nationality for Cacau|date=3 February 2009|access-date=3 February 2009|work=[[VfB Stuttgart]]|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110816155028/http://www.vfb.de/archiv/en/aktuell/news/2008/29328.php|archive-date=16 August 2011}}</ref> having lived and played in Germany for over eight years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/mm/document/affederation/federation/01/24/fifastatuten2009_e.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090823155308/http://www.fifa.com/mm/document/affederation/federation/01/24/fifastatuten2009_e.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=23 August 2009|title=FIFA Status (2009 Edition): REGULATIONS GOVERNING THE APPLICATION OF THE STATUTES Article 17|work=[[FIFA]]|access-date=24 August 2009}}</ref>

On 19 May 2009, Cacau was called up to the Germany national team's coach [[Joachim Löw]] for their friendly matches against [[China national football team|China]] and the [[United Arab Emirates national football team|United Arab Emirates]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=500016&tx_dfbnews_pi1%91showUid%93=18304&tx_dfbnews_pi4%91cat%93=62|title=Four newcomers for Asia-trip|access-date=18 May 2009|date=19 May 2009|work=[[German Football Association|DFB]]}}</ref> He made his international debut on 29 May 2009 in Germany's 1–1 draw against China, playing 27 minutes as a substitute for [[Mario Gómez]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/intligen/intwettbewerbe/spielpaarungsbericht/object/888218/|title=China trotzt dem DFB-Team|language=de|work=[[Kicker (sports magazine)|kicker]]|access-date=29 May 2009|date=29 May 2009}}</ref> He also appeared in Germany's 7–2 win against the UAE four days later, playing the entire second half as a substitute for [[Lukas Podolski]] and providing an assist for Mario Gómez's third and Germany's fifth goal of the match just over a minute into the second half.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/nationalelf/laenderspiele/spielpaarungsbericht/object/888219/liga/1830/saison/2009/naviindex/1|title=Gomez ist wieder da – Neuer überzeugt voll und June 2009}}</ref> He opened his account with the Germany national team, scoring a [[Brace (sports)#In other fields|brace]] in a 3–0 win over [[Malta national football team|Malta]] on 13 May 2010.<ref>{{Cite web | url = https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/cacau-intl.html | title = CACAU Claudemir Jerônimo Barreto - Goals in International Matches | first = Matthias | last = Arnhold | date = 1 December 2016 | access-date = 1 December 2016 | publisher = [[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|RSSSF]]}}</ref> He scored his first International goal for Germany in the group stage of the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]] on 13 June 2010, coming on as a substitute against [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia]], and scoring in 1:52 to make it 4–0.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/world_cup_2010/matches/match_08/default.stm|title=Germany 4–0 Australia|date= 13 June 2010|work=BBC Sport |first=Sam|last=Lyon|access-date =23 June 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Germany vs Aust: As it happened |url=http://tvnz.co.nz/2010-fifa-world-cup-news/germany-vs-aust-happened-3585987|work=[[TVNZ]]|agency=Reuters |access-date=18 October In the third-place World Cup game, Germany faced [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]] on 10 July. He started for his German side but was eventually substituted out as Germany defeated Uruguay 3–2, taking third place at the World Cup.

Cacau remained regular for Germany in the [[UEFA Euro 2012 qualifying|qualifications for UEFA Euro 2012]] in Poland and Ukraine. After making the 30-man preliminary squad, Cacau did not make Germany's 23-man [[UEFA Euro 2012|Euro 2012]] squad.

==Personal life==
Cacau's brother [[Vlademir Jeronimo Barreto]], more commonly known as simply Vlademir, is also a former footballer and lives in [[Mogi das Cruzes]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.spvgg-unterhaching.de/news/news_detail.php3?news_id=934|title=Wolfgang Frank testet Bundesligatauglichkeit von Cacaus Bruder|access-date=12 May 2009|date=27 May 2003|language=de|work=[[SpVgg Unterhaching]]|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071012085642/http://www.spvgg-unterhaching.de/news/news_detail.php3?news_id=934|archive-date=12 October 2007}}</ref>

Cacau is a committed [[Christians|Christian]] and says his faith is a big part of his life.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/newsid=2237830/index.html?intcmp=newsreader_news_box_2|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203005209/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/newsid=2237830/index.html?intcmp=newsreader_news_box_2|url-status=dead|archive-date=3 December 2013|title=Cacau: Football can set things in motion|work=[[FIFA]]|access-date=2 December 2013|date=2 December 2013}}</ref>

Since his [[naturalization]] as a German citizen in early 2009, Cacau's nickname at VfB Stuttgart (and later also at the Germany national team) is [[Helmut]]. This nickname was given to him by his Swiss Stuttgart teammate at the time, [[Ludovic Magnin]], who stated that, as a German, Cacau should also have a proper German name.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bild.de/BILD/sport/fussball-wm-2010-suedafrika/2010/06/21/deutsch/helmut-cacau/ist-der-stuttgarter-stuermer.html|title=Stuttgarts Stürmer Cacau wird bei der Nationalmannschaft Helmut genannt|access-date=14 August 2010|date=21 June 2010|language=de|work=bild.de|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100716125406/http://www.bild.de/BILD/sport/fussball-wm-2010-suedafrika/2010/06/21/deutsch/helmut-cacau/ist-der-stuttgarter-stuermer.html|archive-date=16 July 2010}}</ref>

In 2021, he featured in ''{{ill|Schwarze Adler|de|Schwarze Adler (2021)}}'', a documentary detailing the experiences of Black players in German professional football.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Bülau |first1=Maximilian |title=Von Mbom bis Kostedde: Das sind die Protagonisten der Amazon-Dokumentation "Schwarze Adler" |url=https://www.hna.de/sport/fussball/rassismus-macht-sehr-muede-90466018.html |access-date=18 June 2021 |work=HNA |date=19 April 2021 |language=de}}</ref>
