'''Christian Dannemann Eriksen''' ({{IPA|da|ˈkʰʁɛs.tjæn ˈeː.ʁɛg.sən}}; born 14 February 1992) is a Danish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for the [[Denmark national football team|Denmark national team]].

Eriksen began his senior club career at age 18 in 2010, playing for [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]], where he won three [[Eredivisie]] titles and the [[KNVB Cup]]. In 2013, Eriksen signed for [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] in a [[Transfer (association football)|transfer]] worth £11 million (€12.45 million), where he was twice named the club's Player of the Year, was voted into the [[PFA Team of the Year (2010s)#Premier League 9|2017–18 PFA Team of the Year]], and later also reached the [[2019 UEFA Champions League final]]. In 2020, Eriksen joined [[Inter Milan]] in a transfer worth €19.7 million (£16.9 million), and won a [[Serie A]] title.

During a [[UEFA Euro 2020]] match on 12 June 2021, [[UEFA Euro 2020#Collapse of Christian Eriksen|Eriksen collapsed]] on the pitch after suffering a [[cardiac arrest]]; he was given [[cardiopulmonary resuscitation|CPR]] and was later fitted with an [[implantable cardioverter-defibrillator|ICD]]. He returned to football eight months later with a move to Premier League club [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]], before transferring to [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] the following season. At United, he won an [[FA Cup]] and [[EFL Cup]] before departing the club after the 2024–25 season. He collapsed again during an international friendly against [[Ukraine national football team|Ukraine]] on 7 June 2026.

Eriksen made his senior international debut for Denmark in 2010 at age 18, and is currently the nation's [[Denmark national football team#Most appearances|record appearance holder]] with more than 150 [[Cap (sport)|caps]], including appearing in six major tournaments; he was also the youngest player at the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]].{{refn|group=nb|Eriksen is the youngest Danish player to have reached 100 caps at 28 years and 243 days.<ref>{{cite web |date=14 October 2020 |title=Eriksen og Kjær slår rekord mod england |url=https://acefootball.com/da/fodboldnyheder/eriksen-og-kjaer-slaar-rekord-mod-england/ |access-date=15 October 2020 |publisher=Ace Football}}</ref> The first Dane was [[Morten Olsen]] in 1989.<ref>{{cite web |title=Landstræner Morten Olsen bliver den første mand på kloden til at opnå 100 landskampe først som spiller siden som træner |url=https://www.tipsbladet.dk/nyhed/danmark/morten-olsen-saetter-verdensrekord |access-date=15 October 2020 |website=Tipsbladet |date=7 October 2009 }}</ref>}}

==Club career==
===Middelfart and Odense===
Born in [[Middelfart]], Denmark, Eriksen followed in the footsteps of his father Thomas when he started playing football in the academy of local side, [[Middelfart Boldklub|Middelfart G&BK]].<ref name=":1">{{cite news |last=Ames |first=Nick |date=15 June 2018 |title=The making of Christian Eriksen: from the start he was a 'wow' footballer |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/jun/15/christian-eriksen-making-of-denmark-tottenham |access-date=25 June 2018 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> Eriksen's father was also one of the coaches at the time and in 2004 they helped the youth side finish unbeaten in the local youth championship for the third time in a period of four years.<ref name=":1" />

The following year, he joined [[Odense Boldklub|OB]], who competed in the Danish youth championships, and within a year had helped the club to an age-group title. It was at OB that Eriksen first began showing signs of his technical ability, with his dribbling and free-kick techniques lauded by then-coach, Tonny Hermansen.<ref name=":1" /> His form at youth level attracted the attention of a number of major European clubs, including the likes of [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] and [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]].<ref>{{cite web |date=4 April 2008 |title=FC Barcelona kigger på OB-talent |url=https://www.bt.dk/sport/fc-barcelona-kigger-paa-ob-talent |access-date=21 January 2010 |website=[[B.T. (tabloid)|BT]] |language=da}}</ref> Eriksen ultimately underwent trials with both clubs as well as [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] and [[A.C. Milan|Milan]], but finally decided to move to [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]], stating, "My first step should not be too big. I knew that playing in the Netherlands would be very good for my development. Then Ajax arrived and that was a fantastic option."<ref>{{cite web |title=Update: 'Tomasson gaat zich richten op trainersloopbaan' |url=https://www.voetbalzone.nl/nieuws/doc/139277 |date=28 February 2011 |access-date=28 February 2011 |website=Voetbalzone |language=nl}}</ref>

===Ajax===
====2008–2010: Youth and first-team squad====
On 17 October 2008, Eriksen signed a two-and-a-half-year contract with [[Amsterdam]]-based club, [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]].<ref name="uefastarlet">{{Cite web |date=17 October 2008 |title=Danish starlet Eriksen opts for Ajax |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/01d2-0e7019606ceb-0f297a211d88-1000--danish-starlet-eriksen-opts-for-ajax/ |access-date=19 April 2010 |publisher=UEFA}}</ref> The [[transfer fee]] received by OB was estimated at €1 million (£847,199) while Middelfart also received a sum of €35 000 which they later used to construct a football pitch.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Nigel |date=23 February 2010 |title=Wenger eager to sign up Ajax starlet after Bergkamp's endorsemsent |url=http://www.sport.co.uk/news/Football/34596/_Wenger_eager_to_sign_up_Ajax_starlet_after_Bergkamps_endorsemsent_.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100226101000/http://www.sport.co.uk/news/Football/34596/_Wenger_eager_to_sign_up_Ajax_starlet_after_Bergkamps_endorsemsent_.aspx |archive-date=26 February 2010 |access-date=2 June 2010 |website=Sport.co.uk}}</ref><ref name=":1" /> He worked his way through the youth teams at Ajax and was promoted to the [[first team (association football)|first team]] squad in January 2010, where he was given the number 51 shirt.<ref name=uefafaith/> Later that month, he made his first team debut in a 1–1 [[Eredivisie]] with [[NAC Breda]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=17 January 2010 |title=Eriksen fik debut i Ajax |url=http://www.dr.dk/Sporten/Fodbold/2010/01/17/160629.htm |access-date=17 January 2010 |publisher=[[DR (broadcaster)|Danmarks Radio]] |language=da}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Mannion |first=Damian |date=10 February 2011 |title=Christian Eriksen – The player every club wants: Ten things you need to know |url=https://talksport.com/uncategorized/100325/christian-eriksen-player-every-club-wants-ten-things-you-need-know/ |access-date=25 June 2018 |work=TalkSport |language=en-gb}}</ref> 

He scored his first goal for Ajax on 25 March in a 6–0 win over [[Go Ahead Eagles]] in the [[KNVB Cup|Dutch Cup]] and extended his contract with the club the following month.<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 April 2010 |title=Supertalent Eriksen tot 2014 bij Ajax |url=http://www.elfvoetbal.nl/Overige/181292/Supertalent-Eriksen-tot-2014-bij-Ajax |access-date=11 March 2018 |publisher=ELF Voetbal |language=nl}}</ref> On 6 May, he played in the second match of the final of the [[2009–10 KNVB Cup|2009–10 Dutch Cup]] as Ajax beat [[Feyenoord]] 4–1, prevailing 6–1 on aggregate.<ref name="2010cup">{{Cite web |date=6 May 2010 |title=Report: Feyenoord Rotterdam vs Ajax Amsterdam – Dutch Cup |url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=291558&cc=5739 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100508052455/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=291558&cc=5739 |archive-date=8 May 2010 |access-date=2 June 2010 |publisher=ESPN Soccernet}}</ref> At the end of his first professional season with the club, Eriksen had played 21 competitive matches, scoring one goal, and had made his international debut for Denmark.<ref name="SW">{{Cite web |title=C. Eriksen: Summary |url=https://uk.soccerway.com/players/christian-eriksen/95871/ |access-date=24 April 2019 |website=Soccerway |publisher=Perform Group |archive-date=5 September 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200905110323/https://uk.soccerway.com/players/christian-eriksen/95871/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="debut" /> Eriksen's form throughout the campaign earned praise from manager [[Martin Jol]] who compared him to former youth products [[Wesley Sneijder]] and [[Rafael van der Vaart]] as well as Danish legend, [[Michael Laudrup]] for his reading of the game in the traditional [[Playmaker|number 10 role]].<ref name="uefafaith">{{Cite news |date=13 March 2010 |title=Eriksen puts faith in Ajax way by Berend Scholten |publisher=UEFA |url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/01e3-0f85f38f890d-1604a6c5a997-1000--eriksen-puts-faith-in-ajax-way/|access-date=2026-05-10}}</ref>

====2010–2013: Breakthrough years====
[[File:EriksenAjax2.jpg|thumb|Eriksen (right) playing for [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] in 2011]]
Eriksen took the number eight jersey ahead of the following campaign and began the [[2010–11 Eredivisie|2010–11 season]] well, scoring his first Ajax league goal on 29 August 2010 in an away victory over [[De Graafschap]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=19 July 2010 |title=Ajax maakt rugnummers bekend |language=nl |work=Het Parool |url=https://www.parool.nl/parool/nl/13/AJAX/article/detail/305683/2010/07/16/Ajax-maakt-rugnummers-bekend.dhtml |url-status=dead |access-date=20 July 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110611094050/https://www.parool.nl/parool/nl/13/AJAX/article/detail/305683/2010/07/16/Ajax-maakt-rugnummers-bekend.dhtml |archive-date= 2011-06-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=29 August 2010 |title=De Graafschap vs. Ajax |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2010/08/29/netherlands/eredivisie/bv-de-graafschap/afc-ajax/941442/ |access-date=11 February 2011 |website=Soccerway}}</ref> Over the course of the next few months, he scored his first home goal at the [[Amsterdam Arena]], in a 3–0 Cup victory over [[SC Veendam|BV Veendam]], and his first European goal, in a 3–0 [[UEFA Europa League]] win over [[R.S.C. Anderlecht|Anderlecht]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=11 November 2010 |title=Ajax vs. Veendam |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2010/11/11/netherlands/knvb-beker/afc-ajax/veendam-1894/1038712/ |access-date=11 February 2011 |website=Soccerway}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=17 February 2011 |title=Ruthless Ajax make Anderlecht pay the penalty |url=http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/matches/season%3D2011/round%3D2000129/match%3D2003770/postmatch/report/index.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110221015729/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/matches/season%3D2011/round%3D2000129/match%3D2003770/postmatch/report/index.html |archive-date= 2011-02-21|access-date=6 June 2011 |publisher=UEFA}}</ref> 

In between the milestone goals, Eriksen was also named [[Danish Football Player of the Year#Danish Football Association's award|Danish Talent of the Year]].<ref name="autogenerated1">{{Cite web |last=Darfelt |first=Rikke |date=7 December 2010 |title=Christian Eriksen er Årets Talent 2010 |url=http://www.dr.dk/Sporten/Fodbold/Landsholdet/2010/12/07/215702.htm |access-date=11 February 2011 |publisher=Danmarks Radio |language=da}}</ref> His growing capabilities as the team's playmaker saw him become an undisputed starter in the side and he helped Ajax to their first [[2010–11 Eredivisie|Eredivisie title]] in seven years. At the end of the season he was named Ajax's [[List of AFC Ajax records and statistics#AFC Ajax prize winners|Talent of the Year]].<ref name="ajaxtalent">{{Cite web |date=15 May 2011 |title=Stekelenburg Ajacied van het Jaar, Christian Eriksen Talent van het Jaar |url=http://www.ajax.nl/Nieuws/Nieuwsarchief/Nieuws-artikel/Stekelenburg-Ajacied-van-het-Jaar.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110822224308/http://www.ajax.nl/Nieuws/Nieuwsarchief/Nieuws-artikel/Stekelenburg-Ajacied-van-het-Jaar.htm |archive-date=22 August 2011 |access-date=6 June 2011 |publisher=AFC Ajax |language=nl}}</ref> His form throughout the campaign also earned him the [[Dutch Football Talent of the Year]] award which saw him become only the second Danish player to win the award since [[Jon Dahl Tomasson]] in 1996. [[Johan Cruyff]], whose panel selected Eriksen for the award, described Eriksen as a typical product of the Danish school and added to previous comparisons between him and [[Brian Laudrup|Brian]] and Michael Laudrup.<ref name="talented">{{Cite web |last=Scholten |first=Berend |date=23 May 2011 |title=Janssen named Netherlands' finest |url=http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/news/newsid=1634341.html#janssen+voted+eredivisies+best |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110526024045/http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/news/newsid=1634341.html#janssen+voted+eredivisies+best |url-status=dead |archive-date=26 May 2011 |access-date=6 June 2011 |publisher=UEFA}}</ref>

On 18 October 2011, Eriksen scored his first goal in the [[UEFA Champions League]] when Ajax beat [[GNK Dinamo Zagreb|Dinamo Zagreb]] 2–0 in the [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League group stage|group stage]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Greene |first=Laura |title=Christian Eriksen to Liverpool: Tracking the Evolution of the Rumour |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1642569-christian-eriksen-to-liverpool-tracking-the-evolution-of-the-rumour |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241215004634/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1642569 |date=17 May 2013 |archive-date=15 December 2024 |access-date=25 June 2018 |work=Bleacher Report |url-status=live |language=en-US}}</ref> In the return fixture the following month, he provided assists to teammates [[Gregory van der Wiel]] and [[Siem de Jong]] as Ajax recorded a 4–0 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 November 2011 |title=Stylish Ajax eliminate Dinamo |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0254-0d7d47422419-3635d22c2812-1000--stylish-ajax-eliminate-dinamo/ |publisher=UEFA}}</ref> Five days later he was named [[Danish Football Player of the Year]] in recognition of his role in helping Ajax to the league title the season before and in Denmark's successful [[UEFA Euro 2012]] qualification campaign.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bruun |first=Peter |date=8 November 2011 |title=Eriksen and Pedersen honoured in Denmark |url=http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=den/news/newsid=1714527.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111112000430/http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=den/news/newsid=1714527.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=12 November 2011 |publisher=UEFA}}</ref> Eriksen continued to impress for Ajax and his strong contribution, both in terms of goal and assist returns, helped the club to a second consecutive league title.<ref>{{Cite news |date=11 May 2012 |title=Goal.com's Eredivisie Team of the Season: Vertonghen, Eriksen & Dost make the cut |publisher=Goal |url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/2601/features/2012/05/11/3095096/goalcoms-eredivisie-team-of-the-season-vertonghen-eriksen |access-date=25 June 2018}}</ref>

Eriksen and Ajax repeated the feat in the [[2012–13 Eredivisie|2012–13 season]] following which he opted not to renew his contract with the club. With only one year remaining on his current contract, Eriksen was permitted to search for a new club and he agreed terms with [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] in England. Eriksen departed Ajax having made 162 appearances across all competitions and scored 32 goals. Along with his league success, he had also featured in three consecutive editions of the [[Johan Cruyff Shield]], which Ajax won once.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 August 2013 |title=De statistieken van ruim vier jaar Eriksen |url=http://www.ajaxshowtime.com/bijzaken-en-geruchten/72894/de-statistieken-van-ruim-vier-jaar-eriksen.html |publisher=Ajax Showtime |access-date=31 August 2013 |archive-date=30 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141030054053/http://www.ajaxshowtime.com/bijzaken-en-geruchten/72894/de-statistieken-van-ruim-vier-jaar-eriksen.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Tottenham Hotspur===
====2013–2016: Premier League introduction and League Cup runner-up====
[[File:Eriksen and Soldado.jpg|thumb|upright|Eriksen (right) preparing to kick off for [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] in 2013]]
On 30 August 2013, [[Premier League]] club [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] announced that they had completed the transfer of Eriksen from Ajax in a deal believed to be worth £11 million (€12.45 million).<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 August 2013 |title=Eriksen Arrives |url=http://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/eriksen-arrives-300813/ |access-date=30 August 2013 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C.}}</ref> Eriksen joined the club on the same day as [[Erik Lamela]],<ref name=":8">{{cite news |last=Hytner |first=David |date=30 August 2013 |title=Tottenham's spend passing £110m with Erik Lamela and Christian Eriksen |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/aug/30/tottenham-hotspur-erik-lamela-christian-eriksen |access-date=30 August 2013 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> who joined from [[A.S. Roma|Roma]], and [[Vlad Chiricheș]], who joined from [[FC Steaua București|Steaua București]], and took the club's total spending for the [[List of English football transfers summer 2013|2013 summer transfer window]] to £109.5 million.<ref name=":8" /> 

He made his league debut against [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] on 14 September and provided an assist for [[Gylfi Sigurðsson]] in a 2–0 victory.<ref>{{cite news |last=Reddy |first=Luke |date=14 September 2013 |title=Tottenham 2–0 Norwich |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/23999467 |access-date=14 September 2013 |work=[[BBC Sport]] |language=en-GB}}</ref> After the match, Spurs manager [[André Villas-Boas]] commented: "It was a great debut for Christian, he is a pure number 10, a creative player and his individual quality made all the difference."<ref>{{Cite news |last=Collett |first=Mike |date=14 September 2013 |title=Eriksen proves life goes on for Spurs after Bale |work=Reuters |url=http://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-england-tottenham-idUKBRE98D09O20130914 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160123004834/http://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-england-tottenham-idUKBRE98D09O20130914 |url-status=dead |archive-date=23 January 2016}}</ref>

Five days later, Eriksen "clipped a wonderful dipping shot" over the goalkeeper to score his first Tottenham goal and complete a 3–0 win over [[Tromsø IL]] in the [[2013–14 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=19 September 2013 |title=Europa League: Two Jermain Defoe goals secure Tottenham a 3–0 win over Tromso |publisher=Sky Sports |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/live/match/300996/report |access-date=29 May 2014}}</ref> He added to his Tottenham goal tally with a goal from a free kick in a 1–1 draw against [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] on Boxing Day 2013, and the second goal in Spurs' 1–2 away win against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] on 1 January 2014.<ref>{{cite news |last=Wallace |first=Sam |title=Manchester United 1 Tottenham 2 match report: United unable to muster recovery after Emmanuel Adebayor and Christian Eriksen goals |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/manchester-united-1-tottenham-2-match-report-united-unable-to-muster-recovery-after-emmanuel-adebayor-and-christian-eriksen-goals-9033107.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241215004629/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/manchester-united-1-tottenham-2-match-report-united-unable-to-muster-recovery-after-emmanuel-adebayor-and-christian-eriksen-goals-9033107.html |date=2 January 2014 |archive-date=15 December 2024 |access-date=19 January 2014 |work=[[The Independent]] |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 23 March and two goals down against [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] at [[White Hart Lane]], Eriksen scored twice to level the score and then assisted Sigurðsson to score the winning goal.<ref>{{cite news |last=Lewis |first=Aimee |date=23 March 2014 |title=Tottenham Hotspur 3–2 Southampton |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/26599215 |access-date=24 March 2014 |work=[[BBC Sport]] |language=en-GB}}</ref> 

He continued his goalscoring form on 12 April when he scored a stoppage-time equaliser to help Tottenham come from 3–0 down to draw 3–3 at West Brom.<ref>{{cite news |last=Cryer |first=Andy |date=12 April 2014 |title=West Bromwich Albion 3–3 Tottenham Hotspur |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/26898645 |access-date=12 April 2014 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> By the end of the season, he had scored 10 goals and registered 13 assists across all competitions, won the [[Danish Football Player of the Year]] award and was named Tottenham's Player of the Season.<ref>{{cite web |last=Fitch |first=Dan |date=12 August 2014 |title=Eriksen to follow the Modric-Bale path |url=https://africa.espn.com/football/story/_/id/37400286/christian-eriksen-follow-same-path-luka-modric-gareth-bale-all-way-madrid |access-date=11 December 2017 |website=[[ESPN]]}}</ref><ref name=":9">{{cite web |date=13 May 2017 |title=Christian and Dele's Club awards double 13 May 2017 |url=http://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/christian-and-deleand39s-club-awards-double-130517/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171111144958/http://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/christian-and-deleand39s-club-awards-double-130517/ |archive-date=11 November 2017 |access-date=16 November 2017 |website=Tottenham Hotspur F.C.}}</ref>

Ahead of the [[2014–15 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season|2014–15 campaign]], Tottenham appointed [[Mauricio Pochettino]] as new club manager after the unsuccessful period under Villas-Boas and interim-manager [[Tim Sherwood]]. Between November and December 2014, Eriksen scored late winners against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] and [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]] which he credited to the Argentine manager for raising the team's fitness levels.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Association |first=Press |date=2014-12-15 |title=Christian Eriksen: Tottenham’s late winners down to raised fitness |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/dec/15/christian-eriksen-tottenham-late-winners-fitness |access-date=2026-05-10 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> By the end of the calendar year, Eriksen had scored 12 goals from open play – more than any other player in England – and was soon after awarded his second consecutive Danish Footballer of the Year award.<ref name=":10">{{cite web |title=Christian makes history in Denmark |date=11 January 2016 |url=http://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/christian-eriksen-wins-danish-player-of-the-year-for-third-year-running-2016-110116/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180219210920/http://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/christian-eriksen-wins-danish-player-of-the-year-for-third-year-running-2016-110116/ |archive-date=19 February 2018 |access-date=11 December 2017 |website=Tottenham Hotspur F.C.}}</ref> 

On 28 January 2015, Eriksen scored twice in a 2–2 (3–2 aggregate) win over [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] to send Tottenham into the [[2015 Football League Cup Final|League Cup Final]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Rostance |first=Tom |date= 28 January 2015 |title=Sheffield United 2–2 Tottenham Hotspur (agg 2–3) |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/30910040 |access-date= 18 August 2025 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> His first goal, a 30-yard curling free kick, was later lauded by former professionals [[Michael Owen]] and [[Gary Neville]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Coombs |first=Dan |date=28 January 2015 |title=Eriksen's stunning free-kick: Onomah and ex-Spurs stars react on Twitter |url=http://hereisthecity.com/en-gb/2015/01/28/eriksens-stunning-free-kick-onomah-and-ex-spurs-stars-react-on-t/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150212151948/http://hereisthecity.com/en-gb/2015/01/28/eriksens-stunning-free-kick-onomah-and-ex-spurs-stars-react-on-t/ |archive-date=12 February 2015 |access-date=29 January 2015 |website=Here Is The City}}</ref> The final, played against London rivals [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], took place on 1 March and ended in a 2–0 defeat for Tottenham.<ref name="LC2015">{{cite news |last=McNulty |first=Phil |date=1 March 2015 |title=Chelsea 2–0 Tottenham Hotspur |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31572594 |access-date=3 September 2018 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Eriksen completed the 2014–15 campaign having featured in every Premier League game for Mauricio Pochettino, starting all-but one match, and scored 12 goals across all competitions.<ref>{{cite web |date=22 June 2015 |title=Double figures delight – Christian on his 2014–15 goals |url=https://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news-archive-1/double-figures-delight-christian-on-his-2014-15-goals/ |access-date=11 December 2017 |website=Tottenham Hotspur F.C.}}</ref>

On 9 June 2015, amid speculation that he would be joining Manchester United, Eriksen confirmed to Danish media whilst on international duty that he would stay at Tottenham for the foreseeable future and was quoted as saying: "I feel right at home at Tottenham and I haven't thought about leaving yet."<ref>{{cite news |last=Orr |first=James |date=10 June 2015 |title=Manchester United target Christian Eriksen says does not want to leave Tottenham |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/transfers/manchester-united-target-christian-eriksen-says-he-does-not-want-to-leave-tottenham-10309244.html |access-date=3 August 2020 |work=[[The Independent]]}}</ref> He did in fact remain with the club and scored his first goals of the season in October, netting from two free-kicks in a 2–2 draw with Swansea.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Yury |first=Gazinsky |date=2021-06-13 |title=haywin |url=https://haywin9.io |access-date=2026-05-10 |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Cooper |first=Thomas |title=Why Eriksen Is the Tottenham Player Who Must Produce After International Break |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2575222-why-eriksen-is-the-tottenham-player-who-must-produce-after-international-break |date=6 October 2015 |access-date=11 December 2017 |website=Bleacher Report}}</ref> 

In January 2016, Eriksen was once again named Danish Footballer of the Year. In doing so he became the first ever player to win the award in three consecutive years.<ref name=":10" /> He ultimately scored 6 goals and registered 13 assists as Tottenham ended the league season in third place, thereby qualifying for the following season's [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] campaign.<ref name="BR">{{Cite web |last=Marsden |first=Rory |date=6 September 2017 |title=Christian Eriksen, Tottenham Agree on New Contract: Latest Details and Reaction |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2654675-christian-eriksen-tottenham-agree-on-new-contract-latest-details-and-reaction |access-date=11 December 2017 |website=Bleacher Report}}</ref>

====2016–2020: Premier League runner-up and PFA Team of the Year====
[[File:Eriksen20162(cropped).jpg|thumb|Eriksen playing for Tottenham Hotspur in 2016]]
Ahead of the [[2016–17 Premier League|following season]], Eriksen signed a new long-term contract with Tottenham and starred once again for the club, scoring eight goals and assisting a further 15 as the club ended the league campaign as runners-up to champions Chelsea.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Goal 50 – Journalists from across Goal's 37 editions voted in the 10th annual award for the world's 50 best footballers |url=http://www.goal.com/story/goal-50-english/ |access-date=16 November 2017 |publisher=Goal.com}}</ref> Eriksen's tally of assists was bettered only by [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]]'s [[Kevin De Bruyne]] who set up 18 goals for the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=21 May 2017 |title=Premier League assists 2016/17: Who created the most goals this season? |url=https://talksport.com/football/premier-league-assists-201617-who-created-most-goals-season-170521240072?p=10 |access-date=16 November 2017 |website=talkSPORT}}</ref> Eriksen also recorded the joint-most assists in the [[FA Cup]] and later won the Tottenham Player of the Season award, claiming the award for the second time after previously winning it in his debut season with the club.<ref name="FAC">{{cite web |title=English FA Cup Statistics |url=http://www.espnfc.com/english-fa-cup/40/statistics/assists?season=2016 |access-date=22 October 2017 |publisher=ESPN FC}}</ref><ref name=":9" />

Eriksen broke the record for the most goals scored by a Danish player in the Premier League when he scored his 33rd goal in a 3–2 win over [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] on 23 September 2017, surpassing the record previously held by [[Nicklas Bendtner]].<ref name="DP">{{cite news |date=24 September 2017 |title=Christian Eriksen happy to move Nicklas Bendtner to the side after his record-breaking goal against West Ham |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/tottenham-hotspur-christian-eriksen-record-breaking-premier-league-goal-nicklas-bendtner-arsenal-a7964126.html |access-date=11 December 2017 |work=The Independent}}</ref> On 9 December, he made his 200th appearance for Tottenham and marked the occasion by scoring in a 5–1 league win over [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 December 2017 |title=Spurs 5–1 Stoke – Report from Wembley |url=http://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/first-team/match/report/spurs-v-stoke-city-match-report-091217/ |access-date=10 December 2017 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C.}}</ref> The following month, he scored his 50th goal for the club when he scored after just 11 seconds in the 2–0 league win over Manchester United.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Floyd |first=Thomas |date=31 January 2018 |title=Eriksen scores after 11 seconds for Spurs against Man Utd |url=http://www.goal.com/en-za/news/eriksen-scores-after-11-seconds-for-spurs-against-man-utd/ypvppsdummy71vo012e2g8sfo |access-date=1 February 2018 |publisher=Goal.com}}</ref> Eriksen's goal was the third-fastest goal ever scored in the Premier League, bettered only by [[Alan Shearer]] and former Spurs captain [[Ledley King]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Press |first=Associated |date=2018-01-31 |title=Eriksen scores after 11 seconds for 3rd fastest EPL goal |url=https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2018/jan/31/eriksen-scores-after-11-seconds-for-2nd-fastest-ep/ |access-date=2026-05-10 |website=The Washington Times |language=en-US}}</ref>

On 17 March 2018, Eriksen scored twice in an [[2017–18 FA Cup|FA Cup]] match against Swansea to send Spurs to the semi-final for the second season running.<ref>{{cite news |last=Pearlman |first=Michael |date=17 March 2018 |title=Swansea City 0–3 Tottenham Hotspur |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43353565 |access-date=17 March 2018 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 1 April, Eriksen scored a 25-yard goal in the away match against Chelsea, helping Tottenham to their first win in 28 years at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]] in a match that finished 3–1.<ref>{{Cite news |date=1 April 2018 |title=WATCH: Christian Eriksen's 'rainbow' stunner in Tottenham's win over Chelsea |work=Sky Sports |url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/11313452/watch-christian-eriksens-rainbow-stunner-in-tottenhams-win-over-chelsea}}</ref> Later that month, in the reverse fixture against Stoke, Eriksen scored twice to earn Tottenham a 2–1 win. Following the match, teammate [[Harry Kane]], who was challenging for the season's [[Premier League Golden Boot|Golden Boot]] award, claimed to have made the last touch on the ball for the second goal. Tottenham appealed to the Premier League panel who agreed that the ball touched Kane's shoulder and awarded him the goal.<ref>{{cite news |last=Johnston |first=Neil |date=7 April 2018 |title=Stoke City 1–2 Tottenham Hotspur |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43602488 |access-date=11 April 2018 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=11 April 2018 |title=Premier League: Tottenham goal at Stoke awarded to Harry Kane |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43731208 |access-date=11 April 2018 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 14 April, Eriksen was named in the [[PFA Team of the Year]] for the first time, alongside teammates Kane and [[Jan Vertonghen]].<ref name="1718PFA">{{cite news |date=18 April 2018 |title=Manchester City players dominate PFA team of the year |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43810017 |access-date=5 May 2018 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

In the [[2018–19 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season|2018–19 season]], Eriksen scored his first goal of the season in a Champions League away match against [[Inter Milan]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Brand |first=Gerard |date=19 September 2018 |title=Inter 2–1 Tottenham: Two late goals stun Spurs in Champions League opener |work=Sky Sports |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/inter-vs-tottenham/401830|access-date=2026-05-10}}</ref> The match ended in a 2–1 loss for Tottenham, but in the home game against Inter, Eriksen scored again in the only goal of the game, giving Tottenham a 1–0 victory.<ref>{{cite news |last=Delaney |first=Miguel |title=Christian Eriksen's late goal against Inter Milan gives Tottenham vital Champions League lifeline |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european/tottenham-vs-inter-milan-result-champions-league-2018-goals-score-report-latest-a8657116.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241215004635/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european/tottenham-vs-inter-milan-result-champions-league-2018-goals-score-report-latest-a8657116.html |date=28 November 2018 |archive-date=15 December 2024 |access-date=29 November 2018 |work=The Independent |language=en-GB}}</ref> He scored his first Premier League goal of the season on 15 December 2018 in the home match against [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]], a late goal that earned Tottenham a 1–0 win.<ref>{{cite news |last=Miller |first=Nick |date=15 December 2018 |title=Christian Eriksen's late strike gives Tottenham win over Burnley |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/dec/15/tottenham-burnley-premier-league-match-report |access-date=15 December 2018 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0029-7712}}</ref> On 31 March, during a 2–1 defeat to [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], he became only the second player after [[David Beckham]] to record 10+ assists in four successive Premier League seasons.<ref>{{cite web |last=Sandford |first=Daniel |date=2 April 2019 |title=Christian Eriksen joined Manchester United legend as assist king |url=https://talksport.com/football/521001/christian-eriksen-assists-manchester-united-legend-david-beckham-premier-league-record/ |access-date=4 April 2019 |website=talkSPORT |language=en-gb}}</ref> Three days later, on the occasion of his 200th Premier League appearance, he assisted [[Son Heung-min]] for the first ever goal at the new [[Tottenham Hotspur Stadium]] before scoring a goal of his own in a 2–0 win over [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Harris |first=Daniel |date=3 April 2019 |title=Son and Eriksen seal Spurs victory in opening game at new stadium |publisher=EuroSport |url=https://asia.eurosport.com/football/premier-league/2018-2019/son-and-eriksen-seal-spurs-victory-in-opening-game-at-new-stadium_sto7213126/story.shtml |url-status=dead |access-date=4 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190404084920/https://asia.eurosport.com/football/premier-league/2018-2019/son-and-eriksen-seal-spurs-victory-in-opening-game-at-new-stadium_sto7213126/story.shtml |archive-date=4 April 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Pitt-Brooke |first=Jack |date=3 April 2019 |title=Tottenham vs Crystal Palace player ratings: Heung-Min Son and Christian Eriksen deliver for Spurs |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/tottenham-crystal-palace-new-stadium-player-ratings-heungmin-son-first-goal-eriksen-a8853816.html |access-date=4 April 2019}}</ref> On 23 April, he scored the winning goal in a 1–0 win over [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 April 2019 |title=Spurs v Brighton, 2018/19 |url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/38635 |website=Premier League|access-date=2026-05-10}}</ref> Later on, Eriksen played in the [[2019 UEFA Champions League Final]], which |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2025486--tottenham-vs-liverpool/ |website=UEFA|access-date=2026-05-10}}</ref>

===Inter Milan===
On 28 January 2020, with his contract at Tottenham set to expire in six months, Eriksen signed a four-and-a-half-year deal with [[Serie A]] club Inter Milan that would earn him €10 million per season.<ref>{{Cite news |date=28 January 2020 |title=CHRISTIAN ERIKSEN IS A NEW INTER PLAYER |publisher=Inter Milan |url=https://www.inter.it/en/news/2020/01/28/official-christian-eriksen-inter-player.html |access-date=28 January 2020}}</ref> He made his club debut the following day, coming on as a second-half substitute for [[Alexis Sánchez]] in 2–1 home win over [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] in the [[2019–20 Coppa Italia|Coppa Italia]] quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite news |date=29 January 2020 |title=Inter Milan 2–1 Fiorentina: Christian Eriksen helps secure win on debut |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/51304229 |access-date=30 January 2020 |work=[[BBC Sport]] |language=en-GB}}</ref> 

On 20 February, Eriksen scored his first goal for the club, netting the opener in a 2–0 away victory over [[PFC Ludogorets Razgrad|Ludogorets Razgrad]] in the [[2019–20 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]].<ref>{{cite news |date=20 February 2020 |title=Ludogorets Razgrad 0–2 Inter Milan: Christian Eriksen scores first goal since move |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/51533323 |access-date=20 February 2020 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> He scored his first Serie A goal on 1 July, in a 6–0 win against [[Brescia Calcio|Brescia]].<ref>{{cite news |date=1 July 2020 |title=Inter Milan 6–0 Brescia: Ashley Young, Alexis Sanchez and Christian Eriksen score |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/53257838 |access-date=1 July 2020 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> On 21 August, Eriksen played in Inter's 3–2 loss against [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] in the [[2020 UEFA Europa League Final|2020 Europa League Final]], becoming the first player to lose two consecutive finals in the two current major UEFA competitions;{{refn|group=nb|[[Zinedine Zidane]] was the first player to lose two consecutive European club finals in two different competitions (with [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]] in the [[1996 UEFA Cup Final]] and with [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in the [[1997 UEFA Champions League Final]]).}} he had lost the 2019 Champions League Final with Tottenham the previous year.<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 August 2020 |title=Christian Eriksen Made History In The Europa League Final For All The Wrong Reasons |url=https://www.sportbible.com/football/football-news-stats-christian-eriksen-made-history-in-last-nights-europa-league-final-20200822 |website=Sport Bible |access-date=14 October 2020 |archive-date=27 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210227185218/https://www.sportbible.com/football/football-news-stats-christian-eriksen-made-history-in-last-nights-europa-league-final-20200822 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In December 2020, [[Giuseppe Marotta]] confirmed that Eriksen had been added to the transfer list for 2021; however, his teammate [[Romelu Lukaku]] had previously hinted that Eriksen's struggles at the Italian club were due to the language barrier.<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 December 2020 |title=Eriksen set to leave Inter as CEO Marotta confirms midfielder is available for transfer |url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/eriksen-set-to-leave-inter-as-ceo-marotta-confirms-midfielder-is-/1ckrx7y2bcxa61w7dab2g6e3m5 |website=goal.com|access-date=2026-05-10}}</ref> On 26 January 2021, in the final minutes of Inter's [[2020–21 Coppa Italia|Coppa Italia]] quarter-final match against rivals [[A.C. Milan|Milan]], Eriksen was subbed on with the score at 1–1. In the seventh minute of stoppage time and with the game seemingly headed for extra time, he scored his first goal of the season from a direct free kick to win the match for Inter and send them through to the semi-finals.<ref>{{cite news |date=26 January 2021 |title=Inter Milan 2–1 AC Milan: Christian Eriksen nets winner in dramatic derby |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/55752320 |access-date=6 February 2021 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Following the match, Inter manager [[Antonio Conte]] said that Eriksen would remain with the club, despite being linked with a winter departure.<ref>{{Cite news |date=26 January 2021 |title='Nobody will arrive, nobody will leave' - Conte says 'shy' Eriksen will remain at Inter after Milan derby wonder goal |work=goal.com |url=https://www.goal.com/en/amp/news/conte-shy-eriksen-will-remain-at-inter/18keb01sl6cs01placbx4gxrvm |access-date=6 February 2021}}</ref> On 1 May, he scored Inter's first goal in an important 2–0 away win over [[F.C. Crotone|Crotone]], bringing the club closer to their first league title since [[2009–10 Serie A|2009–10]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=1 May 2021 |title=Crotone 0–2 Inter Milan: Christian Eriksen scores as Nerazzurri close on Serie A title |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/56959181 |access-date=12 June 2021 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Inter were confirmed as league champions the following day, after closest challengers [[Atalanta B.C.|Atalanta]] failed to win their match against [[U.S. Sassuolo Calcio|Sassuolo]]. It ended Juventus's nine-year grasp on the Serie A title.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 May 2021 |title=Inter clinch first Serie A title in 11 years as Juve's era of dominance comes to an end |url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/inter-clinch-first-serie-a-title-in-11-years-as-juves-era-of/1ttw7xvesu7td1wu06icw6z2zr |access-date=2 May 2021 |website=Goal}}</ref><ref name="auto">{{cite web |date=2 May 2021 |title=Inter end Juventus' Serie A dominance with first title in 11 years |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/internazionale/story/4374169/inter-end-juventus-serie-a-dominance-with-first-title-in-11-years |access-date=2 May 2021 |website=ESPN}}</ref>

On 29 October 2021, it was announced that Eriksen was not permitted to play in the Serie A due to the presence of an [[implantable cardioverter-defibrillator]] he had implanted after suffering a [[cardiac arrest]] during a game at [[UEFA Euro 2020]].<ref name="itv.com">{{Cite web |date=29 October 2021 |title=Christian Eriksen: Inter Milan midfielder not allowed to resume career in Italy due to ICD |url=https://www.itv.com/news/2021-10-29/christian-eriksen-not-allowed-to-resume-career-in-italy-due-to-icd |access-date=2 December 2021 |website=tv.com}}</ref> Close to half a year after his cardiac arrest, Eriksen began individual training at the facilities of his youth academy team [[OB Odense|OB]] in [[Odense]] in preparation for a possible comeback to football.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2 December 2021 |title=Christian Eriksen: Inter Milan midfielder 'training by himself' at former club Odense Boldklub |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11860/12484535/christian-eriksen-inter-milan-midfielder-training-by-himself-at-former-club-odense-boldklub |access-date=2 December 2021 |publisher=[[Sky Sports]]}}</ref> On 17 December 2021, Inter confirmed they had terminated their contract with Eriksen.<ref name=":11">{{cite news |date=17 December 2021 |title=Christian Eriksen: Inter Milan terminate Denmark midfielder's contract |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59699440 |access-date=17 December 2021 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last= |date=2021-12-17 |title=Christian Eriksen has Inter contract terminated ‘by mutual consent’ |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/dec/17/christian-eriksen-has-inter-contract-terminated-by-mutual-consent |access-date=2026-05-10 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

===Brentford===
On 31 January 2022, Eriksen signed for Premier League club [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] on a six-month contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=31 January 2022 |title=Brentford confirm signing of Christian Eriksen |url=https://www.brentfordfc.com/news/2022/january/brentford-confirm-signing-of-christian-eriksen/ |access-date=31 January 2022 |publisher=Brentford F.C.}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Harris |first=Jay |date=31 January 2022 |title=Brentford sign Christian Eriksen on six-month contract |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4182993/2022/01/31/brentford-sign-christian-eriksen-on-six-month-contract/ |access-date=7 April 2025 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Hytner |first=David |date=31 January 2022 |title=Brentford sign Christian Eriksen on deal until end of the season |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/jan/31/brentford-sign-christian-eriksen-on-deal-until-end-of-season |access-date=7 April 2025 |work=[[The Guardian]] |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> On 26 February 2022, his first appearance was as a substitute in a 2–0 defeat to [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]]. He replaced [[Mathias Jensen]], who came on in Eriksen's place in the game in which he suffered a cardiac arrest.<ref>{{cite news |date=26 February 2022 |title=Brentford 0-2 Newcastle United: Christian Eriksen returns as Bees lose to Magpies |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60441967 |access-date=26 February 2022 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> He recorded his first assist since his cardiac arrest in a 2–0 win over [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] on 12 March.<ref>{{cite web |date=12 March 2022 |title=Eriksen on form as Brentford beat Burnley |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/premier-league/2022/03/12/622ce55222601d8c548b4570.html |access-date=26 June 2022 |website=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]}}</ref> 

He scored his first goal back in the Premier League in a 4–1 away win against [[West London derby#Brentford vs Chelsea derby|West London rivals]] Chelsea on 2 April, helping the Bees secure their first victory over Chelsea since 1939.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chelsea 1-4 Brentford: Christian Eriksen scores as Bees seal incredible derby win at Stamford Bridge |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/chelsea-vs-brentford/report/446590 |access-date=2 April 2022 |publisher=Sky Sports}}</ref> Between the date of Eriksen's Brentford debut and the end of the season, only [[Kevin De Bruyne]] and [[Martin Ødegaard]] created more chances in the Premier League.<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 June 2022 |title=Christian Eriksen unsure over future amid reports of Tottenham return |url=https://www.squawka.com/en/christian-eriksen-transfer-update-tottenham-brentford/ |access-date=26 June 2022 |website=squawka.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=15 June 2022 |title=Manchester United cannot ignore De Jong and Van de Beek factors in Christian Eriksen pursuit |url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/manchester-united-eriksen-transfer-news-24229499 |access-date=26 June 2022 |website=Manchester Evening News}}</ref>

On 15 July 2022, [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] announced they had reached an agreement to sign Eriksen on a three-year deal.<ref>{{Cite news |date=15 July 2022 |title=Transfer news: Eriksen signs for United |publisher=Manchester United |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/Transfer-news-Man-Utd-complete-signing-of-Christian-Eriksen |access-date=15 July 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Romano |first=Fabrizio |date=4 July 2022 |title=Christian Eriksen agrees to Manchester United move on three-year contract ===VfL Wolfsburg===
On 10 September 2025, Eriksen joined [[Bundesliga]] side [[VfL Wolfsburg]] on a two-year contract, with the option of a further year's extension.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6388188/2025/09/10/christian-eriksen-wolfsburg-manchester-united/|title=Former Manchester United and Tottenham midfielder Christian Eriksen joins Wolfsburg|first=Leon|last=Imber|date=10 September 2025|access-date=10 September 2025|work=[[The Athletic]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vfl-wolfsburg.de/en/newsdetails/news-detail/detail/news/wolves-sign-top-class-playmaker|title=Wolves sign top-class playmaker|date=10 September 2025|access-date=10 September 2025|publisher=VfL Wolfsburg}}</ref> He made his debut for Wolfsburg in a 1–0 loss to [[Borussia Dortmund]] on 21 September,<ref>{{cite web |title=Eriksens debut ender som en fuser |trans-title=Eriksen's debut ends up a flop |website=TV 2 |agency=Ritzau |date=21 September 2025 |url=https://sport.tv2.dk/fodbold/2025-09-21-eriksens-debut-ender-som-en-fuser |language=danish |access-date=14 January 2026}}</ref> and later scored his first goal for the club in a 2–1 victory over [[FC St. Pauli|St. Pauli]] on 14 January 2026.<ref>{{cite web |last=Jensen |first=Mathias Bybjerg |title=Dansk duo strålede i Wolfsburg-triumf |trans-title=Danish duo shine in Wolfsburg triumph |website=Bold |date=14 January 2026 |url=https://bold.dk/fodbold/stillinger/tyskland-1-bundesliga/nyheder/dansk-duo-stralede-i-wolfsburg-triumf |language=danish |access-date=14 January 2026}}</ref>

On 23 September 2026, Eriksen and VfL Wolfsburg mutually agreed to terminate his contract, having not played since his collapse in June.<ref>{{cite |last=Kilpatrick |first=Dan |title=Christian Eriksen leaves Wolfsburg by mutual agreement, three months after collapse |date=23 September 2026 |issn=0362-4331 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7622893/2026/09/23/christian-eriksen-wolfsburg-collapse/ |language=en-US |access-date=23 September 2026 |page=}}</ref>

2011 |website=Soccerway}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=24 June 2010 |title=Denmark vs. Japan |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2010/06/24/world/world-cup/denmark/japan/878799/ |access-date=11 February 2011 |website=Soccerway}}</ref>

On 9 February 2011, in a 2–1 friendly loss at home against [[England national football team|England]], Eriksen was named [[man of the match]], and was praised for his performance by a number of prominent footballing figures, including [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] star [[Frank Lampard]],<ref>{{Cite news |date=9 February 2011 |title=Stjerne: Eriksen kan blive topspiller |language=da |work=Jyllands-Posten Sport |url=http://spn.dk/fodbold/landshold/article2335072.ece |url-status=dead |access-date=10 February 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120531014316/http://spn.dk/fodbold/landshold/article2335072.ece |archive-date=31 May 2012}}</ref> Man Utd star [[Rio Ferdinand]] (on Twitter),<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 February 2011 |title=Ferdinand skamroser Eriksen på Twitter |url=http://www.sporten.dk/fodbold/ferdinand-skamroser-eriksen-paa-twitter |access-date=10 February 2011 |publisher=Sporten.dk |language=da |archive-date=15 August 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120815172856/http://www.sporten.dk/fodbold/ferdinand-skamroser-eriksen-paa-twitter |url-status=dead }}</ref> manager Morten Olsen and several media experts in Denmark and England.<ref>{{Cite news |date=9 February 2011 |title=Engelske medier jubler over Eriksen |language=da |work=Jyllands-Posten Sport |url=http://spn.dk/fodbold/landshold/article2335260.ece |url-status=dead |access-date=10 February 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131002095355/http://jyllands-posten.dk/sport/fodbold/landshold/article2335260.ece |archive-date= 2013-10-02}}</ref> 

On 4 June 2011, Eriksen scored his first national team goal to give Denmark a 2–0 lead over [[Iceland national football team|Iceland]] in their [[UEFA Euro 2012 qualifying Group H|UEFA Euro 2012 qualifier]]. In doing so, he became the youngest Danish player ever to score a goal in European qualification, being nine days younger than Michael Laudrup when he scored his first goal in 1983.<ref>{{Cite web |date=16 May 2011 |title=Ajacied Eriksen speelt Laudrup uit de boeken |url=http://www.ad.nl/ad/nl/1441/Ajax/article/detail/2441812/2011/06/06/Ajacied-Eriksen-speelt-Laudrup-uit-de-boeken.dhtml |access-date=6 June 2011 |publisher=Ad.nl |language=nl}}</ref>

====2018 FIFA World Cup====
In the build-up to the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]], Denmark were drawn in [[2018 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group E|UEFA Group E]] alongside the likes of [[Poland national football team|Poland]] and [[Romania national football team|Romania]]. Eriksen played a key-role during the nation's qualification campaign during which time he scored eight goals to earn Denmark a play-off against the [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Hawkey |first=Ian |date=5 November 2017 |title=Christian Eriksen is danger for Ireland |url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/great-dane-eriksen-is-danger-forireland-372f7gngj |access-date=15 November 2017 |work=[[The Times]]}}</ref> The first leg of the play-off ended in a 0–0 home draw before Eriksen netted a [[hat-trick]] in [[Dublin]]'s [[Aviva Stadium]] in a 5–1 win to earn Denmark a spot at the World Cup.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hafez |first=Shamoon |date=14 November 2017 |title=Republic of Ireland 1–5 Denmark (agg: 1–5) |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/41884909 |access-date=14 November 2017 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> Eriksen's treble took his tally to 11 goals for the qualification campaign, bettered only by Poland's [[Robert Lewandowski]] (16) and [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]]'s [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] (15) in Europe, and earned the praise of national team manager [[Åge Hareide]] who stated that Eriksen was one of the top 10 players in the world.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |date=15 November 2017 |title=Tottenham's Christian Eriksen one of the world's top 10 players, says Denmark boss Age Hareide |url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/17248/11127219/tottenhams-christian-eriksen-one-of-the-worlds-top-10-players-says-denmark-boss-age-hareide |access-date=15 November 2017 |publisher=Sky Sports}}</ref>

In Denmark's opening match at the tournament, Eriksen assisted [[Yussuf Poulsen]] for the only goal in a 1–0 win over [[Peru national football team|Peru]] before scoring his first goal for the tournament in the 1–1 draw with [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia]] the following week.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Miller |first=Nick |date=22 June 2018 |title=World Cup 2018: 'Great things happen' when you play alongside Christian Eriksen, Denmark's shining star |work=The Independent |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/world-cup/christian-eriksen-denmark-world-cup-2018-thomas-delaney-australia-a8411006.html |access-date=22 June 2018}}</ref> Denmark ultimately progressed from their [[2018 FIFA World Cup Group C|group]] after which they were drawn with [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]] in the [[2018 FIFA World Cup knockout stage#Round of 16|Round of 16]]. There they were defeated after a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]], with Eriksen being one of three players to have his spot-kick saved by Croatia goalkeeper [[Danijel Subašić]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite news |last=Pender |first=Kieran |date=1 July 2018 |title=Croatia's Luka Modric fluffs big line but still prevails in duel with Eriksen |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/jul/01/croatia-luka-modric-christian-eriksen-denmark-world-cup |access-date=2 July 2018}}</ref>

On 9 September 2018, Eriksen scored twice in a 2–0 win over [[Wales national football team|Wales]] to lead Denmark to victory in the nation's inaugural [[2018–19 UEFA Nations League B]] match.<ref name="Wales-2018">{{Cite news |last=Candy |first=James |date=9 September 2018 |title=Double from Denmark's Christian Eriksen brings Wales down to earth |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/sep/09/denmark-wales-nations-league-match-report |access-date=11 September 2018}}</ref> On 14 October 2020, Eriksen played his 100th match for Denmark, in which he scored a penalty in a 1–0 away win against [[England national football team|England]] in the [[2020–21 UEFA Nations League]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 October 2020 |title=England 0–1 Denmark |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/54363934 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

====UEFA Euro 2020 cardiac arrest====
Eriksen was included in Denmark's squad for the delayed [[UEFA Euro 2020]] on 25 May 2021.<ref>{{Cite news |date=25 May 2021 |title=26 spillere klar til EM for Danmark |language=da |trans-title=26 players ready for the European Championship for Denmark |work=[[Danish Football Association]] |url=https://dbu.dk/nyheder/2021/maj/26-spillere-klar-til-em-for-danmark/ |access-date=25 May 2021}}</ref> On 12 June, while playing in Denmark's [[UEFA Euro 2020 Group B#Denmark vs Finland|opening group stage match]] against [[Finland national football team|Finland]] at [[Parken Stadium]] in [[Copenhagen]], Eriksen collapsed in the 42nd minute as he was about to receive a throw-in. Eriksen's teammate and captain [[Simon Kjær]] was credited for his response<ref>{{Cite web |title=Euro 2020: Denmark captain Simon Kjaer hailed a hero for 'life-saving' response to Christian Eriksen collapse |url=https://news.sky.com/story/euro-2020-denmark-captain-simon-kjaer-hailed-a-hero-for-life-saving-response-to-christian-eriksen-collapse-12331399 |access-date=28 May 2024 |publisher=Sky News}}</ref> after placing him into the [[recovery position]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=What saved Christian Eriksen? – Thackray Museum of Medicine |url=https://thackraymuseum.co.uk/what-saved-christian-erikson/ |access-date=28 May 2024 |website=thackraymuseum.co.uk|date=16 June 2021 }}</ref> Urgent medical assistance arrived immediately, and [[cardiopulmonary resuscitation]] and [[defibrillation]] were performed on the field before Eriksen was taken off the pitch on a stretcher and the match was suspended.<ref name="Cardiac" /><ref name="Guardian">{{Cite web |last=Christenson |first=Marcus |date=13 June 2021 |title='He was gone': Christian Eriksen had cardiac arrest, Denmark doctor says |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/jun/13/he-was-gone-christian-eriksen-had-cardiac-arrest-denmark-doctor-says |access-date=13 June 2021 |website=The Guardian}}</ref> Around an hour after the incident, [[UEFA]] and [[Danish Football Association]] (DBU) officials confirmed from the [[Rigshospitalet]] Hospital that Eriksen had been stabilized and was awake.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Karen |first=Mattias |date=12 June 2021 |title=Denmark game at Euro 2020 suspended after Eriksen collapses |work=[[Associated Press]] |location=Copenhagen |url=https://apnews.com/article/denmark-europe-euro-2020-soccer-international-soccer-9911d934556c6b181636f47dedf20888 |access-date=12 June 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Eriksen 'awake' after collapsing |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57456002}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=12 June 2021 |title=Christian Eriksen: Denmark player 'awake and stabilised' in hospital after being given CPR following on-pitch collapse |work=Sky News |url=https://news.sky.com/story/denmarks-christian-eriksen-given-cpr-after-collapsing-on-pitch-in-match-against-finland-12331132 |access-date=12 June 2021}}</ref> 

The match continued later that evening, resulting in a 1–0 victory for Finland,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Emons |first=Michael |date=12 June 2021 |title=Denmark 0-1 Finland: Euro 2020 game overshadowed by Christian Eriksen collapse |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51197533 |access-date=13 June 2021 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> with Eriksen chosen by UEFA as the man of the match.<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 June 2021 |title=Denmark 0–1 Finland: Finns win after Eriksen emergency |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro-2020/match/2024449/postmatch/report/ |access-date=14 June 2021 |website=UEFA}}{{dead link|date=March 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> Denmark manager [[Kasper Hjulmand]] and team doctor Morten Boesen both later expressed regret at the match's continuation,<ref>{{Cite web |date=13 June 2021 |title=Christian Eriksen collapse: Denmark coach regrets restart v Finland |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57458978 |access-date=13 June 2021 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> although Eriksen's teammate [[Martin Braithwaite]] said that the decision to do so was the "least bad one".<ref>{{Cite news |title=Playing match was 'least bad' choice |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57468439}}</ref> The decision to continue the match was also criticised by [[Peter Schmeichel]], father of Denmark's keeper [[Kasper Schmeichel|Kasper]], who said that UEFA had threatened the team with a 3–0 loss if they refused to finish the match later on that day or the following day at noon, leaving the players with "no choice" but to continue.<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 June 2021 |title=Peter Schmeichel: Denmark players did not have choice with Finland restart after Christian Eriksen collapse |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/17248/12332297/peter-schmeichel-denmark-players-did-not-have-choice-with-finland-restart-after-christian-eriksen-collapse |access-date=14 June 2021 |publisher=Sky Sports}}</ref> The BBC was also heavily criticised for continuing to stream the incident recording 6,417 complaints.<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 June 2021 |title=BBC gets 6,417 complaints over Eriksen footage |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/entertainment-arts-57600807 |access-date=14 June 2024 |publisher=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref>

The next day, Boesen confirmed Eriksen had suffered a [[cardiac arrest]].<ref name="Guardian" /><ref name="Cardiac">{{Cite web |date=13 June 2021 |title=Christian Eriksen: Denmark midfielder suffered cardiac arrest, says team doctor |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57458630 |access-date=14 June 2021 |publisher=BBC News}}</ref> The incident itself drew comparisons to [[Fabrice Muamba]] and [[Abdelhak Nouri]], two professional footballers who also collapsed during play in similar circumstances. Muamba was forced to retire, and Nouri suffered permanent brain damage.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stubley |first=Peter |date=12 June 2021 |title=Fabrice Muamba says Christian Eriksen collapse 'brought back emotions I never wanted to relive' |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/christian-eriksen-fabrice-muamba-collapse-b1864876.html |access-date=14 June 2021 |website=The Independent}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=13 June 2021 |title=Collapse of Eriksen during Euro match brings back memories of Nouri heart arrhythmias |url=https://nltimes.nl/2021/06/13/collapse-eriksen-euro-match-brings-back-memories-nouri-heart-arrhythmias |access-date=18 June 2021 |website=NL Times}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Verweij |first1=Mike |last2=Kraan van der |first2=Marcel |date=12 June 2021 |title=Vader van Abdelhak Nouri bidt voor Christian Eriksen |trans-title=Father of Abdelhak Nouri prays for Christian Eriksen |url=https://www.telegraaf.nl/sport/1654394667/vader-van-abdelhak-nouri-bidt-voor-christian-eriksen |access-date=18 June 2021 |website=Telegraaf |language=nl |location=Amsterdam}}</ref> On 15 June, Eriksen posted a picture of himself in the hospital on his social media along with a brief statement, stating that he was "fine under the circumstances".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Christian Eriksen on Instagram: "Hello everyone Big thanks for your sweet and amazing greetings and messages from all around the world. It means a lot to me and my family. ♥️🙏 I'm fine - under the circumstances. I still have to go through some examinations at the hospital, but I feel okay. Now, I will cheer on the boys on the Denmark team in the next matches. Play for all of Denmark 🇩🇰 Best Christian" |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/CQIbbREAXo5/ |website=Instagram}}</ref> The following day, it was announced that he would be fitted with an [[implantable cardioverter-defibrillator]] device, a decision described by Boesen as "necessary due to rhythm disturbances" following his cardiac arrest.<ref>{{Cite web |date=17 June 2021 |title=Christian Eriksen to have heart-starting device fitted after collapse |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57508250 |access-date=25 June 2021 |website=BBC News}}</ref> The operation jeopardised his contract with Inter Milan due to Serie A rules, which did not allow players wearing ICD devices to play. His contract was terminated later that year.<ref name="itv.com" /><ref name=":11" /> 

On 18 June, the DBU declared that Eriksen had undergone a successful operation and was discharged from Rigshospitalet. After his discharge, he visited his Danish teammates in [[Helsingør]] before returning home to his family.<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 June 2021 |title=Christian Eriksen visits teammates after discharge |url=https://news.sky.com/story/christian-eriksen-visits-team-after-being-discharged-from-hospital-12336045 |access-date=18 June 2021 |website=Sky News}}</ref> The Danish team later dedicated their 4–1 win over [[Russia national football team|Russia]] in their final group match to Eriksen; the result allowed them to advance to the round of 16.<ref>{{Cite news |date=21 June 2021 |title='This one is for you Christian' – Denmark players celebrate Euro 2020 progress |work=The Guardian|first=Marcus|last=Christenson |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/jun/21/this-one-is-for-you-christian-denmark-players-celebrate-after-euro-progress |access-date=19 June 2022}}</ref> They later went on to reach the semi-finals of the tournament, where they were eliminated following a 2–1 extra-time loss to England at Wembley Stadium, on 7 July.<ref name="SI1">{{Cite magazine |last=Wilson |first=Jonathan |date=7 July 2021 |title=Decisive Drama Tilts England's Way, With Three Lions a Step Away From 'Home' |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/2021/07/07/england-denmark-euro-2020-sterling-penalty-kane |access-date=8 July 2021}}</ref>

====Return to international football====
Eriksen returned to international football on 26 March 2022, coming on at half-time in a 4–2 loss against the Netherlands, scoring two minutes into his return.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Eriksen scores on Denmark return |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/60889501 |access-date=26 March 2022 |publisher=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> He was included in the [[2022 FIFA World Cup squads|squad]] for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]],<ref>{{cite web |date=7 November 2022 |title=De første spillere til VM-truppen er fundet |trans-title=The first players for the World Cup squad have been selected |url=https://dbu.dk/nyheder/2022/november/de-foerste-spillere-til-vm-truppen-er-fundet/ |access-date=7 November 2022 |publisher=[[Danish Football Association]] |language=da}}</ref> playing in every minute of Denmark's campaign as they finished bottom of [[2022 FIFA World Cup Group D|Group D]].<ref name=sb2223/>

Eriksen was included in the [[UEFA Euro 2024 squads|squad]] for [[UEFA Euro 2024]].<ref>{{cite news |date=30 May 2024 |title=Hjulmand har udtaget truppen til EM |trans-title=Hjulmand has selected the squad for the European Championship |url=https://dbu.dk/nyheder/2024/maj/hjulmand-har-udtaget-truppen-til-em/ |access-date=30 May 2024 |publisher=[[Danish Football Association]] |language=da}}</ref> He scored in Denmark's opening [[UEFA Euro 2024 Group C|Group C]] match against [[Slovenia national football team|Slovenia]] that ended in a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{cite web |date=16 June 2024 |title=Eriksen's fairytale Euro comeback spoilt by Slovenia in 1-1 Euro draw |url=https://www.reuters.com/sports/soccer/eriksens-fairytale-euro-comeback-spoilt-by-slovenia-1-1-euro-draw-2024-06-16/ |publisher=Reuters}}</ref> In the last group stage encounter against [[Serbia national football team|Serbia]], he featured in his 133rd international match, becoming the most-capped Danish player ahead of his teammate [[Simon Kjær]].<ref>{{cite web |date=29 June 2024 |title=Denmark's Christian Eriksen on being a record breaker, his fine form and last-16 opponents Germany |url=https://www.uefa.com/euro2024/news/028e-1b3dbf1bdd14-22e2323e9381-1000--denmark-s-christian-eriksen-on-being-a-record-breaker-his/ |publisher=UEFA}}</ref>

In August{{nbsp}}2025, after Eriksen's departure from Manchester United, Danish national team coach [[Brian Riemer]] excluded Eriksen from the national team's squad for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group C|2026 World Cup qualification]] matches in September.<ref>{{cite newspaper |last=Walker |first=Mark |date=26 August 2025 |title=Denmark boss explains Eriksen omission for Scotland clash |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/25415927.denmark-boss-explains-eriksen-omission-scotland-clash/ |access-date=30 August 2025 |newspaper=The Herald}}</ref> Riemer stated weeks prior that he would exclude Eriksen if the midfielder was not signed with a club.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hansen |first1=Jens Fall |last2=Nielsen |first2=Morten Løvig |date=25 August 2025 |title=Christian Eriksen vraget til det danske landshold |trans-title=Christian Eriksen rejected for the Danish national team |url=https://www.dr.dk/sporten/fodbold/landsholdet/landsholdet-udtages-til-vm-kvalifikationen |access-date=30 August 2025 |publisher=DR |language=danish}}</ref><ref>{{cite newspaper |last=Walker |first=Mark |date=2 August 2025 |title=Christian Eriksen told to find new club or he won't play vs Scotland |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/25360565.christian-eriksen-told-find-new-club-wont-play-vs-scotland/ |access-date=30 August 2025 |newspaper=The Herald}}</ref> On 30{{nbsp}}September, after having signed with German club [[VfL Wolfsburg]], Eriksen returned to the national team squad list ahead of two World Cup qualification matches in October.<ref>{{cite web |last=Jensen |first=Michael Sten |date=30 September 2025 |title=Eriksen har overbevist Riemer med blot 50 minutters fodbold på fire måneder |trans-title=Eriksen has convinced Riemer with just 50 minutes of football in four months |url=https://www.dr.dk/sporten/fodbold/landsholdet/eriksen-er-tilbage-paa-landsholdet-se-truppen-her |access-date=3 October 2025 |publisher=DR |language=danish}}</ref>

==== Ukraine friendly collapse ====
Eriksen suffered a second on-field collapse in the 65th minute of an international friendly against [[Ukraine national football team|Ukraine]] on 7 June 2026 at [[Odense Stadium|Nature Energy Park]] in [[Odense]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.sky.com/story/danish-footballer-christian-eriksen-collapses-on-pitch-13551755 |title=Denmark footballer Christian Eriksen collapses on pitch |publisher=Sky News |date=7 June 2026 }}</ref> He regained consciousness shortly afterwards thanks to the [[Implantable cardioverter-defibrillator|ICD]]'s intervention. The match was abandoned.<ref name=":12">{{Cite web |date=2026-06-07 |title=Christian Eriksen conscious after collapsing during Denmark friendly |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/czrxgd2nljno |access-date=2026-06-07 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> He was subsequently confirmed to be doing well and began an individual rehabilitation program in Denmark under medical supervision.<ref>{{cite web |last=Millington |first=Adam |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c78y01090xqo |title=Eriksen to begin rehab in Denmark after collapse |publisher=BBC Sport |date=9 July 2026 }}</ref>

==Style of play==
Described as a "[[Squad number (association football)|classic number ten]]" in the media,<ref name="uefafaith" /><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Barcellona |first=Fabio |date=17 January 2017 |title=L'ultima frontiera del trequartista moderno |url=https://www.ultimouomo.com/eriksen-lultima-frontiera-del-trequartista-moderno/ |access-date=28 January 2020 |publisher=www.ultimouomo.com |language=it}}</ref> Eriksen's favoured position is in a free role in the centre of the pitch as an [[attacking midfielder]] behind the forwards;<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Barcellona |first=Fabio |date=12 February 2018 |title=Il Tottenham è una squadra senza compromessi |url=https://www.ultimouomo.com/tottenham-2018-pochettino/ |access-date=28 January 2020 |publisher=www.ultimouomo.com |language=it}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite web |last=Barcellona |first=Fabio |date=21 January 2020 |title=Eriksen cambierebbe l'Inter |url=https://www.ultimouomo.com/eriksen-inter-tottenham-conte/ |access-date=28 January 2020 |publisher=www.ultimouomo.com |language=it}}</ref> however, he is a tactically versatile player, who is also capable of playing as a [[central midfielder]] or [[mezzala]] in a 4–3–3 system (as was the case during his first years with Ajax),<ref name=":0" /> and as a [[right winger]] in a 4–2–3–1 formation.<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5" /> He has also been used on the left flank on occasion, or as a [[second striker]].<ref name=":5" />

Eriksen is also known for his work-rate and intelligence on the pitch.<ref name="uefafaith" /><ref name=":0" /><ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6">{{Cite web |last=Krogh |first=Karsten |date=16 January 2020 |title=Eriksen the right man for Inter |url=https://www.football-italia.net/148801/eriksen-right-man-inter |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210119090118/https://www.football-italia.net/148801/eriksen-right-man-inter |archive-date=19 January 2021 |access-date=28 January 2020 |website=football-italia.net |publisher=Football Italia}}</ref><ref name=":7">{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Adam |date=23 September 2017 |title=Is Tottenham midfielder Christian Eriksen the Premier League's top creator? |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11662/11047327/is-tottenham-midfielder-christian-eriksen-the-premier-leagues-top-creator |access-date=29 January 2020 |publisher=Sky Sports}}</ref> He is skilled with seeing the goal, and is known for his ability to strike the ball with power and accuracy with either foot, despite being naturally right-footed;<ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6" /><ref name=":7" /> moreover, he has also established himself as a [[Free kick (association football)|free kick]] specialist.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=5 October 2015 |title=Christian Eriksen the Premier League's best free kick taker says Fabianski |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/tottenham-hotspur/story/2650154/christian-eriksen-the-premier-league-free-kick-specialist |access-date=28 January 2020 |publisher=ESPN FC}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=28 January 2020 |title=Eriksen completes transfer to Inter from Tottenham |newspaper=The Washington Post |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/soccer/eriksen-completes-transfer-to-inter-from-tottenham/2020/01/28/84d4c1fe-41d6-11ea-99c7-1dfd4241a2fe_story.html |url-status=dead |access-date=28 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200129172925/https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/soccer/eriksen-completes-transfer-to-inter-from-tottenham/2020/01/28/84d4c1fe-41d6-11ea-99c7-1dfd4241a2fe_story.html |archive-date=29 January 2020}}</ref>

Due to his playing style, nationality, and role, pundits have compared him to his compatriots [[Michael Laudrup|Michael]] and [[Brian Laudrup]],<ref name="uefafaith" /><ref name="talented" /> who were two of his major influences in his youth, as well as [[Wesley Sneijder]] and [[Rafael van der Vaart]];<ref name="uefafaith" /><ref name=":0" /> Eriksen has also cited [[Francesco Totti]] as an inspiration.<ref>{{Cite web |date=5 February 2020 |title=Eriksen: 'Totti il mio idolo. E a Football manager...' |url=https://www.calciomercato.com/news/eriksen-totti-il-mio-idolo-e-a-football-manager-67787 |access-date=14 June 2021 |website=Calciomercato.com |language=it |archive-date=20 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220720175616/https://www.calciomercato.com/news/eriksen-totti-il-mio-idolo-e-a-football-manager-67787 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Eriksen lives with his partner Sabrina Kvist Jensen.<ref>{{Cite web |date=31 December 2018 |title=Christian Eriksen deler sød hemmelighed: Det hedder sønnike |url=https://www.seoghoer.dk/nyheder/det-hedder-soennike |website=SE og HØR |language=da}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=FourFourTwo Staff |date=25 June 2021 |title=Euro 2020 – Who is Christian Eriksen's wife and does he have kids? |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/euro-2020-who-is-christian-eriksens-wife-and-does-he-have-kids |website=fourfourtwo.com|access-date=2026-05-10}}</ref> They have a son and a daughter.<ref>{{Cite web |date=31 December 2018 |title=Har holdt det hemmeligt i månedsvis: Nu afslører Christian Eriksen sønnens navn |url=https://www.bt.dk/fodbold/har-holdt-det-hemmeligt-i-maanedsvis-nu-afsloerer-christian-eriksen-soennens-navn |website=B.T. |language=da|access-date=2026-05-10}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=31 December 2020 |title=Family of 4 😍❤️ |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/CJbmPL2gYkS/ |url-access=subscription |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/instagram/chriseriksen8/2475740589455411474 |archive-date=23 December 2021 |access-date=12 June 2021 |via=Instagram}}{{cbignore}}</ref> His younger sister [[Louise Eriksen]] also plays professional football, and has made appearances for the [[Denmark women's national football team|Danish women's under-16 national team]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 March 2017 |title=Eriksen om lillesøster på landsholdet: Hun har også været lidt jaloux på mig |url=https://www.dr.dk/sporten/fodbold/landsholdet/eriksen-om-lillesoester-paa-landsholdet-hun-har-ogsaa-vaeret-lidt-jaloux |publisher=[[DR (broadcaster)|DR]] |language=da|access-date=2026-05-10}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=22 March 2017 |title=Det bliver i familien: Søster Eriksen udtaget til landsholdet |url=https://www.dr.dk/sporten/fodbold/kvindelandsholdet/det-bliver-i-familien-soester-eriksen-udtaget-til-landsholdet |publisher=[[DR (broadcaster)|DR]] |language=da|access-date=2026-05-10}}</ref>
