{{cite news|title=「佑都くん、篤人くんの凄さをより感じる」名門で成長遂げた酒井宏樹、初のアジア杯で優勝誓う|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/japan/detail/?263460-263460-fl|website=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=6 January 2019|access-date=23 September 2024}}
{{cite news|title=Hiroki Sakai : "Tant que l'OM voudra de moi, je ferai le maximum"|url=https://www.laprovence.com/actu/en-direct/5359551/hiroki-sakai-tant-que-lom-voudra-de-moi-je-ferai-le-maximum.html|website=La Provence|language=fr|date=7 February 2019|access-date=23 September 2024}}
{{cite news|title=OM : "Sakai est l'un des meilleurs à son poste en Ligue 1" (Halilhodzic)|url=https://www.laprovence.com/actu/en-direct/5419857/om-sakai-est-lun-des-meilleurs-a-son-poste-en-ligue-1-halilhodzic.html|website=La Provence|language=fr|date=21 March 2019|access-date=23 September 2024}} He considered himself to be "a proud Marseillais".{{cite web|url=https://www.laprovence.com/article/om/5439236/om-hiroki-sakai-fier-detre-considere-comme-un-marseillais.html|title=OM : Hiroki Sakai, "fier d'être considéré comme un Marseillais"|website=La Provence|language=fr|date=2 April 2019|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20190928232408/https://www.laprovence.com/article/om/5439236/om-hiroki-sakai-fier-detre-considere-comme-un-marseillais.html|archive-date=28 September 2019|url-status=dead}} ===Urawa Red Diamonds=== On 10 June 2021, Sakai made his return to Japan, signing for [[Urawa Red Diamonds]] in the [[J1 League]].{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/175673/|title=酒井宏樹選手 完全移籍加入のお知らせ|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=Japanese|date=10 June 2021|access-date=1 March 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220625112211/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/175673/|archive-date=25 June 2022|url-status=live}} He made his debut for the club, starting the match, in a 2–1 win against [[Sagan Tosu]] on 14 August 2021.{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/177496/|title=第24節 vs 鳥栖「明本2戦連発!江坂が初ゴール!浦和駒場で勝利!」|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=14 August 2021|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240919195107/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/177496/|archive-date=19 September 2024|url-status=live}} Sakai helped Urawa Red Diamonds keep five consecutive clean sheets in the league between 21 August 2021 and 25 September 2021.{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/177680/|title=第25節 vs 徳島「関根がゴール! アウェイで勝利し連勝!」|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=21 August 2021|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240919200236/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/177680/|archive-date=19 September 2024|url-status=live}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/177830/|title=第26節 vs 広島「浦和駒場で2連勝! J1リーグ3連勝! 公式戦4連勝!」|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=25 August 2021|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240919195610/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/177830/|archive-date=19 September 2024|url-status=live}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/177934/|title=第27節 vs 湘南「アウェイで勝ち点を得る」|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=29 August 2021|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240919200547/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/177934/|archive-date=19 September 2024|url-status=live}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/178291/|title=第28節 vs 横浜FC「全員で闘い、2つの初ゴールで快勝!」|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=11 September 2021|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240919200744/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/178291/|archive-date=19 September 2024|url-status=live}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/178540/|title=第29節 vs C大阪「主導権を握り続けて鮮やかに勝利」|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=18 September 2021|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240919200801/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/178540/|archive-date=19 September 2024|url-status=live}} He scored his first goal for the club, in a 2–1 win against [[FC Tokyo]] on 25 September 2021.{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/178737/|title=第30節 vs FC東京「力強く、華麗に逆転勝利」|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=25 September 2021|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240919201325/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/178737/|archive-date=19 September 2024|url-status=live}} His second goal for Urawa Red Diamonds, in a 1–1 draw against [[Kawasaki Frontale]] on 3 November 2021.{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/180096/|title=第34節 vs 川崎「闘い続けてアウェイで勝ち点を獲得」|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=3 November 2021|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240919201519/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/180096/|archive-date=19 September 2024|url-status=live}} Sakai then started in [[2021 Emperor's Cup final|Emperor's Cup final]] against [[Oita Trinita]] and helped the club win 2–1 to win the tournament.{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/181949|title=天皇杯 決勝 vs 大分「劇的展開で4度目の天皇杯優勝!アジアへ!」|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=19 December 2021|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220808072925/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/181949/|archive-date=8 August 2022|url-status=live}} At the end of the 2021 season, Sakai made 18 appearances and scoring 2 times in all competitions. In the [[2022 Japanese Super Cup|Japanese Super Cup]] against Kawasaki Frontale, Sakai set up a goal for [[Ataru Esaka]], who went on to score twice, in a 2–0 win.{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/182923/|title=FUJIFILM SUPER CUP 2022 vs 川崎「2022シーズン初戦で昨季J1リーグ王者に快勝」|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=11 February 2022|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240919202316/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/182923/|archive-date=19 September 2024|url-status=live}} However during a match against [[Júbilo Iwata]] on 19 March 2022, he suffered a foot injury and was substituted in the 53rd minute, resulting in him out for three weeks.{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/184105|title=第5節 vs 磐田「加入後初ゴールと今季初ゴールで快勝」|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=19 March 2022|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240919203946/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/184105|archive-date=19 September 2024|url-status=live}}
{{cite news|title=【日本代表】豪州戦へ緊急事態…ＤＦ酒井宏樹も大迫勇也に続き不参加、中谷進之介を追加招集|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/202203190001535.html|website=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=19 March 2022|access-date=23 September 2024}} On 10 April 2022, Sakai made his return from injury, starting a match, against FC Tokyo and helped Urawa Red Diamonds keep a clean sheet, in a 0–0 draw.{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/184717/|title=第8節 vs FC東京「アウェイで主導権を握り続け、勝ち点を得る」|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=10 April 2022|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220410090253/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/184717/|archive-date=10 April 2022|url-status=live}} In a follow–up match, he captained the club for the first time, and set up one of the goals, in a 4–1 win against [[Lion City Sailors FC|Lion City Sailors]].{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/184911/|title=ACL グループステージ MD1 vs セーラーズ「3年ぶりのACLは快勝スタート」|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=25 April 2022|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220415191536/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/184911/|archive-date=15 April 2022|url-status=live}} However, Sakai's return was short–lived when he suffered a foot injury once again and was out for two months.{{cite news|title=【浦和】酒井宏樹が右足第５中足骨の手術で全治２カ月 ６月の代表戦は絶望的|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/news/202205030000973.html|website=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=3 May 2022|access-date=23 September 2024}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/185697/|title=酒井宏樹の負傷について|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=3 May 2022|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220503193155/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/185697/|archive-date=3 May 2022|url-status=live}} It wasn't until on 26 June 2022 when Sakai made his return from injury, coming on as a second–half substitute, in a 1–0 win against [[Vissel Kobe]].{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/187755/|title=第18節 vs 神戸「モーベルグの決勝ゴールで勝利! 西川はJリーグ記録に並ぶ」|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=26 June 2022|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220813064147/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/187755/|archive-date=13 August 2022|url-status=live}} However during a 3–1 win against Kawasaki Frontale on 30 July 2022, he suffered a knee injury and was substituted in the 61st minute.{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/189229/|title=第23節 vs 川崎「鮮やかに、J1リーグ3連勝!」|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=30 July 2022|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220805111017/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/189229/|archive-date=5 August 2022|url-status=live}}
{{cite news|title=浦和の日本代表DF酒井 左脚内側部の負傷で途中交代 ロドリゲス監督「少し違和感があった」|url=https://www.sponichi.co.jp/soccer/news/2022/07/30/kiji/20220731s00002179007000c.html|website=Sponichi Annex|language=ja|date=30 July 2022|access-date=23 September 2024}} Two weeks later on 10 August 2022, Sakai returned to the starting line–up from injury as captain, in a 3–0 win against [[Nagoya Grampus]] in the second leg of the J.League Cup quarter–finals.{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/189727/|title=ルヴァンカップ 準々決勝 第2戦 vs 名古屋「2年半ぶりに声出し応援が戻ってきた埼スタで完勝し、準決勝進出!」|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=10 August 2022|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240920173452/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/189727/|archive-date=20 September 2024|url-status=live}} In the AFC Champions League semi–finals against [[Jeonbuk Hyundai Motors]], he set up the opening goal of the game and started the whole game all the way to penalty–shootout in a 2–2 draw, as Urawa Red Diamonds won on penalties to help the club reach [[2022 AFC Champions League final|the final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/190531/|title=ACL 準決勝 vs 全北「起死回生の同点ゴールからPK戦で勝利! 3年ぶりの決勝へ!」|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=26 August 2022|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230523190902/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/190531/|archive-date=23 May 2023|url-status=live}} However, his return was short–lived when Sakai suffered a calf injury that saw him out for two matches.{{cite news|title=【浦和】酒井宏樹が右ふくらはぎ肉離れ、ACLで負傷、全治は発表されず|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/news/202209030001391.html|website=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=3 September 2022|access-date=23 September 2024}} On 14 September 2022, he made his return from injury, coming on as a second–half substitute, in a 1–0 loss against Cerezo Osaka.{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/191164/|title=第26節 vs C大阪「ボールを支配しながらも相手の守備を崩しきれず」|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=15 September 2022|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240920180631/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/191164/|archive-date=20 September 2024|url-status=live}} Following this, Sakai started in the next five matches until he missed the last game of the season, due to suspension.{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/188294/|title=酒井「理想は強いレッズでプレーし続けること」|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=8 July 2022|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240920161107/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/188294/|archive-date=20 September 2024|url-status=live}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/192813/|title=第33節 vs 横浜FM「キャスパーが1点返すも敵地で勝ち点得られず」|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=29 October 2022|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221029110203/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/192813/|archive-date=29 October 2022|url-status=live}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/193125/|title=2022年を締めくくる最終戦。過去から学び、未来を見据え、今に全力で臨む選手たちのおもい|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=3 November 2022|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221103114446/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/193125/|archive-date=3 November 2022|url-status=live}} At the end of the 2022 season, Sakai made 28 appearances in all competitions. Ahead of the 2023 season, Sakai was appointed as the new captain of Urawa Red Diamonds.{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/195185/|title=2023シーズン キャプテン決定のお知らせ|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=13 February 2023|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230216204538/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/195185/|archive-date=16 February 2023|url-status=live}} He started in the first seven league matches of the season and led the club on winning their first four consecutive wins in the league for in over six years.{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/195370/|title=第1節 vs FC東京「新たな姿を見せるも開幕戦を勝利で飾れず」|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=18 February 2023|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230223195356/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/195370/|archive-date=23 February 2023|url-status=live}}

{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/197537/|title=「非常に良いスタジアム。良いパフォーマンスを見せ、良いゲームにして、勝ち点3を取ること」マチェイ スコルジャ監督(定例会見 4/13)|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=13 April 2023|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230413140621/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/197537/|archive-date=13 April 2023|url-status=live}} But Sakai was able from injury when he led Urawa Red Diamonds secured a dramatic victory in the 2022 AFC Champions League final. {{Cite web|last=Orlowitz|first=Dan|date=6 May 2023|title=Urawa beats Al Hilal to capture third Asian Champions League title|url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2023/05/06/soccer/acl-final-urawa-alhilal-game2/|access-date=6 May 2023|website=[[The Japan Times]]}} This victory marked the club's third AFC Champions League title, solidifying their position as a powerhouse in Asian club football.{{Cite web |title=AFC Champions League Elite 2024/25|url=https://www.the-afc.com/en/club/afc_champions_league.html |access-date=2024-07-08|website=the-AFC|language=en}} For his performance, he was named AFC Champions League's Most Valuable Player.{{cite web|title=Urawa's Hiroki Sakai crowned Most Valuable Player|url=https://www.the-afc.com/en/club/afc_champions_league/news/urawa%E2%80%99s_sakai_crowned_most_valuable_player_.html|access-date=6 May 2023|language=en|date=6 May 2023|website=the-afc.com|publisher=[[Asian Football Confederation]]}} Following his return from injury, Sakai regained his first team place, as well as, his captaincy.{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/199362/|title=第15節 vs 京都「全員で闘い、FWが結果を出してアウェイで勝利」|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=27 May 2023|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240920194149/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/199362/|archive-date=20 September 2024|url-status=live}}

Marinos, Sakai received a red card for a second bookable offence, in a 1–0 loss.{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/204735/|title=ルヴァンカップ 準決勝 第1戦 vs 横浜FM「最少得点差で第2戦ホーム埼スタへ」|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=11 October 2023|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20231130081633/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/204735/|archive-date=30 November 2023|url-status=live}} After serving a one match, he returned to the starting line–up as captain for the [[2023 J.League Cup final|J.League Cup final]] against [[Avispa Fukuoka]], but was unable to help Urawa Red Diamonds win the final after losing 2–1.{{cite web|url=http://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/205652/|title=ルヴァンカップ決勝 vs 福岡「勝利を目指して闘い続けたが、頂点には立てず準優勝」|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=4 November 2023|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20231105131631/http://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/205652/|archive-date=5 November 2023|url-status=live}} Shortly after, Sakai suffered a meniscus injury on his right knee that expect him to be out for the rest of the season.{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/205676/|title=酒井宏樹の負傷について|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=6 November 2023|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20231206132431/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/205676/|archive-date=6 December 2023|url-status=live}} But he made his return from injury, coming on as an 81st-minute substitute, in a 2–1 win against [[Club León]] in [[2023 FIFA Club World Cup#Second round|the second round]] of the [[2023 FIFA Club World Cup|FIFA Club World Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/207134/|title= FCWC 準々決勝 vs クラブ・レオン「途中出場のシャルクが決めた! |title=Japanese defender Hiroki Sakai joins Auckland FC |website=Auckland FC |date=24 July 2024 |access-date=23 September 2024 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240724220029/https://aucklandfc.co.nz/news/japanese-defender-hiroki-sakai-joins-auckland-fc/ |archive-date=24 July 2024 |url-status=live}} On 15 October, Sakai was named club captain for the inaugural season, with [[Jake Brimmer]] and [[Tommy Smith (footballer, born 1990)|Tommy Smith]] appointed as vice-captains.{{cite web |url=https://aucklandfc.co.nz/news/sakai-appointed-new-auckland-fc-captain-two-vice-captains-named/ |title=Sakai appointed new Auckland FC captain, two vice-captains named |website=Auckland FC |date=15 October 2024 |access-date=6 November 2025}} On 19 October 2024, Sakai made his competitive debut for Auckland FC in the club’s first-ever match, a 2–0 win over [[Brisbane Roar FC|Brisbane Roar]]. He set up the club’s first goal by slicing a cross that was turned into an own goal by [[Harry Van Der Saag]].{{cite web |url=https://aucklandfc.co.nz/news/r1-match-wrap-auckland-fc-2-0-brisbane-roar/ |title=Match Wrap: Auckland FC 2–0 Brisbane Roar |website=Auckland FC |date=19 October 2024 |access-date=6 November 2025}} On 28 December 2024, Sakai scored his first goal for the club in a 4–1 win over the [[Central Coast Mariners FC|Central Coast Mariners]].{{cite web |url=https://aucklandfc.co.nz/news/rd-10-match-report-central-coast-mariners-1-4-auckland-fc/ |title=Match Report: Central Coast Mariners 1–4 Auckland FC |website=Auckland FC |date=28 December 2024 |access-date=6 November 2025}} On 17 February 2025, it was announced that Sakai had extended his contract with Auckland FC until the end of the [[2025–26 Auckland FC season|2025–26 season]].{{cite web |url=https://aucklandfc.co.nz/news/hiroki-sakai-extends-contract-with-auckland-fc/ |title=Hiroki Sakai extends contract with Auckland FC |website=Auckland FC |date=17 February 2025 |access-date=6 November 2025}} Sakai captained Auckland to their first piece of silverware, winning the Premiers Plate at the end of the regular season.{{Cite web |title=Historic debut: Auckland FC win A-League Premier's Plate |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/auckland-fc-makes-history-with-a-league-premiers-plate-victory/6RYS2BQOZNGCJEG4FG33NP5JCI/ |access-date=2026-04-16 |website=NZ Herald |language=en-NZ}}{{Cite web |last=ahayes |date=2025-04-27 |title=Auckland FC Win Premier’s Plate in Debut Season |url=https://aucklandfc.co.nz/news/auckland-fc-win-premiers-plate-in-debut-season/ |access-date=2026-04-16 |website=Auckland |language=en-US}} Sakai also featured in both semi-final legs against [[Melbourne Victory FC|Melbourne Victory]], where Auckland lost 2–1 on aggregate. Sakai ended his debut A-League season with 3 goals, and 4 assists in 25 appearances, earning him a place in the [[Professional Footballers Australia]] (PFA) A-League Team of the Season, alongside teammates [[Louis Verstraete]], [[Francis de Vries]], and [[Alex Paulsen]].{{Cite web |last=D'Urbano |first=Nicholas |date=2025-05-29 |title=Five Grand Finalists named as PFA announces 2024-25 A-League Men Team of the Season |url=https://pfa.net.au/news/five-grand-finalists-named-as-pfa-announces-2024-25-a-league-men-team-of-the-season/ |access-date=2026-04-16 |website=The PFA |language=en-AU}}{{Cite web |last=sachapisani |date=2025-05-29 |title=Auckland dominate PFA's Team of the Season after historic debut as 5 Grand Finalists named |url=https://aleagues.com.au/news/a-league-men-team-of-the-season-squad-coach-pfa-how-its-picked-full-xi/ |access-date=2026-04-16 |website=A-Leagues |language=en-AU}} Sakai captained Auckland FC in their first [[Australia Cup]] campaign during pre-season, assisting [[Jesse Randall]] after 30 seconds in the club's cup debut, a 4–0 win over [[Gold Coast Knights F.C.|Gold Coast Knights]].{{Cite web |last= |date=2025-07-29 |title=Post Match Report: Gold Coast Knights 0 – 4 Auckland FC |url=https://aucklandfc.co.nz/news/post-match-report-gold-coast-knights-0-4-auckland-fc/ |access-date=2026-04-16 |website=Auckland |language=en-US}} Sakai also started in Auckland's opening match of the 2025–26 season, a 0–0 draw away to Melbourne Victory at [[AAMI Park]].{{Cite web |last= |date=2025-10-18 |title=RD 1 Post Match Report: Melbourne Victory 0 - 0 Auckland FC |url=https://aucklandfc.co.nz/news/rd-1-post-match-report-melbourne-victory-00-auckland-fc-0/ |access-date=2026-04-16 |website=Auckland |language=en-US}} During the season, Sakai was sidelined by a recurring hamstring injury. He was substituted early in a 2–1 win over [[Adelaide United FC|Adelaide United]] on 1 November,{{Cite web |last= |date=2025-11-01 |title=RD 3 Post Match Report: Auckland FC 2 – 1 Adelaide United |url=https://aucklandfc.co.nz/news/rd-2-post-match-report-auckland-fc-2-1-adelaide-united/ |access-date=2026-04-16 |website=Auckland |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last= |date=2025-11-11 |title=AFC Update |url=https://aucklandfc.co.nz/news/afc-update/ |access-date=2026-04-16 |website=Auckland |language=en-US}} but returned four weeks later in early December. He was sidelined again for a further four weeks after suffering another hamstring injury in a 3–0 win over [[Melbourne City FC|Melbourne City]],{{Cite web |last=ahayes |date=2026-03-03 |title=AFC Captain Hiroki Sakai out for up to Five Weeks |url=https://aucklandfc.co.nz/news/afc-captain-hiroki-sakai-set-to-miss-five-weeks/ |access-date=2026-04-16 |website=Auckland |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last= |date=2026-02-28 |title=RD 19 Match Report: Auckland FC 3 - 0 Melbourne City FC |url=https://aucklandfc.co.nz/news/rd-19-match-report-auckland-fc-3-0-melbourne-city-fc/ |access-date=2026-04-16 |website=Auckland |language=en-US}} before returning in early April. Shortly after returning from injury, the club announced that Sakai had signed a contract extension until the end of the [[2026–27 Auckland FC season|2026–27 season]].{{Cite web |last=Burgess |first=Michael |title=‘I want to retire here’: Hiroki Sakai eyes long-term future with Auckland FC |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/football/auckland-fc/exclusive-a-league-star-hiroki-sakai-wants-to-make-auckland-home-after-football-career/premium/YH56TZ44SNHRFP357RUMR5DFHY/ |access-date=2026-04-16 |website=NZ Herald |language=en-NZ}}{{Cite web |last=Daily |first=The Chosun |date=2026-04-12 |title=Sakai Hiroki Eyes Retirement, Residency in New Zealand |url=https://www.chosun.com/english/sports-en/2026/04/12/VUYHKDFF6ZGC7FBRCDPFFCQ6GM/ |access-date=2026-04-16 |website=The Chosun Daily |language=en}} Sakai started and captained all four of Auckland FC's finals matches during the club's [[A-League Men finals series]]. This included playing the full 120 minutes in a 1–1 draw with Melbourne City in the elimination final, where he successfully converted his penalty in the shootout as Auckland progressed 7–6 on penalties.{{Cite web |title=Auckland FC beat Melbourne City in penalty shootout|url=https://www.1news.co.nz/2026/05/02/auckland-fc-beat-melbourne-city-in-penalty-shootout/|access-date=2026-05-03|website=1News|language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Voerman|first=Andrew|title=Auckland FC's Dan Hall on how they beat Melbourne City on penalties to advance to A-League Men semifinals|url=https://www.thepost.co.nz/sport/360997171/auckland-fcs-dan-hall-how-they-beat-melbourne-city-penalties-advance-league-men-semifinals|access-date=2026-05-03|website=www.thepost.co.nz}} Following a 4–1 aggregate semi-final victory over Adelaide United, Auckland advanced to their first [[A-League Men Grand Final]].{{Cite web |title=Auckland FC heads to A-League grand final with slick win over Adelaide |url=https://www.1news.co.nz/2026/05/16/auckland-fc-heads-to-a-league-grand-final-with-slick-win-over-adelaide/ |access-date=2026-05-24 |website=1News |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Voerman |first=Andrew |date=2026-05-15 |title=Auckland FC stun Adelaide United to make A-League Men grand final |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/360973515/auckland-fc-stun-adelaide-united-make-league-men-grand-final |access-date=2026-05-24 |website=Stuff |language=en}} Sakai again played the full 90 minutes in a 1–0 win over [[Sydney FC]], captaining Auckland FC to the [[2026 A-League Men Grand Final|A-League Men Championship]] and becoming the first New Zealand club to win the title. The championship was also the second piece of silverware won in the club's first two years of existence.{{Cite web |last=Burgess |first=Michael |title=Champions! Auckland FC win A-League title |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/football/auckland-fc/auckland-fc-v-sydney-fc-live-updates-a-league-men-grand-final/WHAAI5ZPFFH55JMEHIVR62PHVM/ |access-date=2026-05-24 |website=NZ Herald |language=en-NZ}}{{Cite web |last=rcuthbertson |date=2026-05-23 |title=Auckland FC claim A-League Title in Second Season: Grand Final Match Report |url=https://aucklandfc.co.nz/news/auckland-fc-claim-a-league-title-in-second-season-grand-final-match-report/ |access-date=2026-05-24 |website=Auckland |language=en-US}} ==International career== ===Youth and Olympics career === After spending three years between 2008 and 2011, representing Japan's youth system, Sakai was called up by [[Japan national under-23 football team|Japan U23]] squad for the first time in May 2011.{{cite web|url=https://www.reysol.co.jp/news/topteam/031597.html|title=大津選手、酒井選手がU-19日本代表候補キャンプに選出|website=Kashiwa Reysol|language=ja|date=4 March 2008|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240917200507/https://www.reysol.co.jp/news/topteam/031597.html|archive-date=17 September 2024|url-status=live}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.reysol.co.jp/news/topteam/031306.html|title=大津 祐樹選手、酒井 宏樹選手が『U-22日本代表』に選出|website=Kashiwa Reysol|language=ja|date=27 May 2011|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240917204600/https://www.reysol.co.jp/news/topteam/031306.html|archive-date=17 September 2024|url-status=live}} On 1 June 2011, he made his Japan U23 on the same day, in a 3–1 win over [[Australia men's national under-23 soccer team|Australia U23]].{{cite news |script-title=ja:逆転劇の陰で露呈した問題点 Ｕ−２２日本 ３−１ Ｕ−２２オーストラリア|url=https://sports.yahoo.co.jp/column/detail/201106030002-spnavi|publisher=Sports Navi|language=ja|date=3 June 2011|access-date=19 June 2018}}
{{cite news |script-title=ja:Ｕ−２２日本、五輪予選へ真価を問われるオーストラリア戦|url=https://sports.yahoo.co.jp/column/detail/201106010001-spnavi|publisher=Sports Navi|language=ja|date=1 June 2011|access-date=19 June 2018}} Three weeks later on 23 June 2011, Sakai scored his first goal for the U23 side, in [[Football at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's Asian Qualifiers Preliminary Round 2#Second leg|second leg of the Asian Qualifiers Preliminary Round of the Summer Olympics]], in a 2–1 loss against [[Kuwait national under-23 football team|Kuwait U23]], but Japan U23 won 4–3 on aggregate.{{cite news |script-title=ja:酒井宏「難しい試合…集中した」／Ｕ22|url=http://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/f-sc-tp2-20110624-794555.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=24 June 2011|access-date=19 June 2018}} After making his U23 debut, he became a regular for the U23 throughout the year in the right–back position.{{cite news |script-title=ja:世界基準で考える競り合いの技術的な課題 Ｕ−２２日本 ２−１ Ｕ−２２エジプト|url=https://sports.yahoo.co.jp/column/detail/201108110007-spnavi|publisher=Sports Navi|language=ja|date=11 August 2011|access-date=19 June 2018}}
{{cite news |script-title=ja:大津の勝ち越し点を呼び込んだ４つのファインプレー Ｕ−２２日本 ２−１ Ｕ−２２シリア|url=https://sports.yahoo.co.jp/column/detail/201111280004-spnavi|publisher=Sports Navi|language=ja|date=28 November 2011|access-date=19 June 2018}}
{{cite news |script-title=ja:Ｕ22酒井「ゼロに抑える」|url=http://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/f-sc-tp2-20111126-869017.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=26 November 2011|access-date=19 June 2018}} On 22 February 2012, Sakai scored again and set up one of the goals, in a 4–0 win over [[Malaysia national under-23 football team|Malaysia U23]].{{cite news |script-title=ja:【動画】Ｕ－23、４発！シリアが敗れたため首位返り咲き！（五輪）|url=https://www.sakaiku.jp/topics/2012/001924.html|publisher=Saikaiku|language=ja|date=23 February 2012|access-date=19 June 2018}} On 2 July 2012, Sakai was called up for the [[Football at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Summer Olympics Football tournament]] in London.{{cite news |script-title=ja:Ｕ−２３日本代表メンバー選考に見られた２つの特徴 ロンドン五輪での戦い方に変化はあるのか|url=https://sports.yahoo.co.jp/column/detail/201207030003-spnavi|publisher=Sports Navi|language=ja|date=3 July 2012|access-date=19 June 2018}} He started in a match, playing 74 minutes before being substituted, in a 1–0 win over [[Spain national under-23 football team|Spain U23]].{{cite news|title=【スペイン】現地メディアが報じた「五輪代表、日本に敗北」|url=https://sportiva.shueisha.co.jp/clm/football/wfootball/2012/07/27/post_142/|publisher=Sporiva Shueisha|language=ja|date=27 July 2012|access-date=23 September 2024}} Sakai went on to start three more matches in the tournament, as Japan U23 reached the semi–finals and finished fourth place.{{cite news|title=永井!吉田!大津!U-23代表が3発完封で44年ぶりのベスト4進出決定|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?103087-104872-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=4 August 2012|access-date=23 September 2024}}
{{cite news|title=日本、３位決定戦へ サッカー男子、メキシコに敗れる|url=http://www.asahi.com/olympics/news/TKY201208070774.html|website=Asashi|language=ja|date=7 August 2012|access-date=23 September 2024}}
{{cite news|title=Olympic football: South Korea beat Japan to men's bronze|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/olympics/18916123|publisher=BBC Sport|date=10 August 2012|access-date=19 June 2018}} Sakai was named as one of Japan's three over-age players for the [[2020 Summer Olympics|Olympic]] [[Football at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|on home soil]], alongside [[Maya Yoshida]] and [[Wataru Endo]].{{Cite web|title=U-24 Japan National Team Squad - Games of the XXXII Olympiad (Tokyo 2020)【7/21-8/7】, KIRIN CHALLENGE CUP 2021【7/12＠Osaka, 7/17＠Hyogo】|url=https://www.jfa.jp/eng/national_team/u24_2021/news/00027265/|access-date=1 July 2021|website=JFA｜公益財団法人日本サッカー協会|language=ja}} On 22 July 2021, he made his first appearance for the U23 side, starting a match, in a 3–0 win against [[South Africa national under-23 soccer team|South Africa]].{{cite news|title=久保建英が決勝点！ 日本、南アフリカの堅守に苦しむも東京五輪白星発進！|url=https://www.soccer-king.jp/news/japan/national/20210722/1552063.html|website=Soccer King|language=ja|date=22 July 2021|access-date=23 September 2024}}
{{cite news|title=ロンドン五輪で史上最高の成績をあげた選手たちが、日本代表の中核になれなかった理由|url=https://sportiva.shueisha.co.jp/clm/football/jfootball/2021/07/24/post_99/|website=Sportiva Shueisha|language=ja|date=24 July 2021|access-date=23 September 2024}} Sakai scored his first goal of the tournament, in a 4–0 win against [[France Olympic football team|France]].{{cite news|title=U-24日本代表 フランスに勝利してノックアウトステージ進出|url=https://www.jfa.jp/national_team/u24_2021/news/00027600/|website=Japan Football Association|language=ja|date=28 July 2021|access-date=23 September 2024}} After serving a one match suspension, he returned to the starting line–up, losing both matches in [[Football at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament – Knockout stage#Semi-finals|the semi–finals]] and [[Football at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament – Knockout stage#Bronze medal match|bronze medal match]] against [[Spain national under-23 football team|Spain]] and Mexico respectively.{{cite news|title=U-24日本代表、PK戦を制して準決勝進出|url=https://www.jfa.jp/national_team/u24_2021/news/00027629/|website=Japan Football Association|language=ja|date=1 August 2021|access-date=23 September 2024}}
{{cite news|title=U-24日本代表 スペインに敗れ、3位決定戦へ|url=https://www.jfa.jp/national_team/u24_2021/news/00027649/|website=Japan Football Association|language=ja|date=4 August 2021|access-date=23 September 2024}}
{{cite news|title=U-24日本代表 1-3でメキシコに敗れ、東京オリンピックを4位で終える|url=https://www.jfa.jp/national_team/u24_2021/news/00027672/|website=Japan Football Association|language=ja|date=7 August 2021|access-date=23 September 2024}} ===Senior=== [[File:Hiroki Sakai 20180612.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Sakai playing for [[Japan national football team|Japan]] against [[Paraguay national football team|Paraguay]] on 12 June 2018.]] In October 2011, Sakai was called up for the first time to the [[Japan national football team|senior squad]] for a match against [[Vietnam national football team|Vietnam]] and [[Tajikistan national football team|Tajikistan]], but he appeared as an unused substitute instead.{{cite news |script-title=ja:ケガの清武に代わり、酒井（柏）が代表に追加招集|url=https://www.sakaiku.jp/topics/2011/000978.html|publisher=Sakaiku|language=ja|date=4 October 2011|access-date=19 June 2018}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.reysol.co.jp/news/topteam/031285.html|title=酒井 宏樹選手が『日本代表』に選出|website=Kashiwa Reysol|language=ja|date=4 October 2011|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240913070120/https://www.reysol.co.jp/news/topteam/031285.html|archive-date=13 September 2024|url-status=live}} After eight months since being called up to the Japan's national team, Sakai made his debut for the Samurai Blue, coming on as a second–half substitute, in a 2–0 win over [[Azerbaijan national football team|Azerbaijan]] in the [[Kirin Cup|Kirin Challenge Cup]] on 23 May 2012.{{cite news |script-title=ja:【動画】キリンカップ、香川･岡崎ゴールで快勝！|url=https://www.sakaiku.jp/topics/2012/002517.html|publisher=Sakaiku|language=ja|date=24 May 2012|access-date=19 June 2018}} By April 2012, he began to adjust playing under Manager [[Alberto Zaccheroni]], having understood his tactics and management.{{cite news |script-title=ja:酒井３－４－３「頭では分かるけど…」|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/f-sc-tp2-20120424-939493.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=24 April 2012|access-date=19 June 2018}}
{{cite news |script-title=ja:酒井がマンツーマンでザック３バック補習|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/p-sc-tp2-20120424-939019.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=24 April 2012|access-date=19 June 2018}} For the rest of 2012, Sakai continued to get more playing time for Japan, including making his first start for the Samurai Blue against [[United Arab Emirates national football team|United Arab Emirates]] on 6 September 2012.{{cite news |script-title=ja:酒井「やれた」Ａ代表デビュー／親善試合|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/f-sc-tp2-20120523-955898.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=23 May 2012|access-date=19 June 2018}}
{{cite news|title=日本３発！白星発進／Ｗ杯予選詳細|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/f-sc-tp2-20120603-961737.html|website=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=3 June 2012|access-date=23 September 2024}}
{{cite news|title=ザックジャパン１－０勝利！ハーフナーが頭で決めた|url=https://www.sponichi.co.jp/soccer/news/2012/09/06/kiji/K20120906004057740.html|website=Sponichi Annex|language=ja|date=6 September 2012|access-date=23 September 2024}}
{{cite news|title=歴史的勝利は大金星か…強豪撃破で浮かび上がった日本の現在地／フランス戦|url=https://www.soccer-king.jp/sk_column/article/76428.html|website=Soccer King|language=ja|date=13 October 2012|access-date=23 September 2024}}
{{cite news|title=ザックジャパン ブラジルに力の差まざまざ ０－４大敗|url=https://www.sponichi.co.jp/soccer/news/2012/10/16/kiji/K20121016004344770.html|website=Sponichi Annex|language=ja|date=16 October 2012|access-date=23 September 2024}}
{{cite news |script-title=ja:酒井宏「次につながる経験」／Ｗ杯予選|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/f-sc-tp2-20121115-1046994.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=15 November 2012|access-date=19 June 2018}}{{cite web|title=National Team Squad|url=http://www.jfa.or.jp/eng/national_team/squad/|work=jfa.or.jp|publisher=[[Japan Football Association]]|access-date=15 January 2014}} In 2013, Sakai began to compete with [[Atsuto Uchida]] over the right–back position, which saw both each winning the position in number of matches.{{cite news|title=【日本代表】酒井宏樹「僕は、（内田）篤人くんのようなプレイはできない」|url=https://sportiva.shueisha.co.jp/clm/football/jfootball/2013/01/20/___split_36/|website=Sportiva Shueisha|language=ja|date=20 January 2013|access-date=23 September 2024}}
{{cite news |script-title=ja:元日本代表・名良橋晃が徹底解析 長友佑都、内田篤人、酒井宏樹…… 日本のサイドバックは世界を制するか？|url=https://www.footballchannel.jp/2013/06/08/post5221/4/|publisher=Football Channel Website|language=ja|date=8 June 2013|access-date=19 June 2018}}
{{cite news|title=酒井宏、内田とのスタメン争いを語る「篤人君の凄さは身に染みて分かった」|url=https://www.soccer-king.jp/news/japan/national/20140515/190080.html|website=Soccer King|language=ja|date=15 May 2014|access-date=23 September 2024}} Six months later, he was called up by the Samurai Blue for the [[2013 FIFA Confederations Cup|2013 Confederations Cup]] squad.{{cite news|script-title=ja:もし一人足せるとしたら、日本代表に誰を選ぶ？|url=https://www.footballchannel.jp/2013/06/06/post5164/|publisher=Football Channel Website|language=ja|date=6 June 2013|access-date=19 June 2018}} Sakai played two of the three matches in the group stage, losing both matches, and was eliminated from the tournament.{{cite news|title=イタリアに３発も逆転負け／コンフェデ杯|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/f-sc-tp2-20130620-1144904.html|website=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=20 June 2013|access-date=23 September 2024}}
{{cite news |script-title=ja:ザックの期待に応えられなかった酒井宏樹。内田篤人との違いとは何か？|url=https://www.footballchannel.jp/2013/06/24/post5877/|publisher=Football Channel Website|language=es|date=24 June 2013|access-date=19 June 2018}} Following the conclusion of the FIFA Confederations Cup tournament, he then started the next six Japan international matches in the absence of Uchida, who suffered a torn tendon and was eventually out for the 2013–14 season.{{cite news |script-title=ja:内田不在の右ＳＢ 酒井宏＆駒野が行く|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/p-sc-tp2-20140304-1265438.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=4 March 2014|access-date=19 June 2018}}

{{cite news|title=SAMURAI BLUEドイツ遠征に酒井宏樹選手が復帰、旗手、相馬、町野選手も選出|url=https://www.jfa.jp/samuraiblue/news/00030558/|website=Japan Football Association|language=ja|date=16 September 2022|access-date=23 September 2024}} Sakai made his first appearance for the Samurai Blue in eight months, starting a match, in a 2–0 win against [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]].{{cite news|title=日本代表がアメリカ代表に2発快勝！ 先制点の鎌田大地が躍動、三笘薫がトドメの追加点|url=https://www.soccer-king.jp/news/japan/national/20220923/1691894.html|website=Soccer King|language=ja|date=23 September 2022|access-date=23 September 2024}} On 1 November 2022, he was named in the final squad for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] in Qatar.{{cite news|title=FIFAワールドカップカタール2022™ SAMURAI BLUE（日本代表）メンバー|url=https://www.jfa.jp/news/00030869/|website=Japan Football Association|language=ja|date=1 November 2022|access-date=23 September 2024}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/192924/|title=酒井宏樹、FIFAワールドカップカタール2022の抱負を語る|website=Urawa Red Diamonds|language=ja|date=1 November 2022|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221101124355/https://www.urawa-reds.co.jp/topteamtopics/192924/|archive-date=1 November 2022|url-status=live}} On 24 November 2022, Sakai started in the right–back position against [[Germany national football team|Germany]] and played 75 minutes before being substituted for [[Takumi Minamino]], who played a role for the equalising goal, in eventual Japan's 2–1 win.{{cite news|title=【Match Report】SAMURAI BLUE、ドイツに歴史的な逆転勝利で白星発進|url=https://www.jfa.jp/samuraiblue/worldcup_2022/news/00031096/|website=Japan Football Association|language=ja|date=24 November 2022|access-date=23 September 2024}} His next appearance for the Samurai Blue came against [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]] on 5 December 2022, coming on as a 75th-minute substitute, as the match eventually ended 1–1 with Japan crashing out after their defeat on penalties.{{cite news|title=【Match Report】SAMURAI BLUE、クロアチアにPK戦で敗れて16強越えならず|url=http://www.jfa.jp/samuraiblue/worldcup_2022/news/00031190/|website=Japan Football Association|language=ja|date=6 December 2022|access-date=23 September 2024}} Following the end of the tournament, he has not been called up the Samurai Blue's squad since. ==Personal life== Growing up, Sakai comes from a studious family, as his father is a doctor. One of his older brother is a researcher. Sakai said his idol growing up was [[Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)|Ronaldo]] and watched his performance in the [[2002 FIFA World Cup]]. In 2014, Sakai revealed that he married a non-celebrity woman and described her as supportive of his football career.{{cite news |script-title=ja:日本代表ＤＦ酒井宏樹が一般女性と結婚|url=https://www.daily.co.jp/newsflash/soccer/2014/08/24/0007268208.shtml|publisher=Daily Sport Online|language=ja|date=24 August 2014|access-date=19 June 2018}}
{{cite news |script-title=ja:酒井宏樹が結婚！「勝てて伝えることができてよかった」|url=https://www.sponichi.co.jp/soccer/news/2014/08/24/kiji/K20140824008802790.html|publisher=Sponichi|language=ja|date=24 August 2014|access-date=19 June 2018}} It was announced in November 2014 that Sakai would become a father and his wife gave birth to a baby girl in January 2015.{{cite news |script-title=ja:酒井宏がパパに「ハノーバー中が喜び」独紙|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/world/news/f-sc-tp3-20141106-1392779.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=6 November 2014|access-date=19 June 2018}}
{{cite news |script-title=ja:ハノーバー酒井宏がパパに|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/world/news/p-sc-tp3-20141107-1392923.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=7 November 2014|access-date=19 June 2018}}
{{cite news |script-title=ja:ハノーファー酒井宏に第一子が誕生|url=https://www.footballchannel.jp/2015/01/14/post65915/|publisher=Football Channel|language=ja|date=14 January 2015|access-date=19 June 2018}} On 27 September 2019, he announced that he's a father for the second time.{{cite news|title=マルセイユ酒井宏樹に第２子誕生「全ての方に感謝」|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/world/news/201908270000629.html|website=Nikkan Sports|language=fr|date=27 September 2019|access-date=23 September 2024}} Sakai is a fan of [[Miso soup]] and once said: "Take only miso soup because miso soup is a necessity for me."{{cite news |script-title=ja:大津、酒井の海外プレーの"ミソ"は… |url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/japan/news/f-sc-tp2-20120701-976285.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=1 July 2012|access-date=19 June 2018}} In addition to speaking Japanese, Sakai speaks Portuguese, German (having learned the language twice a week during his time at Hannover 96), French and English.{{cite web|url=https://www.hannover96.de/newscenter/news/details/13769-ich-moechte-in-hannover-fuss-fassen.html|title=Ich möchte in Hannover Fuß fassen|website=Hannover 96|language=de|date=4 July 2012|access-date=23 September 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240912192045/https://www.hannover96.de/newscenter/news/details/13769-ich-moechte-in-hannover-fuss-fassen.html|archive-date=12 September 2024|url-status=live}}

{{cite news|title=Les étrangers en Ligue 1, le français sur le bout de la langue|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Article/Les-etrangers-en-ligue-1-le-francais-sur-le-bout-de-la-langue/1220217|website=L’Equipe|language=fr|date=5 February 2021|access-date=23 September 2024}}{{cite news|title=OM – Insolite : quand Sakai parle du temps à Marseille : "Ça caille"|url=https://www.laprovence.com/actu/en-direct/4724620/om-insolite-quand-sakai-parle-du-temps-a-marseille-ca-caille.html|website=La Provence|language=fr|date=25 November 2017|access-date=23 September 2024}} Since moving to Europe, Sakai spoke out the culture in Germany and France.{{cite news |script-title=ja:酒井宏樹、日本の守備文化はヨーロッパと異なると指摘「守備の考え方が違うと感じますね」|url=https://www.footballchannel.jp/2016/11/19/post185777/|publisher=Football Channel Website|language=ja|date=19 November 2016|access-date=19 June 2018}} In May 2018, Sakai published his first book titled "Resetting Power 'Nature and the Mind Becomes Stronger' 46 Concept".{{cite news |script-title=ja:弱気で人見知りがなぜマルセイユで…?酒井宏樹が活躍の秘訣を著書で明かす! |url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?245619-245619-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=25 May 2018|access-date=19 June 2018}}

'''Fernando Javier Llorente Torres''' ({{IPA|es|feɾˈnando ʎoˈɾente ˈtores}}; born 26 February 1985), nicknamed ''El Rey León'' ("[[The Lion King]]" in Spanish),<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2010/05/26/mas_futbol/1274855246_850215.html|title=Un 'rey león' en el área|trans-title=A 'lion king' in the box|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|first=P. P.|last=San Martín|language=es|date=26 May 2010|access-date=1 April 2025}}</ref> is a Spanish former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[striker (association football)|striker]].

He started his career with [[Athletic Bilbao]], working his way through the various youth ranks and, after making his first team debut in 2005, becoming one of the most important offensive players for the club in the following decade. He scored 29 goals in all competitions in the [[2011–12 Athletic Bilbao season|2011–12 season]], and was described as a "Bilbao legend".<ref name=Standard>{{cite news|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/chelsea-on-high-alert-after-striker-fernando-llorente-rejects-new-deal-with-athletic-bilbao-8026359.html|title=Chelsea on high alert after striker Fernando Llorente rejects new deal with Athletic Bilbao|newspaper=[[Evening Standard]]|date=9 August 2012|access-date=10 August 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://athletic.elcorreo.com/noticias/201510/08/pichichi-reune-goleadores-rojiblancos-20151008210636.html|title=Los discípulos de Pichichi|trans-title=Pichichi's disciples|newspaper=[[El Correo]]|first=Javier|last=Ortiz de Lazcano|language=es|date=9 October 2015|access-date=11 February 2016}}</ref> He signed with [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in 2013, and won the [[Serie A]] title twice during his two-year spell there. Subsequently, he spent [[2015–16 La Liga|2015–16]] back in Spain with [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] before moving to [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]] in 2016 and [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] the following year, reaching the [[2019 UEFA Champions League final|2019 Champions League final]] with the latter. He retired aged 38, following stints at [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]], [[Udinese Calcio|Udinese]] and [[SD Eibar|Eibar]].

A [[Spain national football team|Spain international]] from 2008 to 2013, Llorente was a member of the squads which won the [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010 World Cup]] and [[UEFA Euro 2012|Euro 2012]].

==Early years==
Born in [[Pamplona]], Llorente grew up in the municipality of [[Rincón de Soto]] in [[La Rioja (Spain)|La Rioja]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.diariodenavarra.es/actualidad/noticia.asp?not=2009040901275783&dia=20090409&seccion=deportes&seccion2=osasunaFutbol|title=Llorente nació en la capital navarra "de casualidad"|trans-title=Llorente was born in Navarre capital "by chance"|newspaper=[[Diario de Navarra]]|language=es|date=9 April 2009|access-date=12 September 2010|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110724011342/http://www.diariodenavarra.es/actualidad/noticia.asp?not=2009040901275783&dia=20090409&seccion=deportes&seccion2=osasunaFutbol|archive-date=24 July 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.elmundodeportivo.es/preview/2005/01/18/pagina-24/1532732/pdf.html|title=Fue todo tan rápido que ni me lo creía|trans-title=Everything was so fast i could not believe it|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|first=Alberto|last=García|language=es|date=18 January 2005|access-date=12 September 2010}}{{Dead link|date=September 2026|bot=InternetArchiveBot}}</ref> He joined [[Athletic Bilbao]]'s youth system in 1996 at the age of 11, [[Athletic Bilbao signing policy|being eligible]] through his [[Navarre]]se roots.

==Club career==
===Athletic Bilbao===
Llorente spent several seasons in the various junior levels of the club, playing alongside [[Fernando Amorebieta]]<ref>{{cite news|url=http://athletic.elcorreo.com/noticias/2012-03-01/amistoso-entre-llorente-amorebieta-20120301.html|title=Amistoso entre Llorente y Amorebieta|trans-title=Friendly between Llorente and Amorebieta|newspaper=El Correo|first=J.|last=Gómez Peña|language=es|date=1 March 2012|access-date=24 July 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191003103758/https://athletic.elcorreo.com/noticias/2012-03-01/amistoso-entre-llorente-amorebieta-20120301.html|archive-date=3 October 2019}}</ref> and moving to their farm team [[CD Basconia|Basconia]] in [[Tercera División]] in 2003.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=1056&idi=2|title=Staff restructuring|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=26 June 2003|access-date=14 December 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090210184726/http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=1056&idi=2|archive-date=10 February 2009}}</ref> He gradually improved, leading to promotion to [[Bilbao Athletic]] – Athletic's reserves – in the [[Segunda División B]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=1956&idi=2|title=Incorporations of Bilbao Athletic|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=1 June 2004|access-date=14 December 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090210183829/http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=1956&idi=2|archive-date=10 February 2009}}</ref>

After scoring four goals for the B's in the first half of the season, Llorente was rewarded with a contract extension until June 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=2523&idi=2|title=Fernando Llorente's contract extension|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=11 December 2004|access-date=14 December 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090210182116/http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=2523&idi=2|archive-date=10 February 2009}}</ref> On 16 January 2005, he made his first-team and [[La Liga]] debut in a 1–1 home draw against [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=2648&idi=2|title=Athletic Club 1-Espanyol 1: No luck|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=16 January 2005|access-date=14 December 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090210182125/http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=2648&idi=2|archive-date=10 February 2009}}</ref> Three days later, in a [[Copa del Rey]] match against [[UD Lanzarote|Lanzarote]], he scored a [[hat-trick]] in a [[2004–05 Copa del Rey|6–0 victory]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=2664&idi=2|title=Athletic Club 6-Lanzarote 0: It advanced|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=20 January 2005|access-date=14 December 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090210181315/http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=2664&idi=2|archive-date=10 February 2009}}</ref> He went on to feature in all but five of the nineteen remaining league games, scoring three goals, and also played in four domestic cup matches and the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]] [[2004–05 UEFA Cup|round of 32 tie]] against [[FK Austria Wien|Austria Wien]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/diario/2005/02/28/deportes/1109545219_850215.html|title=Pesadilla en San Mamés|trans-title=Nightmare in San Mamés|newspaper=[[El País]]|first=Eduardo|last=Rodrigálvarez|language=es|date=28 February 2005|access-date=20 September 2019}}</ref>

Before [[2005–06 La Liga|2005–06]], Llorente exchanged his squad number of 32 for the number 9 jersey.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=3369&idi=2|title=Numbers for the 2005–2006 season|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=29 July 2005|access-date=14 December 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121006200213/http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=3369&idi=2|archive-date=6 October 2012}}</ref> He scored on the opening day, a [[Basque Country (autonomous community)|Basque]] [[Local derby|derby]] 3–0 win over [[Real Sociedad]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=3466&idi=2|title=Athletic Club 3 Real Sociedad 0: An excellent start to the season|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=28 August 2005|access-date=14 December 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090210181325/http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=3466&idi=2|archive-date=10 February 2009}}</ref> but, throughout the campaign, found goals hard to come by. This could be partly attributed to a series of injuries including a [[knee]] strain,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=3639&idi=2|title=Urzaiz fit to play, Prieto, Guerrero and Llorente sidelined|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=19 October 2005|access-date=14 December 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090210184146/http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=3639&idi=2|archive-date=10 February 2009}}</ref> [[gastroenteritis]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=3905&idi=2|title=Several players injured as a result of the match|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=8 January 2006|access-date=14 December 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090210182145/http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=3905&idi=2|archive-date=10 February 2009}}</ref> and a muscle injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=4253&idi=2|title=Llorente and Lacruz: Muscle overload|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=24 April 2006|access-date=14 December 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090210185150/http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=4253&idi=2|archive-date=10 February 2009}}</ref> He ended the season with just four goals, two in the league and as many in the Cup, both against [[CE L'Hospitalet|Hospitalet]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=3724&idi=2|title=L'Hospitalet 1-Athletic Club 3: To the Round of 16|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=9 November 2005|access-date=14 December 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090210181330/http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=3724&idi=2|archive-date=10 February 2009}}</ref>

On 13 July 2006, Llorente signed a new contract until June 2011, which included a buy-out clause of between [[Euro|€]]30 and 50 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=4416&idi=2|title=Llorente's renewal: press conference|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=13 July 2006|access-date=14 December 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090210181443/http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=4416&idi=2|archive-date=10 February 2009}}</ref> He started [[2006–07 La Liga|the season]] as arguably the club's fourth-choice striker, behind [[Aritz Aduriz]], [[Joseba Etxeberria]] and veteran [[Ismael Urzaiz]]. The team's poor form and lack of goals led to coach [[Félix Sarriugarte]] rotating the players, allowing Llorente to force his way back into the side; he ended the campaign with only two goals in 23 matches, although he did score an important one in the closing minutes of a 1–1 draw at [[Valencia CF|Valencia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/203868?cc=5739|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130102194853/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/203868?cc=5739|url-status=dead|archive-date=2 January 2013|title=Valencia 1–1 Athletic Bilbao|publisher=[[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]]|date=11 November 2006|access-date=2 August 2012}}</ref>

In preparation for [[2007–08 La Liga|2007–08]], Llorente scored six goals in as many pre-season matches, and another against [[CD Numancia|Numancia]] in the ''Caja Duero'' Trophy. His form led to him becoming Athletic's first-choice forward, and although he started the campaign poorly, he ended it with a total of 11 league goals as the side finished in mid-table. His tally included four goals in two games against Valencia, both impressive wins,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=6217&idi=2|title=Valencia 0 – Athletic Club 3: A perfect match|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=2 December 2007|access-date=14 December 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090210183834/http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=6217&idi=2|archive-date=10 February 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=6731&idi=2|title=Athletic Club 5 Valencia 1: A perfect night|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=20 April 2008|access-date=14 December 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090210185218/http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=6731&idi=2|archive-date=10 February 2009}}</ref> and further strikes against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=6417&idi=2|title=Athletic Club 1-FC [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=6518&idi=2|title=Athletic Club 1-Villarreal 2: From better to worse|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=22 February 2008|access-date=14 December [[Atlético Madrid]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=6494&idi=2|title=Atlético de Madrid 1-Athletic Club 2: A step in the right
