Before [[2008–09 La Liga|2008–09]], Llorente was confident of a successful season. "I know that I am capable of scoring goals and having a good year and I want to start this term in the same form that I ended the last one in" he said.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.allthingsmallorca.com/news/?p=324|title=Aduriz move surprised everyone – Llorente|publisher=All Things Mallorca|date=2 September 2008|access-date=14 December 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111003045327/http://www.allthingsmallorca.com/news/?p=324|archive-date=3 October 2011}}</ref> Despite the team's modest start he scored 14 league goals – a career-best – with another four in [[2008–09 Copa del Rey|the Cup]], helping his team reach [[2009 Copa del Rey Final|the final]] against Barcelona (a 4–1 loss).<ref name=COPA>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2009/05/13/futbol/copa_rey/1242251735.html|title=El Barça se corona por aplastamiento|trans-title=Barça crowned through crushing|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|first=Delfín|last=Melero|language=es|date=13 May 2009|access-date=23 January 2018}}</ref>

In the [[2009–10 La Liga|2009–10 season]], Llorente again reached double figures. He led all scorers in the [[2009–10 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] for a long period with eight goals, and added fourteen in the league as Athletic eventually finished in eighth place.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2010/02/08/actualidad/1265617316_850215.html|title=Llorente, el goleador silencioso|trans-title=Llorente, the silent scorer|newspaper=El País|first=Eduardo|last=Rodrigálvarez|language=es|date=8 February 2010|access-date=1 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://sevilla.abc.es/deportes/orgullodenervion/noticias/sevilla-fc/fernando-llorente-casi-20-goles-de-media-por-temporada-89388-1440672433.html|title=Fernando Llorente: casi 20 goles de media por temporada|trans-title=Fernando Llorente: an average of nearly 20 goals per season|newspaper=[[ABC (newspaper)|ABC]]|language=es|date=27 August 2015|access-date=1 March 2018|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180301164512/http://sevilla.abc.es/deportes/orgullodenervion/noticias/sevilla-fc/fernando-llorente-casi-20-goles-de-media-por-temporada-89388-1440672433.html|archive-date=1 March 2018}}</ref>
[[File:Fernando Llorente CAMP NOU 2012 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Llorente (foreground) playing for Athletic Bilbao against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in 2012]]

On 28 August 2010, Llorente scored the first goal of the [[2010–11 La Liga|2010–11 campaign]], in a 1–0 win at [[Hércules CF|Hércules]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/301988?cc=5739|title=Llorente lifts Bilbao|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=28 August 2010|access-date=23 April 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121026124558/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/301988?cc=5739|archive-date=26 October 2012}}</ref> His form continued in the next ten league fixtures as he found the net seven times, eventually finishing the season with 18 goals (19 overall) as Athletic qualified for the Europa League.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2011/05/22/futbol/equipos/athletic/1306017676.html|title=Llorente, entre los 20 máximos goleadores de la historia del Athletic|trans-title=Llorente, 20th in Athletic's all-time scoring list|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=22 May 2011|access-date=18 April 2019}}</ref>

Between January and February 2012, Llorente scored five goals in two away matches in only four days: he started with a hat-trick in a 3–2 win against [[Rayo Vallecano]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/323841?cc=5739|title=Llorente hits hat-trick in Athletic win|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=28 January 2012|access-date=1 February 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120715175030/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/323841?cc=5739|archive-date=15 July 2012}}</ref> and added two in a 2–1 defeat of [[CD Mirandés|Mirandés]] in the [[2011–12 Copa del Rey|Spanish Cup semi-finals]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/marcador/futbol/2011_12/copa/semifinal/ida/mir_ath/|title=El 'Rey León' saca las garras en Anduva|trans-title='Lion King' shows claws in Anduva|newspaper=Marca|first=Diego|last=Acedo|language=es|date=1 February 2012|access-date=1 February 2012}}</ref> In the next two matches, both at home, he scored three more, one against Espanyol in the league<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/323832?cc=5739|title=Albin's late strike earns Espanyol a point|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=4 February 2012|access-date=7 February 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120718000031/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/323832?cc=5739|archive-date=18 July 2012}}</ref> and two against Mirandés.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/marcador/futbol/2011_12/copa/semifinal/vuelta/ath_mir/|title=Grandes y gigantes|trans-title=Great ones and giants|newspaper=Marca|first=Delfín|last=Melero|language=es|date=6 February 2012|access-date=7 February 2012}}</ref>

Llorente scored in both legs of the [[2011–12 UEFA Europa League|2011–12 Europa League round of 16]] against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], as Athletic won both games and went through 5–3 on aggregate.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/01fb-0e7d1140b526-c2e241809842-1000--enterprising-athletic-stun-united-at-old-trafford/|title=Enterprising Athletic stun United at Old Trafford|publisher=UEFA|first=Simon|last=Hart|date=8 March 2012|access-date=27 March 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/01fb-0e8186497a8f-4a3adcb0d228-1000--athletic-see-off-united-with-room-to-spare/|title=Athletic see off United with room to spare|publisher=UEFA|first=Paul|last=Bryan|date=15 March 2012|access-date=27 March 2012}}</ref> In the next round he scored twice at [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]] in a 4–2 win,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/01fb-0e7d82121f3b-189fe08dee7d-1000--schalke-stunned-by-late-athletic-fightback/|title=Schalke stunned by late Athletic fightback|publisher=UEFA|date=29 March 2012|access-date=21 August 2012}}</ref> helping the team eventually reach [[2012 UEFA Europa League final|the final]]. His seven goals in the tournament also made him the club's [[Athletic Bilbao in European football|highest scorer in European competition]], beating the total of 11 set by [[Dani (footballer, born 1951)|Dani]] in the 1980s,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vavel.com/es/futbol/athletic-de-bilbao/123102.html|title=Llorente supera a Dani como máximo goleador del Athletic en Europa|trans-title=Llorente overtakes Dani as Athletic's top scorer in Europe|publisher=Vavel|first=Yolanda|last=Espinosa|language=es|date=16 March 2012|access-date=18 July 2017}}</ref> later surpassed by Aduriz in 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/newsid=2410926.html|title=Aduriz, 'Pichichi' rojiblanco en Europa|trans-title=Aduriz, red-and-white 'Pichichi' in Europe|publisher=UEFA|first=Gonzalo|last=Aguado|language=es|date=3 November 2016|access-date=18 July 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170906163517/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/newsid=2410926.html|archive-date=6 September 2017}}</ref>

In August 2012, Llorente refused to sign a new deal with Athletic Bilbao, fuelling speculation that he might be leaving.<ref name=Standard/> Following a 2–0 [[Basque derby]] loss at Real Sociedad on 29 September, in which he was a late [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]], he got into an argument with manager [[Marcelo Bielsa]]; two days later he walked out of training early and was sent to practice with the youth squad<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1176799/fernando-llorente-walks-out-of-training-after-bielsa-row?cc=5901|title=Llorente walks out of training|publisher=ESPN FC|first=Dermot|last=Corrigan|date=1 October 2012|access-date=2 October 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121005013713/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1176799/fernando-llorente-walks-out-of-training-after-bielsa-row?cc=5901|archive-date=5 October 2012}}</ref> and, as a result, his relationship with the club's supporters and president [[Josu Urrutia]] further deteriorated.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/news/story/_/id/1233014/fernando-llorente-and-bilbao-clash-over-no-show?cc=5739|title=Llorente and Bilbao clash over no-show|publisher=ESPN FC|first=Dermot|last=Corrigan|date=20 November 2012|access-date=27 December 2013}}</ref>

On 3 January 2013, Athletic confirmed that Llorente would be holding talks with [[Juventus FC|Juventus]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/jan/03/fernando-llorente-juventus-athletic-bilbao|title=Fernando Llorente to hold talks with Juventus, Athletic Bilbao confirm|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=3 January 2013|access-date=21 January 2013}}</ref> On 21 January, the latter's sporting director, [[Giuseppe Marotta]], stated that he was "very optimistic" that the player would join on 1 July, with Urrutia believed to be unwilling to allow him to leave in the January [[transfer window]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1307464/juventus-confident-signing-llorente?cc=5739|title=Juventus confident of signing Llorente|publisher=ESPN FC|first=Dermot|last=Corrigan|date=21 January 2013|access-date=21 January 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130126181559/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1307464/juventus-confident-signing-llorente?cc=5739|archive-date=26 January 2013}}</ref> Three days later, the club announced he would sign a four-year deal on 1 July when his contract expired;<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.juventus.com/juve/en/news/24_gen2013_llorente|title=Llorente to join Juventus|publisher=Juventus F.C.|date=24 January 2013|access-date=24 January 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130127005217/http://www.juventus.com/juve/en/news/24_gen2013_llorente|archive-date=27 January 2013}}</ref> Juventus also paid his agent €3.038 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.juventus.com/wps/wcm/connect/8a80cb53-b24f-46b1-966e-73f0eb2787bd/Relazione+finanziaria+semestrale+31+dicembre+2013+definitiva.pdf?MOD=AJPERES&CACHEID=8a80cb53-b24f-46b1-966e-73f0eb2787bd|title=Relazione finanziaria semestrale al 31 dicembre 2013|trans-title=Semestral financial report up to 31 December 2013|publisher=Juventus F.C.|language=it|date=28 February 2014|access-date=27 March 2014}}{{dead link|date=December 2016|bot=InternetArchiveBot|fix-attempted=yes}}</ref>

Llorente scored just five goals in 36 competitive matches in his [[2012–13 La Liga|final year]], playing mainly as a back-up for Aduriz.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2012/12/27/futbol/equipos/athletic/1356597969.html|title=Aduriz eclipsa a Llorente|trans-title=Aduriz eclipses Llorente|newspaper=Marca|first=Macu|last=Briones|language=es|date=27 December 2012|access-date=1 July 2013}}</ref><ref name=FE>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-espana.net/32286/llorente-unveiled-juve-player|title=Llorente unveiled as a Juve player|publisher=Football España|date=2 July 2013|access-date=2 July 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170804053751/http://www.football-espana.net/32286/llorente-unveiled-juve-player|archive-date=4 August 2017}}</ref>

===Juventus===
[[File:Arturo Vidal and Fernando Llorente, Real Madrid vs Juventus, 24 October 2013 Champions League.JPG|thumb|Llorente (right) before a [[UEFA Champions League]] match against [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in 2013]]
Llorente officially became a Juventus player on 1 July 2013 after passing a medical at the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/news/story/_/id/1489465/juventus-unveil-fernando-llorente---live?campaign=rss&source=soccernet&cc=5739#|title=Llorente relishing Tevez link-up|publisher=ESPN FC|first=Ben|last=Gladwell|date=2 July 2013|access-date=2 July 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1502839-juventus-sign-fernando-llorente-on-a-free-transfer|title=Juventus sign Fernando Llorente on a free transfer|publisher=[[Bleacher Report]]|first=Adrian|last=Agius|date=26 January 2013|access-date=1 July 2013}}</ref> He was given the number 14 shirt,<ref name=FE/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/35963/llorente-picks-no-14-shirt|title=Llorente picks No 14 shirt?|publisher=Football Italia|date=1 July 2013|access-date=1 July 2013}}</ref> and scored his first goal in [[Serie A]] on 22 September when he started in a 2–1 home win against [[Hellas Verona FC|Hellas Verona]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.repubblica.it/sport/calcio/serie-a/2013/09/22/news/juventus-verona_2-1_tevez_super_llorente_subito_decisivo-67047082/|title=Juventus-Verona 2–1: Tevez super, Llorente subito decisive|trans-title=Juventus-Verona 2–1: Tevez super, Llorente decisive at once|newspaper=[[La Repubblica]]|first=Francesco|last=Carci|language=it|date=22 September 2013|access-date=18 April 2019}}</ref>

Llorente found the net in his second and third ever appearances in the [[UEFA Champions League]], both times against [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League|2013–14 group stage]] (a 2–1 away loss, and a 2–2 home draw).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/020e-0ea036f32831-eaf70134172e-1000--ronaldo-double-sinks-ten-man-juventus/|title=Ronaldo double sinks ten-man Juventus|publisher=UEFA|first=Paul|last=Bryan|date=23 October 2013|access-date=1 April 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/020f-0e87344576ea-4156919134b9-1000--juventus-fight-back-to-hold-madrid/|title=Juventus fight back to hold Madrid|publisher=UEFA|first=Paolo|last=Menicucci|date=5 November 2013|access-date=1 April 2025}}</ref> In November 2013 he spoke critically about his relationship with former manager Bielsa in an exclusive interview with ''[[La Gazzetta dello Sport]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/es/news/27/liga-de-espa%C3%B1a/2013/11/16/4411985/fernando-llorente-carga-contra-marcelo-bielsa|title=Fernando Llorente carga contra Marcelo Bielsa|trans-title=Fernando Llorente blasts Marcelo Bielsa|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|language=es|date=16 November 2013|access-date=27 December 2013}}</ref> On 1 December he scored in injury time, the only goal of the match at home against [[Udinese Calcio|Udinese]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/uk/en/report/377178/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5739|title=Last-gasp Llorente winner|publisher=ESPN FC|date=1 December 2013|access-date=2 December 2013}}</ref>

Llorente's first two goals of 2014 came on 12 January, from a header and from close range as Juventus defeated [[Cagliari Calcio|Cagliari]] 4–1 away to extend their winning league run to 11 matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/25630488|title=Cagliari 1–4 Juventus|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=12 January 2014|access-date=18 August 2014}}</ref> On 7 April, he scored both of his team's goals in a 2–0 home win over [[US Livorno 1915|Livorno]], guaranteeing at least second place and Champions League qualification.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fourfourtwo.com/au/news/serie-juventus-2-livorno-0|title=Serie A: Juventus 2 Livorno 0|publisher=[[FourFourTwo]]|date=7 April 2014|access-date=18 August 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140819193837/http://www.fourfourtwo.com/au/news/serie-juventus-2-livorno-0|archive-date=19 August 2014}}</ref> On the final day of [[2013–14 Serie A|the season]], again against Cagliari, he contributed one goal as Juve won 3–0 and clinched the championship, finishing with a record 102 points.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/27463440|title=Juventus 3–0 Cagliari|publisher=BBC Sport|date=18 May 2014|access-date=18 August 2014}}</ref>

On 6 June 2015, Llorente came off the bench and played five minutes in [[2015 UEFA Champions League final|the final]] of the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]], lost 3–1 to Barcelona at Berlin's [[Olympiastadion (Berlin)|Olympiastadion]].<ref name=UCL15>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0252-0cd2c6a4864d-8c8d00efd1bd-1000--barcelona-see-off-juventus-to-claim-fifth-title/|title=Barcelona see off Juventus to claim fifth title|publisher=UEFA|first=Andrew|last=Haslam|date=6 June 2015|access-date=7 June 2015}}</ref>

===Sevilla===
On 27 August 2015, [[free agent]] Llorente signed a three-year contract with [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] with a buyout clause of €20 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/71669/official-llorente-sevilla-free|title=Official: Llorente to Sevilla for free|publisher=Football Italia|date=27 August 2015|access-date=27 August 2015}}</ref> He made his league debut three days later, playing the full 90 minutes in a 3–0 home defeat against Atlético Madrid.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/aug/30/atletico-madrid-sevilla-match-report|title=Atlético Madrid enjoy easy win over Sevilla as Koke ends his goal drought|newspaper=The Guardian|date=30 August 2015|access-date=9 November 2015}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club in a 2–1 loss to [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta]], also at the [[Ramón Sánchez Pizjuán Stadium]], on 20 September.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.us/spanish-primera-division/match/433941/sevilla-fc-celta-vigo/report|title=Sevilla's early season struggles continue with home defeat to Celta Vigo|publisher=ESPN FC|date=20 September 2015|access-date=9 November 2015}}</ref>

On 8 November 2015, after replacing newly signed [[Ciro Immobile]] for the final 20 minutes of the league game against Real Madrid, Llorente headed home after only four minutes in an eventual 3–2 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/34749815|title=Sevilla 3–2 Real Madrid|publisher=BBC Sport|date=8 November 2015|access-date=1 September 2020}}</ref> Exactly one month later, also at home, he scored the only goal in a 1–0 victory over his former club Juventus in the final match of the [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League group stage|Champions League group stage]], which meant Sevilla overtook [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]] into third spot and [[2015–16 UEFA Europa League|qualification for the Europa League knockout phase]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0228-0e92cb1b4e74-02de48a3e58c-1000--llorente-deals-juve-blow-to-earn-sevilla-third-place/|title=Llorente deals Juve blow to earn Sevilla third place|publisher=UEFA|first=Nick|last=Aitken|date=8 December 2015|access-date=8 December 2015}}</ref> The club went on to win the competition for the third time in a row, with the player being an unused substitute in [[2016 UEFA Europa League Final|the final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0250-0c51138a700a-9c0eb3116927-1000--sevilla-make-it-three-in-row-at-liverpool-s-expense/|title=Sevilla make it three in row at Liverpool's expense|publisher=UEFA|date=18 May 2016|access-date=17 January 2018}}</ref> He came off the bench during extra time in the [[2016 Copa del Rey Final|Copa del Rey Final]] four days later, which they lost to Barcelona.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/may/22/barcelona-sevilla-copa-del-rey-match-report|title= Jordi Alba and Neymar secure Barcelona Copa del Rey victory|newspaper=The Guardian|first=Sid|last=Lowe|date=22 May 2016|access-date=17 January 2018}}</ref>

===Swansea City===
On 4 August 2016, it was announced that Llorente had signed a two-year deal with [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/aug/04/swansea-agree-sign-fernando-llorente-sevilla|title=Swansea agree terms to sign Fernando Llorente from Sevilla on two-year deal|newspaper=The Guardian|date=4 August 2016|access-date=4 August 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.swanseacity.com/news/article/2016-17/spain-fernando-llorente-joins-swansea-city-sevilla-3227792.aspx|title=World Cup winner Llorente joins Swans|publisher=Swansea City A.F.C.|date=5 August 2016|access-date=5 August 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220706061807/https://www.swanseacity.com/news/article/2016-17/spain-fernando-llorente-joins-swansea-city-sevilla-3227792.aspx|archive-date=6 July 2022}}</ref> He made his [[Premier League]] debut nine days later, playing the full ninety minutes in a 1–0 away win against [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/36994442|title=Burnley 0–1 Swansea City|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Tim|last=Oscroft|date=13 August 2016|access-date=13 August 2016}}</ref>

On 26 November 2016, Llorente scored two injury-time goals to help the hosts defeat [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] 5–4.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/nov/26/swansea-city-crystal-palace-premier-league-match-report|title=Swansea City stun Crystal Palace as Fernando Llorente settles 5–4 thriller|newspaper=The Guardian|first=Stuart|last=James|date=27 November 2016|access-date=11 December 2016}}</ref> He also scored twice two matches later, again at the [[Liberty Stadium]], against [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] (3–0).<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/swansea-vs-sunderland-match-report-a7467436.html|title=Swansea vs Sunderland match report: Fernando Llorente brace puts Black Cats to the sword|newspaper=[[The Independent]]|first=Graham|last=Clutton|date=10 December 2016|access-date=11 December 2016}}</ref> He finished [[2016–17 Swansea City A.F.C. season|his first season]] with 15 goals, as the team avoided relegation.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.walesonline.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/swansea-city-striker-fernando-llorente-13089593|title=Swansea City striker Fernando Llorente will 'wait and see' what happens in the summer amid expected transfer interest|publisher=[[Media Wales#WalesOnline|Wales Online]]|first=Chris|last=Wathan|date=25 May 2017|access-date=6 June 2017}}</ref>

A fractured [[arm]] sustained while cycling during his summer holiday caused Llorente to miss the opening weeks of the [[2017–18 Premier League|2017–18 campaign]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40448715|title=Fernando Llorente: Swansea City striker likely to miss season start with broken arm|publisher=BBC Sport|date=31 July 2017|access-date=1 September 2017}}</ref>

===Tottenham Hotspur===
On 31 August 2017, Llorente joined [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] on a two-year deal for a reported fee of £12.1 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/fernando-llorente-first-interview-310817/|title='I can do more in my career, and my dream is to do that here' – Fernando Llorente|publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C|date=31 August 2017|access-date=31 August 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11675/11013439/fernando-llorente-joins-tottenham-from-swansea|title=Fernando Llorente joins Tottenham from Swansea|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|date=1 September 2017|access-date=2 January 2018}}</ref> He made his debut for the club on 13 September, replacing [[Harry Kane]] for the last minutes of a 3–1 home win over [[Borussia Dortmund]] in the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League|Champions League group stage]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/mauricio-pochettino-call-swayed-me-away-from-chelsea/cpmsdgc8rqu51uj759w3m3cwe|title=Tottenham striker Llorente reveals reason behind Chelsea snub|publisher=Goal|first=Matt|last=Dorman|date=15 September 2017|access-date=15 September 2017}}</ref> He made his first start in the [[2017–18 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] tie against [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]] on 20 September,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/llorente-asks-tottenham-fans-patience-11207894|title=Tottenham new boy Fernando Llorente begs fans for time after unimpressive first start against Championship Barnsley|newspaper=[[Daily Mirror]]|first=Darren|last=Lewis|date=20 September 2017|access-date=27 October 2017}}</ref> then played in the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League|Champions League group stage]] match at Real Madrid which ended 1–1.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/real-madrid-1-tottenham-1-cristiano-ronaldo-penalty-denies-spurs-famous-champions-league-win-a3661216.html|title=Real Madrid 1 Tottenham 1: Cristiano Ronaldo penalty denies Spurs famous UEFA Champions League win|newspaper=Evening Standard|first=James|last=Olley|date=17 October 2017|access-date=21 October 2017}}</ref>

Llorente scored his first goal for Spurs on 6 December 2017, playing the full 90 minutes in the 3–0 Champions League win over [[APOEL FC|APOEL]] after his team had already progressed to the knockout stage as group winners.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/dec/06/tottenham-hotspur-apoel-nicosia-champions-league-match-report|title=Fernando Llorente off the mark for Tottenham in stroll against Apoel|newspaper=The Guardian|first=David|last=Hytner|date=6 December 2017|access-date=6 December 2017}}</ref> He made his first league start the following January, scoring in a 2–0 away win against his former club Swansea.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2018/01/02/swansea-0-tottenham-2-fernando-llorente-scores-return-wales/|title=Swansea 0 Tottenham 2: Fernando Llorente scores on return to Wales as Spurs leapfrog Arsenal|newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|first=Alex|last=Bywater|date=2 January 2018|access-date=2 January 2018}}</ref>

Llorente scored a hat-trick in a 6–1 victory over [[Rochdale A.F.C.|Rochdale]] in the [[2017–18 FA Cup|fifth round]] of the [[FA Cup]], on 28 February 2018.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/tottenham-6-rochdale-1-fa-cup-var-fernando-llorente-hat-trick-wembley-snow-a3778491.html|title=Tottenham 6 Rochdale 1: Fernando Llorente hat-trick seals FA Cup win amid VAR woe and Wembley snow|newspaper=Evening Standard|first=Jack|last=Rosser|date=28 February 2018|access-date=28 February 2018}}</ref> On 4 January 2019, in [[2018–19 FA Cup|the third round]] of the next season's competition, he repeated the feat in a 7–0 away rout of [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/jan/04/tranmere-tottenham-fa-cup-match-report|title=Fernando Llorente hits hat-trick as Spurs steamroller Tranmere|newspaper=The Guardian|first=Paul|last=Wilson|date=4 January 2019|access-date=4 January 2019}}</ref> and helped the club record its biggest ever away win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/46697997|title=Tranmere Rovers 0–7 Tottenham: Fernando Llorente scores hat-trick in thrashing|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Matthew|last=Henry|date=4 January 2019|access-date=5 January 2019}}</ref> His first league start of [[2018–19 Premier League|the season]] took place 16 days later due to an injury to Kane, when Llorente scored an [[own goal]] in a 2–1 away win at [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46853938|title=Fulham 1–2 Tottenham Hotspur|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Mantej|last=Mann|date=20 January 2019|access-date=31 January 2019}}</ref> In the following league game, he scored a late winner to help defeat [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] 2–1 at [[Wembley Stadium]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46968493|title=Tottenham Hotspur 2–1 Watford|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Saj|last=Chowdhury|date=30 January 2019|access-date=31 January 2019}}</ref>

On 13 February 2019, Llorente scored the last goal in a [[2018–19 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|3–0 Champions League]] win over Borussia Dortmund, only three minutes after coming off the bench;<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2019/02/13/tottenham-vs-borussia-dortmund-champions-league-live-score-goals/|title=White-hot Tottenham as Son leads Dortmund destruction to put one foot in Champions League quarter-finals|newspaper=The Daily Telegraph|first=Jason|last=Burt|date=13 February 2019|access-date=14 February 2019}}</ref> it was his first career goal in the knockout stages of that competition, and 11th in total.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/champions-league/2019/02/14/5c649effca4741f7098b461d.html|title=Fernando Llorente, el goleador fiel a la Champions|trans-title=Fernando Llorente, the scorer married to the Champions|newspaper=Marca|first=Luis Alberto|last=Díaz|language=es|date=14 February 2019|access-date=22 February 2019}}</ref> On 17 April, in the same competition, he scored what turned out to be the winning goal in the quarter-final fixture against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] (the tie ended 4–4, Tottenham progressing on the [[away goals rule]]).<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/apr/17/manchester-city-tottenham-hotspur-champions-league-quarter-final-second-leg-match-report|title=Tottenham win Champions League epic as Llorente stuns Manchester City|newspaper=The Guardian|first=Daniel|last=Taylor|date=17 April 2019|access-date=18 April 2019}}</ref> In the second leg of the semi-final away to [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]], he replaced [[Victor Wanyama]] at half time and played a crucial role in helping his team come back from a three-goal aggregate deficit to make it 3–3 and progress again in the same fashion.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2019/05/08/ajax-vs-tottenham-hotspur-champions-league-semi-final-live-score|title=Tottenham into Champions League final after Lucas Moura seals another English miracle|newspaper=The Daily Telegraph|first1=Jason|last1=Burt|first2=Alan|last2=Tyers|date=9 May 2019|access-date=24 May 2019}}</ref><ref name=Praise>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/142041/napoli-leading-llorente-race|title=Napoli leading Llorente race|publisher=Football Italia|date=13 August 2019|access-date=28 November 2019}}</ref> In [[2019 UEFA Champions League final|the final]] played in [[Madrid]], he was introduced off the bench with eight minutes remaining and the side already behind, was unable to affect the outcome as [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] won 2–0 to take the trophy.<ref name=UCL19>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48368443|title=Tottenham Hotspur 0–2 Liverpool|first=Phil|last=McNulty|publisher=BBC Sport|date=1 June 2019|access-date=1 June 2019}}</ref>

Despite his success in the Champions League, Llorente's contract expired on 30 June 2019 with no official statement from Tottenham on his position.<ref name=Gold>{{cite web|url=https://www.football.london/tottenham-hotspur-fc/players/curious-case-fernando-llorente-tottenham-16535954|title=The curious case of Fernando Llorente and his Tottenham Hotspur contract explained|publisher=Football London|first=Alasdair|last=Gold|date=5 July 2019|access-date=2 September 2019}}</ref> His name was included in their 'released players' list submitted to the Premier League on 7 June 2019 (before he was actually released),<ref name=Gold/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/1238381|title=2018/19 Premier League clubs publish released lists|publisher=Premier League|date=10 June 2019|access-date=1 July 2019}}</ref> and his profile was later removed from the first team squad list on the website for the upcoming season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hitc.com/en-gb/2019/07/03/tottenham-drop-subtle-clue-about-fernando-llorente-despite-no-an/|title=Tottenham drop clue about Fernando Llorente despite no announcement|publisher=Here Is The City|first=Shane|last=Callaghan|date=3 July 2019|access-date=9 July 2019}}</ref>

===Napoli===
On 2 September 2019, Llorente joined [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]] on a [[Free transfer (association football)|free transfer]], returning to Italy four years after leaving Juventus.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://uk.sports.yahoo.com/news/napoli-sign-former-juventus-tottenham-070851402.html|title=Napoli sign former Juventus and Tottenham striker Llorente|publisher=[[Yahoo Sports]]|date=2 September 2019|access-date=2 September 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/12691/11800435/fernando-llorente-napoli-sign-former-tottenham-striker|title=Fernando Llorente: Napoli sign former Tottenham striker|publisher=Sky Sports|first=Max|last=Mathews|date=2 September 2019|access-date=2 September 2019}}</ref> He made his league debut against [[UC Sampdoria|Sampdoria]] on 14 September, where he provided an [[Assist (association football)|assist]] for [[Dries Mertens]] within minutes of coming on as a substitute to help the team win 2–0.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/SerieA/match/142391|title=Napoli 2–0 Sampdoria|publisher=Football Italia|date=14 September 2019|access-date=17 September 2019}}</ref> His first goal for the club came three days later in the [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League group stage|Champions League group stage]] game against Liverpool, scoring in injury time to seal a 2–0 victory.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2019/09/17/napoli-vs-liverpool-champions-league-live-score-latest-updates/|title=Liverpool have another off day at Napoli as Dries Mertens penalty and Fernando Llorente secure win for Italians|newspaper=The Daily Telegraph|first=Chris|last=Bascombe|date=17 September 2019|access-date=17 September 2019}}</ref>

Llorente continued to be used in the '[[Substitute (association football)#Super-sub|super-sub]]' role, as was previously the case at Tottenham; although he was rarely started, he was often brought on in the second half of matches, to cause problems for tiring opposition defences with his physical presence.<ref name=Praise/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://tbrfootball.com/jose-mourinho-and-rio-ferdinand-praise-super-sub-fernando-llorente/|title=Jose Mourinho and Rio Ferdinand praise super-sub Fernando Llorente|publisher=The Boot Room|first=Mathew|last=Nash|date=9 May 2019|access-date=28 November 2019}}</ref>

===Udinese===
On 27 January 2021, Llorente signed a one-and-a-half-year contract with Udinese.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.udinese.it/news/squadra/llorente-e-bianconero|title=Llorente è bianconero!|trans-title=Llorente is white-and-black!|publisher=Udinese Calcio|language=it|date=27 January 2021|access-date=27 January 2021}}</ref> In August, however, he was released.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tuttoudinese.it/gli-ex/llorente-verso-il-ritorno-in-spagna/|title=Llorente verso il ritorno in Spagna|trans-title=Back to Spain for Llorente it is|publisher=Tutto Udinese|first=Jessy|last=Specogna|language=it|date=2 August 2021|access-date=22 October 2021|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210926013500/https://www.tuttoudinese.it/gli-ex/llorente-verso-il-ritorno-in-spagna/|archive-date=26 September 2021}}</ref>

===Eibar===
On 27 October 2021, after three months without a club, the 36-year-old Llorente joined [[SD Eibar|Eibar]] on a one-year deal.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elespanol.com/deportes/futbol/20211027/fernando-llorente-regresa-futbol-espanol-jugar-segunda/622688143_0.html|title=Fernando Llorente regresa al fútbol español!|trans-title=Fernando Llorente return to Spanish football!|newspaper=[[El Español]]|first=Ángela|last=Castañeda|language=es|date=27 October 2021|access-date=27 October 2021}}</ref> Once it expired, he left.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.larazon.es/deportes/laotraliga/20220630/2dkytte5kjak7kc2nondkbnxsy.html|title=Fernando Llorente deja el Eibar|trans-title=Fernando Llorente leaves Eibar|newspaper=[[La Razón (Madrid)|La Razón]]|language=es|date=30 June 2022|access-date=4 July 2022}}</ref>

Llorente officially announced his retirement from professional football on 16 February 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://football-italia.net/official-ex-juventus-forward-llorente-retires-aged-37/|title=Official: Ex-Juventus forward Llorente retires aged 37|publisher=Football Italia|first=Apollo|last=Heyes|date=16 February 2023|access-date=16 February 2023}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Spain vs England.jpg|thumb|Llorente (right, number 16, marked by [[Peter Crouch]]) moments before his first goal for [[Spain national football team|Spain]], 11 February 2009]]
Llorente represented [[Spain national under-20 football team|Spain]] at the [[2005 FIFA World Youth Championship]], his five goals winning him the silver boot as the competition's second highest scorer.<ref name=Silver>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=4085&idi=2|title=Silver Boot|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=2 March 2006|access-date=14 December 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090210184750/http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=4085&idi=2|archive-date=10 February 2009}}</ref> He was also [[Cap (sport)|capped]] at [[Spain national under-17 football team|under-17]] and [[Spain national under-21 football team|under-21 levels]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2005/10/11/futbol/1129047178.html|title=Llorente: "Te quedas con cara de tonto"|trans-title=Llorente: "You are left looking rather silly"|newspaper=El Mundo|language=es|date=11 October 2005|access-date=12 August 2019}}</ref>

On 14 November 2008, [[Spain national football team|senior national team]] manager [[Vicente del Bosque]] called Llorente up for a [[Exhibition game|friendly]] against [[Chile national football team|Chile]];<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=7340&idi=2|title=The Spanish national team: Call up|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=14 November 2008|access-date=14 December 2008|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090210182253/http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=2&d=1000&berria=7340&idi=2|archive-date=10 February 2009}}</ref> he was brought on as a substitute in the 72nd minute of the 3–0 win.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.iht.com/articles/ap/2008/11/19/sports/SOC-Spain-Chile.php|title=Spain beats Chile 3–0 to cap historic season|newspaper=[[The New York Times International Edition|International Herald Tribune]]|date=19 November 2008|access-date=14 December 2008}}</ref> He scored his first goal in the 64th minute of a 2–0 friendly win over [[England national football team|England]] on 11 February 2009, after coming off the bench.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/internationals/7874902.stm|title=Spain 2–0 England|first=Mandeep|last=Sanghera|publisher=BBC Sport|date=11 February 2009|access-date=20 June 2009}}</ref> After scoring 14 goals for Athletic in 2008–09, he was named by del Bosque in his 23-man squad for the [[2009 FIFA Confederations Cup]]. He was used as a substitute against hosts [[South Africa national football team|South Africa]], and closed a 2–0 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/internationals/8108987.stm|title=Spain 2–0 South Africa|publisher=BBC Sport|date=20 June 2009|access-date=5 January 2019}}</ref>

Llorente was not selected during the 2009–10 season, as del Bosque favoured [[Álvaro Negredo]]. He was, however, selected for the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]] in South Africa as third-choice striker, where he played in one match for the eventual champions, the last thirty minutes of the 1–0 [[Single-elimination tournament|round of 16]] defeat of [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/spain-vs-portugal/218253|title=Spain send Portugal packing|publisher=Sky Sports|first=Ben|last=Collins|date=30 June 2010|access-date=23 January 2018}}</ref>

On 8 October 2010, benefiting from an injury to [[Fernando Torres]], Llorente started in a [[UEFA Euro 2012|Euro 2012]] [[UEFA Euro 2012 qualifying|qualifier]] against [[Lithuania national football team|Lithuania]] in [[Salamanca]], scoring with two headers in a 3–1 win.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.publico.es/actualidad/goles-llorente-y-silva-dan.html|title=3–1. Dos goles de Llorente y uno de Silva dan el triunfo a España frente a Lituania|trans-title=3–1. Two goals from Llorente and one from Silva give Spain win against Lithuania|newspaper=[[Público (Spain)|Público]]|language=es|date=9 October 2010|access-date=23 January 2018}}</ref> Four days later, as a substitute, he scored the winner against [[Scotland national football team|Scotland]] in a 3–2 victory at [[Hampden Park]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/diario/2010/10/13/deportes/1286920802_850215.html|title=Llorente, el otro 'siete' de España|trans-title=Llorente, Spain's other 'seven'|newspaper=El País|first=José|last=Sámano|language=es|date=13 October 2010|access-date=23 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.walesonline.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/scots-sunk-super-sub-llorente-1891137|title=Scots are sunk by super-sub Llorente|publisher=Wales Online|date=13 October 2010|access-date=28 November 2019}}</ref> He was selected for the final stages in [[Poland]] and [[Ukraine]], and was an unused squad member as Spain won another tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.spherasports.com/ganar-la-eurocopa-sin-jugar-ni-un-minuto-69788/|title=Ganar la Eurocopa sin jugar ni un minuto|trans-title=Winning the Eurocup without playing one single minute|publisher=Sphera Sports|first=Joel|last=Sierra|language=es|date=9 June 2016|access-date=23 January 2018|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180123190423/http://www.spherasports.com/ganar-la-eurocopa-sin-jugar-ni-un-minuto-69788/|archive-date=23 January 2018}}</ref>

Llorente was one of seven players dropped from the final squad for the [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27647635|title=World Cup 2014: Spain drop Alvaro Negredo and Jesus Navas|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=31 May 2014|access-date=31 May 2014}}</ref> He also represented the unofficial [[Basque Country national football team|Basque Country team]] five times, making his debut against [[Cameroon national football team|Cameroon]] in 2005 and scoring once against [[Catalonia national football team|Catalonia]] at the [[Camp Nou]] the following year. His last appearance was in December 2007.<ref name=Athletic>{{Athletic Bilbao profile|id=fernando-llorente-torres}}</ref>

==Style of play==
A tall, large, and physically powerful player, Llorente's main traits were his heading ability and strength in the air, which enabled him to function effectively as a [[Forward (association football)#Centre-forward|target-man]] in the centre of his team's attacking line.<ref name=Gazzetta>{{cite news|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Squadre/Juventus/25-01-2013/tutto-llorente-qualita-difetti-ecco-chi-basco-juventus-913982304034.shtml|title=Tutto su Llorente, qualità e difetti – Ecco chi è il basco della Juventus|trans-title=Everything about Llorente, strengths and faults – Here is Juventus' Basque|newspaper=[[La Gazzetta dello Sport]]|language=it|date=25 January 2013|access-date=10 November 2014}}</ref><ref name=Arrives>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.co.uk/football/blog/name/93/post/1852302/headline|title=Fernando Llorente finally arrives|publisher=ESPN FC|first=Mina|last=Rzouki|date=2 July 2013|access-date=25 February 2017}}</ref><ref name=Big>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.us/english-premier-league/23/blog/post/3045616/fernando-llorente-peter-crouch-show-that-traditional-strikers-still-have-a-place-in-premier-league|title=The 'big man' is back as Fernando Llorente, Peter Crouch are thriving|publisher=ESPN FC|first=Michael|last=Cox|date=24 January 2017|access-date=25 February 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/antonio-conte-wary-of-swansea-boss-paul-clement-and-transfer-target-fernando-llorente-haunting-a3475561.html|title=Antonio Conte wary of Swansea boss Paul Clement and transfer target Fernando Llorente haunting Chelsea|newspaper=London Evening Standard|first=Simon|last=Johnson|date=24 February 2017|access-date=25 February 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/36910960|title=Fernando Llorente: Swansea City complete signing of Sevilla striker|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Dafydd|last=Pritchard|date=5 August 2016|access-date=25 February 2017}}</ref> He was also known for his offensive movement, positional sense, and goalscoring ability inside the penalty area.<ref name=Gazzetta/><ref name=Arrives/><ref name=Big/><ref name=Top>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.us/club/swansea-city/318/blog/post/3006325/sigurdsson-llorente-earn-top-marks-as-swansea-claim-nine-goal-thriller|title=Sigurdsson, Llorente earn top marks as Swansea win nine goal thriller|publisher=ESPN FC|first=Max|last=Hicks|date=27 November 2016|access-date=25 February 2017}}</ref> Additionally, he was also gifted with good technical skills and link-up play, which allowed him to play well with his back to goal and hold up the ball for his teammates in order to create space and scoring opportunities.<ref name=Gazzetta/><ref name=Arrives/><ref name=Big/><ref name=Top/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.canalejuve.it/news/conosciamoli-meglio-fernando-llorente-56567|title=Conosciamoli meglio: Fernando Llorente|trans-title=Let's 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20141110020154/http://www.canalejuve.it/news/conosciamoli-meglio-fernando-llorente-56567|archive-date=10 November 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite The 10 best goalkeepers in the world |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/ranked-10-best-goalkeepers-world?page=0%2C1 |access-date=21 January 2018 |publisher=FourFourTwo |archive-date=8 December 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181208124550/https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/ranked-10-best-goalkeepers-world?page=0%2C1 |url-status=dead }}{{Cite web |last=Edwards |first=Harry |date=9 January 2018 |title=Barcelona 'keeper Marc-Andre ter Stegen is on Manuel Neuer's level – Xavi |url=http://www.squawka.com/news/barcelona-keeper-marc-andre-ter-stegen-is-on-manuel-neuers-level-xavi/1006972 |access-date=21 January 2018 |publisher=squawka.com |archive-date=22 January 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180122001208/http://www.squawka.com/news/barcelona-keeper-marc-andre-ter-stegen-is-on-manuel-neuers-level-xavi/1006972 |url-status=live }}{{Cite web |date=12 June 2017 |title=The 40 most valuable players in world football |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2017/06/12/40-valuable-players-world-football/marc-andre-ter-stegen-25-barcelona/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2017/06/12/40-valuable-players-world-football/marc-andre-ter-stegen-25-barcelona/ |archive-date=12 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |access-date=21 January 2018 |website=The Telegraph}}{{cbignore}}}} After four seasons in the [[Bundesliga]] with [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]], making 108 league appearances, Ter Stegen joined Barcelona for €12 million in 2014. He won the [[Treble (association football)|treble]] in his first season in Spain, playing for Barcelona in [[Copa del Rey]] and [[UEFA Champions League]]. Ter Stegen represented Germany at several youth levels and made his senior international debut in 2012. He was part of the German squads that reached the semi-finals of [[UEFA Euro 2016]] and won the [[2017 FIFA Confederations Cup]], and was also a member of the German side that took part at the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]], [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] and [[UEFA Euro 2024]]. ==Club career== ===Borussia Mönchengladbach=== ====2010–11 season==== Ter Stegen began his career at hometown team [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]]. In the first half of the 2010–11 season, he established himself as the star of [[Borussia Mönchengladbach II|their reserve team]] and was frequently seen on the first-team bench. Whilst he was enjoying a relatively successful season, the same could not be said for his first-team colleagues.{{Cite web |title=Scouting Network:e Marc-André ter Stegen : "The fans already had their support for Ter Stegen, and had known what this teenager was capable of, and thus demanded the new manager to utilise him and give him a taste of football at the highest level, hoping that he would deliver the goods for them" |url=http://www.goaldentimes.org/2013/03/19/scouting-network-marc-andre-ter-stegen/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150216112324/http://www.goaldentimes.org/2013/03/19/scouting-network-marc-andre-ter-stegen/ |archive-date=16 February 2015 |access-date=15 February 2015 |website=goaldentimes.org}} Mönchengladbach's senior side were seemingly failing in their efforts to avoid [[promotion and relegation|relegation]], and on 14 February 2011, manager [[Michael Frontzeck]] was replaced by [[Lucien Favre]], with the team rooted to the bottom of the [[Bundesliga]], having accumulated only 16 points after 22 match days.{{Cite web |date=14 February 2011 |title=Favre soll Gladbach retten |url=http://www.abendzeitung-muenchen.de/inhalt.nachfolger-fuer-frontzeck-favre-soll-gladbach-retten.e8d30e7a-ab9e-4d16-a298-cdeb01553b5c.html |access-date=22 June 2013 |publisher=Abendzeitung München |language=de |archive-date=1 February 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201220703/http://www.abendzeitung-muenchen.de/inhalt.nachfolger-fuer-frontzeck-favre-soll-gladbach-retten.e8d30e7a-ab9e-4d16-a298-cdeb01553b5c.html |url-status=live }} The team’s results soon improved, but the erratic form of first-choice goalkeeper [[Logan Bailly]] held the team back. Whilst he was able to produce match-winning performances such as the one against [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]], these were few and far between, and were frequently cancelled out by uninspiring matches. The fans of Mönchengladbach were quick to discredit the Belgian international, with some accusing him of putting more effort into his modelling career than his football. Ter Stegen's progress for the reserve team had not gone unnoticed by the supporters, and the new manager was inundated with demands to start the young prodigy in the league. Favre eventually lost patience with Bailly, and on 10 April 2011, relegated him to the bench in favour of Ter Stegen for the match against [[1. FC Köln]]. The young German did not disappoint, and the defence boasted a previously unseen solidity. He kept his place in the team for the remainder of the season, keeping four [[Shutout#Association football|clean-sheets]] out of a possible five in the last five matchdays as Mönchengladbach avoided relegation via the playoffs. During this run, he shot to prominence with a last-man-standing display against eventual champions [[Borussia Dortmund]], making a string of world-class saves as Mönchengladbach secured a famous 1–0 victory.{{cite web |last=Achanta |first=Suhas |url=https://barcauniversal.com/marc-andre-ter-stegen-a-look-back-at-his-time-at-borussia-monchengladbach/ |title=Marc-André ter Stegen: A look back at his time at Borussia Mönchengladbach |publisher=Barca Universal |date=16 May 2020 }} ====2011–12 season==== [[File:Marc Andre ter Stegen.jpg|thumb|Ter Stegen with [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]] in 2011]] Ter Stegen's status as first-choice goalkeeper was inevitable when Bailly was sent on loan to Swiss side [[Neuchâtel Xamax]] and the No.1 shirt was delegated to Ter Stegen, who had previously worn 21.{{citation needed|date=June 2020}} During the summer transfer window, [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] had succeeded in their drawn-out pursuit of [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]]'s captain [[Manuel Neuer]]. The German international made his debut against Ter Stegen's Mönchengladbach at the [[Allianz Arena]]. The match did not go the way the pundits predicted, however, with Ter Stegen producing yet another inspired display whilst his counterpart Neuer made the error that condemned Bayern to a 1–0 defeat. Following this match, Borussia Mönchengladbach embarked on an unlikely title challenge, with Ter Stegen and fellow youngster [[Marco Reus]] providing the inspiration for Mönchengladbach.{{citation needed|date=June 2020}} ====2012–13 season==== After the departures of Reus and [[Dante (footballer)|Dante]], Ter Stegen emerged as Mönchengladbach's main star for the season. He was again first-choice, and in February 2013, it was reported that Ter Stegen signed a pre-agreement with [[La Liga]] club [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]].{{Cite web |date=14 February 2013 |title=Ter Stegen signs pre-agreement with Barça |url=http://www.marca.com/2013/02/14/en/football/barcelona/1360861880.html |access-date=8 May 2014 |website=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]] |archive-date=8 May 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140508222534/http://www.marca.com/2013/02/14/en/football/barcelona/1360861880.html |url-status=live }} The deal was later denied by himself.{{Cite web |last=Coerts |first=Stefan |date=4 July 2013 |title=Ter Stegen laughs off Barcelona links |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/11/transfer-zone/2013/07/04/4093119/ter-stegen-laughs-off-barcelona-links |access-date=8 May 2014 |publisher=Goal.com |archive-date=3 July 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140703141542/http://www.goal.com/en/news/11/transfer-zone/2013/07/04/4093119/ter-stegen-laughs-off-barcelona-links |url-status=live }} ====2013–14 season==== After being strongly linked with Barcelona, Ter Stegen remained at Mönchengladbach for the new season. On 6 January 2014, he rejected a new deal from the club,{{Cite web |date=6 January 2014 |title=Marc-Andre ter Stegen rejects Borussia Monchengladbach offer |url=http://www1.skysports.com/news/12040/9104913/ |access-date=8 May 2014 |publisher=[[Sky Sports]] |archive-date=8 May 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140508223557/http://www1.skysports.com/news/12040/9104913/ |url-status=live }} raising the speculation over his future. In the last home match of the season, a 3–1 home success against [[1. FSV Mainz 05|Mainz 05]] on 5 May, Ter Stegen gave an emotional farewell to Borussia Mönchengladbach.{{Cite web |date=5 May 2014 |title=Transfer news: Barcelona-bound Marc-Andre ter Stegen says goodbye to Monchengladbach |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11833/9296578/transfer-news-barcelona-bound-marc-andre-ter-stegen-says-goodbye-to-monchengladbach |access-date=8 May 2014 |publisher=Sky Sports |archive-date=6 May 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140506212827/http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11833/9296578/transfer-news-barcelona-bound-marc-andre-ter-stegen-says-goodbye-to-monchengladbach |url-status=live }} ===Barcelona=== ====2014–15 season==== [[File:Barça - Napoli - 20140806 - Marc-André ter Stegen.jpg|thumb|upright=0.8|Ter Stegen warming up for [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in 2014]] On 19 May 2014, Ter Stegen was announced as the new goalkeeper of Spanish club Barcelona, with goalkeeper [[Claudio Bravo]], after the departures of [[Víctor Valdés]] and [[José Manuel Pinto]], effective during the summer transfer window.{{Cite news |date=19 May 2014 |title=Llega Ter Stegen y se va Pinto |language=es |trans-title=Ter Stegen arrives and Pinto leaves |publisher=FC Barcelona |url=http://www.fcbarcelona.es/futbol/primer-equipo/detalle/noticia/llega-ter-stegen-y-se-va-pinto |access-date=19 May 2014 |archive-date=23 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160323073640/http://www.fcbarcelona.es/futbol/primer-equipo/detalle/noticia/llega-ter-stegen-y-se-va-pinto |url-status=live }} On 22 May 2014, he signed a five-year contract that would keep him at the club until June 2019. is missing the 2026 World Cup for Germany |publisher=World Soccer Talk |date=14 June 2026 }} ==Style of play== Ter Stegen has been described as a tall, agile and consistent goalkeeper, with quick reflexes, good decision-making and excellent shot-stopping abilities between the posts; he is also strong in the air, good in one-on-one situations, and effective at communicating with his back-line courtesy of his strong personality. Due to his ability to read the game and speed when rushing off his line, he is able to anticipate opponents outside the area who have beaten the offside trap. Being highly competent with the ball at his feet, he is known for his control and accurate distribution of the ball, and often functions as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)#Sweeper-keeper|sweeper-keeper]], due to his ability to play the ball out from the back. {{nihongo|'''Takashi Usami'''|宇佐美 貴史|Usami Takashi|born 6 May 1992}} is a Japanese professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays for [[Gamba Osaka]] in the [[J1 League]]. He plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] or a [[Forward (association football)#Winger|winger]].

==Club career==
===Gamba Osaka===
Usami made club history by making his professional debut for [[Gamba Osaka]] at the age of 17 years and 14 days and scoring a goal in the same match to become the youngest player to achieve both feats for the club, breaking the records previously set by [[Junichi Inamoto]]. Usami made his professional debut and goal on 20 May 2009 against [[FC Seoul]] in the [[2009 AFC Champions League|Champions League]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2009/05/20/asia/afc-champions-league/gamba-osaka/fc-seoul/735975/|title=Gamba Osaka vs. Seoul 1 - 2|date=20 May 2009|access-date=6 June 2011|work=Soccerway}}</ref> He finished the [[2009 Gamba Osaka season|2009 season]] with a goal in four matches played, which includes three league matches, and a Champions League match.<ref name="The Guardian Stats">{{cite web | url = http://guardian.touch-line.com/StatsCentre.asp?CTID=63&CPID=147&TEID=2070&PLID=213730&pStr=Player | title = Takashi Usami | work = The Guardian | access-date = 31 March 2015 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110109133537/http://guardian.touch-line.com/StatsCentre.asp?CTID=63&CPID=147&TEID=2070&PLID=213730&pStr=Player | archive-date = 9 January 2011 | df = dmy-all }}</ref><ref name="Soccerway statistics">{{cite news|url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/takashi-usami/74703/|title=Japan – Usami Takashi – Profile with news, career statistics and history|work=Soccerway | access-date = 31 March 2015}}</ref><ref name="Takashi Usami Club matches">{{cite news|url=https://www.worldfootball.net/person/pe145762/takashi-usami/club-matches/|title=Takashi Usami > Club matches|work=Worldfootball.net|access-date=31 March 2015|archive-date=24 July 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110724134542/http://aus.worldfootball.net/spieler_profil/takashi-usami/2/|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2010, he became a more regular face in the Gamba Osaka team and he was named as [[J. League at the annual awards ceremony on 6 December.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.j-league.or.jp/awards/index.html|script-title=ja:２０１０Ｊリーグアウォーズ|date=6 December 2010|access-date=22 April 2011|work=[[J. League]]|language=ja|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110315012826/http://www.j-league.or.jp/awards/index.html|archive-date=15 March 2011}}</ref>

===Bayern Munich===
In June 2011, it was confirmed that Usami would be loaned out to [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=1462047.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110703131606/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=1462047.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=3 July 2011|title=Bayern take Usami on loan|date=27 June 2011|access-date=27 June 2011|work=[[FIFA.com]]}}</ref> with an option to buy next summer. He joined the club in mid-July. Usami told the media in a news conference that a chance like that did not come every day, and that he was looking forward to this big challenge. When he was asked about Bayern's current first-team players, he said: "I want to improve my skills to the point, where I can take their places."
Usami scored his first competitive goal for the Bavarians on 26 October 2011, in a [[DFB-Pokal|DFB Cup]] match against [[FC Ingolstadt 04|FC Ingolstadt]], after coming off the bench in the 73rd minute.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.fcbayern.telekom.de/de/aktuell/news/2011/29925.php|title=FCB leiht Japaner Usami aus|date=27 June 2011|access-date=27 June 2011|work=[[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]]|language=de}}</ref>

===1899 Hoffenheim===
Usami scored two goals in 21 matches played for [[TSG 1899 Hoffenheim|1899 Hoffenheim]].<ref name="2012–13 season">{{cite web |title=Takashi Usami |url=http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/bundesliga/vereine/2012-13/68513/vereinsspieler_usami-takashi.html |website=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |publisher=kicker |access-date=19 June 2018 |language=de |archive-date=19 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180619213754/http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/bundesliga/vereine/2012-13/68513/vereinsspieler_usami-takashi.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===FC Augsburg===
====2016–17 season====
Usami joined Augsburg in the summer of 2016.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2016/06/20/soccer/j-league/usami-returning-germany-augsburg/ | title = Usami returning to Germany with Augsburg | website = japantimes.co.jp | date = 20 June 2016 | access-date = 1 May 2018}}</ref> He played in 11 matches during the [[2016–17 FC Augsburg season|2016–17 season]].<ref name="2016–17 season">{{cite web |title=Takashi Usami |url=http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/bundesliga/vereine/2016-17/68513/vereinsspieler_usami-takashi.html |website=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |publisher=kicker |language=de |access-date=19 June 2018 |archive-date=19 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180619190019/http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/bundesliga/vereine/2016-17/68513/vereinsspieler_usami-takashi.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

====Loan to Fortuna Düsseldorf====
Usami was loaned to [[Fortuna Düsseldorf]] for the [[2017–18 Fortuna Düsseldorf season|2017–18 season]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Usami auf Leihbasis nach Düsseldorf |url=https://www.kicker.de/usami-auf-leihbasis-nach-duesseldorf-705038/artikel |website=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |publisher=kicker |access-date=20 June 2018 |language=de |date=30 August 2017}}</ref> He played a key role in helping them gain promotion to the Bundesliga.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/fortuna-dusseldorf-promoted-takashi-usami-neuhaus-haraguchi-479820.jsp | title = Welcome back to the Bundesliga, Fortuna Düsseldorf! | website = bundesliga.com | date = 29 April 2018 | access-date = 1 May 2018 | archive-date = 1 May 2018 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20180501161131/https://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/fortuna-dusseldorf-promoted-takashi-usami-neuhaus-haraguchi-479820.jsp | url-status = dead }}</ref> He finished the 2017–18 season with eight goals in 28 matches played.<ref name="2017–18 season">{{cite web |title=Takashi Usami |url=http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/bundesliga/vereine/2017-18/68513/vereinsspieler_usami-takashi.html |website=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |publisher=kicker |access-date=19 June 2018 |language=de |archive-date=19 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180619190022/http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/bundesliga/vereine/2017-18/68513/vereinsspieler_usami-takashi.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

====2018–19 season====
Usami returned to Augsburg for the [[2018–19 FC Augsburg season|2018–19 season]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Bernreuther |first1=David |title=Usami: Reuter sagt Düsseldorf vorerst ab |url=https://www.kicker.de/usami_reuter-sagt-duesseldorf-vorerst-ab-725947/artikel |access-date=20 June 2018 |language=de |date=20 June 2018}}</ref>

====Second loan to Fortuna Düsseldorf====
On 4 August 2018, Usami rejoined Fortuna Düsseldorf on a season-long loan for the [[2018–19 Fortuna Düsseldorf season|2018–19 season]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.f95.de/aktuell/news/profis/detail/22651-fortuna-holt-takashi-usami-zurueck/296508c6e81169faf6b0f918777a53b5/ | title = Fortuna holt Takashi Usami zurück | language = de | website = Fortuna Düsseldorf | date = 4 August 2018 | access-date = 9 August 2018 | archive-date = 4 August 2018 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20180804140625/https://www.f95.de/aktuell/news/profis/detail/22651-fortuna-holt-takashi-usami-zurueck/296508c6e81169faf6b0f918777a53b5/ | url-status = live }}</ref>

==International career==
In October 2009, Usami was elected [[Japan national under-17 football team|Japan U17 national team]] for [[2009 FIFA U-17 World Cup]]. He played all three matches. In July 2012, he was elected [[Japan national under-23 football team|Japan U23 national team]] for [[Football at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Summer Olympics]]. He played four matches and Japan won the fourth place.

Usami debuted for [[Japan national football team|Japan]] in a friendly match against [[Tunisia national football team|Tunisia]] on 27 March 2015. He scored his debut goal in a friendly match against [[Uzbekistan national football team|Uzbekistan]] on 31 March 2015. In May 2018 he was named in Japan's preliminary squad for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]] in Russia.<ref>{{cite web|title= World Cup 2018: All the confirmed squads for this summer's finals in Russia|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/440833652018}}{{dead link|date=September 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

His older brother, Honami, played an important role in starting his football career when he searched on the internet for [[Nagoya Grampus]]'s U-15 team and this led Yoshida to join the U-15 team.{{cite web |date=22 July 2008 |title=サッカー男子 吉田麻也（名古屋グランパス） |url=https://www.nagasaki-np.co.jp/sports/2008/gorin/kikaku1/05.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080801190827/https://www.nagasaki-np.co.jp/sports/2008/gorin/kikaku1/05.html |archive-date=1 August 2008 |access-date=5 April 2020 |publisher=Nagasaki |language=ja}} Once Yoshida joined, he relocated to Nagoya to be close at Nagoya Grampus and attended Toyota High School.{{cite news|title=サッカー吉田麻也選手、高校時代から一目置かれる存在|url=https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXNASFD04009_U2A800C1CN8000/|publisher=Nikkei|language=ja|date=5 August 2012|access-date=5 April 2020}}

{{cite news|title=麻也、会見での渾身ギャグを弁解「今回はたまたまスベっただけ」|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?115665-119882-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=13 June 2013|access-date=5 April 2020}} Yoshida joined the club's first team training soon after and started out as a defensive midfielder while playing for Nagoya Grampus's youth team, but was converted to centre back.{{cite web |date=9 February 2007 |title=グラ新人紹介 七人の侍が歴史を作る |url=https://www.chunichi.co.jp/chuspo/hold/grampus/news/2007/200702/CK2007032202103071.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101005064650/https://www.chunichi.co.jp/chuspo/hold/grampus/news/2007/200702/CK2007032202103071.html |archive-date=5 October 2010 |access-date=5 April 2020 |publisher=Chunichi |language=ja}} After spending months on the substitute bench, Yoshida finally made his debut for the club, coming on as a second-half substitute, in a 2–1 loss against [[Oita Trinita]] on 3 May 2007.{{cite web|url=https://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2007/0503/result.html|title=名古屋グランパス １－２大分トリニータ|publisher=Nagoya Grampus|language=ja|date=3 May 2007|access-date=5 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200331210504/https://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2007/0503/result.html|archive-date=31 March 2020|url-status=live}} Since then, he became a first team regular for Nagoya Grampus, playing in the centre–back position.{{cite web|url=https://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2007/0526/nagare.html|title=2007 Jリーグディビジョン1：ラウンド13|publisher=Nagoya Grampus|language=ja|date=26 May 2007|access-date=5 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200401180940/https://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2007/0526/nagare.html|archive-date=1 April 2020|url-status=live}}
{{cite web|url=https://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2007/0825/result.html|title=名古屋グランパス５－０ 大宮アルディージャ|publisher=Nagoya Grampus|language=ja|date=25 August 2007|access-date=5 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200401183824/https://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2007/0825/result.html|archive-date=1 April 2020|url-status=live}}
{{cite web|url=https://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2007/1118/result.html|title=大分トリニータ１－３名古屋グランパス|publisher=Nagoya Grampus|language=ja|date=18 November 2007|access-date=5 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200401184100/https://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2007/1118/result.html|archive-date=1 April 2020|url-status=live}} On 5 November 2007, Yoshida scored his first goal for the club, in a 3–1 win against [[Thespakusatsu Gunma|Thespa Kusatsu]] in the fourth round of the Emperor's Cup.{{cite web|url=https://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2007/1104/result.html|title=テスパ草津1-3名古屋グランパス|publisher=Nagoya Grampus|language=ja|date=4 November 2007|access-date=5 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200401182008/https://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2007/1104/result.html|archive-date=1 April 2020|url-status=live}} At the end of the 2007 season, he went on to make twenty–four appearances and scoring once in all competitions. In the 2008 season, Yoshida began to feature in the starting line-up for most of the league matches, forming a centre–back partnership with his Serbian teammate [[Miloš Bajalica]].{{cite web|url=http://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2008/0308/report.html|title=名古屋グランパス１－１京都サンガ F.C.|website=Nagoya Grampus|language=ja|date=8 March 2008|access-date=25 May 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130307010531/http://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2008/0308/report.html|archive-date=7 March 2013|url-status=live}}
{{cite news|title=名古屋の19歳DF吉田「高原さん抑えれば自信がつく」|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?34601-15288-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=14 March 2008|access-date=5 April 2020|archive-date=1 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200401185302/https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?34601-15288-fl|url-status=dead}}

{{cite web|url=https://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2008/0405/result.html|title=名古屋グランパス２－０ 横浜F・マリノス|website=Nagoya Grampus|language=ja|date=5 April 2008|access-date=25 May 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130307045911/https://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2008/0405/result.html|archive-date=7 March 2013|url-status=live}}
{{cite web|url=http://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2008/0419/result.html|title=名古屋グランパス３－２ ジェフユナイテッド千葉|website=Nagoya Grampus|language=ja|date=19 April 2008|access-date=25 May 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130307163936/http://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2008/0419/result.html|archive-date=7 March 2013|url-status=live}} Yoshida continued to feature in the first team until he was called up to the Japan U23 squad in July.{{cite web|url=http://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2008/0510/result.html|title=名古屋グランパス０－０ヴィッセル神戸|website=Nagoya Grampus|language=ja|date=10 May 2008|access-date=25 May 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130307045541/http://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2008/0510/result.html|archive-date=7 March 2013|url-status=live}}
{{cite news|title=★「あなたの選ぶJ1前半戦ベストイレブン」結果発表|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?38631-19462-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=16 June 2008|access-date=5 April 2020}}
{{cite web|url=https://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2008/0712/result.html|title=名古屋グランパス１－０ 柏レイソル|website=Nagoya Grampus|language=ja|date=12 July 2008|access-date=25 May 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130307163232/https://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2008/0712/result.html|archive-date=7 March 2013|url-status=live}} After Japan U23's elimination in the Summer Olympics, it was not until 23 August 2008 that Yoshida returned to the starting line-up against [[Kashima Antlers]] and scored his first goal of the season, in a 2–1 win.{{cite news|title=名古屋がカシマで念願の初勝利!鹿島は首位陥落|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?41457-22358-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=23 August 2008|access-date=5 April 2020}}
{{cite web|url=http://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2008/0823/result.html|title=鹿島アントラーズ１－２名古屋グランパス|website=Nagoya Grampus|language=ja|date=23 August 2008|access-date=25 May 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130307045947/http://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2008/0823/result.html|archive-date=7 March 2013|url-status=live}} However, he lost his first team place and found himself placed on the substitute bench for the next five matches.{{cite web|url=http://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2008/0827/result.html|title=名古屋グランパス３－２清水エスパルス|website=Nagoya Grampus|language=ja|date=27 August 2008|access-date=25 May 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130307045601/http://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2008/0827/result.html|archive-date=7 March 2013|url-status=live}}
{{cite news|title=名古屋・吉田がナビスコ杯V宣言|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?41852-22767-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=1 September 2008|access-date=5 April 2020|archive-date=1 April 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200401201155/https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?41852-22767-fl|url-status=dead}}
{{cite web|url=https://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2008/0928/result.html|title=名古屋グランパス１－１浦和レッズ|website=Nagoya Grampus|language=ja|date=28 September 2008|access-date=25 May 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130307163242/http://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2008/0928/result.html|archive-date=7 March 2013|url-status=live}} Yoshida's second goal then came on 2 November 2008 against [[FC Gifu]] in the fourth round of the Emperor's Cup and helped them win 1–0.{{cite news |date=2 November 2008 |title=名古屋が格下に大苦戦／天皇杯 |url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/news/f-sc-tp0-20081102-425532.html |access-date=5 April 2020 |publisher=Nikkan Sports |language=ja}} By mid–October, he regained his first team place for the remaining matches of the season and helped the club finish third place in the league.{{cite web|url=http://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2008/1019/result.html|title=名古屋グランパス０－０ 横浜F・マリノス|website=Nagoya Grampus|language=ja|date=19 October 2008|access-date=25 May 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130307045621/http://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2008/1019/result.html|archive-date=7 March 2013|url-status=live}}
{{cite news|title=名古屋ピクシー監督が居残りシュート練習|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/news/f-sc-tp0-20081204-436724.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=4 December 2008|access-date=5 April 2020}}
{{cite web|url=https://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2008/1206/result.html|title=大分トリニータ ０－０ 名古屋グランパス|website=Nagoya Grampus|language=ja|date=6 December 2008|access-date=25 May 2024|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130307045636/https://nagoya-grampus.jp/backnumber/result/2008/1206/result.html|archive-date=7 March 2013|url-status=live}} For his performance, Yoshida won the Rookie of the Year at the 14th Aichi Toyota "Grand Pass Rankle Award".{{cite news |date=25 November 2008 |title=名古屋・小川佳純がグランパスランクル賞で最優秀選手に |url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?45933-26903-fl |access-date=5 April 2020 |publisher=Web Gekisaka |language=ja |archive-date=1 April 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200401204553/https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?45933-26903-fl |url-status=dead }} At the end of the 2008 season, he went on to make twenty–nine appearances and scoring two times in all competitions. At the start of the 2009 season, Yoshida switched number shirt to four.{{cite news|title=名古屋DF吉田、松坂の教えで全戦出場だ|url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/news/p-sc-tp0-20090202-456503.html|publisher=Nikkan Sports|language=ja|date=2 February 2009|access-date=5 April 2020}} He scored [[Nagoya Grampus]]'s historical first goal in the [[AFC Champions League]] in the game against [[Ulsan HD FC|Ulsan Hyundai Horang-i]], winning 3–1 on 10 March 2009.{{cite news|title=名古屋、敵地で３発逆転！ＡＣＬ初陣飾った|url=https://www.sponichi.co.jp/soccer/news/2009/03/10/kiji/K20090310Z00000720.html|website=Sponichi Annex|language=ja|date=10 March 2009|access-date=25 May 2024}} Yoshida continued to regain his first team place for the club, playing in the centre–back position.{{cite news|title=第2節(3月14日)山形vs名古屋プレビュー&予想先発|url=https://web.gekisaka.jp/news/detail/?50912-32105-fl|publisher=Web Gekisaka|language=ja|date=12 March 2009|access-date=5 April 2020}}
