'''César Azpilicueta Tanco''' ({{IPA|es|aθpiliˈkweta}},<ref>{{cite web |title=Video: Chelsea's Cesar Azpilicueta explains how to pronounce his name |url=https://www.joe.ie/uncategorized/video-chelseas-cesar-azpilicueta-explains-how-to-pronounce-his-name-392298 |website=Joe |date=3 December 2013 |access-date=23 November 2023}}</ref> born 28 August 1989) is a Spanish former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[right-back]] or [[centre-back]].<ref name="as">{{Cite web |date=29 August 2025 |title=Cesar Azpilicueta signs |url=https://sevillafc.es/en/actualidad/noticias/cesar-azpilicueta-signs |access-date=30 August 2025 |website=Sevilla Football Club}}</ref>

A youth product of Osasuna, Azpilicueta spent three seasons in [[La Liga]] before switching to [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]]. In the summer of 2012, he moved to [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], winning the [[2013 UEFA Europa League final|Europa League]] in his first season and a domestic [[Double (association football)|double]] [[2014–15 Chelsea F.C. season|two years later]]. He made over 500 appearances for the club and was sixth on their [[List of Chelsea F.C. records and statistics#Most appearances|list of all-time appearances]] when he departed in 2023, with no other non-English person having played more times for them. Described as a [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]] 'legend',<ref>{{cite news |title=Congratulations, Azpi |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/congratulations-azpi |date=6 July 2023 |access-date=18 July 2023 |publisher=Chelsea F.C.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Cesar Azpilicueta - a Chelsea legend |url=https://www.premierleague.com/video/single/3561248 |date=7 July 2023 |access-date=18 July 2023 |publisher=Premier League}}</ref> he captained Chelsea to [[2018–19 UEFA Europa League]], [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League]] and [[2021 FIFA Club World Cup]] victories.

Azpilicueta earned 55 [[Cap (sport)|caps]] for [[Spain national youth football team (disambiguation)|Spain at youth level]] in all age groups, and represented the [[Spain national under-21 football team|under-21s]] in two [[UEFA European Under-21 Championship|European Championships]], winning the [[2011 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|2011 edition]]. He made his first appearance with [[Spain national football team|the senior team]] in 2013 and was selected for [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014]], [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018]] and [[2022 FIFA World Cup|2022]] editions of the [[FIFA World Cup]], as well as [[UEFA Euro 2016]] and [[UEFA Euro 2020]].

==Club career==
===Osasuna===
A product of hometown club [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]]'s [[CA Osasuna Juvenil|youth system]], he made his [[La Liga]] debut on 8 April 2007 in a 0–2 away loss against [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]], while still registered with [[CA Osasuna B|the reserve team]];<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espnfc.com/report/_/id/204057?cc=5739 |title=Real Madrid 2–0 Osasuna |website=ESPN Soccernet |date=8 April 2007|access-date=24 August 2012}}</ref> he started his career as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] then switched to [[midfielder]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://trolacas.wordpress.com/2009/02/20/cesar-azpilicueta-intentad-atacar-por-la-otra-banda/ |title=César Azpilicueta, intentad atacar por la otra banda|trans-title=César Azpilicueta, try the other wing |publisher=El Blog de los Trolacas |language=es |date=20 February 2009|access-date=24 August 2012}}</ref> and, throughout both his club and international career (senior and youth), appeared in several positions, including [[centre-back]] and [[Midfielder#Central midfielder|central midfielder]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.ideal.es/granada/deportes/futbol/seleccion-espanola/201411/12/azpilicueta-nuevo-seguro-bosque-20141112195750-rc.html |title=Azpilicueta, el nuevo 'seguro' de Del Bosque|trans-title=Azpilicueta, Del Bosque's new 'insurance' |newspaper=[[Ideal (newspaper)|Ideal]] |language=es |date=12 November 2014|access-date=20 October 2015}}</ref>

In [[2007–08 La Liga|2007–08]], due to injuries in the main squad, Azpilicueta established himself as a first-team regular at the age of just 18, albeit as a [[right-back]]. He went on to retain this position for [[2008–09 La Liga|the following season]], appearing in all but two league games.

===Marseille===
[[File:César Azpilicueta 5401.jpg|thumb|upright|Azpilicueta playing for [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] in 2010]]
On 21 June 2010, French club [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] confirmed an agreement had been reached with Osasuna for the transfer of Azpilicueta, in a four-year contract for €7 million.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.om.net/fr/Saison/101005/Actualites/47377/Accord_de_principe_pour_le_transfert_de_Cesar_Azpilicueta |title=Accord de principe pour le transfert de César Azpilicueta|work=Olympique de Marseille |trans-title=Deal arranged for transfer of Azpilicueta |language=fr |date=21 June 2010|access-date=23 June 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.les-transferts.com/ligue-1/lom-regle-le-probleme-a-droite.html |title=OM: Azpilicueta et Modesto arrivent! |trans-title=OM: Azpilicueta and Modesto arrive! |publisher=Les Transferts |language=fr |date=22 June 2010 |access-date=15 April 2014 |archive-date=6 August 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180806210759/https://www.les-transferts.com/ligue-1/lom-regle-le-probleme-a-droite.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> A week later, the Navarrese confirmed the agreement, with the transfer fee possibly rising to as much as €9.5 million depending on appearances.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mercato365.com/infos-clubs/marseille/article_429807_OM-Azpi-pour-95-millions-d-euros-.shtml |title=Azpi pour 9.5 million euros? |trans-title=Azpi for 9.5 million euros? |publisher=Mercato 365 |language=fr |date=28 June 2010 |access-date=28 June 2010 |archive-date=9 March 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120309150444/http://www.mercato365.com/infos-clubs/marseille/om-azpi-pour-9-5-millions-d-euros-109997.shtml |url-status=dead }}</ref> On his [[UEFA Champions League]] debut, he scored the match's only goal in a [[2010–11 UEFA Champions League|group stage home match]] against [[FC Spartak Moscow|Spartak Moscow]], though it was into [[Own goal|his own net]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2002819--marseille-vs-spartak-moskva/ |title=Spartak sucker punch downs Marseille |publisher=UEFA |date=15 September 2010|access-date=19 September 2010}}</ref>

On 27 November 2010, in the early minutes of a 4–0 home win against [[Montpellier HSC|Montpellier]] – which meant Marseille [[2010–11 Ligue 1|climbed to the top of the league]] – Azpilicueta ruptured the [[anterior cruciate ligament]] in his left knee.<ref>[https://int.soccerway.com/news/2010/November/28/marseille-go-top-but-pay-high-price/ Marseille go top but pay high price] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101129014337/http://www.soccerway.com/news/2010/November/28/marseille-go-top-but-pay-high-price/|date=29 November 2010}}; Soccerway, 27 November 2010</ref> He was sidelined for six months. On 13 May 2012, he scored his first and only [[Ligue 1]] goal for Marseille in a 3–0 win over [[AJ Auxerre|Auxerre]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/match/olympique-marseille-v-auxerre/lineups/3ruqjhud6smd2ls9lw1wsrpat |title=Olympique Marseille 3–0 Auxerre |website=Goal.com |date=13 May 2012}}</ref>

In August 2012, amid speculation of clubs showing interest in Azpilicueta, including [[Premier League]] club [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], Marseille confirmed that he could leave, saying: "If Chelsea makes a fair offer for Azpi [Azpilicueta], we will let him leave."<ref>{{Cite news|first=Patrick|last=Haond|title=Marseille confirm need to sell|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11668/7988728/Marseille-confirm-need-to-sell|website=[[Sky Sports]]|date=14 August 2012|access-date=6 July 2024}}</ref> Despite his loyalty to Marseille, the footballer said he was willing to leave if his "departure can help Marseille's finances".<ref>{{Cite news|title=Azpilicueta open to Blues move|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/12691/8007076/Azpilicueta-open-to-Blues-move|website=Sky Sports|date=21 August 2012|access-date=6 July 2024}}</ref>

===Chelsea===
====2012–2013: Inaugural season and First Europa League title====
On 24 August 2012, Chelsea completed the signing of Azpilicueta for an undisclosed fee, reported as £7 million.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2898781 |title=Azpilicueta signs |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=24 August 2012|access-date=24 August 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120830171700/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2898781|archive-date=30 August 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11668/8014372/Azpilicueta-joins-Chelsea |title=Azpilicueta joins Chelsea |website=Sky Sports |date=24 August 2012|access-date=24 August 2012}}</ref> According to teammate and countryman [[Juan Mata]], "He is a strong running right-back who has pace as well, so I think he is already a complete player."<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2899038/title/di-matteo%3A-cesar-offers-options |title=Di Matteo: Cesar offers options |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=24 August 2012|access-date=24 August 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120830171757/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/2899038/title/di-matteo:-cesar-offers-options|archive-date=30 August 2012}}</ref> Due to his surname being difficult for some speakers of English to pronounce, club fans gave him the [[Mononymous person|mononymous]] nickname "Dave".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/cesar-dave-azpilicueta-shows-the-attitude-to-delight-chelsea-manager-jose-mourinho-9759011.html |title=Cesar 'Dave' Azpilicueta shows the attitude to delight Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho |newspaper=[[The Independent]] |first=Glenn |last=Moore |date=26 September 2014|access-date=18 October 2014}}</ref>

Azpilicueta made his debut on 25 September 2012, starting in a 6–0 home win against [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] in a [[2012–13 Football League Cup|League Cup]] tie.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19632463 |title=Chelsea 6–0 Wolves |website=BBC Sport |date=25 September 2012|access-date=26 September 2012}}</ref> He played his first Premier League game the following week, coming on as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for [[Branislav Ivanović]] in a 4–1 success over [[Norwich City F.C|Norwich City]], also at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/19776324 |title=Chelsea put their off-field troubles aside as they emphatically beat struggling Norwich to continue to set the Premier League pace. |website=BBC Sport |first=Mandeep |last=Sanghera |date=6 October 2012|access-date=26 July 2017}}</ref>

On 3 November 2012, Azpilicueta made his first league start, appearing against [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]] in a 1–1 away draw.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espnfc.com/report?gameId=345755 |title=Swansea City 1–1 Chelsea |website=ESPN FC |date=3 November 2012|access-date=3 November 2012}}</ref> He played 48 official contests in [[2012–13 Premier League|his first year]] with the [[Rafael Benítez]]-led side, including eight in the Blues' [[2012–13 UEFA Europa League|victorious campaign]] in the [[UEFA Europa League]]. In [[2013 UEFA Europa League Final|the final]] against [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]], his 67th-minute handball led to [[Óscar Cardozo]] equalising through a [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty kick]], in an eventual 2–1 win in [[Amsterdam]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0250-0c50fd9b3ece-eb6083db556a-1000--ivanovic-heads-chelsea-to-europa-league-glory/ |title=Ivanović heads Chelsea to Europa League glory |publisher=UEFA |date=15 May 2013|access-date=16 May 2013}}</ref>

====2013–2017: Two Premier League titles====
[[File:César Azpilicueta Chelsea vs AS-Roma 10AUG2013.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Azpilicueta playing for [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in 2013]]
Azpilicueta scored his first competitive goal for Chelsea on 29 October 2013, netting the first in a 2–0 victory at [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] in the fourth round of the [[2013–14 Football League Cup|League Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/24619361 |title=Arsenal 0–2 Chelsea |website=BBC Sport |first=Alistair |last=Magowan |date=29 October 2013|access-date=30 October 2013}}</ref> Following the arrival of new manager [[José Mourinho]], he began appearing regularly as a left-back, taking the place of longtime incumbent [[Ashley Cole]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/match/122498/fc-schalke-04-vs-chelsea-fc/report |title=Schalke 0–3 Chelsea: Impressive Torres bags double |website=Goal.com |first=Peter |last=Thompson |date=22 October 2013|access-date=18 December 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/chelseas-cesar-azpilicueta-ready-keep-2785715 |title=Chelsea's Cesar Azpilicueta ready to keep sub standard Ashley Cole on the bench |newspaper=[[Daily Mirror]] |first=Darren |last=Lewis |date=12 November 2013|access-date=18 December 2013}}</ref> Mourinho said of him: "Azpilicueta is the kind of player I like a lot. I think a team with 11 Azpilicuetas would probably win the competition (Champions League) because football is not just about pure talent".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://uk.eurosport.yahoo.com/news/premier-league-mourinho-team-azpilicuetas-win-champions-league-094720824--sow.html |title=Premier League – Mourinho: A team of Azpilicuetas would win the Champions League |publisher=Eurosport |date=26 February 2014|access-date=13 May 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140515031426/https://uk.eurosport.yahoo.com/news/premier-league-mourinho-team-azpilicuetas-win-champions-league-094720824--sow.html|archive-date=15 May 2014}}</ref> At the end of [[2013–14 Chelsea F.C. season|the season]], he was voted the club's Players' Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/teams/first-team/cesar-azpilicueta |title=Cesar Azpilicueta |publisher=Chelsea F.C.|access-date=24 August 2012}}</ref>

[[File:César Azpilicueta - Сесар Аспиликуэта (22362918831).jpg|thumb|upright|Azpilicueta playing for Chelsea in 2015]]

Before the start of the [[2014–15 Premier League|2014–15 season]], Cole was released and the club spent £15.8 million on [[Filipe Luís]], but Azpilicueta began the season as first-choice left-back.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/jose-mourinho-has-taught-me-to-put-the-collective-first--chelseas-filipe-luis-happy-to-play-waiting-game-9755093.html |title=Jose Mourinho has taught me to put the collective first – Chelsea's Filipe Luis happy to play waiting game |newspaper=[[London Evening Standard]] |first=Simon |last=Johnson |date=25 September 2014|access-date=19 October 2014}}</ref> On 2 September 2014, he signed a new five-year contract with the club<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2014/09/new-contract-for-azpilicueta.html |title=New contract for Azpilicueta |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=2 September 2014|access-date=2 September 2014}}</ref> and on 18 October, he was [[Ejection (sports)|sent off]] in the first half of a 2–1 win at [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] for a foul on [[Mile Jedinak]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/oct/18/crystal-palace-chelsea-premier-league-match-report |title=Chelsea stay top after Cesc Fàbregas nets winner at Crystal Palace |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |first=Dominic |last=Fifield |date=18 October 2014|access-date=18 October 2014}}</ref>

Azpilicueta started as Chelsea won the [[2015 Football League Cup Final|League Cup]] on 1 March 2015. In the second half, he was injured in a collision with [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]]'s [[Eric Dier]], and had to leave the pitch for a bandage to be wrapped around his head.<ref name=LC>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2015/mar/01/chelsea-v-tottenham-hotspur-capital-one-cup-final-live |title=Chelsea v Tottenham Hotspur: Capital One Cup final – as it happened |newspaper=The Guardian |first=Jacob |last=Steinberg |date=1 March 2015|access-date=2 March 2015}}</ref> [[2014–15 Chelsea F.C. season|The campaign]] ended with the additional conquest of the domestic league title, after a five-year wait.

On 2 August 2015, Azpilicueta featured for 69 minutes in the 1–0 [[2015 FA Community Shield|FA Community Shield]] loss to [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33667216 |title=Arsenal 1–0 Chelsea |website=BBC Sport |first=Andy |last=Cryer |date=2 August 2015|access-date=2 August 2015}}</ref> Nineteen days later, he scored the team's third goal in a 3–2 away win over [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]], for what was his first Premier League goal,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33950789 |title=West Bromwich Albion 2–3 Chelsea |website=BBC Sport |last1=Magowan |first1=Alistair |date=23 August 2015|access-date=23 August 2015}}</ref> and he netted again in a 2–2 draw in the reverse fixture on 13 January 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/35239779 |title=Chelsea 2–2 West Bromwich Albion |website=BBC Sport |first=Mike |last=Henson |date=13 January 2016|access-date=21 August 2016}}</ref>

Although Azpilicueta was initially used as a left-back under new coach [[Antonio Conte]], after two consecutive league defeats, the latter changed to a back-three formation, with the former playing as a centre-back in the following match against [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] on 1 October 2016, which ended in a 2–0 away win.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37459840 |title=Hull City 0–2 Chelsea |website=BBC Sport |first=Mike |last=Henson |date=1 October 2016|access-date=18 October 2016}}</ref> On 13 December 2016, he signed a new three-and-a-half-year contract with Chelsea, running until 2020;<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/dec/13/cesar-azpilicueta-signs-new-three-and-a-half-year-contract-chelsea |title=César Azpilicueta extends Chelsea stay but Terry's situation stays on hold |newspaper=The Guardian |first=Dominic |last=Fifield |date=13 December 2016|access-date=13 December 2016}}</ref> in his first appearance following the agreement he made his 200th competitive appearance for the club, in a 1–0 away victory over [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.chelseafc.com/matches/2016-17/12/sunderland-chelsea-pl.html |title=Sunderland 0–1 Chelsea |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=14 December 2016|access-date=17 December 2016}}</ref>

Azpilicueta played every minute of [[2016–17 Premier League|the season]] as his team won the domestic league, and scored in a 4–3 home win against [[Watford F.C|Watford]] after the title was already won.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.express.co.uk/sport/football/804975/Chelsea-Cesar-Azpilicueta-Watford-Premier-League-goal |title=Chelsea star reflects on 'special moment' after Watford win |newspaper=[[Daily Express]] |first=Charles |last=Perrin |date=16 May 2017|access-date=25 May 2017}}</ref>

====2017–2020: FA Cup victory, second Europa League title and assuming captaincy====
[[File:César Azpilicueta 2017.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Azpilicueta playing for Chelsea in 2017]]
In late July 2017, after the departure of [[John Terry]], he was appointed [[Captain (association football)|vice-captain]] to [[Gary Cahill]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2017/07/captain-cahill--delighted--proud-and-excited.html |title=Captain Cahill: Delighted, proud and excited |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=26 July 2017|access-date=26 July 2017}}</ref> On 12 September that year, he scored his first Champions League goal, in a [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League|6–0 group stage home win]] against [[Qarabağ FK]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2017/09/12/chelsea-6-qarabag-0-davide-zappacosta-marks-full-debut-goal/ |title=Chelsea 6 Qarabag 0: Davide Zappacosta marks full debut with goal as half-strength hosts run riot |newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |first=Matt |last=Law |date=12 September 2017|access-date=12 September 2017}}</ref> On 19 May 2018, he won the FA Cup title after a 1–0 victory for Chelsea over [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] in the [[2018 FA Cup final|final]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2018/may/19/chelsea-v-manchester-united-2018-fa-cup-final-live |title=Chelsea 1-0 Manchester United: 2018 FA Cup final – as it happened |work=The Guardian |date=19 May 2018 }}</ref>

Azpilicueta signed a new deal in December 2018, lasting to 2022.<ref>{{cite news |last1=de Menezes |first1=Jack |title=Cesar Azpilicueta signs new four-year Chelsea deal to 'keep the club where it belongs' |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/chelsea-news-cesar-azpilicueta-contracts-new-deal-four-year-trophies-captain-premier-league-a8666026.html |access-date=25 April 2021 |newspaper=The Independent |date=4 December 2018}}</ref> On 29 May 2019, he won his second Europa League with Chelsea after a 4–1 victory over Arsenal in the [[2019 UEFA Europa League Final|final]] at the [[Baku Olympic Stadium]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2019/05/29/europa-league-final-2019-chelsea-vs-arsenal-live-score-latest/ |title=Eden Hazard inspires Chelsea to win Europa League as they thrash sorry Arsenal |publisher=The Telegraph |date=29 May 2019 }}</ref>

After Cahill left Chelsea, he was named club captain ahead of the [[2019–20 Premier League|2019–20 season]]; he had already worn the armband on the pitch while the Englishman was out of the team, including in the Europa League final victory against Arsenal in Azerbaijan.<ref>{{cite news |title=Cesar Azpilicueta exclusive part one: Captaincy, Gary Cahill and youth international leadership |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2019/09/11/cesar-azpilicueta-exclusive-part-one--captaincy--gary-cahill-and |access-date=8 November 2019 |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=11 September 2019}}</ref> On 23 October 2019, he marked his 350th Chelsea appearance with a [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League|1–0 group stage away win]] against [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] in the Champions League.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/videos/v/2019/10/23/_--one-of-the-best----cesar-azpilicueta-makes-350th-chelsea-appe-I0MjhvaTE6NvWW1h1Js0ECpZmx_T4Swe |title=🎥 "ONE OF THE BEST" {{!}} CESAR AZPILICUETA MAKES 350TH CHELSEA APPEARANCE!👏|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|date=23 October 2019|access-date=24 October 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite tweet |title=Tonight's game will be @CesarAzpi's 3️⃣5️⃣0️⃣th as a Blue! 👏 Go well, Azpi! #AJACHE |number=1187034192841969667 |user=ChelseaFC |date=23 October 2019 |access-date=24 October 2019}}</ref>

On 1 January 2020, Azpilicueta marked his 100th appearance as club captain with a goal and being named man of the match in the 1–1 draw against [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/B6xrpxrpRif/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/iarchive/s/instagram/B6xrpxrpRif |archive-date=26 December 2021 |url-access=registration |title=Set for @CesarAzpi's 100th start as Chelsea captain! 💯 #CFC #Chelsea |date=1 January 2020 |website=Instagram|access-date=1 January 2020}}{{cbignore}}</ref> On 1 August, during the 2–1 defeat to Arsenal in the [[2020 FA Cup Final]], Azpilicueta conceded a penalty and was later injured, leading to his substitution.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Arsenal 2–1 Chelsea |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/53546100 |website=BBC Sport |date=1 August 2020 |access-date=3 August 2020}}</ref>

====2020–21 season: Champions League triumph====
Azpilicueta became the 13th player in Chelsea's history to make 400 appearances, when he featured against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] on 3 January 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Joining the 400 club |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2021/01/04/joining-the-400-club |access-date=25 April 2021 |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=5 January 2021}}</ref> On 23 May, the final matchday of the [[2020–21 Premier League|league season]], he was sent off for appearing to strike [[Aston Villa]]'s [[Jack Grealish]] during a 1–2 defeat, but the three-game suspension was overturned on appeal.<ref>{{cite news|first=Malik|last=Ouzia|title=Chelsea FC defender Cesar Azpilicueta has red card overturned after Jack Grealish clash |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/chelsea-fc-cesar-azpilicueta-red-card-overturned-jack-grealish-b937194.html |access-date=29 May 2021 |newspaper=Evening Standard |date=25 May 2021}}</ref> Six days later, he captained the team to a 1–0 victory in the [[2021 UEFA Champions League Final|UEFA Champions League Final]] against Manchester City at the [[Estádio do Dragão]], [[Porto]], winning their first Champions League title in 9 years.<ref name=cl21>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/57268064 |title=Manchester City 0–1 Chelsea |website=BBC Sport |date=29 May 2021 |access-date=29 May 2021 |first=Phil |last=McNulty}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0269-12650cedca55-37515f69768e-1000--report-chelsea-claim-second-title/ |title=Man. City 0-1 Chelsea: Havertz gives Blues second Champions League triumph |website=[[UEFA]] |date=29 May 2021 |access-date=29 May 2021}}</ref>

On 28 August 2021, Azpilicueta reached a milestone as he became the fourth Chelsea player to reach 300 Premier League appearances after [[John Terry]] (492), [[Frank Lampard]] (429) and [[Petr Čech]] (333). He started against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] in a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://sport.optus.com.au/articles/os30643/liverpool-chelsea-james-red-tuchel-klopp-reaction |title=Thomas Tuchel says Reece James' red card 'spoiled' Liverpool v Chelsea |website=Optus Sport |date=29 August 2021 |access-date=29 August 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2021/08/29/azpilicueta-on-adapting-to-the-challenge-and-his-pride-at-300-ga |title=Azpi on adapting to the challenge and his pride at 300 games in 'the toughest league in the world' |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=29 August 2021 |access-date=29 August 2021}}</ref>

====2021–22 season: UEFA Super Cup and FIFA Club World Cup titles====

[[File:César Azpilicueta & Salem Al-Dawsari, Al Hilal SFC vs Chelsea F.C., 9 February 2022.jpg|thumb|upright|Azpilicueta (right) and [[Al Hilal SFC|Al Hilal]]'s [[Salem Al-Dawsari]] clashing during the [[2021 FIFA Club World Cup]]]]

On 8 October 2021, Azpilicueta was one of five Chelsea players included in the final 30-man shortlist for the 2021 [[Ballon d'Or]].<ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/chelsea/news/official-five-chelsea-players-among-30-man-ballon-dor-shortlist |title=Official: Azpilicueta, Kante, Jorginho, Mount & Lukaku Among Chelsea Players On 30-Man 2021 Ballon d'Or Shortlist |magazine=Sports Illustrated |date=8 October 2021 |access-date=8 October 2021}}</ref>

On 12 February 2022, Azpilicueta lifted the trophy in the [[2021 FIFA Club World Cup Final]] in their second FIFA Club World Cup Final, the first one being in [[2012 FIFA Club World Cup Final|2012]] when Chelsea lost to [[Sport Club Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Club World Cup: Champions League holders Chelsea become eighth European winners|date=12 February 2022|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0271-143308c604e5-48d7851a3e61-1000--chelsea-into-club-world-cup-final/}}</ref> With this trophy and the [[UEFA Super Cup]] secured shortly before, it meant he became the first and only Chelsea player to have won every major trophy at the club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/chelsea/2022/02/13/6208e16f268e3e93698b4585.html|title=Azpilicueta adds to impressive Chelsea trophy haul, with just one title eluding him|date=13 February 2022}}</ref>

====2022–23 season: Appearance records and departure====
On 4 August 2022, he signed a new contract with Chelsea until 2024.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/azpilicueta-commits-to-chelsea |title=Azpilicueta commits to Chelsea |website=Chelsea FC |date=4 August 2022 }}</ref>

On 1 January 2023, Azpilicueta played his 495th game for Chelsea, surpassing [[Petr Čech]] as the non-Englishman with the most appearances for the club.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/nottingham-forest-vs-chelsea-debrief-azpilicueta-breaks-record-in-a-game-of |title=Nottingham Forest vs Chelsea Debrief: Azpilicueta breaks record in a game of two halves |website=Chelsea FC |date=2 January 2023 }}</ref> On 21 January, he played his 500th match for the club, becoming only the sixth player (and first foreigner) in its history to reach that milestone.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/azpilicueta-joins-the-500-club-chelseas-all-time-highest-appearance-makers |title=Azpilicueta joins the 500 club |website=Chelsea FC|date=21 January 2023 }}</ref>

On 18 February, during a game between Chelsea and [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]], Azpilicueta was knocked unconscious after being accidentally kicked in the head by Southampton's [[Sékou Mara]]. Mara was attempting an overhead kick late in the game when he missed the ball and connected with Azpilicueta instead. Azpilicueta was rushed to hospital after the incident after being stretchered off the pitch.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Azpilicueta 'speaking' in hospital after head injury|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64693389|website=[[BBC Sport]]|publisher=[[BBC]]|access-date=19 February 2023}}</ref>

On 6 July 2023, Azpilicueta announced his parting with Chelsea, marking the end of a decade-long association with the club.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cesar Azpilicueta: The Chelsea player who won it all |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/cesar-azpilicueta-the-chelsea-player-who-won-it-all|website=Chelsea FC|access-date=6 July 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|title=Captain Azpilicueta confirms Chelsea departure|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66079631|website=[[BBC Sport]]|publisher=[[BBC]]|access-date=6 July 2023}}</ref> His departure was confirmed via a video message he shared on social media, wherein he signed off as "Your captain Cesar Azpilicueta, aka 'Dave' ".<ref>{{Cite web|title=Congratulations, Azpi|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/congratulations-azpi|website=Chelsea FC|access-date=6 July 2023}}</ref>

=== Atlético Madrid ===
Following the departure from Chelsea, Azpilicueta returned to [[La Liga]] after 13 years and joined [[Atlético Madrid]] by signing a one-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 July 2023 |title=Welcome, Azpilicueta! |url=https://en.atleticodemadrid.com/noticias/welcome-azpilicueta |access-date=6 July 2023 |website=Club Atlético de Madrid}}</ref> He made his debut for the club on 14 August, in a 3–1 [[2023–24 La Liga|league]] win over [[Granada CF|Granada]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 August 2023 |title=Depay belter helps Atletico Madrid to LaLiga win over Granada |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/674013 |access-date=15 August 2023 |website=ESPN}}</ref>

Having played a total number of 34 games in his first season, he renewed his contract with the club for another year in June 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=30 June 2024 |title=César Azpilicueta renueva por una temporada |url=https://www.atleticodemadrid.com/noticias/cesar-azpilicueta-renueva-por-una-temporada |access-date=30 June 2024 |website=Club Atlético de Madrid |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Díaz |first=F.J. |date=30 June 2024 |title=Azpilicueta renueva por una temporada más |url=https://as.com/futbol/primera/azpilicueta-renueva-por-una-temporada-mas-n/ |access-date=30 June 2024 |website=Diario AS |language=es}}</ref> A year later, it was announced that Azpilicueta would not be extending his contract with Atletico Madrid beyond the [[2024–25 La Liga]] season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://en.atleticodemadrid.com/noticias/thank-you-azpilicueta |title=Thank you, Azpilicueta! |publisher=Club Atlético de Madrid |date=30 June 2025}}</ref>

=== Sevilla ===
On 29 August 2025, Azpilicueta signed a one-year deal with La Liga club [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]]. The contract also included an option to extend until 2027.<ref name="as"/> On 22 May 2026, he announced his retirement from professional football by the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://onefootball.com/fr/news/cesar-azpilicueta-announces-retirement-from-professional-football-42905266 |title=César Azpilicueta announces retirement from professional football |publisher=OneFootball |date=22 May 2026}}</ref> Next day, on 23 May 2026, at the 2025–26 La Liga final round against [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]], he played his last professional match.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sevillafc.es/actualidad/noticias/reacciones-jugadores-rc-celta-sevilla-fc-laliga-25-26|title=AZPILICUETA: "ME VOY SATISFECHO POR HABER DEFENDIDO ESTOS COLORES"|date=24 May 2026|access-date=24 May 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
===Youth===
[[File:César Azpilicueta U21.jpg|thumb|upright|Azpilicueta playing for [[Spain national under-21 football team|Spain under-21s]] in 2011]]

In [[2007 UEFA European Under-19 Championship|2007]], Azpilicueta helped the [[Spain national under-19 football team|Spain under-19 team]] win the [[UEFA European Under-19 Championship|UEFA European Championship]].<ref name=under19>{{cite news |last1=Huerta |first1=Daniel |last2=Ashby |first2=Kevin |title=Azpilicueta out to prove a point |url=https://www.uefa.com/under21/news/0257-0de960cbf74e-519220a24d00-1000--azpilicueta-out-to-prove-a-point/ |access-date=25 April 2021 |date=20 June 2009}}</ref> Shortly after he moved to [[Spain national under-21 football team|the under-21s]], being picked for the [[2009 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|2009 European Championships]] in Sweden where he started three matches in an eventual group stage exit.

On 11 May 2010, 20-year-old Azpilicueta was named by [[Spain national football team|senior side]] manager [[Vicente del Bosque]] in a provisional list of 30 players, in view of [[2010 FIFA World Cup|the forthcoming edition]] of the [[FIFA World Cup]]. Eventually, he did not make the final cut.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.marca.com/2010/05/10/futbol/seleccion/1273509662.html |title=Valdés, De Gea, Azpilicueta, Javi Martínez y Pedro entran en la preselección de 30|trans-title=Valdés, De Gea, Azpilicueta, Javi Martínez and Pedro make shortlist of 30 |newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]] |language=es |date=10 May 2010|access-date=15 April 2014}}</ref> A year later, after recovering from a long-term injury, he went to the [[2011 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|European Under-21 Championship]] in Denmark, and won the tournament.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Gabilondo |first1=Aritz |title=Sub-21: con Azpilicueta pero sin Busquets ni ningún madridista|trans-title=Under-21s: with Azpilicueta but without Busquets nor any Real Madrid player |url=https://as.com/opinion/2011/05/26/blogs/1306409466_1161798.html |access-date=25 April 2021 |newspaper=Diario AS |date=26 May 2011 |language=Spanish}}</ref><ref name=sub21>{{cite news |last1=García |first1=Miguel Ángel |title=¿Qué fue de los campeones sub 21 de España de 2011?|trans-title=What happened to Spain Under-21's 2011 champions? |url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/europeo-sub-21/2021/03/24/605b189aca47410b7d8b4605.html |access-date=25 April 2021 |newspaper=Marca |date=24 March 2021 |language=Spanish}}</ref>

Azpilicueta was picked for [[Spain national under-23 football team|Spain's squad]] for the [[2012 Summer Olympics]], after missing out on selection for the [[UEFA Euro 2012]] tournament.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/olympics/18693622 |title=Euro 2012 trio Mata, Alba & Martinez in Spain Olympic squad |website=BBC Sport |date=5 July 2012|access-date=8 September 2017}}</ref> Due to the presence of [[Álvaro Domínguez (footballer, born 1989)|Álvaro Domínguez]], he only appeared in the last group match, a 0–0 draw with Morocco at [[Old Trafford]], as the national team [[Football at the 2012 Summer Olympics|exited in the group stage]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/match/spain-u23-vs-morocco-u23/1281843/report |title=Spain 0–0 Morocco: La Roja fail to fire again to finish bottom of Olympics Group D |website=Goal.com |date=1 August 2012|access-date=14 August 2018}}</ref>

The manager said of the selection: 'Azpilicueta is playing many games for Chelsea. He has a lot of energy, defends well and is always willing to attack. We have a lot of hope for him.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/3061623/title/azpilicueta-called-up-by-spain |title=Azpilicueta called up by Spain |publisher=Chelsea 2013}}</ref>

In June 2014, Azpilicueta was selected to represent Spain in the [[2014 FIFA World Cup]] in Brazil.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/spain/10810213/Spain-World-Cup-2014-squad.html |title=Spain World Cup 2014 squad |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |date=2 June 2014|access-date=14 June 2014}}</ref> He was the starting right-back during the first two fixtures, against the [[Netherlands national football team|Netherlands]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/25285043 |title=Spain 1–5 Netherlands |website=BBC Sport |first=David |last=Ornstein |date=13 June 2014|access-date=26 June 2014}}</ref> and [[Chile national football team|Chile]], as the nation was eliminated at the group stage.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/25285155 |title=Spain 0–2 Chile |website=BBC Sport |first=David |last=Ornstein |date=18 June 2014|access-date=26 June 2014}}</ref>

Azpilicueta was also included in the 23-man squad for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018 World Cup]] in Russia,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/morata-misses-out-on-spain-world-cup-squad/1ub1qz7jod09i1lfvdcy84ea2l |title=Morata misses out on Spain's 23-man World Cup squad |website=Goal.com |date=21 May 2018|access-date=21 May 2018}}</ref> as well as the [[UEFA Euro 2020 squads#Spain|24-man squad]] for [[UEFA Euro 2020]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Westwood |first1=James |title=Real Madrid captain Ramos left out of Spain squad for Euro 2020 but Laporte included after France switch |url=https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/real-madrid-captain-ramos-left-out-of-spains-final-squad-for/1n3dozg35kboi1s580fgohl5ox |access-date=30 June 2021 |website=Goal.com |date=25 May 2021}}</ref> At the latter, he scored his first senior international goal, his team's second of a 5–3 win against [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]] in the [[UEFA Euro 2020 knockout phase|round of 16]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Croatia 1–2 Spain |work=BBC Sport|date=27 June 2021|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/live/football/50941426|url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210628160112/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/live/football/50941426 |archive-date=28 June 2021}}</ref>

Azpilicueta captained Spain for the first time in a [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification]] match against [[Georgia national football team|Georgia]] on 5 September 2021.<ref>{{Cite magazine |title='It's a Great Memento' – César Azpilicueta Expresses Delight at Captaining Chelsea And Spain |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/chelsea/news/its-a-great-memento-cesar-azpilicueta-expresses-delight-at-captaining-chelsea-and-spain|url-status=live |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210907104117/https://www.si.com/soccer/chelsea/news/its-a-great-memento-cesar-azpilicueta-expresses-delight-at-captaining-chelsea-and-spain |archive-date=7 September 2021}}</ref> He was included in Spain's 26-man squad for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup|2022 World Cup]] in Qatar, appearing twice at the tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 Spain Stats (World Cup) |url=https://fbref.com/en/squads/b561dd30/2022/c1/Spain-Men-Stats-World-Cup|website=fbref.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Azpilicueta was born in [[Zizur Mayor/Zizur Nagusia|Zizur Mayor]], [[Navarre]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.noticiasdenavarra.com/osasuna/centenario/2020/10/24/azpilicueta-adn-rojillo/1089124.html |title=Azpilicueta y su 'ADN rojillo' |language=es |publisher=Noticias de Navarra |date=24 October 2020|access-date=23 November 2021}}</ref> to Patxi Azpilicueta, a decorator and Charo Tanco, a primary school teacher.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2012/08/24/actualidad/1345821829_866715.html |title=Azpilicueta también es del Chelsea |newspaper=El País |language=es |date=24 August 2012 | access-date=15 June 2021|last1=Quixano |first1=Jordi }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ondacero.es/programas/radioestadio/audios-podcast/entrevistas/charo-madre-cesar-azpilicueta-tenia-ganas-que-pasara-vacaciones-nosotros-pero-prefiero-que-vaya-eurocopa_2021052960b29ed4a7609600019f93c3.html |title=Charo, la madre de César Azpilicueta: "Tenía ganas de que pasara las vacaciones con nosotros pero prefiero que vaya a la Eurocopa" |website=ondacero.es |language=es |date=29 May 2021 | access-date=15 June 2021}}</ref> Azpilicueta's older brother, Juan Pablo (born 1980), was also a footballer. A midfielder, he competed exclusively in lower-league football.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ivoox.com/entrevista-el-penalty-a-juan-pablo-azpilicueta-audios-mp3_rf_2597911_1.html |title=Entrevista en El Penalty a Juan Pablo Azpilicueta jugador del C.D. Tudelano|trans-title=El Penalty interview to Juan Pablo Azpilicueta C.D. Tudelano player |publisher=iVoox |language=es |date=28 November 2013|access-date=20 October 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.diariodenavarra.es/noticias/deportes/futbol/2014/03/26/juan_pablo_azpilicueta_reaparecio_despues_dos_meses_baja_152926_1022.html |title=Juan Pablo Azpilicueta reapareció después de dos meses de baja|trans-title=Juan Pablo Azpilicueta reappeared after two months out |newspaper=Diario de Navarra |first=Fermín |last=Astráin |language=es |date=26 March 2014|access-date=20 October 2015}}</ref> Since retiring, Juan Pablo has transitioned into management.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.noticiasdenavarra.com/deportes/futbol/2020/05/26/continuidad-banquillos-tercera/1049250.html |title=Continuidad en los banquillos de Tercera |website=noticiasdenavarra.com |language=es |date=26 May 2020 | access-date=15 June 2021}}</ref> Most recently, he served as manager of [[CD Subiza]] in Spain's [[2020–21 Tercera División|Tercera División]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://golsmedia.com/navarra/futbol/cd-subiza-cendea-de-galar/2021/03/24/jorge-sola-sustituye-juan-pablo-azpilicueta/ |title=Jorge Sola sustituye a Juan Pablo Azpilicueta |website=golsmedia.com |language=es |date=24 March 2021 | access-date=15 June 2021}}</ref>

In June 2015, Azpilicueta married his long-term girlfriend Adriana Guerendiain.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.elmundo.es/loc/2015/05/28/5565de9e46163f57388b4591.html |title=Boda española en el Chelsea |website=elmundo.es |language=es |date=28 May 2015 | access-date=15 June 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.elmundo.es/album/loc/famosos/2018/05/26/5b084663468aeb89658b45ae_6.html |title=César Azpilicueta y Adriana Guerendiain |website=elmundo.es |language=es |date=28 May 2018}}</ref> Together, the couple have three children; two daughters and a son.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.diariodenavarra.es/noticias/deportes/futbol/osasuna/2021/05/25/azpilicueta-poder-representar-pais-torneo-esta-magnitud-maximo-727928-1027.html |title=¿Quién es César Azpilicueta, el navarro que ha levantado la Copa de Europa como capitán del Chelsea? |website=diariodenavarra.es |language=es |date=30 May 2021}}</ref> Adriana gave birth to the couple's first daughter, Martina, in March 2014.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/chelseas-cesar-azpilicueta-hoping-celebrate-3339797 |title=Chelsea's Cesar Azpilicueta hoping to celebrate birth of his daughter with Champions League win in Paris |website=mirror.co.uk |language=en |date=2 April 2014 | access-date=15 June 2021}}</ref>

Since 2018, Azpilicueta has been a board member and co-owner of English [[Non-League football|non-league]] side [[Hashtag United F.C.|Hashtag United]], which plays in the {{English football updater|HashtagU}}.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.insider.com/hashtag-united-semi-pro-youtube-football-team-with-500000-fans-2020-11 |title=Meet Hashtag United, the English semi-pro soccer team supported by 500,000 people on YouTube and part-owned by a Chelsea FC star |first=Barnaby |last=Lane |publisher=Insider Inc. |date=14 November 2020|access-date=29 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2020/10/21/media-watch--chelsea-s-defensive-display-lauded-by-ex-blues-star |title=Media Watch: Chelsea's defensive display lauded by ex-Blues star, Cesar Azpilicueta gives half-time talk to non-league side, Maurizio Sarri linked with new coaching job |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=21 October 2020|access-date=29 May 2021}}</ref> In 2020, Azpilicueta announced the formation of his own [[esports]] team, Falcons.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/chelsea/story/4094569/chelsea-boss-cesar-azpilicueta-lining-up-life-after-football-with-his-own-esports-team |title=Chelsea 'boss' Cesar Azpilicueta lining up life after football with his own esports team |website=espn.com |language=en |date=20 May 2020 | access-date=15 June 2021}}</ref> He is part-owner along with Jose Antonio Cacho and Jesus Rincon, both of whom are top players in Spain with millions of [[YouTube]] subscribers.

Azpilicueta is [[trilingualism|trilingual]]. He is fluent in [[Spanish language|Spanish]], [[French language|French]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/chelsea/news/cesar-azpilicueta-reveals-why-the-chelsea-defence-spoke-french-during-crystal-palace-win |title=Cesar Azpilicueta happy to communicate in French with new signings Edoaurd Mendy and Thiago Silva |website=Sports Illustrated Fan Nation |date=8 October 2020|access-date=14 January 2021}}</ref> and [[English language|English]]. As of 2021, he was working to complete an online degree, an MBA in Business Management from the Berlin School of Business and Innovation.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2051321/2020/09/09/cesar-azpilicueta-chelsea-captain-conte-lampard/ |title=Cesar Azpilicueta – assertive, ambitious and the epitome of Chelsea |website=theathletic.com |language=en |date=8 September 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/seleccion/2021/06/03/60b7d14cca47411b218b4651.html |title=El método Azpilicueta ya está al servicio de la España de Luis Enrique |website=marca.com |language=es |date=3 June 2021}}</ref>
In June 2023, Azpilicueta announced on his Instagram page that he had successfully completed a 4-day course and received a certificate in the business of entertainment, media and sports from [[Harvard Business School]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://chelseauniversal.com/cesar-azpilicueta-graduates-from-harvard-business-school-pics/ |title=Cesar Azpilicueta graduates from Harvard Business School (Pics) |website=Chelsea Universal |language=en |date=6 June 2023 |access-date=8 June 2023 |archive-date=6 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230606171242/https://chelseauniversal.com/cesar-azpilicueta-graduates-from-harvard-business-school-pics/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="HBS">{{cite web |title=The Business of Entertainment, Media, and Sports |url=https://pll.harvard.edu/course/business-entertainment-media-and-sports |website=Harvard University |date=5 November 2021 |access-date=July 2, 2024}}</ref>

'''Lucas Vázquez Iglesias''' (born 1 July 1991) is a Spanish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[right-back]] or [[Winger (association football)|winger]] for {{German football updater|BaLeverk}} club [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]].

Starting his career at [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], Vázquez made his first-team debut in 2015 after a season on loan at [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]]. He made his [[La Liga]] debut with the latter. Since returning to Real Madrid in 2015 he has appeared in more than 400 matches for the club in all competitions and has won 23 major trophies including five [[UEFA Champions League|Champions Leagues]] and four [[La Liga]] titles. After leaving Real Madrid as a free agent in summer 2025, Vázquez moved to Bundesliga's Bayer Leverkusen.

Vázquez represented [[Spain national football team|Spain]] at [[UEFA Euro 2016|Euro 2016]] and the [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018 World Cup]].

==Club career==
===Early career===
Born in [[Curtis, Spain|Curtis]], Galicia, Vázquez arrived at [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]]'s youth system in 2007, aged 16.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lucas Vazquez Iglesias |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/football/first-team/players/lucas-vazquez-iglesias |access-date=2025-02-07 |website=www.realmadrid.com}}</ref> He made his senior debut in the [[2010–11 Segunda División B|2010–11 season]] with the [[Real Madrid C|C-team]]. He scored four goals in 23 games in [[2011–12 Segunda División B|the following season]] to help the [[Real Madrid Castilla|reserves]] return to the [[Segunda División]] after a five-year absence. His first goal came on 25 February 2012 in a 2–2 home draw against [[La Roda CF|La Roda]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/ActualidadCantera1112/1330087479318/noticia/Noticia/Fourteen_players_score_for_Castilla.htm|title=Fourteen players score for Castilla|publisher=Real Madrid CF|date=27 February 2012|access-date=24 May 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130201013136/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/ActualidadCantera1112/1330087479318/noticia/Noticia/Fourteen_players_score_for_Castilla.htm|archive-date=1 February 2013}}</ref>

Vázquez made his first appearance in the second level on 17 August 2012, playing six minutes in a 1–2 away loss against [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2012/08/17/futbol/2adivision/1345237033.html|title=Cavenaghi toma los mandos del 'Submarino'|trans-title=Cavenaghi takes charge of the 'Submarine'|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|first=Diego|last=Acedo|language=es|date=17 August 2012|access-date=24 May 2013}}</ref> He scored his first professional goal on 15 October, netting the winner in a 3–2 home success over [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2012/10/15/futbol/2adivision/1350334344.html|title=El 'loco' Castilla enajena a Las Palmas|trans-title='Crazy' Castilla estrange Las Palmas|newspaper=Marca|location=Spain|language=es|date=15 October 2012|access-date=20 August 2014}}</ref>

====Loan to Espanyol====
On 19 August 2014, Vázquez was loaned to [[La Liga]]'s [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]], in a [[2014–15 La Liga|season]]-long deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://rcdespanyol.com/principal.php?modulo=detalleNoticia&idnoticia=18263&idseccion=28&idlinkchk=0&idmenu=9&idsubmenu=108|title=Lucas Vázquez jugarà cedit a l'Espanyol|trans-title=Lucas Vázquez will play on loan at Espanyol|publisher=RCD Espanyol|language=ca|date=19 August 2014|access-date=20 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140820193500/http://rcdespanyol.com/principal.php?modulo=detalleNoticia&idnoticia=18263&idseccion=28&idlinkchk=0&idmenu=9&idsubmenu=108|archive-date=20 August 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his debut in the competition on 30 August, coming on as a second-half [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for [[Salva Sevilla]] in a 1–2 home loss against [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2014_15/primera/jornada_2/esp_sev/|title=El Sevilla impone su oficio ante el Espanyol|trans-title=Sevilla lay down the law against Espanyol|newspaper=Marca|location=Spain|language=es|date=31 August 2014|access-date=3 June 2015}}</ref> 

Vázquez scored his first goal in the [[Spanish football league system|Spanish top flight]] on 5 October 2014, netting the first in a 2–0 home success over [[Real Sociedad]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2014_15/primera/jornada_7/esp_rso/|title=El Espanyol pone a Arrasate contra las cuerdas|trans-title=Espanyol put Arrasate against the wall|newspaper=Marca|location=Spain|language=es|date=5 October 2014|access-date=3 June 2015}}</ref> On 3 June of the following year, he signed a four-year permanent deal with the ''Pericos'',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://rcdespanyol.com/principal.php?modulo=detalleNoticia&idnoticia=20044&idmenu=9|title=Lucas Vázquez, perico|trans-title=Lucas Vázquez, a parakeet|publisher=RCD Espanyol|language=ca|date=3 June 2015|access-date=3 June 2015|archive-date=11 June 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150611122235/http://www.rcdespanyol.com/principal.php?modulo=detalleNoticia&idnoticia=20044&idmenu=9|url-status=dead}}</ref> for a [[Euro|€]]2 million fee.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fichajes.net/noticias/espanyol-comprara-lucas-vazquez-20150529.html|title=El Espanyol comprará a Lucas Vázquez|trans-title=Espanyol will buy Lucas Vázquez|publisher=Fichajes|language=es|date=29 May 2015|access-date=3 June 2015}}</ref>

===Return to Real Madrid===
[[File:Lucas Vazquez.JPG|thumb|Vázquez playing for [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in 2016|left|426x426px]]
On 30 June 2015, Real Madrid exercised their buyback clause and Vázquez returned to the club.<ref>{{cite web |date=2 July 2015 |title=Official announcement: Lucas Vázquez |url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/07/official-announcement-lucas-vazquez |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924144246/http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2015/07/official-announcement-lucas-vazquez |archive-date=24 September 2015 |access-date=2 July 2015 |publisher=Real Madrid CF}}</ref> He made his debut on 12 September in a 6–0 away win over his former team Espanyol,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.laliga.es/noticias/un-historico-ronaldo-lidera-la-goleada-al-espanyol|title=Un histórico Ronaldo lidera la goleada al Espanyol|trans-title=Historical Ronaldo leads routing of Espanyol|publisher=[[La Liga]]|language=es|date=12 September 2015|access-date=12 September 2015}}</ref> and his first start came a week later, in a 1–0 home defeat of [[Granada CF|Granada]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.laliga.es/noticias/el-real-madrid-se-impone-al-granada-por-la-minima|title=El Real Madrid se impone al Granada por la mínima|trans-title=Real Madrid defeat Granada by the odd goal|publisher=La Liga|language=es|date=19 September 2015|access-date=19 September 2015}}</ref>

Vázquez scored his first competitive goal on 30 December 2015, replacing [[Karim Benzema]] for the final 15 minutes of the league fixture against Real Sociedad and netting in a 3–1 success at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/35155089|title=Real Madrid 3–1 Real Sociedad|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=30 December 2015|access-date=30 December 2015}}</ref> He contributed with seven appearances in [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League|the season]]'s [[UEFA Champions League]], as the tournament ended in a win; in [[2016 UEFA Champions League final|the final]] against [[Atlético Madrid]], he again came on for the Frenchman late into the second half of a 1–1 draw, and converted his attempt in the [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shootout]] triumph.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/022d-0e957c5979eb-37493cb53cd0-1000--spot-on-real-madrid-defeat-atletico-in-final-again/|title=Spot-on Real Madrid defeat Atlético in final again|publisher=UEFA|date=28 May 2016|access-date=29 May 2016}}</ref>

Vázquez started the [[2016 UEFA Super Cup]] against fellow Spaniards Sevilla, providing an assist to [[Sergio Ramos]] in injury time to take the game to [[Overtime (sports)|extra time]], where Real Madrid eventually won 3–2.<ref>{{Cite web |last=UEFA.com |date=9 August 2016 |title=Carvajal wonder goal wins Super Cup for Madrid |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefasupercup/news/0250-0c5111919148-7ee9946e9786-1000--carvajal-wonder-goal-wins-super-cup-for-madrid/ |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=UEFA.com |language=en}}</ref> He signed a new contract on 26 October 2016, running until 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 October 2016 |title=Official Announcement: Lucas Vázquez {{!}} Real Madrid CF |url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2016/10/official-statement-lucas-vazquez |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161029043152/http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2016/10/official-statement-lucas-vazquez |archive-date=2016-10-29 |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=Real Madrid C.F. - Web Oficial |language=en}}</ref>

|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/osasuna-vs-r-madrid/362908 |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20241130063808/https://www.skysports.com/football/osasuna-vs-r-madrid/362908 |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0250-0c5117c008df-de0901ea6dae-1000--majestic-real-madrid-win-champions-league-in-cardiff/ |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=UEFA.com |language=en}}</ref> 

Vázquez made ten appearances during the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League|2017–18 Champions League]] and added one goal,<ref>{{Cite web |date=25 May 2018 |title=Así llegan Real Madrid y Liverpool a la final de la Champions |trans-title=That is how Real Madrid and Liverpool arrive to the Champions final |url=https://www.rcnradio.com/deportes/asi-llegan-las-plantillas-de-real-madrid-y-liverpool-la-final-de-la-champions |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=RCN Radio Newsroom |language=es}}</ref> when Real Madrid won their third consecutive and 13th overall title in the competition.<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 May 2018 |title=Madrid beat Liverpool to complete hat-trick |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0245-0e98d7318379-716954065574-1000--madrid-beat-liverpool-to-complete-hat-trick/ |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=UEFA.com |language=en}}</ref> In November 2019, Vázquez broke his toe after dropping a weight on it.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2019-11-21 |title=Lucas Vazquez: Real Madrid winger 'drops weight' which breaks toe |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50507364 |access-date=2026-08-12 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> After returning, he made 18 appearances during the league season, as Real Madrid won the [[2019–20 La Liga]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Español |first=En |date=2020-07-16 |title=Real Madrid win the longest LaLiga Santander season |url=https://e01-marca.uecdn.es/en/football/real-madrid/2020/07/17/5f10db2146163f3c2c8b45d7.html |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=MARCA in English |language=en}}</ref>

[[File:Ofrenda de la Liga y la Champions-57-L.Millán (52109310843).jpg|thumb|299x299px|Vázquez with the squad presenting the [[2021–22 UEFA Champions League|Champions League trophy]] to [[Virgin of Almudena]] in 2022]]

Being a regular starter during the [[2020–21 Real Madrid CF season|2020–21 season]], Vázquez injured himself on 10 April 2021, in a 2–1 [[El Clásico]] win over [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and was ruled out for the remainder of the season with a [[Posterior cruciate ligament injury]] in his left knee.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-04-11 |title=Lucas Vazquez's season is over |url=https://e01-marca.uecdn.es/en/football/real-madrid/2021/04/11/6072e9e022601d0f0e8b45fc.html |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=MARCA |language=en}}</ref> On 3 June 2021, Vázquez signed a new three-year contract, which would keep him until 2024 at Madrid.<ref>{{Cite web |date=3 June 2021 |title=Official Announcement: Lucas Vázquez |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2021/06/03/official-announcement-lucas-vazquez |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624211805/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2021/06/03/official-announcement-lucas-vazquez |archive-date=24 June 2021 |access-date=3 June 2021 |website=Real Madrid CF}}</ref> On 18 July 2024, Vázquez signed a new one-year contract, which runs until 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 July 2024 |title=Official Announcement: Lucas Vázquez |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2021/06/03/official-announcement-lucas-vazquez |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230416222140/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2021/06/03/official-announcement-lucas-vazquez |archive-date=16 April 2023 |access-date=18 July 2024 |website= |publisher=Real Madrid CF}}</ref>

On 24 May 2025, Vázquez made his 400th appearance for Real Madrid in a 2–0 win over Real Sociedad in the final match of the [[2024–25 La Liga|2024–25 season]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Lucas Vázquez, 400 appearances for Real Madrid |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/news/football/first-team/latest-news/lucas-vazquez-400-partidos-con-el-real-madrid-24-05-2025 |access-date=17 July 2025 |work=Real Madrid |date=24 May 2025}}</ref> On 16 July 2025, Vázquez announced that he left Real Madrid after 10 years at the club.<ref>{{cite news |title=Emotivo acto de homenaje y despedida de Lucas Vázquez |url=https://www.realmadrid.com/es-ES/noticias/futbol/primer-equipo/actualidad/emotivo-acto-de-homenaje-y-despedida-de-lucas-vazquez-17-07-2025 |access-date=17 July 2025 |work=www.realmadrid.com |date=17 July 2025 |language=es}}</ref>

===Bayer Leverkusen===
On 26 August 2025, Vázquez joined [[Bundesliga]] club [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen]] as a free agent, signing a deal valid until 2027.<ref>{{cite web |date=26 August 2025 |title=Bayer 04 sign Real legend Lucas Vázquez |url=https://www.bayer04.de/en-us/news/bayer04/bayer-04-sign-real-legend-lucas-vazquez |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250826163955/https://www.bayer04.de/en-us/news/bayer04/bayer-04-sign-real-legend-lucas-vazquez |archive-date=26 August 2025 |access-date=26 August 2025 |publisher=[[Bayer 04 Leverkusen]]}}</ref> He scored his first goal on 24 January 2026, in a 1–0 win over [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]] in the [[2025–26 Bundesliga|Bundesliga]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Leverkusen 1-0 Bremen (Jan 24, 2026) Final Score |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/746883/werder-bremen-bayer-leverkusen |access-date=2026-08-12 |website=www.espn.com}}</ref>

==International career == 

Vázquez did not represent [[Spain national football team|Spain]] at any [[Spain national youth football team|youth level]]. On 17 May 2016 he, [[Saúl (footballer, born 1994)|Saúl]] and [[Sergio Rico]] were the three [[Cap (sport)|uncapped]] players named in [[Vicente del Bosque]]'s provisional squad for [[UEFA Euro 2016]] in France,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36312769|title=Euro 2016: Diego Costa, Juan Mata & Fernando Torres not in Spain squad|work=BBC Sport|date=17 May 2016|access-date=17 May 2016}}</ref> and he also made it to the final list of 23.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://deportes.elpais.com/deportes/2016/05/31/actualidad/1464710610_277737.html?rel=cx_articulo|title=Isco y Saúl fuera de la lista de Del Bosque para la Eurocopa 2016|trans-title=Isco and Saúl out of Del Bosque's list for 2016 European Championship|newspaper=[[El País]]|language=es|date=31 May 2016|access-date=3 June 2016}}</ref> 

He made his debut on 7 June, starting and playing 61 minutes in a 0–1 [[Exhibition game|friendly]] loss to [[Georgia national football team|Georgia]] at the [[Coliseum Alfonso Pérez]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/eurocopa/20160607/402350058688/derrota-preocupante-de-la-roja.html|title=Derrota preocupante de la Roja|trans-title=Worrying defeat for the ''Roja''|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|language=es|date=7 June 2016|access-date=7 June 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160608134034/http://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/eurocopa/20160607/402350058688/derrota-preocupante-de-la-roja.html|archive-date=8 June 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> He appeared once in the tournament, replacing [[Álvaro Morata]] in the 70th minute of a 0–2 [[Single-elimination tournament|round-of-16]] defeat against [[Italy national football team|Italy]] at the [[Stade de France]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Massimo |first=Luongo |date=2026-06-02 |title=mu88 |url=https://mu88a.jp.net |access-date=2026-08-12 |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0253-0d81b24e0059-7534c6d3e771-1000--dominant-italy-brush-aside-holders-spain-in-euro-2016-first/|title=Dominant Italy brush aside champions Spain|publisher=UEFA|date=27 June 2016|access-date=27 June 2016}}</ref> 

He was then included in the final [[2018 FIFA World Cup squads|squad]] for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/morata-misses-out-on-spain-world-cup-squad/1ub1qz7jod09i1lfvdcy84ea2l|title=Morata misses out on Spain's 23-man World Cup squad|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|date=21 May 2018|access-date=21 May 2018}}</ref> making his debut in [[FIFA World Cup|the competition]] on 15 June when he replaced [[David Silva]] for the final four minutes of the 3–3 group stage draw to [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wallace |first=Sam |last2=Bagchi |first2=Rob |date=2018-06-15 |title=Cristiano Ronaldo scores sensational hat-trick as Portugal hold Spain in instant World Cup classic |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-cup/2018/06/15/portugal-vs-spain-world-cup-2018-live-score-latest-updates/ |access-date=2026-08-12 |work=The Telegraph |language=en-GB |issn=0307-1235}}</ref>

He was born in the United States but raised in Japan, where he represented internationally. ==Club career== ===Early career=== Sakai was born in New York to a [[Germans|German]] mother and a [[Japanese people|Japanese]] father. The family moved to [[Japan]] when he was two years old. He grew up in [[Sanjō, Niigata|Sanjō, Niigata prefecture]]. Sakai started playing football at Sanjō junior soccer club, together with his brother [[Noriyoshi Sakai|Noriyoshi]]. At age 15, he joined [[Albirex Niigata]] youth academy and entered Kaishu Gakuen High School. His team played at the [[Prince Takamado Cup|Prince Takamado Premier/Prince League]], [[Japan Club Youth U-18 Football Championship]] and J.League youth tournaments. Years later in his final year at school, he was chosen as one of the designated players for development by [[J. League Division 1]] and [[Japan Football Association|JFA]]. With this status, he was able to register as a J. League club player while he was still eligible to play for his school. He made his Albirex first-team debut, at the age of 17, on 15 November 2008 in the [[Emperor's Cup]] match against [[F.C. Tokyo|FC Tokyo]]. He officially signed with Albirex Niigata in the following season. After becoming professional, he was assigned the number 24 shirt. He made his professional football debut in the opening [[J. League Division 1|J1 League]] match of the 2009 season also against FC Tokyo. ===VfB Stuttgart=== On 1 January 2012, Gōtoku Sakai was loaned out to [[VfB Stuttgart]] until June 2013.
