'''Lorenzo Insigne''' {{postnominals|post-noms=[[Order of Merit of the Italian Republic|Cavaliere OMRI]]}} ({{IPA|it|loˈrɛntso inˈsiɲɲe}}; born 4 June 1991) is an Italian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as an [[attacking midfielder]] or [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for {{Italian football updater|Sampdoria}} club [[UC Sampdoria|Sampdoria]]. He is known in particular for his creativity, versatility, short height, speed and technical ability, as well as his accuracy from [[Free kick (association football)|free kicks]].<ref name="Lorenzo Insigne: 1991 – Italia">{{cite web |title=Lorenzo Insigne: 1991 – Italia |url=http://www.generazioneditalenti.it/lorenzo-insigne-1991-italia/ |access-date=21 December 2014 |website=generazioneditalenti.it |date=3 November 2011 |language=it}}</ref>

Insigne began his professional career with [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]] in 2009, making his [[Serie A]] debut in 2010, but was later sent on consecutive season loan spells to [[SS Cavese 1919|Cavese]], [[US Foggia|Foggia]] and [[Delfino Pescara 1936|Pescara]], before returning to Napoli in 2012. He helped the club win [[Coppa Italia]] titles in [[2013–14 Coppa Italia|2013–14]] and [[2019–20 Coppa Italia|2019–20]], finishing as the competition's top scorer in the former. In [[2020–21 Serie A|2020–21]], he was recognised as the best-performing player in Serie A according to performance data.<ref name=":64">{{Cite web |last=Sagorin|first=Yannick|date=2021-05-03|title=Stats à l’appui, qui sont les meilleurs joueurs d’Europe ?|url=https://www.sports.fr/football/divers/stats-a-lappui-meilleurs-joueurs-deurope-457276.html|access-date=2026-08-05|website=Sports.fr|language=fr-FR}}</ref> After departing Napoli, he later moved to [[Major League Soccer]] side [[Toronto FC]] in 2022.

Insigne represented the [[Italy national under-21 football team|Italy national under-21 team]], with which he won a runner-up medal at the [[2013 UEFA European Under-21 Championship]]. He made his debut for the [[Italy national football team|senior team]] in September 2012, and represented Italy at the [[2014 FIFA World Cup]], [[UEFA Euro 2016]], and [[UEFA Euro 2020]], winning the latter tournament.

==Club career==

===Early career===
In 2006, at age 15, Insigne was signed by [[S.S.C. Napoli|Napoli]] from Olimpia Sant'Arpino for €1,500.<ref>{{cite web |title=Che "colpaccio" di Santoro nel 2006, ecco quanto pagò Lorenzo Insigne |url=http://www.tuttonapoli.net/?action=read&idnotizia=101408 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120627094356/http://www.tuttonapoli.net/?action=read&idnotizia=101408 |archive-date=27 June 2012 |access-date=20 July 2021 |website=tuttonapoli.net |language=it}}</ref> In 2008, he made his debut for the ''Primavera'' team, with whom he scored 15 goals in the 2009–10 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Napoli, il gioiellino Insigne: La pulce azzurra fa passi da gigante - Tutto Napoli |url=https://www.tuttonapoli.net/rassegna-stampa/napoli-il-gioiellino-insigne-la-pulce-azzurra-fa-passi-da-gigante-37950 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401120747/https://www.tuttonapoli.net/rassegna-stampa/napoli-il-gioiellino-insigne-la-pulce-azzurra-fa-passi-da-gigante-37950 |archive-date=1 April 2019 |access-date=14 October 2018}}</ref> He was first called up to the first team under [[Roberto Donadoni]], playing some friendlies in the summer of 2009, before making his [[Serie A]] debut under [[Walter Mazzarri]], on 24 January 2010, in a 2–0 win away to [[A.S. Livorno Calcio|Livorno]].<ref>{{cite web|url = http://www.sempreinter.com/2014/06/02/mazzarri-im-happy-for-insigne-i-made-him-debut-in-serie-a/|title = Mazzarri: "I'm happy for Insigne, I made him debut in Serie A"| date=2 June 2014 |access-date = 9 November 2015}}</ref> He played the remainder of the season on loan at [[S.S. Cavese 1919|Cavese]] in [[Lega Pro Prima Divisione]], where he made 10 appearances.

====Loans to Foggia and Pescara====

The following season, Insigne was loaned to [[U.S. Foggia|Foggia]] in [[Lega Pro Prima Divisione]]. He scored his first professional goal on 14 August, in the [[Coppa Italia Lega Pro]] match against [[L'Aquila Calcio 1927|L'Aquila]], while on 29 August, he scored his first league goal in a 2–3 home defeat to [[A.S. Lucchese Libertas 1905|Lucchese]]. Under the manager [[Zdeněk Zeman]], he totalled 19 goals in the league, in addition to seven goals scored in Coppa Italia Lega Pro.<ref>{{cite web |date=25 May 2011 |title=Foggia, Insigne: "Ora tornerò a Napoli" |url=http://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/?action=read&id=270174 |access-date=20 July 2021 |website=tuttomercatoweb.com |language=it}}</ref>

On 8 July 2011, he was loaned to [[Delfino Pescara 1936|Pescara]] in [[Serie B]], now managed by Zeman.<ref>{{cite news |date=8 July 2011 |title=Ufficiale, colpi Pescara: presi Insigne e Romagnoli |url=http://www.corrieredellosport.it/calcio_mercato/2011/07/08-182661/Ufficiale,+colpi+Pescara%3A+presi+Insigne+e+Romagnoli |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121014035743/http://www.corrieredellosport.it/calcio_mercato/2011/07/08-182661/Ufficiale,+colpi+Pescara:+presi+Insigne+e+Romagnoli |archive-date=14 October 2012 |access-date=30 July 2011 |publisher=Corriere dello Sport – Stadio |language=it}}</ref> He made his debut in the Italian second division on 26 August 2011 in the opening round against [[Hellas Verona]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://ita.worldfootball.net/spielbericht/serie-b-2011-2012-hellas-verona-delfino-pescara-1936/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130413213651/http://ita.worldfootball.net/spielbericht/serie-b-2011-2012-hellas-verona-delfino-pescara-1936/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=13 April 2013 |title=Verona 1:2 Pescara (Serie B 2011/2012 1 day) |website=calcio.com |access-date=20 July 2021}}</ref> and on 4 September scored his first goal for Pescara away against [[Modena F.C. 2018|Modena]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://ita.worldfootball.net/spielbericht/serie-b-2011-2012-modena-fc-delfino-pescara-1936/ |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130413222410/http://ita.worldfootball.net/spielbericht/serie-b-2011-2012-modena-fc-delfino-pescara-1936/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=13 April 2013 |title=Modena - Pescara 3:2 (Serie B 2011/2012 3. Giornata) |website=calcio.com |access-date=20 July 2021}}</ref> Insigne finished the season with 18 goals, making him the second top-scorer of the season behind teammate [[Ciro Immobile]], and 14 assists.<ref>{{cite web |title=Pescara, ecco i gioielli forgiati a Zemanlandia |url=http://www.corrieredellosport.it/calcio/calcio_mercato/2012/05/21-240921/Pescara%2C+ecco+i+gioielli+forgiati+a+Zemanlandia |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151005175416/http://www.corrieredellosport.it/calcio/calcio_mercato/2012/05/21-240921/Pescara%2C+ecco+i+gioielli+forgiati+a+Zemanlandia |archive-date=5 October 2015 |access-date=16 January 2015}}</ref> Among the key players of Pescara's title-winning season and promotion to [[Serie A]], Insigne was subsequently awarded the "Best Player" of the Serie B season, along with teammates Immobile and [[Marco Verratti]].<ref name="areanapoli.it"/>

===Napoli===

At the end of the season, Insigne returned to Napoli, choosing the number 24 jersey.<ref>{{cite web |date=31 July 2012 |title=Ufficializzati i numeri di maglia: il 24 a Insigne, Vargas sceglie il 9. Il 22 di Lavezzi a... |url=http://www.tuttonapoli.net/?action=read&idnotizia=107478 |access-date=20 July 2021 |website=tuttonapoli.net |language=it}}</ref> On 16 September 2012, he scored his first goal in Serie A, after entering as a substitute for [[Edinson Cavani]] in a 3–1 home win over [[Parma Calcio 1913|Parma]].<ref>{{cite web |date=16 September 2012 |title=Napoli a tutto attacco Il Parma cede il passo 3-1 |url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Squadre/Napoli/16-09-2012/cavani-pandev-insigne-napoli-va-parma-si-illude-ma-non-basta-3-1-912620648973.shtml |access-date=16 January 2015 |publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport |language=it}}</ref> Four days later, he made his debut in [[UEFA club competitions]], starting in a 4–0 win against Swedish side [[AIK Fotboll]] in the [[UEFA Europa League]].<ref name="UEFA Profile">{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/teamsandplayers/players/player=250026037/profile/index.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20160109072125/http://www.uefa.com/teamsandplayers/players/player=250026037/profile/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=9 January 2016 |title=Lorenzo Insigne |publisher=UEFA |access-date=25 October 2018}}</ref> Insigne struggled to get a run of consecutive games at many points in the season, but participated in a large successful season at Napoli, who finished in second place in [[2012–13 Serie A|Serie A that season]]. Throughout the season, he made 43 appearances, scoring five goals and providing seven assists. The competition for places with players like [[Edinson Cavani]], [[Goran Pandev]], [[Eduardo Vargas]] and [[Omar El Kaddouri]] meant Insigne often started matches on the substitutes' bench.

[[File:Barça - Napoli - 20140806 - 16 (cropped).jpg|thumb|Insigne playing for [[S.S.C. Napoli|Napoli]] in 2014]]
The [[2013–14 S.S.C. Napoli season|following season]], Insigne made his [[UEFA Champions League]] debut in 2–1 home win over the previous season's finalists [[Borussia Dortmund]], on 18 September 2013. Insigne marked his debut in the competition with a goal from a free-kick.<ref>{{cite web |title=Napoli-Borussia Dortmund 2-1. Gol di Higuain ed Insigne, è notte magica |url=https://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Squadre/Napoli/18-09-2013/napoli-borussia-dortmund-2-1-gol-higuain-ed-insigne-notte-magica-201187475331.shtml |access-date=16 January 2015 |website=Napoli: ultime notizie - Gazzetta dello Sport |language=it}}</ref> In the [[2014 Coppa Italia Final|final]] of the [[2013–14 Coppa Italia|Coppa Italia]] on 3 May 2014, Insigne scored twice in the first half as his side won 3–1 against [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/us/en/report/388636/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5901 |title=Insigne brace seals Coppa |publisher=ESPNFC |date=3 May 2014 |access-date=3 May 2014}}</ref> During the [[2014–15 S.S.C. Napoli season|2014–15 season]], on 9 November 2014, Insigne injured the [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|anterior cruciate ligament]] of his right knee in a match against Fiorentina.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sscnapoli.it/static/news/Insigne,-intervento-perfettamente-riuscito-4161.aspx|title=Insigne, intervento perfettamente riuscito|access-date=16 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.legaseriea.it/en/news-centre/news-detail/-/news/INSIGNE_S_MEDICAL_REPORT/1208398|title=Insigne's medical report|publisher=[[Lega Serie A|legaseriea.it]]|date=11 November 2014|access-date=23 October 2015}}</ref> He returned to the pitch on 4 April 2015 after a five-month absence, coming on as a substitute in a 1–0 away defeat to [[A.S. Roma|Roma]].<ref>{{cite web |author1=Jacopo Manfredi |date=4 April 2015 |title=Roma-Napoli 1-0, Pjanic punisce ancora gli azzurri |trans-title=Roma-Napoli 1-0, Pjanic punishes the Azzurri again. |url=http://www.repubblica.it/sport/calcio/serie-a/roma/2015/04/04/news/roma-napoli_1-0_pjanic_punisce_ancora_gli_azzurri-111194400/ |access-date=18 May 2015 |publisher=La Repubblica |language=it}}</ref> In his next league match, on 26 April, he scored a goal in a 4–2 home win over [[U.C. Sampdoria|Sampdoria]], also wearing the captain's armband during the match, in the absence of teammates [[Marek Hamšík]], [[Christian Maggio]] and [[Gökhan Inler]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Serie-A/Napoli/26-04-2015/napoli-sampdoria-4-2-tabellino-autogol-albiol-gabbiadini-higuain-doppietta-rigore-insigne-muriel-110592141973.shtml|title=Napoli-Sampdoria, 4-2 in rimonta: super Higuain, Benitez a -2 dal terzo posto|trans-title=Napoli-Sampdoria, 4-2 comeback: super Higuain, Benitez 2 points from third place|publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport|author1=Gianluca Monti|language=it|date=26 April 2015|access-date=18 May 2015}}</ref>

On 13 September 2015, Insigne opened the [[2015–16 Serie A|2015–16 Serie A season]] by scoring in a 2–2 draw against [[Empoli F.C.|Empoli]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.us/italian-serie-a/match/432245/empoli-napoli/report|title=Empoli 2-2 Napoli|publisher=ESPN FC|date=13 September 2015|access-date=4 October 2015}}</ref> On 20 September, he scored again in a 5–0 win over [[S.S. Lazio|Lazio]], also setting up [[Allan (footballer, born 1991)|Allan]]'s goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/SerieA/match/69856|title=Napoli 5 - 0 Lazio|publisher=Football Italia|date=20 September 2015|access-date=4 October 2015}}</ref> On 26 September, Insigne made his 100th Serie A appearance with Napoli and scored his third goal of the season in a 2–1 home win over defending Serie A champions [[Juventus FC|Juventus]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.repubblica.it/sport/calcio/serie-a/2015/09/26/news/napoli-juventus_2-1-123760827/|title=Napoli-Juventus 2-1: Insigne e Higuain gol, bianconeri quasi fuori dalla lotta scudetto|trans-title=Napoli-Juventus 2-1: Insigne and Higuain score, bianconeri almost out of the title race|publisher=La Repubblica|language=it|author1=Federico Sala|date=26 September 2015|access-date=5 October 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |date=26 September 2015 |title=Napoli 2-1 Juventus |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/34351097 |access-date=4 October 2015 |work=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> although he was also later forced off the pitch after sustaining an injury during the match; the club, however, later reported the injury was not serious.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/73598/%E2%80%98insigne-injury-nothing-serious%E2%80%99|title=Insigne injury nothing serious|publisher=Football Italia|date=28 September 2015|access-date=4 October 2015}}</ref> He continued his goalscoring run in the following match, scoring twice and setting up Allan's goal in a 4–0 away win over [[A.C. Milan|Milan]], bringing his seasonal tally to five goals in seven games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.us/italian-serie-a/match/432204/ac-milan-napoli/report|title=Lorenzo Insigne inspires as Napoli end AC Milan's perfect home record|publisher=ESPN FC|date=4 October 2015|access-date=5 October 2015}}</ref> Insigne's prolific performances even led to comparisons with former Napoli legend [[Diego Maradona]], which Insigne played down.<ref name="Insigne-Maradona">{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/napoli/story/2649214/lorenzo-insigne-of-napoli-ignores-diego-maradona-comparisons|title=Diego Maradona comparisons of no interest to Napoli star Lorenzo Insigne|publisher=ESPN FC|author1=Ben Gladwell|date=5 October 2015|access-date=5 October 2015}}</ref>

In April 2017, Insigne scored his third brace in four appearances for Napoli to take his tally to 14 goals for the [[2016–17 Serie A|Serie A season]], surpassing his previous personal best for a single campaign.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/100947/serie-week-31-did-you-know|title=Serie A Week 31: Did You Know?|website=Football Italia|last=Campanale|first=Susan|date=10 April 2017|access-date=20 April 2017}}</ref> On 14 October 2017, Insigne scored his 100th career club goal in a 1–0 away win over [[Derby del Sole|rivals]] Roma in Serie A.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Insigne landmark maintains Napoli's flawless s |url=https://www.beinsports.com/en-au/football/serie-a/articles-video/insigne-landmark-maintains-napolis-flawless-s |access-date=2025-04-19 |website=beIN SPORTS |language=en-au}}</ref> After [[Marek Hamšík]]'s departure from the club in February 2019, Insigne was made the official [[Captain (association football)|captain]] of Napoli.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/134444/insigne-proud-be-napoli-captain|title=Insigne: 'Proud to be Napoli captain'|publisher=Football Italia|date=9 February 2019}}</ref> On 24 August, in the opening game of the [[2019–20 Serie A]] season, Insigne scored twice and set up two more goals in a 4–3 away win over Fiorentina.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.football-italia.net/SerieA/match/142368 |title=Fiorentina 3 - 4 Napoli |publisher=Football Italia |date=24 August 2019 |access-date=25 August 2019}}</ref>

On 13 June 2020, Insigne assisted [[Dries Mertens]]'s equalising goal in a 1–1 home draw against [[Inter Milan]] in the second leg of [[2019–20 Coppa Italia]] semi-final; the goal saw the Belgian overtake Hamšík to become Napoli's outright all-time leading goalscorer with 122 goals, while the result also allowed Napoli to advanced to the [[2020 Coppa Italia Final|Coppa Italia Final]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/soccer/mertens-sets-record-as-napoli-advances-to-italian-cup-final/2020/06/13/6aae1e3c-adbb-11ea-a43b-be9f6494a87d_story.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200614015716/https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/soccer/mertens-sets-record-as-napoli-advances-to-italian-cup-final/2020/06/13/6aae1e3c-adbb-11ea-a43b-be9f6494a87d_story.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=14 June 2020 |title=Mertens sets record as Napoli advances to Italian Cup final |newspaper=Washington Post |date=13 June 2020 |access-date=13 June 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |agency=The Canadian Press |date=13 June 2020 |title=Mertens sets record as Napoli advances to Italian Cup final - TSN.ca |url=https://www.tsn.ca/mertens-sets-record-as-napoli-advances-to-italian-cup-final-1.1485818 |access-date=13 June 2020 |website=TSN |language=en}}</ref> In the final on 17 June, Insigne netted Napoli's first spot-kick in a 4–2 penalty shoot-out victory against Juventus following a 0–0 draw after regulation time; Insigne went on to lift the trophy as the club's captain.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/154624/coppa-napoli-beat-juventus-penalties|title=Coppa: Napoli beat Juventus on penalties|publisher=Football Italia|date=17 June 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Napoli wins Italian Cup in penalty shootout over Juventus |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/soccer/napoli-wins-italian-cup-penalty-shootout-juventus/ |date=17 June 2020 |access-date=17 June 2020 |website=www.sportsnet.ca}}</ref>

===Toronto FC===
On 8 January 2022, Insigne signed a pre-contract to join [[Major League Soccer]] club [[Toronto FC]] as a [[Designated Player Rule|designated player]] on a free transfer and four-year contract that began on 1 July,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-01-08 |title=Toronto FC sign Lorenzo Insigne from Napoli in blockbuster deal |url=https://www.thescore.com/ita_fed/news/2267500/amp |access-date=2025-04-19 |website=theScore.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/tfc/2022/01/07/forzo-insigne-tfcs-italian-fans-holding-their-breath-until-napoli-star-is-introduced.html|title=Forza Insigne: TFC's Italian fans holding their breath until Napoli star is introduced|date=7 January 2022|work=[[Toronto Star]]|first=Laura|last=Armstrong}}</ref> with a reported annual salary of $15 million, making him the highest paid player in MLS.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-06-28 |title=Toronto's Insigne: No pressure as MLS top earner |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37629635/toronto-fc-lorenzo-insigne-feels-no-pressure-mls-top-earner |access-date=2025-04-19 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

He made his debut for the club on 23 July, in a 4–0 home victory against [[Charlotte FC]], only featuring in the opening half, but setting up club captain [[Michael Bradley (soccer)|Michael Bradley]]'s second goal of the match with a back-heel pass.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.torontofc.ca/news/debutants-bernardeschi-insigne-breathe-new-life-to-reds-spark-massive-win-over-c|title=Debutants Bernardeschi, Insigne breathe new life to Reds, spark massive win over Charlotte FC|publisher=Toronto FC|date=24 July 2022}}</ref> On 6 August, Insigne scored his first goal for the club, converting a shot from outside the box for the game-winning goal in a 4–3 away victory against [[Nashville SC]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |title="Classic Lorenzo": Toronto FC marvel at Lorenzo Insigne's game-winning golazo |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/classic-lorenzo-toronto-fc-marvel-at-lorenzo-insigne-s-game-winning-wonder-strik |access-date=2025-04-19 |website=mlssoccer |language=en}}</ref> On 1 July 2025, he agreed to a mutual termination of the remainder of his contract with the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.torontofc.ca/news/toronto-fc-and-italian-winger-lorenzo-insigne-agree-on-mutual-contract-termination|title=Toronto FC and Italian Winger Lorenzo Insigne Agree on Mutual Contract Termination|date=1 July 2025|work=Toronto FC}}</ref>

===Return to Pescara===
On 30 January 2026, Insigne returned to [[Delfino Pescara 1936|Pescara]] in the second-tier [[Serie B]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Delfino Pescara 1936|url=https://www.pescaracalcio.com/lorenzo-insigne-torna-in-biancazzurro/|title=Lorenzo Insigne torna in biancazzurro|trans-title=Lorenzo Insigne returns to the white and blue|date=30 January 2026|access-date=30 January 2026|language=it}}</ref>

===Sampdoria===
On 8 July 2026 Insigne signed with Serie B side [[UC Sampdoria|Sampdoria]] on a two-year contract with the option of a further year if he featured in 50% of Sampdoria's matches or if Sampdoria gained promotion to [[Serie A]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tribuna.com/en/news/2026-07-08-lorenzo-insigne-joins-sampdoria-on-twoyear-deal/|title=Lorenzo Insigne joins Sampdoria on two-year deal|work=Tribuna.com|first=Mariana|last=Holovach|date=July 8, 2026|access-date=July 8, 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
===Youth===
A regular member of the [[Italy national under-21 football team|Italy under-21 squad]], Insigne made 15 appearances for the "Azzurrini", scoring seven goals. He made his debut with the under-21 side on 6 October 2011 in a [[2013 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification|European qualifying]] match against [[Liechtenstein national under-21 football team|Liechtenstein]], scoring two goals and providing two assists in a 7–2 victory.<ref>{{cite web |date=6 October 2011 |title=Azzurrini, pioggia di gol dopo la grande paura |url=http://www.repubblica.it/sport/calcio/nazionale/2011/10/06/news/lichtenstein-italia-22808793/ |access-date=16 January 2015 |publisher=La Repubblica |language=it}}</ref> With the under-21 team, he participated in the [[2013 UEFA European Under-21 Championship]] under manager [[Devis Mangia]], playing an important role in Italy's tournament run.

On 5 June 2013, he made his tournament debut against [[England national under-21 football team|England]], scoring a goal from a free-kick in Italy's 1–0 opening victory.<ref>{{cite web |date=5 June 2013 |title=Europei under 21, Italia-Inghilterra 1-0: decide una magia di Insigne |url=http://www.repubblica.it/sport/calcio/nazionale/2013/06/05/news/under_21_italia_batte_inghilterra-60458180/ |access-date=16 January 2015 |publisher=La Repubblica |language=it}}</ref> On 9 June, in Italy's second match against hosts [[Israel national under-21 football team|Israel]], Insigne began the play which led to Italy's first goal of the match in the 18th minute, which was scored by [[Riccardo Saponara]]. He injured himself later during the match and was forced to come off, although Italy won the match 4–0.<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 June 2013 |title=Europei under 21: Italia-Israele 4-0, azzurrini già in semifinale ma Insigne va ko |url=https://www.repubblica.it/sport/calcio/nazionale/2013/06/08/news/italia_israele_under_21-60690156/ |access-date=16 January 2015 |website=la Repubblica |language=it}}</ref> Insigne was able to recuperate in time for the semi-final match against the [[Netherlands national under-21 football team|Netherlands]], and he came on to set up [[Fabio Borini]]'s winner which sent the Italians into the [[2013 UEFA European Under-21 Championship Final|final]].<ref>{{cite web |date=15 June 2013 |title=Europei Under 21, Italia-Olanda 1-0: Borini porta gli azzurrini in finale |url=http://www.repubblica.it/sport/calcio/nazionale/2013/06/15/news/italia_batte_olanda_under_21-61178581/ |access-date=16 January 2015 |publisher=La Repubblica |language=it}}</ref> On 18 June, Italy was defeated 4–2 against [[Spain national under-21 football team|Spain]] in the final, although Insigne was able to set up Italy's second goal of the match, which was scored by Borini.<ref>{{cite web |date=18 June 2013 |title=Under 21, Spagna-Italia 4-2. Gli azzurri si inchinano a Thiago Alcantara |url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Nazionale/18-06-2013/under-21-spagna-italia-4-2-azzurri-si-inchinano-thiago-alcantara-20605325552.shtml |access-date=16 January 2015 |publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport |language=it}}</ref>

===Senior===
At the age of 21 in September 2012, Insigne received his first call-up to the [[Italy national football team|Italian senior team]] by coach [[Cesare Prandelli]] for its [[2014 FIFA World Cup qualifying]] matches against [[Bulgaria national football team|Bulgaria]] and [[Malta national football team|Malta]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Insigne called up for game against Malta |url=http://www.timesofmalta.com/articles/view/20120902/football/insigne-called-up-for-game-against-malta.435390 |newspaper=[[Times of Malta]] |date=2 September 2012 |access-date=11 December 2014}}</ref> He made his senior debut on 11 September during the same tournament against the latter opponent in [[Modena]], coming on as a substitute for [[Alessandro Diamanti]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Un grande Insigne nella Nazionale che non brilla|url=https://www.ilnapolista.it/2012/09/un-grande-insigne-nella-nazionale-che-non-brilla/|website=Il Napolista|date=11 September 2012|access-date=21 June 2025|language=it}}</ref> On 14 August 2013, Insigne scored his first goal in a friendly against [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]], which ended in a 2–1 loss at the [[Stadio Olimpico]] in [[Rome]].<ref>{{cite web|title=International friendly: Argentina claim 2-1 win over Italy |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/live/match/292383/report |website=[[Sky Sports]] |date=14 August 2013 |access-date=16 May 2014}}</ref> Insigne was named in Cesare Prandelli's 30-man provisional squad for the [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014 World Cup]] and was eventually picked in the final 23-man squad.<ref>{{Cite web|title=World Cup 2014: Striker Giuseppe Rossi in Italy's provisional squad|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27402363|access-date=16 May 2014|website=[[BBC Sport]]|date=13 May 2014}}</ref> In Italy's last warm-up match, against [[Fluminense FC|Fluminense]] in Brazil ahead of their World Cup opener against [[England national football team|England]], Insigne and his teammate Ciro Immobile scored five goals, with Insigne scoring two.<ref>{{cite web|title=Immobile & Insigne Impress in Fluminense Win|url=http://soccerly.com/article/Kubani/immobile-insigne-impress-in-fluminense-win|access-date=11 December 2014|website=[[BBC Sport]]|date=9 June 2014}}</ref> On 20 June 2014, Insigne made his debut in the World Cup in Italy's second group match, against [[Costa Rica national football team|Costa Rica]], replacing [[Antonio Candreva]] in the second half of the 1–0 defeat. However, this was Insigne's only appearance in the tournament, as Italy was eliminated in the group stage.<ref>{{cite web|title=Costa Rica produced their second stunning upset in a week to beat a poor Italy side and confirm England's exit from the 2014 World Cup|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/25285190|access-date=11 December 2014|website=[[BBC Sport]]|date=20 June 2014}}</ref>

On 31 May 2016, Insigne was named to [[Antonio Conte]]'s 23-man Italy squad for [[UEFA Euro 2016]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/85206/official-italy-squad-euro-2016|title=OFFICIAL: Italy squad for Euro 2016|website=Football Italia|date=31 May 2016|access-date=31 May 2016}}</ref> He made his first appearance of the tournament on 22 June, coming off the bench in Italy's final group match, which ended in a 1–0 defeat to the [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]], striking the post and later receiving a yellow card in injury time.<ref>{{cite news |first=Sam |last=Adams |title=Brady sends euphoric Ireland into the last 16 |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0253-0d8182c03c0c-a9aab1b99211-1000--brady-header-wins-it-for-ireland-against-italy-in-euro-20/|publisher=UEFA|date=22 June 2016 |access-date=22 June 2016}}</ref> In the round of 16, at the [[Stade de France]] in [[Paris]] on 27 June, he came off the bench once again to help set-up [[Graziano Pellè]]'s 91st minute volley to give the ''Azzurri'' a 2–0 victory against defending champions [[Spain national football team|Spain]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Jim |last=Foulerton |title=Dominant Italy brush aside champions Spain |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0253-0d81b24e0059-7534c6d3e771-1000--dominant-italy-brush-aside-holders-spain-in-euro-2016-first/ |website=[[UEFA]] |publisher=Union of European Football Associations |date=27 June 2016 |access-date=27 June 2016}}</ref> On 2 July, he made a further substitute appearance in the quarter-final fixture against [[Germany national football team|Germany]] and scored Italy's first penalty in the resulting shoot-out, which ended in a 6–5 loss against the reigning World Cup champions.<ref>{{cite news |first=Sam |last=Adams |title=Hector the shoot-out hero as Germany finally defeat Italy |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0253-0d81e3c149c5-d7e77fb31e24-1000--germany-finally-defeat-italy-to-stride-into-euro-2016-semis/|publisher=[[UEFA]]|date=2 July 2016 |access-date=3 July 2016}}</ref>

During Italy's goalless draw with Sweden on 13 November 2017, which resulted in Italy missing out on the World Cup for the first time since 1958, Insigne spent the entire game on the bench. Late in the match, midfielder [[Daniele De Rossi]] was asked to warm up, but refused and asked: "Why the hell should I go on? We don't need to draw, we need to win!", whilst inquiring why Insigne was not being prepared instead.<ref>{{cite news |date=14 November 2017 |title=Italy's Daniele de Rossi angrily protests his own manager's decisions from the bench |first=Mark |last=Critchley |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/international/italy-world-cup-sweden-de-rossi-video-insigne-ventura-a8053366.html |access-date=7 September 2023 |website=The Independent}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Polden|first=Jake|date=14 November 2017|title=What a furious De Rossi said to Italy coach when he asked him to warm up |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/what-daniele-de-rossi-said-11517439|newspaper=[[Daily Mirror]]|access-date=7 September 2023}}</ref>

In June 2021, Insigne was included in Italy's squad for [[UEFA Euro 2020]] by coach [[Roberto Mancini]],<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/mancini-names-uncapped-striker-raspadori-final-italy-euro-2020-squad-2021-06-01/ |title=Mancini names uncapped striker Raspadori in final Italy Euro 2020 squad |work=Reuters |date=1 June 2021 |access-date=5 June 2021}}</ref> and was later assigned the [[Squad number (association football)|number 10 shirt]].<ref>{{cite news |date=4 June 2021 |title=Italia, assegnati i numeri di maglia |url=https://sport.sky.it/calcio/europei/2021/06/02/italia-europei-numeri-maglia#10|website=[[Sky Sport (Italy)|Sky Sport Italy]]|access-date=10 June 2024|language=it}}</ref> In the opening match of the tournament on 11 June, he scored Italy's final goal in a 3–0 victory against [[Turkey national football team|Turkey]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://football-italia.net/turkey-0-3-italy-azzurri-dominate-euro-2020-debut/ |title=Turkey 0–3 Italy: Azzurri dominate Euro 2020 debut |website=Football Italia |last=Campanale |first=Susy |date=11 June 2021 |access-date=12 June 2021}}</ref> On 2 July, he scored Italy's second goal of the match in a 2–1 victory against [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]] in the quarter-finals of the competition, with a curling right-footed effort from outside the box following an individual run;<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/51198657 |title=Italy edge Belgium to set up Spain semi |website=BBC Sport |last=Begley |first=Emlyn |date=2 July 2021 |access-date=2 July 2021}}</ref> for his performance, he was named ''star of the match'' by [[UEFA]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro-2020/news/026b-12a976bf5f65-0c28b8a0c199-1000--italy-edge-past-belgium-into-semis/ |title=Belgium 1–2 Italy: Azzurri outrun Red Devils |publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=2 July 2021 |access-date=3 July 2021}} {{dead link|date=March 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> while the goal later placed second in UEFA's 2020–21 Goal of the Season, behind only [[Mehdi Taremi]]'s overhead kick goal for [[FC Porto|Porto]] against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in the [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.figc.it/en/national-teams/news/insigne-s-curler-against-belgium-comes-second-in-uefa-s-202021-goal-of-the-season/ |title=Insigne's curler against Belgium comes second in UEFA's 2020/21 Goal of the Season |publisher=Italian Football Federation|date=29 July 2021 |access-date=29 July 2021}}</ref> On 11 July, after a 1–1 draw in [[Overtime (sports)|extra-time]], Insigne won the European Championship with Italy following a 3–2 [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] victory against [[England national football team|England]] at [[Wembley Stadium]] in the [[UEFA Euro 2020 final|final]]. He started the match, but was replaced by [[Andrea Belotti]] in the second half of regulation time.<ref name="Euro2020Final">{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51198762|title=England lose shootout in Euro 2020 final |first=Phil |last=McNulty|website=BBC Sport|date=11 July 2021 |access-date=11 July 2021}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Nicknamed "Lorenzo Il Magnifico" ("[[Lorenzo de' Medici|Lorenzo the Magnificent]]", in Italian),<ref>{{cite web |author1=Andrea Tabacco |date=5 October 2015 |title=Da sgobbone a trascinatore, l'evoluzione di Lorenzo Insigne, Il Magnifico |url=http://it.eurosport.com/calcio/serie-a/2015-2016/da-sgobbone-a-trascinatore-levoluzione-di-lorenzo-insigne-il-magnifico_sto4938150/story.shtml |access-date=13 May 2016 |publisher=Eurosport |language=it}}</ref> Insigne is a fast, talented, skillful and diminutive right footed [[Winger (association football)|winger]], with an eye for the goal, who is usually deployed on the left in a [[Formation (association football)#4.E2.80.933.E2.80.933|4–3–3]] or in a [[Formation (association football)#4.E2.80.932.E2.80.933.E2.80.931|4–2–3–1]] formation, which allows him to utilise his acceleration to cut inside and [[Curl (association football)|curl]] shots on goal with his stronger foot, in particular from outside the penalty area.<ref name="wonderkid">{{cite web|url=http://www.eurosport.com/football/meet-lorenzo-insigne-italys-new-wonderkid_sto4716298/story.shtml|title=Meet Lorenzo Insigne, Italy's new wonderkid|publisher=Eurosport|author1=James Horncastle|date=7 May 2015 |access-date=23 January 2017}}</ref><ref name="coming of age">{{Cite news |last=Bandini |first=Nicky |date=5 October 2015 |title=Lorenzo Insigne finally coming of age as Napoli's featherweight fantasista |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2015/oct/05/lorenzo-insigne-napoli-featherweight-fantasista-milan-serie-a |access-date=23 January 2017 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref name="AN">{{Cite news |title=Arsenal v Napoli: Arsenal must be cautious of Lorenzo Insigne and his |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european/arsenal-v-napoli-arsenal-must-be-cautious-of-lorenzo-insigne-and-his-hair-raising-rise-at-napoli-8849805.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200609095530/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european/arsenal-v-napoli-arsenal-must-be-cautious-of-lorenzo-insigne-and-his-hair-raising-rise-at-napoli-8849805.html |date=30 September 2013 |archive-date=9 June 2020 |access-date=23 January 2017 |work=The Independent |language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author1=Domenico Carella |date=20 December 2010 |title=Foggia, Cavese ko: doppietta d'Insigne E la società presenta il progetto stadio |trans-title=Foggia, Cavese defeated: Insigne's brace and the club presents the stadium project. |url=http://corrieredelmezzogiorno.corriere.it/bari/notizie/sport/2010/20-dicembre-2010/foggia-cavese-ko-doppietta-d-insignee-societa-presenta-progetto-stadio-181111916191.shtml |access-date=23 to his penchant for scoring goals in his manner, which according to Insigne was inspired by his "idol" [[Alessandro Del Piero]]'s trademark goals, in 2021, the neologism ''tiraggiro'' – derived from "tir a gir" ("tiro a giro", in Italian, or "curling shot", in English) in Insigne's native Neapolitan dialect – was coined and included in the Italian encyclopedia ''[[Treccani]].''<ref name="Del Piero idolo"/><ref name="GdSTiraggiroTreccaniInsigne">{{cite news |date=26 July 2021 |title=Il "tiraggiro" di Insigne sbarca sulla Treccani. E spunta la "bonucciata" |url=https://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Serie-A/Napoli/26-07-2021/tiraggiro-insigne-treccani-4103070615210.shtml |access-date=29 July 2021 |work=La Gazzetta dello Sport |language=it-IT}}</ref> Although his preferred role is on the left flank, he is a hard-working, tactically intelligent, and versatile [[Forward (association football)|forward]], capable of playing in any offensive position on either [[Outside forward|side]] of the pitch, or even through the [[Centre-forward|centre]]; he is also known for his defensive contribution and ability to cover a lot of ground during matches, in addition to his offensive capabilities, despite his lack of physicality.<ref name="Del Piero idolo"/><ref>{{cite web |date=24 February 2020 |title=Napoli, Gattuso: "Barça superiore, ma noi ce la giochiamo" |url=https://www.sportmediaset.mediaset.it/calcio/napoli/napoli-la-conferenza-di-gattuso-verso-il-barcellona_15253190-202002a.shtml |access-date=6 July 2020 |publisher=www.sportmediaset.mediaset.it |language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=6 July 2020 |title=Insigne: "Il Napoli si è rimesso in corsa con Gattuso" |url=https://m.corrieredellosport.it/news/calcio/serie-a/napoli/2020/07/06-71475634/insigne_il_napoli_si_e_rimesso_in_corsa_con_gattuso_/ |access-date=6 July 2020 |work=www.corrieredellosport.it |language=it}}</ref>

He has often operated in deeper, more creative positions, either in a free role in the centre as an [[attacking midfield]] [[playmaker]] behind the strikers,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/sarri-napoli-formation-change-premeditated|title=Sarri: Napoli formation change premeditated|publisher=FourFourTwo|date=18 September 2015|access-date=23 January 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/49758/world-cup-shapes-insigne-intention|title=World Cup shapes Insigne intention?|publisher=Football Italia|date=28 May 2014|access-date=23 January 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=21 July 2015 |title=Napoli, Sarri: "Insigne trequartista ha fatto bene" |url=http://www.corrieredellosport.it/news/calcio/2015/07/21-2598922/napoli_sarri_insigne_trequartista_ha_fatto_bene/?cookieAccept |access-date=23 January 2017 |publisher=Il Corriere dello Sport |language=it}}</ref> or as a [[Forward (association football)#Second striker|supporting forward]],<ref name="Spurs in for Insigne"/><ref name="Del Piero idolo">{{cite web |author1=Alberto Polverosi |date=3 September 2012 |title=Insigne: "Del Piero idolo. Lo porterei a Napoli" |url=http://www.corrieredellosport.it/Calcio/2012/09/03-263028/Insigne%3A+%C2%ABDel+Piero+idolo.+Lo+porterei+a+Napoli%C2%BB |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305072810/http://www.corrieredellosport.it/Calcio/2012/09/03-263028/Insigne:+%C2%ABDel+Piero+idolo.+Lo+porterei+a+Napoli%C2%BB |archive-date=5 March 2016 |access-date=23 January 2017 |publisher=Il Corriere dello Sport |language=it}}</ref> due to his passing ability and vision, which enable him to link-up with midfielders, create chances, and provide [[Assist (association football)|assists]] for teammates.<ref name="Dear Lorenzo Insigne">{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/85482/dear-lorenzo-insigne|title=Dear Lorenzo Insigne|publisher=Football Italia|author=Andrea Tallarita|date=7 June 2016|access-date=23 January 2017}}</ref><ref name="Euro 2016 Squad Selector">{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/84916/euro-2016-squad-selector-insigne|title=Euro 2016 Squad Selector: Insigne|publisher=Football Italia|author=Vincent Van Genechten|date=25 May 2016|access-date=23 January 2017}}</ref> Insigne stated in 2012 that he preferred assisting goals over scoring them himself.<ref>{{cite news |date=13 December 2012 |title=Ecco Insigne il titolarissimo |url=https://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Squadre/Napoli/13-12-2012/insigne-ormai-titolarissimo-anno-super-meglio-assist-gol-913486420687.shtml |access-date=22 April 2024 |work=La Gazzetta dello Sport |language=it}}</ref> He is also capable of playing in a more offensive central role as a [[false 9]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Currò |first1=Enrico |date=5 June 2019 |title=Insigne: ''Sarri alla Juve? Per i napoletani sarebbe un tradimento, spero cambi idea'' |url=https://www.repubblica.it/sport/calcio/nazionale/2019/06/05/news/insigne_europei_italia_sarri_tifosi-228025625/ |access-date=28 November 2019 |work=La Repubblica |language=it}}</ref> In addition to his ability to set-up goals, he is also capable of scoring them himself,<ref name="coming of age" /><ref name="Dear Lorenzo Insigne"/> and is an accurate [[Set piece (football)|set-piece]] taker.<ref name="Lorenzo Insigne: 1991 – Italia"/><ref name="AN"/> Insigne's resulting low [[Center of mass|centre of gravity]], combined with his ==Personal life==
Lorenzo Insigne has three brothers, all of whom are footballers: his younger brother [[Roberto Insigne|Roberto]], as well as Marco and Antonio.<ref>{{cite news |date=10 September 2012 |title=Lorenzo e i suoi fratelli: alla scoperta della prole Insigne, famiglia di calcio |url=http://www.soccermagazine.it/napoli/lorenzo-e-i-suoi-fratelli-alla-scoperta-della-prole-insigne-famiglia-di-calcio-98375/ |access-date=6 June 2013 |publisher=SoccerMagazine |language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |author1=Monica Scozzafava |date=3 August 2012 |title=Lorenzo, predestinato che faceva l'ambulante ed era pazzo dei dolci |url=http://corrieredelmezzogiorno.corriere.it/napoli/notizie/sport/2012/3-agosto-2012/lorenzo-predestinato-che-faceva-ambulante-ed-era-pazzo-dolci-2111302582154.shtml |access-date=21 January 2017 |publisher=Il Corriere del Mezzogiorno |language=it}}</ref> Lorenzo married Genoveffa "Jenny" Darone on 31 December 2012;<ref>{{cite web |title=Mogli storiche e nuove fidanzate: ecco le Wags azzurre |url=http://sport.sky.it/calcio-estero/fotogallery/2016/06/21/euro-2016-wags-italia.html |access-date=23 January 2017 |publisher=Sky.it |language=it |last1=Sport |first1=Sky}}</ref> they have three children together: Carmine, born on 4 April 2013,<ref>{{cite web |date=4 April 2013 |title=E' nato Carmine il primogenito dell'attaccante azzurro |url=http://www.sscnapoli.it/static/news/Insigne-e-papa-185.aspx |access-date=23 January 2017 |publisher=S.S.C. ==Trivia==
Insigne has contributed to popularising the term ''tiraggiro'' in Italy; following Insigne's goals and role in Italy's victorious Euro 2020 campaign, the word was subsequently included in the ''[[Treccani]]'' encyclopaedia in 2021, as a result of its recurring use as a reference to Insigne, or other players, using his trademark shooting technique, which usually involves him curling shots on goal from outside the box after cutting inside from the left flank onto his stronger right foot.<ref name="GdSTiraggiroTreccaniInsigne" /><ref>{{cite news |date=26 July 2021 |title=Il tiraggiro di Insigne sulla Treccani, polemica social: "E Del Piero?" |url=https://www.corrieredellosport.it/news/calcio/serie-a/napoli/2021/07/26-83883270/il_tiraggiro_di_insigne_sulla_treccani_polemica_social_e_del_piero_ |access-date=31 July 2021 |work=Il Corriere dello Sport |language=Italian}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=25 July 2021 |title=Il termine "tiraggiro" entra nei neologismi della Treccani |url=https://www.ilcorrieredelpallone.it/il-termine-tiraggiro-entra-nei-neologismi-della-treccani/ |access-date=31 July 2021 |publisher=ilcorrieredelpallone.it |language=Italian}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=27 July 2021 |title=Il "tiraggiro" di Lorenzo Insigne diventa una parola e sbarca sulla Treccani |url=https://www.deejay.it/articoli/il-tiraggiro-di-lorenzo-insigne-diventa-una-parola-e- |access-date=31 July 2021 |language=Italian}}</ref> The definition of the neologism is "the curling shot, taken hitting the ball so as to curve it with an inward curl", "adaptation of the spoken Neapolitan ''tir a ggir''": excerpts of newspaper articles about Insigne are frequently cited as an example of the usage of this term.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.treccani.it/vocabolario/tiraggiro_%28Neologismi%29/|title=Tiraggiro|publisher=Treccani|language=Italian|access-date=31 July 2021}}</ref>

'''Mikel Arteta Amatriain''' ({{IPA|eu|mikel arteta amatriãĩn|lang}}; born 26 March 1982) is a Spanish professional [[Manager (association football)|football manager]] and former [[Association football|player]] who is the manager of {{English football updater|Arsenal}} club [[Arsenal F.C.]]

Arteta played as a [[midfielder]] in his playing career. He began his senior club career at [[FC Barcelona]] in 1999, but limited playing time led to a loan move to [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] in 2001, where he won the [[UEFA Intertoto Cup]] in his second season. Arteta joined [[Rangers F.C.]] in 2002 for £6 million and won the [[2002–03 Scottish Premier League|league]] and [[2002–03 Scottish League Cup|league cup]] in his debut season, scoring a 93rd-minute penalty on the final day. After a brief return to his hometown club [[Real Sociedad]], Arteta signed for [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] in 2005 and was named the club's [[List of Everton F.C. records and statistics#Evertonfc.com player awards|Player of the Season]] twice. He joined Arsenal in 2011 for £10 million and won two [[FA Cup]]s before retiring in 2016. Arteta represented [[Spain]] through several youth levels but never played for the senior national team.

Arteta was appointed as an assistant coach to [[Pep Guardiola]] at [[Manchester City F.C.]] in 2016. He returned to Arsenal as manager in 2019 and won the [[2019–20 FA Cup|FA Cup]] in his debut season and their first [[Premier League]] title in 22 years [[2025–26 Premier League|in 2026]]. Arteta has since become Arsenal's [[List of Arsenal F.C. managers#Managers|seventh-longest serving manager by games managed]] and the [[List of current Premier League and English Football League managers|longest-serving current Premier League manager]].

==Club career==
===Early career===
Born in [[San Sebastián]], [[Basque Country (autonomous community)|Basque Country]], Spain, Arteta began his football career at [[Antiguoko]] and befriended fellow midfielder [[Xabi Alonso]] as they played together every weekend.<ref name="Arteta&Alonso">{{cite news |date=19 November 2005 |title=Mikel Arteta: 'It's a long way from San Sebastian...' |work=The Independent |location=London |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/mikel-arteta-its-a-long-way-from-san-sebastian-515944.html |url-status=live |url-access=subscription |access-date=13 August 2010 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220514/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/mikel-arteta-its-a-long-way-from-san-sebastian-515944.html |archive-date=14 May 2022}}</ref> The two often played along the beaches and gutters of San Sebastián and dreamed of playing together at [[Real Sociedad]].<ref name="Arteta&Alonso" /> Arteta left San Sebastián aged 15 in July 1997, with Antiguoko teammates Jon Alvarez and Mikel Yanguas, to trial with [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]]'s youth academy, [[La Masia]].<ref name=":Athletic1">{{Cite news |last=Campbell |first=Jordan |date=23 March 2023 |title=Mikel Arteta, the early years: 'Everyone knew he had a chance at Barca but Xavi was extraordinary' |work=The Athletic |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4302245/2023/03/23/mikel-arteta-barcelona-xavi-iniesta/ |url-access=subscription |access-date=24 March 2023}}</ref> The trio played three trial games and all earned professional contracts with the club.<ref name=":Athletic1" /> Housed in dormitories, the academy lifestyle was notoriously strict and Arteta's Antiguoko teammates would leave the academy shortly after arrival.<ref name=":Athletic1" /> It was in these dormitories where Arteta would become room-mates and friends with [[Víctor Valdés]] and [[Andrés Iniesta]] as teenagers.<ref name=":BBCSport1">{{cite web |last1=Balague |first1=Guillem |title=At home with Arteta – childhood, career and family |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c2qvqn03z4vo |website=BBC Sport |date=16 May 2024 |publisher=BBC}}</ref> Arteta also became a friend of [[Xavi (footballer, born 1980)|Xavi Hernández]] during his tenure at La Masia.<ref name=":BBCSport1" /> Arteta met then-Barcelona captain and his future coaching mentor [[Pep Guardiola]] during this time, while learning the practices of their then-head coach [[Louis van Gaal]].<ref name=":Athletic1" />

Arteta trained regularly with Van Gaal's first team but was limited only to appearances in Spain's [[Segunda División B]] with [[FC Barcelona Atlètic|Barcelona B]].<ref name=":Athletic1" /> Following Van Gaal's departure from the club on 20 May 2000, incoming coach [[Lorenzo Serra Ferrer]] brought [[Emmanuel Petit]] and [[Gerard López]] into Barcelona's midfield, pushing Arteta further back into a queue which already included Guardiola, [[Luis Enrique]], [[Phillip Cocu]], [[Iván de la Peña]], Xavi and Iniesta.<ref name=":Athletic1" /> La Masia teammate [[Jofre Mateu]] believed that Arteta wouldn't make it at Barcelona purely because of his competition, explaining in 2023, "Everyone knew he had a chance because of his quality but Xavi was extraordinary and Iniesta could play every position. I wasn't expecting him to be a Barcelona star because of the others."<ref name=":Athletic1" /> With administrative changes in La Masia during the [[2000–01 FC Barcelona season|2000–01 season]], Arteta and a number of his club mates quickly learnt that their futures were no longer with Barcelona.<ref name=":Athletic1" />

====Loan to Paris Saint-Germain====
Midway through the 2000–01 season, Arteta was transferred to French club [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] on an 18-month loan.<ref name="Arteta&Alonso" /> He joined a star-studded team managed by [[Luis Fernandez]], a team which included the likes of [[Mauricio Pochettino]], [[Gabriel Heinze]], [[Jay-Jay Okocha]] and [[Nicolas Anelka]]. Arteta would also later play with [[Ronaldinho]] when the Brazilian moved to [[Paris]] in the summer of 2001.<ref name=":Athletic1" /> He made his senior debut on 10 February 2001 against [[AJ Auxerre|Auxerre]] in the round of 32 of the [[2000–01 Coupe de France|2000–01 Coupe de France]].{{citation needed|date=November 2024}} Arteta started the match at the [[Parc des Princes]] and played the entire game in which PSG lost 4–0. On 17 February 2001, Arteta made his [[Ligue 1|French Division 1]] debut coming off the bench in the 34th minute for [[Vampeta]] in a 1–0 defeat against [[Le Classique|rivals]] [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]], away at the [[Stade Vélodrome]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Olympique Marseille v Paris St Germain, 17 February 2001 |url=https://www.11v11.com/matches/olympique-marseille-v-paris-st-germain-17-february-2001-5040/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210517160559/https://www.11v11.com/matches/olympique-marseille-v-paris-st-germain-17-february-2001-5040/ |archive-date=17 May 2021 |access-date=25 March 2023 |website=11v11.com |publisher=AFS Enterprises}}</ref> Arteta was used by Fernández primarily as a playmaker during his time in Paris;<ref>{{Cite book |title=100 Most Popular Expatriate Footballers in Spain |publisher=Focus On |year=2018 |edition=4th |page=2056 |language=en |asin=B078C8FX6V}}</ref> he played 11 games in his [[2000–01 Paris Saint-Germain FC season|first season]] and he scored his first senior goal on 12 May 2001 against [[Lille OSC|Lille]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Paris St Germain v Lille, 12 May 2001 |url=https://www.11v11.com/matches/paris-st-germain-v-lille-12-may-2001-7119/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181213003936/https://www.11v11.com/matches/paris-st-germain-v-lille-12-may-2001-7119/ |archive-date=13 December 2018 |access-date=25 March 2023 |website=11v11.com |publisher=AFS Enterprises}}</ref> During Arteta's [[2001–02 Paris Saint-Germain FC season|second season]] with PSG, he won the [[2001 UEFA Intertoto Cup]] in the summer,
