loan spell.

===Rangers===
Arteta signed for Scottish club Rangers in March 2002 in a £6 million transfer deal.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rangers sign Barca boy Arteta |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2002/mar/19/newsstory.sport5 |work=The Guardian |access-date=26 April 2015 |date=19 March 2002}}</ref><ref name=":1" /> He enjoyed a successful first season in [[Glasgow]] and quickly established himself as a first-team regular. Highlights were scoring on his [[Old Firm]] debut,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/2295515.stm |title=Old Firm in thrilling draw |work=BBC Sport |access-date=21 December 2014}}</ref> and converting a late penalty on the final day of the [[2002–03 Scottish Premier League|2002–03 season]], which proved vital for [[goal difference]]<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/2932016.stm |title=Rangers win to clinch title |work=BBC Sport |date=25 May 2003 |access-date=16 July 2017}}</ref> as Rangers completed the [[Treble (association football)|domestic treble]] of the [[Scottish Premier League]] title, [[Scottish Cup]] and [[Scottish League Cup]]. Arteta was injured shortly before the [[2003 Scottish Cup final]] and missed the match.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_div_1/2946904.stm |title=Rangers complete Treble|date=31 May 2003 |work=BBC Sport |access-date=21 December 2014}}</ref>

Arteta started his [[2003–04 in Scottish football|second season]] with Rangers by scoring six goals in the first six games of the season<ref>{{Soccerbase season|24034|2003|name=Mikel Arteta|access-date=21 December 2014}}</ref> as the club qualified for the [[2003–04 UEFA Champions League#Group E|Champions League group stages]], although they did not qualify from that group and ended the campaign without a trophy. Arteta returned to Spain after two seasons in Glasgow; he later credited his spell at Rangers as helping him develop as a player, stating "Scottish football was tough, really tough. It was really physical, people got at you and I had to improve on that a lot. I think I did that to get to the level that the Premier League required of me."<ref>{{cite web |title=Mikel Arteta: Rangers move made me a top flight player |url=http://sport.stv.tv/football/clubs/rangers/293316-mikel-arteta-rangers-move-made-me-a-top-flight-player/ |publisher=STV Sport |access-date=26 April 2015 |date=12 January 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304070016/http://sport.stv.tv/football/clubs/rangers/293316-mikel-arteta-rangers-move-made-me-a-top-flight-player/ |archive-date=4 March 2016 }}</ref>

===Real Sociedad===
He joined [[Real Sociedad]] for €5.2 million in 2004 with the idea being that Arteta and Xabi Alonso could play together. However, Alonso left for [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] and Arteta failed to establish himself in the team,<ref name=Arteta&Alonso/> starting only three league matches in the half-season he spent back in San Sebastián.<ref>[https://www.bdfutbol.com/en/p/j2026.html?temp=2004-05 Arteta: Matches 2004–05], BDFutbol</ref>

===Everton===
[[File:Mikel Arteta vs Bohemians.jpg|thumb|upright|Arteta playing for [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] in 2011]]

[[Everton F.C.|Everton]] manager [[David Moyes]] signed Arteta in the 2005 January transfer window on loan with a view to a permanent transfer. Seen as a replacement for Danish midfielder [[Thomas Gravesen]] who had moved to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]],<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/e/everton/4176451.stm |title=Gravesen completes switch to Real |work=BBC Sport |date=14 January 2005 |access-date=16 July 2017}}</ref> Arteta played a vital part in helping Everton achieve the possibility of qualifying for the Champions League when they finished fourth in the [[2004–05 FA Premier League|Premier League]]; however, they were knocked out controversially by [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] in the [[2005–06 UEFA Champions League qualifying rounds#Third qualifying round|last qualifying round]].<ref name=Arteta&Alonso/> He scored his first Everton goal in a 4–0 victory over [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Everton 4–0 Crystal Palace |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/4403623.stm |access-date=23 April 2019 |work=BBC Sport |date=10 April 2005}}</ref> and signed a permanent five-year deal in July 2005 for a fee of £2 million.<ref>{{cite news |title=David Moyes: We can have a go at Arsenal |url=https://www.whufc.com/news/articles/2020/march/06-march/david-moyes-we-can-have-go-arsenal |access-date=4 April 2020 |work=West Ham United |date=6 March 2020}}</ref>

The [[2005–06 in English football|2005–06]] season saw Arteta pick up both the [[Everton F.C.#Player of the Season|Everton Player of the Season]] and the ''Players' Player of the Season'' awards.<ref name=EFC/> Arteta's good form extended into 2006–07. As well as retaining his starting place, he frequently turned in man-of-the-match displays, and finished the season with nine goals from the 35 league games he played. Arteta was awarded the ''Player of the Season Award'' for the second consecutive year.<ref name=EFC/> He was also voted the Premier League's 'Midfielder of the Year' by the viewers of [[Sky Sports]], beating [[PFA Players' Player of the Year]] [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] to the award.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.evertonfc.com/news/archive/arteta-named-best-midfield.html |publisher=Everton F.C. |title=Midfielder of the year |access-date=17 June 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071018084006/http://www.evertonfc.com/news/archive/arteta-named-best-midfield.html |archive-date=18 October 2007 }}</ref>

Arteta's creativity was an essential part of Everton's attacking play the following season,{{Citation needed|date=August 2010}} and he had scored six goals by the end of January.<ref name="evertonfc.com">[http://www.evertonfc.com/player-profile/mikel-arteta Mikel Arteta / Everton Squad, Everton Players / evertonfc.com – The Official Website of Everton Football Club]. {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091016192213/http://www.evertonfc.com/player-profile/mikel-arteta |date=16 October 2009 }}. Everton F.C. 28 March 1982. Retrieved 11 June 2012.</ref> That improved further a season later, with Arteta scoring nine times in the 2006–07 season and once again ending the season as the Player of the Year. He helped Everton secure a place in the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]] and was ranked by the ACTIM Index as the sixth best player in the Premier League, but it did not earn him a call-up into the full Spain squad.<ref name="evertonfc.com"/> During the summer of 2007, he signed a new five-year contract.<ref name="evertonfc.com"/>

Arteta added another accolade to his growing collection during the [[2007–08 in English football|2007–08 season]], when he picked up the ''North West Footballer of the Year'' award. He then became the first Everton player in five years to receive the [[Liverpool Echo]]'s ''Sports Personality of the Year'' award in January 2008.{{citation needed|date=December 2019}} Arteta suffered a stomach injury in the second half of the season, and shortly before the final game of the campaign, he underwent surgery to rectify the problem.<ref name="evertonfc.com"/> He scored his first goal of the [[2008–09 in English football|2008–09 season]] in the [[Premier League]] opener versus [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] with a free kick. He was named [[Captain (association football)|captain]] for a 2–2 draw with [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]], scoring a penalty in the game. In February, Arteta was carried off on a stretcher in a 0–0 draw with Newcastle having injured a ligament in his knee, days after his first inclusion in the Spain national team squad. The injury kept him out for the rest of the 2008–09 season and the first five months of 2009–10. Over the course of the season, Arteta began to play in the centre of the field again, usually being partnered with a defensive midfielder. This gave him the freedom to dictate the tempo of the game and connect with Pienaar and Osman on the wing.{{citation needed|date=December 2019}}

Arteta made his return from injury in January 2010 as a substitute in an [[FA Cup]] tie against [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]], before starting in a 2–1 home Premier League win against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]. His first two goals of the season were scored in a 5–1 win over [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] in March 2010. In August that year, he signed a five-year contract extension with Everton.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.evertonfc.com/news/archive/2010/08/13/arteta-contract-photo-exclusive |publisher=Everton F.C. |title=Arteta Contract Photo Exclusive |date=13 August 2010 |access-date=13 August 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304134129/http://www.evertonfc.com/news/archive/2010/08/13/arteta-contract-photo-exclusive |archive-date=4 March 2016 }}</ref> The [[2010–11 in English football|2010–11 season]] proved to be not as successful as expected for both the team and the player. After early goals in the season, against Manchester United in a thriller 3–3 comeback at [[Goodison Park]], and in a 2–0 win in the [[Merseyside derby]], Arteta suffered a loss of form that would be crucial in Everton's push for a European spot. He began to show again glimpses of creative power in the final part of the season, when he was played again on the wing, enjoying more freedom and space.{{citation needed|date=December 2019}}

Upon departing Everton, Arteta said "I am 29 years old so I haven't got much time left to take a chance like this one. I have done my best for Everton."<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14744368 |title=Arteta defends move to Arsenal |work=BBC Sport |date=1 September 2011 |access-date=1 December 2011}}</ref> A few weeks later, he stated that the spirit in Everton's dressing room is the 'best in football'.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/everton-fc/everton-fc-news/2011/10/07/mikel-arteta-spirit-in-everton-fc-s-dressing-room-is-the-best-in-football-100252-29554361/ |title=Arteta believes Everton team spirit is the best in football |work=Liverpool Echo |date=7 October 2011 |access-date=1 December 2011}}</ref>

===Arsenal===
[[File:Mikel Arteta with the 2015 FA Cup.jpg|thumb|upright|right|Arteta celebrates winning the [[FA Cup]] with [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] in 2015]]

Arteta signed for [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] on 31 August 2011 on a four-year deal for a reported fee of £10 million.<ref>{{cite news |title=Arteta joins Arsenal on a four-year deal |url=http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/arteta-joins-arsenal-on-a-four-year-deal |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=31 August 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120105042538/http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/arteta-joins-arsenal-on-a-four-year-deal |archive-date=5 January 2012}}</ref> He made his debut on 10 September in a 1–0 home win against [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]],<ref>McNulty, Phil. (10 September 2011) [https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14772989 BBC Sport – Arsenal 1–0 Swansea]. ''BBC Sport''. Retrieved 11 June 2012.</ref> and scored his first Premier League goal for Arsenal in a 4–3 loss against Blackburn Rovers at [[Ewood Park]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Yak attack stuns Gunners|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/blackburn-vs-arsenal/report/237918|access-date=22 April 2021|website=Sky Sports|language=en}}</ref> Arteta got his first chance to captain ''the Gunners'' in the third-round FA Cup victory over Leeds United, a game in that marked the second Arsenal debut of [[Thierry Henry]]. Arteta suffered an ankle sprain in his side's 2–1 loss to [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]] on 16 April, which sidelined him for the remainder of the season.<ref>[http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1051233/arsenal-midfielder-mikel-arteta-ruled-out-of-run-in?cc=5901 Arsenal midfielder Mikel Arteta ruled out of run-in] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120423144827/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1051233/arsenal-midfielder-mikel-arteta-ruled-out-of-run-in?cc=5901 |date=23 April 2012 }}. ''ESPN Soccernet''. 20 April 2012. Retrieved 11 June 2012.</ref> Despite this he made 29 appearances all season, scoring 6 times, and was voted by the fans as the fifth most important player of the 2011–12 campaign in Arsenal's Player of the Season poll.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/player-of-the-season-in-fifth-place-is |first=Rob |last=Kelly |title=Player of the Season – in fifth place is... |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=28 May 2012 |access-date=23 July 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120705024401/http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/player-of-the-season-in-fifth-place-is |archive-date=5 July 2012}}</ref>

Following the departure of captain [[Robin van Persie]], Arteta was made Arsenal's vice-captain for the 2012–13 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/vermaelen-confirmed-as-new-arsenal-captain |title=Vermaelen confirmed as new Arsenal captain |date=17 August 2012 |access-date=23 July 2012}}</ref> He was voted by the fans as the fourth best player of the 2012–13 campaign in Arsenal's Player of the Season poll, after leading the team to their 17th consecutive top four finish. He missed the beginning of 2013–14 due to injury, but returned to the squad by the end of September,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.express.co.uk/sport/football/430915/Mikel-Arteta-back-as-Arsene-Wenger-hails-Aaron-Ramsey-ahead-of-Stoke-clash |title=Mikel Arteta back as Arsene Wenger hails Aaron Ramsey ahead of Stoke clash |website=Daily Express.co.uk|date=20 September 2013 }}</ref> going on to score and be sent off in the same match, a 2–0 win away to [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] in October.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/crystal-palace-0-arsenal-2-match-report-gunners-made-to-work-by-rejuvenated-eagles-8906080.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220514/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/crystal-palace-0-arsenal-2-match-report-gunners-made-to-work-by-rejuvenated-eagles-8906080.html |archive-date=14 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |title=Crystal Palace 0 Arsenal 2 match report: Gunners made to work by rejuvenated Eagles |date=27 October 2013 |work=The Independent}}</ref> Arsenal reached the [[2014 FA Cup final]], with Arteta scoring against former club Everton in the quarter-final, as well as in the semi-final shootout against Wigan Athletic.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/26395193 |title=Arsenal 4–1 Everton |date=8 March 2014 |access-date=18 May 2014 |work=BBC Sport}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/26897266 |title=Arsenal 1–1 Wigan |date=12 April 2014 |access-date=18 May 2014 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> Arteta captained the side for the final at Wembley, leading them to a 3–2 win against [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] and receiving his first major honour in English football.<ref name=2014FACupFinal>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27354148 |title=Arsenal 3–2 Hull City |first=Phil |last=McNulty |work=BBC Sport |date=17 May 2014 |access-date=3 December 2019}}</ref>

Arteta became Arsenal's new [[List of Arsenal F.C. players#Captains|club captain]] ahead of the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/20140810/wenger-on-winning-and-attacking-options |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=10 August 2014 |title=Wenger on winning and attacking options |access-date=9 July 2015}}</ref><ref name="l24">{{cite web |title=Arteta looks to build on Community Shield win and reflects on captaincy |url=http://www.london24.com/sport/football/clubs/arsenal/arteta_looks_to_build_on_community_shield_win_and_reflects_on_captaincy_1_3721077 |publisher=London 24 |access-date=9 July 2015 |date=11 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150710151655/http://www.london24.com/sport/football/clubs/arsenal/arteta_looks_to_build_on_community_shield_win_and_reflects_on_captaincy_1_3721077 |archive-date=10 July 2015}}</ref> He won his first trophy as full-time captain, playing the full 90 minutes as Arsenal beat [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] 3–0 in the [[2014 FA Community Shield]].<ref name="l24" /><ref name=2014CommunityShield>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28647186 |title=Arsenal 3–0 Manchester City |first=Mandeep |last=Sanghera |work=BBC Sport |date=10 August 2014 |access-date=3 December 2019}}</ref> Despite his new appointment, he would only make 11 appearances for the whole season, scoring once. Arteta signed a one-year extension with Arsenal for the 2015–16 season<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/20150708/wenger-arteta-has-signed-new-deal |title=Wenger – Arteta has signed new deal |date=8 July 2015 |access-date=8 July 2015 |publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref> and came on as a substitute as Arsenal beat Chelsea 1–0 to win the [[2015 FA Community Shield]],<ref name=2015CommunityShield>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33667216 |title=Arsenal 1–0 Chelsea |first=Andy |last=Cryer |work=BBC Sport |date=2 August 2015 |access-date=3 December 2019}}</ref> his first competitive appearance for the club since November 2014. His final game for Arsenal came on the last day of the season. Arteta came on as a substitute and forced [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] [[Mark Bunn (English footballer)|Mark Bunn]] into scoring an own goal after his shot went off the crossbar. He received a standing ovation from the crowd at full time.<ref>{{Cite web|date=15 May 2016|title=Arteta receives standing ovation from the fans|url=https://metro.co.uk/video/arteta-receives-standing-ovation-fans-1291488/|access-date=2 December 2021|website=Metro|language=en}}</ref>

==International career==
Arteta played for [[Spain national football team|Spain]] at youth level. He played in the victorious [[1999 UEFA European Under-16 Championship]] campaign,<ref name=RSSSF /> at the [[1999 UEFA–CAF Meridian Cup]], [[1999 FIFA U-17 World Championship]], and captained the side in the [[2004 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification Group 6|2004 U21 European Championships qualifying campaign]].{{citation needed|date=December 2019}} In 2010, there were moves by the English FA and [[Fabio Capello]] to see if Arteta could represent [[England national football team|England]], believing he qualified under [[FIFA]]'s five-year residency rule. FIFA ruled this out, however,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/england/7975748/Fabio-Capello-embarrassed-as-Fifa-rule-confirms-Mikel-Artetas-ineligibility-to-play-for-England.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220111/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/england/7975748/Fabio-Capello-embarrassed-as-Fifa-rule-confirms-Mikel-Artetas-ineligibility-to-play-for-England.html |archive-date=11 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|title=Fabio Capello embarrassed as Fifa rule confirms Mikel Arteta's ineligibility to play for England|publisher=The Telegraph|date=1 September 2010|access-date=6 December 2019}}{{cbignore}}</ref> with Arteta claiming in an interview in 2016 that he "almost went to war with FIFA" over the ruling.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://talksport.com/football/76582/arsenal-captain-mikel-arteta-reveals-i-almost-went-war-fifa-chance-represent-england|title=Arsenal captain Mikel Arteta reveals: I almost went to war with FIFA for chance to represent England|publisher=Talksport|date=14 May 2016|access-date=6 December 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Cahill Calls for Arteta Call Up |url=http://www.evertonfc.com/news/archive/2010/04/01/cahill-calls-for-arteta-call-up |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121009083700/http://www.evertonfc.com/news/archive/2010/04/01/cahill-calls-for-arteta-call-up |archive-date=9 October 2012 |access-date=24 July 2010 |publisher=Everton F.C.}}</ref>

Arteta was believed to be in Spain's squad in February 2009 but a cruciate knee ligament injury meant his name was removed from the list before the squad was announced.<ref name="Pearce">{{Cite web|last=Pearce|first=James|date=19 August 2010|title=Mikel Arteta will never give up on international call-up for Spain|url=http://www.liverpoolecho.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/mikel-arteta-never-give-up-3399266|access-date=22 April 2021|website=Liverpool Echo|language=en}}</ref> Often noted to be one of the best players in modern times to be omitted a senior international cap, Arteta played at a time when Spain had several enormously high quality players available in his position, such as [[Xavi (footballer, born 1980)|Xavi]], [[Andrés Iniesta]], [[Xabi Alonso]], [[Cesc Fàbregas]], [[Marcos Senna]], [[Sergio Busquets]], [[Santi Cazorla]] and [[David Silva]].<ref name="Pearce"/><ref>{{Cite web|last=Football|first=Planet|date=6 September 2020|title=Nine of the best players to never win a cap: Arteta, Di Canio, Bruce|url=https://www.planetfootball.com/quick-reads/nine-best-players-never-win-cap-arteta-di-canio-bruce/|access-date=22 April 2021|website=Planet Football|language=en-US}}</ref>

==Style of play==
[[File:Mikel Arteta corner kick Arsenal vs Swansea.jpg|thumb|Arteta taking a corner kick for Arsenal in 2011]]

Arteta initially started out playing as a number 10 in the Barcelona youth system, and was later shifted to the position of a "pivot" or defensive midfielder, as he was thought to be a player in the mould of [[Pep Guardiola]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2019/11/22/mikel-arteta-integral-pep-guardiolas-transformation-manchester/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220111/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2019/11/22/mikel-arteta-integral-pep-guardiolas-transformation-manchester/ |archive-date=11 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |title=Mikel Arteta is integral to Pep Guardiola's transformation of Manchester City – and the man he sees as his successor |work=The Telegraph |last1=Burt |first1=Jason |date=22 November 2019 |access-date=18 July 2020 }}{{cbignore}}</ref> He was rated as the sixth most effective player in the [[Premier League]] in [[2006–07 FA Premier League|2006–07]] by the official player ratings system the Actim Index. Arteta returned to his original [[Midfielder#Deep-lying playmaker (Strolling 10)|deeper midfield role]] at Arsenal.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11670/8165113/arsenal-midfielder-mikel-arteta-happy-to-adapt-to-a-more-defensive-role |title=Arsenal midfielder Mikel Arteta happy to adapt to a more defensive role |work=Sky Sports |date=14 December 2012 |access-date=8 January 2019}}</ref> in which he excelled as his team's playmaker, due to his technique, skill, vision, passing, awareness, and tactical intelligence.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2012/sep/28/mikel-arteta-arsenal-midfield |title=Mikel Arteta's footballing sense has revived the Arsenal midfield |work=The Guardian |last1=Lawrence |first1=Amy |date=28 September 2012 |access-date=18 July 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1840015-who-is-better-michael-carrick-or-mikel-arteta |title=Who Is Better: Michael Carrick or Mikel Arteta? |publisher=Bleacher Report |last1=Morgan |first1=Richard |date=8 November 2013 |access-date=18 July 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37454678/premier-league-disappointing-lack-deep-lying-playmakers |title=Cox: Lack of deep-lying playmakers in Prem |work=ESPN.com |last1=Cox |first1=Michael |date=23 August 2016 |access-date=18 July 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/829287-arsenal-transfers-5-reasons-mikel-arteta-is-the-answer-for-arsene-wenger |title=Arsenal Transfers: 5 Reasons Mikel Arteta Is the Answer for Arsene Wenger |publisher=Bleacher Report |last1=Dudko |first1=James |access-date=18 July 2020 |date=31 August 2011}}</ref> His total of 12 league assists in the [[2006–07 in English football|2006–07 season]] was third to [[Cesc Fàbregas]] and [[Cristiano Ronaldo]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Statistics |url=http://www.premierleague.com/page/Statistics |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111127233054/http://www.premierleague.com/page/Statistics |archive-date=27 November 2011 |access-date=24 September 2025 |website=Premier League}}</ref> With 100 fouls committed against him in the same season, he was the most fouled player in the Premier League.<ref name="ESPNsoccernet: Mikel Arteta">{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130103035544/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/players/stats?id=9840&cc=5739|title=ESPNsoccernet: Mikel Arteta}}. ''ESPN Soccernet''. 26 March 1982. Retrieved 11 June 2012.</ref>

==Coaching and managerial career==
===Manchester City===
Arteta had three options upon retirement. He was offered to lead the Arsenal Academy, by [[Arsène Wenger]], join [[Mauricio Pochettino]]'s (his teammate from PSG) backroom staff at [[Tottenham Hotspur]] or join Pep Guardiola's coaching team at [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]]. On 3 July 2016, Arteta was appointed an assistant coach at Manchester City,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/first-team/first-team-news/2016/july/mikel-arteta-joined-guardiola|title=Mikel Arteta joins City's coaching staff|last=Clayton|first=David|website=www.mancity.com|language=en|access-date=20 December 2019}}</ref> alongside [[Brian Kidd]] and [[Domènec Torrent]], who operated as deputies to [[Pep Guardiola]].

Guardiola and Arteta first met at the [[La Masia|Barcelona academy]], although Guardiola was already established in the first team, being 11 years older than Arteta. Since then, the two kept in touch. Guardiola was convinced Arteta – who was an Arsenal player at the time – would make a good coach when he called him to get information on Chelsea, prior to their [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League#Semi-finals|2012 Champions League semi-finals against Barcelona]]. Arteta earned his [[UEFA Pro Licence]] after completing the course run by the [[Football Association of Wales]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/65646318 |title=Mikel Arteta: The rejection and determination that made him a manager |work=BBC Sport |date=24 May 2023 |accessdate=9 January 2026}}</ref>

In 2015, when Guardiola was exiting [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]], Arteta, in his final year as a player, re-connected and the two men decided to work together.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1459938/2019/12/20/mikel-arteta-arsenal-manager-manchester-city-pep-guardiola/|title=Mikel Arteta lived alone with tactical diagrams on the walls: what lies behind the eyes of Arsenal's new manager|last=McNicholas|first=Daniel Taylor and David Ornstein and James|website=The Athletic|access-date=20 December 2019}}</ref> Arteta stood in as Man City manager in a 2–1 [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] loss against [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] on 19 September 2018, because of Guardiola's touchline ban.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37502102/lyon-shock-sloppy-manchester-city-nabil-fekir-delivers-goods-big-stage|title=Lyon shock sloppy Manchester City as Nabil Fekir delivers the goods on the big stage|date=19 September 2018|publisher=ESPN|access-date=19 September 2018}}</ref> At Man City, Arteta won two [[Premier League]] titles, an [[FA Cup]], and two [[EFL Cup]]s. In 2018, Arteta became strongly linked with the Arsenal manager's vacancy, following the departure of his former manager Arsène Wenger, but [[Unai Emery]] was eventually hired.<ref>{{cite news |last=Ornstein |first=David |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44094251 |title=Mikel Arteta: Ex-Arsenal midfielder one of options to replace Arsene Wenger |work=BBC Sport |date=12 May 2018 |access-date=8 January 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |author=Hytner, David |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2018/may/12/mikel-arteta-arsenal-managers-job-interest-max-allegri |title=Arsenal's interest in Mikel Arteta grows but Max Allegri still in the frame |work=The Guardian |date=12 May 2018 |access-date=8 January 2019}}</ref>

===Arsenal===
====2019–22: Early years and FA Cup win====
On 20 December 2019, Arteta was appointed head coach at his former club [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], signing a deal until 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/50817660|title=Mikel Arteta: Arsenal appoint ex-midfielder as manager|date=20 December 2019|publisher=BBC|access-date=20 December 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/37580019/mikel-arteta-named-arsenal-head-coach |title=Mikel Arteta named Arsenal head coach |publisher=ESPN |date=20 December 2019 |access-date=20 December 2019}}</ref> Upon his appointment, he stated that he believed the club had lost direction and that he didn't want players to shirk responsibility: "I want people to take responsibility for their jobs and I want people who deliver passion and energy in the football club. Anyone who doesn't buy into this, or that has a negative effect or whatever, is not good enough for this environment or this culture."<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/dec/20/arsenal-appoint-mikel-arteta-as-manager-to-replace-unai-emery|title=Mikel Arteta will not tolerate dissenters as he seeks to revive 'lost' Arsenal|last=Ames|first=Nick|date=20 December 2019|work=The Guardian|access-date=20 December 2019|language=en-GB|issn=0261-3077}}</ref> Arteta named his coaching staff on 24 December, with assistants [[Albert Stuivenberg]] and [[Steve Round]], and goalkeeping coach [[Iñaki Caña]] joining the club. Interim head coach [[Freddie Ljungberg]] remained as assistant coach, and goalkeeping coach [[Sal Bibbo]] stayed to work with Caña.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/coaching-team-named |title=Coaching team named |date=24 December 2019 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=12 October 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/50912761 |title=Mikel Arteta: Arsenal's new boss encouraged by early signs from players |date=26 December 2019 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=12 October 2024}}</ref>

On 26 December 2019, Arteta took charge for the first time as an Arsenal manager for their [[2019–20 Premier League|Premier League]] match against [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]] which ended in a 1–1 draw, thanks to a second half equaliser from [[Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang]]. Despite the draw, he stated he was pleased with the "attitude, passion and the fighting spirit" of his players.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/joshualaw/2019/12/26/mikels-debut-draw-what-we-learned-from-artetas-first-game-as-arsenal-manager/|title=Mikel's Debut Draw: What We Learned From Arteta's First Game As Arsenal Manager|first=Joshua|last=Law|website=Forbes}}</ref> On 1 January 2020, Arteta got his first win as Arsenal coach: a 2–0 win over [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] at the [[Emirates Stadium|Emirates]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/50908732 |title=Arsenal 2–0 Manchester United |work=BBC Sport |date=1 January 2020}}</ref> On 18 July 2020, Arsenal beat Arteta's former employer Manchester City 2–0 in the [[2019–20 FA Cup|FA Cup]] semi-final, leading Arsenal to their fourth [[FA Cup final]] in seven years, and Arteta's first in charge. Arsenal went on to win the [[2020 FA Cup final|final]] 2–1 over [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] for a [[List of FA Cup Finals|record 14th victory]], making Arteta the first person to win the FA Cup as both captain and coach of Arsenal.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53460340 |title=Arsenal 2–0 Manchester City: Mikel Arteta exposes City's deficiencies |work=BBC Sport |date=18 July 2020 }}</ref> Moreover, he became the first head coach or manager to win a major trophy in his first season in charge of the club since [[George Graham (footballer, born 1944)|George Graham]] in 1986–87.<ref>{{Cite news|title='We can win titles together' – Arteta|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53625374|access-date=22 April 2021}}</ref>

Prior to the start of the [[2020–21 Arsenal F.C. season|2020–21 season]], Arsenal announced that assistant coach [[Freddie Ljungberg]] and goalkeeping coach [[Sal Bibbo]] had departed the club; while assistant coaches [[Carlos Cuesta (football manager)|Carlos Cuesta]] and [[Miguel Molina (footballer)|Miguel Molina]], and [[Set piece (football)|set-piece]] coach [[Andreas Georgson]] joined Arteta's backroom staff.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/coaching-and-backroom-team |title=Coaching and backroom team |date=28 August 2020 |website=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=12 October 2024}}</ref> On 29 August, Arteta won his second trophy as manager after Arsenal beat [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] 5–4 on penalties in the [[2020 FA Community Shield|FA Community Shield]].<ref>{{Cite }}</ref> Later on, Arsenal finished 8th in the [[2020–21 Premier League|Premier League]], and the 25-year run of participating in European competitions came to an end.<ref>{{cite web In July 2021, set-piece coach [[Nicolas Jover]] joined Arteta's coaching team, replacing [[Andreas Georgson]] who had departed the club.<ref>{{cite web ==Style of management==
As a manager, Arteta was influenced by his time playing under [[Arsène Wenger]] and serving as an assistant to [[Pep Guardiola]], as well as by the philosophy instilled in him during his spell with the [[La Masia|Barcelona youth academy]]; he had also drawn from tactical elements used by [[José Mourinho]].<ref name="Coaches' Voice"/><ref>{{cite news |title=Mikel Arteta: The rejection and determination that made a manager |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/65646318 |access-date=9 June 2025 |work=BBC Sport |date=24 May 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Mikel Arteta reveals Jose Mourinho 'more than influenced' his managerial style |url=https://www.90min.com/mikel-arteta-reveals-jose-mourinho-more-than-influenced-managerial-style |publisher=90min.com |access-date=9 June 2025 |date=24 September 2024}}</ref> As head coach of Arsenal, Arteta mainly uses a [[4–3–3]] or [[Formation (association football)#4–2–3–1|4–3–2–1 formation]], although he has also been known to use a [[3–4–3 formation]] on occasion. Tactically, his teams look to control games and create chances by dominating possession through fluid, creative passing, often building plays from deep.<ref name="Coaches' Voice">{{cite web |title=Mikel Arteta: Coach Watch |url=https://learning.coachesvoice.com/cv/mikel-arteta-arsenal-pep-guardiola/ |publisher=Coaches' Voice |access-date=9 June 2025 |date=8 September 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Campbell |first1=Jordan |title=Mikel Arteta, 'dominance' and a modern coach's view of attacking football |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6207181/2025/03/17/arteta-arsenal-chelsea-dominance/ |access-date=9 June 2025 |work=The New York Times |date=17 March 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Brown |first1=Cy |title=Mikel Arteta Would Bring The Best Of Both Worlds As Arsenal Manager |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/cybrown/2018/05/16/mikel-arteta-would-bring-the-best-of-both-worlds-as-arsenal-manager/ |date=16 May 2018 |access-date=9 June 2025 |work=Forbes |language=en}}</ref> His team often create wide overloads to allow players to cut back, while the use of 3–2 defensive shell when in possession helps to prevent counter-attacks.<ref name="rigid style">{{cite news |last1=Reporter |first1=James Gheerbrant, Football |title=Mikel Arteta's rigid style has left Arsenal incapable of facing adversity |url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/mikel-arteta-must-make-his-players-tougher-not-give-them-excuses-0ttftzc6m |access-date=9 June 2025 |work=The Times |date=8 May 2025 |language=en}}</ref> His team are also effective at creating chances from attacking set-pieces.<ref name="rigid style"/> 

Defensively, his teams are solid and versatile; they are capable of pressing high up the pitch, but also of making an effective use of an aggressive low block, which becomes a [[Formation (association football)#5–4–1|5–4–1]], [[5-3-2 (association football)|5–3–2]] or [[Formation (association football)#5–2–3|5–2–3]] depending on the opponent, and are even capable of posing a threat from counter-attacks.<ref name="Coaches' Voice"/><ref>{{cite news |last1=Catterson-Reid |first1=Aaron |title=Mikel Arteta's Arsenal and their many different ways of defending |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5792392/2024/09/25/mikel-arteta-arsenal-defensive-adaptability/ |access-date=9 June 2025 |work=The New York Times |date=25 September 2024}}</ref> However, although Arteta has been praised in the media for his ability as a manager, at times his style as Arsenal's manager has also been criticised in the press for being too rigid and formulaic; he has also drawn criticism from pundits at times for his perceived inability to manage the pressure placed on his players, and for not bringing more success to the club.<ref name="rigid style"/><ref>{{cite news |title=Mikel Arteta apologises for failing to deliver Arsenal a Premier League title |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/arsenal-newcastle-mikel-arteta-champions-league-eddie-howe-b2753353.html |access-date=9 June 2025 |work=The Independent |date=18 May 2025 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Blitz |first1=Sam |title=Arsenal: Mikel Arteta's Gunners go another season without a trophy after Champions League exit to PSG – so what now? |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13363668/arsenal-mikel-artetas-gunners-go-another-season-without-a-trophy-after-champions-league-exit-to-psg-so-what-now |access-date=9 June 2025 |work=Sky Sports |date=8 May 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Arteta was born on 26 March 1982 in [[San Sebastián]], in the [[Basque Country (autonomous community)|Basque Country]] of Spain. He is fluent in Spanish, [[Basque language|Basque]], [[Catalan language|Catalan]] and English, and also speaks French, Italian and Portuguese.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.evertonfc.com/news/archive/arteta-s-love-affair.html |title=Arteta's Love Affair with Everton |last=McLeod |first=Scott |date=15 September 2007 |publisher=Everton F.C. |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071018084009/http://www.evertonfc.com/news/archive/arteta-s-love-affair.html |archive-date=18 October 2007 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sportbible.com/football/football-news-reactions-take-a-bow-mikel-arteta-brilliantly-spoke-to-his-players-in-different-languages-20200719 |title=Mikel Arteta Spoke To His Arsenal Players In Three Different Languages During Manchester City Game |last=Marland |first=Daniel |date=19 July 2020 |publisher=[[SPORTbible]] |access-date=3 August 2022 }}</ref> He is married to Argentine-Spanish actress, television host, and model [[Lorena Bernal]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Andrews |first=Connor |date=3 September 2023 |title=Arteta uses hilarious analogy about his wife as he stays calm on Arsenal man's struggles |url=https://talksport.com/football/1554759/mikel-arteta-hilarious-analogy-dating-wife-kai-havertz/ |access-date=8 April 2024 |website=talkSPORT |language=en-gb}}</ref> The couple have three children: Gabriel (born 2009), Daniel (born 2012) and Oliver (born 2015).<ref name="ABC">{{cite web|url=http://www.abc.es/20120627/estilo-gente/abci-lorena-bernal-madre-201206272056.html |title=Lorena Bernal y Mikel Arteta, padres por segunda vez| date= 27 June 2012 |publisher= ABC|access-date=28 June 2012|language= es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=7 June 2015|title=Lorena Bernal y Mikel Arteta presentan a su tercer hijo, Oliver|url=https://www.hola.com/actualidad/2015060779175/lorena-bernal-da-a-luz-tercer-nino/|access-date=22 April 2021|website=HOLA|language=es}}</ref>

Arteta is a [[dual citizen]] of Spain and the United Kingdom. He acquired [[British citizenship]] in 2010, with the hopes of representing the England national football team, although he was later ruled to be ineligible by [[FIFA]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=10 September 2010 |title=Arteta was ready to accept Capello's England offer |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/international/arteta-was-ready-to-accept-capello-s-england-offer-2076252.html |access-date=29 October 2025 |website=The Independent |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Rory |date=17 February 2009 |title=Everton's Mikel Arteta could be eligible for England in January 2010 |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/everton/4681594/Evertons-Mikel-Arteta-could-be-eligible-for-England-in-January-2010.html |access-date=29 October 2025 |website=www.telegraph.co.uk}}</ref>

On 15 May 2024, Arteta was awarded [[Order of Isabella the Catholic|The Royal Order of Isabella the Catholic]] at the [[Spanish Embassy in London|Spanish Embassy]] in London.<ref>{{Cite web |date=16 May 2024 |title=Arsenal news: Mikel Arteta honoured in Spanish Embassy ceremony |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c2x3xel5mx3o |access-date=29 October 2025 |website=[[BBC Sport]] |language=en-GB}}</ref> Commenting on granting the award to Arteta, the Spanish ambassador to the UK, José Pascual Marco Martínez, said: “Mikel is a respected and loved figure in the Spanish and British football community. Through the universal language of football, he has succeeded in making the friendship between the two countries stronger.”<ref name=":2" />

In August 2025, Arteta was appointed a global ambassador and director of performance for sportswear company [[Under Armour]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Collings |first=Simon |date=14 August 2025 |title=Arsenal: Mikel Arteta appointed director of performance at Under Armour |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/arsenal-fc-mikel-arteta-under-armour-b1242558.html |access-date=19 August 2025 |work=Evening Standard}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=White |first=Mark |date=13 August 2025 |title=Mikel Arteta tells FourFourTwo the most important attribute he looks for in new players, during Under Armour launch |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/mikel-arteta-tells-fourfourtwo-the-most-important-attribute-he-looks-for-in-new-players-during-under-armour-launch |access-date=19 August 2025 |work=FourFourTwo}}</ref>

'''Rivaldo Vítor Borba Ferreira''' ({{IPA|pt-BR|ʁiˈvawdu ˈvitoʁ ˈbɔʁbɐ feˈʁe(j)ɾɐ|lang}}; born 19 April 1972),{{cite web |title=Rivaldo |url=https://www.britannica.com/biography/Rivaldo |publisher=[[Encyclopædia Britannica]] |access-date=3 September 2021}} known simply as '''Rivaldo''', is a Brazilian former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played primarily as an [[attacking midfielder]] or [[second striker]], while also operating as a [[winger (association football)|left winger]].{{cite news |last=Smyth |first=Rob |date=19 June 2008 |title=On Second Thoughts: Rivaldo |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2008/jun/19/barcelona.brazil |work=The Guardian |access-date=16 June 2026}} Known for his skill and creativity, Rivaldo was renowned for his [[Curl (football)|bending]] [[Free kick (association football)|free kicks]], [[bicycle kick]]s, [[Dummy (football)#Association football|feints]], powerful ball striking from distance, and ability to both score and [[Assist (association football)|create goals]]. In 1999, he won the [[Ballon d'Or]] and was named [[FIFA World Player of the Year]].{{cite web |title=Rivaldo on top of the world |url=https://www.fifa.com/ballondor/archive/edition=1999901999/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131202232047/http://www.fifa.com/ballondor/archive/edition=1999901999/ |archive-date=2 December 2013 |access-date=17 November 2013 |publisher=FIFA}} In 2004, he was named by [[Pelé]] in the [[FIFA 100]] list of the world's greatest living players.{{cite web |date=4 March 2004 |title=Pele's list of the greatest |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/3533891.stm |publisher=BBC Sport}} With success at club and international level, he is one of eleven players to have won the [[FIFA World Cup]], the [[UEFA Champions League]] and the [[Ballon d'Or]], and is widely regarded as one of the greatest players of all time. In addition, he is also one of a select number of players who have [[List of men's footballers with 1,000 or more official appearances|amassed over 1,000 career appearances]]. Rivaldo started his career in 1991 with Brazilian club [[Santa Cruz Futebol Clube|Santa Cruz]], going on to have spells at [[Mogi Mirim Esporte Clube|Mogi Mirim]], a loan spell at [[Sport Club Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]], and [[Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras|Palmeiras]]. In 1996, he moved to Europe with Spanish side [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]], where his performances in his only season there led him to sign for [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in 1997. At Barcelona, he formed a successful partnership with Dutch international [[Patrick Kluivert]], and won consecutive [[La Liga]] titles in [[1997–98 La Liga|1998]] and [[1998–99 La Liga|1999]], as well as the [[1998 Copa del Rey Final|1998]] [[Copa del Rey]]. Rivaldo notably scored a [[Hattrick (football)|hattrick]] against [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] in June 2001 which qualified Barcelona for the [[2001–02 UEFA Champions League|2001-02 UEFA Champions League]]; the last goal was a last minute 20-yard bicycle kick winner and the hattrick itself is often ranked as the greatest ever. During his five-year tenure there, he scored 130 goals, ranking him among Barcelona's [[List of FC Barcelona records and statistics|highest goalscorers of all time]]. In 2002, Rivaldo signed for Italian club [[A.C. Milan]], winning the [[Coppa Italia]] and the [[UEFA Champions League]] in his only season there, however, his performances were underwhelming and he cancelled his contract with Milan in late 2003. He went on to play for [[Cruzeiro Esporte Clube|Cruzeiro]], [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]], [[AEK Athens F.C.|AEK Athens]], [[FC Bunyodkor|Bunyodkor]], a loan spell at [[São Paulo FC|São Paulo]], [[Kabuscorp S.C.P.|Kabuscorp]] and [[Associação Desportiva São Caetano|São Caetano]]. In March 2014, Rivaldo announced his retirement from professional football, however since June 2015 he made appearances for Mogi Mirim, before retiring again in August 2015. From 1993 to 2003, Rivaldo played 74 matches and scored 35 goals for [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] and is the [[Brazil national football team#Top goalscorers|seventh highest goalscorer]] for the country.[https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/braz-recintlp.html "Goalscoring for Brazil National Team"]. RSSSF. Retrieved 17 May 2014 He helped Brazil reach the final of the [[1998 FIFA World Cup]] and won the [[1999 Copa América]] where he was named player of the tournament. Rivaldo starred in an attacking trio with [[Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)|Ronaldo]] and [[Ronaldinho]] in the [[2002 FIFA World Cup]] winning team. Scoring in five of Brazil's seven games at the tournament, Rivaldo was named in the [[FIFA World Cup All-Star Team]] in 2002 having also previously been selected in 1998. He is an inductee to the [[Brazil national football team#Brazilian Football Museum – Hall of Fame|Brazilian Football Museum Hall of Fame]]. He is a minority shareholder of Romanian [[Liga I]] club [[FCV Farul Constanța|Farul Constanța]].{{cite web|url=https://www.digisport.ro/fotbal/liga-1/de-la-decar-la-decar-rivaldo-a-devenit-actionar-la-farul-si-a-avut-un-mesaj-superb-pentru-gica-hagi-2577697|title=De la decar la decar! Rivaldo a devenit acționar la Farul și a avut un mesaj superb pentru Gică Hagi|publisher=digisport.ro}} ==Early life== Born in Recife, Brazil, Rivaldo had a poor upbringing in the ''[[favelas]]'' of 1989,[https://web.archive.org/web/20071117101103/http://www.fifa.com/classicfootball/awards/gala/news/newsid=74934.html Rivaldo: In the name of the father], ''[[FIFA]]'', 10 October 2000 despite the Paulistano coaches believing him too physically weak to succeed. Rivaldo's father Romildo was killed in a road accident in 1989, but Rivaldo signed his first professional contract later that year.Mike Lee, [http://www.britishcouncil.org/japan-sport-footballculture-players-rivaldo-greatest.htm Overcoming Tragedy to be the Greatest], ''[[British Council]]'' ==Club career== ===Santa Cruz, Mogi Mirim and Corinthians=== He went on to play for [[Santa Cruz Futebol Clube|Santa Cruz]] in 1991. In 1992, he moved south to the state of [[São Paulo (state)|São Paulo]] where he played for [[Mogi Mirim Esporte Clube|Mogi Mirim]] in the second tier of Brazilian football. In 1993, he moved to the state capital to play for [[Sport Club Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]] in the [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|first division]], on loan.{{Cite web|url=https://jovempan.com.br/esportes/futebol/como-pressao-da-torcida-fez-rivaldo-nutrir-raiva-e-odio-mortal-do-corinthians.html|title=Como pressão da torcida fez Rivaldo nutrir "raiva e ódio mortal" do Corinthians – Jovem Pan|date=14 September 2017|website=jovempan.com.br}} ===Palmeiras=== In the next year, he switched local allegiances and moved to [[Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras|Palmeiras]]. His transfer was announced on 11 August 1994, with a fee of [[United States dollar|US$]] 2.5 million ([[Brazilian real|R$]] 2.27 million), as confirmed by Mogi Mirim's vice-president, Helcio Luis Adorno.[https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/fsp/1994/8/11/esporte/16.html Rivaldo é do Palmeiras por US$ 2,5 milhões - 11/8/1994 - folha.uol.com.br] Rivaldo helped Palmeiras successfully defend its league championship in 1994 and win [[Campeonato Paulista]] in [[1996 Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras season|1996]]. In both 1993 and 1994, he was honoured by the authoritative publication ''[[Placar Magazine]]'' with the [[Bola de Ouro]] for the best player in his position.{{citation needed|date=October 2023}} ===Deportivo=== Before the 1996 Olympics, [[Parma F.C.|Parma]] announced that they had signed Rivaldo and his teammate [[Alexandre da Silva Mariano|Amaral]] from Palmeiras.{{cite news | title=Sousa for Chelsea| date=27 June 1996| url =https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/sousa-for-chelsea-1339055.html|work=The Independent | access-date =1 October 2010}} After the Olympics, there was a dispute, and rather than Italy, Rivaldo moved to Spain as he joined [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]] in [[La Liga]]. He only stayed for [[1996–97 La Liga|one season]], but nonetheless it proved to be a successful one for both him and the club. Rivaldo was the joint-fourth top goalscorer of the season, with 21 goals from 41 matches, as Deportivo finished third in the league. ===Barcelona=== Rivaldo switched to [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in 1997 in a [[transfer deal]] securing Deportivo a 4 billion [[Spanish peseta|pesetas]] (around $26 million) transfer fee, with Sir [[Bobby Robson]] convincing Barcelona to sign Rivaldo ahead of [[Steve McManaman]] by saying that Rivaldo would guarantee the team many goals.[https://www.nytimes.com/1997/08/18/sports/18iht-mac.t.html "A New Low in Trading Tactics:Just Ask McManaman"]. ''The New York Times''. Retrieved 11 August 2014[https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/barcelona-move-for-mcmanaman-1245575.html "Barcelona move for McManaman"]. ''The Independent''. Retrieved 11 August 2014 {{Quote box |quote = Rivaldooo...that's magnificent. Ohh wonderful. You just could not envisage such a finish to the season. The Brazilian completes a hat-trick, a minute from time with the most delightful of goals you will ever see. A goal in a million, to earn many many millions next season. |source = — [[Sky Sports]] commentary on Rivaldo's last minute overhead [[bicycle kick]] match winner against Valencia in La Liga on 17 June 2001 to qualify Barcelona for next season's UEFA Champions League."Barcelona vs Valencia. 17 June 2001". Sky Sports 1. |align = right |quoted = 1 | width = 27% }} In his first season at Barcelona, Rivaldo was the second top goalscorer with 19 goals in 34 matches, as Barcelona won [[Double (association football)|The Double]] of [[1997–98 La Liga|La Liga]] and [[1997–98 Copa del Rey|Copa del Rey]].{{cite news |title=10 Most Successful Seasons in Barcelona History |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1207192-10-most-successful-seasons-in-barcelona-history |access-date=24 March 2021 |agency=Bleacher Report}} In [[1998–99 La Liga|1999]], he won another La Liga title with Barcelona, and once again was the league's second highest scorer with 24 goals. In 1999, Rivaldo was named [[FIFA World Player of the Year]] and he also received the [[1999 Ballon d'Or|Ballon d'Or]]. After Barcelona's unsuccessful [[1998–99 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] campaign, Rivaldo was linked with a move away from the [[Camp Nou]]. Then [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] captain [[Roy Keane]] was reported stating Rivaldo was the player he most wanted United to sign.{{cite web|last=Webster|first=Rupert|title=RIVALDO WOULD ONLY MAKE REDS GREATER|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11667/2208114/rivaldo-would-only-make-reds-greater|publisher=Sky Sports}} {{Quote box | quote = At times around the turn of the century he was impossible to play against, and never more so than here. The quality of the goals was outstanding, but the context made his performance legendary. After just 18 months and 17 days, the book on the greatest hat-trick of the 21st century was already closed. | source = — Rob Smyth of ''The Guardian'' on Rivaldo's hat-trick against Valencia in June 2001. | align = left | quoted = 1 | width = 27% }} In his [[1999–2000 La Liga|third season]] at Barcelona, Rivaldo fell out with manager [[Louis van Gaal]], when he insisted playing as a playmaker rather than on the left wing.[http://www.4thegame.com/wanadoo/news/story/70237/RIVALDO+NOT+A+HAPPY+NOU+CAMP-ER.html Rivaldo Not a Happy Nou Camp-er] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090207190347/http://www.4thegame.com/wanadoo/news/story/70237/RIVALDO+NOT+A+HAPPY+NOU+CAMP-ER.html |date=7 February 2009 }}, ''4thegame'', 22 December 1999 Even though he had a strained relationship with Van Gaal, Rivaldo went on to score 10 goals in the season's [[1999–2000 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] as the club reached the semi-finals. Van Gaal was fired in June 2000. In the following [[2000–01 La Liga|2000–01 season]], Rivaldo was once again the second highest goalscorer of the league, with 23 goals. In the decisive last game of the season, against [[2000–01 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] finalist [[Valencia CF|Valencia]], Rivaldo scored a [[Hat-trick#Association football|hat-trick]] to win the game 3–2, pushing Barcelona ahead of Valencia to secure a place in the [[2001–02 UEFA Champions League|2001–02 Champions League]]. Frequently ranked the greatest hat-trick ever,{{cite news |title=Ranked! The 15 best hat-tricks of all-time: starring Bale, Berba, Bergkamp and more |work=FourFourTwo |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/ranked-15-best-hat-tricks-all-time-starring-bale-berba-bergkamp-and-more?page=0%2C2 |access-date=14 October 2018 |quote=A predictable winner? Perhaps. But everything about Rivaldo's hat-trick against Valencia on 17 June 2001 beggared belief}} his first goal was a trademark [[Curl (football)|bending]] free kick that curled into the bottom right corner,{{cite news |title=The Joy of Six: classiest hat-tricks |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2007/sep/11/newsstory.sport9 |access-date=22 August 2014 |work=The Guardian|quote=(1) Rivaldo, Barcelona 3-2 Valencia, La Liga, 17 June 2001}} the second saw him send the Valencia player the wrong way with a [[Dummy (football)#Association football|feint]] before a strike with little back-lift from 25 yards swerved into the bottom left corner of the net,{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2002/jun/30/worldcupfootball2002.sport3|title=A star less bright|work=[[The Observer]]|date=30 June 2002}} and his match-winning third occurred after Rivaldo controlled the ball with the chest from the edge of the [[Penalty area|18-yard box]] and executed an overhead [[bicycle kick]] in the 89th minute, which he regards as the best goal of his career. An ecstatic Rivaldo ripped off his jersey and started swinging it over his head during his [[goal celebration]]s, while Barcelona club president [[Joan Gaspart]] broke with convention in the stadium's VIP box by punching the air with both fists and yelling his delight next to the opposition delegation.{{cite news |title=Rivaldo: Great Goals Retold |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/rivaldo-great-goals-retold |access-date=14 October 2018 |work=FourFourTwo}} After the game Rivaldo stated; "What happened tonight has been incredible. I dedicate the winning goal to all the players who have fought so hard all season and all the supporters who have suffered so much. I'm delighted to have made them happy with my goals."{{cite magazine|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/soccer/news/2001/06/18/barcelona_rivaldo_ap/|title=Rivaldo hat-trick wins all the plaudits|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=18 June 2001|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20010626224249/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/soccer/news/2001/06/18/barcelona_rivaldo_ap/|archive-date=26 June 2001}} He scored a total of 36 goals that season.[https://gentlemanultra.com/2018/05/01/false-dawns-and-quiet-frustration-the-story-of-rivaldo-at-ac-milan/ “False dawns and quiet frustration: The story of Rivaldo at AC Milan”]. gentlemanultra.com. Milan]] in 2002. With Milan, he won the [[2002–03 Coppa Italia|Coppa Italia]] and the [[2002–03 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] in the [[2002–03 A.C. Milan season|2002–03 season]]. In August 2003, he also won the [[2003 UEFA Super Cup|UEFA Super Cup]] before cancelling his contract with Milan in November that year. After leaving Milan, he briefly returned to Brazil, playing for [[Cruzeiro EC|Cruzeiro]] in [[Belo Horizonte]].
