It was my decision because I consider Luxemburgo to be a special person." ===Olympiacos=== On 22 July 2004, Rivaldo joined [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] of [[Super League Greece]]. During the 2004–05 season he scored some stand out goals, one of them coming in his first derby against Panathinaikos that arguably turned out to be his most famous in an Olympiacos shirt: a bending [[Direct free kick|free kick]] to send Olympiacos to victory over their eternal rivals. Another notable goal by Rivaldo came the following week in Olympiacos's matchday 6 [[UEFA Champions League]] group game in England against eventual champions [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] where he scored a deft free-kick in front of the [[Spion Kop (stadiums)|Kop]] and put the Greek giants ahead. However Olympiacos were eliminated after Liverpool talisman [[Steven Gerrard]] scored with a 25-yard half volley 3 minutes from full-time.[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/4068163.stm "Liverpool 3-1 Olympiacos"]. BBC. Retrieved 8 June 2014 In the last game of Rivaldo's first season at Olympiacos, the club needed a victory in order to win the Alpha Ethniki championship, with Panathinaikos just one point behind. Olympiacos went on to beat [[Iraklis F.C. (Thessaloniki)|Iraklis]] 0–1 in an away match in [[Thessaloniki]], thanks to Rivaldo's goal, and secured the championship. Rivaldo renewed his contract with Olympiacos for a third year, despite now being 34 years old. In July 2006, Rivaldo announced that the [[2006–07 in Greek football|2006–07 season]] with Olympiacos would be his last in Europe, before returning to Brazil.[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/5189506.stm Rivaldo to quit at end of season], [[BBC]], 17 July 2006 However, he quickly changed his decision and decided to stay for another year. The 2006–2007 season saw him score 17 goals in 27 Super League matches. Rivaldo scored 43 goals in 81 games for Olympiacos. ===AEK Athens=== Rivaldo was released by Olympiacos after a dispute with the chairman of the club, [[Sokratis Kokkalis]], who had differences about the contract[https://www.sport24.gr/sthles/21-7-2004-o-rivalnto-stin-ellada-gia-ton-olimpiako/]. Later that summer, he signed for Super League club [[AEK Athens F.C.|AEK Athens]] on 29 May 2007. His first [[2007–08 Super League Greece|Super League]] goal with the [[Athens]]' club came through a penalty in their 3–0 win against [[Panionios F.C.|Panionios]]. Rivaldo had another great season and the team. After the winning match against Olympiacos with 4–0, Rivaldo showed his four fingers to the camera. Rivaldo had stated his intention to leave Greece if the ruling went in favour of Olympiakos and AEK Athens were not declared champions. He stated: "A team that was not good enough to win the title on the pitch does not deserve the trophy."{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/story/527822/road-clear-for-olympiakos-to-be-named-champions|title=Road clear for Olympiakos to be named champions|website=espnfc.com|access-date=18 May 2017}} ===Bunyodkor=== Rivaldo announced on 25 August 2008 to a Greek Sport Radio Station that he agreed to continue his career at [[FC Bunyodkor|Bunyodkor]] in Uzbekistan, effective immediately, after what he described as an "extremely tempting contract offer".[https://web.archive.org/web/20121024211828/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=566291&&cc=5739 Rivaldo quits AEK Athens to head to Uzbekistan], ''[[ESPNsoccernet]]'', 25 August 2008 Rivaldo signed a two-year contract worth €10.2 million and later signed an extension to extend the contract to 2011.{{cite news |last1=Slot |first1=Owen |title=World in motion: best rugby interviewees, Ronaldo's regime, cannabis and porn |url=https://www.thetimes.com/article/world-in-motion-best-rugby-interviewees-ronaldos-regime-cannabis-and-porn-2tnpz7bjpvt |work=[[Times Online]] |date=3 February 2009 |language=en}} On his debut for Bunyodkor, Rivaldo scored both goals in a 2–0 win.{{cite web |url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=571331&cc=4716 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024211833/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=571331&cc=4716 |url-status=dead |archive-date=24 October 2012 |title=Veteran Rivaldo nets brace on Bunyodkor debut |date=12 September 2008 |publisher=ESPN |access-date=11 August 2010}} In 2009, Rivaldo became the first player in the world to score one, then two, then three, then four goals in four consecutive matches. He scored one goal in the first match and two goals in the second match against Navbahor. In the third match on 25 June 2009, Rivaldo scored a hat trick in a 4–0 win against Metallurg.{{cite web |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/14/asia/2009/06/26/1347554/uzbekistan-rivaldo-treble-sees-bunyodkor-past-metallurg |title=Uzbekistan: Rivaldo Treble Sees Bunyodkor Past Metallurg |author=Mike Maguire |date=26 June 2009 |work=Goal.com}} In the fourth match, Bunyodkor beat Sogdiana Jizzakh 5–0 and Rivaldo scored four in 17 minutes. After the end of the 2009 season, Rivaldo won [[Uzbekistan Football Federation|UFF]] Topscorer award, having scored 20 league goals, and was runner up for UFF Player of the Year award. He scored 33 goals for the club in total. Rivaldo announced on 11 August 2010 on Twitter that he had cancelled his contract with Bunyodkor.{{cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=1284627.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100815220839/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=1284627.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=15 August 2010 |title=Rivaldo open to European move |date=12 August 2010 |publisher=FIFA}} ===Return to Mogi Mirim=== On 18 November 2010, he announced he would be returning to [[Mogi Mirim Esporte Clube|Mogi Mirim]], the club that he had started his career in the early 1990s, through his Social Networking site, saying: "After sorting out a lot of things outside of the country, I have decided to play the Paulista 2011 for Mogi Mirim, of whom I am President." However, he joined [[São Paulo FC|São Paulo]] in January 2011. ===São Paulo=== On 23 January 2011, Rivaldo joined São Paulo. He scored on his debut for them in the [[Campeonato Paulista|First Division]] against [[Clube Atlético Linense|Linense]] with a wonderful goal. The ball was sent over from the left hand side of the pitch, before Rivaldo controlled the ball and took it over a defender using his left knee, and finished at the near post. He spent most part of March 2011 tending injury, but came back for following fixtures such as a 1–1 draw with Palmeiras and a 2–1 win over Corinthians. Rivaldo stated on his Twitter account that he would leave São Paulo by the end of the season: "I just want to inform everybody that on Saturday, it's going to be my last training session at São Paulo. I've been told by the club's official that this is going to be my last season here." He added: "I'm not saying goodbye to football yet. I still have a lot to accomplish. I just wish I could hang up my boots at the end of 2012."{{cite news | title=Rivaldo to leave Sao Paulo | work=jazeerasport: Rivaldo to leave Sao Paulo | url=http://www.aljazeerasport.net/news/football/2011/12/201112294254116157.html | date=2 December 2011}} ===Kabuscorp=== Rivaldo joined Angolan club [[Kabuscorp S.C.|Kabuscorp]] in January 2012. On 18 March, Rivaldo scored a hat-trick against Recreativo Caala. Rivaldo left Kabuscorp in November 2012 after the expiration of his contract.{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20209381|title=Rivaldo leaves Angola's Kabuscorp|work=BBC Sport }} ===São Caetano=== In January 2013, Rivaldo joined [[Associação Desportiva São Caetano|São Caetano]] of Brazil's [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série B|Serie B]], signing a deal that ran to December.{{cite web |title=Aos 40 anos, pentacampeão Rivaldo é o novo reforço do São Caetano |url=http://br.esporteinterativo.yahoo.com/noticias/pentacampe%C3%A3o-rivaldo-%C3%A9-novo-refor%C3%A7o-s%C3%A3o-caetano-201358887--spt.html |access-date=18 May 2017 |website=yahoo.com |archive-date=5 December 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131205110601/http://br.esporteinterativo.yahoo.com/noticias/pentacampe%c3%a3o-rivaldo-%c3%a9-novo-refor%c3%a7o-s%c3%a3o-caetano-201358887--spt.html |url-status=dead }} He scored his first goal for his new club in his debut against [[Sport Club Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]] on 9 February. During the following match against [[Clube Atlético Bragantino|Bragantino]] Rivaldo once again scored, although his team lost 2–1. In November 2013, he left the club due to knee problems.{{cite web |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/sport/news/article.cfm?c_id=4&objectid=11153705 |title=Veteran Rivaldo leaves 2nd-division club in Brazil |agency=Associated Press |date=8 November 2013 }} === Second return to Mogi Mirim === In December 2013, Rivaldo joined [[Mogi Mirim Esporte Clube|Mogi Mirim]], signing a deal that ran until 2015. His son [[Rivaldinho]] played for the club.{{cite web|url=http://www.sambafoot.com/en/news/55009_rivaldo_signs_contract_with_mogi_until_2015_and_may_play_in_the_sao_paulo_state_championship.html|title=Rivaldo signs contract with Mogi until 2015 and may play in the São Paulo State Championship - Sambafoot.com, all About Brazilian Football|website=www.sambafoot.com|date=19 December 2013|access-date=18 May 2017}} Rivaldo had only made one league appearance for the club when he retired in July 2015.{{Cite news|url=http://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/dec/03/rivaldo-investors-mogi-mirim-brazil|title=Rivaldo appeals for new investors to fund his club in Brazil|date=3 December 2014|work=The Guardian}} ===Retirement=== In March 2014, the Brazilian icon officially retired from football after a career which spanned more than 20 years, and he decided to remain as the president of Mogi Mirim to help run the club and to look after his son, [[Rivaldinho]].[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/26603223 "Barcelona, AC Milan and Brazil legend Rivaldo retires aged 41"]. BBC. Retrieved 17 March 2014 In a released statement, Rivaldo commented: "My history as a player has come to the end. With tears in my eyes today I would like to thank God, my family and all the support, the affection that I received during those 24 years as a player." However, he returned to the team in June 2015. On 14 July 2015, Rivaldo and [[Rivaldinho]] scored goals in the same match for the first time as Mogi Mirim beat [[Macaé Esporte Futebol Clube|Macaé]] 3–1.{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33535435|title=Rivaldo: World Cup winner and son score in same Brazilian match|date=15 July 2015|publisher=BBC Sport}} On 18 January 2019, [[SCC Mohammédia]] announced Rivaldo as their new technical director and coach for the following season.{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46919411|title=Rivaldo denies joining staff at Moroccan club|work=BBC Sport }} The player denied that a deal was made, as he signed a pre-contract in which the club must achieve promotion from [[Amateur National Championship (Moroccan football)|National]] (third tier in the Moroccan league).{{Cite web|url=https://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/futebol-internacional/noticia/rivaldo-e-anunciado-por-time-da-terceira-divisao-de-marrocos.ghtml|title=Rivaldo é anunciado por time da terceira divisão de Marrocos, mas não aceita convite|website=ge|date=17 January 2019 }} ==International career== In 1993, he debuted for the [[Brazil national football team]], scoring the only goal in a [[friendly match]] against [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]].{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/rivaldo-intlg.html|title=Rivaldo Vitor Borba Ferreira – Goals in International Matches|website=[[RSSSF]]|access-date=18 May 2017}} He was selected to represent Brazil at the [[1996 Summer Olympics]]. The Brazilian team won the [[bronze medal]], but Rivaldo was not selected for the third place playoff. Rivaldo returned to the Brazil national team for the [[1998 FIFA World Cup]], where he scored three goals en route to the final, including two in the 3–2 quarter-final win against [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]].{{cite news |last1=Longman |first1=Jere |title=WORLD CUP '98; Redemption for Brazil Over Fearless Denmark |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/07/04/sports/world-cup-98-redemption-for-brazil-over-fearless-denmark.html |access-date=24 July 2025 |work=The New York Times |date=4 July 1998}} Brazil were defeated 3–0 by hosts [[France national football team|France]] in final, failing to defend their 1994 title. Rivaldo had not been a part of the victorious Brazilian team at the [[1997 Copa América|1997 Copa América tournament]], but was part of the successful defence of that title at the [[1999 Copa América]]. Rivaldo finished the tournament as the top scorer, with five goals; one being an equaliser from a free-kick in a 2–1 win over [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] in the quarter-finals, and two in the 3–0 victory over [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]] in the final. He was named the [[Most Valuable Player]] of the tournament.{{cite web|last=Smyth|first=Rob|title=On Second Thoughts: Rivaldo|website=[[TheGuardian.com]]|date=19 June 2008|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2008/jun/19/barcelona.brazil|access-date=25 September 2013}} Rivaldo had been the centre of criticism when Brazil did not win tournaments, ever since the 1996 Olympics.Rodrigo Amaral, [https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport3/worldcup2002/hi/matches_wallchart/england_v_brazil/newsid_2056000/2056726.stm Rivaldo reflects on wheel of fortune], [[BBC]], 20 June 2002 In the 1–0 win against [[Colombia national football team|Colombia]] in November 2000, Rivaldo was booed so heavily that he threatened to retire from playing for his country.[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/1031130.stm Brazil questions Rivaldo's role], [[BBC]], 19 November 2000 {{Quote box|It was a great joy and honour to play alongside [[Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)|Ronaldo]] and [[Ronaldinho]] in the [[2002 FIFA World Cup|2002 World Cup]]. Our teamwork was great and it showed through the results. | source = — Rivaldo on the "three R's".[https://web.archive.org/web/20140715171206/http://www.uefa.com/news/newsid=395064.html "Rivaldo dreams of Germany"]. UEFA.com. Retrieved 21 November 2013 | align = left | quoted = 1 | width = 32% }} The zenith and nadir of Rivaldo's national team career came at the [[2002 FIFA World Cup]], hosted in South Korea and Japan, where he was able to erase the disappointment of the previous World Cup Final defeat, helping Brazil win their fifth World Cup. Featuring in an attacking trio with [[Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)|Ronaldo]] and [[Ronaldinho]], dubbed "the three R's", Rivaldo scored in the first five games while Ronaldo scored in four matches.[https://web.archive.org/web/20090322051546/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/statisticsandrecords/players/player%3D170691/ "FIFA Player Statistics: Rivaldo"]. FIFA.com. Retrieved 8 July 2014{{cite news |last1=Lawrence |first1=Amy |title=Ronaldo's redemption: recalling the Brazil striker's World Cup fairytale 15 years on |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/jun/29/ronaldo-brazil-world-cup-final-2002-japan |date=29 June 2017|work=The Guardian}} Despite a successful tournament, Rivaldo was involved in a controversial incident against [[Turkey national football team|Turkey]].[https://www.theguardian.com/football/2002/jun/04/worldcupfootball2002.sport16 Scolari: Rivaldo did not cheat] ''[[The Guardian]]'' 4 June 2002 Near the end of the match, with the ball out of play, Turkish defender [[Hakan Ünsal]] kicked a ball towards Rivaldo, who was waiting at the corner flag. The ball struck his thigh, but Rivaldo fell to the ground clutching his face.{{cite web |title=Rivaldo acting fail - World Cup 2002 Oscar winning performance |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OiW0IPrv1Ro | archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211103/OiW0IPrv1Ro| archive-date=3 November 2021 | url-status=live|website=YouTube | date=5 September 2011 |publisher=Dunkmaster3333 |access-date=28 April 2021}}{{cbignore}} The referee sent the Turkish player off with a second yellow card. After a video review, Rivaldo was fined 11,670 [[Swiss franc]]s by FIFA. {{Quote box|On the eve of the final, Ronaldo, Rivaldo and Ronaldinho warmed up in the Yokohama Stadium by merrily trying to out-wizard each other in the Japanese drizzle. | source = — Amy Lawrence of ''The Guardian'' on the bond of the "three Rs". | align = right | quoted = 1 | width = 28% }} Rivaldo's goal against [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]] in the second round prompted Belgian coach [[Robert Waseige]] to name him as the deciding factor.John Chapman, [https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport3/worldcup2002/hi/matches_wallchart/brazil_v_belgium/newsid_2048000/2048030.stm Wilmots tells of ref's apology], [[BBC]], 17 June 2002 Ronaldinho assisted Rivaldo to score the equaliser against [[England national football team|England]] in the quarter-finals before Ronaldinho scored the winning goal in a 2–1 victory.[https://web.archive.org/web/20021015110726/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/soccer/world/2002/world_cup/news/2002/06/20/brazil_england_gamer/ "English dream over"], 'CNN Sports Illustrated. June 2002 Brazil met [[Germany national football team|Germany]] in the final, and went on to win the tournament with a 2–0 victory, courtesy of two goals by Ronaldo with Rivaldo involved in both goals. The first came after Rivaldo's shot was saved by German goalkeeper [[Oliver Kahn]] with Ronaldo scoring the rebound, and the second saw Rivaldo fool the German defence with a [[Dummy (football)|dummy]] as the ball ran on to Ronaldo who finished.[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport3/worldcup2002/hi/matches_wallchart/germany_v_brazil/newsid_2067000/2067939.stm "Brazil crowned world champions"]. BBC. Retrieved 8 June 2014 Rivaldo was named by Brazil coach [[Luiz Felipe Scolari]] as the best player of the tournament.[http://www.espnfc.com/story/253464/scolari-rivaldo-was-world-cups-best "Scolari: Rivaldo was World Cup's best"]. ESPN. Retrieved 8 July 2014 Rivaldo along with Ronaldo and Ronaldinho were named in the [[FIFA World Cup All-Star Team]].[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport3/worldcup2002/hi/other_news/newsid_2071000/2071344.stm "Campbell makes All-Star team"]. BBC Sport. Retrieved 21 November 2013 Rivaldo's last cap was on 19 November 2003 in [[Curitiba]] in a 3–3 draw with [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]]. He played 79 minutes before being substituted for [[Luís Fabiano]]. He had scored his last goal just three days earlier from the penalty spot in a 1–1 draw with [[Peru national football team|Peru]]. In his time with the national side, Rivaldo won 74 caps, and scored 35 goals.{{cite web |title=Rivaldo Vitor Borba Ferreira - Goals in International Matches |url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/rivaldo-intlg.html |website=RSSSF |access-date=2 January 2019}} ==Style of play== Regarded as one of the best players of his generation,{{cite encyclopedia|url=http://www.britannica.com/biography/Rivaldo|title=Rivaldo|encyclopedia=Encyclopædia Britannica|access-date=5 January 2016}} Rivaldo was praised for his [[Dribbling#Association football|dribbling]] ability, use of [[Dummy (football)#Association football|feints]], balance, and close ball control.{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/club/history/detail/card/vitor-borba-ferreira-rivaldo|title=Vitor Borba Ferreira 'RIVALDO'|publisher=FC Barcelona.com|access-date=5 January 2016|archive-date=22 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160322065857/http://www.fcbarcelona.com/club/history/detail/card/vitor-borba-ferreira-rivaldo|url-status=dead}} Despite his height, he was also thought to be extremely agile.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/core/world-cup/story/_/page/worldcup101-05142010/ce/us/ruud-gull-all-time-no-10s |title=Perfect 10s |publisher=ESPN FC |last1=Gullit |first1=Ruud |date=14 May 2010 }} A dead-ball specialist, Rivaldo was lauded for his [[Curl (football)|bending]] [[Direct free kick|free kicks]] and [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty]] taking, as well as his ability to score from distance. Left footed and considered highly creative, he was also known for his ball striking from volleys, and for scoring from [[bicycle kick]]s. {{Blockquote|Apart from a right foot, Rivaldo had everything. His wiry strength allowed him to bounce off defenders, he was an outstanding dribbler, and he had a left foot that was both educated and thuggish, subtle and a sledgehammer. Brazil's bandy-legged genius was the most unstoppable footballer since [[Diego Maradona|Maradona]].|Rob Smyth writing for ''[[The Guardian]]'' on Rivaldo's style of play in 2008.}} Although he was not an out-and-out striker, Rivaldo was a prolific goalscorer who could play in several attacking roles, most notably as a [[Winger (association football)|left winger]] or an [[attacking midfielder]]. During his first two seasons at Barcelona under [[Louis van Gaal]], and throughout much of the period that culminated in his 1999 [[Ballon d'Or]] and [[FIFA World Player of the Year]] awards, he was generally deployed on the left side of a 4–1–2–3 formation, from where he frequently cut infield, rather than operating centrally as a [[Squad number (association football)|classic number 10]].{{cite news |last=Liew |first=Jonathan |date=15 August 2014 |title=The Van Gaal Dossier |url=https://s.telegraph.co.uk/graphics/projects/the-van-gaal-dossier/index.html |work=The Daily Telegraph |access-date=16 June 2026}}{{cite news |last=Kuper |first=Simon |date=30 January 2000 |title=Poor boy who became a legend |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2000/jan/30/sport.comment2 |work=The Guardian |access-date=16 June 2026}} Despite his success in this role, Rivaldo considered the centre to be his best position and sought to play there as a number 10. Following a dispute with Van Gaal over his positioning during the 1999–2000 season, he agreed to return to the left wing, although he was subsequently also used centrally at times.{{cite web |last=Baynes |first=Ciaran |title=Rivaldo agrees to play on left |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/2178156/rivaldo-agrees-to-play-on-left |website=Sky Sports |access-date=16 June 2026}} At international level, his role varied according to Brazil's tactical system. At the 1998 FIFA World Cup, he operated as the right-sided attacking midfielder in [[Mário Zagallo]]'s 4–2–2–2 formation, drifting into central areas and cutting inside onto his stronger left foot.{{cite web |title=Mário Zagallo: The Tactical Masters |url=https://learning.coachesvoice.com/cv/mario-zagallo-brazil-tactics-pele-ronaldo-world-cup/ |website=The Coaches' Voice |date=21 December 2021 |access-date=16 June 2026}} At the [[2002 FIFA World Cup]], he played in a more advanced role alongside [[Ronaldinho]] behind [[Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)|Ronaldo]] in [[Luiz Felipe Scolari]]'s 3–4–2–1 formation.{{cite news |date=1 July 2002 |title=Ronaldo squares the rocky cycle for Brazil |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2002/jul/01/worldcupfootball2002.sport |work=The Guardian |access-date=16 June 2026}} Predominantly left-footed, he was noted for his dribbling and his ability to contribute both goals and [[Assist (association football)|assists]] while operating from the left. In 2002, John Carlin of ''The Guardian'' noted that Rivaldo "combines to dazzling effect the two essential qualities of the ideal footballer: artistry and efficiency". His colleague, Rob Smyth, echoed his views in 2008, commenting: "if you could marry British will with continental skill, you would have the perfect footballer. Such a mixed recipe was thrillingly in evidence in Diego Maradona. Since then, however, perhaps only Rivaldo has fused the two qualities", noting that like the Argentinian, the Brazilian had "bronca" (the word used repeatedly in Maradona's autobiography to refer to "anger, fury, hatred, resentment, bitter discontent"). Former Dutch international [[Ruud Gullit]] believed that Rivaldo's ability and qualities were often overlooked, as "he played in the same era as Brazilian counterparts Ronaldo and Ronaldinho." == Personal life == Rivaldo is a devout [[Evangelicalism|Evangelical Christian]].{{Cite web |last=Wasim |first=Umaid |date=2012-10-17 |title=Rivaldo's ‘call from God’ |url=https://www.dawn.com/2012/10/17/rivaldos-call-from-god/ |access-date=2026-07-17 |website=Dawn |language=en}} His son [[Rivaldinho]] is also a professional footballer, who currently plays for [[Thai League]] club [[Bangkok United]].{{cite web|url=https://m.dongqiudi.com/article/5082793.html|title=里瓦尔多：我认为中超和中甲差距不大，我儿子有能力踢中超|trans-title=Rivaldo: My son is capable of playing in the top division|date=8 May 2025|website=Dongqiudi}} Rivaldo supported [[Jair Bolsonaro]] for the [[2018 Brazilian general election]].[https://www.dw.com/en/why-bolsonaro-supporters-wear-brazils-football-shirt/a-64335033#:~:text=%22About%20four%20years%20ago%2C%20it,the%20end%20of%20October%202022. '''Thiago Emiliano da Silva''' ({{IPA|pt-BR|tʃiˈaɡu ˈsiwvɐ|lang}}; born 22 September 1984) is a Brazilian professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[centre-back]] for [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A]] club [[Fluminense FC|Fluminense]]. Regarded as one of the best defenders of his generation, Silva is known for his defensive ability, discipline, and leadership.<ref>Multiple sources:

*{{cite web |title=Thiago Silva Eternal: The “Monster” Conquers Europe at 41 |url=https://www.beinsports.com/en-us/soccer/primeira-liga/articles/thiago-silva-eternal-the-monster-conquers-europe-at-41-2026-05-03 |publisher=beIN SPORTS |access-date=6 May 2026 |language=en-us |date=3 May 2026}}
*{{cite web |date=16 April 2022 |title=Top 10 Best Defenders in the World 2022 |url=https://www.notice.com.ng/lifestyle/top-10-best-defenders-in-the-world-2022 |access-date=26 July 2022 |website=Notice }}</ref> In addition, he is also one of a select number of players who have [[List of men's footballers with 1,000 or more official appearances|amassed over 1,000 career appearances]].

Silva began his senior club career in 2002 playing as a midfielder for [[Pedrabranca Futebol Clube|RS Futebol]], and transitioned to a defensive position while at [[Esporte Clube Juventude|Juventude]]; he then signed with [[FC Porto B|Porto]] in 2004, at age 19, and moved to [[FC Dynamo Moscow|Dynamo Moscow]] on [[Loan (sports)|loan]], where he was hospitalized with a near fatal bout of [[tuberculosis]]. After recovering, he joined Fluminense and won a [[Copa do Brasil]] in [[2007 Copa do Brasil|2007]]. In 2009, Silva moved to Italian side [[AC Milan|Milan]] for a reported fee of €8 million and won the [[2010–11 Serie A]] title with the latter.

In 2012, Silva was the subject of a then-[[List of most expensive association football transfers|record football deal]] when he signed for [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] in a [[Transfer (association football)|transfer]] worth up to €42 million, becoming the most expensive defender ever at the time. There, he would become the club's [[List of Paris Saint-Germain FC records and statistics#Captains|longest serving]] [[Captain (association football)|captain]], winning seven [[List of French football champions|Ligue 1]] titles, six [[Coupe de la Ligue|Coupes de la Ligue]], five [[Coupe de France|Coupes de France]], and playing in the [[2020 UEFA Champions League final|final]] of the [[UEFA Champions League]], which served as his last PSG appearance. He currently ranks [[List of Paris Saint-Germain FC records and statistics#All-time most appearances|eighth in all-time appearances]] for the club. In 2020, the 36-year-old Silva joined Chelsea on a [[Free transfer (association football)|free transfer]], [[2021 UEFA Champions League final|winning the Champions League]] in his first season, and both the [[2021 UEFA Super Cup|UEFA Super Cup]] and [[2021 FIFA Club World Cup|FIFA Club World Cup]] in his second.

Silva made his senior international debut for [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] in 2008 at age 23, and has since received over 110 caps, including appearances in eight major tournaments. He earned a bronze medal at the [[Football at the Summer Olympics|Summer Olympics]] in [[Football at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008]] and a silver in [[Football at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012]], before serving as captain for Brazil on home soil as they won the [[2013 FIFA Confederations Cup]] and finished fourth at the [[2014 FIFA World Cup]]. Silva was also a member of the team that won the [[Copa América]] in [[2019 Copa América|2019]] and finished runners-up in [[2021 Copa América|2021]]. He has not been called up to the Brazilian national football team since December 2022, but has not officially announced his retirement.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.90min.com/posts/thiago-silva-provides-update-brazil-future|title=Thiago Silva provides update on his Brazil future|last=Gallagher|first=Jack|date=26 October 2023|work=90Min}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Early career===
When he was younger, Silva was admitted into a school in the [[Campo Grande, Rio de Janeiro|Campo Grande]] neighborhood of [[Rio de Janeiro|Rio]] – coincidentally a feeder school for [[Fluminense Football Club|Fluminense]]. At the age of 14, Silva impressed Fluminense coach Maurinho during a friendly in [[Xerém]]. He was given a short trial, where he was given the role of a [[Midfielder#Defensive midfielder|defensive midfielder]]. Silva's playing opportunities were few, prompting him to trial for other clubs. In 1999, at the age of 15, Silva auditioned at [[Madureira Esporte Clube|Madureira]], [[Olaria Esporte Clube|Olaria]], and [[Clube de Regatas do Flamengo|Flamengo]]; he was rejected at each club, the trial at Flamengo being the most difficult for him as he was not even observed by coaches.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.noticiasfla.com.br/2013/05/thiago-silva-revela-nao-aprovado-flamengo-botafogo.html|title=Thiago Silva revela nao ter sido aprovado no Flamengo e Botafogo|date=31 May 2013|access-date=21 June 2014|archive-date=14 July 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714124150/http://www.noticiasfla.com.br/2013/05/thiago-silva-revela-nao-aprovado-flamengo-botafogo.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

After another unsuccessful trial at [[Botafogo de Futebol e Regatas|Botafogo]], Silva was taken on by his hometown side [[Barcelona Esporte Clube|Barcelona]], a small Brazilian club in the lower divisions. The following year, Silva played at a showcase tournament in [[São Paulo]] in the hope of attracting the attention of bigger clubs. It is there where he was spotted by [[Paulo César Carpegiani]], who invited him to join [[Pedrabranca Futebol Clube|RS Futebol]] in the south of Brazil. Joining the club in the end of 2001, Silva became a professional in 2002 and competed in the [[Campeonato Gaúcho Série B|third division of the Campeonato Gaúcho]], finishing second and achieving promotion to the state's [[Campeonato Gaúcho Série A2|second division]]. In a tournament played in [[Ancona]], Italy, Silva was spotted by [[Bruno Conti]], a coach with [[A.S. Roma|Roma]]. Conti wanted him to play for Roma, but Silva did not accept the offer.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.pariskop.fr/actualite/thiago-silva-lhistoire-dun-genie/8825|title=Thiago Silva : L'Histoire d'un génie|date=1 November 2013|access-date=21 June 2014}}</ref> Strong performances in his last season as a defensive midfielder led to Silva's move to [[Esporte Clube Juventude|Juventude]].<ref name="globoesporte.globo.com">{{cite news|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/programas/esporte-espetacular/noticia/2013/06/origens-thiago-silva-abre-o-jogo-e-se-emociona-ao-lembrar-das-dificuldades.html|title=Origens: Thiago Silva abre o jogo e se emociona ao lembrar das dificuldades|date=2 June 2013|access-date=21 June 2014}}</ref>

Silva moved to Juventude in 2004, where he played for six months. At 20 years old, Silva transitioned from midfield to defence under the tutelage of [[Ivo Wortmann]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://esporte.hsw.uol.com.br/jogador-thiago-silva.htm|title=Jogadores de futebol – Thiago Silva|access-date=21 June 2014|archive-date=17 September 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160917200608/http://esporte.hsw.uol.com.br/jogador-thiago-silva.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> In his only season at Juventude, Silva was regarded as the revelation of the season. He was rated by the sports magazine ''[[Placar]]'' as the third-best defender in Brazil and was included in the team of the season.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.flumania.com.br/tsilva.htm|title=Thiago Silva|access-date=21 June 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091001142913/http://www.flumania.com.br/tsilva.htm|archive-date=1 October 2009}}</ref> Juventude had made a huge leap in league placement during Silva's time at the club – from finishing 18th with 53 points in [[2003 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|2003]], to finishing 7th with 70 points in [[2004 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|2004]]. Silva had caught the eye of many clubs with his outstanding performances, and he was sold to [[FC Porto|Porto]].

Silva was bought by Porto for €2.5 million in 2004,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.uefa.com/footballeurope/news/kind=2/newsid=272249.html |title=Derlei leads Dinamo influx |date=10 January 2005 |access-date=21 June 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090323001910/http://www.uefa.com/footballeurope/news/kind%3D2/newsid%3D272249.html |archive-date=23 March 2009 }}</ref> but played only for the reserve team. After a year in Portugal, he joined [[FC Dynamo Moscow|Dynamo Moscow]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.uefa.com/footballeurope/news/kind=2/newsid=272249.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090323001910/http://www.uefa.com/footballeurope/news/kind=2/newsid=272249.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=23 March 2009|title=Derlei leads Dinamo influx|date=1 October 2005|access-date=21 June 2014}}</ref> where he was diagnosed with [[tuberculosis]] and was hospitalised for six months.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.stoptb.org/news/stories/2014/ns14_041.asp|title=Thiago Silva: Brazil Captain and TB Survivor|date=13 June 2014|access-date=21 June 2014|archive-date=4 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180504011101/http://www.stoptb.org/news/stories/2014/ns14_041.asp|url-status=dead}}</ref> He is quoted as saying, "Every now and then a doctor would come in and give me an injection, three or four times a day, plus 10-15 pills."<ref name=":0" /> His illness became much worse over time and his doctors told him that if he had been hospitalized two weeks later, he could have died.<ref name=":0">{{cite news|url=http://www.football-italia.net/node/3126|title=Thiago Silva: 'I nearly died in Russia'|date=12 February 2011|access-date=21 June 2014|publisher=JDT Sport Productions}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=30 July 2019 |title=How Thiago Silva overcame tuberculosis and a year out to become one of the world's best defenders |url=https://thesefootballtimes.co/2019/07/31/how-thiago-silva-overcame-tuberculosis-and-a-year-out-to-become-one-of-the-worlds-best-defenders/ |access-date=4 March 2022 |website=These Football Times}}</ref> During his recovery, Silva decided to retire from football but was persuaded to reconsider by his mother.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2014/may/31/world-cup-2014-brazil-profile-thiago-silva|title=World Cup 2014: Brazil profile – Thiago Silva|last=Duarte|first=Fernando|date=21 June 2014|work=The Guardian}}</ref>

===Fluminense===
[[File:Thiago Silva - Fluminense - 2007.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Silva with [[Fluminense FC|Fluminense]] in 2007]]
Silva returned to football with the help of his former coach, Ivo Wortmann. In 2006, Wortmann was signed as a coach by Fluminense and requested to bring Silva with him, despite Silva's health issues.<ref name="globoesporte.globo.com"/> On 14 January, Fluminense announced the signing of Silva from Dynamo Moscow.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.flogao.com.br/siriflu/41331122|title=Fluminense anuncia contratação do zagueiro Thiago Silva|date=15 January 2006|access-date=21 June 2014|archive-date=31 May 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160531075659/http://www.flogao.com.br/siriflu/41331122|url-status=dead}}</ref> Fluminense struggled in the [[2006 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|2006 Brasileirão]], finishing 15th out of 20 teams; however, Silva was described as one of the best players in the season.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://esporte.uol.com.br/futebol/ultimas/2006/11/25/ult59u107805.jhtm|title= Torcedor do Flu, Thiago Silva já foi vascaíno|date=25 November 2006|access-date=21 June 2014}}</ref> It is during this time where Silva developed the nickname of "''O Monstro''" — Portuguese for "The Monster".<ref>{{cite news|url=http://sport24.lefigaro.fr/football/ligue-des-champions/actualites/thiago-silva-est-vraiment-un-monstre-625379|title= Thiago Silva est vraiment un "Monstre"|date=3 April 2013|access-date=21 June 2014}}</ref>

2007 was a much better year for both Fluminense and for Silva. The club finished in fourth place in the [[2007 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|2007 Brasileirão]], conceding only 39 goals in 38 matches, enough for the second-best defence in Brazil. More importantly, Fluminense managed a historic victory in the [[2007 Copa do Brasil]], winning the prestigious trophy for the first time. Silva played a decisive part in the victory; he started in every match, and scored the opening goal in the quarter-final, as well as the equalising goal in the semi-final.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.flumania.com.br/cpbrasil2007b.htm|title=Copa do Brasil 2007 – 2ª Parte|access-date=21 June 2014|archive-date=5 September 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080905181955/http://www.flumania.com.br/cpbrasil2007b.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> Silva's form through the season led him to be selected into [[Brazil national football team|Brazil national team]] manager [[Dunga]]'s preliminary squad for the [[2007 Copa América]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://esporte.uol.com.br/futebol/ultimas/2007/05/28/ult59u121784.jhtm|title=Dunga pré-convoca Zé Roberto e surpresas para Copa América|date=28 May 2007|access-date=21 June 2014}}</ref> After winning the Copa do Brasil, Silva was recognised by fans as the best defender in Brazil.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/ESP/Noticia/Futebol/Fluminense/0,,MUL48900-4284,00-CHORO+EUFORIA+E+REDENCAO+NAS+LARANJEIRAS.html|title=Choro, euforia e redenção nas Laranjeiras|date=7 June 2007|access-date=21 June 2014}}</ref> At the end of the season, he was one of three nominees for the Best Central Defender award, alongside [[Breno Borges|Breno]] and [[Fábio Luciano]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/ESP/Noticia/Futebol/Campeonatos/0,,MUL188549-4276,00-OS+FINALISTAS+DO+CRAQUE+BRASILEIRAO.html|title=Os finalistas do Craque Brasileirão 2007|date=22 November 2007|access-date=21 June 2014}}</ref> The voting results were unveiled on 4 December, where Silva finished second, behind Breno.<ref name="ReferenceA">{{cite news|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/ESP/Noticia/Futebol/Campeonatos/0,,MUL202192-4276,00-BRENO+E+O+MELHOR+ZAGUEIRO+PELA+DIREITA.html|title=Breno é o melhor zagueiro pela direita|date=4 December 2007|access-date=21 June 2014}}</ref>

{{Quote box|width=15%|align=right|quote="Silva is a phenomenon."|source=—[[Dunga]], 2008<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/Esportes/Noticias/Times/Selecao_Brasileira/0,,MUL934276-15071,00-DUNGA+NAO+MEDE+AS+PALAVRAS+PARA+ELOGIAR+THIAGO+SILVA+E+UM+FENOMENO.html|title=Globo.com - Desculpe-nos, ocorreu um erro.|website=Globoesporte.globo.com|access-date=15 June 2026}}</ref>}}

2008 was a bad year for Fluminense, but Silva's best on an individual level. Having devoted much of their efforts towards the [[2008 Copa Libertadores]], the club's league form suffered, finishing in 14th place. On 18 January, Silva was rewarded by Fluminense's board of directors for his 100th match in the ''tricolor'': He was awarded a shirt with the number "100" and a plaque in honour of his achievements.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://esporte.uol.com.br/futebol/ultimas/2008/01/19/ult59u143326.jhtm|title=Thiago Silva é homenageado pela diretoria do Fluminense|date=19 January 2008|access-date=21 June 2014}}</ref> Silva became an idol for young Fluminense supporters with his level of performances — the white wristband that Silva would wear during matches became a trend amongst teenagers in Rio de Janeiro who supported the ''tricolor''.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/ESP/Noticia/Futebol/Fluminense/0,,MUL265485-4284,00-THIAGOMANIA+O+ORGULHO+DO+CRAQUE+TRICOLOR.html|title=Thiagomania, o orgulho do craque tricolor|date=18 January 2008|access-date=21 June 2014}}</ref> In May 2008, four fans painted a flag of Silva to honour what they deemed "the best central defender in Brazil". It was first shown in the [[2008 Copa Libertadores knockout stages#Boca Juniors v Fluminense|Copa Libertadores semi-final]] against [[Boca Juniors]]<ref>{{cite news|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/Esportes/Noticias/Times/Fluminense/0,,MUL584830-9866,00-FOTO+TORCEDOR+FAZ+BANDEIRA+EM+HOMENAGEM+A+THIAGO+SILVA.html|title=Foto: Torcedor faz bandeira em homenagem a Thiago Silva|date=30 May 2008|access-date=21 June 2014}}</ref> — Silva scored a crucial equaliser in the same match.<ref name="ReferenceB">{{cite news|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/Esportes/Futebol/0,,CCF23542-9825,00.html|title=Riquelme faz dois, mas quem vibra com empate é o Tricolor|date=28 May 2008|access-date=21 June 2014}}</ref>

Silva was included in the [[Prêmio Craque do Brasileirão#2008|2008 Brasileirão Team of the Season]] and was selected as the Fans' Player of the Season.<ref name="Globo Esporte">{{cite web|work=Globo Esporte|title=Hexacampeão, São Paulo domina também o Prêmio Craque Brasileirão|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/Esportes/Noticias/Futebol/Brasileirao/Serie_A/0,,MUL915557-9827,00-HEXACAMPEAO+SAO+PAULO+DOMINA+TAMBEM+O+PREMIO+CRAQUE+BRASILEIRAO.html|access-date=21 June 2014}}</ref> Silva was widely regarded as one of Fluminense's most important performers in the [[2008 Copa Libertadores]],<ref name="ReferenceB"/><ref>{{cite news|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/Esportes/Futebol/0,,CCF23529-9825,00.html|title=Gol aos 46 do segundo tempo classifica o Fluminense para semifinal|date=21 May 2008|access-date=21 June 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/Esportes/Futebol/0,,CCF23543-9825,00.html|title=Fluminense vence o Boca Juniors e está na final da Taça Libertadores|date=4 June 2008|access-date=21 June 2014}}</ref> reaching the finals only to lose on penalties to [[LDU Quito]]. Silva's form for Fluminense earned him a call-up to the ''[[Brazil national under-23 football team|Seleção]]'' to take part in the [[2008 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/Esportes/Noticias/Times/Fluminense/0,,MUL775871-9866,00-THIAGO+SILVA+CELEBRA+SUA+MELHOR+FASE.html|title=Thiago Silva celebra sua melhor fase|date=27 September 2008|access-date=21 June 2014}}</ref> Silva was linked with many clubs in 2008, including the likes of [[Inter Milan]], [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] and [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]], though ultimately he opted to join the Brazilian contingent already at [[AC Milan|Milan]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/Esportes/Noticias/Times/Fluminense/0,,MUL919657-9866,00-THIAGO+SILVA+ACERTA+COM+O+MILAN+POR+QUATRO+ANOS.html|title=Thiago Silva acerta com o Milan por quatro anos|date=11 December 2008|access-date=21 June 2014}}</ref> The transfer was confirmed on 12 December.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.corriere.it/sport/08_dicembre_12/thiago_silva_milan_Colombo_4086770a-c81f-11dd-a869-00144f02aabc.shtml |work=Corriere della Sera |language=it |title=Thiago Silva è del barcelona È lui l'erede di Maldini |date=12 December 2008 |access-date=21 June 2014}}</ref> In his final match for Fluminense, Silva was cheered by {{gaps|50|000}} supporters who were witnessing his last performance at the [[Estádio do Maracanã|Maracanã]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/Esportes/Noticias/Futebol/Brasileirao/Serie_A/0,,MUL915340-9827,00-CRAQUE+BRASILEIRAO+THIAGO+SILVA+E+O+ZAGUEIRO+DIREITO+DA+COMPETICAO.html|title=Craque Brasileirão 2008: Thiago Silva é o zagueiro direito da competição|date=8 December 2008|access-date=21 June 2014}}</ref>

===Milan===
After a five-month rundown and a confusing four-hour negotiation period, Silva agreed to a move to Milan for a €10 million fee, with net wages of €2.5 million on a four-year contract.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2008/dicembre/12/Thiago_Silva_Subito_Milan_ga_10_081212048.shtml|title=Sì di Thiago Silva Subito al Milan|date=12 December 2008|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> Although Silva could not play competitive matches, he was able to train with the first team. In his first month at Milan, he was taught new defending techniques from [[Paolo Maldini]] and manager [[Carlo Ancelotti]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/Esportes/Noticias/Futebol/italiano/0,,MUL964232-9848,00-THIAGO+SILVA+FALA+SOBRE+A+NOVA+VIDA+NO+MILAN+JA+ME+SINTO+EM+CASA.html|title=Thiago Silva fala sobre a nova vida no Milan: 'Já me sinto em casa'|date=20 January 2009|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> Silva played his first match for the ''Rossoneri'' in a friendly match against [[Hannover 96]] on 21 January 2009; he played well, making ten tackles. His performance drew praise from Milan executive [[Adriano Galliani]] and teammate [[Clarence Seedorf]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/Esportes/Noticias/Futebol/0,,MUL967555-9842,00-THIAGO+SILVA+EMPOLGA+SEEDORF+E+ASSOMBRA+DIRIGENTE+DO+MILAN.html|title=Thiago Silva empolga Seedorf e 'assombra' dirigente do Milan|date=22 January 2009|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> Silva was officially registered as a Milan player for the [[2009–10 A.C. Milan season|2009–10 season]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2009/luglio/07/tabellone_delle_squadre_serie_A_ga_10_090707022.shtml|title=Il tabellone delle 20 squadre di serie A|date=7 July 2009|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref>

====2009–10: Debut season====
[[File:Thiago Silva by Figiu.jpg|thumb|left|upright|120px|Silva warming up for [[AC Milan|Milan]] in May 2010]]
Silva played his first competitive match of the season against [[A.C. Siena|Siena]] on 22 August 2009. After the match, he was praised for a strong individual performance alongside teammate [[Alessandro Nesta]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2009/agosto/23/PAGELLE_ga_10_090823003.shtml|title=Le Pagelle|date=23 August 2009|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> Milan legend Paolo Maldini claimed that Silva had the "physical and technical characteristics of a champion",<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2009/agosto/25/Maldini_Milan_credici__ga_10_090825047.shtml|title=Maldini "Milan, credici"|date=25 August 2009|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> while Nesta said that Silva would "extend my life as a central defender".<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2009/agosto/26/Elisir_Nesta_Thiago_allunga_vita_ga_10_090826016.shtml|title=Elisir Nesta: "Thiago mi allunga la vita"|date=26 August 2009|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> On 23 September, Silva left training with a muscle strain; he was inactive for the next four matches.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2009/settembre/23/Stop_per_Thiago_Silva_Fuori_ga_10_090923016.shtml|title=Stop per Thiago Silva Fuori anche Ambrosini|date=23 September 2009|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2009/settembre/25/Borriello_Milanello_dopo_Champions_ga_10_090925027.shtml|title=Borriello a Milanello dopo la Champions|date=25 September 2009|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> In October, Silva followed a poor performance against Roma<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2009/ottobre/19/PAGELLE_ga_10_091019024.shtml|title=Le Pagelle|date=19 October 2009|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> with two great displays against [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]];<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2009/ottobre/22/PAGELLE_ga_10_091022004.shtml|title=Le Pagelle|date=22 October 2009|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2009/novembre/04/PAGELLE_ga_10_091104009.shtml|title=Le Pagelle|date=4 November 2009|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> Silva also had a wrongly disallowed goal in Milan's away victory.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2009/ottobre/22/Annullato_autogol_Sergio_Ramos_non_ga_10_091022003.shtml|title=Annullato autogol di Sergio Ramos ma non c' era fallo di Thiago Silva|date=22 October 2009|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2009/oct/21/champions-league-clockwatch-live|title=Champions League: Real Madrid v Milan – as it happened|date=21 October 2009|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref>

{{Quote box
| width = 29%
| align = right
| quote = "Thiago Silva will extend my life as a central defender."
| source = —[[Alessandro Nesta]], 2009<ref>{{cite web|last=Chachra|first=Tanish|date=16 October 2019|title=O Monstro: Thiago Silva, The epitome of determination|url=https://www.elartedf.com/o-monstro-thiago-silva-epitome-determination/|access-date=24 August 2020|website=El Arte Del Futbol}}</ref>
}}

On 8 November, Silva scored a goal – as well as an own-goal – in a 2–1 victory over [[S.S. Lazio|Lazio]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2009/novembre/10/Thiago_Silva_dall_altare_alla_ga_10_091110109.shtml|title=Thiago Silva dall' altare alla polvere|date=10 November 2009|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> His quick transition to European football was met with a lot of interest from Italian media — the investment of €10 million to acquire Silva was regarded as a good decision; the ''[[La Gazzetta dello Sport]]'', the largest daily newspaper in Italy,<ref>{{cite web|title=Indagine sulla lettura dei quotidiani e dei periodici in Italia |work=Audipress |url=http://www.audipress.it/upload/File/Audip%202012_II%20DATI_invio.xlsx |access-date=2 July 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130323060202/http://www.audipress.it/upload/File/Audip%202012_II%20DATI_invio.xlsx |archive-date=23 March 2013 }}</ref> claimed that Silva's value had doubled at that point.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2009/novembre/11/Milito_Poli_colpi_giusti_Huntelaar_ga_10_091111010.shtml|title=Milito e Poli i colpi giusti Huntelaar s' è sgonfiato|date=11 November 2009|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> On 25 November, Silva put in a man of the match performance against [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] to secure passage into the [[2009–10 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|knockout stages]] of the [[UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2009/novembre/26/PAGELLE_ga_10_091126005.shtml|title=Le Pagelle|date=26 November 2009|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> In a match against [[FC Zürich|Zürich]] on 8 December, Silva was substituted after 20 minutes with a muscle injury. ====2010–11: Serie A win====
Silva's season began with a goal against [[U.S. Lecce|Lecce]] in the first match of the [[2010–11 Serie A|2010–11 Serie A season]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2010/agosto/30/Mamma_che_Pato_Effetto_Ibra_ga_10_100830040.shtml|title=Mamma che Pato Effetto Ibra, Milan travolgente|date=30 August 2010|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> In a 3–1 victory over [[A.C. Chievo Verona|Chievo]] on 16 October, Silva was forced to leave the match with a sprained left ankle. The injury forced Silva to miss a [[2010–11 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] [[2010–11 UEFA Champions League group stage|group stage]] match against Real Madrid — Milan CEO Adriano Galliani jokingly said after the match that he would give Silva his healthy foot in order to see him play at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2010/ottobre/17/Thiago_lacrime_Madrid_rischio_ga_3_101017001.shtml|title=Thiago in lacrime Madrid a rischio|date=17 October 2010|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> Silva was inactive for four matches due to his injury. news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2010/novembre/15/PAGELLE_MILAN_ABATE_AIUTA_INTER_ga_3_101115012.shtml|title=Pagelle Milan Abate Aiuta L'Inter, Bentornato Seedorf|date=15 November news|url=http://www.milannews.it/primo-piano/doppia-tegola-per-il-milan-stiramento-per-flamini-e-lesione-del-menisco-per-thiago-40595|title=Doppia tegola per il Milan: stiramento per Flamini e lesione news|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/10/italy/2010/12/09/2253326/milan-rocked-as-thiago-silva-faces-six-months-out-injured|title=Milan Rocked As Thiago Silva Faces Six Months Out Injured, Mathieu news|url=http://www.goal.com/en-india/news/2292/editorials/2010/12/20/2269522/goalcom-special-serie-a-team-of-the-season|title=Goal.com Special: Serie A Team Of The Season|date=20 December Forced to play as an emergency defensive midfielder due to an injury crisis, Silva played extraordinarily well against [[A.C. Cesena|Cesena]], a match which Milan won 2–0. Silva's performance brought comparisons to legendary Milan midfielder [[Marcel Desailly]].<ref name="heir to Desailly">{{cite news|url=http://www.football-italia.net/node/2196|title=The Brazilian heir to Desailly|work=Football Italia|date=26 January 2011|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> In his next match, Silva was rated as the best player in Milan's 2–1 victory over [[U.C. Sampdoria|Sampdoria]] in the [[2010–11 Coppa Italia|Coppa Italia quarter-final]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2011/gennaio/27/MILAN_THIAGO_SILVA_ECLETTICO_MERKEL_ga_10_110127016.shtml|title=Milan Thiago Silva Eclettico, Merkel Utile|date=27 January 2011|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> The midfield "experiment" continued in a 0–0 draw against Lazio, though this time, Silva was compared to another legendary Milan midfielder, [[Frank Rijkaard]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2011/febbraio/02/PAGELLE_ga_10_110202027.shtml|title=Pagelle|date=2 February 2011|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> Silva was lauded by Italian media for his display against [[S.S.C. Napoli|Napoli]], marking-out star striker [[Edinson Cavani]]. In the match that sealed the ''Scudetto'' for Milan, Silva anchored the ''Rossoneri'' to a 3–0 victory in the Derby della Madonnina against city rivals Inter.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2011/aprile/03/PAGELLE_ga_10_110403011.shtml|title=Le Pagelle|date=3 April 2011|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> At the end of the season, Silva extended his contract to June 2016.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.acmilan.com/it/news/breaking_news_show/10367|title=A.C. Milan's season began with a 2–1 victory over Inter in the [[2011 Supercoppa Italiana]]; Silva was the best defender in the match and one of the best overall performers, making a decisive last-man tackle on [[Samuel Eto'o]] to deny a clear chance in the first half.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2011/agosto/07/MILAN_NESTA_SBANDA_THIAGO_SILVA_ga_10_110807006.shtml|title=Milan Nesta Sbanda, Thiago Silva No. Seedorf Si Sveglia Nella Ripresa E Accedne La Luce|date=7 August 2011|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> Milan began the [[2011–12 Serie A]] in poor form, winning only two points in the first three matches, though Silva was one of the better players in the draws against Lazio<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2011/settembre/10/Pagelle_ga_10_1109108031.shtml|title=Le Pagelle|date=10 September 2011|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> and Udinese.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2011/settembre/22/Pagelle_ga_10_110922053.shtml|title=Le Pagelle|date=22 September 2011|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> In a [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League group stage|group stage]] match against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], Silva and Alessandro Nesta were crucial in the 2–2 result; Although Milan originally claimed Silva would be out just four weeks,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.acmilan.com/it/news/breaking_news_show/23641|title=Thiago Silva: A.C. Miland Comunicato Ufficiale|date=25 March 2012|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> instead he missed seven weeks, including the [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League#Quarter-finals|Champions League quarter-finals]] against Barcelona, where Milan fell 1–3 on aggregate.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01fc-0e7d9ac2047c-3313f31c3732-1000--messi-sets-new-mark-as-barcelona-see-off-milan/|title=Messi sets new mark as Barcelona see off Milan|date=3 April 2012|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> Without Silva, Milan stuttered in the league and lost the ''Scudetto'' to rivals Juventus. It was argued that Silva's injury was the turning point in the title race: with Silva, Milan won 2.37 out of a possible 3 points per match, while without him Milan won 2.09 out of a possible 3 points.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://jameshorncastle.com/serie-a-team-of-the-season-2011-12/|title=Serie A Team of the Season 2011–12|date=15 May 2012|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> Silva's strong season finished in another nomination to the Serie A Team of the Year, being joint-best central defender alongside Juve stalwart [[Andrea Barzagli]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://forzaitalianfootball.com/2013/01/gran-gala-del-calcio-2012-winners/|title= Gran Gala del Calcio 2012 – Winners|date=28 January 2013|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref> He was also regarded as one of the best defenders in Italy by multiple independent publications.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/1717/editorial/2012/05/14/3098597/serie-a-team-of-the-season-pirlo-ibrahimovic-di-natale-star|title=Serie A Team of the Season: Pirlo, Ibrahimovic & Di Natale star in the 2011–12 campaign|date=14 May 2012|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref><ref name="just-football.com">{{cite news|url=http://www.just-football.com/2012/05/serie-a-italy-team-of-the-season-2011-2012/|title=Serie A: Just Football's Team of the Season 2011–2012|date=17 May 2012|access-date=2 July 2014}}</ref>

===Paris Saint-Germain===
The negotiations to bring Silva to [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] took place at the end of the 2011–12 season. The saga took over a month to complete. On 11 June 2012, it was reported that Milan legend Paolo Maldini would convince Silva to join PSG in the summer.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.francesoir.fr/sport/football/psg-c-est-maldini-qui-a-convaincu-thiago-silva-236281.html|title=PSG : C'est Maldini qui a convaincu Thiago Silva!|date=11 June 2012|access-date=10 July 2014|archive-date=14 July 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714213930/http://www.francesoir.fr/sport/football/psg-c-est-maldini-qui-a-convaincu-thiago-silva-236281.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Major French newspaper ''[[L'Équipe]]'' claimed that a transfer would be completed by 15 June.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.football-italia.net/19840/thiago-silva-psg-say-l%E2%80%99equipe|title=Thiago Silva to PSG, say L'Equipe|date=11 June 2012|access-date=10 July 2014}}</ref> The same day, PSG sporting director — and former Milan coach — [[Leonardo Araújo|Leonardo]] officially declared interest in acquiring Silva.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.football-italia.net/19847/thiago-silva-edges-towards-psg|title=Thiago Silva edges towards PSG|date=11 June 2012|access-date=10 July 2014}}</ref> The next day, however, Milan general director Ariedo Braida claimed that Silva was not for sale.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.football-italia.net/19870/milan-we%E2%80%99re-not-selling-silva|title=Milan: We're not selling Silva|date=12 June 2012|access-date=10 July 2014}}</ref> On 13 June, Maldini refuted claims that he would play a part in Silva's transfer, asserting the fact that he would never convince Silva to leave.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.tribalfootball.com/articles/ac-milan-legend-maldini-selling-thiago-silva-will-be-sign-weakness-3236591#.U7Yze7GmWqQ|title=AC Milan legend Maldini: Selling Thiago Silva will be sign of weakness|date=13 June 2012|access-date=10 July 2014}}</ref> Milan chairman [[Silvio Berlusconi]] mentioned a potential transfer on 13 June, saying that Silva needed to be sold for €46 million in order to balance the club's accounts.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.leparisien.fr/psg-foot-paris-saint-germain/psg-berlusconi-confirme-le-transfert-de-thiago-silva-13-06-2012-2046950.php|title=PSG : Berlusconi confirme le transfert de Thiago Silva|date=13 June 2012|access-date=10 July 2014}}</ref> The next day, however, Berlusconi confirmed that Silva would be staying at Milan.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.acmilan.com/it/news/show/141895|title=Grazie Presidente!|date=14 June 2012|access-date=10 July 2014}}</ref> Transfer news slowed down, and on 2 July, Milan extended Silva's contract to 2017,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.acmilan.com/en/news/show/142198|title=Milan-Thiago Silva: 2017|date=2 July 2012|access-date=10 July 2014}}</ref> yet just 12 days later, Silva's transfer to PSG was confirmed.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.psg.fr/en/News/003001/Article/58524/Thiago-Silva-signs-for-Paris-Saint-Germain|title=Thiago Silva signs for Paris Saint-Germain|date=14 July 2012|access-date=10 July 2014|archive-date=16 July 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120716225936/http://www.psg.fr/en/News/003001/Article/58524/Thiago-Silva-signs-for-Paris-Saint-Germain|url-status=dead}}</ref> The transfer fee was rumoured to be around €42 million, which would have made Silva the most expensive defender in football history.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.goal.com/en-us/news/69/transfer-zone/2012/07/14/3241934/paris-saint-germain-completes-42-million-euros-signing-of-thiago-|title=Paris Saint-Germain completes 42 million euros signing of Thiago Silva from AC Milan|date=14 June 2012|access-date=10 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2012/07/14/thiago-silva-transfer-psg-fee-ac-milan-brazil_n_1673721.html|title=Thiago Silva To Paris Saint-Germain From AC Milan For 42 Million Euro Fee|date=14 July 2012|access-date=10 July 2014}}</ref> Silva had repeatedly stressed the fact that he never pushed for a transfer, and that he was happy at Milan.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/3274/ligue-1/2013/12/15/4481124/thiago-silva-i-never-wanted-to-leave-ac-milan|title=Thiago Silva: I never wanted to leave AC Milan|date=15 December On 15 January 2014, Manchester United central defender [[Rio Ferdinand]] claimed that Silva was, by a distance, the best defender in the world.<ref name="Ferdinand">{{cite news|url=https://twitter.com/rioferdy5/status/423397345905356800|title=Rio Ferdinand|date=15 January 2014|access-date=10 July 2014}}</ref> Silva was imperious in PSG's 2–0 win against Bordeaux at the [[Parc des Princes]], where he covered for the errors of teammate [[Gregory van der Wiel]] and was even close to scoring himself.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.footmercato.net/ligue1/psg-bordeaux-les-notes-du-match_123497|title=PSG-Bordeaux : les notes du match|date=31 January 2014|access-date=10 July 2014}}</ref> This performance was followed by another strong performance against Monaco; despite scoring an unlucky own-goal, Silva made crucial interventions throughout the match, including a last-man block against striker [[Emmanuel Rivière]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.footmercato.net/ligue1/monaco-psg-les-notes-du-match_124063|title=Monaco-PSG : les notes du match|date=9 February 2014|access-date=10 July 2014}}</ref> In PSG's comprehensive 4–0 win in the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] over [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]], Silva was regarded by ''Le Parisien'' as having "dominated" then [[Bundesliga]] leading-scorer [[Stefan Kießling]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.leparisien.fr/psg-foot-paris-saint-germain/notes-joueurs-psg/?id_match=335|title=Lerverkusen 0 – 4 PSG|access-date=10 July 2014}}</ref> Marseille defender [[Lucas Mendes (footballer, born 1990)|Lucas Mendes]] said that Silva was the best defender in the world, and that Silva was his role model as a footballer.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.goal.com/fr/news/1729/france/2014/02/20/4634680/om-lucas-mendes-sinspire-de-thiago-silva|title=OM, Lucas Mendes s'inspire de Thiago Silva|date=20 February 2014|access-date=10 July 2014}}</ref> On 16 February, [[Ronaldo (Brazilian footballer)|Ronaldo]], the three-time [[FIFA World Player of the Year]], compared the qualities of Silva to legendary German sweeper [[Franz Beckenbauer]].<ref name="Beckenbauer">{{cite news|url=http://www.le10sport.com/football/ligue1/psg/psg-ronaldo-thiago-silva-il-marche-sur-les-traces-de-beckenbauer136274|title=PSG – Ronaldo : "Thiago Silva ? Il marche sur les traces de Beckenbauer"|date=16 February 2014|access-date=10 July 2014}}</ref> Silva managed another accomplished display in ''Le Classique'', marshaling the club's defence to a clean sheet and helping extend its lead to eight points at the top of the Ligue 1 table.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.psg.fr/en/News/003001/Article/65921/A-classic-result-for-Paris|title=A classic result for Paris|date=2 March 2014|access-date=10 July 2014|archive-date=14 July 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714122253/http://www.psg.fr/en/News/003001/Article/65921/A-classic-result-for-Paris|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Quarter-finals|Champions League quarter-finals]] against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], Silva conceded his first penalty in over three years, but recovered well in the 3–1 first leg victory<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.psg.fr/en/News/003001/Article/66395/Paris-put-on-a-show|title=Paris put on a show|date=2 April 2014|access-date=10 July 2014|archive-date=14 July 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714123005/http://www.psg.fr/en/News/003001/Article/66395/Paris-put-on-a-show|url-status=dead}}</ref> — Silva's overall defensive effort was well-recognised by both English and French media.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/apr/02/psg-chelsea-champions-league-player-ratings|title=Paris Saint-Germain 3–1 Chelsea: Champions League player ratings|date=2 April 2014|access-date=10 July 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.footmercato.net/ligue-des-champions/psg-chelsea-les-notes-du-match_127356|title=PSG – Chelsea : les notes du match|date=2 April 2014|access-date=10 July 2014}}</ref> In the second-leg, however, Chelsea prevailed on away goals after a late goal from substitute [[Demba Ba]]. On 19 April, Silva captained PSG to a 2–1 victory in the [[2014 Coupe de la Ligue Final]], the first time the club had won the competition since 1998.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.psg.fr/fr/Calendrier-Resultats/204003/Analyse-de-match/66658/Paris-tient-sa-coupe|title=Paris tient sa coupe !|date=19 April 2014|access-date=10 July 2014}}</ref> Despite losing 1–2 to [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]], PSG clinched the league title; Silva had captained the club to their second consecutive league title, and their first double.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.psg.fr/fr/Actus/003001/Article/66895/Retour-sur-une-saison-exceptionnelle|title=Retour sur une saison exceptionnelle|date=8 May 2014|access-date=10 July 2014}}</ref> Silva again was shortlisted for [[Trophées UNFP du football#Player of the Year|Ligue 1 Player of the Year]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.thescore.com/news/492850|title=PSG trio shortlisted for Ligue 1 player of year|date=1 May 2014|access-date=10 July 2014}}</ref> and named in the [[Trophées UNFP du football#Team of the Year|Ligue 1 Team of the Year]] for the second consecutive season.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.ligue1.com/ligue1/article/ibrahimovic-named-player-of-year.htm|title=Ibrahimovic named Player of Year|date=12 May 2014|access-date=10 July 2014|archive-date=30 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200730230720/http://www.ligue1.com/ligue1/article/ibrahimovic-named-player-of-year.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> Silva was rated by ''France Football'' as the league's fifth-best player, as well as the best defender in Ligue 1.<ref name="auto">{{cite news|title=Classement Étoiles|url=http://www.francefootball.fr/ligue-1/etoiles/|url-status=dead|access-date=10 July 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130608153153/http://www.francefootball.fr/ligue-1/etoiles/|archive-date=8 June 2013}}</ref>

====2014–15: Domestic quadruple====
Silva's season began poorly in PSG's 2–2 draw with Reims; he was rated as one of PSG's worst players in his first match back from the [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Reims 2 – 2 PSG|url=http://www.leparisien.fr/psg-foot-paris-saint-germain/notes-joueurs-psg/?id_match=373|access-date=25 May 2015|date=8 August 2014}}</ref> In his post-match interview, Silva mentioned how he was not fully fit and that he was finding it difficult to forget Brazil's [[Mineirazo|embarrassing loss to Germany]], where Brazil capitulated without him.<ref>{{cite news|title=Thiago Silva : ´Difficile d'oublierª la Coupe du monde|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Thiago-silva-difficile-d-oublier/488856|access-date=25 May 2015|date=8 August 2014}}</ref> Only three days after the match against Reims, Silva's rush to get back to full fitness was halted as he suffered a serious thigh injury in a friendly against Napoli on 11 August; he only lasted 13 minutes before being carried off the pitch.<ref>{{cite news|title=Thiago Silva, la blessure qui va faire parler|url=http://rmcsport.bfmtv.com/football/thiago-silva-blessure-va-faire-parler-640557.html|access-date=25 May 2015|date=11 August 2014}}</ref> After nine weeks, Silva was finally pronounced fit on 16 October by manager [[Laurent Blanc]], who also said that Silva would be able to start the next league match against Bordeaux.<ref>{{cite news|title=PSG : Laurent Blanc Èvoque líÈtat de Thiago Silva|url=http://www.le10sport.com/football/ligue1/psg/psg-laurent-blanc-evoque-letat-de-thiago-silva168344|access-date=25 May 2015|date=16 October 2014}}</ref> In his return, he had an excellent display alongside fellow countryman [[David Luiz]] as PSG dominated Bordeaux, winning 3–0.<ref>{{cite news|title=PSG – Bordeaux : les notes du match|url=http://www.footmercato.net/ligue1/psg-bordeaux-les-notes-du-match_141115|access-date=25 May 2015|date=25 October 2014}}</ref> A third of the way into the season, it was observed that Silva's performances were marked with inconsistency, especially throughout November and December. After PSG's 1–3 loss to Barcelona in December, he was criticised by former PSG player [[Pierre Ducrocq]], who argued that Silva did not have any physical or technical problems, but instead a mentality issue.<ref>{{cite news|title=PSG : Thiago Silva est-il intouchable ?|url=http://www.leparisien.fr/psg-foot-paris-saint-germain/thiago-silva-est-il-intouchable-13-12-2014-4370629.php|access-date=25 May 2015|date=13 December 2014}}</ref> Despite his struggles, Silva was recognised by his peers as being one of the two best central defenders in the world, as he was voted into the [[FIFPro#FIFA FIFPro World XI|2015 FIFPro World XI]] for the second consecutive year.<ref>{{cite news|title=FIFA/FIFPro World XI 2014|url=https://www.fifa.com/ballon-dor/world11/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141225015504/http://www.fifa.com/ballon-dor/world11/|url-status=dead|archive-date=25 December 2014|access-date=25 May 2015|date=15 January 2015}}</ref>

The 2015 calendar year began extremely well for Silva, with a man of the match display against [[AS Saint-Étienne|Saint-Étienne]] in a 1–0 victory.<ref>{{cite news|title=Saint Etienne 0–1 PSG|url=http://www.leparisien.fr/psg-foot-paris-saint-germain/notes-joueurs-psg/?id_match=437|access-date=25 May 2015|date=25 January 2015}}</ref> It was followed by another man of the match performance, this time in a 1–0 win against Rennes.<ref>{{cite news|title=PSG 1–0 Rennes|url=http://www.leparisien.fr/psg-foot-paris-saint-germain/notes-joueurs-psg/?id_match=441|access-date=25 May 2015|date=30 January 2015}}</ref> After the match, Rennes captain [[Sylvain Armand]] had nothing but praise for Silva, saying "he [Silva] is a monster and a phenomenon".<ref>{{cite news|title=Le grand Thiago Silva est de retour au PSG|url=http://www.foot01.com/equipe/paris/le-grand-thiago-silva-est-de-retour-au-psg,167357|access-date=25 May 2015|date=30 January 2015}}</ref> Four days later, Silva Chelsea in the first leg of the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#First leg|2014–15 Champions League Round of 16]], Silva was unanimously praised by the French press for his outstanding ''L'Équipe'' recognised Silva's incredible performances in January and February with a detailed analysis of his performances — in 2015, Silva was winning 89% of his duels, best in Ligue 1; Silva had 2.9 interceptions, 3.4 tackles, and 7.6 clearances per match, best in Ligue 1; lastly, Silva had committed a remarkable 0 fouls in 630 minutes of play.<ref>{{cite news|title=Thiago Silva, "le Monstre" fait ‡ nouveau peur (statistiques)|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/T-silva-le-monstre-refait-peur/538668|access-date=25 May 2015|date=1 March 2015}}</ref> In a 2–0 win against Monaco in the [[Coupe de France]] quarterfinal, Silva was praised for his dominance: one publication noted, "if you thought [[Dimitar Berbatov]] [of Monaco] was silent and invisible throughout the match, it was only due to the work of the Monster".<ref>{{cite news|title=PSG – Monaco : les notes du match|url=http://www.footmercato.net/coupe-de-france/psg-monaco-les-notes-du-match_149403|access-date=25 May 2015|date=4 March 2015}}</ref> In the second leg of the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#First leg|2014–15 Champions League Round of 16]], Silva conceded a controversial penalty in the 96th minute. PSG were poised to be eliminated from the Champions League but in the 114th minute, Silva atoned for his error with a towering header to beat [[Thibaut Courtois]] to help PSG advance to the next stage. Silva was voted by several media sources as the best player in the match as he produced an extraordinary performance.<ref>{{cite news|title=Thiago Silva, Marco Verratti lead Paris Saint-Germain to priceless UCL victory|url=http://www.espnfc.com/club/paris-saint-germain/160/blog/post/2343689/paris-saint-germain-player-ratings-thiago-silva-marco-verratti-lead-psg-to-priceless-ucl-victory|access-date=25 May 2015|date=11 March 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Chelsea-PSG – Les notes : Thiago Silva-David Luiz, c'est vraiment une charniËre qui vaut de l'or|url=http://www.eurosport.fr/football/ligue-des-champions/2014-2015/chelsea-psg-les-notes-thiago-silva-david-luiz-c-est-vraiment-une-charniere-qui-vaut-de-l-or_sto4635465/story.shtml|access-date=25 May 2015|date=12 March 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Chelsea 2–2 PSG|url=http://www.leparisien.fr/psg-foot-paris-saint-germain/notes-joueurs-psg/?id_match=461|access-date=25 May 2015|date=11 March 2015}}</ref>

PSG finally took pole position in the league after their 2–3 win over Marseille; Silva was dominant in his duels and played a crucial role in the victory.<ref>{{cite news|title=OM 2–3 PSG|url=http://www.leparisien.fr/psg-foot-paris-saint-germain/notes-joueurs-psg/?id_match=467|access-date=25 May 2015|date=5 April 2015}}</ref> Three days later, he was voted man of the match in a 4–1 victory against Saint-Étienne in the Coupe de France semi-final.<ref>{{cite news|title=PSG 4–1 Saint Etienne|url=http://www.leparisien.fr/psg-foot-paris-saint-germain/notes-joueurs-psg/?id_match=469|access-date=25 May 2015|date=8 April 2015}}</ref> On 11 April, Silva captained the club to a 4–0 win in the [[2015 Coupe de la Ligue Final|Coupe de la Ligue final]] against Bastia.<ref>{{cite news|title=Coupe de la Ligue.
