====2015–2020: Sustained domestic success, European final====
[[File:Thiago Silva & David Luiz (PSG 2015-2016).jpg|thumb|right|upright|Silva and [[David Luiz]] playing for Paris Saint-Germain in 2016]]
After playing in the [[2015 Copa América]], Silva finally returned to club training on 20 July in [[New Jersey]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.psg.fr/en/News/003001/Article/71680/Marquinhos-and-Thiago-Silva-are-back|title=Marquinhos and Thiago Silva are back|date=20 July 2015|access-date=8 August 2015|archive-date=24 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924083108/http://www.psg.fr/en/News/003001/Article/71680/Marquinhos-and-Thiago-Silva-are-back|url-status=dead}}</ref> The first pre-season match that Silva played in was the final match of the [[2015 International Champions Cup]] against Manchester United, where PSG won 2–0 to win the trophy; Silva was rated as the best player in the match.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.leparisien.fr/psg-foot-paris-saint-germain/le-psg-bat-manchester-united-2-0-et-remporte-l-international-champions-cup-30-07-2015-4979017.php|title=Le PSG bat Manchester United, (2–0) et remporte l'International Champions Cup|date=30 July 2015|access-date=8 August 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/man-utd/player-ratings/player-ratings-manchester-united-0-2-paris-saint-germain_236154.html|title=Player Ratings: Manchester United 0–2 Paris Saint-Germain
|date=30 July 2015|access-date=8 August 2015}}</ref> Two days later, Silva captained PSG to a 2–0 victory in the [[2015 Trophée des Champions]] against Lyon.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.psg.fr/fr/Saison/204002/Match/1515/Paris-Lyon|title=Paris vs Lyon|date=1 August 2015|access-date=8 August 2015}}</ref> Silva had a good match with little to do defensively, as Lyon's star striker [[Alexandre Lacazette]] played an insignificant role in the match.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.footmercato.net/trophee-des-champions/psg-ol-les-notes-du-match_159000|title=PSG – OL : les notes du match|date=1 August 2015|access-date=8 August 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://rmcsport.bfmtv.com/football/psg-lyon-les-notes-905114.html|title=PSG-Lyon : les notes|date=1 August 2015|access-date=8 August 2015}}</ref>

PSG began their [[2015–16 Ligue 1|league campaign]] with a 1–0 victory against Lille, playing with ten-men for two-thirds of the match.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.psg.fr/fr/Calendrier-Resultats/204003/Analyse-de-match/71834/Paris-lance-sa-saison|title=Paris Lance SA Saison|date=7 August 2015|access-date=8 August 2015}}</ref> Silva had a superb display, leading the defence to a hard-fought clean sheet. His performance was described as dominant, showcasing his intelligence and athleticism throughout the match.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.leparisien.fr/psg-foot-paris-saint-germain/notes-joueurs-psg/?id_match=501|title=Lille 0–1 PSG|date=7 August 2015|access-date=8 August 2015}}</ref> On 8 May 2018, he played as PSG won 2–0 against [[Les Herbiers VF]] to clinch the 2017–18 [[Coupe de France]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/live/football/43949707|title=French Cup final - PSG beat Les Herbiers|date=3 May 2018|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

In April 2020, PSG were awarded the [[2019–20 Ligue 1]] title after the season was ended prematurely due to the outbreak of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]; at the time of the League's suspension, PSG were in first place, with a twelve–point lead over second–placed Marseille. This was Silva's record seventh Ligue 1 title with the club, which saw him equal the all–time individual record of most Ligue 1 title victories, along with his club teammate [[Marco Verratti]], which was jointly held by [[Hervé Revelli]] and [[Jean-Michel Larqué]] of Saint-Étienne, as well as [[Grégory Coupet]], [[Juninho Pernambucano|Juninho]] and [[Sidney Govou]] of Lyon.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2020/apr/30/psg-awarded-ligue-1-title-after-season-stopped-by-coronavirus-crisis |title=PSG awarded Ligue 1 title and two teams are relegated after season is scrapped |work=The Guardian |date=30 April 2020 |access-date=13 June 2020 }}</ref><ref name="seventh heaven">{{cite web |url=https://www.ligue1.com/Articles/NEWS/2020/05/07/psg-thiago-silva-and-verratti-in-seventh-heaven |title=Thiago Silva and Verratti in seventh heaven |work=Ligue1 |publisher=Ligue 1 |date=7 May 2020 |access-date=13 June 2020 }}</ref> On 13 June, PSG's sporting director Leonardo revealed that Thiago Silva would be leaving the club at the end of the [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League|Champions League campaign]] in August, alongside his teammate [[Edinson Cavani]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/football/paris-saint-germain/story/4111424/psgs-leonardo-on-edinson-cavani-and-thiago-silva-coming-to-an-end |title=PSG's Leonardo on Edinson Cavani, Thiago Silva: 'Coming to an end' |work=ESPN FC |date=13 June 2020 |access-date=15 June 2020 }}</ref> PSG completed a domestic treble,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/soccer/mbappe-training-return-boosts-psg-atalanta-quarterfinal/ |title=Mbappe training return boosts PSG for Atalanta quarterfinal |website=Sportsnet.ca |date=11 August 2020 |access-date=24 August 2020 }}</ref> while his last competitive match for PSG was the [[2020 UEFA Champions League Final]] on 23 August, which PSG lost 1–0 to [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report?gameId=573698|title=Bayern Munich beat Paris Saint-Germain to win Champions League|publisher=ESPN|date=23 August 2020|access-date=23 August 2020}}</ref> However, Silva became the first Brazilian to start a Champions League Final as a captain.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/53867676|title=Paris Saint-Germain 0–1 Bayern Munich|website=BBC Sport|date=23 August 2020}}</ref>

===Chelsea===
====2020–21: Debut season and European glory====
[[File:Thiago Silva with Club World Cup Trophy 2022.jpg|thumb|upright|Silva celebrating [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] winning the [[2021 FIFA Club World Cup]]]]

On 28 August 2020, Silva joined [[Premier League]] club [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] on a one-year deal with an option for a second.<ref>{{cite news|title=Thiago Silva moves from Paris to London|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2020/08/28/thiago-silva-moves-from-paris-to-london|date=28 August 2020|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|access-date=28 August 2020}}</ref> He made his debut for the club on 23 September, in a 6–0 home win over [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]] in the third round of the [[2020–21 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|title='First of many' - Lampard hails hat-trick star Havertz after Chelsea crush Barnsley in Carabao Cup|url=https://www.goal.com/en-in/news/lampard-hails-havertz-chelsea-barnsley-carabao-cup/7scokrsldvv41nz2np7b0a087|date=23 September 2020|publisher=Goal|access-date=24 September 2020}}</ref> Three days later on 26 September, Silva made his Premier League debut in a 3–3 draw against [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] at [[The Hawthorns]] as captain.<ref>{{cite web|title=Thiago Silva: Theory might explain why Chelsea defender struggled on Premier League debut vs WBA|url=https://www.givemesport.com/1602477-thiago-silva-theory-might-explain-why-chelsea-defender-struggled-on-premier-league-debut-vs-wba|date=27 September 2020|publisher=Givemesport|access-date=27 September 2020}}</ref> On 7 November, Silva scored his first goal for Chelsea in a 4–1 home league win over [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/54758066|title=Chelsea 4-1 Sheffield United: Comfortable win for Blues leaves Sheff Utd bottom|website=BBC Sport|date=7 November 2020|access-date=7 November 2020}}</ref> On 21 December, Silva scored his second goal for Chelsea in a 3–0 victory over [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Rose|first=Gary|date=21 December 2021|title=Chelsea 3–0 West Ham|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/55297949|access-date=3 April 2021|website=BBC Sport}}</ref>

On 3 April 2021, Silva received a second [[Fouls and misconduct (association football)|yellow card]] and got sent off in the 29th minute in Chelsea's 5–2 home defeat to West Bromwich Albion.<ref>{{cite web|last=Steinberg|first=Jacob|date=3 April 2021|title=West Brom beat 10-man Chelsea|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/apr/03/chelsea-west-brom-premier-league-match-report|access-date=3 April 2021|website=The Guardian}}</ref> Silva led the defence as Chelsea reached its third Champions League final, defeating [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in the semi-finals.<ref>{{cite web|last=Newson|first=Adam|date=6 May 2021|title=What Thiago Silva did after Mason Mount's goal as Jorginho tears up after Chelsea reach final|url=https://www.football.london/chelsea-fc/news/thiago-silva-chelsea-mason-mount-20534510|access-date=7 May 2021|website=football.london}}</ref> On 29 May, Silva went off injured in the 39th minute while he won his first Champions League trophy after Chelsea's 1–0 victory against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in the [[2021 UEFA Champions League Final]] at the [[Estádio do Dragão]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0269-12650cedca55-37515f69768e-1000--report-chelsea-claim-second-title/|title=Man. City 0-1 Chelsea: Havertz gives Blues second Champions League triumph|website=[[UEFA]]|date=29 May 2021|access-date=29 May 2021}}</ref>

On 4 June 2021, Chelsea announced the extension of his contract for another year, keeping him at the club until June 2022.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2021/06/04/thiago-silva-contract-extended|title=Thiago Silva contract extended|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|date=4 June 2021|access-date=6 June 2021}}</ref>

====2021–24: 100 Champions League appearances and departure ====
{{quote box
| width = 33%
| author = {{mdash}}Silva, reflecting on a turbulent 2022–23 season for Chelsea.<ref name=david1>{{cite web |title=Thiago Silva reflects on 'frustrating' season full of change, indecision, negligence at Chelsea |url=https://weaintgotnohistory.sbnation.com/2023/4/19/23689228/thiago-silva-reflects-on-frustrating-season-full-of-change-indecision-negligence-at-chelsea?commentID=4c91a5e3-5ea7-4fff-b87e-5df564b807db |date=19 Apr 2023 |last=Pasztor |first=David |work=[[SB Nation]] |archive-url=https://archive.today/20230419122350/https://weaintgotnohistory.sbnation.com/2023/4/19/23689228/thiago-silva-reflects-on-frustrating-season-full-of-change-indecision-negligence-at-chelsea?commentID=4c91a5e3-5ea7-4fff-b87e-5df564b807db |archive-date=19 April 2023}}</ref>
| quote = Life is hard for those who are soft. If it's up to me, I'll get up every time I fall.
}}
On 4 December 2021, Silva scored in a 3–2 league loss to West Ham, becoming, at the age of 37 years and 73 days, the club's oldest ever goalscorer in the Premier League, surpassing the previous record set by Didier Drogba in 2015.<ref name=Cons>{{cite news |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/thiago-silva-a-constant-record-breaker |title=Thiago Silva: A constant record breaker! |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |date=22 September 2022 |access-date=22 June 2025}}</ref> The following month, on 3 January 2022, he extended his contract again, this time until the end of the 2022–23 season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2022/01/03/thiago-silva-extends-chelsea-contract-|title=Thiago Silva extends Chelsea contract|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|date=3 January 2022|access-date=3 January 2022}}</ref> Later that month, on 23 January, he score against Tottenham to seal a 2–0 league win, becoming, at the age of 37 years and 123 days, the oldest player to score in the Premier League since the 39-year-old [[Ryan Giggs]] in February 2013.<ref name=Cons/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/czx7n2wppyxo |title=Chelsea 2-0 Tottenham: Pick of the stats |website=Bbc.com |date=24 January 2022 |access-date=22 June 2025}}</ref> In the first leg of the UCL Round of 16 against [[Lille OSC|Lille]] on 22 February, Silva won possession 12 times, a personal best in a UCL match.<ref name=Cons/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thechelseachronicle.com/analysis/thiago-silva-breaks-his-own-personal-champions-league-record-in-chelsea-vs-lille-match/ |title=Thiago Silva breaks his own personal record in Chelsea win vs Lille |website=Thechelseachronicle.com |date=23 February 2022 |access-date=22 June 2025}}</ref> During a 2–4 league loss to Arsenal on 20 April 2022, he became Chelsea's oldest outfield player in the Premier League (37y and 210d), breaking [[Graham Rix]]'s record from 1995 by seven days.<ref name=Cons/>

On 11 October 2022, Silva made his [[List of footballers with 100 or more UEFA Champions League appearances|100th Champions League appearance]] in a 2–0 away win against his former club Milan.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0257-0e9a10f58015-92c648e6303d-1000--who-has-played-100-champions-league-games/ |title=Who has played 100 Champions League games? |website=UEFA |date=11 October 2022 }}</ref> On 10 February 2023, he extended his contract by another year, taking his contract to the end of the 2023–24 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Thiago Silva extends Chelsea stay |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/thiago-silva-extends-chelsea-stay |access-date=2023-02-11 |website=Chelseafc.com |language=en-gb}}</ref> On 28 February 2023, the club announced he would be out of action for an unspecified time after suffering ligament damage in a game against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Chelsea's Silva sidelined with knee ligament damage |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64797819 |access-date=2023-02-28}}</ref> In April, Silva was in the starting lineup for the two-legged Quarter Final tie against Real Madrid, which Chelsea lost 4–0 on aggregate. In a post-match interview, Silva hinted that he might have played his last game in the Champions League.{{r|david1}}

On 28 May 2023, before Chelsea played their final game of the season against [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle]], Thiago Silva was named [[Chelsea Player of the Year|Chelsea's Player of the Year]], becoming the first defender to win the award since [[John Terry]] in [[2006-06 Chelsea F.C. season|2006]].<ref name="ChelseaPOTY2023" /> On 12 November 2023, Silva scored against Manchester City in a 4–4 draw, becoming, at the age of 39 years and 51 days, the oldest goalscorer in Chelsea's history, breaking a 76-year-old record set by [[Dick Spence]] in 1947.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Antiques collection: Chelsea's 10 oldest Premier League scorers |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/antiques-collection-chelseas-10-oldest-premier-league-scorers |access-date=2023-11-15 |website=Chelseafc.com |language=en-gb}}</ref> Two weeks later, on 25 November, he became the club's oldest-ever outfield player, surpassing Spence again.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://talksport.com/football/1654619/thiago-silva-chelsea-record-oldest-player/ |title=Thiago Silva apologises for horror mistake as record-breaking Chelsea appearance ends in Newcastle thrashing |website=talksport.com |date=25 November 2023 |access-date=22 June 2025}}</ref> On 7 April 2024, he opened the scoring in a 2–2 league draw with Sheffield United, becoming, at the age of 39 years and 198 days, the third-oldest player to score away from home in the Premier League, as well as the third-oldest overall, only behind [[Dean Windass]] and [[Teddy Sheringham]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://theanalyst.com/articles/oldest-premier-league-scorers |title=The Oldest Goalscorers in Premier League History |website=theanalyst.com |date=26 January 2025 |access-date=22 June 2025}}</ref><ref name=McBurnie>{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/3958112#! |title=McBurnie's late goal earns Sheff Utd a point against Chelsea |website=Premierleague.com |date=7 April 2025 |access-date=22 June 2025}}</ref> He also became only the second 39-year-old player to score three or more goals in a single league season, after Sheringham in 2005–06.<ref name=McBurnie/>

On 29 April 2024, Chelsea announced that Silva would depart the club at the [[2023–24 Premier League|end of the season]], after spending four years at the club.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-04-29 |title=Thiago Silva to depart Chelsea at the end of the season |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/article/thiago-silva-to-depart-chelsea-at-the-end-of-the-season |access-date=2024-04-29 |website=Chelsea Football Club |language=en-GB}}</ref>

===Return to Fluminense===
On 7 May 2024, Silva agreed to join [[Fluminense FC|Fluminense]] as a free agent in July 2024 on a two-year deal, returning to his home club fifteen and a half years later. The defender helped Fluminense escape near-guaranteed relegation - the club was 20th when he joined before embarking on a 10-game streak without conceding a single league goal, largely due to the defender's influence.<ref>{{Cite web |date=7 May 2024 |title=O Monstro está de volta! Fluminense acerta a contratação de Thiago Silva |trans-title=The Monster is back! Fluminense agrees to sign Thiago Silva |url=https://www.fluminense.com.br/noticia/o-monstro-esta-de-volta-fluminense-acerta-a-contratacao-de-thiago-silva |access-date=7 May 2024 |website=Fluminense FC |language=pt-br}}</ref>

On 18 December 2025, Silva departed Fluminense to pursue a return to European football, with the aim of securing a place at the World Cup the following summer.<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 December 2025 |title=Thiago Silva leaves Fluminense |url=https://foot-africa.com/en/news/thiago-silva-leaves-fluminense-1006952/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251218171013/https://foot-africa.com/en/news/thiago-silva-leaves-fluminense-1006952/ |archive-date=18 December 2025 |access-date=18 December 2025 |website=Foot-Africa.com |language=en}}</ref>

=== Return to Porto ===
[[File:Thiago Silva (Divulgação FC Porto).webp|thumb|Thiago Silva playing for Porto]]
On 25 December 2025, Silva returned to [[FC Porto|Porto]], this time as part of the main team, signing a contract until the end of the [[2025–26 FC Porto season|2025–26 season]], with an option for a further year.<ref>{{Cite web |date=20 December 2025 |title=Thiago Silva é Dragão |trans-title=Thiago Silva is a Dragon |url=https://www.fcporto.pt/pt/noticias/20251220-pt-thiago-silva-e-dragao |access-date=20 December 2025 |publisher=[[FC Porto]] |language=pt}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-12-20 |title=Thiago Silva, 41, signs for Porto in surprise return to Europe |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/thiago-silva-new-club-porto-transfer-news-b2888346.html |access-date=2026-02-23 |website=The Independent |language=en}}</ref> He made his debut on 14 January 2026, starting in a 1–0 victory over [[O Clássico|rivals]] [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] in the [[2025–26 Taça de Portugal#Quarter-finals|quarter-finals]] of the [[Taça de Portugal]], overtaking [[Pepe (footballer, born 1983)|Pepe]] as the oldest player to ever represent Porto.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Roseiro |first=Bruno |date=14 January 2026 |title=O novo Xerife do Dragão fez uma estreia para a história: Thiago Silva supera Pepe e torna-se o mais velho de sempre a jogar pelo FC Porto |trans-title=The Dragão's new Sheriff made an historic debut: Thiago Silva overcomes Pepe and becomes the oldest to ever play for FC Porto |url=https://observador.pt/2026/01/14/o-novo-xerife-do-dragao-fez-uma-estreia-para-a-historia-thiago-silva-supera-pepe-e-torna-se-o-mais-velho-de-sempre-a-jogar-pelo-fc-porto/ |access-date=14 January 2026 |website=Observador |language=pt}}</ref> He ultimately won the [[2025–26 Primeira Liga|Primeira Liga]] title with the club.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://onefootball.com/en/news/thiago-silva-wins-31st-career-trophy-on-fc-porto-return-42810518 |title=Thiago Silva wins 31st career trophy on FC Porto return |publisher=OneFootball |date=4 May 2026 }}</ref>

===Third stint at Fluminense===
On 22 June 2026, Fluminense confirmed Silva's return to the club, with the player signing a contract valid until December 2026.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fluminense.com.br/noticia/algumas-historias-nunca-vao-ter-fim-thiago-silva-esta-de-volta-ao-fluminense |title=Algumas histórias nunca vão ter fim: Thiago Silva está de volta ao Fluminense |publisher=Fluminense |language=pt |date=22 June 2026 }}</ref>

==International career==
===Early career and 2008 Olympics===

After a strong season with Fluminense, Silva was called up to the [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] preliminary squad for the [[2007 Copa América]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/ESP/Noticia/Futebol/Selecao_Brasileira/0,,MUL91682-4482,00-DEFESA+NOVATA+NA+SELECAO.html|title=Defesa novata na seleção|date=21 August 2007|access-date=16 July 2014}}</ref> though he was not a part of the main team which ultimately won the tournament.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://goal.blogs.nytimes.com/2007/07/15/live-soon-argentina-brazil/|title=Copa America Final: Brazil 3, Argentina 0|date=15 July 2007|access-date=16 July 2014}}</ref> Silva was then called up for a friendly against [[Algeria national football team|Algeria]] on 15 August,<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/ESP/Noticia/Futebol/Selecao_Brasileira/0,,MUL88427-4482,00.html|title=Thiago Silva é convocado para a seleção|date=15 August 2007|access-date=16 July 2014}}</ref> failing to leave the bench, as Brazil won 2–0.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://magharebia.com/en_GB/articles/awi/features/2007/08/23/feature-01|title=Brazil defeats Algeria 2–0 in friendly|date=23 August 2007|access-date=16 July 2014}}</ref> Silva was then selected by [[Dunga]] to play in the [[2008 Summer Olympics]], one of two overage players, alongside [[Ronaldinho]]. Silva won his first two caps for Brazil in pre-Olympic friendlies against [[Singapore national football team|Singapore]] and [[Vietnam national football team|Vietnam]], though he suffered a right calf injury against Vietnam that kept him out of Brazil's first Olympic match.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://olimpiadas.uol.com.br/ultimas/2008/08/08/ult5584u3742.jhtm|title=Thiago Silva volta a treinar e deve jogar contra a Nova Zelândia|date=8 August 2008|access-date=21 July 2014}}</ref> He was finally pronounced fit for the third group match, where Silva started and Brazil won 3–0 against [[China national football team|China]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/tournaments/archive/mensolympic/beijing2008/matches/round=250016/match=300051797/report.html|title=China PR – Brazil|date=13 August 2008|access-date=21 July 2014}}</ref> He did not start any other matches, only coming on in the 71st minute against [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]] in the third-place match, which sealed the bronze medal for Brazil.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/tournaments/archive/mensolympic/beijing2008/matches/round=250024/match=300051813/report.html|title=Belgium – Brazil|date=22 August 2008|access-date=21 July 2014}}</ref>

Silva's next cap came in an international friendly against [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]] on 20 November 2008; Brazil won by a convincing 6–2 scoreline,<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/fabiano-treble-helps-brazil-beat-portugal-6-2|title=Fabiano treble helps Brazil beat Portugal 6–2|date=20 November 2008|access-date=21 July 2014}}</ref> and Silva was praised for having "dominated" the reigning [[FIFA World Player of the Year]], [[Cristiano Ronaldo]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2014/may/31/world-cup-2014-brazil-profile-thiago-silva|title=World Cup 2014: Brazil profile – Thiago Silva|date=31 May 2014|access-date=21 July 2014}}</ref> Silva was praised by his teammates for his performance.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/Esportes/Noticias/Times/Selecao_Brasileira/0,,MUL870264-15071,00-THIAGO+SILVA+AGRADECE+ELOGIOS+DE+ROBINHO.html|title=Thiago Silva agradece elogios de Robinho|date=21 November 2008|access-date=21 July 2014}}</ref> He was not a starter during the [[2010 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)|2010 World Cup qualifications]] for Brazil, despite his high level of club performances for Milan.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/Esportes/Noticias/Futebol/0,,MUL1483537-17852,00-CONVOCADO+PARA+AMISTOSO+THIAGO+SILVA+SE+VE+MAIS+PERTO+DA+COPA+DO+MUNDO.html|title=Convocado para amistoso, Thiago Silva se vê mais perto da Copa do Mundo|date=9 February 2010|access-date=21 July 2014}}</ref> He was still playing in friendly matches, and in a November 2009 friendly against [[England national football team|England]], Silva put in a man of the match display in [[Doha]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/1127/player-ratings/2009/11/14/1625016/international-friendly-player-ratings-brazil-1-0-england|title=International Friendly Player Ratings: Brazil 1–0 England|date=14 November 2009|access-date=21 July 2014}}</ref>

===2010 World Cup, 2011 Copa América, and 2012 Olympics===
Silva was an unused substitute in all matches at the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]], where Brazil were defeated in the quarter-finals by the eventual finalists, the [[Netherlands national football team|Netherlands]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/world_cup_2010/matches/match_57/default.stm|title=Netherlands 2–1 Brazil |website=BBC Sport |date=2 July 2010|access-date=21 July 2014}}</ref> Silva was selected as captain by new Brazil coach [[Mano Menezes]] ahead of the [[2014 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)|2014 World Cup qualifying cycle]], replacing [[Lúcio]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://esporte.uol.com.br/futebol/ultimas-noticias/2010/08/10/renovada-apos-fracasso-selecao-inicia-ciclo-contra-os-eua-de-olho-em-2014.jhtm|title=Renovada após fracasso, seleção inicia ciclo contra os EUA de olho em 2014|date=10 August 2010|access-date=21 July 2014}}</ref> At the [[2011 Copa América]], Brazil lost in a penalty shootout to [[Paraguay national football team|Paraguay]] in the quarter-finals.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.rediff.com/sports/report/copa-america-brazil-chile-fall-to-shock-defeats/20110718.htm|title=Brazil, Chile fall ===2013 Confederations Cup title===
Silva's first international trophy came at the [[2013 FIFA Confederations Cup]], held in Brazil. As a warm-up tournament to the [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014 World Cup]], Brazil won the tournament while scoring 14 goals and conceding 3.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://infosurhoy.com/en_GB/articles/saii/features/sports/2013/07/01/feature-03|title=Brazil defeats Spain for Confederations Cup title|date=1 July 2013|access-date=21 July 2014|archive-date=28 July 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140728134057/http://infosurhoy.com/en_GB/articles/saii/features/sports/2013/07/01/feature-03|url-status=dead}}</ref> Silva was rated as the tenth-best player at the end of the group stages,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/confederationscup/statistics/castrolindex/news/newsid=2117757/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130627135149/http://www.fifa.com/confederationscup/statistics/castrolindex/news/newsid=2117757/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=27 June 2013|title=Ramos sets pace as Fred, Alba lead pursuit|date=24 June 2013|access-date=21 July 2014}}</ref> and by the end of the tournament, he was rated as the fifth-best player of the tournament by the [[Castrol Performance Index]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/confederationscup/statistics/castrolindex/news/newsid=2128960/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130704203252/http://www.fifa.com/confederationscup/statistics/castrolindex/news/newsid=2128960/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=4 July 2013|title=Fred seizes throne on Brazilian-heavy Index|date=1 July 2013|access-date=21 July 2014}}</ref> Silva was also voted into the Confederations Cup Dream Team by FIFA.com users.<ref name="Dream Team">{{Cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/confederationscup/dreamteam/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130609002516/http://www.fifa.com/confederationscup/dreamteam/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=9 June 2013|title=Dream Team|access-date=21 June 2014}}</ref>

In the third-place match, Silva returned in a 3–0 loss to the Netherlands. In the second minute of the game, Silva pulled down [[Arjen Robben]], as he ran into [[Júlio César (footballer, born 1986)|Júlio César]]'s box with the ball for a clear goal-scoring opportunity. Under FIFA rules Silva ought to have been shown a red card, but he was shown a yellow card instead by the Algerian referee [[Djamel Haimoudi]]. The referee called for a penalty, while the foul happened outside the box, which was successfully scored by [[Robin van Persie]].

At the conclusion of the tournament, Silva was rated by FIFA as the third-best central defender, and the eighth-best player overall.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/y=2014/m=7/news=kroos-finishes-up-top-of-castrol-standings-2405228.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140715052510/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/y=2014/m=7/news=kroos-finishes-up-top-of-castrol-standings-2405228.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=15 July 2014|title=Kroos finishes up top of Castrol standings|date=14 July 2014|access-date=25 July 2014}}</ref> Silva was selected into the [[FIFA World Cup awards#All-Star Team|FIFA World Cup Dream Team]] voted by FIFA.com users,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/games/dream-team/index.html |title=Dream Team |access-date=25 July 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141229212753/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/games/dream-team/index.html |archive-date=29 December 2014 }}</ref> and the [[Castrol Performance Index|Castrol World Cup Top XI]] based on statistical merit.<ref name="Castrol Index Top 11">{{Cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/statistics/castrol-index/top11.html |title=Castrol Index Top 11 |access-date=25 July 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141230231236/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/statistics/castrol-index/top11.html |archive-date=30 December 2014 }}</ref>

===2015 Copa América===
Brazil, under Dunga's second stint as manager, went to the [[2015 Copa América]] in Chile with [[Neymar]] as the captain. After his suspension for the remainder of the tournament in their second game, however, the armband did not go back to Silva, but rather to his defensive partner, [[Miranda (footballer, born 1984)|Miranda]]. In Brazil's final [[2015 Copa América Group C|group]] match against [[Venezuela national football team|Venezuela]] at the [[Estadio Monumental David Arellano]] in [[Santiago]], Silva opened the scoring in the ninth minute, volleying in a corner from [[Robinho]]. The eventual 2–1 victory sent Brazil into the quarter-finals as group winners.<ref>{{cite news|title=Brazil 2–1 Venezuela: Thiago Silva and Firmino seal top spot|url=http://www.goal.com/en-ng/match/brazil-vs-venezuela/1947921/report?ICID=MP_MS_5|access-date=21 June 2015|work=Goal.com|date=21 June 2015}}</ref> In the 70th minute of the quarter-final, Silva's handball gave Paraguay the penalty kick from which they equalised for a 1–1 draw; Brazil lost in the subsequent [[penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Brazil 1–1 Paraguay|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33085894|access-date=28 June 2015|website=BBC Sport |date=28 June 2015}}</ref>

===2018 World Cup and 2019 Copa América title===
On 14 May 2018, Silva was named by [[Tite (football manager)|Tite]] to captain the squad for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018 World Cup]] in Russia.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44116590|title=World Cup: Neymar named in Brazil's 23-man squad |website=BBC Sport |date=14 May 2018}}</ref> He would play the full 90 minutes of all five of Brazil's matches at the tournament, before they were eliminated by [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]] in the quarter-finals. Silva managed to score during Brazil's final group stage match on 27 June, getting the second goal in his side's 2–0 win against [[Serbia national football team|Serbia]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/matches/match/300331521/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612142827/https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/matches/match/300331521/|url-status=dead|archive-date=12 June 2018|title=2018 FIFA World Cup Russia - Matches - Serbia - Brazil|website=FIFA.com}}</ref>

In May 2019, Silva was included in Brazil's 23-man squad for the [[2019 Copa América]] on home soil.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.football-italia.net/138152/brazil-name-copa-america-squad |title=Brazil name Copa America squad |publisher=Football Italia |date=17 May 2019 |access-date=21 May 2019 }}</ref> He would go on to play every minute for Brazil as they won the tournament, concluding with a 3–1 [[2019 Copa América final|final]] victory against [[Peru national football team|Peru]] on 7 July at the [[Maracanã Stadium|Maracanã]].<ref name="2019 Copa América Final">{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2019/jul/06/copa-america-final-brazil-peru-live |title=Brazil 3-1 Peru |work=The Guardian |last1=Smyth |first1=Rob |date=7 July 2019 |access-date=8 July 2019 }}</ref>

===2021 Copa América runner-up and appearance milestones===
In June 2021, Silva was included in Brazil's squad for the [[2021 Copa América]], again held on home soil.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://en.as.com/en/2021/07/10/football/1625909312_472586.html |title=Brazil national team squad Copa America 2021: selected players, absences... |website=AS.com |date=10 July 2021 |access-date=11 July 2021 |archive-date=21 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221221053154/https://en.as.com/en/2021/07/10/football/1625909312_472586.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> He played the full 90 minutes for Brazil in two of their group stage games and all three of their knockout stage fixtures, including their 1–0 defeat to rivals [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] in the [[2021 Copa América Final|final]] on 10 July.<ref name="2021CAFinalGuardian">{{cite news |last=Graham |first=Bryan Armen |date=10 July 2021 |title=Argentina 1-0 Brazil: Copa América final – as it happened |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2021/jul/10/argentina-v-brazil-copa-america-final-live |work=The Guardian |access-date=13 July 2021 }}</ref>

On 10 October 2021, Silva made his 100th appearance for Brazil in a goalless [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)|2022 World Cup qualification]] draw against Colombia.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://onefootball.com/en/news/chelsea-defender-thiago-silva-reaches-100-caps-with-brazil-33891786 |title=Chelsea defender Thiago Silva reaches 100 caps with Brazil |website=onefootball.com |date=11 October 2021 }}</ref> In September 2022, he became the most-capped centre-back in the history of the Brazil national team, surpassing [[Lúcio]].<ref>{{cite news |date=25 September 2022 |title=Thiago Silva Sets A New Record As He Becomes The Most Capped Defender For Brazil National Team |url=https://futballnews.com/thiago-silva-sets-a-new-record-as-he-becomes-the-most-capped-defender-for-brazil-national-team/ |access-date=4 October 2022 |website=Futball News}}</ref>

===2022 World Cup===
On 7 November 2022, Silva was named to Brazil's 26-man squad for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup|2022 World Cup]] in Qatar.<ref>{{cite web|title=Seleção Brasileira está convocada para a Copa do Mundo FIFA Qatar 2022|url=https://www.cbf.com.br/selecao-brasileira/noticias/selecao-masculina/selecao-brasileira-esta-convocada-para-a-copa-do-mundo-fifa-qatar-2022|publisher=[[Brazilian Football Confederation|CBF]]|access-date=7 November 2022|date=7 November 2022|language=pt}}</ref>

Silva started and played the full 90 minutes of Brazil's first two group matches against [[Serbia national football team|Serbia]] and [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Brazil vs. Serbia - 24 November 2022|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2022/11/24/world/world-cup/brazil/serbia/3749537/|website=Soccerway|access-date=18 July 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Brazil vs. Switzerland - 28 November 2022|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2022/11/28/world/world-cup/brazil/switzerland/3749539/|website=Soccerway|access-date=18 July 2023}}</ref> He then assisted [[Richarlison]]'s goal in a 4–1 round of 16 victory against [[South Korea national football team|South Korea]] on 5 December.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brazil vs. Korea Republic - 5 December 2022|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2022/12/05/world/world-cup/brazil/korea-republic/3298979/|website=Soccerway|access-date=18 July 2023}}</ref>
Four days later, Silva played the full 120 minutes of Brazil's quarter-final elimination by [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]], losing on penalties after extra time.<ref>{{cite web|title=Croatia vs. Brazil - 9 December 2022 - Soccerway|url=https://uk.soccerway.com/matches/2022/12/09/world/world-cup/croatia/brazil/3298983/|website=Soccerway.com|access-date=18 July 2023}}</ref>

===2026 World Cup===
He was included in the preliminary squad of 55 players for Brazil in the [[2026 World Cup]] announced by [[Carlo Ancelotti]] on 12 May 2026, but did not make the final cut.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://footballtoday.com/2026/05/18/brazil-2026-world-cup-squad-ancelotti-calls-neymar-but-no-room-for-joao-pedro-and-thiago-silva/|title=Brazil 2026 World Cup squad: Ancelotti selects Neymar but no room for Joao Pedro and Thiago Silva|first=Daniel|last=Ochei|website=Footballtoday.com|date=18 May 2026|access-date=15 June 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Silva and his wife Isabele have two sons, Isago and Iago, who are part of the [[Chelsea F.C. Development Squad and Academy]]. Iago is also a youth international for [[England]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://extra.globo.com/famosos/retratos-da-bola/isabelle-mulher-do-capitao-thiago-silva-faz-ensaio-em-segredo-para-surpreender-marido-admite-sou-amelia-12820093.html|title=Isabelle, mulher do web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6754040/2025/10/27/thiago-silva-son-england-brazil/|title=Thiago Silva's son invited to England Under-15 training camp|website=New York Times|date=27 October 2025 }}</ref> Silva is a [[Christianity|Christian]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2014/apr/09/world-cup-2014-hand-of-god-brazil-fred-christian,https://www.christiantoday.com/article/11-world-cup-stars-who-are-also-christians/38050.htm|title=World Cup 2014: Hand of God takes on different meaning for Brazil's Fred|website=[[TheGuardian.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.christianpost.com/news/christian-soccer-players-set-to-light-up-the-world-cup.html|title=Christian Soccer Players Set to Light Up the World Cup|website=Christian Post|date=9 June 2014}}</ref> On 15 March 2019 after playing almost seven years in [[France]] with [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]], Thiago announced that he, his wife and children had also become French citizens.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.europe1.fr/sport/le-defenseur-du-psg-thiago-silva-obtient-la-nationalite-francaise-3874790|title=Le défenseur du PSG Thiago Silva obtient la nationalité française|website=Europe 1|date=15 March 2019 }}</ref> Thiago speaks Italian, English, French, Spanish and Portuguese.<ref>{{cite web |last=Egorov |first=Grigorii |title=Thiago Silva explains why language barrier won't be issue for him at Chelsea |url=https://tribuna.com/en/news/chelsea-2020-09-23-thiago-silva-explains-why-language-barrier-wont-be-issue-for-him-at-chelsea/ |access-date=5 February 2023 |website=Tribuna |date=23 September 2020}}</ref>

Produced by [[Fulwell 73]], [[FIFA]] released ''Captains'' in 2022, an eight-part sports [[docuseries]] following six national team captains in their respective [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification]] campaigns.<ref name=":02">{{cite web |date=12 April 2022 |title=FIFA launches FIFA+ to bring free football entertainment to fans everywhere |url=https://www.fifa.com/about-fifa/organisation/media-releases/fifa-launches-fifa-to-bring-free-football-entertainment-to-fans-everywhere |access-date=17 October 2022 |website=[[FIFA]]}}</ref> Silva, representing Brazil, starred alongside [[Luka Modrić]] ([[Croatia national football team|Croatia]]), [[Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang]] ([[Gabon national football team|Gabon]]), [[Andre Blake]] ([[Jamaica national football team|Jamaica]]), [[Hassan Maatouk]] ([[Lebanon national football team|Lebanon]]) and [[Brian Kaltak]] ([[Vanuatu national football team|Vanuatu]]).<ref name=":02" /> It was released by [[Netflix]] and also shown on FIFA's own streaming platform, [[FIFA+]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zaazaa |first=Bassam |date=14 October 2022 |title=Lebanon's captain Hassan Maatouk to star in Netflix football documentary |url=https://www.arabnews.com/node/2181136/sport |access-date=17 October 2022 |website=[[Arab News]]}}</ref>

'''Stéphane Henchoz''' ({{IPA|fr|ɑ̃ʃo}}; born 7 September 1974) is a Swiss [[association football|football]] coach and a former professional player who played as a [[centre-back]], most notably for the English club [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/intligen/england/barclays-premier-league/2011-12/blackburn-rovers/304/spieler_stephane-henchoz.html | title = Henchoz, Stephane | language = de | publisher = [[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] | access-date = 20 August 2011 | archive-date = 2 December 2017 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20171202115815/http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/intligen/england/barclays-premier-league/2011-12/blackburn-rovers/304/spieler_stephane-henchoz.html | url-status = dead }}</ref> He was [[Cap (sport)|capped]] 72 times and played for the [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland national team]] from his debut in 1993, and played at [[UEFA Euro 1996|Euro 1996]] and [[UEFA Euro 2004|Euro 2004]].

==Club career==
===Early career===
Born in [[Billens-Hennens|Billens]], Switzerland, Henchoz first came to notice playing in the German [[Bundesliga]] for [[Hamburger SV]].

===Blackburn Rovers===
In June 1997, he turned down an opportunity to join [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], instead signing for [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] for a fee of £3 million.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.thefreelibrary.com/ROVERS+GRAB+HEAD+HENCHO.-a065303635 | title=Rovers Grab Head Honcho | work=The Mirror | publisher=MGN | date=17 June 1997 | access-date=14 March 2012 | archive-date=5 March 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305093437/http://www.thefreelibrary.com/ROVERS+GRAB+HEAD+HENCHO.-a065303635 | url-status=live }}</ref> Henchoz enjoyed a very successful debut Premiership season as Rovers finished sixth in 1997–98, although they were then relegated at the end of the [[1998–99 in English football|1998–99]] season. Henchoz, however, remained in the Premiership, after being purchased for £3.5 million by [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]].

===Liverpool===
At Liverpool, Henchoz became a regular member of the first team during his five-and-a-half-year stay at Anfield. Henchoz proved to be an inspirational signing and was popular with the Liverpool fans. He formed an effective central defensive partnership with [[Sami Hyypiä]]. This partnership played an important part in Liverpool's historic cup treble in 2001, although it was Henchoz's clumsy challenge on [[Martin O'Connor (footballer)|Martin O'Connor]] in the 90th minute of the [[Football League Cup|League Cup]] final against [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] that led to extra time (the match itself was only settled on penalties).<ref>{{cite news |title=Blues shot down as Liverpool lift cup |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/worthington_cup/1187654.stm |access-date=6 March 2019 |work=BBC Sport |date=25 February 2001 |archive-date=7 May 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090507180548/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/worthington_cup/1187654.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Henchoz is also remembered for inadvertently blocking a goalbound Thierry Henry shot with his arm in the 17th minute of that year's [[FA Cup]] final, Liverpool then went on to win the match with two [[Michael Owen]] finishes.<ref>{{cite news |title=Owen shatters Arsenal in Cup final |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/fa_cup/1324699.stm |access-date=6 March 2019 |work=BBC Sport |date=12 May 2001 |archive-date=21 May 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190521180304/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/fa_cup/1324699.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

His last two seasons were interrupted due to spells of injury, but he still surpassed the 200 mark of games for Liverpool in 2003–04.

With injury problems and Gerard Houllier preferring [[Igor Bišćan]] at centre half, Henchoz became something of a bit part player appearing as an occasional right back. Eventually, the Henchoz-Hyypiä partnership was rekindled in [[2003–04 in English football|2003–04]], helping Liverpool to fourth place in the league.

===Celtic===
When [[Rafael Benítez]] replaced [[Gérard Houllier]] as manager, his decision to try versatile English defender [[Jamie Carragher]] in partnership with Hyypiä spelled an end to Henchoz's [[Anfield]] career. Carragher, previously employed as a full-back, was a revelation at centre back and Henchoz consequently joined [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] on a six-month contract in January 2005.<ref>{{cite news |title=Henchoz completes Celtic switch |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/c/celtic/4144899.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=29 January 2005 |access-date=25 March 2015 }}</ref>

===Wigan Athletic===
Upon the expiration of his Celtic contract, Henchoz opted to move back to the Premier League, signing a one-year contract with newly promoted [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/w/wigan_athletic/4699447.stm|title=Henchoz signs 12-month Wigan deal|date=26 July 2005|access-date=1 September 2020|archive-date=10 December 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221210113024/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/w/wigan_athletic/4699447.stm|url-status=live}}</ref> He made 26 league appearances during the [[2005–06 in English football|2005–06 season]] as the club exceeded expectations with a top half finish. Henchoz also started for Wigan in the [[2006 Football League Cup Final]].

===Return to Blackburn Rovers===
Henchoz left Wigan after only a year, signing a contract until the end of the [[2006–07 in English football|2006–07 season]] with Blackburn Rovers. He was used sparingly during the season to fill in for injuries, but performed suitably. His second spell at [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn]] came to an end on 19 May, when he was released by [[Mark Hughes]].

Henchoz ended his career on 13 October 2008.

==International career==
Henchoz earned 72 caps for the [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland national team]] from his debut in 1993. He played for the country at [[UEFA Euro 1996|Euro 96]] and [[UEFA Euro 2004|Euro 2004]]. He was expected to play in the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]], but due to health problems he retired from international football on 31 March 2006.

==Coaching career==
[[File:Stéphane Henchoz FC Sion.jpg|thumb|Stéphane Henchoz on the touchline for [[FC Sion]]]]
After retiring, Henchoz became manager of [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]]'s U18 team which he was until June 2009.<ref>[https://footballbh.net/2019/03/23/stephane-henchoz-xamax-swiss-super-league-tactical-analysis-statistics/ How is Stephane Henchoz doing in charge of Neuchatel Xamax?] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190708000309/https://footballbh.net/2019/03/23/stephane-henchoz-xamax-swiss-super-league-tactical-analysis-statistics/ |date=8 July 2019 }}, footballbh.net, 23 March 2019</ref> He then became manager of [[FC Bulle]] for the 2009–10 season.<ref>[https://www.rts.ch/sport/football/suisse/1361482-stephane-henchoz-a-la-tete-du-fc-bulle.html Stéphane Henchoz à la tête du FC Bulle] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190708000305/https://www.rts.ch/sport/football/suisse/1361482-stephane-henchoz-a-la-tete-du-fc-bulle.html |date=8 July 2019 }}, rts.ch, 25 June 2010</ref>

In December 2015, he was appointed assistant manager of [[Neuchâtel Xamax FCS|Neuchâtel Xamax]].{{citation needed|date=January 2025}} On 6 February 2019, the club announced, that they had sacked [[Michel Decastel]] and Henchoz would take charge of the club for the rest of the season.<ref>[http://www.xamax.ch/news-detail.php?idnews=2769 Stéphane Henchoz remplace Michel Decastel à la tête de Neuchâtel Xamax FCS] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190331154214/http://www.xamax.ch/news-detail.php?idnews=2769 |date=31 March 2019 }}, xamax.ch, 6 February 2019</ref> At the end of March 2019, the club confirmed that Henchoz would leave his position at the end of the season.

On 27 May 2019, Henchoz was appointed manager of [[FC Sion|Sion]] for the upcoming 2019–20 season.<ref>[https://eu.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/2019/05/27/former-liverpool-defender-henchoz-to-coach-sion/39518973/ Former Liverpool defender Henchoz to coach Sion] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201108002633/https://eu.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/2019/05/27/former-liverpool-defender-henchoz-to-coach-sion/39518973/ |date=8 November 2020 }}, usatoday.com, 27 May 2019</ref> He resigned on 4 November 2019 following a 3–0 loss to [[FC St. Gallen|St. Gallen]], which was the fifth loss in six league games.<ref>{{cite press release|publisher=[[FC Sion]]|url=http://www.fc-sion.ch/index.php?r=site/text&id=3088&culture=fr|title=COMMUNIQUÉ OFFICIEL DE STÉPHANE HENCHOZ|date=4 November 2019|language=fr}}</ref>

In July 2020, he returned to Neuchâtel Xamax.<ref>{{cite web |title=Xamax setzt ab sofort wieder auf Henchoz |url=https://www.srf.ch/sport/fussball/super-league/joel-magnin-muss-posten-raeumen-xamax-setzt-ab-sofort-wieder-auf-henchoz |website=SRF |access-date=17 July 2020 |language=de |date=5 July 2020 |archive-date=8 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200708040551/https://www.srf.ch/sport/fussball/super-league/joel-magnin-muss-posten-raeumen-xamax-setzt-ab-sofort-wieder-auf-henchoz |url-status=live }}</ref>

'''Mathieu Pierre Flamini''' (born 7 March 1984) is a French [[Entrepreneurship|entrepreneur]] and former professional [[Association football|footballer]]. A [[midfielder]], he played for French side [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]], English sides [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] and [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]], Italian side [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] and Spanish side [[Getafe CF|Getafe]]. At international level, he was capped by the [[France national football team|France national team]] on three occasions.

Flamini is a co-founder of [[GF Biochemicals]], the first company in the world able to mass-produce [[levulinic acid]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.ft.com/content/9ce7490c-184e-11e6-bb7d-ee563a5a1cc1|title=From the pitch to the boardroom|last1=Stacey|first1=Kiran|date=16 May 2016|last2=Correspondent|first2=Energy|newspaper=Financial Times|issn=0307-1766|access-date=13 September 2016}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Marseille===
Born in [[Marseille]], Flamini was a youth team player for his local professional club [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]]. He made his debut for the senior team on 20 December 2003 in the 1–0 victory over [[Toulouse FC|Toulouse]]. He impressed the team as a hardworking midfield player and played 14 times for the club. However, it was his performances in Marseille's [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]] campaign that brought him to the attention of the football world, including the [[2003–04 UEFA Cup|2–0 semi-final victory]] over [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]]. He then started in the [[2004 UEFA Cup Final|Final]] in [[Gothenburg]], a match Spanish club [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] won 2–0. Due to his age, however, Marseille was later unable to offer him a long-term professional [[Association football contracts|contract]].

===Arsenal===
On 23 July 2004, Flamini signed a professional contract for English club [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], rejecting Marseille's long-term senior contract offer to which he had already verbally agreed. Soon after the incident, then-Marseille manager [[José Anigo]] stated, "This is a beautiful treason. He used me."<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.eurosport.fr/football/transferts1/2004/flamini-file-a-l-anglaise_sto616272/story.shtml | publisher = Eurosport | title = Flamini file à l'anglaise |language = fr |date = 22 July 2004 | access-date = 21 June 2012 }}</ref> Arsenal were eventually ordered by The Dispute Resolution Chamber of FIFA to pay Marseille a compensation fee of €480 000 for Flamini.<ref>{{cite news|last=Baron|first=Thomas (15 October 2010)|url=http://www.eurosport.fr/football/transferts/2014-2015/transferts-arsenal-flaire-le-bon-coup-stephane-sparagna-olympique-de-marseille_sto4438970/story.shtml|title=Transferts – Arsenal flaire le bon coup Stéphane Sparagna (Olympique de Marseille)|language=fr|website=Euro Sport |access-date=17 May 2016}}</ref>

Flamini made his Arsenal debut in the 1–4 win at [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] on 15 August 2004. In his first season, he was typically used as a utility player, starting only nine games but used as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] in 12. The following season saw him filling in for a number of injured players, but again unable to command a first team place in his favoured position. He scored his first Arsenal goal on 11 May 2005 in a 7–0 home win against Everton, scoring the seventh goal, the team's last-ever goal scored in their traditional red and white kit at [[Arsenal Stadium|Highbury]].

In the [[2006–07 Arsenal F.C. season|2006–07 season]], Flamini scored the winning goal against [[NK Dinamo Zagreb|Dinamo Zagreb]] in the qualifying stages of the [[2006–07 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]]. He also scored important goals against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] and [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] in the Premier League. Despite these important goals, however, he remained unsatisfied with his "utility player" role at the club and in April 2007, he admitted that he would most likely be leaving Arsenal in the summer. Flamini, however, turned down a proposed [[pound sterling|£]]3m move to [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] and remained with the team.

Flamini started in central midfield for Arsenal's first match of the [[2007–08 Premier League]] season due to the absence of [[Gilberto Silva]] and [[Abou Diaby]]. During Arsenal's [[2007–08 Arsenal F.C. season|2007–08 campaign]], he struck up a strong partnership with [[Cesc Fàbregas]], keeping Gilberto out of the starting XI with displays widely regarded by Arsenal fans as a vast improvement on those during his previous years at the club. Flamini enjoyed a generally good rapport with Arsenal's fans, who provided him with his own [[football chant|song]], an adaptation of the theme tune to British television programme ''[[The Sweeney]]''. On 29 January 2008, he scored an extraordinary {{convert|25|yd|adj=on}} strike in Arsenal's 3–0 win over [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] in the Premier League. He played on 8 April 2008, a [[UEFA Champions League]] match in which Arsenal were knocked out by English rival Liverpool. After the match, he was reported injured and it proved to be his last match for Arsenal.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=738435.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080411110625/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=738435.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=11 April 2008|title=Flamini out for three weeks|agency=AFP  |date=10 April 2008|access-date=15 May 2008}}</ref> In April 2009, he stated in an interview that he is still an Arsenal fan and that he has no hard feelings towards the club: "Arsenal are in my heart and they will be in my heart for ever," he said. "I will always be an Arsenal fan and leaving was not easy."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/a/arsenal/8010235.stm|title=Mathieu Flamini interview |date=23 April 2009|work=BBC Sport  |access-date=23 April 2009}}</ref>

===Milan===
[[File:David Beckham of AC Milan, April 19, 2009.jpg|right|thumb|200px|Flamini with [[David Beckham]] and [[Filippo Inzaghi]] in action for Milan, [[Goal celebration|celebrating]] a [[Goal (sport)|goal]] against [[Torino F.C.|Torino]] in the [[Serie A]], at the [[San Siro]].]]
Flamini signed a contract with Italian club [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] on 5 May 2008.<ref name="sports">{{cite news|url=http://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/young-gunner-flamini-agrees--to-join-milan-1360892.html|title=Young Gunner Flamini agrees to join Milan|work=Independent |location=UK |access-date=28 April 2008|first=Jason|last=Burt|date=28 April 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite news| url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/a/arsenal/7383314.stm |work=BBC News  | title=Flamini seals switch to AC Milan | date=5 May 2008 | access-date=12 May 2010}}</ref> Flamini wore the number 84 on his shirt to represent his year of birth.

He made his Serie A debut on 30 August 2008 in a 2–1 loss to [[Bologna F.C. 1909|Bologna]].<ref>[http://www.serieatalk.com/bologna-ruin-ronaldinho-debut/254 Bologna ruin Ronaldinho debut]. serieatalk.com.</ref> Initially, Flamini did not enjoy the number of starts or appearances for the Italian team, and was regarded as a [[utility player]] at Milan. Nevertheless, injuries to other players and his consistent good form helped him to cement a starting place at [[San Siro]]. With Milan failing to find a stable defence and a lack of a fit, consistent and reliable right back, [[Gianluca Zambrotta]] was switched to the left flank to help Flamini develop as a tenacious right back. After stating that his preferred position is in the midfield, Milan re-deployed him as a defensive midfielder.

Flamini saw limited playing time towards the end of [[2009–10 A.C. Milan season|2009–10 season]] due to the great form of club captain [[Massimo Ambrosini]]. In the following season, Flamini became an important asset of the team that would win its 18th ''[[scudetto]]'', playing many games as starter and scoring two goals against [[A.S. Bari|Bari]] and [[Bologna F.C. 1909|Bologna]], respectively. After playing as a rotation role in the [[2010–11 A.C. Milan season|2010–11 season]], he injured himself in a pre-season training session, suffering a serious knee injury which required an operation.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 30, 2011 |orig-date= |title=Milan's Flamini to miss group stage with knee injury |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01f4-0e796b24f70b-073d32d216a5-1000--milan-s-flamini-to-miss-group-stage-with-knee-injury/ |website=UEFA}}</ref> Flamini spent the entire [[2011–12 A.C. Milan season|2011–12 season]] out.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Prindiville |first=Mike |date=2013-08-29 |title=Arsenal re-sign French midfielder Mathieu Flamini from AC Milan |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/soccer/news/arsenal-re-sign-french-midfielder-mathieu-flamini-from-ac-milan |access-date=2025-05-29 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

On 20 June 2012, it was confirmed by the club that he had left following the expiration of his [[Association football contracts|contract]], as they had ended negotiations with the player, and so he became a [[free agent]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Arsenal sign their former midfielder Mathieu Flamini on a free transfer |website=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |date=29 August 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230309103206/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/arsenal/10273980/Arsenal-sign-their-former-midfielder-Mathieu-Flamini-on-a-free-transfer.html |archive-date=2023-03-09 |url-status=live |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/arsenal/10273980/Arsenal-sign-their-former-midfielder-Mathieu-Flamini-on-a-free-transfer.html}}</ref> Two weeks later, Flamini and [[Adriano Galliani]] reached a new agreement for a one-year contract, with the Frenchman taking a significant cut in his wages.<ref name="Milan confirm Flamini U-turn">{{cite news|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1116167/mathieu-flamini-signs-one-year-extension-with-ac-milan?cc=5901|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120629035826/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1116167/mathieu-flamini-signs-one-year-extension-with-ac-milan?cc=5901|url-status=dead|archive-date=29 June 2012|title=Milan confirm Flamini U-turn|work=[[ESPN]]|access-date=26 June 2012|date=26 June 2012}}</ref> On 7 April 2013, Flamini scored his first goal of the season, and Milan's second of the game, in a 2–2 draw against [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/ac-milan-tops-fiorentina-serie-a-1.1386831|title=AC Milan tops Fiorentina: Serie A|publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation]]|access-date=7 April 2013|date=7 April 2013}}</ref>

===Return to Arsenal===
[[File:Mathieu Flamini (19468174744).jpg|thumb|right|200px|Flamini in 2015]]
Flamini began training with Arsenal midway in early August, with the reason to "solely maintain fitness" with a view to signing for a club in England. Immediately it sparked media attention with claims rising that he would soon sign for Arsenal, but these reports were shunned by many journalists, pointing out that many other ex-Arsenal players had returned to train with Arsenal, including club legends [[Robert Pires]] and [[Thierry Henry]].

Flamini, however, did indeed sign for Arsenal on 29 August 2013 and became Arsenal's second acquisition of the summer, after [[Yaya Sanogo]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Club confirms Mathieu Flamini signing|url=http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/mathieu-flamini-rejoins-arsenal|publisher=Arsenal F.C|date=29 August 2013 |access-date=29 August 2013}}</ref> He made his returning debut on 1 September at [[Emirates Stadium]] against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]], coming on for [[Jack Wilshere]] and helping the team secure a 1–0 win. His performances after signing were lauded by both critics and fans alike, and had featured in all of Arsenal's [[Premier League]], [[Football League Cup]] and [[UEFA|European]] games since, with many seeing his signing, and his combative style of play, as one of the key reasons for Arsenal's excellent early season form.<ref name="Arsenal 1-0 Tottenham">{{cite news|title=Arsenal 1–0 Tottenham|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23831033|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|work=[[BBC]]|date=1 September 2013|access-date=7 September 2013|last=Magowan|first=Alistair}}</ref> He scored his first goal in his second spell at Arsenal on 30 November, the second in a 0–3 away win at [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]]. He has also scored in a crucial 1–1 draw against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] after a run of bad form from Arsenal, helping the club rejuvenate and achieve an eventual top four league finish. At the start of Arsenal's [[2013–14 FA Cup]] run, Flamini expressed his desire to win the Cup, having been left out of the squad when Arsenal won the [[2005 FA Cup Final]].<ref>{{cite web
|url=http://news.arseblog.com/2014/01/flamini-eyes-second-fa-cup-triumph/
|title=Flamini eyes second FA Cup triumph
|publisher=arseblog.com
|date=4 January 2014
|access-date=22 December 2014
|archive-date=8 February 2022
|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220208072335/https://news.arseblog.com/2014/01/flamini-eyes-second-fa-cup-triumph/
|url-status=dead
}}</ref> Arsenal went on to win the tournament, though Flamini was an unused substitute in the [[2014 FA Cup Final|Final]], also remaining on the substitutes' bench when Arsenal repeated the feat, becoming [[2014–15 FA Cup|FA Cup]] champions again in [[2015 FA Cup Final|2015]].

On 23 September 2015, Flamini earned his first start of the [[2015–16 Arsenal F.C. season|2015–16 season]] in the [[2015–16 Football League Cup|Football League Cup]] third round tie against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]]. He scored both of Arsenal's goals with a Man of the Match performance.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/sep/23/tottenham-arsenal-capital-one-cup-match-report|title=Arsenal's Mathieu Flamini rediscovers scoring flair to down Tottenham|last=Lane|first=David Hytner at White Hart|date=23 September 2015|newspaper=The Guardian|language=en-GB|issn=0261-3077|access-date=9 September 2016}}</ref>

===Late career===
Flamini signed as a free-agent for [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] at the beginning of the 2016–17 season,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Flamini Joins Crystal Palace|url=https://www.cpfc.co.uk/news/2016/september/flamini-joins-crystal-palace-/|website=cpfc.co.uk |date=8 September 2016 |access-date=8 September 2016}}</ref> and released by the club at the season's end.<ref>{{cite news|title=Crystal Palace release Fraizer Campbell, Mathieu Flamini and Joe Ledley|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11706/10910054/crystal-palace-release-fraizer-campbell-mathieu-flamini-and-joe-ledley|access-date=9 June 2017|publisher=Sky Sport|date=9 June 2017}}</ref> He joined [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] in February 2018,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Flamini en el Getafe|url=http://getafecf.com/Noticia/tabid/137/Article/5061/Flamini-en-el-Getafe.aspx|website=getafecf.com |date=2 February 2018 |access-date=2 February 2018}}</ref> making eight appearances in [[2017–18 La Liga|La Liga]] before leaving the club at the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title= Mathieu Flamini laissé libre par Getafe |url= https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Mathieu-flamini-laisse-libre-par-getafe/917388 |trans-title= Mathieu Flamini leaves Getafe |website= [[L'Équipe]] |language=fr |date= 30 June 2018 |access-date=5 July 2018}}</ref> He rejoined Getafe in December 2018,<ref>{{cite news|title=El Getafe vuelve a fichar a Flamini|url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/laliga/getafe-vuelve-fichar-flamini-7209419|access-date=20 December 2018|publisher=Sport|date=18 December 2018}}</ref> until his contract expired in July 2019 and officially retired from football in 2020.

==International career==
Flamini accepted his first call up to [[France national football team|France]] by coach [[Raymond Domenech]] for a [[Exhibition game|friendly]] against [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] at the [[Stade de France]] on 7 February 2007 after [[Jérémy Toulalan]] was ruled out due to injury. He later made his international debut in a friendly against [[Morocco national football team|Morocco]] on 16 November 2007 as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]].<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120904131613/http://www.fff.fr/compint/match.php?compet=3641&match=12539&r=90|title=France 2–1 Maroc}}, fff.fr, 16 November 2007, accessed 17 November 2007.</ref>

==Style of play==
A combative, energetic, tactically intelligent, and tenacious [[midfielder]],<ref name="Arsenal 1-0 Tottenham"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cinquantamila.it/storyTellerArticolo.php?storyId=0000000158715 |title="Abbiamo cercato di coprire tutte le carenze e sulla carta ci siamo riusciti. Se Ronaldinho porta qualità, Antonini e Zambrotta portano dinamismo, Flamini intelligenza tattica, Borriello forza e potenza" |publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport |language=it |author1=Marco Pasotto |date=17 July 2008 |access-date=19 November 2018 }}</ref> according to Arsenal manager [[Arsène Wenger]], Flamini was a player with a fantastic work rate, good ball-winning ability and great mentality; he could play anywhere across midfield, in the [[Midfielder#Central midfielder|centre]] as a [[Midfielder#Box-to-box midfielder|box-to-box]] or [[Midfielder#Defensive midfielder|defensive midfielder]], or on either [[Midfielder#Winger|flank]] as a cover at [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|full-back]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23804580|work=bbc.co.uk/sport|title=Mathieu Flamini: Midfielder returns to Arsenal on free transfer|publisher=BBC|last=Ornstein|first=David|access-date=29 August 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/9/england/2008/06/27/753456/english-debate-who-will-anchor-arsenals-midfield|title=English Debate: Who Will Anchor Arsenal's Midfield?|publisher=Goal.com|author1=Alan Dawson|date=27 June 2008|access-date=7 September 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/live-scores/news/y=2008/m=5/news=milan-confirm-flamini-deal-760551.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160809161053/http://www.fifa.com/live-scores/news/y=2008/m=5/news=milan-confirm-flamini-deal-760551.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=9 August 2016|title=Milan confirm Flamini deal|publisher=FIFA.com|date=5 May 2008|access-date=7 September 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2299045/Adebayor-warns-Arsenal-as-Flamini-nears-exit.html|title=Adebayor warns Arsenal as Flamini nears exit|publisher=The Telegraph|author1=Steve Wilson|date=1 May 2008|access-date=7 September 2016}}</ref>{{Excessive citations inline|date=March 2026}}

==Business career==
Flamini is a partner of [[GF Biochemicals]], a leading global producer of [[levulinic acid]] and derivatives. He has stated<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2016-02-19/arsenal-s-flamini-takes-biochemical-battle-against-oil-to-u-s|title=Arsenal Star Mathieu Flamini Buys Stake in U.S. Green Chemical Firm|website=Bloomberg.com|date=19 February 2016 }}</ref> that “we founded GFBiochemicals with the ambition of finding sustainable alternatives to oil-based products”. Levulinic acid includes<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-36037874|title=Mathieu Flamini: Arsenal's biochemical midfielder|work=BBC News|date=14 April 2016}}</ref> grass or woodchips, and can be used in plastics, solvents, fuels and the pharmaceutical industry. Levulinic acid has been identified by the [[United States Department of Energy|U.S. Department of Energy]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ascension-publishing.com/BIZ/HD49.pdf|title=U.S Department of Energy|website=Ascension Publishing.com}}</ref> as one of the 12 molecules that can help unlock a “greener” world.

In addition to GFBiochemicals’ established presence in the Netherlands<ref name="Bioful">{{cite web|url=https://www.bloombergquint.com/technology/2017/03/24/footballer-s-green-chemical-company-signs-deal-for-biorefinery|title=Footballer's Green Chemical Company Signs Deal for Biorefinery|website=Bloombergquint.com|date=24 March 2017 }}</ref> and headquarters in Italy, Flamini has named<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.newstatesman.com/microsites/energy/2016/12/mathieu-flamini-footballer-tackling-climate-change|title=Mathieu Flamini: the footballer tackling climate change|website=Newstatesman.com|date=2 December 2016 }}</ref> China and Brazil as potential new markets for expansion.
In 2016, GFBiochemicals<ref name="Bioful" /> fully controls the Segetis, the leading producer of levulinic acid derivatives, in a move towards downstream integration. Segitis was previously owned by [[SABIC|Sabic]], [[DSM (company)|DSM]], and [[Khosla Ventures]], among other entities, and has invested<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.italy24.ilsole24ore.com/art/business-and-economy/2016-02-18/gfbiochemicals-acquires-one-of-its-competitors-da-passare-204154.php?uuid=ACJPqjXC|title=Italy's Caserta-based biochemical company to buy world leader in levulinic acid derivatives|website=Italy24.Ilsole24ore.com}}</ref> in R&D over the past decade. In 2017, GFBiochemicals announced<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2017-03-24/footballer-s-green-chemical-company-signs-deal-for-biorefinery|title=A Footballer Wants to Turn the World Green|website=Bloomberg.com|date=24 March 2017 }}</ref> that it will build a cellulosic biorefinery in the US, in partnership with biotech company American Process.

Flamini was also part of the team that created BIOCIRCE (Bioeconomy in the [[Circular economy]]),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://masterbiocirce.com/|title=MasterBiocirce|website=masterbiocirce.com/}}</ref> Europe’s first master's degree dedicated to promoting bioeconomy education. It was launched in collaboration with Italian bank [[Intesa Sanpaolo]], Novamont (a producer of bioplastics), and the Universities of [[University of Naples Federico II|Naples]], [[University of Turin|Turin]], [[University of Milano-Bicocca|Milano-Bicocca]] and [[University of Bologna|Bologna]].
In addition, Flamini co-founded The BioJournal<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.thebiojournal.com/|title=thebiojournal|website=thebiojournal.com/}}</ref> the world’s first e-magazine devoted entirely to the bio world and eco-sustainability and managed by Italian environmental journalist [[Mario Bonaccorso]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.52-insights.com/news/crystal-palace-footballer-mathieu-flamini-kicks-off-first-eco-sustainability-portal/.|title = Crystal Palace Footballer Mathieu Flamini Kicks off First Eco-sustainability Portal| date=7 October 2016 }}</ref>
Flamini was also part of the Environmental Excellence Committee for the candidature of Paris as the location for the [[2024 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1038485/paris-2024-unveils-environmental-excellence-committee|title=Paris 2024 unveils Environmental Excellence Committee|website=Inside The Games.biz|date=15 June 2016 }}</ref>

In 2015, Flamini was named one of People of the Year by ''[[NME]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nme.com/blogs/nme-blogs/mathieu-flamini-nme-people-of-the-year-2015-12854|title=Mathieu Flamini – NME People Of The Year 2015|website=NME.com|date=18 December 2015}}</ref>

== Fortune ==

In 2018, Mathieu Flamini denied reports that valued his personal fortune, or his company GF Biochemicals, at 30 billion euros. He explained that the figure represented the estimated size of the entire levulinic acid market that the company sought to enter using its technologies.
