'''Salih Özcan''' (born 11 January 1998) is a professional [[footballer]] who plays as a [[defensive midfielder]] for the [[Süper Lig]] club [[Beşiktaş J.K.|Beşiktaş]]. Born in Germany, he plays for the [[Turkey national football team|Turkey national team]].<ref>{{WorldFootball.net|salih-oezcan}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Köln===
Born in Germany, Özcan is of Turkish descent as he was born into a Turkish family. Özcan spent the majority of his youth career in [[1. FC Köln]]'s youth system. He first featured in 1. FC Köln's first team in September 2016 in a [[Bundesliga]] match against [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://fc.de/fc-info/news/detailseite/details/drei-punkte-auf-schalke/ |title=Drei Punkte auf Schalke |website=1.FC Köln |language=de |access-date=24 May 2018 |archive-date=5 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230405233513/https://fc.de/fc-info/news/detailseite/details/drei-punkte-auf-schalke/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> During the [[2017–18 Bundesliga|2017–18 season]] he consistently started in central midfield. He scored his first league goal on 2 September 2018 in a [[2. Bundesliga]] match against [[FC St. Pauli]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ndr.de/sport/fussball/St-Pauli-verliert-Torspektakel-gegen-Koeln,pauli5392.html |title=St. Pauli verliert Torspektakel gegen Köln |website=NDR.de |language=de |access-date=2 September 2018 }}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

In 2017, Özcan was awarded the golden [[Fritz Walter Medal]] for the best U19 player in Germany.<ref name="FWA">{{cite web|url=https://www.ksta.de/sport/1-fc-koeln/auszeichnung-vor-laenderspiel-fc-talent-oeczan-mit-fritz-walter-medaille-ausgezeichnet-28359238 |title=Auszeichnung vor Länderspiel FC-Talent: Öczan mit Fritz-Walter-Medaille ausgezeichnet |website=Kölner Stadtanzeiger |date=5 September 2017 |language=de |access-date=24 May 2018 }}</ref>

====Loan to Holstein Kiel====
[[File:SalihÖzcan.jpg|thumb|Özcan at [[Holstein Kiel]] in 2019]]
On 23 August 2019, Özcan joined [[Holstein Kiel]] on loan until the end of 2019–20 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.holstein-kiel.de/allgemein/die-ksv-verpflichtet-salih-oezcan-vom-1-fc-koeln/|title=Die KSV verpflichtet Özcan vom 1. FC Köln|publisher=Holstein Kiel|language=German|date=23 August 2019|accessdate=23 August 2019|archive-date=23 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190823213408/https://www.holstein-kiel.de/allgemein/die-ksv-verpflichtet-salih-oezcan-vom-1-fc-koeln/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Three days later, he made his debut with the team as a starter in a [[2. Bundesliga]] away match against [[FC St. Pauli]], which ended in a 2–1 defeat.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/match/_/gameId/548637/holstein-kiel-st-pauli |title=St. Pauli 2–1 Holstein Kiel |publisher=ESPN |date=26 August 2019 }}</ref>

====Return to Köln====
[[File:2021-08-08 FC Carl Zeiss Jena gegen 1. FC Köln (DFB-Pokal) by Sandro Halank–154.jpg|thumb|Özcan playing for [[1. FC Köln]] in 2021]]
On 29 June 2021, in spite of speculations about a possible transfer, the club announced that Özcan had signed a new two-year contract with Köln.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fc.de/fc-info/news/detailseite/details/fc-verlaengert-mit-salih-oezcan/|title=FC verlängert mit Salih Özcan|access-date=2021-06-29|website=[[1. FC Köln]]|language=de|archive-date=19 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230719051553/https://fc.de/fc-info/news/detailseite/details/fc-verlaengert-mit-salih-oezcan/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Borussia Dortmund===
On 23 May 2022, it was reported that Özcan would join [[Borussia Dortmund]] for the [[2022–23 Bundesliga|2022–23 season]] and that he would sign a contract with the club until 2026. The German sports magazine ''[[Kicker (sports magazine)|kicker]]'' estimated the transfer fee to be €5 million.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.kicker.de/vierter-bvb-neuzugang-perfekt-oezcan-kommt-vom-1-fc-koeln-902841/artikel |title=Vierter BVB-Neuzugang perfekt: Özcan kommt vom 1. FC Köln |website=kicker |language=de}}</ref>

On 27 August 2022, he made his debut with the team as a starter in a [[Bundesliga]] match against [[Hertha BSC]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sport.sky.de/fussball/hertha-bsc-vs-dortmund/spielbericht/465788 |title=Hertha BSC - BVB: Borussia Dortmund gewinnt in Berlin |publisher=Sky Sport |language=de |date=27 August 2022 }}</ref> On 6 September 2022, he made his continental debut with the team in a [[UEFA Champions League]] match against [[F.C. Copenhagen|København]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/match/_/gameId/652587/fc-k%C3%B8benhavn-borussia-dortmund |title=Borussia Dortmund 3–0 F.C. København |publisher=ESPN |date=6 September 2022 }}</ref>

====Loan to Wolfsburg====
On 28 August 2024, Özcan moved on loan to [[VfL Wolfsburg]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=VfL Wolfsburg|url=https://www.vfl-wolfsburg.de/newsdetails/news-detail/detail/news/leihe-vom-bvb|title=Leihe vom BVB|trans-title=Loan from BVB|date=28 August 2024|access-date=28 August 2024|language=de}}</ref> Three days later, he made his debut with Wolfsburg in a 2–0 away win against his former club Holstein Kiel.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.vfl-wolfsburg.de/en/newsdetails/news-detail/detail/news/comfortable-away-win-2-1 |title=Comfortable away win |publisher=VfL Wolfsburg |date=31 August 2024 }}</ref>

====Return to Borussia Dortmund====
In late January 2025, Özcan was recalled to Borussia Dortmund following the long-term injury of [[Felix Nmecha]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bvb.de/de/de/aktuelles/news/news.html/2025/1/28/BVB-holt-Salih-Oezcan-zurueck.html |title=BVB holt Salih Özcan zurück |publisher=Borussia Dortmund |date=28 January 2025 }}</ref> In March 2026, the club announced that his contract, which was due to expire at the end of the season, would not be renewed.<ref>{{cite web |last=Pinnow |first=Kevin |url=https://www.ruhrnachrichten.de/bvb/bvb-umbruch-lars-ricken-bestaetigt-aus-salih-oezcan-niklas-suele-kader-zukunft-w1166478-2002002245/ |title=Exklusiv: Ricken bestätigt BVB-Aus für Özcan und Süle Dortmund bastelt am Kader der Zukunft |publisher=Ruhr Nachrichten |language=de |date=13 March 2026 }}</ref> He left the club at the end of the 2025–26 season, with his final game being on May 8 in a 3–2 win over [[Eintracht Frankfurt]] where he came off the bench in the 78th minute for [[Marcel Sabitzer]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/747008/eintracht-frankfurt-borussia-dortmund|title=Dortmund 3-2 Frankfurt (May 8, 2026) Final Score - ESPN|date=May 8, 2026|work=[[ESPN]]}}</ref>

===Beşiktaş===
On 9 July 2026, Özcan joined the [[Süper Lig]] club [[Beşiktaş J.K.|Beşiktaş]] on a permanent three-year deal with an option for another year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bjk.com.tr/tr/mobil/haber?news_id=94700 |title=Beşiktaşımıza Hoş Geldin Salih Özcan |publisher=[[Besiktas J.K.]]|date=9 July 2026|access-date=9 July 2026|language=tr}}</ref>

==International career==
Özcan was eligible for both the [[Turkey national football team|Turkish]] and [[Germany national football team|German]] national teams,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.express.de/sport/fussball/1--fc-koeln/mavraj---oezcan-das-geheimnis-einer-besonderen-fc-freundschaft-25192618-seite3 |title=1. FC Köln: Mergim Mavraj und Salih Özcan sprechen über ihre Freundschaft | Express.de |access-date=5 February 2017 |archive-date=11 January 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170111074358/http://www.express.de/sport/fussball/1--fc-koeln/mavraj---oezcan-das-geheimnis-einer-besonderen-fc-freundschaft-25192618-seite3 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and played for Germany's youth teams.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/datencenter/personen/salih-oezcan/spieler|title=Salih Özcan – Spielerprofil|website=DFB Datencenter}}</ref> He played his last game for [[Germany national under-21 football team|Germany U21]] on 6 June 2021, starting in the [[2021 UEFA European Under-21 Championship final|UEFA European Under-21 Championship final]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Germany U21 1-0 Portugal U21 (Jun 6, 2021) Game Analysis |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/590548 |access-date=2024-10-24 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref>

On 25 March 2022, Özcan was called up to the [[Turkey national football team|Turkey national team]] by head coach [[Stefan Kuntz]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.tff.org/default.aspx?pageID=202&ftxtID=37316|title=Salih Özcan aday kadroya dâhil edildi|website=[[Turkish Football Federation]]|language=tr}}</ref> He debuted in a friendly 3–2 loss to [[Italy national football team|Italy]] on 29 March 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2022/03/29/world/friendlies/turkey/italy/3764998/|title = Turkey vs. Italy – 29 March 2022 – Soccerway}}</ref>

On 7 June 2024, he was named in the final squad of 26 players selected by [[Vincenzo Montella]] to take part in [[UEFA Euro 2024]].<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2024-06-13 |title=A Millî Takımımızın EURO 2024 Kadrosu Açıklandı - A Milli Takım Haber Detayları TFF |url=https://www.tff.org/default.aspx?pageID=202&ftxtID=44561 |website=www.tff.org}}</ref> On 18 November 2025, he scored his first national goal against [[Spain national football team|Spain]] in the [[2026 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|2026 FIFA World Cup qualification]].<ref name="tffgoal">{{Cite web |url=https://www.tff.org/default.aspx?pageID=202&ftxtID=49064 |title=Bileti Mart'ta Alacağız, Teşekkürler Bizim Çocuklar! İSPANYA 2-2 TÜRKİYE |website=TFF.org |access-date=18 November 2025 |date=18 November 2025 |language=tr}}</ref>

On 2 June 2026, Özcan was selected in the 26-man squad for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/worldcup/2026/06/02/turkey-2026-world-cup-team-complete-26-man-roster/90065447007/|title=2026 Turkey World Cup roster: Complete 26-man team|date=2 June 2026|access-date=13 June 2026|language=en}}</ref>

'''Sergej Barbarez''' (born 17 September 1971) is a Bosnian professional [[Manager (association football)|football manager]] and former [[Football player|player]] who is the manager of the [[Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team|Bosnia and Herzegovina national team]].

Mainly used as a [[Forward (association football)#Second striker|second striker]] during his playing career, Barbarez was also deployed as an [[Midfielder#Attacking midfielder|attacking midfielder]] or [[Midfielder#Winger|left winger]]. He started his career at hometown club [[FK Velež Mostar|Velež Mostar]], before going to Germany and joining [[Hannover 96]] in 1992. He went to [[1. FC Union Berlin|Union Berlin]] a year later, and then played in the [[Bundesliga]] for [[F.C. Hansa Rostock|Hansa Rostock]] and [[Borussia Dortmund]]. Barbarez joined [[Hamburger SV]] in 2000, and has since been considered one of the all-time greatest players of the club where he scored 65 goals in 174 Bundesliga games. In the [[2000–01 Bundesliga]] season, he was joint [[List of Bundesliga top scorers|top scorer with 22 goals]] alongside [[Ebbe Sand]] of [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]] at the end of the season. Barbarez left Hamburg in 2006, and signed with [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]], where he retired from professional football in 2008.

Barbarez made his senior international debut for the Bosnia and Herzegovina national team in 1998, earning 47 [[Cap (sport)|caps]] and scoring 17 goals until 2006. He was the [[Captain (association football)|captain]] of the national team between 2004 and 2006.

In April 2024, Barbarez was appointed as Bosnia and Herzegovina's head coach. He guided the nation to the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]], marking their first appearance at the finals since 2014.

==Early life==
Barbarez was born in [[Mostar]], [[Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina|SR Bosnia and Herzegovina]], [[Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia|Yugoslavia]], present-day [[Bosnia and Herzegovina]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.welt.de/print-welt/article477154/Impulsiver_Gefuehlsmensch.html | title = Impulsiver Gefühlsmensch | accessdate = 26 June 2010 | publisher = welt.de | date = 21 September 2001 |language = German}}</ref> His father Ljubo Barbarez was a [[Serbs of Bosnia and Herzegovina|Herzegovinian Serb]] footballer. His mother Zlata ({{nee|Košarić}}) was a handball player from [[Ljubuški]]. His maternal grandmother Ruža ({{nee|Tadinac}}) was a [[Croat]] from [[Trilj]], and his [[Bosniak]] grandfather Omer Košarić was her second husband. In addition to him, Ljubo and Zlata also had a daughter, Maja, who also played handball.<ref name="VJ">{{cite web |url=https://www.telegraf.rs/sport/fudbal/4300528-otac-mu-je-srbin-majka-iz-braka-hrvata-i-bosnjaka-pokusali-da-je-ubiju-heroj-iz-bih-ispunio-san-u-zenici |title=Otac mu je Srbin, majka iz braka Hrvata i Bošnjaka, pokušali da je ubiju: Heroj iz BiH ispunio san u Zenici! |website=Telegraf.rs |author=V. J. |date=1 April 2026 |access-date=5 April 2026 |language=sr}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ljportal.com/zivot-ga-nije-stedio-rat-ga-oblikovao-majka-zlata-je-ljubusanka-iz-braka-ruze-i-omera-otac-srbin-prica-barbareza-koja-je-dirnula-hercegovinu-124679/ |title=Život ga nije štedio, rat ga oblikovao: ‘Majka Zlata je Ljubušanka iz braka Ruže i Omera, otac Srbin’ – priča Barbareza koja je dirnula Hercegovinu |website=Ljubuški na dlanu |language=hr |date=1 April 2026 |author=I. A. |access-date=5 April 2026}}</ref>

During his childhood, Barbarez was interested in [[track and field]], naming [[400 metres]] his specialty. However, due to the lack of resources in the former Yugoslavia, he resorted to football. In the winter of 1991, in the midst of the [[Yugoslav Wars]], Barbarez was sent by his father to his maternal uncle in [[Hanover]], as wars were already raging in [[Slovenian War of Independence|Slovenia]] and [[Croatian War of Independence|Croatia]]. His father had mistakenly believed that the wars would not last and that Barbarez would return in a couple of weeks. However, as the [[Bosnian War]] continued, Barbarez remained in Germany permanently.<ref name="VJ" />

==Club career==
In 1984, Barbarez took a step further and started playing football for the youth team of [[FK Velež Mostar|Velež]] in his native city of Mostar.

Some six years later, he signed with the first team of Velež at the age of 19. However, briefly after, Barbarez served in the [[Yugoslav People's Army]] in [[Zagreb]] in 1991 before returning to Mostar to continue his career.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.24sata.info/sport/svijet-sporta/3091-Barbarez-Fudbalskog-saveza-BiH-nisu-dali-karte-Belgiju.html | title = Barbarez: "Iz Fudbalskog saveza BiH mi nisu dali karte za Belgiju" | publisher = 24sata.info | date = 14 March 2009 | accessdate = 26 June 2010 | url-status = dead | archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20110728175520/http://www.24sata.info/sport/svijet-sporta/3091-Barbarez-Fudbalskog-saveza-BiH-nisu-dali-karte-Belgiju.html | archivedate = 28 July 2011 | df = dmy-all }}</ref> In 1991, he returned to Velež and soon after everyone realized that Barbarez was a true talent.

The same year, he visited his uncle who was living in Germany. Some time later, Barbarez was preparing to return to Mostar but his uncle surprised him by extending his stay in Germany for two weeks. The uncle had arranged for him a two-week try-out practise with [[Hannover 96]]. The coach of Hannover 96 was so impressed by Barbarez that he signed him for the club. During those same two weeks the political situation throughout the [[former Yugoslavia]] was deteriorating by the minute and fighting was even occurring in some places. Subsequently, Barbarez came to an agreement with his father to stay with his uncle in Germany for the foreseeable future.

In April 1992, the [[Bosnian War]] escalated in the city of Mostar. A month prior to the actual war, Barbarez's father and sister fled with his high school sweetheart Ana to the city of [[Hanover]] in Germany. His mother Zlata stayed in Mostar throughout the entire war.

Barbarez played for Hannover 96 during the second half of the [[1991–92 2. Bundesliga|1991–92]] and the whole [[1992–93 2. Bundesliga|1992–93]] season. Between 1993 and 1996, he played for [[1. FC Union Berlin|Union Berlin]] at the third level<ref>{{Cite web | url = https://www.rsssf.org/players/barbarezdata.html | title = Sergej Barbarez – Matches and Goals in Bundesliga | author = Matthias Arnhold | date = 21 April 2011 | accessdate = 2 May 2011 | publisher = Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation}}</ref> before signing with [[F.C. Hansa Rostock|Hansa Rostock]]. Barbarez played there between 1996 and 1998.

In 1998, he signed with [[Borussia Dortmund]] and played there until joining [[Hamburger SV]] in July 2000.

During the first season with Hamburger SV, Barbarez became the top scorer for his club with 22 goals and joint [[List of Bundesliga top scorers|top scorer]] of the [[Bundesliga]] with [[Ebbe Sand]]. Though, he could not help Hamburg's elimination from the [[2000–01 UEFA Champions League]] at the group stages despite his two goals, when the club qualified for that competition for the first time, after a third place in the previous domestic Bundesliga season.

On 17 May 2006, Barbarez signed a two-year deal with [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]]. He finished his career at Bayer after his contract with the club expired in June 2008.

==International career==
[[File:Friendly football match, Iran 5-2 Bosnia and Herzegovina (06).jpg|thumb|250px|Barbarez playing for [[Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team|Bosnia and Herzegovina]] against [[Iran national football team|Iran]] in 2006]]

Amid ethnically motivated threats, including attempted kidnappings and attempts on his mother's life, Barbarez stated that he would only represent [[Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team|Bosnia and Herzegovina]] once her safety had been assured, with protection ultimately guaranteed following political intervention.<ref name="VJ" /> On 14 May 1998, he made his debut for the Bosnia and Herzegovina national team against [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] in a [[Exhibition game|friendly match]].

Barbarez scored two goals against [[Liechtenstein national football team|Liechtenstein]] in a [[2002 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group 7|World Cup qualification]] match on 28 March 2001.<ref name="Lichtenstein" /> He was denied a hat-trick as his second-half penalty was saved by Lichtenstein goalkeeper [[Peter Jehle]].<ref name="Lichtenstein">Connelly 2002, 142</ref>

Before retiring from international football in October 2005, Barbarez was the [[Captain (association football)|captain]] of the Bosnian national team.

On 2 December 2005, he announced his comeback to the national team and played in the [[UEFA Euro 2008 qualifying|UEFA Euro 2008 qualifiers]]. He became captain of the team once again.

On 12 October 2006, Barbarez officially stepped down from playing for the Bosnia and Herzegovina national team and retired permanently from professional football in June 2008. His final international was an October 2006 [[UEFA Euro 2008 qualifying|European Championship qualification]] match against [[Moldova national football team|Moldova]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://eu-football.info/_player.php?id=1252|title=Player Database|website=eu-football.info|accessdate=28 January 2021}}</ref>

==Managerial career==
Barbarez announced on 14 December 2009 that he wanted to be the head coach of the [[Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team|Bosnia and Herzegovina national team]] in the [[UEFA Euro 2012 qualifying|UEFA Euro 2012 qualifiers]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.bihfoot.com/2009/12/barbarez-wants-to-be-nationaltea-coach/comment-page-1/ | title = Barbarez Wants To Be National Team Coach | accessdate = 4 April 2010 | date = 14 December 2010 | publisher = bihfoot.com }}{{dead link|date=December 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> However, the [[Football Association of Republika Srpska]] blocked his entry<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.nezavisne.com/sport/fudbal/Barbarez-bez-podrske-FS-RS/51024 | title = Barbarez bez podrške FS RS | accessdate = 29 September 2020 | date = 25 December 2009 | publisher = nezavisne.com}}</ref> and later on, [[Safet Sušić]] was selected as the new head coach of the Bosnia and Herzegovina national team.

On 5 January 2011, Barbarez received his [[UEFA Pro Licence]] in the [[Football Association of Bosnia and Herzegovina]]'s educational facility in [[Jablanica, Bosnia and Herzegovina|Jablanica]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.sarajevo-x.com/sport/nogomet/clanak/110105084 | title = Profesionalne licence Barbarezu, Piplici i kolegama | publisher = sarajevo-x.com | date = 5 January 2011 | accessdate = 7 August 2011 | language = Bosnian}}</ref>

==Personal life==
[[File:10. Tag der Legenden 2014 08 (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Barbarez in 2014]]

Barbarez is married to his high-school sweetheart Ana, who is also from [[Mostar]]. They have two sons together, Filip-André (born 1994) and Sergio-Luis (1999).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://azra.ba/lifestyle/287946/sergej-barbarez-ponosno-pokazao-sinove-s-njima-proslavio-51-rodjendan/|title=Sergej Barbarez ponosno pokazao sinove, s njima proslavio 51. rođendan|date=18 September 2022|access-date=18 September 2022|language=bs|author=S.P.|website=azra.ba}}</ref> Barbarez was a member of the board of directors of [[Hamburger SV]] between 25 January 2009 and 28 May 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.klix.ba/sport/nogomet/sergej-barbarez-clan-uprave-hsv-a/090126077|title=Sergej Barbarez član uprave HSV-a|date=26 January 2009|access-date=19 April 2024|language=bs|website=Klix.ba}}</ref>

After retiring from football, Barbarez played poker professionally for 10 years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/soccer/article/69-days-to-the-world-cup-the-former-poker-pro-who-leads-bosnia-herzegovina-120000935.html|title=69 days to the World Cup: The former poker pro who leads Bosnia-Herzegovina|date=3 April 2026|access-date=7 June 2026|author=Sean Leahy|website=sports.yahoo.com}}</ref>

'''Cristiano Marques Gomes''' (born 3 June 1977), or simply '''Cris''', is a Brazilian [[Association football|football]] [[Manager (association football)|manager]] and a former [[Football player|player]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/bundesliga/vereine/2010-11/29391/vereinsspieler_cris.html | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20121017173202/http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/bundesliga/vereine/2010-11/29391/vereinsspieler_cris.html | url-status = dead | archive-date = 17 October 2012 | title = Cris | language = de | publisher=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] | access-date =23 April 2011}}</ref> A former [[centre-back]], Cris is known as ''Le policier'' ("The Policeman") due to his authoritative manner on the pitch.<ref>{{cite news |title="Une fille en boîte de nuit, tu as envie de la ni****" : un discours du "Policier" Cris fait beaucoup de bruit en France |trans-title="A girl in a nightclub, you feel like f***ing her": a speech by "Policeman" Cris causes lots of noise in France|url=https://www.dhnet.be/sports/football/2025/02/19/une-fille-en-boite-de-nuit-tu-as-envie-de-la-ni-un-discours-du-policier-cris-fait-beaucoup-de-bruit-en-france-VBG6POR6BFDIPEDSE4O67OZNXE/ |access-date=3 October 2025 |work=[[La Dernière Heure]] |date=19 February 2025 |language=French}}</ref>

He won four consecutive [[Ligue 1]] titles with French club [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] between 2005 and 2008, as well as the [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|Brazilian Championship]] in 1998 with [[Sport Club Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]], and in 2003 with [[Cruzeiro Esporte Clube|Cruzeiro]], and he also won the [[Copa do Brasil]] in 1995 with Corinthians, and in 2000 with Cruzeiro. Cris played 17 games for [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] between 2001 and 2009, winning the [[Copa América]] in [[2004 Copa América|2004]]. He was also chosen for the [[2001 Copa América]] and the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]].

Cris began coaching with Lyon's under-19 team in 2016. He then managed several senior clubs in France's lower leagues.

==Club career==

===Early career===
Cris spent a three-year spell in [[São Paulo]] playing for [[Sport Club Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]] (1995–98) before joining [[Cruzeiro Esporte Clube|Cruzeiro]]. There, he won his first cap for the national team, playing on 4 April 1999 against the United States in [[Brasília]] (a match won 7–0 by Brazil). In 2000, Brazilian magazine ''Placar'' named Cris as the leading player in his position during the Brazilian Championship, awarding him the Silver Ball title. In 2002, he secured a transfer to Europe, moving to [[Bundesliga]] club [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]]. This move, however, did not prove successful as he struggled to adapt to his new surroundings both on and off the field. The following year saw him return to his native country, rejoining Cruzeiro as part of their Brazilian championship-winning team of that year.

===Lyon===
In August 2004, Cris left Brazil once more, this time moving to [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] for a transfer fee close to €3.5 million. Having been involved in a brawl during a match in June earlier that year, Cris ran the risk of a six-month suspension that the [[Brazilian Football Confederation]] eventually decided not to extend to matches outside of Brazil. This affair, along with the physical duel he enjoyed with [[Thierry Henry]] during the [[France national football team|France]]–Brazil international at the [[Stade de France]] on 20 May 2004, earned Cris the reputation of a rough, rugged defender.

After an unconvincing first spell in Europe, Cris quickly imposed himself at the heart of Lyon's defense. His [[2004–05 Ligue 1|first season]] in [[Ligue 1]] saw the club crowned league champions and Cris was selected to the UNFP Ligue 1 Team of the Year. His second season was one of consolidation: Cris again had an excellent season with Lyon leaving no doubt as to his overall class. He was crowned "étoile d'or" ("Gold Star") by ''[[France Football]]'' magazine. The newspaper ''[[L'Equipe]]'' considered him the best defender of the [[2005–06 Ligue 1|2005–06 season]] and he was once more voted to the Ligue 1 Team of the Year by his fellow professionals. This season earned him an upwardly revised salary as well as a one-year extension to his contract, tying him to the French club until 2010. Cris later extended his contract an additional year, keeping him at Lyon until 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.frenchleague.com/ligue1/lireArticle.asp?idArticle=8436 |title=French Football League : Cris commits to Lyon |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070928033721/http://www.frenchleague.com/ligue1/lireArticle.asp?idArticle=8436 |archive-date=28 September 2007}}</ref>

For the [[2007–08 Ligue 1|2007–08 season]], newly appointed Lyon manager [[Alain Perrin]] appointed Cris as the new captain . On 11 August 2007, Cris was injured in a game between Lyon and [[Toulouse FC|Toulouse]], tearing ligaments in his right knee during a collision with [[Johan Elmander]]. Cris made his return to the squad on 1 March 2008 in a 1–0 win over [[Lille OSC|Lille]]. The match was held at the Stade de France. On 17 March 2012, Cris suffered a calf injury in a 1–0 [[Olympique Lyonnais–AS Saint-Étienne rivalry|derby]] win over [[AS Saint-Étienne|Saint-Étienne]] that ruled him out for a month.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1037734/lyon-defender-cris-ruled-out-for-one-month?cc=5901 | archive-url = https://archive.today/20120731031126/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1037734/lyon-defender-cris-ruled-out-for-one-month?cc=5901 | url-status = dead | archive-date = 31 July 2012 | title = Cris blow for Lyon | publisher = ESPN Soccernet | date = 19 March 2012 | access-date = 20 June 2012}}</ref> [[File:Cristiano Marques GS.JPG|thumb|left|upright|Cris in [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]] colours, 2012]]

===Galatasaray===
On 3 September 2012, after eight years with Lyon, Cris signed for Turkish side [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]] for a €1.25 million transfer, plus bonuses, and signed a 1+1-year contract.<ref>{{cite news | date= 3 September 2012 | url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/futebol-internacional/noticia/2012/09/galatasaray-anuncia-cris-ex-lyon.html | title=Galatasaray anuncia Cris, ex-Lyon | publisher=Globoesporte.com | access-date= 3 September 2012 | language = pt}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Cristiano Marques Gomes Galatasaray'da|url=http://www.galatasaray.org/futbol/futbol_as/haber/14296.php|publisher=Galatasaray SK|access-date=4 September 2012| language = tr}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.kap.gov.tr/yay/Bildirim/Bildirim.aspx?id=235555|title=Cristiano Marques Gomes transferi|date=3 September 2012|access-date=19 September 2012|work=Galatasaray |publisher=Turkish Public Disclosure System (KAP)|language=tr}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Communiqué du club|url=http://www.olweb.fr/fr/Accueil/100007/Article/60245/Communique-du-club|publisher=Olympique Lyonnais|access-date=4 September 2012| language = fr}}</ref> He scored his first goal for Galatasaray on 28 October 2012 in the [[Süper Lig]] match against [[Kayserispor]], a 3–0 home win. On 2 January 2013, after just four months in Turkey, Galatasaray terminated Cris' contract, prompting him to return to his native Brazil where he signed for [[Grêmio Foot-Ball Porto Alegrense|Grêmio]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.estadao.com.br/noticias/esportes,cris-deixa-o-galatasaray-e-pode-reforcar-o-gremio,979818,0.htm | title = Cris deixa o Galatasaray e pode reforçar o Grêmio | language = pt | publisher = estadao.com.br | date =  January 2013 | access-date = 2 February 2013}}</ref>

===Grêmio===
On 3 January 2013, one day after breaking his contract with Galatasaray, Cris signed with Brazilian side Grêmio. He arrived at the club as a direct replacement for [[Gilberto Silva]], who had consequently transferred to [[Clube Atlético Mineiro|Atlético Mineiro]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://br.esporteinterativo.yahoo.com/noticias/veterano-cris-chega-ao-gr%C3%AAmio-comandar-zaga-210000906--spt.html | title = Veterano Cris chega ao Grêmio para comandar a zaga | language = pt | publisher = br.esporteinterativo.yahoo.com | date = 3 January 2013 | access-date = 2 February 2013 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20130106160754/http://br.esporteinterativo.yahoo.com/noticias/veterano-cris-chega-ao-gr%C3%AAmio-comandar-zaga-210000906--spt.html | archive-date = 6 January 2013 | url-status = dead }}</ref>

===Vasco da Gama===
On 31 July 2013, Cris signed with [[CR Vasco da Gama|Vasco da Gama]]. His first match was against Grêmio, a 2–3 loss. Cris was released from the club in January 2014 after his contract was not renewed.

==International career==
Cris earned 17 [[Cap (sport)|caps]] with the [[Brazil national football team|Brazil national team]], the first earned in July 2001. Later that month he played at the [[2001 Copa América]], in which his team lost in the quarter-finals to [[Honduras national football team|Honduras]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Scragg |first1=Steven |title=Honduras and the legendary Copa América odyssey of 2001 |url=https://thesefootballtimes.co/2015/02/16/honduras-legendary-copa-america-odyssey/ |access-date=3 October 2025 |work=These Football Times |date=16 February 2015}}</ref> His only goal for Brazil came in a 6–0 [[Exhibition game#International football|friendly]] victory over [[Bolivia national football team|Bolivia]] on 31 January 2002.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Strack-Zimmermann|first=Benjamin|title=Cris|url=http://www.national-football-teams.com/player/999/Cris.html|access-date=29 December 2020|website=www.national-football-teams.com}}</ref> He was a regular under incoming manager [[Luiz Felipe Scolari]], who had coached him at Cruzeiro, but was excluded from the [[2002 FIFA World Cup]] squad that ended up winning the tournament due to receiving too many [[Penalty card|red cards]] for his club; Scolari filled his place with [[Ânderson Polga]] but preferred to start [[Roque Júnior]], [[Lúcio]] and [[Edmílson]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Ídolo do Cruzeiro revela motivo que o tirou da Copa do Mundo de 2002|trans-title=Cruzeiro idol reveals reason that took him out of the 2002 World Cup|url=https://noataque.com.br/futebol/copa-do-mundo/time/cruzeiro/noticia/2025/08/01/idolo-do-cruzeiro-revela-motivo-que-o-tirou-da-copa-do-mundo-de-2002/ |access-date=3 October 2025 |work=No Ataque |date=1 August 2025 |language=Portuguese}}</ref>

Cris was chosen for the [[2004 Copa América]]; he came on as a substitute in the [[2004 Copa América final|final]] against [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]], replacing [[Luisão]] for the final eight minutes and the [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shootout]] victory, in which he was not chosen to shoot.<ref>{{cite news |title=Brazil win Copa shoot-out |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/internationals/3922603.stm |access-date=3 October 2025 |work=[[BBC Sport]] |date=25 July 2004}}</ref> He was a late addition to the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]] squad in Germany due to Roque Júnior's injury.<ref>{{cite news |title=Brazil boast impressive Cup squad |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/world_cup_2006/teams/brazil/4773881.stm|access-date=3 October 2025 |work=[[BBC Sport]] |date=15 May 2006}}</ref> 

Having not played since a game with Russia on 1 March 2006 – including at the World Cup – Cris was recalled to the Brazil squad in November 2009 for friendlies against [[Oman national football team|Oman]] and [[England national football team|England]] in Qatar. He was called up by [[Dunga]] due to issues with other centre-backs, including [[Juan (footballer, born 1979)|Juan]] not being allowed to travel by [[A.S. Roma]], Luisão's [[appendicitis]], [[Thiago Silva]]'s document issues and [[Naldo (footballer, born 1982)|Naldo]]'s injury.<ref>{{cite news |title=Zagueiro Cris é convocado para lugar de Juan na seleção |url=https://www.gazetadopovo.com.br/esportes/zagueiro-cris-e-convocado-para-lugar-de-juan-na-selecao-bzne42ilxltvu2mln17p8ldfy/ |access-date=3 October 2025 |work=Gazeta do Povo |date=13 November 2009 |language=Portuguese}}</ref> On 17 November, he played as a substitute in a 2–0 win over Oman in his final game.<ref>{{cite news |title=Brasil encerra temporada vitoriosa com 2 x 0 contra Omã|trans-title=Brazil cap off victorious season with 2–0 win over Oman|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/world/brasil-encerra-temporada-vitoriosa-com-2-x-0-contra-om-idUSSPE5AG0AZ/ |access-date=3 October 2025 |work=[[Reuters]] |date=17 November 2009 |language=Portuguese}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
Cris returned to Lyon, initially as under-15 manager, before taking the under-19 team in 2016–17. In [[2017–18 Championnat National 2|2017–18]], he led the [[reserve team]] in the fourth-tier [[Championnat National 2 (1993–2026)|Championnat National 2]], before leaving the club in June 2018.<ref>{{cite news |title=Cris quitte l'Olympique lyonnais|trans-title=Cris leaves Olympique Lyonnais|url=https://www.leprogres.fr/ol/2018/06/27/cris-quitte-l-ol |access-date=28 September 2025 |work=[[Le Progrès]] |date=27 June 2018 |language=French}}</ref> A year later, he was hired at [[Monts d'Or Azergues]] in the same division.<ref>{{cite news |title=Cris rebondit au club des Monts-d'Or de Chasselay|trans-title=Cris rebounds at Monts-d'Or from Chasselay|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Cris-rebondit-au-club-des-monts-d-or-de-chasselay/1026620 |access-date=28 September 2025 |work=[[L'Équipe]] |date=6 June 2019 |language=French}}</ref>

On 31 May 2021, Cris signed for [[Le Mans FC|Le Mans]] in the third-tier [[Championnat National]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Huguen |first1=Morgane |title=Football. Officiel : le nouvel entraîneur du Mans FC s'appelle Cris (ancien joueur de l'OL)|trans-title=Football. Official: Le Mans FC's new manager is called Cris (former OL player) |url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/sport/football/le-mans-fc/football-officiel-le-nouvel-entraineur-du-mans-fc-s-appelle-cris-ancien-joueur-de-l-ol-dffd1bcc-c1fe-11eb-b272-500c49682f10 |access-date=28 September 2025 |work=[[Ouest-France]] |date=31 May 2021 |language=French}}</ref> He was sacked on 11 November 2022 with the club 13th after 11 games, and following elimination from the [[Coupe de France]] by {{ill|Union sportive Fougères|fr}} from two leagues below.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Nédélec |first1=Guillaume |title=Football. C'est officiel : Cris n'est plus l'entraîneur du Mans FC|trans-title=Football. It's official: Cris is no longer the manager of Le Mans FC |url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/sport/football/le-mans-fc/football-officiel-cris-n-est-plus-l-entraineur-du-mans-fc-3c087a78-5dc2-11ed-9cf9-ac215ad008b8 |access-date=28 September 2025 |work=[[Ouest-France]] |date=7 November 2022 |language=French}}</ref>

Days after his exit from Le Mans, Cris was hired by [[FC Versailles 78|Versailles]] in the same league. He won 2–0 away to [[FC Villefranche Beaujolais|Villefranche]] on his debut on 25 November 2022, and set a target of promotion to [[Ligue 2]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Caillaud |first1=Raphaël |title=Football. National : Cris, ex-entraîneur du Mans FC, a réussi sa première avec Versailles|trans-title=Football. Championnat National: Cris, ex-Le Mans FC manager, succeeded on his debut with Versailles|url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/sport/football/le-mans-fc/football-national-cris-ex-entraineur-du-mans-fc-a-reussi-sa-premiere-avec-versailles-64466112-6e5c-11ed-8a4c-ae62722f8615 |access-date=28 September 2025 |work=[[Ouest-France]] |date=27 November 2022 |language=French}}</ref> He quit the club at the end of the [[2022–23 Championnat National|season]], having missed his aim by finishing fifth.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Marque |first1=Alexandre |title=Football : six mois après son arrivée, Cris quitte déjà le banc du FC Versailles|trans-title=Football: six months after his arrival, Cris already leaves the FC Versailles bench |url=https://actu.fr/ile-de-france/versailles_78646/football-six-mois-apres-son-arrivee-cris-quitte-deja-le-banc-du-fc-versailles_59667350.html |access-date=28 September 2025 |work=Actu.fr |date=31 May 2023 |language=French}}</ref>

On 28 October 2024, Cris was hired at [[LB Châteauroux|Châteauroux]], last-placed in the Championnat National.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Collin |first1=Jérôme |title=Football : Cris devient le nouvel entraîneur de la Berrichonne de Châteauroux|trans-title=Football: Cris becomes the new manager of La Berrichonne de Châteauroux|url=https://www.francebleu.fr/sports/football/football-cris-devient-le-nouvel-entraineur-de-la-berrichonne-de-chateauroux-3847108 |access-date=28 September 2025 |publisher=[[France Bleu]] |date=20 October 2024 |language=French}}</ref> In February, before a game against [[US Quevilly-Rouen Métropole|Quevilly-Rouen]], he made a speech to his players in which he likened winning a game to having sex with women; a video was posted to the club's social media accounts, for which he and the club apologised.<ref>{{cite news |title=Former Brazil defender turned manager Cris causes uproar with misogynistic comments during pep talk |url=https://apnews.com/article/france-soccer-cris-misogynistic-comments-ed1bb4cbe5e68c6fb55f991d345118ea |access-date=28 September 2025 |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |date=19 February 2025}}</ref> He left at the end of the [[2024–25 Championnat National|season]], with his team having been relegated.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Le Ruyet |first1=Jean-Marc |title=Berrichonne de Châteauroux : un nouveau coach jeune, ambitieux, estampillé National 2|trans-title=Berrichonne de Châteauroux: a new young, ambitious coach with Championnat National 2 experience|url=https://www.lanouvellerepublique.fr/chateauroux/berrichonne-de-chateauroux-un-nouveau-coach-estampille-national-2-1748961877 |access-date=28 September 2025 |work=[[La Nouvelle République du Centre-Ouest]] |date=3 June 2025 |language=French}}</ref>

'''Manuel Agudo Durán''' ({{IPA|es|maˈnwel aˈɣuðo ðuˈɾan}};{{efn-ua|In isolation, ''Durán'' is pronounced {{IPA|es|duˈɾan|}}.}} born 15 October 1986), known as '''Nolito''' ({{IPA|es|noˈlito|}}), is a Spanish former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[winger (association football)|winger]] or a [[forward (association football)|forward]].

Having begun his career at lower league clubs he signed for [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in 2008, playing predominantly with its [[FC Barcelona Atlètic|reserves]]. He totalled 243 games and 60 goals in [[La Liga]], where he also represented [[Granada CF|Granada]], [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta]] and [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]]. Abroad, he played two seasons for [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] in Portugal, and one in the English [[Premier League]] with [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/segunda/nolito-aterriza-en-el-ibiza-para-solucionar-sus-problemas-en-ataque-n/|title=Nolito, un fichaje de cinco estrellas para el Ibiza|trans-title=Nolito, five-star signing for Ibiza|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Paco|last=Murillo|language=es|date=5 September 2022|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref>

Nolito made his debut for [[Spain national football team|Spain]] in November 2014, representing the nation at [[UEFA Euro 2016|Euro 2016]].

==Club career==
===Early career===
Born in [[Sanlúcar de Barrameda]], [[Province of Cádiz|Cádiz]], [[Andalusia]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://observador.pt/2016/11/16/o-bom-filho-a-casa-paga-como-a-mae-de-nolito-o-fintou/|title=O bom filho a casa paga. Como a mãe de Nolito o fintou|trans-title=Return of the paying son. How Nolito's mother dribbled him|newspaper=[[Observador]]|language=pt|date=16 November 2016|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref> Nolito began his career with UD Algaida in his hometown before joining [[Atlético Sanluqueño CF|Atlético Sanluqueño]] in 2000. He made his first-team debut in [[Tercera División]] with the latter club at the age of just 15, scoring on his debut,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://sevilla.abc.es/orgullodenervion/noticias-sevilla-fc/sevi-descubre-cinco-curiosidades-nolito-156829-1539698430-201810161702_noticia.html|title=Descubre las cinco curiosidades de Nolito|trans-title=Find out the five curiosities about Nolito|newspaper=[[ABC (newspaper)|ABC]]|first=Pablo|last=Pintinho|language=es|date=16 October 2018|access-date=21 June 2021}}</ref> and moved to [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] in 2003, where he wrapped up his formative years.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://sevilla.abc.es/orgullodenervion/noticias-sevilla-fc/sevi-pasado-valencianista-nolito-141782-1520622821-201803092013_noticia.html|title=El pasado valencianista de Nolito|trans-title=The Valencian past of Nolito|newspaper=ABC|first=Álvaro|last=Galván|language=es|date=9 March 2018|access-date=21 June 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.abc.es/deportes/futbol/20141113/abci-nolito-seleccion-entrevista-201411122036.html|title=Nolito, el gol callejero de España|trans-title=Nolito, Spain's street goal|newspaper=ABC|first=Enrique|last=Yunta|language=es|date=13 November 2014|access-date=25 September 2015}}</ref>

Nolito returned to Sanluqueño in 2005,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.diariocordoba.com/deportes/2005/11/22/nolito-sigue-cabeza-38707232.html|title=Nolito sigue en cabeza|trans-title=Nolito still in front|newspaper=Diario Córdoba|language=es|date=22 November 2005|access-date=21 June 2021}}</ref> and was their top scorer in the [[2005–06 Tercera División|2005–06 season]] with 27 goals (24 in the regular season).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lavozdigital.es/canal-amarillo/noticias-cadiz-cf/lvdi-nolito-vuelve-estadio-club-no-quiso-hace-quince-anos-202104171803_noticia.html|title=Nolito vuelve al estadio de un club que no lo quiso hace quince años|trans-title=Nolito returns to stadium of a club that did not want him fifteen years ago|publisher=La Voz Digital|first=Alfonso|last=Carbonell|language=es|date=17 April 2021|access-date=21 June 2021}}</ref> He then signed with [[Écija Balompié|Écija]] of the [[Segunda División B]], where he scored in a 1–1 home draw against [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in the [[2006–07 Copa del Rey]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2015/04/26/primera/1430017959_100475.html|title=Nolito le marcó un gol al Real Madrid militando en el Écija|trans-title=Nolito scored against Real Madrid when at Écija|newspaper=Diario AS|language=es|date=26 April 2015|access-date=21 June 2021}}</ref>

===Barcelona===
Nolito arrived at [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]]'s youth academy at nearly 22 years of age, after scoring 13 times for Écija the [[2007–08 Segunda División B|previous campaign]]. With the [[Catalonia|Catalans]]' [[FC Barcelona Atlètic|B team]], also in the third tier, he scored 16 league goals over two seasons – 12 in [[2009–10 Segunda División B|the second]]<ref name=Origins>{{cite news|url=https://www.publico.pt/2016/07/01/desporto/noticia/nolito-e-uma-carreira-de-avancos-e-recuos-da-origem-humilde-ao-milionario-city-1737009|title=Nolito: da origem humilde ao milionário City|trans-title=Nolito: from humble origins to millionaire City|newspaper=[[Público (Portugal)|Público]]|first=Pedro|last=Queiroz da Costa|language=pt|date=1 July 2016|access-date=9 October 2018}}</ref>– as the side returned to the [[Segunda División]] after an 11-year absence.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2010/06/20/futbol/mas_futbol/1277060846.html|title=El filial del Barcelona vuelve a Segunda doce años después|trans-title=Barcelona reserves return to ''Segunda'' twelve years later|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=20 June 2010|access-date=7 March 2021}}</ref>

On 3 October 2010, Nolito made his [[La Liga]] debut for Barcelona, coming on as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for [[Pedro (footballer, born 1987)|Pedro]] in a 1–1 home draw against [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/302013?cc=5739|title=Nsue shocks Barca|publisher=[[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]]|date=3 October 2010|access-date=27 February 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110628233912/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/302013?cc=5739|archive-date=28 June 2011}}</ref> On 10 November, he opened the 5–1 home win over [[AD Ceuta|Ceuta]] in the [[2010–11 Copa del Rey|round of 32]] of the [[Copa del Rey]] (7–1 on aggregate).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/match/_/id/309641?cc=5739|title=Barcelona 5–1 Ceuta|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=10 November 2010|access-date=27 February 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110628233944/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/match/_/id/309641?cc=5739|archive-date=28 June 2011}}</ref>

===Benfica===
[[File:Nolito on Benfica (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|Nolito with [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] in 2011]]
In late May 2011, Nolito rejected Barcelona's offer of a professional contract and instead signed a five-year deal with Portuguese club [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]], effective as of 1 July.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2011/05/21/futbol/equipos/barcelona_b/1305974790.html|title=Nolito confirma su fichaje por el Benfica|trans-title=Nolito confirms deal with Benfica|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=21 May 2011|access-date=7 June 2011}}</ref> He scored on his official debut on the 27th, a 2–0 home win against [[Trabzonspor]] in the [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League|third qualifying round]] of the [[UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01f3-0e7907170079-e581ea06b1da-1000--benfica-leave-trabzonspor-up-against-it/|title=Benfica leave Trabzonspor up against it|publisher=UEFA|date=27 July 2011|access-date=28 July 2011}}</ref> He also netted in the second leg, a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01f4-0e79158cc147-adfa8c517081-1000--benfica-ease-past-ten-man-trabzonspor/|title=Benfica ease past ten-man Trabzonspor|publisher=UEFA|first=Türker|last=Tozar|date=3 August 2011|access-date=4 August 2011}}</ref>

On 20 August 2011, Nolito scored once in a 3–1 home victory over [[C.D. Feirense|Feirense]], making him alongside [[Eusébio]] the only player to score in his first five official matches.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.record.pt/futebol/futebol-nacional/liga-betclic/benfica/detalhe/nolito-iguala-eusebio-713139|title=Nolito iguala Eusébio|trans-title=Nolito equals Eusébio|newspaper=[[Record (Portuguese newspaper)|Record]]|language=pt|date=20 August 2011|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref> He managed 15 goals in 48 competitive appearances in his [[2011–12 Primeira Liga|first season]],<ref name=Origins/> [[2011–12 Taça da Liga|helping]] his team to win the [[Taça da Liga]].<ref name=LC>{{cite news|url=https://www.record.pt/futebol/futebol-nacional/liga-betclic/benfica/detalhe/nolito-sabiamos-que-era-dificil-754163?ref=Detalhe_Relacionadas|title=Nolito: «Sabíamos que era difícil»|trans-title=Nolito: "We knew it was hard"|newspaper=Record|language=pt|date=29 April 2012|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref>

Nolito returned to his country and his native region on 29 January 2013, being loaned to [[Granada CF|Granada]] for six months and a fee of €600,000, without the possibility of making the move permanent in June.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.granadacf.es/index.php?seccion=leer_mas&ref=noticias+&id_noticia=1399|title=Nolito será rojiblanco hasta junio de 2013|trans-title=Nolito will be ''rojiblanco'' until June 2013|publisher=Granada CF|language=es|date=29 January 2013|access-date=29 January 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sabado.pt/ultima-hora/detalhe/20130129-1732-jesus-confirma-saida-de-nolito|title=Jesus confirma saída de Nolito|trans-title=Jesus confirms Nolito exit|publisher=[[Sábado (magazine)|Sábado]]|language=pt|date=29 January 2013|access-date=23 February 2026}}</ref> In his first match, four days after signing, he took the [[Corner kick|corner]] which resulted in [[Cristiano Ronaldo]]'s [[own goal]] for the game's only, giving Granada their first win over Real Madrid in 40 years.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/match/85443/granada-vs-real-madrid/report|title=Granada 1–0 Real Madrid: Ronaldo own goal gifts Andalusians three precious points|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|date=2 February 2013|access-date=2 February 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/real-madrid/result/result-ronaldo-own-goal-gives-granada-the-win_67383.html|title=Result: Cristiano Ronaldo own goal gives Granada the win|publisher=Sportsmole|first=Paul|last=Gorst|date=2 February 2013|access-date=2 February 2013}}</ref>

===Celta===
[[File:Nolito Jugador.JPG|thumb|right|Nolito talking to an assistant referee in 2015]]
Nolito signed with [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta de Vigo]] on 1 July 2013, penning a four-year deal and reuniting with former Barcelona B boss [[Luis Enrique]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.celtavigo.net/es/primer-equipo/noticias/6586-nolito-refuerza-la-delantera-del-real-club-celta|title=Nolito refuerza la delantera del Real Club Celta|trans-title=Nolito strengthens Real Club Celta's offense|publisher=Celta Vigo|language=es|date=1 July 2013|access-date=1 July 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923202035/http://www.celtavigo.net/es/primer-equipo/noticias/6586-nolito-refuerza-la-delantera-del-real-club-celta|archive-date=23 September 2015}}</ref> He finished his [[2013–14 La Liga|debut campaign]] as team top scorer with 14.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.lavozdegalicia.es/noticia/celta/2014/05/26/temporada-oro-nolito/0003_201405V26P42991.htm|title=La temporada de oro de Nolito|trans-title=Nolito's golden season|newspaper=[[La Voz de Galicia]]|first=Lorena|last=García Calvo|language=es|date=26 May 2014|access-date=3 June 2014}}</ref>

Nolito was named [[La Liga Player of the Month]] for September 2014, with four goals during a month which ended with the side in [[2014–15 La Liga|sixth position]].<ref name=LFP>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.es/noticias/premios-bbva-a-los-mejores-de-septiembre|title=Premios BBVA a los mejores de septiembre|trans-title=BBVA awards for the best in September|publisher=[[Liga Nacional de Fútbol Profesional]]|language=es|date=6 October 2014|access-date=8 November 2014}}</ref> He created 96 scoring opportunities over the campaign, the most in the Spanish league and fourth most in Europe's five leading leagues.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33686731|title=Kevin de Bruyne: Manchester City sign Wolfsburg midfielder|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=30 August 2015|access-date=30 August 2015}}</ref>

On 23 September 2015, Nolito took his league tally to five after scoring once and providing two [[Assist (association football)|assists]] for [[Iago Aspas]] in a 4–1 home defeat of former club Barcelona.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2015/sep/23/celta-vigo-barcelona-match-report|title=Iago Aspas scores twice as Celta Vigo give Barcelona shock thrashing|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=23 September 2015|access-date=24 September 2015}}</ref> He totalled three goals and an assist that month to help them remain unbeaten, earning him a second Player of the Month accolade.<ref name=LFP2>{{cite web|url=http://www.laliga.es/en/news/nolito-named-liga-bbva-player-of-the-month-of-september|title=Nolito named Liga BBVA Player of the Month for September|publisher=[[La Liga]]|date=1 October 2015|access-date=10 November 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180705150738/http://www.laliga.es/en/news/nolito-named-liga-bbva-player-of-the-month-of-september|archive-date=5 July 2018}}</ref> In mid-December, however, he suffered a [[hamstring]] injury against [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] which sidelined him for two months.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/la-liga-bbva/20151213/30764686315/nolito-preocupa-lesion-ecografia-muslo-fichajes.html|title=Preocupa la lesión de Nolito|trans-title=Nolito's injury is a concern|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|language=es|date=13 December 2015|access-date=11 May 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2599251-nolito-injury-updates-on-celta-vigo-stars-hamstring-and-return|title=Nolito injury: Updates on Celta Vigo Star's hamstring and return|publisher=[[Bleacher Report]]|first=Matt|last=Jones|date=15 December 2015|access-date=10 May 2016}}</ref>

Nolito returned to action on 20 February 2016, featuring roughly 20 minutes in a 3–2 home win over [[SD Eibar|Eibar]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/celta-vigo/20160220/302311091079/el-celta-gana-y-se-gusta-en-el-regreso-de-nolito.html|title=El Celta gana y se gusta en el regreso de Nolito|trans-title=Celta win and enjoy themselves in return of Nolito|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Pablo|last=Planas|language=es|date=21 February 2016|access-date=11 May 2016}}</ref> In the following round, he scored the game's only goal at [[Getafe CF|Getafe]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://deportes.elpais.com/deportes/2016/02/27/actualidad/1456600119_306570.html|title=El Getafe no puede con Nolito|trans-title=Getafe cannot handle Nolito|newspaper=[[El País]]|first=Juan Luis|last=Cudeiro|language=es|date=27 February 2016|access-date=11 May 2016}}</ref> and Celta eventually [[2015–16 La Liga|finished in sixth place]].

===Manchester City===
{{wikinews|Footballers Neymar, Zlatan, Nolito sign contracts}}
On 1 July 2016, Nolito signed with [[Premier League]] side [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] on a four-year deal for a fee of £13.8 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mancity.com/news/first-team/2016/07/01/nolito-signs-for-city/1467215591004|title=Nolito signs for Manchester City|publisher=Manchester City F.C.|date=1 July 2016|access-date=1 July 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160704031415/http://www.mancity.com/news/first-team/2016/07/01/nolito-signs-for-city/1467215591004|archive-date=4 July 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36670719|title=Nolito: Manchester City sign Spain forward on four-year deal|publisher=BBC Sport|date=1 July 2016|access-date=1 July 2016}}</ref> He made his debut on 13 August, playing 59 minutes in a 2–1 home victory against [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/36994521|title=Manchester City 2–1 Sunderland|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Chris|last=Osborne|date=13 August 2016|access-date=14 August 2016}}</ref> Three days later he scored his first goal, and also provided an assist to [[Sergio Agüero]] in a 5–0 away rout of [[FC Steaua București|Steaua București]] in the [[2016–17 UEFA Champions League|Champions League play-off round]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0230-0e94b08c6dd2-08e10b43d082-1000--city-set-fair-to-progress-after-steaua-stroll/|title=City set fair to progress after Steaua stroll|publisher=UEFA|first=Paul-Daniel|last=Zaharia|date=16 August 2016|access-date=16 August 2016}}</ref>

Nolito made a few appearances during his time in Manchester, but he and his family were unsettled by life in England.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40193329|title=Nolito: Man City striker claims English weather has 'changed colour' of daughter's face|publisher=BBC Sport|date=7 June 2017|access-date=5 July 2018}}</ref>

===Sevilla===
In July 2017, [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] signed Nolito on a three-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40622173|title=Nolito: Sevilla sign Spain forward from Man City on three-year deal|publisher=BBC Sport|date=16 July 2017|access-date=16 July 2017}}</ref> He spent the better part of [[2018–19 La Liga|2018–19]] on the sidelines, nursing a [[fibula]] injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://eldesmarque.com/sevilla/sevilla-futbol-club/1134622-lesion-nolito-tres-meses-de-baja|title=La mala suerte de Nolito|trans-title=Nolito's bad luck|publisher=El Desmarque|language=es|date=12 January 2019|access-date=1 October 2019}}</ref>

===Return to Celta===
On 18 June 2020, Nolito rejoined Celta on a reported one-year deal. His Sevilla contract was set to expire at the end of the month, and the former were granted an emergency exception to acquire him outside of the [[transfer window]] because of a long-term injury to goalkeeper [[Sergio Álvarez (footballer, born 1986)|Sergio Álvarez]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rccelta.es/index.php/en/nolito-returns-to-rc-celta|title=Nolito returns to RC Celta|publisher=Celta Vigo|date=18 June 2020|access-date=18 June 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://uk.sports.yahoo.com/news/celta-vigo-sign-winger-nolito-150003192.html|title=Celta Vigo sign winger Nolito after being granted emergency transfer to replace a goalkeeper|publisher=[[Yahoo Sports]]|date=18 June 2020|access-date=18 June 2020}}</ref> Three days later, in his first game back, he came off the bench to assist [[Santi Mina]] and score a [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty]] in a 6–0 home thrashing of [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2020/06/21/primera/1592746989_042641.html|title=Nolito empieza a lo grande|trans-title=Nolito starts off great|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Clemente|last=Garrido|language=es|date=21 June 2020|access-date=21 June 2020}}</ref>

===Ibiza===
On 5 September 2022, Nolito joined second-tier [[UD Ibiza|Ibiza]] on a [[Free transfer (association football)|free transfer]], on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.periodicodeibiza.es/deportes/deporte-ibiza/2022/09/05/1786647/ibiza-ficha-nolito.html|title=Oficial: Nolito firma por la UD Ibiza|trans-title=Official: Nolito signs for UD Ibiza|newspaper=Periódico de Ibiza|first=Sergio|last=García|language=es|date=5 September 2022|access-date=7 June 2023}}</ref> He played 28 times in his [[2022–23 Segunda División|only season]] as the [[Balearic Islands|Balearic]] side were relegated,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.diariodeibiza.es/ud-ibiza/2023/04/28/ud-ibiza-certifica-descenso-primera-86646786.html|title=La UD Ibiza certifica el descenso a Primera RFEF tras caer en Santander|trans-title=UD Ibiza confirm relegation to ''Primera RFEF'' after falling in Santander|newspaper=Diario de Ibiza|first=Rubén J.|last=Palomo|language=es|date=28 April 2023|access-date=14 September 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ojogo.pt/futebol/1a-liga/benfica/noticias/nolito-terminou-a-carreira-e-o-benfica-nao-deixou-escapar-17018655.html|title=Nolito terminou a carreira de futebolista e o Benfica não deixou escapar|trans-title=Nolito ended footballing career and Benfica noted that|newspaper=[[O Jogo]]|language=pt|date=13 September 2023|access-date=14 September 2023}}</ref> scoring just once in a 3–2 home win over [[CD Lugo|Lugo]] on 2 October.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/ibiza/2023/02/27/63fce924e2704ef0168b459d.html|title=La fugaz aparición de un Nolito que no acaba de convencer|trans-title=The fleeting appearance of a Nolito who does not quite convince|newspaper=Marca|first=Sergio|last=García|language=es|date=27 February 2023|access-date=7 June 2023}}</ref>

Nolito's contract was terminated in June 2023, and he announced his retirement at 36 on 13 September.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/primera/nolito-se-retira-n/|title=Nolito se retira|trans-title=Nolito retires|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Guillermo|last=Pérez|language=es|date=13 September 2023|access-date=10 October 2023}}</ref>

==International career==
Nolito did not earn a single [[Cap (sport)|cap]] for [[Spain national youth football team|Spain at youth level]]. On 7 November 2014, he was called up by [[Spain national football team|full side]] manager [[Vicente del Bosque]] for a [[UEFA Euro 2016]] [[UEFA Euro 2016 qualifying|qualifier]] against [[Belarus national football team|Belarus]] and a [[Exhibition game|friendly]] with [[Germany national football team|Germany]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/nov/07/diego-costa-spain-squad-chelsea-left-out|title=Chelsea's Diego Costa left out of Spain squad to play Belarus and Germany|newspaper=The Guardian|date=7 November 2014|access-date=7 November 2014}}</ref> He made his debut against the latter on the 18th, starting at his club ground of [[Balaídos Stadium]] in a 1–0 loss.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2014_15/amistosos_seleccion/5/spa_ale/|title=Experimento pasado por agua|trans-title=Soggy experiment|newspaper=Marca|first=Delfín|last=Melero|language=es|date=18 November 2014|access-date=19 November 2014}}</ref>

On 17 May 2016, Nolito was named in the preliminary squad for the final tournament in France.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36312769|title=Euro 2016: Diego Costa, Juan Mata & Fernando Torres not in Spain squad|publisher=BBC Sport|date=17 May 2016|access-date=17 May 2016}}</ref> Twelve days later, in a friendly against [[Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team|Bosnia and Herzegovina]], he scored his first goals, striking twice in the first half of a 3–1 win in Switzerland.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/spain-vs-bosnia-herzegovina/2209809/report|title=Spain 3–1 Bosnia: Nolito fires La Roja to success|publisher=Goal|date=29 May 2016|access-date=29 May 2016}}</ref> he repeated the feat the following match, a 6–1 rout of [[South Korea national football team|South Korea]] in Austria.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ibtimes.com/video-spain-6-1-south-korea-highlights-salzburg-friendly-ahead-euro-2016-2376728|title=VIDEO Spain 6–1 South Korea: Highlights from Salzburg friendly ahead of Euro 2016|newspaper=[[International Business Times]]|first=Jason|last=Le Miere|date=1 June 2016|access-date=1 June 2016}}</ref>

Selected for the squad of 23,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://deportes.elpais.com/deportes/2016/05/31/actualidad/1464710610_277737.html?rel=cx_articulo|title=Isco y Saúl fuera de la lista de Del Bosque para la Eurocopa 2016|trans-title=Isco and Saúl out of Del Bosque's list for 2016 European Championship|newspaper=El País|first=Luis|last=Martín|language=es|date=31 May 2016|access-date=17 June 2016}}</ref> Nolito acted often as starter, scoring from close range in a 3–0 group stage victory over [[Turkey national football team|Turkey]] at the [[Allianz Riviera|Stade de Nice]] and also assisting [[Álvaro Morata]] for the opener.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.co.uk/report?gameId=438184|title=Spain cruise past Turkey to advance to knockout stage|publisher=ESPN FC|date=17 June 2016|access-date=17 June 2016}}</ref>
