'''Iker Muniain Goñi''' ({{IPA|eu|iker muniain ɡoɲi|lang}}, {{IPA|es|ˈikeɾ muˈnjajŋ ˈɡoɲi|lang}};{{efn-lg|In isolation, ''Muniain'' is pronounced {{IPA|es|muˈnjajn|}}.}} born 19 December 1992) is a Spanish former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played mainly as a [[Winger (association football)|winger]] but also as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]]. He is currently [[Manager (association football)|manager]] of [[Segunda Federación]] club [[Salamanca CF UDS|Salamanca UDS]].

He began his career with [[Athletic Bilbao]], debuting aged 16 in 2009 as their youngest player in a competitive match. He helped the team reach the final of the [[UEFA Europa League]] in [[2012 UEFA Europa League final|2012]] and played in [[Copa del Rey]] finals in [[2012 Copa del Rey final|2012]], [[2020 Copa del Rey final|2020]] and [[2021 Copa del Rey final|2021]], but finished on the losing side each time. He took part in 560 games for the club while scoring 76 goals, and lifted the Spanish Cup as [[Captain (association football)|captain]] in [[2024 Copa del Rey final|2024]] a few months before leaving to end a 19-year association. Following his departure, he joined [[San Lorenzo de Almagro|San Lorenzo]] of Argentina.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ole.com.ar/san-lorenzo/san-lorenzo_0_N8Vha59hiA.html|title=Muniain: los números de su carrera y su último partido oficial|trans-title=Muniain: his career numbers and his last official match|newspaper=[[Olé (sports newspaper)|Olé]]|first=Matías|last=Arena|language=es|date=4 September 2024|access-date=6 May 2026}}</ref>

Muniain made 59 appearances for [[Spain national youth football team|Spain at youth level]], winning the [[UEFA European Under-21 Championship|European Under-21 Championship]] in [[2011 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|2011]] and [[2013 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|2013]]. He also featured at the [[Football at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Olympics]], in the same year as his senior [[Spain national football team|Spain]] debut. He was selected again in 2019, gaining a second international [[Cap (sport)|cap]] seven years after the first.

==Club career==
===Athletic Bilbao===
====Precocious debut====
Born in [[Pamplona]], [[Navarre]], Muniain was a product of [[Basque Country (autonomous community)|Basque]] giants [[Athletic Bilbao]]'s youth ranks after joining at the age of 12.<ref name=Reaches>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2011/12/19/futbol/equipos/athletic/1324289157.html|title=Muniain alcanza los 19|trans-title=Muniain reaches 19|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|first=Endika|last=Martínez|language=es|date=19 December 2011|access-date=27 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2012/01/09/actualidad/1326097323_850215.html|title=Burgui & Muni|newspaper=[[El País]]|first=Eduardo|last=Rodrigálvarez|language=es|date=9 January 2012|access-date=15 July 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.athletic-club.eus/en/news/2021/01/27/athletic-club-a-way-of-life|title=Athletic Club: a way of life|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=27 January 2021|access-date=28 January 2021}}</ref> In January 2009, he made his debut for the reserve team [[Athletic Bilbao B|Bilbao Athletic]] in the [[Segunda División B]], aged 16 years and 16 days, and scored his first goal at that level 19 days later.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.eus/en/players/924/muniain.html|title=Muniain – 2008–09 season|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|access-date=23 September 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170802131503/http://www.athletic-club.eus/en/players/924/muniain.html|archive-date=2 August 2017}}</ref>

Muniain made his first-team debut on 30 July 2009, in a [[UEFA Europa League]] [[2009–10 UEFA Europa League|qualifying match]] against [[BSC Young Boys]]: he entered the field as a 59th-minute [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for [[Gaizka Toquero]] in an eventual 1–0 home defeat, thus becoming the youngest player in 94 years to wear Athletic's shirt in an official game at 16 years, 7 months and 11 days old,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2009/07/30/mas_futbol/1248904863_850215.html|title=El Young Boys toma La Catedral|trans-title=Young Boys take The Cathedral|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|first=Abel|last=Romera|language=es|date=30 July 2009|access-date=31 December 2015}}</ref> only behind [[Domingo Acedo]] who scored on his debut in 1914.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.europapress.es/deportes/futbol-00162/noticia-futbol-iker-muniain-16-anos-convierte-segundo-jugador-mas-joven-debutar-athletic-20090730234739.html|title=Iker Muniain, con 16 años, se convierte en el segundo jugador más joven en debutar con el Athletic|trans-title=Iker Muniain, 16, becomes the second youngest player to debut with Athletic|publisher=[[Europa Press]]|language=es|date=31 July 2009|access-date=27 July 2017}}</ref> One week later, in the return leg in [[Switzerland]], he netted his first goal, in a 2–1 win that qualified for the playoff rounds; he again entered the club's record books as the joint-second-youngest player to find the net (16 years, 7 months and 18 days) in a competitive match – behind Acedo and level with [[Agustín Gaínza]]<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/20090730/muniain-se-cita-con-la-historia_53754562211.html|title=Muniain se cita con la historia|trans-title=Muniain has an appointment with history|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|language=es|date=30 July 2009|access-date=30 July 2017}}</ref>– and the youngest ever [[Athletic Bilbao in European football|in a European match]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/01dc-0e72937dc75b-e2de610e8c1a-1000--spirit-shows-through-on-exciting-night/|title=Spirit shows through on exciting night|publisher=UEFA|date=6 August 2009|access-date=24 August 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2009/08/06/futbol/equipos/athletic/1249591514.html|title=Muniain, el más joven en marcar con el Athletic |trans-title=Muniain, the youngest to score for Athletic|newspaper=Marca|first1=Manuel|last1=Malagón|first2=Juan Antonio|last2=Jiménez|language=es|date=6 August 2009|access-date=17 July 2017}}</ref>

Another record fell on 30 August 2009, as Muniain started in the 1–0 home victory over [[RCD Espanyol]], [[2009–10 La Liga|2009–10]]'s opener, becoming the youngest player to have donned the club's shirt in [[La Liga]] (overtaking [[Patxi Ferreira]]).<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/20090901/muniain-ya-es-el-leon-mas-joven-en-la-historia-de-la-liga_53776358316.html|title=Muniain ya es el león más joven en la historia de la Liga|trans-title=Muniain is now the youngest lion in the history of the League|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Álvaro|last=Suso|language=es|date=1 September 2009|access-date=30 July 2017}}</ref> Two weeks later he scored again in European competition, 3–0 at home against [[FK Austria Wien]], after a good team move involving [[Andoni Iraola]] and veteran [[Joseba Etxeberria]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=283502&cc=5739&league=UEFA.EUROPA|title=Muniaín to the fore for brilliant Bilbao|publisher=[[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]]|date=17 September 2009|access-date=24 October 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604112449/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=283502&cc=5739&league=UEFA.EUROPA|archive-date=4 June 2011}}</ref>

On 4 October 2009, Muniain became the youngest player to score in a first division match as he achieved that feat in a 2–2 draw at [[Real Valladolid]], aged 16 years and 289 days<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/12/spain/2009/10/05/1542701/athletic-bilbao-prodigy-iker-Muniaín-becomes-primera|title=Athletic Bilbao prodigy Iker Muniaín becomes Primera Division's youngest ever goalscorer|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|first=Anthony|last=Wright|date=5 October 2009|access-date=19 January 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=275879&cc=5739&league=ESP.1|title=Valladolid and Bilbao share thriller|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=4 October 2009|access-date=24 October 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604112513/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=275879&cc=5739&league=ESP.1|archive-date=4 June 2011}}</ref>– that record was surpassed by [[Málaga CF]]'s [[Fabrice Olinga]] in August 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://bizkaia.eldesmarque.com/athletic-club/noticias/31987-muniain-se-queda-sin-el-recrod-de-goleador-mas-joven-de-la-liga|title=Muniain se queda sin el récord de goleador más joven de la Liga|trans-title=Muniain loses the League's youngest scorer record|publisher=El Desmarque|first=Álvaro|last=Moscoso|language=es|date=19 August 2012|access-date=27 July 2017}}</ref> On 1 December he signed his first professional contract, running until June 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=1142164.html|title=Muniaín signs Athletic deal|publisher=FIFA|date=1 December 2009|access-date=19 January 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091204155731/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=1142164.html|archive-date=4 December 2009}}</ref> On the 6th, after nearly one month out due to injury, he returned to action, scoring as a 51st-minute substitute to give his team the lead, albeit in a 2–1 loss to [[Valencia CF]]. He [[Assist (association football)|set up]] both goals in the next game, a 2–1 win at [[Real Zaragoza]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2009/12/12/futbol/1260645437.html|title=El Athletic firma el finiquito de Marcelino|trans-title=Marcelino runs out of credit courtesy of Athletic|newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]|language=es|date=13 December 2009|access-date=1 January 2016}}</ref> and finished his [[2009–10 La Liga|first senior season]] with 35 appearances and six goals across all competitions.

====2010s====
[[File:Шахтер-Атлетик (4).jpg|thumb|left|upright|Muniain in a [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] game against [[FC Shakhtar Donetsk|Shakhtar Donetsk]] in 2014]]
Muniain was an undisputed starter in the [[2010–11 La Liga|2010–11 campaign]], featuring as a left winger for the [[Joaquín Caparrós]]-led side. On 17 April 2011, he scored a [[last-minute goal]] in a 2–1 away defeat of [[CA Osasuna]] in his hometown;<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=302016&cc=5739|title=Last-gasp Athletic rattle Rojillos|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=17 April 2011|access-date=28 April 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024180008/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=302016&cc=5739|archive-date=24 October 2012}}</ref> he was initially booked for taking his hand to his ear during his celebrations (before signing for Athletic he played for [[UDC Txantrea]] in Pamplona, and always considered Osasuna a rival organisation. He did clarify that, just because he had affection for a particular organisation, it did not mean he held any animosity towards any others)<ref>{{cite news|url=http://athletic.elcorreo.com/noticias/2010-11-25/muniain-athletic-desde-siempre-201011251626.html|title=Muniain:"Soy del Athletic desde siempre, Osasuna nunca me ha dado nada"|trans-title=Muniain: "I've always been from Athletic, Osasuna has never given me anything"|newspaper=[[El Correo]]|language=es|date=25 November 2010|access-date=31 August 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.resultados-futbol.com/noticia/iker-muniain-explica-declaraciones-osasuna|title=Iker Muniain explica las declaraciones sobre Osasuna|trans-title=Iker Muniain explains statements on Osasuna|publisher=Resultados Fútbol|language=es|date=April 2011|access-date=30 October 2020}}</ref> which meant a suspension for his fifth [[Penalty card#Yellow card|yellow card]] of the season,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.europapress.es/deportes/futbol-00162/noticia-futbol-athletic-recurrira-cedd-tarjeta-Muniaín-solicitara-suspension-cautelar-sancion-20110420171537.html|title=El Athletic recurrirá ante el CEDD la tarjeta de Muniaín y solicitará la suspensión cautelar de la sanción|trans-title=Athletic to appeal CEDD on Muniaín yellow card, asking for temporary suspension lift|publisher=Europa Press|language=es|date=20 April 2011|access-date=12 June 2013}}</ref> but it was later lifted. Now allowed to take part in the following matchday, the [[Basque derby|derby]] against [[Real Sociedad]], he netted another in a 2–1 home victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=302070&cc=5739|title=Athletic claim derby spoils|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=23 April 2011|access-date=28 April 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024180028/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=302070&cc=5739|archive-date=24 October 2012}}</ref>

Muniain took part in 58 games overall in [[2011–12 La Liga|2011–12]], scoring on nine occasions as the ''Lions'' reached both the [[2012 UEFA Europa League Final|Europa League]] and the [[Copa del Rey]] finals.<ref name=Tattoo>{{cite news|url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/20120503/futbol/europa-league/muniain-promete-tatuarse-la-copa-de-la-liga-europa-si-gana-la-final_54288987254.html|title=Muniain promete tatuarse la copa de la Liga Europa si gana la final|trans-title=Muniain promises to tattoo Europa League cup if he wins final|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|language=es|date=3 May 2012|access-date=2 December 2013}}</ref> In early 2012, he was linked with a move away from Athletic, although a move never materialised as he did not push for a move with three years still left on his contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://insidefutbol.com/2012/03/30/in-demand-athletic-bilbao-forward-iker-muniain-quashes-transfer-talk/60310/|title=In-demand Athletic Bilbao forward Iker Muniain quashes transfer talk|publisher=Inside Futbol|date=30 March 2012|access-date=30 October 2020}}</ref> He scored just once in 33 league appearances the [[2012–13 La Liga|following campaign]], netting the only goal on 10 March 2013 in a home win over Valencia which eased doubts over a possible relegation battle.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rtve.es/deportes/20130310/athletic-abate-a-buen-valencia/615280.shtml|title=El Athletic abate a un buen Valencia|trans-title=Athletic down a good Valencia|publisher=[[RTVE]]|language=es|date=10 March 2013|access-date=15 January 2019}}</ref>

On 1 December 2013, Muniain was again the sole name on the scoresheet at the new [[San Mamés Stadium (2013)|San Mamés Stadium]], to hand [[FC Barcelona]] their first league loss of [[2013–14 La Liga|that season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/en/report/373069/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=null|title=Barca stunned by Muniain|publisher=ESPN FC|date=1 December 2013|access-date=2 December 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203225407/http://espnfc.com/en/report/373069/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=null|archive-date=3 December 2013}}</ref> Eighteen days later, he celebrated his 21st birthday by grabbing a brace in a 4–0 [[2013–14 Copa del Rey|domestic cup home victory]] against [[RC Celta de Vigo]], which signified his team progressed through to the [[Single-elimination tournament|round of 16]] 4–1 on aggregate.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2013_14/copa/dieciseisavos/vuelta/ath_cel/|title=Muniain aúpa al Athletic a octavos|trans-title=Muniain propels Athletic to last-16|newspaper=Marca|first=Diego|last=Acedo|language=es|date=19 December 2013|access-date=20 December 2013}}</ref> In that period, media reports suggested that his progression as a footballer in his 20s had slowed after showing such high potential as a young teenager.<ref name=Explosive>{{cite news|url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/20130116/athletic-bilbao/iker-muniain-temporada-balance_54361959122.html|title=Iker Muniain: El futbolista 'explosivo' necesita chispa|trans-title=Iker Muniain: The 'explosive' footballer needs a spark|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Iñaki|last=Ugalde|language=es|date=16 January 2013|access-date=9 March 2017}}</ref><ref name=Puzzle>{{cite web|url=https://worldfootballanalytics.com/2014/02/07/the-puzzle-that-is-iker-muniain/|title=The puzzle that is Iker Muniain|publisher=World Football Analytics|first=Pranav|last=Dar|date=7 February 2014|access-date=10 March 2021}}</ref>

====Knee injuries====
On 4 April 2015, during a game against [[Sevilla FC]], Muniain suffered the first serious injury of his career, being sidelined for several months with an [[anterior cruciate ligament]] ailment to his left knee<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2015/04/07/futbol/equipos/athletic/1428410768.html|title=Muniain estará siete meses de baja|trans-title=Muniain to miss seven months|newspaper=Marca|first=Juanma|last=Velasco|language=es|date=7 April 2015|access-date=8 April 2015}}</ref>– this meant he was unable to take any part in the year's [[2015 Copa del Rey Final|Spanish Cup]] or [[2015 Supercopa de España|Supercopa de España finals]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2015/10/23/primera/1445618997_126577.html|title=Iker Muniain: "La lesión me ha enseñado a valorar el día a día"|trans-title=Iker Muniain: "The injury has taught me to appreciate every day"|newspaper=Diario AS|language=es|date=23 October 2015|access-date=29 December 2016}}</ref> After suffering some setbacks in his recovery process<ref>{{cite web|url=http://cadenaser.com/emisora/2015/10/26/radio_bilbao/1445852754_180362.html|title=Se retrasa la reaparición de Muniain|trans-title=Muniain return delayed|publisher=[[Cadena SER]]|first=Iñigo|last=Markinez|language=es|date=26 October 2015|access-date=31 December 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2015/11/16/futbol/equipos/athletic/1447700938.html|title=Se retrasa, otra vez, el regreso de Muniain|trans-title=Muniain return delayed, again|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=16 November 2015|access-date=31 December 2015}}</ref> he returned to action on 20 December, replacing [[Iñaki Williams]] for the last minutes of a 2–0 home defeat of [[Levante UD]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2015/12/20/primera/1450627864_691465.html|title=El Athletic gana con solvencia al colista y se coloca séptimo|trans-title=Athletic defeat bottom-placed easily and rank seventh|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Nika|last=Cuenca|language=es|date=20 December 2015|access-date=31 December 2015}}</ref>

Muniain successfully regained his first-team place in December 2015 and made 86 further appearances between then and 28 September 2017, when he suffered another serious ACL injury (this time to his right knee) in the closing stages of a [[2017–18 UEFA Europa League group stage#Group J|Europa League]] fixture at home to [[FC Zorya Luhansk]], potentially ending his season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2017/09/29/59ce6ad3e5fdea97578b4628.html|title=Muniain to miss up to eight months after knee injury|newspaper=Marca|first1=Juanma|last1=Velasco|first2=Chris|last2=Winterburn|date=29 September 2017|access-date=1 October 2017}}</ref> After an absence of just over six months, he returned to action as a substitute in a [[2017–18 La Liga|domestic league]] match against [[Villarreal CF]] on 9 April 2018, scoring his side's third in a 3–1 away win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/12040/11324679/villarreal-slump-to-3-1-home-defeat-to-athletic-bilbao-in-la-liga|title=Villarreal slump to 3–1 home defeat to Athletic Bilbao in La Liga|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|date=9 April 2018|access-date=9 April 2018}}</ref>

Muniain signed a new deal with Athletic Bilbao in November 2018 to run until summer 2024, as his link was set to expire;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://insideathletic.com/2018/11/03/iker-muniain-has-no-desire-to-leave-athletic-despite-interest-from-other-clubs/|title=Iker Muniain has no desire to leave Athletic despite interest from other clubs|publisher=Inside Athletic|date=3 November 2018|access-date=30 October 2020}}</ref> unusually, it did not include any [[buyout clause]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.athletic-club.eus/en/news/19616/renewal-of-iker-muniain.html|title=Renewal of Iker Muniain|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=21 November 2018|access-date=22 November 2018}}</ref> He said: "I didn't want a release clause because I do not want to have a price or be for sale. I want to go hand in hand with Athletic to the end... I want to be here for the rest of my career helping the club achieve nice things."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://insideathletic.com/2018/11/22/iker-muniain-i-didnt-want-a-release-clause-because-i-dont-want-to-be-for-sale/|title=Iker Muniain "I didn't want a release clause because I don't want to be for sale"|publisher=Inside Athletic|date=22 November 2018|access-date=6 February 2020}}</ref> Following the departures of [[Ander Iturraspe]] and [[Markel Susaeta]] in summer 2019 he was appointed as the club [[Captain (association football)|captain]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.athletic-club.eus/en/news/2019/07/09/iker-muniain-los-mejores-fichajes-son-los-chavales-de-casa|title=Iker Muniain: "The best sign-ups are people from home"|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=9 July 2019|access-date=18 July 2019}}</ref> and also reached the milestone of ten years with the first team.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2019/07/30/primera/1564480720_144012.html|title=Muniain: 10 años del 10 del Athletic|trans-title=Muniain: 10 years of Athletic's 10|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Alfonso|last=Herrán|language=es|date=30 July 2019|access-date=27 September 2019}}</ref>

====2020s====
On 19 January 2020, Muniain became the [[List of Athletic Bilbao players|18th player in Athletic's history to play 400 official games]], against Celta.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/deportes/20200119/472974982543/muniain-alcanza-su-partido-400-con-el-athletic-con-27-anos.html|title=Muniain alcanza su partido 400 con el Athletic con 27 años|trans-title=Muniain reaches 400 games with Athletic at age 27|newspaper=[[La Vanguardia]]|language=es|date=19 January 2020|access-date=8 November 2020}}</ref> In July of that year, his 420th match set the club record for a player from Navarre, surpassing [[Ismael Urzaiz]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/athletic-bilbao/20200712/482247815101/athletic-muniain-navarra-partidos-ranking.html|title=Muniain entra en el olimpo navarro del Athletic|trans-title=Muniain enters the Navarrese Olympus of Athletic|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Endika|last=Río|language=es|date=12 July 2020|access-date=11 March 2021}}</ref> On 8 November, he made his 430th appearance to enter its top 10 (equalling [[Julen Guerrero]]'s total) at the age of 27.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cope.es/deportes/futbol/noticias/muniain-entra-top-historico-jugadores-con-mas-partidos-disputados-athletic-20201108_986848|title=Muniain entra en el 'Top' 10 histórico de jugadores con más partidos disputados en el Athletic|trans-title=Muniain enters Athletic's all-time Top 10 of players with most appearances|publisher=[[Cadena COPE]]|language=es|date=8 November 2020|access-date=8 November 2020}}</ref>

In early 2021, with the team playing a more attacking style under new coach [[Marcelino García Toral]], Muniain recorded eight assists in three competitions between 17 January and 15 February (bettering his total for some entire seasons previously),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.athletic-club.eus/en/news/2021/02/19/eight-assists-in-a-month-for-iker-muniain/|title=Eight assists in a month for Iker Muniain|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=19 February 2021|access-date=20 February 2021}}</ref> including two in the [[2021 Supercopa de España Final|Spanish Supercup final]] as his team won the trophy.<ref name=SC>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/supercopa-espana/barcelona-vs-athletic/cronica/2021/01/17/60047a8f22601dac578b45e8.html|title=La Supercopa de Williams|trans-title=Williams' Supercup|newspaper=Marca|first=Fernando|last=Carnerero|language=es|date=17 January 2021|access-date=17 January 2021}}</ref> During April of that year he took the field in the [[2020 Copa del Rey Final|2020]] (delayed due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain|COVID-19 pandemic]]) and [[2021 Copa del Rey Final|2021 Spanish Cup finals]], both played in an empty [[Estadio de la Cartuja]] – the same venue as the Supercup win – due to the pandemic restrictions. Athletic lost the first match 1–0 to Real Sociedad,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/apr/03/athletic-bilbao-real-sociedad-copa-del-rey-2020-final-match-report|title=Real Sociedad beat Athletic to claim Copa del Rey and Basque glory|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|first=Sid|last=Lowe|date=3 April 2021|access-date=24 May 2021}}</ref> with Muniain breaking a footballing superstition before kick-off by touching the trophy (considered to be 'bad luck')<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.deia.eus/athletic/2021/04/04/tocas-iker/1110751.html|title=¿Para qué tocas la Copa, Iker?|trans-title=Why do you touch the Cup, Iker?|newspaper=[[Deia (newspaper)|Deia]]|first=Aitor|last=Martínez|language=es|date=4 April 2021|access-date=25 May 2021}}</ref> but praised for his sportsmanship for staying on the pitch after the final whistle to applaud the winners.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football24.news/sport-today/195549/muniains-gesture-of-sportsmanship-in-the-celebration-of-the-real.html|title=Muniain's gesture of sportsmanship in the celebration of the Real|publisher=Football 24 News|date=4 April 2021|access-date=24 May 2021}}</ref> A pre-match injury doubt for the second final two weeks later, he stated to the press "Cups and trophies are not won or lost because one touches it or not. They are won on the pitch, and that is the only reality", but this time it was noted he kept his hands well away from the prize;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://noticias24chile.com/muniain-la-mira-pero-no-la-toca/|title=Muniain la mira, pero no la toca|trans-title=Muniain looks, but does not touch|publisher=Noticias 24 Chile|language=es|date=17 April 2021|access-date=24 May 2021|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210524144916/https://noticias24chile.com/muniain-la-mira-pero-no-la-toca/|archive-date=24 May 2021}}</ref> nevertheless, his team were defeated 4–0 by Barcelona, he was withdrawn at half-time with the score at 0–0<ref name=Thrash>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/apr/17/messi-stars-as-barcelona-thrash-athletic-bilbao-to-lift-copa-del-rey|title=Messi stars as Barcelona thrash Athletic Bilbao to lift Copa del Rey|newspaper=The Guardian|first=Sid|last=Lowe|date=17 April 2021|access-date=19 April 2021}}</ref> and did not feature again that season, missing the last eight league fixtures.

On 31 October 2021, Muniain scored a late equaliser in the Basque derby via a [[Free kick (association football)|free kick]] and was again conspicuous for his sportsmanship in consoling the opposing goalkeeper [[Álex Remiro]], a former Athletic player whose error had contributed to the goal.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2021/nov/01/athletic-bilbao-real-sociedad-iker-muniain-basque-derby|title=Muniain emerges from wild night to show why Basque derby is different|newspaper=The Guardian|first=Sid|last=Lowe|date=1 November 2021|access-date=4 November 2021}}</ref> In February 2022, it was assessed that he had created 60 scoring chances in that [[2021–22 La Liga|league campaign]] and 72 in all competitions, the most by any player by both counts.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://theanalyst.com/eu/2022/02/iker-muniain-the-athletic-bilbao-magician-out-to-break-his-copa-del-rey-curse/|title=Iker Muniain: The Athletic Bilbao magician out to break his Copa del Rey curse|publisher=The Analyst|first=Joe|last=Wright|date=2 February 2022|access-date=8 February 2022}}</ref> Despite knocking both Barcelona and Real Madrid out of the domestic cup, they lost in the [[2021–22 Copa del Rey|semi-finals]] to Valencia, and finished the league campaign in eighth, just out of the European qualification places.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2022/jun/04/its-the-sids-2022-the-complete-review-of-la-liga-2021-22-season|title=It’s the Sids 2022! The complete review of La Liga’s 2021–22 season|newspaper=The Guardian|first=Sid|last=Lowe|date=4 June 2022|access-date=8 April 2024}}</ref>

Muniain made his 500th appearance for Athletic on the first matchday of [[2022–23 La Liga|2022–23]] against [[RCD Mallorca]], reaching the milestone at a younger age than the five other players to do so.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.athletic-club.eus/en/news/2022/08/14/muniain-makes-his-500th-official-appearance|title=Muniain makes his 500th official appearance|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=15 August 2022|access-date=23 August 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eldesmarque.com/bizkaia/athletic-club/noticias/325780-muniain-emocionado-por-el-carino-recibido-tras-cumplir-500-partidos-con-el-athletic-sigamos-recorriendo-este-camino-juntos|title=Muniain, emocionado por el cariño recibido tras cumplir 500 partidos con el Athletic: "Sigamos recorriendo este camino juntos"|trans-title=Muniain, moved by the love received after completing 500 games with Athletic: "Let's continue down this path together"|publisher=El Desmarque|first=Pablo|last=Sánchez|language=es|date=16 August 2022|access-date=23 August 2022}}</ref> He was honoured in a reception after that match,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-espana.net/2022/08/16/iker-muniain-breaks-record-as-he-reaches-500-games-with-athletic-club/amp|title=Iker Muniain breaks record as he reaches 500 games with Athletic Club|publisher=Football España|first=Ruairidh|last=Barlow|date=16 August 2022|access-date=23 August 2022}}</ref> and was presented with a memento by two of those men – [[José Ángel Iribar]] and Susaeta – on the pitch before the next fixture against Valencia six days later.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.athletic-club.eus/en/news/2022/08/20/muniain-to-be-given-symbolic-trophy-for-his-500-matches|title=Muniain to be given symbolic trophy for his 500 matches|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=20 August 2022|access-date=23 August 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.diariodenavarra.es/noticias/deportes/futbol/2022/08/21/iker-muniain-recibe-simbolico-trofeo-500-partidos-el-athletic-538546-1022.html|title=Iker Muniain recibe un simbólico trofeo por sus 500 partidos con el Athletic|trans-title=Iker Muniain receives a symbolic trophy for his 500 games with Athletic|newspaper=[[Diario de Navarra]]|language=es|date=21 August 2022|access-date=23 August 2022}}</ref> After a promising start under returning coach [[Ernesto Valverde]] the team again finished eighth and lost narrowly in the [[2022–23 Copa del Rey|cup semi-finals]] (this time to Osasuna);<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/ibanez-goal-sends-osasuna-into-copa-del-rey-final-after-dramatic-draw-2023-04-04/|title=Ibanez goal sends Osasuna into Copa del Rey final after dramatic draw|publisher=[[Reuters]]|date=5 April 2023|access-date=21 December 2023}}</ref> he featured regularly but became less of a habitual starter, coming off the bench in 11 of his 30 league appearances.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/athletic-bilbao/20230711/1002036191/ano-mas-importante-capitan-athletic.html|title=El año más importante del capitán del Athletic|trans-title=The most important year of Athletic's captain|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Carlos|last=Zaballa|language=es|date=11 July 2023|access-date=25 January 2024}}</ref>

Athletic also began [[2023–24 La Liga|2023–24]] strongly, but Muniain was selected rarely during the first half of the season, with Valverde opting for [[Oihan Sancet]] as the starting attacking midfielder and either [[Álex Berenguer]] or rookie [[Unai Gómez]] as an offensive substitute.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.deia.eus/athletic/2023/12/05/encrucijada-iker-muniain-athletic-7603039.html|title=La encrucijada de Iker Muniain y del Athletic|trans-title=The crossroads of Iker Muniain and Athletic|newspaper=Deia|first=José Luis|last=Artetxe|language=es|date=5 December 2023|access-date=21 December 2023}}</ref> On 30 September against Real Sociedad, he reached 542 appearances for the club, surpassing [[Txetxu Rojo]]'s record for an outfield player (albeit with far fewer minutes overall)<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elcorreo.com/athletic/ranking-justo-jugado-athletic-rojo-muniain-20231017180940-nt.html|title=Un ranking más justo, ¿quién ha jugado más en el Athletic, Rojo o Muniain?|trans-title=A fairer ranking: who has played more for Athletic, Rojo or Muniain?|newspaper=El Correo|first=Juan Carlos|last=Latxaga|language=es|date=17 October 2023|access-date=4 November 2024|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bdfutbol.com/en/e/egols6.html|title=Players list of Athletic Club] [Sort applied: Minutes]|publisher=BDFutbol|access-date=4 November 2024}}</ref> and trailing Iribar alone.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://athletic.elcorreo.com/muniain-entra-club-elegidos-20230930194959-nt.html|title=Muniain entra en el club de los elegidos|trans-title=Muniain enters into the chosen club|newspaper=El Correo|first=Juanma|last=Mallo|language=es|date=30 September 2023|access-date=23 December 2023}}</ref> In the [[2024 Copa del Rey final|Spanish Cup final]] against Mallorca, he was brought on as a substitute at the start of extra time with the score at 1–1. He narrowly missed the target with a free kick, and then scored his penalty in the subsequent shootout; Berenguer converted the winning kick, and the team claimed the trophy for the first time in 40 years.<ref name=COPA>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/copa_del_rey/final-de-copa-del-rey-en-directo-ultima-hora-de-mallorca-y-athletic-n/|title=Athletic 1–1 (4–2) Mallorca, en directo: final de Copa del Rey 2024 {{!}} Celebración del Athletic, campeón de Copa|trans-title=Athletic 1–1 (4–2) Mallorca, live: 2024 King's Cup final {{!}} Celebrations of Athletic, Cup champions|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Mario|last=Reinoso del Real|language=es|date=7 April 2024|access-date=7 April 2024}}</ref>

Although there was some expectation that he may remain for the upcoming European campaign,<ref name=Abroad>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/primera/muniain-jugara-en-el-extranjero-n/|title=Muniain jugará en el extranjero|trans-title=Muniain will play abroad|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Javier|last=Rodríguez Beltrán|language=es|date=24 April 2024|access-date=24 April 2024}}</ref> on 24 April 2024 Muniain announced he would leave Athletic on 30 June, marking the end of his 15-year tenure in which he became the second-highest appearance maker in the club's history (560 matches); he declared himself happy with the timing of his departure having won the cup,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.athletic-club.eus/en/news/2024/04/24/muniain-decides-to-leave-athletic-on-top/|title=Muniain decides to leave Athletic on top|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=24 April 2024|access-date=24 April 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.deia.eus/athletic/2024/04/24/iker-muniain-athletic-anuncia-salida-8154587.html|title=Muniain no seguirá en el Athletic: "Me voy feliz"|trans-title=Muniain will not continue at Athletic: "I am leaving happy"|newspaper=Deia|first=Aitor|last=Martínez|language=es|date=24 April 2024|access-date=24 April 2024}}</ref> and it was speculated that he would move abroad to continue his playing career.<ref name=Abroad/> His appearance record stood for just over a year before being overtaken in February 2025 by long-time teammate [[Óscar de Marcos]], who had also replaced him as captain.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.athletic-club.eus/en/news/2025/02/23/de-marcos-becomes-second-most-capped-athletic-player-ever/|title=De Marcos becomes second most capped Athletic player ever|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=25 February 2025|access-date=25 February 2025}}</ref>

===San Lorenzo===
Muniain made several trips to Argentina, declaring that he wanted to play in that country, and held talks with [[Leandro Romagnoli]], the coach of [[San Lorenzo de Almagro]]; on 3 September 2024 he signed a contract running to December 2025, with the latter declaring that the former's role would be as a playmaker located behind the striker.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.infobae.com/deportes/2024/09/03/el-espanol-iker-muniain-a-un-paso-de-ser-refuerzo-de-san-lorenzo-esta-avanzado-lo-vi-con-ganas-de-venir/|title=El español Iker Muniain, a un paso de ser refuerzo de San Lorenzo: "Lo vi con ganas de venir"|trans-title=Spaniard Iker Muniain, one step away from being a San Lorenzo reinforcement: "I saw him wanting to come"|newspaper=[[Infobae]]|language=es|date=3 September 2024|access-date=7 September 2024}}</ref> He became the tenth Spaniard to play for the club, one of the most prominent being [[Ángel Zubieta]] who also represented Athletic Bilbao.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mundoazulgrana.com.ar/sanlorenzo/noticias/38517/los_jugadores_espa%C3%83%E2%80%98oles_en_san_lorenzo_de_almagro.html|title=Los jugadores españoles que pasaron por San Lorenzo|trans-title=The Spanish players who passed through San Lorenzo|publisher=Mundo Azulgrana|first=Leandro|last=D'Ambrosio|language=es|date=28 August 2024|access-date=7 September 2024}}</ref>

On 28 September 2024, Muniain scored his first [[Argentine Primera División|Primera División]] goals, a brace in the 2–1 home win over [[Club Atlético Banfield]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lavoz.com.ar/deportes/futbol/con-doblete-de-muniain-san-lorenzo-vencio-2-a-1-a-banfield/|title=Liga Profesional. Con doblete de Muniain, San Lorenzo venció 2 a 1 a Banfield|trans-title=Professional League. With Muniain brace, San Lorenzo beat Banfield 2 to 1|newspaper=[[La Voz del Interior]]|language=es|date=28 September 2024|access-date=8 November 2024}}</ref> In June 2025, he announced he was leaving the [[Estadio Pedro Bidegain]] in order to return to Spain.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.infobae.com/deportes/2025/06/20/iker-muniain-anuncio-su-salida-de-san-lorenzo-y-puso-en-duda-su-futuro-como-futbolista/|title=Iker Muniain anunció su salida de San Lorenzo y puso en duda su futuro como futbolista|trans-title=Iker Muniain announced his departure from San Lorenzo and cast doubt over his future as a footballer|newspaper=Infobae|language=es|date=20 June 2025|access-date=29 June 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Abdelatif Noussir (cropped2).jpg|thumb|Muniain (back) chasing [[Abdelatif Noussir]] at the 2012 Olympics]]
On 8 February 2011, at the age of only 18, Muniain made his debut with the [[Spain national under-21 football team|Spain under-21 team]] in a match against [[Denmark national under-21 football team|Denmark]], replacing [[Adrián López]]. Subsequently, he was selected by manager [[Luis Milla (footballer, born 1966)|Luis Milla]] to the squad that appeared in the [[2011 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|2011 UEFA European Championship]], appearing in all the games as the nation won its third title in the category<ref name=U21>{{cite web|url=http://www.diariosdefutbol.com/2011/06/25/espana-sub-21-campeona-de-europa-el-ciclo-continua/|title=España sub-21, campeona de Europa: El ciclo continúa|trans-title=Spain under-21, European champion: The cycle continues|publisher=Diarios de Fútbol|first=Pol|last=Gustems|language=es|date=25 June 2011|access-date=8 September 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208051124/http://www.diariosdefutbol.com/2011/06/25/espana-sub-21-campeona-de-europa-el-ciclo-continua/|archive-date=8 December 2015}}</ref> and qualified for the [[Football at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Summer Olympics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/olympics/18693622|title=Euro 2012 trio Mata, Alba & Martinez in Spain Olympic squad|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=5 July 2012|access-date=8 September 2017}}</ref>

On 24 February 2012, Muniain was called up to the [[Spain national football team|senior side]] for the first time, for a [[Exhibition game|friendly]] with [[Venezuela national football team|Venezuela]]. Five days later, he came on for [[Cesc Fàbregas]] in the 74th minute of the 5–0 win in [[Málaga]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/marcador/futbol/2011_12/amistosos_seleccion/1/spa_vnz/|title=Celestiales|trans-title=Heavenly|newspaper=Marca|first=Fran|last=Villalobos|language=es|date=29 February 2012|access-date=29 February 2012}}</ref> Later [[2012 Summer Olympics|that year]], at the [[Summer Olympic Games]] in London, he made two appearances as [[Spain national under-23 football team|Spain]] exited in the [[Football at the 2012 Summer Olympics|group stage]] without scoring a goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/match/spain-u23-vs-morocco-u23/1281843/report|title=Spain 0–0 Morocco: La Roja fail to fire again to finish bottom of Olympics Group D|publisher=Goal|date=1 August 2012|access-date=2 October 2017}}</ref>

Muniain earned 31 [[Cap (sport)|caps]] for the under-21s, which was a national record<ref>{{cite web|url=http://bizkaia.eldesmarque.com/athletic-club/noticias/43116-muniain-se-despide-de-la-seleccion-sub-21|title=Muniain se despide de la selección sub-21|trans-title=Muniain bids farewell to under-21 national team|publisher=El Desmarque|language=es|date=8 November 2014|access-date=23 September 2016}}</ref> for three years before being surpassed by [[Gerard Deulofeu]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://es.uefa.com/under21/news/0257-0dedfbf209a9-635929edec4e-1000--celebracion-feliz-para-el-hombre-record/|title=Celebración feliz para el hombre récord|trans-title=Happy celebration for the recordman|publisher=UEFA|first=Santi|last=Retortillo|language=es|date=15 November 2016|access-date=24 April 2024}}</ref> In 2019, after showing fine form for his club, he was selected in the senior squad for two [[UEFA Euro 2020 qualifying]] matches;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sefutbol.com/en/official-call-first-two-euro-qualifier-matches|title=Official: Call-up for the first two EURO Qualifier matches|publisher=[[Royal Spanish Football Federation]]|date=15 March 2019|access-date=15 March 2019|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190327091031/https://www.sefutbol.com/en/official-call-first-two-euro-qualifier-matches|archive-date=27 March 2019}}</ref> he played his second match more than seven years after the first, as well as his competitive debut, as a substitute in a 2–0 victory over [[Malta national football team|Malta]] on 26 March.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47714650|title=Euro 2020 qualifying: Alvaro Morata helps Spain edge past Malta|publisher=BBC Sport|date=26 March 2019|access-date=26 March 2019}}</ref>

Muniain also featured for the unofficial [[Basque Country national football team|Basque Country regional team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eff-fvf.eus/pub/verFichaPartido.asp?idioma=ca&idPartido=1261|title=Catalunya 0–1 Euskal Selekzioa|trans-title=Catalonia 0–1 Basque XI|publisher=[[Basque Football Federation]]|language=es|date=26 December 2015|access-date=29 December 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190327090021/http://www.eff-fvf.eus/pub/verFichaPartido.asp?idioma=ca&idPartido=1261|archive-date=27 March 2019}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
On 28 June 2025, Muniain announced his retirement at age 32. He was immediately appointed as manager of [[Tercera Federación]] side [[CD Derio]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/2025/06/28/bombazo-muniain-nuevo-entrenador-cd-derio.html|title=Bombazo: Muniain, nuevo entrenador del CD Derio|trans-title=Bomb: Muniain, new manager of CD Derio|newspaper=Marca|first=Mario|last=Jiménez|language=es|date=28 June 2025|access-date=29 June 2025}}</ref>

Muniain became head coach of [[Segunda Federación]]'s [[Salamanca CF UDS]] on 15 June 2026.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/2026/06/15/iker-muniain-nuevo-entrenador-salamanca-uds.html|title=Iker Muniain, nuevo entrenador del Salamanca UDS|trans-title=Iker Muniain, new manager of Salamanca UDS|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=15 June 2026|access-date=21 September 2026}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Due to his style of play and stature, Muniain was dubbed "the Spanish [[Lionel Messi|Messi]]" by the media as a teenager.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportsvibe.co.uk/news/football/manchester-united-given-go-ahead-to-sign-the-new-messi-11778|title=Manchester United given go-ahead to sign the "New Messi"|publisher=Sports Vibe|date=19 October 2011|access-date=7 March 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111222045046/http://www.sportsvibe.co.uk/news/football/manchester-united-given-go-ahead-to-sign-the-new-messi-11778|archive-date=22 December 2011}}</ref>

'''Franck Jurietti''' (born 30 March 1975) is a French former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Full-back (association football)|full-back]]. He spent most of his career with [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]].

==Club career==
Jurietti's professional career started at [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]], having already been part of their youth team. However, he did not get to play a single game and was transferred to [[FC Gueugnon|Gueugnon]] at the end of the season. There he achieved promotion to [[Ligue 1|Division 1]] for his first year at the club, and on 19 July 1995, he played his first Ligue 1 match against [[FC Metz|Metz]]. At the end of the season, Gueugnon were again relegated, and, after one more year in Ligue 2 where they were unable to achieve back promotion, Jurietti left the club to [[SC Bastia]], where he stayed for three years.{{citation needed|date=April 2025}}

In 2000, he was transferred to [[AS Monaco|Monaco]] where he was never quite able to settle and after 6 months, he was loaned for the rest of the season to rivals [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]]. He returned to Monaco for one more season and had a trial spell with [[Premier League]] side [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] in 2003 but did not secure a contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11671/2255577/jurietti-explains-toffees-snub|title=Jurietti explains Toffees snub|date=February 2003|accessdate=6 April 2018}}</ref> He then joined [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]], the club in which he has been the most successful so far, winning the championship once (after finishing twice runner-up) and the [[Coupe de la Ligue]] twice. He was the captain during the [[Coupe de la Ligue Final 2009|final]] against [[Vannes OC|Vannes]] that Bordeaux won 4–0.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lfp.fr/coupeLigueFinale2009/|title=Coupe de la Ligue Final 2009|language=French|date=25 April 2009|accessdate=30 May 2009|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090429133307/http://www.lfp.fr/coupeLigueFinale2009/|archivedate=29 April 2009}}</ref>

His contract expired in 2010, and he was notified by manager [[Laurent Blanc]] that it would not be renewed,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sofoot.com/bordeaux-lateraux-en-peril-129349-news.html|title=Bordeaux, latéraux en péril|language=French|date=19 July 2010|accessdate=9 October 2010 }}</ref> effectively putting an end to his playing career.{{citation needed|date=April 2025}}

==International career==
In 2005, after an excellent start of season with Bordeaux, Jurietti was called up by [[Raymond Domenech]] for the [[France national football team|France national team]] for the final two [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006 World Cup]] [[2006 FIFA World Cup qualification - UEFA Group 4|qualifying]] matches.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lematin.ma/Actualite/Express/ArticlePrint.asp?id=54845|title=Franck Jurietti, joueur de devoir|language=French|date=7 October 2005|accessdate=21 May 2009|archive-date=16 July 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716060028/http://www.lematin.ma/Actualite/Express/ArticlePrint.asp?id=54845|url-status=dead}}</ref> After remaining an unused substitute against [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]], Jurietti made his international debut on 12 October 2005 during the 4–0 victory against [[Cyprus national football team|Cyprus]], but only came on for the last five seconds in what was to remain his sole international appearance. This makes him the French player with the shortest international career ever, ahead of [[Bernard Boissier]], who had played two minutes for France in 1975.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.foot-news.com/index.php?2006/03/10/150-equipe-de-france-les-records|title=Équipe de France : Les records !|language=French|date=10 March 2006|accessdate=21 May 2009 }}</ref>

==Style of play==
Jurietti could play on both sides of the defence, and was also known to fill in as a midfielder when called upon. He  developed a reputation for being one of the most "dangerous" players in the French league.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.chezlesgirondins.com/effectif/grands-mystere-de-la-science-jurietti/20060923191.html|title=Les grands mystères de la Science : Franck Jurietti|language=French|date=23 September 2006|accessdate=9 October 2010|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120522055907/http://www.chezlesgirondins.com/effectif/grands-mystere-de-la-science-jurietti/20060923191.html|archivedate=22 May 2012}}</ref>

'''Salvatore Lanna''' (born 31 July 1976 in [[Carpi (Modena)|Carpi]], [[Province of Modena|Modena]]) is the [[Italy|Italian]] [[association football]] former player who spent his career playing as a [[Defender (football)|defender]]. He is currently [[Eugenio Corini]]'s assistant coach at [[Union Brescia]].

==Biography==
===Playing career===
====From Chievo to Torino====
He is one of the most famous players in the history of [[A.C. ChievoVerona|Chievo]], having played there for eleven seasons.

After Chievo were relegated to [[Serie B]] in 2007, he was transferred to [[Torino F.C.|Torino]] on a three-year contract.

In August 2008, newly promoted [[Bologna F.C. 1909|Bologna]] agreed a fee with [[Torino F.C.|Torino]] to sign Lanna in a co-ownership deal.

====Reggiana====
He has played for [[A.C. Reggiana 1919|Reggiana]] from the 2010–11 season until the end of December 2011.

====Italy national team====
Late in 2002, he was called up twice to the [[Italy national football team|Italy national team]] by their then-coach, [[Giovanni Trapattoni]], but did not play a game either time.

===Coaching career===
On 3 January 2012, he was announced as the new assistant coach of [[A.C. Reggiana 1919|Reggiana]] in [[Lega Pro Prima Divisione]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.reggianacalcio.it/index.php?prt=newsp&id=0003402|title = AC Reggiana 1919 - Sito Ufficiale|date = 17 January 2017}}</ref>

In December 2016, he was named the new assistant coach at [[Palermo FC|Palermo]] as part of [[Eugenio Corini]]'s backroom staff. He left the club following Corini's resignation in January 2017.

He successively followed Corini on his coaching experiences at [[Novara Calcio|Novara]], [[Brescia Calcio|Brescia]] and [[U.S. Lecce|Lecce]]. In August 2022, he again followed Corini after he agreed to return to Palermo.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.palermofc.com/it/news/nuovi-componenti-nello-staff-tecnico_38090/ |publisher=[[Palermo FC]] |language=it-IT |date=10 August 2022 |title=NUOVI COMPONENTI NELLO STAFF TECNICO}}</ref> He went on to work with Corini also at [[US Cremonese|Cremonese]] in 2024, and [[Union Brescia]] from 2025.
