'''Konstantinos''' "'''Kostas'''" '''Manolas''' ({{langx|el|Κωνσταντίνος "Κώστας" Μανωλάς}}; {{IPA|el|konsta(n)ˈdinos ˈkostaz manoˈlas|pron}};{{efn|In isolation, ''Κώστας'' is pronounced {{IPA|el|ˈkostas|}}.}} born 14 June 1991) is a Greek [[Association football|footballer]] who plays for Greek club [[Pannaxiakos F.C.|Pannaxiakos]]. A [[Defender (association football)|defender]] throughout his career, Manolas also plays as a [[Striker (association football)|striker]] for [[Pannaxiakos F.C.|Pannaxiakos]] since 2024.

==Club career==

===AEK Athens===

====2009–10 season====
Manolas began his youth career at [[Thrasyvoulos F.C.|Thrasyvoulos]] in 2008.<ref name="Super League Greece Profile">{{cite web |url=https://www.slgr.gr/el/player/124/ |title=Kostas Manolas Profile |publisher=Super League Greece |date=10 September 2022 |access-date=30 September 2022 }}</ref> In 2009, his uncle [[Stelios Manolas]], who was the [[technical director]] of [[AEK Athens F.C.|AEK Athens]] at the time, was scouting his nephew at a youth match with AEK manager [[Dušan Bajević]] and was impressed with his performance.<ref name="Roma Profile">{{cite web |url=https://www.asroma.com/en/player-profile-bios/kostas-manolas-profile-new |title=Kostas Manolas Profile New |publisher=A.S. Roma |date=14 August 2018 |access-date=30 September 2019 }}</ref>

On 16 June 2009, Manolas signed a three-year deal with AEK.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.aekfc.gr/index.asp?a_id=74&n_id=5107|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090619202819/http://www.aekfc.gr/index.asp?a_id=74&n_id=5107|url-status=dead|title=AEK FC signs Manolas|archivedate=19 June 2009}}</ref> After signing, Manolas said, "I am very happy signing for the team I support, hopefully I can be a legend at the club like my uncle and end my career at AEK." He made his debut against [[Nea Kavala F.C.|Kavala]] and was named [[man of the match]]. After the game, he stated, "It's a dream to play for the club I love." Manolas was also rewarded with man of the match honours the following week against [[PAOK FC|PAOK]]. In his first seven matches, Manolas was named man of the match in five of them.

Manolas scored his first professional goal against archrivals [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] on 19 May 2010.<ref name="sway">{{cite web|title=K Manolas|url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/kostas-manolas/74396/|publisher=Soccerway|access-date=21 August 2014}}</ref> Although he was playing with a broken [[jugal bone]] since the first minute of the match after a dangerous nudge by [[Kostas Mitroglou]], he scored in the sixth minute, though he later left the match in the 15th minute. He refused to be taken to the hospital before the match was over, despite being urged by his uncle [[Stelios Manolas]]. The next day, he underwent a successful three-hour surgery, recovered and quickly returned to training sessions.

====2010–11 season====
Manolas was a key figure for AEK Athens in the [[2010–11 AEK Athens F.C. season|2010–11 season]], playing impressive performances in the [[Super League Greece]] but also in the [[2010–11 UEFA Europa League]], which drew interest from many European teams such as [[Genoa C.F.C.|Genoa]], [[Udinese Calcio|Udinese]], [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] and [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]]. Manolas scored a very important goal for AEK against [[HNK Hajduk Split|Hajduk Split]], securing the win for the Greek side. The following week, Manolas found the back of the net again, this time against [[Athlitiki Enosi Larissa F.C.|AEL]] in the [[Greek Cup]], which AEK would later go on to win. His impressive performances convinced then AEK Athens coach [[Manuel Jiménez Jiménez|Manolo Jiménez]] and earned him a spot in the starting line-up, forcing [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]] loanee [[David Mateos]] to the substitutes' bench.

Manolas developed massively while playing alongside AEK icon and [[UEFA Euro 2004]] winner [[Traianos Dellas]], stating to the press: "It is an honour to play alongside such a great player like Dellas, I have developed and become a better player. His experience has helped me become confident on the ball and the decisions I make in the game. I have learned a lot from him and he is basically like a teacher to me who I look up to."

On 30 April 2011, Manolas won the first trophy of his career, the [[2010–11 Greek Cup|Greek Cup]].<ref name="sway" /><ref name="cup11">{{cite web|title=Atromitos vs. AEK Athens 0 – 3 (30 April 2011) |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2011/04/30/greece/cup/pae-aps-atromitos-athens/aek-athens-fc/1095614/|publisher=Soccerway|access-date=21 August 2014}}</ref> He played a large role in winning the trophy and played solid throughout the match against [[Atromitos F.C.|Atromitos]], where at one point he cleared an opposition shot off his line. Manolas also received man of the match honours due to his outstanding display. After the [[2011 Greek Cup Final|0–3]] victory, Manolas stated, "It is a dream for me to win a trophy with my childhood club AEK, and I hope there's many more to come in the future." He finished the 2010–11 season playing 36 matches, scoring three goals.

====2011–12 season====
On 11 July 2011, Manolas signed a three-year contract extension with AEK, keeping him at the club until 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.aekfc.gr/index.asp?a_id=1355&n_id=6934|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110714050545/http://www.aekfc.gr/index.asp?a_id=1355&n_id=6934|url-status=dead|title=Manolas signs new 3-year deal|archivedate=14 July 2011}}</ref> His contract was worth €900,000 earning €300,000 per-season including bonuses that could reach up to €1.4 million. Manolas renewed his contract despite interested from big European outfits [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]], [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], [[VfL Wolfsburg|Wolfsburg]] and [[Hamburger SV]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sentragoal.gr/article.asp?catid=10523&subid=2&pubid=128713497|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150116182912/http://www.sentragoal.gr/article.asp?catid=10523&subid=2&pubid=128713497|url-status=dead|title=ΣΤΟΙΧΗΜΑ | STOIXIMA LIVE - Sentragoal.gr|archivedate=16 January 2015}}</ref> Manolas agreed with AEK on €4 million buyout clause for foreign teams and a €10 million buyout clause for Greek teams.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.aek365.gr/a-131762/porta-se-osfp-pao.htm|title=Πόρτα σε ΟΣΦΠ – ΠΑΟ - 11/07 20:47}}</ref>[[File:Kostas Manolas 2011.jpg|thumb|Manolas playing for AEK in 2011.|alt=|left]] Shortly after signing the contract, Manolas stated to the press, "I am extremely happy that I am going to continue playing for the team of my heart and it is an honour to wear the AEK Jersey for the next three years with my childhood club. I applaud AEK president Stavros Adamidis who believes in me and declined great offers from European teams to keep me at the club despite the huge economical problems the club is suffering. My dream now is to become the team's captain and win the league just like my uncle Stelios Manolas, who achieved this when he joined AEK."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gazzetta.gr/article/item/208632-manolas-opos-o-theios-mou|title=Μανωλάς: «Όπως ο θείος μου» | Gazzetta|website=www.gazzetta.gr}}</ref>

Manolas started the season positively, playing his first competitive match of the [[2011–12 AEK Athens F.C. season|2011–12 season]] against [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]]n side [[FC Dinamo Tbilisi|Dinamo Tbilisi]] in a [[2011–12 UEFA Europa League]] qualifier, helping AEK to 1–0 victory. He was given heavy praise from Manolo Jiménez.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.aek365.gr/a-138510/h-kritikh-ths-aek.htm|title=Η Κριτικη Τησ Αεκ - 19/08 08:39}}</ref> Manolas scored his first goal of the season in a 0–1 away victory over [[Panionios F.C.|Panionios]]. He dedicated the goal to Jiménez, who had been taking criticism in recent weeks for his team's poor performances.<ref>[http://www.sport.gr/default.asp?pid=4&aid=106755 Manolas scored against Panionios] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111205141713/http://www.sport.gr/default.asp?pid=4&aid=106755 |date=5 December 2011 }}</ref> Manolas also scored the first goal for AEK Athens in a 1–3 away win against Austrian club [[SK Sturm Graz|Sturm Graz]] in the Europa League. During the January transfer period, the English [[Premier League]]'s [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] showed sincere interest in the young centre back, with the team's then-manager [[David Moyes]] stating: "Manolas has huge talent and is a player for the future."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/everton/9042703/Everton-v-Fulham-David-Moyes-eyes-Kostas-Manolas-signing-as-he-urges-team-to-prosper-in-FA-Cup.html|title=Everton v Fulham: David Moyes eyes Kostas Manolas signing as he urges team to prosper in FA Cup|first=Chris|last=Bascombe|date=11 April 2018|via=www.telegraph.co.uk}}</ref> On 30 January 2012, it was said that AEK and Everton had agreed on terms to sell Manolas to Everton.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16794752|title=Everton agree deal to sign Greek defender Kostas Manolas|work=BBC Sport |date=11 April 2018}}</ref> Manolas, however, declined the offer, as he felt he would be leaving his club in a bad situation as the club would have only had three centre backs in the squad: [[Traianos Dellas]] and two youth players [[Mavroudis Bougaidis]] and [[Elfar Freyr Helgason]] after the departure of loanee [[Cala (footballer, born 1989)|Cala]], who was recalled back to his club [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]]. AEK Chairman Stavros Adamidis stated: "It was Manolas who declined the offer, not AEK."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sportdog.gr/article/83615/oristiko-den-pheugei-o-manolas|title="Mε οδηγό το Φρίουλι"|date=21 February 2012|website=Αθλητικά Νέα & Αθλητικές Ειδήσεις στο Sportdog}}</ref> He left AEK Athens having 85 appearances (6 goals) in all competitions.

===Olympiacos===
====2012–13 season====
On 1 July 2012, Manolas joined rivals [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] on a free transfer until 30 June 2016 after his contract with AEK Athens had expired. "I am very happy that I'm at Olympiacos and I can't wait to play with the red and white shirt in front of a full Karaiskaki and our fans," Manolas said. At a time where AEK were struggling to pay off crippling debts, the departure of one of the club's key players came as another major blow. Ahead of the next season, AEK were only able to buy and sell Greek players up to the age of 22 and were barred from purchasing foreign players, as punishment for failing to meet the Greek [[Super League]]'s financial criteria. AEK were allowed to renew the contracts of any player already at the club, whether their highest earners would be willing to remain at a club that has a history of failing to pay player wages remained to be seen. Moreover, AEK were also banned from taking part in the Europa League that season by the [[Hellenic Football Federation]], with their place taken by [[Asteras Tripolis F.C.|Asteras Tripolis]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.footballhellas.com/2012/07/03/olympiacos-sign-kostas-manolas-from-debt-ridden-aek-athens/|publisher=footballhellas.com|title=Olympiacos sign Kostas Manolas from debt-ridden AEK Athens|date=3 July 2012}}{{Dead link|date=June 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

Manolas made his Olympiacos debut against [[PAS Giannina F.C.|PAS Giannina]] on 15 September in a 1–2 away win, then scored his first goal for his new side against [[Xanthi F.C.|Skoda Xanthi]] in a 4–0 home win.<ref name="sway" /> Manolas made 24 appearances for Olympiacos in the league that season, helping them win the Super League.<ref name="sway" /> On 11 May 2013, he played in the Greek Cup Final against Asteras Tripoli, winning 3–1 to clinch a league and cup double for the season.<ref name="sway" /><ref name="cup13">{{cite web|title=Κυπελλούχος 2013 ο Ολυμπιακός!|url=http://www.epo.gr/News.aspx?a_id=43756&NewsType=24&Country=82|publisher=epo.gr|access-date=21 August 2014|date=11 May 2013}}</ref>

====2013–14 season====
Reports in Greece suggested that English clubs [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]], [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] and [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] were all keeping an eye on Manolas ahead of the January transfer window.{{citation needed|date=December 2015}} According to Gazzetta.gr, Manolas had captured the attention of Premier League scouts since moving to Olympiacos on a free transfer from AEK the previous summer. It was thought that Manolas could be interested in a move to the Premier League to push his case for continued inclusion in the [[Greece national football team|Greece national team]] manager [[Fernando Santos (Portuguese footballer)|Fernando Santos]]' plans, with Greece at the time in second place in their [[2014 FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] qualifying group behind [[Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team|Bosnia and Herzegovina]]. Manolas, however, was unlikely to seriously consider any move that would see his chances of first-team football jeopardised.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.express.co.uk/sport/football/432666/Tottenham-Sunderland-and-Fulham-targeting-Greek-defender-Kostas-Manolas|publisher=express.co.uk|title=Tottenham, Sunderland and Fulham targeting Greek defender Kostas Manolas|date=27 September 2013}}</ref> It was also reported that then-[[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] head coach [[David Moyes]] targeted the Olympiacos defender as a replacement for [[Nemanja Vidić]] after confirming the latter's departure from [[Old Trafford]] at the end of 2013–14 season to [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]], while United's other starting central defender, [[Rio Ferdinand]], would later follow his teammate out, leaving United short of quality in central defence. Moyes would end up being sacked and rumours of a move immediately ceased.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.caughtoffside.com/2014/04/01/manchester-united-target-olympiakos-defender-as-nemanja-vidic-replacement/|publisher=caughtoffside.com|title=Manchester United Target Olympiakos Defender as Nemanja Vidic Replacement|date=1 April 2014}}</ref>

Manolas scored his first goal for Olympiacos in the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League]] in a 1–0 home win against [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]], building the foundations for the next round.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/2011820--olympiacos-vs-benfica/ |title=Olympiacos – Benfica 1–0 |publisher=UEFA |date=5 November 2013 }}</ref> He scored his second goal in the Champions League in a 2–1 away loss against [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.rapgenius.com/Uefa-champions-league-2013-2014-matchday-5-highlights-annotated#note-2487759|title=Paris Saint Germain 2 – Olympiakos 1 |date=26 November 2013 }}</ref> though nonetheless the squad secured a spot in the [[2013–14 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|round of 16]]—the first time the club had reached the stage since [[2009–10 Olympiacos F.C. season|2009–10]]—in matchup against Manchester United. With United failing to display their usual dominant domestic form that term, Manolas thought the Greek champions had what it takes to make the Champions League quarter-finals for only the second time: "I believe we will give a good performance. I hope Manchester United will not get better than they are now, so we can defeat them."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/025a-0ea887bafae9-9496cdb66445-1000--manolas-and-roberto-ready-for-united-test/|publisher=[[UEFA]]|title=Manolas and Roberto ready for United test|date=2014-02-25}}</ref> Despite winning the first leg 2–0 at home, Olympiacos fell as Manchester United's [[Robin van Persie]] hit a hat-trick in the return leg in [[Manchester]] to progress 3–2 on aggregate.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/mar/19/manchester-united-olympiakos-champions-league-match-report|work=theguardian|title=Man Utd 3 Olympiacos 0|date=2014-03-19}}</ref>

On 22 March 2014, Manolas extended his contract with Olympiacos for another year, keeping him at the club until the summer of 2017.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://ksipnistere.blogspot.gr/2014/03/2017.html|script-title=el:Νέο συμβόλαιο έως το 2017 ο Μανωλάς|language=el|date=22 March 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.thetoc.gr/athlitika/article/olumpiakos--ananewse-me-manwla-ews-to-2017|script-title=el:Ολυμπιακός : Ανανέωσε με Μανωλά έως το 2017|language=el|date=22 March 2014}}</ref> He left Olympiacos having 73 appearances (6 goals, 2 assists) in all competitions.

===Roma===

====2014–15 season====
On 27 August 2014, Italian [[Serie A]] side [[A.S. Roma|Roma]] announced the signing of Manolas for an estimated fee of €15 million. Upon joining Roma, Manolas said, "I had offers from several big clubs, including [[Juventus F.C.|Juve]]. But it was my decision to come here to Roma. I wanted to come to Roma. Lots of people told me good things. Their advice and my decision is what brought me here. The club has big goals. I want to win the [[Scudetto]], as does the whole squad. We can also go far in the Champions League."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/54960/manolas-i-always-wanted-roma|title=Manolas: I always wanted Roma - Football Italia|website=www.football-italia.net|date=27 August 2014 }}</ref>
[[File:CSKA-Roma (6).jpg|thumb|300x300px|Manolas (top, left-centre) lining up for Roma before the match against CSKA Moscow, 25 November 2014.]]
On 30 August 2014, Manolas made his official debut for Roma as they beat [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] 2–0 in the opening game of the [[2014–15 Serie A]] season. On 17 September, he made his first European appearance with Roma in the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] as they cruised to an impressive 5–1 victory over [[PFC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/teams/italy/as-roma/1241/matches/|title=Italy - AS Roma - Results and fixtures - Soccerway|website=int.soccerway.com}}</ref> On 5 October, Manolas was sent off in a match against Juventus for retaliating after being fouled by [[Álvaro Morata]], who was sent off as well.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Sheringham|first1=Sam|title=Juventus 3–2 Roma|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29476538|access-date=5 October 2014|work=BBC Sport|date=5 October 2014}}</ref> The [[Italian Football Federation]] (FIGC) subsequently banned Manolas for two games for his part in the altercation.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://forzaitalianfootball.com/2014/10/roma-and-juventus-both-fined-for-fan-behaviour-in-fiery-fixture/|title=Roma and Juventus both fined for fan behaviour in fiery fixture - Forza Italian Football|website=forzaitalianfootball.com|date=6 October 2014 }}</ref>

Manolas' impressive first year with his club garnered interest from many other European sides, including Premier League giants [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], though the player's agent, [[Mino Raiola]], said that Manolas was not interested in discussing the rumours: "Kostas is a Roma player, and anyone who wants him will have to ask the club. All I can say is the lad has a contract until 2019. Roma paid a lot for him, and that means they have a lot of expectations for him."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/64992/manolas-agent-%E2%80%99arsenal-ask-roma%E2%80%A6%E2%80%99|title=Manolas agent: 'Arsenal? Ask Roma…' - Football Italia|website=www.football-italia.net}}</ref>

Manolas enjoyed an excellent first season in Serie A, cementing his place at the heart of manager [[Rudi Garcia]]'s defence as his side finished second in the league table. In the ensuing close season, [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] offered Roma £15 million for the player, whom they originally tried to sign last summer before being beaten by Roma.<ref>[http://metro.co.uk/2015/04/10/arsenal-offered-fresh-hope-of-pushing-through-15million-kostas-manolas-transfer-5144493/  Arsenal ‘offered fresh hope of pushing through £15million Kostas Manolas transfer’] Retrieved 10 April 2015</ref> On 19 June 2015, at the end of the [[2014–15 A.S. Roma season|season]], Manolas, via a Roma fan poll, was named the club's "best purchase of the season" after capturing 56% of the vote, in front of the likes of [[Seydou Keita (footballer)|Seydou Keita]] (18%) and [[Juan Iturbe]] (8%).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://romanews.eu/2015/roma-awards-e-manolas-il-miglior-acquisto-della-stagione/|title=Roma Awards. E' Manolas il miglior acquisto della stagione - Romanews|date=19 June 2015}}</ref>

====2015–16 season====
Manolas began the [[2015–16 A.S. Roma season|2015–16 campaign]] as the de facto leader of the Roma defence. According to ''Tuttomercatoweb'', [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] manager [[José Mourinho]] attempted to bring the Greek international to [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]] the previous season, and will try again in the New Year, with Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur continuing their interest.<ref>[http://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/chelsea/transfer-talk/news/chelsea-want-kostas-manolas_247681.html#$$nv9ytx&&cC5EkmQmEeW3qQoazxP+vQ$$  Report: Chelsea to make January bid for Roma defender Kostas Manolas] Retrieved 21 September 2015</ref> On 17 September 2015, after the 1–1 home draw against [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League|2014–15 Champions League]] title holders [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], Manolas praised his club's tactical performance: "We played a great game on a tactical level. We've been doing well in defence, and I think it's an important step for the team," he told [[Sky Sports]].<ref>[http://www.football-italia.net/73145/manolas-%E2%80%99bar%C3%A7a-important-step%E2%80%99 Manolas: ’Barça an important step’] Retrieved 18 September 2015</ref> On 23 September, Roma's unbeaten start to the season ended after losing 2–1 away at [[U.C. Sampdoria|Sampdoria]], with Manolas scoring an own goal.<ref>[http://www.stopandgoal.net/2015/09/23/prima-pagina/cronaca-samp-roma-2-1-decide-un-autogoal-di-manolas/ Sampdoria – Roma 2–1: decide un clamoroso autogoal di Manolas] Retrieved 23 September 2015</ref>

On 26 September, Manolas scored his first goal in the [[2015–16 Serie A]] as Roma comfortably defeated newly promoted side [[Carpi F.C. 1909|Carpi]] 5–1. He opened the scoring after netting [[Lucas Digne]]'s clever assist with his right boot besides the challenge in the box from Carpi's [[Gabriel Silva (footballer, born 1991)|Gabriel Silva]].<ref>[http://www.football-italia.net/SerieA/match/69877 Roma 5 – 1 Carpi] Retrieved 26 September 2015</ref>

On 5 December, in a dramatic 1–1 away draw against [[Torino F.C.|Torino]] in domestic league action, Manolas brought down [[Andrea Belotti]] inside the area, whereupon [[Maxi López]] coolly converted the subsequent 94th-minute penalty kick. Despite replays suggesting the Greek defender may well have gotten the ball in the challenge, the referee nonetheless awarded the penalty.<ref>[http://www.football-italia.net/SerieA/match/69969 Torino 1 – 1 Roma] Retrieved 5 December 2015</ref><ref>[http://www.goal.com/en-us/match/torino-vs-roma/2120525/report Torino 1 – 1 Roma] Retrieved 5 December 2015</ref> On 11 December, towards the end of a [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] match against Belarusians [[FC BATE Borisov|BATE Borisov]], Manolas engaged in a quarrel with teammate [[Miralem Pjanić]] for mishandling a ball possession. As reported by ''[[La Gazzetta dello Sport]]'', the two players continued the fighting into the team's locker room.<ref>[http://www.vocegiallorossa.it/rassegna-stampa/nervosismo-tra-pjanic-e-manolas-al-termine-di-roma-bate-99506 Nervosismo tra Pjanic e Manolas al termine di Roma-BATE] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151214161424/http://www.vocegiallorossa.it/rassegna-stampa/nervosismo-tra-pjanic-e-manolas-al-termine-di-roma-bate-99506 |date=14 December 2015 }} Retrieved 11 December 2015</ref><ref>[http://www.goal.com/it/news/2/serie-a/2015/12/11/18232422/scintille-in-casa-roma-lite-tra-manolas-e-pjanic-nel-dopo Scintille in casa Roma: lite tra Manolas e Pjanic nel dopo BATE] Retrieved 11 December 2015</ref>

On 17 February 2016, in a 1st leg [[UEFA Champions League]] game for the last 16, he was the indisputable leader of the defence, despite the 2–0 home loss from the Spanish giants [[Real Madrid]].<ref>[http://www.sport24.gr/football/omades/Roma/toixos-o-manwlas-koryfaios-ths-roma.3913735.html "Τοίχος" ο Μανωλάς, κορυφαίος της Ρόμα] Retrieved 18 February 2016</ref> Manolas closed down [[Karim Benzema]] quite well throughout the game. Most of the low crosses were taken care of well by him but he could do nothing about the two goals.<ref>[http://www.sportskeeda.com/football/as-roma-0-2-real-madrid-player-ratings AS Roma 0–2 Real Madrid: Player Ratings] Retrieved 18 February 2016</ref> On 20 April 2016, in a match for [[Serie A]], Manolas scored his second goal in the season, giving an assist in a glorious home win against [[Torino F.C.|Torino]].<ref>[http://www.sport24.gr/football/Italy/SerieA/me-manwla-toti-h-roma-astamathth-h-gioyventoys.4019370.html Τεράστια ανατροπή με Τότι η Ρόμα] Retrieved 20 April 2016</ref>

====2016–17 season====
On 25 July 2016, coach [[Luciano Spalletti]] has insisted that the international defender is happy at [[A.S. Roma|Roma]] and will stay at the club, despite every summer speculations involving [[Manchester United]], [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] and [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]'s interest about the Greek defender.<ref>[http://www.calciomercato.com/news/spalletti-manolas-resta-juve-sempre-forte-noi-vogliamo-vincerle--243654 Spalletti: Manolas resta alla Roma.] Retrieved 25 July 2016</ref> Arsenal were so displeased by the way Roma handled the talks that they later refused to allow [[Jack Wilshere]] to go there on loan.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/37218234|title=Jack Wilshere: Bournemouth sign Arsenal midfielder on loan|work=BBC Sport |date=31 August 2016}}</ref> Manolas began the [[2016–17 A.S. Roma season|2016–17 campaign]] as the de facto leader of the Roma defence.

In September 2016, [[A.S. Roma|Roma]] are obliged to pay the sum of €6.5 million to Olympiacos for the international defender. Roma did not want to sell the Greek defender this summer as Olympiacos had a 50% next percentage sale until this August. Roma also rejected a bid from [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] in the region of €39 million for Manolas and therefore the player stayed put. Thus, Olympiacos received from Roma the fee of €6.5 million and Roma activated the clause obtaining the 100% of the player.<ref>[http://www.sdna.gr/monimes-stiles/paraskinia/article/239748/zesto-xrima-se-olympiako-apo-roma-gia-manola «Ζεστό» χρήμα σε Ολυμπιακό από Ρόμα για Μανωλά] Retrieved 3 September 2016</ref> Manolas was considered the best marker in 'calcio' and [[Barcelona]] had been following him for a while. The Greek international had always been on a list of defenders that Barcelona were been interested in. With [[Thomas Vermaelen]]'s loan to Roma, they received an option to buy on Manolas at the summer of 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sport-english.com/en/news/barca/barcelona-target-manolas-for-move-the-end-the-season-5470876|title=FC Barcelona target Manolas for move at the end of the season|last=Sport|date=7 October 2016|publisher=Sport English}}</ref> On 2 October 2016, he scored the second goal sealing a 2–1 home win against rivals [[Inter Milan|Inter]], as well as making the Inter captain [[Mauro Icardi]] disappear.<ref>[http://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Serie-A/Inter/02-10-2016/roma-inter-2-1-gol-dzeko-banega-manolas-170286863347.shtml Roma-Inter 2–1: gol di Dzeko, Banega e Manolas] Retrieved 2 October 2016</ref> On 18 October 2016, Manolas rejected [[A.S. Roma|Roma]]'s proposal on the extension of his contract, which expired in 2019, despite the fact that the management were ready to raise the salary of the Greek centre back from €1.8 million to €2.5 million per year. According to the newspapers sources, the 25-year-old international player saw that almost 12 players had a higher salary than his and now expects an improved offer.<ref>[http://www.football-italia.net/93100/manolas-rejects-roma-renewal Manolas rejects Roma renewal?] Retrieved 18 October 2016</ref>

On 23 October 2016, Manolas reached 100 appearances with the jersey of Roma, in a 4–1 home win [[Serie A]] game against [[U.S. Città di Palermo|Palermo]]. On 31 October, he broke his nose in [[AS Roma|Roma]]'s 0–0 away draw against [[Empoli F.C.|Empoli]], in a game where the Greek defender simply covered every possible hole, thus missing the [[Europa League]] clash against [[FK Austria Wien|Austria Wien]] and a [[Serie A]] match against [[Bologna F.C. 1909|Bologna]] at the Olimpico.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/93727/manolas-out-two-weeks|title=Manolas out for two weeks - Football Italia|website=www.football-italia.net}}</ref> On 4 December 2016, in one of the most spectacular Roman derbies in history, Manolas showed the usual ability both in anticipating and blocking his opponents, giving [[Balde Diao Keita]] and [[Ciro Immobile]] a very difficult afternoon.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurosport.com/football/serie-a/2016-2017/live-lazio-as-roma_mtc886524/live.shtml|title=LIVE SS Lazio - AS Roma - Serie A - 4 December 2016|date=4 December 2016|publisher=Eurosport}}</ref> On 13 December 2016, Roma's center-back trio had an amazing performance, especially Manolas and [[Federico Fazio]], who combined 15 clearances, 11 interceptions and won 12 duels. Manolas' impact surpassed just defensive duties, as he assisted for [[Radja Nainggolan]]'s 1–0 winner against [[A.C. Milan]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sport.ilmessaggero.it/calcio/roma_milan_diretta_risultato_finale_live_score_serie_a-2136534.html|title=Roma-Milan 1-0: Nainggolan avverte la Juve, giallorossi da soli al 2° posto|date=12 December 2016 |publisher=sport.il}}</ref> On 18 December 2016, it was announced that Manolas, according to a doctors' report, would be out for around two weeks after picking up another injury in Roma's 1–0 defeat to Juventus. Manolas was forced off in the latter stages at the Juventus Stadium, and he subsequently missed Roma's match against [[Chievo]], with the defender having already been struck down with a broken nose and muscle strain this season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sdna.gr/podosfairo/serie/article/276389/traymatistike-o-manolas|title=Τραυματίστηκε ο Μανωλάς!|date=17 December 2016 |publisher=SDNA}}</ref> On 8 January 2017, he returned to the squad playing as a late substitute in a 1–0 away win against [[Genoa C.F.C.|Genoa]]. On 25 May 2017, a week before the end of the [[2016–17 Serie A|season]], Manolas and [[Diego Perotti]] came a step away from getting into a physical conflict during training. To avoid the worst, only the provisional intervention of teammates, along with [[Luciano Spalletti]]'s decision to send them to the dressing room without even finishing the training, helped to lower the tension.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Serie-A/Roma/25-05-2017/roma-tensione-allenamento-manolas-perotti-rissa-sfiorata-200537217663.shtml|title=Roma, tensione in allenamento: Manolas e Perotti a un passo dalla rissa|date=25 November 2017|website=La Gazzetta dello Sport - Tutto il rosa della vita}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/it/notizie/roma-nervi-tesi-a-trigoria-lite-tra-manolas-e-perotti/znkzaf9rfksm1f4pxuj751j2u|title=Roma, nervi tesi a Trigoria: lite tra Manolas e Perotti - Goal.com|publisher=Goal.com}}</ref>

====2017–18 season====
Despite a possible move to [[FC Zenit|Zenit]], potentially following teammate [[Leandro Paredes]] during the summer of 2017,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/104565/manolas-set-zenit|title=Manolas set for Zenit - Football Italia|website=www.football-italia.net}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/104675/sky-manolas-paredes-zenit-done|title=Sky: Manolas-Paredes to Zenit done - Football Italia|website=www.football-italia.net}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/104891/manolas-keeps-zenit-waiting|title=Manolas keeps Zenit waiting - Football Italia|website=www.football-italia.net|date=28 June 2017 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidefutbol.com/2017/07/05/chelsea-angle-to-kostas-manolas-rejecting-zenit-switch/342084/|title=Chelsea Angle To Kostas Manolas Rejecting Zenit Switch|date=5 July 2017}}</ref> Manolas remained at Roma for the [[2017–18 Serie A|2017–18 season]]. On 27 September 2017, he opened the scoring in a 2–1 away win against [[Qarabağ FK|Qarabağ]] in the [[UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League Group stage]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gazzetta.gr/football/article/1142483/gkol-sta-asteria-o-manolas-vid|title=Γκολ στα... αστέρια ο Μανωλάς! (vid) | Gazzetta|website=www.gazzetta.gr}}</ref>

On 2 December 2017, the Greek international renewed his contract with the Giallorossi, until 2022, with a release clause set at €35 million.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.corrieredellosport.it/news/calcio/calcio-mercato/2017/10/12-32175766/calciomercato_roma_manolas_firma_il_rinnovo?cookieAccept=|title=Calciomercato Roma, Manolas firma il rinnovo|date=12 October 2017|website=corrieredellosport.it}}</ref> On 15 October 2017, the Greek defender was substituted during the [[Serie A]] match against Napoli that took place at the [[Stadio Olimpico]] in Rome. The Greek defender was out for almost a month due to a Grade I strain of his left adductor longus (thigh) muscle.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.altsantiri.gr/sports/den-borouse-na-perpatisi-meta-mats-tis-roma-o-manolas-video/|title=Δεν μπορούσε να περπατήσει μετά το ματς της Ρόμα ο Μανωλάς (video) - altsantiri.gr|date=15 October 2017|access-date=4 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180617143733/https://www.altsantiri.gr/sports/den-borouse-na-perpatisi-meta-mats-tis-roma-o-manolas-video/|archive-date=17 June 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 31 October 2017, he returned to the squad in a convincing 3–0 [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] home game against English champions [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/match-reports/roma-3-chelsea-0-no-11444611?service=responsive|title=Five talking points as Roma run riot against sorry Chelsea|first=Rik|last=Sharma|website=[[Daily Mirror]] |date=31 October 2017}}</ref> On 5 November 2017, he scored his first goal in [[2017–18 Serie A|2017-18 season]] from an [[Edin Džeko]] assist in a 4–2 away win against [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Serie-A/Fiorentina/05-11-2017/fiorentina-roma-2-4-doppietta-gerson-gol-veretout-simeone-manolas-perotti-230400712387.shtml|title=Fiorentina-Roma 2-4: doppietta di Gerson, gol di Veretout, Simeone, Manolas e Perotti|date=5 November 2017|website=La Gazzetta dello Sport - Tutto il rosa della vita}}</ref>

On 9 March 2018, he scored the first goal in a 3–0 win with a header against [[Torino F.C.|Torino]] after an assist by [[Alessandro Florenzi]] with a cross following a corner. After his goal, Manolas dropped to his knees and pointed to the sky in tribute to [[Davide Astori]], the Fiorentina captain who died on 4 March.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sport24.gr/football/Italy/SerieA/gkol-o-manwlas-kai-afierwsh-ston-astori-sto-3-0-epi-ths-torino.5114201.html |script-title=el:Γκολ ο Μανωλάς και αφιέρωση στον Αστόρι, στο 3-0 επί της Τορίνο|website=sport24.gr |language=el}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.repubblica.it/sport/calcio/serie-a/roma/2018/03/09/news/roma-torino_3-0_i_giallorossi_consolidano_il_terzo_posto-190901387/|title=Roma-Torino 3-0, i giallorossi fanno le prove di Champions|date=9 March 2018}}</ref> On 4 April 2018, in a frustrating 4–1 away loss for [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League knockout phase|2017–18 Champions League quarter finals first leg]] to [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], Manolas scored Roma's second own-goal after a clearance that in turn hit the right post, [[Samuel Umtiti]] and the Greek defender.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/barcelona-vs-roma/388719|title=Barcelona 4-1 Roma: Late Luis Suarez strike gives Ernesto Valverde's side advantage|website=Sky Sports}}</ref> However, Manolas more than compensated for the first leg performance as he brilliantly headed the final goal in the Giallorossi's 3–0 dominant victory over the Blaugrana in the return leg, [[A.S. Roma in European football|sending Roma to the Champions League semi-finals for the first time since 1984]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.contra.gr/Soccer/Europe/ChL/megas-manwlas-kserane-mesi-valverde-kai-esteile-th-roma-sta-hmitelika.5155754.html |script-title=el:Μέγας Μανωλάς... ξέρανε Μέσι - Βαλβέρδε και έστειλε τη Ρόμα στα ημιτελικά!|work=Contra.gr |date=10 April 2018 |language=el |access-date=2018-04-10}}</ref> On 21 April 2018, Manolas captained his first match with the club against [[S.P.A.L. 2013|SPAL]] during a 3–0 away win in [[Serie A]], after receiving the armband from his teammate [[Radja Nainggolan]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.gazzetta.gr/football/serie-a/article/1222114/arhigos-tis-roma-o-manolas-pic  |script-title=el:Αρχηγός της Ρόμα ο Μανωλάς! |publisher =gazzetta.gr|access-date=2018-04-21|language=el |date=21 April 2018 }}</ref>

Manolas was one of Roma's most consistent players over the course of the campaign, proving to be a reliable figure in the Italians' defence.

====2018–19 season====
Despite the yearly summer rumours surrounding his possible departure from the club, Manolas remained at Roma for a fifth season, aiming to win his first title with the club during the 2018–19 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/125832/manolas-%E2%80%98won%E2%80%99t-leave-roma%E2%80%99|title=Manolas: 'Won't leave Roma'|website=www.football-italia.net}}</ref> On 27 August 2018, Manolas scored against [[Atalanta B.C.|Atalanta]], as he tapped in [[Javier Pastore]]'s chipped free kick at the far post, helping Roma complete a comeback from 3–1 down to 3–3 at the [[Stadio Olimpico]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sport24.gr/football/Italy/SerieA/o-manwlas-eswse-th-roma-3-3-me-atalanta.5294685.html |title=Ο Μανωλάς έσωσε τη Ρόμα, 3-3 με Αταλάντα |website=www.sport24.gr}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Serie-A/Roma/27-08-2018/roma-atalanta-3-3-gol-pastore-castagne-rigoni-2-florenzi-manolas-290518277832.shtml |title=Roma-Atalanta 3-3: gol di Pastore, Castagne, Rigoni (2), Florenzi e Manolas |website=www.gazzetta.it |language=it |date=27 August 2018 }}</ref> On 7 November, Manolas scored with a glancing header from very close range, placing the ball high and in the centre of the goal, from an assist by [[Lorenzo Pellegrini]] with a [[Cross (football)|cross]] following a corner, helping his club to a vital 2–1 away win against [[PFC CSKA Moscow|CSKA Moscow]] in the [[2018–19 UEFA Champions League|group stage of the UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/130398/cl-roma-march-moscow |title=CL: Roma march on Moscow |website=www.football-italia.net}}</ref> His impressive performance saw him included in [[UEFA Champions League]]'s team of the week the following day.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/024b-0e99349d6a9a-d1e82ef4063d-1000--champions-league-fantasy-football-team-of-the-week/ |title=Champions League Fantasy Football Team of the Week |website=[[UEFA]]|date=8 November 2018 }}</ref> On 15 November, Manolas was forced off during Greece's 1–0 win over Finland due to a blow to the adductor magnus muscle in his leg.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.chiesaditotti.com/2018/11/16/18097650/roma-suffer-manolas-injury-blow |title=Manolas Ankle Injury Not Major |date=16 November 2018 |publisher=chiesaditotti.com}}</ref>

On 6 March 2019, Manolas made his 200th appearance in all competitions with Roma in the second leg of the club's round of 16 UEFA Champions League tie against [[FC Porto|Porto]]; Manolas played the full 120 minutes as Roma lost 3–1 at home to exit the Champions League. Reports from the Italian media later confirmed that the 27-year-old had strained a muscle, and would miss around three weeks of action, meaning that he would not be expected to participate in his nation's [[UEFA Euro 2020 qualifying]] matches against [[Liechtenstein national football team|Liechtenstein]] and [[Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team|Bosnia and Herzegovina]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.to10.gr/podosfero/serie-a/577245/ektos-gia-tris-evdomades-o-manolas-chani-ta-mats-tis-ethnikis/ |title=Εκτός για τρεις εβδομάδες ο Μανωλάς, χάνει τα ματς της Εθνικής |date=8 March 2019 |publisher=to10.gr}}</ref>

===Napoli===

====2019–20 season====
On 27 June 2019, Manolas was said to be close to a move to [[S.S.C. Napoli|Napoli]], after Roma and the Neapolitan club reached a deal for him. Manolas agreed to pen a five-year contract with the latter club, with annual earnings of €4.5 million (including bonuses). Napoli officially purchased the defender for €34m plus a €2m signing-on fee, effectively activating his release clause. However, in the agreement between the two Italian sides, Roma purchased defensive midfielder [[Amadou Diawara]] for €18m plus €3m in add-ons. Manolas had also been linked with Juventus, Milan and Arsenal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sport.sky.it/calciomercato/serie-a/2019/06/26/calciomercato-roma-napoli-scambio-diawara-manolas.html |title=Calciomercato, Manolas al Napoli e Diawara alla Roma: scambio in chiusura |publisher=sport.sky.it |language=it |date=26 June 2019 }}</ref> He officially signed for Napoli on 30 June.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.newsit.gr/athlitika/podosfairo/episimo-sti-napoli-o-manolas-anakoinose-to-antio-i-roma-video-6/2814675/|title=Επίσημο: Στη Νάπολι ο Μανωλάς!|date=30 June 2019|website=newsit.gr}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Manolas signs for Napoli |url=https://www.football-italia.net/140159/manolas-signs-napoli |website=Football Italia |date=30 June 2019 |access-date=30 June 2019 }}</ref>

On 24 August 2019, he made his debut with the club, starting in the 4–3 away win against [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://it.eurosport.com/calcio/serie-a/2019-2020/le-pagelle-di-fiorentina-napoli-3-4-pulgar-e-chiesa-super-deludono-koulibaly-e-manolas_sto7419485/story.shtml |title=Le pagelle di Fiorentina-Napoli 3-4: Pulgar e Chiesa super, deludono Koulibaly e Manolas |publisher=Eurosport |language=it |last1=Pegoraro |first1=Paolo |date=24 August 2019 |access-date=30 September 2019 }}</ref> A week later he scored his first goal for the club in a thrilling 4–3 away loss against Juventus, netting a goal with a header after a beautiful free-kick from [[Mário Rui]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2019/aug/31/juventus-v-napoli-serie-a-live |title=Juventus vs Napoli 4-3 |work=theguardian|date=31 August 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://sport.sky.it/calcio/serie-a/2019/08/31/juventus-napoli-risultato-gol.html |title=Juve Napoli 4-3: gol e highlights della partita. Decide un autogol di Koulibaly al 92'|date=31 August 2019 |publisher=sport.sky.it}}</ref> On 28 September, Manolas scored his second goal of the season with a header after [[Nikola Maksimović]]'s corner, helping his club seal a 2–1 home win game against [[Brescia Calcio|Brescia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tuttonapoli.net/in-primo-piano/rileggi-live-napoli-brescia-2-1-13-mertens-49-pt-manolas-67-balotelli-gli-azzurri-soffrono-e-vincono-408432 |title=Napoli-Brescia 2-1|publisher=tuttonapoli.net|language=it|date=29 September 2019}}</ref>

On 31 December, Manolas was included in the [[A.S. Roma|Roma Team of the Decade]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://forzaitalianfootball.com/2019/12/roma-team-of-the-decade/ |title=Roma – Team of the Decade|publisher=forzaitalianfootball.com|language=en|date=31 December 2019}}</ref>

On 29 February 2020, Manolas connected with [[Lorenzo Insigne]]'s free-kick from the right wing, thumping a header into the net to give Napoli the lead in a 2–1 home win game against [[Torino F.C.|Torino]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sport.sky.it/calcio/serie-a/2020/02/29/napoli-torino-risultato-gol |title=Napoli-Torino 2-1, gol e highlights. Reti di Manolas e Di Lorenzo, Gattuso vince ancora |publisher=sport.sky.it|language=it|date=29 February 2020}}</ref>

On 16 May, Manolas was the first Napoli player to get injured since training resumed after the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Italy]]. His club did not mention how long he would be out for, but 'Corriere dello Sport' reported that he would miss six weeks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.besoccer.com/new/manolas-could-be-out-for-six-weeks-835386 |title=Manolas could be out for six weeks |publisher=www.besoccer.com|language=en|date=16 May 2020}}</ref>

====2020–21 season====
On 20 September 2020, Manolas was a starter in a 2–0 away win against [[Parma Calcio 1913|Parma]].

On 12 January 2021, Napoli confirmed that Manolas had suffered a first-degree muscle injury. The Partenopei defender was replaced by Nikola Maksimovic after 15 minutes of the 2–1 win against [[Udinese Calcio|Udinese]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/164695/napoli-muscle-injury-manolas |title=Napoli: Muscle injury for Manolas |publisher=www.football-italia.net|language=en}}</ref>

On 8 February 2021, Napoli confirmed that Manolas would be out for three weeks, as he suffered a second-degree sprain and damaged the ligament in the right ankle. The Greek defender was substituted at the [[Stadio Luigi Ferraris|Marassi]] and carried out tests at the Pineta Grande clinic.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/166067/manolas-out-three-weeks |title=Manolas out for three weeks |publisher=www.football-italia.net|language=en}}</ref> He made his return to the squad as a late substitute against [[U.S. Sassuolo Calcio|Sassuolo]] on 3 March, but conceded a late penalty which Sassuolo converted to end the match in a 3–3 draw.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sport.sky.it/calcio/serie-a/2021/03/03/sassuolo-napoli-risultato-gol |title=Sassuolo-Napoli 3-3: gol, rigori ed emozioni fino alla fine al Mapei |publisher=sport.sky.it|language=it|date=3 March 2021}}</ref>

====2021–22 season====
In August 2021, it was reported that Olympiacos had started negotiations with Napoli for the purchase of Manolas, with the player telling the club that he desired a return to Greece.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sport24.gr/football/sportitalia-i-napoli-den-katevainei-apo-ta-10-ekatommyria-eyro-syn-mponoys-gia-ton-manola.9329483.html |title=Sportitalia: "Η Νάπολι ζητάει 10 εκατομμύρια ευρώ συν μπόνους, αλλιώς δεν δίνει τον Μανωλά" |publisher=www.sport24.gr |language=el|date=21 August 2021}}</ref> Despite the transfer rumours, he was a starter in the opening [[2021–22 Serie A|Serie A]] match of the season against [[Venezia F.C.|Venezia]].

On 21 October 2021, Manolas suffered an injury during Napoli's [[2021–22 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] clash against [[Legia Warsaw]]. He was forced off the pitch in the 72nd minute with a suspected muscle injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.italy24news.com/sports/news/136309.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211028215004/https://www.italy24news.com/sports/news/136309.html |url-status=usurped |archive-date=28 October 2021 |title=Naples, Manolas exams: muscle injury to the buttock |publisher=www.italy24news.com |language=en|date=23 October 2021}}</ref> In December 2021, having lost his place in the starting lineup to [[Amir Rrahmani]], Manolas again expressed his desire to leave the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sdna.gr/podosfairo/907857_manolas-se-napoli-thelo-na-epistrepso-stin-ellada |title=Μανωλάς σε Νάπολι: "Θέλω να επιστρέψω στην Ελλάδα"|publisher=www.sdna.gr |language=el|date=5 December 2021}}</ref> On 10 December, he made his first appearance for almost two months as a late substitute in a 3–2 home win game against [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] in the Europa League.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.90min.com/posts/napoli-3-2-leicester-player-ratings |title=Napoli 3-2 Leicester: Player ratings as Foxes crash out of Europa League|publisher=www.90min.com |language=en|date=9 December 2021}}</ref>

=== Return to Olympiacos ===

====2021–22 season====
On 16 December 2021, Napoli announced an agreement for the sale of Manolas to Olympiacos in January 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|date=16 December 2021|title=Agreement between Napoli and Olympiakos for Manolas' sale|url=https://www.besoccer.com/new/agreement-between-napoli-and-olympiakos-for-manolas-sale-1081146|access-date=16 December 2021|website=BeSoccer}}</ref> The fee of the deal was reportedly €2.5 million.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Campanale|first=Susy|date=16 December 2021|title=Official: Napoli sell Manolas to Olympiacos|url=https://football-italia.net/official-napoli-sell-manolas-to-olympiacos/|access-date=16 December 2021|website=Football Italia}}</ref> On April 16, 2014, and in the second game of the semifinals of the [[Greek Cup]] against [[PAOK]], Manolas had made his last appearance with the jersey of Olympiacos and eight years later, he came on as a substitute in the game against [[Apollon Smyrnis F.C.|Apollon Smyrnis]] in the [[Georgios Kamaras Stadium]], replacing [[Avraam Papadopoulos]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sport24.gr/football/olympiakos-proti-symmetochi-toy-manola-meta-tin-epistrofi-toy.9484508.html |title=Ολυμπιακός: Πρώτη συμμετοχή του Μανωλά μετά την επιστροφή του|publisher=www.sport24.gr |language=el|date=5 January 2022}}</ref>

=== Sharjah ===
In late September 2022, Manolas joined Emirati club [[Sharjah FC|Sharjah]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/sport/football/2022/09/24/sharjah-sign-former-roma-defender-kostas-manolas/ |title=Sharjah sign former Roma defender Kostas Manolas |website=The National News |date=24 September 2022 }}</ref> On 17 January 2024, after 18 months with the side, his contract was terminated by mutual agreement.<ref>{{Cite web |date=17 January 2024 |title=Manolas lascia lo Sharjah: l'ex Roma e Napoli ha risolto il contratto {{!}} Goal.com Italia |trans-title=Manolas leaves Sharjah: former Roma and Napoli has terminated the contract |url=https://www.goal.com/it/liste/manolas-sharjah-addio-ufficiale-contratto-risoluzione/blt1f3047a0d113c3f9 |access-date=17 January 2024 |website=GOAL |language=it}}</ref>

=== Salernitana ===
On 8 February 2024, Manolas returned to [[Serie A]] to sign a short-term deal with [[US Salernitana 1919|Salernitana]]. He joined [[Filippo Inzaghi]]'s side on a contract that expired in June 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 February 2024|title=Επιστρέφει στην Ιταλία ο Μανωλάς! |url=https://www.to10.gr/podosfero/serie-a/2810209/epistrefi-stin-italia-o-manolas/ |access-date=8 February 2024 |language=el}}</ref>

=== Pannaxiakos ===
On 16 October 2024, Manolas returned to his boyhood club, [[Pannaxiakos F.C.|Pannaxiakos]] in the [[Local football championships of Greece|Cyclades FCA First Division]], signing a one-year deal. He scored five goals on his debut against Marpissaikos five days later, as Pannaxiakos ran out 12–1 winners.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.givemesport.com/kostas-manolas-five-goals-pannaxiakos-debut/|title=Ex-Champions League defender, now 33, scores FIVE goals in just 34 mins on debut for new side|first=Callum|last=Altimas|date=21 October 2024|website=GiveMeSport}}</ref>

In the 2025-26 season, Manolas helped Pannaxiakos win the Cyclades championship and secure promotion to the Gamma Ethniki for the 2026-27 season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-03-29 |title=Πανναξιακός: Ανέβηκε στη Γ' Εθνική η ομάδα των Μανωλά - Σιόβα {{!}} Gazzetta |url=https://www.gazzetta.gr/football/g-ethniki/2527629/pannaxiakos-anebike-sti-g-ethniki-i-omada-ton-manola-sioba |access-date=2026-09-10 |website=www.gazzetta.gr |language=el}}</ref>

==International career==
Following a continued stretch of form from Manolas, former [[Greece national football team|Greece national team]] manager [[Otto Rehhagel]] called Manolas up for the 30-man provisional World Cup squad for the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]], though he failed to make the final 23-man squad. Manolas would wait roughly three more years before eventually making his international debut against [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]] in a friendly. Leading up to the [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014 World Cup]], Manolas' strong 2013–14 season with Olympiacos earned him a spot in manager [[Fernando Santos (football coach)|Fernando Santos]]' final 23-man squad for the tournament.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/greece/10810255/Greece-World-Cup-2014-squad.html|work=telegraph|title=Greece World Cup 2014 squad|date=19 May 2014}}</ref> It was in Brazil where the centre-back really caught the attention of the watching world, with a string of imperious displays that carried Greece into the knockout stages of the tournament for the first time in its history. He was named by ''[[The Independent]]'' as being among the 50 best players at the World Cup, as the Greeks ultimately fell to [[Costa Rica national football team|Costa Rica]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/worldcup/world-cup-2014-the-50-best-players-of-the-world-cup-9595764.html|work=independent|title=World Cup 2014: The 50 best players of the World Cup }}</ref>

On 9 June 2017, Manolas and his Roma teammate [[Edin Dzeko]] came to blows during an ugly brawl in [[2018 FIFA World Cup qualification|World Cup qualifier game]] between [[Bosnia national football team|Bosnia-Herzegovina]] and Greece. The game ended 0–0 and descended into chaos after the final whistle, when numerous players and members of staff clashed.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sportbible.com/football/news-watch-roma-teammates-dzeko-and-manolas-kick-off-a-mass-brawl-20170610 |publisher=sportbible.com |title=Roma Teammates Dzeko And Manolas Kick Off A Mass Brawl}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.voetbalprimeur.nl/videos/745230/grote-vechtpartij-na-ruzie-tussen-roma-ploeggenoten-dzeko-en-manolas.html |publisher=voetbalprimeur.nl |title=Grote vechtpartij na ruzie tussen Roma-ploeggenoten Dzeko en Manolas}}</ref>

On 12 September 2018, Manolas netted his first goal with [[Greece national football team|Greece]], leaping over his marker to head a free kick through the goalkeeper's hands in a 2–1 away loss against [[Hungary national football team|Hungary]] for the [[UEFA Nations League|Nations League]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sport24.gr/football/nations-league/anwmalh-prosgeiwsh-kai-htta-me-1-2-gia-thn-ellada-sth-voydapesth.5306454.html |publisher=sport24.gr |title=Ανώμαλη προσγείωση και ήττα με 1–2 για την Ελλάδα στη Βουδαπέστη}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Manolas profile includes the speed to keep track of agile attackers and have the strength used in physical challenges. During defensive role, he is attentive in marking of opponents. When playing other roles, he is able to sweep up behind a high-line but also having the versatility to play deeper. Although his primary role is that of a stopper, he also participates in the team's build-up play through his passing. His playing style combines traditional [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|centre-half]] defense characteristics with modern tactical forms for ball distribution. Additionally he is noted for his tackling and ability in the air.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/kostas-manolas-roma-rock-being-eyed-chelsea#:jYr2FqVEWbkxrA |title=Kostas Manolas: The Roma rock being eyed up by Chelsea |work=FourFourTwo |last=Digby |first=Adam |date=2 October 2015 |access-date=2 October 2015 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.o-posts.com/news/teams/uk/arsenal/kostas-manolas-greeces-defensive-star-adapting-seamlessly-rigours-serie/ Kostas Manolas: Greece's defensive star adapting seamlessly to the rigours of Serie A] Retrieved 19 June 2015</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2017/05/09/top-25-best-defenders-world/kostas-manolas/|title=The top 25 best defenders in the world|work=The Telegraph|date=9 May 2017|access-date=9 May 2017}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Manolas is the nephew of the legendary Greek footballer [[Stelios Manolas]],<ref name="Roma Profile"/> and the cousin of [[Konstantinos Manolas (footballer, born 1993)|Konstantinos Manolas]].{{citation needed|date=October 2025}}

He is a fluent speaker of Greek, Italian, and English.{{citation needed|date=October 2025}}

'''Diego Ribas da Cunha''' (born 28 February 1985), commonly known as just '''Diego''' or '''Diego Ribas''', is a Brazilian former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as an [[attacking midfielder]]. A full international for [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] since 2003, Diego earned 34 caps and scored four international goals. He was part of the Brazilian squads which finished as runners-up at the [[2003 CONCACAF Gold Cup]], won the [[Copa América]] in [[2004 Copa América|2004]] and [[2007 Copa América|2007]], and earned a bronze medal at the [[Football at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008 Olympics]].

Diego began his career at [[Santos FC|Santos]], where he won two [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A]] titles before moving to [[FC Porto|Porto]] in 2004. Despite winning further trophies in Portugal, his personal form dropped. After two seasons, he moved for €6 million to [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]] where his form improved, winning domestic honours and helping them to the [[2009 UEFA Cup Final]]. He also won honours at [[Atlético Madrid]], including the [[UEFA Europa League]] in [[2011–12 UEFA Europa League|2012]]. From 2016 to 2022, he played for Brazilian club Flamengo, with whom he won the [[2019 Copa Libertadores Final|Copa Libertadores]] among other domestic and international honours.

==Club career==
===Santos===
At age six, Diego started to show his talent when training with Comercial FC in [[Ribeirão Preto]]. After joining another team, São Carlos, when he was nine, Diego decided to take trials in the hope of impressing a bigger club.<ref>{{cite news|title=Diego Ribas da Cunha Biography|url=http://worldsoccer.about.com/od/players/a/Diego.htm|publisher=World Soccer|access-date=7 March 2012|archive-date=17 October 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111017102913/http://worldsoccer.about.com/od/players/a/Diego.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> Diego was first signed by the São Paulo team [[Santos FC|Santos]] at the age of 12. He developed while in the Santos youth system, making his first team debut at the age of 16 in the [[Torneio Rio-São Paulo|Rio-São Paulo Championship]] in 2002 and in the same year won the domestic [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|Campeonato Brasileiro]] championship. He, [[Robinho]], [[Elano]] and [[Alex (footballer, born June 1982)|Alex]] were known as a famous group when they played for Santos.

===Porto===
Diego was then signed by [[Primeira Liga]] club [[FC Porto|Porto]] in July 2004 as a replacement and the potential successor for [[Deco]], but he could not produce the same calibre of performances as he did at Santos. Diego made his debut for Porto in a 1–1 draw against [[U.D. Leiria|União de Leiria]] on 22 August and on 30 October, he scored his first goal for Porto in a 2–2 draw against [[C.D. Nacional|Nacional]]. As Porto triumphed in the [[2004 Intercontinental Cup|Intercontinental Cup]] against [[Once Caldas]] via a [[penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shootout]], Diego was sent off for swearing at goalkeeper [[Juan Carlos Henao]] after scoring his effort. Journalist [[Tim Vickery]] ascribed this action to Diego's experiences against the team in the previous season's [[Copa Libertadores]], in which the physical Colombian side eliminated Santos in the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Vickery|first1=Tim|title=Diego relishes downfall of Caldas|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/4090073.stm|access-date=10 May 2015|work=BBC Sport|date=12 December 2004}}</ref> In his first season at Porto, Diego made 30 appearances, scoring two goals against [[Sporting Clube de Portugal|Sporting CP]] and [[S.C. Braga|Braga]]. In [[2005–06 Primeira Liga|2005–06]], however, he did not maintain a stable place in the Porto team under coach [[Co Adriaanse]] and also found life difficult at Porto. He eventually left the club to sign with [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]].

===Werder Bremen===
====2006–07 season====
[[File:Diego Ribas da Cunha.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Diego training with [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]] in 2006]]

In May 2006, Diego signed a contract with German [[Bundesliga]] side Werder Bremen until 2010 for a transfer fee of €6 million.<ref name="Diego making his mark in Bremen"/> His first match for Bremen came in the [[DFB-Ligapokal]]. Werder Bremen won the cup, beating [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] in the final on 5 August. The [[2006–07 Bundesliga]] season began well for Diego. He scored the first goal and set up two more for Bremen in their 4–2 win over [[Hannover 96]], on 13 August. In his second match in the Bundesliga, he set up both goals in the 2–1 win over [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]].

[[File:Diego ribas.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Diego in 2007]]

Thanks to his good performances in August, both in the Bundesliga and in the Ligapokal, Diego won the August Player of the Month award.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.fussballer-des-monats.de/| title = Fußballer des Monats – August 2006| access-date =6 October 2007| language = de}}</ref> As the Bundesliga season progressed, Diego made several amazing performances and became one of the most valuable players for Bremen, along with his teammate [[Torsten Frings]]. Together, they were called the "two motors of Bremen's midfield". In October 2006, he won a second Player of the Month award, as well as again in December 2006. He was then named as the Best Player of the first half of the Bundesliga season.

Werder Bremen finished in third place in Group A in the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] group stages, and they moved to the [[2006–07 UEFA Cup|UEFA Cup]], where they reached the semi-finals after beating [[AZ Alkmaar|AZ]] in the quarter-finals due in part to Diego's creative play. On 15 April, Diego again played well, scoring in the 2–0 win over [[Borussia Dortmund]]. Five days later, on 20 April, Bremen played against [[Alemannia Aachen]]. Although Diego's performance was good, he did not score until stoppage time when he scored from 62.5 metres, which later was elected as goal of the year. Bremen won the game 3–1 and topped the table with 60 points.

Following his good performances in the first half of the Bundesliga, Diego got called up to the [[Brazil national football team|Brazil national team]] in November. After the 2006–07 season ended, Diego won the Bundesliga Player of the Season award organised by popular magazine ''[[Kicker (sports magazine)|kicker]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://uk.eurosport.yahoo.com/29052007/58/bundesliga-diego-crowned-bundesliga-s-best.html |title=Bundesliga – Diego crowned Bundesliga's best |publisher=Eurosport.com |date=29 May 2007 |access-date=6 October 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080513125305/http://uk.eurosport.yahoo.com/29052007/58/bundesliga-diego-crowned-bundesliga-s-best.html |archive-date=13 May 2008 }}</ref> He received just over 50 percent of the votes. Unfortunately, his team did not win the Bundesliga after finishing third in the table, behind champions [[VfB Stuttgart]] and [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]].

====2007–08 season====
[[File:10diego.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Diego signing autographs in 2007]]

Diego started his season well, scoring a penalty on the first matchday. Diego gave many outstanding performances. He was crucial as Bremen progressed to the [[2007–08 UEFA Champions League|2007–08 Champions League]] [[2007–08 UEFA Champions League group stage|group stage]]. They beat Croatian club [[GNK Dinamo Zagreb|Dinamo Zagreb]] 3–2 in [[Zagreb]], with Diego scoring two penalties. On the first Champions League group stage matchday, Bremen lost 2–1 to [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]], but Diego's performance aroused interest in Real Madrid's coach [[Bernd Schuster]]. Rumours of his departure, however, were put to an end when Diego signed a new contract which would last until 2011.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.werder.de/english/news/meldung.php?id=963| title = Diego Extends Until 2011| access-date = 6 October 2007| date = 22 September 2007| publisher = werder.de }}{{dead link|date=January 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

After the loss to Real Madrid, Bremen faced VfB Stuttgart, the defending German champions, at home. Werder won 4–1, with Diego leading the midfield. Later on in the season, Bremen achieved a historical 8–1 win over [[Arminia Bielefeld]], with Diego assisting three goals and scoring one himself. Diego was voted Player of the Month in September.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.fussballer-des-monats.de/ |title=Fußballer des Monats – September 2007 |access-date=6 October 2007 |language=de}}</ref> He then scored two goals en route to the [[2007–08 UEFA Cup final phase|UEFA Cup round of 16]] with Bremen, where they lost to [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].

====2008–09 season====
[[File:Diego-Naldo.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Diego celebrating the [[2009 DFB-Pokal Final|2009 DFB-Pokal]] title alongside teammate [[Naldo (footballer, born 1982)|Naldo]]]]

Diego's last season with Bremen was his most successful. He scored 20 goals in total (more than his two first seasons in the club), although Bremen did finish just tenth in the [[2008–09 Bundesliga]] and were knocked out of the [[2008–09 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] at the [[2008–09 UEFA Champions League group stage|group stage]] after finishing third in their group. In the [[2008–09 UEFA Cup|UEFA Cup]] that season, Diego scored six goals, all in the knockout stages. He also scored against [[A.C. Milan|Milan]] in the round of 32, equalizing after 84 minutes, and assisting [[Claudio Pizarro]] in the second leg's only goal. He helped his team through the round of 16, and scored four of the six goals, and managed one assist in the quarter-final knockout of [[Udinese Calcio|Udinese]].

In the semi-finals, after losing 1–0 in their hometown to "North Derby" rivals [[Hamburger SV]], Diego helped his team back in the second leg with an early equalizer to [[Ivica Olić]]'s early critical goal. Later on that game, he assisted a corner to [[Frank Baumann (footballer)|Frank Baumann]]'s third Bremen goal. In that game, Diego received an unfortunate yellow card, preventing him from playing in the final, and with a 3–2 away win, he ended his UEFA Cup participation, leading Bremen to their first UEFA Cup final ever. Without Diego in the [[2009 UEFA Cup Final]], Bremen lost the game 2–1 in extra time to Ukrainian team [[FC Shakhtar Donetsk|Shakhtar Donetsk]]. In his last match with Bremen, Diego gave the assist to [[Mesut Özil]]'s winning goal against [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] in the [[2009 DFB-Pokal Final|DFB-Pokal final]] to secure Bremen's sixth title in the competition.

===Juventus===
[[File:AS Bari v Juventus, 12 December 2009 - Diego (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|upright|Diego playing for [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in 2009]]
On 26 May 2009, Diego signed a five-year contract to join [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] of [[Serie A]] at the end of the season 2008–09 season. The fee paid to Bremen by Juventus was worth €24.5 million, though the price can rise by a further €2.5 million in case of the fulfillment of established sports objectives in the next five years.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://juventus.com/site/eng/NEWS_newsseriea_65E44289495641DF881D1CE321ACABB5.asp| title = Diego is officially a Juventus player| publisher = Juventus Football Club| date = 26 May 2009| access-date = 26 May 2009| url-status = dead| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20090530071531/http://www.juventus.com/site/eng/NEWS_newsseriea_65E44289495641DF881D1CE321ACABB5.asp| archive-date = 30 May 2009| df = dmy-all }}</ref> Diego made his Juventus debut against the Korean side [[Seongnam Ilhwa Chunma|Seongnam]], a game they won 3–0. In the first half, Diego made the pass to [[Mauro Camoranesi]], whose pass followed up to a goal. Diego then scored in the second half and was subbed out at the 60th minute.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.totalprosports.com/blog/index.php/2009/07/diego-scores-a-cheeky-goal-in-juventus-debut/| title = Diego Scores A Cheeky Goal In Juventus Debut| publisher = totalprosports.com| access-date = 23 September 2009| date = 29 July 2009| archive-date = 1 August 2009| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20090801060933/http://www.totalprosports.com/blog/index.php/2009/07/diego-scores-a-cheeky-goal-in-juventus-debut/| url-status = dead}}</ref> On his Serie A debut, he assisted [[Vincenzo Iaquinta]]'s goal from a set-piece.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://english.gazzetta.it/Football/23-08-2009/diego-s-idea-iaquinta-s-headerjuve-down-chievo-501117857512.shtml| title = Diego's idea, Iaquinta's header Juve down Chievo| publisher = La Gazzetta dello Sport| access-date = 23 September 2009| date = 23 August 2009| url-status = dead| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20090827183110/http://english.gazzetta.it/Football/23-08-2009/diego-s-idea-iaquinta-s-headerjuve-down-chievo-501117857512.shtml| archive-date = 27 August 2009| df = dmy-all}}</ref> In the second fixture of the campaign, Diego recorded his first Serie A goal, scoring twice in Juventus' 3–1 victory against [[A.S. Roma|Roma]] on 30 August 2009. He also scored goals against [[Bologna F.C. 1909|Bologna]], [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] and [[S.S.C. Napoli|Napoli]]. One of his most noted assists was his backheel to [[Alessandro Del Piero]]'s goal against [[Genoa C.F.C.|Genoa]]. He has also scored in the [[2010 TIM Trophy]] against Milan.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=672234&sec=europe&cc=5739| title = Serie A: Diego double spells trouble for Roma| publisher = [[ESPN]]| access-date = 23 September 2009| date = 30 August 2009| archive-date = 6 September 2009| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20090906112559/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=672234&sec=europe&cc=5739| url-status = dead}}</ref>

Diego's swaggering displays he produced during his time in Bremen were met with anger and confusion from Juventus fans; the formation did not suit him and he had a fall-out with then coach [[Ciro Ferrara]]. Juventus announced Diego would leave Juventus despite pleading to stay at the club. German clubs like [[VfL Wolfsburg]], [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] and his former club Werder Bremen were linked to sign him; however, Bremen ruled out signing him due to sporting director Klaus Allofs believing a deal to bring him back to Bremen would be "economically impossible",<ref>{{cite news|title=Bremen rule out Diego return|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11095/6319923/|publisher=Sky Sports|date=18 August 2010|access-date=7 March 2012}}</ref> and Diego reiterated his desire to stay.<ref>{{cite news|title=Diego confirms Juve desire|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11854/6283782/|publisher=Sky Sports|date=28 July 2010|access-date=7 March 2012}}</ref>

===VfL Wolfsburg===
[[File:Diego-Ribas-da-Cunha.jpg|thumb|left|Diego in 2010]]

Eventually, on 27 August 2010, Diego moved from Juventus to [[VfL Wolfsburg]] for a club record transfer fee of €15.5 million, of which Juve would only receive €14.75 million as 5% of the transfer fee transferred to his youth clubs as [[Solidarity Contribution (football)|solidarity contribution]].<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.juventus.com/wps/wcm/connect/19f4429c-c935-4d87-bb61-e3c83a50a616/JUVE_SEMESTRE_INGLESE.pdf?MOD=AJPERES&CACHEID=19f4429c-c935-4d87-bb61-e3c83a50a616| title = Half-yearly Financial Report at 31 December 10| date = 31 December 2010| access-date = 15 May 2011| publisher = Juventus| archive-date = 2 June 2015| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150602180059/http://www.juventus.com/wps/wcm/connect/19f4429c-c935-4d87-bb61-e3c83a50a616/JUVE_SEMESTRE_INGLESE.pdf?MOD=AJPERES&CACHEID=19f4429c-c935-4d87-bb61-e3c83a50a616| url-status = dead}}</ref> Following his move to Wolfsburg, Diego criticized Juventus general director [[Giuseppe Marotta]] for his exit and is the blame for letting Juventus make huge losses on some high-profile players.<ref>{{cite news|title=Diego blames Marotta for exit|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11854/6354393/| publisher=Sky Sports|date=2 September 2010|access-date=7 March 2012}}</ref>

In Diego's first match for Wolfsburg, he scored his debut goal in a game which Wolfsburg lost 3–4 to [[1. FSV Mainz 05|Mainz 05]]. On 5 February 2011, he won a penalty for Wolfsburg; he subsequently took the ball from designated spot-kick taker [[Patrick Helmes]], then hit the woodwork ten minutes from time. Wolfsburg later lost the match by one goal, prompting Wolfsburg manager [[Steve McClaren]] to fine him €100,000 (£86,000) for failing to follow instructions. Diego was defended by [[Dieter Hoeneß]], claiming that Diego does not believe he should be banned for the incident.<ref>{{cite news|title=Hoeness defends Diego|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11095/6454328/|publisher=Sky Sports|date=19 October 2010|access-date=7 March 2012}}</ref> Nonetheless, Diego was also informed that he would be removed from the first team for Wolfsburg's upcoming game against [[Hamburger SV]].<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.whoateallthepies.tv/videos/64192/diego-fined-e100k-and-steve-mcclaren-sacked-over-botched-penalty-video.html| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110209205554/http://www.whoateallthepies.tv/videos/64192/diego-fined-e100k-and-steve-mcclaren-sacked-over-botched-penalty-video.html| url-status = usurped| archive-date = 9 February 2011| title = Diego Fined €100k For Penalty Miss, Steve McClaren Then Sacked By Wolfsburg (Video)| access-date =10 February 2011| first = Chris| last = Wright| publisher=whoateallthepies.tv}}</ref>

On 14 May, before a crucial relegation game against [[TSG 1899 Hoffenheim|1899 Hoffenheim]], Diego once again got in trouble with the management of Wolfsburg, when he left the hotel in which the team was staying when he was informed he would not be starting the game.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.goal.com/en/news/15/germany/2011/05/14/2486122/diego-storms-out-after-being-omitted-from-wolfsburg-squad| title = Diego storms out after being omitted from Wolfsburg squad for Hoffenheim clash| date = 14 May 2011| access-date =14 May 2011| first = Daniel| last = Edwards| publisher=goal.com}}</ref> This left Wolfsburg with only six players on the bench for the game that would determine whether they would play another season in the Bundesliga or be relegated. Wolfsburg went on to win the game 3–1 without Diego, ensuring another top flight season for the club, though Diego was fined €500,000 for his actions.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.goal.com/en/news/15/germany/2011/06/22/2543534/wolfsburgs-diego-fined-500000-for-abandoning-team-mates| title = Wolfsburg's Diego fined €500,000 for abandoning team-mates – report| date = 22 June 2011| access-date =28 August 2011| first = Luke| last = Matthews| publisher=goal.com}}</ref>

====Loan to Atlético Madrid====
After the [[2010–11 Bundesliga|2010–11 season]] at Wolfsburg, new manager [[Felix Magath]] told Diego in May he had no future with the club. On the last day of the transfer season, Diego joined [[Atlético Madrid]] in [[La Liga]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.adifferentleague.co.uk/p6_1_9295_atl%C3%A9tico-madrid-snare-wolfsburg%E2%80%99s-diego-on-season-long-loan.html| title = Atlético Madrid snare Wolfsburg's Diego on season-long loan| date = 1 September 2011| access-date = 6 September 2011| first = David| last = Redshaw| publisher = adifferentleague.co.uk| url-status = dead| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110926062335/http://www.adifferentleague.co.uk/p6_1_9295_atl%C3%A9tico-madrid-snare-wolfsburg%E2%80%99s-diego-on-season-long-loan.html| archive-date = 26 September 2011| df = dmy-all }}</ref> On 10 September 2011, he made his debut for Atlético against [[Valencia CF|Valencia]].<ref>{{cite web |url = http://uk.eurosport.yahoo.com/football/liga/2011-2012/valencia-cf-atletico-madrid-458795.html| title = Valencia CF 1 – 0 Atlético Madrid| publisher = eurosport.yahoo.com| date = 10 September 2011| access-date =11 September 2011}}</ref> He scored his first goal for Atlético in the 60th minute of a [[UEFA Europa League]] game against [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] to make it 2–0 and made an assist to [[Radamel Falcao]] in the third minute. The match finished in a 2–0 win for Atlético.<ref>{{cite news|title=Europa League: Atletico Madrid 2 Celtic 0|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/football/spl/celtic/2011/09/16/europa-league-atletico-madrid-2-celtic-0-86908-23423894/|publisher=Daily Record|date=16 September 2011|access-date=7 March 2012}}</ref> Diego scored his first league goal in a 3–2 win over [[Levante UD|Levante]] on 20 November 2011. As a key player for Atlético, Diego provided assists and established himself in the first team. But on 19 February 2012, against [[Sporting de Gijón]], Diego sustained a hamstring injury in the second half.<ref>{{cite news|title=Diego suffered a hamstring injury and is doubtful for Barca|trans-title=Diego sufre una lesión muscular y es duda para recibir al Barça|url=http://www.marca.com/2012/02/19/futbol/equipos/atletico/1329681918.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=19 February 2012|access-date=11 June 2014}}</ref> It was announced that Diego would be out for a month.<ref>{{cite news|title=Diego will be out for a month|trans-title=Diego estará un mes de baja|url=http://www.marca.com/2012/02/20/futbol/equipos/atletico/1329757876.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=20 February 2012|access-date=11 June 2014}}</ref> After a month out, Diego recovered from his injury and made his return to training.<ref>{{cite news|title=Diego returns to full training|trans-title=Diego vuelve a entrenar con normalidad|url=http://www.marca.com/2012/03/23/futbol/equipos/atletico/1332503141.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=23 March 2012|access-date=11 June 2014}}</ref> Diego made his return against [[Real Zaragoza]] on 26 March 2012.<ref>{{cite news|title=Godin names the tilefish miracle|trans-title=Godín da nombre al milagro blanquillo|url=http://www.marca.com/marcador/futbol/2011_12/primera/jornada_30/zar_atm/|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=26 March 2012|access-date=11 June 2014}}</ref>

On 9 May 2012, Diego scored the third goal on Atlético's win over [[Athletic Bilbao]] in the [[2012 UEFA Europa League Final|Europa League Final]], assuring the capital side won the title for the second time in three years.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=341106&cc=5901| title = Falcao inspires Atletico| publisher = ESPN Soccernet| date = 9 May 2012| access-date = 9 May 2012| archive-date = 12 May 2012| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120512060222/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=341106&cc=5901| url-status = dead}}</ref> After the match, Diego told [[UEFA]]'s official website, "We played against a tough rival like Athletic, but we played an almost perfect match, it was a difficult match, we never said it was going to be easy.
