====Return to VfL Wolfsburg====
Diego returned to VfL Wolfsburg following the end of his loan spell in Madrid. Upon his return, his relationship with manager Felix Magath continued to deteriorate: he was placed in the reserve side<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/15/germany/2012/07/21/3255502/diego-may-be-banished-to-wolfsburg-ii-in-german-fourth-tier|title=Diego may be banished to Wolfsburg II in German fourth tier|publisher=Goal.com|date=21 June 2012|access-date=21 June 2012}}</ref> after Magath criticised his attitude on his first training session back.<ref>{{cite news|title=Magath unimpressed by Diego workrate in training|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/15/germany/2012/07/19/3251691/magath-unimpressed-by-diego-workrate-in-training|publisher=Goal.com|date=19 June 2012|access-date=14 November 2012}}</ref> Despite the strained relationship between the two, he was selected by Magath in a series of pre-season friendlies in a tour of China.<ref>{{cite news|title=Wolfsburg take Diego on pre-season tour of China|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/15/germany/2012/07/25/3265012/wolfsburg-take-diego-on-pre-season-tour-of-china|publisher=Goal.com|date=25 July 2012|access-date=14 November 2012}}</ref> Although he was told by Magath he has no future in Wolfsburg, Diego nonetheless announced that he would stay at the club, as clubs overseas had no apparent interest in signing him.<ref>{{cite news|title=Magath: Diego will stay at Wolfsburg if nothing happens in the next few days|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/15/germany/2012/07/31/3277870/magath-diego-will-stay-at-wolfsburg-if-nothing-happens-in|publisher=Goal.com|date=31 July 2012|access-date=14 November 2012}}</ref>

Diego played his first game for the club in a 1–0 victory over VfB Stuttgart in the opening game of the [[2012–13 Bundesliga]]. In the club's first game without Magath, who had been sacked with only five points in eight matches (and no goals and points in the last four games), Diego scored his first goal and provided his first assist of the Bundesliga season in Wolfsburg's 4–1 defeat of [[Fortuna Düsseldorf]] on 27 October 2012, which ended a run of four-straight defeats.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/match?id=346331&cc=5901 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130102230525/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/match?id=346331&cc=5901 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2 chance under new interim manager [[Lorenz-Günther Köstner]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Köstner lets Diego play |trans-title = Köstner lässt Diego spielen|url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/lorenz-guenther-koestner/laesst-diego-spielen-26901240.bild.html|publisher=Bild|language=de|date=26 October 2012|access-date=21 February 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Wolfsburg have rediscovered their freedom after Magath's exit, hints Diego|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/15/germany/2012/10/30/3487965/wolfsburg-have-rediscovered-their-freedom-after-magaths-exit|publisher=Goal.com|date=30 October 2012|access-date=14 November 2012}}</ref> Four days later, in the [[2012–13 DFB-Pokal|DFB-Pokal]], Diego opened the scoring before providing an assist for [[Bas Dost]] as Wolfsburg defeated [[FSV Frankfurt]] 2–0.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/match?id=355561&cc=5901 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130102232957/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/match?id=355561&cc=5901 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2 January 2013 |title=VfL Wolfsburg 2 – 0 FSV Frankfurt |publisher=ESPNFC |date=31 October 2012 }}</ref> He then netted a brace in Wolfsburg's 3–1 victory over Bayer Leverkusen on 11 November, bringing to an end Bayer's 11-game unbeaten run and giving Wolfsburg their first home win of the Bundesliga campaign.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/us/en/report/346305/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5901 |title=VfL Wolfsburg 3–1 Bayer Leverkusen |publisher=ESPNFC |date=11 November 2012 }}</ref> Then, on 8 December 2012, Diego scored and set up the second and third goal in match in a 3–2 win over Borussia Dortmund.<ref>{{cite news|title=Dortmund suffer blow|url=http://espnfc.com/uk/en/report/346268/report.html?ex_cid=espnapi_internal&soccernet=true|publisher=ESPN|date=8 December Throughout the 2012–13 season, Diego continued to make an impressive display for the club, scoring 10 goals in 37 appearances in all competitions, making him the club's top-scorer. Before and during the [[2013–14 Bundesliga]] season, Diego was linked with a move back to Santos in Brazil,<ref>{{cite news|trans-title=Santos offers 377000 euros a mont h| title= Santos bietet 377000 Euro im Monat|url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/diego/santos-bietet-377000-im-monat-30593602.bild.html|publisher=Bild|language=de|date=28 May 2013|access-date=21 February 2014}}</ref> as well as with English [[Premier League]] side [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]].<ref>{{cite news|trans-title= Diego asserts: Arsenal wants me!| title= Diego behauptet: Arsenal will mich!|url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/diego/behauptet-arsenal-will-ihn-33559410.bild.html |publisher=Bild|language=de|date=27 November 2013|access-date=21 February 2014}}</ref> Despite the rumours, Diego stayed with Wolfsburg for the first half of the season, scoring 3 times in 15 appearances. Throughout the first half of the season, however, Diego's future at Wolfsburg was uncertain after he disagreed with sporting director [[Klaus Allofs]].<ref>{{cite news|trans-title=Allofs angry because of Diego's reaction| title= Allofs sauer über Diego-Reaktion|url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/vfl-wolfsburg/allofs-sauer-auf-diego-33862024.bild.html|publisher=Bild.de|language=de|date=15 December 2012|access-date=21 February 2014}}</ref> At this time, Diego earned the highest wages at the club.<ref>{{cite news| trans-title=2.7m less for Diego| title= 2,7 Mio weniger für Diego |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/vfl-wolfsburg/diego-verdient-weniger-wenn-er-bleibt-33893566.bild.html|publisher=Bild|language=de|date=17 December 2013|access-date=21 February 2014}}</ref> The club was keen to extend Diego's contract.<ref>{{cite news|trans-title=VW Boss wants to extend with Diego|title= VW-Boss will mit Diego verlängern|url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/vfl-wolfsburg/vw-boss-will-diego-halten-33339154.bild.html|publisher=Bild|language=de|date=11 November 2013|access-date=21 February 2014}}</ref>

===Atlético Madrid===
On 31 January 2014, Diego moved back from Wolfsburg to Atlético Madrid. He signed a contract for the rest of the [[2013–14 La Liga|2013–14 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/news/story/_/id/1699694/atletico-madrid-snap-diego-wolfsburg?cc=5739|title=Atletico Madrid snap up Diego|date=31 January 2014|work=ESPNFC|access-date=31 January 2014}}</ref> Prior the move, Diego desired to leave Wolfsburg in order to play in the Champions League.<ref>{{cite news|trans-title=Diego speaks about the Champions League| title= Diego spricht von der Champions League|url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/diego/spricht-von-der-champions-league-34113664.bild.html|publisher=Bild|language=de|date=7 January 2014|access-date=21 February 2014}}</ref> Diego debuted on 2 February on Atlético's victory 4–0 against [[Real Sociedad]], scoring the match's fourth and final goal.<ref>{{cite news|title=Atletico Madrid 4–0 Real Sociedad|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25999816|publisher=BBC Sport|date=2 February 2014|access-date=21 February 2014}}</ref> On 1 April, Diego scored from a long-range shot against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in the Champions League,<ref>{{cite news|title=Barcelona 1–1 Atlético Madrid|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/26811624|access-date=10 April 2014|newspaper=[[BBC Sport]]|date=1 April 2014}}</ref> as Atlético reached the semi-finals for the first time since 1974. Atlético would reach the final of the Champions League for the second time since 1974, after beating [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] 3–1 to face their rivals Real Madrid in their first ever [[Madrid derby]] in the Champions League final. Diego was an unused substitute in the final as Atlético Madrid lost 4–1.<ref>{{cite news| url = https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/27383593| title = Real Madrid 4–1 Atlético Madrid| publisher = [[BBC Sport]]| date = 24 May 2014| access-date = 11 June 2014}}</ref> Nevertheless, Diego helped the club win the La Liga championship to earn his team its first league title in 18 years.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/competitions/la-liga/10838338/Barcelona-v-Atletico-Madrid-La-Liga-live.html|title=Barcelona 1 Atletico Madrid 1, La Liga: match report|publisher=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|last=Martin|first=Richard|date=17 May 2014|access-date=11 June 2014}}</ref> After being linked a move away, Diego wrote on his [[Instagram]] account, giving the Atlético supporters a farewell message, as he left the club for the second time.<ref>{{cite news|title=Diego Atletico farewell: "Thank you, I'll always be a fan of this club"|trans-title=Diego se despide del Atlético: "Gracias, siempre seré un aficionado de este club"|url=http://www.marca.com/2014/05/28/futbol/equipos/atletico/1401289152.html|publisher=Marca|language=es|date=28 May 2014|access-date=11 June 2014}}</ref>

After various failed attempts to sign Diego in previous years, [[Clube de Regatas do Flamengo|Flamengo]] was finally able to hire the player for three years on 19 July 2016.<ref>{{cite news|trans-title=Diego Atletico farewell: "Thank you, I'll always be a fan of this club'|title=Final feliz: após 12 anos, Diego volta ao Brasil e é o novo reforço do Fla|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/times/flamengo/noticia/2016/07/fim-de-novela-apos-12-anos-diego-volta-ao-brasil-e-o-novo-reforco-do-fla.htmlpublisher=globoesporte.com|language=pt|date=19 July 2016|access-date=19 July 2016}}{{dead link|date=September 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> The player, who had already expressed a wish of playing for a Brazilian club chose Flamengo over other rival clubs. The great moment lived by [[Clube de Regatas do Flamengo|Rubro-Negro]], in the [[2016 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|Brazilian Série A]], according to Diego, resulted from "complicity and generosity."<ref>{{cite web| url = http://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/times/flamengo/noticia/2016/09/gentileza-gera-diego-ve-fla-no-topo-por-cumplicidade-e-generosidade.html| title = Gentileza gera... ==International career==
[[File:Diego061115.jpg|thumb|150px|right|Diego with the Brazil national team in 2006]]
Diego made his international debut in April 2003 in a friendly match against [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]]. He was later included in [[Brazil Olympic football team|Brazil under-23]] team that competed in [[2003 CONCACAF Gold Cup]] alongside Santos' teammate [[Robinho]]. Although Brazil compete as an under-23 team, the international appearances and goals were recorded as [[FIFA]] acknowledge the tournament as senior team matches. He appeared five times and scored two goals as Brazil U-23 lost out to the Mexico senior team in the final. In 2004, Diego was called up for the [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] national squad for the [[2004 Copa América]], and he was instrumental in securing the tournament victory for Brazil when he scored in the [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shootout]] against [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] in the final.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/internationals/3922603.stm| title=Brazil win Copa shoot-out| website = BBC Sport| date=25 July 2004| access-date=2 July 2019}}</ref>

Due to his decline in performance with Porto between 2004 and 2006, Diego was often left out of the Brazil squad. He was mostly playing as deputy to [[Kaká]] and was also left out of the Brazil squad for the [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006 World Cup]]. He was then included in Brazil's squad for the [[2007 Copa América]], which Brazil went on to win, once again defeating Argentina in the final. Before the [[Football at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008 Summer Olympics]], he was involved in squad controversy. Specifically, Werder Bremen (to send Diego) along with [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]] ([[Rafinha (footballer, born 1985)|Rafinha]]), both to [[Brazil national under-23 football team|Brazil]], and [[Barcelona FC|Barcelona]] ([[Lionel Messi]]) to [[Argentina national under-23 football team|Argentina]], did not want to release their players for the Olympic games so that they could help them in their domestic and European competitions. The case was taken to [[FIFA]], which ruled that all clubs should release their players aged under 23 for the Games.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Lynch |first=Robin |date=30 July 2008 |title=Clubs must release U-23s for Olympics, says Fifa |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/jul/30/olympicgames20081 |access-date=12 September 2024 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Soccer Players Must Be Released for Olympics, FIFA Rules – DW – 07/30/2008 |url=https://www.dw.com/en/soccer-players-must-be-released-for-olympics-fifa-rules/a-3523245 |access-date=12 September 2024 |website=dw.com |language=en}}</ref>

Schalke, Werder Bremen, and Barcelona took their case to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) who eventually ruled in the clubs' favour, stating, "The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) has upheld the appeals filed by FC Schalke 04, SV Werder Bremen and FC Barcelona against the decision issued on 30 July 2008 by the Single Judge of the FIFA's Players' Status Committee that consequently has been set aside in its entirety because the Olympics is not on the [[FIFA International Match Calendar|FIFA's International Calendar]] to avoid competing with the [[FIFA World Cup awards|World Cup]]."<ref>{{cite web |date=6 August 2008 |title=Trio win Olympics appeal |url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,14935_3940112,00.html |access-date=24 September 2008 |publisher=skysports.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=6 August 2008 |title=Arbitration CAS 2008/A/1622 FC Schalke 04 v. Fédération Internationale de Football Association (FIFA), CAS 2008/A/1623 SV Werder Bremen v. Fédération Internationale de Football Association (FIFA) & CAS 2008/A/1624 FC Barcelona v. Fédération Internationale de Football Association (FIFA), award of 2 October 2008 |url=https://www.tas-cas.org/fileadmin/user_upload/CAS_Award_6785___internet__.pdf |access-date=2 October 2008 |website=The Court of Arbitration for Sport}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=6 August 2008 |title=FIFA ruling on soccer players in Games overturned |url=https://www.espn.com/olympics/summer08/soccer/news/story?id=3521312 |access-date=12 September 2024 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Nutbrown |first=Charlie |date=6 August 2008 |title=Olympics: CAS steps in to stop players heading to Beijing |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2008/aug/06/olympics2008.olympicsfootball |access-date=12 September 2024 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> Despite his club's wishes, he ultimately did compete for the Brazil squad under the provision that their salaries were paid for by the [[Brazilian Football Confederation]],<ref name="thestar">{{cite web |last=Lisi |first=Clemente |date=8 August 2008 |title=Messi Allowed to Play in Beijing |url=https://nypost.com/2008/08/08/messi-allowed-to-play-in-beijing/ |access-date=9 April 2017 |website=thestar.com.my}}</ref> which won bronze.<ref>{{Cite web |date=22 July 2008 |title=Players defy clubs, join Brazil's soccer team |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna25800894 |access-date=12 September 2024 |website=NBC News |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=22 August 2008 |title=Brazil beats Belgium to claim Olympic bronze |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/08/22/sports/22iht-olysoc22.15556260.html |access-date=12 September 2024 |website=[[New York Times]]}}</ref> On 19 January 2017, he came back to Brazilian team being called up by coach [[Tite (football manager)|Tite]] for a friendly game against [[Colombia national football team|Colombia]], six days later. Only footballers playing for Brazilian clubs were called up.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.acritica.com/channels/esportes/news/confira-convocados-para-amistoso-da-selecao-brasileira-contra-a-colombia| title = Confira convocados para amistoso da Seleção Brasileira contra a Colômbia| language = br| website = acritica.com| date = 19 January 2017| access-date = 20 January 2017| archive-date = 22 January 2017| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20170122214038/http://www.acritica.com/channels/esportes/news/confira-convocados-para-amistoso-da-selecao-brasileira-contra-a-colombia| url-status = dead}}</ref> Brazil won the game 1–0.<ref>{{cite web |title=Brazil 1–0 Colombia |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/470420/colombia-brazil |publisher=www.espn.com |access-date=13 July 2026}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Diego was a creative offensive [[playmaker]] known for his technique, [[dribbling (association football)|dribbling]] ability, vision and accurate passing; usually deployed as an [[attacking midfielder]], he was also capable of playing as a [[Second striker|supporting forward]] or on the [[winger (association football)|wing]] on occasion.<ref name="Sbarca Diego: Amo la Juve">{{cite web|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2004/marzo/16/Sbarca_Diego_Amo_Juve__ga_10_0403165231.shtml|title=Sbarca Diego "Amo la Juve"|publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport|language=it|date=16 March 2004|access-date=17 September 2014}}</ref> As well as being an effective [[Assist (football)|assist]] provider, he was also known for his goalscoring ability,<ref name="Diego making his mark in Bremen">{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=106944.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090531090522/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=106944.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=31 May 2009|title=Diego making his mark in Bremen|publisher=fifa.com|date=25 October 2006|access-date=15 February 2012}}</ref> and he was an accurate [[Direct free kick|set-piece]] taker.<ref name="Sbarca Diego: Amo la Juve"/> Diego was also known for his trickery and [[Keepie uppie|ball-skills]], such as his use of [[Backheel|back-heels]], [[dummy (association football)|feints]] and [[Bicycle kick|overhead kicks]], among an assortment of other [[Association football tactics and skills|tricks]].<ref name="Diego making his mark in Bremen"/>

==Personal life==
Diego is of Italian ancestry, with both of his paternal great-grandparents emigrating from Italy to Brazil. His great-grandfather, Carlo Lazzari, came from [[Ferrara]], and his great-grandmother, Maria Concetta Viola, came from [[Naples]]. As a result of his Italian ancestry, Diego received his Italian passport in 2004.<ref>{{cite web| url = http://www.ilsussidiario.net/articolo.aspx?articolo=19691| title = ESCLUSIVA CALCIOMERCATO/ Juventus, avvocato Basile: io interista, ho dato a Diego la cittadinanza italiana| date = 29 January 2009| access-date = 29 January 2010| language = it| publisher = ilsussidiario.net| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20100114140500/http://www.ilsussidiario.net/articolo.aspx?articolo=19691| archive-date = 14 January 2010| url-status = dead| df = dmy-all }}</ref> Diego is married to Bruna Letícia Araújo, the couple have three children; two sons Davi (born in 2011) Matteo (born in 2013) and a daughter Letícia (born in 2021).<ref>{{cite news|trans-title=Sarah Connor's ex married|title= Sarah Connors Ex hat geheiratet|url=http://www.gala.de/stars/news/diego-ribas-da-cunha-sarah-connors-ex-hat-geheiratet_22357.html |publisher=Gala.de |language=de|date=14 June 2010|access-date=21 February 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|trans-title=Son born to Brazilian player Diego|title=Nasce filho do jogador brasileiro Diego|url=http://www.fofoki.com/noticias/nasce-filho-jogador-brasileiro-diego|publisher=Fo Foki|language=pt|date=2 February 2011|access-date=21 February 2014|archive-date=28 October 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171028201132/http://www.fofoki.com/noticias/nasce-filho-jogador-brasileiro-diego|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|trans-title=Diego wants a girl| title=Diego wünscht sich ein Mädchen|url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/diego/wuenscht-sich-ein-maedchen-29368716.bild.html|publisher=Bild|language=de|date=4 March 2013|access-date=21 February 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://revistaquem.globo.com/QUEM-News/noticia/2021/07/diego-ribas-anuncia-nascimento-da-filha-mundo-cor-de-rosa.html | title=Diego Ribas anuncia nascimento da filha: "Mundo cor-de-rosa" | date=28 August 2022 }}</ref>

'''Jesse Ellis Lingard''' (born 15 December 1992) is an English professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as an [[attacking midfielder]] or [[Winger (association football)|winger]] for [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A]] club [[SC Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]]. He has won the [[UEFA Europa League]], [[FA Cup]], [[EFL Cup]], and [[FA Community Shield]], being one of only three players to score in all of the latter three finals.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.manutd.com/en/players-and-staff/detail/jesse-lingard|title=Jesse Lingard |website=ManUtd.com|publisher=Manchester United}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://metro.co.uk/2017/02/27/manchester-united-ace-jesse-lingard-joins-elite-group-of-players-with-efl-cup-final-goal-6475405/|title=Jesse Lingard joins elite group of TWO legends with third goal at Wembley|first=Tom|last=Olver|date=27 February 2017}}</ref>

Lingard made his senior debut while on [[Loan (association football)|loan]] at [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] in 2012, and spent time on loan at [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] and [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]] during the 2013–14 season and at [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]] in 2015. He broke into the [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] first-team under [[Louis van Gaal]] in 2015, and was a regular in the side until 2019, when he fell out of favour under [[Ole Gunnar Solskjær]] and struggled to regain his place in the team. A productive loan spell with [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] in 2021 saw Lingard rediscover his form, scoring nine goals in 16 appearances. He returned to Manchester United for one more year until he was released at the end of the [[2021–22 Manchester United F.C. season|2021–22 season]]. He signed a one-year contract at [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]], before being released at the end of the [[2022–23 Nottingham Forest F.C. season|2022–23 season]]. Seven months later, he joined South Korean club [[FC Seoul]]. He joined Corinthians in 2026.

Lingard represented England at [[England national under-17 football team|under-17]] and [[England national under-21 football team|under-21]] levels, before making his [[England national football team|senior]] international debut in October 2016 and representing his country at the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]], where England finished fourth.

|last=Johnston |website=BBC Sport |date=7 February 2016 |access-date=3 August 2016}}.</ref> On 21 May 2016, Lingard scored the winning goal for Manchester United in the [[2016 FA Cup Final]] against Crystal Palace, having come on as a second-half substitute for other goalscorer [[Juan Mata]].<ref name=2016FAC>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Crystal Palace 1–2 Manchester United |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36292265 |website=BBC Sport |date=21 May 2016 |access-date=22 May 2016}}</ref>

====2016–17 season====
Lingard scored the opening goal as Manchester United beat Premier League champions Leicester City 2–1 to win the [[2016 FA Community Shield]].<ref name=2016FACS>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36934956 |title=Leicester City 1–2 Manchester United |first=Chris |last=Bevan |website=BBC Sport |date=7 August 2016 |access-date=15 December 2017}}</ref> He scored another important goal in February 2017, this time United's second of a 3–2 win over [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] in the [[2017 EFL Cup Final]].<ref name=2017EFLC>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39018813 |title=Manchester United 3–2 Southampton |website=BBC Sport |first=Phil |last=McNulty |date=26 February 2017 |access-date=7 April 2017}}</ref> On 6 April 2017, Lingard signed a new contract with Manchester United, of four years with an option for a fifth.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11667/10827468/jesse-lingard-agrees-new-four-year-deal-at-manchester-united |title=Manchester United confirm Jesse Lingard has signed new deal |website=Sky Sports |date=6 April 2017 |access-date=22 February 2018}}</ref>

====2018–19 season====
On 5 December 2018, Lingard scored his first domestic goal of the season in a 2–2 draw against [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/11572509/manchester-united-2-2-arsenal-spoils-shared-after-frantic-clash|title=Manchester United 2–2 Arsenal: Spoils shared after frantic clash|website=Sky Sports}}</ref> Two weeks later, in the [[Liverpool F.C.–Manchester United F.C. rivalry|North West derby]], Lingard scored his second of the season in a 3–1 loss to Liverpool.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11669/11583137/liverpool-3-1-manchester-united-xherdan-shaqiri-sends-liverpool-top-with-second-half-double|title=Liverpool 3–1 Manchester United: Xherdan Shaqiri sends Liverpool top with second-half double|website=Sky Sports}}</ref> During United's first game under new interim manager [[Ole Gunnar Solskjær]], Lingard doubled his season's tally, scoring a penalty and a goal from open play in United's 5–1 win over [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]], in addition to an assist for [[Anthony Martial]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/match-report-cardiff-1-manchester-united-5-premier-league|title=Report: Cardiff City 1 Manchester United 5|website=www.manutd.com}}</ref> On 25 January 2019, Lingard scored the second goal in a 3–1 win over Arsenal in the fourth round of the FA Cup.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2019/01/25/arsenal-vs-manchester-united-fa-cup-fourth-round-live-score/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2019/01/25/arsenal-vs-manchester-united-fa-cup-fourth-round-live-score/ |archive-date=12 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|title=Ole Gunnar Solskjaer keeps perfect record as Man Utd beat Arsenal with clinical counter-attacks|first1=Jason|last1=Burt|first2=J. J.|last2=Bull|newspaper=The Telegraph |date=25 January 2019|via=www.telegraph.co.uk}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

====2019–20 season====
On 26 July 2020, Lingard scored his first goal in the final matchday of Premier League; his first since December 2018 in the 98th minute to seal a 2–0 win at Leicester City. His goal secured qualification for the [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League]] and was the final goal of the [[2019–20 Premier League]] season.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Leicester City 0–2 Manchester United: Visitors secure Champions League place |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53460592 |website=BBC Sport |date=26 July 2020 |access-date=26 July 2020 }}</ref>

====2020–21 season: Loan to West Ham United====
[[File:Jesse Lingard WHU.jpeg|thumb|upright|Lingard playing for [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] in 2021]]

On 29 January 2021, Lingard joined [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] on loan until the end of the season, where he reunited with former Manchester United boss David Moyes.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.whufc.com/news/articles/2021/january/29-january/west-ham-united-sign-england-international-jesse-lingard-loan|title=West Ham United sign England international Jesse Lingard on loan|publisher=West Ham United F.C. |date=29 January 2021|access-date=29 January 2021}}</ref> On his debut on 3 February 2021, Lingard scored two goals against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] as West Ham won 3–1.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Aston Villa vs West Ham LIVE!|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/a-villa-vs-west-ham/live/429047|access-date=3 February 2021|website=Sky Sports}}</ref>

In a match against [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolves]] on 5 April, Lingard carried the ball 52 metres before firing past [[Rui Patrício]], the furthest a player had travelled with the ball before scoring in the Premier League during the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.unitedinfocus.com/news/jesse-lingard-set-season-record-with-impressive-goal/|title=Jesse Lingard set season record with impressive goal|website=United in Focus|date=8 April 2021|accessdate=22 April 2021}}</ref> Lingard continued his good form during his loan spell, contributing nine goals and four assists in his first 10 Premier League games for West Ham.<ref name=NBC /> His ninth goal was scored from the penalty spot in the club's 2–3 defeat at Newcastle United on 17 April. The goal meant he had scored more Premier League goals for West Ham than he ever managed in a single season at Manchester United.<ref name=NBC>{{cite web|url=https://soccer.nbcsports.com/2021/04/17/three-things-we-learned-from-newcastle-west-ham/|title=Three things we learned from Newcastle – West Ham|website=NBC Sports|date=17 April 2021|accessdate=22 April 2021}}</ref>

For his goal performances in April and for his goal against Wolves, Lingard won both the [[Premier League Player of the Month]] and the [[Premier League Goal of the Month]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.premierleague.com/news/2139232|title=Lingard wins EA SPORTS Player of the Month award |publisher=Premier League |date=14 May 2021 |access-date=14 May 2021}}</ref><ref name=GOM/> He played 16 games during his loan spell, scoring nine and assisting five goals.<ref name=whuloan>{{Cite web|url=https://www.whufc.com/news/articles/2021/may/25-may/declan-rice-and-jesse-lingard-named-provisional-england-squad-uefa|title=Declan Rice and Jesse Lingard named in provisional England squad for UEFA Euro 2020 | West Ham United|website=www.whufc.com}}</ref>

====2021–22 season====
On 11 September 2021, Lingard scored the fourth goal for Manchester United in a 4–1 win over [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Stone|first=Simon|date=11 September 2021|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/58437003|title=Cristiano Ronaldo scores twice as United beat Newcastle|work=BBC Sport|access-date=12 September 2021}}</ref> On 19 September, Lingard scored an 89th minute winner in 2–1 defeat of West Ham.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/66390|title=De Gea and Lingard hand Manchester United a dramatic win|publisher=Premier League|access-date=19 September 2021}}</ref>

On 1 June 2022, [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] announced that Lingard would leave the club following the expiration of his contract.<ref>{{cite news |title=Lingard to leave United |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/Jesse-Lingard-to-leave-Man-Utd-in-June-after-20-years-at-the-club |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=1 June 2022 |access-date=1 June 2022 }}</ref>

===Nottingham Forest===
On 21 July 2022, Lingard signed for newly promoted Premier League club [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] on a one-year contract,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3452653/2022/07/21/jesse-lingard-joins-nottingham-forest-on-one-year-deal/ |title=Jesse Lingard joins Nottingham Forest on one-year deal |first=David |last=Ornstein |website=The Athletic |date=21 July 2022 |access-date=21 July 2022}}</ref> becoming their highest-paid player for the 2022–23 season.<ref name="Sky 230602"/> Although he neither scored nor assisted a goal in his 17 league appearances, he made two assists and scored twice to help the team reach the [[2022–23 EFL Cup#Semi-finals|EFL Cup semi-finals]].<ref name="Sky 230602">{{cite news |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12894980/jesse-lingard-nottingham-forest-release-forward-12-months-after-making-him-top-earner |title=Jesse Lingard: Nottingham Forest release forward 12 months after making him top earner |website=Sky Sports |date=2 June 2023 |access-date=12 June 2023}}</ref> Lingard and five other senior players were released when their contracts expired at the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nottinghamforest.co.uk/news/2023/june/02/forest-confirm-retained-list/ |title=Forest confirm retained list |publisher=Nottingham Forest F.C. |date=2 June 2023 |access-date=12 June 2023}}</ref>

===FC Seoul===
On 7 February 2024, Lingard signed a two-year contract with South Korean [[K League 1|K League]] club [[FC Seoul]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jesse Lingard: Former Man Utd forward completes move to South Korean club FC Seoul |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13066093/jesse-lingard-former-man-utd-forward-completes-move-to-south-korean-club-fc-seoul |access-date=8 February 2024 |website=Sky Sports |language=en}}</ref> The signing of Lingard by FC Seoul was described by South Korean football journalist Lee Sungmo as, "the biggest signing in the K League's history".<ref>{{cite web | title='Biggest signing in K League history' | website=BBC Sport | date=8 February 2024 | url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68240046 | access-date=8 February 2024}}</ref>

After a 2–0 victory against [[Jeju United FC]] on 16 March, Lingard was publicly criticised by FC Seoul's head coach, [[Kim Gi-dong]], citing a lack of effort and physicality.<ref>{{Cite web |date=17 March 2024 |title='He didn't work hard' – Jesse Lingard slammed by FC Seoul boss Kim Gi-dong as ex-Man Utd man warned he's some way off breaking into starting XI |url=https://www.msn.com/en-gb/sport/football/he-didn-t-work-hard-jesse-lingard-slammed-by-fc-seoul-boss-kim-gi-dong-as-ex-man-utd-man-warned-he-s-some-way-off-breaking-into-starting-xi/ar-BB1k2yar |access-date=10 April 2024 |website=MSN.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=18 March 2024 |title=Lingard's 'underperformance' displeases FC Seoul coach |url=https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/www/sports/2024/04/600_370795.html |access-date=10 April 2024 |website=Korea Times |language=en}}</ref>

Lingard appeared for 105 minutes during FC Seoul's first six games of the season, before undergoing knee surgery.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68812570|title=Inside Lingard's stuttering start to life in Seoul|work=BBC Sport |date=15 April 2024 }}</ref>

Lingard scored his first goal for the club in a 2–0 home win against [[Gangwon FC]] on 26 June, kicking the ball into the corner from the penalty spot.<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 June 2024 |title=FC Seoul 2-0 Gangwon FC Recap: Lingard scores first goal in K League; have FC Seoul turned a corner? |url=https://www.kleagueunited.com/2024/06/fc-seoul-2-0-gangwon-fc-recap-lingard.html |access-date=18 September 2024 |website= K League United |language=en}}</ref>

In January 2025, he was named club captain ahead of the 2025 season.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://koreajoongangdaily.joins.com/news/2025-01-15/sports/football/Jesse-Lingard-named-FC-Seoul-captain-for-2025-season/2222952 |title=Jesse Lingard named FC Seoul captain for 2025 season |author=Paik Ji-hwan |newspaper=Korea JoongAng Daily |date=15 January 2025 |access-date=20 January 2025}}</ref>

On 5 December 2025, Lingard and FC Seoul agreed to terminate his contract after two years.<ref>{{cite web |title=Jesse Lingard to leave FC Seoul after two seasons |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cnv2m5glgz3o |website=BBC Sport |access-date=5 December 2025 |date=5 December 2025}}</ref> He made his final appearance for the club on 10 December, scoring in a 1–1 draw against [[Melbourne City FC|Melbourne City]] in the league stage of the [[2025–26 AFC Champions League Elite|AFC Champions League Elite]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/jesse-lingard-scores-final-game-162842405.html?guccounter=1&guce_referrer=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZ29vZ2xlLmNvbS8&guce_referrer_sig=AQAAAIVfe5mgkDQsU0EIk5Wrcuj8nGB1pL2iQ4L7Im9g4Tpz3a3NOahjfGVBBi0av6ZNpC6zs55ez_NsoGRteqA7trEp8PiZukxRwCVHU-GG0F8c33_nEsaedkIR6DsNrzr9CG4IZKvT14VecJdPRbN0Ty1oZ4eQuOTogN1c0nndrg6j|title=Jesse Lingard scores in final game but FC Seoul held to a draw in Asian Champions League|website=Yahoo|date=10 December 2025|access-date=10 December 2025}}</ref>

===Corinthians===
On 6 March 2026, Lingard signed a one-year contract with Brazilian club [[SC Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/futebol/times/corinthians/noticia/2026/03/06/novo-louco-do-bando-corinthians-anuncia-a-contratacao-do-atacante-ingles-jesse-lingard.ghtml|title="Novo louco do bando": Corinthians anuncia a contratação do atacante inglês Jesse Lingard|publisher=ge.globo.com|date=2026-03-06|access-date=2026-03-06}}</ref> On 21 April 2026, he became the first British player to score a goal in the [[Copa do Brasil]], securing a 1–0 away win over [[Barra Futebol Clube (SC)|Barra]] in the [[2026 Copa do Brasil|fifth round]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Collins |first1=Ben |title=Jesse Lingard becomes first British player to score in Copa do Brasil as Corinthians win |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c1mkv1gglmvo |access-date=22 April 2026 |work=BBC Sport |date=22 April 2026}}</ref> Later that month, on 30 April, he netted his first [[Copa Libertadores]] goal in a 2–0 victory over [[Peñarol]] in the [[2026 Copa Libertadores group stage|group stage]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://onefootball.com/en/news/jesse-lingard-scores-first-international-goal-for-corinthians-42800203 |title=Jesse Lingard scores first international goal for Corinthians |publisher=OneFootball |date=2 May 2026 }}</ref>

==International career==
===Youth===
Lingard played three times for [[England national under-17 football team|England at under-17 level]] in the 2008 Nordic Tournament.<ref name=FAprofile>{{cite web |url=http://www.thefa.com/england/All-Teams/Players/L/jesse-lingard |title=Jesse Lingard |publisher=The Football Association |access-date=19 September 2013 |archive-date=10 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141010032635/http://www.thefa.com/england/all-teams/players/l/jesse-lingard |url-status=dead }}</ref> He received his first call-up for the [[England national under-21 football team|under-21 team]] for the [[Friendly (association football)|friendly match]] against [[Scotland national under-21 football team|Scotland under-21s]] on 13 August 2013, and made his debut as a second-half substitute for [[Nathan Redmond]] as England won 6–0.<ref name=FAprofile/><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23690472 |title=England Under-21s thrash Scotland 6–0 in friendly |website=BBC Sport |date=13 August 2013 |access-date=11 April 2017}}</ref> On 21 June 2015, Lingard came off the bench to score the winner in a [[2015 UEFA European Under-21 Championship]] group match against [[Sweden national under-21 football team|Sweden]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Brendan |last=McLoughlin |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33085670 |title=Sweden U21 0–1 England U21 |website=BBC Sport |date=21 June 2015 |access-date=11 April 2017}}</ref>

===Senior===
[[File:Jesse Lingard 2018.jpg|thumb|upright|Lingard playing for [[England national football team|England]] at the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]]]]

After [[Michael Carrick]] and [[Jamie Vardy]] withdrew through injury, Lingard received his first call-up to the [[England national football team|full England squad]], for a friendly against [[France national football team|France]] on 17 November 2015.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34825726 |title=England v France: Jesse Lingard & Ryan Mason join squad |website=BBC Sport |date=15 November 2015 |access-date=11 April 2017}}</ref> He did not appear in the match.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/34129999|title=England 2–0 France|work=BBC Sport }}</ref>

Lingard received his next call-up for [[2018 FIFA World Cup qualification|2018 FIFA World Cup qualifiers]] against [[Malta national football team|Malta]] and [[Slovenia national football team|Slovenia]] in October 2016.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37530593 |title=Jesse Lingard: England call up Man Utd winger for World Cup qualifiers |website=BBC Sport |date=2 October 2016 |access-date=3 October 2016}}</ref> He made his debut against Malta, starting on the left wing as England won 2–0.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2016/oct/08/england-malta-2-0-world-cup-qualifier-five-talking-points-waybe-rooney-jesse-lingard-roberto-mancini|title=England 2–0 Malta: Five talking points from Wembley|last=Fifield|first=Dominic|date=8 October 2016 |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |access-date=8 October 2016}}</ref> Lingard scored his first goal on 23 March 2018, in a 1–0 win over the [[Netherlands national football team|Netherlands]] in a friendly.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43380175 |title=Netherlands 0–1 England |first=Phil |last=McNulty |website=BBC Sport |date=23 March 2018 |access-date=6 June 2018}}</ref>

In May 2018, Lingard was named in the 23-man England squad for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44138600 |title=England World Cup squad: Trent Alexander-Arnold in 23-man squad |website=BBC Sport |date=16 May 2018 |access-date=17 May 2018}}</ref> On 24 June, Lingard scored his first [[FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] goal in a 6–1 victory over [[Panama national football team|Panama]] during their second group stage match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/soccer/2018/06/24/england-panama-world-cup-goals-video-highlights-kane-rashford-sterling|title=WATCH: Kane Hat Trick, Stones, Lingard Pace England's Rout of Panama|date=24 June 2018 |publisher=Sports Illustrated|access-date=24 June 2018}}</ref> During the tournament, Lingard received five starts, plus a substitute appearance in the third place play off against Belgium which saw England finish fourth in the tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mykhel.com/football/fifa-world-cup-2018-england-jesse-lingard-p109322-tp114-l4/|title=Jesse Lingard FIFA World Cup 2018 Stats, Records, Position – myKhel|website=mykhelcom}}</ref>

During the November international break, Lingard scored the first goal in Wayne Rooney's farewell match against the USA on 15 November.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/45174412|title=England 3–0 USA|website=BBC Sport|date=15 November 2018}}</ref> On the following Sunday, Lingard scored the equaliser in 2–1 win over Croatia which put England top of their group and qualified them for the [[UEFA Nations League]] semi-finals to be held in June 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2018/nov/18/england-v-croatia-nations-league-live|title=England 2–1 Croatia: Nations League – as it happened|first=Rob|last=Smyth|date=18 November 2018|website=The Guardian|access-date=29 August 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2018/11/18/england-vs-croatia-nations-league-live-score-updates/ |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2018/11/18/england-vs-croatia-nations-league-live-score-updates/ |archive-date=12 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|title=Harry Kane gives England battling win over Croatia and Nations League qualification|first1=Jason|last1=Burt|first2=Alan|last2=Tyers|date=18 November 2018|website=The Telegraph|access-date=29 August 2019}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

Lingard was left out of the England squad for [[UEFA Euro 2020 qualifying]] matches in October 2019.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49921214 |title=Dele Alli & Jesse Lingard left out of England squad for Euro 2020 qualifiers |website=BBC Sport |date=3 October 2019 |access-date=3 October 2019}}</ref> His performances while on loan with West Ham United, since January 2021, earned Lingard a recall to the England squad in March 2021.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56440087|title=Lingard, Shaw & Stones return for England|work=BBC Sport }}</ref> In May 2021, he was named in the provisional England squad for [[UEFA Euro 2020|Euro 2020]],<ref name=whuloan/> but was omitted from the final squad and instead named as a stand-by player for the tournament.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57250378|title=Lingard can show me I'm wrong – Southgate|website=BBC Sport|date=2 June 2021|access-date=2 June 2021}}</ref>

During the September 2021 international break, Lingard scored two goals in a [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification|2022 World Cup qualification]] match against [[Andorra national football team|Andorra]], an eventual 4–0 win.<ref name="Andorra050921"/>

==Personal life==
Lingard was born in England, and his paternal grandparents are emigrants from [[Saint Vincent and the Grenadines]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/world-cup/2018/07/06/5b3f3e7cca47417e648b45fe.html|title=FIFA World Cup 2018: The children of immigrants who want to bring World Cup glory to England|date=6 July 2018|website=MARCA in English}}</ref> He is a cousin of [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] and [[England women's national football team|England]] women's international footballer [[Gabby George]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/av/football/43527545|title=England goalscorer Lingard takes on footballing cousin |website=BBC Sport |date=25 March 2018|access-date=25 March 2018}}</ref>

His parents separated when Lingard was very young, and his grandfather would take him to training and was his biggest supporter. He lived partially with his grandparents and also with his mother, as she suffered with depression, and struggled to get out of bed.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Diary Of A CEO with Steven Bartlett: E214: Jesse Lingard Reveals The Dark Reality Of Being A World Class Football Player on Apple Podcasts |url=https://podcasts.apple.com/gb/podcast/e214-jesse-lingard-reveals-the-dark-reality-of/id1291423644?i=1000595370589 |access-date=20 January 2023 |website=Apple Podcasts }}</ref> Due to his mother suffering from mental health issues, Lingard needed to care for his younger siblings, Jasper, and Daisy-Boo.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Whaling |first=James |date=13 December 2019 |title=Lingard details heartbreaking family agony with star's mother battling illness |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/jesse-lingard-details-heartbreaking-family-21094143 |access-date=20 January 2023 |website=Mirror }}</ref>

Lingard has a daughter from a relationship with fitness model and former girlfriend Rebecca Halliday.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Whetstone |first=Sean |date=7 September 2021 |title=Jesse had other reasons for his Manchester stay |url=https://www.claretandhugh.info/jesse-had-other-reasons-for-his-manchester-stay/ |access-date=20 January 2023 |website=Claretandhugh }}</ref>

In 2018, Lingard launched his own clothing brand, ''JLingz''. The company was criticised by Manchester United former players [[Roy Keane]] and [[Gary Neville]] as being a distraction from football.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://talksport.com/football/461496/manchester-united-roy-keane-gary-neville-jesse-lingard-liverpool/|title=Roy Keane lays into Man United star for what he did before Liverpool clash|date=16 December 2018}}</ref> It recorded losses of over £200,000 in its first year of trading.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/manchester-united-jesse-lingard-jlingz-17159805|title=United star Jesse Lingard's clothing range loses £200k in first year|first=Chris|last=Slater|date=28 October 2019|access-date=13 April 2021|website=Manchester Evening News}}</ref>

In September 2023, Lingard was banned from driving for 18 months and fined £57,000, a week's wages, having been found guilty of [[Drunk driving|drink driving]]. Lingard was stopped in [[Sale, Greater Manchester]], driving a [[Lamborghini Urus]] and was found to be more than twice over the drink driving limit for micrograms of alcohol in a breath sample given.<ref>{{cite web | last1=Leonard | first1=Ian | last2=Scheerhout | first2=John | title=Jesse Lingard hit with 18-month drink-drive ban but denies racing Lamborghini | website=Manchester Evening News | date=21 September 2023 | url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/greater-manchester-news/jesse-lingard-hit-18-month-27761841 | access-date=24 September 2023}}</ref>

'''Thomas Andrew Huddlestone''' (born 28 December 1986) is an English professional [[Association football|football]] coach and former player who played as a [[midfielder#Defensive midfielder|defensive midfielder]]. He is first team assistant coach at [[EFL Championship]] club [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]].

Having progressed through the youth ranks at [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] and [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]], Huddlestone began his professional career in 2003 with the latter club. He quickly broke into the first team, and made 88 league appearances before switching to [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] in 2005. Having spent some of the [[2005–06 Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C. season|2005–06 season]] on [[Loan (sports)|loan]] to [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]], where he made 13 league appearances, he began to break into the Tottenham team during the [[2006–07 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season|2006–07 season]], and became a regular player for the club. However, he struggled with injury problems during the [[2011–12 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season|2011–12 season]], and fell out of favour. He joined [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] in August 2013, having made 144 league appearances for Tottenham.

In 2013, Huddlestone joined [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] where he played a role in helping the club reach the [[2014 FA Cup final]], scoring a goal in the [[2013–14 FA Cup|FA Cup]] third semi-final victory, as they ended up runners-up in the competition, this cup run ensured Hull would qualify for Europe via the [[UEFA Europa League]] for the first time in the club's history, Huddlestone would spend four years at Hull and would play 161 times, scoring 8 goals. In July 2017, Huddlestone returned to Derby County, but after two failed play-off campaigns to gain promotion to the Premier League in 2018 and 2019, Huddlestone left Derby in July 2020 after rejecting a contact offer. In his second spell at Derby, Huddlestone played 90 times, scoring 3 goals. After 13 months out of game, Huddlestone returned to Hull City in August 2021, where he spent a season, before ending his career with a two-year spell at [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] where he was [[Manchester United F.C. Under-21s and Academy|Under-21s]] player-coach.

Huddlestone represented [[England national football team|England]] at [[England national under-16 football team|under-16]], [[England national under-17 football team|under-17]], [[England national under-19 football team|under-19]] and [[England national under-20 football team|under-20]] levels before making his [[England national under-21 football team|under-21]] debut in 2005. He was a regular for the under-21 team between 2005 and 2009, and made 33 appearances. He made senior full England debut in 2009, and made three further appearances, his last being in 2012.

==Club career==
===Derby County===
Born in [[Nottingham]], Nottinghamshire,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.11v11.com/players/tom-huddlestone-20341/ |title=Tom Huddlestone |website=11v11.com |publisher=AFS Enterprises |access-date=4 April 2020}}</ref> Huddlestone was taken on by [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] at an early age but was released at 12 as he was claimed to be "not strong enough".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/jan/10/hull-city-tom-huddlestone-andre-villas-boas-tottenham-england-world-cup |title=Hull City's Tom Huddlestone out to prove André Villas-Boas wrong |first=Louise |last=Taylor |work=The Guardian |date=10 January 2014 |access-date=18 September 2022}}</ref> He joined [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]] and after progressing well, made his debut for Derby County's reserve team at the age of just 15, when he appeared as an 80th minute [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] at right wingback in a match against [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.derbytelegraph.co.uk/Level-headed-Mason-making-good-progress-landmark-reserves-outing/story-11624917-detail/story.html |title=Level-headed Mason making good progress after landmark reserves outing |access-date=21 April 2016 |date=29 October 2010 |newspaper=Derby Telegraph}}{{Dead link|date=July 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=no }}</ref>

He was given his first-team debut by [[George Burley]] at the age of 16 on the opening day of the [[2003–04 Derby County F.C. season|2003–04]] season in a 3–0 home defeat to [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]], where he was voted man of the match.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_div_1/3113043.stm |title=Derby 0–3 Stoke |publisher=BBC Sport |date=9 August 2003 |access-date=18 September 2022}}</ref>{{citation needed|date=April 2016}} Though Derby struggled in Huddlestone's first full season, Huddlestone was one of Derby's few bright points, with Burley saying "He's a terrific talent. As a young player, he (is) the best passer of a ball I (have) ever seen, and I've worked with some good young players."<ref>{{cite news |url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/player/_/id/26412/tom-huddlestone?cc=4716 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121023200238/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/player/_/id/26412/tom-huddlestone?cc=4716 |url-status=dead |archive-date=23 October 2012 |title=Tom Huddlestone Bio Send To Friend |access-date=29 October 2010 |date=29 October 2010 |website=ESPN Soccernet}}</ref> He eventually went on to appear in 43 of Derby's 46 league matches that season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=33696&season_id=133 |title=Tom Huddlestone 2003/04 |publisher=Soccerbase |access-date=18 September 2022}}</ref> He enjoyed an equally successful [[2004–05 Derby County F.C. season|2004–05]] as Derby reached the First Division play-offs, where they lost to [[Preston North End F.C.|Preston North End]] in the semi-final.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_div_1/4537183.stm |title=Derby County 0–0 Preston North End |website=BBC Sport |date=19 May 2005 |access-date=18 September 2022}}</ref> However, halfway through the season Huddlestone signed for [[Premier League]] club [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] in January 2005 for a fee reported to be worth up to £2.5 million, though he remained at Derby for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/t/tottenham_hotspur/4227853.stm |title=Spurs agree deal for Huddlestone |website=BBC Sport |date=1 February 2005 |access-date=28 August 2009}}</ref> He had made a total of 95 appearances for Derby, without scoring.

===Tottenham Hotspur===
[[File:Huddlestone (cropped).jpg|thumb|upright|Huddlestone in 2007]]

Huddlestone spent a few months of the [[2005–06 Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C. season|2005–06 season]] on [[Loan (sports)|loan]] to [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/w/wolverhampton_wanderers/4374622.stm |title=Huddlestone joins Wolves on loan |publisher=BBC Sport |date=25 October 2005 |access-date=18 September 2022}}</ref> scoring his first league goal, at Derby,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_div_1/4430984.stm |title=Derby 0–3 Wolves |website=BBC Sport |date=18 November 2005 |access-date=23 October 2009}}</ref> before returning to make his debut for Tottenham as a substitute in the 1–0 defeat away at [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] on 31 January 2006.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/w/wolverhampton_wanderers/4581284.stm |title=Huddlestone to stay at Molineux |website=BBC Sport |date=4 January 2006 |access-date=28 August 2009}}</ref>

His first start for Tottenham came on 14 September 2006, away to [[SK Slavia Prague|Slavia Prague]] in the [[UEFA Cup]], a match that Tottenham won 1–0.{{citation needed|date=April 2016}} His first goal for Tottenham came in the [[EFL Cup|League Cup]] fourth round match against [[Port Vale F.C.|Port Vale]] on 8 November 2006.<ref name="Tottenham 3-1 Port Vale aet">{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/league_cup/6116418.stm  |title=Tottenham 3–1 Port Vale (aet) |website=BBC Sport |date=8 November 2006 |access-date=27 February 2021}}</ref> Huddlestone scored two goals in this match, his second goal proving decisive in [[extra time]], taking Tottenham through to the quarter-final of the competition.<ref name="Tottenham 3-1 Port Vale aet"/> Huddlestone got his first league goal for Tottenham on 17 December 2006 against Manchester City with an excellent half-volley on 24 minutes, hit first-time after assisting with teammate [[Calum Davenport]]'s first goal with a free-kick.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/6164455.stm |title=Man City 1–2 Tottenham |website=BBC Sport |date=17 December 2006 |first=Pranav |last=Soneji |access-date=28 August 2009}}</ref> Huddlestone established himself as one of the most promising young English central midfielders in the Premier League towards the end of the [[2006–07 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season|2006–07 season]] and head coach Martin Jol compared Tom Huddlestone with German legend Franz Beckenbauer due to his playmaking abilities, ferocious shot power and versatility.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11675_2402128,00.html |title=Huddlestone: Size not important |first=Lewis |last=Rutledge |access-date=28 August 2009 |website=Sky Sports}}</ref>

On 25 December 2006, he signed a new four-and-a-half-year contract – keeping him at the club until 2011.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/t/tottenham_hotspur/6211123.stm |title=Huddlestone agrees new Spurs deal |website=BBC Sport |date=26 December 2006 |access-date=28 August 2009}}</ref> Tom signed a new and improved five-year contract on 30 June 2008 committing his future to Tottenham until 2013.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/articles/newdealfortom300608.html |title=New deal for Tom |access-date=28 August 2009 |date=30 June 2008 |publisher=Tottenham Hotspur F.C.}}</ref> He came on as a substitute as Tottenham beat Chelsea in the [[2008 Football League Cup final|2008 League Cup final]] at [[Wembley Stadium]].<ref name=2008LC>{{cite news |first=Jonathan |last=Stevenson |title=Tottenham 2–1 Chelsea |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/7256729.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=24 February 2008 |access-date=7 January 2018}}</ref> During the [[2009–10 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season|2009–10]] season, he became a regular under [[Harry Redknapp]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/869174-tottenham-hotspur-tom-huddlestone-surgery-could-seal-his-fate-at-spurs |title=Tottenham Hotspur: Tom Huddlestone Surgery Could Seal His Fate at Spurs |first=Nick |last=Young |publisher=Bleacher Report |date=28 September 2011 |access-date=18 September 2022}}</ref> In March 2010, he extended his contract until 2015.<ref>{{cite news |title=Midfielder Tom Huddlestone signs new Tottenham deal |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/t/tottenham_hotspur/8568600.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=15 March 2010 |access-date=16 March 2010}}</ref> Huddlestone was plagued with injury during the [[2011–12 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season|2011–12]] season and managed only four appearances for the club.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/17041778 |title=Injured Tom Huddlestone out for the rest of the season |website=BBC Sport |date=15 February 2012 |access-date=18 September 2022}}</ref> Huddlestone returned for the [[2012–13 Tottenham Hotspur F.C. season|2012–13]] season and made his first appearance as a substitute for [[Jermain Defoe]] against [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] on 1 September 2012.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/19377918 |title=Tottenham Hotspur 1–1 Norwich City |first=Ben |last=Smith |website=BBC Sport |date=1 September 2012 |access-date=18 September 2022}}</ref> He was shown a red card for serious foul play, the match ended in a 1–1 draw. The red card was later rescinded.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19482119 |title=Tom Huddlestone red card for Tottenham rescinded by FA |date=4 September 2012 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=27 September 2014}}</ref>

===Hull City===
[[File:Tom Huddlestone 17-07-2015 1.jpg|thumb|upright|Huddlestone playing for [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] in 2015]]

On 14 August 2013, Huddlestone moved to [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] for an undisclosed fee believed to be about £5.25 million.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23699608 |title=Hull sign Tottenham's Tom Huddlestone & Jake Livermore |website=BBC Sport |date=14 August 2013 |access-date=14 August 2013}}</ref> He made his debut on the first day of the [[2013–14 Hull City A.F.C. season|2013–14 season]] when he came off the bench in a 2–0 loss away at [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23653975 |title=Chelsea 2–0 Hull |date=18 August 2013 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=18 August 2013}}</ref> On 28 December, he scored his first goal for Hull in a 6–0 home win against Fulham, his first goal since April 2011.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25474691 |title=Hull City 6–0 Fulham |date=28 December 2013 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=28 December 2013}}</ref> On 28 January 2014, Huddlestone acted as emergency goalkeeper after Hull City's goalkeeper [[Allan McGregor]] was sent off for squaring up with [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]]'s player [[Stuart O'Keefe]]. With Hull already making three substitutions, Hull's manager [[Steve Bruce]] ordered Huddlestone to take over the goalkeeping role.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Fifield |first1=Dominic |title=Crystal Palace's Jason Puncheon on target again to see off Hull City |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/jan/28/crystal-palace-hull-city-premier-league-match-report |access-date=15 September 2020 |work=The Guardian |date=28 January 2014}}</ref>

On 13 April 2014, he scored Hull's third goal in their 5–3 [[2013–14 FA Cup|FA Cup]] semi-final victory over [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] at Wembley Stadium.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/26908665 |title=Hull 5–3 Sheff Utd |date=13 April 2014 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=14 April 2014}}</ref> On 17 May 2014, Huddlestone started in the [[2014 FA Cup final]] against [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] at Wembley Stadium, in which Hull were beaten 3–2 after extra time.<ref name=2014FAC>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27354148 |title=Arsenal 3–2 Hull City |website=BBC Sport |date=17 May 2014 |access-date=7 January 2018}}</ref>

On 1 July 2016, he signed a new two-year deal with the club.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36687944 |title=Tom Huddlestone: Hull City midfielder signs new contract |date=1 July 2016 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=1 July 2016}}</ref>

[[File:Tom Huddlestone 22-01-2017 1.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Huddlestone playing for [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] in 2017.]]

===Return to Derby County===
On 15 July 2017, Huddlestone returned to boyhood club [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]], by signing a two-year contract, with an option of a third season, for an undisclosed fee, believed to be around £2 million.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40621728 |title=Tom Huddlestone: Derby County sign Hull City midfielder on two-year deal |website=BBC Sport |date=15 July 2017 |access-date=16 July 2017}}</ref> He scored his first goal for Derby in a 3–0 home win against [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] on 3 February 2018, more than 14 years after his debut for the club.<ref>{{cite news |title=EFL: Groundhog Day comes to Accrington as Huddlestone ends long wait |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42932651 |access-date=5 February 2018 |website=BBC Sport |date=3 February 2018}}</ref>

On 1 July 2020, Huddlestone revealed that he and Derby County had failed to agree a contract extension and he would be leaving the club.<ref>{{cite news|title=Tom Huddlestone: Derby County midfielder fails to agree contract extension|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53249208 |access-date=3 July 2020 |website=BBC Sport |date=1 July 2020}}</ref>

===Return to Hull City===
On 17 August 2021, Huddlestone re-signed for [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] on a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58243716|title=Tom Huddlestone: Former England midfielder returns to Hull City on short-term deal|date=17 August 2021|website=BBC Sport|access-date=17 August 2021}}</ref> He made his debut the following day when he came on as a 73rd-minute substitute for [[Richard Smallwood (footballer)|Richie Smallwood]] in the home 1–0 loss to [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]].<ref>{{cite news
 | url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58168106
 | title = Hull City 0–1 Derby County
 | date = 18 August 2021
 | website = BBC Sport
 | access-date = 18 August 2021}}</ref> Huddlestone was one of three senior players to be released at the end of the [[2021–22 Hull City A.F.C. season|2021–22 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.wearehullcity.co.uk/news/2022/may/retained-list-confirmed/|title=Retained List Confirmed|website=www.wearehullcity.co.uk|date=18 May 2022|accessdate=18 May 2022}}</ref>

===Manchester United===
On 2 August 2022, Huddlestone signed for [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]], primarily to act as a player-coach for [[Manchester United F.C. Under-21s and Academy|its under-21 team]]. He replaced [[Paul McShane (footballer)|Paul McShane]] in this role, who retired from playing at the end of the 2021–22 season.<ref>{{cite news |title=United issue academy coaching update |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-academy-coaching-update-includes-tom-huddlestone-appointment |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=2 August 2022 |accessdate=2 August 2022 }}</ref>

Huddlestone played in the [[2022–23 EFL Trophy|2022–23]] and [[2023–24 EFL Trophy|2023–24]] editions of EFL Trophy, wearing the number 35.

On 5 June 2024, the club announced he would be leaving.<ref>{{cite news |title=Club announces official retained list |url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/man-utd-announce-official-list-of-retained-and-released-players-2024 |website=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=5 June 2024 |accessdate=5 June 2024 }}</ref> On 2 July 2024, Huddlestone announced his retirement from football.<ref>{{cite news |title=Hull City send classy message to Tom Huddlestone as ex-Tottenham midfielder confirms retirement |url=https://www.hulldailymail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/hull-city-send-classy-message-9383006 |first=Dominick |last=Howson |date=2 July 2024 |access-date=2 July 2024 |website=HullDailyMail.co.uk }}</ref>

==Coaching career==

On 2 July 2024, it was announced that he had been appointed as a first team coach at [[EFL League One]] side [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]] along with [[Shadab Iftikhar]].<ref>https://wiganathletic.com/news/2024/july/02/Tom-Huddlestone-and-Shadab-Iftikhar-join-Shaun-Maloney-s-backroom-staff--/, Tom Huddlestone and Shadab Iftikhar join Shaun Maloney's backroom staff, Wigan Athletic FC, 2 July 2024</ref>

On 23 August 2024, Huddlestone joined [[Ben Futcher]]'s interim backroom staff with the [[England national under-21 football team|England U21s]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.englandfootball.com/articles/2024/Aug/23/lee-carsley-coaching-team-development-coaches-confirmed-20242308|title=England men's coaching teams confirmed|publisher=England Football|date=23 August 2024|accessdate=27 August 2024}}</ref>

On 18 September 2024, Huddlestone left Wigan Athletic to join fellow League One side Birmingham City.<ref>{{cite news  |url=https://wiganathletic.com/news/2024/september/18/tom-huddlestone-leaves-wigan-to-take-up-a-coaching-offer-with-birmingham/ |title=Tom Huddlestone leaves Wigan to take up a coaching offer with Birmingham |publisher=Wigan Athletic |date=18 September 2024 |access-date=18 September 2024}}</ref>

==International career==
===Youth===
Having been capped at the U-17 and U-19 levels, Huddlestone was a regular in the [[England national under-21 football team|England under-21s]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.englandfootballonline.com/TeamPlyrsBios/PlayersH/BioHuddlestoneT.html |title=Tom Huddlestone |publisher=England Football Online |access-date=18 September 2022}}</ref> He played twice in the [[2007 UEFA European Under-21 Championship]] before a red card for dissent ruled him out of the semi-final and final.<ref>{{cite news |title=Huddlestone handed two-game ban |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/internationals/6764825.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=19 June 2007 |access-date=28 August 2009}}</ref> In October 2008, he scored the opening goal from a free kick in the second leg of the [[2009 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification play-offs]] against Wales.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/internationals/7665226.stm |title=England U21 2–2 Wales U21 |first=Chris |last=Bevan |website=BBC Sport |date=14 October 2008 |access-date=18 September 2022}}</ref> Although the match ended in a draw which ensured qualification for England, it was marred by his sending-off in the second half for a reckless challenge on [[Darcy Blake]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Pearce relieved to pass Welsh test |url=http://www.uefa.com/competitions/under21/news/kind=1/newsid=761634.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081017181229/http://www.uefa.com/competitions/under21/news/kind=1/newsid=761634.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=17 October 2008 |publisher=UEFA |date=15 October 2009 |access-date=20 November 2009}}</ref> He missed the tournament through injury.{{citation needed|date=April 2016}}

===Senior team===
He was called up into the [[England national football team|England]] squad for the first time by coach [[Fabio Capello]] to face the [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]] and [[Trinidad and Tobago national football team|Trinidad and Tobago]] in [[Exhibition game#Association football|friendlies]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/england/2300206/Capello-picks-Joe-Hart-for-USA-England-squad.html |title=Capello picks Joe Hart for USA England squad |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |date=12 May 2008 |access-date=30 August 2011}}</ref> On 14 November 2009, he received his first cap for the senior team in the 1–0 loss in a friendly against [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]], after coming on as a substitute in the 81st minute.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/internationals/8353751.stm |title=Brazil 1–0 England |website=BBC Sport |date=14 November 2009 |access-date=30 August 2011}}</ref> His next appearances came in a [[2010 FIFA World Cup]] warm up match against [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]], where he came on as a substitute in the 61st minute.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/world_cup_2010/8699042.stm |title=England 3–1 Mexico |website=BBC Sport |date=24 May 2010 |access-date=30 August 2011}}</ref> His latest appearance for England also came in a World Cup warm-up match against [[Japan national football team|Japan]] where he started for the first time in 2–1 victory.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/world_cup_2010/8712673.stm |title=Japan 1–2 England |website=BBC Sport |date=30 May 2010 |access-date=30 August 2011}}</ref>

In May 2010, Fabio Capello announced that Huddlestone would be in his preliminary World Cup squad of 30 players.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/world_cup_2010/8673706.stm |title=Fabio Capello makes surprise England World Cup choices |website=BBC Sport |date=11 May 2010 |access-date=30 August 2011}}</ref> However, was not selected for the final 23-man squad.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/world_cup_2010/8713742.stm |title=World Cup 2010: Theo Walcott left out of England squad |website=BBC Sport |date=1 June 2010 |access-date=30 August 2011}}</ref> On 11 November 2012, new England manager [[Roy Hodgson]] gave Huddlestone his first call up to the squad for two years for a friendly match against [[Sweden men's national football team|Sweden]] on 14 November.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20293234 |title=Wilfried Zaha & Carl Jenkinson get England nod as five pull out |website=BBC Sport |date=11 November 2012 |access-date=12 November 2012}}</ref>

==Style of play==
He is known for his passing ability, which has led to comparisons with former Tottenham player [[Glenn Hoddle]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/leagues/premierleague/tottenham/3501927/Tottenhams-Tom-Huddlestone-can-become-the-next-Glenn-Hoddle-Football.html |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150626002202/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/tottenham-hotspur/3501927/Tottenhams-Tom-Huddlestone-can-become-the-next-Glenn-Hoddle-Football.html |url-status=dead |archivedate=26 June 2015 |location=London |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |title=Tottenham's Tom Huddlestone can become the next Glenn Hoddle |first=Duncan |last=White |date=22 November 2008 |access-date=29 May 2010}}</ref> He also has a powerful shot that has enabled him to score long-range goals from midfield.{{citation needed|date=April 2016}}

==Personal life==
Shortly after scoring a goal for Tottenham against Arsenal in April 2011, Huddlestone accepted a challenge not to cut his hair until he scored again, to raise money for charity.<ref>{{cite web |title=Hull's Tom Huddlestone gets haircut after goal drought ends |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25580824 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=16 January 2014 |date=2 January 2014}}</ref> It took him two and a half years, and 55 matches, before he finally scored his next goal (in a Premier League match for Hull against Fulham on 28 December 2013), and he raised more than £57,000 for [[Cancer Research UK]] as a result.<ref>{{cite news |title=Tom Huddlestone goes under the scissors after breaking scoring duck |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/jan/02/tom-huddlestone-haircut-hull-city-fulham |newspaper=The Guardian |location=London |access-date=16 January 2014 |date=2 January 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.justgiving.com/huddlefro |title=tom huddlestone is fundraising for Cancer Research UK |website=Justgiving.com |date=13 October 2011 |access-date=21 April 2016}}</ref>
