'''Jimmy Julien Briand''' (born 2 August 1985) is a French former professional [[association football|footballer]]. He started his career as a [[striker (association football)|striker]], but was later used as a [[winger (association football)|winger]], playing in [[Ligue 1]] for [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]], [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]], [[En Avant Guingamp|Guingamp]] and [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]], as well as in the [[Bundesliga]] with [[Hannover 96]] in a professional career lasting 20 years.

A graduate of the [[INF Clairefontaine|Clairefontaine]] academy, Briand was a [[France national youth football team|France youth international]] at [[France national under-21 football team|U21]] level, and later made five appearances for the [[France national football team|France senior national team]] from 2008 to 2012, making his debut on 11 October 2008 against [[Romania national football team|Romania]].<ref name="sw">{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/jimmy-briand/1473/|title=J. Briand|website=Soccerway}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Rennes===
[[File:Jimmy Briand 2008.jpg|thumb|upright|Briand playing for [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]] in 2008]]

Born in [[Vitry-sur-Seine]], Val-de-Marne,<ref name="lequipe"/> Briand began his career at [[US Ivry|Ivry]], before joining CSF Brétigny. Thereafter, he was selected to attend the [[INF Clairefontaine]]. After finishing his stint at the INF Clairefontaine, Briand joined the youth academy of [[Ligue 1]] club [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]].{{citation needed|date=September 2021}}

While in Rennes' [[youth system]], Briand won the [[Coupe Gambardella]] in 2003. He made his first team debut on 20 May 2003 during the [[2002–03 Ligue 1]] season, at the age of 17, in a Ligue 1 match against [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]], coming on as a substitute and playing 25 minutes. The match finished 0–0.<ref>[http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuilleMatch.asp?saison=2002/2003&code_evt=D1&code_jr_tr=J37&num_ordre=8 PSG v. Rennes Match Report] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090206171317/http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuilleMatch.asp?saison=2002%2F2003&code_evt=D1&code_jr_tr=J37&num_ordre=8 |date=6 February 2009 }}</ref> Over the next two seasons, his play was limited to appearing in only 17 Ligue 1 matches and scoring just one Ligue 1 goal (his first ever), against [[Montpellier HSC|Montpellier]] in a 4–0 victory.{{citation needed|date=September 2021}}

Briand finally broke into the first team for the [[Ligue 1 season 2005–06|2005–06 season]], appearing in 29 Ligue 1 matches and scoring three Ligue 1 goals to help Rennes finish in 7th position in the 2005-06 Ligue 1; they just missed qualifying for the [[2006 UEFA Intertoto Cup]] by one spot. Over the next two years, he appeared in all but four of the club's Ligue 1 matches, due to his consistently good performances in competitive matches and his not sustaining injuries. Despite being linked to clubs outside France, Briand decided to stay with Rennes for the [[Ligue 1 2008-09|2008–09 season]], during which he scored a club-high eight Ligue 1 goals. On 26 March 2009, Briand ruptured his [[Cruciate ligament|anterior cruciate ligament]] in his left knee, while training with the France national team.<ref>[http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11800_5102470,00.html Briand 'disaster' for Rennes]</ref> The injury required six months to heal. As a result, Briand only made his [[2009–10 Ligue 1]] season debut for Rennes on 29 October, in a Ligue 1 match against [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]]. He finished the 2009–10 season with 23 appearances, scoring five goals.{{citation needed|date=September 2021}}

===Lyon===
On 14 June 2010, [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] president and chairman [[Jean-Michel Aulas]] announced that the club had signed Briand to a four-year contract effective on 1 July. The transfer fee was priced at €7.4 million.<ref>{{cite news |title=Striker Briand to join Lyon on four-year deal |url=http://football.uk.reuters.com/leagues/ligue1/news/2010/06/08/LDE6571X2.php |work=France Football |date=8 June 2010 |access-date=12 June 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120703170053/http://football.uk.reuters.com/leagues/ligue1/news/2010/06/08/LDE6571X2.php |archive-date=3 July 2012}}</ref><ref>[http://www.olweb.fr/fr/Accueil/100007/Article/53402/Jimmy-Briand-est-lyonnais Jimmy Briand est lyonnais !] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110611183558/http://www.olweb.fr/fr/Accueil/100007/Article/53402/Jimmy-Briand-est-lyonnais |date=11 June 2011 }}</ref> On 7 August 2010, he made his competitive debut for the club in a 0–0 home draw against Monaco, playing every minute of the match. On 18 February 2011, Briand scored an overhead bicycle kick goal in a 4–0 home win over [[AS Nancy|Nancy]].<ref name="sw"/>

===Hannover 96===
[[Bundesliga]] club [[Hannover 96]] confirmed the signing of Briand on 22 August 2014.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hannover 96 verpflichtet Jimmy Briand |url=http://www.hannover96.de/CDA/aktuelles/alle-news/detailansicht/news/Hannover_96_verpflichtet_Offensivspieler_Jimmy_Briand.html |website=hannover96.de |publisher=Hannover 96 |access-date=25 March 2015 |language=de |date=22 August 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141107234331/http://www.hannover96.de/CDA/aktuelles/alle-news/detailansicht/news/Hannover_96_verpflichtet_Offensivspieler_Jimmy_Briand.html |archive-date= 7 November 2014 }}</ref>

===Guingamp===
On 3 August 2015, Briand joined [[En Avant Guingamp|Guingamp]] on a two-year contract. On 17 May 2017, Briand extended his contract by two years, keeping him with the club until 30 June 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.getfootballnewsfrance.com/2017/jimmy-briand-to-sign-two-year-extension-with-ea-guingamp/|title = Jimmy Briand to sign two-year extension with EA Guingamp | Get French Football News | date=17 May 2017 }}</ref>

On 11 May 2018, Briand scored a goal from the [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty]] spot, his fifth goal in his last six Ligue 1 matches, in the 3–3 Ligue 1 home draw against [[Olympique de Marseille]]; it was also his 30th career Ligue 1 goal for Guingamp since joining them in August 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ligue1.com/ligue1/article/thauvin-rescues-draw-for-10-man-marseille.htm|title=Thauvin rescues draw for 10-man Marseille|website=www.ligue1.com|date=11 May 2018}}</ref>

===Bordeaux===
On 10 August 2018, Briand joined Guingamp's Ligue 1 rivals, [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]], on a two-year contract.<ref name="bordeaux">{{cite news |title=Mercato. Jimmy Briand rejoint Bordeaux pour deux ans ! |url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/sport/football/transferts/mercato-jimmy-briand-rejoint-bordeaux-pour-deux-ans-5917995 |access-date=10 August 2018 |work=Ouest-France |date=10 August 2018 |language=fr}}</ref> He was released by Guingamp just three weeks before joining Bordeaux, with one year left on his contract with Guingamp. He had a "moral agreement" that he would not join another Ligue 1 club. Briand had secured a tentative deal to join [[Major League Soccer]] club [[Montreal Impact (2012–2020)|Montreal Impact]], but it fell through on 26 July 2018.<ref name="bordeaux"/><ref>{{cite news |title=French striker Jimmy Briand snubs Impact, refuses to sign MLS contract |url=https://montrealgazette.com/sports/soccer/mls/montreal-impact/french-striker-jimmy-briand-snubs-impact-refuses-to-sign-mls-contract |access-date=10 August 2018 |work=Montreal Gazette |date=26 July 2018}}</ref>

On 31 August 2019, Briand scored the equalizer for Bordeaux, in an 1–1 away draw against Lyon, to become only the second player to score in 15 different Ligue 1 seasons in the 21st century, following in the footsteps of [[Souleymane Camara]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ligue1.com/ligue1/article/bordeaux-hold-ten-man-ol.htm|title=Bordeaux hold ten-men OL|publisher=www.ligue1.com|date=31 August 2019}}</ref> On 25 October 2020, Briand scored his 100th Ligue 1 goal in a 2–0 win over [[Nîmes Olympique|Nîmes]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.leparisien.fr/sports/football/ligue-1-jimmy-briand-atteint-la-barre-des-100-buts-25-10-2020-8404929.php |title=Ligue 1 : Jimmy Briand atteint la barre des 100 buts |trans-title=Ligue 1: Jimmy Briand reaches the 100-goal mark |access-date=9 June 2022 |date=25 October 2020 |website=[[Le Parisien]] |language=fr}}</ref> In June 2022, he confirmed his departure from Bordeaux.<ref>{{Cite web |date=23 June 2022 |title=Official {{!}} Jimmy Briand leaves Bordeaux |url=https://www.getfootballnewsfrance.com/2022/official-jimmy-briand-leaves-bordeaux/ |access-date=27 June 2022 |website=Get French Football News}}</ref>

Briand announced his retirement from playing in September 2022.<ref>{{cite news |title=Football. L'international français Jimmy Briand prend sa retraite |url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/sport/football/ligue-1/football-l-international-francais-jimmy-briand-prend-sa-retraite-70010ae4-2e2d-11ed-82ab-ca288831284e |access-date=23 March 2023 |work=Ouest France |date=7 September 2022 |language=French}}</ref>

==International career==
Briand played for the [[France national under-21 football team|under-21]] team from 2004 to 2006, scoring 9 goals in 25 appearances. He was a member of the French squad that participated in the [[2006 UEFA European Under-21 Championship]] helping France reach the semi-finals before losing to [[Netherlands national under-21 football team|the Netherlands]].{{citation needed|date=September 2021}}

Briand received his first call-up to the [[France national football team|senior side]] in May 2007 for France's [[UEFA Euro 2008 qualifying|Euro 2008 qualification]] matches against [[Ukraine national football team|Ukraine]] and [[Georgia national football team|Georgia]]. He would not make his debut in those matches. On 11 October 2008, Briand made his international debut, coming on as a substitute for [[Franck Ribéry]] in the 90th minute, against [[Romania national football team|Romania]], in a [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010 World Cup]] [[2010 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|away qualifying match]] that ended in a 2–2 draw.<ref name="sw"/>

'''Anthony Stéphane Bernard Modeste''' (born 14 April 1988) is a French professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Striker (association football)|striker]].

He started his career at [[OGC Nice|Nice]], then spent a season on loan at [[Angers SCO|Angers]]. In 2010, he joined [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]], where he was loaned out to [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] and [[SC Bastia|Bastia]]. He later played for [[Bundesliga]] clubs [[TSG 1899 Hoffenheim|1899 Hoffenheim]] and [[1. FC Köln]], before playing a season at [[Tianjin Quanjian F.C.|Tianjin Quanjian]] in China. He returned to his former club 1. FC Köln in 2018, then loaned out to [[AS Saint-Étienne|Saint-Étienne]] in 2021. He joined [[Borussia Dortmund]] for the 2022–23 season. In September 2023, Modeste signed for Egyptian club [[Al Ahly SC|Al Ahly]].

==Club career==
===Nice===
Modeste started his career as a teenager at French club Nice. He showed glimpses of his huge potential when he played for Nice, with several very impressive performances for one so young. During the 2009–2010 season, Modeste was loaned out to Angers. At only 21 years of age, Modeste proved to be a huge success at Angers, scoring 20 league goals during that season and also being named in the League's team of the season. His eye catching performances during his loan spell at Angers attracted the interest of several big French and English clubs.

===Bordeaux===
On 13 August 2010, Modeste joined [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]] from [[OGC Nice]] for an undisclosed fee thought to be €3.5 million and signed a four-year contract with the club.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ontheminute.com/news/news.php?news=24812 |publisher=Ontheminute.com |title=Bordeaux signs Nice forward |date=13 August 2010 |access-date=12 August 2013 |archive-date=3 March 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120303043714/http://www.ontheminute.com/news/news.php?news=24812 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 19 January 2012, Modeste joined [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] on loan for the rest of the [[2011–12 Premier League]] season, with his French employers insisting there would be no option to buy at the end of the loan period.<ref name="blackburn1">{{cite web | url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2012/jan/19/blackburn-girondins-bordeaux-anthony-modeste?newsfeed=true | title=Blackburn sign Bordeaux's Anthony Modeste on loan for rest of season |work=The Guardian |location=UK | date=19 January 2012 | access-date=20 January 2012}}</ref>

Blackburn Rovers got relegated in the 2011–12 Premier League season after Modeste got a red card in one of the final games of the season against [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] which Blackburn ultimately lost 3–0 and made survival for the next season practically impossible.<ref name="blackburn2">{{cite web | url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2012/apr/07/west-bromwich-albion-blackburn-rovers-premier-league | title= West Bromwich Albion 3–0 Blackburn Rovers Premier League match report |work=The Guardian |location=UK | date=19 January 2012 | access-date=20 January 2012}}</ref>

On 31 July 2012, he signed on loan for [[SC Bastia|Bastia]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.sc-bastia.net/v4/?p=16350 | title = Anthony Modeste décide de rejoindre Bastia ! | language = fr | publisher = [[SC Bastia]] | date = 31 July 2012 | access-date = 12 August 2013 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20141008135925/http://www.sc-bastia.net/v4/?p=16350 | archive-date = 8 October 2014 | url-status = dead }}</ref> He scored on his debut in a 3–2 victory over Sochaux. His lone season at Bastia was a huge success, as he scored 15 league goals in the French top division and he set up many other goals for teammates. He was Bastia's best player of that season.

===1899 Hoffenheim===
On 9 July 2013, Modeste signed with [[TSG 1899 Hoffenheim|1899 Hoffenheim]] on a three-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Anthony Modeste joins Hoffenheim|url=http://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/bordeaux/transfer-talk/news/modeste-joins-hoffenheim_92667.html|access-date=10 August 2015|date=9 July 2015}}</ref> Modeste made his club debut in the [[2013–14 DFB-Pokal|DFB-Pokal]] at fifth-tier [[SG Aumund-Vegesack]] on 3 August, scoring two goals and assisting one.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.kicker.de/aumund-vegesack-gegen-hoffenheim-2013-dfb-pokal-1888110/spielbericht |title=Modeste feiert einen Zwei-Tore-Einstand |work=Kicker |language=de |trans-title=Modeste celebrates a two-goal debut |date=3 August 2013}}</ref> Modeste's [[Bundesliga]] debut came on 10 August against [[1. FC Nürnberg|Nürnberg]], scoring a goal in the 2–2 draw.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.skysports.com/football/hoffenheim-vs-nurnberg/290900 |title=Plenty to think about for Hoffenheim |work=Sky Sports |date=10 August 2013}}</ref> The following weekend at [[Hamburger SV|Hamburg]], Modeste scored a brace in the 1–5 victory,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.kicker.de/hsv-gegen-hoffenheim-2013-bundesliga-1894890/analyse |title=Modeste & Co. demontieren den HSV |work=Kicker |language=de |trans-title=Modeste & Co. dismantle HSV |date=17 August 2013}}</ref> en route to scoring six goals in his first seven games in the Bundesliga with Hoffenheim.

After having started his first 15 matches with Hoffenheim, Modeste was demoted from the starting lineup in favor of [[Sven Schipplock]] after a string of three consecutive losses, and four in five matches. On 8 February 2014, entering as a substitute, Modeste scored a late equaliser against [[SC Freiburg|Freiburg]], scoring for the first time since late September.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.wiwo.de/sport-freiburg-hadert-mit-remis-modeste-rettet-hoffenheim-1-1/9453450.html |title=Freiburg hadert mit Remis – Modeste rettet Hoffenheim 1:1 |work=Wirtschafts Woche |agency=[[Deutsche Presse-Agentur|DPA]] |language=de |date=8 February 2014 |access-date=4 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161104075932/http://www.wiwo.de/sport-freiburg-hadert-mit-remis-modeste-rettet-hoffenheim-1-1/9453450.html |archive-date=4 November 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On 2 March against [[VfL Wolfsburg|Wolfsburg]], Modeste made his first start since late November, scoring two goals and assisting another in the 6–2 victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.kicker.de/hoffenheim-gegen-wolfsburg-2014-bundesliga-1895076/analyse |title=Schipplock macht das halbe Dutzend voll |work=Kicker |language=de |trans-title=Schipplock rounds off the half dozen |date=2 March 2014}}</ref> Modeste scored in three consecutive matches in late March, including the first goal of a 3–3 draw at defending champions [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] before being forced off with injury. On 26 April against [[Eintracht Frankfurt]], Modeste picked up a red card for a violent reaction towards opponent [[Carlos Zambrano (footballer)|Carlos Zambrano]], who appeared to have initiated the incident and went unpunished.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.achtzehn99.de/newsarchive/news-archive-2014/april-2014/hoffenheim-and-frankfurt-share-the-spoils-in-exciting-encounter/ |title=Hoffenheim and Frankfurt Share the Spoils in Exciting Encounter |work=TSG 1899 Hoffenheim |date=26 April 2014}}</ref> Modeste was banned by the [[German Football Association|DFB]] for the final two matches of the season, finishing his year with 14 goals in 33 appearances in all competitions.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.welt.de/newsticker/sport-news/article127388527/Sperre-beendet-Saison-fuer-Hoffenheimer-Modeste.html |title=Sperre beendet Saison für Hoffenheimer Modeste |work=Welt |language=de |trans-title=Ban ends season for Hoffenheim's Modeste |date=28 April 2014}}</ref>

The summer signing of [[Ádám Szalai]] entering the [[2014–15 Bundesliga|2014–15 season]] provided competition for Modeste at the lone striker position,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/hoffenheim/stuermt-modeste-oder-szalai-37057080.bild.html |title=Stürm Modeste Oder Szalai Für Hoffenheim? |work=Bild |first=Andreas |last=Hoffmann |language=de |trans-title=Will Modeste or Szalai strike for Hoffenheim? |date=1 August 2014}}</ref> and the two, along with Schipplock, all shared time throughout the year. As a result, Modeste's playing time was sporadic, and while he only made four fewer starts in the Bundesliga than the previous season, he only started two consecutive matches once prior to a six-game run in the starting lineup to end the season, compared to a thirteen-game run as well as a six-game run in the previous season. Modeste scored in four of his first five starts, but after a five-month scoring drought, he finished with just 7 goals in the Bundesliga. All told, in two seasons with Hoffenheim, Modeste featured in 62 competitive matches, scoring 23 goals in the process.<ref name="Joins Koln" />

===Return to 1. FC Köln===
In August 2018, Modeste went AWOL and returned to Germany. On 17 November, he was given a contract to return to 1. FC Köln until 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://fc.de/fc-info/news/detailseite/details/anthony-modeste-unterschreibt-beim-fc/|title=Anthony Modeste unterschreibt beim FC|trans-title=Anthony Modeste signs with FC|language=de|website=fc.de|publisher=1. FC Köln|date=17 November 2018|access-date=23 March 2020|archive-date=16 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221016010412/https://fc.de/fc-info/news/detailseite/details/anthony-modeste-unterschreibt-beim-fc/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Modeste also sued Tianjin Quanjian to FIFA in order to cancel the player contract, which the Chinese club made a counter-sue.<ref name=Tianjin>{{cite press release|url=http://www.chinaquanjianfc.com/n1/2018/1118/c410955-30406913.html|script-title=zh:关于球员莫德斯特签约科隆俱乐部的严正声明|date=18 November 2018|access-date=10 January 2019|publisher=Tianjin Quanjian F.C.|language=zh-cn|archive-date=29 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181229230210/http://www.chinaquanjianfc.com/n1/2018/1118/c410955-30406913.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

====Loan to Saint-Étienne====
On 1 February 2021, Köln announced that Modeste would join [[Ligue 1]] club [[AS Saint-Étienne]] on a loan deal until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://fc.de/fc-info/news/detailseite/details/fc-verleiht-anthony-modeste/|title=FC verleiht Anthony Modeste|access-date=2021-02-01|website=1. FC Köln|archive-date=1 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210201210723/https://fc.de/fc-info/news/detailseite/details/fc-verleiht-anthony-modeste/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Borussia Dortmund===
On 8 August 2022, [[Borussia Dortmund]] announced the arrival of Modeste in a tweet, "Bienvenue Tony!" from [[1. FC Köln]] on a one-year contract to replace [[Sébastien Haller]] whilst Haller fought cancer. The 34-year-old forward was assigned the number 20.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Anthony Modeste unterschreibt bis 2023 |trans-title=Anthony Modeste signs until 2023 |url=http://www.bvb.de/News/Uebersicht/Anthony-Modeste-unterschreibt-bis-2023/ |access-date=9 August 2022 |date=8 August 2022 |publisher=Borussia Dortmund|website=www.bvb.de |language=de-DE}}</ref> On 8 October, he scored a 95th-minute equalizer in [[Der Klassiker]] against Bayern Munich in the Bundesliga to make the score 2–2.<ref>{{cite web |last=McVitie |first=Peter |title=Modeste madness! Winners and losers as Borussia Dortmund veteran completes wild comeback vs Bayern Munich |url=https://www.goal.com/en/lists/modeste-madness-winners-losers-borussia-dortmund-bayern-munich/blt31f2686f3843721c |website=Goal.com |date=8 October 2023 }}</ref>

On 29 May 2023, Dortmund announced the departure of five players, including Modeste.<ref>{{cite web |title=BVB bid farewell to five players |url=https://www.bvb.de/eng/News/Overview/BVB-bid-farewell-to-five-players |website=Borussia Dortmund official website |publisher=Borussia Dortmund |access-date=29 May 2023 |date=28 May 2023 |archive-date=29 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230529201107/https://www.bvb.de/eng/News/Overview/BVB-bid-farewell-to-five-players |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Al Ahly===
On 11 September 2023, Modeste joined Egyptian club [[Al Ahly SC|Al Ahly]] by signing a one-year contract with an option for a further season.<ref>{{cite web |title=OFFICIAL: Al Ahly announce signing of Anthony Modeste |url=https://www.kingfut.com/2023/09/11/al-ahly-sign-anthony-modeste-2/ |website=kingfut.com |publisher=KingFut |date=11 September 2023 }}</ref> A month later, on 11 November, he scored his first goal in a 1–1 away draw against [[El Gouna FC|El Gouna]].<ref>{{cite web |title=French striker Modeste opens his Ahly account in 1-1 League draw with Gouna |url=https://english.ahram.org.eg/News/512046.aspx |website=ahram.org |date=11 November 2023 }}</ref> On 28 December, he won his first title at the club, by scoring the third goal in a 4–2 victory over [[Modern Future FC|Modern Future]] after extra time in the [[2023–24 Egyptian Super Cup|Egyptian Super Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Marcel Koller hails 'great' Anthony Modeste after Egypt Super Cup win |url=https://www.kingfut.com/2023/12/29/marcel-koller-hails-great-anthony-modeste/ |publisher=KingFut |date=29 December 2023 }}</ref> On 1 July 2024, he departed the club after his contract concluded.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.kingfut.com/2024/07/01/anthony-modeste-departs-al-ahly/ |title=OFFICIAL: Anthony Modeste departs Al Ahly |publisher=KingFut |date=1 July 2024 }}</ref>

===CF Intercity===
On 3 February 2025, Modeste joined Spanish club [[CF Intercity]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cfintercity.com/el-ex-de-borussia-y-colonia-anthony-modeste-firma-por-el-cf-intercity/|title=El ex de Borussia y Colonia, Anthony Modeste, firma por el CF Intercity|language=es|date=3 February 2025|accessdate=6 February 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
His father [[Guy Modeste]] was also a footballer.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://la1ere.francetvinfo.fr/martinique/footballeur-pierrotain-guy-modeste-est-decede-663303.html|title=Le Footballeur Pierrotain Guy Modeste est décédé|date=19 December 2018|access-date=21 December 2018|author=Manuel Larade|language=fr|publisher=France TV Info}}</ref> Anthony is of Martiniquais descent.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.martinique.franceantilles.fr/actualite/sports/anthony-modeste-a-signe-a-dortmund-491739.php|title=Anthony Modeste a signé à Dortmund|date=20 September 2023|website=martinique.franceantilles.fr}}</ref>

'''Franck Yannick Kessié''' (born 19 December 1996) is an Ivorian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for [[Serie A]] club [[Atalanta BC|Atalanta]] and [[captain (association football)|captain]]s the [[Ivory Coast national football team|Ivory Coast national team]]. A versatile player, Kessié plays predominantly as a [[box-to-box midfielder|box-to-box central midfielder]], but has also been deployed as a [[defensive midfielder]] and on rare occasions, a [[centre-back]].

After advancing through [[Atalanta BC|Atalanta]], Kessié joined [[AC Milan]] in 2017 on loan, securing a permanent move two years later and playing a pivotal role in their [[Serie A]] success in the 2021–22 season. In 2022, he joined [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], clinching titles in [[La Liga]] and [[Supercopa de España]], before his transfer to [[Al-Ahli Saudi FC|Al-Ahli]] in 2023.

An Ivorian international since 2014, Kessié was part of the squad that won the [[2023 Africa Cup of Nations]] on home soil.

== Club career ==
Born in [[Ouragahio]], Kessié began his career in [[Stella Club d'Adjamé]], joining their youth setup in 2010.<ref name="outsideoftheboot.com">{{cite web|url=http://outsideoftheboot.com/2017/04/30/scout-report-franck-kessie/|title=Charles Onwuakpa writes a detailed scout report about Franck Kessié|publisher=outsideoftheboot.com|date=15 April 2017|access-date=26 May 2019|archive-date=18 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220518134152/http://outsideoftheboot.com/2017/04/30/scout-report-franck-kessie/|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2014, he was promoted to the first team.<ref name="outsideoftheboot.com" />

=== Atalanta ===
On 29 January 2015, Kessié signed a three-year contract with [[Serie A]] club [[Atalanta B.C.|Atalanta]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.afrik-foot.com/stella-club-kessie-signe-a-l-atalanta-bergame|title=Stella Club: Kessié signe à l'Atalanta Bergame|trans-title=Stella Club: Kessié signs with Atalanta Bergamo|publisher=Afrik-Foot|language=fr|date=30 January 2015|access-date=25 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170326135543/http://www.afrik-foot.com/stella-club-kessie-signe-a-l-atalanta-bergame|archive-date=26 March 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was assigned to the club's [[Atalanta B.C. Primavera|Primavera]] squad upon his arrival and contributed with seven appearances for the side. His first match in Europe occurred on 1 March, as he started in a 2–0 away win against [[A.C. Milan Primavera|AC Milan Primavera]].{{citation needed|date=August 2017}}

On 18 April 2015, Kessié was called up to the first team for a match against [[A.S. Roma|Roma]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.calcionews24.com/atalanta-22-convocati-per-roma-prima-per-kessie-437342|title=Atalanta, 22 convocati per Roma: prima per Kessie|trans-title=Atalanta, 22 called up for Roma: first for Kessie|publisher=Calcio News 24|language=it|date=18 April 2015|access-date=25 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170517141758/http://www.calcionews24.com/atalanta-22-convocati-per-roma-prima-per-kessie-437342|archive-date=17 May 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> but remained an unused [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] in the 1–1 draw the following day.

==== Cesena (loan) ====
On 26 August 2015, Kessié joined [[A.C. Cesena|Cesena]] in the [[Serie B]] on a one-year loan deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cesenacalcio.it/it/news/2015/08/26/kessie-%C3%A8-un-giocatore-del-cesena-3706.html|title=Kessie è un giocatore del Cesena|trans-title=Kessie is a Cesena player|publisher=A.C. Cesena|language=it|date=26 August 2015|access-date=26 May 2016|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304071132/http://www.cesenacalcio.it/it/news/2015/08/26/kessie-%C3%A8-un-giocatore-del-cesena-3706.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his professional debut on 26 September, coming on as a substitute for [[Antonino Ragusa]] in a 0–0 away draw against [[A.C. Perugia Calcio|Perugia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.umbriaon.it/perugia-cesena-0-0-ecco-la-diretta/|title=Perugia–Cesena 0–0, tensioni dopo la gara|trans-title=Perugia–Cesena 0–0, tension after the match|publisher=Umbria On|language=it|date=26 September 2015|access-date=25 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170517095140/http://www.umbriaon.it/perugia-cesena-0-0-ecco-la-diretta/|archive-date=17 May 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Kessié scored his first professional goal on 31 October 2015, netting the last in a 2–0 home win against [[S.S. Virtus Lanciano 1924|Virtus Lanciano]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ilcentro.gelocal.it/sport/2015/10/31/news/torna-la-difesa-titolare-per-fermare-il-cesena-1.12362905|title=Il Lanciano gioca bene ma perde a Cesena per 2 a 0|trans-title=Lanciano play well but lose to Cesena by 2–0|publisher=Il Centro|language=it|date=31 October 2015|access-date=25 March 2017|archive-date=26 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170326051307/http://ilcentro.gelocal.it/sport/2015/10/31/news/torna-la-difesa-titolare-per-fermare-il-cesena-1.12362905|url-status=dead}}</ref> He became an undisputed starter afterwards, appearing in 37 matches and scoring four goals as his side missed out promotion in [[2015–16 Serie B#Promotion play-offs|the play-offs]].

==== Back to Atalanta ====
After returning from loan, Kessié was promoted to the first team by manager [[Gian Piero Gasperini]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/calcio/nuove-forze-calcio/18-07-2016/atalanta-gasperini-scopre-kessie-nuovo-yaya-toure-ivoriano-prestito-cesena-centrocampista-160395068337.shtml|title=Atalanta, Gasperini scopre il jolly Kessie, ivoriano che sogna Yaya Touré|trans-title=Atalanta, Gasperini discovers the wildcard Kessie, Ivorian who resembles Yaya Touré|publisher=[[La Gazzetta dello Sport]]|language=it|date=18 July 2016|access-date=25 March 2017|archive-date=17 May 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170517101245/http://www.gazzetta.it/calcio/nuove-forze-calcio/18-07-2016/atalanta-gasperini-scopre-kessie-nuovo-yaya-toure-ivoriano-prestito-cesena-centrocampista-160395068337.shtml|url-status=live}}</ref> After appearing with the main squad during the pre-season, he made his debut for ''La Dea'' on 13 August 2016, starting and scoring the last in a 3–0 [[Coppa Italia]] home win against [[U.S. Cremonese|Cremonese]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bergamopost.it/rubriche/l-atalanta-siamo-noi/alla-dea-basta-un-tempo-cremonese-battuta-3-0/|title=Alla Dea basta un tempo: 3–0|trans-title=To ''Dea'' one half is enough: 3–0|publisher=Ecco di Bergamo|language=it|date=14 August 2016|access-date=25 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170326052317/http://www.bergamopost.it/rubriche/l-atalanta-siamo-noi/alla-dea-basta-un-tempo-cremonese-battuta-3-0/|archive-date=26 March 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> Six days later, he renewed his contract until 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.atalanta.it/site/paginalive/comunicati-dal-club/Stagione-2016-2017/2016-08/19-08-Kessie-sino-al-2021.html|title=Franck Kessie rinnova fino al 30 giugno 2021|trans-title=Franck Kessie renews until 30 June 2021|publisher=Atalanta B.C.|language=it|date=19 August 2016|access-date=25 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170326135828/https://www.atalanta.it/site/paginalive/comunicati-dal-club/Stagione-2016-2017/2016-08/19-08-Kessie-sino-al-2021.html|archive-date=26 March 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Kessié made his debut in the main category of Italian football on 21 August 2016, as he started and scored a brace in a 4–3 home loss against [[S.S. Lazio|Lazio]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/SerieA/match/87826|title=Atalanta 3–4 Lazio|publisher=Football Italia|date=21 August 2016|access-date=25 March 2017|archive-date=1 October 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191001062607/https://www.football-italia.net/SerieA/match/87826|url-status=live}}</ref> He scored another goal seven days later, in a 2–1 away defeat to [[U.C. Sampdoria|Sampdoria]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/SerieA/match/87842|title=Sampdoria 2–1 Atalanta|publisher=Football Italia|date=28 August 2016|access-date=25 March 2017|archive-date=15 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190915075245/https://www.football-italia.net/SerieA/match/87842|url-status=live}}</ref>

Kessié subsequently became a mainstay in Gasperini's starting eleven, scoring the winners against [[Torino F.C.|Torino]] (2–1 home win)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/SerieA/match/87846|title=Atalanta 2–1 Torino|publisher=Football Italia|date=11 September 2016|access-date=25 March 2017|archive-date=30 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190830154553/https://www.football-italia.net/SerieA/match/87846|url-status=live}}</ref> and Roma (2–1 home win),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/SerieA/match/87946|title=Atalanta 2–1 Roma|publisher=Football Italia|date=20 November 2016|access-date=25 March 2017|archive-date=30 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190830154551/https://www.football-italia.net/SerieA/match/87946|url-status=live}}</ref> both through [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalties]]. He also scored the equalizer against [[Empoli F.C.|Empoli]] on 20 December 2016, with [[Marco D'Alessandro]] scoring a [[Last-minute goal|last-minute winner]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/SerieA/match/87996|title=Atalanta 2–1 Empoli|publisher=Football Italia|date=20 December 2016|access-date=25 March 2017|archive-date=30 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190830154531/https://www.football-italia.net/SerieA/match/87996|url-status=live}}</ref>

=== AC Milan ===
On 2 June 2017, Kessié joined fellow Serie A side [[A.C. Milan|AC Milan]] on a two-year loan deal with the obligation to buy.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Official: Kessie is now red and black |url=https://www.acmilan.com/en/news/official-statement/2017-06-02/official-kessie-is-now-red-and-black |publisher=A.C. Milan Official Site |date=2 June 2017 |access-date=2 June 2017 |archive-date=17 June 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170617121550/https://www.acmilan.com/en/news/official-statement/2017-06-02/official-kessie-is-now-red-and-black |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40136347|title=Ivory Coast's Franck Kessie joins AC Milan from Atalanta|date=2 June 2017|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=27 August 2019|archive-date=30 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190830154522/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40136347|url-status=live}}</ref> Originally, he chose 19 as his [[Squad number (association football)|shirt number]] but soon was persuaded by the club's management to leave it for [[Leonardo Bonucci]], who transferred to Milan a few weeks later; as a result, Kessié changed it to 79.

He made his debut for Milan and helped the club to win the first leg of Europa League qualification match against [[CS Universitatea Craiova|CS U Craiova]] on 27 July.<ref>{{cite news|title=Newcomers Ricardo Rodriguez, Franck Kessie lift Milan past FC U Craiova|url=http://www.espnfc.com/club/ac-milan/103/blog/post/3166878/newcomers-ricardo-rodriguez-franck-kessie-lift-milan-past-universitatea-craiova|access-date=28 July 2017|work=ESPN|date=27 July 2017|archive-date=30 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190830130450/http://www.espnfc.com/club/ac-milan/103/blog/post/3166878/newcomers-ricardo-rodriguez-franck-kessie-lift-milan-past-universitatea-craiova|url-status=live}}</ref> On 20 August 2017, in Milan's opening Serie A match of the season, he scored a penalty in a 3–0 victory over [[F.C. Crotone|Crotone]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Kessie, Cutrone, Suso in form as Milan begins Serie A campaign with win |url=http://www.espnfc.com/club/ac-milan/103/blog/post/3184887/ac-milan-make-easy-work-of-serie-a-opener-winning-at-crotone |publisher=ESPN |date=20 August 2017 |access-date=29 August 2017}}</ref> In a match against [[Cagliari Calcio|Cagliari]] on 21 January 2018, Kessié scored two goals, one being from the penalty spot, to give Milan the win.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cagliari 1-2 Milan: Kessie double inspires comeback win |url=https://sempremilan.com/cagliari-1-2-milan-kessie-double-inspires-comeback-win |website=sempremilan |date=21 January 2018 |access-date=18 February 2022 |archive-date=18 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220218194615/https://sempremilan.com/cagliari-1-2-milan-kessie-double-inspires-comeback-win |url-status=live }}</ref> Milan reached the Coppa Italia final, but lost 4–0 to Juventus, Kessié playing the full game. Following Bonucci's departure he was offered his original shirt number back yet refused, citing that he did not want to force Milan fans to spend any extra money on his personalized shirts due to yet another number change.<ref>{{cite web |date=14 February 2019 |title=AC Milan, Kessie: 'Gasperini is angrier than Gattuso!' |url=https://www.calciomercato.com/en/news/ac-milan-kessie-gasperini-is-angrier-than-gattuso-80241 |publisher=www.calciomercato.com |access-date=15 February 2019 |archive-date=15 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190215115352/https://www.calciomercato.com/en/news/ac-milan-kessie-gasperini-is-angrier-than-gattuso-80241 |url-status=live }}</ref> As Juventus won the league-cup double, Milan qualified for the [[2018 Supercoppa Italiana]] final against Juventus. They lost 1–0 and Kessié was sent off in the 74th minute.<ref>{{cite news |title=Juventus beat Milan to Supercoppa Italiana after Cristiano Ronaldo winner |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/jan/16/juventus-milan-cristiano-ronaldo-supercoppa-italiana |access-date=18 February 2022 |agency=The Guardian |date=16 January 2019 |archive-date=3 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221103135647/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/jan/16/juventus-milan-cristiano-ronaldo-supercoppa-italiana |url-status=live }}</ref>

Milan finished the [[2020–21 Serie A]] season in second place, with Kessié scoring 13 times in 37 appearances, and qualified for the [[2021–22 UEFA Champions League]] after an eight-year absence.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.football-italia.net/171087/atalanta-0-2-milan-kessie-seals-second-place |title=Atalanta 0-2 Milan: Kessie seals second place |website=football-italia.net |date=23 May 2021 }}</ref>
Kessie became the first player to score at least ten penalties for AC Milan in a Serie A season since [[Zlatan Ibrahimovic]] in 2011–12; he played 50 matches this season in all competitions, a record between Serie A players with [[Matteo Politano|Politano]],<ref>{{cite web |title=ATALANTA V AC MILAN: THE NUMBERS FROM THE GAME |url=https://www.acmilan.com/en/news/articles/stats/2021-05-23/atalanta-v-ac-milan-the-numbers-from-the-game |website=acmilan |access-date=18 February 2022 |archive-date=10 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220210233044/https://www.acmilan.com/en/news/articles/stats/2021-05-23/atalanta-v-ac-milan-the-numbers-from-the-game |url-status=live }}</ref> and was described as player of the season for Milan by some critics.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Pickering |first1=Joe |title=Franck Kessié: Milan's player of the year? |url=https://milanreports.com/2021/05/31/kessie-player-of-the-year/ |website=MILAN REPORTS |date=31 May 2021 |access-date=18 February 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Burns |first1=Euan |title=A SEASON IN REVIEW: AC MILAN 2020/21 |date=8 June 2021 |url=https://forzaitalianfootball.com/2021/06/a-season-in-review-ac-milan-2020-21/ |access-date=18 February 2022}}</ref>

==== 2021–22: Scudetto winner and departure ====
On 12 September 2021, Kessié won a penalty kick against Lazio but failed to convert it; Milan still managed to win the match 2–0.<ref>{{cite web |title=AC MILAN MAKE IT THREE WINS FROM THREE |url=https://www.acmilan.com/en/news/articles/serie-a/2021-09-12/ac-milan-make-it-three-wins-from-three |website=acmilan |access-date=19 February 2022}}</ref> On 28 September, in a UEFA Champions League match against [[Atlético Madrid]], as Milan was leading by 1–0, Kessié was sent off in the 29th minute, his side eventually lost 1–2.<ref>{{cite news |title=AC Milan 1–2 Atletico Madrid |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/58705891 |access-date=18 February 2022 |archive-date=18 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220218191052/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/58705891 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 31 October against Roma, he converted a penalty kick to score the second and seal a 2–1 victory for Milan.<ref>{{cite web |title=THREE BIG POINTS IN THE CAPITAL |url=https://www.acmilan.com/en/news/articles/serie-a/2021-10-31/three-big-points-in-the-capital |website=acmilan |access-date=18 February 2022 |archive-date=18 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220218194904/https://www.acmilan.com/en/news/articles/serie-a/2021-10-31/three-big-points-in-the-capital |url-status=live }}</ref> On 7 November, while playing [[Derby della Madonnina|against Inter]] he fouled [[Hakan Çalhanoğlu]] in the penalty box, causing a penalty kick which the latter scored in a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{cite news |title=Soccer-Milan and Inter share spoils in derby thriller |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-italy-mil-int-report-idUKKBN2HS0I7 |access-date=18 February 2022 |work=Reuters |date=8 November 2021 |archive-date=18 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220218191754/https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-italy-mil-int-report-idUKKBN2HS0I7 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 4 December, Kessié scored the first goal against Salernitana in an eventual 2–0 win.<ref>{{cite web |title=AC MILAN V SALERNITANA: THE STATS FROM THE GAME |url=https://www.acmilan.com/en/news/articles/stats/2021-12-04/ac-milan-v-salernitana-the-stats-from-the-game |website=acmilan |access-date=19 February 2022 |archive-date=19 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220219064200/https://www.acmilan.com/en/news/articles/stats/2021-12-04/ac-milan-v-salernitana-the-stats-from-the-game |url-status=live }}</ref> On 22 December, Kessié scored a brace against [[Empoli F.C.|Empoli]], reaching 14 Serie A goals during the 2021 calendar year; the last AC Milan midfielder to score so much in a single calendar year was [[Kaká]] in 2008.<ref>{{cite web |title=EMPOLI V AC MILAN: THE NUMBERS FROM THE GAME |url=https://www.acmilan.com/en/news/articles/stats/2021-12-22/empoli-v-ac-milan-the-numbers-from-the-game |website=acmilan |access-date=18 February 2022 |archive-date=27 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221127020432/https://www.acmilan.com/en/news/articles/stats/2021-12-22/empoli-v-ac-milan-the-numbers-from-the-game |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 22 May 2022, Kessié scored the third goal in a 3–0 rout against Sassuolo, sealing the [[Scudetto]] title for the club; after the goal, Kessié went to Milan fans at the [[Mapei Stadium – Città del Tricolore|Mapei Stadium]] and did his trademark salute, it was Kessié's last match and goal with Milan, as he announced his departure a few days later and thanked the fans.<ref>{{cite web |title=Barcelona-Bound Kessié: "No Better Way to Leave Milan" |url=https://cultofcalcio.com/barcelona-bound-kessie-no-better-way-to-say-goodbye-to-milan/?amp=1 |website=cult of calcio|access-date=22 May 2022}}</ref>

=== Barcelona ===
On 4 July 2022, [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] announced that they had reached an agreement with Kessié after his contract expired with [[AC Milan]] and on 6 July, he signed a four-year deal until 30 June 2026, and his buy out was set at €500m.<ref>{{Cite web |title=FC Barcelona sign Franck Kessie |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2666705/fc-barcelona-sign-franck-kessie |access-date=2022-07-04 |website=www.fcbarcelona.com |language=en |archive-date=4 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220704145341/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/2666705/fc-barcelona-sign-franck-kessie |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 13 August 2022, he made his debut for the club, as a substitute to [[Pedri]], in a 0–0 draw against [[Rayo Vallecano]] in the league.<ref>{{Cite web |date=13 August 2022 |title=Barcelona frustrated by Rayo Vallecano as Lewandowski & Raphinha's La Liga debuts spoiled |url=https://www.goal.com/en-in/news/barcelona-frustrated-rayo-vallecano-opening-night/bltcd5e7b01eea1ab09 |access-date=16 August 2022 |language=en |archive-date=16 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220816104641/https://www.goal.com/en-in/news/barcelona-frustrated-rayo-vallecano-opening-night/bltcd5e7b01eea1ab09 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 19 March 2023, Kessié scored the winning goal against [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in ''[[El Clasico]]'', his first for the club, hitting home [[Alejandro Balde]]'s cutback in the 92nd minute to make it 2–1 for the ''Blaugrana''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=FC Barcelona – Real Madrid La Liga Matchday 26 |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/matches/78066/fc-barcelona-r-madrid-la-liga-2022-2023 |access-date=2023-03-21 |website=www.fcbarcelona.com |language=en}}</ref> Kessié's strike was the 3,000th goal scored by Barcelona at the [[Camp Nou]] in [[La Liga]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kessie scores goal number 3,000 at Spotify Camp Nou in La Liga |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/3116980/kessie-scores-goal-number-3000-at-spotify-camp-nou-in-la-liga |access-date=2023-03-21 |website=www.fcbarcelona.com |language=en |archive-date=20 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230320185418/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/3116980/kessie-scores-goal-number-3000-at-spotify-camp-nou-in-la-liga |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Al-Ahli ===
On 9 August 2023, Kessié joined [[Saudi Pro League]] club [[Al Ahli Saudi FC|Al-Ahli]] in a €12.5m deal.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kessie transfer to Al-Ahli SC agreed |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/3621056/kessie-transfer-to-al-ahli-sc-agreed |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]] |access-date=9 August 2023 |date=9 August 2023 |archive-date=9 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230809205304/https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/football/first-team/news/3621056/kessie-transfer-to-al-ahli-sc-agreed |url-status=live }}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club in a 1–0 win over [[Al-Okhdood Club|Al-Okhdood]] on 24 August. Kessié also scored another winning goal in a 1–0 win over [[Al-Khaleej FC|Al-Khaleej]] on 29 December.

During the [[2024–25 AFC Champions League Elite]] on 16 September 2024, Kessié scored the only goal in the match against Iranian club [[Persepolis F.C.|Persepolis]] to secured the 3 points for Al-Ahli. In the final match held in Jeddah on 3 May 2025, he won the competition, after previously scoring a goal in the 42nd minute when defeating the Japanese representative, [[Kawasaki Frontale]].<ref name=":02">{{Cite web |last=Lynch |first=Joey |date=3 May 2025 |title=Never taking their eyes off the prize, Al Ahli are champions of Asia at long last |url=https://global.espn.com/football/story/_/id/44984369/never-taking-eyes-prize-al-ahli-champions-asia-long-last |access-date=4 May 2025 |website=ESPN}}</ref> In the following season, he was named the Most Valuable Player in the [[2025–26 AFC Champions League Elite]] as his club secured a 1–0 extra-time victory over [[FC Machida Zelvia|Machida Zelvia]] in the [[2026 AFC Champions League Elite final|final]].<ref name="afc26">{{cite web |url=https://www.the-afc.com/en/club/afc_champions_league_elite.html/news/al-ahli%E2%80%99s-kessie-named-most-valuable-player |title=Al Ahli's Kessie named Most Valuable Player |publisher=The AFC |date=25 April 2026 }}</ref> He departed the club at the conclusion of the 2025–26 season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://dailysports.net/news/franck-kessie-leaves-al-ahli-sc/ |title=Franck Kessié leaves Al Ahli SC |publisher=Dailysports |date=2 July 2026 }}</ref>

=== Return to Atalanta ===
On 29 August 2026, Kessié rejoined Serie A club Atalanta, signing a multi-year contract as a free agent.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://en.atalanta.it/news/welcome-back-franck |title=Welcome back, Franck! |publisher=Atalanta BC |date=29 August 2026 }}</ref>

== International career ==

=== Youth ===
Kessié represented [[Ivory Coast national football team|Ivory Coast]] at [[Ivory Coast national under-17 football team|under-17]] and [[Ivory Coast national under-20 football team|under-20 levels]], appearing in the [[2013 FIFA U-17 World Cup]] and [[2015 Toulon Tournament]]. During the former tournament, the [[Royal Moroccan Football Federation]] submitted a complaint to [[FIFA]] claiming that Kessié was aged 22 and not 16;<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espoirsdufootball.com/cm-u17-scandale-franck-kessie-16-ans-aurait-22-ans-31003|title=CM U17 – Scandale, Franck Kessié (16 ans) aurait 22 ans|trans-title=U17 WC – Scandal, Franck Kessié (16 years) 22 years old|publisher=Espoirs du Football|language=fr|date=30 October 2013|access-date=25 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170603010318/http://www.espoirsdufootball.com/cm-u17-scandale-franck-kessie-16-ans-aurait-22-ans-31003|archive-date=3 June 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> FIFA later denied that claim.

=== Senior ===
At the age of 17, Kessié played his first international game with the senior national team on 6 September 2014, starting in a 2–1 home win against [[Sierra Leone national football team|Sierra Leone]] for the [[2015 Africa Cup of Nations qualification]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-gh/news/4351/africa/2014/09/06/5088565/cote-divoire-2-1-sierra-leone-the-elephants-toil-to-overturn|title=Cote D'Ivoire 2–1 Sierra Leone: The Elephants toil to overturn lead|publisher=Goal.com|date=6 September 2014|access-date=8 September 2014|archive-date=3 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220503204552/https://www.goal.com/en-gh/news/4351/africa/2014/09/06/5088565/cote-divoire-2-1-sierra-leone-the-elephants-toil-to-overturn|url-status=live}}</ref> On 4 January 2017, he was included in [[Michel Dussuyer]]'s 23-man squad ahead of the [[2017 Africa Cup of Nations]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/38451141|title=Afcon 2017: Wilfried Zaha in Ivory Coast's final squad|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=4 January 2017|access-date=25 March 2017|archive-date=2 August 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190802000846/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/38451141|url-status=live}}</ref> starting in all matches as his side was knocked out in the group stage.

At the [[2019 Africa Cup of Nations]], he finished as the joint-top assist provider of the tournament, alongside [[Ismaël Bennacer]], with three assists. His team were eliminated in the quarter-finals by eventual champions [[Algeria national football team|Algeria]] after losing 4–3 on penalties following a 1–1 draw on 11 July; Kessié converted his nation's first penalty in the shoot-out.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://futaa.com/article/188128/top-assists-charts-at-the-2019-african-cup-of-nations |title=Top Assists charts at the 2019 African Cup of Nations |publisher=futaa.com |last1=Otieno |first1=Imran |date=20 July 2019 |access-date=4 August 2019 |archive-date=3 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220503204545/https://futaa.com/article/188128/top-assists-charts-at-the-2019-african-cup-of-nations |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cafonline.com/total-africa-cup-of-nations/matches/47/ |title=Côte d'Ivoire 1-1 Algeria |publisher=www.cafonline.com |date=11 July 2019 |access-date=4 August 2019 |archive-date=30 March 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200330202738/https://www.cafonline.com/total-africa-cup-of-nations/matches/47/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/jul/19/senegal-algeria-africa-cup-of-nations-final-match-report|title=Algeria claim second Afcon title after Bounedjah's lucky strike sinks Senegal|website=theguardian.com|publisher=Guardian News & Media Limited|date=19 July 2019|access-date=19 July 2019|archive-date=20 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190720130642/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/jul/19/senegal-algeria-africa-cup-of-nations-final-match-report|url-status=live}}</ref>

Kessié started in all four of the Ivory Coast's matches at the [[2021 Africa Cup of Nations]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/team/squad/_/id/4789/league/CAF.NATIONS/season/2021|title=Ivory Coast Squad|access-date=16 January 2024|website=ESPN|archive-date=16 January 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240116135914/https://www.espn.com/soccer/team/squad/_/id/4789/league/CAF.NATIONS/season/2021|url-status=live}}</ref> scoring once in a 3–1 win over Algeria in [[2021 Africa Cup of Nations Group E|Group E]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59975483|title=Afcon 2021: Holders Algeria crash out after Ivory Coast defeat|date=20 January 2022|access-date=16 January 2024|website=ESPN|archive-date=28 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220128134139/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/59975483|url-status=live}}</ref> He was substituted with an injury 30 minutes into the round of 16 loss to [[Egypt national football team|Egypt]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://supersport.com/football/wta/news/23b19666-cddd-4098-b1f8-193fa240f797/egypt-defeat-elephants-on-penalties-to-book-quarters-berth|title=Egypt defeat Elephants on penalties to book quarters berth|date=27 January 2022|access-date=16 January 2024|website=SuperSport|archive-date=12 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241212184324/https://supersport.com/football/wta/news/23b19666-cddd-4098-b1f8-193fa240f797/egypt-defeat-elephants-on-penalties-to-book-quarters-berth|url-status=live}}</ref>
[[File:Franck Yannick Kessié.jpg|thumb|317x317px|Kessié with [[Ivory Coast national football team|Ivory Coast]] in 2024]]
In December 2023, Kessié was named in the Ivory Coast's squad for the [[2023 Africa Cup of Nations]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/federationivoiriennedefootball/posts/pfbid02GVkTYXjhv2yBQizHRNxngTGoMrFLXgcUg3kQeXgEk3gZ158w6cxqRFjDBXCCU3ihl|title=LA LISTE|publisher=[[Ivorian Football Federation]]|date=28 December 2023|access-date=16 January 2024|language=pt|via=[[Facebook]]|archive-date=28 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231228204941/https://www.facebook.com/federationivoiriennedefootball/posts/pfbid02GVkTYXjhv2yBQizHRNxngTGoMrFLXgcUg3kQeXgEk3gZ158w6cxqRFjDBXCCU3ihl|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cafonline.com/media/ow2obxrw/c%C3%B4te-divoire.pdf|title=CÔTE D'IVOIRE|publisher=Confederation of African Football|date=5 January 2024|access-date=16 January 2024|archive-date=13 February 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240213160033/https://www.cafonline.com/media/ow2obxrw/c%C3%B4te-divoire.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref> He captained the team in the tournament's opening match, a 2–0 win over [[Guinea-Bissau national football team|Guinea-Bissau]] on 14 January 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2024/1/14/afcon-ivory-coast-vs-guinea-bissau-africa-cup-of-nations-2023|title=Ivory Coast open AFCON 2023 with 2-0 win over Guinea-Bissau|date=14 January 2024|access-date=16 January 2024|website=Al Jazeera}}</ref> During the round of 16 match against defending champions [[Senegal national football team|Senegal]], he came off the bench in the second half, in which he managed to score the equalizer from a penalty in the 86th minute in a 1–1 tie. He eventually netted the last penalty in the shoot-outs in a 5–4 win, which qualified his country to the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2024/jan/29/kessie-brings-ivory-coast-back-to-life-as-afcon-hosts-bury-senegal |title=Kessié brings Ivory Coast back to life as Afcon hosts bury Senegal |work=The Guardian |date=30 January 2024 }}</ref> He later scored a goal in the [[2023 Africa Cup of Nations final|final]] match against [[Nigeria national football team|Nigeria]] which ended in a 2–1 victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68196261 |title=Nigeria 1–2 Ivory Coast |publisher=BBC Sport |date=11 February 2024 |access-date=11 February 2024 |archive-date=12 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240212182429/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68196261 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Kessié later became the captain of his national team in 2024, succeeding [[Max-Alain Gradel]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.africatopsports.com/2024/03/23/cote-divoire-max-alain-gradel-dit-elephants/ |title=Côte d'Ivoire : Max-Alain Gradel dit au revoir aux Eléphants |publisher=Africa Top Sports |language=fr |date=23 March 2024 }}</ref> On 6 January 2026, he made his 100th international appearance in a 3–0 win over [[Burkina Faso national football team|Burkina Faso]] during the [[2025 Africa Cup of Nations]] round of 16.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/football/match/_/gameId/732176/burkina-faso-ivory-coast |title=Ivory Coast 3–0 Burkina Faso |publisher=ESPN |date=6 January 2026 }}</ref>

On 15 May 2026, Kessié was integrated by Ivory Coast coach [[Emerse Faé]] in his list of 26 players in order to participate in the [[2026 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|access-date=2 June 2026 |date=15 May 2026 |language=fr |title=La liste de la Côte d'Ivoire pour la Coupe du Monde 2026 |url=https://www.fifa.com/fr/articles/liste-cote-d-ivoire-coupe-du-monde-2026 |website=[[FIFA]]}}</ref> He scored his first World Cup goal, opening the scoring in a 2–1 defeat against [[Germany national football team|Germany]] in the second group-stage match.<ref>{{cite web |last=Rajan |first=Adwaidh |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cn8q9pp0p94t |title=Germany 2–1 Ivory Coast |publisher=BBC Sport |date=20 June 2026 }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
When Kessié was 11 years old, his father, who used to be a professional footballer in his youth before enlisting in the Ivorian army, died due to an illness. Therefore, one of his goal celebrations is a [[military salute]] performed in order to pay tribute to his late father.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/it/notizie/milan-kessie-e-lesultanza-da-militare-una-dedica-al-padre/1brwxoeypry9u12vjtw5yo804w|title=MILAN, KESSIÉ E L'ESULTANZA DA MILITARE: UNA DEDICA AL PADRE|trans-title=MILAN, KESSIÉ AND THE MILITARY GESTURE: A DEDICATION TO FATHER|publisher=Goal|date=21 September 2017|access-date=22 September 2017|archive-date=22 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170922194540/http://www.goal.com/it/notizie/milan-kessie-e-lesultanza-da-militare-una-dedica-al-padre/1brwxoeypry9u12vjtw5yo804w|url-status=live}}</ref> Growing up, his idol was [[Yaya Touré]].<ref>{{Citation |title=WHO IS YOUR IDOL? {{!}} KESSIE FACES THE #90SECONDSCHALLENGE |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eDug8l_9_DY&t=61s |language=en |access-date=2022-09-07}}</ref>
