'''Adem Ljajić''' ({{lang-sr-Cyrl|Адем Љајић}}, {{IPA|sh|ǎːdem ʎǎːjitɕ|pron}}; born 29 September 1991) is a Serbian professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as an [[attacking midfielder]] for [[Serbian SuperLiga]] club [[FK Novi Pazar|Novi Pazar]].

Ljajić began his career with FK Jošanica, and later [[FK Partizan|Partizan]], with whom he made his debut in the [[Serbian SuperLiga]] and [[UEFA Champions League]]. In January 2010, he was set to join England's [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]],<ref name="ademq&a1">{{cite web |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Exclusive-Interviews/2009/Mar/Exclusive-Adem-Ljajic-QA.aspx |title=Exclusive: Adem Ljajic Q&A |access-date=17 March 2011 |work=Manchester United FC |date=4 March 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160810075546/http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Exclusive-Interviews/2009/Mar/Exclusive-Adem-Ljajic-QA.aspx |archive-date=10 August 2016 }}</ref> but the club withdrew its option to sign him in December 2009.<ref>{{cite news |title=Manchester United end interest in Serbian Adem Ljajic |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/m/man_utd/8392789.stm |work=BBC Sport |date=2 December 2009 |access-date=2 December 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091205175104/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/m/man_utd/8392789.stm |archive-date=5 December 2009 |url-status=live }}</ref> Instead, he joined [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] for a reported fee of around €8 million in January 2010.<ref name="fiorentina">{{cite news|title=Partizan prodigy Ljajić joins Viola |url=http://www.uefa.com/competitions/ucl/news/kind=1/newsid=942745.html |work=[[UEFA]] |date=13 January 2010 |access-date=13 January 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100116042735/http://www.uefa.com/competitions/ucl/news/kind%3D1/newsid%3D942745.html |archive-date=16 January 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In August 2013, after three years in Florence, Ljajić joined [[AS Roma|Roma]] for an €11 million fee, signing a four-year contract.<ref name="roma">{{cite press release |title=Adem Ljajić |language=it |date=28 August 2013 |publisher=Associazione Sportiva Roma |url=http://www.asroma.it/pdf/corporate/operazioni_di_mercato/2013_-_08_28_Ljajic.pdf |access-date=28 August 2013 }}</ref> In July 2016, he was sold to Torino. Ljajić was sent on loan to [[Beşiktaş J.K.|Beşiktaş]] in 2018, before signing with the Turkish side in 2019. He then joined [[Fatih Karagümrük S.K.|Fatih Karagümrük]] in 2022.<ref name="beinsports">{{cite web|url=https://beinsports.com.tr/haber/adem-ljajicin-yeni-adresi-belli-oldu|access-date=12 January 2023|title=Adem Ljajic'in yeni adresi belli oldu}}</ref> In September 2023, Ljajić signed with hometown club [[FK Novi Pazar|Novi Pazar]]. In August 2025, he left Novi Pazar and joined Bosnian side Sarajevo.<ref name="klix">{{cite web|url=https://www.klix.ba/sport/nogomet/adem-ljajic-zvanicno-potpisao-ugovor-sa-fk-sarajevo-jako-sam-sretan-sto-sam-dio-ovog-kluba/250807158|title=Adem Ljajić zvanično potpisao ugovor sa FK Sarajevo: "Jako sam sretan što sam dio ovog kluba"|date=7 August 2025|access-date=7 August 2025|language=bs|author=H.H.|publisher=Klix.ba}}</ref>

Ljajić made his senior international debut for Serbia in 2010. From 2012 to 2014, he was frozen out of the team by manager [[Siniša Mihajlović]] for objecting to singing the [[Bože pravde|Serbian national anthem]]. Ljajić was part of the Serbian squad at the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]]. He earned a total of 47 caps, scoring 9 goals,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/joeg-recintlp.html|title=Yugoslavia (Serbia (and Montenegro)) - Record International Players|access-date=10 November 2024|website=[[RSSSF]]}}</ref> and his final international was an October 2020 [[2020–21 UEFA Nations League B|Nations League]] match against [[Hungary national football team|Hungary]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://eu-football.info/_player.php?id=27191|title=Adem Ljajić, international football player|access-date=10 November 2024|website=EU-football.info}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Partizan===
Born in [[Novi Pazar]] in the [[Socialist Republic of Serbia|Serbian]] region of the [[Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia]], Ljajić joined [[FK Partizan|Partizan]] at age 14 in 2005, signing from Serbian lower-tier club FK Jošanica.<ref>{{cite news |title=Od prodaje Ljajića, Jošanica dobila 31.945 eura |url=http://www.sandzak-sport.com/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=1022:od-prodaje-ljajia-joanica-dobila-31-945-eura&catid=34:football&Itemid=88 |work=Sandzak Live |publisher=SandžakLive.rs |date=24 June 2010 |access-date=27 June 2010 |language=sr |trans-title=From the sale of Ljajić, Jošanica got 31,945 euros |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716003355/http://www.sandzak-sport.com/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=1022:od-prodaje-ljajia-joanica-dobila-31-945-eura&catid=34:football&Itemid=88 |archive-date=16 July 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Ljajić was the first player to wear the number 22 for Partizan after [[Saša Ilić (footballer, born 1977)|Saša Ilić]] transferred to [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]] in 2005.<ref name="Trojica prekobrojnih, Ljajiću 22!">{{cite web |url=http://www.b92.net/sport/vesti.php?yyyy=2008&mm=07&dd=27&nav_id=310415 |publisher=[[B92]] |title=Trojica prekobrojnih, Ljajiću 22! |access-date=22 December 2011 |date=27 July 2008 |language=sr}}</ref> Ljajić made an appearance for Partizan in the first leg of the second qualifying round of the [[2008–09 UEFA Champions League]] on 29 July 2008 as a second-half substitute.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20081019042457/http://www.uefa.com/competitions/ucl/fixturesresults/round=15274/match=303498/report=ev.html|title=UEFA Champions League – Fixtures & Results}}</ref> He made a second substitute appearance in the second leg and another substitute appearance in the second leg of the third qualifying round. He scored his first competitive goal for Partizan on 23 November 2008 in a league match against [[OFK Beograd]].

In October 2008, [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] had given Ljajić a trial, although no information was given about the length of the trial initially.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.manutd.com/default.sps?pagegid={B4CEE8FA-9A47-47BC-B069-3F7A2F35DB70}&newsid=6620488 |title=Papers: Reds eye 'Little Kaka'? |work=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=15 October 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081221223824/http://www.manutd.com/default.sps?pagegid=%7BB4CEE8FA-9A47-47BC-B069-3F7A2F35DB70%7D&newsid=6620488 |archive-date=21 December 2008 |access-date=6 May 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref> On 2 January 2009, Manchester United announced the signings of both Ljajić and his Partizan teammate, [[Zoran Tošić]]. Tošić would join the club immediately while Ljajić would remain at Partizan for the remainder of 2009, joining United in January 2010.<ref name="serbians-to-join-united">{{cite news |title=Serbians to join United |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Football-News/2009/Jan/Serbians-to-join-United.aspx |work=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=2 January 2009 |access-date=17 March 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303234914/http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Football-News/2009/Jan/Serbians-to-join-United.aspx |archive-date=3 March 2016 }}</ref>

Despite being unable to officially join the club until January 2010, Ljajić made regular trips to [[Manchester]] throughout 2009 to train with the United first team, so the club's coaches could monitor his progress.<ref name="serbians-to-join-united" /> However, United decided not to take up their option to sign Ljajić due to issues surrounding the club's application for a work permit.<ref>{{cite news |first=Ben |last=Hibbs |title=Reds won't pursue Ljajic |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Football-News/2009/Dec/Reds-wont-pursue-Ljajic.aspx |work=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=3 December 2009 |access-date=17 March 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304043058/http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Football-News/2009/Dec/Reds-wont-pursue-Ljajic.aspx |archive-date=4 March 2016 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |first=Matt |last=Nichols |title=Ljajic decision explained |url=http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Football-News/2009/Dec/Ljajic-decision-explained.aspx |work=ManUtd.com |publisher=Manchester United |date=4 December 2009 |access-date=17 March 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304051505/http://www.manutd.com/en/News-And-Features/Football-News/2009/Dec/Ljajic-decision-explained.aspx |archive-date=4 March 2016 }}</ref> Following the transfer's collapse, Partizan manager [[Goran Stevanović]] claimed the situation had put Ljajić into "psychological shock" but that Ljajić was "handling the situation well".<ref name="guardian">{{cite news |first1=Daniel |last1=Taylor |first2=Jonathan |last2=Wilson |title=Manchester United accused of causing 'psychological shock' to Adem Ljajic |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2009/dec/04/manchester-united-adem-ljajic |work=guardian.co.uk |publisher=Guardian News and Media |date=4 December 2009 |access-date=6 December 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091207113813/http://www.guardian.co.uk/football/2009/dec/04/manchester-united-adem-ljajic |archive-date=7 December 2009 |url-status=live}}</ref> Partizan director of football [[Ivan Tomić]] said, "I think that they will regret this decision in future."<ref name="guardian"/>

===Fiorentina===
[[File:Adem Ljajić.JPG|thumb|upright|right|Ljajić playing for [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] in 2010]]

On 13 January 2010, Italian [[Serie A]] club [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] announced the signing of Ljajić. After passing a medical, Ljajić signed a five-year contract,<ref>{{cite news |title=Definito l'accordo per Ljajic |url=http://it.violachannel.tv/dettaglio-ultimora/items/definito-laccordo-per-ljiajic.html |language=it |work=ViolaChannel |publisher=ACF Fiorentina |date=13 January 2010 |access-date=13 January 2010 }}</ref> with Partizan receiving a reported fee of €8 million for the player.<ref name="fiorentina"/> Ljajić made his debut in Fiorentina's 2–2 draw away to [[Cagliari Calcio|Cagliari]] on 31 January 2010, coming on as an 82nd-minute substitute for [[Manuel Pasqual]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Serie A / Cagliari – Fiorentina |url=http://it.violachannel.tv/tempo-reale-generic/items/302062.html |work=ViolaChannel |publisher=ACF Fiorentina |date=31 January 2010 |access-date=31 January 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091018121530/http://it.violachannel.tv/tempo-reale-generic/items/302062.html |archive-date=18 October 2009 |url-status=dead}}</ref> However, his first half-season at the club under head coach [[Cesare Prandelli]] was spent settling into the new surroundings.

The arrival of Ljajić's compatriot [[Siniša Mihajlović]] as head coach saw increased first-team opportunities for Ljajić. He scored his first ''Viola'' goal from the [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty spot]] against [[SS Lazio|Lazio]] on 18 September 2010, which Fiorentina lost 1–2.

On 2 May 2012, Ljajić was substituted in a match against [[Novara Calcio|Novara]]. His reaction to this substitution was to sarcastically applaud the manager [[Delio Rossi]], who grabbed and attempted to punch Ljajić. Fiorentina announced after the match that Rossi had been dismissed as manager and that they would take proportionate measures against Ljajić. Ljajić's teammate [[Valon Behrami]], who was on the substitutes' bench at the time of the incident, said no one, including him, had heard Ljajić insult Rossi, which disproved Rossi's claims Ljajić insulted his family. Behrami added Rossi should be ashamed for his actions as well as for lying to the media.<ref>{{Cite news |last=makonda.com |title=Blic Sport {{!}} Behrami: Rosi je slagao šta mu je Ljajić rekao |url=http://sport.blic.rs/Fudbal/Evropski-fudbal/214285/Behrami-Rosi-je-slagao-sta-mu-je-Ljajic-rekao |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120716024258/http://sport.blic.rs/Fudbal/Evropski-fudbal/214285/Behrami-Rosi-je-slagao-sta-mu-je-Ljajic-rekao |archive-date=16 July 2012 |access-date=2025-02-25 |work=Blic Sport |url-status=live }}</ref>

Ljajić scored a brace as ''La Viola'' beat [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]] 4–1 on 17 February 2013.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://espnfc.com/us/en/report/351841/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5901 |title=Fiorentina 4–1 Internazionale |publisher=ESPNFC |date=17 February 2013 }}</ref>

===Roma===
Ljajić signed with [[AS Roma|Roma]] on 28 August 2013 for a fee of €11 million, potentially rising to €15 million depending on the club's success, with Ljajić signing a four-year contract.<ref name="roma"/> He chose the number 8 jersey, left vacant by [[Erik Lamela]], which Ljajić also used with the [[Serbia national football team|Serbia national team]]. On 1 September 2013, Ljajić made his Roma debut in a match against [[Hellas Verona FC|Hellas Verona]], replacing [[Alessandro Florenzi]]; Ljajić scored the final goal in 3–0 win. In his first season in [[Rome]], Ljajić scored 6 goals in 32 appearances.

On 30 August 2014, Ljajić made his [[2014–15 Serie A|2014–15 season]] debut in a 2–0 win for the ''Giallorossi'' over Fiorentina. On 24 September, he scored his first goal of the season in a 2–1 Roma victory over [[Parma Calcio 1913|Parma]]. On 6 December, he scored his first brace for Roma, which allowed Roma to come back and draw the home match against [[US Sassuolo Calcio|Sassuolo]], which finished 2–2. On 26 February 2015, he scored his first goal in the [[UEFA Europa League]] for the club, the opener in a 2–1 win away to [[Feyenoord]]. He concluded the season with 41 appearances and 9 goals, making him the club's second-highest goalscorer of the season, after [[Francesco Totti]].

====Loan to Inter Milan====
On 31 August 2015, Ljajić signed for Inter Milan on a season-long loan, with Inter paying Roma €1.75 million and including an option to make the transfer permanent at the [[2015–16 Serie A|end of the season]] for €11 million.<ref>[http://res.cloudinary.com/as-roma-turbine-sandbox/image/upload/v1445278197/asroma-uat/lrgbjxolsok8kpfimt5g.pdf OPERAZIONI DI MERCATO] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220423080209/http://res.cloudinary.com/as-roma-turbine-sandbox/image/upload/v1445278197/asroma-uat/lrgbjxolsok8kpfimt5g.pdf |date=23 April 2022 }} 31 August 2015 AS Roma</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Adem Ljajic joins Inter |url=http://www.inter.it/en/news/48880 |website=inter.it |publisher=FC Internazionale Milano |date=31 August 2015 |access-date=2 September 2015 |archive-date=26 March 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190326042409/http://www.inter.it/en/news/48880 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On 1 December 2015, Ljajić scored his first Inter goal in a 2–1 away loss to [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Napoli 2-1 Inter Milan|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34899294|website=BBC Sport|access-date=2 December 2015}}</ref>

===Torino===
After Inter opted not to exercise their purchase option, Ljajić was sold to [[Torino FC|Torino]] on 18 July 2016 for €8.5 million, plus €500,000 in potential bonuses.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.asroma.com/en/news/2016/7/adem-ljajic-joins-torino-on-permanent-deal |title=Adem Ljajic joins Torino on permanent deal |publisher=Asroma.com |date=2016-07-18 |accessdate=2022-03-21 |archive-date=17 August 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160817021744/http://www.asroma.com/en/news/2016/7/adem-ljajic-joins-torino-on-permanent-deal |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Beşiktaş===
On 31 August 2018, Ljajić joined Turkish [[Süper Lig]] club [[Beşiktaş J.K.|Beşiktaş]] on a [[2018–19 Beşiktaş J.K. season|season-long]] loan.<ref>{{cite web|title=Beşiktaş'a Hoş Geldin Adem Ljajic |url=http://bjk.com.tr/tr/haber/74070/besiktasa-hos-geldin-adem-ljajic.html|publisher=Beşiktaş JK|date=31 August 2018|access-date=31 August 2018|language=tr}}</ref> On 29 May 2019, Beşiktaş signed Ljajić on a permanent deal for a reported fee of €6.5 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://m.tuttomercatoweb.com/serie-a/ufficiale-besiktas-il-club-turco-ha-riscattato-ljajic-dal-torino-1252476|access-date=30 May 2019|title=UFFICIALE: Besiktas, il club turco ha riscattato Ljajic dal Torino|language=it}}</ref>

===Fatih Karagümrük===
On 28 September 2022, Ljajić joined [[Fatih Karagümrük S.K.|Fatih Karagümrük]] on a one-and-a-half-year contract. He only became available for the team's official matches starting January 2023.<ref name="beinsports"/>

===Novi Pazar===
On 14 September 2023, Ljajić returned to his hometown and signed for [[FK Novi Pazar|Novi Pazar]]. It is also stated that Ljajić had one condition, and it concerns his salary. Namely, he asked to play for the club for free. Three days later, he scored the winning goal on his debut in a 2–1 win over [[FK Napredak Kruševac|Napredak]], coming on in the 58th minute as a substitute for [[Adetunji Adeshina]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2023/09/17/serbia/super-liga/fk-novi-pazar/fk-napredak-krusevac/4185528/|title=NOVI PAZAR VS. NAPREDAK 2 - 1|website=Soccerway|date=17 September 2023}}</ref>

===Sarajevo===
In August 2025, Ljajić left Novi Pazar and signed a two-year contract with [[Premier League of Bosnia and Herzegovina|Bosnian Premier League]] club [[FK Sarajevo|Sarajevo]].<ref name="klix"/>

===Return to Novi Pazar===
On 31 August 2026, Ljajić returned to Novi Pazar, signing a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://info.fknovipazar.com/prvi-tim/1450 |title=Adem Ljajić ponovo u plavom dresu! |publisher=FK Novi Pazar |language=bs |date=31 August 2026 }}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:FWC 2018 - Group E - SRB v BRA - Photo 068.jpg|thumb|Ljajić (''in red'') and [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]]'s [[Gabriel Jesus]] at the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]]]]

Ljajić represented the Serbia [[Serbia national under-17 football team|under-17]] and [[Serbia national under-19 football team|under-19]] teams. On 7 September 2008, he made his international debut for the [[Serbia national under-21 football team|under-21]] squad in a [[2009 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification|European Championship qualification]] match against [[Hungary national under-21 football team|Hungary]]. On 26 October 2010, it was announced by Serbia coach [[Vladimir Petrović]] that Ljajić would receive his first [[Serbia national football team|senior]] call-up against [[Bulgaria national football team|Bulgaria]] in a friendly match on 17 November 2010.

Ljajić was removed from his country's squad by head coach Siniša Mihajlović after refusing to sing the Serbian national anthem in a 2–0 friendly loss against [[Spain national football team|Spain]] on 28 May 2012 for personal reasons.<ref>{{cite news |title=Sportsday – Monday 28 May as it happened |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/18232776 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120529080849/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/18232776 |url-status=dead |archive-date=29 May 2012 |work=BBC Sport |date=28 May 2012 |access-date=28 May 2012 }}</ref> Ljajić previously signed a code of conduct established by Mihajlović that included, among other things, to sing the Serbian national anthem, "[[Bože pravde]]" (''God of Justice'').<ref name="The Večernje novosti">{{cite news | url=http://www.novosti.rs/vesti/sport.294.html:381861-Mihajlovic-Ljajic-je-znao-pravila| title=Mihajlović: Ljajić je znao pravila (Mihajlović: Ljajić knew the rules) |publisher=The [[Večernje novosti]]| access-date=26 January 2013}}</ref> Ljajić confirmed Mihajlović's statement, also claiming he loves Serbia and that he has a will to play for its national team, but added he must respect himself, implying he was no longer going to play under Mihajlović.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.b92.net/sport/fudbal/vesti.php?yyyy=2012&mm=05&dd=28&nav_id=613464 |title=Ljajić: Volim Srbiju, poštujem sebe |trans-title=Ljajić:I love Serbia, I respect myself |language=sr |publisher=The [[B92]] |access-date=26 January 2013 }}</ref>

On 17 February 2014, the new head coach of the Serbia national team, [[Ljubinko Drulović]], said he would not require players to sing the national anthem but to give their all for their country on the field.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.telegraf.rs/sport/953616-drulovic-ja-cu-pevati-himnu-igraci-ne-moraju |title=DRULOVIĆ: Ja ću pevati himnu, igrači ne moraju! |trans-title=Drulović:I will sing the anthem, the players don't have to |language=sr |publisher=Telegraf |access-date=24 February 2014 }}</ref> Ljajić scored his first goal for the senior side on 7 June 2015 in a 4–1 friendly win against [[Azerbaijan national football team|Azerbaijan]].

In June 2018, Ljajić was included in the 23-man Serbian squad for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]] in Russia,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44083365 |title=World Cup 2018: All the confirmed squads for this summer's finals in Russia |website=BBC Sport |date=4 June 2018 |access-date=25 June 2018 }}</ref> where he played in all three group matches as Serbia was eliminated during the group stage.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44427970 |title=Costa Rica 0–1 Serbia |website=BBC Sport |first=Timothy |last=Abraham |date=17 June 2018 |access-date=25 June 2018 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44439145 |title=Serbia 1–2 Switzerland |website=BBC Sport |first=Matthew |last=Henry |date=23 June 2018 |access-date=25 June 2018 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/06/27/sports/world-cup/brazil-vs-serbia.html|title=World Cup: Brazil cruises into next round with easy victory|newspaper=The New York Times|first=Andrew |last=Das|date=27 June 2018|access-date=27 June 2018}}</ref>

==Basketball career==
On 7 November 2024, Ljajić signed a contract with KK Novi Pazar 1969. The club announced that Ljajić would "be available to coach Hadžerić when he balances his obligations with the football team".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sportske.net - Adem Ljajić postaje košarkaš, ali stvarno! |url=https://sportske.net/vest/domaci-fudbal/adem-ljajic-postaje-kosarkas-ali-stvarno-533664 |access-date=2024-11-07 |website=Sportske.net |language=sr}}</ref>
