'''Siniša Mihajlović''' ({{lang-sr-Cyrl|Синиша Михајловић}}, {{IPA|sh|sǐniʃa mixǎːjloʋitɕ|pron}}; 20 February 1969 – 16 December 2022) was a Serbian [[Association football|football]] manager and player. Though starting out as a [[midfielder]], he spent the majority of his illustrious playing career in [[Defender (association football)|defence]].

Mihajlović won the [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]] with [[Red Star Belgrade]] in [[1991 European Cup Final|1991]] before moving to Italy, making 353 appearances for [[Serie A]] sides [[AS Roma|Roma]], [[UC Sampdoria|Sampdoria]], [[SS Lazio|Lazio]] and [[Inter Milan]] and winning league titles with the latter two clubs. Considered by many to be among the best [[Direct free kick|free kick]] takers of all time,{{refn|group=nb|In 2009, ''[[The Guardian]]'' placed Mihajlović at No. 5 of the 6 top free kick specialists,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/blog/2009/aug/28/joy-of-six-free-kick-specialists|title=The Joy of Six: free-kick specialists|first=Rob|last=Smyth|date=28 August 2009|website=The Guardian|access-date=7 July 2017}}</ref> in September 2009, ''[[The Independent]]'' placed him at No. 8 of "The Ten Best Free-Kick Specialists",<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/news-and-comment/the-ten-best-freekick-specialists-1785081.html?action=Popup&ino=8|title=The Ten Best Free-Kick Specialists|date=11 September 2009|website=Independent.co.uk|access-date=7 July 2017}}</ref> In January 2009, ''Soccerlens'' placed him at No. 2 of "Top Ten Free Kick Specialists of All Time",<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccerlens.com/top-ten-free-kick-specialists-of-all-time/20493/|title=Top Ten Free Kick Specialists of All Time - Sportslens|date=27 January 2009|website=Soccerlens.com|access-date=7 July 2017}}</ref> and Gianni Verschueren's December 2012 "Ranking the Greatest Free-Kick Takers of All Time" top ten list on [[Bleacher Report]] placed him at No. 5,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1437739-world-football-ranking-the-greatest-free-kick-takers-of-all-time|title=Ranking the Greatest Free-Kick Takers of All Time|first=Gianni|last=Verschueren|publisher=[[Bleacher Report]]|access-date=7 July 2017}}</ref> followed by Alex Richards' December 2013 "Ranking the 16 Greatest Free-Kick Takers of All Time" list on the same site placed him at No. 2.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1886357-ranking-the-16-greatest-free-kick-takers-of-all-time|title=Ranking the 16 Greatest Free-Kick Takers of All Time|first=Alex|last=Richards|publisher=[[Bleacher Report]]|access-date=7 July 2017}}</ref>}} he holds the all-time record in [[Serie A]] for [[Football records in Italy#Most goals from a free kick|most goals from free kicks]] with 28 goals. He won 63 caps and scored 10 goals for [[Serbia and Montenegro national football team|Yugoslavia from 1991 to 2003]], of which his first four caps in 1991 represented [[Yugoslavia national football team|SFR Yugoslavia]], and played in the [[1998 FIFA World Cup]] and [[UEFA Euro 2000]] tournaments.

Mihajlović retired from playing in 2006, becoming assistant manager at Inter. He managed six Serie A clubs from 2008 to 2022, starting and finishing with [[Bologna FC 1909|Bologna]] and also including [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]], [[Torino FC|Torino]] and [[AC Milan]]. He was the coach of the [[Serbia national football team|Serbia national team]] from May 2012 to November 2013. He was diagnosed with [[leukemia]] in 2019 and died from the disease in 2022.

==Early life==
Born in [[Vukovar]] into a working-class family of a [[Serbs of Bosnia and Herzegovina|Bosnian Serb]] father<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mondo.ba/Sport/Fudbal/a1187842/mihajlovici-iz-kukulja-rodjaci-sinise-mihajlovica.html|title=Rodbina Siniše Mihajlovića iz mjesta nedaleko od Banjaluke: Bog je tako htio - da bude sahranjen na krsnu slavu!|website=Mondo Bosna}}</ref> and a [[Croats|Croat]] mother,<ref name=Seba-Sinisa>{{citation|author=Suzana Vermelinger|work=Internazionale Magazine XI|year=2004|title=Seba & Sinisa – tako slicni a tako razliciti}}</ref> Mihajlović was raised in [[Borovo Naselje]] with a younger brother, Dražen (b. 1973).<ref name=Vreme-1054255>{{cite news|title=Nisam od onih koji kukaju|url=http://www.vreme.com/cms/view.php?id=1054255|publisher=Vreme|date=24 May 2012}}</ref> Their father Bogdan (d. 2011) was a [[truck driver]] at the Građevinar construction company in Vukovar, while their mother Viktorija worked in the [[Borovo (company)|Borovo shoe factory]].<ref name=Vreme-1054255/> Mihajlović identified as a [[Serbs|Serb]], but said that he viewed Croatia as his country as well.<ref name=Novosti-404298>{{cite news|url=http://www.novosti.rs/vesti/sport.294.html:404298-Mihajlovic-I-Hrvatska-je-moja-zemlja|title=Mihajlović: I Hrvatska je moja zemlja!|date=2 November 2012|publisher=Novosti|language=sr|location=Belgrade}}</ref>

During the [[Croatian War of Independence]], his home was destroyed by Croatian forces, among whom was his childhood best friend, an ethnic Croat, forcing his parents to flee.<ref name=Seba-Sinisa/> His maternal uncle called his mother and said that she should stay in Borovo, and that Siniša's father was to be killed.<ref name=Seba-Sinisa/> His uncle was arrested when the [[Serbian Volunteer Guard]] took over Borovo, but was freed because he was related to Mihajlović.<ref name=Seba-Sinisa/> In a 2016 interview Mihajlović said he had forgiven his childhood friend in a meeting in [[Zagreb]] prior to the crucial [[UEFA Euro 2000 qualifying Group 8|Euro 2000 qualification]] match between [[Serbia and Montenegro national football team|FR Yugoslavia]] and [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://video.sky.it/sport/calcio-italiano/mister_cond_mihajlovic_e_lorrore_della_guerra_in_serbia/v277726.vid|title=Mister Condò, Mihajlovic e l'orrore della guerra in Serbia|access-date=15 April 2016|archive-date=6 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160406071144/http://video.sky.it/sport/calcio-italiano/mister_cond_mihajlovic_e_lorrore_della_guerra_in_serbia/v277726.vid|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Early career===
Mihajlović started playing organized football with his hometown team [[NK Borovo]]. He quickly marked himself out as a talented youngster, making the [[Socialist Republic of Croatia|SR Croatia]] select squad for the Yugoslav inter-republic youth football tournaments.

In 1986, he was attached to NK Borovo's first team. Playing in the SR Croatia provincial league (third tier competition on the Yugoslav club football pyramid), his first team debut took place on 25 May 1986 against Šparta in [[Beli Manastir]]. The match ended 1–1 with Mihajlović scoring a goal. The 17-year-old also got his first taste of professionalism with his first monthly salary being [[Swiss franc|CHF]]500.<ref name="globus.jutarnji.hr">[http://globus.jutarnji.hr/zivot/stimac--pobijedit-cu-te-usred-maksimira- Štimac, pobijedit ću te usred Maksimira!] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120722181532/http://globus.jutarnji.hr/zivot/stimac--pobijedit-cu-te-usred-maksimira- |date=22 July 2012 }};''Globus'', July 2012</ref>

In late 1986, [[Red Star Belgrade]] representatives led by scout [[Jovan Aćimović|Kule Aćimović]] came to watch the seventeen-year-old in a friendly Borovo played against [[FK Rad]], but decided not to sign him.<ref name="Veče sa Ivanom Ivanovićem">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KsB8SvXigTI Veče sa Ivanom Ivanovićem], Prva TV, December 2011</ref>

Then in late spring 1987, with [[NK Rijeka]] and [[NK Dinamo Vinkovci|Dinamo Vinkovci]] both seeking to sign Mihajlović, [[NK Dinamo Zagreb|Dinamo Zagreb]]—led by club president Ivo Vrhovec and head coach [[Ćiro Blažević]]—also expressed an interest; their youth players [[Zvonimir Boban]] and [[Robert Prosinečki]] had been playing with Mihajlović on the SR Croatia select youth team at inter-republic and provincial youth tournaments and recommended him to the team.<ref name="globus.jutarnji.hr"/> After seeing Mihajlović in a training session, Blažević took him with the rest of the first team to [[Sassari]] for an impromptu getaway between two league matches towards the end of the [[1986–87 Yugoslav First League|season]], and gave him a substitute appearance in Dinamo shirt in a friendly against local club [[Sassari Torres|Torres Sassari]].<ref name="globus.jutarnji.hr"/>

In September 1987, Mihajlović was invited to join Dinamo's youth squad for a friendly tournament in [[Salem, Baden-Württemberg|Salem]], [[West Germany]] where he performed well.<ref name="Ciro-zidak">{{cite news|last=Židak |first=Tomislav |url=http://www.jutarnji.hr/ovo-je-slika-koju-jos-nikad-niste-vidjeli--sinisa-mihajlovic-u-dresu-dinama-/1052377 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120908031838/http://www.jutarnji.hr/ovo-je-slika-koju-jos-nikad-niste-vidjeli--sinisa-mihajlovic-u-dresu-dinama-/1052377/ |archive-date=8 September 2012 |url-status=dead |title=Ovo je slika koju još nikad niste vidjeli: Siniša Mihajlović u dresu Dinama! |agency=[[Jutarnji list]] |date=6 September 2012 |access-date=17 December 2022}}</ref> However, no deal was agreed again as the club's head coach Ćiro Blažević felt that Dinamo already had players for the central midfield position that were "just as good if not better", such as incoming [[Haris Škoro]] as well as club mainstay [[Marko Mlinarić]] and returnee [[Stjepan Deverić]]. With Dinamo only prepared to offer a [[stipend]]-based agreement rather than a professional contract, Mihajlović decided to continue with NK Borovo.

The decision not to take Dinamo's offer cost Mihajlović a place in the [[Yugoslavia national under-20 football team|Yugoslavia under-20]]; head coach [[Mirko Jozić]] had told him that he would not be called up for the upcoming [[1987 FIFA World Youth Championship|FIFA World Youth Championship]] in Chile unless he signed with the Zagreb club.<ref name="globus.jutarnji.hr"/><ref name="miha-orlic">{{cite news|last=Orlić |first=Alen |url=http://www.jutarnji.hr/mihajlovic---ciro-me-potjerao-iz-dinama-zbog-frizure--a-bilica-sam-molio-da-me-dovede-u-hajduk-/1024100/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120427015004/http://www.jutarnji.hr/mihajlovic---ciro-me-potjerao-iz-dinama-zbog-frizure--a-bilica-sam-molio-da-me-dovede-u-hajduk-/1024100/ |archive-date=27 April 2012 |url-status=dead |title=Mihajlović: 'Ćiro me potjerao iz Dinama zbog frizure, a Bilića sam molio da me dovede u Hajduk' |agency=[[Jutarnji list]] |date=25 April 2012 |access-date=17 December 2022}}</ref>

===Vojvodina===
Mihajlović signed for [[FK Vojvodina]] in 1988, as part of a group of players acquired by the club, which included defensive midfielder [[Slaviša Jokanović]], and defenders [[Budimir Vujačić]] and [[Miroslav Tanjga]].<ref name="miha-kosan-mondo">{{cite news|last=Vujičić |first=Milutin |url=https://mondo.rs/Sport/Fudbal/a1725598/Milorad-Kosanovic-o-Sinisi-Mihajlovicu-za-MONDO.html |title=Znam, zlato, zašto me zoveš... Kosanović se za MONDO oprostio od Mihe: Najbolje potrošeni milion u istoriji Zvezde! |agency=Mondo.rs |date=16 December 2022 |access-date=17 December 2022}}</ref> The club won the Yugoslav league title, with Mihajlović scoring four goals in 31 appearances. The following 1989–90 season saw Vojvodina compete in the [[1989–90 European Cup|European Cup]] for only the second time in their history, but lost in the first round to Hungarian champions [[Budapest Honvéd FC|Honvéd]].<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q9dXaA9KWNw Vojvodina-Honved 2:1];European Cup, 27 September 1989</ref>

===Red Star Belgrade===
Mihajlović joined Red Star Belgrade on 10 December 1990 in a high-profile transfer with a transfer fee of [[Deutsche Mark|DM]]1 million paid out to Vojvodina.<ref name="miha-kosan-mondo"/> Arriving at a club coached by his old Vojvodina mentor Ljupko Petrović, Mihajlović was brought in to establish a robust presence on the left side of midfield as well as to score set-piece goals. In the European Cup [[1990–91 European Cup|semi-final]] return leg versus [[Bayern Munich]], Mihajlović scored both Red Star goals—a free-kick opener and the injury time winner with a shot that deflected off [[Klaus Augenthaler]]. In the [[1991 European Cup Final|final]], Red Star defeated [[Olympique de Marseille]] on penalties, after a 0–0 draw at full time, with Mihajlović being one of the shootout scorers.

Mihajlović was also in the team later that year when [[Red Star Belgrade]] won the [[Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)|Intercontinental Cup]], defeating [[Colo-Colo]] 3–0. He was then included by [[Yugoslavia national football team]] to [[UEFA Euro 1992]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1992/05/27/pagina-27/1245648/pdf.html|website=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|title=Pancev también renuncia a la Eurocopa|language=es|date=25 May 1992|access-date=5 June 2019}}</ref> but the nation was disqualified from the competition by [[United Nations Security Council Resolution 757|United Nations sanctions]] due to the [[Yugoslav Wars]].

===Roma===
In the summer of 1992, amid interest from Juventus, Mihajlović signed for [[AS Roma|Roma]] for a reported [[Italian lira|ITL]]8.5 billion (~US$5.9 million) transfer fee,<ref>Calciatori ‒ La raccolta completa Panini 1961-2012, Vol. 9 (1992-1993), Panini, 2 luglio 2012, p. 10</ref> at the request of head coach [[Vujadin Boškov]], also a new arrival to [[Stadio Olimpico|Olimpico]]. The club were looking to improve on their previous season's 5th place league finish.

Mihajlović secured a regular first team spot in the left midfield, and the team finished 10th in the league. Mihajlović also played a significant part in Roma's [[1992–93 UEFA Cup|UEFA Cup campaign]] where they reached the [[1992–93 UEFA Cup#Quarter-finals|quarterfinals]]—losing to [[Borussia Dortmund]] in a tie that saw the Serb score a trademark free-kick for a 1–0 first leg lead, before being beaten 2–0 in the return. Due to a long-term injury to Roma's [[left back]] [[Amedeo Carboni]] midway through the season, coach Boškov moved Mihajlović to the left back position.

The 1993–94 season started with new head coach [[Carlo Mazzone]] in charge after Boškov was sacked. In addition to the four foreigners already at the club, the club brought in Argentine [[Abel Balbo]] thus increasing competition for three foreign spots. Mihajlović continued as a left back under the new manager. In the [[1993–94 AS Roma season|1993–94 season]], the club finished 7th, and out of Europe for the second season running.

Years later, talking about his playing days, Mihajlović referred to his stay in Roma as "the two worst seasons of my entire career".<ref name="Veče sa Ivanom Ivanovićem"/>

===Sampdoria===
In 1994, Mihajlović joined [[UC Sampdoria|Sampdoria]], who were the third-placed club in [[1993–94 Serie A|previous season]]'s Serie A standings and the Coppa Italia winners, coached by [[Sven-Göran Eriksson]]. Also arriving the same summer were Inter stalwarts [[Walter Zenga]] and [[Riccardo Ferri]] as part of the deal that took goalkeeper [[Gianluca Pagliuca]] the other way.

In his four seasons at Sampdoria, Mihajlović saw limited success in the Serie A. In the European competitions, however, he helped Sampdoria reach the [[1994–95 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup]] [[1994–95 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup#Semi-finals|semifinal]], where they were defeated by [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] on penalties.

In June 1998, Mihajlović represented FR Yugoslavia at the [[1998 FIFA World Cup]], playing all Yugoslav matches in the tournament. He scored a goal against [[Iran national football team|Iran]], and conceded an [[own goal]] against [[Germany national football team|Germany]]. This made Mihajlović one of five players to score both a goal and an own goal in the World Cup; the other ones being [[Ernie Brandts]], [[Ruud Krol]], [[Gustavo Peña]] and [[Mario Mandžukić]].{{citation needed|date=May 2023}}

===Lazio===
In the summer of 1998, Mihajlović was brought to [[SS Lazio|Lazio]] by head coach Sven-Göran Eriksson and club president [[Sergio Cragnotti]] for [[British pound|£]]8.5 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dOSWgzSB4xk |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211212/dOSWgzSB4xk| archive-date=12 December 2021 |url-status=live|title=Interview with Sinisa Mihajlovic - top free kick scorer|last=Mirko Rados|date=25 May 2008|publisher=YouTube|access-date=7 July 2017}}{{cbignore}}</ref> He won his first trophy in Italy as Lazio beat [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in the [[1998 Supercoppa Italiana|Supercoppa Italiana]] during late August 1998. The club [[1997–98 Serie A|finished 7th]] in Serie A.

Strengthening the squad for a serious run at the Serie A title, in addition to Mihajlović, the summer 1998 transfer window also saw Cragnotti bring in [[Dejan Stanković]] from [[Red Star Belgrade]], established goalscorer [[Marcelo Salas]] from [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]], and finally striker [[Christian Vieri]] from [[Atlético Madrid]].

With Lazio, Mihajlović reached the final of the 1999 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup, winning the last edition of that competition with a 2–1 victory against [[RCD Mallorca]]. Lazio also won the 1999 [[UEFA Super Cup]]. Mihajlović played 26 times and scored seven goals during the [[1999–2000 Serie A]] season as Lazio won their second ''Scudetto''. Mihajlović completed the double by helping Lazio win the 2000 [[Coppa Italia]].

Mihajlović represented Yugoslavia internationally again, at the [[2000 UEFA European Football Championship|Euro 2000]] tournament. In the first Yugoslav game of the tournament, he was sent off against [[Slovenia national football team|Slovenia]]. He served a one-game suspension before playing the last two games of the tournament.

Mihajlović won his last trophy with Lazio in 2004, beating Juventus in the Coppa Italia final.

===Inter Milan===
In 2004, Mihajlović was released from Lazio and joined his friend and former teammate [[Roberto Mancini]] at [[Inter Milan]] on a free transfer, signing a one-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.inter.it/it/news/23398|title=MERCATO: MIHAJLOVIC È DELL'INTER|date=30 July 2004|access-date=5 June 2015|publisher=FC Internazionale Milano|language=it|archive-date=6 April 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180406041514/https://www.inter.it/it/news/23398|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 16 June 2005 Mihajlović signed a one-year extension.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.inter.it/it/news/28125|title=MIHAJLOVIC: CON L'INTER FINO AL 2006|date=16 June 2006|access-date=5 June 2015|publisher=FC Internazionale Milano|language=it|archive-date=6 April 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180406040307/https://www.inter.it/it/news/28125|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 9 April 2006, in a league away game versus [[Ascoli Calcio 1898|Ascoli]], he scored his 27th career [[Direct free kick|free-kick]] goal in the [[Serie A]] championship. He retired after the 2005–06 season.

During his time with Inter, he made 43 appearances and scored 6 goals, all from [[direct free kick]]s.

==International career==
Playing as a youth international, Mihajlović featured in 5 games at the [[1990 UEFA European Under-21 Championship]].<ref name="auto1">{{WorldFootball.net|sinisa-mihajlovic}}</ref>

Between 1991 and 2003, Mihajlović was capped 63 times and scored 10 goals for the [[Yugoslavia national football team|Yugoslavia]]/[[Serbia and Montenegro national football team|Serbia and Montenegro]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/joeg-recintlp.html|title=Yugoslavia (Serbia (and Montenegro)) - Record International Players|access-date=14 December 2024|website=[[RSSSF]]}}</ref> He participated at the [[1998 FIFA World Cup]] where he scored a free-kick against [[Iran national football team|Iran]] as Yugoslavia reached the second round. He also participated at [[UEFA Euro 2000]]. He was sent off in Yugoslavia's opening game against [[Slovenia national football team|Slovenia]] but returned after a one match ban with Yugoslavia reaching the quarterfinal. His final international was a June 2003 [[UEFA Euro 2004 qualifying|European Championship qualification]] match away against [[Finland national football team|Finland]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://eu-football.info/_player.php?id=13955|title=Siniša Mihajlović, international football player|access-date=14 December 2024|website=EU-football.info}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Early into his playing career, Mihajlović marked himself out with an extraordinary long-distance [[Shooting (association football)|striking]], [[Cross (football)|crossing]], and [[Passing (association football)|passing]] ability. His precise [[Curl (football)|curling]] yet hard-driven left-footed shot allowed him to score  [[Direct free kick|free-kick]] goals on a regular basis. A set-piece and [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty kick]] specialist,<ref name="Bologna, ecco Mihajlovic">{{cite web|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/SerieA/Squadre/Bologna/Primo_Piano/2008/11/04/mihajlovic.shtml|title=Bologna, ecco Mihajlovic "Non voglio giocatori mosci"|trans-title=Bologna, here is Mihajlovic "I don't want soft players"|publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport|language=it|author1=Gianluca Orefice|date=4 November 2008|access-date=26 August 2015}}</ref> Mihajlović has said that he has scored free-kicks from as far as 35 yards, adding in a 2000 interview with BBC Sport: "I like to shoot with a swerve into both sides of the net. I often try scoring directly from the corners.".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/euro2000/teams/yugoslavia/786501.stm|title=BBC SPORT - EURO2000 - YUGOSLAVIA - Mihajlovic to the rescue|website=news.bbc.co.uk|access-date=7 July 2017}}</ref> Regarded as one of the greatest free kick takers of all time, he was capable of both scoring and creating chances from dead ball opportunities,<ref name="Mihajlovic laureato in punizioni">{{cite web|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/1997/febbraio/26/Mihajlovic_laureato_punizioni_ga_0_97022610753.shtml|title=Mihajlovic laureato in punizioni|trans-title=Mihajlovic degree in free-kicks|publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport|language=it|author1=Germano Bovolenta|date=26 February 1997|access-date=26 August 2015}}</ref> and holds the record for the [[Football records in Italy#Most goals from a free kick|most goals in Serie A from free-kicks]], as well as the record for second most goals from free kicks in all competitions, with 43, behind [[Alessandro Del Piero]]. Along with [[Giuseppe Signori]], he is one of only two players who have scored a hat-trick from free kicks in Serie A, a feat which he accomplished during his time with Lazio, in a 5–2 win over Sampdoria, on 13 December 1998, during the 1998–99 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/1998/dicembre/14/Record_Mihajlovic_mai_gol_punizione_ga_0_9812144971.shtml|title=Record Mihajlovic: mai 3 gol su punizione diretta|trans-title=Mihajlovic record: never before 3 goals from direct free-kicks|publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport|language=it|author1=Lanfredo Birelli|date=14 December 1998|access-date=26 August 2015}}</ref><ref name="calciomercato.com">{{cite web |url=http://www.calciomercato.com/altre-notizie/juventus-del-piero-vs-mihajlovic-512508 |title=Juventus, Del Piero: Due gol... per Mihajlovic | Altre notizie |work=Calciomercato.com | Tutte le news sul calcio in tempo reale |publisher=Calciomercato.com |language=it |date=4 February 2014 |access-date=14 January 2018 |archive-date=29 November 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129012226/http://www.calciomercato.com/altre-notizie/juventus-del-piero-vs-mihajlovic-512508 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

During his club career in Yugoslavia with Vojvodina and Red Star Belgrade as well as during his early spell at Roma, he played on the left side of midfield as [[Left winger|winger]], or as an [[attacking midfielder]] or [[second striker]] on occasion, where he was known for his stamina, speed, foot-work, and ability to cover the flank with his runs, as well as his excellent ball-striking ability with his left foot, and his ability to dictate attacking plays in midfield.<ref name="Mihajlovic laureato in punizioni"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://thesefootballtimes.co/2015/08/17/red-star-triumph-of-1991/ |title=Red Star and the immortal triumph of 1991 |publisher=hesefootballtimes.co |last1=Aspey |first1=Jonathon |date=17 August 2015 |access-date=14 July 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/the-team-dismantled-by-war-red-star-belgrades-final-european-triumph/ |title=The Team Dismantled by War: Red Star Belgrade's Final European Triumph |work=Vice |last1=O'Connor |first1=Robert |date=5 June 2015 |access-date=14 July 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://football-italia.net/eriksson-miha-became-one-of-the-best/ |title=Eriksson: 'Miha became one of the best' |publisher=Football Italia |date=26 March 2020 |access-date=11 June 2024 }}</ref> Upon moving to Italy, midway through his first season in Serie A, Mihajlović was moved to the position of [[left back]] by Roma head coach [[Vujadin Boškov]]. The following season, under Roma's new head coach [[Carlo Mazzone]], he mostly continued at left back while occasionally being deployed as a [[Defensive Midfielder|defensive midfielder]], although his performances in this position were somewhat inconsistent due to his limited tactical sense. In 1994, after transferring to Sampdoria under head coach [[Sven-Göran Eriksson]], Mihajlović was moved to the centre of the team's defensive line, and remained in this position for the rest of his career. He later excelled in this newfound [[Centre-back|centre back]] role, where he functioned as a [[Sweeper (association football)|sweeper]], due to his consistent defensive displays, physique, intelligence, leadership, and tenacity, as well as his good technique, touch on the ball, and long passing ability, which enabled him to play the ball out from the back; he drew praise from manager Carlo Mazzone, in particular, who described him as one of the best players in the world in his position.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://archiviostorico.corriere.it/1999/ottobre/21/Mihajlovic_merita_Pallone_oro_co_10_9910215391.shtml|title=Mihajlovic merita il Pallone d' oro|trans-title=Mihajlovic deserves the Ballon d'Or|publisher=Il Corriere della Sera|language=it|author1=Giuseppe Toti|date=21 October 1999|access-date=26 August 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://archiviostorico.corriere.it/1999/ottobre/22/Mazzone_Mihajlovic_piu_forte_tutti_co_10_9910225476.shtml|title=Mazzone: "Mihajlovic e' il piu' forte di tutti"|trans-title=Mazzone: "Mihajlovic is the best of them all"|publisher=Il Corriere della Sera|language=it|author1=Stefano Petrucci|date=22 October 1999|access-date=26 August 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/euro2000/teams/yugoslavia/squad/746760.stm |title=Sinisa Mihajlovic |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=26 October 2019}}</ref>

==Managerial career==
===Assistant at Inter Milan===
After retiring from playing at [[Inter Milan]], Mihajlović began a coaching career at San Siro as assistant to head coach [[Roberto Mancini]]. Mihajlović and Mancini had played together for five seasons at Sampdoria and Lazio.

Mihajlović's free-kick expertise has been praised by [[Zlatan Ibrahimović]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.footballpress.net/?action=read&idsel=46855|title=FOOTBALLpress.net news: BARCA, Ibrahimovic: " Mihajlovic {{sic|teac|hed|nolink=y}} me how to score from free kicks"|date=23 July 2011|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110723131955/http://www.footballpress.net/?action=read&idsel=46855|archive-date=23 July 2011}}</ref> who after several successful free-kicks thanked the then assistant coach Mihajlović who had trained him for two years at Inter.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.fotbollsverige.se/news_show_tranade-frisparkar-med-mihajlovic.html?id=8834668 | title = Tränade frisparkar med Mihajlovic | language = sv | publisher = fotbollsverige.se | date = 26 October 2009 | access-date =26 May 2012}}</ref>

Mancini was fired in June 2008 by club president [[Massimo Moratti]] at the end of the [[2007–08 Serie A|2007–08 season]] to make way for [[José Mourinho]]. Mihajlović left the club at the same time.

===Bologna===
On 3 November 2008, Mihajlović was appointed to replace [[Daniele Arrigoni]] at Serie A relegation-battling club [[Bologna FC 1909|Bologna]].<ref name="mihajlovic_bologna">{{cite news|publisher=Bologna FC 1909 |url=http://www.bolognafc.it/pagen.asp?c=4915&m=11&l=1 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20090919123831/http://www.bolognafc.it/pagen.asp?c=4915&m=11&l=1 |url-status=dead |archive-date=19 September 2009 |title=Il Bologna a Mihajlovic |date=3 November 2008 |access-date=3 November 2008 |language=it }}</ref> His Serie A bench debut came on 8 November 2008 at home versus [[AS Roma|Roma]]. The match ended in a 1–1 draw. His tenure began with five consecutive league draws before a 5–2 victory against relegation rivals [[Torino FC|Torino]] on 13 December 2008.

Mihajlović was sacked by Bologna on 14 April 2009 in the wake of a 1–4 home defeat against [[AC Siena|Siena]], which dragged the team back into the relegation zone with seven matches remaining in the season. His tenure suffered from media rumours that he had numerous high-profile disagreements with senior players at the club which led to the poor form that eventually cost him the job.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/10/italy/2009/04/14/1208405/breaking-news-bologna-sack-sinisa-mihajlovic-appoint-giuseppe-pa|title=Official: Bologna Sack Sinisa Mihajlovic, Appoint Giuseppe Papadopulo |website=Goal.com|date=14 April 2009|access-date=7 July 2017}}</ref> Under new head coach [[Giuseppe Papadopulo]], Bologna avoided relegation to the [[Serie B]] on the last day of the season with a win over [[Calcio Catania|Catania]].

===Catania===
On 8 December 2009, Mihajlović was appointed new head coach of [[Calcio Catania|Catania]], taking over from [[Gianluca Atzori]].
<ref name="mihajlovic_catania">{{cite news|url=http://calciocatania.net/comunicati/comunicati.php?id=18160|language=it|publisher=Calcio Catania|access-date=8 December 2009|date=8 December 2009|title=Sinisa Mihajlovic è il nuovo allenatore del Catania|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100620224300/http://calciocatania.net/comunicati/comunicati.php?id=18160|archive-date=20 June 2010}}</ref> He signed a contract until June 2011 with ''gli elefanti'', hiring [[Dario Marcolin]]—his former teammate at Lazio and colleague on Mancini's coaching staff at Inter—to be his assistant.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ontheminute.com/news/news.php?news=19748|title=Man City defender returns to action |website=Ontheminute.com|date=8 December 2009 |access-date=7 July 2017}}</ref> Arriving at the club [[2009–10 Serie A#Positions by round|last in Serie A]], Mihajlović made his debut with a home loss against relegation rivals [[AS Livorno Calcio|Livorno]]. However, the following week, his team beat heavily favoured Juventus away in Turin with a 1–2 scoreline.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.b92.net/sport/intervjui/intervjui.php?yyyy=2009&mm=12&nav_category=91&nav_id=399623|title=Mihajlović za B92: "Verovao sam u pobedu"|website=B92.net|date=21 December 2009 |access-date=7 July 2017}}</ref>

A string of good results, together with a number of key January signings such as former Argentine international striker [[Maxi López]], helped Mihajlović keep the team out of the relegation zone. On 13 March 2010, Catania won 3–1 against league leaders and Mihajlović's former team [[Inter Milan]].

Led by Mihajlović, Catania finished the season in 13th spot, well out of the relegation zone.

He resigned at the end of the season on 24 May 2010 amid reports linking him to incumbent [[UEFA Champions League]] winners Inter as a replacement for outgoing boss [[José Mourinho]],<ref name="mihajlovic_catania_resigned">{{cite news |url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/SerieA/Catania/24-05-2010/mihajlovic-saluta-catania-604106965941.shtml|publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport |language=it |access-date=24 May 2010 |date=24 May 2010 |title=Mihajlovic saluta Catania C'è l'Inter dietro l'angolo}}</ref> which did not come to anything in the end.

===Fiorentina===
On 3 June 2010, Mihajlović was announced as the new head coach of [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]], replacing outgoing [[Cesare Prandelli]] who had left the Tuscan club to become the manager of the [[Italy national football team|Italy national team]].

Fiorentina had finished the [[2009–10 Serie A]] campaign in eleventh place, but had made the [[2009–10 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Round of 16|Champions League round-of-16 stage]] where they were eliminated by [[Bayern Munich]] on away goals.  Mihajlović signed a two-year contract on a salary of just under €1 million per year.<ref>[http://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/?action=read&id=209847 Da Prandelli a Sinisa: come cambia la Fiorentina];TuttoMercatoWeb, 28 May 2010</ref> Mihajlović stated that making Europe was a realistic goal for the season.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120729195342/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/columns/story/_/id/981809/gotta:-fiorentina's-axing-of-sinisa-mihajlovic?cc=5901|title=Mihajlovic carved up}};ESPNSoccernet, 10 November 2011</ref>

====2010–11 season====
The team suffered poor form in the first part of the season, with injuries to some key players. They finished the first half of the season in twelfth spot. Mihajlović signed winger [[Valon Behrami]] from [[West Ham United]], but the alternating home and away form improved only slightly as the head coach experimented with various tactical formations.

In February 2011, Fiorentina won on the road for the first time in the season with a win at Palermo. In March 2011, the team recorded two straight wins for the first time in the season, climbing up to eighth spot. The club finished the [[2010–11 Serie A|league season]] with 12 wins (only three of those away from home), 11 losses, and 15 draws, which secured ninth place – twelve points out of a European spot.

====2011–12 season====
During the summer 2011 transfer season, Mihajlović was strongly linked with a return to Inter in head coaching capacity, with some Italian papers even reporting the specific date of his unveiling at the ''nerazzurri'' following supposed successful negotiations with Inter's sporting director [[Marco Branca]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sport.blic.rs/Fudbal/Evropski-fudbal/199086/Korejere-delo-Sport-Mihajlovic-u-Interu|title="Korejere delo Sport": Mihajlović u Interu!|date=21 November 2015|website=Sport.blic.rs|access-date=7 July 2017 |last1=Com |first1=Makonda }}</ref> However, Mihajlović denied those claims, pledging to stay on in Florence.<ref>[http://sport.blic.rs/Fudbal/Evropski-fudbal/199121/Mihajlovic-Zelim-da-ostanem-u-Fiorentini-jos-dugo Mihajlović: Želim da ostanem u Fiorentini još dugo];''Blic'', 19 June 2011</ref>

The [[2011–12 ACF Fiorentina season|season]] began in August 2011, with a [[2011–12 Coppa Italia|Coppa Italia]] [[2011–12 Coppa Italia#Fiorentina v Cittadella|win over]] [[AS Cittadella]]. However, poor league form including five matches without a win put Mihajlović's position under pressure. At a home match against Genoa in October 2011, Fiorentina's supporters shouted abuse from the terraces throughout the match with calls for Mihajlović's sacking and even racist banners and chants targeting the coach's ethnicity.<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120804005821/http://www.kurir-info.rs/navijaci-fjorentine-sinisa-zlobni-srbine-clanak-120026|title=Navijači Fjorentine: Siniša, zlobni Srbine!}};''Kurir'', 2 November 2011</ref> The fans' verbal abuse of Mihajlović made headlines for the next couple of days and sections of Fiorentina support issued an apology to the coach by hanging a banner outside of the stadium.<ref>[http://sg.news.yahoo.com/fiorentina-fans-apologise-racist-mihajlovic-chant-130144564.html Fiorentina fans apologise for racist Mihajlovic chant];AFP News, 2 November 2011</ref><ref>[http://www.goal.com/en/news/10/italy/2011/11/03/2741138/fiorentina-supporters-apologise-for-criticising-sinisa Fiorentina supporters apologise for criticising Sinisa Mihajlovic – report];goal.com, 3 November 2011</ref> Mihajlović was sacked on 7 November 2011, one day after a 1–0 away loss to [[ChievoVerona]].<ref>[https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european/sinisa-mihajlovic-steps-down-as-fiorentina-manager-6258802.html Sinisa Mihajlovic steps down as Fiorentina manager];''The Independent'', 8 November 2011</ref> The team was in 13th place in the league with 12 points from 10 matches.

===Serbia===
In May 2012, the [[Football Association of Serbia]] signed Mihajlović to become the head coach of the [[Serbia national football team|Serbia national team]] until the end of the [[2014 FIFA World Cup]] in Brazil.<ref name="B92 selektor">{{cite web |url=https://www.b92.net/sport/fudbal/vesti.php?yyyy=2012&mm=05&dd=19&nav_id=610687 |author=[[B92]] |title=B92: Mihajlović zvanično selektor |accessdate=16 April 2022 |date=19 May 2012 |language=Serbian}}</ref> Serbia finished third in [[2014 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group A|Group A]] of the [[2014 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|qualifying phase]] in October 2013 after which he resigned.

===Sampdoria===
On 20 November 2013, Sampdoria named Mihajlović as the new head coach in place for [[Delio Rossi]]. He signed a one-year rolling contract with automatic extension in case of a successful escape from relegation in the ongoing season, with his assistant coach [[Nenad Sakić]] (a former Sampdoria player himself) following him too.

During his first season in charge, he guided Sampdoria to significant improvements in results and easily escaped relegation. He successively agreed to stay for one more season, after talks with new president [[:it: Massimo Ferrero|Massimo Ferrero]], who took over from the Garrone family in July 2014. In the first weeks of the 2014–15 season, he managed to obtain eight points and no defeats in the first four games of the season, overseeing quality performances from players such as [[Stefano Okaka]]. On 1 June 2015 he wrote an open letter to confirm his departure as the head coach of Sampdoria.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sampdoria.it/lettera-aperta-di-sinisa-mihajlovic-arrivederci-samp-resterai-casa-mia/|title=Lettera aperta di Sinisa Mihajlovic: "Arrivederci Samp, resterai casa mia"|date=1 June 2015|access-date=4 June 2015|publisher=UC Sampdoria|language=it}}</ref>

===Milan===
[[File:Sinisa 2015 (cropped).jpg|220px|thumb|right|Mihajlović in 2015]]
On 16 June 2015, [[AC Milan|Milan]] officially sacked [[Filippo Inzaghi]], appointing Mihajlović as their new manager, with a contract until 30 June 2017.<ref>{{cite web |title=sinisa Mihajlovic ha firmato un contratto |trans-title=Sinisa Mihajlovic signed a two-year contract |url=http://www.acmilan.com/it/news/show/157688 |work=acmilan.com |publisher=Associazione Calcio Milan |access-date=16 June 2015|language=it}}</ref> During his tenure at the club, he was highly praised for trusting and giving playing opportunities to [[Gianluigi Donnarumma]], who was only 16 years old at the time.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/100256/%E2%80%98donnarumma-won%E2%80%99t-be-fazed%E2%80%99|title='Donnarumma won't be fazed' {{!}} Football Italia|website=Football-italia.net|access-date=28 March 2017}}</ref> Mihajlović was sacked on 12 April 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/82702/official-milan-sack-mihajlovic|title=Official: Milan sack Mihajlovic - Football Italia|website=Football-italia.net|date=12 April 2016 |access-date=7 July 2017}}</ref>

===Torino===

On 25 May 2016,  Mihajlović was officially appointed as the new manager of [[Torino FC|Torino]], taking over from [[Gian Piero Ventura]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/84911/official-miha-ventura-out-torino|title=Official: Miha in, Ventura out at Torino|date=25 May 2016|access-date=25 May 2016|publisher=Football Italia}}</ref> He made his debut on the ''Granata'' bench on 13 August 2016 at the [[Stadio Olimpico Grande Torino]] with a 4–1 home win over [[Pro Vercelli]] in the third round of the [[Coppa Italia]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://torinofc.it/news/13/08/2016/torino-pro-vercelli-4-1_12021|title=Torino-Pro Vercelli 4-1|website=TORINO FC 1906 SITO UFFICIALE}}</ref> Mihajlović fielded Torino with an aggressive 4-3-3 formation and by the midway point of the season registered a record for points (29) whilst under the presidency of [[Urbano Cairo]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://torinofc.it/news/09/01/2017/mihajlovic-servono-pi%C3%B9-cattiveria-e-lucidit%C3%A0_13490|title=Mihajlovic: "Servono più cattiveria e lucidità"|website=TORINO FC 1906 SITO UFFICIALE|date=6 November 2023 }}</ref> but a less brilliant second half of the season ended with Torino in ninth place. He was sacked on 4 January 2018 following a 2–0 defeat to Juventus in the Coppa Italia.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/115098/official-torino-sack-mihajlovic|title=Official: Torino sack Mihajlovic - Football Italia|website=football-italia.net|date=4 January 2018 }}</ref>

===Sporting CP===
On 18 June 2018, Mihajlović took over as manager of [[Sporting CP]], signing a three-year contract with the Portuguese club.<ref>{{Cite web | title = Sporting unveil Sinisa Mihajlovic as coach to defuse crisis | work = The Times of India| date = 18 June 2018 | access-date = 18 June 2018 | url = https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/top-stories/sporting-unveil-sinisa-mihajlovic-as-coach-to-defuse-crisis/articleshow/64634660.cms}}</ref> Nine days after his arrival, he was sacked due to change of executive staff.<ref name="SportingSacked18">{{cite news |title=Sporting Lisbon: Sinisa Mihajlovic sacked after just nine days |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/44637931 |access-date=29 June 2018 |work=bbc.com |date=27 June 2018}}</ref>

===Return to Bologna===
On 28 January 2019, Bologna parted ways with [[Filippo Inzaghi]] due to a series of poor results, and Mihajlović took over at the club for the second time in his managerial career.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bologna: esonerato Inzaghi. Mihajlovic è il nuovo tecnico |url=https://www.repubblica.it/sport/calcio/serie-a/bologna/2019/01/28/news/bologna_inzaghi_verso_l_esonero_mihajlovic_in_pole-217665789/ |date=28 January 2019 |access-date=28 January 2019 |work=Repubblica.it}}</ref>

The team scored 30 points in his first 17 games, in comparison with 14 points achieved under Inzaghi; thanks to those results, Mihajlović managed to keep Bologna into the top flight with ease, and he was retained as manager for the following season.

On 13 July 2019, Mihajlović announced that he had been diagnosed with an acute form of [[leukemia]], but that he planned to stay in charge of the club while undergoing treatment.<ref name=leukemia>{{cite news |url=https://www.football-italia.net/140736/live-mihajlovic-i-have-leukemia |publisher=Football Italia |access-date=13 July 2019 |date=13 July 2019 |title=Mihajlovic: 'I have leukemia'}}</ref>

Mihajlović was sacked on 6 September 2022, after Bologna secured only three points from its first five matches in [[2022–23 Serie A|Serie A]], ending his three-and-a-half-year spell with the club.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sport |first=Redazione |date=9 June 2022 |title=Mihajlovic esonerato dal Bologna: per i rossoblu 3 punti in 5 gare |url=https://www.corriere.it/sport/calcio/serie-a/22_settembre_06/mihajlovic-esonero-bologna-8e02eef8-2d34-11ed-82e8-8adda605a86c.shtml |access-date=6 September 2022 |website=Corriere della Sera |language=it-IT}}</ref>

==Controversies==
===As a player===
Mihajlović developed and fostered a reputation as a hard-nosed, tough-tackling player with a short fuse and no fear. As such he had many physical and verbal run-ins with opposing players that occasionally spilled outside of the pitch.{{citation needed|date=March 2012}}<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bergamopost.it/chi-e/mihajlovic-il-burbero-che-tutti-vogliono/|title=Sinisa, il burbero che tutti vogliono|trans-title=Sinisa, the tough guy that everyone wants|work=Bergamo Post|language=it|date=16 April 2015|access-date=26 August 2015}}</ref>

Already known as a player not backing away from physical play, the 22-year-old was one of the main protagonists of the ill-tempered [[1991 Yugoslav Cup Final]] between Red Star and Hajduk Split on 8 May 1991 at the [[JNA Stadium]] in front of 7,000 spectators.<ref name="Kup-1991">{{cite web|url=https://mondo.rs/Sport/Fudbal/a1468737/finale-kup-marsala-tita-crvena-zvezda-hajduk-split-godisnjica-30-godina.html|title=Jugoslavija se raspadala na JNA, a Hajduk Zvezdi odneo i sakrio pehar: 30 godina od poslednjeg finala Kupa maršala Tita!|publisher=Mondo.rs|language=sr|date=8 May 2021|access-date=8 May 2021}}</ref> Although of secondary importance to Red Star, which was getting ready for the European Cup Final three weeks later, the match still featured a degree of tension due to pitting a Serbian side against a Croatian one in an atmosphere of inter-ethnic incidents between Croats and [[Serbs of Croatia|Croatian Serbs]] in eastern [[Slavonia]] and [[Dalmatia]] regions of SR Croatia, including Mihajlović's hometown Borovo that saw a [[Battle of Borovo Selo|massacre]] only six days before the final. Early in the match Hajduk's 23-year-old defender [[Igor Štimac]] and Mihajlović began insulting each other, and according to Mihajlović during one of their exchanges Štimac told him: "I hope our guys kill all of your family in Borovo."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XvxIsjkj3GE#t=1922s |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211212/XvxIsjkj3GE| archive-date=12 December 2021 |url-status=live|title=TifoTV SERIES .. HAJDUKOV RATNI TROFEJ|last=Ultras Channel TifoTV|date=21 August 2012|publisher=YouTube|access-date=7 July 2017}}{{cbignore}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.alo.rs/sport/48907/Sprema_se_novi_duel_Miha_vs_Stimac |title=Alo | Sport | Sprema se novi duel Miha vs Štimac! |access-date=5 May 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120508042819/http://www.alo.rs/sport/48907/Sprema_se_novi_duel_Miha_vs_Stimac|archive-date=8 May 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://mondo.rs/Sport/Fudbal/a1397055/sinisa-mihajlovic-igor-stimac-arkan-pretnje-smrcu.html|title=Mihajlović o poseti Arkanovoj vili i pretnjama smrću: Štimac mi je u tunelu rekao da se moli Bogu za smrt moje porodice!|publisher=Mondo.rs|language=sr|date=12 November 2020|access-date=8 May 2021}}</ref> In the 70th minute Mihajlović slid in for a hard tackle on another Hajduk player [[Grgica Kovač]] that led to play temporarily being stopped as both sets of players confronted each other. Mihajlović was led away by Hajduk player [[Ante Miše]] (the two knew each other as they were both from Borovo) who grabbed him by the hair while Red Star's [[Ilija Najdoski]] grabbed Hajduk's [[Slaven Bilić]] by the hair at which point Štimac jumped into the fracas with a raised fist attempting to punch Najdoski. Mihajlović received a second yellow for the challenge on Kovač, and the referee Adem Fazlagić also gave Štimac a second yellow, which meant both players got sent off.<ref name="Kup-1991"/>

Several years later, in October 2000, Mihajlović raised a storm of controversy due to allegedly directing racist remarks at [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]]'s [[Patrick Vieira]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Stefano|last=Boldrini|url=http://archiviostorico.corriere.it/2000/ottobre/19/Mihajlovic_gli_insulti_razzisti_Non_co_0_001019839.shtml|title=Mihajlovic e gli insulti razzisti: "Non mi pento"|trans-title=Mihajlovic and his racist insults: "I don't regret them"|publisher=[[Corriere della Sera]]|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20091213055725/http://archiviostorico.corriere.it/2000/ottobre/19/Mihajlovic_gli_insulti_razzisti_Non_co_0_001019839.shtml|language=it|date=19 October 2000|access-date=26 August 2015|archivedate=13 December 2009|url-status=dead}}</ref> The incident occurred during an ill-tempered Lazio vs Arsenal [[2000–01 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] [[2000–01 UEFA Champions League first group stage#Lazio v Arsenal|match]] on 17 October 2000 at [[Stadio Olimpico]]. Throughout the contest, Mihajlović had run-ins with several Arsenal players, including [[Martin Keown]] and [[Robert Pires]]. After the final whistle, Mihajlović and Vieira were seen trading insults and trying to get at one another physically before being restrained by teammates. After the match, Vieira spoke to the media, accusing Mihajlović of [[Racism in association football|racist]] abuse, saying that Mihajlović had called him "nero di merda" (black piece of shit) or "fucking black monkey."<ref name="auto">{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2003/nov/06/sport.comment1|title=Is Sinisa Mihajlovic the nastiest man in football?|first1=Matt|last1=Scott|first2=Ian|last2=Traynor|date=6 November 2003|website=The Guardian|access-date=29 August 2019}}</ref> Mihajlović subsequently apologized, but contended that his words were in retaliation to Vieira calling him a "zingaro di merda" ([[Antiziganism|Gypsy piece of shit]]).<ref name = "marcotti">{{cite web|author=[[Gabriele Marcotti]]|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/inside_game/gabriele_marcotti/news/2001/01/02/marcotti_insider/|title=Making Mihajlovic into a villain not really fair|publisher=[[CNNSI.com]]|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20010124064900/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/inside_game/gabriele_marcotti/news/2001/01/02/marcotti_insider/|date=2 January 2001|access-date=17 December 2022|archivedate=24 January 2001|url-status=dead}}</ref> Two months later, in December 2000, Mihajlović came under police investigation over the event for possibly violating an anti-racism law in Italy. Italian investigators planned on using Mihajlović's own post-game admission about insulting Vieira to file charges of violating a 1993 law that criminalizes the "spreading ... of ideas based on racial or ethnic superiority or hate",<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/soccer/news/2000/12/22/lazio_racism_ap/|title=Possible conviction: Lazio star faces criminal charges for racist episode|publisher=[[CNNSI.com]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20010124040200/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/soccer/news/2000/12/22/lazio_racism_ap/|date=22 December 2000|access-date=17 December 2022|archivedate=24 January 2001|url-status=dead}}</ref> but no charges were made. Six years later Mihajlović and Vieira became part of the same team when the Senegalese-born Frenchman joined Inter where Mihajlović was already assistant to head coach Roberto Mancini. Vieira was later one of the guests for Mihajlović's [[testimonial match]] on 28 May 2007 in [[Novi Sad]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eGjHZ41V-b4#t=4908s |title=YouTube|website=Youtube.com|access-date=7 July 2017}}</ref>

On 7 November 2003, Mihajlović received an eight-match suspension by [[UEFA]] for spitting at and kicking [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]'s [[Adrian Mutu]] during a [[2003–04 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] [[2003–04 UEFA Champions League group stage#Lazio v Chelsea|group stage match]].<ref>[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/champions_league/3251405.stm Uefa bans Mihajlovic], BBC Sport, 7 November 2003</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.repubblica.it/2003/k/sezioni/sport/calcio/champions_league/miha/miha/miha.html|title=Mihajlovic, otto turni di stop per lo sputo in Champions League|trans-title=Mihajlovic, eight match suspension for spitting in the Champions League|publisher=La Repubblica|language=it|date=7 November 2003|access-date=26 August 2015}}</ref> Six and a half years later, Mihajlović became the head coach of [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]], where Mutu was playing at the time.

===As a manager===
A vocal and outspoken presence, known for his leadership,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.repubblica.it/sport/calcio/serie-a/milan/2015/08/16/news/milan_mihajlovic_cita_boniperti_conta_solo_vincere_-121074984/|title=Mihajlovic si prende il Milan: ''Sarò io il tuo leader''|publisher=La Repubblica|language=it|author1=STEFANO SCACCHI|date=16 August 2015|access-date=10 December 2016}}</ref> Mihajlović attracted much controversy throughout both his playing and coaching careers, for his political views and affiliations.<ref name="Bologna, ecco Mihajlovic"/><ref name="auto"/>

Amid [[Javier Clemente]]'s failure to qualify the [[Serbia national football team|Serbia national team]] for [[Euro 2008]], and Serbian press reports that then [[Inter Milan]] assistant coach Mihajlović was set to take over,<ref>[http://www.pressonline.rs/sport/ostali-sportovi/19378/sinisa-selektor-srbije.html SINIŠA SELEKTOR SRBIJE!];''Press'', 5 September 2007</ref> Mihajlović publicly came out against the [[Football Association of Serbia|Serbia FA]] (FSS) president [[Zvezdan Terzić]], accusing him in October 2007 of "giving national team call-ups to players [he had private contracts with] in order to boost their transfer value".<ref>[http://www.b92.net/info/vesti/index.php?yyyy=2011&mm=01&dd=16&nav_category=120&nav_id=486201 Počinje suđenje Zvezdanu Terziću];B92, 16 January 2011</ref> Terzić did not directly respond to the accusation, which Mihajlović repeated several months later during early March 2008 in the wake of Terzić's time on the run from Serbian law enforcement over accusations of player transfer fee skimming.<ref>[http://www.pressonline.rs/sport/ostali-sportovi/31458/terzic-me-ucenjivao.html TERZIĆ ME UCENJIVAO!];''[[Press (Belgrade newspaper)|Press]]'', 5 March 2008</ref>

In May 2012, Mihajlović landed the Serbia national team head coaching job (under the new FA president [[Tomislav Karadžić]]) and instituted a new code-of-conduct to be signed by players called up for international duty. One of the central points was his insistence that players sing the national anthem before matches. On 28 May, after [[Adem Ljajić]] failed to do so despite signing the code-of-conduct, Mihajlović removed him from the national team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.repubblica.it/sport/calcio/esteri/2012/05/28/news/serbia_ljajic-36082513/|title=Ljajic non canta l'inno Mihajlovic lo caccia|trans-title=Ljajic doesn't sing the national anthem Mihajlovic sends him away|publisher=La Repubblica|language=it|date=28 May 2012|access-date=26 August 2015}}</ref>

In December 2012, Mihajlović sued [[Sports agent#Association football|football agent]] Zoran Đurić for libel over his claims expressed during SOS channel's ''Total Soccer'' programme that "sports agents Fali Ramadani and [[Sergio Berti]] have a large influence on Mihajlović's national team squad selection".<ref>[http://www.b92.net/sport/fudbal/vesti.php?yyyy=2012&mm=12&dd=07&nav_id=667085 Miha tuži menadžera zbog Faljija];B92, 7 December 2012</ref><ref>[http://www.kurir-info.rs/mihajlovic-tuzi-menadzera-zbog-dusevnog-bola-clanak-549347 Mihajlović tuži menadžera zbog duševnog bola];''Kurir'', 7 December 2012</ref>

In late March 2013, in the wake of the [[2014 FIFA World Cup]] [[2014 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group A|qualifier]] loss to Croatia, Mihajlović and Terzić reignited their public feud from six years prior, with the former Serbian FA president—who had in the meantime returned to the country from being on the run and completed a prison term following a plea deal—repeating Đurić's accusation about Mihajlović having "his national team match day squads selected by Sergio Berti".<ref>[http://www.kurir-info.rs/menadzeri-su-nam-upropastili-fudbal-clanak-711395 Menadžeri su nam upropastili fudbal!];''Kurir'', 24 March 2013</ref> Mihajlović announced plans to sue Terzić for libel over the remark.<ref>[http://sport.blic.rs/Fudbal/Svetski-fudbal/230491/Mihajlovic-Tuzicu-Terzica-zato-sto-je-rekao-da-mi-Serdjo-Berti-sastavlja-tim Mihajlović: Tužiću Terzića zato što je rekao da mi Serđo Berti sastavlja tim];''Blic'', 26 March 2013</ref>

==Personal life and death==
Mihajlović was married to Arianna Rapaccioni, an Italian former television presenter, with whom he had five children: three sons and two daughters.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ilsecoloxix.it/sport/2013/11/14/news/sinisa-e-la-moglieil-punto-di-forza-1.32343811|title=Sinisa? È la moglieil punto di forza|publisher=ilsecoloxix.it|date=14 November 2013|language=it}}</ref> On 13 July 2019, Mihajlović announced that he had been diagnosed with an acute form of [[leukemia]], but would stay on as manager of Bologna.<ref name=leukemia/> He underwent a [[bone marrow transplant]] after three cycles of chemotherapy.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/148259/mihajlovic-every-moment-priceless|title=Mihajlovic: 'Every moment priceless'|publisher=Football Italia|date=4 January 2020}}</ref>

In October 2021, he became a grandfather, after his daughter Virginia gave birth to a daughter. The father is [[Alessandro Vogliacco]], who, at the time, played for [[Genoa CFC|Genoa]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sport.sky.it/calcio/serie-a/2021/10/28/virginia-mihajlovic-figlia-sinisa-mamma |publisher=SKY Sport |language=it |access-date=25 November 2021 |date=28 October 2021 |title=Sinisa Mihajlovic è nonno: la figlia Virginia è diventata mamma di Violante}}</ref>

Mihajlović died on 16 December 2022 at a clinic in [[Rome]], following complications of leukemia.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Serie-A/16-12-2022/morto-sinisa-mihajlovic-aveva-53-anni-2019-era-malato-leucemia-4501530840933.shtml |publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport |language=it |title=Addio a Mihajlovic, il duro dal cuore grande: è morto di leucemia a 53 anni|date=16 December 2022}}</ref><ref name="AP-Obit">{{cite news |title=Siniša Mihajlović, soccer player and coach, dies at 53 |url=https://apnews.com/article/world-cup-sports-soccer-rome-leukemia-ab738ef546fa9460bdbfa3fff708f7a5 |access-date=16 December 2022 |work=AP NEWS |date=16 December 2022 |language=en}}</ref>

'''Giovanni "Gio" Alejandro Reyna ''' (born November 13, 2002) is an American professional [[Association football|soccer]] player<!--Do not change to "football". Wikipedia articles are written in the style of English most associated with the subject, and as Reyna is American, please use American English --> who plays as an [[attacking midfielder]] for [[Ligue 1]] club [[RC Strasbourg Alsace|Strasbourg]] and the [[United States men's national soccer team|United States national team]].

Reyna began his youth career with his hometown club, [[New York City FC]], and had his breakthrough with Bundesliga club [[Borussia Dortmund]]. During the [[2019–20 DFB-Pokal]] he became the youngest scorer in the German Cup's history at the age of 17, and was a part of the team that won the following [[2020–21 DFB-Pokal]].<ref name="CBS" /> In 2020 he became the youngest Bundesliga player to create a hat trick of assists.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gio Reyna makes history with assist hat-trick for Borussia Dortmund |url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/gio-reyna-makes-history-assist-hat-trick-for-borussia-dortmund-usa-usmnt-13112 |access-date=June 6, 2023 |website=bundesliga.com - the official Bundesliga website |language=en}}</ref> He was on the final shortlist of the 2021 [[Kopa Trophy]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |date=November 23, 2021 |title=Pedri wins prestigious Golden Boy award for 2021 |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/soccer/news/golden-boy-award-2021-pedri-full-list-rankings |access-date=October 15, 2023 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> He moved to Borussia Mönchengladbach in August 2025.

Born to U.S. national team players [[Claudio Reyna]] and [[Danielle Reyna]], he has represented the United States at several youth levels, scoring 16 goals in 31 youth caps. Reyna made his debut for the senior team in November 2020 and won the [[CONCACAF Nations League]] in [[2021 CONCACAF Nations League Finals|2021]], [[2023 CONCACAF Nations League Finals|2023]], and [[2024 CONCACAF Nations League Finals|2024]], winning the best player overall of the latter.<ref name=":1" /> Individually he won a [[U.S. Soccer Player of the Year|U.S. Soccer Young Male Player of the Year]] award in 2020.

==Early life==
Reyna was born in [[Sunderland|Sunderland, England]], to American parents, [[Claudio Reyna]] and [[Danielle Reyna]], when his father was playing for [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]]. Both of his parents are former soccer players, who played for the United States [[United States men's national soccer team|men's]] and [[United States women's national soccer team|women's]] national teams, respectively. His family moved back to the United States, settling in [[Bedford (town), New York|Bedford, New York]], in 2007 when Reyna was five years old.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://jr10corp.com/pages/about-jr10-corp |title=ABOUT JR10 CORP - Jr10clothing |access-date=August 17, 2021 |archive-date=September 18, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210918131841/https://jr10corp.com/pages/about-jr10-corp |url-status=dead }}</ref> He joined the academy team of his hometown club, [[New York City FC]], in 2015 and kept playing with the City academy teams until 2019, when he moved to [[Germany]] to join [[Borussia Dortmund]]'s academy.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dortmund sign U.S. youth Gio Reyna from NYCFC |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/soccer-transfers/story/3890386/dortmund-sign-us-youth-gio-reyna-from-nycfc |website=ESPN FC |access-date=May 25, 2020 |date=July 1, 2019 |archive-date=July 30, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190730173218/https://www.espn.com/soccer/soccer-transfers/story/3890386/dortmund-sign-us-youth-gio-reyna-from-nycfc |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Club career==
===Borussia Dortmund===
====2019–20 season: Breakthrough====
On January 18, 2020, Reyna made his [[Bundesliga]] debut for [[Borussia Dortmund]], coming on as a substitute in the 72nd minute, in a 5–3 win against [[FC Augsburg]].<ref name="mlssoccer">{{cite web|url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2020/01/18/new-york-city-fc-academy-alum-giovanni-reyna-makes-bundesliga-debut-borussia|title=New York City FC academy alum Giovanni Reyna makes Bundesliga debut in Borussia Dortmund win|website=mlssoccer.com|date=January 18, 2020|access-date=January 18, 2020|archive-date=February 6, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200206131154/https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2020/01/18/new-york-city-fc-academy-alum-giovanni-reyna-makes-bundesliga-debut-borussia|url-status=live}}</ref> Hence, he became the youngest American, aged 17 years and 66 days, ever to appear in the Bundesliga, breaking a record previously set by [[Christian Pulisic]].<ref name="mlssoccer" />

On February 4, Reyna scored his first professional goal in a 3–2 defeat to [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]] in the [[2019–20 DFB-Pokal|DFB-Pokal]] Round of 16.<ref name="CBS" /> In doing so, he became the youngest goalscorer in [[DFB-Pokal|German Cup]] history.<ref name="CBS">{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/soccer/news/gio-reyna-rising-u-s-soccer-star-scores-gorgeous-strike-for-first-professional-goal-with-dortmund/|title=Gio Reyna, rising U.S. soccer star, scores gorgeous strike for first professional goal with Dortmund|website=CBS Sports|date=February 4, 2020|access-date=February 5, 2020|archive-date=February 6, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200206013615/https://www.cbssports.com/soccer/news/gio-reyna-rising-u-s-soccer-star-scores-gorgeous-strike-for-first-professional-goal-with-dortmund/|url-status=live}}</ref> On February 18, 2020, Reyna became the third-youngest player ever to appear in a knockout game of the [[UEFA Champions League]] when he came on as a substitute in the 67th minute against [[Paris Saint-Germain]]. Nine minutes later, Reyna set up [[Erling Haaland]]'s game-winning goal for Borussia Dortmund in the first leg of the Round of 16, becoming the youngest American to play and record an assist in a Champions League fixture.<ref>{{Cite web|title=USA teenager Gio Reyna overtakes Christian Pulisic in Borussia Dortmund and UEFA Champions League history books|url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/gio-reyna-makes-champions-league-history-with-debut-assist-overtakes-pulisic-dortmund-psg-10029|access-date=May 15, 2021|website=bundesliga.com - the official Bundesliga website|language=en|archive-date=May 15, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210515015330/https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/gio-reyna-makes-champions-league-history-with-debut-assist-overtakes-pulisic-dortmund-psg-10029|url-status=live}}</ref>

On May 16, Reyna was set to start his first Bundesliga match for Borussia Dortmund in their derby against [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]], but suffered a calf injury during warm-ups.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hamilton |first1=Tom |title=Dortmund, USMNT prospect Giovanni Reyna injured when set for first start |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/borussia-dortmund/story/4095121/dortmundusmnt-prospect-giovanni-reyna-injured-when-set-for-first-start |website=ESPN |access-date=May 16, 2020 |date=May 16, 2020 |archive-date=May 16, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200516200230/https://www.espn.com/soccer/borussia-dortmund/story/4095121/dortmundusmnt-prospect-giovanni-reyna-injured-when-set-for-first-start |url-status=live }}</ref> Reyna returned on May 23 and played in the final 11 minutes of a 2–0 victory at [[VfL Wolfsburg]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Uersfeld |first1=Stephan |date=May 22, 2020 |title=USMNT hopeful Gio Reyna back for Dortmund, Favre admits Bundesliga return a 'danger' |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/borussia-dortmund/story/4098146/usmnt-hopeful-gio-reyna-back-for-dortmundfavre-admits-return-a-danger |access-date=May 24, 2020 |website=ESPN FC}}</ref>

==== 2020–21 season: DFB-Pokal win ====

On September 14, 2020, Reyna started in a [[DFB-Pokal]] match and scored with a free kick in a 5–0 win against [[MSV Duisburg]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Meyers |first=Brian |date=September 14, 2020 |title=BVB Post Match Report: BVB dismantle Duisburg 5-0 |url=https://www.fearthewall.com/2020/9/14/21436817/bvb-post-match-report-bvb-dismantle-duisburg-5-0 |access-date=September 17, 2020 second youngest American scorer in Bundesliga history behind [[Christian Pulisic]], who was aged 17 years and 211 days.<ref>{{cite web |date=September 19, 2020 |title=WATCH: Gio Reyna scores first career Bundesliga goal |url=https://www.starsandstripesfc.com/2020/9/19/21446787/watch-gio-reyna-scores-first-career-bundesliga-goal |website=Stars and Stripes FC |access-date=September 19, 2020 |archive-date=September 23, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200923205251/https://www.starsandstripesfc.com/2020/9/19/21446787/watch-gio-reyna-scores-first-career-bundesliga-goal |url-status=live }}</ref>[[File:Borussia Dortmund vs FC Zenit 10-28-2020 (1).jpg|thumb|Reyna playing for Dortmund in 2020.]]On October 3, 2020, in his third league appearance of the 2020–21 season, Reyna assisted 3 goals—a brace to [[Erling Haaland]] and an [[Emre Can]] header from a corner kick, to beat [[SC Freiburg]] 4–0.<ref>{{Cite web|agency=Associated Press|date=October 3, 2020|title=Reyna Bundesliga.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dortmund teenager Reyna makes history with three-assist display against Freiburg {{!}} On December 5, Reyna scored his second [[Bundesliga]] goal against [[Eintracht Frankfurt]], with a near post finish just inside the 18-yard box. This goal made him the second youngest American to score twice in the league after [[Christian Pulisic]] did so for the same club as Reyna, [[Borussia Dortmund]].<ref>{{Cite magazine|last=Jackson|first=Wilton|title=USMNT's Reyna Scores Stunner for Dortmund|url=https://www.si.com/soccer/2020/12/05/gio-reyna-scores-second-bundesliga-goal-dortmund-video|access-date=December 5, 2020|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=December 5, 2020|language=en-us|archive-date=December 5, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201205180010/https://www.si.com/soccer/2020/12/05/gio-reyna-scores-second-bundesliga-goal-dortmund-video|url-status=live}}</ref> On December 22, he was voted the U.S. Soccer's Young Male Player of the Year for 2020.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=December 22, 2020|title=Dortmund's Gio Reyna named U.S. Soccer's Young Male Player of the Year|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/united-states-usa/story/4271615/dortmunds-gio-reyna-named-us-soccers-young-male-player-of-the-year|access-date=December 22, 2020|website=ESPN|archive-date=February 13, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210213144615/https://www.espn.com/soccer/united-states-usa/story/4271615/dortmunds-gio-reyna-named-us-soccers-young-male-player-of-the-year|url-status=live}}</ref>

Reyna was a second-half substitute for Dortmund in their 4–1 victory over [[RB Leipzig]] in the [[2021 DFB-Pokal Final]] on May 13, 2021. His involvement in the match marked him as the youngest American to appear in a domestic cup final in Europe, a record previously held by his international teammate Christian Pulisic.<ref name=DFBW>{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/article/bundesliga-borussia-dortmund-dortmund-europe-leipzig-57d576ad46190c226251b8f92669dbf8|title=Borussia Dortmund beats Leipzig 4-1 in German Cup final|website=AP|date=May 13, 2021|access-date=May 14, 2021|archive-date=May 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210514002044/https://apnews.com/article/bundesliga-borussia-dortmund-dortmund-europe-leipzig-57d576ad46190c226251b8f92669dbf8|url-status=live}}</ref> For his strong youth performances, he was on the final shortlist for the 2021 [[Golden Boy (award)|Golden Boy]]; finishing 6th, and [[2021 Ballon d'Or|2021 Kopa Trophy]]; finishing 9th.<ref name=":3" />
