6, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241206113206/https://www.eurosport.com/football/bundesliga/2022-2023/borussia-dortmund-v-fc-augsburg-bundesliga-live_sto9338717/story.shtml |url-status=live }}</ref> Three days later, he scored another game-winning goal off the bench in stoppage time in the 93rd minute against [[Mainz 05]], winning 2–1.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 25, 2023 |title=WATCH: USMNT star Gio Reyna scores stoppage time winner for Dortmund vs Mainz |url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/usmnt-gio-reyna-scores-stoppage-time-winner-dortmund-vs-mainz/blt5610e7324c419ee3 |access-date=May 23, 2023 |website=www.goal.com |archive-date=June 20, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230620203021/https://www.goal.com/en-us/news/usmnt-gio-reyna-scores-stoppage-time-winner-dortmund-vs-mainz/blt5610e7324c419ee3 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Coming into his final season match against Mainz, Reyna had the second best minute-per-goal ratio of a [[Big Five (association football)|top five European league]] player for the 2022–23 season after [[Erling Haaland]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=20-year-old Gio Reyna assisted both of BVB's goals today while only being subbed on in the 63rd minute! |url=https://twitter.com/FOXSoccer/status/1662502581749559296?s=20 |access-date=May 28, 2023 |website=FOX Sports Twitter}}</ref> On May 27, during the final game of the [[2022–23 Bundesliga]] where Dortmund was in first place, Reyna came off the bench in the 63rd minute when Dortmund were 2–0 down against [[Mainz 05]] and created two assists to level the game 2–2. The game ended in a draw and Dortmund was the league runner-up to Bayern.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 27, 2023 |title=Dortmund throw away chance at Bundesliga title as USMNT's Gio Reyna is unable to save the day against Bayern |url=https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/dortmund-mainz-bundesliga-reyna-usmnt/blt454acff9ac212851 |access-date=May 27, 2023 |website=www.goal.com}}</ref> Reyna finished the season with four assists and his highest Bundesliga goal amount with seven goals, five of which were as a substitute.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Giovanni Reyna Stats - Goals, xG, Assists & xA |url=https://footystats.org/players/usa/giovanni-reyna |access-date=May 28, 2023 |website=footystats.org }}</ref>

==== 2024–2025: Loan and playtime decline ====
On January 31, 2024, Reyna extended his contract with Borussia Dortmund until June 30, 2026, and was subsequently loaned to [[Premier League]] club [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] until the end of the [[2023–24 Nottingham Forest F.C. season|2023–24 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=January 31, 2024 |title=Reyna verlängert und wechselt bis Saisonende nach England |trans-title=Reyna extends and moves to England until the end of the season |url=http://www.bvb.de/ger/News/Uebersicht/Reyna-verlaengert-und-wechselt-bis-Saisonende-nach-England/ |access-date=January 31, 2024 |publisher=Borussia Dortmund |language=de |archive-date=February 6, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240206030556/https://www.bvb.de/ger/News/Uebersicht/Reyna-verlaengert-und-wechselt-bis-Saisonende-nach-England/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=January 31, 2024 |title=Forest complete Gio Reyna signing |url=https://www.nottinghamforest.co.uk/news/2024/january/31/forest-complete-gio-reyna-signing/ |access-date=January 31, 2024 |website= |publisher=Nottingham Forest F.C. |archive-date=January 31, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240131213102/https://www.nottinghamforest.co.uk/news/2024/january/31/forest-complete-gio-reyna-signing/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

He made his debut for Forest as a 78th-minute substitute for [[Anthony Elanga]] in a 1–1 draw against [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]] in the [[2023–24 Premier League|Premier League]] on February 4.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68120825|title=AFC Bournemouth 1-1 Nottm Forest|website=BBC Sport|date=February 4, 2024|access-date=February 4, 2024|archive-date=February 26, 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240226080153/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/68120825|url-status=live}}</ref> On April 13, Reyna recorded an assist against [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] in his first start of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 13, 2024 |title=Gio Reyna makes huge statement as USMNT star provides big assist against Wolves in first Nottingham Forest start |url=https://www.goal.com/en-in/lists/gio-reyna-usmnt-nottingham-forest-wolves-assist/bltade0ad9d9fa59a73 |access-date=April 14, 2024 |website=www.goal.com}}</ref> He ultimately only featured in 10 matches for Forest and returned to Dortmund, finishing the 2023–24 season with no goals for both clubs.

Reyna played only sporadically throughout the [[2024–25 Borussia Dortmund season|2024–25 season]], playing only 341 league minutes and scoring two goals with one assist.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 21, 2025 |title=Career crossroads: As Dortmund's Gio Reyna seeks an express lane out of limbo, it's possible a soccer-free summer is exactly what 22-year-old USMNT midfielder needs {{!}} Goal.com US |url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/lists/as-dortmund-s-gio-reyna-looks-for-an-express-lane-out-of-career-limbo-it-s-possible-soccer-free-summer-is-exactly-what-22-year-old-usmnt-midfielder-needs/blta63b6acdf1d63da3 |access-date=May 22, 2025 |website=www.goal.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Borussia Mönchengladbach ===
On August 23, 2025, Reyna made a permanent move to [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]] until 2028 for around €7 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=read |first=Bulinews·1 min |date=August 23, 2025 |title=Official: Gio Reyna joins Borussia Mönchengladbach |url=https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/news/official-gio-reyna-joins-borussia-155800206.html |access-date=August 23, 2025 |website=Yahoo Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club in the stoppage time of a 3–1 away defeat against FC Augsburg on May 9, 2026.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/match/_/gameId/747009/borussia-monchengladbach-fc-augsburg |title=FC Augsburg 3–1 Borussia Mönchengladbach |publisher=ESPN |date=May 9, 2026 }}</ref> However, his debut season at the club was hampered by recurring injuries and inconsistent minutes, as he managed only four league starts and one goal across all competitions.<ref>{{cite web |last=Carlisle |first=Jeff |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/48911140/usa-gio-reyna-mature-controversy-world-cup-2022-2026 |title='Matured' Gio Reyna tired of discussing World Cup controversy |publisher=ESPN |date=May 29, 2026 |access-date=May 30, 2026 |archive-date=May 31, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260531071617/https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/48911140/usa-gio-reyna-mature-controversy-world-cup-2022-2026 |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Strasbourg ===
On 4 August 2026, Reyna joined [[Ligue 1]] club [[RC Strasbourg Alsace|Strasbourg]], signing a contract until 2031.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.getfootballnewsfrance.com/2026/official-strasbourg-sign-borussia-monchengladbach-attacking-midfielder-giovanni-reyna/ |title=Official {{!}} Strasbourg sign Borussia Mönchengladbach attacking midfielder Giovanni Reyna |publisher=Get Football News France |date=4 August 2026 }}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Gio Reyna USMNT v Belgium Mar 28 2026-194.jpg|thumb|upright|Reyna in 2026]]
After representing the United States at several youth levels, Reyna received his first call up to the senior [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]] squad for matches against [[Wales national football team|Wales]] and [[Panama national football team|Panama]] in November 2020.<ref name=":1">{{cite web |url=https://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2020/11/usmnt-roster-announcement-berhalter-24-players-november-camp-friendlies-wales-panama |title=USMNT ROSTER ANNOUNCEMENT: BERHALTER CALLS 24 PLAYERS FOR NOVEMBER CAMP MATCHES VS WALES AND PANAMA |date=November 3, 2020 |publisher=ussoccer.com |access-date=November 3, 2020 |archive-date=February 28, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210228013445/https://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2020/11/usmnt-roster-announcement-berhalter-24-players-november-camp-friendlies-wales-panama |url-status=live }}</ref> On November 12, 2020, a day before his 18th birthday, Reyna made his senior national team debut against Wales.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2020/11/usmnt-0-wales-0-match-report-stats|title=USA 0 - Wales 0: Match Report & Stats|access-date=November 15, 2020|archive-date=February 28, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210228012738/https://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2020/11/usmnt-0-wales-0-match-report-stats|url-status=live}}</ref> In the following game, a 6–2 friendly victory over Panama, Reyna started and scored his first senior goal directly from a free kick.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2020/11/usmnt-6-panama-2-match-report-stats|title=USA 6 - Panama 2: Match Report & Stats|access-date=November 17, 2020|archive-date=January 20, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210120174409/https://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2020/11/usmnt-6-panama-2-match-report-stats|url-status=live}}</ref>

In 2021, Reyna won the inaugural [[2019–20 CONCACAF Nations League|CONCACAF Nations League]] and scored in the 3–2 victory against [[Mexico–United States soccer rivalry|rivals]] [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]] in [[2021 CONCACAF Nations League final|the final]].<ref name=":2" />

On March 24, 2022, during a third-round [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification – CONCACAF third round#Matchday 12|2022 World Cup qualification match]] against [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]] at [[Estadio Azteca]], Reyna dribbled past six Mexican defenders in a single run before being dispossessed; after the match it was compared to [[Diego Maradona]]'s "Goal of the Century" run during the quarter-finals of the [[Argentina v England (1986 FIFA World Cup)|1986 World Cup]], which was also at the Azteca.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Creditor |first=Avi |title=USMNT's Reyna Dazzles With Slaloming Dribble vs. Mexico |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/2022/03/25/gio-reyna-dribble-usmnt-mexico-video-world-cup-qualifying |access-date=September 10, 2022 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |date=March 25, 2022 |language=en-us}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=mlssoccer |title=USMNT's Gio Reyna draws Maradona comparison after solo run vs. Mexico {{!}} MLSSoccer.com |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/usmnt-s-gio-reyna-draws-maradona-comparison-after-solo-run-vs-mexico |access-date=September 10, 2022 |website=mlssoccer |language=en}}</ref>

In the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]], Reyna played only 52 minutes in four games. His sidelining throughout the group stage of the tournament led to speculation from analysts of possible issues within the team.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stejskal |first=Paul Tenorio and Sam |title=Gio Reyna minutes limited |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3991695/2022/12/11/gio-reyna-usmnt-gregg-berhalter/ |access-date=December 12, 2022 |website=The Athletic |language=en |archive-date=June 12, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240612170707/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3991695/2022/12/11/gio-reyna-usmnt-gregg-berhalter/ |url-status=live }}</ref> USMNT head coach [[Gregg Berhalter]] publicly addressed issues regarding an anonymous player for a lack of commitment and poor attitude, and confirmed that the team had held a meeting to determine if that player were to remain with the team in Qatar for the remainder of the tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://worldsoccertalk.com/news/gregg-berhalter-airs-out-dirty-laundry-on-gio-reyna-20221212-WST-412086.html|title=Gregg Berhalter airs dirty laundry on Gio Reyna|author=Kyle Fansler|website=worldsoccertalk.com|date=December 12, 2022|accessdate=January 4, 2023}}</ref> On December 12, 2022, Reyna confirmed that he was the aforementioned player about whom Berhalter was speaking, and apologized for his behavior while criticizing the decision to publicize the information.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gio Reyna criticizes Gregg Berhalter in Instagram post |url=https://worldsoccertalk.com/news/gio-reyna-criticizes-gregg-berhalter-in-instagram-post-20221212-WST-412150.html |access-date=January 4, 2023 |website=World Soccer Talk |date=December 12, 2022 |language=en |archive-date=January 4, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230104232736/https://worldsoccertalk.com/news/gio-reyna-criticizes-gregg-berhalter-in-instagram-post-20221212-WST-412150.html |url-status=live }}</ref> In January 2023, it was revealed that Berhalter had been confronted during the tournament about damaging personal information that was floated to superiors. [[Danielle Reyna]], Reyna's mother, confirmed that she was the one who informed the [[United States Soccer Federation|U.S. Soccer Federation]] about the episode of violent behavior between Berhalter and his wife from 1991.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 4, 2023 |title=Gio Reyna's mother gave USSF Berhalter info |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/united-states-usa/story/4844539/reynas-told-us-soccer-about-past-gregg-berhalter-domestic-violence-incident-sources |access-date=January 4, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |language=en |archive-date=May 10, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230510195129/https://www.espn.com/soccer/united-states-usa/story/4844539/reynas-told-us-soccer-about-past-gregg-berhalter-domestic-violence-incident-sources |url-status=live }}</ref> Ultimately this led to an investigation of Berhalter that found the incident to be isolated and no reason to not employ him as a coach.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Tenorio |first=Paul |date=March 26, 2024 |title=U.S. Soccer Gregg Berhalter investigation: What was found, Reynas' involvement and what's next |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4304622/2023/03/13/gregg-berhalter-us-soccer-investigation-explained/ |access-date=November 24, 2025 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331 |archive-date=February 28, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250228195606/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4304622/2023/03/13/gregg-berhalter-us-soccer-investigation-explained/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

During the [[2023 CONCACAF Nations League Finals|2023 CONCACAF Nations League]], Reyna recorded two assists in the United States' 2–0 victory over [[Canada men's national soccer team|Canada]] in the [[2023 CONCACAF Nations League final|final]], where he was named man of the match.<ref>{{Cite web |last=mlssoccer |title=USMNT Player Ratings: Gio Reyna dismantles Canada in Nations League final {{!}} MLSSoccer.com |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/usmnt-player-ratings-gio-reyna-dismantles-canada-in-nations-league-final |access-date=June 19, 2023 |website=mlssoccer |language=en |archive-date=June 19, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230619063211/https://www.mlssoccer.com/news/usmnt-player-ratings-gio-reyna-dismantles-canada-in-nations-league-final |url-status=live }}</ref> On October 17, 2023, he recorded his first international brace in a 4–0 friendly win over [[Ghana national football team|Ghana]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Goff |first=Steven |date=October 18, 2023 |title=Gio Reyna scores twice as the USMNT rolls to a rout of Ghana |language=en-US |newspaper=Washington Post |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2023/10/17/usmnt-ghana-gio-reyna/ |access-date=October 19, 2023 |issn=0190-8286}}</ref> During the [[2024 CONCACAF Nations League Finals]], Reyna assisted two goals in the United States' 3–1 semi-final victory over [[Jamaica national football team|Jamaica]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 22, 2024 |title='Gio Reyna's quality is unquestionable' - Gregg Berhalter fires back at critics after Nottingham Forest midfielder's two-assist masterclass against Jamaica in CONCACAF Nations League win {{!}} Goal.com US |url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/lists/gio-reyna-usmnt-gregg-berhalter-jamaica-concacaf-nations-league/blt14ed9b92b26a85cf |access-date=March 25, 2024 |website=www.goal.com |language=en-US |archive-date=March 25, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240325034210/https://www.goal.com/en-us/lists/gio-reyna-usmnt-gregg-berhalter-jamaica-concacaf-nations-league/blt14ed9b92b26a85cf |url-status=live }}</ref> In the following game, he scored in the 2–0 [[2024 CONCACAF Nations League final|final]] victory against [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]], again being named man of the match as well as the best player of the tournament.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.starsandstripesfc.com/2024/3/28/24114240/usa-usmnt-mexico-2024-concacaf-nations-league-finals-man-of-the-match-reyna-pulisic-adams |title=USA vs. Mexico, 2024 Concacaf Nations League Final: Man of the Match |publisher=Stars and Stripes FC |date=March 28, 2024 |access-date=May 30, 2026 |archive-date=September 19, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240919153114/https://www.starsandstripesfc.com/2024/3/28/24114240/usa-usmnt-mexico-2024-concacaf-nations-league-finals-man-of-the-match-reyna-pulisic-adams |url-status=live }}</ref>

On May 26, 2026, Reyna was named in the 26-man squad for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]] hosted on home soil.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2026/05/usmnt/us-mens-national-team-head-coach-mauricio-pochettino-names-26-player-roster-for-fifa-world-cup-2026 |title=U.S. Men's National Team Head Coach Mauricio Pochettino Names 26-Player Roster for FIFA World Cup 2026 |publisher=[[United States Soccer Federation]] |date=May 26, 2026 |access-date=May 26, 2026}}</ref> On June 12, 2026, Reyna scored a [[Curl (association football)|''trivela'']] in the last touch of the 4-1 win over [[Paraguay national football team|Paraguay]] in their opening match of the World Cup. <ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/soccer/story/2026-06-12/world-cup-united-states-win-paraguay-opener|title=Christian Pulisic, Folarin Balogun lead U.S. to impressive World Cup win over Paraguay |date=12 June 2026|access-date=12 June 2026|language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Giovanni is the son of former professional soccer player and [[United States men's national soccer team|United States men's national team]] player [[Claudio Reyna]],<ref name="US Soccer">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ussoccer.com/players/r/giovanni-reyna|title=Giovanni Reyna {{!}} U.S. Soccer Official Website|website=ussoccer.com|language=en|access-date=October 27, 2019|archive-date=October 31, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191031153335/https://www.ussoccer.com/players/r/giovanni-reyna|url-status=live}}</ref> and [[Danielle Reyna]], a former member of the [[United States women's national soccer team]].<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/gio-reyna-who-is-borussia-dortmund-s-latest-american-sensation-new-york-city-fc-3914 | title=Gio Reyna: Who is Borussia Dortmund's latest American sensation? | access-date=January 18, 2020 | website=bundesliga.com | archive-date=August 15, 2019 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190815053952/https://www.bundesliga.com/en/bundesliga/news/gio-reyna-who-is-borussia-dortmund-s-latest-american-sensation-new-york-city-fc-3914 | url-status=live }}</ref> Reyna is of Argentine-Portuguese descent through his father's parents and of [[Irish Americans|Irish-American]] descent through his mother.<ref name="Wahl 2018">{{cite magazine | last=Wahl | first=Grant | title=The Reyna Family's Story of Loss and Legacy | magazine=Sports Illustrated | date=December 12, 2018 | url=https://www.si.com/soccer/2018/12/12/claudio-reyna-family-jack-death-giovanni-dortmund | access-date=April 7, 2021 | archive-date=November 28, 2020 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201128204324/https://www.si.com/soccer/2018/12/12/claudio-reyna-family-jack-death-giovanni-dortmund | url-status=live }}</ref> His older brother, Jack, died of brain cancer in 2012, at the age of 13.<ref>{{cite magazine|title=The Reyna Family's Story of Loss and Legacy|url=https://www.si.com/soccer/2018/12/12/claudio-reyna-family-jack-death-giovanni-dortmund|access-date=November 29, 2022|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=December 12, 2018|first=Grant|last=Wahl|archive-date=November 28, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201128204324/https://www.si.com/soccer/2018/12/12/claudio-reyna-family-jack-death-giovanni-dortmund|url-status=live}}</ref>

Reyna started his international career by playing with the United States' youth teams, but after impressing with Borussia Dortmund, he attracted interest from the [[Portugal national football team|Portuguese]], [[England national football team|English]] and [[Argentina national football team|Argentine]] national teams.<ref>{{Cite web|title='The U.S. is my home' - Reyna shuts down reports of England call-up {{!}} Goal.com|url=https://www.goal.com/en-ph/news/the-us-is-my-home-reyna-shuts-down-reports-of-england-call/nmxe1kebyysf1169c3gxzuoug|access-date=March 26, 2021|website=www.goal.com|archive-date=July 17, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210717225454/https://www.goal.com/en-ph/news/the-us-is-my-home-reyna-shuts-down-reports-of-england-call/nmxe1kebyysf1169c3gxzuoug|url-status=live}}</ref> Ultimately, in a March 2020 interview with ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'', Reyna declared his intent to play for the United States: "I'm aware of the rumors, but it's quite clear for me. I only want to play for the United States. That's my home country."<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/2020/03/05/gio-reyna-usa-international-choice-borussia-dortmund |title=Gio Reyna Ends Faux Suspense Over His International 'Choice', Will Play for USA |website=si.com |date=March 5, 2020 |access-date=April 8, 2020 |archive-date=June 21, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200621140753/https://www.si.com/soccer/2020/03/05/gio-reyna-usa-international-choice-borussia-dortmund |url-status=live }}</ref>

He was named after his father's former [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] teammate [[Giovanni van Bronckhorst]].<ref name="US Soccer"/> His high level of play has earned him the nickname "The American Dream" from his former teammate [[Erling Haaland]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 21, 2020 |title=Erling Haaland Reveals Nickname for Wonderkid Teammate Gio Reyna |url=https://www.90min.com/posts/erling-haaland-nickname-wonderkid-gio-reyna |access-date=September 10, 2022 |website=90min.com |language=en-GB}}</ref> Reyna is close friends with United States teammate [[Joe Scally]]; both players began attending the New York City FC youth academy in 2015.<ref>{{Citation |title=Tim Ream INTERVIEWS Gio Reyna & Joe Scally 😂 {{!}} The American Dream |date=October 14, 2023 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=shIxbglFYc0 |access-date=November 13, 2023 |language=en |archive-date=November 13, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231113233335/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=shIxbglFYc0 |url-status=live }}</ref> Reyna is also close friends with his former Dortmund teammate, [[Jude Bellingham]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Clark |first1=Gill |title='Great memories' - Jude Bellingham hangs out with ex-Borussia Dortmund team-mates after Real Madrid Champions League triumph as he sends message to absent Gio Reyna |url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/lists/ude-bellingham-ex-borussia-dortmund-team-mates-real-madrid-champions-league-triumph-gio-reyna/blt188695391f818507 |website=Goal.com |access-date=June 26, 2026}}</ref>

Reyna married his wife Chloe Reyna (née Ortolano) in July 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mendez |first=Emmanuel |date=June 12, 2026 |title=Who Is Giovanni Reyna’s Wife? Meet Chloe Ortolano, a Former Soccer Player |url=https://athlonsports.com/soccer/who-giovanni-reynas-wife-chloe-ortolano-soccer-player}}</ref> In June 2026, he announced that Chloe was pregnant with their first child.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 13, 2026 |title=USA midfielder Gio Reyna reveals his wife is pregnant during goal celebration |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/sports/soccer/usa-midfielder-gio-reyna-reveals-wife-pregnant-goal-celebration-rcna349952}}</ref>

'''Aly Cissokho''' ({{IPA|fr|ali sisɔko}}, born 15 September 1987) is a French professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[left-back]] for [[Thai League 1]] club [[Lamphun Warriors F.C.|Lamphun Warriors]]. He has been described as a "sprightly left-back with good speed and stamina".<ref name="cissokho_uefa">{{cite web | url = http://www.uefa.com/teamsandplayers/players/player=250003441/profile/index.html | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20121103005805/http://www.uefa.com/teamsandplayers/players/player=250003441/profile/index.html | url-status = dead | archive-date = 3 November 2012 | title = Aly Cissokho | access-date =22 August 2010 | publisher=[[UEFA|Union of European Football Associations]] }}</ref>

Cissokho began his career playing for local clubs within his hometown, such as [[Blois Foot 41|Blois Foot]]. In 2004, he signed with professional club [[FC Gueugnon|Gueugnon]] and spent three years in the club's youth system before making his debut in the [[2006–07 Ligue 2|2006–07 season]]. He spent only one season at the club and, in June 2008, signed with Portuguese club [[Vitória F.C.|Vitória Setúbal]] in the [[Primeira Liga]]. After spending only half a season with the club, Cissokho departed Vitória for the league's [[2007–08 Primeira Liga|defending champions]] [[FC Porto|Porto]], where he won the Portuguese [[2008–09 Primeira Liga|league]] and [[2008–09 Taça de Portugal|cup]] [[Double (association football)|double]] and played in the [[UEFA Champions League]] for the first time. In July 2009, after a failed transfer attempt to Italian club [[A.C. Milan|AC Milan]], he signed a five-year contract with French club [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] for a fee of €15 million. At the beginning of the [[2012–13 Olympique Lyonnais season|2012–13 season]] Cissokho was sold to [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] and was subsequently loaned to [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] for the [[2013–14 Liverpool F.C. season|2013–14 season]].<ref>{{cite news | url = http://www.skysports.com/football/match_commentary/0,19764,11065_3260189,00.html | title = The complete guide to Aly Cissokho | access-date = 19 November 2013 | publisher = Sky Sports | date = 20 August 2013}}</ref>

Cissokho is also a [[France national football team|French international]] and earned his first call-up to the team in November 2009. He made his senior debut a year later in August 2010 in a [[Exhibition match|friendly match]] against [[Norway national football team|Norway]].<ref>{{cite news | url = http://www.skysports.com/football/match_commentary/0,19764,11065_3260189,00.html | title = Live Commentary: Norway 2 France 1 | access-date =22 August 2010 | publisher=[[Sky Sports]] | date=11 August 2010}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Early career===
Cissokho was born and raised in [[Blois]], the capital city of the [[Loir-et-Cher]] département, to Senegalese parents. He grew up learning the sport of [[association football|football]] from his three older brothers who are also football players. Mamadou, the eldest, and Demba remain in Blois playing for local amateur clubs AFM Blois and [[Blois Foot 41]], respectively, while [[Issa Cissokho (footballer)|Issa]] plays for professional club [[FC Nantes|Nantes]] in [[Ligue 1]].<ref name="cissokho_brothers">{{cite web | url = http://www.blois.maville.com/actu/actudet_-DU-BLOIS-FOOT-41-AU-FC-PORTO-_spo-814288_actu.Htm | title = Du Blois Foot 41 au FC Porto | access-date = 22 August 2010 | publisher = Blois Maville | language = fr | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20090411060245/http://www.blois.maville.com/actu/actudet_-DU-BLOIS-FOOT-41-AU-FC-PORTO-_spo-814288_actu.Htm | archive-date = 11 April 2009 | url-status = dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.nantes.maville.com/sport/fc-nantes-detail_-I.-Cissokho-signe-a-Nantes-K.-Diop-dans-le-viseur-colere-du-president-de-Carquefou_37314-1410426_actu.Htm | publisher = Nantes Maville | title = I. Cissokho signe à Nantes, K. Diop dans le viseur: colère du président de Carquefou | language = fr | date = 12 June 2010 | access-date = 23 April 2011 | archive-date = 17 June 2010 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20100617033721/http://www.nantes.maville.com/sport/fc-nantes-detail_-I.-Cissokho-signe-a-Nantes-K.-Diop-dans-le-viseur-colere-du-president-de-Carquefou_37314-1410426_actu.Htm | url-status = dead }}</ref>

Cissokho began his football career at the age of eight playing for AMJ Blois. He spent four years in the club's ''benjamins'' section and, in 1999, joined the biggest club in the city, Blois Foot 41. While at the club, Cissokho settled into his role as a left back with his coaches describing him as a player with great potential.<ref name="cissokho_brothers"/> Following his move from Porto to Lyon, Blois were compensated €162,500 due to an agreement Blois reached with both Gueugnon and Porto. The payment helped the club achieve some stability after a few years of financial difficulties.<ref>{{cite news|url = http://www.football.fr/footballfr/cmc/scanner/transferts/200941/aly-cissokho-permet-au-blois-foot-41-de-toucher-162-500-euros_74812.html?popup|archive-url = https://archive.today/20091125060800/http://www.football.fr/footballfr/cmc/scanner/transferts/200941/aly-cissokho-permet-au-blois-foot-41-de-toucher-162-500-euros_74812.html?popup|url-status = dead|archive-date = 25 November 2009|title=Aly Cissokho permet au Blois Foot 41 de toucher 162 500 euros |date=10 August 2009 |access-date=7 November 2009 |publisher=Football.fr | language = fr}}</ref> After four years at Blois, Cissokho had a year's stint at FCO [[Saint-Jean-de-la-Ruelle]]. In 2004, while playing with Saint-Jean-de-la-Ruelle, Cissokho was spotted by the assistant manager of professional club [[FC Gueugnon]] Jean Acédo who recommended the player join his club, who were playing in the second division of [[French football]], [[Ligue 2]].<ref name="cissokho_brothers"/> In July 2004, he signed with the club and was inserted into the club's youth academy.

After two years in the club's academy and another two years in the reserves, Cissokho made his professional debut on 25 May 2007 in a league match against [[FC Metz|Metz]]. He started and played the entire match in a 2–1 victory. Following the season, Cissokho signed his first professional contract agreeing to a three-year deal until June 2010. He was, subsequently, promoted to the senior team for the [[2007–08 Ligue 2|2007–08 season]] and assigned the number 3 shirt by manager Alain Ravera. Under Ravera, Cissokho struggled for playing time often being utilized as a substitute, however, after the sacking of Ravera in October 2007, he was inserted into the starting lineup by new manager [[Alex Dupont (footballer)|Alex Dupont]]. He appeared in 22 league matches during the campaign, starting in 15, but could not prevent Gueugnon from finishing last in the league, which meant relegation to the [[Championnat National]].

On 2 June 2008, [[Primeira Liga]] club [[Vitória F.C.|Vitória de Setúbal]] confirmed on its website that the club had signed Cissokho to a three-year contract until 2011.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.vfc.pt/noticias/modalidades/futebol/02_06_08_aly_cissikho |title=Aly Cissokho |date=2 June 2008 |access-date=3 June 2008 |publisher=[[Vitória F.C.]] |language=pt |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080616010909/http://www.vfc.pt/noticias/modalidades/futebol/02_06_08_aly_cissikho |archive-date=16 June 2008 |url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his debut for the club on 22 August 2008 in a match against [[Vitória S.C.|Vitória de Guimarães]] playing the entire match in a 1–1 draw.{{citation needed|date=July 2025}} Cissokho appeared in 15 league matches for the club and, also, made his European debut in a [[UEFA Cup]] match against Dutch club [[SC Heerenveen]].

===Porto===
After positive displays for Vitória de Setúbal, on 9 January 2009, the [[2007–08 Primeira Liga|defending champions]] [[FC Porto|Porto]] announced the club had acquired 60% of Cissokho's rights for a modest fee of €300,000.<ref>{{cite news| url= http://www.record.pt/noticia.asp?id=818766&idCanal=17| title= Cissokho reforça turma de Jesualdo Ferreira| date= 9 January 2009| access-date= 11 January 2009| language= pt| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090110115837/http://www.record.pt/noticia.asp?id=818766&idCanal=17| archive-date= 10 January 2009| url-status= dead}}</ref> Upon his arrival, Cissokho was given the number 28 shirt and immediately inserted into the starting lineup by manager [[Jesualdo Ferreira]] making his debut 17 January in a [[Taça da Liga]] match against [[Associação Académica de Coimbra – O.A.F.|Académica de Coimbra]].{{citation needed|date=July 2025}} In the league, Cissokho appeared in 15 matches with the club going undefeated in that span.<ref name="cissokho_uefa"/> The unbeaten streak led to the club winning its fourth consecutive league title and giving Cissokho his first major honour.

In the [[UEFA Champions League]], Cissokho made his debut on 24 February 2009 in the opening leg of the team's first knockout round tie against Spanish club [[Atlético Madrid]]. The match finished 2–2 and Porto won the tie by the same scoreline via the away goals rule.<ref>{{cite news|url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/7909103.stm |title=Atletico Madrid 2–2 FC Porto  |date=24 February 2009 |access-date=22 August 2010 |publisher=[[BBC]] }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/7938684.stm |title=FC Porto 0–0 A Madrid (agg 2–2) |date=11 March 2009 |access-date=22 August 2010 |publisher=[[BBC]] }}</ref>{{citation needed|date=July 2025}} In the quarter-finals, Porto faced English club [[Manchester United ====Transfer saga====
On 14 June 2009, Italian club [[A.C. Milan]] announced the club had signed Cissokho, subject to medical, with a reported deal of €15 million.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://fourfourtwo.com/news/italy/32858/default.aspx |title=Cissokho finally seals Milan deal |date=17 June 2009 |access-date=22 August 2010 |work=FourFourTwo |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120327102745/http://fourfourtwo.com/news/italy/32858/default.aspx |archive-date=27 March 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Cissokho underwent his medical on 16 June, but the next day, it was revealed he had failed it due to a problem with his teeth that could indicate potential spinal problems, and that the move was in jeopardy of collapse.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11854_5386096,00.html |title=Cissokho deal under threat |date=17 June 2009 |access-date=17 June 2009 |publisher=[[Sky Sports]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090619141224/http://www.skysports.com/story/0%2C19528%2C11854_5386096%2C00.html |archive-date=19 June 2009 |url-status=live }}</ref> Later that day, Cissokho declared he had passed a second medical he undertook, and that he had subsequently signed a pre-contract. In the meantime, Milan tried to re-negotiate the bid on a loan basis due to Cissokho's health concerns. As the parties failed to reach an agreement, Milan general manager [[Adriano Galliani]] announced the deal was cancelled.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://fourfourtwo.com/news/restofeurope/32904/default.aspx |title=Cissokho move to Milan cancelled |date=18 June 2009 |access-date=22 August 2010 |work=FourFourTwo}}</ref>

===Lyon===
[[File:Aly Cissokho.jpg|thumb|Cissokho playing for [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] in 2010|150px]]
On 18 July, French club [[Olympique Lyonnais]] announced the club had reached an agreement with Porto for the transfer of Cissokho, in a deal which equaled Milan's €15 million bid.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.uefa.com/competitions/ucl/news/kind=1/newsid=848299.html | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20090720071634/http://www.uefa.com/competitions/ucl/news/kind=1/newsid=848299.html | url-status = dead | archive-date = 20 July 2009 | title = Lyon lure Cissokho from Porto | date = 18 July 2010 | access-date =22 August 2010 | publisher=[[UEFA|Union of European Football Associations]] }}</ref> However, Porto remain eligible to receive 20% of the added value/differential value if Lyon sold him for a higher price.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcporto.pt/IncFCP/PDF/Investor_Relations/FactosRelevantes/VendaCissoko.pdf|title=COMUNICADO|trans-title=Communication|date=18 June 2009|access-date=18 August 2011|publisher=FC Porto|language=pt|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111224080056/http://www.fcporto.pt/IncFCP/PDF/Investor_Relations/FactosRelevantes/VendaCissoko.pdf|archive-date=24 December 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> Cissokho successfully passed his medical and agreed to a five-year contract. He was presented to the media, along with fellow new signing [[Michel Bastos]], on 20 July and was assigned the number 20 shirt.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.olweb.fr/fr/Accueil/100007/Article/50580/Presentation-de-M-Bastos-et-A-Cissokho | title = Présentation de M.Bastos et A.Cissokho | date = 20 July 2010 | access-date = 22 August 2010 | publisher = [[Olympique Lyonnais]] | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20091003100748/http://www.olweb.fr/fr/Accueil/100007/Article/50580/Presentation-de-M-Bastos-et-A-Cissokho | archive-date = 3 October 2009 | url-status = dead}}</ref>

[[File:Presentació Aly Cissokho València.JPG|200px|thumbnail|right|Cissokho at his presentation at the [[Mestalla Stadium]] as a Valencia player]]

Cissokho was immediately inserted to the starting 11 by manager [[Claude Puel]], replacing the [[Italy national football team|Italian international]] [[Fabio Grosso]], who departed for [[Juventus FC|Juventus]]. He made his debut for Lyon in the team's opening league match of the season, a 2–2 draw with [[Le Mans FC|Le Mans]] in which Cissokho played the entire match.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://lfp.fr/ligue1/feuilleMatch.asp?saison=2009/2010&code_evt=D1&code_jr_tr=J01&num_ordre=4 |title=Le Mans v.Lyon Match Report |date=8 August 2009 |access-date=22 August 2010 |publisher=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] |language=fr |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091201153711/http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuilleMatch.asp?saison=2009%2F2010&code_evt=D1&num_ordre=4&code_jr_tr=J01 |archive-date=1 December 2009 |url-status=dead}}</ref> On 26 September 2009, Cissokho assisted on the [[Equaliser (sports)|equalizing]] goal, scored by [[Yannis Tafer]], in the 52nd minute of a league match against [[Toulouse FC|Toulouse]]. Lyon later won 2–1 with a goal from [[Bafétimbi Gomis]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://lfp.fr/ligue1/feuilleMatch.asp?saison=2009/2010&code_evt=D1&code_jr_tr=J07&num_ordre=6 |title=Lyon v. Toulouse Match Report |date=26 September 2009 |access-date=22 August 2010 |publisher=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] |language=fr |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100106124140/http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuilleMatch.asp?saison=2009%2F2010&code_evt=D1&num_ordre=6&code_jr_tr=J07 |archive-date=6 January 2010 |url-status=dead}}</ref> On 9 December, he scored his first professional goal in Lyon's 4–0 thrashing of Hungarian club [[Debreceni VSC|Debrecen]]. Two weeks later, he provided his second league assist of the season on Lyon's only goal in the team's 2–1 loss to [[Montpellier HSC|Montpellier]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuilleMatch.asp?saison=2009/2010&code_evt=D1&code_jr_tr=J19&num_ordre=4 |title=Lyon v. Montpellier Match Report |date=23 December 2009 |access-date=22 August 2010 |publisher=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] |language=fr |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100403100210/http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuilleMatch.asp?saison=2009%2F2010&code_evt=D1&num_ordre=4&code_jr_tr=J19 |archive-date=3 April 2010 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Valencia===
On 23 August 2012, [[Valencia CF]] announced on their official website they had completed a deal to sign Cissokho for the next four seasons,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.valenciacf.com/contenidos/Actualidad/Noticias/2012/08/Noticia_90424.html?__locale=en |title=Aly Cissokho signs for Valencia |publisher=valenciacf |date=23 August 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120827173041/http://www.valenciacf.com/contenidos/Actualidad/Noticias/2012/08/Noticia_90424.html?__locale=en |archive-date=27 August 2012 }}</ref> in exchange for a €5 million and €1 million variable and a portion of future transfer fee Valencia received.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.actusnews.com/documents_communiques/ACTUS-0-29249-cp-ol-groupe-100912.pdf|title=Winner of the Trophée des Champions in New York; Summer 2012 trading window; New sponsors and renewal of sponsorship agreements|date=10 September 2012|access-date=11 July 2017|publisher=Olympique Lyonnais Group}}</ref> He made his official debut against [[FC Barcelona]], at an eventual 1–0 away loss. On 15 September, Cissokho's 25th birthday, he scored his first goal, which also turned out to be the winning goal, for Valencia in a 2–1 win over [[Celta de Vigo]] at the [[Mestalla Stadium]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.valenciacf.com/contenidos/Actualidad/Noticias/2012/09/Noticia_90556.html?__locale=es|title=Aly Cissokho's birthday gift|publisher=valenciacf|date=15 September 2012|access-date=16 September 2012|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130205104151/http://www.valenciacf.com/contenidos/Actualidad/Noticias/2012/09/Noticia_90556.html?__locale=es|archive-date=5 February 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref>

====Liverpool (loan)====
[[File:A Cissokho, K Jones, M Sakho 2014.jpg|thumb|left|Cissokho playing with [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] challenging [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]]'s [[Kenwyne Jones]] in 2014]]

On 20 August 2013, Cissokho signed for English side [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] on a season-long loan deal.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23726857 "Aly Cissokho: Liverpool sign Valencia left-back on loan"] BBC Sport. 20 August 2013. Retrieved 20 August 2013.</ref> He made his [[Premier League]] debut four days later away to [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], being substituted on in the 69th minute.<ref>{{cite news |title=Daniel Sturridge the difference at Villa Park |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/sport/soccer/english-soccer/daniel-sturridge-the-difference-at-villa-park-1.1505004 |access-date=30 September 2020 |work=The Irish Times |date=24 August 2013}}</ref> He was ruled out for six weeks after an injury which caused him to be taken off after ten minutes in the [[2013–14 Football League Cup|League Cup]] match against [[Notts County F.C.|Notts County]]. He made his first assist for [[Luis Suárez (Uruguayan footballer)|Luis Suárez]]'s second goal in a 4–1 victory over [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]], via an inadvertent rebound. He soon fell out of favour after making six appearances for the senior team. Cissokho returned to first-team action on 26 December against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] in the absence of injured [[Jon Flanagan]] in a narrow 2–1 defeat at the [[City of Manchester Stadium]]. Cissokho made his second and final goal contribution for Liverpool at [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] in January, when his shot deflected off the groin of [[Ryan Shawcross]] for an [[own goal]] after five minutes to open a 5–3 win.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Premier League: Liverpool overcame Stoke 5-3 at the Britannia Stadium|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/stoke-vs-liverpool/report/287494|access-date=16 February 2021|website=Sky Sports|language=en}}</ref>

===Aston Villa===
On 8 August 2014, Cissokho signed a four-year deal with Premier League club Aston Villa.<ref>{{cite press release|url=https://www.avfc.co.uk/news/2014/08/08/cissokho-delighted-as-he-signs-four-year-villa-deal|title=Cissokho delighted as he signs four-year Villa deal|date=8 August 2014|access-date=16 July 2017|publisher=Aston Villa F.C.}}</ref> He impressed during his debut – the first match of the [[2014–15 Premier League]] season against Stoke City, which Villa won 1–0. On 23 August 2014, in the match against [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]], Cissokho suffered an ankle injury, sidelining him for one week. On 20 September 2014, he scored an own goal while attempting to clear [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]]'s [[Kieran Gibbs]]' shot.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29187273|title=Aston Villa 0-3 Arsenal|work=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 24 February 2015, he sustained a groin/pelvis injury during training, sidelining him for two months. He made a total of 27 appearances and helped Villa reach the [[2015 FA Cup Final|FA Cup final]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/32856754|title=Arsenal 4 Aston Villa 0|date=30 May 2015|work=BBC Sport|access-date=3 June 2015}}</ref>

====Loan to Porto and premature return====
On 5 August 2015, Cissokho returned to Portuguese club Porto on a [[2015–16 FC Porto season|season-long]] loan, rejoining the side after a short spell in 2009. However, on 18 December, after only two appearances in the [[Primeira Liga]], he was recalled to Aston Villa by new Villa manager [[Rémi Garde]] – who had managed him at Lyon – to cover after [[Jordan Amavi]] was ruled out for the season, although Cissokho was not eligible to play until the new year.<ref>{{cite news|title=Aston Villa recall Aly Cissokho from Porto|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35135508|access-date=18 December 2015|work=BBC Sport|date=18 December 2015}}</ref> He was eventually issued squad number 43 and went straight into the starting 11 against fellow relegation candidates [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] in a 3–1 defeat on 2 January 2016.

====Loan to Olympiacos====
On 14 January 2017, [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] officially announced Cissokho had joined the club on a six-month loan from Aston Villa, with the option of permanently purchasing the player during the summer 2017 transfer window, subject to satisfactory performances.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sport24.gr/football/omades/Olympiakos/epishmo-ston-olympiako-o-sisoko.4480897.html|title=Επίσημο: Στον Ολυμπιακό ο Σισοκό!|access-date=17 January 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release|url=https://www.avfc.co.uk/News/2017/01/16/cissokho-joins-olympiacos|title=Cissokho joins Olympiacos|date=16 January 2017|access-date=16 July 2017|publisher=Aston Villa F.C.}}</ref> At the end of season, Cissokho returned to Aston Villa.

==International career==
Due to hovering in the [[Ligue 2|second division]] with Gueugnon, Cissokho never earned call-ups with any of [[France national youth football team|France's international youth teams]]. However, he did earn the attention of the [[Senegalese Football Federation]] ("FSF"), which governs the [[Senegal national football team|Senegal national team]]. The FSF wanted the player to play for the nation of his ancestors, and Cissokho initially accepted; however, he lost confidence in the FSF when it lost his passport and informed him it preferred homegrown players on the national team. After excelling in Portugal, the FSF contacted him again, but Cissokho refused contact, stating he had not made up his mind.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,12025_5604354,00.html |title= Cissokho turns down Senegal |date=3 October 2009 |access-date=22 August 2010 |publisher=[[Sky Sports]]}}</ref> On 3 October 2009, Cissokho announced he would be open to representing the [[France national football team|France national team]], but his main focus was currently with his new club.

On 5 November 2009, Cissokho was included in the France squad by coach [[Raymond Domenech]] for the team's [[2010 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|2010 FIFA World Cup qualification playoff round tie]] against the [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]] to serve as backup to [[Patrice Evra]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.extrafootie.co.uk/news/article/30708/ |title=France name squad for Republic of Ireland clash |date=5 November 2009 |access-date=22 August 2010 |publisher=Extra Footie |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111008195527/http://www.extrafootie.co.uk/news/article/30708/ |archive-date=8 October 2011 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Cissokho described the call up as a "childhood dream".<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.fff.fr/bleus/actu/531181.shtml |title=Cissokho: "Un rêve d'enfant" |date=6 November 2009 |access-date=22 August 2010|publisher=[[French Football Federation]] |language = fr }}</ref> He made the substitutes' bench for the first match played at [[Croke Park]], Dublin, but remained unused. In the second leg, he did not make the bench as France nonetheless earned a place in the [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010 World Cup]]. On 25 February 2010, he received his second call-up to the team for the [[Exhibition match|friendly]] against [[Spain national football team|Spain]] on 3 March, but did not make an appearance. On 11 May, he was named to the 30-man preliminary list by Domenech to play in the 2010 World Cup finals, but failed to make the final 23-man squad.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/newsid=1209066/index.html#vieira+benzema+left |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100514103044/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/newsid=1209066/index.html#vieira+benzema+left |url-status=dead |archive-date=14 May 2010 | title = Vieira and Benzema left out|date= 11 May 2010 | access-date =22 August 2010 | publisher=FIFA }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.france24.com/en/20100517-football-world-cup-raymond-domenech-france-marseilles-valbuena-ben-arfa | title = Domenech picks Marseille's Valbuena but leaves Ben Arfa behind  |date= 17 May 2010 | access-date =22 August 2010 | publisher=France24 }}</ref>

On 5 August 2010, Cissokho was called up to the team by new manager [[Laurent Blanc]] for the nation's friendly against [[Norway national football team|Norway]] on 11 August. He made his international debut in the match, starting and playing the full match as left-back.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/2898/euro-2012/2010/10/07/2155066/aly-cissokho-replaces-injured-benoit-tremoulinas-in-france|title=Aly Cissokho Replaces Injured Benoit Tremoulinas In France Squad For Romania Clash | Goal.com|website=goal.com}}</ref>

'''Juan Carlos Valerón Santana''' (born 17 June 1975) is a Spanish former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as an [[attacking midfielder]].

Over 15 seasons, he amassed [[La Liga]] totals of 390 matches and 29 goals with [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]], [[Atlético Madrid]] and [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo]], spending 13 years with the latter club. He started and finished his 22-year senior career with [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]]. 

Valerón represented [[Spain men's national football team|Spain]] in the [[2002 FIFA World Cup|2002 World Cup]] and two [[UEFA European Championship|European Championships]], earning 46 [[Cap (sport)|caps]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2013/06/01/futbol/1370123267.html|title=Un genio dice adiós|trans-title=A genius says goodbye|newspaper=El Mundo|language=es|date=1 June 2013|access-date=21 June 2024}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Early years===
Born in [[Arguineguín]], [[Gran Canaria]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vavel.com/es/futbol-internacional/2011/08/26/eldesvan/12684.html|title=Valerón, el hechicero de Arguineguín|trans-title=Valerón, the wizard of Arguineguín|publisher=Vavel|first=Mariano|last=Jesús Camacho|language=es|date=26 August 2011|access-date=16 July 2020}}</ref> Valerón started playing with hometown's [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]], but switched to the [[Balearic Islands]] in the [[1997–98 La Liga|1997–98 season]], representing [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] and making his [[La Liga]] debut on 31 August 1997 by playing ten minutes in a 2–1 home win over [[Valencia CF|Valencia]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.abc.es/nav/Navigate.exe/hemeroteca/madrid/abc/1997/09/01/081.html|title=Venganza en Mallorca|trans-title=Revenge in Mallorca|newspaper=[[ABC (newspaper)|ABC]]|first=Cristina|last=Infante|language=es|date=1 September 1997|access-date=14 March 2016}}</ref>

He was an instrumental figure in the club's [[1998–99 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup|qualification]] for the [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup]], with the team also finishing fifth in the league and [[1998 Copa del Rey Final|reaching the final]] of the [[Copa del Rey]], lost to eventual champions [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca-paginas.mundodeportivo.com/EMD03/HEM/1998/04/30/MD19980430-004.pdf|title=La Copa más histórica|trans-title=The most historical Cup|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|first=Andrés|last=Astruells|language=es|date=30 April 1998|access-date=14 March 2016}}</ref>

===Atlético and Deportivo===
In the next two years, Valerón played for [[Atlético Madrid]] where he was an undisputed starter but, following the side's relegation in [[1999–2000 La Liga|2000]], he joined [[Deportivo de La Coruña]], sharing club and position with equally talented Brazilian [[Djalminha]]. He gradually would become first choice,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://elpais.com/diario/2001/10/26/deportes/1004047204_850215.html|title=Djalminha exige la titularidad|trans-title=Djalminha demands to start|newspaper=[[El País]]|first=Diego|last=Torres|language=es|date=26 October 2001|access-date=12 April 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2003/11/10/mas_futbol/1068418804_850215.html|title=Djalminha volvió para demostrar que Valerón tiene sustituto|trans-title=Djalminha returned to show Valerón is replaceable|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|language=es|date=10 November 2003|access-date=12 April 2016}}</ref> signing a contract to eventually see off the remainder of his career with the [[Galicia (Spain)|Galicians]] in February 2004.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/019a-0e6acb8bb72a-b9b1949d54f4-1000--valeron-shows-devotion-to-depor/|title=Valerón shows devotion to Depor|publisher=UEFA|date=9 February 2004|access-date=18 February 2009}}</ref>

In January 2006, however, Valerón started a bad run with injuries. He suffered a [[anterior cruciate ligament|knee]] injury<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/025e-0f90a0644408-453c872ca28e-1000--valeron-suffers-injury-blow/|title=Valerón suffers injury blow|publisher=UEFA|date=22 January 2006|access-date=22 March 2025}}</ref> which relapsed in July<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/news/newsid=440661.html|title=Tottenham hit by King injury blow|publisher=UEFA|date=30 July 2006|access-date=14 November 2018}}{{dead link|date=March 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> and early 2007 (with him only managing two league appearances in the process), leading to another surgery.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/news/newsid=518254.html|title=Crucial surgery nears for Valerón|publisher=UEFA|date=20 March 2007|access-date=14 November 2018}}{{dead link|date=March 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> Consequently, he did not reappear until midway through the [[2007–08 La Liga|2007–08 campaign]].
[[File:Juan Carlos Valerón.jpg|thumb|Valerón with Deportivo in 2008]]
On 27 January 2008, Valerón returned to the bench in Deportivo's 3–1 home win against [[Real Valladolid]], coming on as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for [[Andrés Guardado]] for the final 15 minutes – his first match for over a year.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.20minutos.es/deportes/noticia/cronica-deportivo-valladolid-339848/0/|title=Lotina respira tras vencer al Valladolid en la vuelta de Valerón (3–1)|trans-title=Lotina breathes after beating Valladolid in return of Valerón (3–1)|newspaper=[[20 minutos]]|language=es|date=27 January 2008|access-date=6 November 2017}}</ref> In [[2008–09 La Liga|2008–09]], aged 33, he eventually became an important first-team fixture again,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/01d5-0e70c82c481e-aae45705ddcc-1000--valeron-thankful-for-new-lease-of-life/|title=Valerón thankful for new lease of life|publisher=UEFA|first=Paul|last=Bryan|date=28 January 2009|access-date=18 February 2009}}</ref> both on domestic and [[UEFA|European]] fronts.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/competitions/intertotocup/fixturesresults/round=15293/match=302906/report=rp.html|title=Valerón fires Depor through|publisher=UEFA|first=Paul|last=Bryan|date=26 July 2008|access-date=18 February 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081012100433/http://www.uefa.com/competitions/intertotocup/fixturesresults/round%3D15293/match%3D302906/report%3Drp.html|archive-date=12 October 2008}}</ref>

The 36-year-old Valerón was an undisputed starter for Depor in the [[2011–12 Segunda División|2011–12 season]], scoring a career-best five goals in nearly 3,000 minutes of action in [[Segunda División]] as his team returned to the top flight after one year out, as champions.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://eldia.es/2013-04-15/deportes/14-Valeron-anos-genio.htm|title=Valerón, 37 años de un genio|trans-title=Valerón, 37 years of a genius|newspaper=[[El Día (Canary Islands)|El Día]]|first=Carlos Alberto|last=Fernández|language=es|date=15 April 2013|access-date=16 May 2013}}</ref> Even though he had a contract until 2015, he chose to leave in June 2013,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-espana.net/31396/valeron-announces-depor-exit|title=Valeron announces Depor exit|publisher=Football España|date=2 June 2013|access-date=22 October 2015}}</ref> having taken part in 422 games in all competitions (32 goals).<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.laopinioncoruna.es/deportivo/2024/06/29/valeron-depor-cuestion-tiempo-104568748.html|title=Valerón y el Dépor, cuestión de tiempo|trans-title=Valerón and Dépor, a matter of time|newspaper=La Opinión A Coruña|first1=Carlos|last1=Miranda|first2=Marcos|last2=Otero|language=es|date=29 June 2024|access-date=12 July 2024}}</ref>

===Return to Las Palmas===
On 14 July 2013, following [[2012–13 La Liga|another Deportivo relegation]], Valerón returned to his first club Las Palmas after 16 years, signing a one-year contract with an option for a second.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.udlaspalmas.es/actualidad-noticias-4811|title=Juan Carlos Valerón vuelve a la Unión Deportiva Las Palmas|trans-title=Juan Carlos Valerón returns to Unión Deportiva Las Palmas|publisher=UD Las Palmas|language=es|date=14 July 2013|access-date=16 July 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130717122524/http://udlaspalmas.es/actualidad-noticias-4811|archive-date=17 July 2013}}</ref> He continued to be an important first-team member during his tenure, achieving promotion to the top flight [[2014–15 Segunda División|in 2015]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2015/05/06/segunda/1430875241_039265.html|title=Valerón: "Hace ya varios años que yo me planteo el final"|trans-title=Valerón: "I have been brooding over the end for several years"|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Rafael|last=León|language=es|date=6 May 2015|access-date=13 July 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://es.eurosport.yahoo.com/noticias/valer%c3%b3n-despedirse-espa%c3%b1a-ascenso-palmas-142730382--sow.html|title=Valerón podrá despedirse por toda España después del ascenso de Las Palmas|trans-title=Valerón will be able to say goodbye throughout Spain after Las Palmas' promotion|publisher=[[Eurosport]]|language=es|date=22 June 2015|access-date=13 July 2015}}</ref>

In summer 2015, Valerón renewed his contract with the ''Amarillos'' for a further year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.udlaspalmas.es/-/valeron-renueva-por-una-temporada|title=Valerón renueva por una temporada|trans-title=Valerón renews for a season|publisher=UD Las Palmas|language=es|date=15 July 2015|access-date=16 July 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150716085138/http://www.udlaspalmas.es/-/valeron-renueva-por-una-temporada|archive-date=16 July 2015}}</ref> On 26 September, he first appeared with the club in the top flight, featuring 22 minutes in a 1–2 away loss to Barcelona in what was his first game in the competition in 847 days,<ref name=Marca>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2015/09/27/futbol/equipos/las_palmas/1443368447.html|title=Valerón volvió a jugar en Primera 847 días después|trans-title=Valerón played again in ''Primera'' 847 days later|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=27 September 2015|access-date=21 October 2015}}</ref> and becoming the fifth oldest player to play there at the age of 40 years and 101 days;<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.joe.co.uk/sport/evergreen-juan-carlos-valeron-returns-to-la-liga-action-aged-40/16981|title=Evergreen Juan Carlos Valeron returns to La Liga action aged 40|publisher=[[Joe (website)|Joe]]|first=Tom|last=Victor|date=26 September 2015|access-date=21 October 2015}}</ref> he climbed one position on 12 December after coming on as substitute against [[Real Betis]], surpassing former Deportivo teammate [[Donato (footballer)|Donato]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.laprovincia.es/ud-las-palmas/2015/12/13/valeron-cuarto-jugador-veterano-jugar/772862.html|title=Valerón es el cuarto jugador más veterano en jugar en Primera|trans-title=Valerón is the fourth most veteran player to play in ''Primera''|newspaper=[[La Provincia (Canary Islands)|La Provincia]]|language=es|date=13 December 2015|access-date=13 December 2015}}</ref>

On 1 March 2016, after being featured in a 4–0 home win against [[Getafe CF|Getafe]], Valerón appeared in his 400th game in the Spanish top tier.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sport-english.com/en/news/liga-bbva/congratulations-juan-carlos-valeron-played-his-400th-liga-game-4942095|title=Congratulations! Juan Carlos Valeron played his 400th La Liga game|newspaper=[[Sport (Spanish newspaper)|Sport]]|date=2 March 2016|access-date=14 March 2016}}</ref> On 7 May, he announced his retirement.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.lavozdegalicia.es/noticia/torremarathon/2016/05/07/valeron-anuncia-retirada/00031462625141310765788.htm|title=Valerón anuncia su retirada|trans-title=Valerón announces his retirement|newspaper=[[La Voz de Galicia]]|first=Alexandre|last=Centeno|language=es|date=7 May 2016|access-date=25 June 2016}}</ref>

==International career==
A [[Spain men's national football team|Spain international]] since 18 November 1998 in a 2–2 [[Exhibition game|friendly]] draw with [[Italy national football team|Italy]] in [[Salerno]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1998/11/19/pagina-17/400568/pdf.html|title=Notable alto|trans-title=B Plus|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Javier|last=Gascón|language=es|date=19 November 1998|access-date=16 May 2013}}</ref> Valerón appeared with the national side at [[UEFA Euro 2000]], the [[2002 FIFA World Cup]] (where he scored in a 3–1 win against [[Slovenia national football team|Slovenia]])<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport3/worldcup2002/hi/matches_wallchart/spain_v_slovenia/default.stm|title=Spain see off Slovenia|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=2 June 2002|access-date=16 May 2012}}</ref> and [[UEFA Euro 2004|Euro 2004]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro-2020/news/0254-0d7b44fc5b75-bb339e5a3edf-1000--saez-selects-spain-squad/|title=Sáez selects Spain squad|publisher=UEFA|first=Iván|last=Modia|date=20 May 2004|access-date=16 July 2020|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201125060158/https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro-2020/news/0254-0d7b44fc5b75-bb339e5a3edf-1000--saez-selects-spain-squad/|archive-date=25 November 2020}}</ref> netting immediately after coming from the bench in a 1–0 victory over [[Russia national football team|Russia]] in the latter competition.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/euro_2004/3787463.stm|title=Spain 1–0 Russia|publisher=BBC Sport|date=12 June 2004|access-date=15 June 2011}}</ref>

He made his last appearance for his country on 26 March 2005, a 3–0 defeat of [[China national football team|China]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/2005/03/27/pagina-4/1309544/pdf.html|title=Aperitivo oriental|trans-title=Oriental hors d'oeuvre|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Manuel|last=Segura|language=es|date=27 March 2005|access-date=17 May 2013}}</ref> In late July 2019, he was hired by the Canarian Football Federation to be responsible for the several teams in the region that took part in the corresponding competitions.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.udlaspalmas.net/2019/07/29/juan-carlos-valeron-nuevo-seleccionador-canario/|title=Juan Carlos Valerón, nuevo seleccionador canario|trans-title=Juan Carlos Valerón, new Canarian team manager|publisher=UD Las Palmas.net|language=es|date=29 July 2019|access-date=16 December 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/mas-futbol/2019/07/29/5d3f3dd2ca4741971e8b459b.html|title=Juan Carlos Valerón, nuevo seleccionador canario|trans-title=Juan Carlos Valerón, new Canarian team manager|newspaper=Marca|first=Mario|last=De la Santa|language=es|date=29 July 2019|access-date=16 December 2019}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
Shortly after retiring, Valerón began working as a manager after completing the UEFA B course. He was appointed youth coach at Las Palmas<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tintaamarilla.es/noticia/2016/09/14/164/21325-Valeron_debuta_como_entrenador.html|title=Valerón debuta como entrenador|trans-title=Valerón has debut as coach|publisher=Tinta Amarilla|language=es|date=14 September 2016|access-date=16 December 2019}}</ref> and, ahead of the [[2017–18 La Liga|2017–18 season]], was named assistant to [[Manolo Márquez]] in the first team;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.udlaspalmas.es/noticias/noticia/valeron-y-paquito-ortiz-miembros-del-nuevo-equipo-tecnico-de-la-ud-las-palmas|title=Valerón y Paquito Ortiz, miembros del nuevo equipo técnico de la UD Las Palmas|trans-title=Valerón and Paquito Ortiz, members of UD Las Palmas' new coaching staff|publisher=UD Las Palmas|language=es|date=3 July 2017|access-date=16 December 2019}}</ref> the latter left his position three months later, however, and the former returned to the academy.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.udlaspalmas.net/2017/10/02/video-valeron-estrena-su-cargo-como-entrenador-del-infantil-b/|title=(VÍDEO) Valerón estrena su cargo como entrenador del Infantil B|trans-title=(VIDEO) Valerón starts as ''Infantil B'' manager|publisher=UD Las Palmas.net|language=es|date=2 October 2017|access-date=16 December 2019}}</ref>

On 24 January 2018, Valerón agreed to join [[Juan Manuel Rodríguez (football manager)|Juan Manuel Rodríguez]]'s staff at [[UD Las Palmas Atlético|Las Palmas B]], the [[reserve team]]. He resigned from his post in June for personal reasons,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.udlaspalmas.es/en/news/new/valeron-leaves-ud-las-palmas|title=Valerón leaves UD Las Palmas|publisher=UD Las Palmas|date=27 June 2018|access-date=16 December 2019}}</ref> but the following January resumed his work with the youth sides.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.canarias7.es/deportes/futbol/juan-carlos-valeron-vuelve-a-trabajar-con-la-cantera-de-la-ud-las-palmas-YB6425463|title=Juan Carlos Valerón vuelve a trabajar con la cantera de la UD Las Palmas|trans-title=Juan Carlos Valerón returns to work with UD Las Palmas youth system|newspaper=[[Canarias7]]|language=es|date=22 January 2019|access-date=16 December 2019}}</ref>

Valerón returned to his former club Deportivo in June 2020, being appointed manager of [[Deportivo Fabril|the reserves]] in the [[Tercera División]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lavozdegalicia.es/noticia/torremarathon/2020/06/27/deportivo-repesca-valeron-entrenador-fabril/00031593287141408313871.htm|title=El Deportivo repesca a Valerón como entrenador para el Fabril|trans-title=Deportivo bring back Valerón as manager for Fabril|newspaper=La Voz de Galicia|first=M.|last=García|language=es|date=27 June 2020|access-date=8 August 2020}}</ref>

==Player profile==
===Style of play===
Valerón was known for his passing skills and ball control while also having the ability to score goals. However, he was also injury-prone and inconsistent.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/euro_2004/spain/players_to_watch/3602295.stm|title=Juan Carlos Valeron|publisher=BBC Sport|date=25 May 2004|access-date=17 May 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.diariosdefutbol.com/2007/03/21/juan-carlos-valeron-cronologia-de-una-lesion-maldita/|title=Juan Carlos Valerón, cronología de una lesión maldita|trans-title=Juan Carlos Valerón, chronology of a damn injury|publisher=Diarios de Fútbol|language=es|date=21 March 2007|access-date=15 May 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rcdm.es/jugadores-de-ayer-y-de-hoy-juan-carlos-valeron/|title=Jugadores de ayer y de hoy: Juan Carlos Valerón|trans-title=Players of yesterday and today: Juan Carlos Valerón|publisher=RCDM|first=Ángel|last=Berastain|language=es|date=20 May 2010|access-date=17 May 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100608202648/http://www.rcdm.es/jugadores-de-ayer-y-de-hoy-juan-carlos-valeron/|archive-date=8 June 2010}}</ref><ref name=Retire>{{cite web|url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/us/news/deportivo-great-valeron-announces-retirement|title=Deportivo great Valeron announces retirement|publisher=[[FourFourTwo]]|date=7 May 2016|access-date=17 May 2020}}</ref> 

===Reception===
[[File:Camisetavaleron.JPG|thumb|upright|A shirt worn by Valerón for Deportivo.]]
Valerón was widely regarded as one of the most respected players in Spain, and as an important figure for Deportivo. [[Andrés Iniesta]] said he would pay to watch him play,<ref name=Marca/><ref name=Retire/> whilst manager [[Juan Antonio Anquela]] called him a reference for Spanish football<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.riazor.org/anquela-si-no-somos-un-equipo-serio-lo-vamos-a-pasar-mal/|title=Anquela: "Si no somos un equipo serio, lo vamos a pasar mal"|trans-title=Anquela: "If we are not a serious team, we are going to suffer"|publisher=Riazor|language=es|date=15 September 2012|access-date=21 October 2015}}</ref> and fellow coach [[Vicente del Bosque]] admitted that he would always fit in the national team.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.diariovasco.com/agencias/20111026/deportes/futbol/valeron-agradece-bosque-dijera-encajaria_201110261750.html|title=Valerón agradece que Del Bosque dijera que "encajaría" en la selección|trans-title=Valerón thanks Del Bosque for saying he would always "fit" in the national team|newspaper=[[El Diario Vasco]]|language=es|date=26 November 2011|access-date=21 October 2015}}</ref> His Las Palmas teammate, [[Javi Castellano]], praised him for his honesty and modesty.<ref name=SKY>{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/32837/9953684/juan-carlos-valeron-makes-la-liga-return-at-40-with-las-palmas|title=Juan Carlos Valeron makes La Liga return at 40 with Las Palmas|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|first=Adam|last=Bate|date=22 August 2015|access-date=21 October 2015}}</ref>

Miguel Ángel Ramírez, Las Palmas president, said in 2015 he was trying to persuade Valerón to play another season so that he would be able to say goodbye to all the stadia in Spain where he was consistently cheered<ref name=SKY/>– this was exemplified by his last game at the [[Camp Nou]], with former national teammate [[Luis Enrique]] and coach of the opposing team applauding as he took the pitch.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://as.com/m/diarioas/2015/09/26/english/1443292713_250378.html|title=I'm sad about Messi but the team did what they had to do|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Moisés|last=Llorens|date=26 September 2015|access-date=22 October 2015}}</ref> Former Dutch internationals [[Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink]] and [[Roy Makaay]] claimed he was the best player they had ever played with.<ref name=SKY/>

Ahead of his return to the [[Estadio Riazor]] in April 2016, Deportivo manager [[Víctor Sánchez (footballer, born 1976)|Víctor Sánchez]] said that Valerón would have won the [[Ballon d'Or]] had he played for a more fashionable club.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/futbol/deportivo/2016/04/10/570a465a22601d01708b4583.html|title=Víctor: "Valerón en un grande habría sido Balón de Oro"|trans-title=Víctor: "Valerón in a big team would have been Ballon d'Or"|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=10 April 2016|access-date=11 April 2016}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Valerón's older brother, Miguel Ángel, was also a footballer and a midfielder;<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bdfutbol.com/en/j/j6588.html|title=Valerón: Miguel Ángel Valerón Santana|publisher=BDFutbol|access-date=4 May 2009}}</ref> having represented Las Palmas and [[RCD Mallorca B|Mallorca B]], his career was also curtailed by injuries.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.diariosigloxxi.com/texto-diario/mostrar/73720/miguel-angel-valeron-puse-la-pierna-quizas-ingenuamente|title=Miguel Angel Valerón: "Puse la pierna, quizás ingenuamente"|trans-title=Miguel Angel Valerón: "I went for the challenge, maybe i was naive"|newspaper=[[Diario Siglo XXI]]|first=Antonio|last=Sánchez|language=es|date=18 August 2011|access-date=4 May 2009}}</ref> Later, together with another sibling, Pedro, they created a football club/school named Abrisajac, from biblical characters [[Abraham]], [[Isaac]] and [[Jacob]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.teinteresa.es/deportes/familia-Valeron-vuelca-Abrisajac-necesitados_0_1032497683.html|title=La familia Valerón se vuelca con Abrisajac para ayudar a los más necesitados|trans-title=Valerón family joins forces with Abrisajac to help those in need|publisher=Te Interesa|first=Ulises|last=Sánchez Flor|language=es|date=19 November 2013|access-date=21 October 2015}}</ref> and Juan Carlos still played there one year before retiring for good.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/primera-plana/2016/09/07/57cf36f2e5fdeaa5328b461a.html|title=Valerón: disfrutar a los 41|trans-title=Valerón: enjoying at 41|newspaper=Marca|first=Jesús|last=Izquierdo|language=es|date=7 September 2016|access-date=22 June 2021}}</ref>

Valerón was a close friend of fellow [[Canarian people|Canarian]] [[Manuel Pablo]], who also played for Las Palmas, Deportivo and Spain.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2015/07/03/primera/1435923825_692721.html|title=Manuel Pablo: "Yo no me retiro hasta que se retire Valerón"|trans-title=Manuel Pablo: Manuel Pablo: "I will not retire until Valerón does the same"|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Luis|last=De la Cruz|language=es|date=3 July 2015|access-date=21 October 2015}}</ref> He was also known for his devotion to God, but admitted that he and his family did not follow any religion.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2015/08/09/futbol/equipos/las_palmas/1439135859.html|title=Valerón, querido abuelo|trans-title=Valerón, dear grandfather|newspaper=Marca|first=Jesús|last=Izquierdo|language=es|date=9 August 2015|access-date=21 October 2015}}</ref>

Valerón's nephew, Manu, also played youth football for Las Palmas.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tintaamarilla.es/noticia.php?id=1867|title=Manu, el tercer Valerón|trans-title=Manu, the third Valerón|publisher=Tinta Amarilla|language=es|date=7 December 2011|access-date=21 October 2015}}</ref>
