'''David Rozehnal''' (born 5 July 1980) is a Czech former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[centre-back]]. He played for a host of European clubs, making over 400 appearances in a career spanning almost two decades, and retired from the professional game in April 2018. Internationally Rozehnal made 60 appearances for the Czech Republic, appearing in three major tournaments: [[UEFA Euro 2004|Euro 2004]], the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]] and [[UEFA Euro 2008|Euro 2008]].

==Early life==
Rozehnal was born in [[Šternberk]] and raised in [[Kožušany-Tážaly|Kožušany]]. He comes from a sports family, his father was a second-league football player, his mother played competitive handball. His father then trained amateur club Sokol Kožušany, where Rozehnal started with football.<ref>{{Cite web|title=David Rozehnal|url=https://www.ceskatelevize.cz/lide/david-rozehnal/|publisher=[[Czech Television]]|access-date=7 May 2022|language=cs}}</ref>

==Club career==

=== Sigma Olomouc ===
Rozehnal joined the senior team at [[SK Sigma Olomouc|Sigma Olomouc]] in 1999 from the Sigma Olomouc B youth team.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=David Rozehnal |url=https://www.national-football-teams.com/player/1831/David_Rozehnal.html |website=National Football Teams}}</ref> He finished as a runner-up in the [[2000 UEFA Intertoto Cup]],<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080408172526/http://www.rsssf.com/tablesu/uic00.html 2000 UEFA Intertoto Cup Results at Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation]</ref> and he was also part of the Sigma Olomouc team which finished in third place in [[2000–01 Czech First League|2000–01]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Divácké statistiky Gambrinus liga 2000/2001 |url=http://fotbal.idnes.cz/db_fotbal.asp?st_divaci=1000000 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050106202508/http://fotbal.idnes.cz/db_fotbal.asp?st_divaci=1000000 |archive-date=6 January 2005 |access-date=24 February 2012 |publisher=idnes.cz |language=cs}}</ref>

===Club Brugge===
In 2003, Rozehnal joined [[Belgium|Belgian]] club [[Club Brugge K.V.|Club Brugge]]. Shortly after joining the club he was part of the side which defeated [[AC Milan]] at the [[San Siro]] in the [[UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rozehnalův fotbalový sen pokračoval v Miláně|url=https://www.idnes.cz/fotbal/pohary/rozehnaluv-fotbalovy-sen-pokracoval-v-milane.A031023_172339_fot_pohary_rav|publisher=[[Mladá fronta Dnes]]|date=23 October 2023|access-date=17 December 2024|language=cs}}</ref> He won the [[Belgian Cup]] in his first season with Brugge and the [[Belgian League]] in the 2004–05 season.<ref name="jerabek">{{cite book|first=Luboš|last=Jeřábek|title=Český a československý fotbal – lexikon osobností a klubů|publisher=Grada Publishing|language=cs|year=2007|location=Prague, Czech Republic|isbn=978-80-247-1656-5|page=174}}</ref>

===Paris Saint-Germain===
[[File:David Rozehnal & Killian Brennan.jpg|thumb|Rozehnal with [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] in 2006]]
Rozehnal signed for [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]] in June 2005.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Rozehnal closes on switch to PSG|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/4105494.stm|website=[[BBC Sport]]|publisher=[[BBC]]|date=17 June 2005|access-date=5 October 2007}}</ref> His form resulted in reported interest from [[Borussia Dortmund]], [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] and [[Sevilla F.C.|Sevilla]].<ref name=to-newc>{{cite news|title=Newcastle complete Rozehnal deal|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/n/newcastle_united/6232364.stm|website=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=29 June 2007}}</ref> Sources close to the defender confirmed that he would prefer a move to Newcastle.<ref>{{cite news|first=Saj|last=Chowdhury|title=Rozehnal eager to join Newcastle|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/n/newcastle_united/6723321.stm|website=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=5 June 2007|access-date=1 October 2014}}</ref>

===Newcastle United===
On 22 June 2007, Rozehnal's agent confirmed that a "definite agreement" had been reached for the player to join Newcastle United. Rozehnal underwent a medical check on 25 June and Newcastle confirmed the transfer had been completed on 29 June for a fee of £2.9 million, with the player signing a four-year contract.<ref name=to-newc/> He made his league debut against [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] the same year on 11 August.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/6931059.stm|website=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=11 August 2007|access-date=5 October 2007 |title=Bolton 1-3 Newcastle }}</ref>

===Lazio===
On 31 January 2008, Rozehnal left Newcastle for [[S.S. Lazio|Lazio]] on loan until the end of the 2007–08 Serie A despite having only signed in June 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/serie-a/2007-2008/rozehnal-in-lazio-loan_sto1464489/story.shtml|title=Rozehnal in Lazio loan|work=[[Eurosport]]|date=31 January 2008|access-date=17 December 2024}}</ref> After only playing seven times for Lazio during his loan spell, it remained unclear if they wanted to sign him permanently. On 9 June 2008, Lazio officially announced they had signed Rozehnal on a permanent basis,<ref>{{Cite news|title=La Lazio riscatta Rozehnal|url=http://www.sslazio.it/cms/view/home/news/archivio/elenco_news/la_lazio_riscatta_rozenhal/s152/c1630|url-status=dead|website=S.S. Lazio|date=10 June 2008|language=it|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080612024316/http://www.sslazio.it/cms/view/home/news/archivio/elenco_news/la_lazio_riscatta_rozenhal/s152/c1630|archive-date=12 June 2008}}</ref> with Newcastle recouping the full £2.9 million which they initially paid for the defender.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Rozehnal completes move to Lazio|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/n/newcastle_united/7221163.st|website=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=10 June 2008}}{{dead link|date=September 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

===Later career and retirement===
[[File:Krasnodar-Lille (28).jpg|thumb|Rozehnal with [[Lille OSC|Lille]] in 2014]]
After only one year in [[Italy]], Rozehnal left Lazio on 29 July 2009 for German club [[Hamburger SV]], signing a contract until 30 June 2012. Due to a poor season with several costly errors by Rozehnal, he was removed from the first team and asked to find a new club.<ref>{{Cite magazine|title=Veh streicht Tavares und Rozehnal|url=https://www.kicker.de/veh-streicht-tavares-und-rozehnal-540694/artikel|magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]]|date=4 August 2010|access-date=6 August 2010|language=de}}</ref>

On 31 August 2010, Hamburg confirmed that Rozehnal had left for French side [[Lille OSC|Lille]] on loan, with the German club still paying part of his salary.<ref>{{Cite news|title=HSV-Ladenhüter Rozehnal geht!|url=http://www.mopo.de/2010/20100831/sport/hsv/hsv_ladenhueter_rozehnal_geht.html|date=31 August 2010|access-date=1 September 2010|website=Hamburger Morgenpost|language=de|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20100902015620/http://www.mopo.de/2010/20100831/sport/hsv/hsv_ladenhueter_rozehnal_geht.html|archive-date=2 September 2010}}</ref> He made a permanent move to Lille in June 2011, signing a contract until 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Francouzské Lille vykoupilo z Hamburku Davida Rozehnala|url=https://sport.ceskatelevize.cz/clanek/fotbal/francouzske-lille-vykoupilo-z-hamburku-davida-rozehnala/5bdfe08c0d663b6fe810e150|website=[[ČT Sport]]|publisher=[[Czech Television]]|date=23 June 2011|access-date=17 December 2024|language=cs}}</ref>

Rozehnal retired from professional football on 4 April 2018 and joined Sokol Kožušany alongside his brother, Marek.<ref>{{Cite web|first=Kurt|last=Desplenter|title=Rozehnal kvůli rodině rozvázal smlouvu v Ostende a ukončil kariéru|url=https://sport.ceskatelevize.cz/clanek/fotbal/rozehnal-kvuli-rodine-rozvazal-smlouvu-v-ostende-a-ukoncil-karieru/5bca1ddf59841d79e18aafec|website=ČT Sport|publisher=[[Czech Television]]|date=4 April 2018|access-date=17 December 2024|language=cs}}</ref> He made his debut for the club the following weekend.<ref>{{Cite news|first=Miroslav|last=Mazal|title=Rozehnalova premiéra za Kožušany: ztracené vedení, sporný moment a prohra|url=https://olomoucky.denik.cz/fotbal_region/rozehnalova-premiera-za-kozusany-ztracene-vedeni-sporny-moment-a-prohra-20180409.html|website=[[Deník]]|location=Olomouc|publisher=Vltave Labe Media|date=9 April 2018|access-date=8 May 2018|language=cs}}</ref>

==International career==
Rozehnal was part of the Czech Republic national youth football team which won the [[UEFA European Under-21 Football Championship|UEFA U-21 Championships]] in 2002.<ref>{{Cite news|title=European U-21 Championship 2002 {{!}} Final Tournament Details|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/eur-u21-2002det.html|website=[[RSSSF]]|access-date=19 April 2022}}</ref> In 2004, Rozehnal made his debut for the [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic]] in a 2–2 friendly draw against [[Italy national football team|Italy]] on 18 February 2004.<ref>{{Cite web|title=David Rozehnal se stal hráčem Hamburku!|url=https://www.efotbal.cz/clanek-59695-David-Rozehnal-se-stal-hracem-Hamburku.html|website=efotbal.cz|date=29 July 2009|language=cs}}</ref> He went on to play for his country at [[UEFA Euro 2004|Euro 2004]],<ref name="jerabek"/> where the team made it to the semi-finals before being knocked out by [[Greece national football team|Greece]]. He also played in the group stage at the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]], although his nation did not advance to the knockout stages.<ref name="jerabek"/> Rozehnal played in his third major tournament at [[UEFA Euro 2008|Euro 2008]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Nejlépe zahrál Sionko, nejhorší známku dostal Rozehnal|url=https://www.idnes.cz/fotbal/euro-2008/nejlepe-zahral-sionko-nejhorsi-znamku-dostal-rozehnal.A080611_235934_euro-2008_pes|newspaper=[[Mladá fronta Dnes]]|publisher=[[Mafra (company)|Mafra]]|date=12 June 2008|access-date=17 December 2024|language=cs}}</ref> He scored his only international goal in his 57th appearance for his country, finding the net in a 3–1 friendly win against [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|title=Rozehnalův první gól v reprezentaci. Po pěti letech|first=Filip|last=Saiver|url=https://www.idnes.cz/fotbal/reprezentace/rozehnaluv-prvni-gol-v-nbsp-reprezentaci-po-peti-letech.A090812_220501_fot_reprez_par|newspaper=[[Mladá fronta Dnes]]|publisher=Mafra|date=13 August 2009|access-date=17 December 2024|language=cs}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Rozehnal is married to Petra with two children.<ref>{{Cite news|first=Václav|last=Havlíček|title=David už umí fotbal oželet, říká Rozehnalová. Zášť k Brücknerovi necítí|url=https://www.idnes.cz/fotbal/euro-2024/petra-rozehnalova-david-rozehnal-rozhovor-fotbalove-manzelky.A240627_163732_euro-2024_malu|newspaper=Mladá fronta Dnes|publisher=Mafra|date=11 July 2024|access-date=31 December 2024|language=cs}}</ref> Their first child, Luka, was born on 3 October 2007.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nufc.premiumtv.co.uk/page/NewsDetail/0,,10278~1128139,00.html|title=Baby Joy For Czech Mate|date=5 October 2007|publisher=Newcastle United F.C.|via=Premium TV|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070616180251/http://www.nufc.premiumtv.co.uk/page/NewsDetail/0%2C%2C10278~1128139%2C00.html|archive-date=16 June 2007|url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''Aleix Vidal Parreu''' ({{IPA|ca|əˈleʒ βiˈðal}};{{efn|In isolation, ''Aleix'' and ''Vidal'' are pronounced {{IPA|ca|əˈleʃ|}} and {{IPA|ca|biˈðal|}} respectively.}} born 21 August 1989) is a Spanish professional [[association football|footballer]]. Mainly a [[right winger (association football)|right winger]] and a player of great speed, he can also operate as a [[right-back]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.barcablaugranes.com/2015/6/7/8743767/official-barcelona-sign-aleix-vidal-from-sevilla|title=Official: Barcelona sign Aleix Vidal from Sevilla|publisher=Barça Blaugranes|first=Luis|last=Mazariegos|date=7 June 2015|access-date=23 July 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2496268-breaking-down-what-aleix-vidal-will-bring-to-barcelona-next-season|title=Breaking down what Aleix Vidal will bring to Barcelona next season|publisher=[[Bleacher Report]]|first=Tim|last=Collins|date=15 June 2015|access-date=23 July 2015}}</ref>

Having spent his early career at a string of lower-league and reserve teams, he became a regular at [[UD Almería|Almería]], helping them to promotion to [[La Liga]], and also won the [[UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] with [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] before signing for [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in 2015 for €17 million. Three seasons later, he returned to Sevilla.

Vidal won one [[Cap (sport)|cap]] for [[Spain national football team|Spain]], in 2015.

==Club career==
===Early years===
Born in [[Valls]], [[Province of Tarragona|Tarragona]], [[Catalonia]], and raised in neighbouring [[Puigpelat]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.arabalears.cat/esports/aleix-vidal-sera-jugador-blaugrana_1_3570293.html|title=Aleix Vidal serà jugador blaugrana|trans-title=Aleix Vidal will be a ''blaugrana'' player|newspaper=[[Ara (newspaper)|Ara]]|language=ca|date=7 June 2015|access-date=24 December 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.diaridetarragona.com/deportes/Puigpelat-El-municipio-sin-campo-de-futbol-20150608-0008.html|title=Puigpelat: El municipio sin campo de fútbol|trans-title=Puigpelat: The municipality without a football field|newspaper=[[Diari de Tarragona]]|first=Francesc|last=Joan|language=es|date=8 June 2015|access-date=2 August 2019}}</ref> Vidal started his career as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]]. He signed for [[RCD Espanyol]] in 2007 to further his development<ref>{{cite news|url=https://futbol.as.com/futbol/2016/01/06/copa_del_rey/1452049729_007525.html|title=Aleix Vidal se planteó dejar el fútbol en el club perico|trans-title=Aleix Vidal thought about quitting football in the ''perico'' club|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Iván|last=Molero|language=es|date=6 January 2016|access-date=16 January 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/barca/increible-historia-aleix-vidal-4293605|title=La increíble historia de Aleix Vidal|trans-title=The incredible story of Aleix Vidal|newspaper=[[Sport (Spanish newspaper)|Sport]]|first=Jordi|last=Gil|language=es|date=22 June 2015|access-date=10 November 2016}}</ref> after having already made his senior debut with [[CF Reus Deportiu]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/fc-barcelona/20150610/20411214905/las-claves-de-la-evolucion-de-aleix-vidal.html|title=Las claves de la evolución de Aleix Vidal|trans-title=The keys to Aleix Vidal's evolution|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|first=Fabio|last=Marchi|language=es|date=10 June 2015|access-date=16 January 2016}}</ref> but never appeared for the former's first team, finishing his only senior season with the club on loan to [[Panthrakikos F.C.]] from Greece.

On 31 August 2009, Vidal moved to [[Segunda División]] side [[Gimnàstic de Tarragona]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.esfutbol.net/?action=read&idnotizia=45764|title=Gimnastic: se incorpora Aleix Vidal|trans-title=Gimnastic: Aleix Vidal added|publisher=esFutbol|language=es|date=1 September 2009|access-date=1 September 2009}}</ref> but spent the vast majority of [[2009–10 Segunda División|the season]] with [[CF Pobla de Mafumet]], the [[farm team]]. He joined [[RCD Mallorca]] in the middle of 2010, being assigned to [[RCD Mallorca B|the reserves]] in the [[Segunda División B]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.diariodemallorca.es/rcd-mallorca/2015/05/27/aleix-vidal-son-bibiloni-lista-3736794.html|title=Aleix Vidal, de Son Bibiloni a la lista de Del Bosque|trans-title=Aleix Vidal, from Son Bibiloni to Del Bosque's list|newspaper=[[Diario de Mallorca]]|first=M.|last=Fernández|language=es|date=27 May 2015|access-date=20 December 2023}}</ref>

===Almería===
In mid-June 2011, after [[2010–11 Segunda División B|suffering relegation]], Vidal joined another [[reserve team]] also in that tier, [[UD Almería B]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://udalmeria.ideal.es/noticias/2011-06-17/almeria-ficha-aleix-vidal-20110617.html|title=El Almería B ficha a Aleix Vidal, del Mallorca, y a Javi Manzano, del Poli|trans-title=Almería B sign Aleix Vidal, from Mallorca, and Javi Manzano, from Poli|newspaper=[[Ideal (newspaper)|Ideal]]|first=José Gabriel|last=Gutiérrez|language=es|date=17 June 2011|access-date=16 July 2021|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304185930/http://udalmeria.ideal.es/noticias/2011-06-17/almeria-ficha-aleix-vidal-20110617.html|archive-date=4 March 2016}}</ref> He made his debut for the [[Andalusia]]ns' [[UD Almería|main squad]] on 27 August 2011, against [[Córdoba CF]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2011/08/27/futbol/2adivision/1314476662.html|title=Córdoba y Almería empiezan con un punto|trans-title=Córdoba and Almería start with one point|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=27 August 2011|access-date=28 July 2015}}</ref> Shortly after, he was promoted to the first team and received the No. 8 jersey following the departure of [[Albert Crusat]] to [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.udalmeriasad.com/uda/index.php/inicio/noticias/4066-el-almeria-ficha-a-omar-del-tenerife-y-sube-a-aleix-vidal-al-primer-equipo-|title=El Almería ficha a Omar, del Tenerife, y sube a Aleix Vidal al primer equipo|trans-title=Almería sign Omar from Tenerife, and promote Aleix Vidal to first team|publisher=UD Almería|language=es|date=31 August 2011|access-date=2 September 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120330084000/http://www.udalmeriasad.com/uda/index.php/inicio/noticias/4066-el-almeria-ficha-a-omar-del-tenerife-y-sube-a-aleix-vidal-al-primer-equipo-|archive-date=30 March 2012}}</ref>

In his [[2012–13 Segunda División|second season]], Vidal scored four goals in 37 games – 30 starts, nearly 2,600 minutes of action – helping to a return to [[La Liga]] after two years. On 6 August 2013, he renewed his link with Almería until 2017,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.udalmeriasad.com/uda/index.php/inicio/noticias/5572-aleix-vidal-seguira-vistiendo-de-rojiblanco-hasta-junio-de-2017|title=Aleix Vidal seguirá vistiendo de rojiblanco hasta junio de 2017|trans-title=Aleix Vidal will wear the red-and-white shirt until June 2017|publisher=UD Almería|language=es|date=6 August 2013|access-date=7 August 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130810052432/http://www.udalmeriasad.com/uda/index.php/inicio/noticias/5572-aleix-vidal-seguira-vistiendo-de-rojiblanco-hasta-junio-de-2017|archive-date=10 August 2013}}</ref> making his top-flight debut on 19 August by starting in a 2–3 home loss to [[Villarreal CF]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/en/report/373216/report.html|title=Valiant Villarreal open with win|publisher=[[ESPN FC]]|date=19 August 2013|access-date=18 February 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140118091610/http://espnfc.com/en/report/373216/report.html|archive-date=18 January 2014}}</ref> and scored his first goal roughly a month later, in a 4–2 defeat at [[Atlético Madrid]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/en/report/373177/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=3888|title=Atleti maintain perfect start|publisher=ESPN FC|date=14 September 2013|access-date=18 February 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131023103025/http://espnfc.com/en/report/373177/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=3888|archive-date=23 October 2013}}</ref>

===Sevilla===
[[File:Zenit-Sevilla (3).jpg|thumb|left|181px|Vidal playing for [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] in 2015]]
On 16 June 2014, Vidal signed with [[Sevilla FC]] for a [[Euro|€]]3 million fee, penning a four-year contract.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2014/06/16/futbol/equipos/sevilla/1402909705.html|title=Aleix Vidal pasa reconocimiento médico con el Sevilla|trans-title=Aleix Vidal passes medical with Sevilla|newspaper=Marca|first=Miguel Ángel|last=Morán|language=es|date=16 June 2014|access-date=16 June 2014}}</ref> He made his competitive debut on 12 August in the [[2014 UEFA Super Cup]] at the [[Cardiff City Stadium]], playing 66 minutes before being [[Substitute (association football)|substituted]] for fellow debutant [[Iago Aspas]] in a 2–0 loss to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28741099|title=Super Cup: Cristiano Ronaldo scores twice in Real Madrid win|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|first=Rob|last=Phillips|date=12 August 2014|access-date=13 August 2014}}</ref> He found the net on his league debut 11 days later, opening the 1–1 home draw against [[Valencia CF]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidespanishfootball.com/121701/sevilla-1-1-valencia-vidals-goal-cancelled-out-by-orban/|title=Sevilla 1–1 Valencia: Vidal's goal cancelled out by Orbán|publisher=Inside Spanish Football|first=Jamie|last=Kemp|date=23 August 2014|access-date=25 August 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141030110647/http://www.insidespanishfootball.com/121701/sevilla-1-1-valencia-vidals-goal-cancelled-out-by-orban/|archive-date=30 October 2014}}</ref>

On 7 May 2015, in a game in which he featured as [[right-back]] until [[Coke (footballer)|Coke]] entered the field in the 58th minute – he was often used by manager [[Unai Emery]] in that position during [[2014–15 La Liga|the campaign]]<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2014/11/14/futbol/equipos/sevilla/1415959281.html|title=Chico para todo|trans-title=Factotum|newspaper=Marca|location=Madrid|first=Rocío|last=Guevara|language=es|date=14 November 2014|access-date=7 May 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://sevilla.eldesmarque.com/sevilla-futbol-club/67797-aleix-vidal-acepta-su-papel-de-lateral|title=Aleix Vidal acepta su papel de lateral|trans-title=Aleix Vidal accepts full-back role|publisher=El Desmarque|language=es|date=1 December 2014|access-date=7 May 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107012447/http://sevilla.eldesmarque.com/sevilla-futbol-club/67797-aleix-vidal-acepta-su-papel-de-lateral|archive-date=7 November 2017}}</ref>– Vidal scored twice and also provided an [[Assist (association football)|assist]] to [[Kevin Gameiro]], in a 3–0 home win over [[ACF Fiorentina]] in [[2014–15 UEFA Europa League|the semi-finals]] of the [[UEFA Europa League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0221-0e9b4c1ba9b2-5cc91c893306-1000--sevilla-s-vidal-typhoon-flattens-fiorentina/|title=Sevilla's Vidal typhoon flattens Fiorentina|publisher=UEFA|date=7 May 2015|access-date=7 May 2015}}</ref> He started in [[2015 UEFA Europa League final|the final]] 20 days later, a 3–2 defeat of [[FC Dnipro]] in [[Warsaw]].<ref name=EL>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/32908634|title=Dnipropetrovsk 2–3 Sevilla|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Gary|last=Rose|date=27 May 2015|access-date=28 September 2020}}</ref>

===Barcelona===
On 7 June 2015, Vidal signed a five-year contract with [[FC Barcelona]], for an [[Euro|€]]18 million fee plus four in add-ons.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/aleix-vidal-signs-up-till-2020|title=Aleix Vidal signs up till 2020|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=7 June 2015|access-date=7 June 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150609023647/http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/aleix-vidal-signs-up-till-2020|archive-date=9 June 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/barca/mestre-barcelona-pagado-millones-fijos-mas-cuatro-variables-por-aleix-vidal-4255804|title=Mestre: "El Barcelona ha pagado 18 millones fijos más cuatro de variables por Aleix Vidal"|trans-title=Mestre: "Barcelona paid 18 million plus four variable fixed for Aleix Vidal"|newspaper=Sport|language=es|date=7 June 2015|access-date=8 July 2015}}</ref> He underwent a medical on the following day, being also officially presented.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/20150608/20392110657/cat-futbol-barcelona.html|title=Aleix Vidal pasa la revisión médica y firma por el Barça|trans-title=Aleix Vidal pass medical review and signed by the club|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|language=es|date=8 June 2015|access-date=8 July 2015}}</ref> Due to an embargo placed on the club by [[FIFA]] for breaking rules on signing under-age foreign players, he was not permitted to appear in competitive games until January 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33044583|title=Aleix Vidal: Barcelona sign £16m Sevilla defender despite ban|publisher=BBC Sport|date=8 June 2015|access-date=8 June 2015}}</ref>

Vidal made his official debut for the ''Blaugrana'' on 6 January 2016, replacing [[Dani Alves]] midway through the second half of a 4–1 home victory against former club Espanyol in the [[2015–16 Copa del Rey|round of 16]] of the [[Copa del Rey]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/copa-del-rey/1-8-1st-leg/fc-barcelona_rcd-espanyol|title=FC Barcelona v RCD Espanyol: Messi delivers first-leg victory (4–1)|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=6 January 2016|access-date=6 January 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160109093103/http://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/match-archive/2015-2016/copa-del-rey/1-8-1st-leg/fc-barcelona_rcd-espanyol|archive-date=9 January 2016}}</ref> Subsequently, he was completely ostracised by manager [[Luis Enrique]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espnfc.com/club/barcelona/83/blog/post/2859199/why-barcelona-full-back-aleix-vidal-has-fallen-out-of-favour-with-luis-enrique|title=Why Barcelona full-back Aleix Vidal has fallen out of favour with Luis Enrique|publisher=ESPN FC|first=Samuel|last=Marsden|date=26 April 2016|access-date=16 January 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/barcelona/2016/11/15/582b3a82e5fdea06028b45b6.html|title=Is Aleix Vidal plotting his Sevilla return?|newspaper=Marca|first1=Rocío|last1=Guevara|first2=Aldo|last2=Sainati|date=15 November 2016|access-date=16 January 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/fc-barcelona/20161218/412706647985/andre-gomes-aleix-vidal-y-masip-se-caen-del-derbi.html|title=André Gomes, Aleix Vidal y Masip se caen del derbi|trans-title=André Gomes, Aleix Vidal and Masip ousted for derby|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|language=es|date=18 December 2016|access-date=16 January 2017}}</ref>

On 14 January 2017, profiting from the absence of habitual starting right-back [[Sergi Roberto]], Vidal opened his league account for Barcelona, contributing to a 5–0 rout of [[UD Las Palmas]] at the [[Camp Nou]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/barca/banquillo-celebro-grande-gol-aleix-vidal-barca-las-palmas-5743394|title=El banquillo celebró a lo grande el gol de Aleix Vidal en el Barça – UD Las Palmas|trans-title=Bench had a blast with Aleix Vidal's goal in Barça – UD Las Palmas|newspaper=Sport|first=Juan Manuel|last=Díaz|language=es|date=14 January 2017|access-date=16 January 2017}}</ref> On 11 February, in the last minutes of a 6–0 away win against [[Deportivo Alavés]], he dislocated his ankle following a challenge by [[Théo Hernandez]], being ruled out for the rest of [[2016–17 La Liga|the season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2016-2017/aleix-vidal-suffers-right-ankle-injury-against-alaves|title=Aleix Vidal out five months|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=11 February 2017|access-date=12 February 2017}}</ref>

===Return to Sevilla===
On 4 August 2018, Vidal returned to Sevilla for a fee of €8.5 million plus 2 million in variables.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2018-2019/agreement-sevilla-fc-transfer-aleix-vidal|title=Agreement with Sevilla FC for the transfer of Aleix Vidal|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=4 August 2018|access-date=4 August 2018}}</ref> However, he struggled to settle in the first team, being also deemed surplus to requirements by new manager [[Julen Lopetegui]] in July 2019.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2019/07/02/primera/1562093903_831937.html|title=Aleix Vidal, un nuevo nombre sobre la mesa de Miñambres|trans-title=Aleix Vidal, a new name on Miñambres' table|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Clemente|last=Garrido|language=es|date=2 July 2019|access-date=30 July 2019}}</ref>

On 28 July 2019, Vidal was loaned out to fellow top-tier club Alavés in a [[2019–20 La Liga|season]]-long deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sevillafc.es/en/actual/news/agreement-principle-loan-aleix-vidal-alaves|title=Sevilla FC and Alavés agree loan deal for Aleix Vidal|publisher=Sevilla FC|date=28 July 2019|access-date=29 July 2019}}</ref> On 1 July 2021, he and Sevilla parted ways by mutual consent.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sevillafc.es/en/actual/news/rescind-contract-aleix-vidal-2021|title=Sevilla FC and Aleix Vidal have come to an agreement to rescind the player's contract|publisher=Sevilla FC|date=1 July 2021|access-date=1 July 2021}}</ref>

===Espanyol===
Vidal returned to Espanyol on 18 August 2021, after agreeing to a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rcdespanyol.com/es/actualidad/aleix-vidal-nuevo-jugador-del-rcd-espanyol/_n:12986/|title=Aleix Vidal, nuevo jugador del RCD Espanyol|trans-title=Aleix Vidal, new player of RCD Espanyol|publisher=RCD Espanyol|language=es|date=18 August 2021|access-date=18 August 2021}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Aleix Vidal 2013 Catalonia.jpg|thumb|150px|Vidal during his debut match for [[Catalonia national football team|Catalonia]]]]
Vidal made his debut for [[Catalonia national football team|Catalonia]] on 30 December 2013, playing the second half of a 4–1 win over [[Cape Verde national football team|Cape Verde]] at the [[Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/detail/article/catalonia-cape-verde-catalonia-claim-victory-with-eight-fc-barcelona-players-4-1|title=Catalonia – Cape Verde: Catalonia claim victory with eight FC Barcelona players (4–1)|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=30 December 2013|access-date=15 September 2014}}</ref> On 26 May 2015, he and Sevilla teammate [[Sergio Rico]] were the two players called up to the [[Spain national football team|Spain national team]] for the first time, ahead of a friendly against [[Costa Rica national football team|Costa Rica]] and a [[UEFA Euro 2016]] [[UEFA Euro 2016 qualifying|qualifying match]] against [[Belarus national football team|Belarus]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.beinsports.tv/soccer/article/8fmekfgmj7141sxmbdb6mijvl/title/sevilla-duo-sergio-rico-and-aleix-vidal-handed-spain-calls|title=Sevilla duo Sergio Rico and Aleix Vidal handed Spain calls|publisher=[[beIN Sports]]|date=26 May 2015|access-date=26 May 2015|archive-date=26 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150526155023/http://www.beinsports.tv/soccer/article/8fmekfgmj7141sxmbdb6mijvl/title/sevilla-duo-sergio-rico-and-aleix-vidal-handed-spain-calls|url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his debut in the 2–1 victory against the former at the [[Estadio Reino de León]], playing the entire first half before being substituted for his former Sevilla partner [[Vitolo (footballer, born 1989)|Vitolo]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/spain-vs-costa-rica/2030701/report?ICID=MP_MS_5|title=Spain 2–1 Costa Rica: Alcacer and Fabregas clinch comeback win|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|date=11 June 2015|access-date=11 June 2015}}</ref>

'''Federico Marchetti''' ({{IPA|it|fedeˈriːko marˈketti}}; born 7 February 1983) is an Italian former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/players/player/313831/|url-status=dead|title=2018 FIFA World Cup Russia Players: Federico Marchetti|publisher=FIFA|access-date=16 December 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190110014416/https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/players/player/313831/|archive-date=10 January 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://it.uefa.com/teamsandplayers/players/player=65304/profile/index.html|title=Federico Marchetti|publisher=UEFA|access-date=16 December 2018}}{{Dead link|date=June 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.national-football-teams.com/player/31637/Federico_Marchetti.html|title=Federico Marchetti|website=National Football Teams|access-date=16 December 2018}}</ref>

Marchetti began his professional club career with [[Torino F.C.|Torino]] in 2002. He moved to [[U.S. Pro Vercelli Calcio|Pro Vercelli]], [[F.C. Crotone|Crotone]] on loan, before signing permanently for [[Treviso F.B.C. 1993|Treviso]]. In 2005, Marchetti spent one season with [[A.S. Biellese 1902|Biellese]] and for [[U.C. AlbinoLeffe|AlbinoLeffe]] as well as [[Cagliari Calcio|Cagliari]], before moving to Lazio in 2011, where he won the [[Coppa Italia]] in 2013. At international level, Marchetti has represented Italy at the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]], at the [[2013 FIFA Confederations Cup]] (winning a bronze medal), and at [[UEFA Euro 2016]].

== Club career ==
=== Early career ===
A Torino [[Torino F.C. Primavera|youth system]] trainee, Marchetti made his professional debut on loan to Pro Vercelli, moving on loan to numberous other [[Serie C1]] and [[Serie C2]] teams in the following years.{{Specify|date=June 2026}}. He spent the 2003–04 season as second choice goalkeeper for Crotone and Treviso, only to lack any appearance with said teams. Marchetti started the 2004–05 season as third-choice goalkeeper at Torino, making only one appearance in his time with the ''granata'' as a substitute.{{Citation needed|date=July 2010}} In January 2005, after Torino signed another goalkeeper, [[Gianluca Berti]], he subsequently moved to Pro Vercelli on loan the remainder of the season.{{Citation needed|date=June 2026}}

=== AlbinoLeffe ===
In mid-2005, Torino – which originally promoted to Serie A – went bankrupt and a new team restarted in Serie B as a successor, with all former Torino players being allowed to leave for free. He was signed by AlbinoLeffe and left for Biellese in [[Co-ownership (football)|co-ownership]] deal.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/torino/?action=read&idnotizia=6651|website=TuttoMercatoWeb |language=it |access-date=21 June 2009 |date=3 June 2009 |title=Marchetti, l'eterna preghiera |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120524134321/http://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/torino/?action=read&idnotizia=6651 |archive-date=24 May 2012}}</ref> In June 2006, Marchetti was bought back by [[Serie B]] club AlbinoLeffe, initially as reserve to [[Paolo Acerbis]]. In his first season with the ''celeste'', he made 13 appearances,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.lega-calcio.it/it/Serie-A-TIM/Giocatore.page?idplayer=357FC7D1-1D1C-5050-1BD0-BA22D14C9201 |publisher=Lega Calcio |language=it |access-date=21 June 2009 |title=Marchetti Federico |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090628234037/http://www.lega-calcio.it/it/Serie-A-TIM/Giocatore.page?idplayer=357FC7D1-1D1C-5050-1BD0-BA22D14C9201|archive-date=28 June 2009}}</ref> being successively promoted as first choice goalkeeper the following season.

During the 2007–08 season, his performances proved to be instrumental in AlbinoLeffe's historic first qualification to the promotion playoffs, where his club narrowly missed promotion to [[U.S. Lecce|Lecce]]. He subsequently won the Serie B best goalkeeper award, thus raising significant interest from top-flight teams.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/cagliari/?action=read&idnotizia=1349|url-status=dead|title=I protagonisti – Marchetti, la stagione della maturità|website=TuttoMercatoWeb|language=it|access-date=21 June 2009 |date=17 November 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090603054727/http://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/cagliari/?action=read&idnotizia=1349 |archive-date=3 June 2009}}</ref>

=== Cagliari ===
In July 2008, Cagliari agreed a loan bid with AlbinoLeffe for Marchetti, with the former club an option to buy 50% of players' rights to an agreed price.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.realsports.it/index.php?method=section&action=zoom&id=68822|website=RealSports.it |language=it |access-date=21 June 2009 |date=15 June 2009 |title=Calciomercato – "Marchetti è dell'Albinoleffe" parola di Andreoletti|url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120524134326/http://www.realsports.it/index.php?method=section&action=zoom&id=68822 |archive-date=24 May 2012}}</ref> In his first season in [[Serie A]], Marchetti confirmed his performances, gaining a place in the starting line-up. His performances were also praised by several football pundits and defined by [[Gianluigi Buffon]] as his favourite young Italian goalkeeper.<ref name=buffonchat>{{cite news |url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Primo_Piano/2008/11/17/buffonchat.shtml|newspaper=La Gazzetta dello Sport|publisher=RCS Media Group|language=it |access-date=21 June 2009 |date=17 November 2008 |title=Buffon: "Juve seconda pelle Ma ero quasi del Milan"}}</ref> On 1 February 2010, Cagliari bought the remaining rights from AlbinoLeffe.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cagliaricalcio.net/news/8799/marchetti-e-tutto-del-cagliari.html|title=Marchetti è tutto del Cagliari|date=1 February 2010|access-date=3 April 2011|work=Cagliari Calcio|language=it|archive-date=1 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140101105936/http://www.cagliaricalcio.net/news/8799/marchetti-e-tutto-del-cagliari.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

However, he was frozen out by the club in the 2010–11 season, as his transfer request denied.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11854_6350619,00.html|title=Cagliari deny Marchetti talk|website=Sky Sports|date=31 August 2010|access-date=3 April 2011}}</ref> He became the third keeper, behind [[Michael Agazzi]] and [[Ivan Pelizzoli]]. He was unfrozen on 3 April 2011, winning [[Genoa C.F.C.|Genoa]] as unused bench.

=== Lazio ===
Following the departure of their [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]] international [[Fernando Muslera]] at the end of the [[2010–11 Serie A|2010–11]] season, Marchetti joined Lazio. President [[Claudio Lotito]] activated Marchetti's €5.2 million release clause.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sslazio.it/images/stories/documenti/pdf/investor_relator/relazione_finanziaria%20al%2031-12-11.pdf|title=Relazione Finanziaria|date=29 February 2012|access-date=22 May 2012|website=SS Lazio|language=it|archive-date=24 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924105450/http://www.sslazio.it/images/stories/documenti/pdf/investor_relator/relazione_finanziaria%20al%2031-12-11.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> Marchetti arrived in Rome on 5 July to undertake a medical and sign a five-year contract. He described his move to Lazio as "the end of a nightmare".<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.corrieredellosport.it/calcio/serie_a/lazio/2011/07/05-182028/Marchetti%3A+%C2%ABGrazie+Lazio.+%C3%88+la+fine+di+un+incubo%C2%BB |title=Marchetti: "Grazie Lazio. È la fine di un incubo" |access-date=5 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110809201251/http://www.corrieredellosport.it/calcio/serie_a/lazio/2011/07/05-182028/Marchetti%3A+%C2%ABGrazie+Lazio.+%C3%88+la+fine+di+un+incubo%C2%BB |archive-date=9 August 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
Marchetti played a terrific season for Lazio and his presence and command over the defence together with his numerous saves helped Lazio achieve two consecutive Europa League qualifications with 5th and 4th-place finishes in the 2010–11 and [[2011–12 Serie A|2011–12]] Serie A campaigns respectively.

Federico Marchetti's continued period of good form during the [[2012–13 Serie A|2012–13 season]] saw become one of the club's protagonists; on 26 May 2013, he won the [[2013 Coppa Italia Final|Coppa Italia]] with Lazio, keeping a clean sheet in a historic 1–0 [[Derby della Capitale|Rome derby]] final victory against cross-city rivals [[A.S. Roma|Roma]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22676789|title=Lazio beat rivals Roma in Coppa Italia final|date=26 May 2013|work=BBC Sport|access-date=6 June 2013 }}</ref> His performances led him to be called up once again to the Italy national team.

===Later career===
Marchetti was acquired by [[Genoa C.F.C.|Genoa]] on 2 July 2018 on a free transfer after his contract with Lazio expired.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football-italia.net/123894/official-genoa-pick-marchetti|title=Official: Genoa pick up Marchetti|website=Football Italia|date=2 July 2018}}</ref> On 21 January 2023, signed a six-month contract for [[Spezia Calcio|Spezia]] until the end of the season.{{Citation needed|date=June 2026}}

On 4 July 2023, Marchetti signed a one-year contract with [[Maltese Premier League]] club [[Ħamrun Spartans F.C.|Ħamrun Spartans]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Watch: Ħamrun Spartans complete the signing of former Italy goalkeeper Federico Marchetti |url=https://sport.timesofmalta.com/2023/07/04/watch-hamrun-spartans-complete-the-signing-of-former-italy-goalkeeper-federico-marchetti/|last=Camilleri|first=Valhmor|newspaper=Times of Malta|date=4 July 2023|access-date=5 July 2023}}</ref> He made his debut in the first qualifying round of the [[UEFA Champions League]] during the controversial match against [[Maccabi Haifa F.C.|Maccabi Haifa]].{{When?|date=June 2026}} Marchetti debuted in the Maltese Premier League during Ħamrun Spartans' match against [[Balzan F.C.|Balzan FC]].{{When?|date=June 2026}} He also made three appearances in the [[Maltese FA Trophy]] and contributed to Ħamrun's victory against [[Birkirkara F.C.|Birkirkara FC]] in the [[Maltese Super Cup]] final.{{When?|date=June 2026}} Marchetti also played in the decisive match against [[Floriana F.C.|Floriana FC]],{{When?|date=June 2026}} which ended in a 5–0 victory for Ħamrun Spartans, leading the club to be crowned as champions.{{Citation needed|date=June 2026}} In December 2024, he signed a six-month contract with another Maltese club [[Marsaxlokk F.C.]], a club from the [[Maltese Premier League]]<ref>{{Cite news |title=Marsaxlokk FC sign former Italy international goalkeeper Marchetti|last=Camilleri|first=Valhmor|url=https://sport.timesofmalta.com/2024/12/05/marsaxlokk-fc-sign-former-italy-international-goalkeeper-marchetti/|newspaper=Times of Malta|date=5 December 2024|access-date=23 June 2026}}</ref>

In 2025, Marchetti retired from professional football at the age of 42 and joined the Radio TV Serie A team as a pundit.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fm-world.it/news/radio-tv-serie-a-presenta-due-nuovi-talent-dambrosio-e-marchetti-entrano-in-squadra/|title=Radio Tv Serie A presenta due nuovi talent: D’Ambrosio e Marchetti entrano in squadra|website=FM World|date=20 November 2025|access-date=20 November 2025|language=it}}</ref>

==International career==
In May 2009, following his impressive performances with Cagliari, Marchetti received his first call-up to Italy national team for [[Marcello Lippi]] for a friendly match against [[Northern Ireland national football team|Northern Ireland]].<ref>{{Cite magazine|title=Italy squad for Northern Ireland friendly|url=http://fourfourtwo.com/news/italy/31705/default.aspx|magazine=FourFourTwo|date=28 May 2009|access-date=21 June 2009|archive-date=18 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110718062520/http://fourfourtwo.com/news/italy/31705/default.aspx |url-status=dead }}</ref> He debuted as a starter in said match and played the whole match whilst keeping a clean sheet, ending in a 3–0 victory for the Italians.<ref>{{Cite news|first=Marcello|last=Di Dio|title=Sogno italiano: dall'Albinoleffe ai mondiali|url=https://www.ilgiornale.it/news/sogno-italiano-dall-albinoleffe-ai-mondiali.html|newspaper=[[Il Giornale]]|date=16 June 2010|access-date=23 July 2024|language=it}}</ref>

Marchetti made his competitive debut at the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]], replacing the injured starter Gianluigi Buffon at half-time during Italy's opening Group F clash with [[Paraguay national football team|Paraguay]], which ended in a 1–1 draw. Marchetti kept a clean sheet, as Italy were already 1–0 down at the time of his introduction.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/world_cup_2010/8740361.stm|title=World Cup 2010: Gianluigi Buffon's World Cup in doubt|website=[[BBC Sport]]|publisher=[[BBC]]|date=15 June 2010|access-date=15 June 2010}}</ref> In Marchetti's next two matches, he allowed four goals from five shots on goal, as Italy suffered a 1–1 draw against [[New Zealand men's national football team|New Zealand]],<ref>{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Whyatt|title=Italy 1–1 New Zealand|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/world_cup_2010/matches/match_28/default.stm|website=BBC Sport|publisher=BBC|date=20 June 2010|access-date=14 July 2016}}</ref> and a 3–2 defeat to [[Slovakia national football team|Slovakia]], and were ultimately eliminated from the tournament in the first round, failing to win a match, and finishing last in their group with only two points.<ref>{{cite news|first=Paul|last=Wilson|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2010/jun/24/italy-slovakia-world-cup-match-report|title=World Cup 2010: Italy exit as Slovakia turf out reigning champions|newspaper=The Guardian|date=24 June 2010|access-date=28 June 2012|location=London}}</ref>

Marchetti played only one game for the Italy national team under new coach [[Cesare Prandelli]] between 2010 and 2012. However, in 2013, was recalled by Prandelli to represent Italy in a friendly match against [[Netherlands national football team|Netherlands]]. Marchetti was also selected for Prandelli's 23-man Italy squad for the 2013 FIFA Confederations Cup, as a back-up behind Buffon and [[Salvatore Sirigu]];<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.figc.it/it/204/36469/2013/06/News.shtml|title=Inviata alla FIFA la lista per la Confederations Cup: c'è anche Barzagli|trans-title=Confederations Cup list submitted to FIFA: Barzagli is also included|publisher=[[Italian Football Federation]]|date=3 June 2013|access-date=4 May 2015|language=it|archive-date=8 June 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130608215150/http://www.figc.it/it/204/36469/2013/06/News.shtml|url-status=dead}}</ref> the Confederations Cup 2013 was Marchetti's second major international tournament with Italy, after previously featuring in the 2010 World Cup, and the Italians went on to earn a third-place finish.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/confederationscup/matches/round=255209/match=300222463/summary.html |title=Buffon stars as Italy win shootout & bronze |publisher=[[FIFA]]|date=30 June 2013 |access-date=30 June 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140709035458/http://www.fifa.com/confederationscup/matches/round%3D255209/match%3D300222463/summary.html |archive-date=9 July 2014}}</ref> On 14 August 2013, in honour of [[Pope Francis]], Marchetti was brought on for the second half of an international friendly match between Italy and [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]], played in Rome.<ref>{{cite news|title=International friendly: Argentina claim 2–1 win over Italy|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/live/match/292383/report|website=[[Sky Sports News]]|publisher=Sky Group|date=14 August 2013|access-date=16 May 2014}}</ref>

On 31 May 2016, Marchetti was included in [[Antonio Conte]]'s 23-man Italy squad for UEFA Euro 2016, but remained as the only member of the squad not to play in the tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/85206/official-italy-squad-euro-2016|title=Official: Italy squad for Euro 2016|website=Football Italia|date=31 May 2016|access-date=31 May 2016}}</ref>

==Style of play==
A strong, agile and reliable shot-stopper, Marchetti is considered to be one of the best Italian goalkeepers of his generation; due to his promising performances in his youth, he was considered a possible heir to Gianluigi Buffon as Italy's starting goalkeeper, who himself praised the youngster.<ref name=buffonchat/><ref name=storia>{{cite web|url=http://www.figc.it/it/204/25087/2010/06/News.shtml|title=Marchetti racconta la sua storia: "Un incidente mi ha cambiato la vita"|publisher=Italian Football Federation|language=it|date=17 June 2010|access-date=18 October 2016}}</ref><ref name="Marchetti è il top">{{cite web|url=http://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/altre-notizie/lazio-terraneo-marchetti-e-il-top-sara-il-dopo-buffon-in-nazionale-418912|first=Marco Valerio|last=Bava|title=Lazio, Terraneo: "Marchetti è il top, sarà il dopo-Buffon in Nazionale"|website=TuttoMercatoWeb|language=it|date=25 January 2013|access-date=18 October 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://in.reuters.com/article/idINIndia-49064320100605|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170824012809/https://in.reuters.com/article/idINIndia-49064320100605|url-status=dead|archive-date=24 August 2017|title=Penpix of Italy squad|agency=Reuters|date=5 June 2010|access-date=18 October 2016}}</ref> He is known in particular for his composure, concentration, and his explosive reactions in goal, as well as his speed and bravery when [[Goalkeeper (association football)#Sweeper-keeper|rushing off his line]].<ref name=storia/><ref name="Marchetti è il top"/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ecodibergamo.it/stories/Sport/138663_mondonico_e_la_favola_marchetti__un_grande_buffon_si_preoccupi/ |title=Mondonico e la favola Marchetti "Un grande, Buffon si preoccupi"|newspaper=L'Eco di Bergamo |language=it |date=16 June 2010 |access-date=3 September 2018 }}</ref> In his youth, he played as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] before switching to the role of goalkeeper.<ref name=storia/> Due to his long hair, he earned the nickname ''[[Tarzan]]'' from the Lazio fans.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportmediaset.mediaset.it/calcio/calcio/articoli/89959/il-vocabolario-dei-telecronisti-faziosi.shtml|title=Il vocabolario dei telecronisti faziosi|website=SportMediaSet|language=it|date=24 September 2012|access-date=18 October 2016}}</ref>

'''Roman Bürki''' (born 14 November 1990) is a Swiss professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] for [[Major League Soccer]] club [[St. Louis City SC]]. From 2014 to 2018, he played for the [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland national team]].

==Club career==
===Switzerland===
Bürki began his career in 2007 with the reserve squad of the [[BSC Young Boys]]. In 2009, he moved to [[FC Thun]], and half a year later to [[FC Schaffhausen]]. In the summer of 2010 he went back to BSC Young Boys, and again half a year later he was transferred to [[Grasshopper Club Zürich]]. First, he was the back-up goalkeeper, later the first goalkeeper. He was on loan until 2013, when Grasshoppers bought his rights.

===SC Freiburg===
On 24 May 2014, he signed a contract with [[SC Freiburg]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Herzlich Willkommen, Roman Bürki!|url=http://www.scfreiburg.com/node/8327|publisher=SC Freiburg|access-date=24 May 2014|language=de|date=24 May 2014}}</ref>

For [[2014–15 Bundesliga]] season he succeeded [[Oliver Baumann]] as number one goalkeeper.<ref>[http://www.scfreiburg.com/node/8327 message]</ref> He played in all 34 games, while being unable to prevent the team from being relegated to [[2. Bundesliga]].

===Borussia Dortmund===
On 14 June 2015, he signed for [[Borussia Dortmund]].<ref>[http://www.profutbal.sk/ligy/prestupy-a-spekulacie/clanok193305-Dortmund_ziskal_svajciarskeho_brankara_Burkiho.htm Dortmund získal švajčiarskeho brankára Bürkiho] (in Slovak)</ref> He made his formal debut for the team on 15 August 2015, in a 4–0 win over [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/33541336|title=Borussia Dortmund 4-0 Borussia Monchengladbach|date=15 August 2015|work=BBC Sport|access-date=1 August 2018|language=en-GB}}</ref> He kept 12 clean sheets for Dortmund in the league, making 33 appearances.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www2.squawka.com/players/roman-burki/stats#performance-score#borussia-dortmund-(current)#german-bundesliga#22#season-2015/2016#169#all-matches#1-34#by-match|title=Roman Bürki {{!}} Football Statistics {{!}} Form Guide {{!}} Squawka.com|website=www2.squawka.com|language=en-US|access-date=1 August 2018}}</ref> In the [[2016–17 Borussia Dortmund season|2016–17 season]], he made 27 league appearances, keeping nine clean sheets.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www2.squawka.com/players/roman-burki/stats#performance-score#borussia-dortmund-(current)#german-bundesliga#22#season-2016/2017#682#all-matches#1-34#by-match|title=Roman Bürki {{!}} Football Statistics {{!}} Form Guide {{!}} Squawka.com|website=www2.squawka.com|language=en-US|access-date=1 August 2018}}</ref>

In the [[2017–18 Borussia Dortmund season|2017–18 season]], Bürki became the first goalkeeper to keep five clean sheets in the first five Bundesliga games.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/41340074|title=Hamburger SV 0-3 Borussia Dortmund|date=20 September 2017|work=BBC Sport|access-date=1 August 2018|language=en-GB}}</ref>

===St. Louis City SC===
On 16 March 2022, Bürki agreed to a deal that would send him to [[Major League Soccer]] expansion franchise [[St. Louis City SC]] for their inaugural season in 2023.<ref>{{cite news |title=St. Louis CITY SC Signs Swiss Goalkeeper Roman Bürki From Bundesliga Club Borussia Dortmund |url=https://www.stlcitysc.com/news/st-louis-city-sc-signs-swiss-goalkeeper-roman-burki-from-bundesliga-club-borussi |access-date=30 March 2022 |publisher=St. Louis City SC}}</ref> He is the highest-paid goalkeeper in the league and would earn a $1.5 million base salary.<ref>{{cite news |last=Hochman |first=Benjamin |date=16 February 2023 |title=Hochman: With goalie Roman Burki, City SC tries to 'catch up to his standard' |url=https://www.stltoday.com/sports/soccer/professional/hochman-with-goalie-roman-burki-city-sc-tries-to-catch-up-to-his-standard/article_8d3a6bef-07c9-5227-b6c8-db4008aa8250.html |work=St. Louis Post-Dispatch |accessdate=7 July 2023}}</ref> Bürki played four matches for reserve squad [[St. Louis City 2]] in 2022 along with several other future St. Louis players.<ref>{{cite news |last=Moore-Bloom |first=Arlo |date=18 November 2022 |title=St. Louis City SC celebrates new stadium as roster takes shape for MLS debut |url=https://www.socceramerica.com/publications/article/94317/st-louis-city-sc-celebrates-new-stadium-as-roster.html |work=[[Soccer America]] |url-access=subscription |accessdate=7 July 2023}}</ref> 

On 20 February 2023, Bürki was named the club's captain.<ref>{{cite news |title=Roman Bürki Named St. Louis CITY SC's First Captain|url=https://www.stlcitysc.com/news/st-louis-city-sc-introduces-captain-and-vice-captain|access-date=21 March 2023 |publisher=St. Louis City SC}}</ref>

In November of 2023, Bürki was named MLS Goalkeeper of the Year<ref>{{Cite web |last=SC |first=St Louis CITY |title=St. Louis CITY SC Captain Roman Bürki Named 2023 Allstate MLS Goalkeeper of the Year {{!}} St. Louis SC |url=https://www.stlcitysc.com/news/st-louis-city-sc-captain-roman-burki-named-2023-mls-goalkeeper-of-the-year |access-date=2025-07-13 |website=St. Louis CITY SC |language=en}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:AUT vs. SUI 2015-11-17 (248).jpg|thumb|Bürki with [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]]<nowiki> in 2015</nowiki>]]
Bürki played for [[Switzerland national under-21 football team|Switzerland U-21]] in the [[2011 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|2011 European Under-21 Championship]].

In 2014, Bürki was first called up for [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]] and was also in the  [[2014 FIFA World Cup squads#Switzerland|squad]] for the [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014 World Cup]] in Brazil. On 18 November 2014, he made his debut in a friendly match against [[Poland national football team|Poland]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2014/11/18/world/friendlies/poland/switzerland/1694857/|title=Poland vs. Switzerland – 18 November 2014|website=soccerway.com|publisher=Soccerway|date=18 November 2014|access-date=17 March 2020}}</ref> He was part of the squad for the [[UEFA Euro 2016|2016 European Championships]], but never made it to any match.<ref name="ntdebut">{{cite news|title=Switzerland include three teenagers in final squad for Euro 2016|url=http://www.espnfc.com/switzerland/story/2883266/switzerland-include-three-teenagers-in-final-squad-for-euro-2016|access-date=9 June 2017|work=ESPN FC|date=30 May 2016}}</ref> Ultimately, his team was eliminated in the round of 16 away after losing 5–4 on penalties against [[Poland national football team|Poland]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro-2020/match/2017996--switzerland-vs-poland/postmatch/report/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200918193303/https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro-2020/match/2017996--switzerland-vs-poland/postmatch/report/|url-status=dead|archive-date=18 September 2020|title = Poland edge past Switzerland on penalties in EURO 2016 round of 16|date = 25 June 2016}}</ref>

He was included in Switzerland's 23-man squad for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018 World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44360966|title=2018 World Cup: Switzerland name Granit Xhaka and Xherdan Shaqiri in squad|website=BBC Sport|publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation|date=4 June 2018|access-date=17 March 2020}}</ref>

In 2018, Burki stated that he did not want to be called up to the Switzerland squad in order to focus on the 2018–19 season at Dortmund.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bvb.de/News/Uebersicht/Roman-Buerki-Im-Nationalteam-auf-Standby|title=Roman Bürki: Im Nationalteam auf Standby|work=bvb.de}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Bürki is the older brother of [[FC Thun]] defender [[Marco Bürki]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.srf.ch/play/tv/sport-clip/video/buerki-ueber-die-beziehung-zu-bruder-roman?id=25556690-201a-4409-9713-ffd409fabbc6|title=Bürki über die Beziehung zu Bruder Roman|website=SRF|date=14 November 2018|access-date=1 June 2020|language=de}}</ref> He is married to Oana, with whom he has three children: a daughter born in 2010, and two sons born in 2012 and 2013, respectively.{{citation needed|date=August 2026}}

'''Ulrich Jean Eugène Ramé''' (born 19 September 1972) is a French former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]].

In a professional career which spanned two decades, he played mainly for [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]] (14 seasons), appearing in more than 500 official matches and winning six major titles.

A [[France national football team|French international]] during four years, Ramé represented the nation at [[UEFA Euro 2000|Euro 2000]].

==Club career==
Born in [[Nantes]], Loire-Atlantique,<ref name="lequipe"/> Ramé started playing professionally with [[SCO Angers]], making his [[Ligue 1]] debut in [[1993–94 French Division 1|1993–94]] but being immediately relegated. [[1995–96 French Division 2|Two years later]] the [[Maine-et-Loire]] club dropped down [[Championnat National|another division]], but the player returned to the top flight the following season, signing for [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux]].{{citation needed|date=December 2020}}

After 23 appearances in [[1997–98 French Division 1|his debut campaign]], helping his team finish fifth and reach the [[Coupe de la Ligue|domestic League Cup]] [[1998 Coupe de la Ligue Final|final the following year]], Ramé became Bordeaux's undisputed first-choice. He helped the side win two national championships – separated by ten years – and three more league cups.{{citation needed|date=December 2020}}

In the [[2009–10 Ligue 1|2009–10 campaign]], after [[Cédric Carrasso]]'s signing, 37-year-old Ramé became the backup. In June 2011, after 520 matches played with the ''Girondins'' all competitions comprised, he returned to [[Ligue 2]] and joined [[CS Sedan Ardennes]].<ref>[http://www.francefootball.fr/#!/news/2011/06/10/191757_rame-a-sedan.html Ramé à Sedan (Ramé to Sedan)]; [[France Football]], 10 June 2011 (in French)</ref>

==International career==
Ramé made his debut for [[France national football team|France]] on 9 June 1999, in a [[UEFA Euro 2000]] [[UEFA Euro 2000 qualifying|qualifying]] 1–0 win in [[Andorra national football team|Andorra]]. He was subsequently picked for the final stages' squad, with the national team winning the tournament; after [[Bernard Lama]]'s international retirement, he became second-choice.{{citation needed|date=December 2020}}

Ramé played three matches at the [[2001 FIFA Confederations Cup]], with France again emerging victorious. Again as a backup, he represented the nation in the [[2002 FIFA World Cup]], also in [[South Korea]]; after making a blunder against [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic]] on 12 February 2003, however, he fell out of favor with manager [[Jacques Santini]] and was not recalled again.{{citation needed|date=December 2020}}

'''Hugo Guillamón Sanmartín''' (born 31 January 2000) is a Spanish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[defensive midfielder]] or [[centre-back]] for [[Sporting de Gijón]].

Guillamón came through the youth ranks at [[Valencia CF|Valencia]], where he made his first-team debut in 2020. He made his senior international debut for Spain in 2021, and was chosen for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]].

==Club career==
Born in [[San Sebastián]], [[Gipuzkoa]], [[Basque Country (autonomous community)|Basque Country]], Guillamón moved to [[L'Eliana]], [[Valencian Community]] at the age of two.<ref name="Nacio">{{cite web|url=https://www.superdeporte.es/valencia/2020/02/22/hugo-guillamon-debuta-san-sebastian/442973.html|title=Hugo Guillamón debuta en San Sebastián... ¡Donde nació!|trans-title=Hugo Guillamón makes his debut in San Sebastián... Where he was born!|publisher=[[Super Deporte]]|language=es|date=22 February 2020|accessdate=28 June 2020}}</ref> He made his senior debut with [[Valencia CF Mestalla|the reserves]] on 16 December 2017, coming on as a first-half [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for [[Ivan Zotko]] in a 0–0 [[Segunda División B]] home draw against [[CF Badalona|Badalona]].

On 23 December 2017, Guillamón renewed his contract with the ''Che'' until 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.levante-emv.com/valencia-cf/2017/12/23/valencia-renueva-hugo-guillamon/1658719.html|title=El Valencia renueva a Hugo Guillamón|trans-title=Valencia renew Hugo Guillamón|publisher=[[Levante-EMV]]|language=es|date=23 December 2017|accessdate=28 June 2020}}</ref> The following 27 October, he scored his first senior goal, netting the opener in a 3–2 home loss against [[CD Alcoyano|Alcoyano]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.elespanol.com/deportes/futbol/segunda-division-b/20181028/alcoyano-vence-antonio-puchades/1001396900345_29.html|title=El Alcoyano vence en el Antonio Puchades (2–3)|trans-title=Alcoyano win at the Antonio Puchades (2–3)|publisher=El Español|language=es|date=28 October 2018|accessdate=28 June 2020}}</ref>

Guillamón made his first team – and [[La Liga]] – debut on 22 February 2020, replacing injured [[Eliaquim Mangala]] at half-time in a 3–0 defeat away to [[Real Sociedad]].<ref name="Nacio"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/primera-division/cronica/2020/02/22/5e5162f4268e3e6e3a8b45ee.html|title=La Real se exhibe ante un Valencia hundido|trans-title=Real put on a show against a sunken Valencia|publisher=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=22 February 2020|accessdate=28 June 2020}}</ref> On 22 July, he renewed his contract until 2023, being definitely promoted to the main squad.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.valenciacf.com/en/article/en-official-statement-i-hugo-guillamon-2020-07-22|title=Official Statement {{!}} Hugo Guillamón|publisher=Valencia CF|date=22 July 2020|accessdate=8 August 2020}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the team on 22 November in a 2–2 draw at [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Fuster |first1=Vicente |title=(2-2) El Valencia paga su mal inicio con un empate en Vitoria|trans-title=(2-2) Valencia pay for their bad start with a draw in Vitoria|url=https://plazadeportiva.valenciaplaza.com/cronica-alaves-valencia-cf1 |publisher=Plaza Deportiva|date=22 November 2020|access-date=6 September 2021 |language=Spanish}}</ref>

On 13 August 2021, in the first game of the season at home to [[Getafe CF|Getafe]], Guillamón fouled [[Nemanja Maksimović]] after 39 seconds. After consulting the [[video assistant referee]], his third-minute [[Ejection (sports)|dismissal]] was the earliest on a La Liga opening weekend; his team nonetheless won 1–0.<ref>{{cite web |title=Football: Ten-man Valencia overcome third-minute red card to beat Getafe in season opener |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/sport/football/football-ten-man-valencia-overcome-third-minute-red-card-to-beat-getafe-in-season |publisher=[[The Straits Times]] |access-date=6 September 2021 |date=14 August 2021}}</ref>

Guillamón started in the [[2022 Copa del Rey Final]], being substituted in the 85th minute as Valencia lost on penalties to [[Real Betis]].<ref>{{cite news |title=El Betis levanta su tercera Copa del Rey tras ganar en los penaltis en una final histórica|trans-title=Betis lift their third Copa del Rey after winning on penalties in a historic final |url=https://www.cope.es/deportes/futbol/copa-del-rey/noticias/directo-final-copa-del-rey-betis-valencia-23-04-2022-20220423_2043293 |access-date=17 November 2022 |publisher=[[Cadena COPE]] |date=23 April 2022 |language=Spanish}}</ref> On 3 October that year, he extended his contract to last until June 2026.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Fuster |first1=Vicente |title=Oficial: Hugo Guillamón renueva con el Valencia hasta junio de 2026|trans-title=Official: Hugo Guillamón renews with Valencia until June 2026|url=https://plazadeportiva.valenciaplaza.com/oficial-hugo-guillamon-renueva-con-el-valencia-hasta-junio-de-2026 |access-date=17 November 2022 |publisher=Plaza Deportiva |date=3 October 2022 |language=Spanish}}</ref>

On 26 August 2025, after five seasons with Valencia's first team, Guillamón joined Croatian side [[HNK Hajduk Split]] on a free transfer, signing a two-year contract with the club.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hugo Guillamón Transfer from Valencia to Hajduk Split |url=https://www.transferfeed.com/transfers/hugo-guillamon-valencia-hajduk-split/16128286 |access-date=2025-09-12 |website=www.transferfeed.com |language=en}}</ref> On 28 July of the following year, he returned to Spain after agreeing to a two-year deal with [[Segunda División]] side [[Sporting de Gijón]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realsporting.com/noticias/comunicado-oficial-hugo-guillamon|title=Comunicado oficial: Hugo Guillamón|trans-title=Official statement: Hugo Guillamón|publisher=Sporting Gijón|language=es|date=28 July 2026|accessdate=28 July 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
Guillamón represented [[Spain national football team|Spain]] at [[Spain national under-17 football team|under-17]] and [[Spain national under-19 football team|under-19]] levels, having won the [[2017 UEFA European Under-17 Championship]] for the former<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/under17/history/season=2017/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170606164420/http://www.uefa.com/under17/history/season=2017/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=6 June 2017|title=Spain secure record third U17 EURO title|publisher=[[UEFA]]|date=19 May 2017|access-date=28 June 2020}}</ref> and [[2019 UEFA European Under-19 Championship]] for the latter.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://plazadeportiva.valenciaplaza.com/hugo-guillamon-un-campeon-de-europa-sub19-en-apuros|title=Hugo Guillamón, un campeón de Europa sub19 en apuros|trans-title=Hugo Guillamón, a champion of the European Under-19 Championship in troubles|publisher=Plaza Deportiva|language=es|date=18 October 2019|accessdate=28 June 2020}}</ref>

Due to the isolation of some national team players following the positive [[COVID-19]] test of [[Sergio Busquets]], Spain's under-21 squad were called up for the international friendly against [[Lithuania national football team|Lithuania]] on 8 June 2021.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://sefutbol.com/oficial-lista-convocados-encuentro-lituania |title=Oficial {{!}} Lista de convocados para el encuentro ante Lituania |trans-title=Official {{!}} Squad list for the match against Lithuania |work=[[Royal Spanish Football Federation]] |date=6 June 2021 |access-date=7 June 2021 |language=es |archive-date=8 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211008070336/https://sefutbol.com/oficial-lista-convocados-encuentro-lituania |url-status=dead }}</ref> Guillamón made his senior debut in the match and scored in the 3rd minute of their 4–0 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/international-football/espana-vs-lituania/cronica/2021/06/08/60bfd85222601dc65d8b458f.html|title=Spain youngsters impress in Lithuania rout|website=Marca|date=8 June 2021|accessdate=8 June 2021}}</ref>

Guillamón was chosen for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]] in [[Qatar]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Azzoni |first1=Tales |title=University student Guillamón among Spain defenders in Qatar |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/soccer/university-student-guillamon-among-spain-defenders-in-qatar/ |access-date=17 November 2022 |work=[[The Seattle Times]] |date=15 November 2022}}</ref> He took no part in Spain's four matches, and the side were eliminated in the last 16 by [[Morocco national football team|Morocco]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Torres |first1=David |title=Guillamón se vuelve para casa sin debutar: lo que cobra el Valencia por su Mundial |trans-title=Guillamón returns home without debuting: what Valencia make from his World Cup|url=https://www.eldesmarque.com/valencia/valencia-cf/380605-guillamon-se-vuelve-para-casa-sin-debutar-lo-que-cobra-el-valencia-por-su-mundial?ssp |access-date=6 December 2022 |publisher=El Desmarque |date=6 December 2022 |language=Spanish}}</ref>

==Personal life==
As of November 2022, Guillamón was combining his professional football career with a degree in [[biomedical engineering]] from the [[Technical University of Valencia]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Hidalgo |first1=Jorge |title=Hugo Guillamón, el universitario que irá con la selección española a Qatar|trans-title=Hugo Guillamón, the university student who will go with the Spanish national team to Qatar|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/valencia/2022/11/11/636e822a22601d1d5f8b458c.html |access-date=17 November 2022 |work=Marca |date=11 November 2022 |language=Spanish}}</ref>

'''Pedro Munitis Álvarez''' (born 19 June 1975) is a Spanish former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played mainly as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]], currently a [[Manager (association football)|manager]].

His 20-year senior career was mainly associated with [[Racing de Santander]] – he also represented [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] for two years – and he played 447 [[La Liga]] matches over 17 seasons, scoring 43 goals.<ref name=LEGEND>{{cite news|url=http://racing.eldiariomontanes.es/leyendas/munitis.html|title=Munitis|newspaper=[[El Diario Montañés]]|language=es|access-date=13 February 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131019203451/http://racing.eldiariomontanes.es/leyendas/munitis.html|archive-date=19 October 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2011/12/12/futbol/equipos/racing/1323720915.html|title=Munitis es ya el racinguista con más partidos en Primera|trans-title=Munitis is already Racing player with more games in ''Primera''|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=12 December 2011|access-date=31 January 2014}}</ref>

A [[Spain national football team|Spain international]] in the late 1990s/early 2000s, Munitis represented the country at [[UEFA Euro 2000|Euro 2000]].

==Club career==
Born in [[Santander, Spain|Santander]], [[Cantabria]], Munitis played in three separate periods for hometown [[Racing de Santander]]. He first appeared with its first team on 22 January 1995, in a 0–0 home draw against [[Real Sociedad]].<ref name=LEGEND/>

After a loan to [[CD Badajoz|Badajoz]] ([[Segunda División]])<ref name=LEGEND/> and scoring 14 goals in 72 league games with Racing from 1998 to 2000,<ref name=Bio/> Munitis attracted attention from [[La Liga]] giants [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], who signed him for [[Pound sterling|£]]6.8 million.<ref name=Dream>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/829329.stm|title=Munitis in "dream move"|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=11 July 2000|access-date=15 February 2011}}</ref> He was relatively used in his two-year spell at the [[Madrid|capital]] club, helping it to [[2000–01 La Liga|one league]] and the [[2001–02 UEFA Champions League]].

Munitis spent the [[2002–03 La Liga|2002–03 season]] on loan at Racing Santander, notably netting (and celebrating) against Real Madrid in a 2–0 home win on 19 October 2002.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/025e-0f90780df6ba-7d0816154ce1-1000--spain-round-up-madrid-stumble-at-santander/|title=Spain round-up: Madrid stumble at Santander|publisher=UEFA|date=19 October 2002|access-date=23 February 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XEh5tn1eFH4|title=Racing 2 Real Madrid 0 (golazo de Munitis en la 02/03)|trans-title=Racing 2 Real Madrid 0 (Munitis wonder goal in 02/03)|publisher=[[YouTube]]|language=es|date=4 June 2006|access-date=16 October 2008}}</ref> In the following off-season, he was purchased up by [[Deportivo de La Coruña]] on a [[Free transfer (association football)|free transfer]];<ref name=Depor>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/025a-0eaada92ddc8-cad11046a643-1000--munitis-makes-depor-move/|title=Munitis makes Depor move|publisher=UEFA|date=28 August 2003|access-date=1 May 2010}}</ref> after a poor [[2003–04 La Liga|first year]] he would be one of the [[Galicia (Spain)|Galicia]] side's most important attacking players, also being used as a [[Midfielder#Winger|left winger]] in order to provide rest for veteran [[Captain (association football)|captain]] [[Fran (footballer, born 1969)|Fran]] and being his replacement when he retired at the end of [[2004–05 La Liga|2004–05]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.libertaddigital.com/deportes/munitis-si-soy-suplente-mi-rendimiento-baja-y-me-perjudica-1276203211/|title=Munitis: "Si soy suplente mi rendimiento baja y me perjudica"|trans-title=Munitis: "If i do not start i don't contribute as much and that is harmful to me"|newspaper=[[Libertad Digital]]|language=es|date=3 October 2003|access-date=30 October 2017}}</ref>

news|url=https://www.eldiariomontanes.es/prensa/20061030/deportes/munitis-zigic-pareja-letal_20061030.html|title=Munitis y Zigic, pareja letal|trans-title=Munitis and Zigic, lethal duo|newspaper=El 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.eldiariomontanes.es/20090420/deportes/racing/triste-celebracion-para-munitis-20090420.html|title=Triste celebración para Munitis y Luis Fernández|trans-title=Sad celebration for Munitis and Luis Fernández|newspaper=El Diario Montañés|language=es|date=20 April 2009|access-date=30 October 2017}}</ref>

In [[2009–10 La Liga|2009–10]], the 34-year-old Munitis was again an undisputed starter, but did not manage to find the net in 29 appearances, and his season was over during a 3–1 home victory over Espanyol due to a knee injury, on 14 April 2010;<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2010/04/15/futbol/equipos/racing/1271284643.html|title=Munitis se perderá el resto de la temporada por sufrir una rotura del ligamento lateral interno de su rodilla {{sic|nolink=y|dercha}}|trans-title=Munitis to lose rest of the season after internal lateral ligament rupture to his right knee|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=15 April 2010|access-date=31 January 2014}}</ref> at that time he ranked second in [[Assist (association football)|assists]], only trailing [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]]'s [[Lionel Messi]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2010/01/19/mas_futbol/1263886023_850215.html|title=Munitis es clave en la recuperación del equipo|trans-title=Munitis is key in team recovery|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|first=Pedro|last=López|language=es|date=19 January 2010|access-date=31 January 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/barca/messi-goleador-asistente-835277|title=Messi, goleador y asistente|trans-title=Messi, scorer and passer|newspaper=[[Sport (Spanish newspaper)|Sport]]|first=D.|last=Salinas|language=es|date=4 February 2010|access-date=23 February 2022}}</ref>

On 17 October 2010, after more than one year without scoring, Munitis netted from 30 metres for the only goal of the home fixture against [[UD Almería|Almería]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/302132?cc=5739|title=Racing Santander 1–0 Almeria|publisher=[[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]]|date=17 October 2010|access-date=15 February 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110628223243/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/302132?cc=5739|archive-date=28 June 2011}}</ref> During [[2010–11 La Liga|the season]], he again featured prominently in the starting XI under both [[Miguel Ángel Portugal]] and his successor [[Marcelino García Toral]], the latter returned to the [[Campos de Sport de El Sardinero]] after nearly three years. In [[2011–12 La Liga|the following campaign]] he failed to score in 32 matches, and Racing returned to the second tier after one decade, with the player announcing shortly after his decision to leave his main club.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realracingclub.es/comunicacion/actualidad/ampliar.php?Id_contenido=9828|title=Munitis se despide orgulloso de su carrera racinguista|trans-title=Munitis bids farewell to Racing career with pride|publisher=Racing Santander|language=es|date=18 May 2012|access-date=31 May 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117020526/http://www.realracingclub.es/comunicacion/actualidad/ampliar.php?Id_contenido=9828|archive-date=17 November 2015}}</ref>

==International career==
Munitis earned 21 [[Cap (sport)|caps]] for [[Spain national football team|Spain]], scoring two goals. He represented the nation at [[UEFA Euro 2000]], appearing as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] and netting in a 4–3 group stage win over [[Yugoslavia national football team|Yugoslavia]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/euro2000/800459.stm|title=Spain survive in seven-goal classic|publisher=BBC Sport|date=21 June 2000|access-date=16 July 2013}}</ref> and starting in the quarter-final loss to [[France national football team|France]] (2–1).<ref name=Dream/>

Munitis' debut came on 27 March 1999 in a [[UEFA Euro 2000 qualifying|Euro 2000 qualifier]] against [[Austria national football team|Austria]], playing 30 minutes in a 9–0 thrashing in [[Valencia]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://elpais.com/diario/1999/03/28/deportes/922575601_850215.html|title=España vive una noche idílica|trans-title=Spain live idyllic night|newspaper=El País|first=Cayetano|last=Ros|language=es|date=28 March 1999|access-date=26 November 2015}}</ref>
