==Style of play==
Described as a "poacher" in the media, Munitis was capable of playing either as a forward or [[midfielder]] but was usually deployed as a [[Midfielder#Winger|left winger]], and was one of the shortest players in the Spanish top flight throughout his career. He was best known for his speed, [[Dribbling#Association football|dribbling]] skills, creative ability, direct movement and fighting spirit, which made him an effective offensive threat inside the penalty box and difficult for opposing defenders to mark, with Frenchman [[Lilian Thuram]] labelling him as one of his most difficult opponents.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2002/oct/21/europeanfootball.sport1|title=Pocket Pedro delights in Real revenge|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|first=Sid|last=Lowe|date=21 October 2002|access-date=3 January 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/copa-del-rey/2005-2006/depor-edge-valencia_sto816169/story.shtml|title=Depor edge Valencia|publisher=[[Eurosport]]|date=19 January 2006|access-date=3 January 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/la-liga/2006-2007/munitis-back-at-racing_sto940528/story.shtml|title=Munitis back at Racing|publisher=Eurosport|date=8 August 2006|access-date=3 January 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2007/mar/19/europeanfootball.sport1|title=Little and Large deliver the perfect punch-line for Racing|newspaper=The Guardian|first=Sid|last=Lowe|date=19 March 2007|access-date=3 January 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://en.as.com/en/2021/12/12/soccer/1639310224_161076.html|title=Barcelona, Zidane, Ronaldo... Thuram reveals player anecdotes|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Calum|last=Roche|date=12 December 2021|access-date=3 January 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en-US/the-club/history/football-legends/pedro-manuel-munitis-alvarez|title=An electrifying forward in Madrid's Ninth European Cup win|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=15 February 2024}}</ref><ref name=Depor/>

==Coaching career==
Still not having announced his retirement, Munitis began his managerial career, with [[Women's association football|women's football]] club [[SD Reocín (women)|Reocín]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.eldiariomontanes.es/v/20120910/deportes/futbol-regional/minuto-final-priva-munitis-20120910.html|title=Un gol en el minuto final priva a Munitis de un estreno con triunfo en el banquillo|trans-title=A goal in the last minute deprives Munitis of win in his bench debut|newspaper=El Diario Montañés|first=Yésica|last=Mata|language=es|date=10 September 2012|access-date=11 September 2012}}</ref> In 2014 he was appointed at Bansander, taking charge of the youth squads.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://contrameta.com/pedro-munitis-dirigira-al-juvenil-del-bansander/|title=Pedro Munitis dirigirá al Juvenil del Bansander|trans-title=Pedro Munitis will manage Bansander's ''Juvenil''|publisher=Contrameta|language=es|date=25 April 2014|access-date=4 March 2015}}</ref>

Munitis returned to Racing on 3 March 2015, being appointed assistant manager along with former teammate [[Gonzalo Colsa]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2015/03/03/segunda/1425387927_662618.html|title=Hoy comienza la quinta era de Pedro Munitis en el Racing|trans-title=Pedro Munitis' fifth spell at Racing begins today|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Roberto|last=González|language=es|date=3 March 2015|access-date=4 March 2015}}</ref> After [[2014–15 Segunda División|their relegation]], he took the reins of the team in [[Segunda División B]] and [[2015-16 Segunda Division B|won the group]], but left in June 2016 following elimination by [[Cádiz CF|Cádiz]] in [[2016 Segunda División B playoffs|the playoffs]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/mas-futbol/2016/06/12/575dca4b268e3ef90d8b4587.html|title=Munitis deja de ser entrenador del Racing|trans-title=Pedro Munitis no longer manager of Racing|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=12 June 2016|access-date=15 February 2019}}</ref>

On 17 October 2016, Munitis succeeded [[Manolo Herrero (footballer, born 1970)|Manolo Herrero]] as manager of newly relegated [[SD Ponferradina|Ponferradina]], with Colsa as his assistant.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2016/10/17/mas_futbol/1476717714_621264.html|title=Pedro Munitis, nuevo entrenador de la Ponferradina|trans-title=Pedro Munitis, new manager of Ponferradina|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Álvaro|last=Carrera|language=es|date=17 October 2016|access-date=15 February 2019}}</ref> He resigned five months later with the team lying in sixth in division three, having won exactly a third of his games.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2017/03/19/segunda/1489947896_736001.html|title=Munitis dimite como entrenador de la Ponferradina|trans-title=Munitis resigns as manager of Ponferradina|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Pedro|last=Iranzo|language=es|date=19 March 2017|access-date=15 February 2019}}</ref>

Munitis returned to third-tier management on 26 March 2018, when he was hired by [[UCAM Murcia CF|UCAM Murcia]] until the end of [[2017–18 Segunda División B|the season]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/deportes/20180326/441974341173/el-ucam-cf-ficha-al-cantabro-pedro-munitis-como-entrenador.html|title=El UCAM CF ficha al cántabro Pedro Munitis como entrenador|trans-title=UCAM CF sign Cantabrian Pedro Munitis as manager|newspaper=[[La Vanguardia]]|language=es|date=26 March 2018|access-date=15 February 2019}}</ref> Despite missing his objective of a [[2018 Segunda División B play-offs|play-off place]], he was given another year in the job.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.laopiniondemurcia.es/deportes/2018/06/13/pedro-munitis-llega-acuerdo-seguir/930315.html|title=Pedro Munitis llega a un acuerdo para seguir en el UCAM Murcia|trans-title=Pedro Munitis reaches an agreement to continue at UCAM Murcia|newspaper=La Opinión de Murcia|first=Alberto|last=F. Martínez|language=es|date=13 June 2018|access-date=15 February 2019}}</ref> He was dismissed on 29 April 2019 with the team still in contention for the [[2019 Segunda División B play-offs|play-offs]] with three rounds to go, and replaced by [[Juan Merino]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2019/04/29/mas_futbol/1556551804_338158.html|title=Munitis, despedido del UCAM|trans-title=Munitis, fired by UCAM|newspaper=Diario AS|language=es|date=29 April 2019|access-date=16 August 2019}}</ref>

On 4 February 2020, Munitis succeeded [[Mehdi Nafti]] at Badajoz, where he had played over two decades ago.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/mas-futbol/segunda-b-grupo-iiii/2020/02/04/5e394c22ca4741f56e8b4606.html|title=Pedro Munitis nuevo entrenador del Badajoz|trans-title=Pedro Munitis new manager of Badajoz|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=4 February 2020|access-date=27 April 2020}}</ref> After [[2019–20 Segunda División B|the season]] was truncated by the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain|COVID-19 pandemic]], the team lost in the [[2020 Segunda División B play-offs|playoff]] semi-finals on [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]] to [[FC Barcelona Atlètic|Barcelona B]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.canalextremadura.es/deportes/futbol/barcelona-b-1-1-badajoz-el-badajoz-se-queda-fuera-del-sueno-del-ascenso-en-los|title=Barcelona B 1–1 Badajoz: El Badajoz se queda fuera del sueño del ascenso en los penaltis|trans-title=Barcelona B 1–1 Badajoz: Badajoz miss out on promotion dream on penalties|publisher=[[Canal Extremadura Televisión]]|first=David|last=Bris|language=es|date=23 July 2020|access-date=17 December 2021}}</ref> He left on his own terms in October, shortly before the start of the [[2020–21 Segunda División B|new campaign]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.hoy.es/deportes/futbol/liga-segunda-b/munitis-dice-deja-20201013210023-nt.html|title=Munitis se va del Badajoz «por voluntad propia»|trans-title=Munitis leaves Badajoz "by own free will"|newspaper=[[Hoy (Extremadura)|Hoy]]|first=Javi|last=Pérez|language=es|date=14 October 2020|access-date=17 December 2021}}</ref>

Munitis was appointed at [[CE Sabadell FC|Sabadell]] of the [[Primera División RFEF]] on 23 November 2021, until the end of the [[2021–22 Primera División RFEF|season]] and with the option of another year.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.diaridesabadell.com/2021/11/23/pedro-munitis-ce-sabadell-banqueta-hidalgo/|title=Pedro Munitis és l'escollit per substituir Antonio Hidalgo|trans-title=Pedro Munitis is chosen to replace Antonio Hidalgo|newspaper=Diari de Sabadell|first=Pere|last=Figueras|language=ca|date=23 November 2021|access-date=17 December 2021}}</ref> He took the team out of the relegation zone and challenged for the [[2022 Primera División RFEF play-offs|play-offs]] until the penultimate round of fixtures; in June, he left after turning down a contract renewal.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.diaridesabadell.com/2022/06/25/ce-sabadell-munitis-banqueta-candidats/|title=Pedro Munitis no continuarà com a entrenador del CE Sabadell|trans-title=Pedro Munitis will not continue as manager of CE Sabadell|newspaper=Diari de Sabadell|first=Pere|last=Figueras|language=ca|date=25 June 2022|access-date=7 October 2022}}</ref>

On 21 June 2023, Munitis was named in charge of [[CD Lugo|Lugo]], [[2022–23 Segunda División|recently relegated to the third division]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cdlugo.com/noticias/pedro-munitis-nuevo-entrenador-del-cd-lugo|title=Pedro Munitis, nuevo entrenador del CD Lugo|trans-title=Pedro Munitis, new manager of CD Lugo|publisher=CD Lugo|language=es|date=21 June 2023|access-date=21 June 2023}}</ref> On 16 December, he was sacked.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cdlugo.com/noticias/comunicado-oficial-pedro-munitis|title=Comunicado oficial. Pedro Munitis|trans-title=Official announcement. Pedro Munitis|publisher=CD Lugo|language=es|date=16 December 2023|access-date=17 December 2023}}</ref>

'''Layvin Marc Kurzawa''' (born 4 September 1992) is a French professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[left-back]].

Kurzawa began his career at [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] in 2010, and played 96 games for the team, scoring eight goals. In 2015, he joined [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] for €23 million. Kurzawa won 16 domestic trophies with PSG, including four [[Ligue 1]] titles. He made his senior international debut for [[France national football team|France]] in 2014.

==Club career==
===Monaco===
[[File:Zenit-Monako (7).jpg|thumb|upright|Kurzawa playing for [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] in 2014]]

Kurzawa was born in [[Fréjus]], France.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/person/pe230562/layvin-kurzawa/ |title=Layvin Kurzawa: Profile |website=worldfootball.net |publisher=HEIM:SPIEL |access-date=20 May 2020}}</ref> He made his professional debut on 22 September 2010, soon after his 18th birthday, in a [[Coupe de la Ligue]] third round match against [[RC Lens|Lens]] at the [[Stade Louis II]]. He started the match and played 65 minutes before being substituted in a 1–0 victory.<ref>{{cite news |title=Monaco v. Lens Match Report |url=http://www.lfp.fr/coupeLigue/feuilleMatch.asp?saison=2010/2011&code_evt=CL&num_ordre=5&code_jr_tr=T95 |date=22 September 2010 |publisher=Ligue de Football Professionnel |access-date=22 September 2010 |language=fr |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100926104033/http://www.lfp.fr/coupeLigue/feuilleMatch.asp?saison=2010%2F2011&code_evt=CL&num_ordre=5&code_jr_tr=T95 |archive-date=26 September 2010}}</ref> Three days later he made his [[Ligue 1]] debut, starting in a 1–2 defeat at [[FC Lorient|Lorient]]. Kurzawa played four more league matches, all of them starts, as the season ended with relegation to [[Ligue 2]]; he was sent off on 1 May 2011 in a 1–1 draw at [[AS Saint-Étienne|Saint-Étienne]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Layvin Kurzawa suspendu face au PSG|trans-title=Layvin Kurzawa suspended against PSG |url=https://www.planete-asm.fr/actualite/7685-layvin-kurzawa-suspendu-face-au-psg.html |access-date=13 March 2016 |publisher=PLANETE ASM |date=1 May 2011 |language=fr}}</ref> He made four appearances as they [[2011–12 Ligue 2|returned to the top flight at the first attempt as champions]].{{citation needed|date=May 2020}}

Kurzawa established himself in the first team for the [[2013–14 Ligue 1|2013–14 season]], with 28 league appearances as Monaco finished runner-up to [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]]. He also scored five goals, the first of his professional career confirming a 2–0 win at [[En Avant de Guingamp|Guingamp]] on 14 December 2013.<ref>{{cite news |title=Martial magic for Monaco |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/live/match/290053/report |access-date=4 December 2014 |website=Sky Sports |date=14 December 2013}}</ref>

He scored in each leg of Monaco's 7–1 aggregate win over [[BSC Young Boys|Young Boys]] in the third qualifying round of the [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Creek |first1=Stephen |title=Champions League round-up: Ajax crash out and Monaco cruise through |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/1716/champions-league/2015/08/04/14165312/champions-league-round-up-ajax-crash-out-and-monaco-cruise |access-date=5 August 2015 |website=Goal.com |date=4 August 2015}}</ref>

===Paris Saint-Germain===
On 27 August 2015, Kurzawa joined Ligue 1 champions Paris Saint-Germain for €23 million on a five-year contract.<ref>{{cite news |title=KURZAWA SIGNS WITH PARIS SAINT-GERMAIN UNTIL 2020 |url=http://www.psg.fr/en/News/003001/Article/72000/Kurzawa-signs-with-Paris-Saint-Germain-until-2020 |access-date=27 August 2015 |publisher=Paris Saint-Germain F.C. |date=27 August 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Johnson |first1=Jonathan |title=Layvin Kurzawa from Monaco to PSG a shrewd move by Ligue 1 champions |url=http://www.espnfc.co.uk/club/paris-saint-germain/160/blog/post/2584843/psg-sign-layvin-kurzawa-monaco |access-date=28 November 2015 |website=ESPN FC |date=28 August 2015}}</ref> He made his debut on 11 September, coming on for [[Maxwell (footballer, born 1981)|Maxwell]] in the 67th minute of an eventual 2–2 draw with [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]] at the [[Parc des Princes]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Paris Saint-Germain 2–2 Bordeaux: Trapp howler sees hosts slip against 10-man visitors |url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/match/psg-vs-bordeaux/2045896/report |access-date=28 November 2015 |website=Goal.com |date=11 September 2015}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the team from the [[Paris|capital]] on 25 October, opening a 4–1 home win over Saint-Étienne when set up by [[Marco Verratti]].<ref>{{cite news |title=PSG 4–1 St Etienne: Leaders stay unbeaten |url=http://www.skysports.com/football/psg-vs-st-etienne/341675 |access-date=28 November 2015 |website=Sky Sports |date=25 October 2015}}</ref>

Kurzawa scored and assisted [[Javier Pastore]] on 6 August 2016 as PSG won the [[Trophée des Champions]] against [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] with a [[2016 Trophée des Champions|4–1 win]] in [[Klagenfurt]], Austria.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.espnfc.com/club/paris-saint-germain/160/blog/post/2924572/psg-and-unai-emery-impress-in-trophee-des-champions-win-vs-lyon |title=New-look Paris Saint-Germain rout Lyon to win Trophee des Champions |website=ESPN FC |date=6 August 2016 |access-date=8 March 2017}}</ref> Six days later, he recorded the team's first league goal of the [[2016–17 Ligue 1|new season]], the game's only against [[SC Bastia|Bastia]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.skysports.com/football/bastia-vs-psg/355174 |title=Bastia 0–1 PSG |date=12 August 2016 |website=Sky Sports}}</ref> On 8 March 2017, he scored an [[own goal]] in a [[FC Barcelona 6–1 Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|6–1]] loss to [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in the last 16 of the Champions League; as [[Unai Emery]]'s team squandered a 4–0 advantage from the first leg.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/mar/08/barcelona-psg-champions-league-match-report |title=Barcelona shatter PSG as Roberto caps absurd 6–1 comeback win |newspaper=The Guardian |date=8 March 2017 |access-date=9 March 2017}}</ref>

On 31 October 2017, Kurzawa scored his first career hat-trick against [[R.S.C. Anderlecht|Anderlecht]] in the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] group phase.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.beinsports.com/au/uefa-champions-league/video/kurzawa-hat-trick-sees-psg-through/695959 |title=KURZAWA HAT-TRICK SEES PSG THROUGH |date=1 November 2017 |website=BeinSports}}</ref> Kurzawa became the first defender in modern Champions League history to achieve this feat in the competition.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2 November 2017 |title=Kurzawa is first defender to score hat-trick in Champions League |work=[[Egypt Today]] |url=https://www.egypttoday.com/Article/8/30551/Kurzawa-is-first-defender-to-score-hat-trick-in-Champions |access-date=28 February 2023}}</ref>

On 29 June 2020, Kurzawa signed a four-year contract extension with [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Layvin Kurzawa signs 4-year contract extension with PSG|url=https://www.getfootballnewsfrance.com/2020/layvin-kurzawa-signs-4-year-contract-extension-with-psg/|access-date=29 June 2020|website=Get French Football News}}</ref> On 13 September 2020, Kurzawa was one of many players involved in a brawl in [[Le Classique]], which resulted in five red cards. He was given a six match suspension for his actions.<ref>{{Cite web|date=17 September 2020|title=Neymar cops two-match ban|url=https://www.ligue1.com/Articles/NEWS/2020/09/17/psg-marseille-neymar-cops-two-match-ban|access-date=20 September 2020|website=Ligue 1}}</ref>

====Loan to Fulham====
On 1 September 2022, Kurzawa joined [[Premier League]] side [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] on a season-long loan.<ref>{{cite web|last=Pruce|first=Geoff|url=https://www.fulhamfc.com/news/2022/september/01/kurzawa-joins-on-loan/|title=Kurzawa Joins On Loan |date=1 September 2022|access-date=1 September 2022|publisher=Fulham F.C.}}</ref> Kurzawa scored his first goal for Fulham on 7 January 2023 against [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] in the [[FA Cup]] 3rd round.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Fulham see off Hull to reach FA Cup fourth round |language=en-GB |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/64167919 |access-date=2023-01-08}}</ref>

====Final season====
On 13 May 2024, Kurzawa announced the end of his career with PSG after appearing in just one match throughout the [[2023–24 Paris Saint-Germain F.C. season|2023–24 season]].<ref>[https://paris-supporters.fr/2024/05/13/buzz-psg/un-nouveau-parisien-annonce-son-depart-96394.html]</ref>

===Boavista===
On 12 February 2025, Kurzawa was one of 9 players [[Boavista FC|Boavista]] signed on free transfers, a day after [[FIFA]] lifted a transfer ban that had prevented the club from making signings in each of the past five transfer windows.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-02-13 |title=Boavista: Portuguese club sign nine players in one day |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cx2q3pqdv78o |access-date=2025-08-07 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> He signed a deal that would run until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Layvin Kurzawa set for Boavista move|url=https://www.getfootballnewsfrance.com/2025/layvin-kurzawa-set-for-boavista-move/|work=Get French Football News|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Costa |first=Pedro |date=2025-02-12 |title=Plantel reforçado com nove jogadores |url=https://boavistafc.pt/plantel-reforcado-com-nove-jogadores/ |access-date=2025-08-07 |website=BOAVISTA Futebol Clube |language=pt-PT}}</ref> On 14 February 2025, he made his debut for Boavista, coming on as a substitute in a 1–0 loss against [[C.F. Estrela da Amadora|Estrela Amadora]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Summary - Layvin Kurzawa - Results, fixtures, squad, statistics, photos, videos - Soccerway |url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/layvin-kurzawa/155095/ |access-date=2025-08-07 |website=int.soccerway.com}}</ref>

===Persib Bandung===
On 25 January 2026, Kurzawa signed for Indonesian club [[Persib Bandung]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://persib.co.id/article-details/wilujeng-sumping-layvin-kurzawa|title= Wilujeng Sumping Layvin Kurzawa|trans-title=Welcome Layvin Kurzawa|language=id|date=25 January 2026|publisher=persib.co.id}}</ref> Kurzawa chose 3 as his squad number.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DT8CAhGk2m4/?img_index=1&igsh=cW9hNm42eDMyMnAy |title= Amunisi baru #PERSIB dimumkan malam ini di GBLA 💙 Wilujeng sumping @kurzawa & @dion.markx 🤝 |language=id|date=25 January 2026|publisher=Instagram}}</ref> He made his debut on 11 February in the first leg of the [[2025–26 AFC Champions League Two|AFC Champions League Two]] round of 16 tie against Thai club [[Ratchaburi F.C.|Ratchaburi]].

==International career==
Kurzawa was born to a [[Guadeloupean]] father,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://la1ere.francetvinfo.fr/2014/11/10/le-guadeloupeen-layvin-kurzawa-appele-en-equipe-de-france-par-didier-deschamps-205436.html |title=Le Guadeloupéen Layvin Kurzawa appelé en équipe de France par Didier Deschamps|trans-title=Guadeloupean Layvin Kurzawa called up for the French team by Didier Deschamps |website=France Info |publisher=France TV |language=fr |date=10 November 2014 |access-date=30 March 2020}}</ref> and a Polish mother, and was approached to play for the [[Poland national football team|Poland national team]].<ref>{{cite news |title=La fédération polonaise recrute sur Facebook |trans-title=The Polish FA is recruiting on Facebook |url=http://www.20min.ch/ro/sports/football/story/La-f-d-ration-polonaise-recrute-sur-Facebook-10339232 |date=18 January 2011 |website=20 Minutes |access-date=18 January 2011 |language=fr |archive-date=18 October 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191018055410/https://www.20min.ch/ro/sports/football/story/La-f-d-ration-polonaise-recrute-sur-Facebook-10339232 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.20min.ch/ro/sports/football/story/La-f-d-ration-polonaise-recrute-sur-Facebook-10339232 |title=La fédération polonaise recrute sur Facebook |access-date=18 January 2011 |archive-date=18 October 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191018055410/https://www.20min.ch/ro/sports/football/story/La-f-d-ration-polonaise-recrute-sur-Facebook-10339232 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He was a [[France national youth football team|French youth international]] and has earned caps with the [[France national under-19 football team|under-19]] team.<ref>{{cite news |title=Kurzawa: "Un rêve éveillé" |url=http://www.fff.fr/selections/m19ans/actualite/534657.shtml |date=2 September 2010 |publisher=French Football Federation |access-date=22 September 2010 |language=fr}}</ref> On 14 October 2014, during the final leg of the [[2015 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification play-offs]] against [[Sweden national under-21 football team|Sweden]], Kurzawa celebrated a goal for France by mocking the Swedish players with a salute. Shortly after, Sweden scored a goal and won the game 4–1, thus eliminating [[France national under-21 football team|France]] from the [[2015 UEFA European Under-21 Championship]]. Afterwards the Swedish players celebrated their victory by saluting, in direct reference to Kurzawa's celebration earlier.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/soccer-dirty-tackle/france-u-21-defender-learns-why-you-should-never-mock-your-opponents-before-the-final-whistle-034614627.html |title=France U-21 defender learns why you should never mock your opponents before the final whistle |website=Yahoo Sports |date=15 October 2014 |access-date=30 March 2020}}</ref>

On 14 November 2014, he made his full international debut, replacing [[Lucas Digne]] for the last 20 minutes of a 1–1 friendly draw with [[Albania national football team|Albania]] in [[Rennes]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Griezmann earns France draw with Albania |url=https://www.uefa.com/friendlies/season=2016/matches/round=2000543/match=2014079/postmatch/report/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141120055300/http://www.uefa.com/friendlies/season=2016/matches/round=2000543/match=2014079/postmatch/report/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=20 November 2014 |access-date=15 November 2014 |publisher=UEFA |date=14 November 2014}}</ref> Four days later, he made his first start, in a 1–0 friendly win over [[Sweden men's national football team|Sweden]] in [[Marseille]], being substituted later on for Digne.<ref>{{cite news |title=France 1–0 Sweden: Varane secures win for dominant Bleus |url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/france-vs-sweden/1946143/report |access-date=19 November 2014 |website=Goal.com |date=18 November 2014}}</ref>

Kurzawa scored his first international goal on 1 September 2016, concluding a 3–1 friendly win over [[Italy national football team|Italy]] at the [[Stadio San Nicola]] in [[Bari]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Italy 1–3 France: Anthony Martial and Olivier Giroud score in French away win |url=http://www.skysports.com/football/italy-vs-france/365519 |access-date=11 March 2017 |website=Sky Sports |date=1 September 2016}}</ref>

'''Emiliano Moretti''' {{postnominals|post-noms=[[Order of Merit of the Italian Republic|Cavaliere OMRI]]}} ({{IPA|it|emiˈljaːno moˈretti}}; born 11 June 1981) is an Italian former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|centre back]].

He began his career at [[AS Lodigiani|Lodigiani]] and was signed by [[AC Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] in 1998. In March 2001 he made his debut in [[Serie A]] under [[Roberto Mancini]], before spending periods at [[Juventus FC|Juventus]], [[Modena FC|Modena]], [[Parma FC|Parma]] and [[Bologna FC 1909|Bologna]]. In 2004, he was signed by Spaniards [[Valencia CF|Valencia]], where he won the [[Copa del Rey]] in [[2007–08 Copa del Rey|2007–08]]. In 2009, he returned to Italy where he spent four seasons with [[Genoa CFC|Genoa]]. In August 2013, he was signed by [[Torino FC|Torino]], where he remained until his retirement in 2019, having collected over 600 career appearances at club level.

Internationally, Moretti represented Italy at under-16 and [[Italy national under-20 football team|under-20]] youth levels. He was also part of the [[Italy national under-21 football team|under-21 team]] that won the [[UEFA European Under-21 Championship]] and a bronze medal at the [[Football at the 2004 Summer Olympics|2004 Summer Olympics]]. On 18 November 2014, at the age of 33, he became the oldest player to debut for the [[Italy national football team]], playing as a starter in a friendly against [[Albania national football team|Albania]]. In total, he collected 2 appearances for Italy at senior level between 2014 and 2015.

==Club career==
===Early career===
Moretti started his career with local club [[AS Lodigiani|Lodigiani]], and in 1998 transferred to [[AC Fiorentina|Fiorentina]]. He made his Serie A debut in March 2001, and was a member of the team that won the 2001 [[Coppa Italia]]. In the 2001–02 season, he played in 27 matches. Right before the Fiorentina [[bankruptcy]], Moretti moved to [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in June 2002 for a fee of €2.6 million,<ref name=Juventus2003bilancio/> and was loaned to [[Modena FC|Modena]] to help them avoid relegation.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://en.archive.uefa.com/footballeurope/news/Kind=2/newsId=51537.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140531113009/http://en.archive.uefa.com/footballeurope/news/Kind=2/newsId=51537.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=31 May 2014 |title=Modena draft Moretti |date=29 January 2003 |access-date=31 May 2014 |publisher=[[UEFA]] }}</ref> In 2003, [[Parma AC|Parma]] signed Moretti for €1.8 million<ref name=Juventus2003bilancio>{{cite web|url=http://www.juventus.com/media/native/investor-relations-docs/english/financial-statemet-and-reports/2002-2003/28_ott_2003_eng.pdf|title=Reports and Financial Statements at 30 June 2003|date=28 October 2003|access-date=18 December 2017|location=Turin|publisher=Juventus FC}}</ref> (part of [[Stephen Appiah]]'s €2 million loan<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.juventus.com/media/native/investor-relations-docs/english/price-sensitive-press-releases/2003-2004/comunicato%2030062003%20appiah%20eng.pdf |title=Agreements with Parma A.C. S.p.A. |date=30 June 2003 |access-date=18 December 2017|location=Turin|publisher=Juventus FC}}</ref>), loaning him to Serie A team [[Bologna FC 1909|Bologna]]. In 2004, with Parma facing financial problems and [[Claudio Ranieri]] becoming head coach of [[Valencia CF|Valencia]], the left defender was traded to Valencia.<ref name="vivoazzurro.it">{{cite web|url=http://vivoazzurro.it/soccer-player/emiliano-moretti/|title=Emiliano Moretti|publisher=Vivo Azzurro|language=it|date=10 November 2014|access-date=10 February 2016}}</ref>

===Valencia===
In the summer of 2004 he was transferred outright to Spanish club Valencia, who had already purchased fellow Italians [[Bernardo Corradi]], [[Marco Di Vaio]] and [[Stefano Fiore]]. On 27 August, while remaining on the bench, he was part of the team that won the [[UEFA Super Cup]], beating Porto 2–1. [[Claudio Ranieri]] would use Moretti predominantly at left-back, and, despite a difficult start due to competition with [[Fábio Aurélio]] and compatriot [[Amedeo Carboni]], would soon earn the starting spot. He scored his first goal for Valencia on 28 November 2004 in the [[La Liga|Primera División]] in a 2–0 home win against [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]]. In the [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] he played 4 games against [[Inter Milan]], [[Werder Bremen]] and [[Anderlecht]], with 29 appearances during the season.

The following season, he was a starter, making 33 appearances and a decisive contribution to the achievement of a third-place finish. At the beginning of the following season, on 6 November 2006, in the match against [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]], Moretti was seriously injured, damaging his lateral ligament of the knee, forcing him to the sidelines for more than three months. Despite the injury, the season remained one of the most important on a personal level and as a team, which reached the quarter-finals of the Champions League, defeated only by [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]. Moretti ended the year with 34 total appearances.

The 2007–08 season was not as positive, which concluded with Valencia tenth. Moretti remained a protagonist of the side, leading to Valencia's victory on 16 April 2008 in the [[2008 Copa del Rey final]], playing all the matches from the initial stage to the final.

The following season, he was still a starter in the Spanish side, which reached the first knockout round of the [[UEFA Cup]], which concludes the year sixth place in the Primera División. Moretti disputed 32 games.

===Genoa===
After 172 appearances and 4 goals with the Spanish club, he returned to Italy to play for [[Genoa CFC|Genoa]], engaged in the [[Europa League]]. The transfer fee was €3.5 million, according to Genoa.<ref>{{cite book|chapter=Nota Integrativa|title=Genoa C.F.C. S.p.A. bilancio al 2009-12-31|trans-title=Genoa C.F.C. S.p.A. financial report at 31 December 2009|date=2010|publisher=Italian [[Camera di Commercio, Industria, Agricoltura e Artigianato|C.C.I.A.A.]]|location=Genoa|page=Capitolo 2|no-pp=y|language=it}}</ref>

He made his debut for Genoa on 23 August 2009, a 3–2 victory at home against [[AS Roma|Roma]]. A week later he scored his first goal in red and blue colours against [[Atalanta BC|Atalanta]]. His first season with the ''Grifoni'' finished with 37 appearances and 1 goal in total. The following year, he only made 18 appearances under [[Gian Piero Gasperini]], while the team finished the season in tenth place. The 2011–12 season is even more difficult for the team, and despite 27 appearances and a goal (against Inter Milan), Genoa finished in fourth last position. He was confirmed part of the Genoa defence for the 2012–13 season, contributing 33 total appearances.

On 5 May 2013, he celebrated his hundredth appearances in [[Serie A]] with the shirt of Genoa, on the occasion of a match ending 4–1 against [[Pescara Calcio|Pescara]].

===Torino===

After being close to a renewal with Genoa,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/serie-a/esclusiva-tmw-genoa-moretti-verso-il-rinnovo-idea-biennale-453991|title=ESCLUSIVA TMW - Genoa, Moretti verso il rinnovo. Idea biennale|website=TUTTOmercatoWEB.com|access-date=7 July 2017}}</ref> on 11 July 2013 he was signed by [[Torino FC|Torino]]<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://genoacfc.it/notizie/moretti-passa-al-torino/ |title=MORETTI PASSA AL TORINO |date=11 July 2013 |access-date=31 May 2014 |publisher=Genoa CFC |language=it |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140531162411/http://genoacfc.it/notizie/moretti-passa-al-torino/ |archive-date=31 May 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://torinofc.it/news/09/07/2013/moretti-al-toro_2348|title=Moretti al Toro!|date=11 July 2013|access-date=31 May 2014|publisher=Torino FC|language=it}}</ref> on a free transfer,<ref>{{cite book|chapter=Nota Integrativa|title=Genoa C.F.C. S.p.A. bilancio al 2013-12-31|trans-title=Genoa C.F.C. S.p.A. financial report at 31 December 2013|date=2014|publisher=Italian C.C.I.A.A.|location=Genoa|page=40|language=it}}</ref> on a two-year contract. He made his competitive debut for the ''Granata'' on 17 August, in [[Coppa Italia]] against [[Pescara Calcio|Pescara]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2013/08/17/italy/coppa-italia/torino-fc/pescara-calcio/1568297/ |title=Torino vs. Pescara - 17 August 2013 - Soccerway |publisher=Au.soccerway.com |date=17 August 2013 |access-date=2 June 2014}}</ref> He scored his first official goal for Torino on 24 December in a 4–1 win against [[Catania Calcio|Catania]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2013/11/24/italy/serie-a/torino-fc/calcio-catania/1552086/|title=Torino vs. Catania - 24 November 2013 - Soccerway|website=au.soccerway.com|access-date=7 July 2017}}</ref> At the end of the season he extended his contract until 2016.

On 25 January 2015, he scored a goal in the 94th minute in which Torino defeated [[Inter Milan]] at [[San Siro]] after 27 years.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://forzaitalianfootball.com/2015/01/torino-defender-breaks-27-year-san-siro-curse/|title=Torino defender breaks 27-year San Siro curse|website=Forzaitalianfootball.com|date=25 January 2015 |access-date=7 July 2017}}</ref> It was his second goal for Torino.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fourfourtwo.com/au/news/inter-0-torino-1-moretti-ends-unbeaten-run-top-four-hopefuls|title=Australian FourFourTwo|website=FourFourTwo|access-date=7 July 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2015/01/25/italy/serie-a/fc-internazionale-milano/torino-fc/1836495/?ICID=PL_MS_07|title=Inter vs. Torino - 25 gennaio 2015 - Soccerway|website=it.soccerway.com|access-date=7 July 2017}}</ref>

On 30 August, he scored his first goal of the [[2015–16 Serie A|2015–16 season]], the equaliser in a 3–1 home win against [[AC Fiorentina|Fiorentina]]. On 25 November, his contract was renewed until 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.repubblica.it/sport/calcio/serie-a/torino/2015/11/25/news/rinnovi_bovo_gazzi_moretti_vives-128150869/|title=Torino, dopo Maxi Lopez tocca alla vecchia guardia. Arrivano altri quattro rinnovi|date=25 November 2015|website=Repubblica.it|access-date=7 July 2017}}</ref> On 2 April 2017, he scored his first goal of the [[2016–17 Serie A|2016–17 season]] in a 2–2 home draw against [[Udinese Calcio|Udinese]]. On 5 April, his contract was renewed until 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://torinofc.it/news/05/04/2017/moretti-rinnova-sino-al-2018_14188|title=Moretti rinnova sino al 2018|website=Torinofc.it|access-date=7 July 2017}}</ref>

On 26 May 2019, he made his last appearance for Torino and of his football career, coming on as a substitute for [[Armando Izzo]], and helped Torino beat [[SS Lazio|Lazio]] 3–1 at home, after which he retired from professional football; in total, he collected over 600 career appearances at club level<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.corrieredellosport.it/news/calcio/serie-a/2019/05/26-57319655/torino-lazio_3-1_lultima_va_a_mazzarri_festa_per_moretti/ |title=Torino-Lazio 3-1: l'ultima va a Mazzarri. Festa per Moretti |publisher=Il Corriere dello Sport |language=it |date=26 May 2019 |access-date=27 May 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.repubblica.it/sport/calcio/serie-a/2019/05/26/news/torino_lazio_partita-227228771/ |title=Torino-Lazio 3-1: Iago Falque, Lukic e De Silvestri firmano il successo granata |publisher=La Repubblica |language=it |author1=Fabrizio Turco |date=26 May 2019 |access-date=27 May 2019 }}</ref>

==International career==
Moretti was in Italy's squad in the [[1998 UEFA European Under-16 Championship]], which the ''Azzurrini'' lost to Republic of Ireland in the final. With the [[Italy national under-21 football team|under-21]], he won the [[UEFA European Under-21 Championship]] and a bronze medal at the [[2004 Summer Olympics]] [[Football at the 2004 Summer Olympics|football tournament]].<ref name="vivoazzurro.it"/>

On 9 November 2014, he was called up to the senior [[Italy national football team|national team]] by [[Antonio Conte]] ahead of a [[UEFA Euro 2016 qualifying]] match against [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]] and a friendly against [[Albania national football team|Albania]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Liverpool's Mario Balotelli recalled to Italy squad for Euro qualifier|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/nov/09/liverpool-mario-balotelli-recalled-italy-euro-qualifier|access-date=10 November 2014|work=[[The Guardian]]|agency=[[Press Association]]|date=10 November 2014}}</ref> On 18 November, he was deployed as a starter in [[Genoa]] during a 1–0 win against [[Albania national football team|Albania]], becoming, at 33 years, 5 months and 7 days, the [[Italy national football team records#Appearances|oldest player to debut for Italy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-italia.net/58828/italy-okaka-breaks-albania|title=Italy: Okaka breaks Albania|publisher=Football Italia|date=18 November 2014|access-date=10 February 2016}}</ref> He made his second and final appearance for Italy a 1–1 friendly draw against [[England national football team|England]] in Turin on 31 March 2015.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/32028730 |title=Italy 1–1 England |publisher=BBC Sport |author1=Phil McNulty |date=31 March 2015 |access-date=27 May 2019 }}</ref>

==Style of play==
A naturally left-footed [[Defender (association football)|defender]], Moretti was originally an attacking [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|left-back]], but throughout his career he has often been used as a [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|central defender]]. He is noted for his physicality, good positional sense, excellent technique, and ability in the air.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gazzettagranata.com/?2E33ekXH|title=Il pagellone 2014/2015: Gaston Silva|publisher=Gazzetta Granata|language=it|author1=Giulia Abbate|date=5 June 2015|access-date=10 February 2016}}</ref>

'''Nemanja Matić''' ({{lang-sr-Cyrl|Немања Матић}}, {{IPA|sh|němaɲa mǎːtitɕ|pron}}; born 1 August 1988) is a Serbian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[defensive midfielder]] for {{Italian football updater|Sassuolo}} club [[US Sassuolo Calcio|Sassuolo]].

Matić began his senior career at [[FK Kolubara|Kolubara]], before joining Slovak side [[FC VSS Košice|Košice]] in 2007. He moved to English club [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] for £1.5 million in 2009. Used sparingly during his first spell at the club, he spent the [[2010–11 Eredivisie|2010–11 season]] on loan at Dutch club [[SBV Vitesse|Vitesse]], and in the summer of 2011, he moved to Benfica as part of a swap deal involving [[David Luiz]]. He won the [[LPFP Primeira Liga Player of the Year|Primeira Liga Player of the Year]] award for his performances in the [[2012–13 S.L. Benfica season|2012–13]] season.<ref name="Ref1" />

Matić returned to Chelsea in January 2014, for £21 million. He was an integral part of a Chelsea team that won two Premier League titles. He was named in the [[PFA Team of the Year]] for the 2014–15 season. In July 2017, he was reunited with former Chelsea manager [[José Mourinho]] after signing for [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]. He played with Manchester United until 2022 when he again was reunited with Mourinho at [[AS Roma|Roma]]. After one season with Roma, he joined [[Stade Rennais FC|Rennes]] in 2023.<ref name=":0" />

Matić represented Serbia at [[Serbia national under-21 football team|under-21]] level. He made his [[Serbia national football team|senior]] international debut in 2008 and scored two goals in 48 appearances. He was part of Serbia's squad at the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]].<ref name=":1" />

==Club career==
===Early career===
Matić was born in [[Šabac]], SR Serbia.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/person/pe109573/nemanja-matic/ |title=Nemanja Matić|website=WorldFootball|publisher=Heim: Spiel|access-date=6 July 2020 |archive-date=6 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200706194500/https://www.worldfootball.net/player_summary/nemanja-matic/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He began playing football at age five with FK Vrelo from the eponymous [[Vrelo (Ub)|village]], coached by his own father.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Teenage Kicks: Nemanja Matic |url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2014/11/teenage-kicks--nemanja-matic.html|website=Chelsea F.C.|date=19 November 2014 |access-date=10 June 2017 |archive-date=30 July 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170730223400/http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2014/11/teenage-kicks--nemanja-matic.html |url-status=dead}}</ref> He began his senior career at [[FK Kolubara|Kolubara]] before signing for Slovak club [[FC VSS Košice|Košice]] in 2007.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Matic accepts Chelsea contract offer |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/matic-accepts-chelsea-contract-offer |magazine=FourFourTwo |date=15 July 2009 |access-date=26 June 2017 |archive-date=22 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180922135909/https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/matic-accepts-chelsea-contract-offer |url-status=dead }}</ref> While living in the country, he also received [[Slovak nationality law|Slovak citizenship]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://sport.sme.sk/c/4033074/matic-so-slovenskym-obcianstvom-do-repre-az-o-tri-roky.html |title=Matič so slovenským občianstvom, do repre až o tri roky|website=[[Sme]]|publisher=Petit Press|date=2 January 2014 |access-date=11 February 2015|language=sk|archive-date=4 November 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141104181415/http://sport.sme.sk/c/4033074/matic-so-slovenskym-obcianstvom-do-repre-az-o-tri-roky.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Chelsea===
On 18 August 2009, Matić signed for [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] from Košice for a fee of around £1.5 million on a four-year contract, having been on trial at [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/c/chelsea/8206912.stm |title=Chelsea confirm signing of Matic |date=18 August 2009 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=18 August 2009 |archive-date=18 August 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090818101835/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/c/chelsea/8206912.stm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11661/4658145/matic-impressed-with-boro |title=Nemanja Matić on trial at Middlesbrough |website=Sky Sports |date=14 February 2014 |access-date=14 February 2014 |archive-date=22 February 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222015833/http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11661/4658145/matic-impressed-with-boro |url-status=live }}</ref> He was given the number 24 shirt by Chelsea but could not debut immediately due to the injury he picked up at the [[2009 UEFA European Under-21 Football Championship]]. He was on the bench for Chelsea's [[EFL Cup|League Cup]] match against [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] on 23 September 2009, but did not take any part in the 1–0 victory. Matić made his [[Premier League]] debut for Chelsea on 21 November, coming on as a substitute for [[Florent Malouda]] in the 69th minute in a 4–0 victory against [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/8365169.stm |website=BBC Sport |last=Lyon |first=Sam |title=Chelsea 4–0 Wolves |date=21 November 2009 |access-date=21 November 2009 |archive-date=26 October 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101026160810/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/8365169.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 23 August 2010, Matić transferred to [[Eredivisie]] club [[SBV Vitesse|Vitesse]] on a one-year loan, together with teammates [[Slobodan Rajković]] and [[Matej Delač]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://nos.nl/artikel/180339-vitesse-huurt-drietal-van-chelsea.html |title=Vitesse huurt drietal van Chelsea |publisher=Nederlandse Omroep Stiching|date=23 August 2010 |access-date=24 August 2010 |archive-date=25 August 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100825163430/http://nos.nl/artikel/180339-vitesse-huurt-drietal-van-chelsea.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Benfica===
[[File:Nemanja Matić.jpg|thumb|upright=0.7|Matić playing for [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] in 2012]]
On 31 January 2011, Matić agreed to join Portuguese club [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] next summer as part of a transfer for Chelsea to sign Brazilian centre-back [[David Luiz]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea sign David Luiz from Benfica for £21.3m |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/c/chelsea/9372540.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=1 February 2011 |access-date=17 January 2019 |archive-date=3 September 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170903134923/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/c/chelsea/9372540.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> Under Benfica manager [[Jorge Jesus]], Matić was converted from a [[playmaker]] into a defensive midfielder.<ref name=interview>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/mar/14/nemanja-matic-chelsea-interview |title=Nemanja Matic: 'We spoke for one minute. I had no doubt in coming back' |date=15 March 2014 |newspaper=The Guardian |access-date=12 December 2016 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304100426/http://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/mar/14/nemanja-matic-chelsea-interview |url-status=live }}</ref> On 14 April 2012, Matić started for Benfica in the [[2012 Taça da Liga Final]] against [[Gil Vicente F.C.|Gil Vicente]], where he won his first trophy with the [[Lisbon]]-based club.<ref name=interview/>

On 13 January 2013, Matić scored Benfica's first goal in a 2–2 draw against ''[[O Clássico]]'' rivals [[FC Porto|Porto]].{{Citation needed|date=July 2025}} The next day, he was awarded with a contract extension until 2018, with the buyout clause set at €45 million.<ref>{{Cite web|title=PortuGOAL: Matic handed new Benfica deal|url=http://www.portugoal.net/index.php/more-benfica-news/38833-matic-handed-new-benfica-deal|url-status=dead|website=PortuGOAL|date=14 January 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140427012546/http://www.portugoal.net/index.php/more-benfica-news/38833-matic-handed-new-benfica-deal|archive-date=27 April 2014}}</ref>

In the second leg of Benfica's [[2012–13 UEFA Europa League knockout phase#Round of 32|Europa League round of 32 tie]] against [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]], Matić headed in a late goal after a cross from [[Lima (footballer, born 1983)|Lima]] to seal a 3–1 aggregate victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0206-0e9eac3dec62-0e224d82455e-1000--stylish-benfica-put-an-end-to-leverkusen/ |title=Stylish Benfica put an end to Leverkusen |publisher=UEFA |date=21 February 2013 |access-date=5 July 2013 |archive-date=5 June 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130605001756/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/season=2013/matches/round=2000357/match=2010056/postmatch/report/index.html |url-status=dead}}</ref> He was a key member throughout the [[2012–13 Primeira Liga]] as Benfica looked to claim their club's first league championship since [[2009–10 Primeira Liga|2010]]. Going into the penultimate game of the season against Porto, both teams were undefeated in league play,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.goal.com/en-us/match/85403/porto-vs-benfica/preview |title=Primeira Liga Preview: Porto – Benfica: Jorge Jesus' men could lift their first Primeira Liga in three years with victory, while the Dragao would go top if they can triumph in front of their own fans. |website=Goal.com |date=10 May 2013 |access-date=5 July 2013 |archive-date=29 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170829005042/http://www.goal.com/en-us/match/85403/porto-vs-benfica/preview |url-status=dead}}</ref> but a stoppage-time winner from substitute [[Kelvin Mateus de Oliveira|Kelvin]] gave Porto a 2–1 victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://espnfc.com/news/story/_/id/1454181/porto-clinches-3rd-straight-portuguese-title?cc=5901 |title=Porto claims 27th title on last day |website=ESPN FC|date=19 May 2013 |access-date=5 July 2013 |archive-date=26 April 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140426211138/http://www.espnfc.com/news/story/_/id/1454181/porto-clinches-3rd-straight-portuguese-title?cc=5901 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 15 May, Matić faced former employers Chelsea in the [[2013 UEFA Europa League Final|Europa League]] final in Amsterdam but was on the losing club as Benfica fell to a 2–1 defeat, courtesy of a last minute [[Branislav Ivanović]] header.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22445388 |title=Rafael Benitez's reign as Chelsea's interim manager will end in triumph after Branislav Ivanovic's injury-time header won the Europa League final against Benfica in Amsterdam. |website=BBC Sport |date=15 May 2013 |access-date=5 July 2013 |archive-date=25 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160125232101/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/22445388 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 4 July 2013, he was named [[LPFP Primeira Liga Player of the Year|Primeira Liga Player of the Year]] after having won the monthly award three times over the course of the season.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.abola.pt/nnh/ver.aspx?id=413063 |title=Matic eleito melhor jogador do último campeonato, Vítor Pereira melhor treinador |trans-title=Matic voted best player of the last championship, Vítor Pereira best manager |newspaper=A Bola |language=pt |date=4 July 2013 |access-date=5 July 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130707100436/http://www.abola.pt/nnh/ver.aspx?id=413063 |archive-date=7 July 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="Ref1">{{Cite news|url=http://www.record.xl.pt/Futebol/Nacional/1a_liga//interior.aspx?content_id=831393 |title=Matic foi o melhor jogador da época 2012/13|trans-title=Matic was the best player of the 2012/13 season |newspaper=[[Record (Portuguese newspaper)|Record]]|language=pt |date=4 July 2013 |access-date=5 July 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130706173900/http://www.record.xl.pt/Futebol/Nacional/1a_liga/interior.aspx?content_id=831393|archive-date=6 July 2013|url-status=dead }}</ref>

In the [[2013–14 S.L. Benfica season|2013–14 season]], Matić played half of the season, with 22 matches and three goals, he helped Benfica to win the [[2013–14 Primeira Liga|Primeira Liga]] and [[2013–14 Taça de Portugal|Taça de Portugal]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Benfica lift cup to seal historic treble |url=http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=por/news/newsid=2107634.html |publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=18 May 2014 |access-date=20 May 2014 |archive-date=20 May 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140520031322/http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=por/news/newsid=2107634.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://pt.fifa.com/world-match-centre/news/newsid/234/083/7/ |title=Benfica conquista Taça e consegue o triplete em Portugal |trans-title=Benfica conquers Portuguese Cup and achieves the treble in Portugal |language=pt |date=18 May 2014 |publisher=[[FIFA]] |access-date=18 May 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140519023449/http://pt.fifa.com/world-match-centre/news/newsid/234/083/7/ |archive-date=19 May 2014}}</ref> On 13 January 2014, Matić placed second in the 2013 [[FIFA Puskás Award#2013|FIFA Puskás Award]].<ref>{{cite web |title=FIFA Puskás award 2013 – results |url=https://www.fifa.com/mm/document/ballond%27or/pusk%C3%A1saward/02/26/04/11/13_01_2014_puskas_results_neutral.pd|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140114024109/http://www.fifa.com/mm/document/ballond%27or/pusk%C3%A1saward/02/26/04/11/13_01_2014_puskas_results_neutral.pd|url-status=dead|archive-date=14 January 2014|publisher=FIFA|access-date=11 February 2015}}</ref>

===Return to Chelsea===
[[File:DK-Chel15 (5).jpg|thumb|upright|left|Matić playing for Chelsea in 2015]]
On 15 January 2014, Matić rejoined Chelsea for a fee of £21 million (€25M),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25743128 |title=Nemanja Matic completes £21m Chelsea return |website=BBC Sport |date=15 January 2014 |access-date=15 January 2014 |archive-date=16 January 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140116000121/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/25743128 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://web3.cmvm.pt/sdi2004/emitentes/docs/FR48184.pdf |title=Comunicado|trans-title=Announcement|date=15 January 2014 |publisher=Portuguese Securities Market Commission |access-date=31 December 2014|language=pt|archive-date=9 July 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140709205954/http://web3.cmvm.pt/sdi2004/emitentes/docs/FR48184.pdf |url-status=dead}}</ref> on a five-and-a-half-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |title=Matic Signs |url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/3622226/title/matic-signs|website=Chelsea F.C.|date=15 January 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140117232133/http://www.chelseafc.com/news-article/article/3622226/title/matic-signs |archive-date=17 January 2014}}</ref> He made his second debut for the club four days later, replacing [[Willian (footballer, born 1988)|Willian]] in a 3–1 victory against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]].<ref>{{Cite web|first=Phil|last=McNulty|title=Chelsea 3–1 Manchester United|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/25701613|website=BBC Sport|date=19 January 2014|access-date=20 January 2014}}</ref>

On 3 February, Matić made his first [[2013–14 Premier League|Premier League]] start in Chelsea's fixture away at championship rivals [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/feb/03/manchester-city-chelsea-player-ratings |title=Manchester City v Chelsea: player ratings |date=3 February 2014 |newspaper=The Guardian |access-date=12 December 2016 |archive-date=5 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305023826/http://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/feb/03/manchester-city-chelsea-player-ratings |url-status=live }}</ref> He was named [[man of the match]] by [[Sky Sports]] as Chelsea ended City's unbeaten run at the [[City of Manchester Stadium]] with a 1–0 victory.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/live/match/287521/report |title=Premier League: Ivanovic strike sees Chelsea beat title rivals Manchester City |date=4 February 2014 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=17 March 2014 |archive-date=17 March 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140317062713/http://www1.skysports.com/football/live/match/287521/report |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 30 August 2014, Matić scored his first Premier League goal in a 6–3 victory against [[Everton F.C.|Everton]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Everton 3–6 Chelsea |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28906778 |access-date=30 August 2014 |website=BBC Sport |date=30 August 2014 |archive-date=30 August 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140830232756/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/28906778 |url-status=live }}</ref> One month later, he scored the only goal as Chelsea won away at [[Sporting CP]] in the group stage of the [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Sporting 0–1 Chelsea |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29362602 |access-date=30 September 2014 |website=BBC Sport |date=30 September 2014 |archive-date=1 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141001003421/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/29362602 |url-status=live }}</ref> In the same competition on 5 November, his goal earned Chelsea a 1–1 draw against [[NK Maribor|Maribor]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Sever |first=Grega |title=Handanovič helps Maribor to Chelsea draw |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/025a-0ea736b2c866-97de091f2838-1000--handanovic-helps-maribor-to-chelsea-draw/ |access-date=5 November 2014 |publisher=UEFA |date=5 November 2014 |archive-date=8 November 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141108022613/http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/season=2015/matches/round=2000548/match=2014360/postmatch/report/index.html |url-status=dead}}</ref>

In Chelsea's 1–1 home draw against [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] on 21 February 2015, Matić was given a straight red card for pushing over [[Ashley Barnes]] following a high tackle by him, which resulted in the bending of Matić's shin.<ref>{{cite news |last=Sanghera |first=Mandeep |title=Chelsea 1–1 Burnley |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31466726 |access-date=22 February 2015 |website=BBC Sport |date=21 February 2015 |archive-date=22 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150222044724/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/31466726 |url-status=live }}</ref> On appeal, his suspension was shortened to two matches, including the [[2015 Football League Cup Final|League Cup Final]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Nemanja Matic: Chelsea player's ban reduced to two games |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31613184 |access-date=24 February 2015 |website=BBC Sport |date=24 February 2015 |archive-date=25 February 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150225080539/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/31613184 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 26 April, Matić was named as one of four midfielders in the [[PFA Team of the Year]], alongside teammate [[Eden Hazard]]. Four more Chelsea players were included in the selection.<ref name=PFATOTY1415/>

On 12 September 2015, Matić scored his first goal of the [[2015–16 Premier League]] season against Everton, but it was not enough to save Chelsea from a 3–1 loss.<ref>{{citation|title=Everton 3–1 Chelsea|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2015/09/12/england/premier-league/everton-football-club/chelsea-football-club/2043087/|access-date=1 July 2016|website=Soccerway|date=12 September 2015|archive-date=20 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820164227/http://int.soccerway.com/matches/2015/09/12/england/premier-league/everton-football-club/chelsea-football-club/2043087/|url-status=live}}</ref> he was sent off for two yellow cards in the first half of Chelsea's 2–1 loss against [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] on 24 October.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Bevan |first1=Chris |title=West Ham 2–1 Chelsea |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34558482 |access-date=24 October 2015 |website=BBC Sport |date=24 October 2015 |archive-date=24 October 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151024044239/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/34558482 |url-status=live }}</ref>

For the majority of the [[2016–17 Premier League]] season, Matić played as a central midfielder in a 3–4–3 formation. He scored the 4th goal in Chelsea's 4–2 FA Cup semi-final victory against Tottenham Hotspur on 22 April 2017.<ref>{{citation|title=Chelsea 4–2 Tottenham|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39604653|website=BBC Sport|date=22 April 2017|access-date=12 February 2018|archive-date=13 June 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180613040448/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39604653|url-status=live}}</ref> On 8 May 2017, Matić scored his first ever goal at Stamford Bridge, in a 3–0 victory against [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]].<ref>{{citation|title=Chelsea 3–0 Middlesbrough|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39767793|website=BBC Sport|date=8 May 2017|access-date=12 February 2018|archive-date=9 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180109111124/http://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39767793|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Roma===
[[File:FC Salzburg gegen AS Roma (UEFA Euroleague play-off, 2023-02-16) 64.jpg|thumb|right|Matić defending against [[FC Red Bull Salzburg]]'s [[Nicolás Capaldo]] in [[2022–23 UEFA Europa League#Knockout round play-offs|February 2023]]]]
On 14 June 2022, it was announced that Matić had agreed to join [[AS Roma|Roma]] on a one-year contract, following the expiry of his Manchester United contract.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Nemanja Matic signs for AS Roma |url=https://www.asroma.com/en/news/2022/6/nemanja-matic-signs-for-roma|website=AS Roma|access-date=17 June 2022|archive-date=23 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220623204008/https://www.asroma.com/en/news/2022/6/nemanja-matic-signs-for-roma |url-status=live }}</ref> He joined on a free transfer. This was his third reunion with manager José Mourinho, having also played under him for Chelsea and Manchester United. "I already worked with him, we have a good connection and he is one of the reasons why I came here." Matić on Mourinho.<ref>{{Cite web |date=14 June 2022 |title=Nemanja Matic explains why he keeps signing for Jose Mourinho |url=https://www.90min.com/posts/nemanja-matic-why-he-keeps-signing-for-jose-mourinho|website=90min.com|access-date=17 January 2023|archive-date=17 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230117035257/https://www.90min.com/posts/nemanja-matic-why-he-keeps-signing-for-jose-mourinho |url-status=live }}</ref> On 14 August, he made his debut for the club, as a substitute, in a 1–0 away win against [[US Salernitana 1919|Salernitana]] in the Serie A.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Roma hang on for narrow win over Salernitana with Bryan Cristante goal|url=https://www.espn.in/football/report/_/gameId/644619|location=India|publisher=ESPN|access-date=16 August 2022|archive-date=16 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220816051449/https://www.espn.in/football/report/_/gameId/644619 |url-status=live }}</ref> He started in the [[2023 UEFA Europa League final|Europa League final]], but was replaced in the extra-time as Roma went on to lose the match on penalties.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Jose Mourinho handed four-match UEFA ban after abuse of referee Anthony Taylor in Europa League final defeat|url=https://www.eurosport.com/football/europa-league/2023-2024/jose-mourinho-roma-boss-banned-for-four-matches-after-abuse-of-anthony-taylor-in-europa-league-final_sto9668811/story.shtml|website=[[Eurosport]]|date=21 June 2023|access-date=26 June 2026}}</ref>

In 2025, years after his departure from AS Roma, Matić revealed in an interview that he decided to leave the club as they did not respect him.<ref>{{Cite web|first=Francesco|last=Balzani|title=Matic, veleno sulla Roma: "Promesse non mantenute, meritavo più rispetto"|url=https://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Serie-A/Roma/07-10-2025/matic-e-l-addio-alla-roma-promesse-non-mantenute-meritavo-piu-rispetto.shtml|newspaper=[[La Gazzetta dello Sport]]|date=7 October 2025|access-date=26 June 2026}}</ref>

===Later career===
[[File:Lens - Stade Rennais (20-08-2023) 47.jpg|thumb|upright|Matić with Rennes in 2023]]
On 14 August 2023, Matić joined [[Ligue 1]] club [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]] on a two-year contract for a reported transfer fee of €3 million.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=14 August 2023|title=Nemanja Matić est Rennais !|url=https://www.staderennais.com/nemanja-matic-est-rennais|website=Stade Rennais F.C.|access-date=14 August 2023|language=fr}}</ref> He played in 13 [[Ligue 1]] matches and received seven yellow cards, incurring two yellow card suspensions. Rennes won two matches that Matić played in. He was left out of the squad after 18 December, with Rennes winning all five matches until his departure. However, Matić played in all six Europa League group stage matches, providing an assist in all three home ones as Rennes advanced from their group.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Rennes {{!}} UEFA Europa League 2023/24 |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/clubs/55031--rennes/ |access-date=27 January 2024 |website=[[UEFA]]}}</ref>

On 27 January 2024, Matić joined fellow Ligue 1 club [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] on a two-and-a-half-year contract, for a transfer fee of €2.6 million.<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 January 2024 |title=The Serbian International, Nemanja Matić, joins Olympique Lyonnais until 2026 |url=https://www.ol.fr/en/news/the-serbian-international-nemanja-matic-joins-olympique-lyonnais-until-2026 |access-date=27 January 2024 |website=Olympique Lyonnais}}</ref> On 17 May 2025, Matić played in a Ligue 1 match against Angers SCO with a white tape on the sleeve of his jersey covering [[Ligue 1]]'s anti-homophobia badge. He was given a two-game ban for his action.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nemanja Matic: Lyon midfielder given two-game ban for covering Ligue 1's anti-homophobia badge |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/12040/13380024/nemanja-matic-lyon-midfielder-given-two-game-ban-for-covering-ligue-1s-anti-homophobia-badge?dicbo=v2-wJGF1cq|website=Sky Sports|date=6 June 2025|access-date=10 June 2025}}</ref> On 14 August 2025, his contract with Lyon was terminated by mutual consent.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ol.fr/fr/actualites/nemanja-matic-et-l-ol-mettent-fin-a-leur-collaboration|title=Nemanja Matić et l’OL mettent fin à leur collaboration|trans-title=Nemanja Matić and OL end their collaboration|website=Olympique Lyonnais|date=14 August 2025|access-date=14 August 2025|language=fr}}</ref>

On 26 August 2025, Matić signed for newly-promoted Serie A club [[US Sassuolo Calcio|Sassuolo]] until 2026.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sassuolocalcio.it/prima-squadra/nemanja-matic-benvenuto-in-neroverde/ |title=Nemanja Matić, benvenuto in neroverde!|website=US Sassuolo Calcio |language=it |date=26 August 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
===Youth and senior debut===
In August 2008, while playing for [[FC VSS Košice|MFK Košice]] in Slovak [[Slovak First Football League|Corgoň Liga]], Matić received Slovak citizenship. Initially, he expressed an interest in playing for Slovakia at international level, refusing to play for his country of birth: "They can lure me into the A-team or the U21 [team], but I don't want to [play for Serbia] any more. I've already decided."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://aktualne.centrum.sk/sport/futbal/clanek.phtml?id=1163779|title=Košičan Matič upútal srbskú reprezentáciu|date=27 December 2008|website=centrum.sk|language=sk|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141213192830/http://aktualne.atlas.sk/kosican-matic-uputal-srbsku-reprezentaciu/sport/futbal/|archive-date=13 December 2014}}</ref>

However, on 11 October 2008, he debuted for the [[Serbia national under-21 football team|Serbia under-21 team]] in a match against [[Denmark national under-21 football team|Denmark]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.uefa.com/competitions/under21/fixturesresults/round=15085/match=304060/report=lu.html |title=UEFA stats for Denmark U21 vs. Serbia U21 game |publisher=UEFA |access-date=16 January 2009 |archive-date=14 October 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081014013547/http://www.uefa.com/competitions/under21/fixturesresults/round%3D15085/match%3D304060/report%3Dlu.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> After three matches and two goals for the Serbia under-21 squad, he was called up to the [[Serbia national football team|senior team]], debuting in a friendly match against [[Poland national football team|Poland]] on 14 December 2008, in a 1–0 loss.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.profutbal.sk/clanok67269.htm |title=Matić debutoval v srbskom drese |date=14 December 2008 |publisher=Profutbal|language=sk |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120314093302/http://www.profutbal.sk/clanok67269.htm |archive-date=14 March 2012 }}</ref> Matić played in the [[Cyprus International Football Tournament]] in 2009 where Serbia made it to the final.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.reprezentacija.rs/670-kipar-srbija-0-2/|title=(2009) Kipar – Srbija 0:2|date=10 February 2009|access-date=26 January 2020|archive-date=5 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200805173457/http://www.reprezentacija.rs/670-kipar-srbija-0-2/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>[http://www.rsssf.com/tablesc/cypr-intltourn09.html RSSSF info]</ref>

Matić took part in the 2009 UEFA Euro Under-21 Championship, where he played 85 minutes in the first group match against [[Italy national under-21 football team|Italy]] in a 0–0 draw. Matić, however, injured himself after contact with Italian forward [[Sebastian Giovinco]]. He broke the fifth metatarsal in his right foot and was forced to undergo surgery.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.uefa.com/competitions/under21/news/kind=1/newsid=838973.html |title=Broken bone robs Serbia of Matić |access-date=6 July 2009 |date=17 June 2009 |publisher=UEFA |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090620083943/http://www.uefa.com/competitions/under21/news/kind=1/newsid=838973.html |archive-date=20 June 2009}}</ref>

===Refusal to play and first senior goal===
In December 2012, Matić announced he would not play for the Serbia national team while [[Siniša Mihajlović]] was the coach. The reason was that Matić felt he was not given the right opportunity by the coach not playing a single minute in his last five call-ups.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rts.rs/page/sport/sr/story/36/Fudbal/1206072/Nemanja+Mati%C4%87%3A+Dok+ne+ode+Miha....html |title=Nemanja Matić: Dok ne ode Miha... |access-date=30 May 2013 |date=6 November 2012 |publisher=Radio Television of Serbia|language=sr |archive-date=14 November 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121114063131/http://www.rts.rs/page/sport/sr/story/36/Fudbal/1206072/Nemanja+Mati%C4%87%3A+Dok+ne+ode+Miha....html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.reprezentacija.rs/index.php/en/component/content/article/3068-selektor-treba-da-zove-igrace-ili-oni-njega |title=Selector should be called players or they did? |access-date=30 May 2013 |date=21 May 2013 |website=reprezentacija.rs |archive-date=4 November 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141104205051/http://www.reprezentacija.rs/index.php/en/component/content/article/3068-selektor-treba-da-zove-igrace-ili-oni-njega |url-status=live }}</ref> On 6 September 2013, Matić returned to the senior team on a [[2014 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group A#Serbia v Croatia|2014 FIFA World Cup qualification]] match against [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]], being [[Sent off#Association football|sent off]] in the 75th minute.<ref>{{cite web |title=Matic back for Serbia's crunch qualifiers |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/soccer-matic-back-serbias-crunch-qualifiers-125005809--sow.html |website=Yahoo Sports |access-date=6 September 2013 |date=6 September 2013 |archive-date=20 October 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131020233021/http://sports.yahoo.com/news/soccer-matic-back-serbias-crunch-qualifiers-125005809--sow.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Serbia 1–1 Croatia |url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/preliminaries/europe/matches/round=258374/match=300182196/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130907233825/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/preliminaries/europe/matches/round=258374/match=300182196/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=7 September 2013 |publisher=FIFA |access-date=6 September 2013}}</ref>

On 29 March 2015, Matić scored his first international goal in a [[UEFA Euro 2016 qualifying]] away match against [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]] at the [[Estádio da Luz]] – equalising via an [[overhead kick]] –  albeit in a 2–1 defeat.<ref>{{cite news |title=Portugal see off Serbia to top Group I |url=https://www.uefa.com/european-qualifiers/news/0253-0d7ff0cbb8bf-7677474ee0fd-1000--portugal-see-off-serbia-to-top-group-i/ |access-date=29 March 2015 |publisher=UEFA |date=29 March 2015 |archive-date=31 March 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150331025458/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/qualifiers/season=2016/matches/round=2000446/match=2013943/postmatch/report/index.html#portugal+serbia |url-status=live }}</ref> On 11 October, in a loss against the same opponents by the same score at the [[Partizan Stadium]], Matić received a straight red card within a minute of teammate [[Aleksandar Kolarov]]'s dismissal.<ref>{{cite news |last=Nikčević |first=Sonja |title=Moutinho magic seals top spot for Portugal |url=https://www.uefa.com/european-qualifiers/news/0253-0d80bb1e606e-c87470da5bea-1000--moutinho-magic-keeps-portugal-buoyant/ |access-date=11 October 2015 |publisher=UEFA |date=11 October 2015 |archive-date=15 October 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151015024918/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/qualifiers/season=2016/matches/round=2000446/match=2014055/postmatch/report/index.html#portugal+seal+spot |url-status=live }}</ref>

===2018 World Cup and retirement===
[[File:Ser-Swi (27).jpg|thumb|upright|Matić playing for Serbia at the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]]]]
In June 2018, Matić was selected to represent the Serbian team at the [[2018 FIFA World Cup|2018 World Cup]],<ref name=":1">{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/44083365 |title=World Cup 2018: All the confirmed squads for this summer's finals in Russia |website=BBC Sport |date=4 June 2018 |access-date=25 June 2018 |archive-date=24 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190724145334/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/44083365 |url-status=live }}</ref> playing all three group stage matches.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44427970 |title=Costa Rica 0–1 Serbia |website=BBC Sport |first=Timothy |last=Abraham |date=17 June 2018 |access-date=25 June 2018 |archive-date=20 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180620120510/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44427970 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/44439145 |title=Serbia 1–2 Switzerland |website=BBC Sport |first=Matthew |last=Henry |date=23 June 2018 |access-date=25 June 2018 |archive-date=22 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180622150330/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/44439145 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/06/27/sports/world-cup/brazil-vs-serbia.html|url-access=subscription|title=World Cup: Brazil cruises into next round with easy victory|newspaper=The New York Times |first=Andrew |last=Das |date=27 June 2018 |access-date=27 June 2018 |archive-date=5 May 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190505092244/https://www.nytimes.com/2018/06/27/sports/world-cup/brazil-vs-serbia.html |url-status=live}}</ref>

On 28 August 2020, the [[Football Association of Serbia]] announced that Matić had retired from international football. He made 48 appearances and scored two goals for Serbia.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/17249/12058362/nemanja-matic-manchester-united-midfielder-retires-from-playing-for-serbia |title=Nemanja Matic: Manchester United midfielder retires from playing for Serbia |website=Sky Sports |date=28 August 2020 |access-date=28 August 2020 |archive-date=29 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200829091326/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/17249/12058362/nemanja-matic-manchester-united-midfielder-retires-from-playing-for-serbia |url-status=live }}</ref> He earned his final cap against [[Luxembourg national football team|Luxembourg]] on 10 September 2019.<ref name=eustats/>

==Style of play==
A left-footed [[defensive midfielder]], Matić's poise and power, in addition to his in-game intelligence and tactical awareness, have enabled his attacking teammates to flourish. He is often used at a holding position and screens the defence while providing cover for attacking movements. Just before he joined Manchester United, he had a tackle success rate of 75% in 123 Premier League appearances, a higher rate than [[N'Golo Kante]], [[Ander Herrera]], [[Fernandinho (footballer, born May 1985)|Fernandinho]] and [[Jordan Henderson]].<ref name="Bibby">{{cite AV media |people=Bibby, Stephen |date=31 July 2017 |title=Seven quick facts about Nemanja Matic In November 2018, Matić refused to wear a [[remembrance poppy]] on his shirt for a match against Bournemouth.<ref name="bbc.com">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/46099843 |title=Nemanja Matic: Man Utd midfielder explains why he will not wear poppy |date=5 November 2018 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=5 November 2018 |archive-date=5 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181105142031/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/46099843 |url-status=live }}</ref> After the match, he was castigated and got threats by a number of people via social networks for not respecting servicemen who have died in war.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thetimes.com/article/memory-of-bombing-raid-is-why-ive-stopped-wearing-poppy-says-matic-zqch809b3 |title=Memory of bombing raid is why I've stopped wearing poppy |date=5 November 2018 |newspaper=The Times |access-date=5 November 2018 |archive-date=6 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181106044608/https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/memory-of-bombing-raid-is-why-ive-stopped-wearing-poppy-says-matic-zqch809b3 |url-status=live }}</ref> He stated that he will not wear a poppy because his village of [[Vrelo (Ub)|Vrelo]] was hit by the [[NATO bombing of Yugoslavia]] in 1999.<ref name="bbc.com"/> On 17 May 2025, the [[International Day Against Homophobia, Biphobia and Transphobia]], Matić played in Lyon's match against [[Angers SCO|Angers]] with an [[anti-homophobia]] logo on his shirt appearing to be covered.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Joseph |first=Sam |date=2025-05-18 |title=Nemanja Matic plays for Lyon with LBGTQ+ logo covered up on shirt |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6365800/2025/05/18/lyon-nemanja-matic-anti-homophobia/ |access-date=2025-05-19 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>
