Givet-Viaros''' (born 9 October 1981), known as '''Gaël Givet''', is a French former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a left-footed [[centre back]] and as a [[left-back]]. Givet was a [[UEFA Champions League]] runner-up with [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] in 2004 and was part of the [[France national football team|France national team]] which reached the [[2006 FIFA World Cup Final]]. ==Club career== ===Monaco=== Born in [[Arles]], France, Givet started his professional career at [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] as a left-back before moving to centre-back. He made his debut in a 2–2 draw against [[En Avant de Guingamp|Guingamp]] in December 2000. He played for Monaco between 2000 and 2007, making 178 league appearances and scoring eight goals. The highlights of his time at the club were winning the [[Coupe de la Ligue]] in 2003 and reaching the [[2004 UEFA Champions League Final|UEFA Champions League final]] in 2004, where he missed out on a winner's medal with a 3–0 defeat against [[José Mourinho]]'s [[FC Porto|Porto]]. He played a pivotal role in their success, making 13 Champions League appearances during the campaign. He made a name for himself in the [[2003–04 AS Monaco FC season|2003–04 season]] where he blossomed in the Monaco defense alongside [[Patrice Evra]], [[Julien Rodriguez]] and [[Sébastien Squillaci]].{{citation needed|date=June 2021}} ===Marseille=== [[File:Gaël Givet.jpg|thumb|upright|Givet playing for [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] in 2008]] After a successful career at Monaco, Givet moved to [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]]. During the [[2007–08 Olympique de Marseille season|2007–08 season]] he featured 29 times in the [[Ligue 1|French league]] and made nine appearances in the Champions League. At the beginning of the next season, however, he found his opportunities very limited in the first team.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}} ===Blackburn Rovers=== On 10 January 2009, ''[[L'Équipe]]'' reported that Givet would be flying to England to finalize a six-month loan deal with English club [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] on 12 January. On 14 January, [[Sky Sports]] announced that Blackburn had completed the signing of Givet on a six-month loan deal with a view to a permanent move at the end of the season. This was confirmed by Marseille on 15 January. He appeared in his first match for Blackburn against [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] at the [[Stadium of Light]], entering as a substitute in the [[FA Cup]] fourth round on 24 January 2009.{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120805154758/http://www.rovers.premiumtv.co.uk/page/NewsDetail/0,,10303~1520028,00.html|title=Givet Completes Loan Move to Blackburn Rovers}}, Blackburn Rovers F.C., accessed 15 January 2009.{{cite web|author=Wilson, Zack |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/1109/marseille/2009/01/13/1059024/gael-givet-set-to-join-blackburn-rovers |title=Gael Givet set to join Blackburn Rovers |website=Goal.com |date=13 January 2009 |access-date=19 January 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090319031507/http://www.goal.com/en/news/1109/marseille/2009/01/13/1059024/gael-givet-set-to-join-blackburn-rovers |archive-date=19 March 2009 }} The match finished 0–0, which resulted in a return fixture at [[Ewood Park]] on 4 February. Givet made his home debut in that match, which resulted in a 2–1 win for Blackburn. On 21 February 2009, he started and played the full 90 minutes against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] at [[Old Trafford]] in a 2–1 defeat.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}} On 15 May 2009, an agreement in principle was made with Marseille to make his loan switch to Blackburn permanent.[https://web.archive.org/web/20090517062841/http://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/blackburnrovers/4371300.Deal_agreed_for_on_loan_Blackburn_Rovers_defender/ Deal agreed for on-loan Blackburn Rovers defender]. lancashiretelegraph.co.uk. 15 May 2009 On 26 June 2009, Blackburn completed the signing of Givet on a four-year contract for £3.5 million. He scored his first goal in over three years against Sunderland on 22 August 2009 in a 2–1 away defeat.{{cite news|url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/8209577.stm |title=Sunderland 2–1 Blackburn |publisher=BBC Sport |date=22 August 2009 |access-date=27 May 2011}} He scored his second goal for Rovers at home against [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] at Ewood Park on 21 February 2010 in a 3–0 victory. Following the [[2009–10 Blackburn Rovers F.C. season|2009–10 season]], Givet was awarded the Player's Player of the Year award by the club.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}} On 14 August 2010, Givet started and completed the full 90 minutes in the 1–0 win over [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] on the opening day of the new Premier League season. On 22 September 2010, he scored a volley from the edge of the area on 34 minutes against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] at [[Villa Park]] in the [[EFL Cup|League Cup]] third round 3–1 defeat. On 13 November 2010, he scored a goal against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] at [[White Hart Lane]] and played the full 90 minutes at left-back in a 4–2 defeat. On 8 January 2011, he suffered a knee injury whilst playing in the FA Cup third round fixture against [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] in a 1–0 win for Rovers when he accidentally collided with [[Jamie Mackie]] and both players had to be stretchered off the field on around about the half-hour stage. In April 2011, Givet was left out of the squad as his future is in doubt after a £275,000 tax dispute with the club.{{citation needed|date=June 2020}} At the end of the 2010–11 season, he made 32 appearances and scored two goals in all competitions.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}} On 24 August 2011, Givet made his first appearance of the [[2011–12 Blackburn Rovers F.C. season|2011–12 season]], playing the full 90 minutes against [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]] at Ewood Park in the second round of the League Cup. On 27 August, he started and played the full 90 minutes alongside [[Christopher Samba]] in a 1–0 defeat against Everton at Ewood Park. On 11 September, he started and played the full 90 minutes against [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] in a 1–1 draw at [[Craven Cottage]]. On 17 September, he started the league game with [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] and completed the full 90 minutes at Ewood Park in a 4–3 victory in the left-back berth. On 20 September, he captained Rovers in their League Cup third round tie against [[Leyton Orient F.C.|Leyton Orient]] at Ewood Park which ended in a 3–2 win for Rovers and also played the full 90 minutes alongside [[Grant Hanley]]. On 24 September, Givet started and played the full 90 minutes against [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] at [[St. James' Park]] in a 3–1 defeat. On 1 October 2011, he started and played the full 90 minutes at left-back in a 4–0 loss against [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] at Ewood Park.{{cite web |author=Blackburn Rovers |url=http://www.rovers.co.uk/page/NewsDetail/0,,10303~2412092,00.html |title=Givet 90 vs Kilmarcnock |publisher=Blackburn Rovers |date=6 August 2011 |access-date=20 August 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110929205256/http://www.rovers.co.uk/page/NewsDetail/0%2C%2C10303~2412092%2C00.html |archive-date=29 September 2011 }} He was forced to leave the game against Sunderland on 11 December due to heart palpitations.{{cite web |url=http://uk.eurosport.yahoo.com/11122011/58/premier-league-heart-worry-blackburn-givet.html |title=Heart worry for Blackburn's Givet |publisher=PA Sport |date=11 December 2011 |access-date=12 December 2011}} Immediately suffering heart palpitations, Givet was taken to hospital and was to be monitored by club doctors, tested for an ongoing heart condition and the club are hopeful that the routine tests would show no problems.{{cite news|title=Givet to under-go heart tests|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11095/7380842/|publisher=Sky Sports|date=December 2011|access-date=15 April 2012}} After suffering heart palpitations, manager [[Steve Kean]] recalled Givet suffering heart palpitations, told Givet to get off pitch before he collapsed and club doctor was unable to regulate heart beat.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}} {{cquote|We had a taste of this (what happened to [[Fabrice Muamba]]), although not to this level, with Gaël Givet. Gaël's heart went into a state where we couldn't regulate it. We were fortunate to get him off the pitch before we got to the state where he collapsed. We felt we got away with it there. The doc was telling me, 'You need to get him off, this is very dangerous' He actually said to the doc: 'I'm struggling here.' We stuck a heart rate monitor on him and it was going through the roof. The doc tried to calm it down but he couldn't regulate it, we had to get him off." Of the 30-year-old's recovery Kean added: "The doctors said it was a very straight forward procedure, even if it didn't sound like it – burning nerve-endings and all that. He had a problem near one of the chambers and it moved to another so they had to do it but since then he's been great. Kean recalls Gaël Givet's heart palpitations{{cite news|title=Steve Kean recalls Gaël Givet's heart palpitations at Blackburn Rovers|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2012/mar/19/steve-kean-gael-givet-palpitations|work=The Guardian|date=19 March 2012|access-date=15 April 2012}}}} [[File:Gaël Givet Blackburn.jpg|thumb|upright|Givet playing for [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] in 2012]] Also in the match between Blackburn Rovers and [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]], the second half was delayed due to Givet and paramedics were treating him. This was a scare, but thankfully they revealed it was because he had suffered a hamstring strain.{{citation needed|date=June 2021}} On 4 February 2012, Givet received a red card just two minutes before half-time after a challenge on [[Robin van Persie]] as Blackburn were heavily defeated by Arsenal, 7–1.{{citation needed|date=June 2020}} Since his sending off, he did not make his first appearance and rumors began to spread that Kean had been leaving Givet out because of a contract clause but Kean dismissed them.{{cite news|title=Kean scotches Givet rumours|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/7655788|publisher=Sky Sports|date=7 April 2012|access-date=15 April 2012}} Despite not on the bench for Blackburn in a 3–0 defeat to [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]], Kean revealed he did not choose Givet stating was "not in the right frame of mind" to play.{{cite news|title=Kean – Givet not right to play|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11095/7673707/|publisher=Sky Sports|date=14 April 2012|access-date=15 April 2012}} Afterwards, Givet said that he wanted to leave Blackburn in the summer. On 21 April 2012, he, however, was selected to start against [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] at Ewood Park in the Premier League and played the full 90 minutes, replacing the injured Scottish defender Grant Hanley. On 7 May 2012, Givet started the Premier League game alongside [[Scott Dann]] against Wigan at Ewood Park in a crucial game knowing that a win would put them on course for survival, but during half-time, he suffered a heart scare after a row with manager Steve Kean and from being upset that Rovers were going down. He therefore was substituted for midfielder [[Radosav Petrović]]. The match finished 1–0 to Wigan, relegating Blackburn.{{citation needed|date=June 2020}} ===Arles-Avignon=== On 20 August 2013, Givet made a return to his boyhood team [[AC Arles-Avignon|Arles-Avignon]] after four and a half years with Blackburn.{{cite news|title=Au revoir Gael|url=http://www.rovers.co.uk/news/article/au-revoir-gael-1019396.aspx|publisher=Blackburn Rovers|date=30 August 2013|access-date=30 August 2013}} He left the club in September 2014, signing for [[Evian Thonon Gaillard F.C.|Evian Thonon Gaillard]].{{cite news|url=http://www.arlesavignon.net/givet-evian/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140903204347/http://www.arlesavignon.net/givet-evian/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=3 September 2014 |title=Gaël Givet à Evian Thonon-Gaillard |publisher=[[AC Arles-Avignon|arlesavignon.net]] |date=1 September 2014 |access-date=28 January 2015 |language=fr }} However, after only one [[Ligue 1]] game against his former team Marseille, he returned to Arles after falling out with Evian as they described his beard as "jihadist" and ordered him to shave it.{{cite news |url=http://www.arlesavignon.net/gael-givet-revient/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141127204026/http://www.arlesavignon.net/gael-givet-revient/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=27 November 2014 |title=Gaël Givet revient ! |publisher=[[AC Arles-Avignon|arlesavignon.net]] |date=25 November 2014 |access-date=28 January 2015 |language=fr }} ==International career== Givet represented [[France national football team|France]] at international level. He made his debut as a half-time substitute for Monaco clubmate and fellow debutant Sébastien Squillaci on 18 August 2004 in a 1–1 friendly draw with [[Bosnia-Herzegovina national football team|Bosnia-Herzegovina]].{{cite web|title=France 1-1 Bosnia|url=http://eu-football.info/_match.php?id=2832|publisher=EU-football.info|access-date=22 March 2014}} In 2006, he was a member of the French squad that reached the [[2006 FIFA World Cup Final|Final]] of the [[2006 FIFA World Cup|FIFA World Cup]] held in Germany, though he did not play. He earned 12 caps for his country, last appearing on 16 August 2006.{{cite web|title=Gael Givet|url=http://eu-football.info/_player.php?id=26425|publisher=EU-football.info|access-date=22 March 2014}} '''Naby Laye Keïta''' (born 10 February 1995) is a Guinean professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[central midfielder]] for [[Nemzeti Bajnokság I|NB I]] club [[Ferencvárosi TC|Ferencváros]], and [[Captain (association football)|captains]] the [[Guinea national football team|Guinea national team]]. 

Keïta began his professional career with [[Ligue 2]] club [[FC Istres]] in 2013, and a year later he moved to [[FC Red Bull Salzburg|Red Bull Salzburg]], where he won the [[Austrian Football Bundesliga]] and [[Austrian Cup]] [[Double (association football)|double]] in both of his seasons. He then moved to [[RB Leipzig]] in 2016, making the [[Bundesliga]] team of the season in his first year and the [[UEFA Europa League]] squad of the season in his second. He agreed to join Liverpool in 2017, and completed the move a year later, winning the [[2019 UEFA Champions League Final|UEFA Champions League]] in his first season at the club, and the [[2019 FIFA Club World Cup|FIFA Club World Cup]] and [[2019–20 Premier League|Premier League]] the following season.

Keïta made his senior international debut for Guinea in 2012. He has earned over 50 [[Cap (association football)|caps]] and was part of their squad at the [[Africa Cup of Nations]] in [[2015 Africa Cup of Nations|2015]], [[2019 Africa Cup of Nations|2019]], [[2021 Africa Cup of Nations|2021]] and [[2023 Africa Cup of Nations|2023]]. He represented Guinea at the [[Football at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2024 Summer Olympics]] and was chosen as his country's flag bearer.

==Early life==
Naby Laye Keïta was born on 10 February 1995 in [[Conakry]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/naby-keita-10-things-on-rb-leipzig-s-liverpool-bound-guinea-midfielder-473425.jsp |title=Naby Keita: 10 things on RB Leipzig's Liverpool-bound Guinea midfielder |publisher=Bundesliga |date=15 February 2018 |access-date=1 June 2018 |archive-date=18 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220318080037/https://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/naby-keita-10-things-on-rb-leipzig-s-liverpool-bound-guinea-midfielder-473425.jsp |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://tournament.fifadata.com/documents/FCWC/2019/pdf/FCWC_2019_SQUADLISTS.PDF |title=FIFA Club World Cup Qatar 2019: List of Players: Liverpool FC |publisher=FIFA |page=7 |date=5 December 2019 |access-date=17 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191205105526/https://tournament.fifadata.com/documents/FCWC/2019/pdf/FCWC_2019_SQUADLISTS.PDF |archive-date=5 December 2019 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/team/first-team/player/naby-keita |title=Naby Keita |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |access-date=12 December 2022 |archive-date=12 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221212235529/https://www.liverpoolfc.com/team/first-team/player/naby-keita |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Club career==
===Istres===
Keïta joined hometown club [[Horoya AC]] aged nine.<ref name="Ten things on RB Leipzig's new African star Naby Keita">{{cite web |title=Ten things on RB Leipzig's new African star Naby Keita |url=http://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/noblsp-ten-things-on-rb-leipzigs-new-african-star-naby-keita.jsp |publisher=Bundesliga |access-date=18 December 2016 |archive-date=13 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210613144537/https://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/noblsp-ten-things-on-rb-leipzigs-new-african-star-naby-keita.jsp |url-status=dead }}</ref> He moved to France in 2012, joining the youth team of [[FC Istres]] after unsuccessful trials at [[FC Lorient]] and [[Le Mans FC]].<ref name="Ten things on RB Leipzig's new African star Naby Keita" />

In 2013, he was promoted to the first team of Istres. He made his [[Ligue 2]] debut on 22 November 2013 against [[Nîmes Olympique]].<ref name="soccerway2">{{cite web |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2013/11/22/france/ligue-2/football-club-istres-ouest-provence/nimes-olympique/1479823/ |title=Istres vs. Nîmes – 22 November 2013 |website=Soccerway |access-date=28 July 2014 |archive-date=10 May 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210510083733/https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2013/11/22/france/ligue-2/football-club-istres-ouest-provence/nimes-olympique/1479823/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He scored 11 goals in 23 games in his first season as a professional,  before his team was relegated to the [[Championnat National]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ligue 2 table. |url=http://www.lfp.fr/ligue2/classement#sai=82&journee1=1&journee2=38&cat=Gen |access-date=31 August 2017 |archive-date=9 September 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120909015202/http://www.lfp.fr/ligue2/classement#sai=82&journee1=1&journee2=38&cat=Gen |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Red Bull Salzburg===
[[File:RB Leipzig vs. FC Liefering (Testspiel 9. August 2016) 24.jpg|thumb|upright|Keïta playing for [[RB Leipzig]] in 2016]]

In July 2014, he joined Austrian top division side [[FC Red Bull Salzburg|Red Bull Salzburg]].<ref name="Ten things on RB Leipzig's new African star Naby Keita" /> He made his league debut on 26 July 2014 against [[SC Wiener Neustadt|Wiener Neustadt]].<ref name="soccerway3">{{cite web |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2014/07/26/austria/bundesliga/fc-magna-wiener-neustadt/fc-red-bull-salzburg/1692303/ |title=Wiener Neustadt vs. Red Bull Salzburg – 26 July 2014 |website=Soccerway |access-date=28 July 2014 |archive-date=30 September 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200930123024/https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2014/07/26/austria/bundesliga/fc-magna-wiener-neustadt/fc-red-bull-salzburg/1692303/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Keïta ended the season with five goals and two assists in 30 games, winning the league and cup double. The following season, he was selected as the Austrian Bundesliga Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/app/transfer/news/21476/10893751/who-is-liverpool-target-naby-keita-we-profile-the-rb-leipzig-midfielder |title=Who is Liverpool target Naby Keita? We profile the RB Leipzig midfielder |publisher=skysports.com |first=Michael |last=Hincks |date=4 July 2017 |accessdate=30 January 2023 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20230129140158/https://www.skysports.com/app/transfer/news/21476/10893751/who-is-liverpool-target-naby-keita-we-profile-the-rb-leipzig-midfielder |archivedate=29 January 2023 |url-status=live }}</ref>

He would make his debut in the [[2015–16 FC Red Bull Salzburg season|2015–16 season]] on 25 July 2015 against where he scored the teams only goal as they lost 2–1. Keïta would finish the season with twelve goals and 7 assists in 29 games.

===RB Leipzig===
In June 2016, Keïta moved to Red Bull Salzburg sister-club [[RB Leipzig]], who had just been promoted to the German [[Bundesliga]].<ref name="Ten things on RB Leipzig's new African star Naby Keita" /><ref>[http://www.salzburg.com/nachrichten/oesterreich/sport/fussball/sn/artikel/fussball-naby-keita-wechselt-von-salzburg-zu-leipzig-201595/ Fußball: Naby Keita wechselt von Salzburg zu Leipzig] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170519041515/http://www.salzburg.com/nachrichten/oesterreich/sport/fussball/sn/artikel/fussball-naby-keita-wechselt-von-salzburg-zu-leipzig-201595/ |date=19 May 2017 }}, salzburg.com, 20 June 2016</ref> He scored the winner on his league debut against [[Borussia Dortmund]]<ref>{{cite news |agency=Associated Press |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/sep/10/leipzig-borussia-dortmund-bundesliga-match-report |title=Leipzig get first Bundesliga win with Keïta goal against Borussia Dortmund |newspaper=The Guardian |date=10 September 2016 |access-date=26 June 2017 |archive-date=2 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201002161553/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/sep/10/leipzig-borussia-dortmund-bundesliga-match-report |url-status=live }}</ref> and scored seven more goals in his debut Bundesliga season. He was named in the league's team of the season.<ref name=bundesliga/>

Keïta was named in the squad of the season for the [[2017–18 UEFA Europa League]], in which his team were quarter-finalists.<ref name=europa/> He would finish the [[2017–18 RB Leipzig season|2017–18 season]] with six goals and five assists in 31 games.

==== 2022–23 season ====
On 17 May 2023, Liverpool announced that Keita would be leaving the club once his contract expired in the summer. Injuries meant he started only 49 Premier League games during his time with the club.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Hunter |first=Andy |date=2023-05-17 |title=Liverpool confirm Oxlade-Chamberlain, Milner and Keïta leaving with Firmino |language=en-GB |work=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2023/may/17/liverpool-confirm-oxlade-chamberlain-milner-keita-firmino-leaving-contract |access-date=2023-05-17 |issn=0261-3077}}</ref> 

=== Werder Bremen ===
On 9 June 2023, [[Bundesliga]] club [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]] announced that Keita would join the club as a free agent.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Der SV Werder Bremen verpflichtet Naby Keita {{!}} SV Werder Bremen |url=https://www.werder.de/aktuell/news/profis/20222023/pm-neuzugang-keita-09062023 |access-date=2023-06-09 |website=www.werder.de |language=de-DE |archive-date=9 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230609112550/https://www.werder.de/aktuell/news/profis/20222023/pm-neuzugang-keita-09062023 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Transfercoup perfekt: Werder holt Keita aus Liverpool |url=https://www.kicker.de/transfercoup-perfekt-werder-holt-keita-aus-liverpool-955201/artikel |access-date=2023-06-09 |website=kicker |language=de-DE |archive-date=9 June 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230609112830/https://www.kicker.de/transfercoup-perfekt-werder-holt-keita-aus-liverpool-955201/artikel |url-status=live }}</ref> While sporting director [[Frank Baumann (footballer)|Frank Baumann]] labelled Keita's signing as a "no-brainer" ahead of the season, Keita eventually failed to impress, starting just one competitive game. Ahead of Bremen's Bundesliga match against [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] on 14 April 2024, Keita refused to board the team bus to the stadium and headed home, after being told he would not be part of the starting line-up. The club subsequently suspended him and fined him "a significant amount".<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lüddecke |first1=Tim |title=Suspendierung nach Streik: Das Kapitel Keita ist für Werder eines zum Vergessen |url=https://www.kicker.de/suspendierung-nach-streik-das-kapitel-keita-ist-fuer-werder-eines-zum-vergessen-1015194/artikel |access-date=16 April 2024 |work=[[Kicker (magazine)|kicker]] |date=16 April 2024 |language=German |trans-title=Suspension after Strike: The Chapter Keita Is One to Forget for Werder |archive-date=16 April 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240416123743/https://www.kicker.de/suspendierung-nach-streik-das-kapitel-keita-ist-fuer-werder-eines-zum-vergessen-1015194/artikel |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Ferencváros ===
On 10 December 2024, it was announced that Keita would join [[Nemzeti Bajnokság I]] club [[Ferencvárosi TC]] on loan in January.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-12-10 |title=Naby Keita leaves Werder Bremen to join Ferencvaros |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cy4plln7ye7o |access-date=2024-12-10 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB |archive-date=10 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241210141140/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cy4plln7ye7o |url-status=live }}</ref> The deal reportedly included an option to purchase and would last until the end of the year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=BL-győztes, korábbi Liverpool-játékossal erősítettünk |url=https://www.fradi.hu/labdarugas/elso-csapat/hirek/bl-gyoztes-korabbi-liverpool-jatekossal-erositettunk |access-date=2024-12-10 |website=www.fradi.hu |language=hu |archive-date=10 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241210143849/https://www.fradi.hu/labdarugas/elso-csapat/hirek/bl-gyoztes-korabbi-liverpool-jatekossal-erositettunk |url-status=live }}</ref>On 23 February he would make his debut for Ferencváros getting subbed on for [[Adama Traoré (footballer, born 5 June 1995)|Adama Traoré]]; they won the match 3–1 against [[Fehérvár FC|Fehérvár]]. He would get his first assist for the club on 2 March with a goal scored by [[Aleksandar Pešić]]. The match ended in a 2–2 tie. He would start his first game on 9 March against [[Debreceni VSC|Debreceni]] which they won 1–0.

The transfer was made permanent on 14 January 2026.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Ferencvárosi TC|url=https://www.fradi.hu/labdarugas/elso-csapat/hirek/szerzodest-hosszabbitottunk-naby-keitaval|title=Szerződést hosszabbítottunk Naby Keitával!|trans-title=We have extended the contract with Naby Keita!|date=14 January 2026|access-date=15 January 2026|language=hu}}</ref> On 9 May 2026, he won the [[2025–26 Magyar Kupa]] season with Ferencváros by beating [[Zalaegerszegi TE]] 1–0 in the [[2026 Magyar Kupa final]] at [[Puskás Aréna]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-09 |title=Gundel-Takács tizenegyest védett, de Raemaekers a Fradi javára döntötte el a kupadöntőt |url=https://www.nemzetisport.hu/labdarugo-nb-i/2026/05/gundel-takacs-tizenegyest-vedett-de-raemaekers-a-fradi-javara-dontotte-el-a-kupadontot |access-date=2026-05-10 |website=Nemzeti Sport |language=hu}}</ref>

==International career==
On 14 December 2012, Keïta made his international debut for the [[Guinea national football team|Guinea national team]] against [[Sierra Leone national football team|Sierra Leone]] in a [[2014 African Nations Championship qualification]] match. He scored the opener for his side in a 1–1 away draw.<ref name="NFT"/>

Keïta was included in [[Michel Dussuyer]]'s 23-man squad for the [[2015 Africa Cup of Nations]] in [[Equatorial Guinea]].<ref>{{cite news |title=2015 Nations Cup: Constant included in Guinea squad |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30636144 |access-date=4 November 2018 |website=BBC Sport |date=31 December 2014 |archive-date=16 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230316203755/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/30636144 |url-status=live }}</ref> In the opening match against the [[Ivory Coast national football team|Ivory Coast]], he was struck in the face by [[Gervinho]], who was red carded for it.<ref>{{cite news |title=Afcon 2015: Two-match ban as Gervinho apologises for red card |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30907505 |access-date=4 November 2018 |website=BBC Sport |date=21 January 2015 |archive-date=16 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230316203935/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/30907505 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 12 November 2015, Keïta scored his first international goal in three years, in a 1–0 away win against [[Namibia national football team|Namibia]] in [[2018 FIFA World Cup qualification – CAF second round|the first leg of the second round]] of [[2018 FIFA World Cup qualification]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Coupe du monde 2018 : la Guinée s'en sort bien en Namibie |trans-title=2018 World Cup: Guinea travel well in Namibia |url=http://afriquefoot.rfi.fr/20151112-football-coupe-monde-2018-eliminatoires-namibie-guinee-luis-fernandez |access-date=4 November 2018 |publisher=Radio France Internationale |date=12 November 2015 |language=fr |archive-date=16 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230316204137/https://www.rfi.fr/fr/afrique-foot/20151112-football-coupe-monde-2018-eliminatoires-namibie-guinee-luis-fernandez |url-status=live }}</ref> Three days later in the return leg – in Morocco due to the [[Ebola virus epidemic in Guinea]] – he scored again in a 2–0 win.<ref>{{cite news |title=CM 2018 : La Guinée confirme et se qualifie |trans-title=WC 2018: Guinea confirm and qualify |url=http://www.afrik-foot.com/cm-2018-la-guinee-confirme-et-se-qualifie |access-date=4 November 2018 |publisher=Afrik Foot |date=15 November 2015 |language=fr |archive-date=16 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230316004701/https://www.afrik-foot.com/cm-2018-la-guinee-confirme-et-se-qualifie |url-status=live }}</ref>

Manager [[Paul Put]] chose Keïta for the [[2019 Africa Cup of Nations]] in Egypt, where he was affected by injuries.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Creek |first1=Stephen |title=AFCON: Naby Keita in contention despite Nigeria withdrawal |url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/football/burundi-guinea-afcon-match-preview-naby-keita-liverpool-nigeria-injury-news/article28230017.ece |access-date=24 September 2021 |newspaper=The Hindu |date=29 June 2019 |archive-date=14 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230314141202/https://sportstar.thehindu.com/football/burundi-guinea-afcon-match-preview-naby-keita-liverpool-nigeria-injury-news/article64705057.ece |url-status=live }}</ref> In January 2022, Keïta helped Guinea qualify for the round of 16 of the [[2021 Africa Cup of Nations]] in Cameroon. His performances saw him earn a place in the tournament's best eleven of the group stage. However, Guinea were eliminated after a loss to [[Gambia national football team|Gambia]], a match Keïta could not play due to yellow cards accumulation.<ref>{{cite web |last=WaterWorldIsMyNightmare |date=23 January 2022 |title=Naby Keïta Named to AFCON Group stage Best XI |url=https://liverpooloffside.sbnation.com/2022/1/23/22897536/naby-keita-named-afcon-africa-cup-of-nations-group-stage-best-xi-liverpool-salah-mane |access-date=3 February 2022 |website=The Liverpool Offside |archive-date=16 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230316203421/https://liverpooloffside.sbnation.com/2022/1/23/22897536/naby-keita-named-afcon-africa-cup-of-nations-group-stage-best-xi-liverpool-salah-mane |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Style of play==
While writing for ''[[The Guardian]]'', Nick Ames and Nick Miller described Keïta as "a dynamic, [[Midfielder#Box-to-box midfielder|box-to-box]] central midfielder," likening him to [[N'Golo Kanté]]. They also noted, however, that he is able to distribute the ball with range and accuracy, and score goals, which has instead frequently led him to be compared to Brazilian-Portuguese former [[playmaker]] [[Deco]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/dec/28/rising-stars-10-players-watch-2017 |title=Rising football stars: 10 players to watch in 2017 |newspaper=The Guardian |author=Nick Ames and Nick Miller |date=28 December 2016 |access-date=26 June 2017 |archive-date=14 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230314141257/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/dec/28/rising-stars-10-players-watch-2017 |url-status=live }}</ref> David Usher of [[ESPN]] has described Keïta as an energetic [[midfielder]], with good defensive qualities, which also allows him to play in a [[Midfielder#Defensive midfielder|holding role]] if necessary. Usher went on to note that Keïta is "quick, skillful, creative and direct. He can [[Dribbling (association football)|dribble]], pass and shoot, and he frequently makes the spectacular look routine". [[Ralf Rangnick]] attributes him having a natural 360° radar.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rql1pilF3kA&t=342s Interview Ralf Rangnick] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211125120812/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rql1pilF3kA&t=342s |date=25 November 2021 }}, [[Ralf Rangnick]] on training eye tracking, 2019.</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.espn.com/soccer/club/liverpool/364/blog/post/3548415/liverpools-naby-keita-promises-to-provide-fireworks-in-the-no-8-shirt |title=Liverpool's Naby Keita promises to provide fireworks in the No. 8 shirt |publisher=ESPN |author1=David Usher |date=28 June 2018 |access-date=27 March 2019 |archive-date=16 March 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230316203641/https://www.espn.com/soccer/club/liverpool/364/blog/post/3548415/liverpools-naby-keita-promises-to-provide-fireworks-in-the-no-8-shirt |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Keïta has a younger brother, Petit Keïta, who was previously on the books with German side [[Inter Leipzig]]. In October 2018, it was reported that he had been training at [[Liverpool F.C. Reserves and Academy|Liverpool's Academy]], although he was not offered a contract.<ref>{{cite web |title=Defensive duo hail attack & Keita's brother training with Reds |url=https://www.thisisanfield.com/2018/10/defensive-duo-hail-attack-keitas-brother-training-with-reds-thursdays-liverpool-fc-news-roundup/ |website=This Is Anfield |date=25 October 2018 |access-date=12 March 2021 |archive-date=21 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210921061047/https://www.thisisanfield.com/2018/10/defensive-duo-hail-attack-keitas-brother-training-with-reds-thursdays-liverpool-fc-news-roundup/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2017, Keïta was charged with presenting false documents. The German newspaper ''[[Bild]]'' reported that, in early December 2016 and again six weeks later, he had presented two fake Guinean driving licences in order to obtain a driving licence in Germany. The district court in [[Leipzig]] ''(Amtsgericht Leipzig)'' fined him €415,000, basing the sentence on Keïta's estimated annual income of around €3 million. Keïta's lawyer filed an appeal.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/article170393361/Leipzig-Star-soll-ein-Vermoegen-an-Strafe-zahlen.html |title=Leipzig-Star soll ein Vermögen an Strafe zahlen |date=7 November 2017 |newspaper=Die Welt |access-date=8 November 2017 |archive-date=8 November 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171108072809/https://www.welt.de/sport/article170393361/Leipzig-Star-soll-ein-Vermoegen-an-Strafe-zahlen.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The appeals court reduced the fine to €250,000.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/2018/03/23/leipzigs-naby-keita-fined-for-false-driving-licenses/33215643/ |title=Leipzig's Naby Keita fined for false driving licenses |website=USA Today |access-date=11 April 2019 |archive-date=11 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190411103909/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/2018/03/23/leipzigs-naby-keita-fined-for-false-driving-licenses/33215643/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In September 2021, Keïta, his Guinean teammates and their opponents from [[Morocco national football team|Morocco]] were stranded during the [[2021 Guinean coup d'état]]. All returned home safely.<ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool's Naby Keita returning from Guinea following military coup in country |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58481875 |access-date=24 September 2021 |website=BBC Sport |date=7 September 2021 |archive-date=24 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210924195732/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58481875 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In July 2024, Keïta was named in [[Guinea national under-23 football team|Guinea]]'s squad for the [[Football at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2024 Olympics]] in France, as one of the three overage players.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.cafonline.com/fr/infos/paris-2024-naby-keita-designe-porte-drapeau-de-la-delegation-guineenne/ |title=Paris 2024 : Naby Keita désigné porte-drapeau de la délégation guinéenne |publisher=Confederation of African Football |access-date=24 July 2024 |archive-date=27 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240727034312/https://www.cafonline.com/fr/infos/paris-2024-naby-keita-designe-porte-drapeau-de-la-delegation-guineenne/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He was then chosen to be his country's flag bearer during the opening ceremony of the event.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/photo?fbid=805044741719074&set=a.444695037754048|title=18 joueurs, 4 réservistes, voici le groupe retenu par le sélectionneur Kaba Diawara en vue des JO Paris 2024|trans-title=18 players, 4 reservists, here is the group selected by coach Kaba Diawara for the Paris 2024 Olympics|publisher=[[Guinean Football Federation]]|date=4 July 2024|website=Facebook|lang=fr|access-date=24 July 2024|archive-date=15 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240715011348/https://www.facebook.com/photo?fbid=805044741719074&set=a.444695037754048|url-status=live}}</ref>

'''Ainsley Cory Maitland-Niles''' (born 29 August 1997) is an English professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[right-back]] for {{English football updater|Everton}} club [[Everton F.C.|Everton]].

Maitland-Niles started his career at [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] and made his professional debut in 2014. He spent the 2015–16 season on [[loan (sports)|loan]] at [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]], and the second half of the 2020–21 and 2021–22 seasons on loan at [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] and [[AS Roma|Roma]] respectively. During the 2022–23 season, he was on loan at [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] before joining Lyon after his contract at Arsenal expired. Maitland-Niles joined [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] in 2026. Internationally, he has represented [[England national football team|England]] from [[England national under-17 football team|under-17]] to senior level.

==Early life==
Maitland-Niles was born in [[Goodmayes]], Greater London, being raised in [[Ilford]], East London and attended [[Oaks Park High School, Ilford|Oaks Park High School]], Ilford.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.ilfordrecorder.co.uk/sport/football/redbridge-trio-earn-fa-cup-rewards-1-4868280 |title=Redbridge trio earn FA Cup rewards |newspaper=Ilford Recorder |date=30 January 2017 |access-date=10 September 2020 |archive-date=16 October 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201016215542/https://www.ilfordrecorder.co.uk/sport/football/redbridge-trio-earn-fa-cup-rewards-1-4868280 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He grew up in a single parent family with his mother, Jule Niles, and his brother, Cordi.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Jones|first=Mark|date=2018-03-05|title=Arsenal star's homeless mum forced to sleep in a storage unit|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/arsenal-star-ainsley-maitland-niles-12122394|access-date=2021-02-10|website=mirror|language=en}}</ref> He is of Jamaican descent.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://rjrnewsonline.com/sports/england-born-players-could-represent-reggae-boyz-despite-english-fa-interest |title=England-born Players Could Represent Reggae Boyz Despite English FA Interest |website=RJR News}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Arsenal===
[[File:1 Ainsley Maitland-Niles 2018.jpg|thumb|upright|Maitland-Niles playing for [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] in 2018.]]
====Early career====

Maitland-Niles is a product of [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]]'s [[Arsenal F.C. Academy|academy]] having joined the club at the age of six.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IZYVpwqZnvE |title=Arsenal: Introducing Ainsley Maitland-Niles |date=27 June 2014 |via=YouTube}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=55. Ainsley Maitland-Niles |url=https://arsenalyouth.wordpress.com/youngpros/ainsley-niles/ |website=Arsenal Youth |date=5 November 2012 |access-date=9 December 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170607024209/https://arsenalyouth.wordpress.com/youngpros/ainsley-niles/ |archive-date=7 June 2017}}</ref> Maitland-Niles made the step up to Arsenal's U21s during the 2013–14 season, having broken into the U18 set up the season before.<ref name=Arsenal>{{cite web |url=http://www.arsenal.com/academy/players/ainsley-maitland-niles |title=Ainsley Maitland-Niles |date=13 July 2023 |publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref> He signed his first professional contract with Arsenal on 24 October 2014.<ref>{{cite web |title=Young duo sign professional terms |url=http://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/20141024/young-duo-sign-professional-terms |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=9 December 2014}}</ref>

On 9 December 2014, Maitland-Niles made his professional debut at the age of 17 years and 102 days in a [[UEFA Champions League]] match against [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]], replacing [[Aaron Ramsey]] at half time in an eventual 4–1 win for Arsenal.<ref>{{cite web |title=Galatasaray vs Arsenal 0–3 |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2014/12/09/europe/uefa-champions-league/galatasaray-sk/arsenal-fc/1923715/ |website=Soccerway |access-date=9 December 2014}}</ref> In doing so he became the second youngest player to have represented Arsenal in the Champions League, behind [[Jack Wilshere]]. Four days later, he made his [[Premier League]] debut, replacing [[Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain]] in added time in a 4–1 win against [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Arsenal vs. Newcastle United |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2014/12/13/england/premier-league/arsenal-fc/newcastle-united-football-club/1703795/?ICID=PL_MS_07 |website=Soccerway |access-date=13 December 2014}}</ref>

====2015–16: Loan to Ipswich Town====

====2017–2020====
On his return to Arsenal in the following season, Maitland-Niles started a match away at the [[City Ground]] against [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] in the [[EFL Cup]] at [[right-back]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.skysports.com/football/n-forest-vs-arsenal/teams/366837 |title=Starting Lineups – N Forest vs Arsenal {{!}} 20 September 2016 |date=20 September 2016 |website=Sky Sports |access-date=21 September 2016}}</ref> Maitland-Niles again started at [[centre midfield]] against [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] in an [[FA Cup]] fourth-round game in an eventual 5–0 win for Arsenal.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.squawka.com/news/looked-like-a-veteran-arsenal-fans-delighted-with-maitland-niles-performance-against-southampton/890194 |title=Looked like a veteran!" – Arsenal fans delighted with Maitland-Niles' performance against Southampton |website=Squawka}}</ref> He came on as a substitute in the 74th minute in Arsenal's 2–0 win against [[Sutton United F.C.|Sutton United]] in the fifth round of the FA Cup.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/38952752 |title=Sutton United 0–2 Arsenal |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> Maitland-Niles established himself as a regular first-team player in [[Arsène Wenger]]'s [[2017–18 Arsenal F.C. season|final season]] as manager of the club, making 28 total appearances in all competitions. On 12 June 2018, he signed a long-term contract at Arsenal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/ainsley-signs-new-long-term-contract-2 |title=Ainsley signs new long-term contract |date=13 July 2023 |publisher=Arsenal F.C.}}</ref>

On 12 August 2018, in [[Unai Emery]]'s first match as manager, Maitland-Niles started at [[left-back]]. However, he would be subbed off 35 minutes into the match, after suffering a broken leg.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/45208516 |title=Ainsley Maitland-Niles: Arsenal midfielder suffers leg fracture |date=16 August 2018 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> After his return from his leg break, and a season-ending injury for [[Héctor Bellerín]], Maitland-Niles established himself as Emery's starting right-back for the remainder of the season. On 29 December 2018, he scored his first goal for the club, in a 5–1 Premier League defeat to [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] at [[Anfield]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.caughtoffside.com/2018/12/29/video-ainsley-maitland-niles-scores-first-ever-arsenal-goal-to-hand-gunners-lead-vs-liverpool/ |title=Video: Ainsley Maitland-Niles scores first ever Arsenal goal to hand Gunners lead vs Liverpool |last=Wilkins |first=Sam |website=CaughtOffside |date=29 December 2018 |access-date=8 August 2019}}</ref> Maitland-Niles scored his first [[UEFA Europa League]] goal on 14 March 2019, scoring Arsenal's second in a 3–0 quarter-final second-leg victory against [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Stade Rennais]] at the [[Emirates Stadium]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2825705-arsenal-complete-comeback-beat-rennes-3-0-to-advance-to-europa-league-quarters |title=Arsenal Complete Comeback, Beat Rennes 3–0 to Advance to Europa League Quarters |last=Blanchette |first=Rob |website=Bleacher Report |access-date=8 August 2019}}</ref>

With Bellerín still working his way back from injury, Maitland-Niles kept his place as Arsenal's starting right-back for the opening games of the [[2019–20 Premier League]]. On 22 September 2019, Maitland-Niles received a red card during the first half of Arsenal's 3–2 victory against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] at the Emirates Stadium.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/fixture/arsenal/2019-Sep-22/arsenal-3-2-aston-villa-match-report |title=Match Report: Arsenal 3–2 Aston Villa |date=22 September 2019 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=25 September 2019}}</ref> His [[sending off]] came after he received yellow cards in both the eleventh and 41st minutes. He scored his first EFL Cup goal against Liverpool in a 5–5 draw (Liverpool won on penalties) at Anfield.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50148250 | title=Shootout decides 10-goal Anfield thriller | work=BBC Sport }}</ref> On 1 August 2020, Maitland-Niles was selected to start in the [[2020 FA Cup Final|FA Cup Final]] against Chelsea, as Arsenal won their 14th FA Cup.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53546100 |title=Arsenal 2–1 Chelsea |first=Phil |last=McNulty |website=BBC Sport |date=1 August 2020 |access-date=2 August 2020}}</ref>

Maitland-Niles started the [[2020 FA Community Shield]] on 29 August, taking and scoring the second penalty in a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] win against Liverpool after the match ended 1–1.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2020/aug/29/arsenal-liverpool-mens-fa-community-shield-match-report-290820 |title=ARSENAL BEAT LIVERPOOL 5–4 ON PENALTIES TO WIN THE FA COMMUNITY SHIELD |publisher=The Football Association |date=29 August 2020 |access-date=30 August 2020}}</ref> In the FA Community Shield, Maitland-Niles was awarded the man of the match.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-liverpool/427352 |title=Arsenal 1–1 Liverpool (5–4 on pens): Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang secures Community Shield shootout win |website=Sky Sports |date=29 August 2020 |access-date=26 September 2020}}</ref> Maitland-Niles later struggled to secure a place in Mikel Arteta's first team, with interest coming from West Brom and Southampton to sign him on loan.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ainsley Maitland-Niles: West Brom leading race to sign England international from Arsenal|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11698/12202123/ainsley-maitland-niles-west-brom-leading-race-to-sign-england-international-from-arsenal|access-date=2021-01-29|website=Sky Sports|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-01-29|title=Southampton join race for Arsenal's Ainsley Maitland-Niles|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/arsenal/maitland-niles-transfer-news-southampton-b1794764.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210129144907/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/arsenal/maitland-niles-transfer-news-southampton-b1794764.html |archive-date=2021-01-29 |url-access=limited |url-status=live|access-date=2021-01-29|website=The Independent|language=en}}</ref>

====2021–2023: Loans to West Bromwich Albion, Roma and Southampton====
On 1 February 2021, Maitland-Niles joined fellow [[Premier League]] club [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] on a loan deal until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Maitland-Niles joins Albion on loan|url=https://www.wba.co.uk/news/maitland-niles-joins-albion-loan|access-date=2021-02-01|website=West Bromwich Albion|language=en}}</ref> He made his debut in a 0–2 defeat to [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham]] in the Premier League on 7 February.<ref>{{Cite web|last1=Gold|first1=Alasdair|last2=Guest|first2=Rob|date=2021-02-07|title=Tottenham vs West Brom highlights as Kane and Son goals seal vital win|url=https://www.football.london/tottenham-hotspur-fc/fixtures-results/tottenham-west-brom-live-match-19787821|access-date=2021-02-09|website=Football.London|language=en}}</ref>

During the summer of 2021, Maitland-Niles was linked with a move away from Arsenal, with Everton reportedly interested in signing him on loan.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11661/12392678/ainsley-maitland-niles-everton-keen-on-signing-arsenal-right-wing-back-on-loan|title = Ainsley Maitland-Niles: Everton keen on signing Arsenal right wing-back on loan|work=skysports.com}}</ref> The potential move fell through however, and on 30 August 2021, Maitland-Niles publicly expressed his desire to leave the club via social media, stating that he wished to go where he was "wanted" and where he was going to play.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/aug/30/embarrassment-for-arsenal-as-maitland-niles-asks-to-leave-on-instagram|title =Embarrassment for Arsenal as Maitland-Niles asks to leave on Instagram|work=The Guardian|date = 30 August 2021}}</ref>

On 8 January 2022, Maitland-Niles joined [[Serie A]] club [[A.S. Roma|Roma]] on a loan deal until the end of the season.<ref name="roma-loan">{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/ainsley-maitland-niles-joins-roma-loan-transfer-window|title=Ainsley Maitland-Niles joins AS Roma on loan|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=8 January 2022|access-date=8 January 2022}}</ref><ref name="roma">{{cite web|url=https://www.asroma.com/en/news/2022/1/ainsley-maitland-niles-completes-roma-move|title=Maitland-Niles completes Roma move!|publisher=A.S. Roma|date=8 January 2022|access-date=8 January 2022|archive-date=8 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220108152922/https://www.asroma.com/en/news/2022/1/ainsley-maitland-niles-completes-roma-move|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 1 September 2022, Maitland-Niles joined Southampton on a season-long loan.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1 September 2022 |title=Maitland-Niles joins Saints on loan |url=https://www.southamptonfc.com/news/2022-09-01/ainsley-maitland-niles-announcement-southampton-arsenal-loan |access-date=1 September 2022 |website=Southampton FC |archive-date=24 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221024201826/https://www.southamptonfc.com/news/2022-09-01/ainsley-maitland-niles-announcement-southampton-arsenal-loan |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 16 June 2023, Arsenal announced that Maitland-Niles would be leaving the club following the expiration of his contract.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/13-players-depart-end-their-contracts|title=13 players to depart at end of their contracts|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|date=16 June 2023|access-date=16 June 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/maitland-niles-its-been-emotional-journey|title=Maitland-Niles:"It's been an emotional journey"|publisher=Arsenal F.C.|first=Jonathon|last=Rogers|date=16 June 2023|access-date=16 June 2023}}</ref>

===Lyon===
On 7 August 2023, Maitland-Niles joined French club [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] on a four-year deal on a free transfer.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ainsley Maitland-Niles: Ex-Arsenal midfielder agrees deal with Lyon |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/66434183 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=7 August 2023 |date=7 August 2023 }}</ref> On 7 January 2024, he scored his first goal against [[CA Pontarlier|Pontarlier]] in a round of 64 match in the [[2023–24 Coupe de France|Coupe de France]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Lyon 3-0 Pontarlier (7 Jan, 2024) Final Score - ESPN (UK) |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/match/_/gameId/690867/lyon-pontarlier |access-date=2024-12-19 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Foot |first=Lyon |date=2024-01-12 |title=Lyon Foot |url=https://www.lyonfoot.com/article/5255/ainsley-maitland-niles-avant-le-havre-ol-c-est-agreable-de-se-sentir-comme-une-equipe |access-date=2024-12-19 |website=Lyon Foot |language=fr-FR}}</ref>

===Everton===
On 1 September 2026, Maitland-Niles signed a three-year contract with [[Everton F.C.|Everton]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.evertonfc.com/news/2026/september/01/everton-complete-/ |title=Everton Complete Maitland-Niles Signing |publisher=Everton F.C. |date=1 September 2026 }}</ref> On 6 September, Maitland-Niles came on as a substitute for his Everton debut and scored from outside the box in stoppage time to equalise against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] and secure a 2–2 draw.<ref>{{Cite web |date=6 September 2026 |title=Man United denied victory as Ainsley Maitland-Niles stunner rescues Everton |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/bulletin/sport/everton-vs-man-utd-score-maitland-niles-b3045526.html |access-date=6 September 2026 |website=The Independent |language=en}}</ref>

==International career==
Maitland-Niles has played for England at various levels within the youth setup of the Three Lions. He made three appearances for [[England national under-17 football team|England U17]] in 2014.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ainsley Maitland-Niles: All you need to know about the Arsenal youngster |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/arsenal/11572667/Ainsley-Maitland-Niles-All-you-need-to-know-about-the-Arsenal-youngster.html |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |date=29 April 2015 |access-date=29 June 2017}}</ref>

He was then called up by [[England national under-18 football team|England U18]] in November 2014<ref>{{cite news |title=ENGLAND U18S SQUAD NAMED FOR POLAND DOUBLE-HEADER |url=http://www.thefa.com/news/2014/Nov/05/england-u18-squad-named-for-poland-double-header-051114 |publisher=The Football Association |date=5 November 2014 |access-date=29 June 2017}}</ref> and scored on his debut, in a 3–2 win over [[Poland national under-18 football team|Poland U18]].<ref>{{cite news |title=CONNOLLY, MAITLAND-NILES AND ARMSTRONG SEAL WIN |url=http://www.thefa.com/news/2014/nov/15/poland-u18s-v-england-u18s-match-report-151114 |publisher=The Football Association |date=15 November 2014 |access-date=29 June 2017}}</ref> He went on to make four appearances for the England U18 side.

In September 2015, Maitland-Niles was called up by [[England national under-19 football team|England U19]]<ref>{{cite news |title=Maitland-Niles in England U19 Squad |url=https://www.twtd.co.uk/ipswich-town-news/27983/maitland-niles-in-england-u19-squad |website=TWTD |date=27 August 2015 |access-date=29 June 2017}}</ref> and scored on his England U19 debut, in a 3–2 win over Germany U19 on 4 September 2015.<ref>{{cite news |title=ENGLAND U19S PICK UP THRILLING VICTORY IN GERMANY |url=http://www.thefa.com/news/2015/sep/04/match-report-germany-v-england-u19s-040915 |publisher=The Football Association |date=4 September 2015 |access-date=29 June 2017}}</ref> He scored again the following month, in a 2–0 win over [[Macedonia national under-19 football team|Macedonia U19]].<ref>{{cite news |title=ENGLAND U19S GET EURO QUALIFYING CAMPAIGN OFF TO FINE START |url=http://www.thefa.com/news/2015/Oct/08/england-u19s-v-fyr-macedonia-report |publisher=The Football Association |date=8 October 2015 |access-date=29 June 2017}}</ref> He was then included in the England U19 squad for the [[2016 UEFA European Under-19 Championship|UEFA European Under-19 Championship]] that saw them reach the semi-final of the tournament.<ref>{{cite news |title=ENGLAND UNDER-19S SQUAD NAMED FOR EURO FINALS CHALLENGE |url=http://www.thefa.com/news/2016/jul/06/under-19s-euro-squad-named-060716 |publisher=The Football Association |date=6 July 2016 |access-date=29 June 2017}}</ref>

On 1 September 2016, Maitland-Niles scored on his England U20 debut, in a 1–1 draw against [[Brazil national under-20 football team|Brazil U20]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Maitland-Niles scores for England |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/20160902/maitland-niles-scores-for-england |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=2 September 2016 |access-date=29 June 2017}}</ref> In May 2017 he was called up to [[England national under-20 football team|England]]'s squad for the [[2017 FIFA U-20 World Cup]] in South Korea.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.football.london/arsenal-fc/players/revealed-arsenal-player-who-wont-13003890 |title=Revealed: The Arsenal player who won't be involved again this season after England U20s call-up |website=Football London|date=8 May 2017 }}</ref> England eventually got to the final of the tournament where they were up against Venezuela. Maitland-Niles, who came on in the 75th minute of play, went on to win the 2017 FIFA U-20 World Cup as England beat Venezuela by a 1–0 margin. This was the first time England had ever won the Under-20 World Cup.<ref name=WCup>{{cite news |url=http://www.bbc.com/sport/football/40237981 |title=Under 20 World Cup: England beat Venezuela in final |website=BBC Sport|date=11 June 2017 }}</ref>

On 29 August 2020, Maitland-Niles was called up to the [[England national football team|England senior squad]] by [[Gareth Southgate]] for the [[UEFA Nations League]] matches against [[Iceland national football team|Iceland]] and [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Coady & Maitland-Niles called up by England |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53962211 |website=BBC Sport |access-date=29 August 2020}}</ref> He made his debut on 8 September coming on as a substitute against Denmark.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/53980518 |title=Denmark 0–0 England |website=BBC Sport |date=8 September 2020}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Maitland-Niles is known for his versatility, with his pace and energy, he can play as a [[Winger (football)|winger]], [[Central Midfielder|central midfielder]], [[Full back (association football)|full-back]], and [[Wing-back (association football)|wing-back]],<ref>{{Cite web|last=Association|first=The Football|title=England player profile: Ainsley Maitland-Niles|url=http://www.thefa.com/england/mens-seniors/squad/ainsley-maitland-niles|access-date=2021-02-09|website=www.thefa.com|language=en}}</ref> though he prefers playing on the wing, describing it as "his natural position."<ref>{{cite news |title=Maitland-Niles – Why I love the wing |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/news-archive/20150519/maitland-niles-why-i-love-the-wing |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |date=19 May 2015 |access-date=29 June 2017}}</ref>

In December 2017, his then-Arsenal manager, [[Arsène Wenger|Arsene Wenger]], praised Maitland-Niles as "a good defender", saying that "he has that sense of one against one" and "has very quick recovery runs."<ref>{{Cite web|date=2017-12-18|title=Arsene Wenger Hails Maitland-Niles as 'the Future' After an Excellent Performance Against Newcastle|url=https://www.90min.com/posts/5921943-arsene-wenger-hails-maitland-niles-as-the-future-after-an-excellent-performance-against-newcastle|access-date=2021-02-09|website=90min.com|language=en}}</ref>

==Media==
Maitland-Niles was involved in the [[List of Amazon Prime Video original programming|Amazon Original]] sports [[docuseries]] ''[[All or Nothing: Arsenal]]'', which documented the club by spending time with the coaching staff and players behind the scenes both on and off the field throughout their [[2021–22 Arsenal F.C. season|2021–22 season]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/full-all-or-nothing-trailer-released |title=Full 'All Or Nothing' trailer released |date=19 July 2022 |publisher=Arsenal F.C. |access-date=21 July 2022 }}</ref><ref>{{cite AV media |date=19 July 2022 |title=All or Nothing: Arsenal {{pipe}} Official Full Trailer 🎬 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ta3CLkX-bzk |access-date=21 July 2022 |publisher=[[Amazon Prime Video|Amazon Prime Video Sport]] |via=[[YouTube]] }}</ref>

[[Defensive midfielder]] | currentclub = | youthyears1 = 1997–2003 | youthclubs1 = US Lormont | youthyears2 = 2003–2006 | youthclubs2 = [[Stade Bordelais (football)|Stade Bordelais]] | youthyears3 = 2008–2009 | youthclubs3 = [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]] | years1 = 2006–2007 | clubs1 = [[RCO Agde|Agde]] | caps1 = 25 | goals1 = 1 | years2 = 2007–2008 | clubs2 = [[Lormont|US Lormont]] | caps2 = | goals2 = | years3 = 2009–2016 | clubs3 = [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]] | caps3 = 188 | goals3 = 7 | years4 = 2016–2018 | clubs4 = [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]] | caps4 = 38 | goals4 = 2 | years5 = 2018–2019 | clubs5 = [[Orlando City SC|Orlando City]] | caps5 = 42 | goals5 = 1 | years6 = 2020 | clubs6 = [[FC Utrecht]] | caps6 = 1 | goals6 = 0 | nationalyears1 = 2010–2015 | nationalteam1 = [[Senegal national football team|Senegal]] | nationalcaps1 = 35 | nationalgoals1 = 0 }} '''Ludovic Lamine Sané''' (born 22 March 1987) is a former professional [[association football|footballer]]. He played primarily as a [[centre-back]] but was also used as a [[holding midfielder]]. Born in France, he represented [[Senegal national football team|Senegal]] at the international level. ==Career== ===Early career=== Sané was born in [[Villeneuve-sur-Lot]] in southwestern France and began his football career playing for local club US Lormont on the outskirts of [[Bordeaux]]. He later joined [[Stade Bordelais (football)|Stade Bordelais]] before signing a contract with [[Championnat de France amateur]] club [[RCO Agde]] at the age of 19. Sané spent one season at Agde, appearing in 25 matches and scoring one goal. Following the season, he returned to Lormont and spent a season playing in the Division d'Honneur. During the summer of 2008, Sané jumped five divisions by signing a three-year professional contract with [[Ligue 1]] club [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]].{{cite web|publisher=Enquete Plus|author=Badji, Mamadou Lamine|title=Lamine SANÉ : un Ludovic incarné|trans-title=Lamine SANÉ : Ludovic incarnate|url=http://www.enqueteplus.com/?q=content/23-lions-can-2012-lamine-san%C3%A9-un-ludovic-incarn%C3%A9|language=French|date=2012|access-date=25 May 2012|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304122501/http://www.enqueteplus.com/?q=content%2F23-lions-can-2012-lamine-san%C3%A9-un-ludovic-incarn%C3%A9|url-status=dead}} ===Bordeaux=== Sané initially played with the club's reserve team upon his arrival appearing in 15 matches during the [[2008–09 Championnat de France Amateur|2008–09 season]]. While playing with the amateurs, the young player impressed manager [[Laurent Blanc]] and assistant [[Jean-Louis Gasset]]. For the [[2009–10 Ligue 1|2009–10 pre-season]], Sané featured regularly and performed well, most notably in a 3–1 win over Spanish club [[Athletic Bilbao]] after appearing as a second-half substitute. On 19 September 2009, Sané was called up to the first team for the first time for Bordeaux's league match against [[US Boulogne|Boulogne]]. He didn't appear in the match, but eventually became a regular in the first 18 often appearing on the bench as a backup for [[France national football team|French international]] [[Alou Diarra]]. On 3 November, Sané made his professional debut in the club's 2–0 victory over German club [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] in the [[UEFA Champions League]] appearing as a substitute in the 84th minute. The following month, he earned his first start playing the entire match in Bordeaux's 1–0 victory over [[Israel]]i club [[Maccabi Haifa F.C.|Maccabi Haifa]]. Sané made his league debut four days later in Bordeaux's important tie with [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]]. Bordeaux won the match 1–0 with Sané playing the full 90 minutes. On 8 January 2010, Sané agreed to a contract extension with Bordeaux which will tie him to the club until 2014. He scored his first goal for Bordeaux in a 3–1 loss to [[Olympique de Marseille]] in a [[Coupe de la Ligue]] final at the [[Stade de France]]. ===Werder Bremen=== After spending seven senior years at Bordeaux, Sané departed the club and signed for [[Bundesliga]] side [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]] for an undisclosed fee.{{cite web | url=http://www.werder.de/en/news/news/werder-bremen-news/20162017/sane-04082016/ | title=Done deal: Lamine Sané is a Green-White | publisher=SV Werder Bremen | work=www.werder.de/en | date=4 August 2016 | accessdate=4 August 2016 | archive-date=7 August 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160807022918/http://www.werder.de/en/news/news/werder-bremen-news/20162017/sane-04082016 | url-status=dead }}{{cite web|title=Lamine Sane leaves Bordeaux to join Werder Bremen|url=http://www.espnfc.com/story/2923193/lamine-sane-leaves-bordeaux-to-join-werder-bremen|website=ESPNFC|accessdate=5 August 2016|date=4 August 2016}} In January 2018, the club's sporting director [[Frank Baumann (footballer)|Frank Baumann]] announced that Sané would not be part of the team "for the time being" because he had been absent from training on two days without a valid excuse. Sané would also be allowed to settle his personal sporting future.{{cite news|title="Bis auf Weiteres": Sané nicht mehr im Werder-Team|url=https://www.kicker.de/bis-auf-weiteres_sanc3a9-nicht-mehr-im-werder-team-716022/artikel|access-date=27 January 2018|work=kicker Online|date=27 January 2018|language=German}} ===Orlando City=== On 20 February 2018, Sané signed for [[Major League Soccer]] side [[Orlando City SC]].{{cite news|title=Orlando City acquires Senegal international defender Lamine Sane|url=http://global.espn.com/football/soccer-transfers/story/3389928/orlando-city-acquires-senegal-international-defender-lamine-sane|accessdate=21 February 2018|work=ESPN FC|date=20 February 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://www.orlandocitysc.com/post/2018/02/20/orlando-city-sc-acquires-defender-lamine-san-sv-werder-bremen|title=Orlando City SC Acquires Defender Lamine Sané from SV Werder Bremen|date=20 February 2018}} He made his debut as a halftime substitute away to [[New York City FC|New York City]] on 17 March and scored his first goal for the club against [[Real Salt Lake]] in a 3–1 home victory on 6 May. After an injury-troubled first season with the club in which they set a new MLS record for goals conceded in a season, Sané formed a strong central partnership with [[Robin Jansson]] in [[2019 Orlando City SC season|2019]] and was a regular starter as Orlando turned things around defensively, conceding a team-record low number of goals.{{cite web |title=2019 Orlando City Season in Review: Lamine Sané |url=https://www.themaneland.com/2019/11/5/20946879/2019-orlando-city-season-in-review-lamine-sane |website=The Mane Land |language=en |date=5 November 2019}} Despite this, on 21 November 2019, it was announced Sané had his contract option for the 2020 season declined by Orlando as part of the end-of-season roster decisions.{{cite web|url=https://www.orlandocitysc.com/post/2019/11/21/orlando-city-sc-announces-2019-end-season-roster-decisions|title=Orlando City SC Announces 2019 End-of-Season Roster Decisions|website=Orlando City SC|date=21 November 2019}} ===FC Utrecht=== On 8 February 2020, Sané signed for [[FC Utrecht]] until the end of the season.{{cite web|url=https://www.fcutrecht.nl/nieuws/2020/februari/defensieve-versterking-lamine-sane-vastgelegd/|title=Defensieve versterking: Lamine Sané vastgelegd|website=FC Utrecht|date=8 February 2020|language=Dutch}} He made his debut on 16 February as an 89th minute substitute against [[Willem II (football club)|Willem II]], entering with Utrecht leading 1–0. The game finished 1–1 after Willem II scored a stoppage time equalizer.{{cite web |title=Willem II - FC Utrecht: 1 - 1 (16 februari 2020) |url=https://m.fcupdate.nl/voetbaluitslagen/310137/eredivisie-willem-ii-fc-utrecht/ |website=FCUpdate.nl}} Sané was an unused substitute in the next three league games as well as a 2–0 [[KNVB Cup]] semi-final win over [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] before the season was canceled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] in April.{{cite news |title='Bitter day' as Dutch league cancelled |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/52418048 }} He was released at the end of his contract having made one appearance.{{cite web |title=Opties in contracten Joosten, Arweiler en 5 spelers beloftenploeg gelicht |url=https://www.fcutrecht.nl/nieuws/2020/maart/opties-in-contracten-joosten-arweiler-en-5-spelers-beloftenploeg-gelicht/ |website=FC Utrecht}} ==Personal life== Ludovic's younger brother [[Salif Sané]] is also a professional footballer and Senegalese international.{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22716979|title=Senegal's Salif Sane signs for German club Hannover|first=Oluwashina|last=Okeleji|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=30 May 2013}} ==Career statistics== ===Club=== {{updated|6 October 2020}}{{cite news|url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/ludovic-sane/88248/|title=L.
