'''Aritz Aduriz Zubeldia''' ({{IPA|eu|aɾits̻ aðuɾis̻|lang}}; {{IPA|es|ˈaɾits aˈðuɾiθ|lang}};<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=35dabvevkbg&t=5s|title=Yo amo el futbol por... Aritz Aduriz, jugador del Athletic Club|trans-title=I love football by... Aritz Aduriz, Athletic Club player|publisher=[[YouTube]]|language=es|date=7 December 2016|access-date=26 February 2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/35dabvevkbg|archive-date=21 December 2021}}{{cbignore}}</ref> born 11 February 1981) is a Spanish former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[striker (association football)|striker]].

He spent most of his career with [[Athletic Bilbao]], scoring 172 goals across all competitions for the team over three spells.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://athletic.elcorreo.com/noticias/201510/08/pichichi-reune-goleadores-rojiblancos-20151008210636.html|title=Los discípulos de Pichichi|trans-title=Pichichi's disciples|newspaper=[[El Correo]]|last=Ortiz de Lazcano|first=Javier|language=es|date=9 October 2015|access-date=11 February 2016}}</ref> He also surpassed a century of goals (104) in [[La Liga]], in which he additionally represented [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] and [[Valencia CF|Valencia]].

In addition to playing for [[Spain national football team|Spain]], Aduriz was a regular goalscorer for the [[Basque Country national football team|Basque national side]]. He appeared for the former at [[UEFA Euro 2016|Euro 2016]], at the age of 35.

==Early life==
Born in [[San Sebastián]], [[Gipuzkoa]], Aduriz came from a family keen on sport but more inclined towards the likes of [[surfing]], [[mountaineering]] and [[cross-country skiing]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2016/11/14/artiz-aduriz-takes-the-latest-step-in-his-fairy-tale-career/|title=Aritz Aduriz takes the latest step in his fairy-tale career|newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|last=Wilson|first=Jeremy|date=14 November 2016|access-date=19 February 2018}}</ref> He excelled at the latter as a child, finishing runner-up in the junior national championship.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2020/may/22/aritz-aduriz-athletic-bilbao-forced-to-retire|title='An exceptional case' – Aritz Aduriz, the striker who got better and better|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|last=Lowe|first=Sid|date=22 May 2020|access-date=15 June 2020}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Athletic Bilbao===
Learning to play football on the sand at ''La Concha'' beach,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/live-scores/news/y=2016/m=3/news=aduriz-showing-age-is-just-a-number-2768323.html|title=Aduriz showing age is just a number|publisher=FIFA|date=3 March 2016|access-date=19 February 2018|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160407050159/http://www.fifa.com/live-scores/news/y=2016/m=3/news=aduriz-showing-age-is-just-a-number-2768323.html|archive-date=7 April 2016}}</ref> he was brought through the ranks of local youth club [[Antiguoko]] where he shared teams with future elite players [[Xabi Alonso]], [[Mikel Arteta]] and [[Andoni Iraola]], but was not initially picked up by a professional club like his teammates.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://antiguoko.org/club-historia/|title=El club – Historia|trans-title=The club – History|publisher=Antiguoko KE|language=es|access-date=19 February 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2014/02/02/futbol/equipos/real_madrid/1391340786.html|title=El descubridor de cracks|trans-title=The finder of stars|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|last=Velasco|first=Juanma|date=2 February 2014|access-date=19 February 2018}}</ref> He became part of the famed [[Lezama Facilities|Lezama]] youth system at [[Athletic Bilbao]], although he was already 19 when he arrived from amateurs [[CD Aurrerá de Vitoria|Aurrerá de Vitoria]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/2000/05/15/pagina-30/704383/pdf.html|title=Aritz sentencia a los cachorros en Lezama|trans-title=Aritz sentences puppies in Lezama|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|last=Gutiérrez|first=Jon|language=es|date=15 May 2000|access-date=15 December 2013}}</ref>

[[File:Aritz aduriz.jpg|thumb|left|upright=0.7|Aduriz in 2008]]
After two seasons in [[Bilbao Athletic|the reserves]], Aduriz made his first-team debut on 14 September 2002 against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in a 0–2 home loss,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/diario/2002/09/15/deportes/1032040815_850215.html|title=El Barça recibe el alta en San Mamés|trans-title=Barça get medical release in San Mamés|newspaper=[[El País]]|last=Rodrigálvarez|first=Eduardo|language=es|date=15 September 2002|access-date=21 June 2016}}</ref> but made only two more league appearances during the campaign, still turning out for the B-side where he made just short of 100 appearances in the [[Segunda División B]]. He went on to spend almost three seasons elsewhere (one with [[Burgos CF|Burgos]], one and a half at [[Real Valladolid]] in the [[Segunda División]]) before returning to Athletic in December 2005.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.eus/en/news/3837/aritz-aduriz-to-play-for-athletic-club-.html|title=Aritz Aduriz to play for Athletic Club|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=18 December 2005|access-date=8 March 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/news/newsid=380726.html|title=Aduriz back in Bilbao|publisher=UEFA|date=19 December 2005|access-date=6 December 2018|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200104005419/https://www.uefa.com/news/newsid=380726.html|archive-date=4 January 2020}}</ref>

Aduriz showed continuous progress, attested by his nine [[La Liga]] goals in 34 games in [[2006–07 La Liga|2006–07]], including a [[hat-trick]] against [[Real Zaragoza]] on 19 May 2007, albeit in a 3–4 defeat.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=204117&cc=5739|title=Real Zaragoza 4–3 Athletic Bilbao|publisher=[[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]]|date=19 May 2007|access-date=22 June 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121016121533/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=204117&cc=5739|archive-date=16 October 2012}}</ref> He was overshadowed by the younger [[Fernando Llorente]] in the [[2007–08 La Liga|following campaign]], but still managed to net seven times in 33 league appearances.<ref name=MD>{{cite news|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/20120628/athletic-bilbao/aduriz-11-goles-por-campana_54317554648.html|title=Aduriz, 11 goles por campaña|trans-title=Aduriz, 11 goals per campaign|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|last=San Cristóbal|first=Ainara|language=es|date=28 June 2012|access-date=21 June 2016}}</ref>

===Mallorca===
On 4 August 2008, Aduriz became the first player to score at the [[Colchester Community Stadium]], in a [[Exhibition game|friendly match]] with [[Colchester United F.C.|Colchester United]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.gazette-news.co.uk/sport/colchesterunited/3570427.U_s_beaten_by_late_penalty/|title=U's beaten by late penalty|newspaper=Gazette News|last=Waldron|first=Jonathan|date=4 August 2008|access-date=28 March 2016}}</ref> He was sold to [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] on the 23rd, signing a four-year contract.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2008/08/23/futbol/1219516788.html|title=El Mallorca ficha a Aduriz|trans-title=Mallorca sign Aduriz|newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]|last=Goikoetxea|first=Igor|language=es|date=23 August 2008|access-date=7 November 2015}}</ref>

On 26 October 2008, Aduriz scored a brace for his new club in a 3–0 home victory over [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/252833?cc=5739|title=Mallorca 3–0 Espanyol|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=26 October 2008|access-date=25 May 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120718081340/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/252833?cc=5739|archive-date=18 July 2012}}</ref> and finished his [[2008–09 La Liga|first year]] as team top scorer, for a final ninth position. He repeated the individual feat in [[2009–10 La Liga|2009–10]] – improving to 12<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.diariodemallorca.es/deportes/2009/12/12/aduriz-marcara-once-goles/529498.html|title=´Aduriz marcará más de once goles´|trans-title='Aduriz will score more than eleven goals'|newspaper=[[Diario de Mallorca]]|language=es|date=12 December 2009|access-date=21 June 2016}}</ref><ref name=MD/>– as the [[Balearic Islands]] side ranked fifth, with [[2010–11 UEFA Europa League|qualification]] for the [[UEFA Europa League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://rcdm.es/jugador-rcdmallorca/biografia-de-aritz-aduriz/|title=Biografía de Aritz {{sic|nolink=y|Adúriz}}|trans-title=Aritz Aduriz biography|publisher=RCDM|last=Busquets|first=Damià|language=es|date=5 January 2009|access-date=4 May 2020}}</ref>

===Valencia===
[[File:Aritz Aduriz 2011.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Aduriz in action for [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] in 2011]]
Aged 29, Aduriz moved to [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] on 14 July 2010, for about [[Euro|€]]4 million.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2010/07/14/futbol/equipos/valencia/1279131028.html|title=Aduriz ya es jugador del Valencia|trans-title=Aduriz is already a Valencia player|newspaper=Marca|last=Álvarez|first=Fernando|language=es|date=14 July 2010|access-date=7 November 2015}}</ref> He scored on his official debut on 28 August, opening an eventual 3–1 win at [[Málaga CF|Málaga]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=301928&cc=5739|title=Valencia shrug off departures|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=28 August 2010|access-date=7 March 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024113210/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=301928&cc=5739|archive-date=24 October 2012}}</ref>

From January 2011, after the arrival of Brazilian [[Jonas (footballer, born 1984)|Jonas]] in the winter [[transfer window]], and due to the fact manager [[Unai Emery]] often only played with one pure striker – [[Roberto Soldado]] – Aduriz found himself on [[Substitute (association football)|the bench]] more often than not.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://futbol.as.com/futbol/2011/11/05/mas_futbol/1320478035_850215.html|title=Soldado y Aduriz para derribar a Ballesteros|trans-title=Soldado and Aduriz to take down Ballesteros|newspaper=Diario AS|last=Valle|first=Conrado|language=es|date=5 November 2011|access-date=10 February 2016}}</ref> He still managed to finish his [[2010–11 La Liga|first season]] as a ''Che'' with 14 competitive goals, including two in their [[2010–11 UEFA Champions League|campaign]] in the [[UEFA Champions League]], one in each of the games against [[Bursaspor]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2010/09/14/mas_futbol/1284415241_850215.html|title=El Valencia sale líder del infierno turco|trans-title=Valencia emerge leader from Turkish hell|newspaper=Diario AS|last=Pardo Latre|first=Clara|language=es|date=14 September 2010|access-date=19 September 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/307802?cc=5739|title=Los Che run riot|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=24 November 2010|access-date=25 May 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120713214342/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/307802?cc=5739|archive-date=13 July 2012}}</ref>

===Return to Athletic===
====2012–2016====
On 27 June 2012, Aduriz rejoined first professional club Athletic Bilbao for a fee in the region of €2.5 million, signing for three years.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1116924/athletic-agree-fee-for-aritz-aduriz-return?cc=5739|title=Athletic seal Aduriz return|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=27 June 2012|access-date=27 June 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130103144552/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/1116924/athletic-agree-fee-for-aritz-aduriz-return?cc=5739|archive-date=3 January 2013}}</ref> On 23 August, he scored his first goals in his second spell, netting a brace in a 6–0 home rout of [[HJK Helsinki]] in the [[2012–13 UEFA Europa League|Europa League playoff round]] (9–3 on aggregate).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0200-0e7eccc08636-db90f84c6a7d-1000--bielsa-delighted-as-athletic-get-back-on-track/|title=Bielsa delighted as Athletic get back on track|publisher=UEFA|last=Bryan|first=Paul|date=24 August 2012|access-date=9 April 2025}}</ref> On 20 October, he returned to the [[Mestalla Stadium]] to face his previous team and netted twice, albeit in a 3–2 loss.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2012_13/primera/jornada_8/val_ath/|title=La épica silencia los silbidos|trans-title=Epics quiet booing|newspaper=Marca|last=Malagón|first=Manuel|language=es|date=20 October 2012|access-date=20 October 2012}}</ref>

Aduriz continued with his form on 4 November 2012, scoring two goals in a 2–1 away win over [[Granada CF|Granada]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/us/en/report/348415/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5901|title=Bilbao back on track|publisher=ESPN FC|date=4 November 2012|access-date=5 November 2012}}</ref> He quickly profited from Llorente's shaky contractual situation to become first-choice,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.20minutos.es/noticia/1666379/0/aduriz/llorente/tranquilidad/|title=Aduriz: "Llorente es el primero que quiere tranquilidad"|trans-title=Aduriz: "Llorente is the first to want tranquility"|newspaper=[[20 minutos]]|language=es|date=3 December 2012|access-date=15 May 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2012/12/27/futbol/equipos/athletic/1356597969.html|title=Aduriz eclipsa a Llorente|trans-title=Aduriz eclipses Llorente|newspaper=Marca|last=Briones|first=Macu|language=es|date=27 December 2012|access-date=15 May 2013}}</ref> and finished his [[2012–13 La Liga|first season]] in his second spell with 18 official goals, 14 in the league.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tudn.com/futbol/la-liga/aritz-aduriz-el-orgullo-de-ser-del-athletic-club-de-bilbao-fotos|title=Aritz Aduriz: el orgullo de ser del Athletic Club de Bilbao|trans-title=Aritz Aduriz: the pride of being of Athletic Club de Bilbao|publisher=[[TUDN (Mexican TV channel)|TUDN]]|language=es|date=10 August 2019|access-date=19 September 2024}}</ref>

Llorente left for [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in summer 2013, and Aduriz was made the starter by new manager [[Ernesto Valverde]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2014/apr/28/ernesto-valverde-athletic-bilbao|title=Ernesto Valverde's Athletic Bilbao sequel betters the original|newspaper=The Guardian|last=Lowe|first=Sid|date=28 April 2014|access-date=19 September 2024}}</ref> On 28 February of the following year, he scored three of his team's goals to help the hosts beat [[Granada CF|Granada]] 4–0.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2013_14/primera/jornada_26/ath_gda/|title=Aduriz lidera a un Athletic de Champions|trans-title=Aduriz leads Champions-bound Athletic|newspaper=Marca|last=Campos|first=Tomás|language=es|date=28 February 2014|access-date=3 March 2014}}</ref>

On 8 February 2015, Aduriz scored in a 2–5 home loss to Barcelona to complete a century of goals in Spain's top flight.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2015/02/08/futbol/equipos/athletic/1423431592.html|title=Aduriz se hace centenario|trans-title=Aduriz becomes a centenarian|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=9 February 2015|access-date=27 November 2015}}</ref> In the last match of [[2014–15 La Liga|the campaign]] on 23 May, he netted twice in a 4–0 home victory against [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] to clinch the [[Zarra Trophy]] by surpassing [[Rayo Vallecano]]'s [[Alberto Bueno]], whilst also [[2015–16 UEFA Europa League|qualifying for the Europa League]]. In the 24th minute, he ceded a [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty kick]] to Iraola who was leaving the club after 16 years, but his teammate declined, so he converted it instead.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2014_15/la-liga/jornada_38/ath_vil/|title=El Athletic monta la fiesta|trans-title=Athletic get the party started|newspaper=Marca|last=Estepa|first=Javier|language=es|date=23 May 2015|access-date=24 May 2015}}</ref>

Aduriz scored a hat-trick as Athletic [[2015 Supercopa de España|won 4–0]] against Barcelona in the first leg of the [[Supercopa de España]], on 14 August 2015,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/match/athletic-club-vs-barcelona/2038737?ICID=HP_HN_1|title=Athletic Bilbao 4–0 Barcelona: Aduriz hits hat-trick in Supercopa shocker|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|date=14 August 2015|access-date=14 August 2015}}</ref> and equalised in a 1–1 draw in the return match to hand his team the trophy, the first of his career.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33969001|title=Barcelona lose Super Cup final to Athletic Bilbao|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=17 August 2015|access-date=17 August 2015}}</ref> On 16 October, after starting [[2015–16 La Liga|the season]] strongly with 11 goals in 14 matches in all competitions, the 34-year-old agreed to a contract extension until 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/athletic-bilbao/story/2665961/aritz-aduriz-agrees-athletic-bilbao-contract-extension|title=Aritz Aduriz agrees Athletic Bilbao contract extension|publisher=ESPN FC|date=16 October 2015|access-date=16 October 2015}}</ref>

Aduriz again proved influential for his team on 5 November, scoring one goal and [[Assist (association football)|assisting]] a further two in a 5–1 defeat of [[FK Partizan|Partizan]] in the [[2015–16 UEFA Europa League|Europa League group stage]] – in the process, he reached the 100-goal mark with the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0227-0e927571a3a4-d1ea2800096c-1000--williams-at-the-double-as-athletic-go-clear/|title=Williams at the double as Athletic go clear|publisher=UEFA|date=5 November 2015|access-date=5 November 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2015/11/05/futbol/equipos/athletic/1446762991.html|title=Aduriz se pone a cien|trans-title=Aduriz gets to one hundred|newspaper=Marca|last=Rincón|first=Jaime|language=es|date=5 November 2015|access-date=6 November 2015}}</ref> On 24 January 2016, he netted through a [[bicycle kick]] to help his team come back from a 1–0 deficit to win 5–2 over neighbouring [[SD Eibar|Eibar]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/35393008|title=European football: Things you may have missed this weekend|publisher=BBC Sport|date=24 January 2016|access-date=19 February 2016}}</ref> On 18 February, in the Europa League's [[Single-elimination tournament|round-of-32]] tie at [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]], he scored what was described as a "wonderful" and "incredible" goal, the only one at the [[Stade Vélodrome]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/022a-0e935786d471-146a8a624664-1000--aduriz-wonder-goal-earns-athletic-win-at-marseille/|title=Aduriz wonder goal earns Athletic win at Marseille|publisher=UEFA|access-date=18 February 2016|date=19 February 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/planet-futbol/2016/02/18/aritz-aduriz-volley-europa-league-athletic-bilbao-marseille|title=Watch: Aritz Aduriz scores on incredible Europa League volley|publisher=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=18 February 2016|access-date=19 February 2016}}</ref>

Aduriz was the [[La Liga Player of the Month]] for March 2016 after scoring three goals, becoming the first Athletic player to win the award since its introduction in 2013. In that month, he also struck to eliminate former side Valencia from the last 16 in Europe.<ref name=pom16>{{cite web|url=http://www.laliga.es/en/news/aduriz-named-liga-bbva-player-of-the-month-for-march|title=Aduriz named Liga BBVA Player of the Month for March|publisher=[[La Liga]]|date=1 April 2016|access-date=1 April 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160417065829/http://www.laliga.es/en/news/aduriz-named-liga-bbva-player-of-the-month-for-march|archive-date=17 April 2016}}</ref> Even though the team was eliminated in the following round by eventual winners [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], he finished as the [[2015–16 UEFA Europa League#Top goalscorers|competition's top scorer]] with ten successful strikes,<ref name=UEFA>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0250-0c51138a59e3-328577f87a3c-1000--aduriz-finishes-uefa-europa-league-top-scorer/|title=Aduriz finishes UEFA Europa League top scorer|publisher=UEFA|date=18 May 2016|access-date=23 May 2016}}</ref> totalling 36 overall and only trailing [[Telmo Zarra]] (47) and [[Bata (footballer)|Bata]] (37) for goals during a single season with the club.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://en.as.com/en/2016/05/16/football/1463410783_391232.html|title=Aritz Aduriz enters into Athletic Bilbao folklore|newspaper=Diario AS|last=Cuenca|first=Nika|date=16 May 2016|access-date=22 May 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://athletic.elcorreo.com/noticias/201605/14/aduriz-paso-pichichi-nacional-20160514223139.html|title=Aduriz, pichichi nacional|trans-title=Aduriz, national ''pichichi''|newspaper=El Correo|language=es|date=16 May 2016|access-date=22 May 2016}}</ref>

====2016–2020, retirement====
[[File:SM-AB 2018 (4).jpg|thumb|Aduriz playing with Athletic in the [[2017–18 UEFA Europa League|2017–18 Europa League]]]]
On 3 November 2016, in a [[2016–17 UEFA Europa League group stage|Europa League group stage]] home fixture to [[K.R.C. Genk|Genk]], Aduriz scored all five of his team's goals (including three penalties) in a 5–3 victory, becoming the first player to accomplish this feat in the competition in the process.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0233-0e959b033563-859439aa0326-1000--aduriz-makes-history-with-five-goals-against-genk/|title=Aduriz makes history with five goals against Genk|publisher=UEFA|date=3 November 2016|access-date=9 April 2025}}</ref> Having previously been level with Llorente on 16, that achievement also took him clear as the club's [[Athletic Bilbao in European football|top scorer in European matches]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/newsid=2410926.html|title=Aduriz, 'Pichichi' rojiblanco en Europa|trans-title=Aduriz, red-and-white 'Pichichi' in Europe|publisher=UEFA|last=Aguado|first=Gonzalo|language=es|date=3 November 2016|access-date=17 July 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170906163517/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/newsid=2410926.html|archive-date=6 September 2017}}</ref>

Aduriz renewed his contract with Athletic once more in November 2017, this time to run until summer 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.eus/en/news/18466/aritz-adurizs-contract-renewal.html|title=Aritz Aduriz's contract renewal|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=15 November 2017|access-date=15 November 2017}}</ref> The following month, he became the club's oldest goalscorer after surpassing [[Agustín Gaínza]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/athletic/2017/12/10/5a2d7acae5fdea0c098b456f.html|title=Aduriz, el jugador más veterano en marcar con el Athletic en Liga|trans-title=Aduriz, the oldest player to score with Athletic in League|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=10 December 2017|access-date=20 May 2018}}</ref>

Aduriz was named the league's Player of the Month for the second time, winning the January 2018 award after showing good [[sportsmanship]] during a [[Basque football derbies|derby]] against Eibar: he fell in the penalty area going for a loose ball between two defenders, but immediately signalled to the referee and the supporters that no foul should be awarded (he also scored a few minutes earlier, one of two strikes during the month).<ref name=pom18>{{cite web|url=http://www.laliga.es/en/news/aritz-aduriz-named-laliga-santander-player-of-the-month-for-january|title=Aritz Aduriz named LaLiga Santander Player of the Month for January|publisher=La Liga|date=7 February 2018|access-date=10 February 2018|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180214124404/http://www.laliga.es/en/news/aritz-aduriz-named-laliga-santander-player-of-the-month-for-january|archive-date=14 February 2018}}</ref>

Despite the club being eliminated from the [[2017–18 UEFA Europa League|2017–18 Europa League]] at the last-16 stage, 37-year-old Aduriz finished as the competition's top scorer – along with [[SS Lazio|Lazio]]'s [[Ciro Immobile]] – with eight goals in the tournament proper.<ref name=scorer18>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/season=2018/statistics/round=2000890/players/kind=goals/index.html#order=4desc|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171001101716/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/season=2018/statistics/round=2000890/players/kind=goals/index.html#order=4desc|url-status=dead|archive-date=1 October 2017|title=Statistics — Tournament phase — Players — Goals (Assists)|publisher=UEFA|access-date=17 May 2018}}</ref> His [[2018–19 Athletic Bilbao season|2018–19 campaign]] was severely curtailed by injuries<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2019/04/07/5caa07b6ca4741fd1d8b4598.html|title=Aduriz returns to action after 87 days out|newspaper=Marca|last1=Velasco|first1=Juanma|last2=Quaile|first2=Kieran|date=7 April 2019|access-date=20 May 2020}}</ref> as the team generally struggled to score and collect points, and he scored only two league goals from 20 appearances; both were penalties in successive home fixtures, the first in a [[Panenka (penalty kick)|Panenka-style]] against [[Girona FC|Girona]] past former teammate [[Gorka Iraizoz]] for a last-minute 1–0 victory,<ref name=step>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2018/dec/24/aritz-aduriz-athletic-bilbao-la-liga|title=Aritz Aduriz offers a one-step solution to Athletic Bilbao's season of gloom|newspaper=The Guardian|last=Lowe|first=Sid|date=24 December 2018|access-date=27 February 2019}}</ref><ref name=jawdropping>{{cite web|url=https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-spain-atb-rev-idUKKCN1OL0OP|title=Athletic Bilbao's Aduriz scores jaw-dropping penalty|publisher=[[Reuters]]|last1=Martin|first1=Richard|last2=Herman|first2=Martyn|date=22 December 2018|access-date=27 February 2019|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181228063958/https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-spain-atb-rev-idUKKCN1OL0OP|archive-date=28 December 2018}}</ref><ref name=fiveaside>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/world-news/and-finally/watch-aritz-aduriz-scores-onestep-fiveaside-penalty-in-la-liga-game-37653583.html|title=Watch: Aritz Aduriz scores one-step 'five-a-side' penalty in La Liga game|newspaper=[[Irish Independent]]|last=Jones|first=Stephen|date=23 December 2019|access-date=27 February 2019}}</ref> and the second against Valladolid an unusual precise kick with no run-up, described as a "remarkable... [[five-a-side]]... minimalist" technique.<ref name=step/><ref name=jawdropping/><ref name=fiveaside/> He agreed a new one-year contract in May 2019,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.athletic-club.eus/en/news/2019/05/22/aritz-aduriz-will-continue-one-more-year-as-a-lion|title=Aritz Aduriz will continue one more year as a lion|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=22 May 2019|access-date=7 June 2019}}</ref> later confirming at the outset of [[2019–20 Athletic Bilbao season|2019–20]] that it would be his last season as a player before retiring.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.athletic-club.eus/en/news/2019/08/09/aduriz-colgara-las-botas-al-final-de-temporada|title=Aduriz will hang up his boots at the end of the season|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=8 August 2019|access-date=9 August 2019}}</ref>

On 16 August 2019, Aduriz scored the only goal in a 1–0 victory against Barcelona through a [[bicycle kick]] in the last minute of the first league fixture, helping his side to their first league win against that opposition since 2013 and also equalling [[Lionel Messi]]'s record of scoring in 15 consecutive league seasons.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/football/aduriz-matches-messi-feat-with-sensational-winner-against-barcelona|title=Aduriz matches Messi feat with sensational winner against Barcelona|publisher=Sportskeeda|date=16 August 2019|access-date=17 August 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/49371762|title=Athletic Bilbao 1–0 Barcelona|publisher=BBC Sport|date=17 August 2019|access-date=17 August 2019}}</ref><ref name=Picked>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/05/19/sports/soccer/aritz-aduriz-bilbao.html|title=He had picked the last day of his career. Now it may never come|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|last=Smith|first=Rory|date=19 May 2020|access-date=20 May 2020}}</ref> He had a stoppage-time penalty saved in a match away to previous employers Mallorca four weeks later,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/deportes/futbol/20190913/47326768669/athletic-mallorca-partido-resultado-aduriz-penaltis.html|title=Mallorca y Athletic se reparten los puntos y los penaltis fallados|trans-title=Mallorca and Athletic share points and missed penalties|newspaper=[[La Vanguardia]]|language=es|date=13 September 2019|access-date=6 June 2020}}</ref> and injuries then caused him to miss three months of matches over that winter. He returned to play a role from the bench in wins over Barcelona and Granada in February that helped the team qualify for the [[2020 Copa del Rey final]],<ref name=Picked/> but did not score again himself before the season was suspended due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Spain|COVID-19 pandemic]]<ref name=Picked/>– his last appearance being as a last-minute substitute in a win over another former club, Valladolid.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rtve.es/deportes/20200308/athletic-valladolid-cronica-jornada-27/2007082.shtml|title=El Athletic sigue de fiesta con una goleada en Valladolid|trans-title=Athletic party on with rout in Valladolid|publisher=[[RTVE]]|language=es|date=8 March 2020|access-date=6 June 2020}}</ref><ref name=Picked/>

On 20 May 2020, Aduriz announced his retirement as a professional footballer.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2020/05/20/5ec5590eca47418b1c8b45b6.html|title=Aritz Aduriz announces retirement: Unfortunately, my body has said enough|newspaper=Marca|date=20 May 2020|access-date=20 May 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.athletic-club.eus/en/news/2020/05/20/aduriz-cuelga-las-botas-en-el-athletic-club|title=Aduriz hangs up his boots at Athletic Club|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=20 May 2020|access-date=20 May 2020}}</ref>

==International career==
===Spain===
After an impressive start to his Valencia career, 29-year-old Aduriz earned a first call-up to the [[Spain national football team|Spain national team]], being picked for two [[UEFA Euro 2012]] [[UEFA Euro 2012 qualifying|qualifiers]] in October 2010. He made his debut on the 8th, replacing Llorente for the last 15 minutes of a 3–1 home win against [[Lithuania national football team|Lithuania]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0252-0ce21dd8fdc2-cefc3711a0c7-1000--mata-the-catalyst-as-spain-win-in-lithuania/|title=Mata the catalyst as Spain win in Lithuania|publisher=UEFA|last=Januška|first=Vaidotas|date=29 March 2011|access-date=9 April 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2016/mar/03/aritz-aduriz-better-age-athletic-bilbao|title=Aritz Aduriz proving some things get better with age at Athletic Bilbao|newspaper=The Guardian|last=Lowe|first=Sid|date=3 March 2016|access-date=9 April 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.deia.eus/athletic/2016/05/18/san-jose-aduriz-jugaran-eurocopa-5035448.html|title=San José y Aduriz jugarán la Eurocopa|trans-title=San José and Aduriz will play the Eurocup|newspaper=[[Deia (newspaper)|Deia]]|last=Artetxe|first=José Luis|language=es|date=18 May 2016|access-date=9 April 2025}}</ref>

Six years later, at the age of 35, Aduriz was recalled by manager [[Vicente del Bosque]] for friendlies with [[Italy national football team|Italy]] and [[Romania national football team|Romania]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-espana.net/56864/aduriz-earns-spain-call|title=Aduriz earns Spain call-up|publisher=Football España|date=20 February 2016|access-date=28 February 2016}}</ref> He started and scored in the first match, a 1–1 draw at the [[Stadio Friuli]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0253-0d80da7f7f06-76564055489d-1000--friendlies-go-well-for-aduriz-turkey-and-ukraine/|title=Friendlies go well for Aduriz, Turkey and Ukraine|publisher=UEFA|date=24 March 2016|access-date=24 March 2016}}</ref> and was selected for [[UEFA Euro 2016]] in France.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36312769|title=Euro 2016: Diego Costa, Juan Mata & Fernando Torres not in Spain squad|publisher=BBC Sport|date=17 May 2016|access-date=17 May 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://deportes.elpais.com/deportes/2016/05/31/actualidad/1464710610_277737.html?rel=cx_articulo|title=Isco y Saúl fuera de la lista de Del Bosque para la Eurocopa 2016|trans-title=Isco and Saúl out of Del Bosque's list for 2016 European Championship|newspaper=El País|last=Martín|first=Luis|language=es|date=31 May 2016|access-date=17 June 2016}}</ref> He made two substitute appearances in the group stage, always replacing Juventus' [[Álvaro Morata]] in the second half.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0253-0d81aa7c1443-3ec05ce3d198-1000--pique-pounces-late-as-spain-beat-czech-republic-in-euro-20/|title=Piqué pounces late as Spain beat Czech Republic in EURO 2016 Group D|publisher=UEFA|last=Saffer|first=Paul|date=13 June 2016|access-date=21 June 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro-2020/match/2017899--croatia-vs-spain/postmatch/report/|title=Perišić's late goal means Croatia pip Spain|publisher=UEFA|last=Saffer|first=Paul|date=21 June June, in the round-of-16 clash against Italy at the [[Stade de France]], he came out for [[Nolito]] at the start of the second half, but had to leave the pitch injured in an eventual 0–2 On 12 November 2016, after contributing to a 4–0 victory over [[Macedonia national football team|Macedonia]] in the [[2018 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|2018 World Cup qualifying phase]] in [[Granada]], Aduriz became Spain's oldest ever goal scorer at the age of 35 years and 275 days.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2016/11/12/582797de22601df53e8b4610.html|title=Aduriz becomes Spain's oldest scorer in Macedonia rout|newspaper=Marca|date=12 November 2016|access-date=13 November 2016}}</ref>

===Basque Country===
Aduriz made his debut for the [[Basque Country national football team|Basque representative team]] on 8 October 2006, opening a 2–2 draw at the [[Camp Nou]] against [[Catalonia national football team|Catalonia]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.diariovasco.com/prensa/20061009/deportes/tablas-catalunya-euskadi_20061009.html|title=Tablas en el Catalunya-Euskadi|trans-title=All square in Catalonia-Basque Country|newspaper=[[El Diario Vasco]]|language=es|date=9 October 2006|access-date=27 December 2015}}</ref> He also scored braces in victories over [[FIFA]] members [[Estonia national football team|Estonia]], [[Bolivia national football team|Bolivia]] and [[Peru national football team|Peru]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2011/05/25/futbol/1306360138.html|title=Aduriz puede con Estonia|trans-title=Aduriz deals with Estonia|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=25 May 2011|access-date=27 December 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2012/12/29/futbol/1356816676.html|title=Euskadi se divierte con Bolivia|trans-title=Basque Country have fun with Bolivia|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=29 December 2012|access-date=27 December 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2013/12/28/futbol/1388268706.html|title=Euskadi se divierte con una floja Perú|trans-title=Basque Country have fun with a weak Peru|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=28 December 2013|access-date=27 December 2015}}</ref>

As of 2017, Aduriz had 12 goals in friendly matches for the Basque team, making him their record goalscorer.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.deia.eus/futbol/2016/12/31/interminable-racha-aduriz-4987345.html|title=La interminable racha de Aduriz|trans-title=The endless streak of Aduriz|newspaper=Deia|language=es|date=31 December 2016|access-date=9 April 2025}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Aduriz was known for his aerial ability and first touch.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/athletic-bilbao/20171104/432566637417/athletic-aduriz-ostersunds-europa-league-llorente-kepa-arrizabalaga-urrutia.html|title=Las lecciones de Aduriz no tienen precio|trans-title=The lessons of Aduriz are priceless|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|last=Ugalde|first=Iñaki|language=es|date=4 November 2017|access-date=5 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/laliga/aduriz-record-cristiano-ronaldo-athletic-madrid-6435994|title=Aduriz le arrebata un record a Cristiano|trans-title=Aduriz takes record from Cristiano|newspaper=[[Sport (Spanish newspaper)|Sport]]|language=es|date=20 November 2017|access-date=5 January 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.whoscored.com/Players/9294|title=Aduriz|publisher=Who Scored|access-date=12 October 2016}}</ref>

He played for the [[Cameroon national football team|Cameroon national team]] from 2003 to 2015. ==Club career== ===Lille=== [[File:Makoun.jpg|thumb|200px|left|Makoun during his time with [[Lille OSC|Lille]].]] Born in [[Yaoundé]], Cameroon, Makoun began his career in his native Cameroon at [[Cotonsport Garoua]], where he was part of the team's youth setup.{{cite news|title=Jean Makoun: Ready for battle|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/jean-makoun-ready-for-battle-1.899768|publisher=CBC Sports|date=9 June 2010|access-date=30 June 2020}}{{cite news|title=Jean II Makoun : " Si je peux aider et apporter mon expérience "|url=https://www.francefootball.fr/news/Jean-ii-makoun-si-je-peux-aider-et-apporter-mon-experience/1141946|publisher=France Football|language=fr|date=10 June 2020|access-date=30 June 2020}} Following this, he spent time at other Cameroonian clubs Jeunesse Star and [[Tonnerre Yaoundé]], before moving to France, to join [[Ligue 1]] club [[Lille OSC|Lille]].{{cite web|url=https://www.ol.fr/en/contents/players/j/jean-ii-makoun|title=JEAN IIMAKOUN|publisher=Olympique Lyonnais|language=fr|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200627163805/https://www.ol.fr/en/contents/players/j/jean-ii-makoun|archive-date=27 June 2020|url-status=live}}{{cite news|title=Interview : Jean II Makoun - Le futur Lion de Lille (Afrik.com)|url=https://www.camfoot.com/interview/interview-jean-ii-makoun-le-futur,1843.html|publisher=Cam Foot|language=fr|date=22 September 2003|access-date=30 June 2020}} Makoun started out playing in the centre–back position but when he was at Lille, Makoun began playing in the centre–back position. Having progressed through the ranks of Lille youth system, he signed his professional contract, keeping him until 2006.{{cite news|title=Les joueurs camerounais ont la cote en Europe (CT)|url=https://www.camfoot.com/actualites/les-joueurs-camerounais-ont-la,1646.html|publisher=Cam Foot|language=fr|date=16 July 2003|access-date=30 June 2020}} Makoun was called up to the first team by Manager [[Claude Puel]] during the 2002–03 season. He made his Lille debut, coming on as a 63rd-minute substitute, in a 1–0 loss against [[SC Bastia]] on 2 November 2002.{{cite news|title=Hommage de Lille à Jean II Makoun|url=https://www.camfoot.com/les-lions-en-club/hommage-de-lille-a-jean-ii-makoun,9443|publisher=Cam Foot|language=fr|date=2 November 2002|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-date=1 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200701075557/https://www.camfoot.com/les-lions-en-club/hommage-de-lille-a-jean-ii-makoun,9443|url-status=dead}} Makoun made his first start for the side, starting the whole game, in a 2–0 loss against [[OGC Nice]] on 10 January 2003.{{cite web|url=https://www.ogcnice.com/fr/actualite/209/nice-2-0-lille|title=NICE 2-0 LILLE|publisher=OGC Nice|language=fr|date=10 January 2003|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200627203107/https://www.ogcnice.com/fr/actualite/209/nice-2-0-lille|archive-date=27 June 2020|url-status=live}} At the end of the 2002–03 season, he went on to make thirteen appearances in all competitions. At the start of the 2003–04 season, Makoun scored his first goal for the club, as they beat the defending champion, Lyon, to win 1–0.{{cite news|title=Lions en club : Jean II Makoun entre dans l'histoire du championnat français de L1 (Camfoot.com)|url=https://www.camfoot.com/les-lions-en-club/lions-en-club-jean-ii-makoun-entre,1715.html|publisher=Cam Foot|language=fr|date=4 August 2003|access-date=30 June 2020}} He quickly became a first team regular for the side under the management of Puel, who was impressed with his quality performance.{{cite news|title=Les lions en club : Pierre Womé montre le chemin des filets dès la 1re journée (Camfoot.com)|url=https://www.camfoot.com/les-lions-en-club/les-lions-en-club-pierre-wome,1789.html|publisher=Cam Foot|language=fr|date=1 September 2003|access-date=30 June 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Les lions en club : Job marque et offre la première victoire de la saison à M'boro (Camfoot.com)|url=https://www.camfoot.com/les-lions-en-club/les-lions-en-club-job-marque-et,1840.html|publisher=Cam Foot|language=fr|date=22 September 2003|access-date=30 June 2020}}

{{cite news|title=Corners fatals!|url=https://www.football.fr/ligue-1/corners-fatals-138129.html|publisher=Football France|language=fr|date=12 August 2007|access-date=30 June 2020}} Two weeks later on 26 August 2007, he scored his first goal of the season, in a 1–1 draw against Paris Saint-Germain.{{cite news|title=Le PSG sauve sa peau|url=https://www.football.fr/psg/le-psg-sauve-sa-peau-137914.html|publisher=Football France|language=fr|date=26 August 2007|access-date=30 June 2020}} Since the start of the 2007–08 season, Makoun started in the next eleven league matches before being sidelined with an abdominal wall.{{cite news|title=Lens-Lille en direct|url=https://www.football.fr/lille/lens-lille-en-direct-3-137527.html|publisher=Football France|language=fr|date=26 September 2007|access-date=30 June 2020}}

Following this, Makoun's performances attracted interest from clubs around Europe, including [[Premier League]] clubs [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] and [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]], as well as [[Serie A]] club [[Juventus]], and French clubs [[AS Monaco]], [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]], and [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]].{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11670_3555755,00.html|title=Prem rivals battle for Makoun|publisher=Sky Sports|date=12 May 2008|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080513190813/http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11670_3555755,00.html|archive-date=13 May 2008|url-status=dead}}
{{cite news|title=Spurs' Makoun bid set to fail|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11675/3674950|publisher=Sky Sports|date=10 June 2008|access-date=30 June 2020}} He became a firm fixture in the Lille side, making more than 150 appearances for the team in the league, and playing [[UEFA Champions League]] football. Upon leaving the club, Lille pay tribute to him, praising his courage, commitment and his loyalty. ===Lyon=== [[File:Bastos, Briand, Makoun 2010.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Makoun (third right) jogging, along with [[Michel Bastos]] and [[Jimmy Briand]] at Lyon, during the club's training sessions.]] On 16 June 2008, Makoun signed with seven-time French champions [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] on a four-year contract, where he re–joined Manager Claude Puel shortly after.[http://www.olweb.fr/index.php?lng=fr&a=39963&pid=101002 Jean II Makoun est lyonnais]{{in lang|fr}} {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081204101710/http://www.olweb.fr/index.php?lng=fr&a=39963&pid=101002 |date=4 December 2008}} The fee was worth €14 million with Lille set to receive another €1 million based on incentives. During his time with Lyon, Makoun wore the number 17 shirt, which was retired in 2003 after the death of Cameroonian midfielder [[Marc-Vivien Foé]].{{Citation|last=Lomas|first=Mark|title=The biggest stories of the decade|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/columns/story?id=713046&sec=reviewofthedecade&root=reviewofthedecade&cc=5901|work=[[ESPN]]|date=14 December 2009|access-date=14 December 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091218032814/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/columns/story?id=713046&sec=reviewofthedecade&root=reviewofthedecade&cc=5901|archive-date=18 December 2009|url-status=dead}} Makoun, also from Cameroon and a native of [[Yaoundé]], stated on wearing the number: "In memory of Marc, for me and for the whole Cameroon, this will be for something." Makoun started well on his debut for Olympique Lyonnais when he scored the club's first goal of the season, in a 3–0 win over [[Toulouse FC|Toulouse]].{{cite web|url=https://www.ol.fr/fr-fr/contenus/articles/2008/08/10/lol-demarre-fort-9536|title=L'OL DÉMARRE FORT|publisher=Olympique Lyonnais|language=fr|date=10 August 2008|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200628162638/https://www.ol.fr/fr-fr/contenus/articles/2008/08/10/lol-demarre-fort-9536|archive-date=28 June 2020|url-status=live}} Two weeks later on 23 August 2008, Makoun scored his second goal of the game, in a 2–0 win against [[Grenoble Foot 38|Grenoble Foot]].{{cite web|url=https://www.ol.fr/fr-fr/contenus/articles/2008/08/23/lol-remporte-son-derby-aperitif-9588|title= L'OL REMPORTE SON DERBY "APÉRITIF"...|publisher=Olympique Lyonnais|language=fr|date=23 August 2008|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200628163603/https://www.ol.fr/fr-fr/contenus/articles/2008/08/23/lol-remporte-son-derby-aperitif-9588|archive-date=28 June 2020|url-status=live}} Since making his debut for Olympique Lyonnais, he quickly established himself in the starting eleven for the side, playing in the midfield position.{{cite news|title=Makoun change de dimension|url=https://www.camfoot.com/les-lions-en-club/makoun-change-de-dimension,9778.html|publisher=Cam Foot|language=fr|date=3 October 2008|access-date=30 June 2020}}

{{cite news|title=Barcelona 5-2 Lyon (agg 6-3)|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/7938676.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|date=11 March 2009|access-date=30 June 2020}} Two months later on 12 May 2009, he scored twice for the side, as they won 3–0 against FC Nantes.{{cite web|url=https://www.ol.fr/fr-fr/contenus/articles/2009/04/30/le-point-presse-de-claude-puel-11154|title=LE POINT PRESSE DE CLAUDE PUEL|publisher=Olympique Lyonnais|language=fr|date=30 April 2009|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200628172312/https://www.ol.fr/fr-fr/contenus/articles/2009/04/30/le-point-presse-de-claude-puel-11154|archive-date=28 June 2020|url-status=live}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.ol.fr/fr-fr/contenus/articles/2009/05/12/rassurant-11221|title=RASSURANT !|publisher=Olympique Lyonnais|language=fr|date=12 May 2009|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200628172303/https://www.ol.fr/fr-fr/contenus/articles/2009/05/12/rassurant-11221|archive-date=28 June 2020|url-status=live}} At the end of the 2008–09 season, Makoun made forty–six appearances and scoring ten times in all competitions.{{cite web|url=https://www.ol.fr/fr-fr/contenus/articles/2009/06/02/la-saison-lyonnaise-11363|title=LA SAISON LYONNAISE|publisher=Olympique Lyonnais|language=fr|date=2 June 2009|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200628172253/https://www.ol.fr/fr-fr/contenus/articles/2009/06/02/la-saison-lyonnaise-11363|archive-date=28 June 2020|url-status=live}} At the start of the 2009–10 season, Makoun continued to regain his first team place, playing in the midfield position.{{cite web|url=https://www.ol.fr/fr-fr/contenus/articles/2009/08/15/lol-assure-lessentiel-11660|title=L'OL ASSURE L'ESSENTIEL|publisher=Olympique Lyonnais|language=fr|date=15 August 2009|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200628184119/https://www.ol.fr/fr-fr/contenus/articles/2009/08/15/lol-assure-lessentiel-11660|archive-date=28 June 2020|url-status=live}}

2020|url-status=live}} By the time Makoun departed Olympique Lyonnais, he made seventeen appearances and scoring once in all competitions. ===Aston Villa=== [[2010-11 avfc|On 12 January 2011]], Lyon revealed via their official website that Makoun had travelled to England in order to discuss a possible move to Premier League club [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], managed by former Lyon boss [[Gérard Houllier]].{{cite web|url=https://www.ol.fr/fr-fr/contenus/articles/2011/01/12/communique-15499|title=COMMUNIQUÉ|publisher=Olympique Lyonnais|language=fr|date=12 January 2011|access-date=30 15 January 2011, Aston Villa completed the signing of Makoun on a three-and-a-half-year deal for an undisclosed fee believed to be in the region of £6.2m.{{cite news|title=Aston Villa complete deal for Lyon's Jean Makoun|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/a/aston_villa/9359867.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|date=15 January 2011|access-date=30 June 2020}} On 21 January 2011, Villa and Makoun were handed international clearance and a work permit, with this announcement it was also revealed that he would take over the number 17 shirt from fellow West African [[Moustapha Salifou]].{{cite news|title=Aston Villa: Jean Makoun should be fit for Wigan debut|url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/aston-villa-jean-makoun-should-147097|publisher=Birmingham Mail|date=21 January 2011|access-date=30 June 2020}} He made his [[Premier League]] debut for Aston Villa in an away match against [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]] at the [[DW Stadium]] on 25 January 2011 in a 2–1 win.{{cite news|title=Wigan 1 Aston Villa 2: Mat Kendrick's big match report and stats|url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/wigan-1-aston-villa-2-147302|publisher=Birmingham Mail|date=25 January 2011|access-date=30 news|title=Blackpool 1–1 Aston Villa|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/9391041.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|date=12 February 2011|access-date=6 January 2013}} After a match, Makoun weeks|url=http://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/aston-villa-jean-makoun-could-148492|publisher=Birmingham Mail|date=14 February 2011|access-date=6 January 2013}} Upon his return length|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11095/6813092/|publisher=Sky Sports|date=14 March 2011|access-date=6 January 2013}} Makoun made his return in a 0–1 defeat against [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] on 19 March 2011.{{cite news|title=Aston Villa 0 Wolves 1: Full time report|url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/aston-villa-0-wolves-1-150719|publisher=Birmingham Mail|date=19 March 2011|access-date=30 June 2020}} However, he began to find himself behind the pecking order in midfield position and never played for the club for the rest of the 2010–11 season.{{cite news|title=Aston Villa: Gary McAllister plans to give youth a chance against Arsenal|url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/aston-villa-gary-mcallister-plans-154408|publisher=Birmingham Mail|date=14 May 2011|access-date=30 June 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Aston Villa: Big guns to return for Wigan clash|url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/aston-villa-big-guns-to-return-153736|publisher=Birmingham Mail|date=4 May 2011|access-date=30 June 2020}}

Following the departure of Houllier, Makoun struggled to hold down a first-team position at [[Villa Park]].{{cite news|title=McLeish may let Makoun move|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11095/7117422/|publisher=Sky Sports|date=22 August 2011|access-date=6 January 2013}} His first and only appearance of the [[2011-12 Aston Villa F.C. season|2011–12 season]] came in a 2–0 [[Football League Cup|League Cup]] victory over [[Hereford United F.C.|Hereford United]] on 23 August 2011.{{cite news|title=Villa reject Makoun approach|url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11095_7120219,00.html|work=Sky Sports|date=23 August 2011}} After his work permit was delayed, he left [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] at the end of the [[2012–13 Premier League|2012–13 season]], with [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]] deciding to make his [[Loan (sports)|loan move]] permanent for an undisclosed amount.{{cite news|title=Cameroon's Jean Makoun signs permanent deal with Rennes|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21993433|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=1 April 2013|access-date=1 April 2013}}

ASSE / SRFC : LES COMPOS|publisher=Stade Rennais F.C.|language=fr|date=26 October 2012|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629162419/https://www.staderennais.com/j10-asse-srfc-les-compos|archive-date=29 June 2020|url-status=live}} Having established himself in the first team, Manager [[Frédéric Antonetti]] praised Makoun's performance, with one goal in five starts and said to L'Equipe: ''"He is an experienced player, positive and generous, It is such big help for a young team as ours."''{{cite news|title=Rennes coach Frederic Antonetti hails Jean II Makoun|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11095/8196966/|publisher=Sky Sports|date=26 October 2012|access-date=6 January 2013}} In a 2–1 win over [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] on 17 November 2012, Makoun received a red card after second bookable offence.{{cite web|url=https://www.staderennais.com/j13-psg-srfc-1-2-heroiques|title=J13. PSG / SRFC (1-2) : HÉROÏQUES !|publisher=Stade Rennais F.C.|language=fr|date=17 November 2012|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629164132/https://www.staderennais.com/j13-psg-srfc-1-2-heroiques|archive-date=29 June 2020|url-status=live}} After serving a one match suspension, he returned to the starting line–up, starting the whole game, in a 3–2 win against Troyes on 2 December 2012.{{cite web|url=https://www.staderennais.com/j14-srfc-evian-tg-adoucoure-en-renfort|title=J14. SRFC / EVIAN TG : A.DOUCOURÉ EN RENFORT|publisher=Stade Rennais F.C.|language=fr|date=3 December 2012|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629164950/https://www.staderennais.com/j14-srfc-evian-tg-adoucoure-en-renfort|archive-date=29 June 2020|url-status=live}}
{{cite news|title=Ce Stade rennais-là a du caractère !|url=https://www.stade-rennais-online.com/Ce-Stade-rennais-la-a-du-caractere.html|publisher=Stade Rennais Online|language=fr|date=2 December 2012|access-date=30 June 2020}} However, his return was short–lived when Makoun suffered a thigh injury and was substituted at half time, as Stade Rennais drew 2–2 against [[Stade Brestois 29]] on 8 December 2012.{{cite web|url=https://www.staderennais.com/j17-nice-srfc-premiere-pour-smoreira|title=J17. NICE / SRFC : PREMIÈRE POUR S.MOREIRA|publisher=Stade Rennais F.C.|language=fr|date=10 December 2012|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629164958/https://www.staderennais.com/j17-nice-srfc-premiere-pour-smoreira|archive-date=29 June 2020|url-status=live}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.staderennais.com/jean-ii-makoun-out-jusqua-la-treve|title=JEAN II MAKOUN OUT JUSQU'À LA TRÊVE|publisher=Stade Rennais F.C.|language=fr|date=10 December 2012|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629165022/https://www.staderennais.com/jean-ii-makoun-out-jusqua-la-treve|archive-date=29 June 2020|url-status=live}} On 12 January 2013, he returned to the starting line–up, in a 2–0 loss against [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]].{{cite web|url=https://www.staderennais.com/stade-rennais-fc-bordeaux-0-2-score-final|title=STADE RENNAIS F.C. / BORDEAUX : 0-2 SCORE FINAL|publisher=Stade Rennais F.C.|language=fr|date=12 January 2013|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629165010/https://www.staderennais.com/stade-rennais-fc-bordeaux-0-2-score-final|archive-date=29 June 2020|url-status=live}} Makoun then contributed two assists for [[Mevlüt Erdinç]], setting up a goal against SC Bastia on 20 January 2013 and then set up another goal against Lorient two weeks later on 2 February 2013.{{cite web|url=https://www.staderennais.com/j21-bastia-srfc-0-2-score-final|title=J21. BASTIA / SRFC : 0-2 SCORE FINAL|publisher=Stade Rennais F.C.|language=fr|date=20 January 2013|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629165020/https://www.staderennais.com/j21-bastia-srfc-0-2-score-final|archive-date=29 June 2020|url-status=live}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.staderennais.com/j22-fcl-srfc-2-2-score-final|title= J22. FCL / SRFC : 2-2 SCORE FINAL|publisher=Stade Rennais F.C.|language=fr|date=3 February 2013|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629165017/https://www.staderennais.com/j22-fcl-srfc-2-2-score-final|archive-date=29 June 2020|url-status=live}} On 23 February 2013, Makoun scored his second goal for the club in a 2–2 draw against [[FC Sochaux-Montbéliard|Sochaux]].{{cite web|url=https://www.staderennais.com/j26-srfc-sochaux-2-2-score-final|title=J26. SRFC / SOCHAUX : 2-2 SCORE FINAL|publisher=Stade Rennais F.C.|language=fr|date=23 February 2013|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629165015/https://www.staderennais.com/j26-srfc-sochaux-2-2-score-final|archive-date=29 June 2020|url-status=live}} It was announced on 1 April that he would be joining Rennes on a permanent basis from 1 July.{{cite news|title=Aston Villa midfielder Makoun set to sign Rennes deal|url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/2892/transfer-zone/2013/03/30/3866461/aston-villa-midfielder-makoun-set-to-sign-rennes-deal|publisher=Goal.com|date=30 March 2013|access-date=1 April 2013}} Makoun started the whole game in the [[2013 Coupe de la Ligue Final|Coupe de la Ligue Final]], losing 1–0 against Saint-Étienne.{{cite web|url=https://www.staderennais.com/finale-cdl-asse-srfc-1-0|title=FINALE CDL : ASSE - SRFC : 1 - 0|publisher=Stade Rennais F.C.|language=fr|date=20 April 2013|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200516123029/https://www.staderennais.com/finale-cdl-asse-srfc-1-0|archive-date=16 May 2020|url-status=live}}

SRFC / TROYES : 1-2 SCORE FINAL|publisher=Stade Rennais FC|language=fr|date=24 April 2014|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200613184320/https://www.staderennais.com/j33-srfc-troyes-1-2-score-final|archive-date=13 June 2020|url-status=live}} At the end of the 2012–13 season, he went on to make thirty–two appearances and scoring two times in all competitions. At the start of the 2013–14 season, Makoun continued to be a first team regular for the side, playing in the midfield positions.{{cite web|url=https://www.staderennais.com/jean-ii-makoun-evian-ca-tient-la-route|title=JEAN II MAKOUN : " EVIAN, ÇA TIENT LA ROUTE "|publisher=Stade Rennais F.C.|language=fr|date=21 August 2013|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629185927/https://www.staderennais.com/jean-ii-makoun-evian-ca-tient-la-route|archive-date=29 June 2020|url-status=live}}

TFC / SRFC : 0-5 SCORE FINAL|publisher=Stade Rennais F.C.|language=fr|date=26 October 2013|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629191524/https://www.staderennais.com/j11-tfc-srfc-0-5-score-final|archive-date=29 June 2020|url-status=live}} However, on 18 March 2014, French media reported claims that Makoun was involved in a bust up with Manager [[Philippe Montanier]], which the player, himself, denied the claims.{{cite news|title=Altercation verbale entre Montanier et Makoun|url=https://www.stade-rennais-online.com/+Altercation-verbale-entre+.html|publisher=Stade Rennais Online|language=fr|date=18 March 2014|access-date=30 June 2020}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.staderennais.com/jean-ii-makoun-il-ny-pas-de-polemique|title=JEAN II MAKOUN : " IL N'Y A PAS DE POLÉMIQUE "|publisher=Stade Rennais F.C.|language=fr|date=20 March 2014|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629192445/https://www.staderennais.com/jean-ii-makoun-il-ny-pas-de-polemique|archive-date=29 June 2020|url-status=live}} Amid to the incident, he scored his first goal of the season, in a 3–0 win against Bastia on 30 March 2014.{{cite web|url= https://www.staderennais.com/j31-srfc-bastia-3-0-score-final|title=J31. SRFC / BASTIA : 3 - 0 SCORE FINAL|publisher=Stade Rennais F.C.|language=fr|date=30 March 2014|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629194948/https://www.staderennais.com/j31-srfc-bastia-3-0-score-final|archive-date=29 June 2020|url-status=live}} This was followed up by setting up the club's first goal of the game, in a 2–2 draw against Bordeaux.{{cite web|url=https://www.staderennais.com/j32-bordeaux-srfc-2-2-score-final|title=J32. BORDEAUX / SRFC : 2-2 SCORE FINAL|publisher=Stade Rennais F.C.|language=fr|date=5 April 2014|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629194950/https://www.staderennais.com/j32-bordeaux-srfc-2-2-score-final|archive-date=29 June 2020|url-status=live}} A week later on 15 April 2014, Makoun scored the club's third goal of the game, in a 3–2 win against [[Angers SCO]] in the semi–finals of Coupe de France to send them to the final.{{cite web|url=https://www.staderennais.com/stade-de-france-nous-revoila|title=STADE DE FRANCE : NOUS REVOILÀ !|publisher=Stade Rennais F.C.|language=fr|date=15 April 2014|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629194222/https://www.staderennais.com/stade-de-france-nous-revoila|archive-date=29 June 2020|url-status=live}} However, he appeared in the starting line–up and played 68 minutes before being substituted in the [[2014 Coupe de France Final|Coupe de France Final]] against Guingamp, as Stade Rennais lost 2–0.{{cite news|title=Guingamp en champion, Rennes en spectateur|url=http://www.stade-rennais-online.com/Guingamp-en-champion-Rennes-en.html|publisher=Stade Rennais Online|language=fr|date=3 May 2014|access-date=30 June 2020}}
