DANZÉ : "GUINGAMP N'EST PAS UN SI PETIT CLUB QUE ÇA!"|publisher=Stade Rennais F.C.|language=fr|date=29 April 2014|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200516151107/https://www.staderennais.com/r-danze-guingamp-nest-pas-un-si-petit-club-que-ca|archive-date=16 May 2020|url-status=live}} During the match, Makoun suffered ankle injury that kept him out of the 2013–14 season.{{cite web|url=https://www.staderennais.com/entorse-de-la-cheville-pour-j-makoun|title=ENTORSE DE LA CHEVILLE POUR J. MAKOUN|publisher=Stade Rennais F.C.|language=fr|date=5 May 2014|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629194214/https://www.staderennais.com/entorse-de-la-cheville-pour-j-makoun|archive-date=29 June 2020|url-status=live}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.staderennais.com/jean-ii-makoun-pas-apte-reprendre|title=JEAN II MAKOUN PAS APTE À REPRENDRE|publisher=Stade Rennais F.C.|language=fr|date=15 May 2014|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629194212/https://www.staderennais.com/jean-ii-makoun-pas-apte-reprendre|archive-date=29 June 2020|url-status=live}} Despite this, he went on to make thirty–five appearances and scoring two times in all competitions. [[File:Entrainement SRFC St-Malo 2013 (78).JPG|thumb|right|300px|Makoun prepare to do training at Marville stadium.]] In the opening game of the 2014–15 season, Makoun made his first appearance, starting and playing 63 minutes before being substituted, in a 2–0 loss against Lyon.{{cite news|title=Rennes n'a pas fait le poids|url=https://www.stade-rennais-online.com/Rennes-n-a-pas-fait-le-poids.html|publisher=Stade Rennais Online|language=fr|date=10 August 2014|access-date=30 June 2020}} However, this turns out to be his only appearance for the side, as he was dropped from the first team, due to his poor relationship with Manager Philippe Montanier.{{cite news|title=André forfait, Makoun écarté|url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/bretagne/andre-forfait-makoun-ecarte-2766084|publisher=Ouest France|language=fr|date=16 August 2014|access-date=30 June 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Stade Rennais express|url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/bretagne/stade-rennais-express-2940894|publisher=Ouest France|language=fr|date=28 October 2014|access-date=30 June 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Rennes, Makoun était-il le milieu de trop ?|url=https://www.goal.com/fr/news/33/transferts/2014/08/16/5038143/rennes-makoun-était-il-le-milieu-de-trop|publisher=Goal.com|language=fr|date=16 August 2014|access-date=30 June 2020}} As a result, the club was keen on selling him but the move was never materialised.{{cite news|title=Habib Habibou, la onzième recrue rennaise|url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/bretagne/habib-habibou-la-onzieme-recrue-rennaise-2797598|publisher=Ouest France|language=fr|date=1 September 2014|access-date=30 June 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Stade Rennais express|url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/bretagne/stade-rennais-express-3103299|publisher=Ouest France|language=fr|date=7 January 2015|access-date=30 June 2020}} Because Makoun stayed at the club, he spent most of the 2014–15 season, training with the first team and playing in the reserve match.{{cite news|title=Stade Rennais express|url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/bretagne/stade-rennais-express-2780937|publisher=Ouest France|language=fr|date=25 August 2014|access-date=30 June 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Konradsen et Makoun, comme un malaise|url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/bretagne/konradsen-et-makoun-comme-un-malaise-2924572|publisher=Ouest France|language=fr|date=21 October 2014|access-date=30 June 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Stade Rennais express|url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/bretagne/stade-rennais-express-3092528|publisher=Ouest France|language=fr|date=30 December 2014|access-date=30 June 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Rennes: André de retour à Lille|url=https://www.beinsports.com/france/football/news/rennes-andre-de-retour-a-lille/39247|publisher=Bein Sports|language=fr|date=14 March 2015|access-date=30 June 2020}} At the end of the 2014–15 season, Makoun was released by the club.{{cite news|title=Le mercato|url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/bretagne/le-mercato-3530398|publisher=Ouest France|language=fr|date=30 June 2015|access-date=30 June 2020}} ===Antalyaspor=== It was announced on 27 August 2015 that Makoun joined Turkish side [[Antalyaspor]] after impressing the side at the trial.{{cite news|title=Jean Makoun, Antalyaspor'da|url=https://www.milliyet.com.tr/skorer/jean-makoun-antalyasporda-2105070|publisher=Milliyet|language=tr|date=20 August 2015|access-date=30 June 2020}}
{{cite web|url=http://www.antalyaspor.com.tr/tr/futbol-haberleri/jean_makoun_antalyasporda.html|title=Jean Makoun Antalyaspor'da|publisher=Antalyaspor|language=tr|date=27 August 2015|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200630092009/http://www.antalyaspor.com.tr/tr/futbol-haberleri/jean_makoun_antalyasporda.html|archive-date=30 June 2020|url-status=live}} Makoun made his Antalyaspor debut, coming on as a 77th-minute substitute, in a 2–0 win against [[Eskişehirspor]] on 12 September 2015.{{cite news|title=Antalyaspor 2 - 0 Eskişehirspor|url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/antalyaspor-2-0-eskisehirspor-30058745|publisher=Hurriyet|language=tr|date=12 September 2015|access-date=30 June 2020}} Since making his debut for the club, he found himself in and out of the starting line–up, due to being placed on the substitute bench.{{cite news|title=Bursaspor 0–2 Antalyaspor|url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/bursaspor-0-2-antalyaspor-30335685|publisher=Hurriyet|language=tr|date=17 October 2015|access-date=30 June 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Antalyaspor 3-2 Mersin İdman Yurdu|url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/antalyaspor-3-2-mersin-idman-yurdu-40026264|publisher=Hurriyet|language=tr|date=12 December 2015|access-date=30 June 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Antalyaspor 1-0 Torku Konyaspor|url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/antalyaspor-1-0-torku-konyaspor-40097632|publisher=Hurriyet|language=tr|date=1 May 2016|access-date=30 June 2020}}
{{cite news|title= Mersin İdmanyurdu 0-1 Antalyaspor|url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/mersin-idmanyurdu-1-0-antalyaspor-40101043|publisher=Hurriyet|language=tr|date=8 May 2016|access-date=30 June 2020}} On 5 February 2016, Makoun scored his first Antalyaspor goal, in a 4–2 win against [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (football)|Fenerbahçe]].{{cite news|title=Antalyaspor-Fenerbahçe: 4-2|url=https://tr.beinsports.com/haber/antalyaspor-fenerbahce-2|publisher=Bein Sports|language=tr|date=5 February 2016|access-date=30 June 2020}} Two months later on 3 April 2016, he scored his second goal for the club, in a 2–2 draw against [[Akhisar Belediyespor]].{{cite news|title=Antalyaspor 2-2 Akhisar Belediyespor|url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/antalyaspor-2-2-akhisar-belediyespor-40080316|publisher=Hurriyet|language=tr|date=3 April 2016|access-date=30 June 2020}} Two weeks later on 16 August 2016, Makoun set up two goals for Antalyaspor, as they won 4–2 against [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]].{{cite news|title=Antalyaspor 4-2 Galatasaray|url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/antalyaspor-galatasaray-saat-16-00da-40089415|publisher=Hurriyet|language=tr|date=16 April 2016|access-date=30 June 2020}} He scored his third goal of the season, as well as, setting up a goal, in a 7–0 win against [[Trabzonspor]] on 13 May 2016.{{cite news|title=Antalyaspor 7-0 Trabzonspor|url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/antalyaspor-7-0-trabzonspor-40103571|publisher=Hurriyet|language=tr|date=13 May 2016|access-date=30 June 2020}} At the end of the 2015–16 season, Makoun went on to make thirty–one appearances and scoring three times in all competitions. At the start of the 2016–17 season, Makoun appeared in the first three league matches before suffering a muscle injury.{{cite news|title=Antalyaspor'da Makoun şoku|url=https://www.milliyet.com.tr/skorer/antalyasporda-makoun-soku-2311374|publisher=Milliyet|language=tr|date=15 September 2016|access-date=30 June 2020}}
{{cite web|url=http://www.antalyaspor.com.tr/tr/futbol-haberleri/aytemiz_alanyaspor_2_-_1_antalyaspor_2016-08-29_150827.html|title=Aytemiz Alanyaspor 2 - 1 Antalyaspor|publisher=Antalyaspor|language=tr|date=29 August 2016|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200630170302/http://www.antalyaspor.com.tr/tr/futbol-haberleri/aytemiz_alanyaspor_2_-_1_antalyaspor_2016-08-29_150827.html|archive-date=30 June 2020|url-status=live}}
{{cite news|title=Antalyaspor 1-3 Atiker Konyaspor / MAÇIN ÖZETİ|url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/antalyaspor-1-3-atiker-konyaspor-macin-ozeti-40222056|publisher=Hurriyet|language=tr|date=11 September 2016|access-date=30 June 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Antalyaspor 0-0 Osmanlıspor / MAÇIN ÖZETİ|url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/antalyaspor-0-0-osmanlispor-macin-ozeti-40204504|publisher=Hurriyet|language=tr|date=21 August 2016|access-date=30 June 2020}} Following this, he lost his first team place and was placed on the substitute bench for most of the 2016–17 season.{{cite web|url=http://www.antalyaspor.com.tr/tr/futbol-haberleri/antalyasporumuzun_ilk_11i_belli_oldu_2016-11-05_172228.html|title=Antalyasporumuzun İlk 11'i Belli Oldu|publisher=Antalyaspor|language=tr|date=5 November 2016|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200630192037/http://www.antalyaspor.com.tr/tr/futbol-haberleri/antalyasporumuzun_ilk_11i_belli_oldu_2016-11-05_172228.html|archive-date=30 June 2020|url-status=live}}
{{cite web|url=http://www.antalyaspor.com.tr/tr/futbol-haberleri/antalyasporumuz_istanbula_gitti_2016-12-02_125735.html|title=Antalyasporumuz İstanbul'a Gitti|publisher=Antalyaspor|language=tr|date=2 December 2016|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200630192027/http://www.antalyaspor.com.tr/tr/futbol-haberleri/antalyasporumuz_istanbula_gitti_2016-12-02_125735.html|archive-date=30 June 2020|url-status=live}}
{{cite web|url=http://www.antalyaspor.com.tr/tr/futbol-haberleri/centilmen_savasci_ondrej_celustka_2016-12-28_193855.html|title=Centilmen Savaşçı: Ondrej Celustka|publisher=Antalyaspor|language=tr|date=28 December 2016|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200630192015/http://www.antalyaspor.com.tr/tr/futbol-haberleri/centilmen_savasci_ondrej_celustka_2016-12-28_193855.html|archive-date=30 June 2020|url-status=live}} On 25 December 2016, Makoun scored his first goal of the season, in a 2–1 win against [[Kasımpaşa S.K.|Kasımpaşa]].{{cite news|title=Antalyaspor: 2 - Kasımpaşa: 1|url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/antalyaspor-2-kasimpasa-1-40317178|publisher=Hurriyet|language=tr|date=25 December 2016|access-date=30 June 2020}} After spending months on leave, he made his first starts of the season, in a 4–1 win against [[Gaziantepspor]] in the last game of the season.{{cite web|url=http://www.antalyaspor.com.tr/tr/futbol-haberleri/_2017-03-31_145935.html|title=Antalyasporumuz Kampa Girdi|publisher=Antalyaspor|language=tr|date=31 March 2017|access-date=30 June 2020}}
{{cite web|url=http://www.antalyaspor.com.tr/tr/futbol-haberleri/antalyaspor_2_-_1_gaziantepspor_2017-06-02_205852.html|title=Antalyaspor 4 - 1 Gaziantepspor|publisher=Antalyaspor|language=tr|date=2 June 2017|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200630191911/http://www.antalyaspor.com.tr/tr/futbol-haberleri/antalyaspor_2_-_1_gaziantepspor_2017-06-02_205852.html|archive-date=30 June 2020|url-status=live}} At the end of the 2016–17 season, Makoun went on to make nine appearances and scoring once in all competitions. Following this, he was released by the club.{{cite web|url=http://www.antalyaspor.com.tr/tr/futbol-haberleri/baskanimiz_sezonu_degerlendirdi_2017-06-05_154925.html|title=Başkanımız Sezonu Değerlendirdi|publisher=Antalyaspor|language=tr|date=5 June 2017|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200630191909/http://www.antalyaspor.com.tr/tr/futbol-haberleri/baskanimiz_sezonu_degerlendirdi_2017-06-05_154925.html|archive-date=30 June 2020|url-status=live}} ===Later career=== Following his release by Antalyaspor, Makoun remained a free agent until he joined Turkish Cypriot club {{ill|Merit Alsancak Yeşilova|tr|Alsancak Yeşilova SK}} on 2 October 2018.{{cite news|title=Entretien - À la recherche d'un club, Jean II Makoun a toujours "l'oeil du tigre"|url=https://www.goal.com/fr/news/entretien-a-la-recherche-dun-club-jean-ii-makoun-a-toujours/1nstz0dwp3se6zl9dlsvbka5v|publisher=Goal.com|language=fr|date=19 June 2019|access-date=30 June 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Transfert: Jean II Makoun rebondit à Chypre|url=https://www.camerounsports.info/28018-transfert-jean-ii-makoun-rebondit-a-chypre.html|publisher=Cameroun Sports|language=fr|date=2 October 2018|access-date=30 June 2020}} Makoun spent two years there before becoming a free agent in May 2020, where he was linked with a move to [[TP Mazembe]], but the move broke down.{{cite news|title=MAKOUN AU TP MAZEMBE ? LE CLUB DÉMENT CATÉGORIQUEMENT|url=https://www.football365.fr/makoun-tp-mazembe-club-dement-categoriquement-9831437.html|publisher=Football 365|language=fr|date=13 May 2016|access-date=30 June 2020}}
{{cite news|title=MAKOUN REVIENT SUR LA RUMEUR MAZEMBE ET VISE UN RETOUR EN AFRIQUE|url=https://www.football365.fr/jean-ii-makoun-9833072.html|publisher=Football 365|language=fr|date=16 May 2020|access-date=30 June 2020}} Despite the failing move, Makoun said in an interview that he has ruled out from professional football and would like to make a return to France.{{cite news|title=Jean II Makoun : " Si je peux aider et apporter mon expérience "|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Jean-ii-makoun-si-je-peux-aider-et-apporter-mon-experience/1141945|publisher=L’Equipe|language=fr|date=10 June 2020|access-date=30 June 2020}} ==International career== Having been called up to [[Cameroon national football team|Cameroon]] squad on two occasions, Makoun finally made his Cameroon debut, where he started the whole game, in a 0–0 draw against [[Japan national football team|Japan]] on 19 November 2003.{{cite news|title=CAN 2004 : Lions Sharpen Claws For Tunisia (CT)|url=https://www.camfoot.com/actualites/can-2004-lions-sharpen-claws-for,1866.html|publisher=Cam Foot|date=3 October 2004|access-date=30 June 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Cameroon name squad for Japan friendly (Reuters)|url=https://www.camfoot.com/actualites/cameroon-name-squad-for-japan,1993.html|publisher=Cam Foot|date=14 November 2003|access-date=30 June 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Cameroon held in Japan : 0-0 (BBC)|url=https://www.camfoot.com/actualites/cameroon-held-in-japan-0-0-bbc,2006|publisher=Cam Foot|date=19 November 2004|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200630204140/https://www.camfoot.com/actualites/cameroon-held-in-japan-0-0-bbc,2006|url-status=dead}} Two months later, Makoun was called up to the national squad to be part of the Cameroonian [[2004 African Nations Cup]] team.{{cite news|title=Cameroon choose squad|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/africa/3395739.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|date=12 January 2004|access-date=30 June 2020}} He made his debut in the tournament, starting a match and playing 75 minutes before being substituted, as Cameroon won 5–3 against [[Zimbabwe national football team|Zimbabwe]].{{cite news|title=Mboma sees off Zimbabwe|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/africa/3439759.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|date=29 January 2004|access-date=30 June 2020}} Cameroon went on to finish at the top of its group in the first round of competition before failing to secure qualification for the semi-finals.{{cite news|title=Nigeria reach semi-finals|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/africa/3465675.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|date=8 February 2004|access-date=30 June 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Jean II Makoun face à Camfoot : " Contre l'Égypte il nous faut un point, mais nous avons besoin des 3 points... "|url=https://www.camfoot.com/competitions/can2004/can2004-en-vedette/jean-ii-makoun-face-a-camfoot,4266.html|publisher=Cam Foot|language=fr|date=4 October 2004|access-date=30 June 2020}} Following Cameroon's failure qualify for the [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006 World Cup]], finishing one point behind qualifiers [[Ivory Coast national football team|Ivory Coast]] in their table, Makoun was called up to the national squad to be part of the Cameroonian [[2006 African Nations Cup]] team.{{cite news|title=Cameroun 1 - Egypte 1 : Le faux-pas cruel des Lions (in)domptables|url=https://www.camfoot.com/a-la-une/cameroun-1-egypte-1-le-faux-pas,6607|publisher=Cam Foot|language=fr|date=9 October 2005|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-date=3 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200703043721/https://www.camfoot.com/a-la-une/cameroun-1-egypte-1-le-faux-pas,6607|url-status=dead}}
{{cite news|title=BBC SPORT {{!}} Football {{!}} African {{!}} Atouba makes Nations Cup U-turn|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/africa/4599510.stm|access-date=30 June 2020|work=BBC Sport|date=10 January 2006}} He played an important role in a match against [[Togo national football team|Togo]], setting up a goal for [[Samuel Eto'o]], in a 2–0 win.{{cite news|title=Cameroon 2-0 Togo|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/africa/4642826.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|date=25 January 2006|access-date=30 June 2020}} However, Makoun started and played the whole game, as he scored in the epic 11–12 [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shootout]] quarter-final loss against [[Ivory Coast national football team|Ivory Coast]].{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/africa/4675316.stm|title=Cameroon 1–1 Ivory Coast|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=4 February 2006|access-date=30 June 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Jean II Makoun : " On a fait deux entraînements de qualité "|url=https://www.camfoot.com/interview/jean-ii-makoun-on-a-fait-deux,7747.html|publisher=Cam Foot|language=fr|date=6 October 2006|access-date=30 June 2020}} Makoun was named by [[Otto Pfister]] in Cameroon's squad for the [[2008 Africa Cup of Nations]] in [[Ghana]].{{cite news | title=Cameroon cancel Kenya camp|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/africa/7166292.stm|first=Martin|last=Etonge| work=BBC Sport|date=31 December 2007|access-date=30 June 2020}} Though he played three times in the tournament, Makoun was placed on the substitute bench for the other three matches, including [[2008 Africa Cup of Nations Final|the final]], which Cameroon lost 1–0 against [[Egypt national football team|Egypt]], having lost to them in the opening game of the tournament.{{cite news|title=CAN 2008 : La grosse désillusion|url=https://www.camfoot.com/competitions/can-2008-ghana/can-2008-la-grosse-desillusion,9004.html|publisher=Cam Foot|language=fr|date=23 January 2008|access-date=30 June 2020}}
{{cite web|publisher=BBC SPOR|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/africa/7215763.stm|title=Cameroon 3-0 Sudan|date=30 January 2008|access-date=30 June 2020}}
{{cite web|publisher=BBC SPOR|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/africa/7229132.stm|title=Ghana 0-1 Cameroon|date=7 February 2008|access-date=30 June 2020}}
{{cite web|publisher=BBC SPOR|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/africa/7236614.stm|title=Egypt 1-0 Cameroon|date=10 February 2008|access-date=30 June 2020}} Later in the year, he scored his first Cameroon goal, in a 5–0 win against [[Mauritius national football team|Mauritius]] on 10 October 2008.{{cite web|url=https://www.ol.fr/en/contents/articles/2008/10/13/ols-international-players-on-duty-this-week-end|title=OL'S INTERNATIONAL PLAYERS ON DUTY THIS WEEK-END.|publisher=Olympique Lyonnais|date=13 October 2008|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629211115/https://www.ol.fr/en/contents/articles/2008/10/13/ols-international-players-on-duty-this-week-end|archive-date=29 June 2020|url-status=live}} A year later, Makoun added two more goals against [[Gabon national football team|Gabon]] and Togo.{{cite web|url=https://www.ol.fr/fr-fr/contenus/articles/2009/09/07/les-resultats-des-internationaux-11831|title=LES RÉSULTATS DES INTERNATIONAUX|publisher=Olympique Lyonnais|language=fr|date=7 September 2009|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200628184212/https://www.ol.fr/fr-fr/contenus/articles/2009/09/07/les-resultats-des-internationaux-11831|archive-date=28 June 2020|url-status=live}}{{cite news|title=Cameroun - Togo : 3-0|url=https://www.camfoot.com/competitions/can-cm2010/cameroun-togo-3-0,10919.htm|publisher=Cam Foot|language=fr|date=10 October 2009|access-date=30 June 2020}}{{Dead link|date=October 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}{{cite web|url=http://uk.eurosport.yahoo.com/10022008/58/african-cup-nations-finalists-profile-cameroon.html|title=African Cup of Nations - Finalists in profile: Cameroon|publisher=Yahoo! Eurosport|date=10 February 2008|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080213211743/http://uk.eurosport.yahoo.com/10022008/58/african-cup-nations-finalists-profile-cameroon.html|archive-date=13 February 2008|url-status=dead}} A month later, he later helped Cameroon qualify for the [[2010 FIFA World Cup|next year World Cup]] after beating [[Morocco national football team|Morocco]] 2–0.{{cite web|url=https://www.ol.fr/fr-fr/contenus/articles/2009/11/15/du-cote-des-internationaux-12352|title=DU CÔTÉ DES INTERNATIONAUX...|publisher=Olympique Lyonnais|language=fr|date=15 November 2009|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200628192855/https://www.ol.fr/fr-fr/contenus/articles/2009/11/15/du-cote-des-internationaux-12352|archive-date=28 June 2020|url-status=live}} In May 2010, Makoun was named in Cameroon's 23 man squad for the World Cup.{{cite web|url=https://www.ol.fr/fr-fr/contenus/articles/2010/05/11/jean-ii-makoun-et-michel-bastos-en-selection-13775|title=JEAN II MAKOUN ET MICHEL BASTOS EN SÉLECTION|publisher=Olympique Lyonnais|language=fr|date=11 May 2010|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200628195011/https://www.ol.fr/fr-fr/contenus/articles/2010/05/11/jean-ii-makoun-et-michel-bastos-en-selection-13775|archive-date=28 June 2020|url-status=live}} He made his World Cup debut, starting a match and played 75 minutes before substituted, as Cameroon lost 1–0 against Japan.{{cite news|title=Cameroun - Japon : 0 - 1 - Le jeu et les joueurs|url=https://www.camfoot.com/competitions/can-cm2010/cameroun-japon-0-1-le-jeu-et-les,11878.html|publisher=Cam Foot|language=fr|date=14 June 2010|access-date=30 June 2020}} Makoun participated in all of Cameroon's games in their disappointing [[2010 FIFA World Cup]].{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/y=2010/m=6/news=danish-fightback-crushes-cameroon-1250315.html|title=Danish fightback crushes Cameroon|publisher=FIFA.com|date=19 June 2010|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160328193543/https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/y=2010/m=6/news=danish-fightback-crushes-cameroon-1250315.html|archive-date=28 March 2016|url-status=dead}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/matches/round=249722/match=300061473/report.html|title=Cameroon-Netherlands|publisher=FIFA.com|date=24 June 2010|access-date=23 July 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100627140354/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/matches/round%3D249722/match%3D300061473/report.html|archive-date=27 June 2010|url-status=dead}} After [[Samuel Eto'o]] was suspended 15 games by the [[Cameroonian Football Federation]], both Makoun and [[Benoît Angbwa]] issued an ultimatum to the federation, stating that they would not play for the national team unless his suspension was rescinded.{{cite news|title=Eto'o gets support from Cameroon stars in strike row|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16355824|publisher=BBC Sport|date=29 December 2011|access-date=30 June 2020}} Eventually, the ban was reduced to eight months in January 2012, meaning Eto'o would only miss four competitive matches.{{cite news|title=Fecafoot slashes Samuel Eto'o ban to eight months|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16455302|publisher=BBC Sport| date=7 January 2012| access-date=30 June 2020}} In October 2012, Makoun was called up to the national squad for the first time in over a year.{{cite web|url=https://www.staderennais.com/cameroun-1ere-pour-kana-makoun-de-retour|title=CAMEROUN : 1ÈRE POUR KANA, MAKOUN DE RETOUR|publisher=Stade Rennais FC|language=fr|date=3 October 2012|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629162449/https://www.staderennais.com/cameroun-1ere-pour-kana-makoun-de-retour|archive-date=29 June 2020|url-status=live}} He made his first appearance in two years for the national side, starting the whole game, in a 2–1 win against [[Cape Verde national football team|Cape Verde]].{{cite web|url=https://www.staderennais.com/diverses-fortunes-pour-les-rennais-en-selections|title=DIVERSES FORTUNES POUR LES RENNAIS EN SÉLECTIONS|publisher= Stade Rennais FC|language=fr|date=15 October 2012|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629162436/https://www.staderennais.com/diverses-fortunes-pour-les-rennais-en-selections|archive-date=29 June 2020|url-status=live}} Makoun then scored twice against [[Tunisia national football team|Tunisia]] to seal a 4–1 victory in the return match of the [[2014 FIFA World Cup qualification – CAF third round|CAF Third Qualification Round]] for [[2014 FIFA World Cup]] on 18 November 2013.{{cite web|url=https://www.staderennais.com/cameroun-qualifie-j-makoun-marque|title=CAMEROUN QUALIFIÉ. J. MAKOUN MARQUE|publisher=Stade Rennais F.C.|language=fr|date=18 November 2013|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629185455/https://www.staderennais.com/cameroun-qualifie-j-makoun-marque|archive-date=29 June 2020|url-status=live}} This ensured Cameroon qualification to the World Cup.{{cite web|title=World Cup 2014: Your guide to Group A - Brazil; Croatia; Mexico; Cameroon|date=6 December 2013|url =https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/international/world-cup-2014-your-guide-to-group-a--brazil-croatia-mexico-cameroon-8989410.html|work=The Independent|access-date=15 January 2014}} It was announced on 21 May 2014 that Makoun was included in Cameroon's squad for the World Cup.{{cite web|url=https://www.staderennais.com/les-rennais-en-selection-2|title=LES RENNAIS EN SÉLECTION|publisher=Stade Rennais F.C.|language=fr|date=21 May 2014|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629194209/https://www.staderennais.com/les-rennais-en-selection-2|archive-date=29 June 2020|url-status=live}} Having appeared as an unused substitute in the first two matches in the group stage and witnessing the national side elimination, he made his first appearance of the tournament, coming on as an 81st-minute substitute, in a 4–1 loss against [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]], in what turns out his last appearance for Cameroon.{{cite web|url=https://www.staderennais.com/le-cameroun-elimine-de-la-coupe-du-monde|title=LE CAMEROUN ÉLIMINÉ DE LA COUPE DU MONDE|publisher=Stade Rennais F.C.|language=fr|date=19 June 2014|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629194149/https://www.staderennais.com/le-cameroun-elimine-de-la-coupe-du-monde|archive-date=29 June 2020|url-status=live}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.staderennais.com/le-cameroun-sort-par-la-petite-porte|title=LE CAMEROUN SORT PAR LA PETITE PORTE|publisher=Stade Rennais F.C.|language=fr|date=24 June 2014|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629194145/https://www.staderennais.com/le-cameroun-sort-par-la-petite-porte|archive-date=29 June 2020|url-status=live}} On 27 August 2014, Makoun announced his retirement from international competition, which coincidentally Eto'o announced on the same day.{{cite news|title=JEAN II MAKOUN PREND SA RETRAITE INTERNATIONALE|url=https://www.africatopsports.com/2014/08/27/jean-ii-makoun-prend-retraite-internationale/|publisher=African Top Sports|date=27 August 2014|access-date=30 June 2020}} ==Personal life== Makoun likes to be referred to as Jean II since his father, Jean Sr., is also a footballer.{{cite web|url=https://www.staderennais.com/appelez-le-jean-ii|title=APPELEZ-LE " JEAN II " !|publisher=Stade Rennais FC|language=fr|date=28 August 2012|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200629160543/https://www.staderennais.com/appelez-le-jean-ii|archive-date=29 June 2020|url-status=live}} Makoun is married and has four children, including Jean III Makoun, who followed his footstep to be a footballer.{{cite news|title=OL – 1er contrat pro pour Jean III Makoun, le fils de Jean II Makoun|url=https://www.footballfrance.fr/football/france/2019/06/ol-1er-contrat-pro-pour-jean-iii-makoun-fils-jean-ii-makoun/16838|publisher=France Football|language=fr|date=19 June 2019|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-date=27 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200627225255/https://www.footballfrance.fr/football/france/2019/06/ol-1er-contrat-pro-pour-jean-iii-makoun-fils-jean-ii-makoun/16838|url-status=dead}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.ol.fr/fr-fr/contenus/articles/2009/01/23/makoun-vu-du-cameroun-10515|title=MAKOUN VU DU CAMEROUN|publisher=Olympique Lyonnais|language=fr|date=23 January 2009|access-date=30 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200628164805/https://www.ol.fr/fr-fr/contenus/articles/2009/01/23/makoun-vu-du-cameroun-10515|archive-date=28 June 2020|url-status=live}} In April '''Nanitamo Jonathan Ikoné''' (born 2 May 1998) is a French professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] or [[wide midfielder]] for French {{French football updater|Paris FC}} club [[Paris FC]].

Ikoné scored one goal in four appearances for the [[France national football team|France national team]] in 2019.<ref name="soccerway">{{Soccerway|nanitamo-ikone/373465}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Paris Saint-Germain===
Ikone made his professional debut on 28 September 2016 in the [[UEFA Champions League]] against [[PFC Ludogorets Razgrad|Ludogorets]] replacing [[Ángel Di María]] after 88 minutes in a 1–3 away win.<ref name="soccerway2">{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2016/09/28/europe/uefa-champions-league/fk-razgrad-2000/paris-saint-germain-fc/2348315/|title=Ludogorets vs. PSG - 28 September 2016 - Soccerway|publisher=soccerway.com|access-date=29 September 2016}}</ref> He made his [[Ligue 1]] debut three days later against [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]], once again coming on in place of Di María after 88 minutes in a 2–0 home win.<ref name="soccerway3">{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2016/10/01/france/ligue-1/paris-saint-germain-fc/fc-girondins-de-bordeaux/2236909/|title=PSG vs. Bordeaux - 1 October 2016 - Soccerway|publisher=soccerway.com|access-date=1 October 2016}}</ref>

====Loan to Montpellier====
On 18 January 2017, Ikoné was loaned to fellow [[Ligue 1]] side [[Montpellier HSC|Montpellier]] for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sport24.lefigaro.fr/football/transferts/fil-info/psg-ikone-officiellement-prete-a-montpellier-841927|title=PSG: Ikoné officiellement prêté à Montpellier|trans-title=PSG: Ikoné officially loaned to Montpellier|publisher=[[Le Figaro]]|language=fr|date=18 January 2017|access-date=18 January 2017}}</ref> He made his debut against [[FC Metz|Metz]] three days later and played the whole match.<ref name="soccerway4">{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2017/01/21/france/ligue-1/fc-de-metz/montpellier-herault-sport-club/2236865/|title=Metz vs. Montpellier - 21 January 2017 - Soccerway|publisher=soccerway.com|access-date= 23 January 2017}}</ref>

===Lille===
On 1 July 2018, Ikoné joined [[Ligue 1]] side [[Lille OSC|Lille]] on a five-year contract.<ref>{{cite news |title=PSG : Jonathan Ikoné part à Lille |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Psg-jonathan-ikone-part-a-lille/918154 |access-date=2 July 2018 |work=L'Équipe |date=2 July 2018 |language=fr}}</ref>

===Fiorentina===
On 31 December 2021, Ikoné signed for [[Serie A]] club [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]], effective from 3 January 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|date=31 December 2021|title=Accord total avec la Fiorentina pour le transfert de Jonathan Ikoné|trans-title=Total agreement with Fiorentina for the transfer of Jonathan Ikoné|url=https://www.losc.fr/actualites-foot-lille/%E2%80%8Baccord-total-avec-la-fiorentina-pour-le-transfert-de-jonathan-ikon%C3%A9|access-date=31 December 2021|website=|publisher=[[Lille OSC]]|language=fr}}</ref> The deal was worth a reported €15 million.<ref>{{Cite web|date=31 December 2021|title=Jonathan Ikone leaving Lille to join Italian club Fiorentina - Sportsnet.ca|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/ligue-1/article/jonathan-ikone-leaving-lille-join-italian-club-fiorentina/|access-date=31 December 2021|website=Sportsnet}}</ref>

====Loan to Como====
On 31 January 2025, Ikoné moved on loan to [[Como 1907|Como]], with an option to buy.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Como 1907|url=https://comofootball.com/en/como-1907-announces-the-signing-french-international-jonathan-ikone/|title=Como 1907 Announces the signing of French International Jonathan Ikoné|date=31 January 2025|access-date=31 January 2025}}</ref>

In July 2025, [[Botafogo FR|Botafogo]] showed interest in the French striker, who was then on loan to Como 1907.<ref>{{Cite web |last=FNR |first=Redação |date=2025-08-09 |title=Botafogo tem interesse no atacante Jonathan Ikoné, da Fiorentina, diz site italiano |url=https://fogonarede.com.br/botafogo-tem-interesse-no-atacante-jonathan-ikone-da-fiorentina-diz-site-italiano/ |access-date=2025-08-09 |website=Fogo na Rede |language=pt-br}}</ref>

===Paris FC===
On 1 September 2025, Ikone signed for French Ligue 1 side [[Paris FC]] until 2027, the deal was worth €2 million.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://parisfc.fr/en/pro-mens-team/jonathan-ikone-rejoint-le-paris-fc/ |title=Jonathan Ikoné joins Paris FC |publisher=Paris FC |date=2 September 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.getfootballnewsfrance.com/2025/official-jonathan-ikone-joins-paris-fc-from-serie-a-side-como/ |title=Official {{!}} Jonathan Ikoné joins Paris FC from Serie A side Como |publisher=Get Football News France |date=1 September 2025 }}</ref> Later that year, on 20 December, he netted his first goals for the club by scoring a hat-trick in a 3–0 away win over [[US Raon-l'Étape]] in the [[2025–26 Coupe de France|Coupe de France]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://parisfc.fr/en/pro-mens-team/coupe-de-france-le-paris-fc-simpose-a-raon-letape-et-se-qualifie-pour-les-16es/ |title=Coupe de France: Paris FC win at Raon-l’Étape to qualify for the last 16 |publisher=Paris FC |date=21 December 2025 }}</ref>

On 12 January 2026, Ikone score the only goal in a 1–0 away win over his former club Paris Saint-Germain during the Coupe de France round of 32, securing his club's first ever win in the [[Paris derby]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Paris FC Win Their First Ever Paris Derby 1-0 at Parc des Princes {{!}} Coupe de France Highlights |url=https://www.soccerstat.com.ng/2026/01/paris-fc-win-their-first-ever-paris.html |access-date=2026-01-15}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.france24.com/en/sport/20260113-ikone-stuns-paris-saint-germain-as-paris-fc-reach-french-cup-last-16 |title=Ikoné stuns Paris Saint-Germain as Paris FC reach French Cup last 16 |publisher=France 24 |date=12 January 2026 }}</ref>

==International career==
Ikoné was born in France and is of DR Congolese descent.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.leparisien.fr/espace-premium/essonne-91/la-releve-du-psg-c-est-peut-etre-lui-30-10-2013-3269985.php|title=La relève du PSG, c'est peut-être lui|trans-title=The next generation of PSG, it may be him|language=fr|website=leparisien.fr|publisher=Le Parisien|date=30 October 2013|access-date=5 April 2020}}</ref> He is a youth international footballer for France.<ref>{{cite news|title=Svanberg receives first Sweden call-up  |url=https://www.bolognafc.it/en/svanberg-receives-first-sweden-call-up/ |access-date=3 September 2019|website=bolognafc.it |date=12 November 2018}}</ref> He was called up to the senior [[France national football team|France]] squad for games against [[Albania national football team|Albania]] and [[Andorra national football team|Andorra]] in September 2019.<ref>{{cite news|title=Aymeric Laporte Finally Gets France Call-Up  |url=https://www.beinsports.com/us/euro-2020-qualifiers/news/aymeric-laporte-finally-gets-france-call-up/1278528 |access-date=3 September 2019|website=beinsports.com |date=29 August 2019}}</ref> He scored on his debut on 7 September against Albania after coming on as a 77th-minute substitute for [[Kingsley Coman]].<ref>{{cite news|title=France win after Albania national anthem mix-up |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/49574096 |access-date=8 September 2019|website=bbc.co.uk |date=7 September 2019}}</ref>

'''Stéphane Mbia Etoundi''' (born 20 May 1986) is a Cameroonian former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[defensive midfielder]] or [[defender (association football)|defender]].

He played 179 games and scored nine goals in [[Ligue 1]] over nine seasons playing for [[Stade Rennais|Rennes]], [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] and [[Toulouse FC|Toulouse]]. He spent two years at [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], winning the [[UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] in both.
He also played for Cameroon 68 times from 2005 to 2016 and scored five goals for the national team. He was included in the squads for the [[Football at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008 Olympics]], two [[Africa Cup of Nations]] tournaments and two [[FIFA World Cup]]s.

==Club career==

===Rennes===
Born in [[Yaoundé]], Mbia made his debut for the [[Stade Rennais|Rennes]] first team during the 2005–06 season, going on to make a handful of appearances over the campaign. The Cameroonian scored his first [[Ligue 1]] goal in November 2006 against the incumbent French champions [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]].

On 18 April 2007, Mbia was abused by Lyon player [[Milan Baroš]]. This led to disciplinary action being taken against Baroš by the [[French Football Federation]], who banned the striker for three matches.<ref>[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/africa/6573067.stm BBC SPORT | Football | African | Baros in racism row over Mbia]. BBC News (20 April 2007). Retrieved on 3 December 2011.</ref><ref>[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/africa/6623671.stm BBC SPORT | Football | African | Baros banned for Mbia incident]. BBC News (4 May 2007). Retrieved on 3 December 2011.</ref>

===Marseille===
On 14 July 2009, Mbia completed his £10.4 million move to [[Marseille]] from Rennes, going on to play a vital role in Marseille's victorious Ligue 1 campaign that season, starting off as a [[defensive midfielder]] but later making the transition to the role of centre back alongside former [[Charlton Athletic]] player [[Souleymane Diawara]]. His redeployment at centre back was a success and he went on to play the rest of the season in this position, where he was considered to be one of the best performers in [[Didier Deschamps]]' talented squad, as he formed a formidable defensive partnership with Diawara.

===Queens Park Rangers===
On 31 August 2012 Mbia signed a two-year deal with English [[Premier League]] club [[Queens Park Rangers]], signing for an undisclosed fee, with [[Joey Barton]] heading in the opposite direction on a season-long loan.<ref>{{cite news | title = EXCLUSIVE: STEPHANE SEALS SWITCH | url = http://www.qpr.co.uk/news/article/310812-mbia-signs-345843.aspx | publisher = QPR | date = 31 August 2012 | access-date = 31 August 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | title = EXCLUSIVE: BARTON JOINS MARSEILLE | url = http://www.qpr.co.uk/news/article/310812-barton-loan-345833.aspx | publisher = QPR | date = 31 August 2012 | access-date = 31 August 2012}}</ref>

On 27 October 2012, Mbia was sent off seventeen minutes from the end of only his fourth league appearance for QPR, a 1–0 defeat to [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] at the [[Emirates Stadium]]. He was dismissed in the 79th minute for violent conduct after kicking Gunners defender [[Thomas Vermaelen]] in retaliation to a strong challenge that had left Mbia floored.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/20014281 |title=Mikel Arteta's late winner ended bottom-club Queens Park Rangers' resistance as Arsenal finished a turbulent week with a vital victory. |publisher=BBC Sport |date=27 October 2012 |access-date=1 May 2014}}</ref> He received the standard three-match ban from the [[The FA|FA]], and became ineligible for QPR's league games against [[Reading F.C.|Reading]], [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] and [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]].<ref>{{cite news | title = Mbia sent off versus Arsenal; match report 27 October 2012 | url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20014281}}</ref> On 6 May 2013, Mbia tweeted to Joey Barton, asking him if he would like to switch seats with him at Marseille in hinting that he wanted to leave Queen Park Rangers after they were relegated from the Premier League. In July 2013 Mbia scored his first goal for the club in a pre-season friendly against [[Southend United]] and expressed desire to stay at QPR.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.westlondonsport.com/qpr/mbia-insists-he-is-100-committed-to-qpr |title=Mbia insists he is '100% committed' to QPR |publisher=westlondonsport.com |date=29 July 2013 |access-date=21 June 2016}}</ref>

===Sevilla===
[[File:Zenit-Sevilla (2).jpg|thumb|left|200px|Mbia playing for Sevilla against [[FC Zenit Saint Petersburg|Zenit]] in 2015]]
On 26 August 2013, Mbia was loaned out to Spanish [[La Liga]] club [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=QPR midfielder Stephane Mbia joins Sevilla on loan|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23844401|access-date=24 April 2014|newspaper=[[BBC Sport]]|date=26 August 2013}}</ref> Mbia made his Sevilla debut on 1 September, providing an assist for [[Kevin Gameiro]]'s first goal in a 2–2 draw with [[Málaga CF|Málaga]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/en/report/373194/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=null |title=Gameiro double thwarts Málaga |publisher=ESPNFC |date=1 September 2013 |access-date=1 May 2014 }}</ref> On 27 October, Mbia provided assists for both [[Ivan Rakitić]] and [[Jairo Samperio]] as Sevilla overcame 10-man [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]] 2–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/en/report/373122/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=null |title=Sevilla see off 10-man Osasuna |publisher=ESPNFC |date=27 October 2013 |access-date=1 May 2014 }}</ref> His first goal in [[2013-14 La Liga|La Liga]] came in the [[Seville derby]] against [[Real Betis]] on 24 November, heading in Sevilla's second goal in a 4–0 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/en/report/373083/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=null |title=Sevilla ease to victory over Betis |publisher=ESPNFC |date=24 November 2013 |access-date=1 May 2014 }}</ref>

Mbia scored with a back-heel in the first leg of their Europa League semi-final against compatriots [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] on 24 April 2014 in a 2–0 home win.<ref>{{cite news|title=Sevilla 2–0 Valencia|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27147999|access-date=24 April 2014|newspaper=[[BBC Sport]]|date=24 April 2014}}</ref> In the second leg on 1 May, he scored the winning away goal with a header in the fourth minute of added time to take Sevilla into [[2014 UEFA Europa League Final|the final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/us/en/report/391820/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5901 |title=Sevilla advance with last-gasp winner |publisher=ESPNFC |date=1 May 2014 |access-date=1 May 2014 }}</ref> Sevilla subsequently won the final in a shootout against [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] at the [[Juventus Stadium]] in Turin on 14 May, with Mbia converting his penalty kick after the match had ended 0—0.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0250-0c510740b3cf-c46f4d5f782f-1000--spot-on-sevilla-leave-benfica-dreams-in-tatters/ |title=Spot-on Sevilla leave Benfica dreams in tatters |publisher=UEFA |date=14 May 2014 |access-date=1 June 2014 }}</ref> On 3 June, Mbia was selected in the 18-man Europa League "Team of the Year" along with teammates [[Ivan Rakitić]], [[Nicolás Pareja]] and [[Beto (Portuguese footballer, born 1982)|Beto]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0250-0c5109b21129-db53e4c1b485-1000--uefa-europa-league-squad-of-the-season/ |title=UEFA Europa League squad of the season |publisher=UEFA |date=3 June 2014 |access-date=6 June 2014 }}</ref> At the [[LFP Awards]], he was a nominee for the league's best African player, alongside the [[Granada CF|Granada]] duo of [[Yacine Brahimi]] and [[Youssef El-Arabi]].<ref>{{cite web|title=gala de premios LFP 2013/14|trans-title=LFP Awards show 2013/14|url=http://www.lfp.es/gala-lfp-2013-2014|publisher=[[Liga de Fútbol Profesional]]|access-date=10 November 2014|language=es}}</ref>

On 31 August 2014, Mbia rejoined Sevilla on permanent basis.<ref>{{cite web|title=STÉPHANE MBIA NUEVO JUGADOR DEL SEVILLA FC|url=http://www.sevillafc.es/nuevaweb/actualidad/noticias/34526|publisher=Sevilla FC|access-date=31 August 2014|date=31 August 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140831220527/http://www.sevillafc.es/nuevaweb/actualidad/noticias/34526|archive-date=31 August 2014}}</ref> He scored his first goal of the new season on 18 September, heading in a cross from [[Gerard Deulofeu]] as Sevilla started the defense of their Europa League title with a 2–0 win over [[Feyenoord Rotterdam|Feyenoord]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0219-0e8c6e5813f8-1f5c6803ca40-1000--quick-fire-sevilla-catch-feyenoord-cold/ |title=Quick-fire Sevilla catch Feyenoord cold |work=UEFA |date=18 September 2014 |access-date=18 September 2014 }}</ref> Mbia netted a brace as Sevilla earned a comfortable 4–1 victory over [[Deportivo de La Coruña]] at the Ramon Sanchez Pizjuan stadium on 5 October.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/spanish-primera-divisi%C3%B3n/match/402563/sevilla-fc-deportivo-la-coru%C3%B1a/report |title=Mbia double sinks Depor |work=ESPNFC |date=5 October 2014 |access-date=5 October 2014 }}</ref>

On 27 May 2015, Mbia started for Sevilla in the [[2015 UEFA Europa League Final]] defeat of [[FC Dnipro|Dnipro]] at Poland's [[National Stadium, Warsaw|National Stadium]], thus retaining their [[UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] crown, and qualifying the team for [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League|next season's Champions League]]<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0221-0e90e6fca8ef-a1811c0e7d3d-1000--sevilla-defeat-dnipro-to-land-record-fourth-title/|title=Sevilla defeat Dnipro to land record fourth title|publisher=[[UEFA]]|date=27 May 2015|access-date=13 June 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0221-0e90e94010ee-d2f48f00cca8-1000--sevilla-overwhelmed-by-historic-success/|title=Sevilla overwhelmed by historic success|publisher=[[UEFA]]|date=27 May 2015|access-date=6 June 2015}}</ref>

===Later career===
On 2 July 2015, Mbia joined [[Trabzonspor]] on a free transfer, signing a three-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.trabzonspor.org.tr/default.asp?Sayfa=HaberDetay&IND=17743#Icerik |title=M'bia için imza töreni düzenlendi |publisher=Trabzonspor |access-date=2 July 2015 |language=tr }}</ref>

On 29 January 2016, Mbia signed for [[Chinese Super League]] club [[Hebei China Fortune F.C.|Hebei China Fortune]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35438889|title=Cameroon captain Stephane Mbia joins Gervinho in China|work=BBC Sport |date=29 January 2016 |access-date=29 January 2016 |language=en}}</ref> In March 2018, he left the club by mutual consent.<ref name="toulouse">{{cite news |title=Toulouse unveil former Cameroon captain Stephane Mbia |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/45220133 |access-date=18 August 2018 |work=BBC Sport |date=17 August 2018}}</ref>

In August 2018, Mbia joined Ligue 1 side [[Toulouse FC|Toulouse]] on a season-long contract.<ref name="toulouse"/> He left the club in January 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46892793|title=Cameroon's Stephane Mbia leaves French club Toulouse|date=16 January 2019|website=BBC Sport|access-date=27 August 2019}}</ref>

On 3 February 2019, Mbia returned to China to join top-flight newcomers [[Wuhan Yangtze River F.C.|Wuhan Zall]].<ref>[http://sports.sina.com.cn/china/j/2019-02-03/doc-ihqfskcp2772348.shtml 卓尔官方宣布姆比亚加盟 前华夏兽妖重返中超联赛] at sina.com 2 February 2019 Retrieved 2 February 2019 {{in lang|zh}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47115679|title=Cameroon's Stephane Mbia returns to play in China|date=4 February 2019|website=BBC Sport|access-date=27 August 2019|author=Mohamed Fajah Barrie}}</ref> A year later, he moved across the league to [[Shanghai Greenland Shenhua]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Cameroon's Stephane Mbia on the move in China |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51237355 |access-date=12 March 2020 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=24 January 2020}}</ref> He left after one season to re-join Wuhan Zall, now renamed Wuhan F.C., and reunited with his former Sevilla team-mate [[Daniel Carriço]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cameroonconcordnews.com/chinese-football-stephane-mbia-re-joins-wuhan-fc/|title = Chinese Football: Stephane M'bia re-joins Wuhan FC – Cameroon Concord News}}</ref>

On 31 August 2021, Mbia returned to Spain after six years, and joined [[CF Fuenlabrada|Fuenlabrada]] in the [[Segunda División]] on a one-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cffuenlabrada.es/noticia/el-cf-fuenlabrada-ficha-a-mbia|title=El CF Fuenlabrada ficha a Mbia|trans-title=CF Fuenlabrada sign Mbia|publisher=CF Fuenlabrada|language=es|date=31 August 2021|accessdate=31 August 2021|archive-date=21 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220521193426/https://www.cffuenlabrada.es/noticia/el-cf-fuenlabrada-ficha-a-mbia|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 21 January, he left the club after alleging "personal problems".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cffuenlabrada.es/noticia/comunicado-oficial-stephane-mbia|title=Comunicado oficial Stephane Mbia|trans-title=Official announcement Stephane Mbia|publisher=CF Fuenlabrada|language=es|date=21 January 2022|accessdate=30 January 2022}}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Gol fred.jpg|thumb|right|270px|[[Fred (footballer, born 1983)|Fred]] scoring a goal for [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] as Mbia (left) and goalkeeper [[Charles Itandje]] look on alongside their compatriots during a group stage match at the [[2014 FIFA World Cup]]]]
Mbia has played international football at junior level for Cameroon. He was part of the Cameroon squad that competed in the [[2003 FIFA U-17 World Championship]] in Finland, where his side were eliminated at the group stage.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080810132812/http://www.fifa.com/mensolympic/news/newsid=842364.html#mbia+the+place Mbia: The place to be]. Fifa.com. Retrieved on 3 December 2011.</ref>

He made his debut for the full [[Cameroon national football team|Cameroon national team]] in 2005. He was part of the squad which were runners up at the [[2008 Africa Cup of Nations]] in Ghana, where he scored twice in a 3–2 win against [[Tunisia national football team|Tunisia]] in the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2008/feb/04/minutebyminute.africannationscup2008 |title=Tunisia 2–3 Cameroon |work=The Guardian |date=4 February 2008 |access-date=1 May 2014 }}</ref>

Mbia was part of the Cameroon squad for the [[2008 Olympics]] in [[China]], playing in all four of his team's matches, and scoring once against [[Honduras national football team|Honduras]].<ref>{{FIFA player|id=200935|name=Stéphane Mbia }}</ref> Mbia was also selected to represent Cameroon at the [[2010 Africa Cup of Nations]] in Angola<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/africa/8427094.stm |title=Cameroon omit defender Sebastien Bassong from squad |publisher=BBC |date=23 December 2009 |access-date=1 May 2014 }}</ref> and the [[2010 FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] in South Africa.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/world_cup_2010/8675101.stm |title=World Cup 2010: Cameroon finalise World Cup squad |publisher=BBC Sport |date=11 May 2010 |access-date=1 May 2014 }}</ref>

On 2 June 2014, Mbia was included by Cameroon manager [[Volker Finke]] in the final 23-man squad for the [[2014 FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] in Brazil.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/news/y=2014/m=6/news=eto-o-song-headline-cameroon-s-final-23-2353337.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140602190841/http://www.fifa.com//worldcup/news/y=2014/m=6/news=eto-o-song-headline-cameroon-s-final-23-2353337.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2 June 2014 |title=Eto'o, Song headline Cameroon's final 23 |publisher=FIFA |date=2 June 2014 |access-date=6 June 2014 }}</ref> The team were eliminated after losing all of their group games amidst a bonuses dispute that led to Mbia replacing [[Samuel Eto'o]] as [[Captain (association football)|captain]] of the national team.<ref>{{cite news|title=Mbia replaces Eto'o as Cameroon captain|url=http://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/mbia-replaces-etoo-cameroon-captain#:JtdV7YVn8NBY5A|access-date=27 December 2015|publisher=FourFourTwo|date=26 August 2014}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Mbia is the older brother of footballer [[Franck Etoundi]], who was also a Cameroonian international.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lionindomptable.com/2014/04/24/franck-etoundi-vainqueur-de-la-coupe-de-suisse/ |title=Franck Etoundi, vainqueur de la coupe de Suisse |publisher=Lion Indomptable |date=24 April 2014 |access-date=1 May 2014 |language=fr |archive-date=2 May 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140502070925/http://www.lionindomptable.com/2014/04/24/franck-etoundi-vainqueur-de-la-coupe-de-suisse/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Career statistics==
