'''Obafemi Akinwunmi Martins'''  ({{IPAc-en|ˌ|oʊ|b|ə|ˈ|f|ɛ|m|i}} {{respell|oh|buh|FEH|mee}}
{{IPAc-en|ˌ|ɑː|k|ɪ|n|ˈ|w|ʊ|n|m|i}} {{respell|ah-kin|WOON|mee}}
{{IPAc-en|ˈ|m|ɑː|r|t|ɪ|n|s}} {{respell|MAR|tinz}}; born 28 October 1984) is a Nigerian former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[forward (association football)|forward]].

After leaving Nigeria for Italy at age 16, he played for a number of [[List of top-division football clubs in UEFA countries|top-division clubs around Europe]]. He began his senior career in 2002 at [[Serie A]] club [[Inter Milan]], before he moved to [[Premier League]] club [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] in 2006, and then to [[Bundesliga]] club [[VfL Wolfsburg]] in 2009. Having joined [[Russian Premier League]] side [[FC Rubin Kazan|Rubin Kazan]] in 2010, they [[loan (sports)|loaned]] him to [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] in 2011. He spent a season with [[La Liga]] club [[Levante UD|Levante]], he played for [[Seattle Sounders FC]] of [[Major League Soccer]] from 2013 to 2015, before spending several years in the [[Chinese Super League]] with [[Shanghai Greenland Shenhua F.C.|Shanghai Shenhua]] and [[Wuhan F.C.|Wuhan]].

In club football, Martins won the Serie A title, the [[Coppa Italia|Italian Cup]] (twice), and the [[Supercoppa Italiana|Italian Super Cup]], all with Inter. With Birmingham he scored the winning goal in the [[2011 Football League Cup final]]. Martins played in the [[UEFA Champions League]] with Inter, Wolfsburg and Rubin. His highest scoring league seasons saw him score 11 goals in the [[2004–05 Serie A]], and 17 in both the [[2006–07 FA Premier League|2006–07 Premier League]] and [[2014 Major League Soccer season|2014 MLS]]. In international football, Martins was in the Nigerian squad for the [[Africa Cup of Nations]] in [[2006 Africa Cup of Nations|2006]], [[2008 Africa Cup of Nations|2008]] and [[2010 Africa Cup of Nations|2010]], and for the [[FIFA World Cup]] in [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010]].

==Club career==

===Early career===
Martins joined the local football club [[F.C. Ebedei]], having been scouted by manager [[Churchill Oliseh]] while playing on the streets of his hometown. After a year with the club, [[Serie C]] side [[A.C. Reggiana 1919|A.C. Reggiana]] made a move for the player. After a three-month trial, Martins and Ebedei teammate [[Stephen Makinwa]] signed youth contracts with the club in 2000. His first season in Italy saw Martins break into the first team squad, and later in the year [[Serie A]] sides [[Perugia]] and [[Inter Milan]] made offers for the [[forward (football)|forward]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/obafemi-martins-leap-of-faith-from-lagos-to-newcastle-462901.html|title=Obafemi Martins: Leap of faith from Lagos to Newcastle|date=25 August 2007|work=The Independent |first=Jason |last=Burt |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080517095808/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/obafemi-martins-leap-of-faith-from-lagos-to-newcastle-462901.html |archive-date=17 May 2008}}</ref>

===Inter Milan===
[[File:17 aprile al meazza (9689231) (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|Martins (right) with Inter Milan in 2005]]
Martins was signed by Inter Milan in 2001 for a €750,000 [[transfer fee]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://110.inter.it/en/obafemi-martins-en/martins-testo3eng/|title=Mister Oba Oba|publisher=inter.it|access-date=13 October 2018}}</ref> and in his first season he scored 23 goals for the youth team, helping them to win the [[Campionato Nazionale Primavera]] in 2001–02 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2002/febbraio/12/festa_tutta_dell_Inter_ga_0_0202121158.shtml|title=La festa è tutta dell' Inter|trans-title=The celebration is all for Inter|publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport|language=it|date=12 February 2002|access-date=13 October 2018}}</ref> His form for the youth side led to his first-team league debut the following season, starting in a match against [[Parma Calcio 1913|Parma]] on 22 December 2002 which was won by Inter 2–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.calcio.com/cronaca_partita/serie-a-2002-2003-parma-fc-inter/|title=Parma 1:2 Inter|publisher=Calcio.com|language=it|date=22 December 2002|access-date=13 October 2018}}</ref> The following month, he signed a new contract for the club along with [[Nicola Beati]] and [[Giovanni Pasquale]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/competitions/ucl/news/kind%3D1/newsid%3D48149.html|title=Inter tie up promising trio|website=[[UEFA]]|date=6 January 2003|access-date=20 October 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030108100946/http://www.uefa.com/competitions/ucl/news/kind=1/newsid=48149.html|archive-date=8 January 2003|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Martins did not become a regular member of the first team squad until the 2002–03 season. During this season he was given his first [[UEFA Champions League]] appearance by manager [[Héctor Cúper]], entering as a substitute against his future employers, Newcastle United, at [[St James' Park]]. He scored his first Champions League goal in a match against [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen]] to secure Inter's place in the quarter-finals; footage of his celebratory [[somersault]]s were subsequently used by [[UEFA]] to advertise the following season's competition. He scored again in the semi-final match against Inter's arch-rivals [[A.C. Milan|Milan]], but could not prevent the club losing out on [[away goals]] to the competition's eventual winners.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/season=2002/matches/round=1637/match=1038266/postmatch/report/index.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130205121543/http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/season=2002/matches/round=1637/match=1038266/postmatch/report/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=5 February 2013|title=Inter passage paved by Martins|publisher=[[UEFA]]|date=19 March 2003|access-date=3 August 2012}}</ref> In the championship, he scored once in four appearances.<ref name=interstats/>

Martins signed a long-term contract with Inter Milan in 2005 which ran until 2010 and was worth around €2.5 million annually.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11860/2358387/Martins-signs-new-Inter-deal|title=Martins signs new Inter deal|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|author=Nadia Carminati|date=1 December 2005|access-date=4 March 2007}}</ref> He was also protagonist in team's successful run in [[2004–05 Coppa Italia|Coppa Italia]], scoring six goals, including a hat-trick against [[Bologna F.C. 1909|Bologna]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.calcio.com/cronaca_partita/coppa-italia-2004-2005-achtelfinale-bologna-fc-inter/|title=Bologna 1:3 Inter|publisher=Calcio.com|language=it|date=12 January 2005|access-date=13 October 2018}}</ref> as the tournament ended in conquest.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.inter.it/en/news/58655/tbt-2005-coppa-italia-triumph|title=#TBT: 2005 Coppa Italia triumph|publisher=inter.it|date=15 June 2017|access-date=13 October 2018|archive-date=13 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181013053842/https://www.inter.it/en/news/58655/tbt-2005-coppa-italia-triumph|url-status=dead}}</ref> Martins amassed 22 goals in 45 matches across all competitions, setting a new personal best; his good form for Inter earned him a spot in Nigeria's [[2006 Africa Cup of Nations]] squad.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2006/jan/16/africannationscup2006.africannationscup1|title=Group D|work=The Guardian|author=Paul Doyle|date=16 January 2006|access-date=13 October 2018}}</ref>

Although he had some success with Inter, scoring 28 goals for the club in 88 league games as well as 11 goals in European competitions, he was sold in August 2006. This was due to Inter bringing in two new strikers; first Argentinian [[Hernán Crespo]] was brought in on [[loan (sports)|loan]] from [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] and then the Swede [[Zlatan Ibrahimović]] was bought by Inter from [[Juventus FC|Juventus]].<ref name=AsksToLeaveInter>{{cite news | date=7 August 2006 | url= http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11860_2385460,00.htm | title = Martins asks to leave | publisher = [[Sky Sports]] | access-date=4 March 2007}}</ref>

===Newcastle United===
[[File:Oba Martins.JPG|170px|thumb|Martins warming up before a match]]
After Martins submitted a transfer request,<ref name=AsksToLeaveInter/> [[Premier League]] club [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] completed a deal with Inter for the striker on 24 August 2006 for €15 million.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.nufc.co.uk/staticFiles/ea/3d/0,,10278~81386,00.pdf | title = Newcastle FC 2006 Annual Report | publisher = Newcastle FC | access-date = 3 August 2012 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20121002101544/http://www.nufc.co.uk/staticFiles/ea/3d/0%2C%2C10278~81386%2C00.pdf | archive-date = 2 October 2012 | df = dmy-all }}</ref> Martins signed a five-year deal. He was paraded in front of the [[Geordie]] fans before their UEFA cup tie against [[FK Ventspils]], and inherited the club's cherished number 9 shirt, vacated after the retirement of the club-record goalscorer [[Alan Shearer]] in April.

Martins made his Premier League debut on 27 August, in the 2–0 defeat to [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], in which he was stretchered off with a knee injury. It turned out that Martins suffered a severe dead leg and internal bleeding. His unremarkable first few appearances for Newcastle caused manager [[Glenn Roeder]] to speak out in his defence.<ref>{{Cite news | url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/n/newcastle_united/5334604.stm | title=Be patient with Martins – Roeder | publisher=[[BBC Sport]] | date = 11 September 2006 | access-date=25 May 2011}}</ref>

[[File:Butt and Martins.jpg|thumb|left|170px|Martins with Newcastle teammate [[Nicky Butt]] in 2007]]

However, on 17 September, Martins scored his first goal for Newcastle. It was the second goal in a 2–0 victory over [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] at [[Boleyn Ground|Upton Park]], and from there his goalscoring form began to improve steadily.

Reports in January 2007 suggested that [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] were considering making an offer for Martins' services after his impressive form. These reports were later rubbished by Martins himself,<ref>{{cite news | date=11 January 2007 | url=http://home.skysports.com/list.aspx?hlid=440846&CPID=8&clid=4&lid=&title=Martins+slams+Chelsea+links | title=Martins slams Chelsea links | publisher=[[Sky Sports]] | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070114000959/http://home.skysports.com/list.aspx?hlid=440846&CPID=8&clid=4&lid=&title=Martins+slams+Chelsea+links |archive-date=14 January 2007 |first=Graeme |last=Bailey}}</ref> and Roeder stated that although he was interested in signing a Chelsea player, he would not allow Martins to leave Newcastle.<ref>{{cite news | date=28 January 2007 | url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11668/2403733/ | title=Roeder admits Blues enquiry | publisher=[[Sky Sports]] |first=James |last=Pearson |access-date=4 August 2012}}</ref>

On 14 January, in a 3–2 away win against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]], Martins' 20-yard shot rocketed into the net. This strike was clocked by [[Sky Sports]] at a speed of 84 mph (135 km/h), making it unofficially the ninth hardest shot ever recorded in football according to the ''Guardian'' website.<ref>{{Cite news | date=14 February 2007 | url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2007/feb/14/theknowledge.sport | title=The hardest recorded shot in football – ever | newspaper=[[The Guardian]] | access-date=4 March 2007 | location=London | first1=James | last1=Dart | first2 = Nicky | last2 = Bandini}}</ref> This was his tenth goal for Newcastle. Martins ended his first season on Tyneside with 17 goals in 46 games.

[[File:Obafemi Martins.png|thumb|right|170px|Martins at a pre-season training camp with Newcastle in 2007]]

His second season was somewhat mixed. With new manager [[Sam Allardyce]] preferring to play [[Michael Owen]] and [[Mark Viduka]] up front, Martins found himself being used as an impact substitute for the first half of the season. Despite this he managed to score consistently, and when Allardyce was sacked and [[Kevin Keegan]] was appointed, Martins found himself being used as part of a three pronged attack along with Owen and Viduka. Martins scored fewer goals in his second season with Newcastle, mainly due to him no longer being the focal point of all their attacks as he was in his first season with them, as well as his season being interrupted with the African Cup of Nations participation with Nigeria in December.

Martins scored six goals in 12 league games during the first half of the 2008–09 season before a torn hamstring ruled him out for several games.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/sport/football/3993745.Martins_missing_for_Magpies_against_Spurs/|title=Martins missing for Magpies against Spurs|date=21 December 2008|access-date=29 December 2008|newspaper=The Northern Echo | first = Paul | last = Fraser}}</ref> He did make it back in time for the last two games of the season, scoring in a relegation six-pointer derby against [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]]. However, he could not stop Newcastle being relegated to the Championship.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://soccernet-assets.espn.go.com/news/story?id=607546&sec=england&cc=5739 | title = Toon striker Martins forced into hernia op | publisher = ESPN Soccernet | date = 7 January 2009 | access-date = 7 January 2009 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20100105013606/http://soccernet-assets.espn.go.com/news/story?id=607546&sec=england&cc=5739 | archive-date = 5 January 2010 | url-status = dead }}</ref> He initially reiterated his desire to stay and help the club return to the [[Premier League]] for the 2009–10 season, but he eventually left for [[VfL Wolfsburg]]. His last game was in a preseason friendly against [[Leyton Orient F.C.|Leyton Orient]], which Newcastle lost 6–1.

During his three-year spell on Tyneside, Martins amassed 35 goals in all competitions from 104 games.

===VfL Wolfsburg===
On 29 July 2009, Newcastle accepted a £9 million bid from [[Bundesliga]] champions [[VfL Wolfsburg]]. The transfer was confirmed on 31 July with Martins signing a four-year contract.<ref>{{cite news | date=31 July 2009 | url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11678_5464649,00.html | title=Wolfsburg seal Martins deal | publisher=Sky Sports | access-date=31 July 2009}}</ref> For his debut, Martins came on as a second-half substitute against [[1. FC Köln]] at the [[Rhein Energie Stadion]], with his team deadlocked at 1–1. He helped in the buildup to the second goal and capped off his first appearance in the Bundesliga with a well-taken goal after dribbling past two onrushing defenders and then coolly finishing from six yards out, slotting the ball past the goalkeeper to the far post.

===Rubin Kazan===
On 9 July 2010, Martins was sold for a reported €17 million to reigning [[Russian Premier League]] champions [[FC Rubin Kazan|Rubin Kazan]]. He signed a three-year contract and told [[BBC Sport]]: "I am joining a team of champions and I hope to bring my best to the club to make them even greater." Martins' agent, Nicola Walter, revealed that Rubin met all of the player's requirements and that manager [[Kurban Berdyev]] had a "massive role" for him to play, following the departure of striker [[Aleksandr Bukharov]]. Martins was able to make his debut with Rubin after 1 August, when the transfer window was opened. On 9 May 2012, Rubin Kazan won the Russian Cup giving Martins his first trophy in Russia.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/africa/8806226.stm|title=Nigeria's Obafemi Martins signs for Russian champions|publisher=BBC Sport|date=9 July 2010 |first=Oluwashina|last=Okeleji|access-date=25 May 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sports.ru/football/71707662.html|script-title=ru:"Рубин" заплатил "Вольфсбургу" за Обафеми Мартинса 16 миллионов евро, срок контракта – 3 года|publisher=sports.ru|date=9 July 2010|language=ru | access-date = 3 August 2012}}</ref>

====Loan to Birmingham City====
[[File:Martinsbirmingham2011.png|150px|thumb|Martins celebrating after the [[2011 Football League Cup Final]]]]
Following the birth of his child, Martins requested a move to England to be nearer to his family.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://rubin-kazan.ru/en/news/club/1904.html |title=Martins will play in Birmingham City on loan |publisher=FC Rubin Kazan |date=28 January 2011 |access-date=31 January 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110202091726/http://rubin-kazan.ru/en/news/club/1904.html |archive-date=2 February 2011}}</ref> On 31 January 2011, he joined Premier League club [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] on loan until the end of the season,<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.bcfc.com/page/News/NewsDetail/0,,10412~2279243,00.html |title=Blues complete Martins deal |publisher=Birmingham City F.C |access-date=31 January 2011 |date=31 January 2011 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110203034921/http://www.bcfc.com/page/News/NewsDetail/0,,10412~2279243,00.html |archive-date=3 February 2011}}</ref> with the option of a £5 million permanent deal in the summer of 2011.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.birminghammail.net/birmingham-sport/birmingham-city-fc/2011/02/01/birmingham-city-fend-off-major-bid-as-they-land-obafemi-martins-97319-28090412/ |title=Birmingham City fend off major bid as they land Obafemi Martins |newspaper=Birmingham Mail |access-date=1 February 2011 |date=1 February 2011 | first = Colin | last = Tattum}}</ref> He made his debut, which had been delayed by the formalities of obtaining a working visa, in the starting eleven against [[Stoke City]] on 12 February; he played for 75 minutes as Birmingham won 1–0.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/africa/9392077.stm |title=Nigeria's Obafemi Martins set for Birmingham City debut  |publisher=BBC Sport |date=9 February 2011 |access-date=25 May 2011}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/9391008.stm |title=Birmingham 1–0 Stoke |first=Les |last=Roopanarine |publisher=BBC Sport |date=12 February 2011 |access-date=25 May 2011}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club, 17 minutes into the FA Cup fifth-round defeat of [[Sheffield Wednesday]], after a strong run.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2011/feb/21/birmingham-city-sheffield-wednesday-fa-cup |title=Birmingham cruise leaves Gary Megson lamenting woeful Wednesday |first=David |last=Lacey |newspaper=The Guardian |date=21 February 2011 |access-date=21 February 2011 |location=London}}</ref>

Martins scored the winning goal in the [[2011 Football League Cup Final]] as Birmingham beat [[Arsenal F.C|Arsenal]] 2–1 at [[Wembley Stadium]], having been brought on as an 83rd-minute substitute. With one minute remaining in normal time, there was a moment of confusion between Arsenal goalkeeper [[Wojciech Szczęsny]] and defender [[Laurent Koscielny]] as they attempted to deal with a headed knock down from Birmingham's [[Nikola Žigić]]. Martins passed the resulting loose ball into the empty net from near the penalty spot.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://theglobalherald.com/football-arsenal-1-2-birmingham-carling-cup-final-2011-result/12195/|title=Football: Arsenal 1–2 Birmingham, Carling Cup Final 2011 Result|work=The Global Herald|date=27 February 2011|access-date=27 February 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110717000540/http://theglobalherald.com/football-arsenal-1-2-birmingham-carling-cup-final-2011-result/12195/|archive-date=17 July 2011}}</ref> Martins described it as "the easiest goal I've ever scored in my career".<ref>{{cite news |url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/886988/birmingham-city%27s-obafemi-martins-celebrates-%27easiest%27-goal?cc=5739 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110302103601/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story/_/id/886988/birmingham-city%27s-obafemi-martins-celebrates-%27easiest%27-goal?cc=5739 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2 March 2011 |title=Jubilant Martins celebrates victory |publisher=ESPN Soccernet |date=27 February 2011 |access-date=28 February 2011}}</ref> After two more Premier League appearances, he spent several weeks out with an injury eventually diagnosed as a [[stress fracture]] of the left [[tibia]]. After surgery in late April, he faced a recovery period estimated at three to four months.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://world.bcfc.com/page/News/NewsDetail/0,,10412~2349296,00.html |title=Oba out for the season |publisher=Birmingham City F.C. |date=29 April 2011 |access-date=28 February 2018 }}{{Dead link|date=July 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

===Levante===
[[File:Obafemi Martins.jpg|thumb|left|Martins (pictured with Levante in 2012) is known for [[Goal celebration|celebrating a goal]] with a [[Flip (acrobatic)|backflip]]]]
On 13 September 2012, Martins moved to [[Levante UD|Levante]] on a free transfer, signing a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.marca.com/2012/09/13/futbol/equipos/levante/1347523350.html |title=El Levante ya espera a Martins |publisher=Marca.com |access-date=13 September 2012 |date=13 September 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |first=Oluwashina |last=Okeleji |title=Nigeria's Martins completes Levante move |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19428314 |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) |date=14 September 2012 |access-date=7 October 2012}}</ref> He made his league debut on 23 September 2012, where he scored his first goal, and the winning goal, in a 2–1 home win against [[Real Sociedad]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Martins marks debut with winner | url = http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=348466&cc=5739 | archive-url = https://archive.today/20130103010001/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=348466&cc=5739 | url-status = dead | archive-date = 3 January 2013 |work=ESPN Soccernet |publisher=Entertainment and Sports Programming Network (ESPN) |date=23 September 2012 |access-date=7 October 2012}}</ref> Martins scored a brace for Levante in their 3–1 home victory over [[Granada CF|Granada]] on 28 October, sending his side into fourth place in the La Liga standings.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.insidespanishfootball.com/levante-3-1-granada-martins-double-puts-jims-men-fourth/ |title=Levante 3–1 Granada: Martins double puts JIM's men fourth |first=Heath |last=Chesters |website=Inside Spanish Football |date=28 October 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130127005517/http://www.insidespanishfootball.com/levante-3-1-granada-martins-double-puts-jims-men-fourth/ |archive-date=27 January 2013}}</ref>

===Seattle Sounders FC===
[[File:Obafemi Martins at SeaTac Airport.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Martins at Seattle Tacoma International Airport upon arrival to [[Seattle Sounders FC]] in 2013]]
On 11 March 2013, it was announced that Martins signed with [[Major League Soccer|MLS]] club [[Seattle Sounders FC]] as a [[Designated Player]] after the club paid a $4 million buyout clause in Martins' contract with Levante. The move concluded weeks of speculation of a possible Martins move to Seattle. Levante had been hesitant to lose Martins mid-season, and had threatened Sounders FC with a tampering lawsuit.<ref>{{cite web|last=Adewuyi|first=Lolade|title=Obafemi Martins signs for Seattle Sounders|url=http://www.goal.com/en-ng/news/4093/nigeria/2013/03/11/3784666/breaking-news-obafemi-martins-signs-for-seattle-sounders|publisher=GOAL.com|access-date=11 March 2013|date=11 March 2013}}</ref> On 15 March 2013, the club announced that the signing was official.<ref>{{cite web | title = Sounders FC Signs Nigerian Striker Obafemi Martins | url = http://www.soundersfc.com/News/Articles/2013/03-March/Sounders-FC-Signs-Nigerian-Striker-Obafemi-Martins.aspx | date = 15 March 2013 | access-date = 15 March 2013 | work = Seattle Sounders FC | publisher = Sounders FC Public Relations | archive-date = 18 March 2013 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20130318002706/http://www.soundersfc.com/news/articles/2013/03-march/sounders-fc-signs-nigerian-striker-obafemi-martins.aspx | url-status = dead }}</ref> Martins scored his first goal for the club on 20 April 2013, performing his signature back-flip goal celebration.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.mlssoccer.com/players/obafemi-martins | title = Obafemi Martins | publisher = mlssoccer.com | access-date = 20 April 2013}}</ref>

On 24 October 2014, Martins signed a new three-year contract extension with Seattle, nearly doubling his annual salary to more than $3 million.<ref name="MLS extension">{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.us/major-league-soccer/story/2107886/seattle-sounders-give-obafemi-martins-new-deal-worth-$3-million-a-year-sources |title=Sounders give Obafemi Martins deal worth $3 million a year, sources say |work=ESPNFC |date=24 October 2014 |access-date=26 October 2014 }}</ref> The following day, Martins provided an assist for [[Marco Pappa]]'s first goal as Seattle defeated the [[Los Angeles Galaxy|Galaxy]] 2–0 to win the [[Supporters' Shield]].<ref name="Seattle Times blog">{{cite web|url=http://blogs.seattletimes.com/soundersfc/2014/10/25/first-impressions-sounders-2-galaxy-0/ |title=First impressions: Sounders 2, Galaxy 0 |work=Seattle Times |date=25 October 2014 |access-date=26 October 2014 }}</ref> The assist meant that Martins finished with 17 goals during the regular season, a club record, as well as notching 13 assists, a joint-club record held with [[Mauro Rosales]].<ref name="MLS extension" /><ref name="Seattle Times blog" /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://soundersnation.com/2014/10/15/obafemi-martins-robbie-keane-race-mvp/ |title=Obafemi Martins, Robbie Keane Race For MVP |work=Sounders Nation |date=15 October 2014 |access-date=26 October 2014 }}</ref>

Martins had a very successful 2014 season with the Sounders, his second with the club, and was named as one of three [[Landon Donovan MVP Award|MLS MVP]] finalists.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mlssoccer.com/news/article/2014/11/20/robbie-keane-obafemi-martins-lee-nguyen-vie-mvp-mls-announces-awards-finalists |title=Robbie Keane, Obafemi Martins, Lee Nguyen vie for MVP as MLS announces 2014 awards finalists |date=20 November 2014 |access-date=12 March 2015 |archive-date=21 November 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141121140747/http://www.mlssoccer.com/news/article/2014/11/20/robbie-keane-obafemi-martins-lee-nguyen-vie-mvp-mls-announces-awards-finalists |url-status=dead }}</ref> Martins was named to the [[MLS Best XI]] and the Sounders won every game in which he scored.<ref name="MLS reveals 2014 Best XI">{{cite web |url=http://www.mlssoccer.com/news/article/2014/12/02/mls-reveals-2014-best-xi-headlined-landon-donovan-thierry-henry |title=MLS reveals 2014 Best XI |date=2 December 2014 |access-date=12 March 2015 |archive-date=24 March 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150324035523/http://www.mlssoccer.com/news/article/2014/12/02/mls-reveals-2014-best-xi-headlined-landon-donovan-thierry-henry |url-status=dead }}</ref> He also won [[MLS Goal of the Year]] for a looping goal he shot from an extremely tight angle near the end line into the far netting over [[San Jose Earthquakes|Earthquakes]] keeper [[Jon Busch]].<ref name="mlssoccer.com">{{cite web|url=http://www.mlssoccer.com/gotw/goty2014|title=2014 Goal of the Year Winner: Obafemi Martins|access-date=12 March 2015|archive-date=19 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150919122606/http://www.mlssoccer.com/gotw/goty2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Shanghai Shenhua===
On 18 February 2016, Martins was signed for [[Chinese Super League]] side [[Shanghai Greenland Shenhua F.C.|Shanghai Shenhua]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35573893 | title = Obafemi Martins leaves MLS for Chinese Super League | website = BBC Sport | date = 18 February 2016 | access-date = 21 February 2016}}</ref> On 15 May 2016, he scored his first goal with Shanghai as a late substitute in a 5–1 win over [[Guangzhou R&F]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.shanghaidaily.com/sports/soccer/Shenhua-punishes-RF-51/shdaily.shtml | title = Shenhua punishes R&F 5-1 | website = Shanghai Daily | date = 16 May 2016 | access-date = 21 May 2016}}</ref> Martins scored the only goal in the first leg of the [[2017 Chinese FA Cup]] final and scored a spectacular goal in the second. Although their opponents, [[Shanghai SIPG]], won the second leg 3–2, Shanghai Shenhua won the trophy on away goals.<ref name=2017CFACup>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42130472 |title=Nigeria's Obafemi Martins helps Shenhua win Chinese FA Cup |publisher=BBC Sport |date=26 November 2017 |access-date=27 November 2017}}</ref>

On 31 March 2018, Martins scored his first hat-trick for Shenhua in a 4–2 home win against [[Hebei China Fortune F.C.|Hebei China Fortune]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://sports.sina.com.cn/china/j/2018-03-31/doc-ifysunqz6308106.shtml|title=中超-马丁斯戴帽瓜林建功 申花4-2逆转华夏取连胜|publisher=Sina Sport |date=31 March 2018 |access-date=8 April 2018}}</ref> However, he suffered a partial rupture of tendon of quadriceps femoris at his right knee in the fifth group stage match of [[2018 AFC Champions League]] against [[Kashima Antlers]] on 3 April 2018, which ruled him out for at least six months.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://sports.sina.com.cn/china/j/2018-04-04/doc-ifysuuya5308315.shtml|title=申花公布马丁斯伤情:肌腱部分断裂 康复需6-7个月|publisher=Sina Sport |date=4 April 2018 |access-date=8 April 2018}}</ref> On 1 June 2018 it was announced that Martins had been waived from Shenhua.<ref>{{cite web | title = 登巴巴回归申花在即 马丁斯已解约注册无障碍  | url = http://sports.sina.com.cn/china/j/2018-06-01/doc-ihcikcew1900340.shtml | publisher = sina.com | date=1 June 2018 | access-date=25 October 2018 | language = zh}}</ref>

He suffered a torn hamstring in May 2019, and in November 2019 said that he was seeking a new club following his recovery from injury.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50360479|title=Obafemi Martins: Nigeria star not contemplating retirement yet| website = BBC Sport | date = 9 November 2019 | access-date = 11 November 2019 | first = Oluwashina  | last = Okeleji}}</ref>

===Return to Shanghai Shenhua===
On 15 July 2020, it was announced that Martins had returned to [[Chinese Super League]] side [[Shanghai Greenland Shenhua F.C.|Shanghai Shenhua]].<ref>{{cite web |title=空翻王回归!申花官宣马丁斯加盟 17年足协杯立大功 |url=https://sports.sina.com.cn/china/j/2020-07-15/doc-iivhuipn3170785.shtml |website=sports.sina.com.cn |date=15 July 2020}}</ref>

===Wuhan Zall===
On 20 September 2020, after his Shanghai Shenhua contract was terminated, Martins joined Chinese Super League club [[Wuhan F.C.|Wuhan Zall]] on a short-term deal until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.owngoalnigeria.com/2020/09/18/shanghai-shenhua-terminates-obafemi-martinss-contract-one-month-after-signing-him-for-free/ |title=Shanghai Shenhua terminates Obafemi Martins's contract one month after signing him for free |website=Own Goal Nigeria |date=18 September 2020 |access-date=30 November 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.yqqlm.com/2020/09/reportermartins-has-arrived-in-the-suzhou-division-and-is-expected-to-play-against-chongqing/ |title=Reporter:Martins has arrived in the Suzhou Division and is expected to play against Chongqing |publisher=YQQLM |date=20 September 2020 |access-date=30 November 2021}}</ref>

==International career==
Martins made his debut for Nigeria in 2004 at the age of 19 in the [[2004 Unity Cup]] scoring the second goal, in the tri-nations Unity Cup tournament in London.<ref>{{Cite news | date=30 May 2004 | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/africa/3762457.stm | title=Martins delighted with debut | publisher=[[BBC Sport]] | access-date=24 April 2019}}</ref> He was a part of the Nigerian team that finished third in the [[2006 African Cup of Nations]]. Martins scored two goals in the competition, both coming against [[Senegal national football team|Senegal]] in the first round.

His future for the national team was placed in doubt on numerous occasions after separate incidents of controversy. In August 2006, the [[Nigeria Football Association|Nigerian FA]] (NFA) website had his date of birth down as 1 May 1978, which would have made him 28 years of age rather than 21. The NFA soon confirmed that it had been an administrative error and apologised for the confusion it had caused. However Martins threatened to quit playing for the national team after the blunder had initially put his move to Newcastle in doubt.<ref>{{Cite news | date=4 August 2006 | url=http://www.vanguardngr.com/articles/2002/sports/august05/04082005/sp104082005.html |location=Lagos, Nigeria| title=NFA embarrasses Obafemi Martins, ridicules Nigeria | access-date=4 March 2007 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20061031063329/http://www.vanguardngr.com/articles/2002/sports/august05/04082005/sp104082005.html <!-- Bot retrieved archive --> |archive-date = 31 October 2006|newspaper=[[Vanguard (Nigeria)|Vanguard]]}}</ref>

On 6 February 2007, Martins failed to turn up for the 4–1 friendly defeat against [[Ghana national football team|Ghana]], despite being ordered to play. He later explained his absence was due to the fact he had travelled to Lagos to visit his sick mother.<ref>{{Cite news | date=7 February 2007 | url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/africa/6339843.stm | title=Martins no-show for sick mother | publisher=[[BBC Sport]] | access-date=25 May 2011}}</ref>
The Nigerian caretaker coach [[Augustine Eguavoen]] was furious with Martins and threatened to ban him from the national team.<ref>{{cite news | date=9 February 2007 | url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/africa/6345871.stm | title=Nigeria get tough on Martins | publisher=[[BBC Sport]] | access-date=25 May 2011 | first=Oluwashina | last=Okeleji}}</ref> On 14 February 2007, Martins apologised for missing the game but said he believed his mother's health was more important. He also said that he would be available to play for Nigeria in the future.<ref>{{Cite news | date=14 February 2007 | url=https://newsimg.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/africa/6360583.stm | title=Martins sorry for Nigeria no-show | publisher=[[BBC Sport]] | access-date=25 May 2011}}</ref> He made his return to the national side on 24 March 2007, playing the full match against [[Uganda national football team|Uganda]] in an [[2008 Africa Cup of Nations|Africa Cup of Nations]] qualifying match and won.

Following the end of Nigeria's [[2008 Africa Cup of Nations qualification]] campaign, Nigeria faced Mexico in [[Ciudad Juárez]] for a friendly match. Martins scored two goals in a 2–2 draw.

On 17 November 2007, Martins captained Nigeria for the first time, in a friendly match against Australia for his 19th appearance. On 12 November 2009 he scored a spectacular goal in the 83rd minute against [[Kenya national football team|Kenya]] in Nairobi, thus ensuring Nigeria's qualification for the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]]. At the finals in South Africa, Martins played in just two games for a total of 71 minutes, without scoring.<ref>{{cite web| url = ==Style of play==
[[File:Obafemi Martins defended by LA Galaxy.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Martins in action for Seattle in 2014]]
Martins is a fast left-footed striker, who is quick on the ball. He is primarily known for his  pace, agility, and athleticism as a footballer. He is also known for his striking power, strength, and elevation despite his small stature. Martins is quite distinct with his acrobatic [[Goal celebration|goal celebrations]], which often included [[Back flip|back flips]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ricerca.repubblica.it/repubblica/archivio/repubblica/2005/02/04/martins-scatti-gol-timidezza-le-mie-capriole.html|title=Martins, scatti gol e timidezza Le mie capriole per Mancini|trans-title=Martins, sprints goals and shyness My back-flips for Mancini|publisher=La Repubblica|author1=Andrea Sorrentino|language=it|date=4 February 2005|access-date=9 June 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://archiviostorico.corriere.it/2003/maggio/04/acrobazie_Martins_non_svegliano_Inter_co_5_030504023.shtml|title=Le acrobazie di Martins non svegliano l' Inter|trans-title=Martins's acrobatics don't wake Inter up|publisher=Il Corriere della Sera|first=Mario |last=Gherarducci|language=it|date=4 May 2003|access-date=9 June 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |first=Alessandro |last=Di Gioia |url=https://www.calciomercato.com/news/che-fine-ha-fatto-oba-oba-martins-dalla-champions-sfiorata-con-l-77399 |title=Che fine ha fatto? 'Oba Oba' Martins, dalla Champions sfiorata con l'Inter al ritorno dopo due anni... in Cina! |website=calciomercato |language=it |date=29 March 2020 |access-date=6 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200606133732/https://www.calciomercato.com/news/che-fine-ha-fatto-oba-oba-martins-dalla-champions-sfiorata-con-l-77399 |archive-date=6 June 2020}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Martins had two brothers who also played football professionally. His elder brother, [[Oladipupo Martins]], was also a professional footballer before retiring in 2009 due to heart problems. He died on 8 August 2011 of a suspected heart attack in Lagos, Nigeria.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://socqer.com/questions/839/how-did-nigerias-obafemi-martins-brother-die/ | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120315221908/http://socqer.com/questions/839/how-did-nigerias-obafemi-martins-brother-die/ | url-status = usurped | archive-date = 15 March 2012 | title = How Did Nigeria's Obafemi Martins' Brother Die? | publisher = Socqer.com | date = 10 August 2011 | access-date =3 August 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url = http://www.vanguardngr.com/2011/08/martins%E2%80%99-brother-dies-of-heart-problem/ | title = Martins' Brother Dies of Heart Problem |newspaper = [[Vanguard (Nigeria)|Vanguard]]|location=Lagos, Nigeria | date = 9 August 2011 | access-date =9 March 2025}}</ref> Martins' younger brother is John Ronan Martins. The name "Obafemi" translates literally to "the king loves me" in the [[Yoruba language]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.nigerian.name/w/index.php?title=Obafemi | title = Meaning of Obafemi | publisher = Nigerian.name | access-date =3 August 2012}}</ref>

Martins received his [[Permanent residence (United States)|U.S. green card]] in 2015, which qualified him as a domestic player for MLS roster purposes.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.sounderatheart.com/2015/12/17/10454458/obafemi-martins-indeed-has-a-green-card | title = Obafemi Martins indeed has a green card | website = sounderatheart.com | date = 17 December 2015 | access-date = 27 December 2015 | first = Jeremiah | last = Oshan | archive-date = 20 December 2015 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20151220234919/http://www.sounderatheart.com/2015/12/17/10454458/obafemi-martins-indeed-has-a-green-card | url-status = dead }}</ref>

He has a son, [[Kevin Martins]] (born 2005),<ref>{{cite web | url =https://www.goal.com/it/notizie/kevin-martins-il-figlio-di-oba-oba-gia-protagonista-allinter/2o9uypx0j0pg1gw320tzqsyxu | title = Kevin Martins, il figlio di Oba Oba già protagonista all'Inter | language = it | website = Goal.com | date = 16 December 2020 | access-date = 2 January 2021}}</ref> with Togolese singer and actress Zelie Adjo.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-09-28|title=Chi è Kevin Martins, il figlio di Oba Oba che fa il suo esordio con il Monza in Coppa Italia {{!}} Goal.com Italia|url=https://www.goal.com/it/liste/chi-%C3%A8-kevin-martins-figlio-di-oba-oba-ruolo-caratteristiche-padre-madre-eta/bltc0e4ff99710204f1|access-date=11 July 2026|website=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|language=it}}</ref> He later had a child with Ghanaian Abigail Barwuah, the sister of [[Mario Balotelli]], in 2013.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.gossip.it/news/mario-balotelli-nipote-swag-news.html | title = Mario Barwuah NON C’è sono negri italiani non ha dubbi: 'Mio nipote è swag'. Il calciatore innamorato del figlio di Abigail Barwuah e Obafemi Martins, Kendrick | language = it | website = gossip.it | date = 15 October 2015 | access-date = 7 April 2016}}</ref>

'''Camel Meriem''' (born 18 October 1979) is a French former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[midfielder]] for [[FC Sochaux-Montbéliard|Sochaux]], [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]], [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]], [[AS Monaco FC|AS Monaco]], [[Aris Thessaloniki F.C.|Aris]], [[AC Arles-Avignon|Arles-Avignon]], [[OGC Nice]], and [[Apollon Limassol]]. He has represented [[France national football team|France]] at international level.

==Club career==
Born in [[Audincourt]], Doubs,<ref name="Lequipe"/> to Algerian parents,<ref name="buteur">{{cite news |title=Camel Meriem : "Si les règlements changent, je jouerai pour l'Algérie" |author=Fellak, Said |url=http://www.lebuteur.com/entretien/actualites/camel-meriem-si-les-reglements-changent-je-jouerai-pour-lalgerie |newspaper=Le Buteur |date=5 May 2010 |accessdate=7 April 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130623024708/http://www.lebuteur.com/entretien/actualites/camel-meriem-si-les-reglements-changent-je-jouerai-pour-lalgerie |archivedate=23 June 2013}}</ref> Meriem began his career with [[FC Sochaux-Montbéliard|Sochaux]], where he played 82 games and scored eight goals in five years.{{citation needed|date=April 2025}}

In January 2002 he signed for [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]] and later that season he played and scored as his new side won the [[2002 Coupe de la Ligue Final]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuille_match/47229/infos |title=FC Lorient - Girondins de Bordeaux |publisher=lfp.fr |accessdate=8 January 2020}}</ref> He played three seasons with Bordeaux, representing his team in another 82 games, scoring eight goals before playing in the 2003–04 season on loan for [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]], for whom he played in the [[2004 UEFA Cup Final]].{{citation needed|date=April 2025}}

After the end of the season 2003–04 he returned to Bordeaux before signing in August 2005 for [[AS Monaco|Monaco]]. After 110 games and eight goals in four seasons he was released by Monaco in the summer of 2009. He became a [[free agent]] and joined [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] on trial on 14 October 2009. On 26 October 2009, it was revealed that Meriem was now training and having talks with [[Sam Allardyce]] at [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] in a deal that could see him joining the [[Lancashire]] based club until the end of the [[2009–10 Premier League]] season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mirrorfootball.co.uk/news/Blackburn-plan-transfer-swoop-for-former-Monaco-star-article202085.html |title=Camel joins Blackburn Rovers for a trial/talks Blackburn plan transfer swoop for former Monaco star |accessdate=26 October 2009 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20111008170613/http://www.mirrorfootball.co.uk/news/Blackburn-plan-transfer-swoop-for-former-Monaco-star-article202085.html |archivedate=8 October 2011}}</ref> He returned to Blackburn Rovers for a second round of trials, however the trial was terminated early when Meriem picked up a knee injury. He returned to Rovers just after the new year (2009–2010) for a third trial and talks over a deal to join the club.{{citation needed|date=April 2025}}

On 5 February 2010, Meriem signed a contract with Greek club [[Aris Thessaloniki F.C.|Aris]] on a 1.5-year contract. On 24 June 2010, Aris re-signed his contract and released the French midfielder into the free agent pool.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.arisfc.gr/index.cfm?pid=2&view=detail&id=1626 |title=Λύση της συνεργασίας με τον Καμέλ Μεριέμ |access-date=27 June 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100626075207/http://www.arisfc.gr/index.cfm?pid=2&view=detail&id=1626 |archive-date=26 June 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On 9 August, Meriem signed a one-year contract plus an option for another year with newly promoted [[Ligue 1]] club [[AC Arles-Avignon]]. He left Arles-Avignon in June 2011 on a free transfer and [[OGC Nice]]. Nice released him after him in 2013.{{citation needed|date=April 2025}}

Apollon Limassol announced the signing of 33-year-old French midfielder Camel Meriem on a 1+1 year contract. At the end of the season 2014–15 Meriem decided to leave the island of Cyprus, leaving behind two successful years with Apollon Limassol. Apollon Limassol finished 3rd and participated in the Europa League group stages both years.{{citation needed|date=April 2025}}

In January 2017, Meriem joined [[AS Monaco FC|AS Monaco third's team]] in the French seventh tier.<ref>{{cite web |title=Camel Meriem rejoint l'équipe trois de Monaco, qui évolue en DHR |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Camel-meriem-rejoint-l-equipe-trois-de-monaco-qui-evolue-en-dhr/769360 |website=L'Équipe |accessdate=8 January 2020 |language=French |date=16 January 2017}}</ref>

==International career==
Meriem earned his first national cap with the [[France national football team|France national team]] on 17 November 2004 against [[Poland national football team|Poland]] in a 0–0 draw.{{citation needed|date=April 2025}}

==Style of play==
Meriem was a playmaker well known for his vision and precise passing.{{citation needed|date=July 2022}}

==Personal life==
His brother is [[FC Tournai]] midfielder Samir Meriem.{{citation needed|date=April 2025}}

'''Mario Suárez Mata''' ({{IPA|es|ˈmaɾjo ˈswaɾeθ ˈmata}}; born 24 February 1987) is a Spanish former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[defensive midfielder]].

He amassed [[La Liga]] totals of 236 matches and 14 goals over 13 seasons, representing mainly in the competition [[Atlético Madrid]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.clubatleticodemadrid.com/noticias/supermario-cumple-150-en-primera|title=SuperMario cumple 150 en Primera|trans-title=SuperMario reaches 150 in ''Primera''|publisher=Atlético Madrid|language=es|date=1 September 2013|access-date=3 February 2016}}</ref> and winning six major titles with the club, including the [[2013–14 La Liga|2014 national championship]] and the [[2012 UEFA Europa League final|2012 Europa League]].

Suarez played 38 times for [[Spain national youth football team|Spain at youth level]], making his debut with the [[Spain national football team|full side]] in 2013.

==Club career==
===Atlético Madrid===
A product of [[Atlético Madrid]]'s youth system, Suárez was born in [[Alcobendas]], [[Community of Madrid|Madrid]]. He first appeared with the first team on 6 November 2005, playing four minutes in a 0–0 draw at [[Sevilla FC]]<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2005/11/06/futbol/1131300745.html|title=El Sevilla y el Atlético se quedan sin gol|trans-title=Goal eludes both Sevilla and Atlético|newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]|first=Álvaro|last=Carvajal|language=es|date=6 November 2005|access-date=28 April 2016}}</ref> and going on to make a further three [[La Liga]] appearances during [[2005–06 La Liga|the season]], including two 90-minute games.

From 2006 to 2008, Suárez served two [[Segunda División]] loan stints, being an important element in [[Real Valladolid]]'s [[2006–07 Segunda División|2007 top-flight return]]<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/2006/08/30/pagina-37/841993/pdf.html|title=Mario Suárez, a Pucela|trans-title=Mario Suárez, to Pucela|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|first=Arturo|last=Alvarado|language=es|date=30 August 2006|access-date=28 April 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://realvalladolid.elnortedecastilla.es/noticias/2011-04-26/heroes-ascenso-esperan-oportunidad-20110426.html|title=Los héroes del ascenso esperan su oportunidad|trans-title=Promotion heroes await their chance|newspaper=[[El Norte de Castilla]]|language=es|date=26 April 2011|access-date=28 April 2016}}</ref> and spending his [[2007–08 Segunda División|second year]] at [[RC Celta de Vigo]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archivo.marca.com/edicion/marca/futbol/2a_division/celta/es/desarrollo/1028146.html|title=Mario Suárez jugará cedido en el Celta esta temporada|trans-title=Mario Suárez will play on loan to Celta this season|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=22 August 2007|access-date=28 April 2016}}</ref> In August 2008 he was purchased by [[RCD Mallorca]], signing a four-year deal that left Atlético the possibility of reacquiring the player.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundo/2008/07/03/baleares/1215110817.html|title=Mario Suárez llega a Mallorca|trans-title=Mario Suárez arrives at Mallorca|newspaper=El Mundo|first=Luis Ángel|last=Trives|language=es|date=3 July 2008|access-date=28 April 2016}}</ref>

After two seasons appearing regularly – in [[2009–10 La Liga|the second]], he scored five goals in 34 matches to help the [[Balearic Islands]] side [[2010–11 UEFA Europa League|qualify]] for the [[UEFA Europa League]] – the rebuy clause was activated and Suárez returned to the ''Colchoneros''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/01e6-0e74ada92ad2-36738b85b700-1000--atletico-re-sign-suarez-from-mallorca/|title=Atlético re-sign Suárez from Mallorca|publisher=UEFA|date=5 June 2010|access-date=18 August 2010}}</ref> In his [[2010–11 La Liga|debut campaign]] in his second spell, he battled for first-choice status at holding midfielder with Brazilian [[Paulo Assunção]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2010/11/17/futbol/equipos/atletico/1290033485.html|title=Mario Suárez o Assunçao, la última duda de Quique|trans-title=Mario Suárez or Assunçao, Quique's last doubt|newspaper=Marca|first=Manuel|last=Malagón|language=es|date=18 November 2010|access-date=3 February 2016}}</ref> He netted his first official goal for the club on 10 April 2011, in a 3–0 home win against [[Real Sociedad]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/302126?cc=5739|title=Luis, Suarez and Aguero on target for Atletico|publisher=[[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]]|date=10 April 2011|access-date=10 April 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120713193109/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/302126?cc=5739|archive-date=13 July 2012}}</ref>

On 10 August 2014, Suárez was knocked unconscious in a [[Exhibition game#Club football|friendly]] against [[VfL Wolfsburg]], after teammate [[Cristian Ansaldi]]'s hip hit his head. He suffered a "traumatic brain injury" and stayed for treatment in Germany, while the rest of the team returned to Spain.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://soccer.nbcsports.com/2014/08/10/atleticos-mario-suarez-suffers-traumatic-brain-injury-in-wolfsburg-friendly/related/|title=Atletico's Mario Suarez suffers "traumatic brain injury" in Wolfsburg friendly|publisher=[[NBC Sports]]|first=Kyle|last=Bonn|date=10 August 2014|access-date=29 September 2020}}</ref> However, on 19 August, he played the entire first leg of the [[Supercopa de España]], a [[2014 Supercopa de España|1–1 draw away]] to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/live/match/325067/report|title=Spanish Super Copa: Real Madrid and Atletico draw 1–1 in first leg|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|date=19 August 2014|access-date=20 August 2014}}</ref>

Suárez scored his second competitive goal of [[2014–15 La Liga|2014–15]] on 17 March 2015, through a 27th-minute deflected effort for the only goal against [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen]] in the [[UEFA Champions League]]'s [[Single-elimination tournament|round of 16]]. He also converted his [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shootout]] attempt, in an eventual [[2014–15 UEFA Champions League|3–2 win]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/021f-0e8fd98f1f48-c77e9f3f7bb8-1000--atletico-edge-past-leverkusen-on-penalties/|title=Atlético edge past Leverkusen on penalties|publisher=UEFA|date=17 March 2015|access-date=17 March 2015}}</ref>

===Fiorentina===
On 24 July 2015, Suárez signed for [[Serie A]] club [[ACF Fiorentina]], with [[Stefan Savić]] moving in the opposite direction.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/story/2535454/mario-suarez-seals-move-to-fiorentina-from-atletico-madrid|title=Mario Suarez seals move to Fiorentina from Atletico Madrid|publisher=ESPN FC|date=24 July 2015|access-date=24 July 2015}}</ref> He appeared in only 13 competitive games during his six-month tenure, his maiden league appearance occurring on 23 August in a 2–0 home victory over [[AC Milan]] (23 minutes played).<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.corrieredellosport.it/news/calcio/serie-a/2015/08/23-3423906/la_fiorentina_stende_il_milan_alonso-ilicic_show_e_2-0/|title=La Fiorentina stende il Milan: Alonso-Ilicic show e 2–0|trans-title=Fiorentina knock Milan out: Alonso-Ilicic show and 2–0|newspaper=[[Corriere dello Sport]]|language=it|date=23 August 2015|access-date=30 January 2016}}</ref>

Suárez's sole goal for the ''Viola'' came on 1 November 2015, in a 4–1 rout of [[Frosinone Calcio]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/soccer/2015/11/01/planet-futbol-fiorentina-beats-frosinone-return-top-serie|title=Fiorentina beats Frosinone to return to top of Serie A|publisher=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=1 November 2015|access-date=29 September 2020}}</ref>

===Watford===
On 30 January 2016, after weeks of negotiations, [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] announced the signing of Suárez on a four-and-a-half-year contract, for a €4 million transfer fee.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.watfordfc.com/news/article/160126-mario-suarez-signs-for-watford-fc-from-fiorentina-2922298.aspx|title=Official: Suárez signs on|publisher=Watford F.C.|date=30 January 2016|access-date=30 January 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160130224135/http://www.watfordfc.com/news/article/160126-mario-suarez-signs-for-watford-fc-from-fiorentina-2922298.aspx|archive-date=30 January 2016}}</ref><ref>ACF Fiorentina S.p.A. ''bilancio'' (financial report and accounts) on 31 December 2015 (in Italian), [http://www.registroimprese.it PDF purchased from Italian C.C.I.A.A.]</ref> His first [[Premier League]] appearance occurred four days later, as he came on as an 87th-minute [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for [[Étienne Capoue]] in a 0–0 home draw against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/35416324|title=Watford 0–0 Chelsea|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|first=Gary|last=Rose|date=3 February 2016|access-date=3 February 2016}}</ref>

Suárez signed for [[Valencia CF]] on a [[2016–17 La Liga|season]]-long loan deal on 16 August 2016, with an option of a subsequent purchase.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://en.valenciacf.com/ver/60099/vcf-official-statement--mario-suarez.html|title=VCF official statement {{!}} Mario Suárez|publisher=Valencia CF|date=16 August 2016|access-date=16 August 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160820130948/http://en.valenciacf.com/ver/60099/vcf-official-statement--mario-suarez.html|archive-date=20 August 2016}}</ref> He scored his first brace as a senior on 16 October, in a 2–1 victory at [[Sporting de Gijón]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2016/10/16/actualidad/1476643075_408660.html|title=Mario Suárez alegra el debut de Prandelli en el Valencia|trans-title=Mario Suárez sweetens Prandelli debut at Valencia|newspaper=[[El País]]|language=es|date=16 October 2016|access-date=11 September 2017}}</ref>

===Later career===
On 11 July 2017, Suárez transferred to [[Chinese Super League]] side [[Guizhou Hengfeng Zhicheng F.C.|Guizhou Hengfeng Zhicheng FC]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.sina.com.cn/china/j/2017-07-11/doc-ifyhwefp0584677.shtml|title=贵州官宣西班牙中场正式加盟 曾随马竞登顶西甲|trans-title=Guizhou officially announced arrival of Spanish midfielder|publisher=[[Sina Sports]]|language=zh|date=11 July 2017|access-date=11 July 2017}}</ref> He returned to Spain on 31 January 2019, joining [[Rayo Vallecano]] on a six-month contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rayovallecano.es/noticia/mario-suarez-nuevo-jugador-del-rayo-vallecano|title=Mario Suárez nuevo jugador del Rayo Vallecano|trans-title=Mario Suárez new Rayo Vallecano player|publisher=Rayo Vallecano|language=es|date=31 January 2019|access-date=1 February 2019}}</ref> He helped the latter to achieve top-tier promotion at the end of the [[2020–21 Segunda División|2020–21 campaign]], contributing 30 games and two goals (110 and 12 during his spell).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.unionrayo.es/datos-temporada-2021-22-mario-suarez-rayo-vallecano/|title=Los datos de la temporada 2021–22 de Mario Suárez|trans-title=Mario Suárez 2021–22 season data|publisher=Unión Rayo|first=Daniel|last=Calderón Aguado|language=es|date=25 July 2022|access-date=4 October 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/rayo-vallecano/20230710/1002035965/mario-suarez-mi-corazon-siempre-quedara-trocito-rayo.html|title=Mario Suárez: "He disfrutado con la pasión que transmite este barrio"|trans-title=Mario Suárez: "I've enjoyed the passion that this neighbourhood displays"|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|language=es|date=10 July 2023|access-date=4 October 2023}}</ref>

Suárez announced his retirement from football in October 2023, aged 36.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/primera/mario-suarez-se-retira-n/|title=Mario Suárez se retira|trans-title=Mario Suárez retires|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Maite|last=Martín|language=es|date=1 October 2023|access-date=2 October 2023}}</ref>

==International career==
Suárez played for [[Spain national under-20 football team|Spain]] in the [[2007 FIFA U-20 World Cup]] in Canada. He scored a [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty]] in the match against [[Zambia national football team|Zambia]], in a 2–1 win.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.20minutos.es/noticia/256006/0/mundia/sub20/seleccion/|title=España sufre pero gana ante Zambia|trans-title=Spain struggle but win against Zambia|newspaper=[[20 minutos]]|language=es|date=5 July 2007|access-date=10 May 2012}}</ref> Subsequently, he appeared for the [[Spain national under-21 football team|under-21s]] at the [[2009 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|2009 UEFA European Championship]] in Sweden, in an eventual group-stage exit.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/under21/news/0257-0de9640247b4-9391c746a885-1000--too-little-too-late-for-spain/|title=Too little too late for Spain|publisher=UEFA|first=John|last=Atkin|date=23 June 2009|access-date=4 April 2018}}</ref>

On 6 February 2013, Suárez earned his first [[Cap (sport)|cap]] for the [[Spain national football team|full side]], playing the last 20 minutes of the 3–1 [[Exhibition game#International football|friendly]] win over [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]] in [[Doha]], Qatar.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2012_13/amistosos_seleccion/4/spa_uru/|title=Campeón hasta en los simulacros|trans-title=Champions even in drills|newspaper=Marca|first=Ramiro|last=Aldunate|language=es|date=6 February 2013|access-date=6 February 2013}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In June 2017, Suárez married model [[Malena Costa Sjögren]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://us.hola.com/novias/2017061996032/malena-costa-mario-suarez-boda/|title=Boda sorpresa de Malena Costa y Mario Suárez en Mallorca|trans-title=Surprise wedding of Malena Costa and Mario Suárez in Mallorca|publisher=[[¡Hola!]]|language=es|date=19 June 2017|access-date=5 September 2020}}</ref>

'''Ben Anthony Foster''' (born 3 April 1983) is an English former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]].

Foster began his professional career in 2001 with [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]], having joined from [[Racing Club Warwick F.C.|Racing Club Warwick]]. However, he never made an appearance for Stoke, and spent time on loan with [[Bristol City F.C.|Bristol City]], [[Tiverton Town F.C.|Tiverton Town]], [[Stafford Rangers F.C.|Stafford Rangers]], [[Kidderminster Harriers F.C.|Kidderminster Harriers]], and [[Wrexham A.F.C.|Wrexham]]. He switched permanently to [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] in July 2005, but again struggled to break into the first team, and spent two successive seasons on loan to [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] from August 2005 until the end of the [[2006–07 Watford F.C. season|2006–07 season]].

Having played just 23 times for Manchester United (although he also played in the [[EFL Cup|League Cup]]-winning teams of [[2009 Football League Cup final|2009]] and [[2010 Football League Cup final|2010]]), Foster switched to [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] in May 2010. An ever-present in the league for Birmingham, he was also part of the Birmingham team that won the [[2011 Football League Cup final|2011 League Cup]]. Following Birmingham's relegation to the [[EFL Championship|Championship]] at the end of the season, he was loaned to West Bromwich Albion, and moved there permanently in June 2012. He returned to Watford in July 2018. He announced his retirement from football in September 2022 before returning to Wrexham in March 2023. He again retired in August 2023 after helping Wrexham to the [[National League (division)|National League]] title.

Foster made his international debut for [[England national football team|England]] in February 2007 against [[Spain national football team|Spain]]. Although he announced his retirement from international football in May 2011, he returned in February 2013, and was selected in England's squad for the [[2014 FIFA World Cup]]. He also runs a [[YouTube]] channel, "The Cycling GK", and The Fozcast podcast.

==Club career==
===Stoke City===
Foster was born in [[Leamington Spa]], Warwickshire.<ref name=Hugman1011/> He started his football career as a youngster at [[Racing Club Warwick F.C.|Racing Club Warwick]] of the [[Southern Football League|Southern League Division One West]]. He became their first-choice goalkeeper in December 2000,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.leamingtoncourier.co.uk/sport/racing-keeper-foster-in-talks-with-stoke-1-1052778 |title=Racing keeper Foster in talks with Stoke |newspaper=Leamington Courier |date=30 March 2001 |access-date=8 July 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170915161206/http://www.leamingtoncourier.co.uk/sport/racing-keeper-foster-in-talks-with-stoke-1-1052778 |archive-date=15 September 2017}}</ref> and was also training as an apprentice chef at [[Café Rouge]] in Leamington Spa.<ref name="House">{{cite news |title=Flavour of family life tops menu for Ben Foster |url=https://www.expressandstar.com/sport/west-bromwich-albion-fc/2012/08/17/flavour-of-family-life-tops-menu-for-ben-foster/ |newspaper=Express & Star |location=Wolverhampton |date=17 August 2012 |access-date=18 August 2012 }}{{Dead link|date=September 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

In April 2001 Foster turned professional with [[Football League Second Division|Second Division]] club [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] after being spotted by scout [[Colin Dobson]]. He signed a one-year contract with an option for a further two years; the "five-figure" fee was undisclosed, and RC Warwick would benefit from the inclusion of a sell-on clause.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.leamingtoncourier.co.uk/sport/racing-keeper-foster-goes-pro-1-1052776 |title=Racing keeper Foster goes pro |newspaper=Leamington Courier |date=20 April 2001 |access-date=8 July 2017 ===Manchester United===
While playing for Wrexham on loan from Stoke, Foster was spotted by [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] manager [[Alex Ferguson]], who was watching Foster's teammate and his son, [[Darren Ferguson|Darren]], in the [[2005 Football League Trophy final]]. United had been struggling for several years to replace former goalkeeper [[Peter Schmeichel]], and Ferguson decided to move for the young Foster, making a bid of £1 million for the player.<ref>{{cite news |first=Graeme |last=Bailey |title=United eye Stoke starlet |url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11667_2341839,00.html |website=Sky Sports |date=13 July 2005 |access-date=7 November 2008}}</ref> Stoke agreed a deal with United on 15 July 2005,<ref>{{cite news |first=Graeme |last=Bailey |title=United agree keeper deal |url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11667_2342183,00.html |website=Sky Sports |date=15 July 2005 |access-date=7 November 2008}}</ref> and the transfer was completed on 19 July.<ref>{{cite news |first=Graeme |last=Bailey |title=United finalise Foster move |url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11667_2342374,00.html |website=Sky Sports |date=19 July 2005 |access-date=7 November 2008}}</ref>

==== Loan to Watford ====
[[File:Ben Foster.jpg|thumb|upright|Foster training with [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] in 2007]]

Not ready for first team action, Foster was sent on a season-long loan to [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] on 1 August 2005,<ref>{{cite news |first=Mark |last=Buckingham |title=Hornets land United keeper |url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11667_2343859,00.html |website=Sky Sports |date=1 August 2005 |access-date=7 November 2008}}</ref> with the expectation of a second loan the season after.<ref>{{cite news |first=Mark |last=Buckingham |title=Foster to stay out on loan |url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11667_2346667,00.html |website=Sky Sports |date=29 August 2005 |access-date=7 November 2008}}</ref> Watford manager [[Aidy Boothroyd]] claimed that "he's better than current Manchester United goalkeeper [[Edwin van der Sar]]" and claimed Foster would be "the best goalkeeper in the world".<ref>{{cite news |first=Tom |last=Adams |title=Aidy: Foster to come to the fore |url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11667_2406894,00.html |website=Sky Sports |date=28 February 2007 |access-date=7 November 2008}}</ref> Manchester United manager Ferguson suggested that Foster would succeed Van der Sar as first-choice keeper at United and eventually replace [[Paul Robinson (footballer, born 1979)|Paul Robinson]] as "England's next goalkeeper".<ref>{{cite news |first=James |last=Pearson |title=Fergie: Foster to edge out Robbo |url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11667_2403862,00.html |website=Sky Sports |date=28 January 2007 |access-date=7 November 2008}}</ref> Foster helped Watford reach the [[Premier League]] by beating [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] 3–0 in the [[2006 Football League Championship play-off final|Championship play-off final]].<ref name="POF">{{cite news |title=Leeds 0–3 Watford |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_div_1/4771857.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=21 May 2006 |access-date=14 June 2016}}</ref>

He re-signed for Watford on a second season-long loan on 10 August 2006 after Manchester United secured the services of [[Poland national football team|Poland international]] goalkeeper [[Tomasz Kuszczak]] on loan from [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Lewis |last=Rutledge |title=United clinch Kuszczak capture |url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11667_2386486,00.html |website=Sky Sports |date=10 August 2006 |access-date=7 November 2008}}</ref> Foster's performances during Watford's Premier League campaign earnt him the club's [[Watford F.C. Player of the Season|Player of the Season]] award.<ref name=WFCPOTS>{{cite web |title=Foster Voted Player of the Season |url=http://www.watfordfc.com/page/NewsDetail/0,,10400~1022199,00.html |publisher=Watford F.C. |date=8 May 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111005215840/http://www.watfordfc.com/page/NewsDetail/0%2C%2C10400~1022199%2C00.html |archive-date=5 October 2011 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Aidy Boothroyd expressed his desire to keep Foster at Watford for a third season on a number of occasions during the 2006–07 season, but his hopes were dashed in January 2007 when Alex Ferguson announced his intention to bring Foster back to [[Old Trafford]] at the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news |first=Chris |last=Stanton |title=Fergie confirms Foster return |url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11667_2403913,00.html |website=Sky Sports |date=29 January 2007 |access-date=7 November 2008}}</ref>

==== Return to Manchester United ====
In June 2007, it was announced that Foster would undergo surgery on a cruciate ligament injury in his right knee, forcing him to miss the start of the 2007–08 season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Knee surgery for Man Utd's Foster |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/m/man_utd/6707485.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=6 June 2007 |access-date=6 June 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070630190647/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/m/man_utd/6707485.stm |archive-date=30 June 2007 |url-status=live}}</ref> He returned to light training towards the end of 2007, setting a February 2008 target for his return.<ref>{{cite web |first=Steve |last=Bartram |title=Foster eyes February return |url=http://www.manutd.com/default.sps?pagegid={B4CEE8FA-9A47-47BC-B069-3F7A2F35DB70}&newsid=505469 |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=8 November 2007 |access-date=8 November 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071110123243/http://www.manutd.com/default.sps?pagegid=%7BB4CEE8FA-9A47-47BC-B069-3F7A2F35DB70%7D&newsid=505469 |archive-date=10 November 2007 |url-status=dead}}</ref> He made a comeback in a reserve match against [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] on 6 March 2008,<ref>{{cite web |first=Steve |last=Bartram |title=Foster set for Reds comeback |url=http://www.manutd.com/default.sps?pagegid={B4CEE8FA-9A47-47BC-B069-3F7A2F35DB70}&newsid=538655 |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=6 March 2008 |access-date=7 November 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090202130330/http://www.manutd.com/default.sps?pagegid=%7BB4CEE8FA-9A47-47BC-B069-3F7A2F35DB70%7D&newsid=538655 |archive-date=2 February 2009 |url-status=dead}}</ref> before making his debut for the Manchester United first team on 15 March 2008. With Edwin van der Sar injured and Tomasz Kuszczak suspended for a red card against [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] in the FA Cup sixth round the previous Saturday, Alex Ferguson had to shelve plans to ship Foster out on loan again, and the young goalkeeper was started for the away match against [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]]. United won the match 1–0, with Foster making two crucial saves en route to keeping a clean sheet.<ref>{{cite web |first=Steve |last=Bartram |title=Report: Derby 0 United 1 |url=http://www.manutd.com/default.sps?pagegid={B4CEE8FA-9A47-47BC-B069-3F7A2F35DB70}&newsid=541058 |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=15 March 2008 |access-date=15 March 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170408091616/http://www.manutd.com/default.sps?pagegid=%7BB4CEE8FA-9A47-47BC-B069-3F7A2F35DB70%7D&newsid=541058 |archive-date=8 April 2017 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Although he was impressed with Foster's performance in the match against Derby,<ref>{{cite web |first=Steve |last=Bartram |title=Foster's bow impresses Boss |url=http://www.manutd.com/default.sps?pagegid={B4CEE8FA-9A47-47BC-B069-3F7A2F35DB70}&newsid=541360 |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=17 March 2008 |access-date=7 November 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090201185608/http://www.manutd.com/default.sps?pagegid=%7BB4CEE8FA-9A47-47BC-B069-3F7A2F35DB70%7D&newsid=541360 |archive-date=1 February 2009 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Ferguson did not start him for the following match against [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]], opting for the returning Kuszczak.<ref>{{cite news |first=Paul |last=Fletcher |title=Man Utd 2–0 Bolton |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/7298123.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=19 March 2008 |access-date=7 November 2008}}</ref>

After being selected as a substitute for Manchester United's opening match of the [[2008–09 UEFA Champions League|2008–09 Champions League]] against [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] on 17 September 2008,<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Man Utd 0–0 Villarreal |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/7614132.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=17 September 2008 |access-date=7 November 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080922154116/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/europe/7614132.stm |archive-date=22 September 2008 |url-status=live}}</ref> Foster then played for the reserves against [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] the following day. During the match, he fell awkwardly and suffered a twisted ankle, putting him out of contention for six to eight weeks.<ref>{{cite news |title=Foster sidelined for United |url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11095_4166746,00.html |website=Sky Sports |date=19 September 2008 |access-date=7 November 2008}}</ref> Fortunately for Foster, his recovery time was quicker than was first estimated and he returned to reserve team action on 14 October 2008, playing the full 90 minutes in a 2–1 win over [[Oldham Athletic A.F.C.|Oldham Athletic reserves]].<ref>{{cite web |first=Ben |last=Hibbs |title=Foster given Reserves return |url=http://www.manutd.com/default.sps?pagegid={B4CEE8FA-9A47-47BC-B069-3F7A2F35DB70}&newsid=6620426 |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=14 October 2008 |access-date=7 November 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081018163001/http://www.manutd.com/default.sps?pagegid=%7BB4CEE8FA%2D9A47%2D47BC%2DB069%2D3F7A2F35DB70%7D&newsid=6620426 |archive-date=18 October 2008 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Foster then made his first [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] appearance – his second for the Manchester United first team – on 5 November 2008, in a 1–1 away draw to [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Keir |last=Murray |title=Celtic 1–1 Man Utd |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/7697254.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=5 November 2008 |access-date=7 November 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081108065737/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/europe/7697254.stm |archive-date=8 November 2008 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Foster was originally selected in Manchester United's squad for the [[2008 FIFA Club World Cup]], but after suffering a broken finger in training the day before the squad was due to depart for Japan, he was replaced by [[Ben Amos]].<ref>{{cite web |first=Steve |last=Bartram |title=Gamba book United date |url=http://www.manutd.com/default.sps?pagegid={F9E570E6-407E-44BC-800F-4A3110258114}&newsid=6624039 |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=14 December 2008 |access-date=14 December 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171102180521/http://www.manutd.com/default.sps?pagegid=%7BF9E570E6-407E-44BC-800F-4A3110258114%7D&newsid=6624039 |archive-date=2 November 2017 |url-status=dead}}</ref> On 1 March 2009, Alex Ferguson named Foster in goal for the [[2009 Football League Cup final|2009 League Cup final]] at Wembley Stadium. After keeping a clean sheet in normal time, Foster then made a save from Tottenham's [[Jamie O'Hara (footballer)|Jamie O'Hara]] in the consequent penalty shoot-out. This, combined with a miss from [[David Bentley]], gave United a 4–1 win in the shootout and the 2009 League Cup title.<ref name=2009LCF>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Man Utd 0–0 Tottenham (aet) |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/league_cup/7905889.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=1 March 2009 |access-date=14 June 2016}}</ref> After the match, Foster was given the [[Alan Hardaker Trophy]] for his man of the match performance.<ref name=Hardaker>{{cite web |title=Alan Hardaker Trophy Winners |url=http://www.football-league.co.uk/page/AlanHardakerTrophyWinners/0,,10794~1354852,00.html |publisher=The Football League |date=24 February 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140114094945/http://www.football-league.co.uk/page/AlanHardakerTrophyWinners/0%2C%2C10794~1354852%2C00.html |archive-date=14 January 2014 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

It was revealed after the match that Foster had used an [[iPod]] to help with his preparations in the penalty shootout, prompting discussion about the use of technology in the match.<ref>{{cite news |first=Mike |last=Collett |title=Foster in the clear after using iPod |url=http://uk.reuters.com/article/idUKTRE52158020090302 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090308044344/http://uk.reuters.com/article/idUKTRE52158020090302 |url-status=dead |archive-date=8 March 2009 |work=Reuters |date=3 March 2009 |access-date=11 November 2009}}</ref>

Foster was rewarded for his performance by being made United's second-choice goalkeeper for the remainder of the season, starting three more matches when [[Alex Ferguson]] chose to rest Edwin van der Sar ahead of important matches. However, he had been attempting to play with a ruptured ligament in his right thumb, which became aggravated, necessitating surgery which ruled him out of United's title run-in, the [[2009 UEFA Champions League final|Champions League final]] against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and [[England national football team|England]]'s [[2010 FIFA World Cup qualification – UEFA Group 6|2010 World Cup qualifiers]] in June.<ref>{{cite web |first=Ben |last=Hibbs |title=Injury blow for Foster |url=http://www.manutd.com/default.sps?pagegid={F9E570E6-407E-44BC-800F-4A3110258114}&newsid=6632752 |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=18 May 2009 |access-date=18 May 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090521113726/http://www.manutd.com/default.sps?pagegid=%7BF9E570E6-407E-44BC-800F-4A3110258114%7D&newsid=6632752 |archive-date=21 May 2009 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Following speculation that United were in the market for a new goalkeeper to replace the soon-to-retire Edwin van der Sar, Foster signed a new four-year contract with the club. Alex Ferguson commented that Manchester United "genuinely see him [Foster] as a successor to Edwin van der Sar".<ref>{{cite web |first=Ben |last=Hibbs |title=Foster pens new Reds deal |url=http://www.manutd.com/default.sps?pagegid={F9E570E6-407E-44BC-800F-4A3110258114}&newsid=6635838 |publisher=Manchester United F.C. |date=7 July 2009 |access-date=7 July 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090904001322/http://www.manutd.com/default.sps?pagegid=%7BF9E570E6-407E-44BC-800F-4A3110258114%7D&newsid=6635838 |archive-date=4 September 2009 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

F.C.|Chelsea]], where his mistakes led to two Chelsea goals and made no saves in the penalty shootout.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Chelsea 2–2 Man Utd |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/8190061.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=9 August 2009 |access-date=13 March 2010}}</ref> Foster continued to play in the League, starting with the opening
