===West Bromwich Albion===
[[File:Foster wba.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Foster at his presentation as a [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] player in 2011]]

Foster joined Premier League club West Bromwich Albion on 29 July 2011, changing places with Albion goalkeeper [[Boaz Myhill]], both players signing a loan deal for the whole of the 2011–12 season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ben Foster joins West Bromwich Albion on loan |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14311963 |website=BBC Sport |date=29 July 2011 |access-date=29 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110728072026/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/14311963.stm |archive-date=28 July 2011 |url-status=live}}</ref> Foster played in 37 of their 38 league matches, only missing the final match of the season with a minor groin strain. He kept 10 league clean sheets, equalling West Brom's Premier League clean sheets record, as the club finished in 10th place, their highest league finish in 30 years.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.sportinglife.com/football/news/article/165/7853055/foster-move-was-a-no-brainer |title=Foster: Move was a no-brainer |website=Sporting Life |date=30 June 2012 |access-date=30 June 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160815082632/http://www.sportinglife.com/football/news/article/165/7853055/foster-move-was-a-no-brainer |archive-date=15 August 2016 |url-status=dead}}</ref> At the end of the season, Foster was given the supporters' player of the year and the players' player of the year awards.<ref name=BBCWBA>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/18648707 |title=Ben Foster signs for West Brom from Birmingham City |website=BBC Sport |date=29 June 2012 |access-date=14 June 2016}}</ref>

On 29 June 2012, Foster signed permanently with West Brom for an undisclosed fee,<ref name=BBCWBA/> widely reported to be £4 million.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.expressandstar.com/sport/west-bromwich-albion-fc/2012/06/30/ben-foster-happy-at-home-with-west-brom/ |title=Ben Foster happy at home with West Brom |newspaper=Express & Star |location=Wolverhampton |date=30 June 2012 |access-date=30 June 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/west-bromwich-albion/9365056/West-Bromwich-Albion-sign-Birmingham-City-goalkeeper-Ben-Foster-for-4m-a-permanent-deal.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220112/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/west-bromwich-albion/9365056/West-Bromwich-Albion-sign-Birmingham-City-goalkeeper-Ben-Foster-for-4m-a-permanent-deal.html |archive-date=12 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |title=West Bromwich Albion sign Birmingham City goalkeeper Ben Foster for £4m a permanent deal |first=John |last=Percy |newspaper=The Daily Telegraph |location=London |date=29 June 2012 |access-date=30 June 2012}}{{cbignore}}</ref> He signed a three-year contract with an option for a further two years in the club's favour.<ref name=BBCWBA/> Foster continued to perform impressively in his second season with the club, keeping 7 clean sheets in 30 league matches,<ref name=sb1213/> and helping to guide West Brom to their record high Premier League position of 8th for the [[2012–13 Premier League|2012–13 season]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39912021 |title=Swansea City 2–1 West Brom |first=Dafydd |last=Pritchard |website=BBC Sport |date=21 May 2017 |access-date=13 July 2022}}</ref> A highlight of that season was saving a [[Steven Gerrard]] penalty against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] at [[Anfield]]. The score was 0–0 at the time and West Brom went on to win 2–0.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21318809|title=Liverpool 0–2 West Brom |website=BBC Sport |date=11 February 2013 |access-date=8 January 2018}}</ref> Despite missing 4 months of the following season through injury, Foster went on to win both fans player, and player's player of the year awards for the second time in three years after a series of impressive performances throughout the [[2013–14 West Bromwich Albion F.C. season|2013–14 season]].<ref name=WBAAwards>{{cite web |url=http://www.wba.co.uk/news/article/albion-announce-end-of-season-awards-winners-1546059.aspx |title=Albion Albion announce end-of-season awards winners |publisher=West Bromwich Albion F.C. |date=11 May 2014 |access-date=14 June 2016}}</ref> Foster's impressive form for the club saw him called up to the 2014 England World Cup squad, becoming the first West Bromwich Albion player to represent England in a world cup squad since [[Jeff Astle]] in 1970.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wba.co.uk/news/article/foster-delighted-to-be-off-to-brazil-1547682.aspx|title=Ben Foster delighted to be off to Brazil after being named in England squad for World Cup finals|publisher=West Bromwich Albion F.C.}}</ref>

After an impressive 2016–17 season, Foster was nominated for the Football Writers' Association Footballer of the Year award. He was also the West Brom supporters' club player of the season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.expressandstar.com/sport/football/west-bromwich-albion/2017/05/08/ben-foster-named-west-brom-supporters-club-player-of-the-season/|title=Ben Foster named West Brom supporters' club player of the season|last=Wilson|first=Matt|newspaper=Express & Star|access-date=22 May 2017}}</ref>

===Return to Watford===
After West Brom's relegation to the Championship, Foster re-signed for Premier League club Watford on 5 July 2018 on a two-year contract, with the option of an additional year, for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44732427 |title=Ben Foster and Ken Sema sign for Watford |website=BBC Sport |date=5 July 2018 |access-date=6 July 2018}}</ref> He immediately overtook Brazilian teammate [[Heurelho Gomes]] to the Watford number one shirt and remained Watford's first-choice goalkeeper after their relegation from the Premier League in 2020. Foster signed a further two-year contract with Watford in June 2020.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/52951365 |title=Ben Foster: Goalkeeper signs new Watford deal |website=BBC Sport |date=9 June 2020 |access-date=22 April 2021}}</ref> On 16 May 2022, Foster revealed he would be leaving the club at the end of his contract in June.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3491023/2022/05/16/ben-foster-announces-he-will-leave-watford-at-the-end-of-the-season/ |title=Ben Foster announces he will leave Watford at the end of the season |last=Humayun |first=Ali |website=The Athletic |date=16 May 2022 |access-date=16 May 2022}}</ref>

==International career==
On 26 May 2006, Foster was named on the stand-by list for England's [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006 World Cup]] squad, because of [[Robert Green]]'s injury in a "B" international against Belarus.<ref>{{cite news |title=Carson promoted to England squad |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/world_cup_2006/teams/england/5020060.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=26 May 2006 |access-date=7 November 2008}}</ref> After Foster re-signed on loan for Watford, he was called up to [[Steve McClaren]]'s first England squad as one of three goalkeepers for the friendly against [[Greece national football team|Greece]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Ashton receives England call-up |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/internationals/4784203.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=11 August 2006 |access-date=7 November 2008}}</ref> Since his first call-up but prior to his injury, Foster was named in every England squad, and made his England debut in the 1–0 defeat against [[Spain national football team|Spain]] on 7 February 2007.<ref>{{cite news |first=John |last=Sinnott |title=England 0–1 Spain |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/internationals/6330177.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=7 February 2007 |access-date=7 November 2008}}</ref>

After not playing for England for two years and never being called to the first team, he was finally selected by [[Fabio Capello]] after his performance during the League Cup Final and earned his second cap as a second-half substitute in a 4–0 victory over [[Slovakia national football team|Slovakia]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/england/5068714/England-v-Slovakia-How-the-English-players-rated.html |title=England v Slovakia: How the English players rated |first=Rory |last=Smith |publisher=The Telegraph |date=29 March 2009 |access-date=13 July 2022}}</ref> Inconsistent performances in Manchester United's first fixtures of the [[2009–10 Manchester United F.C. season|2009–10 season]], as well as bruised ribs, meant that Foster was left out of Capello's initial squad for their final two World Cup qualifiers. However, after Robert Green was sent off in the match against [[Ukraine national football team|Ukraine]] on 10 October, Foster was recalled in his place for the following match against [[Belarus national football team|Belarus]]. It had been expected that [[David James (footballer, born 1970)|David James]] would take Green's place in the starting line-up, but James was injured in the warm-up and Foster was given his third England cap instead. England won the match 3–0, with Foster making a one-handed save from [[Syarhey Amelyanchuk]] in the 63rd minute.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=England 3–0 Belarus |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/internationals/8301471.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=14 October 2009 |access-date=15 October 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140512225358/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/internationals/8301471.stm |archive-date=12 May 2014 |url-status=live}}</ref> Foster won his fourth cap against [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]], where he played the whole match in a 1–0 loss on 14 November 2009, the friendly match was played in Qatar, with forward [[Nilmar]] scoring the only goal of the match from a header in the 47th minute.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Brazil 1–0 England |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/internationals/8353751.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=14 November 2009 |access-date=13 March 2010}}</ref> He was overlooked for England's [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010 World Cup]] squad, Joe Hart being preferred for the third goalkeeping spot.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.football365.com/news/old-folks-xi-we-start-with-goalkeeper-ben-foster |title=Old Folks XI: We start with goalkeeper Ben Foster |first=Sarah |last=Winterburn |publisher=Football365 |date=7 January 2020 |access-date=13 July 2022}}</ref>

Foster stated in a 2020 interview that he found Capello difficult to work with, not only as a manager but also as a person. Foster had been training with England for a friendly match when his pregnant wife went into labour. Capello initially refused to allow Foster to leave for his child's birth, before reluctantly allowing it only after Foster pleaded with him. Three hours after his child's birth, Capello called Foster and urged him to return to the training camp immediately, promising Foster that he would play the second half of the upcoming match. Ultimately, Foster was not brought on in the second half and played no role in the match; Capello offered no acknowledgement or explanation to Foster.<ref>{{cite web|title=BBC Radio 5 live – That Peter Crouch Podcast, WFH: With Ben Foster|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p08bykrr|website=BBC|date=30 April 2020 |access-date=4 May 2020}}</ref> Shortly after, in May 2011, Foster announced that he would be making himself unavailable for international selection for an indefinite period. He intended to "prolong [his] club career for as long as possible" by allowing his body "a proper rest period between games" to reduce "niggling" injuries.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/13361020 |title=Birmingham's Ben Foster halts England career |website=BBC Sport |date=11 May 2011 |access-date=11 May 2011}}</ref> It was not until February 2013 – after Capello had been succeeded by [[Roy Hodgson]] – that he made himself available for selection again.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21621732 |title=Ben Foster: Goalkeeper available for England again |website=BBC Sport |date=28 February 2013 |access-date=12 May 2014}}</ref> In the next international break, he was called up to the England squad for World Cup qualifiers against San Marino and Montenegro.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21782595 |title=Rio Ferdinand recalled to England squad for World Cup qualifiers |website=BBC Sport |date=14 March 2013 |access-date=12 May 2014}}</ref> On 29 May 2013 Foster represented England in a friendly fixture against the [[Republic of Ireland national football team|Republic of Ireland]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/soccer/england-keeper-ben-foster-out-for-12-weeks-after-breaking-bone-in-foot-29530735.html |title=England keeper Ben Foster out for 12 weeks after breaking bone in foot |publisher=The Irish Independent |date=27 August 2013 |access-date=13 July 2022}}</ref>

Foster was selected in the final 23 for England's [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014 World Cup]] squad,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27362447 |title=World Cup 2014: England name Ross Barkley in squad |website=BBC Sport |date=12 May 2014 |access-date=12 May 2014}}</ref> and played in the 2–2 draw with [[Ecuador national football team|Ecuador]] in preparation for the tournament. With England unable to advance to the last 16, he played the whole 90 minutes of the last group match against [[Costa Rica national football team|Costa Rica]], and kept a [[clean sheet]] in the 0–0 draw in [[Belo Horizonte]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Taylor|first1=Daniel|title=England end disappointing World Cup with barren draw against Costa Rica|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/jun/24/costa-rica-england-world-cup-group-d-match-report|access-date=24 June 2014|newspaper=The Guardian|location=London|date=24 June 2014}}</ref>

Foster has a verified YouTube channel called "Ben Foster – The Cycling GK", which he started in 2020 during the UK's COVID-19 lockdown. He posts cycling videos and matchday vlogs, including [[GoPro]] footage of the games in the back of his goal;<ref>{{cite web|last=Bacon|first=Jake|date=5 January 2021|title=Ben Foster has 'put a bit of a target on his back' with YouTube channel, says Deeney|url=https://talksport.com/football/efl/812169/ben-foster-gopro-youtube-watford-troy-deeney/|access-date=29 January 2021|website=talkSPORT}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Vincent|first=Gareth|title=Lowe makes Foster's YouTube channel|website=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55532619|access-date=29 January 2021}}</ref> he occasionally wears an [[Insta360]] camera fastened to his chest to provide a [[first-person (video games)|first-person]] viewpoint.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IMghCOEKnzw|title="WREXHAM IS HOW A CLUB SHOULD BE RUN!" ✅ Ben Foster REVEALS why he signed a contract extension!|via=www.youtube.com}}</ref> {{As of|2023|4}}, the channel has amassed over 1.43 million subscribers and over 138 million views.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ben Foster – The Cycling GK – YouTube|url=https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCi33DX7KG3M3bI0ipjOP2Eg/featured|access-date=16 March 2021|website=www.youtube.com}}</ref>

He also has a podcast called "Fozcast – The Ben Foster Podcast", which he hosts with Tom Ochoa.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.essentiallysports.com/soccer-football-news-ryan-reynolds-2500000-million-teams-latest-blockbuster-signing-ben-foster-teases-real-madrid-following-retirement-u-turn-its-wrexham/|title=Ryan Reynolds' $2,500,000 Million Team's Latest Blockbuster Signing Ben Foster Teases 'Real Madrid' Following Retirement U-Turn – "It's Wrexham.."|date=24 March 2023|website=EssentiallySports|access-date=30 March 2023|archive-date=30 November 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241130132549/https://www.essentiallysports.com/soccer-football-news-ryan-reynolds-2500000-million-teams-latest-blockbuster-signing-ben-foster-teases-real-madrid-following-retirement-u-turn-its-wrexham/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thepfa.com/news/2022/3/14/maheta-molango-ben-foster-fozcast|title=PFA CEO Maheta Molango caught up with Ben Foster I The Fozcast}}</ref> Foster also has a golf channel called "The Golfing GK",<ref>{{cite web|url=https://youtube.com/@TheGolfingGK/|title=Ben Foster – The Golfing GK – YouTube|website=[[YouTube]]}}</ref> and hosts a debate show on his channel called "The Football Fill-In", which began during the [[2022–23 Premier League]] season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://youtube.com/playlist?list=PLzGaD8Zmd51siBmYVLBX2xqWCqyqZSWi4|title=The Football Fill-In|website=[[YouTube]]}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Foster attended North Leamington School in [[Leamington Spa]], Warwickshire.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.leamingtoncourier.co.uk/sport/football/foster-returns-school-ahead-brazil-mission-2287658|title=Foster returns to school ahead of Brazil mission | WarwickshireWorld}}</ref>

Foster lives with his wife and two children in a house he helped design on a 30-acre farm in [[Henley-in-Arden]], [[Warwickshire]].<ref name="House"/><ref name="Cycling">{{cite news|title=Ben Foster: 'I want to be a cyclist after football. The Alps, Vuelta, Giro'|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2020/sep/10/ben-foster-watford-cyclist-after-football-the-alps-vuelta-giro|newspaper=The Guardian|access-date=12 September 2020|date=10 September 2020}}</ref> He is an enthusiastic cyclist.<ref name="Cycling"/><ref>{{cite news|title=Foster puts Focus team through brutal workout|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/av/football/52249457|website=BBC Sport|access-date=12 September 2020|date=11 April 2020}}</ref>

In March 2022, Foster was fined £2,250 and banned from driving for six months after he was caught driving at {{convert|99|mph|abbr=on}} on the [[M40 motorway|M40]], an offence he committed in April 2021.<ref>{{cite news|title=Watford goalkeeper Ben Foster hit with driving ban after speeding|url=https://www.watfordobserver.co.uk/sport/20020283.watford-goalkeeper-ben-foster-hit-driving-ban-speeding/|newspaper=Watford Observer|access-date=25 March 2022|date=25 March 2022}}</ref>

'''Arthur Henrique Ramos de Oliveira Melo''' (born 12 August 1996), known as '''Arthur''' or '''Arthur Melo''', is a Brazilian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A]] club [[Santos FC|Santos]].

Born in [[Goiânia]], Arthur began his career with [[Grêmio FBPA|Grêmio]], and won the [[Copa Libertadores]] in [[2017 Copa Libertadores|2017]]. He signed for [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] for an initial fee of €31 million in 2018. Arthur joined Italian club Juventus in 2020. He was loaned out to [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] in the 2022–23 season, only making one appearance for the club. The following season he was loaned to [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]].

Arthur made his senior debut for [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] in 2018 after previously being [[Cap (sport)|capped]] by Brazil youth team at [[Brazil national under-17 football team|under-17]] level. He was later part of the squad that won the [[2019 Copa América]].

==Club career==
===Grêmio===
[[File:Arthur Melo.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Arthur playing for [[Grêmio Foot-Ball Porto Alegrense|Grêmio]] in 2017]]
Arthur began his career with his hometown club [[Esporte Clube Goiás|Goiás]] aged 12. In 2010, after being spotted in a youth tournament, he moved to [[Grêmio Foot-Ball Porto Alegrense|Grêmio]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Criação da base: conheça trajetória de Arthur, volante goiano que conquista torcida gremista|url=https://www.vavel.com/br/futebol/gremio/824050-criacoes-da-base-conheca-trajetoria-de-arthur-volante-goiano-que-conquista-torcida-gremista.html|publisher=Vavel|date=September 2017|access-date=13 September 2017}}</ref>

In January 2015, following Arthur's impressive performances at the [[Copa São Paulo de Futebol Júnior]], he was promoted from Grêmio's youth team under first-team manager [[Luiz Felipe Scolari]]. He unexpectedly started in his first team debut, against [[Clube Esportivo Aimoré|Aimoré]] for the [[Campeonato Gaúcho]]. However, he was substituted at half-time by [[Argentine people|Argentine]] full-back [[Matías Rodríguez (footballer, born 1986)|Matías Rodríguez]] and made no more senior appearances that season. In 2016, Arthur made his [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|league]] debut in the last match of the season, a 1–0 home loss against [[Botafogo de Futebol e Regatas|Botafogo]], replacing [[Kaio Mendes|Kaio]] in the second half.

In 2017, Arthur become a first-team regular after a string of good performances in [[2017 Primeira Liga|Primeira Liga]] and Campeonato Gaúcho. In his [[2017 Copa Libertadores|Copa Libertadores]] debut, a 1–1 away draw against [[Club Guaraní]], he was named man-of-the-match after completing 40 passes, with an impressive 100% success rate. His playing style and build earned drawn comparisons with Spanish midfielders [[Andrés Iniesta]] and [[Thiago Alcântara]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Para Ricardo Rocha, Arthur cairia como uma luva no Barça: "Lembra o Iniesta"|url=http://sportv.globo.com/site/programas/troca-de-passes/noticia/2017/06/para-ricardo-rocha-arthur-cairia-como-uma-luva-no-barca-lembra-o-iniesta.html|publisher=Sportv|date=June 2017|access-date=13 September 2017}}</ref> and attracted interest from European clubs such as [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Grêmio recusa proposta de mais de R$ 40 milhões por Arthur|url=http://www.90min.com/pt-BR/posts/5086373-gremio-recusa-proposta-de-mais-de-r-40-milhoes-por-arthur|publisher=90Min.com|date=June 2017|access-date=13 September 2017|archive-date=14 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170914124749/http://www.90min.com/pt-BR/posts/5086373-gremio-recusa-proposta-de-mais-de-r-40-milhoes-por-arthur|url-status=dead}}</ref> [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and [[Atlético Madrid]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Atlético de Madrid envia olheiro para observar Arthur, do Grêmio|url=http://zh.clicrbs.com.br/rs/esportes/gremio/noticia/2017/05/atletico-de-madrid-envia-olheiro-para-observar-arthur-do-gremio-9800247.html#showNoticia=UUAwL3t1QF84MTYyODUwOTYyMzk0OTMxMjAwIzskMjE0NDI5OTEzNDMzODE3NTI3NHNvWjY3MDg5NTAyNDQzMTIyMTk2NDhkOF4tS3RdTnReajpmJnNePTI=|publisher=Zero Hora|date=May 2017|access-date=13 September 2017}}</ref> In May, Arthur scored his first professional goal, the opener in a 3–1 victory against [[Fluminense FC|Fluminense]] for the [[2017 Copa do Brasil|Copa do Brasil]]. In July, he scored his first league goal, the second in a 3–1 away victory against [[Esporte Clube Vitória|Vitória]]. In November, was elected by Conmebol the man of match in the second leg of the [[Copa Libertadores]] final against [[Club Atlético Lanús|Lanús]], despite playing only 50 minutes due to an injury.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/barca/arthur-doctora-ante-robert-fernandez-6459907|title=Arthur se doctora ante Robert Fernández|last=Sport|date=2017-11-30|work=sport|access-date=2018-09-03|language=es}}</ref>

===Barcelona===
[[File:Arthur Melo 2019 03 17 1 (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|180px|Arthur with [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in 2019]]
On 11 March 2018, Barcelona reached an agreement with Grêmio for the transfer of Arthur. The Catalans agreed to pay an initial fee of €31 million plus €9 million in added variables.<ref>{{cite web |date=11 March 2018 |title=Barça and Gremio reach agreement on option for Arthur transfer |url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2017-2018/agreement-signing-option-rights-fc-barcelona-arthur-gremio-brazil-porto-alegre |access-date=11 March 2018 |publisher=[[FC Barcelona]]}}</ref> Arthur signed a six-year contract and was officially announced as a ''Barça'' player on 9 July 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Agreement for the transfer of Arthur
|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2018-2019/fc-barcelona-signs-brazilian-midfielder-arthur-from-gremio|publisher=FC Barcelona|date=9 July 2018|access-date=9 July 2018}}</ref> On 28 July, Arthur scored a goal on his debut against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] in a pre-season friendly match.<ref>{{cite web|title=Espectacular estreno de Arthur: golazo y partidazo
|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/fc-barcelona/20180729/451159926128/arthur-barca-gol-tottenham-champions-international-cup.html|publisher=Mundo Deportivo|date=28 July 2018|access-date=29 July 2018}}</ref>

Arthur made his competitive debut at the [[2018 Supercopa de España]] on 12 August, in which Barcelona won 2–1 over [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/football/first-team/news/2018-2019/fc-barcelona-win-13th-spanish-super-cup|title=FC Barcelona win 13th Spanish Super Cup|publisher=FC Barcelona}}</ref> Arthur made his league debut during the first league match of the season, also registering his first assist for the club in a 3–0 win against [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]]. On 31 August, Arthur scored his first goal for Barcelona in 2–2 away draw against [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sport-english.com/en/news/barca/arthur-melo-scores-his-first-ever-barcelona-goal-in-draw-with-osasuna-7614258|title=Arthur Melo scores his first-ever Barcelona goal in draw with Osasuna|last=Sport|date=2019-08-31|website=sport|language=en|access-date=2019-09-02|archive-date=2 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190902123646/https://www.sport-english.com/en/news/barca/arthur-melo-scores-his-first-ever-barcelona-goal-in-draw-with-osasuna-7614258|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.juventusnews24.com/arthur-felice-per-il-mio-debutto-in-serie-a-buon-lavoro-di-squadra/ |title=Arthur: "Felice per il mio debutto in Serie A. Buon lavoro di squadra" |publisher=Juventus News 24 |language=it |date=27 September 2020 |access-date=28 September 2020 }}</ref>

===Juventus===
On 29 June 2020, Barcelona announced that they had reached an agreement with [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] for the transfer of Arthur on a five-year contract for €72 million, plus €10 million in variables; the deal was also coordinated with a swap of [[Miralem Pjanić]].<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=29 June 2020 |title=OFFICIAL {{!}} Arthur & Pjanic, agreements with FC Barcelona |url=https://www.juventus.com/en/news/articles/official-arthur-pjanic-agreements-with-fc-barcelona |access-date=9 August 2020 |website= |publisher=[[Juventus FC]] |language=en}}</ref> He made his club and [[Serie A]] debut on 27 September, coming on as substitute in a 2–2 away draw against [[A.S. Roma|Roma]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report?gameId=583144 |title=AS Roma vs. Juventus - Football Match Report |work=ESPN.com |date=27 September 2020 |access-date=27 September 2020 }}</ref>

====Loan to Liverpool====
On 1 September 2022, [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] announced the loan signing of Arthur.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/liverpool-complete-signing-arthur-melo-loan|title=Liverpool complete signing of Arthur Melo on loan|publisher=[[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool Football Club]]|date=1 September 2022|accessdate=1 September 2022}}</ref> Juventus specified that Liverpool had paid €4.5 million in loan fees, with an option to purchase the player for €37.5 million at the end of the one-year loan.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.juventus.com/images/image/upload/dev/plpj5ddnr5dgproo5oc3.pdf|title=Agreement with Liverpool for the temporary disposal of player Arthur (PDF)|publisher=[[Juventus FC|Juventus Football Club]]|date=1 September 2022|accessdate=1 September 2022}}</ref>

Arthur made his Liverpool debut in a [[2022–23 UEFA Champions League group stage#Napoli v Liverpool|4–1 UEFA Champions League defeat]] to [[S.S.C. Napoli|Napoli]] on 7 September 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=Napoli 4 Liverpool 1 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62815794 |website=[[BBC Sport]] |date=6 September 2022 |access-date=8 September 2022}}</ref> However, his experience at the club was blighted by physical condition problems after having been forced to train alone while he was at Juventus.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Sport |first=Sky |title=Arthur nel Liverpool U21 per ritrovare condizione |url=https://sport.sky.it/calcio/premier-league/2022/09/20/liverpool-arthur-squadra-u21 |access-date=2022-09-28 |website=sport.sky.it |date=20 September 2022 |language=it}}</ref> He returned to Italy at the end of his loan spell having made just one substitute appearance totalling 13 minutes all season.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.lfchistory.net/Players/Player/Profile/1404|title=LFC History Profile|date=31 May 2024|work=LFC History.net|accessdate=31 May 2024}}</ref>

====Loan to Fiorentina====
On 22 July 2023, Arthur joined Serie A club [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] on loan.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.acffiorentina.com/it/news/tutte/prima-squadra-maschile/2023-07-22/arthur-e-un-nuovo-calciatore-viola |title=Arthur è un nuovo calciatore viola |work=ACF Fiorentina |language=it |date=22 July 2023 |access-date=22 July 2023 |archive-date=22 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230722191543/https://www.acffiorentina.com/it/news/tutte/prima-squadra-maschile/2023-07-22/arthur-e-un-nuovo-calciatore-viola |url-status=dead }}</ref> On 29 May, he started in Fiorentina's 1–0 [[Extra time (association football)|extra-time]] defeat to [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] in the [[2024 UEFA Europa Conference League final|2024 UEFA Conference League final]].<ref name="El Kaabi floors Fiorentina">{{cite news |last1=Media |first1=P. A. |title=Olympiakos win Europa Conference League after El Kaabi floors Fiorentina |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/article/2024/may/29/olympiakos-fiorentina-europa-conference-league-final-match-report |access-date=30 May 2024 |work=The Guardian |date=29 May 2024}}</ref>

====Loan to Girona====
On 1 February 2025, Arthur joined Spanish club [[Girona FC|Girona]] for the remainder of the [[2024–25 Girona FC season|2024–25 season]].<ref>{{cite web |date=1 February 2025 |title=Arthur Melo, new Girona player |url=https://www.gironafc.cat/en/news/arthur-melo-nou-jugador-del-girona |access-date=1 February 2025 |publisher=[[Girona FC]]}}</ref>

====Loan to Grêmio====
He returned to [[Grêmio]] on loan for the 2025 and 2026 seasons.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.beinsports.com/en-us/soccer/serie-a/articles/arthur-completes-loan-return-to-gremio-from-juventus-2025-08-27|title=Arthur completes loan return to Gremio from Juventus|first=Arthur Melo will spend the upcoming season on loan with Gremio in his native Brazil, after they agreed a deal with|last=Juventus|website=beIN SPORTS}}</ref>

====Return to Juventus and contract termination====
Arthur rejoined Juventus in summer 2026, ahead of [[2026–27 Juventus FC season|their 2026–27 season]]; however on 21 August 2026, Juventus terminated his contract.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.beinsports.com/en-us/soccer/serie-a/articles/juventus-terminate-arthurs-contract-2026-08-21 |title=Juventus terminate Arthur's contract |publisher=beIN SPORTS |date=21 August 2026 }}</ref>

===Santos===
On 31 August 2026, Arthur was announced at [[Santos FC|Santos]] on a contract until December.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.santosfc.com.br/santos-fc-contrata-volante-arthur/|title=Santos FC contrata volante Arthur|trans-title=Santos FC sign defensive midfielder Arthur|publisher=Santos FC|language=pt-BR|date=31 August 2026|accessdate=31 August 2026}}</ref> He made his club debut on 6 September, replacing [[Gustavo Caballero]] in a 3–2 away win over [[SC Internacional|Internacional]].

==International career==
[[File:Headshot of Arthur Melo.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Arthur with the [[Brazil national football team|Brazil national team]] in the [[2019 Copa América Final]]]]
Arthur has represented Brazil in [[Brazil national under-17 football team|under-17]] level. He was part of the [[Brazil national under-17 football team|Brazil under-17]] squad selected to play in the [[2013 South American Under-17 Football Championship]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Volante Arthur é convocado para a Seleção Brasileira Sub-17|url=http://www2.gremio.net/news/view.aspx?id=15735&language=0|work=Portal Oficial do Grêmio|date=February 2013|access-date=13 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170914124835/http://www2.gremio.net/news/view.aspx?id=15735&language=0|archive-date=14 September 2017|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

On 15 September 2017, Arthur received his first senior call-up to the [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] squad to face [[Bolivia national football team|Bolivia]] and [[Chile national football team|Chile]] for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)|2018 FIFA World Cup qualification]]. In May 2018, he was named in the standby list for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Lista de 35 de Tite para a Copa tem três novatos: Dedé, Maicon e Paquetá|trans-title=Tite's 35-man list for the Cup has three new players: Dedé, Maicon and Paquetá|url=https://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/selecao-brasileira/noticia/lista-de-35-de-tite-para-a-copa-tem-tres-novatos-dede-maicon-e-paqueta.ghtml|work=Globo Esporte|language=pt|date=25 May 2018|access-date=9 July 2018}}</ref>

He made his international debut against [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]] in a 2–0 [[Exhibition game|friendly]] win on 7 September 2018 coming on as a substitute. The [[Brazilians|Brazilian]]'s first start was against [[El Salvador national football team|El Salvador]] in a 5–0 win on 12 September.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.barcablaugranes.com/2018/9/12/17849783/philippe-coutinho-on-target-for-brazil-as-arthur-makes-firts-start |title=Philippe Coutinho on target as Arthur makes first start |date=12 September 2018 |publisher=Barca Blaugranes |access-date=13 October 2018 }}{{Dead link|date=September 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>
[[Tite (football manager)|Tite]] praised the [[midfielder]]'s playing style saying, "He always finds the best escape, the best pass out. Even if he doesn't provide the assist, he comes up with the pass that will help a player."<ref name="escape">{{cite web |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/barcelona/2018/09/08/5b9428fce2704e64988b4615.html |title=Barcelona: Tite: Arthur always finds the best escape, the best pass out |date=8 September 2018 |publisher=Marca |access-date=9 September 2018}}</ref>

In May 2019, Arthur was included in Brazil's 23-man squad for the [[2019 Copa América]] on home soil.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.football-italia.net/138152/brazil-name-copa-america-squad |title=Brazil name Copa America squad |publisher=Football Italia |date=17 May 2019 |access-date=21 May 2019 }}</ref> In the [[2019 Copa América Final]] against hosts [[Peru national football team|Peru]] on 7 July, at the [[Maracanã Stadium]], Arthur assisted [[Gabriel Jesus]]'s match-winning goal towards the end of the first half; the match eventually ended in a 3–1 victory to Brazil.<ref name="2019 Copa América Final">{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2019/jul/06/copa-america-final-brazil-peru-live |title=Brazil 3-1 Peru |work=The Guardian |last1=Smyth |first1=Rob |date=7 July 2019 |access-date=8 July 2019 }}</ref>

Arthur scored his first senior international goal for Brazil on 17 November 2020, the opener in an eventual 2–0 away win over [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]] in a [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)|2022 FIFA World Cup qualifier]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.beinsports.com/en/football/news/arthur-enjoys-first-international-goal-as-b-1/1585213 |title=Arthur enjoys first international goal as Brazil stay perfect |publisher=beIN SPORTS |date=17 November 2020 |access-date=18 November 2020 }}</ref>

==Style of play==
{{quote box
| width = 33%
| align = right
| quote = "Arthur can mark an era at Barcelona."
| source = —Former Barcelona midfielder [[Xavi (footballer, born 1980)|Xavi]] on Arthur<ref name="Arthur can mark an era">{{Cite news |url=https://www.sport-english.com/en/news/barca/xavi-hernandez-arthur-can-mark-an-era-at-barcelona-7097503 |title=Xavi Hernandez "Arthur can mark an era at Barcelona" |work=Sport-English.com |last=Sport |date=12 October 2018 |access-date=23 October 2018 }}</ref>}}

Arthur is capable of playing as a [[deep-lying playmaker]], [[central midfielder]], [[box-to-box midfielder]], and occasionally also as a [[holding midfielder]]. His [[agility]], technical ability, [[Dribbling#Association football|dribbling]] and movement – both on and off the ball – allow him to create space and control the flow of play in [[midfield]], whilst his exceptional vision, [[Playmaker|playmaking]] ability, and precise passing allow him to retain possession, create chances, and make decisive passes for teammates.<ref name="escape" /> In 2020, former midfielder [[Enzo Maresca]] stated that he felt Arthur was best suited to the roles of either an [[Midfielder#Attacking midfielder|attacking midfielder]] or a ''[[Midfielder#Mezzala|mezzala]]''.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/altre-notizie/tmw-radio-maresca-sarri-va-aspettato-champions-attenti-al-manchester-city-e-pericoloso-1395897 |title=Maresca: "Sarri va aspettato. Champions? Attenti al Manchester City, è pericoloso" |publisher=Tutto Mercato Web |language=it |last1=Conti |first1=Dimitri |date=18 June 2020 |access-date=18 June 2020 }}</ref>

'''Gorka Iraizoz Moreno''' (born 6 March 1981) is a Spanish former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]]. He is currently a [[Manager (association football)|manager]].

He spent most of his 20-year senior career with [[Athletic Bilbao]], appearing in 392 official games.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.noticiasdenavarra.com/2016/04/22/deportes/futbol/gorka-iraizoz-batira-el-record-de-partidos-en-primera-de-unzue|title=Gorka Iraizoz batirá el récord de partidos en Primera de Unzué|trans-title=Gorka Iraizoz will break Unzué's record of games in ''Primera''|newspaper=Noticias de Navarra|language=es|date=22 April 2016|access-date=9 December 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220080623/http://www.noticiasdenavarra.com/2016/04/22/deportes/futbol/gorka-iraizoz-batira-el-record-de-partidos-en-primera-de-unzue|archive-date=20 December 2016}}</ref> In [[La Liga]] he also represented [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] and [[Girona FC|Girona]], winning the [[2006 Copa del Rey final|2006 Copa del Rey]] with the first club.

==Club career==
===Early career and Espanyol===
Iraizoz was born in [[Pamplona]], [[Navarre]] and raised in nearby [[Ansoáin]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.diariodenavarra.es/20090409/deportes/a-orbaiz-e-iraizoz-les-gusta-reyno.html|title=A Orbaiz e Iraizoz sí les gusta el Reyno|trans-title=Orbaiz and Iraizoz sure do like Reyno|newspaper=[[Diario de Navarra]]|first=Fernando|last=Ciordia|language=es|date=9 April 2009|access-date=2 August 2019}}</ref><ref name=Tugged>{{cite web|url=https://eldesmarque.com/bizkaia/athletic-club/noticias/60183-iraizoz-toco-la-fibra-de-los-athleticzales|title=Iraizoz tocó la fibra de los athleticzales|trans-title=Iraizoz tugged the heartstrings of the Athletic fans|publisher=El Desmarque|language=es|date=11 May 2017|access-date=2 August 2019}}</ref> After beginning his football career with local club [[UDC Chantrea]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundo/2010/02/08/paisvasco/1265621459.html|title=El fértil vivero navarro del Athletic|trans-title=Athletic's fertile Navarrese nursery|newspaper=El Mundo|first=Xabier|last=Garmendia|language=es|date=8 February 2010|access-date=27 June 2017}}</ref> he moved to the [[Basque Country (autonomous community)|Basque Country]] with [[Athletic Bilbao]], serving stints with affiliates [[CD Basconia]] and [[Bilbao Athletic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://bizkaia.eldesmarque.com/athletic-club/noticias/40757-mendilibar-iraizoz-es-el-mejor-portero-que-he-tenido-y-eso-que-le-eche-del-basconia|title=Mendilibar: "Iraizoz es el mejor portero que he tenido, y eso que le eché del Basconia"|trans-title=Mendilibar: "Iraizoz is the best goalkeeper I have ever had, and keep in mind I kicked him from Basconia"|publisher=El Desmarque|language=es|date=26 May 2014|access-date=27 June 2017}}</ref>

Arriving at [[RCD Espanyol]] in July 2002, Iraizoz spent two seasons with its [[RCD Espanyol B|B side]], also having a loan spell at [[SD Eibar]] in the [[Segunda División]].<ref name=Speaks>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2006/02/04/mas_futbol/1139038017_850215.html|title=Un navarro que habla catalán, que aprendió de Iríbar y creció en Éibar|trans-title=A Navarrese who speaks Catalan, who learned from Iríbar and grew in Éibar|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|first=Quique|last=Iglesias|language=es|date=4 February 2006|access-date=6 May 2016}}</ref> He made his [[La Liga]] debut on 21 December 2005, in a 2–1 away win against [[Deportivo de La Coruña]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2005/12/21/futbol/1135198921.html|title=El Espanyol alivia sus penas con dos zarpazos en Riazor|trans-title=Espanyol chase woes away with two blows at Riazor|newspaper=El Mundo|language=es|date=21 December 2005|access-date=15 June 2017}}</ref> He was second choice behind [[Carlos Kameni]] for the [[2006–07 La Liga|2006–07 season]],<ref>{{cite Cup|publisher=UEFA|first=Graham|last=Hunter|date=15 May 2007|access-date=10 March 2025}}</ref> but was the regular in the team's [[2006–07 UEFA Cup|run to the final]] of the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/competitions/uefacup/fixturesresults/round=2369/match=300124/report=fc.html|title=Iraizoz hoping for career During his time in [[Barcelona]], Iraizoz learned to speak fluent [[Catalan language|Catalan]].<ref name=Speaks/>

===Athletic Bilbao===
On 7 August 2007, Iraizoz signed for Athletic Bilbao for [[Euro|€]]4.6 million, returning to the club he spent one-and-a-half seasons with,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/01c4-0f84b48f5d12-72a07ceae4e3-1000--athletic-swoop-to-capture-iraizoz/|title=Athletic swoop to capture Iraizoz|publisher=UEFA|date=7 August 2007|access-date=10 March 2025}}</ref> this time as the undisputed starter.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://blogs.elcorreo.com/bizkaiasport/2008/12/07/futbol-athletic-iraizoz-veces-superman-veces/|title=FÚTBOL ATHLETIC. Iraizoz, a veces ''Superman'', a veces Aranzubia|trans-title=FOOTBALL ATHLETIC. Iraizoz, sometimes Superman, sometimes Aranzubia|newspaper=[[El Correo]]|language=es|date=7 December 2008|access-date=6 May 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160920041759/http://blogs.elcorreo.com/bizkaiasport/2008/12/07/futbol-athletic-iraizoz-veces-superman-veces/|archive-date=20 September 2016}}</ref> However, due to a severe injury, he was left out of the squad for the second part of [[2007–08 La Liga|the campaign]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/01c9-0f84b48f5c61-80e7d1043894-1000--athletic-lose-iraizoz-for-season/|title=Athletic lose Iraizoz for season|publisher=UEFA|date=18 January 2008|access-date=10 March 2025}}</ref> and his place (and shirt number) was taken by 37-year-old [[Armando Ribeiro|Armando]], signed from [[Cádiz CF]] until June 2008.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archivo.marca.com/edicion/marca/futbol/1a_division/athletic/es/desarrollo/1083333.html|title=El Athletic se refuerza con el meta Armando|trans-title=Athletic bolster with keeper Armando|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=28 January 2008|access-date=10 March 2025}}</ref>

In the opening match of [[2014–15 La Liga|2014–15]], at [[Málaga CF]], Iraizoz appeared to score a last-minute equaliser with a header, but the goal was disallowed, apparently incorrectly.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.foxsports.com/soccer/story/athletic-bilbao-robbed-of-late-goal-in-loss-to-malaga-082314|title=Malaga claim nervy win; Sevilla drop points to Valencia|publisher=[[Fox Sports]]|date=23 August 2014|access-date=29 August 2014}}</ref> Having lost his starting place to [[Kepa Arrizabalaga]], at the end of the [[2016–17 La Liga|2016–17 season]] Athletic announced that the 36-year-old would be leaving the club at the end of his contract.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://ecodiario.eleconomista.es/futbol/noticias/8335824/05/17/Urrutia-confirma-que-Iraizoz-no-seguira-en-el-Athletic-la-proxima-temporada.html|title=Urrutia confirma que Iraizoz no seguirá en el Athletic la próxima temporada|trans-title=Urrutia confirms Iraizoz will not continue at Athletic the next season|newspaper=[[El Economista (Spain)|El Economista]]|language=es|date=4 May 2017|access-date=24 May 2017}}</ref><ref name=Tugged/>

===Girona===
On 14 June 2017, Iraizoz agreed to a two-year deal at [[Girona FC]], [[2016–17 Segunda División|promoted to the top flight]] for the first time ever.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/fichajes/20170614/423397282864/gorka-iraizoz-primer-refuerzo-del-girona.html|title=Gorka Iraizoz, primer refuerzo del Girona|trans-title=Gorka Iraizoz, first Girona addition|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Sara|last=Giménez|language=es|date=14 June 2017|access-date=15 June 2017}}</ref> He spent most of his spell at the [[Estadi Montilivi]] as backup to [[Yassine Bounou]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/girona/2017/10/24/59ef22cd268e3e4e698b461c.html|title=Crónica de una suplencia anunciada|trans-title=Chronicle of a reserve foretold|newspaper=Marca|first=Alejandro|last=Segura|language=es|date=24 October 2017|access-date=14 December 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://eldesmarque.com/bizkaia/athletic-club/187206-iraizoz-se-deja-ver-de-nuevo-en-laliga|title=Iraizoz se deja ver de nuevo en LaLiga|trans-title=Iraizoz shows up in LaLiga again|publisher=El Desmarque|language=es|date=3 December 2018|access-date=14 December 2018}}</ref>

Iraizoz left the club at the end of the [[2018–19 La Liga|2018–19 campaign]], which ended in relegation.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/girona/2019/05/28/5ced392046163f55b68b45be.html|title=Aleix García y Gorka Iraizoz se despiden del Girona|trans-title=Aleix García and Gorka Iraizoz say goodbye to Girona|newspaper=Marca|first=Alejandro|last=Segura|language=es|date=28 May 2019|access-date=2 August 2019}}</ref> 

==International career==
Iraizoz never earned any [[Cap (sport)|caps]] for [[Spain national football team|Spain]] at any level. He did feature for the unofficial [[Basque Country national football team|Basque Country regional team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eff-fvf.eus/pub/verFichaPartido.asp?idioma=ca&idPartido=1261|title=Catalunya 0–1 Euskal Selekzioa|trans-title=Catalonia 0–1 Basque XI|publisher=[[Basque Football Federation]]|language=es|date=26 December 2015|access-date=29 December 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190327090021/http://www.eff-fvf.eus/pub/verFichaPartido.asp?idioma=ca&idPartido=1261|archive-date=27 March 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eitb.eus/es/deportes/futbol/detalle/7631821/seleccion-vasca-euskal-selekzioa-jugadores-partidos-1979/|title=Xabi Prieto, el jugador con más partidos desde 1979|trans-title=Xabi Prieto, the player with the most matches since 1979|publisher=[[EITB]]|language=es|date=13 November 2020|access-date=11 March 2025}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
After retiring aged 38, Iraizoz later worked as manager of Barakaldo's youths, goalkeeper coach of its first team and assistant at [[Gernika Club]] and [[SD Logroñés]] under former Athletic player [[Aitor Larrazábal]]. After the latter became Gernika's [[sporting director]] in May 2024, he named him head coach at the [[Segunda Federación]] side;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.eldesmarque.com/futbol/athletic-club/20240522/aitor-larrazabal-iraizoz-gernika_300341494.html|title=Aitor Larrazabal y Gorka Iraizoz, caras del nuevo proyecto del Gernika|trans-title=Aitor Larrazabal and Gorka Iraizoz, faces of Gernika's new project|publisher=El Desmarque|first=Asís|last=Martín|language=es|date=22 May 2024|access-date=10 March 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.deia.eus/futbol/2024/06/14/gorka-irairoz-sube-escalafon-gernika-8360281.html|title=Gorka Iraizoz sube de escalafón en el Gernika|trans-title=Gorka Iraizoz moves up the ranks at Gernika|newspaper=[[Deia (newspaper)|Deia]]|first=Unai|last=Muñoz|language=es|date=14 June 2024|access-date=11 October 2024}}</ref> he [[2024–25 Segunda Federación|avoided relegation]] in the last match of his sole season, then left.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.deia.eus/futbol/2025/06/06/gorka-iraizoz-deja-banquillo-gernika-9728581.html|title=Gorka Iraizoz deja el banquillo del Gernika tras una campaña complicada|trans-title=Gorka Iraizoz leaves bench of Gernika after difficult campaign|newspaper=Deia|first=Pako|last=Ruiz|language=es|date=6 June 2025|access-date=23 September 2026}}</ref>

'''Renato Dirnei Florêncio Santos''' (born 15 May 1979), known simply as '''Renato''', is a Brazilian former professional [[association football|footballer]].

A [[central midfielder]] with good heading ability in spite of a small frame, he played most of his professional career in Spain with [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]], appearing in 286 official games with the club (39 goals scored).

A [[Brazil national football team|Brazilian international]] during two years, Renato was part of the squads that won [[2004 Copa América|one]] [[Copa América]] and [[2005 FIFA Confederations Cup|one]] [[FIFA Confederations Cup|Confederations Cup]].

==Club career==
===Guarani===
Renato was born in [[Santa Mercedes]], [[São Paulo (state)|São Paulo]]. Known as ''Renatinho'' during his beginnings, he was a [[Guarani FC]] youth graduate, and made his senior debut on 17 April 1996 when he started in a 1–0 [[Campeonato Paulista]] home loss against [[São Paulo FC]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.jogosdoguarani.com/1996/1996.html|title=Guarani 0x1 São Paulo|publisher=Jogos do Guarani|language=pt|access-date=7 December 2015}}</ref> He scored his first professional goal on 6 September 1998, netting the first in a 2–0 home win over [[Sport Club Internacional]].

===Santos===
In June 2000, Renato moved to fellow top-level club [[Santos FC]] for a [[Brazilian real|R$]]2 million fee.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://acervo.folha.uol.com.br/fsp/2000/07/11/20//588435|title=Santos negocia volta de Viola após um ano|trans-title=Santos negotiate Viola's return after a year|newspaper=[[Folha de S.Paulo]]|language=pt|date=11 July 2000|access-date=7 December 2015}}</ref> He made his competitive debut on 2 August, starting in a 2–0 home success over [[Esporte Clube Vitória]].

Renato scored his first goal for the ''Fish'' on 7 February 2001, netting the first in a 3–0 home win against [[CR Vasco da Gama]] for the [[Torneio Rio–São Paulo]] championship.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://acervo.folha.uol.com.br/fsp/2001/02/08/20//7188|title=Santos derrota o Vasco e avança no Rio-São Paulo|trans-title=Santos defeat Vasco and advance in Rio-São Paulo|newspaper=Folha de S.Paulo|language=pt|date=11 July 2000|access-date=7 December 2015}}</ref> He added a further five during [[2001 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|the campaign]], being a regular starter.

In 2003, Renato scored a career-best nine goals in the year's ''Brasileirão'', and was also an ever-present figure for the team in their [[Copa Libertadores]] run.

===Sevilla===
[[File:Renato.jpg|thumb|left|160px|Renato in training with [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]]]]
On 7 July 2004, Renato signed a five-year contract with [[Sevilla FC]] from Spain, aged 25.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0257-0de66d15078f-eaa8ab3bf085-1000--renato-and-sales-head-for-seville/|title=Renato and Sales head for Seville|publisher=UEFA|date=7 July 2004|access-date=23 June 2016}}</ref> Alongside compatriots [[Adriano (footballer, born 1984)|Adriano]] and [[Dani Alves|Daniel Alves]], as well as several club youth graduates, he would play an essential part in the [[Andalusia]]ns' [[La Liga]] consolidation, making his competition debut on 29 August: after just one minute on the pitch, in the start of the second half of the home fixture against [[Albacete Balompié]], he scored the game's only goal.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Fuertes |first1=Santiago Fernández |url=http://elpais.com/diario/2004/08/30/deportes/1093816830_850215.html|title=Renato debuta y salva la papeleta al Sevilla|trans-title=Renato makes debut and saves Sevilla's bacon|newspaper=[[El País]]|language=es|date=30 August 2004|access-date=23 June 2016}}</ref>

From 2005 to 2007, Renato played 16 [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]] games in both seasons combined, as Sevilla won the tournament twice in a row. His only goal was a decisive one, as he scored in the 2–0 home win against [[CA Osasuna]] in the second leg of the semi-finals of the [[2006–07 UEFA Cup|2006–07 edition]] (2–1 on aggregate);<ref>{{cite web|url=http://archivo.marca.com/edicion/marca/futbol/uefa/previaxcronica/es/desarrollo/987135.html|title=El Sevilla sigue soñando con el triplete|trans-title=Sevilla are still dreaming of treble|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=3 May 2007|access-date=23 June 2016}}</ref> he was also utilized in both finals.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0252-0cd9b1313b03-1633022547b9-1000--sevilla-run-away-with-the-trophy/|title=Sevilla run away with the trophy|publisher=UEFA|date=11 May 2006|access-date=23 June 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/01c1-0e82f2d9a67d-e255bf07c44c-1000--palop-ensures-cup-joy-for-sevilla/|title=Palop ensures cup joy for Sevilla|publisher=UEFA|date=17 May 2007|access-date=23 June 2016}}</ref>

In the [[2008–09 La Liga|2008–09 season]], Renato netted eight times in 32 matches to help the side finish in third position. Four of those came from December 2008 to January 2009, against [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] (4–3 win, away),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1202817745826/1202757180081/noticia/Cronica/Great_effort_goes_unrewarded.htm|title=Great effort goes unrewarded|publisher=Real Madrid C.F|date=7 December 2008|access-date=3 May 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120915051948/http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/en/1202817745826/1202757180081/noticia/Cronica/Great_effort_goes_unrewarded.htm|archive-date=15 September 2012}}</ref> [[Villarreal CF]] (1–0, at home),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=978374.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120829082220/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=978374.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=29 August 2012|title=Sevilla's Renato plays hero again|publisher=FIFA|date=14 December 2008|access-date=3 May 2011}}</ref> [[Deportivo de La Coruña]] (3–1 triumph, away)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2009/01/10/mas_futbol/1231542041_850215.html|title=El Sevilla se levanta con uno menos y remonta ante el Deportivo|trans-title=Sevilla rise with one less and come back from behind against Deportivo|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|language=es|date=10 January 2009|access-date=23 June 2016}}</ref> and [[CD Numancia]] (1–0, at home).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/marcador/futbol/2008_09/primera/jornada_19/sev_num/|title=Renato rescata un barco a la deriva|trans-title=Renato rescues drifting boat|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=17 January 2009|access-date=15 May 2014}}</ref>

On 4 October 2009, Renato scored through a header in a 2–1 home win against Real Madrid.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2009/oct/04/real-madrid-sevilla-renato|title=Renato uses his head to earn Sevilla victory against Real Madrid|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=4 October 2009|access-date=3 May 2011}}</ref> He contributed with 33 games and four goals to Sevilla's [[2009–10 La Liga|fourth-place finish]], with the subsequent [[2010–11 UEFA Champions League|qualification]] to the [[UEFA Champions League]]; at the end of the campaign he extended his link to the club for a further year, until June 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01e5-0e74a6b7522c-03a728dda28f-1000--renato-signs-on-at-sevilla/|title=Renato signs on at Sevilla|publisher=UEFA|date=28 May 2010|access-date=3 May 2011}}</ref>

===Botafogo===
On 26 May 2011, Renato cut ties with Sevilla by mutual agreement and signed a three-year contract with [[Botafogo de Futebol e Regatas]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/584/brazil/2011/05/26/2504824/official-renato-leaves-sevilla-for-botafogo|title=Official: Renato leaves Sevilla for Botafogo|publisher=Goal|date=26 May 2011|access-date=26 May 2011}}</ref> He was a regular starter during his first two years at the club, forming a strong midfield unit alongside internationals [[Nicolás Lodeiro]] and [[Clarence Seedorf]], but later served as a backup to [[Gabriel Girotto Franco|Gabriel]]; he was also marred by injuries during the [[2013 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|2013 season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://esporte.uol.com.br/futebol/campeonatos/brasileiro/serie-a/ultimas-noticias/2013/11/18/artesao-renato-vira-picasso-e-salvador-dali-e-renasce-no-botafogo.htm|title="Artesão", Renato renasce no Bota em fase decisiva e briga por espaço|trans-title="Craftsman", Renato is reborn at ''Bota'' in decisive phase and fights for a place|work=[[Universo Online]]|language=pt|date=18 November 2013|access-date=17 May 2014}}</ref>

===Santos return===
[[File:Renato em partida válida pelo Campeonato Brasileiro de 2017 (35019226533) (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|upright|Renato in action for [[Santos FC|Santos]] in 2017]]
On 13 May 2014, Renato left Botafogo and returned to Santos, signing a deal until the end of [[2014 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|the campaign]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Movenext. Com. Br|first1=Movenext -.|url=http://santosfc.com.br/2014/05/santos-fc-acerta-retorno-volante-renato/|title=Santos FC acerta retorno do volante Renato|work=Santos Futebol Clube - Site Oficial|trans-title=Santos FC agree return of defensive midfielder Renato|publisher=Santos FC|language=pt|date=13 May 2014|access-date=17 May 2014|archive-date=17 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140517133041/http://santosfc.com.br/2014/05/santos-fc-acerta-retorno-volante-renato/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was named among the [[Substitute (association football)|substitutes]] two days later, but remained unused during the 4–2 home win against [[Princesa do Solimões Esporte Clube]].

After struggling with injuries, Renato was mainly used as a backup to [[Arouca (footballer)|Arouca]] and [[Alison Lopes Ferreira|Alison]], playing as a [[defensive midfielder]]. On 13 January 2015, despite appearing in only 14 matches after his return, he renewed his contract for a further year.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Clube|first1=Santos Futebol|url=http://santosfc.com.br/2015/01/renato-assina-contrato-por-mais-uma-temporada/|title=Renato assina contrato por mais uma temporada|work=Santos Futebol Clube - Site Oficial|trans-title=Renato signs contract for a further season|publisher=Santos FC|language=pt|date=13 January 2015|access-date=15 January 2015|archive-date=16 January 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150116021820/http://santosfc.com.br/2015/01/renato-assina-contrato-por-mais-uma-temporada/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 1 March 2015, Renato scored his first goal after his return, netting his team's second in a 4–2 home win over [[Clube Atlético Linense]]. He was a regular starter during [[2015 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|the season]], partnering [[Thiago Maia]] and contributing with 53 appearances and two goals.

On 13 April 2016, aged already 36, Renato agreed to an extension with Santos until the end of 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.santosfc.com.br/2016/04/idolo-volante-renato-renova-contrato-com-o-peixe-ate-dezembro-de-2017/|title=Ídolo, volante Renato renova contrato com o Peixe até dezembro de 2017|trans-title=Idol, defensive midfielder Renato renews contract with the Fish until December 2017|publisher=Santos FC|language=pt|date=13 April 2016|access-date=17 April 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160817173721/http://www.santosfc.com.br/2016/04/idolo-volante-renato-renova-contrato-com-o-peixe-ate-dezembro-de-2017/|archive-date=17 August 2016}}</ref> The following 27 January, after being an ever-present figure during [[2016 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|the year]], he renewed his contract until December 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.santosfc.com.br/2017/01/idolo-do-santos-fc-meia-renato-prorroga-contrato-ate-31-de-dezembro-de-2018/|title=Ídolo do Santos FC, meia Renato prorroga contrato até 31 de dezembro de 2018|trans-title=Santos FC idol, midfielder Renato extends contract until 31 December 2018|publisher=Santos FC|language=pt|date=27 January 2017|access-date=28 January 2017|archive-date=2 February 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202061923/http://www.santosfc.com.br/2017/01/idolo-do-santos-fc-meia-renato-prorroga-contrato-ate-31-de-dezembro-de-2018/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 18 September 2018, Renato was announced the new [[director of football]] of Santos in immediate effect, whilst acting also as a player until the expiration of his contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://globoesporte.globo.com/sp/santos-e-regiao/futebol/times/santos/noticia/renato-e-o-novo-executivo-de-futebol-do-santos.ghtml|title=Renato é o novo executivo de futebol do '''Celestine Hycieth Babayaro''' (born 29 August 1978) is a Nigerian former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|left-back]] or a [[midfielder]].

Babayaro spent the majority of his career playing in the [[Premier League]], mainly for [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] from 1997 to 2005, and then later for [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]], from 2005 to 2008. He had a brief stint at [[Major League Soccer|MLS]] club [[LA Galaxy]], but never officially played for the club. He retired as a free agent in 2010.

Babayaro represented the [[Nigeria national football team]] from 1995 to 2004 and was part of two [[Summer Olympics|Olympic]] squads, two [[FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] squads and three [[African Cup of Nations]] squads.

==Club career==
===Early career===
Born in [[Kaduna (city)|Kaduna]],<ref name="Hugman"/> Babayaro began his playing career at Nigerian side [[Plateau United]], before moving to Belgian club [[RSC Anderlecht|Anderlecht]] in 1994, and eventually would make a name for himself, quickly gaining first-choice status although still a [[teenager]]. Babayaro set records as the youngest player to make an appearance and to receive a red card in the [[UEFA Champions League]]. He was sent off in a match against [[FC Steaua București|Steaua București]] in a 1–1 draw, aged 16 years and 86 days.

===Chelsea===
Babayaro was signed by [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] after being spotted by scout Lewis Durkin in April 1997. He moved for a transfer fee of £2.25 million,<ref>{{cite news |title=Babayaro to join Bridge foreign legion |first=Tommy |last=Staniforth |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/babayaro-to-join-bridge-foreign-legion-1268683.html |work=The Independent |publisher=Independent Print Limited |date=22 April 1997 |access-date=18 April 2012 }}</ref> a club record paid for a teenager at the time.{{Citation needed|date=August 2008}} He made his debut in the [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup]] against [[ŠK Slovan Bratislava|Slovan Bratislava]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sportinglife.com/football/news/article/165/7811687/slovan-bratislava-0-chelsea-2-agg-0-4|title=Slovan Bratislava 0 Chelsea 2 (Agg 0–4)|publisher=Sporting Life|date=2 October 1997|access-date=1 December 2013|archive-date=4 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131204023919/http://www.sportinglife.com/football/news/article/165/7811687/slovan-bratislava-0-chelsea-2-agg-0-4|url-status=dead}}</ref> but an injury sustained in the 6–1 win over rivals [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] in December 1997<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-tottenhams-revival-hopes-threatened-by-venglos-factor-1287524.html|title=Tottenham's revival hopes threatened by Venglos factor |newspaper=The Independent|date=8 December 1997 |access-date=1 December 2013}}</ref> ruled him out for the rest of the season. This meant he missed their victories in the [[1998 Football League Cup final]] and the [[1998 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup final]]. However, with Chelsea he went on to win the [[1998 UEFA Super Cup]], the [[2000 FA Cup final|FA Cup]]<ref>{{cite news |title=Chelsea claim FA Cup glory |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/sport/football/fa_cup/756784.stm |work=BBC News |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=20 May 2000 |access-date=18 April 2012 }}</ref> and [[2000 FA Charity Shield|Charity Shield]] in 2000,<ref>{{cite news |title=Keane sees red as Chelsea triumph |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/879061.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=13 August 2000 |access-date=18 April 2012 }}</ref> and reached the [[2002 FA Cup final]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/fa_cup/1959840.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=16 February 2003 |access-date=18 April 2012 |title=Arsenal lift FA Cup}}</ref> He was also instrumental in Chelsea's run in the [[1999–2000 UEFA Champions League]]. Babayaro was sent off in extra time against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], as they bowed out of the competition at the quarter final stage.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/sport/football/champions_league/717082.stm|title=Chelsea's European dream shattered|publisher=[[BBC]]|date=18 April 2000 |access-date=1 December 2013}}</ref> He faced competition from [[Graeme Le Saux]] during his seven-year spell, but managed to play over 200 games for the club. His acrobatic celebrations with [[Flip (acrobatic)|backflips]] were noted by the fans of the club.

The steady form of [[Wayne Bridge]] saw Babayaro start only four [[The Football Association|FA]] [[Premier League]] matches for Chelsea in [[2004–05 Chelsea F.C. season|2004–05]] under new manager [[José Mourinho]]. Chelsea ended the season as Premier League champions.

===Newcastle United===
In January 2005, he left [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] to join [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] on an undisclosed fee,<ref>{{cite news |title=Newcastle to unveil Babayaro |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/n/newcastle_united/4131987.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=30 December 2004 |access-date=18 April 2012 }}</ref> where he established himself as first-choice left-back. He scored his first and what turned out to be his only Newcastle goal in a 3–1 win over [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]] in the [[2004–05 FA Cup|FA Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/fa_cup/4197699.stm|title=Newcastle 3–1 Coventry |publisher=BBC|date=29 January 2005 |access-date=6 November 2009}}</ref>

In September 2006, Babayaro was given a three-match ban by [[The Football Association]] for slapping [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] striker [[Dirk Kuyt]] in the face,<ref>{{cite news |title=Babayaro hit with three-match ban |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/n/newcastle_united/5370844.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=22 September 2006 |access-date=18 April 2012 }}</ref> while Liverpool took a corner. The slap was not seen by the referee [[Mark Halsey]], but later footage showed Babayaro punch the Dutchman in the face. Babayaro accepted the allegations and apologised to Kuyt.
[[File:Babayaro.jpg|thumb|upright|Babayaro in 2007]]
On 10 February 2007, after a 2–1 win over Liverpool, then-Newcastle manager [[Glenn Roeder]] revealed that just 12 hours before kick-off, Babayaro had called him saying his younger brother David had died from [[tuberculosis]]. Despite this, Babayaro insisted he would still play and put in a solid performance which earned him praise from Roeder and the fans. This fine form continued into United's 3–1 away victory against [[S.V. Zulte Waregem|Zulte Waregem]], in the [[2006–07 UEFA Cup|UEFA Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nufc.co.uk.p.preprod.performgroup.com/page/News/Features/0,,10278~979304,00.html|title=Brave Baba's secret sorrow|publisher=Nufc.premiumtv.co.uk|access-date=5 April 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180406163408/http://www.nufc.co.uk.p.preprod.performgroup.com/page/News/Features/0,,10278~979304,00.html|archive-date=6 April 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Due to his many injury problems it was mutually decided, on 10 December 2007, that Babayaro should be released from his contract with immediate effect and a compensation figure was agreed.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/nufc/newcastle-united-news/tm_headline=bye-bye-babayaro%26method=full%26objectid=20229434%26siteid=72703-name_page.html |title=Bye Bye Babayaro |date=4 November 2023 |publisher=Chroniclelive.co.uk }}</ref>

In January 2009, former Newcastle chairman [[Freddy Shepherd]] described Babayaro as a "disgrace" who "didn't pull his weight" during a televised BBC interview.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/7856971.stm | work=BBC News | title=Shepherd regrets over missed opportunity | date=28 January 2009 | access-date=28 April 2010}}</ref>

===Later career===
On 21 January 2008, 30-year-old Babayaro came to an agreement with the [[LA Galaxy]] to join them on a three-year contract, effective immediately.<ref>{{cite web|last=Idaho |first=Duncan |url=http://mlssoccernews.blogspot.com/2008/01/babayaro-to-la-galaxy.html |title=MLS Soccer News – Transfers | Trades | Signings | Rumors: Babayaro to LA Galaxy |publisher=Mlssoccernews.blogspot.com |date=21 January 2008 }}</ref>

With this move, the Nigerian re-joined Galaxy coach [[Ruud Gullit]] who previously brought him to [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in 1997 and spent a season coaching him there. This time again, it was the recently hired Gullit who wanted Babayaro at his new club. However, it did not take long for the move to turn sour. Thinking that he had arrived at sort of an American superclub that only a year earlier gave [[David Beckham]] what was widely reported to be the $250 million contract, Babayaro was agitated by what he considered to be "shabby" accommodations – from having to fly in the economy class to sharing a hotel room on the road.<ref>''The Beckham Experiment'', Grant Wahl, Three Rivers Press (paperback edition), New York, Pp.177–178</ref> His lack of commitment in training and preseason games{{citation needed|date=December 2021}} reflected those feelings, and he soon got on Gullit's and club president and general manager [[Alexi Lalas]]'s bad side.

On 3 March, Babayaro was waived by the Galaxy after playing only 45 minutes in a preseason friendly against [[FC Seoul]], receiving a yellow card and conceding a penalty in the process. The reason for this unexpected release was not stated explicitly by Galaxy front office. "After a period of evaluation, it was decided that it would be in the best interest of the club and the player to part ways," Lalas said in a statement. "It is unfortunate that it did not work out, but Ruud and our technical staff are hard at work putting together this team and difficult decisions have to be made."<ref>{{cite news |year=2008 |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/soccer/la-spw-soccer7mar07,1,1631712.story |title=Babayaro doesn't last with Galaxy |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |access-date=5 February 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080312030646/http://www.latimes.com/sports/soccer/la-spw-soccer7mar07%2C1%2C1631712.story |archive-date=12 March 2008 |url-status=dead  }}</ref>

During pre-season for the 2008–09 English league season, Babayaro trained with [[Premier League]] club [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] at the invitation of manager [[Harry Redknapp]] with a view to signing for the [[FA Cup]] holders.<ref>{{cite web | year=2008 | url=http://www.portsmouthfc.co.uk/index.php?cms_ref=news&fm_type=&fm_string=&fm_article_page_num=&qs_articleid=1330&qs_media=html&qs_slideshow_b3b4_index=2 | title=New Season, Same Hunger | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120309182744/http://www.portsmouthfc.co.uk/index.php?cms_ref=news&fm_type=&fm_string=&fm_article_page_num=&qs_articleid=1330&qs_media=html&qs_slideshow_b3b4_index=2 | archive-date=9 March 2012 | df=dmy-all }}</ref> On 14 August 2008, Redknapp revealed that he would not offer Babayaro a contract at [[Fratton Park]].<ref>{{cite web | year=2008 | url=http://www.portsmouth.co.uk/sport/Babayaro-no-go-but-Jordi.4389328.jp | archive-url=https://archive.today/20120907104606/http://www.portsmouth.co.uk/sport/Babayaro-no-go-but-Jordi.4389328.jp | url-status=dead | archive-date=7 September 2012 | title=Babayaro a no go but Jordi has a chance }}</ref>

On 8 July 2010, Babayaro officially announced his retirement from football.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://allafrica.com/stories/201007080155.html|title=Nigeria: Babayaro Quits Professional Football|date=8 July 2010|work=Daily Champion (Lagos)|access-date=14 May 2018}}</ref>

==International career==
After being part of the victorious Nigerian team at the Under-17 World Championships in 1993, Babayaro made his [[Nigeria national football team|international senior]] debut in the [[Afro-Asian Cup of Nations#1995 Afro-Asian Cup of Nations|Afro-Asian Cup of Nations]] in 1995, against [[Uzbekistan national football team|Uzbekistan]]. The following year, he was part of the Nigeria Olympic [[gold medal]] winning team at the [[Football at the 1996 Summer Olympics|1996 Summer Olympics]] in [[Atlanta]], making the tournament's all-star team. He scored in the gold medal game itself against Argentina. After getting a knee injury in December 1997 in the Premier League, Babayaro recovered just in time to make the [[1998 FIFA World Cup|France 98]] squad. He was also Nigeria's captain at the [[Football at the 2000 Summer Olympics|2000 Summer Olympics]] in [[Sydney]], and took part in the [[2002 FIFA World Cup|Korea/Japan 2002 FIFA World Cup]].

Babayaro was part of Nigeria's squad for the [[2004 African Nations Cup]] in [[Tunisia]], but was controversially{{according to whom|date=December 2021}} sent home, alongside [[Yakubu (footballer)|Yakubu]] and [[Victor Agali]] for indiscipline. Although never officially announcing his retirement from international football, his final appearance from the national team was against [[Morocco national football team|Morocco]] in a group stage match.

==Personal life==
Celestine Babayaro's brother, [[Emmanuel Babayaro|Emmanuel]], a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]], was also part of Nigeria's 1996 Olympics gold medal-winning team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.spiegel.de/spiegel/print/d-17114495.html |title=Migration: Der Doppelpass des Nigerianers |publisher=Spiegel.de |date=14 August 2000 }}</ref>

Babayaro was acquitted of indecent assault in 1999.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/uk/410396.stm |title=Footballer cleared of indecent assault |work=BBC News |publisher=BBC |date=2 August 1999 |access-date=25 August 2013}}</ref> He later sued the ''[[Daily Star (United Kingdom)|Daily Star]]'' for a headline suggesting he had been charged with rape and won an apology and damages.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11668/2188426/babayaro-wins-libel-case|title=BABAYARO WINS LIBEL CASE|publisher=Sky Sports|access-date=26 June 2017}}</ref>
