'''Luca Marchegiani''' ({{IPA|it|ˈluːka markeˈdʒaːni}}; born 22 February 1966) is an Italian former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]].

He represented several Italian clubs throughout his career, in particular [[Torino FC|Torino]] and [[SS Lazio|Lazio]], where he won various titles. At international level, he played for the [[Italy national football team|Italy national team]] in the [[1994 FIFA World Cup]], where they reached the [[1994 FIFA World Cup Final|final]].

He holds the longest unbeaten streak in Lazio's history, as well as the joint [[Football records in Italy#Goalkeeping|eighth-highest unbeaten streak in Serie A]], alongside [[Gianluigi Buffon]], having gone 745 consecutive minutes without conceding a goal in the Italian top division.<ref>{{cite web|language=Italian|url=https://www.repubblica.it/sport/2016/03/10/foto/buffon_e_gli_altri_i_record_di_imbattibilita_della_serie_a-135170251/1/#8|title=Buffon e gli altri: i record di imbattibilità. Il n.1 della Juventus sul trono con 974'|website=repubblica.it|date=20 March 2016|accessdate=2 July 2020}}</ref>

==Club career==
After beginning his professional career with [[Jesina Calcio|Jesi]] in 1986, for one season in the lower divisions, and subsequently [[Brescia Calcio|Brescia]] for a [[1987–88 Serie B|season]], in [[Serie B]], Marchegiani spent the majority of his career at [[Torino FC]] and [[SS Lazio]]. With Torino (1988–1993), he won the [[1992–93 Coppa Italia|Coppa Italia]] in 1993, and a [[1990–91 Serie B|Serie B title]] and a [[Mitropa Cup]] in 1991, earning promotion to [[Serie A]]; he also finished runner-up in the [[1993 Supercoppa Italiana]] and the [[1991–92 UEFA Cup]], and managed a third-place finish in [[Serie A]] during the [[1991–92 Serie A|1991–92 season]], whilst playing for the club.<ref name="Treccani">{{cite book|language=Italian|author=Enrico Maida|url=http://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/luca-marchegiani_(Enciclopedia-dello-Sport)|chapter=MARCHEGIANI, Luca|title=Enciclopedia dello Sport|year=2002|pages=754–755}}</ref>

At one point in his career, Marchegiani was the most expensive goalkeeper in the world, when he joined Lazio from Torino in 1993 for £6m;<ref name=refindependant>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080530122355/http://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/scottish/pound9m-custodian-who-breaks-footballs-no-1-rule-460631.html £9m custodian who breaks football's No 1 rule]</ref> during this period he was regarded as one of the best and most reliable goalkeepers in Italy and in world football. During his time with Lazio he won the [[1999–2000 Serie A|Serie A]], two [[Coppa Italia|Italian Cups]], two [[Supercoppa Italiana|Italian Supercups]], an [[1998–99 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup|UEFA Cup Winners' Cup]], and an [[1999 UEFA Super Cup|UEFA Super Cup]], also reaching another [[1998 UEFA Cup Final|UEFA Cup Final in 1998]]. In 2003, he moved to and ended his playing career at [[AC ChievoVerona|ChievoVerona]], where he remained until retiring in 2005.<ref name="Treccani"/>

==International career==
Marchegiani played for [[Italy national football team]] on 9 occasions between 1991 and 1996. He was initially selected by [[Arrigo Sacchi]] as the successor of the former first-choice keeper [[Walter Zenga]],<ref>{{cite news|language=Italian|title=Sacchi ha deciso: fuori Zenga|newspaper=Corriere della Sera|author=Fabio Monti|page=34|date=5 September 1992}}</ref> but lost his place after a mediocre performance in a 2–2 draw against [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]] during the [[1994 FIFA World Cup qualification]]:<ref name=garanzini>{{cite news|title=Le pagelle di un anno|newspaper=[[Corriere della Sera]]|author=Gigi Garanzini|language=Italian|page=29|date=28 June 1993}}</ref> he conceded the first goal, scored by [[Christophe Ohrel]], after failing to catch a cross, an unusual mistake for him, and then poorly controlled a [[Back-pass rule|back-pass]] with his feet, enabling the opposing striker [[Stéphane Chapuisat]] to score for the second time.<ref>{{cite news|language=Italian|title=Il cuore è grande, ma l'Italia no|author=Giancarlo Padovan|newspaper=Corriere della Sera|page=42|date=15 October 1992}}</ref>

At the [[1994 FIFA World Cup]] he was selected as Italy's second-choice keeper behind [[Gianluca Pagliuca]], who was more skilled with the ball at his feet,<ref>{{cite web|language=Italian|author=Matteo Botti|url=https://www.lalaziosiamonoi.it/non-solo-lazio/marchegiani-ricorda-orgoglioso-la-sua-parata-piu-bella-in-supercoppa-europea-con-la-lazio-un-intervento-impossibile-40283|title=Marchegiani ricorda orgoglioso la sua parata più bella: "In Supercoppa Europea con la Lazio, un intervento impossibile"|website=lalaziosiamonoi.it|date=2 January 2014}}</ref> but still managed to play three matches:<ref name=reffifa>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080701162440/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/statisticsandrecords/players/player=77250/index.html FIFA Player Statistics: Luca Marchegiani]</ref> his first appearance was as a substitute against [[Norway national football team|Norway]], following the sending off of Pagliuca, coming on for [[Roberto Baggio]], and helping the 10-man Italian squad to keep a clean sheet and win the match 1–0; he also appeared in the final group match against [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]] (a 1–1 draw), and in the 2–1 extra-time victory over [[Nigeria national football team|Nigeria]] in the round of 16.<ref name=fifa2>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/archive/edition=84/results/matches/match=3064/report.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071014125714/http://fifa.com/worldcup/archive/edition=84/results/matches/match=3064/report.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=14 October 2007|title=1994 FIFA World Cup USA|publisher=FIFA.com|accessdate=16 December 2015}}</ref> Despite Marchegiani's excellent performances, which led some pundits to advocate his confirmation, Pagliuca recovered the starting spot after his two-game suspension,<ref>{{cite news|language=Italian|author=Fabrizio Bocca|url=http://ricerca.repubblica.it/repubblica/archivio/repubblica/1994/07/09/pagliuca-il-posto-mio-marchegiani.html|title=Pagliuca: "Il posto è mio". Marchegiani in silenzio|newspaper=la Repubblica|date=9 July 1994}}</ref> and played the remaining games. Italy reached the [[1994 FIFA World Cup Final|final]], where they lost to [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] on [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.figc.it/nazionali/DettaglioConvocato|title=Nazionale in cifre: Marchegiani, Luca|website=www.figc.it|language=Italian|accessdate=22 April 2015}}</ref>

==Style of play==
A consistent, elegant, intelligent, composed and complete goalkeeper, Marchegiani is regarded as one of the best goalkeepers of his generation. He was known in particular for his agility, positional sense, reactions, and his speed when [[Goalkeeper (association football)#Sweeper-keeper|rushing off his line]], as well as his efficient technique, reliable handling, movement, and his ability to read the game; in particular, he stood out throughout his career for his outstanding ability to come out and claim crosses and high balls. In addition to his shot-stopping abilities, he was also remembered for his professionalism, as well as his dedication.<ref name="Treccani"/><ref name=ilportiere>{{cite web|url=http://ilportiere.com/interviste/interviste-portieri/luca-marchegiani-storia-di-un-portiere-vero/964-luca-marchegiani-storia-di-un-portiere-vero.html|title=Luca Marchegiani: "storia di un portiere vero".|accessdate=12 November 2014 |last1=Com |first1=Ilportiere }}</ref><ref name="Sarti vota Marchegiani">{{cite web|url=http://www.archiviolastampa.it/component/option,com_lastampa/task,search/mod,libera/action,viewer/Itemid,3/page,33/articleid,0696_01_1995_0056_0041_10284763/|title=Sarti vota Marchegiani|publisher=La Stampa|page=41|language=Italian|date=26 February 1995|accessdate=1 September 2016}}</ref><ref name="lalaziosiamonoi">{{cite web|url=http://www.lalaziosiamonoi.it/news/marchegiani-svela-ho-avuto-la-possibilita-di-giocare-nella-roma-ma-poi-su-gascoigne-32329|title=Marchegiani svela: "Ho avuto la possibilità di giocare nella Roma, ma...". 18 penalties in Serie A from 69 attempts in 422 appearances between 1988 and 2005, with a career save percentage of 26.1%; he has saved the [[Football records in Italy#Most penalties saved|fourth–highest number of penalties in Serie A history]]. During the [[2003–04 Serie A|2003–04 season]], he saved five spot kicks.<ref name="I 7 portieri pararigori della storia della Serie A">{{cite web|url=http://www.today.it/sport/portieri-pararigori-serie-a.html|title=I 7 portieri pararigori della storia della Serie A|publisher=Today.it|language=Italian|author1=Davide Martini|date=27 January 2014|accessdate=1 September 2016}}</ref><ref name="Rigori, riparte la sfida degli Infallibili">{{cite web|url=http://archiviostorico.corriere.it/2008/ottobre/25/Rigori_riparte_sfida_degli_Infallibili_co_9_081025099.shtml|title=Rigori, riparte la sfida degli infallibili|publisher=Corriere della Sera|language=Italian|author1=Tomaselli Paolo|date=25 October 2008|accessdate=11 May 2015}}</ref><ref name="Handanovic come Pagliuca">{{cite web|url=https://sport.sky.it/calcio/serie-a/2020/01/12/handanovic-rigori-parati-serie-a-classifica|title=Handanovic come Pagliuca, la classifica dei migliori pararigori della storia della Serie A|publisher=sport.sky.it|language=Italian|date=12 January 2020}}</ref>

Because of his calm and composure, he was nicknamed ''Il Conte'' ("The Count").<ref>{{cite book|title=Dizionario della grande Lazio|author1=Sandro Bocchio|author2=Giovanni Tosco|publisher=Newton Compton Editori|year=2000|page=112}}</ref> He has cited [[Giovanni Galli]] as one of his major influences as a goalkeeper.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ilportiere.com/dal-sito/interviste/item/964-luca-marchegiani-storia-di-un-portiere-vero.html |title=Luca Marchegiani: "storia di un portiere vero". |publisher=www.ilportiere.com |language=Italian |date=5 June 2007 |access-date=6 June 2021 |last1=Com |first1=Ilportiere }}</ref>

==Retirement==
Marchegiani works as a pundit for [[Sky Italia]]. He features in [[Konami]]'s ''[[Pro Evolution Soccer]]'' series as a technical commentator; from the [[Pro Evolution Soccer 2012|2012]] edition to the [[Pro Evolution Soccer 2014|2014]] edition, he featured alongside [[Pierluigi Pardo]], while he was subsequently partnered with [[Fabio Caressa]] from the [[Pro Evolution Soccer 2015|2015]] edition onwards.

==Personal life==
His son [[Gabriele Marchegiani]] made his professional debut as a goalkeeper in 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Serie-B/02-12-2016/marchegiani-ora-non-dite-che-sono-figlio-papa-1701081040863.shtml|title=Marchegiani: "Ora non dite che sono figlio di papà"|trans-title=Marchegiani: "Now you do not say I am the son of Dad"|publisher=[[La Gazzetta dello Sport]]|language=Italian|date=2 December 2016}}</ref>

'''Felipe Dias da Silva dal Belo''', commonly known as '''Felipe''' (born 31 July 1984),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Felipe Dias da Silva dal Belo - S.P.A.L{{!}}Player Profile |url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/player/felipe-dias-da-silva-dal-belo?__cf_chl_rt_tk=M65sDDC4v5Op0vqEbN9n0Pcvm4wb3v3fj8oSwwFTZsI-1744123038-1.0.1.1-8LYj7DqtAT4.6ukXLpxCdBj7U2ObM1NuDHDjYxPMwI8 |access-date=2025-04-08 |website=www.sportskeeda.com}}</ref> is a Brazilian former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]]. He has spent most of his professional career in [[Serie A]].

== Club career ==
=== Udinese ===
Felipe began his career with [[Udinese Calcio]], where he made his first team debut in April 2003. He has proven himself as a reliable central defender in Serie A, especially in the 2005–06 season for the club in the [[2005–06 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]].

Felipe signed a new four-year contract with Udinese in March 2008 which would see him stay until 2012.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://int.soccerway.com/news/2008/February/29/felipe-extends-udinese-contract/|title=Felipe extends Udinese contract|date=1 March 2008|access-date=1 January 2010|publisher=Soccerway }}</ref> He also signed an improved contract in November 2005.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.uefa.com/competitions/ucl/news/kind=1/newsid=365599.html|title=Felipe fixes Udinese future|date=10 November 2005|access-date=1 January 2010|publisher=[[UEFA]]}}{{dead link|date=March 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

In the 2006–07 season, Felipe missed the rest of the season after he was injured in January. He returned to the team in September 2007 and became one of the key players who helped Udinese qualify for the [[2008–09 UEFA Cup]]. But another injury in March 2008 meant he would miss the rest of the season and he returned in November 2008.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/SerieA/Squadre/Udinese/Primo_Piano/2008/11/30/udi_chi.shtml|title=Felipe fa felice il Chievo Udinese, quarto k.o. di fila|date=30 November 2008|access-date=1 January 2010|publisher=[[La Gazzetta dello Sport]]|language=it}}</ref> He played 6 matches in 2008–09 UEFA Cup, which he missed the front part of the tournament.

In the 2009–10 season, Felipe was not a regular; the coach preferred [[Andrea Coda]] and [[Cristian Zapata]] (who changed his role from fullback) as the central defensive pair. He only played 3 league matches.

=== Fiorentina ===
A week before the opening of the transfer window, Felipe was allowed to train with [[ACF Fiorentina]] and have medical and aptitudinal tests to finalize a possible transfer on 28 December 2009.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://it.violachannel.tv/dettaglio-ultimora/items/comunicato-stampa.3462.html|title=Comunicato stampa|date=28 December 2009|access-date=1 January 2010|work=Viola Channel|publisher=ACF Fiorentina|language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.udinese.it/ENG/script/view_flsh_news.php?id=26|title=Press Release about Felipe Dias Da Silva Dalbelo|date=28 December 2009|access-date=1 January 2010|publisher=Udinese Calcio|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716203009/http://www.udinese.it/ENG/script/view_flsh_news.php?id=26|archive-date=16 July 2011}}</ref>

On 2 January 2010, Felipe completed the transfer, signed a loan contract with option to purchase.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://it.violachannel.tv/dettaglio-ultimora/items/acquisito-felipe.html|title=Acquisito Felipe, lunedì la presentazione|date=2 January 2010|access-date=2 January 2010|work=Viola Channel|publisher=ACF Fiorentina|language=it}}</ref> The loan fee was €3 million.<ref name=Fiorentina2010bilancio>ACF Fiorentina Report and Accounts on 31 December 2010 {{in lang|it}} [http://www.registroimprese.it/ Require purchase in CCIAA]</ref> He made his debut for the ''Viola'' in a 5–1 away win to [[A.C. Siena|Siena]]. In June 2010 ''la Viola'' excised the rights to sign him for €6 million.<ref name=Fiorentina2010bilancio/> After a disappointing performance, he was loaned out to [[A.C. Cesena|Cesena]] on 31 January 2011. On 21 August 2012, he was signed by Siena.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.acsiena.it/2012/08/21/felipe-e-un-giocatore-del-siena|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120824020752/http://www.acsiena.it/2012/08/21/felipe-e-un-giocatore-del-siena|title=Felipe è un giocatore del Siena
|date=21 August 2012|archive-date=24 August 2012|language=it|publisher=AC Siena}}</ref>

=== Internazionale ===
After being released from [[Parma F.C.|Parma]], Felipe joined [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]] on 26 February 2015, on a six-month deal, he will wear shirt no 26.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.corrieredellosport.it/calcio/2015/02/26-398270/Felipe+%C3%A8+dell'Inter|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150226010101/http://www.corrieredellosport.it/calcio/2015/02/26%2D398270/Felipe%2B%C3%A8%2Bdell%27Inter|title=Felipe è dell'Inter: contratto di sei mesi|date=26 February 2015|archive-date=26 February 2015|language=it|url-status=dead|publisher=Corriere dello Sport}}</ref>

===Return to Udinese===
On 30 August 2015, he returned to Udinese, signing a two-year contract with an option for a third year.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-09-01 |title=Udinese, torna Felipe: il difensore firmerà un biennale - TuttoMercatoWeb.com |url=http://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/serie-a/udinese-torna-felipe-il-difensore-firmera-un-biennale-722623 |access-date=2025-04-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150901042634/http://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/serie-a/udinese-torna-felipe-il-difensore-firmera-un-biennale-722623 |archive-date=1 September 2015 }}</ref> In 4 October, he made his debut on a draw against [[Genoa CFC|Genoa]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Udinese 1-1 Genoa (4 Oct, 2015) Final Score - ESPN (IN) |url=https://www.espn.in/football/match/_/gameId/432202/genoa-udinese |access-date=2025-04-08 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref>

=== SPAL ===
On 3 July 2017, he moved to [[SPAL]] and signed a three-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2017-07-07 |title=IL DIFENSORE FELIPE DAL BELO HA FIRMATO PER LA SOCIETA' BIANCAZZURRA {{!}} SPAL Ferrara |url=http://www.spalferrara.it/difensore-felipe-dal-belo-firmato-la-societa-biancazzurra/ |access-date=2025-04-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170707182954/http://www.spalferrara.it/difensore-felipe-dal-belo-firmato-la-societa-biancazzurra/ |archive-date=7 July 2017 }}</ref> 

=== Semi-professional league ===
On 20 February 2021, after spending one year being a free agent, he was signed by [[ASD Manzanese]], a club playing in [[Serie D]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-02-20 |title=Manzanese Calcio {{!}} UFFICIALE - Felipe si lega alla Manzanese Calcio per i prossimi due anni |url=https://manzanesecalcio.it/2021/02/20/ufficiale-felipe-si-lega-alla-manzanese-calcio-per-i-prossimi-due-anni/ |access-date=2025-04-08 |website=Manzanese Calcio |language=it-IT}}</ref> 13 July 2022, Felipe signed for another club that used to play in Serie D, signed for Torviscosa.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Redazione |date=2022-07-13 |title=Torviscosa, tutta l'esperienza di Felipe per la Serie D |url=https://www.seried24.com/calciomercato/calciomercato-felipe-dal-bello-torviscosa-13-luglio-2022/ |access-date=2025-04-08 |website=SerieD24 |language=it-IT}}</ref>

'''José Paolo Guerrero González''' ({{IPA|es|xoˈse paˈolo ɣeˈreɾo ɣonˈsales}}; born 1 January 1984) is a Peruvian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)#Striker|striker]] for [[Liga 1 (Peru)|Liga 1]] club [[Club Alianza Lima|Alianza Lima]] and the [[Peru national football team|Peru national team]]. Known as one of the best Peruvian and South American strikers of his time, he was key to Peru's successes in the 2000s through 2010s, giving him the nickname, ''el Depredador'' (the Predator).

"A legend in South American football" for the ''New York Times'', he has been Peru's most important football player for two decades.<ref>Lang, Jack (21 June 2024). [https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/live-blogs/peru-chile-live-updates-2024-copa-america-score-result/I5Y8KCARg8sJ/S57HEwG1rD4z/ Novel doping defense] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240925221629/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/live-blogs/peru-chile-live-updates-2024-copa-america-score-result/I5Y8KCARg8sJ/S57HEwG1rD4z/ |date=25 September 2024 }}. ''The New York Times.''</ref> Forging his career in Germany, Guerrero started at giants [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]], before making his name at [[Hamburger SV]], scoring 47 goals across eight [[Bundesliga]] seasons. His greatest successes came in Brazil, where he scored the winning goal of the [[2012 FIFA Club World Cup final]] for [[Sport Club Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]].

With 40 goals in 128 matches for Peru since debuting at 20, Guerrero holds the honour of being the highest goalscorer for his national team. He has represented them at six [[Copa América|Copas América]] and one [[FIFA World Cup|World Cup]]. He led them to third place in the [[2011 Copa América|2011]] and [[2015 Copa América|2015]] Copas, and to runners-up in [[2019 Copa América|2019]], finishing as top scorer in all three of these tournaments.<ref name="NB-2019CA"/> He is also the top scoring active player in the [[Copa América]]. He was one of 59 nominees for the [[2015 FIFA Ballon d'Or]], becoming the first Peruvian to receive that recognition.<ref name=":1">{{cite web |title=Paolo Guerrero nominado al Balón de Oro 2015 de la FIFA |url=http://depor.pe/futbol-internacional/paolo-guerrero-candidato-al-balon-oro-2015-junto-lionel-messi-1055163 |language=es |date=3 October 2015 |website=Depor.pe |access-date=6 November 2015 |archive-date=24 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160124032028/http://depor.pe/futbol-internacional/paolo-guerrero-candidato-al-balon-oro-2015-junto-lionel-messi-1055163 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He's also the oldest Peruvian player to appear in a World Cup, at the age of 34 years and 177 days.

In 2021, the [[International Federation of Football History & Statistics|IFFHS]] included Guerrero in their best South American team of the last decade, being recognized as the best South American center forward between 2010 and 2020 (joining the podium with [[Neymar]] and [[Sergio Agüero]]).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://iffhs.com/en/news/iffhs-man-team-conmebol-of-the-decade-2011-2020-921|title=IFFHS MAN TEAM - CONMEBOL - OF THE DECADE 2011-2020|editor=IFFHS|date=30 January 2021|access-date=12 June 2021|archive-date=31 May 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220531011044/https://www.iffhs.com/index.php/posts/921|url-status=live}}</ref>
In addition, he was voted the "best centre forward in America" in 2012 and 2017 by the newspaper ''[[El País (Uruguay)|El País]]'', based on the opinion of some two hundred journalists from the region. He has also been named included by [[CONMEBOL]] in the teams of the tournament for the 2011, 2015 and 2019 Copas América.

==Club career==
===Early career===
Guerrero was born in [[Lima]], starting his football career in the youth teams of [[Alianza Lima]]. In 2003, he signed a contract with [[Bavaria]]n giants [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]]. During the 2003–04 season, Guerrero played in the [[Regionalliga Süd (1994–2012)|Regionalliga Süd]] where he scored 21 goals in 23 games. During the [[2004–05 FC Bayern Munich season|2004–05 season]], he joined fellow countryman [[Claudio Pizarro]] as a member of the Bayern first team.

=== Bayern Munich ===
[[File:Persepolis VS Bayern Munich in 13 January 2006 4.jpg|left|thumb|Guerrero (right) playing for [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] in 2006]]
At the beginning of 2002, after rejecting an offer from [[K.R.C. Genk]] of Belgium, [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]] of Germany announced his incorporation to the second team. This signing led to a conflict between [[Alianza Lima]] and Bayern. The case was raised to [[FIFA]], which decided that the German club should pay for training rights since, although Guerrero had a formal contract with Alianza, it was not of a professional nature. Once the problem was solved, Guerrero began playing with Bayern Munich II in the Regionalliga South, which at that time was the third division of German football. On May 30, 2004 he was crowned champion in this category.

At the team level, he played his first game with the Bayern professional team on October 23, 2004 against [[FC Hansa Rostock|Hansa Rostock]].with the number "33", while his first goal in the Bundesliga was scored against [[Hannover 96]]. In total, Guerrero spent four seasons at Bayern Munich, alternating the last two in the first team, the same team with which he scored ten goals in the [[Bundesliga]] and two in the [[UEFA Champions League]].

In June 2006 he left Bayern Munich. His destination was [[Hamburger SV]], a club with which he signed a four-year contract.

===Hamburger SV===
[[File:Guerrero_2008.jpg|thumb|upright|Guerrero with [[Hamburger SV]] in 2008]]
In June 2006, it was announced that Guerrero had transferred to [[Hamburger SV]] and signed a contract with the club through 2010.<ref>{{cite web |date=14 June 2006 |title=Guerrero wechselt zum HSV |url=https://www.kicker.de/guerrero-wechselt-zum-hsv-350967/artikel |access-date=11 May 2008 |publisher=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=de |archive-date=25 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210225060920/https://www.kicker.de/guerrero-wechselt-zum-hsv-350967/artikel |url-status=live }}</ref> His first season was marred by an injury, which took away half his season, and his low productivity, being a substitute most of the season. Near the end, he did score three goals, making his season total 5 goals in 20 games. One of these goals was against former club Bayern Munich in a 1–2 victory which left Bayern with no possibilities of making it to the [[UEFA Champions League]]. In the 2007–08 season, his second at Hamburg, Guerrero played 29 of 34 games in the [[Bundesliga]], scoring nine goals and getting four assists, as well as becoming an undisputed starter and a vital part of the side; he was the third top scorer, behind [[Rafael van der Vaart]] (12 goals) and [[Ivica Olić]] (14 goals). In the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]] and qualification, he played nine games, scoring five goals and getting three assists. His first [[hat-trick]] in his professional career was against [[Karlsruher SC]], in the last game of the Bundesliga, scoring the second, third, and fourth goals in a 7–0 victory. This victory secured them fourth place and a UEFA Cup spot for next season.

By the beginning of the [[2008–09 Bundesliga|2008–09 season]], Guerrero had become first choice striker for Hamburger SV. Coach [[Martin Jol]] even went as far as saying that Guerrero better not catch even a cold during the season. Guerrero was fined a club record (somewhere in the region of €50,000–100,000), in April 2010 for an incident at the end of a league game with [[Hannover 96]], where after apparently having been abused by a Hamburg fan, Guerrero threw his drink bottle into the crowd, striking that fan in the face.<ref name="zdf12">{{cite web |date=5 April 2010 |title=Rekordgeldstrafe für Guerrero |url=http://fussball.zdf.de/ZDFsport/inhalt/30/0,5676,8061342,00.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111007083419/http://fussball.zdf.de/ZDFsport/inhalt/30/0,5676,8061342,00.html?dr=1 |archive-date=7 October 2011 |access-date=5 April 2010 |publisher=[[ZDF]] |language=de |df=dmy-all}}</ref> The [[German Football Association]] (DFB) suspended Guerrero for five league games and fined him €20,000.<ref name="zdf22">{{cite web |date=8 April 2010 |title=Fünf Spiele Sperre für den Flaschenwerfer |url=http://fussball.zdf.de/ZDFsport/inhalt/27/0,5676,8061915,00.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111007083502/http://fussball.zdf.de/ZDFsport/inhalt/27/0,5676,8061915,00.html?dr=1 |archive-date=7 October 2011 |access-date=8 April 2010 |publisher=[[ZDF]] |language=de |df=dmy-all}}</ref>

===Corinthians===
[[File:Paulo_Guerrero_2012_FIFA_Club_World_Cup.jpg|left|thumb|upright|Guerrero with [[Sport Club Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]] in 2012]]
Guerrero joined Brazilian club [[Sport Club Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]] on 13 July 2012, on a three-year deal for a fee of [[Brazilian real|R$]]7.5 million.<ref>{{cite news |date=13 July 2012 |title=Timão anuncia acordo com Guerrero. Apresentação será segunda-feira |url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/times/corinthians/noticia/2012/07/timao-anuncia-acordo-com-guerrero-apresentacao-sera-segunda-feira.html |access-date=1 January 2013 |publisher=Globoesporte |language=pt |archive-date=17 July 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120717021759/http://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/times/corinthians/noticia/2012/07/timao-anuncia-acordo-com-guerrero-apresentacao-sera-segunda-feira.html |url-status=live }}</ref> On 25 July 2012, he made his debut in a match against [[Cruzeiro Esporte Clube|Cruzeiro]] in the [[2012 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|2012 Brasileiro Série A]], where Corinthians won 2–0. His debut in the "Timao" attracted the immediate attention of the Peruvian media to [[São Paulo]]. In the 26th round of the Brasileiro, he played against [[Botafogo de Futebol e Regatas|Botafogo]] and scored his first goal for his team. Guerrero grew in the later rounds of the Brazilian championship, scoring several goals that secured his place in the team's starting lineup.

On November 27, 2012, days before embarking to Japan to compete in the [[2012 FIFA Club World Cup]], the athlete was honored by the Peruvian consulate in Brazil "in recognition of his sporting merits and professionalism, showing all the high values of Peruvian sport in Brazil and being considered as a starter in most of the matches played." It was at the [[FIFA Club World Cup]] where Guerrero would make his most historic performance with Corinthians. On December 12, 2012, in the semifinals of the tournament against [[Al Ahly SC|Al Ahly]] of Egypt, Guerrero scored the only goal of the match with a header that took Corinthians to the final. On 16 December 2012, in the Club World Cup final against [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League]] winners [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], Guerrero scored, again with a header, to give Corinthians the title of World Champions at club level.<ref>{{cite web |date=16 December 2012 |title=Corinthians 1 Chelsea 0 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20746503 |access-date=17 December 2012 |publisher=BBC Sport |archive-date=12 January 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160112051202/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/20746503 |url-status=live }}</ref> Paolo Guerrero was awarded the Bronze Ball as the third top goalscorer of the tournament.<ref>{{Cite news |last=DT |first=Redacción |date=2018-12-16 |title=Paolo Guerrero: Corinthians recordó histórico gol del peruano en el Mundial de Clubes 2012 {{!}} VIDEO |url=https://elcomercio.pe/deporte-total/peruanos-en-el-mundo/paolo-guerrero-corinthians-recordo-gol-depredador-chelsea-mundial-clubes-2012-video-youtube-viral-noticia-nndc-588293-noticia/ |access-date=2025-03-01 |work=El Comercio |language=es-PE |issn=1605-3052 |archive-date=8 July 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250708230434/https://elcomercio.pe/deporte-total/peruanos-en-el-mundo/paolo-guerrero-corinthians-recordo-gol-depredador-chelsea-mundial-clubes-2012-video-youtube-viral-noticia-nndc-588293-noticia/ |url-status=live }}</ref>
[[File:Corinthians celebrate FIFA Club World Cup win.jpg|thumb|Guerrero with Corinthians, celebrating their [[FIFA Club World Cup]] win]]
In May 2013, Guerrero became the first Peruvian footballer to appear on the cover of ''[[Placar]]'', Brazil's biggest football magazine. The cover featured him as a warrior ("''guerrero''" is similar to the Portuguese word "''guerreiro''", both meaning "warrior") fresh out of battle, with blood on his legs, and carrying a Corinthians flag.<ref>{{cite news |date=23 May 2013 |title=Placar de maio tem Guerrero, Seedorf, Barcos e o novo Cruzeiro na capa |url=http://placar.abril.com.br/materia/placar-de-maio-tem-guerrero-seedorf-barcos-e-o-novo-cruzeiro-na-capa |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130502044637/http://placar.abril.com.br/materia/placar-de-maio-tem-guerrero-seedorf-barcos-e-o-novo-cruzeiro-na-capa |archive-date=2 May 2013 |access-date=24 April 2013 |publisher=Placar |language=pt |df=dmy-all}}</ref>

In July 2013, Corinthians won the [[2013 Recopa Sudamericana]], defeating city rivals [[São Paulo FC]] 4–1 on aggregate. Guerrero scored in the first leg, a 2–1 away win.<ref>{{cite news |date=17 July 2017 |title=Há quatro anos, Corinthians conquistava Recopa Sul-Americana com vitória sobre São Paulo |url=https://www.corinthians.com.br/ha-quatro-anos-corinthians-conquistava-recopa-sul-americana-com-vitoria-sobre-sao-paulo/ |access-date=1 June 2018 |publisher=Corinthians |language=pt}}</ref> At the end of the year, Guerrero ended up consecrated as his team's top scorer in the season by scoring 18 goals in 46 games and winning 2 titles. He was awarded as the best striker of the Brasileirao in the 2014 season.

On March 17, 2015, Guerrero became the foreign player who scored the most goals for Corinthians, with 47 goals, surpassing Argentina's [[Carlos Tevez]] who scored 46 goals. The record was obtained in a match against the Uruguayan club [[Danubio F.C.]] for the third round of the second phase of the [[2015 Copa Libertadores]]. In that match he was the great figure by scoring his first hat trick with Corinthians, the match ended 4–0 in favor of ''Coringao''. Guerrero became the top scorer of the post-relegation era, breaking the record that previously belonged to [[Dentinho]].

In 2015, Guerrero and Corinthians were not able to reach a deal on the renegotiation of his contract, due to end on 15 July. Corinthians fans asked for his permanence and subsequent retirement at the club, since they considered him an idol and his contract ended in the middle of the year. But after being eliminated by Guaraní from the Copa Libertadores, finally, in June it was confirmed that Paolo would no longer continue in Corinthians for not reaching an economic agreement for his renewal. His last game for Corinthians was against [[Fluminense FC|Fluminense]] on 24 May. Corinthians confirmed his release three days later.<ref>{{cite news |date=27 May 2015 |title=Corinthians libera Guerrero |url=http://www.corinthians.com.br/site/noticias/2015/05/27/11h00-id26329-corinthians-libera-guerrero.shtml |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150530003458/http://www.corinthians.com.br/site/noticias/2015/05/27/11h00-id26329-corinthians-libera-guerrero.shtml#.VWXkGUPOrzw |archive-date=30 May 2015 |access-date=27 April 2015 |publisher=corinthians.com.br |language=pt}}</ref>

===Flamengo===
[[File:Campeonato_Carioca_-_Flamengo_-_Guerrero.jpg|right|thumb|Guerrero playing for [[Clube de Regatas do Flamengo|Flamengo]] in 2016]]
It was announced on 29 May 2015, that Guerrero would join [[Clube de Regatas do Flamengo|Flamengo]] after performing well for [[Peru national football team|Peru]] at the [[2015 Copa América]] in Chile, where Peru achieved Third place.<ref>{{cite web |date=29 May 2015 |title=Paolo Guerrero é o novo atacante do Flamengo |url=http://www.flamengo.com.br/site/noticia/detalhe/21281/paolo-guerrero-e-o-novo-atacante-do-flamengo |access-date=26 June 2015 |work=CR Flamengo |language=pt |archive-date=3 February 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180203073228/http://www.flamengo.com.br/site/noticia/detalhe/21281/paolo-guerrero-e-o-novo-atacante-do-flamengo |url-status=live }}</ref> He traveled to [[Rio de Janeiro]] just one day after returning in Peru from the tournament. On 9 July 2015, having trained only one morning with the 'Mengão', he debuts in the evening against [[Internacional]], scoring a goal and providing an assist for a goal, sentenced a streak of 5 goals in less than 2 weeks, with which he would win the admiration of the Carioca fans, who created the anthem 'Acabou o caô. O Guerrero chegou' in his honor.

Guerrero started 2017 season by scoring a brace at the [[Taça Guanabara]], scoring the first and third goals in Flamengo's 4–1 win over [[Boavista Sport Club|Boavista]] on the first date of the group stage of the tournament, his compatriot [[Miguel Trauco]] would also be present to score ''Mengao's'' second goal. In the final, Flamengo lost to Fluminense.

In the [[2017 Campeonato Carioca]], Guerrero scored both of Flamengo's goals in a 2–1 semi-final win over [[Botafogo de Futebol e Regatas|Botafogo]] leading Flamengo to the final.<ref>{{cite news |date=23 April 2017 |title=Com dois de Guerrero, Flamengo derrota Botafogo e faz final contra o Fluminense |url=http://www.espn.com.br/noticia/689053_com-dois-de-guerrero-flamengo-derrota-botafogo-e-faz-final-contra-o-fluminense |access-date=1 June 2018 |publisher=ESPN |language=pt |archive-date=6 August 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200806044829/http://www.espn.com.br/noticia/689053_com-dois-de-guerrero-flamengo-derrota-botafogo-e-faz-final-contra-o-fluminense |url-status=live }}</ref> In the final, Guerrero scored a goal for Flamengo's temporary 1–1 against [[Fluminense FC|Fluminense]]. In extra time, [[Rodinei]] would score the winning goal for Flamengo to be crowned champion of the tournament, this would be the first title that Guerrero won since his arrival at the club. Paolo Guerrero was consecrated as the top scorer with 10 in 11 games goals and was distinguished as the best player of the tournament being included in the ideal 11.<ref>{{cite news |date=7 May 2017 |title=Guerrero brilha, Flamengo bate Fluminense e é campeão estadual |url=http://www1.folha.uol.com.br/esporte/2017/05/1881933-guerrero-brilha-flamengo-bate-fluminense-e-e-campeao-estadual.shtml |access-date=1 June 2018 |publisher=UOL |language=pt |archive-date=25 May 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180525201331/http://www1.folha.uol.com.br/esporte/2017/05/1881933-guerrero-brilha-flamengo-bate-fluminense-e-e-campeao-estadual.shtml |url-status=live }}</ref>

After his suspension for testing positive in anti-doping control, he returns to the field on 7 May 2018 in a match against [[SC Internacional|Internacional]] which ended in a 2–0 victory. However, on May 13 he scored his first goal of the season against [[Chapecoense]] after a drought of 7 games without scoring, the CAS increased his suspension, which would mean he would miss the rest of the season until his return on July 18 against [[São Paulo FC|São Paulo]]. During his suspension in 2017, Flamengo lost the [[2017 Copa Sudamericana]] final, with his suspension contributing to the loss. Although he was greeted with enthusiasm, he has not scored since his second return. This complicated his chances of renewing, since sectors of the fans were very dissatisfied with his performance on the field and even off it. Finally, when his contract expired, he signed for Internacional.

===Internacional===
On 12 August 2018, Guerrero signed with [[S.C. Internacional]] on a three-year contract, after leaving Flamengo on a [[Free transfer (association football)|free transfer]].<ref>{{cite news |date=9 August 2018 |title=Peru striker Guerrero secures Internacional move |url=http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2018-08/09/c_137377757.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180809015301/http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2018-08/09/c_137377757.htm |archive-date=9 August 2018 |access-date=16 September 2019 |publisher=XINHUANET}}</ref> He was given the number 79, to commemorate [[1979 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|the last time Inter won the Campeonato Brasileiro]].<ref>{{cite news |date=14 August 2018 |title=Guerrero vestirá a camisa 79 no Internacional |url=https://oglobo.globo.com/esportes/guerrero-vestira-camisa-79-no-internacional-22978601 |access-date=16 September 2019 |publisher=O GLOBO |language=pt |archive-date=25 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190825194638/https://oglobo.globo.com/esportes/guerrero-vestira-camisa-79-no-internacional-22978601 |url-status=live }}</ref> However, days before he was to debut, on 24 August, his FIFA ban was upheld, preventing him from playing his first match until April 2019.

In 2019, Guerrero's number changed from 79 to 9, due to the departure of [[Leandro Damião]]. After his ban expired, Guerrero finally made his debut for Inter in the [[Campeonato Gaúcho]] against [[Sociedade Esportiva e Recreativa Caxias do Sul|Caxias]], on 6 April, scoring in the 2–0 semi-final win. His [[Copa Libertadores]] debut came against [[Club Deportivo Palestino|Palestino]] of Chile, a match where he scored twice.<ref>{{cite news |date=9 April 2019 |title=Paolo Guerrero Scores Brace In First Copa Libertadores Match Following Doping Ban |url=https://www.beinsports.com/us/copa-libertadores/video/paolo-guerrero-scores-brace-in-first-copa-lib/1162142 |access-date=17 September 2019 |publisher=beIN Sports |language=en}}</ref> Guerrero ended the 2019 season as the teams top goalscorer, with 20 goals in 41 games.

In the midst of a goal drought of several weeks and rumors that he would be declared transferable, journalist Eduardo de Conto reported that Guerrero asked the board to terminate his contract to treat a knee injury. This was confirmed on 26 October 2021, when Inter released him on a  "mutual agreement" to treat the alleged injury that had afflicted him since August last year.<ref>{{cite web |date=26 October 2021 |title=Oficial: Guerrero não é mais jogador do Internacional |url=https://www.lance.com.br/internacional/oficial-guerrero-nao-mais-jogador.html |accessdate=26 November 2021 |publisher=Lance! |language=pt-BR |archive-date=26 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211126142337/https://www.lance.com.br/internacional/oficial-guerrero-nao-mais-jogador.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Avaí ===
On 21 July 2022, Guerrero joined [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|Brazilian Série A]] side [[Avaí FC|Avaí]] for the remainder of the [[2022 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|2022 season]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=21 July 2022 |title=Avaí Futebol Clube » #NovoReforçoDoLeão: COMO PREPARAR UM VERDADEIRO CEVICHE MANEZINHO! |url=https://www.avai.com.br/novo/como-preparar-um-verdadeiro-ceviche-manezinho/ |access-date=2022-07-28 |language=pt-BR |archive-date=21 July 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220721130046/https://www.avai.com.br/novo/como-preparar-um-verdadeiro-ceviche-manezinho/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On 5 November 2022, Avaí got relegated to the [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série B|Série B]], being the first time team that Guerrero has played for that got relegated. Guerrero play 10 games with Avaí but did not score any goals.

=== LDU Quito ===
On 14 July 2023, Guerrero signed for [[LDU Quito]] of Ecuador. On 3 August 2023, he made his debut away with LDU against [[Ñublense]] scoring the winning goal in the 60th minute of play, with the match ending 1-0 in favor of the Ecuadorian team.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Inostroza |first=Wilfredo |date=2023-08-04 |title=Con gol de Guerrero, LDU ganó a Ñublense y saca ventaja en la llave de la Sudamericana |url=https://libero.pe/futbol-internacional/copa-sudamericana/2023/08/02/nublense-vs-liga-quito-en-vivo-paolo-guerrero-copa-sudamericana-via-directv-sports-dgo-cuando-juega-horario-canal-donde-ver-partido-hoy-chile-ecuador-lbev-121944 |access-date=2025-03-02 |website=Diario Líbero |language=es |archive-date=5 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230805181150/https://libero.pe/futbol-internacional/copa-sudamericana/2023/08/02/nublense-vs-liga-quito-en-vivo-paolo-guerrero-copa-sudamericana-via-directv-sports-dgo-cuando-juega-horario-canal-donde-ver-partido-hoy-chile-ecuador-lbev-121944 |url-status=live }}</ref> He would score again on 27 September against [[Defensa y Justicia]] in the first leg of the [[2023 Copa Sudamericana]] semifinal. Finally, in this same tournament Guerrero with LDU managed to beat [[Fortaleza Esporte Clube|Fortaleza]] via penalties despite having missed the first penalty of their team. He thus became the first Peruvian in history to win the Copa Sudamericana with a foreign club. He scored 3 goals in 7 games.

He won the [[2023 Ecuadorian Serie A]] scoring 5 goals in 15 games played, most of his goals were scored at the end of the tournament. He decided not to renew with the Ecuadorian club after learning that manager Zubeldía would not continue and ran the risk of not playing as a starter anymore.

==International career==
Guerrero's national career began at the [[2001 Bolivarian Games]] where he won gold with the [[Peru national under-17 football team|U-17 squad]]. His career with the [[Peru national football team|senior team]] began in the unsuccessful [[2006 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)|2006 FIFA World Cup qualification campaign]], but he managed to score twice for the national side. His first goal was the winner against [[Chile national football team|Chile]] in Lima's Estadio Nacional. It was followed by a first-minute goal in the next match against [[Ecuador national football team|Ecuador]] at the same venue, though the Ecuadorians fought back to secure a 2–2 away draw. In the opening game of the [[2007 Copa América]] in [[Mérida, Mérida|Mérida, Venezuela]], Guerrero concluded a 3–0 win over [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]] as Peru went on to reach the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite news |title=Perú goleó 3–0 a Uruguay en Copa América |trans-title=Peru thrash Uruguay 3–0 at the Copa América |url=http://www.eluniverso.com/2007/06/26/0001/15/FD82407067B549AA86F2B9E22E58F44A.html |access-date=26 June 2015 |work=El Universo |date=26 June 2007 |language=es |archive-date=28 June 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150628232939/http://www.eluniverso.com/2007/06/26/0001/15/FD82407067B549AA86F2B9E22E58F44A.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== 2011 Copa América ===
Guerrero was ruled out of Peru's first two [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010 World Cup]] qualifying games because of injury. A further blow to Peru was laid down by [[FIFA]] when Guerrero was suspended six games for insulting the referee during the match against [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]] in June 2008.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://int.soccerway.com/news/2008/August/12/peru-striker-guerrero-suspended-for-six-games/n130625/ |title=Peru striker Guerrero suspended for six games |work=Soccerway |date=12 August 2008 |access-date=26 June 2015}}</ref> Following Peru's disastrous qualifying campaign for the 2010 World Cup, [[José del Solar]] was replaced with Uruguayan manager [[Sergio Markarián]] and Guerrero was called up for the [[2011 Copa América]]. In place of an injured Pizarro, Guerrero played as the team's starting striker in the competition and scored five times, making him the tournament's top scorer, one each against Uruguay and [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]] followed by a [[hat-trick]] against [[Venezuela national football team|Venezuela]] in the [[2015 Copa América#Third place playoff|third place play-off]] match which Peru won 4–1.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/match/peru-vs-venezuela/1064743/report |title=Peru 4–1 Venezuela: Paolo Guerrero nets second half hat trick as Peruvians finish third in 2011 Copa America |website=Goal.com |date=23 July 2011 |access-date=26 June 2015 |archive-date=24 September 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924122353/http://www.goal.com/en-gb/match/peru-vs-venezuela/1064743/report |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== 2015 Copa América and Copa América Centenario ===
At the [[2015 Copa América]] held in Chile, Guerrero scored a hat-trick in a 3–1 win against [[Bolivia national football team|Bolivia]] in the quarter-final in [[Temuco]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://prosoccertalk.nbcsports.com/2015/06/25/bolivia-1-3-peru-guerreros-hat-trick-books-copa-america-semifinal-date-with-chile/ |title=Bolivia 1–3 Peru: Guerrero's hat trick books Copa America semifinal date with Chile |work=NBC Sports |date=25 June 2015 |access-date=26 June 2015 |archive-date=30 June 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150630021432/http://prosoccertalk.nbcsports.com/2015/06/25/bolivia-1-3-peru-guerreros-hat-trick-books-copa-america-semifinal-date-with-chile/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He scored the second goal in Peru's 2–0 win over Paraguay in the [[2015 Copa América#Third place playoff|third place play-off]], thus helping Peru to third place at the Copa América for a second consecutive time and finishing as joint top-goalscorer with Chile's [[Eduardo Vargas]].

Guerrero became the all-time leading goalscorer for Peru on 4 June 2016, after scoring against [[Haiti national football team|Haiti]] in a 1–0 win at the [[Copa América Centenario]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Guerrero González |first1=José |title=Guerrero plays down goal-scoring record |url=http://www.fourfourtwo.com/au/news/guerrero-plays-down-goal-scoring-record#:sfgQ8fqQJ8awiA |publisher=FourFourTwo |access-date=5 June 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160608105749/http://www.fourfourtwo.com/au/news/guerrero-plays-down-goal-scoring-record#:sfgQ8fqQJ8awiA |archive-date=8 June 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Lead-up to the 2018 FIFA World Cup===
[[File:Paolo Guerrero ECUADOR VS PERU RUSIA 2018 (36910642261) cropped.jpg|thumb|upright|Guerrero with [[Peru national football team|Peru]] in a [[2018 FIFA World Cup]] qualifying match against [[Ecuador national football team|Ecuador]]]]
Guerrero made 17 appearances and scored five goals in the [[2018 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)|2018 FIFA World Cup qualifying campaign]], leading the Peru team in their successful World Cup qualifying campaign.<ref name="nytimes.com">Burke, Elias (16 Marzo 2024). [https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5321166/2024/03/16/paolo-guerrero-peru-copa-america/ The wild career of Paolo Guerrero – failed drugs test, Inca mummies and captaining Peru at 40]. ''The New York Times.''</ref> On 3 November 2017, it was announced that Guerrero had failed the doping control test after the match against Argentina in the previous month for what was initially reported as a ''social drug''. He received a preemptive 30-day suspension from [[FIFA]], making him miss the [[2018 FIFA World Cup qualification (OFC–CONMEBOL play-off)|World Cup play-off tie]] against [[New Zealand men's national football team|New Zealand]], eventually won by Peru.<ref>{{cite news |title=Peru's Paolo Guerrero provisionally suspended for failing doping test |url=http://www.espn.com/soccer/peru/story/3257286/peru-star-paolo-guerrero-tested-positive-for-banned-substance |publisher=ESPN |date=3 November 2017}}</ref>

On 8 December 2017, it was revealed that Guerrero had tested positive for [[benzoylecgonine]], the primary metabolite of [[cocaine]]. As a result, he was banned by FIFA from all competitions for one year, meaning that he would not have been able to participate in the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Peru: Paolo Guerrero to miss World Cup after failing drugs test |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/41866814 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=8 December 2017 |archive-date=25 December 2017 |access-date=11 February 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171225213956/http://www.bbc.com/sport/football/41866814 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Peru captain Paolo Guerrero to miss World Cup, banned 1 year |url=http://www.nydailynews.com/newswires/sports/peru-captain-paolo-guerrero-world-cup-banned-1-year-article-1.3685580 |work=Daily News |location=New York |access-date=9 December 2017 |archive-date=10 December 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171210015827/http://www.nydailynews.com/newswires/sports/peru-captain-paolo-guerrero-world-cup-banned-1-year-article-1.3685580 |url-status=live }}</ref> The ban was reduced on appeal 12 days later.<ref>{{cite news |title=Peru: Paolo Guerrero has drugs ban reduced before World Cup |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/42434114 |access-date=20 December 2017 |archive-date=21 December 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171221111508/http://www.bbc.com/sport/football/42434114 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=FIFA cut Peru captain Paolo Guerrero's drug ban in half making striker available for World Cup in Russia |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/fifa-cut-peru-captain-paolo-11730154 |work=Mirror |date=20 December 2017 |archive-date=15 May 2018 |access-date=5 April 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180515044111/https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/fifa-cut-peru-captain-paolo-11730154 |url-status=live }}</ref> Guerrero's lawyers had argued that the failed test had occurred as a result of the consumption of a traditional [[coca tea]], using forensic analysis of the [[Children of Llullaillaco]] as evidence.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cocaine, the captain & the frozen mummies: Paolo Guerrero's World Cup journey |first=Patrick |last=Jennings |publisher=BBC Sport |date=15 June 2018 |access-date=15 June 2018 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44415647 |archive-date=15 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180615092427/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44415647 |url-status=live }}</ref>

However, on 14 May 2018, the [[Court of Arbitration for Sport]] upheld the appeal filed by the [[World Anti-Doping Agency]], extending the ban to 14 months and ruling him out of the tournament. It accepted that Guerrero did not intend to enhance performance but said he was at fault, even if not significantly.<ref>{{cite news |title=Peru Captain Guerrero to Miss World Cup After Doping Ban Increased |url=https://www.nytimes.com/reuters/2018/05/14/sports/soccer/14reuters-soccer-worldcup-per.html |work=The New York Times |date=14 May 2018 |access-date=14 May 2018 |archive-date=15 May 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180515050914/https://www.nytimes.com/reuters/2018/05/14/sports/soccer/14reuters-soccer-worldcup-per.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Captains of Peru's group-stage competitors, [[Hugo Lloris]] (France), [[Simon Kjaer]] (Denmark) and [[Mile Jedinak]] (Australia) supported Guerrero's appeal and released a letter urging FIFA to lift the ban.<ref name="nytimes.com"/>

On 31 May 2018, it was announced Guerrero would be allowed to play at the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]] after the [[Swiss Federal Tribunal]] lifted the ban for the tournament.<ref>{{Cite web |title=World Cup 2018: Peru captain Paolo Guerrero cleared to play |publisher=BBC Sport |date=31 May 2018 |access-date=31 May 2018 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44316806 |archive-date=31 May 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180531135855/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44316806 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 3 June 2018, Guerrero made his comeback after a seven-month absence from the national team scoring twice in the 3–0 friendly win against [[Saudi Arabia national football team|Saudi Arabia]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Saudi Arabia 0 – 3 Peru |publisher=BBC Sport |date=3 June 2018 |access-date=3 June 2018 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44320596 |archive-date=4 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180604195529/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44320596 |url-status=live }}</ref>

A 2018 report of investigative journalists of German broadcasting station [[ARD (broadcaster)|ARD]] revealed [[doping in sport|doping]] practices in Brazil, involving physician Mohamad Barakat who reportedly treated Guerrero and who had already posed with him many years ago.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.sportschau.de/doping/doping-fussball-brasilien-100.html |title=Profifußballer besuchen dubiosen brasilianischen Mediziner |language=de |website=sportschau.de |date=1 July 2018 |access-date=2 July 2018 |first1=Hajo |last1=Seppelt |first2=Florian |last2=Riesewieck |first3=Edmund |last3=Willison |first4=Sebastian |last4=Münster |archive-date=2 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180702064854/https://www.sportschau.de/doping/doping-fussball-brasilien-100.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://blogdoperrone.blogosfera.uol.com.br/2013/11/medico-de-fora-do-corinthians-diz-que-guerrero-pede-ajuda-e-amplia-desgaste/ |title=Médico de fora do Corinthians diz que Guerrero pede ajuda e amplia desgaste |language=pt |website=Blog do Perrone |date=2 November 2013 |access-date=2 July 2018 |first=Ricardo |last=Perrone |archive-date=2 July 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180702122628/https://blogdoperrone.blogosfera.uol.com.br/2013/11/medico-de-fora-do-corinthians-diz-que-guerrero-pede-ajuda-e-amplia-desgaste/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===2018 FIFA World Cup===
[[File:Австралия Перу ЧМ 2018 Сочи.jpg|thumb|Guerrero celebrating his goal against [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia]] at the 2018 World Cup]]
Guerrero made his World Cup debut on 16 June 2018, coming off the bench in the 1–0 loss to [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Denmark do just enough to edge out Peru |publisher=FIFA |date=16 June 2018 |access-date=26 June 2018 |url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/matches/match/300331528/#match-summary|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612142834/https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/matches/match/300331528/#match-summary|url-status=dead|archive-date=12 June 2018}}</ref> On 26 June, he assisted [[André Carrillo]]'s goal, which was Peru's first World Cup goal in 36 years, and scored the second goal in Peru's 2–0 win over [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia]], in the team's final group match, as his side suffered a first-round exit from the competition.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/matches/match/300331506/#match-summary |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612140345/https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/matches/match/300331506/#match-summary |url-status=dead |archive-date=12 June 2018 |title=Peru sign off in style |publisher=FIFA |date=26 June 2018 |access-date=26 June 2018}}</ref> At the age of 34 and 177 days, he became the oldest Peruvian player to appear in a FIFA World Cup.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://statbunker.com/alltimestats/AllTimeOldestAppearances?comp_code=WC&club_id=411 |title=All time - Oldest Appearances Peru World Cup |website=statbunker.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210828042710/https://statbunker.com/alltimestats/AllTimeOldestAppearances?comp_code=WC&club_id=411 |archive-date=2021-08-28}}</ref>

===2019 Copa América===
In May 2019, Guerrero was included in [[Ricardo Gareca]]'s final 23-man squad for the [[2019 Copa América]] in Brazil.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://peru.as.com/peru/2019/05/30/futbol/1559216143_556296.html |title=Lista de 23 de Gareca para Copa América: horario, cómo ver y TV |publisher=As.com |language=es |date=30 May 2019 |access-date=8 July 2019 |archive-date=25 September 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200925113146/https://peru.as.com/peru/2019/05/30/futbol/1559216143_556296.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He scored the opening goal in Peru's second group game of the tournament on 18 June – a 3–1 victory over Bolivia.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.euronews.com/2019/06/19/peru-come-from-behind-to-beat-bolivia-3-1-in-copa-america |title=Peru come from behind to beat Bolivia 3–1 in Copa America |work=Euronews |date=19 June 2019 |access-date=19 June 2019 |archive-date=19 June 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190619041548/https://www.euronews.com/2019/06/19/peru-come-from-behind-to-beat-bolivia-3-1-in-copa-america |url-status=live }}</ref> In the semi-finals against defending champions Chile on 3 July, Guerrero scored the final goal of a 3–0 win, which saw Peru advance to the final of the tournament for the first time since [[1975 Copa América|1975]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report?gameId=548672 |title=Peru beat Chile, set up Copa final with Brazil |publisher=ESPN FC |date=3 July 2019 |access-date=8 July 2019 |archive-date=5 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190705063613/https://www.espn.com/soccer/report?gameId=548672 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In the [[2019 Copa América Final]] against hosts [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] on 7 July, at the [[Maracanã Stadium]], Guerrero scored the temporary equaliser from the penalty spot in the first half; the match eventually ended in a 3–1 victory to Brazil.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2019/jul/06/copa-america-final-brazil-peru-live |title=Brazil 3–1 Peru |work=The Guardian |last1=Smyth |first1=Rob |date=7 July 2019 |access-date=8 July 2019 |archive-date=7 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190707215929/https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2019/jul/06/copa-america-final-brazil-peru-live |url-status=live }}</ref> Guerrero finished the tournament as the top scorer with 3 goals, alongside Brazil's [[Everton Soares]], who won the Golden Boot Award due to having played fewer minutes than the Peruvian throughout the tournament.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://esporte.uol.com.br/futebol/ultimas-noticias/2019/07/07/cebolinha-enlouquece-galvao-com-gol-em-final-e-artilharia-da-copa-america.htm |title=BCebolinha é eleito melhor da final, vira artilheiro e enlouquece Galvão |work=UOL |language=pt |date=7 July 2019 |access-date=7 July 2019 |archive-date=8 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190708132443/https://esporte.uol.com.br/futebol/ultimas-noticias/2019/07/07/cebolinha-enlouquece-galvao-com-gol-em-final-e-artilharia-da-copa-america.htm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="prêmios">{{cite web |url=https://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/selecao-brasileira/noticia/copa-america-selecao-recebe-o-trofeu-fair-play.ghtml |title=Daniel Alves é eleito craque da Copa América; Alisson e Everton também ganham prêmios |trans-title=Daniel Alves is elected the best player of the Copa América; Alisson and Everton also win awards |publisher=Globo |language=pt |date=7 July 2019 |access-date=8 July 2019 |archive-date=8 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190708112205/https://globoesporte.globo.com/futebol/selecao-brasileira/noticia/copa-america-selecao-recebe-o-trofeu-fair-play.ghtml |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Late career===
On 11 October 2019, Guerrero made his 100th international appearance for Peru in a friendly match against [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://peru.as.com/peru/2019/10/11/futbol/1570792981_043150.html |title=Paolo Guerrero, a un gol de los 40 con la selección de Perú |publisher=as.com |language=es |date=11 October 2019 |access-date=17 October 2023 |archive-date=10 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231110010537/https://peru.as.com/peru/2019/10/11/futbol/1570792981_043150.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Failing to appear in a single match for Peru in 2020, he finally made his return to the international scene in June 2021, playing two [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)|2022 World Cup qualifiers]] against Colombia and Ecuador.<ref name=RSSSF/> However, he was excluded from the squad for the [[2021 Copa América]] by coach [[Ricardo Gareca]], who deemed him to not yet be in good enough shape to be useful to team, following an injury that had laid him off for seven months.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/br/not%C3%ADcias/por-que-paolo-guerrero-nao-vai-jogar-a-copa-america-com-o-peru/14lrinef821ngzbx98puhpgt1 |title=Por que Paolo Guerrero não vai jogar a Copa América com o Peru? |trans-title=Why won't Paolo Guerrero play in the Copa América with Peru? |language=es |website=www.goal.com |date=11 June 2021 |access-date=24 June 2025 |archive-date=15 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250815235801/https://www.goal.com/br/not%C3%ADcias/por-que-paolo-guerrero-nao-vai-jogar-a-copa-america-com-o-peru/14lrinef821ngzbx98puhpgt1 |url-status=live }}</ref> He then failed to appear in a single match for Peru in 2022, including that [[2022 FIFA World Cup|year's world cup]], making his return to the international scene in June 2023, in a friendly against [[South Korea national football team|South Korea]].<ref name=RSSSF/>

On 26 March 2024, Guerrero scored a stoppage time penalty to seal a 4–1 win in a friendly against [[Dominican Republic national football team|Dominican Republic]], becoming, at the age of 40 years and 86 days, the oldest-ever goalscorer in the history of the Peruvian national team, breaking a 63-year-old record set by [[Faustino Delgado]] in 1961 by just 7 days.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.infobae.com/peru/2024/03/27/paolo-guerrero-y-los-goleadores-mas-veteranos-en-la-historia-de-la-seleccion-peruana/ |title=Paolo Guerrero y los goleadores más veteranos en la historia de la selección peruana |trans-title=Paolo Guerrero and the oldest scorers in the history of the Peruvian national team |language=es |website=www.infobae.com |date=27 March 2024 |access-date=24 June 2025 |archive-date=16 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250816022715/https://www.infobae.com/peru/2024/03/27/paolo-guerrero-y-los-goleadores-mas-veteranos-en-la-historia-de-la-seleccion-peruana/ |url-status=live }}</ref> By overtaking Delgado, he also became the oldest-ever goalscorer in CONMEBOL.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://iffhs.com/en/news/oldest-national-team-scorers-4089 |title=Oldest national team scorers |website=www.iffhs.com |date=28 December 2024 |access-date=24 June 2025 |archive-date=15 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250815102122/https://www.iffhs.com/index.php/posts/4089 |url-status=live }}</ref> Later that year, he was a member of the Peru team that competed in the [[2024 Copa América]], becoming the third Peruvian player to participate in six tournaments, only after [[Lolo Fernández]] and [[Chemo del Solar]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://elpopular.pe/deportes/2024/06/22/paolo-guerrero-disputa-su-sexta-copa-america-con-peru-seleccion-peruana-peru-vs-chile-2117720 |title=Al igual que Lolo Fernández y Chemo del Solar: Paolo Guerrero disputa su sexta Copa América con Perú |trans-title=Like Lolo Fernández and Chemo del Solar, Paolo Guerrero is playing his sixth Copa América with Peru |language=es |website=elpopular.pe |date=22 June 2024 |access-date=24 June 2025 |archive-date=27 November 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251127235153/https://elpopular.pe/deportes/2024/06/22/paolo-guerrero-disputa-su-sexta-copa-america-con-peru-seleccion-peruana-peru-vs-chile-2117720 |url-status=live }}</ref>

Guerrero announced his retirement from international football on 7 January 2025, with 124 appearances and 39 goals scored.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |title=Peru's Top Scorer Paolo Guerrero Retires From International Football |url=https://www.barrons.com/news/peru-s-top-scorer-paolo-guerrero-retires-from-international-football-74e3bb38 |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=barrons |language=en-us |archive-date=15 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250815102207/https://www.barrons.com/news/peru-s-top-scorer-paolo-guerrero-retires-from-international-football-74e3bb38 |url-status=live }}</ref> Two months later, however, on 9 March 2025, he came out of retirement by accepting a call back from the new Peruvian coach [[Óscar Ibáñez]] for the upcoming qualifiers against [[Bolivia]] and [[Venezuela]], scoring his 40th international goal in a 3–1 victory vs Bolivia at the age of 41 years and 78 days, becoming the oldest player to ever score in the World Cup South American qualifiers, surpassing [[Gabriel González (Paraguayan footballer)|Gabriel González]]'s record from 2000, aged 39 years and 168 days.<ref name=Vet>{{Cite web |url=https://buenapepa.pe/guerrero-el-mas-veterano-en-marcar-en-clasificatorias/ |title=El jugador más veterano en marcar en Clasificatorias es peruano y se llama Paolo Guerrero |trans-title=The oldest player to score in the Qualifiers is Peruvian and his name is Paolo Guerrero |language=es |website=buenapepa.pe |date=21 March 2025 |access-date=24 June 2025 |archive-date=9 August 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250809092146/https://buenapepa.pe/guerrero-el-mas-veterano-en-marcar-en-clasificatorias/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He also became the second-oldest goalscorer in any World Cup qualifier, behind only [[Keithroy Cornelius]], who scored for the [[United States Virgin Islands national soccer team|Virgin Islands]] at the age of 43 years in 2011.<ref name=Vet/>

==Personal life==
[[File:Paolo Guerrero.JPG|thumb|Guerrero in 2010]]
Guerrero has a [[fear of flying]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dw-world.de/dw/article/0,,5216622,00.html |title=Fear of flying grounds Hamburg striker's soccer career |date=5 February 2010 |access-date=7 September 2011 |publisher=Deutsche Weller}}</ref> Media reports claim his fear of flying is due to the death of his uncle [[José González Ganoza]] in the [[1987 Alianza Lima air disaster]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.as.com/futbol/articulo/paolo-guerrero-afirma-superara-miedo/20100203dasdasftb_47/Tes |title=Paolo Guerrero afirma que superará su miedo a volar |language=es |date=3 February 2010 |access-date=13 October 2011 |publisher=as.com}}</ref>

Guerrero's older brother, [[Julio Rivera (footballer)|Julio Rivera]], was also a footballer for the Peru national team who progressed through the Alianza Lima youth system.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://tribunaroja.blogspot.com/2008/08/entrevista-al-coyote-rivera.html |title=Entrevista al "coyote" Rivera |language=es |date=15 August 2008 |access-date=8 October 2011 |publisher=tribunaroja.blogspot.com |archive-date=25 April 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120425062743/http://tribunaroja.blogspot.com/2008/08/entrevista-al-coyote-rivera.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The brothers were both following in the path of their uncle who had represented Alianza Lima and the Peru national team before them.

Guerrero is [[Roman Catholic]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://esportes.terra.com.br/noticias/0,,OI6412476-EI2011,00-Guerrero+gasta+bicho+do+Mundial+em+carro+de+quase+US+mil.html |title=Guerrero gasta bicho do Mundial em carro de quase US$ 100 mil |language=pt |website=terra |date=30 December 2012 |access-date=20 November 2015 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304204813/http://esportes.terra.com.br/noticias/0,,OI6412476-EI2011,00-Guerrero+gasta+bicho+do+Mundial+em+carro+de+quase+US+mil.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://noticias.gospelmais.com.br/jogadores-corinthians-dedicam-deus-titulo-mundial-sobre-chelsea-46348.html |title=Corinthians Bicampeão Mundial: Jogadores do timão dedicam a Deus o título e a vitória sobre o Chelsea |language=pt |website=Gnotícias |date=17 December 2012 |access-date=20 November 2015 |first=Dan |last=Martins |archive-date=21 November 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151121100804/http://noticias.gospelmais.com.br/jogadores-corinthians-dedicam-deus-titulo-mundial-sobre-chelsea-46348.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.falandodeflamengo.com.br/2015/11/20/baita-clima-de-fim-de-festa/ |title=Baita clima de fim de festa |language=pt |website=falandodeflamengo.com.br |date=20 November 2015 |access-date=20 November 2015 |first=Felippe |last=Fogli |archive-date=17 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180617021034/http://www.falandodeflamengo.com.br/2015/11/20/baita-clima-de-fim-de-festa/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

His nephew, also named Julio Rivera, was found dead from a robbery in [[Lima]] in 2019. Guerrero held his death with sorrow and honor to his late nephew.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://elbocon.pe/actualidad/sobrino-de-paolo-guerrero-fallece-en-fatal-accidente-en-chorrillos-182858/ |title=Sobrino de Paolo Guerrero muere en fatal accidente |language=es |website=elbocon.pe |date=9 March 2019 |access-date=14 October 2019 |archive-date=14 October 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191014183151/https://elbocon.pe/actualidad/sobrino-de-paolo-guerrero-fallece-en-fatal-accidente-en-chorrillos-182858/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2024, his mother was targeted for extortion by gangs.<ref name="france24.com"/>

In 2016, the film ''[[Guerrero (film)|Guerrero]]'' was released, featuring Paolo Guerrero and the story of his rise to success. On 5 October 2022, [[Netflix]] released Paolo Guerrero's series, ''Contigo capitán'' (The Fight for Justice: Paolo Guerrero in English), showing the story of Guerrero's false doping leading up to the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Redacción EC |date=2022-10-06 |title="Contigo capitán" en Netflix: lo que debes saber de la serie peruana en estreno |url=https://elcomercio.pe/saltar-intro/netflix/series/contigo-capitan-en-netflix-lo-que-debes-saber-de-la-serie-peruana-en-estreno-paolo-guerrero-noticia/#google_vignette |access-date=2025-03-17 |work=El Comercio |language=es-PE |issn=1605-3052 |archive-date=6 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260106165527/https://elcomercio.pe/saltar-intro/netflix/series/contigo-capitan-en-netflix-lo-que-debes-saber-de-la-serie-peruana-en-estreno-paolo-guerrero-noticia/#google_vignette |url-status=live }}</ref>
