'''Marvin Compper''' (born 14 June 1985) is a German [[Association football|football]] manager and a former player who played as a [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|centre back]]. He is the manager of [[Belgian Pro League]] club [[Royal Antwerp FC|Antwerp]]. He won one cap for the [[Germany national football team|Germany national team]].<ref>{{Cite web | url = https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/compper-intl.html | title = Marvin Compper - International Appearances | first = Matthias | last = Arnhold | date = 8 April 2021 | accessdate = 16 April 2021 | publisher = [[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|RSSSF.com]]}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Borussia Mönchengladbach===
[[File:Marvin Compper.jpg|thumb|left|175px|Compper in the [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]] shirt during his three–year spell there.]]

During the 2002–03 season, Compper moved from the youth team of the [[VfB Stuttgart]] to the amateur team of [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]].<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Magath holt Horst Heldt |url=https://www.kicker.de/magath-holt-horst-heldt-277327/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=6 January 2003 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> Shortly after joining the club, he was assigned to the U19 side and eventually to the [[Borussia Mönchengladbach II]] side.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Torjäger Mayer darf wieder ran |url=https://www.kicker.de/torjaeger-mayer-darf-wieder-ran-290195/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=30 October 2003 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title=Fortuna war Uerdingen haushoch überlegen |url=https://www.kicker.de/fortuna-war-uerdingen-haushoch-ueberlegen-294917/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=23 February 2004 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> In July 2005, he signed his first professional contract which ran until 2008.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Compper erhält Vertrag bis 2008 |url=https://www.kicker.de/compper-erhaelt-vertrag-bis-2008-317736/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=12 July 2005 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref>

Shortly after signing his first professional contract, Compper was promoted to the first team and made his debut during the [[2005–06 Bundesliga|2005–06 season]].<ref name="Marvin Compper » Club matches">{{cite web |title=Marvin Compper " Club matches |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/person/pe473/marvin-compper/club-matches/ |publisher=World Football |access-date=8 January 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title=Bögelund muss Gips tragen |url=https://www.kicker.de/boegelund-muss-gips-tragen-320930/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=19 September 2005 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> His first appearance for the club came on 1 October 2005, coming on as a second–half substitute for injured [[Jeff Strasser]], in a 1–0 loss against [[1. FSV Mainz 05]].<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Knieverletzung bei Jeff Strasser |url=https://www.kicker.de/knieverletzung-bei-jeff-strasser-321483/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=2 October 2005 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> Because he spent most of the season on the substitute bench, Compper ended up making only five appearances during the season.<ref name="2005–06 season">{{cite web |title=Marvin Compper |url=http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/bundesliga/vereine/2005-06/34173/vereinsspieler_marvin-compper.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091207035402/http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/bundesliga/vereine/2005-06/34173/vereinsspieler_marvin-compper.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=7 December 2009 |website=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |publisher=kicker |access-date=8 January 2017 |language=German}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title=Trotz Elber und Helveg: Pander plant keine Kurskorrektur |url=https://www.kicker.de/trotz-elber-und-helveg_pander-plant-keine-kurskorrektur-325102/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=15 December 2005 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref>

In the 2006–07 season, Compper made four appearances for the [[Borussia Mönchengladbach II|reserve team]]<ref name="Marvin Compper » Club matches"/> in August 2006.<ref>{{cite web |title=Marvin Compper " Regionalliga Nord 2006/2007 |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/person/pe473/marvin-compper/ |publisher=World Football |access-date=8 January 2017}}</ref> On 14 October 2006, he made his first appearance (as well as his first start), in a 3–1 win over [[VfL Wolfsburg|Wolfsburg]].<ref>{{cite magazine |title=M'gladbach dreht das Spiel |url=https://www.kicker.de/mgladbach-gegen-wolfsburg-2006-bundesliga-763373/analyse |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=14 October 2006 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> Because of the injuries of both [[Filip Daems]] and the national defender [[Marcell Jansen]], he became a regular player in the autumn of 2006 in the [[Bundesliga]].<ref>{{cite magazine |title=M'gladbach dreht das Spiel |url=https://www.kicker.de/mgladbach-gegen-wolfsburg-2006-bundesliga-763373/analyse |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=14 November 2006 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> He had a handful of first team appearances until he was dropped from the first team after criticising Manager [[Jupp Heynckes]] following a 1–1 draw against 1. FSV Mainz 05 on 9 December 2006.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Heynckes suspendiert Compper |url=https://www.kicker.de/heynckes-suspendiert-compper-359067/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=14 December 2006 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> On 30 January 2007, he returned to the first team from suspension, in a 0–0 draw against [[1. FC Nürnberg]], in what turned out to be Heynckes' last game as Manager.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Gladbachs Steigerung reicht nicht |url=https://www.kicker.de/mgladbach-gegen-nuernberg-2007-bundesliga-763480/analyse |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=30 January 2007 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> Following Heynckes' resignation, Compper was given more first team opportunities under new manager [[Jos Luhukay]].<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Luhukay belebt die Borussia |url=https://www.kicker.de/luhukay-belebt-die-borussia-362067/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=26 February 2007 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> He finished the season with 23 league appearances, but the club was relegated at the end of the season, finishing last in the Bundesliga table.<ref name="Marvin Compper » Club matches"/>

In the first half of the 2007–08 season, Compper played only three games for [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]].<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Coulibaly und Gohouri suspendiert |url=https://www.kicker.de/coulibaly-und-gohouri-suspendiert-371076/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=21 October 2007 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title=Paauwe ist unverzichtbar |url=https://www.kicker.de/paauwe-ist-unverzichtbar-138695/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=16 August 2007 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title=Luhukay sieht große Probleme |url=https://www.kicker.de/luhukay-sieht-grosse-probleme-134512/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=30 July 2007 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> Although he did not play regularly at Borussia Mönchengladbach, Compper reflected on his time at the club: "This is the best for my personal development. At Borussia, nobody gave me the feeling that I was needed."<ref>{{cite news |title=Zukunft in Hoffenheim |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/moenchengladbach-3418082.bild.html |work=Bild |language=German |date=7 January 2008 |accessdate=25 December 2017}}</ref>

===TSG 1899 Hoffenheim===
[[File:Marvin Compper 5.jpg|thumb|left|175px|Compper with [[TSG 1899 Hoffenheim]] in 2009.]]
Due to a lack of first-team action, Compper joined [[TSG 1899 Hoffenheim]] in January 2008.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Compper geht nach Hoffenheim |url=https://www.kicker.de/compper-geht-nach-hoffenheim-373750/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=6 January 2008 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref>

Compper made his TSG 1899 Hoffenheim debut on 1 February 2008, where he started the whole game in the centre–back position, in a 2–0 win over [[SV Wehen Wiesbaden|Wehen Wiesbaden]].<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Salihovic trifft und bereitet vor |url=https://www.kicker.de/wiesbaden-gegen-hoffenheim-2008-bundesliga-808026/analyse |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=1 February 2008 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> Ahead of the follow-up match against his former club, Borussia Mönchengladbach, on 10 February 2008, Compper made an interview with [[Bild]], where he said he had no grudge on his departure from the club.<ref>{{cite news |title=Gladbach steht als Aufsteiger fest! |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/compper-interview-3719306.bild.html |work=Bild |language=German |date=10 February 2008 |accessdate=25 December 2017}}</ref> He played the whole match against his former club, where he set up a goal for [[Demba Ba]], in a 4–2 win.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Joker Copado nicht zu bremsen |url=https://www.kicker.de/hoffenheim-gegen-mgladbach-2008-bundesliga-808029/analyse |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=10 February 2008 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> Compper quickly established himself in the first team, where he played in mostly at centre–back.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Geht da noch was? Compper heimlich in Leipzig gelandet |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/marvin-compper/compper-heimlich-in-leipzig-gelandet-37078446.bild.html |work=Bild |language=German |date=1 August 2014 |accessdate=25 December 2017}}</ref> He was previously heavily linked with a move to [[Hellas Verona F.C.|Hellas Verona]] over the summer.<ref>{{cite news |title=Hellas Verona, sul taccuino anche Lazzari e Compper |url=https://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/serie-a/hellas-verona-sul-taccuino-anche-lazzari-e-compper-562333 |publisher=Tutto Mercato Web |language=Italian |date=7 June 2014 |accessdate=25 December 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Hellas, Sogliano conferma: "Seguiamo Compper della Fiorentina" |url=http://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/serie-a/hellas-sogliano-conferma-seguiamo-compper-della-fiorentina-564310 |publisher=Tutto Mercato Web |language=Italian |date=13 June 2014 |accessdate=25 December 2017}}</ref> However, it was made clear he wanted to play in the Bundesliga before joining RB Leipzig.<ref>{{cite news |title=Fiorentina, possibile frenata Compper-Verona. "Vorrei tornare in Bundesliga" |url=https://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/serie-a/fiorentina-possibile-frenata-compper-verona-vorrei-tornare-in-bundesliga-569521 |publisher=Tutto Mercato Web |language=Italian |date=30 June 2014 |accessdate=25 December 2017}}</ref> Upon joining the club, he was given a number 33 shirt ahead of the new season.<ref>{{cite news |title=NEUZUGANG MARVIN COMPPER: So hat mich RB Leipzig überzeugt |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/marvin-compper/so-hat-rb-leipzig-compper-ueberzeugt-37095968.bild.html |work=Bild |language=German |date=4 August 2014 |accessdate=25 December 2017}}</ref>

After being an unused substitute in the first two matches,<ref>{{cite news |title=RB LEIPZIG GEGEN 1860 MÜNCHEN: Sieg-Ansage von Alexander Zorniger |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/rb-leipzig/sieg-ansage-von-zorniger-37169994.bild.html |work=Bild |language=German |date=9 August 2014 |accessdate=25 December 2017}}</ref> Compper made his RB Leipzig debut on 22 August 2014, where he came on as a substitute for injured [[Niklas Hoheneder]], in a 1–0 win over [[FC Erzgebirge Aue|Erzgebirge Aue]].<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Frahn kann's doch noch |url=https://www.kicker.de/leipzig-gegen-aue-2014-bundesliga-2407558/analyse |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=22 August 2014 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> Since making his debut, Compper started every match for the side, alongside [[Tim Sebastian (footballer)|Tim Sebastain]] and [[Lukas Klostermann]] in the central–defence position.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Kimmich & Co. mit breitester Brust |url=https://www.kicker.de/kimmich-26-co-mit-breitester-brust-611855/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=16 September 2009 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title=RB-Trio bestraft Auer Kläglichkeit |url=https://www.kicker.de/leipzig-gegen-aue-2014-dfb-pokal-2788812/analyse |magazine=[[Kicker magazine |title=RB schlägt nochmal zu – Rodnei kommt für die Abwehr |url=https://www.kicker.de/rb-schlaegt-nochmal-zu---rodnei-kommt-fuer-die-abwehr-620279/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=2 February 2015 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> After returning, Compper was given the captaincy for a match against [[FSV Frankfurt]] on 15 February 2015, which they lost 1–0.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Roshi nutzt Coltortis Blackout |url=https://www.kicker.de/leipzig-gegen-fsv-frankfurt-2015-bundesliga-2407720/analyse |magazine=[[Kicker SC]] on 9 March 2015, resulting in him serving a two match ban.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Coltorti rettet einen Punkt in Unterzahl |url=https://www.kicker.de/karlsruhe-gegen-leipzig-2015-bundesliga-2407742/analyse |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=9 March 2015 |access-date=25 December fast eine komplette Elf aus |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/rb-leipzig/gegen-braunschweig-fehlt-fast-die-komplette-elf-37630290.bild.html |work=Bild |language=German |date=12 September 2014 |accessdate=25 December 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title=Kimmich erleidet Außenbandanriss |url=https://www.kicker.de/kimmich-erleidet-aussenbandanriss-613889/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker finished his first season, making a total of 27 appearances in all competitions.

However, at the start of the 2015–16 season, Compper suffered a knee injury that kept him out of the first team for months.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Nukan und Leipzig: Millionen-Deal vorm Abschluss |url=https://www.kicker.de/nukan-und-leipzig_millionen-deal-vorm-abschluss-629895/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=30 June 2015 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> After returning to training from injury in September, he was assigned to the reserve side in order to regain his fitness.<ref>{{cite news |title=Rangnick bringt den 40. Neuen |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/rb-leipzig/spielt-gegen-paderborn-42529170.bild.html |work=Bild |language=German |date=11 September 2015 |accessdate=25 December 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Orban spielt auf Bewährung |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/rb-leipzig/orban-spielt-auf-bewaehrung-42693874.bild.html |work=Bild |language=German |date=24 September 2015 |accessdate=25 December 2017}}</ref> On 4 October 2015, he made his first appearance since returning from injury in a 3–2 win over 1. FC Nürnberg.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=RB zittert sich gegen dezimierten FCN zum Sieg |url=https://www.kicker.de/leipzig-gegen-nuernberg-2015-bundesliga-2855521/analyse |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=4 October 2015 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> Following his return, Compper regained his first team place despite facing new competitions this season.<ref>{{cite news |title=DESHALB FEHLT MARVIN COMPPER BEI RB LEIPZIG ZUM SAISONSTART: Der Knie-Fall |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/rb-leipzig/knie-fall-compper-41819650.bild.html |work=Bild |language=German |date=17 July 2015 |accessdate=25 December 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=LEIPZIGS COMPPER: "So regelmäßig habe ich noch nie getroffen" |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/marvin-compper/hat-noch-nie-so-regelmaessig-getroffen-44798392.bild.html |work=Bild |language=German |date=4 March 2016 |accessdate=25 December 2017}}</ref> He was given a handful of first team appearances until he suffered a muscle injury that kept him out for two weeks in December 2015.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Rangnick: "Wir sind auf Kurs" |url=https://www.kicker.de/rangnick_wir-sind-auf-kurs-640739/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=7 December 2015 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> Compper scored on his return from injury two months later on 7 February 2016, in a 2–0 win over [[Eintracht Braunschweig]].<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Leipzig furios – Gikiewicz pariert und patzt |url=https://www.kicker.de/leipzig-gegen-braunschweig-2016-bundesliga-2855611/analyse |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=7 February 2016 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> Compper later helped the club get promoted to the [[Bundesliga]] for the first time after beating Karlsruher SC 2–0 on 8 May 2016.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Forsberg legt den Grundstein für den Aufstieg |url=https://www.kicker.de/leipzig-gegen-karlsruhe-2016-bundesliga-2855729/analyse |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=8 May 2016 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> At the end of the 2015–16 season, he had made a total of 23 appearances and scoring three times in all competitions.

Despite struggling to regain his fitness ahead of the 2016–17 season,<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Marvin Comppers schnelle Rückkehr |url=https://www.kicker.de/comppers-schnelle-rueckkehr-658021/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=13 August 2016 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> Compper managed to regain his first team place in central defence at the start of the season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Baustelle Abwehr: RB Leipzig benötigt dringend Verteidiger |url=http://www.bild.de/regional/aktuelles/sachsen/rb-leipzig-ist-auf-der-suche-nach-neuem-innenverteidiger-47231978.bild.html |work=Bild |language=German |date=9 August 2016 |accessdate=25 December 2017}}</ref> He appeared in every match for the side since the start of the season.<ref>{{cite news |title=BILD FRAGT ABWEHR-OLDIE COMPPER: Werden Sie wieder Herbstmeister? |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/marvin-compper/werden-sie-wieder-herbstmeister-48469746.bild.html |work=Bild |language=German |date=26 October 2016 |accessdate=25 December 2017}}</ref> However, in November 2016, Compper suffered a tear in a joint capsule that kept him out for the whole year.<ref>{{cite news |title=RB Leipzig möglicherweise länger ohne Compper |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/aktuelles/fussball/rb-leipzig-moeglicherweise-laenger-ohne-compper-48898958.bild.html |work=Bild |language=German |date=23 November 2016 |accessdate=25 December 2017}}</ref> Compper then scored on his return from injury on 21 January 2017, in a 3–0 win over [[Eintracht Frankfurt]].<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Hradecky-Fauxpas öffnet RB die Tore |url=https://www.kicker.de/leipzig-gegen-frankfurt-2017-bundesliga-3317406/analyse |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=21 January 2017 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> Since returning from injury, Compper continued to regain his first team place towards the end of the season and helped the side finish in the second place to qualify for the [[UEFA Champions League]] next season.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=25-Spiele-Hürde: Compper vor Vertragsverlängerung |url=https://www.kicker.de/25-spiele-huerde_compper-vor-vertragsverlaengerung-677447/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=7 May 2017 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title=Poulsen bringt Leipzig auf Siegkurs |url=https://www.kicker.de/leipzig-gegen-freiburg-2017-bundesliga-3317514/analyse |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=15 April 2017 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> Despite being sidelined on three occasions later in the 2016–17 season,<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Hasenhüttl warnt vor Rangnick-Lehrling Gisdol |url=https://www.kicker.de/hasenhuettl-warnt-vor-rangnick-lehrling-gisdol-670789/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=9 February 2017 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |title=Werner meldet sich fit: Hasenhüttl kündigt Rotation an |url=https://www.kicker.de/werner-meldet-sich-fit_hasenhuettl-kuendigt-rotation-an-674889/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=4 April 2017 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=RB Leipzig: Orban und Compper fehlen gegen Ingolstadt |url=http://www.bild.de/regional/aktuelles/sachsen/rb-leipzig-orban-und-compper-fehlen-gegen-51522214.bild.html |work=Bild |language=German |date=29 April 2017 |accessdate=25 December 2017}}</ref> he went on to make a total of 26 appearances and scoring twice in all competitions. At the end of the 2016–17 season, Compper signed a contract extension until 2019.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Compper verlängert – Khedira sagt Adieu |url=https://www.kicker.de/compper-verlaengert---khedira-sagt-adieu-678553/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=21 May 2017 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref>

Ahead of the 2017–18 season, Compper suffered a calf injury during the club's pre–season tour.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Bei Compper hat die Wade zugemacht |url=https://www.kicker.de/bei-compper-hat-die-wade-zugemacht-702276/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=23 July 2017 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> Despite returning to training from injury, just in time for the league started,<ref>{{cite news |title=Hasenhüttls Problemzonen |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/ralph-hasenhuettl/hasenhuettels-problemzonen-52860212.bild.html |work=Bild |language=German |date=14 August 2017 |accessdate=25 December 2017}}</ref> Compper, however, found himself on the substitute bench, as he was fallen behind [[Willi Orban]], [[Dayot Upamecano]], [[Ibrahima Konaté]] and [[Stefan Ilsanker (footballer)|Stefan Ilsanker]]. This was also combined with a strained relationship with Manager [[Ralph Hasenhüttl]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Diese Stars haben keine Chance mehr in ihren Klubs |url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/1-bundesliga/die-aussortierten-stars-der-liga-54008420.bild.html |work=Bild |language=German |date=28 November 2017 |accessdate=25 December 2017}}</ref> By the time of his departure, Compper made three appearances for the side in the first half of 2017–18 season.

===Celtic===
It was reported that [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] had a £1 million bid accepted from RB Leipzig for Compper.<ref name="Commper"/> Compper agreed a move to [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in December 2017, with the deal to take effect on 1 January 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42414457 |title=Celtic: Marvin Compper completes move to Scottish champions |work=BBC Sport |date=20 December 2017 |accessdate=20 December 2017}}</ref> He never made a league appearance for the Scottish giants in one and half years.<ref>{{Cite web | url = https://www.rsssf.org/players/compperdata.html | title = Marvin Compper - Matches and Goals in Bundesliga | first = Matthias | last = Arnhold | date = 8 April 2021 | accessdate = 16 April 2021 | publisher = [[Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation|RSSSF.com]]}}</ref>

===MSV Duisburg===
On 2 July 2019, he signed for [[MSV Duisburg]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.msv-duisburg.de/aktuelles/artikel/hartnaeckigkeit-hat-sich-gelohnt-compper-zwei-jahre-in-zebrastreifen/|title="Hartnäckigkeit hat sich gelohnt": Compper zwei Jahre im Zebrastreifen|publisher=msv-duisburg.de|date=2 July 2019|accessdate=2 July 2019}}</ref> On 1 August 2020, he announced his retirement and moved to the coaching staff.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.msv-duisburg.de/aktuelles/artikel/aktiver-schritt-marvin-compper-wird-co-trainer-beim-msv-duisburg/|title="Aktiver Schritt": Marvin Compper wird Co-Trainer beim MSV Duisburg|publisher=msv-duisburg.de|date=1 August 2020|accessdate=1 August 2020}}</ref>

==International career==
Compper was eligible to play for [[Germany national football team|Germany]] and [[France national football team|France]], as he got a citizenship.<ref name="Compper French"/>

Having previously represented the Germany U17 and Germany U18 side, Compper was called up by [[Germany national under-20 football team|Germany U20]] for the first time, making his debut against [[Italy national under-20 football team|Italy U20]] on 16 February 2005.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Skibbe-Elf trifft auf Italien |url=https://www.kicker.de/skibbe-elf-trifft-auf-italien-310861/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=14 February 2005 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> Three months after making his debut, Compper was called to the Germany U20 squad for the [[2005 FIFA World Youth Championship|FIFA World Youth Championship]] in Netherlands.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=U 20: Aufgebot für die WM 2005 – Vier U-21-Akteure dabei |url=https://www.kicker.de/vier-u-21-akteure-dabei-315410/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=23 May 2005 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> After appearing twice as a substitute in the first two matches, he played his first match of the tournament, where he came on as a second–half substitute, in a 1–0 loss against [[Argentina national under-20 football team|Argentina U20]] on 18 June 2005.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Skibbe-Elf trotz Niederlage weiter |url=https://www.kicker.de/argentinien-gegen-deutschland-2005-u-wm-718701/spielbericht |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=18 June 2005 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> Compper started for the first time in the tournament, as Germany U20 lost 2–1 to [[Brazil national under-20 football team|Brazil]] after the game went to extra time, eliminating the side from the competitions.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=U 20 gibt Sieg aus der Hand |url=https://www.kicker.de/deutschland-gegen-brasilien-2005-u-wm-718724/spielbericht |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=24 June 2005 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> He went on to make eleven appearances for the U20 side.

On 13 November 2008, Compper was called up by [[Germany national football team|Germany]] for the first time.<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Mit Compper, Weis und Schäfer |url=https://www.kicker.de/mit-compper-weis-und-schaefer-500373/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=13 November 2008 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> Five days later after being called up again, on 19 November 2008, Compper received his sole international cap in a friendly against [[England national football team|England]],<ref name="Commper">{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42379004 |title=Marvin Compper: Celtic close in on £1m signing of RB Leipzig defender |first=Chris |last=McLaughlin |work=BBC Sport |date=16 December 2017 |accessdate=19 December 2017}}</ref> making him the first [[TSG 1899 Hoffenheim|Hoffenheim]] player to be capped by [[Germany national football team|Germany]].<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Terry macht's mit Köpfchen |url=https://www.kicker.de/deutschland-gegen-england-2008-nationalteams-freundschaftsspiele-843715/analyse |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=19 November 2008 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref> After the match, Compper reflected on his debut, saying: "I was very happy to play from the start, but my debut was only marred by the defeat, it's a shame we could not finish the year successfully."<ref>{{cite magazine |title=Löw: "Schlechter Tag" |url=https://www.kicker.de/loew_schlechter-tag-500642/artikel |magazine=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |language=German |date=19 November 2008 |access-date=25 December 2017}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
On 26 October 2021, Compper was hired by [[Russian Premier League]] club [[FC Lokomotiv Moscow]] as an assistant coach.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=[[FC Lokomotiv Moscow]]|url=https://www.fclm.ru/ru/publications/news/25098|title=Марвин Комппер вошёл в тренерский штаб ФК "Локомотив"|date=26 October 2021|language=ru}}</ref> On 1 March 2022, Lokomotiv manager [[Markus Gisdol]] resigned due to the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|Russian invasion of Ukraine]] and Compper was appointed [[caretaker manager]].<ref>{{cite press release|publisher=[[FC Lokomotiv Moscow]]|url=https://www.fclm.ru/ru/publications/news/25694|title=Марвин Комппер будет готовить команду к ближайшим матчам|date=1 March 2022|language=ru}}</ref> [[Dmitri Loskov]] and then [[Oleg Pashinin]] were officially registered with the league as Lokomotiv's caretaker managers as Compper did not possess the mandatory [[UEFA Pro Licence]].<ref>{{cite press release|publisher=[[FC Lokomotiv Moscow]]|url=https://www.fclm.ru/ru/publications/news/25708|title=Лоськов: Нужно работать над ошибками и двигаться дальше|date=3 March 2022|language=ru}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release|publisher=[[FC Lokomotiv Moscow]]|url=https://www.fclm.ru/ru/publications/news/25721|title=Пашинин: Считаю, что мы победили заслуженно|date=6 March 2022|language=ru}}</ref> On 4 April 2022, [[Zaur Khapov]] was appointed Lokomotiv manager, but club's [[sporting director]] Thomas Zorn commented that this is a formality as Khapov possesses a proper license, and Compper will continue performing most of the manager's duties.<ref>{{cite press release|publisher=[[FC Lokomotiv Moscow]]|url=https://www.fclm.ru/news/n/zaur-khapov-glavnyy-trener-fk-lokomotiv/|title=ЗАУР ХАПОВ — ГЛАВНЫЙ ТРЕНЕР ФК "ЛОКОМОТИВ"|date=4 April 2022|access-date=4 April 2022|language=ru}}</ref> On 30 June 2022, [[Josef Zinnbauer]] was appointed head coach of Lokomotiv, with Compper continuing to work at the club.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Lokomotiv Moscow|url=https://www.fclm.ru/news/n/josef-zinnbauer-new-head-coach/|title=НА ДОЛЖНОСТЬ ГЛАВНОГО ТРЕНЕРА "ЛОКОМОТИВА" НАЗНАЧЕН ЙОЗЕФ ЦИННБАУЭР|date=30 June 2022|access-date=30 June 2022|language=ru}}</ref> Compper was dismissed by Lokomotiv on 5 September 2022, following a weak start of the 2022–23 season.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=[[FC Lokomotiv Moscow]]|url=https://www.fclm.ru/news/n/marvin-kompper/|title=МАРВИН КОМППЕР ПОКИДАЕТ ТРЕНЕРСКИЙ ШТАБ|date=5 September 2022|language=ru}}</ref>

On 3 August 2026, Compper was hired as the head coach of [[Belgian Pro League]] club [[Royal Antwerp FC|Antwerp]] with a two-season contract.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Royal Antwerp FC|url=https://www.royalantwerpfc.be/nieuws/nieuws/marvin-compper-nieuwe-t1|title=Marvin Compper nieuwe T1 van RAFC|trans-title=Marvin Compper new T1 of RAFC|date=3 August 2026|access-date=20 August 2026|language=nl}}</ref>

'''Martín Zubimendi Ibáñez''' (born 2 February 1999) is a Spanish professional [[footballer]] who plays as a [[defensive midfielder]] for {{English football updater|Arsenal}} club [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] and the [[Spain national football team|Spain national team]].

Zubimendi began his career at [[Real Sociedad]], making his first-team debut in 2019. He made over 200 appearances and won the [[2019–20 Copa del Rey]] with the club. In July 2025, he signed for Arsenal for a reported initial fee of £55.8m.

Zubimendi made his senior debut for [[Spain national football team|Spain]] in 2021, having previously represented them at various youth levels. He was part of Spain's victorious squads at the [[2023 UEFA Nations League Finals]], [[UEFA Euro 2024]] and the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].

==Club career==
===Real Sociedad===
Zubimendi joined [[Real Sociedad]]'s youth setup in 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cadenaser.com/emisora/2020/06/26/radio_san_sebastian/1593182504_401676.html|title=Zubimendi llega para quedarse|trans-title=Zubimendi arrives to stay|publisher=[[Cadena SER]]|language=es|date=26 June 2020|accessdate=28 June 2020}}</ref> He made his senior debut with [[Real Sociedad C]] on 27 August 2016, playing the last seven minutes in a 0–0 [[Tercera División]] home draw against [[SCD Durango|Durango]].{{citation needed|date=August 2021}}

On 25 July 2018, Zubimendi renewed his contract until 2022, and was definitely promoted to [[Real Sociedad B|the reserves]] in [[Segunda División B]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/real-sociedad/20180725/451101213696/la-real-renueva-a-martin-zubimendi-hasta-2022.html|title=La Real renueva a Martín Zubimendi hasta 2022|trans-title=Real renew Martín Zubimendi until 2022|publisher=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|language=es|date=25 July 2018|accessdate=28 June 2020}}</ref> The following 28 April, he made his first team – and [[La Liga]] – debut, coming on as a late [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for [[Rubén Pardo (footballer)|Rubén Pardo]] in a 2–1 home win over [[Getafe CF|Getafe]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/2019/04/28/primera/1556471966_052236.html|title=La Real respira y complica la Champions al Getafe|trans-title=Real breathe and complicate Getafe's Champions place|publisher=[[Diario AS]]|language=es|date=28 April 2019|accessdate=28 June 2020}}</ref> On 24 July 2020, he renewed his contract with the ''Txuri-urdin'' until 2025, being definitively promoted to the main squad.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realsociedad.eus/en/news/details/until-2025|title=Until 2025|publisher=Real Sociedad|date=24 July 2020|accessdate=8 August 2020}}</ref>

On 24 February 2022, Zubimendi scored his first goal in European competitions in a 3–1 home defeat against [[RB Leipzig]] during the [[2021–22 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] knockout round play-offs.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/europa-league/r-sociedad-vs-leipzig/cronica/2022/02/24/6217c1f2e2704e089d8b45c0.html |title=Un sueño que se esfuma |publisher=Marca |language=es |date=24 February 2022 }}</ref> A month later, on 13 March, he scored his first La Liga goal in a 1–0 victory over [[Deportivo Alavés|Alavés]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.realsociedad.eus/en/news/details/la-real-record-another-victory |title=La Real record another victory |publisher=Real Sociedad |date=13 March 2022 }}</ref> In October, he extended his contract with the club until 2027.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.football-espana.net/2022/10/15/real-sociedad-confirm-martin-zubimendi-extension-until-2027 |title=Real Sociedad confirm Martin Zubimendi extension until 2027 |publisher=Football España |date=15 October 2022 }}</ref> On 20 September 2023, he made his [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] debut in a 1–1 draw against [[Inter Milan]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.tribalfootball.com/articles/real-sociedad-midfielder-zubimendi-so-proud-to-play-champions-league-in-my-hometown-4470888 |title=Real Sociedad midfielder Zubimendi: So proud to play Champions League in my hometown |publisher=Tribal Football |date=20 September 2023 }}</ref>

for Arsenal |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/martin-zubimendi-signs-arsenal |access-date=6 July 2025 |website=Arsenal F.C. |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=de Roché |first1=Art ==International career==
Zubimendi represented the [[Spain national under-19 football team|Spain under-19]]s in a [[Exhibition match|friendly]] 2–1 loss to the [[Portugal national under-19 football team|Portugal under-19]]s on 15 November 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.futboljuvenil.es/espana-sub-19-ofrece-una-buena-imagen-ante-portugal/|title=España Sub-19 ofrece una buena imagen ante Portugal|trans-title=Spain under-19 offer a good image against Portugal|publisher=Fútbol Juvenil|first=Cristina|last=Ripoll|language=es|date=15 November 2017|accessdate=14 June 2020}}</ref>

Due to the isolation of some national team players following the positive [[COVID-19]] test of [[Sergio Busquets]], Spain's under-21 squad were called up for the international friendly against [[Lithuania national football team|Lithuania]] on 8 June 2021.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://sefutbol.com/oficial-lista-convocados-encuentro-lituania |title=Oficial {{!}} Lista de convocados para el encuentro ante Lituania |trans-title=Official {{!}} Squad list for the match against Lithuania |work=[[Royal Spanish Football Federation]] |date=6 June 2021 |access-date=7 June 2021 |language=es |archive-date=8 October 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211008070336/https://sefutbol.com/oficial-lista-convocados-encuentro-lituania |url-status=dead }}</ref> Zubimendi made his senior debut in the match.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/international-football/espana-vs-lituania/cronica/2021/06/08/60bfd85222601dc65d8b458f.html|title=Spain youngsters impress in Lithuania rout|website=MARCA|date=8 June 2021|accessdate=8 June 2021}}</ref>

On 7 June 2024, he was selected in the 26-man squad for [[UEFA Euro 2024]].<ref>{{cite news |date=7 June 2024 |title=Official {{!}} Final Spain squad for the Euro 2024 finals |url=https://rfef.es/en/noticias/final-spain-squad-for-the-euro-2024-finals |publisher=[[Royal Spanish Football Federation]] |access-date=13 July 2024}}</ref> On 15 June, he made his first appearance in the Euros against [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]] as a substitute. He went on to play the full match against [[Albania national football team|Albania]] on 24 June, and came off the bench in both the semi-final victory over [[France national football team|France]] on 9 July and in [[UEFA Euro 2024 final|the final]] against [[England national football team|England]] on 14 July as Spain won the tournament.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/euro2024/news/028f-1b5e5c2b7b67-d5faab9be20b-1000--spain-2-1-england-late-oyarzabal-winner-earns-la-roja-reco/ |title=Spain 2–1 England: Late Oyarzabal winner earns La Roja record fourth EURO crown|website=UEFA|date=14 July 2024 |access-date=16 July 2024 }}</ref>

On 25 May 2026, Zubimendi was named in Spain's squad for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/spain-squad-announcement-luis-de-la-fuente|title=Yamal, Rodri and Cucurella in strong Spain squad|date=25 May 2026|access-date=12 June 2026}}</ref> He had limited involvement in the tournament with [[Pedri]], [[Dani Olmo]], [[Fabián Ruiz]] and [[Rodri]] preferred for the midfield places, but came on as a substitute for Rodri in extra time of [[2026 FIFA World Cup final|the final]] as Spain defeated [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] to win the trophy.<ref>[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cgk4ymn3n72t#Report Spain 1–0 Argentina], Phil McNulty, ''BBC Sport'', 19 July 2026</ref>

==Style of play==
Zubimendi's versatile style of play draws comparisons to renowned players, notably [[Sergio Busquets]]. He showcases composure and control, guiding plays and adjusting the game's tempo. His role involves initiating plays from deep positions, displaying precise decision-making. Zubimendi's aptitude for receiving passes and creating space is reminiscent of Busquets, reflecting a deep understanding of the game and the art of crafting opportunities. Additionally, his technical abilities, including dribbling and deep runs, align with top midfielders, while his ball retention in tight spaces mirrors qualities seen in players like [[Xabi Alonso]] and [[David Silva]].<ref name="Lowe-2022" /><ref>{{cite web |last=Kemp |first=Jamie |url=https://theanalyst.com/eu/2022/10/zubimendi-the-real-sociedad-midfielder-finding-stardom-in-simplicity/ |title=Martín Zubimendi: The Real Sociedad Midfielder Finding Stardom in Simplicity |publisher=The Analyst |date=14 October 2022 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Harris |first=Thom |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4600543/2023/06/13/martin-zubimendi-is-the-calm-and-methodical-heart-of-real-sociedads-midfield/ |title=Martin Zubimendi is the Gen-Z Sergio Busquets at the heart of Real Sociedad’s midfield |publisher=The Athletic |date=13 June 2023 }}</ref>

'''Benjamin Fernand Lucien François Stambouli''' (born 13 August 1990) is a French former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[defensive midfielder]] or [[centre-back]].

Stambouli began his professional career with [[Montpellier HSC|Montpellier]], playing 130 games from 2010 to 2014 and winning Ligue 1 in 2012. After a season each with [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] and [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] – winning five domestic trophies with the latter – he signed for [[Schalke 04|Schalke]] in 2016. Stambouli made twelve appearances for [[France national under-21 football team|France at under-21 level]] from 2010 to 2012.

==Early life==
Benjamin Fernand Lucien François Stambouli<ref>{{cite web |url=https://tff.org/Default.aspx?pageId=526&kisiId=2294053 |title=Benjamin Fernand Lucien Francois Stambouli |publisher=Turkish Football Federation |access-date=28 October 2022}}</ref> was born on 13 August 1990 in [[Marseille]], Bouches-du-Rhône.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/FootballFicheJoueur35770.html |title=Benjamin Stambouli |newspaper=L'Équipe |location=Paris |access-date=28 October 2022 |language=fr}}</ref> His father was [[Henri Stambouli]], a former football player and former head coach of French club [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]].<ref>{{cite news |title=OM. Henri Stambouli, ancien entraîneur de Marseille, est mort à 62 ans |url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/sport/football/olympique-de-marseille/om-henri-stambouli-ancien-entraineur-de-marseille-est-mort-a-62-ans-c59969a8-853c-11ee-9611-92c86d4d078f |access-date=29 November 2023 |publisher=Ouest France |date=17 November 2023}}</ref> One of his grandfathers is former manager [[Gérard Banide]], and his uncle is manager [[Laurent Banide]].<ref name="Daniez 2015">{{cite web |last=Daniez |first= Clément |title=Qui est Benjamin Stambouli, la dernière recrue du PSG? |website=L'Express |date=20 July 2015 |url=https://www.lexpress.fr/actualite/sport/football/qui-est-benjamin-stambouli-la-derniere-recrue-du-psg_1700185.html |language=fr | access-date=23 November 2020}}</ref><ref name="leparisien.fr 2011">{{cite web |title=Les Stambouli, au nom du pèreâ?¦ [''sic''] et du fils |website=Le Parisien |date=23 April 2011 |url=https://www.leparisien.fr/sports/les-stambouli-au-nom-du-pere-et-du-fils-23-04-2011-1419577.php |language=fr | access-date=23 November 2020}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Montpellier===
[[File:Benjamin STAMBOULI.JPG|thumb|upright|Stambouli with [[Montpellier HSC|Montpellier]] in 2012]]

Stambouli spent eight months as a child at [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]], and also had two years at [[CS Sedan Ardennes|Sedan]] before joining the ranks of [[Montpellier HSC|Montpellier]] in July 2004.<ref name=fff/> On 3 March 2010, he signed his first professional contract, a three-year deal with Montpellier.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mhscfoot.com/liste-saisons/saison-2009-2010/articles/benjamin-stambouli-passe-professionnel |publisher=Montpellier HSC |title=Benjamin Stambouli passe professionnel |date=3 March 2010 |access-date=8 January 2011 |language=fr |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100306162749/http://www.mhscfoot.com/liste-saisons/saison-2009-2010/articles/benjamin-stambouli-passe-professionnel |archive-date=6 March 2010}}</ref>

Stambouli made his professional debut on 8 August 2010 on the first day of the [[2010–11 Ligue 1]] season, playing the full 90 minutes of a 1–0 home win over [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Ligue 1, Montpellier – Stambouli satisfait |url=http://m.goal.com/e/fr/news/29/ligue-1/2010/08/08/2061975/ligue-1-montpellier-stambouli-satisfait |access-date=26 February 2019 |website=Goal.com |date=8 August 2010 |language=fr}}</ref> During the 2011–12 season, he played 26 league games as Montpellier won the Ligue 1 title for the first time in the club's history. During the 2013–14 season, Stambouli played 37 out of Montpellier's 38 league games and was promoted to position of vice-captain behind Brazilian [[Vitorino Hilton]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://frenchfootballweekly.com/2013/12/22/three-pailladins-benjamin-stambouli |website=French Football weekly |title=Three Pailladins – Benjamin Stambouli |date=22 December 2013 | access-date = 23 September 2015 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150121165844/http://frenchfootballweekly.com/2013/12/22/three-pailladins-benjamin-stambouli/ | archive-date = 21 January 2015 | url-status = dead}}</ref>

===Tottenham Hotspur===
On 1 September 2014, Stambouli signed for [[Premier League]] team [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] for an undisclosed fee, rumoured to be in the region of £4.7 million.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/29021810 |website=BBC Sport |title=Tottenham sign Benjamin Stambouli |date=1 September 2014 |access-date=21 July 2015}}</ref><ref>[http://www.tottenhamhotspur.com/news/stambouli-completes-move-010914/ Stambouli completes move]. Retrieved 1 September 2014</ref> He scored his only goal for the club in a [[UEFA Europa League]] match against [[FK Partizan|Partizan]] on 27 November, following up a shot from [[Roberto Soldado]], which had rebounded off of the post. Stambouli appeared in every round of the [[EFL Cup|League Cup]] as Tottenham reached the final at [[Wembley Stadium|Wembley]] where, however, Stambouli was an unused substitute as Tottenham were beaten 2–0 by Chelsea.<ref name=2015LeagueCupFinal>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/31572594 |title=Chelsea 2–0 Tottenham Hotspur |first=Phil |last=McNulty |website=BBC Sport |date=1 March 2015 |access-date=28 April 2019}}</ref> At the conclusion of his first year at Spurs, Stambouli had made just 12 appearances in the Premier League.<ref name="auto">{{cite web |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/11/transfer-zone/2015/07/20/13734542/stambouli-joining-psg-confirms-blanc |website=Goal.com |title=Stambouli joining PSG, confirms Blanc |date=20 July 2015 | access-date = 21 July 2015}}</ref>

===Paris Saint-Germain===
On 20 July 2015, [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] manager [[Laurent Blanc]] confirmed Stambouli would be joining PSG for a fee of £6 million, £1.3 million more than Tottenham had paid a year earlier.<ref name="auto"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33605384 |website=BBC Sport |title=Benjamin Stambouli: Tottenham midfielder joins Paris St-Germain |date=21 July 2015|access-date = 21 July 2015}}</ref> He made his debut on 1 August in the [[2015 Trophée des Champions]] at the [[Stade Saputo]] in Montreal, playing the final 20 minutes in place of [[Marco Verratti]] in a 2–0 victory over [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=West |first1=Harry |title=Paris Saint-Germain 2–0 Lyon: Aurier and Cavani seal more silverware |url=http://www.goal.com/en-ca/news/4181/france/2015/08/01/14082652/paris-saint-germain-2-0-lyon-aurier-and-cavani-seal-more|access-date=3 August 2015 |website=Goal.com |date=1 August 2015}}</ref> Stambouli played 40 total matches for PSG, winning all four domestic trophies in his one whole season, but did not score and assist and was unpopular with some fans due to his connections to their rival Marseille.<ref>{{cite news |title=Benjamin Stambouli signe à Schalke 04 (Officiel) |url=https://sport.francetvinfo.fr/football/ligue-1/benjamin-stambouli-signe-schalke-04-officiel-355997 |access-date=26 February 2019 |publisher=France TV |date=26 August 2016 |language=fr}}</ref><ref name=espn>{{cite news |last1=Johnson |first1=Jonathan |title=Benjamin Stambouli completes move to Schalke after one year at PSG |url=http://www.espn.in/football/soccer-transfers/story/2937914/benjamin-stambouli-completes-move-to-schalke-after-one-year-at-psg |access-date=26 February 2019 |publisher=ESPN |date=26 August 2016 |quote=The man from Marseille – something which did not add to his popularity with PSG supporters – made 40 appearances across all competitions in his time in the French capital, failing to score a single goal or provide an assist.}}</ref> His final match was the [[2016 Trophée des Champions]], which his team won 4–1 against Lyon in Austria.<ref name=espn/>

===Schalke 04===
After spending only one season with the French champions, Stambouli joined Germany's [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]] on a four-year contract on 26 August 2016.<ref>{{cite web |date=26 August 2016 |title=Benjamin Stambouli erhält Vierjahresvertrag bis 30 June 2020 |url=http://www.schalke04.de/de/aktuell/news/160826_stambouli/page/8284--10-213-.html |access-date=26 August 2016 |publisher=FC Schalke 04 |language=de |archive-date=28 August 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160828102017/http://www.schalke04.de/de/aktuell/news/160826_stambouli/page/8284--10-213-.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> He made his debut on 9 September in a 2–0 home loss to reigning champions [[FC Bayern Munich]].<ref>{{cite news |title=FC Schalke 04 0–2 Bayern Munich |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37268666 |access-date=26 February 2019 |website=BBC Sport |date=9 September 2016}}</ref> On 20 May, he was sent off for unsportsmanlike conduct in the last game of the season, a 1–1 draw at [[FC Ingolstadt 04]], and suspended for two matches.<ref>{{cite news |title=Zwei Spiele Sperre für Schalkes Stambouli |url=https://www.dfb.de/news/detail/zwei-spiele-sperre-fuer-schalkes-stambouli-167851/ |access-date=26 February 2019 |publisher=German Football Association |date=22 May 2017 |language=de}}</ref>

Stambouli suffered a [[metatarsal]] injury in October 2019, ruling him out for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Fayiga |first1=Kunle |title=Schalke sporting director Schneider hopeful of Stambouli contract renewal |url=https://www.goal.com/en-ie/news/schalke-sporting-director-schneider-hopeful-of-stambouli/fptefzfx1dpm190ie136m3yib |access-date=21 June 2020 |website=Goal.com |date=17 June 2020}}</ref> On 4 August 2020, he extended his contract with Schalke until 2023.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://schalke04.de/en/team/benjamin-stambouli-stays-a-royal-blue/ |title=Benjamin Stambouli stays a Royal Blue |publisher=FC Schalke 04 |date=4 August 2020}}</ref> Due to a clause in that deal, he left following their relegation in May 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Shkodran Mustafi among 10 to leave relegated Schalke |url=https://apnews.com/article/ligue-1-bundesliga-premier-league-shkodran-mustafi-international-soccer-f6b6197d935fcd21aec65de8c40150f7 |access-date=8 July 2021 |work=Associated Press News |date=20 May 2021}}</ref>

===Adana Demirspor===
On 26 July 2021, Stambouli joined Turkish club [[Adana Demirspor]] on a two-year contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 July 2021 |title=Takımımız, Montpellier, Tottenham ve Paris Saint Germain'in yanı sıra son olarak Schalke 04 forması giymiş 30 yaşındaki orta saha oyuncusu Benjamin #Stambouli ile 2 yıllık anlaşmaya varmıştır. |url=https://twitter.com/adskulubu/status/1419596858490507265|url-status=live|access-date=26 July 2021 |via=Twitter |publisher=Adana Demirspor |language=tr|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210726095411/https://twitter.com/AdsKulubu/status/1419596858490507265 |archive-date=26 July 2021}}</ref> He was one of a number of high-profile players joining the newly promoted [[Süper Lig]] club that summer, including [[Mario Balotelli]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Winterburn |first1=Chris |title=Adana Demirspor hoping to take Turkish Super Lig by storm with ambitious recruitment drive |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/international-football/2021/07/27/61001e7346163f75898b4592.html |access-date=13 September 2021 |newspaper=Marca |location=Madrid |date=27 July 2021}}</ref> He contributed two goals and four assists in 32 league matches in his first season, and one goal and five assists from 30 games in his second. His contract was then extended for another two years.<ref>{{cite news |title=Adana Demirspor Benjamin Stambouli ile sözleşme yeniledi (Turkish) |url=https://www.haberturk.com/adana-demirspor-benjamin-stambouli-ile-sozlesme-yeniledi-3604169-spor |access-date=13 Sep 2023 |publisher=haberturk.com |date=1 July 2023}}</ref> He was the captain of the team in the 2023–24 season. He scored the first goal of Adana Demirspor in the European cup qualifying history against [[CFR Cluj|Cluj]] in the [[UEFA Europa Conference League|UEFA European Conference League]] in that season. On 31 January 2024, the club announced a mutual agreement with Stambouli to end his contract.

===Reims===
On 1 February 2024, Stambouli signed with [[Stade de Reims|Reims]] until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Reims|url=https://www.stade-de-reims.com/benjamin-stambouli-encadreur-de-jeunesse/|title=Benjamin Stambouli, encadreur de jeunesse|trans-title=Benjamin Stambouli, youth supervisor|date=1 February 2024|access-date=2 February 2024|language=fr}}</ref>

==International career==
Stambouli played 14 times for France at [[France national under-21 football team|under-21 level]], from his debut on 8 October 2010 in a 2–0 friendly win over [[Turkey national under-21 football team|Turkey]] in [[Troyes]].<ref name=fff>{{cite web |title=Benjamin Stambouli |url=https://www.fff.fr/equipes-de-france/tous-les-joueurs/fiche-joueur/2017114279-benjamin-stambouli |publisher=French Football Federation |access-date=26 February 2019 |language=fr |archive-date=27 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190227181948/https://www.fff.fr/equipes-de-france/tous-les-joueurs/fiche-joueur/2017114279-benjamin-stambouli |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Stambouli is eligible for the [[Algeria national football team|Algeria national team]] because his father was born there; in November 2018 he denied rumours that he would play for them.<ref>{{cite news |title=Algérie : la position ferme de Benjamin Stambouli |url=http://www.footmercato.net/flash-mercato/benjamin-stambouli-ne-jouera-pas-avec-la-selection-algerienne_240376 |access-date=26 February 2019 |website=Foot Mercato |date=6 November 2018 |language=fr}}</ref>

Atlante|Atlante]] | caps8 = 4 | goals8 = 0 | years9 = 2013 | clubs9 = → [[Levante UD|Levante]] (loan) | caps9 = 13 | goals9 = 0 | years10 = 2014 | clubs10 = [[Asteras Tripolis F.C.|Asteras Tripoli]] | caps10 = 9 | goals10 = 0 | years11 = 2015 | clubs11 = [[Racing de Santander|Racing Santander]] | caps11 = 1 | goals11 = 0 | years12 = 2015 | clubs12 = [[ATK (football club)|Atlético Kolkata]] | caps12 = 9 | goals12 = 1 | years13 = 2016–2017 | clubs13 = [[CD Lealtad|Lealtad]] | caps13 = 19 | goals13 = 1 | years14 = 2017–2018 | clubs14 = [[Peña Sport FC|Peña Sport]] | caps14 = 33 | goals14 = 6 | years15 = 2019–2020 | clubs15 = [[CD Izarra|Izarra]] | caps15 = 32 | goals15 = 1 | nationalyears1 = 2003 | nationalteam1 = [[Spain national under-21 football team|Spain U21]] | nationalcaps1 = 6 | nationalgoals1 = 3 | nationalyears2 = 2011 | nationalteam2 = [[Cape Verde national football team|Cape Verde]] | nationalcaps2 = 2 | nationalgoals2 = 1 | club-update = 26 February 2020 | nationalteam-update = }} '''Valmiro Lopes Rocha''' (born 23 April 1981), known as '''Valdo''', is a former [[Cape Verde]]an professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played mainly as a [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]]. Valdo had played for several clubs in [[La Liga]] during his professional career, notably [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]], [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] and [[Levante UD|Levante]]. Over 12 seasons in the competition, he appeared in 258 matches and scored 34 goals. ==Early years== Valdo was born in [[Villablino]], [[León, Spain|León]], in the region of [[Laciana]], where his parents had moved after migrating from Cape Verde to work in the coal mines.{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/suplementos/cronica/2007/587/1169938804.html |title=El Bierzo no es Alcorcón|trans-title=El Bierzo is not Alcorcón|work=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]|date=28 January 2007|language=es}} He started playing football with the amateur side [[CF Pozuelo de Alarcón]] in [[Madrid]] and stayed there for the following seven years. A Spanish Movie, Llenos de Gracias, is loosely based on his early years and how he was discovered while playing for a local soccer team. ==Club career== ===Real Madrid / Osasuna=== In 2001, [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] signed him for its reserve teams. He played in 2001–02 with [[Real Madrid Castilla]] and, also during [[2001–02 La Liga|that season]], received first-team opportunities in [[La Liga]], the [[Copa del Rey]] and the [[UEFA Champions League]], with the ''Merengues'' eventually [[2001–02 UEFA Champions League|winning the latter competition]].{{cite news|url=https://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2001/10/30/champions/1004471704.html|title=Aterrizaje de emergencia del Madrid en Moscú|trans-title=Emergency landing for Madrid in Moscow|work=El Mundo|language=es|date=30 October 2001|access-date=28 March 2020}}
- {{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/diario/2002/03/21/deportes/1016665205_850215.html|title=Portillo deja huella|trans-title=Portillo makes a mark|work=[[El País]]|language=es|date=21 March 2002|access-date=28 March 2020}} In January 2003, Valdo moved to the league club [[CA Osasuna]], first on loan,{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/0192-0f844ea9d899-9171faddf26e-1000--valdo-move-made-permanent/ |title=Valdo move made permanent|publisher=UEFA|date=7 June 2003}} where he developed as a top division player, scoring five goals in 35 games in [[2003–04 La Liga|his first full season]].{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2003/08/31/liga/1062282035.html|title=Regreso amargo del Albacete|trans-title=Bitter return for Albacete|work=El Mundo|date=31 August 2003|access-date=22 December 2016|language=es}} On 11 April 2004, he scored in a 3–0 away win against his former club.{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=148966&cc=5739 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040912153351/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=148966&cc=5739 |url-status=dead |archive-date=12 September 2004 |title=Real Madrid 0–3 Osasuna|website=[[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]]|date=11 April 2004}} In the [[2005–06 La Liga|2005–06 season]], although he featured much less mainly due to a [[groin]] ailment,{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/01b3-0f848398fbd9-58f4e728c40b-1000--valdo-falls-victim-to-groin-injury/ |title=Valdo falls victim to groin injury|publisher=UEFA|date=23 March 2006}} Valdo scored in a 2–1 home victory over [[FC Barcelona]] on 12 March 2006, as Osasuna qualified for the first time for the [[2006–07 UEFA Champions League|Champions League qualifying rounds]]. After the [[2006–07 UEFA Cup|demotion]] to the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]], he helped the team reach the last-four against [[Sevilla FC]], scoring twice in ten matches. ===Espanyol=== [[RCD Espanyol]] signed Valdo at the end of [[2006–07 La Liga|2006–07]] to a four-year deal.{{cite web|url=http://www.as.com/futbol/articulo/valdo-jugara-espanyol-proximas-temporadas/dasftb/20070623dasdasftb_10/Tes |title=Valdo jugará en el Espanyol las cuatro próximas temporadas|trans-title=Valdo to play in Espanyol the next four seasons|website=[[Diario AS]]|date=23 June 2007|language=es}} He played his first game for the [[Barcelona]]-based side against [[CF Peralada]] during the pre-season. On 14 July 2009, after having appeared sparingly, Valdo moved to [[Málaga CF]] in a [[2009–10 La Liga|season]]-long loan. After being dropped from the squad for several months due to his bad performances, he was brought back on 27 February 2010; he scored his first goal for the club against Barcelona on the same day, but Málaga lost 1–2 away at [[Camp Nou]].{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/275907?cc=5739 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130102222851/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/275907?cc=5739 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2 January 2013 |title=Barca battle back to stay top|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=7 February 2010}} ===Levante=== On 13 August 2010, Valdo left Espanyol and signed with [[Levante UD]], reuniting with his Málaga teammates [[Gustavo Munúa]] and [[Xavi Torres]].{{cite web|url=http://es.levanteud.com/noticias/levante11347.html |title=Valdo, nuevo fichaje del Levante UD |trans-title=Valdo, new Levante UD signing|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720180238/http://es.levanteud.com/noticias/levante11347.html|archivedate=20 July 2011|publisher=Levante UD|date=13 August 2010|language=es}} He contributed heavily during [[2010–11 La Liga|his first season]] – 2,119 minutes, 25 starts – as Levante retained their top-flight status, scoring against [[Getafe CF]] in a 2–0 home win{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=302094&cc=5739 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121102085627/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=302094&cc=5739 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2 November 2012 |title=Valdo and Caicedo on target|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=29 January 2011}} and [[Villarreal CF]] for a 1–0 away victory.{{cite |archive-date=2 November 2012 |title=Villarreal shocked by Levante|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=5 February 2011}} Valdo was even more important in [[2011–12 La Liga|2011–12]] and scored on six occasions as Levante [[2012–13 UEFA Europa League|qualified for the Europa League]] for the first time ever after finishing sixth. Two of those goals near the end of the season, in home defeats of [[Atlético Madrid]] (2–0){{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/323742?cc=5739 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120414010421/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/323742?cc=5739 |url-status=dead |archive-date=14 April 2012 |title=Granotas leap into top four|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=8 April 2012}} and [[Granada CF]] (3–1).{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/327690?cc=5739 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130102222048/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/327690?cc=5739 |url-status=dead |archive-date=2 January 2013 |title=Levante leap back into top four|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=28 April 2012}} ===Later career=== After leaving Levante, Valdo rarely settled with a club, playing in quick succession with [[Asteras Tripolis F.C.|Asteras Tripoli]] in [[Greece]], [[Racing de Santander]] of Spain and [[ATK (football club)|Atlético de Kolkata]] of the [[Indian Super League]].{{cite web|url=http://en.clubatleticodemadrid.com/noticias/doutie-and-valdo-new-players-of-atletico-kolkata|title=Doutie and Valdo, new players of Atlético Kolkata|publisher=Atlético Madrid|date=3 July 2015|access-date=6 July 2015|archive-date=6 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150706131243/http://en.clubatleticodemadrid.com/noticias/doutie-and-valdo-new-players-of-atletico-kolkata|url-status=dead}} On 1 September 2016, he returned to Spain to sign for [[CD Lealtad]].{{cite web|url=http://www.futbolasturiano.es/noticias6/1593.htm|title=Valdo completa la plantilla del Lealtad|trans-title=Valdo completes Lealtad roster|publisher=Fútbol Asturiano|language=es|date=1 September 2016|access-date=1 September 2016}} ==International career== Valdo played for the [[Spain national under-21 football team|Spanish under-21s]] in the early 2000s. '''Sergio Sánchez Ortega''' ({{IPA|es|ˈseɾxjo ˈsantʃeθ}}; born 3 April 1986) is a Spanish former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as either a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|right-back]] or a [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|central defender]].

He amassed [[La Liga]] totals of 168 games and three goals over the course of 12 seasons, representing [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]], [[Racing de Santander]], [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] and [[Málaga CF|Málaga]] in the competition. He won one [[Copa del Rey]] with the third club.

==Club career==
[[File:Ssanchez.jpg|thumb|left|Sánchez playing with [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] in 2009]]

===Espanyol===
Born in [[Mataró]], [[Province of Barcelona|Barcelona]], [[Catalonia]], Sánchez was a product of [[RCD Espanyol]]'s youth system. He made his debut for the first team on 24 April 2005, playing 85 minutes [[Substitute (association football)|from the bench]] in a 3–1 home win against [[Real Zaragoza]]<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2005/04/24/liga/1114364350.html|title=El Espanyol se crece ante el Zaragoza|trans-title=Espanyol get in Zaragoza's face|newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]|language=Spanish|date=24 April 2005|accessdate=4 July 2016}}</ref> in what was his sole appearance of [[2004–05 La Liga|the season]].

Sánchez was loaned to [[Segunda División]]'s [[Real Madrid Castilla]] in January 2007 and, at the end of [[2006–07 Segunda División|the campaign]], which ended in relegation,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vavel.com/es/futbol/2013/11/26/real-madrid/305872.html|title=La última plantilla que descendió con el Castilla. ¿Qué fue de ellos?|trans-title=The last squad to be relegated with Castilla. What happened to them?|publisher=Vavel|first=Miguel Ángel|last=Balderas|language=Spanish|date=26 November 2013|accessdate=20 January 2020}}</ref> was loaned again, to [[Racing de Santander]] in [[La Liga]], appearing significantly as the [[Cantabria]]n side [[2007–08 La Liga|achieved]] a first-ever [[2008–09 UEFA Cup|qualification]] for the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]].

In July 2008, Sánchez returned to Espanyol, scoring his first official goal for the club in a 1–1 home draw with [[Getafe CF]] on 20 September.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.diariovasco.com/20080921/deportes/mas-futbol/espanyol-reacciona-mantiene-liderato-20080921.html|title=El Espanyol reacciona y mantiene el liderato|trans-title=Espanyol react and are still first|newspaper=[[El Diario Vasco]]|language=Spanish|date=21 September 2008|accessdate=4 July 2016}}</ref> He spent the entire [[2008–09 La Liga|season]] on the right flank, as the ''Pericos'' eventually avoided relegation.

===Sevilla===
Sánchez agreed to join [[Sevilla FC]] in July 2009 in a four-year deal worth [[Euro|€]]4 million, with an additional one million being added if the [[Andalusia]]ns attained certain goals.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,12875_5449385,00.html|title=Sevilla sign Sánchez|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|first=Richard|last=Bailey|date=23 July 2009|accessdate=19 January 2011}}</ref> On 1 January 2010, it was announced that he would be unable to play football again until 'rigorous tests' were carried out on his heart, after he complained of pains.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2010/01/01/futbol/1262369191.html|title=El Sevilla detecta una patología cardiaca a Sergio Sánchez|trans-title=Sevilla detect cardiac pathology to Sergio Sánchez|newspaper=El Mundo|language=Spanish|date=1 January 2010|accessdate=4 July 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2010/03/20/futbol/equipos/sevilla/1269045888.html|title=Sergio Sánchez se someterá a una compleja operación de corazón para intentar volver a jugar|trans-title=Sergio Sánchez will undergo complex heart surgery to try and play again|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=Spanish|date=20 March 2010|accessdate=4 July 2016}}</ref> His [[2009–10 La Liga|season]] outputs consisted of seven league games – helping Sevilla to the fourth place – and two in the [[Copa del Rey]] which the club [[2009–10 Copa del Rey|won]], both legs of the clash against [[CF Atlético Ciudad]] (9–3 on aggregate).<ref name=COPA>{{cite news|url=https://www.laverdad.es/murcia/20091028/deportes_murcia/mas-futbol/sevilla-sufre-para-tumbar-20091028.html|title=El Sevilla sufre para tumbar a un buen Ciudad (2–4)|trans-title=Sevilla suffer to down a good Ciudad (2–4)|newspaper=[[La Verdad (Murcia)|La Verdad]]|first=Francisco J.|last=Moya|language=Spanish|date=28 October 2009|accessdate=4 July 2016}}</ref><ref name=COPA2>{{cite news|url=https://futbol.as.com/futbol/2009/11/10/mas_futbol/1257807656_850215.html|title=El Sevilla vuelve a golear y pasa a octavos tras un partido de trámite|trans-title=Sevilla rout again and reach last 16 after formality of a match|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|language=Spanish|date=10 November 2009|accessdate=4 July 2016}}</ref>

On 18 January 2011, after more than one year out of football, Sánchez returned to active – he had already been an unused substitute the previous week against former side Espanyol – starting in a Spanish Cup match against [[Villarreal CF]], and helping the title holders to [[2010–11 Copa del Rey|reach the semi-finals]] after a 3–0 home win (6–3 on aggregate).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=soccer&id=6035144|title=Tevez blasts City into fourth round of FA Cup|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=18 January 2011|accessdate=19 January 2011}}</ref>

===Málaga===
On 23 June 2011, Sánchez left Sevilla and joined neighbours [[Málaga CF]] for €2.8 million, signing a four-year contract.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2011/06/23/futbol/equipos/malaga/1308816038.html|title=El Málaga ficha a Sergio Sánchez por 2,8 millones|trans-title=Málaga sign Sergio Sánchez for 2,8 million|newspaper=Marca|first1=J.|last1=Ballesteros|first2=F.|last2=Quintero|language=Spanish|date=23 June 2011|accessdate=3 October 2011}}</ref> He made his debut for his new club on 25 September, appearing as a right-back in the 0–0 draw at Zaragoza.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=323978&cc=5739|title=Malaga denied at the last|publisher=[[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]]|date=25 September 2011|accessdate=13 December 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130103082047/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=323978&cc=5739|archive-date=3 January 2013}}</ref>

Sánchez opened the scoring in a [[2011–12 Copa del Rey|Spanish Cup tie]] against [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] on 3 January 2012, through a [[Header (association football)|header]] in an eventual 3–2 away loss (4–2 aggregate).<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/marcador/futbol/2011_12/copa/octavos/ida/rma_mga/|title=El Madrid se aferra a la Copa|trans-title=Madrid cling on to Cup|newspaper=Marca|first=Tomás|last=Campos|language=Spanish|date=3 January 2012|accessdate=6 February 2012}}</ref>

===Panathinaikos===
On 28 June 2015, after being linked to former club Espanyol and [[Beşiktaş J.K.|Beşiktaş JK]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sdna.gr/gr/news-in-english/arthro-news-in-english/47395/sanchez-on-the-verge-of-completing-panathinaikos-move/|title=Sanchez on the verge of sealing Panathinaikos move|publisher=SDNA|date=25 June 2015|accessdate=29 June 2015}}</ref> the 29-year-old Sánchez moved abroad for the first time in his career and signed with [[Panathinaikos F.C.|Panathinaikos FC]], earning a reported annual salary of €800,000 including objectives.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/20150626/20611358402/sergio-sanchez-podria-fichar-por-el-panathinaikos.html|title=Sergio Sánchez ficha por el Panathinaikos|trans-title=Sergio Sánchez signs for Panathinaikos|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|language=Spanish|date=26 June 2015|accessdate=1 July 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sdna.gr/gr/news-in-english/arthro-news-in-english/48223/sanchez-arrives-by-tuesday/|title=Sanchez arrives by Tuesday|publisher=SDNA|date=26 June 2015|accessdate=29 June 2015}}</ref> In his debut, at home against [[Club Brugge KV]] in the [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League|third qualifying round]] of the [[UEFA Champions League]], he was [[Ejection (sports)|sent off]] late into the first half, but the hosts eventually came from behind with one player less to win 2–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pao.gr/en/news/match/?itemid=67743de8-6c1c-4a88-9fd7-73c18dad2220|title=Panathinaikos-Club Brugge 2–1|publisher=Panathinaikos FC|date=28 July 2015|accessdate=1 August 2015|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924082110/http://www.pao.gr/en/news/match/?itemid=67743de8-6c1c-4a88-9fd7-73c18dad2220|archivedate=24 September 2015}}</ref>

Sánchez suffered an arm injury during an away game against [[PAS Giannina F.C.]] on 7 January 2016 after colliding with teammate [[Stefanos Kotsolis]], going on to be sidelined for approximately three months.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sdna.gr/news-english/article/154041/serious-injury-sanchez-greek-cup-clash-vid|title=Sanchez suffers serious injury during Greek Cup clash|publisher=SDNA|date=7 January 2016|accessdate=7 January 2016}}</ref>

===Rubin and Espanyol===
On 27 June 2016, Sánchez moved to Russia after signing with [[FC Rubin Kazan]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://rubin-kazan.ru/news_items/5844|script-title=ru:«Рубин» подписал контракт с Серхио Санчесом|trans-title=Rubin signed a contract with Sergio Sánchez|publisher=FC Rubin Kazan|language=Russian|date=27 June 2016|accessdate=27 June 2016|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160702072138/http://rubin-kazan.ru/news_items/5844|archivedate=2 July 2016}}</ref> On 1 September 2017, he returned to Espanyol after agreeing to a one-year loan.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rcdespanyol.com/ca/actualitat/sergio-sanchez-ultim-fitxatge/_n:5697/|title=Sergio Sánchez, últim fitxage|trans-title=Sergio Sánchez, last signing|publisher=RCD Espanyol|language=Catalan|date=1 September 2017|accessdate=2 September 2017}}</ref>

Sánchez subsequently joined the latter on a permanent deal,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/espanyol/2018/05/23/5b0543dfca4741df648b4571.html|title=Sergio Sánchez firmó... ¡hasta 2019!|trans-title=Sergio Sánchez signed... until 2019!|newspaper=Marca|first=Cristina|last=Navarro|language=Spanish|date=23 May 2018|accessdate=2 September 2018}}</ref> leaving the [[RCDE Stadium]] in August 2018.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/espanyol/sergio-sanchez-abandona-espanyol-7012758|title=Sergio Sánchez abandona el Espanyol|trans-title=Sergio Sánchez leaves Espanyol|newspaper=[[Sport (Spanish newspaper)|Sport]]|first=Albert|last=Roche|language=Spanish|date=31 August 2018|accessdate=2 September 2018}}</ref>

===Cádiz===
On 21 September 2018, Sánchez signed a two-year contract with [[Cádiz CF]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cadizcf.com/noticia/sergio-sanchez-refuerza-la-zaga-cadista|title=Sergio Sánchez refuerza la zaga cadista|trans-title=Sergio Sánchez bolsters Cádiz's defense|publisher=Cádiz CF|language=Spanish|date=21 September 2018|accessdate=24 September 2018}}</ref> On 31 January 2020, after falling down the pecking order,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://eldesmarque.com/cadiz/cadiz-cf/noticias-cadiz/171882-el-gran-dilema-de-sergio-sanchez|title=El gran dilema de Sergio Sánchez|trans-title=The great dilemma of Sergio Sánchez|publisher=El Desmarque|first=Francisco José|last=Jiménez|language=Spanish|date=19 November 2019|accessdate=19 February 2020}}</ref> he was loaned to fellow second division side [[Albacete Balompié]] for six months.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cadizcf.com/noticia/cesion-de-sergio-sanchez-al-albacete|title=Cesión de Sergio Sánchez al Albacete|trans-title=Loan of Sergio Sánchez to Albacete|publisher=Cádiz CF|language=Spanish|date=31 January 2020|accessdate=17 February 2020}}</ref>

On 8 August 2020, despite his contract was automatically extended for a further year after Cádiz [[2019–20 Segunda División|achieved promotion]], Sánchez was released.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cadizcf.com/noticia/sergio-sanchez-deja-de-pertenecer-al-club|title=Sergio Sánchez deja de pertenecer al club|trans-title=Sergio Sánchez is no longer part of the club|publisher=Cádiz CF|language=Spanish|date=8 August 2020|accessdate=9 August 2020}}</ref>
