'''Paolo Negro''' {{postnominals|post-noms=[[Order of Merit of the Italian Republic|Cavaliere OMRI]]}} ({{IPA|it|ˈpaːolo ˈneːɡro}}; born 16 April 1972) is an Italian former professional [[Association football|footballer]] and manager who played as a [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|centre back]] or as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|right back]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Negro |first1=Andrea |last2=Spuntarelli |first2=Valerio |last3=Sciattella |first3=Paolo |last4=Martelletti |first4=Paolo |date=2020-03-02 |title=Rapid referral for headache management from Emergency Department to Headache Centre: four years data |url=https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.2.21980/v2 |access-date=2026-08-11 |website=doi.org |doi=10.21203/rs.2.21980/v2 }}</ref>

In an eighteen-year professional [[career]], Negro amassed [[Serie A]] totals of ''362'' games and 24 goals, mainly for [[SS Lazio|Lazio]], winning eight major titles with the club, including one national championship and the [[1999 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup final|1999 Cup Winners' Cup]]. He also appeared with [[Italy national football team|Italy]] at [[UEFA Euro 2000|Euro 2000]], where they finished in 2nd place.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Negro |first1=Andrea |last2=Spuntarelli |first2=Valerio |last3=Sciattella |first3=Paolo |last4=Martelletti |first4=Paolo |date=2020-01-28 |title=Rapid referral for headache management from Emergency Department to Headache Centre: four years data |url=https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.2.21980/v1 |access-date=2026-08-11 |website=doi.org |doi=10.21203/rs.2.21980/v1 }}</ref>

==Club career==
===Early career: Brescia and Bologna===
Negro was born in [[Arzignano]], [[Province of Vicenza]]. A youth player at [[Brescia Calcio|Brescia]], he joined [[Bologna FC 1909|Bologna]] in 1990,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/the-gentleman-ultra/2016/dec/03/lazio-roma-rome-derby-own-goal-paolo-negro|title=The unforgettable own goal that changed Paolo Negro|date=3 December 2016|access-date=16 May 2019|work=[[The Guardian]]}}</ref> and made his [[Serie A]] debut against [[Genoa CFC|Genoa]], on 28 October 1990,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.pianetagenoa1893.net/la-storia-del-genoa/correva-lanno-1990-un-derelitto-bologna-fece-uscire-dal-campo-il-genoa-tra-i-fischi/|title=Bologna fece uscire dal campo il Genoa tra i fischi|trans-title=Genoa booed off the pitch at Bologna|work=www.pianetagenoa1893.net|language=it|date=16 May 2019|access-date=30 September 2017}}</ref> amassing over 50 overall appearances in his first two professional seasons, [[1991–92 Serie B|the latter]] spent in [[Serie B]].<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Brescia |first1=R. |last2=De Tuglie |first2=E. |last3=Torelli |first3=F.  |title=2003 IEEE Bologna Power Tech Conference Proceedings |chapter=Nodal unbundling of transmission losses |date=2003 |publisher=IEEE |volume=3 |pages=584–588 |doi=10.1109/ptc.2003.1304452 |bibcode=2003ptc.....3...90B |isbn=0-7803-7967-5 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Poensgen |first=Georg |date=1935 |title=Die Ausstellungen italienischer Spatbarockmalerei in Bologna und Brescia |url=https://doi.org/10.2307/1480804 |journal=Zeitschrift für Kunstgeschichte |volume=4 |issue=4 |pages=228–236 |doi=10.2307/1480804 |jstor=1480804 |issn=0044-2992|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

===Brescia and Lazio===
After a quick return to Brescia,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.seriebnews.com/2019/02/14/calciomercato-brescia-top11-giocatori-hamsik-pirlo/|title=Calciomercato Brescia, la top 11 dei giocatori lanciati|trans-title=Brescia transfers, top 11 best players|date=14 February 2019|access-date=16 May 2019|work=seriebnews.com|language=it}}</ref> he then moved to Rome's [[SS Lazio|Lazio]] in the summer of 1993.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.corrieredellosport.it/news/calcio/serie-a/lazio/2019/03/11-54411438/lazio_radu_acciuffa_puccinelli_nella_classifica_dei_piu_presenti/|title=Lazio, Radu aggancia Puccinelli|trans-title=Lazio, Radu catches Puccinelli|date=11 March 2019|access-date=16 May 2019|work=www.corrieredellosport.it|language=it}}</ref>

Negro won the [[1997–98 Coppa Italia|Coppa Italia]] during the [[1997–98 Serie A|1997–98 season]], also reaching the [[1998 UEFA Cup Final|UEFA Cup final]] that year with Lazio, losing out to [[FC Internazionale Milano|Inter]]. The following season, [[Lazio]] won the [[Supercoppa Italiana]], and placed second in [[1998–99 Serie A|Serie A]] behind [[AC Milan|Milan]], but won the [[1998–99 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup]], although he was an unused [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] in the club's 2–1 defeat of [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] in the [[1999 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup final|final]]. These successes were immediately followed by the [[1999 UEFA Super Cup|UEFA Super Cup]] in 1999, defeating [[1998–99 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League winners]] [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] in the final.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/the-gentleman-ultra/2016/dec/03/lazio-roma-rome-derby-own-goal-paolo-negro|title=The unforgettable own goal that changed Paolo Negro|work=[[The Guardian]]|date=3 December 2016|access-date=16 May 2019}}</ref> [[1999–2000 Serie A|During the 1999–2000 season]], he helped Lazio win the Serie A title, with two goals in 26, appearances, also helping Lazio to capture the [[1999–2000 Coppa Italia|Coppa Italia]] and the [[Supercoppa Italiana]] over Inter, winning the first edition of the [[Pallone d'Argento]] in 2000.<ref name="ussi">{{cite news|url=https://ussi.it/2016/a-florenzi-il-pallone-dargento-coppa-giaime-fiumano/|title=A Florenzi il "Pallone d'Argento"|trans-title=To Florenzi the “Pallone d’Argento”|date=8 May 2016|access-date=16 May 2019|work=www.ussi.it|language=it}}</ref> The prize is awarded to a player who has stood out during the course of a season, both for their discipline as well as for their footballing performances. Lazio also reached the quarter-finals of the [[1999–2000 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] that season<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Grieco |first1=M. |last2=Lorenzon |first2=L. |last3=Marino |first3=P. |last4=Carlini |first4=M. |last5=Brescia |first5=A. |last6=Satntoro |first6=R. |last7=Crucitti |first7=A. |last8=Macarone Palmieri |first8=R. |last9=Santoro |first9=E. |last10=Stipa |first10=F. |last11=Sacchi |first11=M. |last12=Carlini |first12=Massimo |last13=Brescia |first13=Antonio |last14=Santoro |first14=Roberto |last15=Crucitti |first15=Antonio |date=June 2019 |title=Eras program implementation in colorectal surgery: A multi-institution study based on the "lazio network" collective database including 1200 patients over two years |url=https://doi.org/10.1016/j.clnesp.2019.03.093 |journal=Clinical Nutrition ESPEN |volume=31 |pages=129–130 |doi=10.1016/j.clnesp.2019.03.093 |issn=2405-4577|url-access=subscription }}</ref>.

The following [[season]], however, on 17 December 2000, Negro scored an [[own goal]] in a [[Local derby|derby]] match against [[AS Roma|Roma]], who eventually lifted the [[List of Italian football champions|''scudetto'']], while Lazio finished the season in third place.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.esquire.com/it/sport/calcio/a26625696/derby-roma-lazio-storia-marcatori/|title=Gli eroi improbabili del derby|trans-title=The unlikely heroes of the derby|date=5 March 2019|access-date=16 May 2019|work=[[Esquire (magazine)|Esquire]]|language=it}}</ref> During the [[2003–04 Serie A|2003–04 season]], Negro was able to capture his third [[2003–04 Coppa Italia|Coppa Italia]] title with Lazio, beating [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in the [[2004 Coppa Italia final|final]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.repubblica.it/2003/l/sezioni/sport/calcio/coppaita/finanda/finanda.html?ref=search|title=Juve, caduta senza fine la Lazio signora dell'Olimpico |trans-title=Juventus, fallen, Lazio champion of Olimpico|date=4 January 2010|access-date=16 May 2019|work=[[la Repubblica]]|language=it}}</ref>

===Siena===
Having joined [[AC Siena|Siena]] in 2005, Negro scored a dramatic 85th-minute goal to defeat former side Lazio 2–1 on the final day of the [[2006–07 Serie B|2006–07 season]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ilmessaggero.it/roma/cronaca/estorsione_a_paolo_negro_arrivano_altre_3_condanne-1681291.html|title=Estorsione all'ex calciatore della Lazio Paolo Negro|trans-title=Ex'Laxio player Paolo Negro extorted|date=20 April 2016|access-date=16 May 2019|work=www.ilmessaggero.it|language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2005/oct/04/europeanfootball.sport |title=Anyone remember Paolo Negro? |work=The Guardian |last1=Richardson |first1=James |date=4 October 2005 |access-date=29 February 2020 }}</ref> Without it, Siena would have been relegated to the second division, instead of [[AC ChievoVerona|Chievo]]. He appeared a further 50 times in the league in two campaigns, for a total of 363 official games.

In August 2008, almost one year after retiring, 36-year-old Negro underwent a trial at [[Serie B]] club [[Modena FC|Modena]], but nothing came of it.

==International career==
On 16 November 1994, Negro made his debut for [[Italy national football team|Italy]], in a 2–1 home loss against [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]] in a [[UEFA Euro 1996]] [[UEFA Euro 1996 qualifying|qualifier]]. He received a total of eight caps with the ''Azzurri'' between 1994, and 2000, and he was selected by manager [[Dino Zoff]] to be a member of the Italian squad that took part at [[UEFA Euro 2000|Euro 2000]], tournament, where the national team reached the [[UEFA Euro 2000 final|final]], finishing the tournament in second place behind [[France national football team|France]].

Previously, Negro was an essential member of the [[Italy national under-21 football team|Italy U21 side]] under [[Cesare Maldini]], as they defeated [[Portugal national under-21 football team|Portugal]] in the [[1994 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|1994 European Championship]] final, in [[Montpellier]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.figc.it/nazionali/DettaglioConvocato?codiceConvocato=740&squadra=1|title=Nazionale in cifre: Negro, Paolo|website=figc.it|publisher=FIGC|language=it|access-date=20 April 2015|archive-date=22 December 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222103735/http://www.figc.it/nazionali/DettaglioConvocato?codiceConvocato=740&squadra=1|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Negro was a strong, aggressive, hard-tackling, physical player who excelled in the air and who possessed a powerful shot from distance. He was also a tactically intelligent, reliable, and versatile player and disciplined defender, who excelled at zonal marking. He was also an attentive man-marker, with reliable technique and distribution, as well as good pace and stamina, which allowed him to be effective when moving forward along the right flank after winning back possession.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/euro2000/teams/italy/squad/773575.stm|title=Paolo Negro|publisher=BBC|access-date=22 September 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/euro2000/italy/player/Negro.html|title=Profile: Paolo Negro|publisher=ESPN FC|date=13 July 2000|access-date=22 February 2017}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
In June 2011, he passed the category 2 coaching exams, which made him eligible to coach [[Lega Pro]] teams.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://english.gazzetta.it/Football/18-07-2011/baggio-s-new-life-802081638321.shtml|title=Baggio's new life as a professional coach|publisher=[[La Gazzetta dello Sport]]|date=18 July 2011|access-date=20 July 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110722114856/http://english.gazzetta.it/Football/18-07-2011/baggio-s-new-life-802081638321.shtml|archive-date=22 July 2011}}</ref>

On 30 December 2010, Negro took his first coaching job, becoming the boss of [[Promozione]] amateurs Cerveteri, a team from Lazio with former experiences in the professional tiers of Italian football.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://ilcorrierelaziale.it/tags/news/promozione-il-cerveteri-cambia-panchina-teloni-il-nuovo-tecnico-paolo-negro |publisher=Il Corriere Laziale |language=it |access-date=27 January 2012 |date=30 December 2010 |title=Promozione, il Città di Cerveteri cambia in panchina: via Teloni, il nuovo tecnico è Paolo Negro |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304041725/http://ilcorrierelaziale.it/tags/news/promozione-il-cerveteri-cambia-panchina-teloni-il-nuovo-tecnico-paolo-negro |archive-date=4 March 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He left the club after only three months, resigning on 23 March 2011 due to poor results.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://ilcorrierelaziale.it/tags/news/promozione-paolo-negro-si-dimette-da-tecnico-del-cerveteri-al-suo-posto-fabrizio-carbone |publisher=Il Corriere Laziale |language=it |access-date=27 January 2012 |date=23 March 2011 |title=Promozione, Paolo Negro si dimette da tecnico del Cerveteri. Al suo posto Fabrizio Carbone |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303215848/http://ilcorrierelaziale.it/tags/news/promozione-paolo-negro-si-dimette-da-tecnico-del-cerveteri-al-suo-posto-fabrizio-carbone |archive-date=3 March 2016 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On 26 January 2012, Negro accepted a job offer as head coach of [[Serie D]] amateurs [[USD Zagarolo|Zagarolo]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.resport.it/serie_d/ex_lazio_negro_nuovo_allenatore_zagarolo.aspx |website=Resport.it |language=it |access-date=27 January 2012 |date=26 January 2012 |title=L'ex Lazio Negro nuovo allenatore del Zagarolo |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120909201845/http://www.resport.it/serie_d/ex_lazio_negro_nuovo_allenatore_zagarolo.aspx |archive-date=9 September 2012}}</ref>

On 5 January 2015, after [[Mark Iuliano]]'s promotion as new head coach of [[Latina Calcio|Latina]], Negro was appointed as a new youth coach for the club.<ref>{{ cite news |url=http://www.uslatinacalcio.it/paolo-negro-nuovo-mister-della-primavera/ |language=it |access-date=5 January 2015 |publisher=US Latina Calcio |date=5 January 2015 |title=Paolo Negro nuovo mister della Primavera |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150105171042/http://www.uslatinacalcio.it/paolo-negro-nuovo-mister-della-primavera/ |archive-date=5 January 2015}}</ref>

In 2017 he became a youth coach for Cragnotti FC, a youth-only club founded by Massimo Cragnotti, son of former Lazio owner [[Sergio Cragnotti]].

On 15 December 2021 he took on his first role as head coach in a professional club, joining [[ACN Siena 1904|Siena]], with [[Franco Paleari]] as his assistant.<ref>{{ cite news |url=https://www.acnsiena.it/notizie/guida-tecnica-affidata-a-paolo-negro-vice-franco-paleari/ |language=it |access-date=15 December 2021 |publisher=[[ACN Siena 1904]] |date=15 December 2021 |title=Guida tecnica affidata a Paolo Negro, vice Franco Paleari}}</ref> He left his role at Siena only two weeks later, on 29 December, following the appointment of [[Pasquale Padalino]] as new head coach.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=[[ACN Siena 1904]]|url=https://www.acnsiena.it/notizie/pasquale-padalino-nuovo-tecnico-dellacn-siena/|title=Pasquale Padalino nuovo tecnico dell'Acn Siena |date=29 December 2021|language=it}}</ref>

'''Giampiero Pinzi''' {{postnominals|post-noms=[[Order of Merit of the Italian Republic|Cavaliere OMRI]]}} ({{IPA|it|dʒamˈpjɛːro ˈpintsi}}; born 11 March 1981) is an Italian former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[midfielder]].

==Club career==

===Lazio===
{{expand section|date=September 2015}}
Pinzi came through [[SS Lazio|Lazio]]'s youth system, joining from Almas Roma, and was promoted to Lazio's first team in 1999.  He made his senior debut in the [[UEFA Champions League]] on 2 November 1999, coming on in the match against [[FC Dynamo Kyiv|Dynamo Kyiv]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=31 August 2017 |title=Giampiero Pinzi è un giocatore del Calcio Padova |url=https://archivio.padovacalcio.it/giampiero-pinzi-padova/ |access-date=20 September 2025 |website=Padova Calcio |language=it-IT}}</ref> During the 1999–2000 season, he also made three appearances in the [[Coppa Italia]] for Lazio, winning both the [[Serie A]] title and Coppa Italia, although he did not feature in the league.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Jenkins |first=Dag |date=17 November 2022 |title=Giampiero Pinzi |url=https://www.laziostories.com/post/gianpiero-pinzi |access-date=20 September 2025 |website=Lazio Stories |language=en}}</ref>

===Udinese===
{{expand section|date=September 2015}}
After one-year with [Lazio in the Serie A Pinzi signed with league rivals [[Udinese Calcio|Udinese]].

===Chievo===
On 17 July 2009, [[AC ChievoVerona|Chievo]] announced that they would be keeping Pinzi on loan for another season.<ref>[http://www.goal.com/en/news/10/italy/2009/06/18/1331992/giampiero-pinzi-dreams-of-lazio-move Giampiero Pinzi Dreams Of Lazio Move]</ref>

===Return to Udinese===
Pinzi returned to Udinese for the [[2010–11 Serie A]] season, after the departure of [[Gaetano D'Agostino]] and [[Simone Pepe]]. Pinzi formed the club's central midfield trio with the energetic [[Gökhan Inler]] and [[Kwadwo Asamoah]] in Udinese's new 3–5–2 (or 5–3–2 formation); he provided six assists.

After the departure of [[Alexis Sánchez]], Pinzi changed to play attacking midfielder role, partnered with forward [[Antonio Di Natale]] in new 4–1–4–1 (or 4–4–1–1) formation, with Asamoah and [[Emmanuel Agyemang-Badu]] as cover against [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]]. With the new signing [[Gabriel Torje]] and [[Diego Fabbrini]] arrived, Pinzi again formed a new partnership role with either or both players. After the departure of Torje and arrival of [[Maicosuel]], Pinzi was still able to secure a place in starting XI.

In October 2012, he signed a new contract which lasted until 30 June 2016.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.udinese.it/script/view.php?id=2653 |title=Pinzi rinnova fino al 2016! |date=17 October 2012 |access-date=19 October 2012 |publisher=Udinese Calcio |language=it }}{{dead link|date=January 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

===Return to Chievo===
After 15 years played for Udinese, on 31 August 2015, the last day of [[transfer market]], Pinzi returned to Chievo, where he had played between 2008 and 2010.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://messaggeroveneto.gelocal.it/sport/2015/08/31/news/ore-decisive-per-il-futuro-di-pinzi-1.12016403|title=La bandiera Pinzi saluta: va al Chievo|date=31 August 2015|publisher=Messaggero Veneto|language=it}}</ref>

===Brescia===
On 10 August 2016, Pinzi signed for Serie B club [[Brescia Calcio|Brescia]] on a free transfer.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bresciacalcio.it/stagione/news/4824-pinzi-e-un-nuovo-giocatore-biancazzurro.html|title= Pinzi è un nuovo giocatore biancazzurro!|date=10 August 2016|access-date=14 August 2016|publisher=Brescia Calcio|language=it}}</ref>

===Padova===
On 8 January 2019, he was released from his contract by [[Calcio Padova|Padova]] by mutual consent.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=[[Calcio Padova|Padova]]|url=http://www.padovacalcio.it/rescissione-giampiero-pinzi/|title=Risolto il contratto tra Calcio Padova e Giampiero Pinzi|trans-title=Contract between Calcio Padova and Giampiero Pinzi dissolved|date=8 January 2019|language=it}}</ref>

==International career==
With the [[Italy national under-21 football team|Italy under-21 national team]], Pinzi won the [[2004 UEFA European Under-21 Championship]] and a bronze medal at [[Football at the 2004 Summer Olympics|2004 Summer Olympics]]. He made his [[Italy national football team|senior international]] debut and only cap for Italy in a friendly match against [[Iceland national football team|Iceland]] on 30 March 2005, coming off the bench in the 0–0 draw in Padova.<ref name=FIGC>{{cite web|url=http://www.figc.it/nazionali/DettaglioConvocato?codiceConvocato=1783&squadra=1|title=Statistiche in Nazionale - Pinzi, Giampiero|publisher=FIGC|language=it|access-date=8 August 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160826071255/http://www.figc.it/nazionali/DettaglioConvocato?codiceConvocato=1783&squadra=1|archive-date=26 August 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Style of play and discipline==
Pinzi was a versatile, hard-working, and physical right-footed [[midfielder]], who primarily operated as a [[central midfielder]] in the ''[[mezzala]]'' role, although could also play in front of the [[Defender (association football)|defence]] as a [[defensive midfielder]], or even behind the [[Forward (association football)|forwards]] as an [[attacking midfielder]]. He was known for his ability to read the game and provide balance to his teams by supporting the attack with his runs or by building attacking plays from deep, but also by providing defensive cover.<ref name="tuttocalciatori-Pinzi">{{cite web |title=Giampiero Pinzi - Carriera - stagioni, presenze, goal - TuttoCalciatori.Net - |url=https://www.tuttocalciatori.net/Pinzi_Giampiero |publisher=www.tuttocalciatori.net |access-date=10 May 2026 |language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Bertelli |first1=Luca |title=Calcio mercato, al Brescia dal Chievo arriva Giampiero Pinzi |url=https://brescia.corriere.it/notizie/sport/16_agosto_10/calcio-mercato-brescia-chievo-arriva-giampiero-pinzi-90bf78da-5f10-11e6-bfed-33aa6b5e1635.shtml |access-date=10 May 2026 |work=Corriere della Sera |date=8 October 2016 |language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Martorano |first1=Stefano |title=Pinzi, l'anima dell'Udinese |url=https://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Squadre/Udinese/04-01-2012/pinzi-anima-udinese-a-30-anni-mi-sento-maturo-804203094917.shtml |access-date=10 May 2026 |work=Gazzetta dello Sport |date=4 January 2012 |language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Le qualificazioni europee più inattese della Serie A – Ultimo Uomo |url=https://ultimouomo.com/le-qualificazioni-europee-piu-inattese-della-serie-a |publisher=ultimouomo.com |access-date=10 May 2026 |language=it |date=28 May 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=«A trentasei anni è un po' dura fare la mezzala» |url=https://www.ilgazzettino.it/AMP/pay/a_trentasei_anni_e_un_po_dura_fare_la_mezzala-3221722.html |access-date=10 May 2026 |work=www.ilgazzettino.it |date=6 September 2017 |language=it}}</ref> He was also capable of playing on the [[Midfielder#Wide midfielder|right flank]], a position in which he was deployed on occasion in his early career.<ref>{{cite web |title=Azzurrini da leggenda |url=https://it.uefa.com/under21/news/0257-0de66c97715d-37f582719960-1000--azzurrini-da-leggenda/ |publisher=UEFA.com |access-date=10 May 2026 |language=it |date=8 June 2004}}</ref>

Pinzi was also known for his lack of discipline and tenacity on the pitch, and his resulting tendency to commit fouls and pick-up many cards throughout his playing career. With [[Football records and statistics in Italy#Discipline|twelve red cards and 147 yellow cards in 389 Serie A appearances, he has the joint-second highest number of sending offs in Serie A history, and the most bookings in the league's history alongside]] [[Daniele Conti]]. He also has the most red cards resulting from double bookings in Serie A history (nine).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.contra-ataque.it/2016/02/16/calciatori-espulsi-serie-a-montero.html |title=I calciatori più espulsi nella storia della Serie A: Montero irraggiungibile |publisher=contra-ataque.it |language=it |author1=Claudio Agave |work=Contrataque |date=16 February 2016 |access-date=2 May 2017 |archive-date=1 June 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170601024056/http://www.contra-ataque.it/2016/02/16/calciatori-espulsi-serie-a-montero.html |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Un amore 'giallo': Giampiero Pinzi, il più ammonito della storia della Serie A {{!}} Goal.com Italia |url=https://www.goal.com/it/notizie/un-amore-giallo-giampiero-pinzi-piu-ammonito-storia-serie-a/blt84f2d42e7c186728 |publisher=www.goal.com |access-date=10 May 2026 |language=it |date=11 March 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=I 10 calciatori più ammoniti della storia della Serie A |url=https://www.90min.com/it/posts/i-10-calciatori-piu-ammoniti-della-storia-della-serie-a |publisher=90min.com |access-date=10 May 2026 |language=it-IT |date=24 November 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Sotto la doccia: ecco i più espulsi di sempre in A |url=https://sport.sky.it/calcio/serie-a/2018/02/28/classifica-espulsi-serie-a-montero-primo |publisher=sport.sky.it |access-date=10 May 2026 |language=it |date=20 September 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Udinese, sei un esempio: tanti gol e pochi gialli |url=https://sport.sky.it/calcio/2011/03/30/statistiche_udinese_gol_ammonizioni |access-date=10 May 2026 |work=sport.sky.it |date=30 March 2011 |language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Elogio della tenacia < Memories < News < Udinese |url=https://www.udinese.it/news/memories/elogio-della-tenacia |publisher=www.udinese.it |access-date=10 May 2026 |language=it |date=18 July 2019}}</ref>

However, at the start of the 2011–12 season, Demme was plagued by injuries.{{cite news|title=Schönfeld in guter Form|url=https://www.kicker.de/schoenfeld-in-guter-form-554753/artikel|publisher=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]]|language=de|date=5 July 2011|access-date=7 January 2018}}

A great comeback."{{cite news|title=Demme verrät: Mit diesem Plan drehte RB das Spiel|url=https://rblive.de/2017/08/27/demme-verraet-mit-diesem-plan-drehte-rb-das-spiel/|publisher=RB Live|language=de|date=27 August 2017|access-date=3 August 2019}} Upon returning from injury, Demme regained his first team place in the defensive midfield position.{{cite news|title=SO GEWINNT EINTRACHT IN LEIPZIG: Früh angreifen und Demme eindämmen|url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/eintracht-frankfurt/eintracht-in-leipzig-prognose-53306322.bild.html|publisher=Bild.de|language=de|date=23 September 2017|access-date=7 January 2018}}

Bundesliga]].{{cite web|publisher=Hertha BSC|url=https://www.herthabsc.com/de/nachrichten/2024/07/verpflichtung-diego-demme-2425|title=Diego Demme wird Herthaner!|trans-title=Diego Demme becomes Hertha player!|date=6 July 2024|access-date=6 July 2024|language=de}} ==International career== Although Demme is eligible to play for [[Germany national football team|Germany]] and [[Italy national football team|Italy]], he said: "If you come first, I'll take it right away."{{cite news|title=Leipzigs Demme träumt von der Nationalmannschaft|url=http://www.bild.de/sport/aktuelles/fussball/leipzigs-demme-traeumt-von-der-nationalmannschaft-51367002.bild.html|publisher=Bild.de|language=de|date=24 April 2017|access-date=7 January 2018}} Demme was first called up to the [[Germany national football team|Germany national team]] in 2017, for the friendly against [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]] on 6 June 2017, for the 2018 World Cup qualification match against [[San Marino national football team|San Marino]] on 10 June 2017, in which he made his international debut, and for the [[2017 FIFA Confederations Cup|Confederations Cup]], but withdrew from the squad ahead of the tournament due to a back injury.{{cite web|url=http://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/diego-demme-ruled-out-of-confederations-cup-with-germany-rb-leipzig-446656.jsp|title=Leipzig's Demme, Hoffenheim's Demirbay and Wagner, Hertha's Plattenhardt and Gladbach's Stindl all included in Germany squad for Confederations Cup|website=bundesliga.com|date=17 May 2017|access-date=10 June 2017}}

{{cite web|url=http://www.bundesliga.com/en/news/Bundesliga/leipzig-demme-hoffenheim-demirbay-wagner-hertha-plattenhardt-gladbach-stindl-germany-low-confederations-cup-444461.jsp|title=RB Leipzig's Diego Demme out of Confederations Cup with Germany|website=bundesliga.com|date=14 June 2017|access-date=17 June 2017}} ==Personal life== Born in [[Herford]], Germany, Demme was born to an Italian father and a German mother, making him German-Italian.{{cite news|title=Diego Demme: Ein Ostwestfale in Sachsen|url=http://www.nw.de/sport/sc_paderborn_07/20565650_Diego-Demme-Ein-Ostwestfale-in-Sachsen.html|publisher=Neue Westfalische|language=de|date=11 September 2015|access-date=7 January 2018}} Demme's father was a huge fan of [[Diego Maradona]], and named his son after him.{{cite news|title=Di Gregorio und Demme stärken Arminias Mittelfeld|url=http://www.nw.de/sport/dsc_arminia_bielefeld/4151250_Di-Gregorio-und-Demme-staerken-Arminias-Mittelfeld.html|publisher=Neue Westfalische|language=de|date=5 January 2011|access-date=7 January 2018}}
{{cite news|title=Diego Demme in Neapel mit eigener Fanklub-Unterstützung|url=https://rblive.de/2018/02/14/diego-demme-in-ssc-neapel-rb-leipzig-mit-fanklub-unterstuetzung/|publisher=RB Live|language=de|date=14 February 2018|access-date=3 August 2019}}
{{cite news|title=Diego Demme: "Kein jüngerer Trainer ist ehrgeiziger als Rangnick"|url=https://rblive.de/2018/10/17/diego-demme-rb-leipzig-ralf-rangnick-bruma-interview/|publisher=RB Live|language=de|date=17 October 2018|access-date=3 August 2019}} Because of his Italian father, he has an [[Italy|Italian]] passport.{{cite news|title=Rangnick: "Rolle des Jägers passt viel besser"|url=https://www.kicker.de/rangnick_rolle-des-jaegers-passt-viel-besser-667188/artikel|publisher=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]]|language=de|date=19 December 2016|access-date=7 January 2018}} Demme said about his fitness, quoting: "In the past, I ate a lot of meat. But now I just feel better, I regenerate faster. The body is no longer so acidified, I have hardly any muscular problems."{{cite news|title=Demme verrät sein Fitness-Geheimnis|url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/demmediego/verraet-sein-fitness-geheimnis-49489298.bild.html|publisher=Bild.de|language=de|date=26 December 2016|access-date=7 January 2018}} Growing up, Demme said he idolised [[Gennaro Gattuso]].{{cite news|title=Diego Demme: Heimlicher Spielmacher vor besonderem Duell|url=https://rblive.de/2018/02/13/diego-demme-heimlicher-spielmacher-vor-besonderem-duell/|publisher=RB Live|language=de|date=13 February 2018|access-date=3 August 2019}} In December 2018, Demme married his long–term girlfriend, Alina.{{cite news|title=Hochzeitsfoto auf Zehenspitzen: Diego Demme heiratet Freundin Alina|url=https://rblive.de/2018/12/28/hochzeitsfoto-auf-zehenspitzen-diego-demme-heiratet-freundin-alina/|publisher=RB Live|language=de|date=28 December 2018|access-date=3 August 2019}} The couple has two daughters Gia and Ellie.{{Cite web |date=29 June 2020 |title=Demme, un amore tutto azzurro: "Benvenuta Gia", la figlia napoletana |url=https://www.ilmattino.it/sport/sscnapoli/demme_un_amore_tutto_azzurro_benvenuta_gia_la_figlia_napoletana-5316568.html |access-date=18 January 2023 |website=www.ilmattino.it |language=it}}{{Cite web |last=Sepe |first=Alessandro |date=17 January 2023 |title=Grande gioia in casa Demme, è nata Ellie. '''Sergi Enrich Ametller''' (born 26 February 1990) is a Spanish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Primera Federación]] club [[SD Huesca|Huesca]].

He made 197 total appearances for [[SD Eibar|Eibar]], scoring 39 goals. In [[La Liga]], he also represented [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]], where he started his career.

==Club career==
===Mallorca===
Enrich was born in [[Ciutadella de Menorca]], [[Menorca]], [[Balearic Islands]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.deportebalear.com/2017/03/29/sergi-enrich-el-as-de-ciutadella/|title=Sergi Enrich, el as de Ciutadella|trans-title=Sergi Enrich, the ace from Ciutadella|publisher=Deporte Balear|first=Joan Antoni|last=Perelló|language=es|date=29 March 2017|access-date=7 September 2022}}</ref> A product of [[RCD Mallorca]]'s youth ranks, he made his first-team – and [[La Liga]] – debut on 24 January 2010, playing the last 22 minutes in a 1–1 away draw against [[RCD Espanyol]] after coming on as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for [[Fernando Varela (Spanish footballer)|Fernando Varela]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/275635?cc=5739|title=Espanyol frustrated by penalty|publisher=[[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]]|date=24 January 2010|access-date=23 July 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130103055727/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/275635?cc=5739|archive-date=3 January 2013}}</ref> He spent the vast majority of his [[2009–10 Segunda División B|first professional season]] with the [[RCD Mallorca B|reserve team]] in the [[Segunda División B]].

Enrich spent [[2011–12 Segunda División|2011–12]] on loan to [[Segunda División]] club [[Recreativo de Huelva]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2011/06/29/futbol/equipos/recreativo/1309374792.html|title=El delantero Sergi Enrich llega cedido al Recreativo|trans-title=Forward Sergi Enrich arrives on loan to Recreativo|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=29 June 2011|access-date=27 February 2014}}</ref> The [[2012–13 Segunda División|following campaign]], he joined [[AD Alcorcón]] on the same basis.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.adalcorcon.com/index.php/the-news/1483-sergi-enrich-llega-cedido-por-el-mallorca|title=Sergi Enrich llega cedido por el Mallorca|trans-title=Sergi Enrich arrives loaned by Mallorca|publisher=AD Alcorcón|language=es|date=31 August 2012|access-date=27 February 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140302191807/http://www.adalcorcon.com/index.php/the-news/1483-sergi-enrich-llega-cedido-por-el-mallorca|archive-date=2 March 2014}}</ref>

===Numancia===
In summer 2013, Enrich signed a two-year contract with [[CD Numancia]] still in the second tier.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cdnumancia.com/-/sergi-enrich-nuevo-delantero-para-el-c-d-numancia|title=Sergi Enrich, nuevo delantero para el C. D. Numancia|trans-title=Sergi Enrich, new forward for C. D. Numancia|publisher=CD Numancia|language=es|date=24 August 2013|access-date=22 December 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141222013736/http://www.cdnumancia.com/-/sergi-enrich-nuevo-delantero-para-el-c-d-numancia|archive-date=22 December 2014}}</ref> He was the [[Segunda División Player of the Month]] in November 2014 as his five goals in four games took the [[Soria]]-based side out of the relegation places;<ref name=POTM>{{cite web|url=https://menorcaaldia.com/2014/12/18/sergi-enrich-recibe-el-premio-al-mejor-jugador-de-noviembre-en-segunda/|title=Sergi Enrich recibe el premio al mejor jugador de noviembre en Segunda|trans-title=Sergi Enrich receives the prize for ''Segunda''{{'}}s best player in November|publisher=Menorca al Día|language=es|date=18 December 2014|access-date=19 June 2022}}</ref> on 20 December that year, he contributed a brace to a 6–6 home draw against [[CD Lugo]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2014/12/20/futbol/2adivision/1419112687.html|title=Bendita locura para despedir el año en Soria|trans-title=Heavenly madness to say goodbye to year in Soria|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=20 December 2014|access-date=22 December 2014}}</ref>

===Eibar===
On 12 July 2015, Enrich moved to top-division [[SD Eibar]] after agreeing to a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sdeibar.com/-/eddy-silvestre-y-sergi-enrich-nuevos-jugadores-de-la-sd-eibar-para-la-temporada-2015-2016|title=Eddy Silvestre y Sergi Enrich, nuevos jugadores de la SD Eibar para la temporada 2015–2016|trans-title=Eddy Silvestre and Sergi Enrich, new players of SD Eibar for the 2015–2016 season|publisher=SD Eibar|language=es|date=12 July 2015|access-date=12 July 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150713090326/http://www.sdeibar.com/-/eddy-silvestre-y-sergi-enrich-nuevos-jugadores-de-la-sd-eibar-para-la-temporada-2015-2016|archive-date=13 July 2015}}</ref> He scored 11 goals during his [[2016–17 La Liga|second season]] to help to a tenth-place finish,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.laopiniondemalaga.es/malagacf/2017/08/16/eibar-mendilibar-bajas-dudas/950178.html|title=El Eibar de Mendilibar, con bajas y algunas dudas|trans-title=Mendilibar's Eibar, with unavailable and some doubts|newspaper=La Opinión de Málaga|first=José|last=Criado|language=es|date=16 August 2017|access-date=16 November 2017}}</ref> and was [[La Liga Player of the Month]] in February 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.laliga.es/noticias/sergi-enrich-mejor-jugador-de-laliga-santander-en-febrero|title=Sergi Enrich, Mejor Jugador de LaLiga Santander en febrero|trans-title=Sergi Enrich, Best Player of LaLiga Santander in February|publisher=[[La Liga]]|language=es|date=10 March 2017|access-date=11 January 2025}}</ref>

Enrich remained at the [[Basque Country (autonomous community)|Basque]] club in the ensuing seasons, signing new contracts in February 2017<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/20170209/414194843118/sergi-enrich-amplia-su-contrato-con-el-eibar-hasta-2019.html|title=Sergi Enrich amplía su contrato con el Eibar hasta 2019|trans-title=Sergi Enrich extends his contract with Eibar to 2019|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|language=es|date=9 February 2017|access-date=15 December 2020}}</ref> and May 2019, tying him to them until June 2022.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lavanguardia.com/deportes/20190510/462146749901/el-eibar-renueva-al-delantero-sergi-enrich-hasta-junio-de-2022.html|title=El Eibar renueva al delantero Sergi Enrich hasta junio de 2022|trans-title=Eibar renew forward Sergi Enrich until June 2022|newspaper=[[La Vanguardia]]|language=es|date=10 May 2019|access-date=15 December 2020}}</ref> Due to a clause in his contract allowing him to leave Eibar in case of relegation, he ended his six-year stay in June 2021;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://cadenaser.com/emisora/2021/06/29/radio_menorca/1624958595_612362.html|title=Sergi Enrich es desvincula de l'Eibar|trans-title=Sergi Enrich cuts ties with Eibar|publisher=[[Cadena SER]]|language=ca|date=29 June 2021|access-date=19 September 2021}}</ref> two months later, he was close to joining newly-relegated [[2. Bundesliga]] team [[FC Schalke 04]] in Germany, but the move was called off when fans rebelled over his criminal record.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elmundo.es/deportes/futbol/bundesliga/2021/09/09/613a4306e4d4d8e10b8b45d0.html|title=De {{sic|nolink=y|Zozulia}} a Sergi Enrich: cuando las aficiones mandan en los fichajes|trans-title=From Zozulya to Sergi Enrich: when supporters direct the signings|newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]|first=Gonzalo|last=Navarro|language=es|date=9 September 2021|access-date=19 September 2021}}</ref>

===Ponferradina===
On 22 September 2021, Enrich agreed to a deal at [[SD Ponferradina]], recently returned to the second tier.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sdponferradina.com/noticias/noticia/el-delantero-sergi-enrich-se-une-a-la-sd-ponferradina|title=El delantero Sergi Enrich se une a la SD Ponferradina|trans-title=Forward Sergi Enrich joins SD Ponferradina|publisher=SD Ponferradina|language=es|date=22 September 2021|access-date=20 October 2021}}</ref> He contributed six goals and as many [[Assist (association football)|assists]] in his [[2021–22 Segunda División|only campaign]], and then turned down a new contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.menorca.info/deportes/futbol/2022/06/08/1744069/sergi-enrich-seguira-ponferradina.html|title=Sergi Enrich no seguirá en la Ponferradina|trans-title=Sergi Enrich will not carry on at Ponferradina|publisher=Menorca.info|first=Joan|last=Juanico|language=es|date=8 June 2022|access-date=19 June 2022}}</ref>

===Later career===
Enrich continued to compete in division two subsequently, representing [[Real Oviedo]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realoviedo.es/en/new/sergi-enrich-signs-for-real-oviedo|title=Sergi Enrich signs for Real Oviedo|publisher=Real Oviedo|date=18 July 2022|access-date=14 August 2022}}</ref>– where he was voted Player of the Month in April 2023,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.laliga.com/en-GB/news/sergi-enrich-named-laliga-smartbank-player-of-the-month-for-april|title=Sergi Enrich named LaLiga SmartBank Player of the Month for April|publisher=La Liga|date=4 May 2023|access-date=29 October 2024}}</ref>– [[Real Zaragoza]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realzaragoza.com/noticias/principio-de-acuerdo-con-sergi-enrich|title=Principio de acuerdo con Sergi Enrich|trans-title=Agreement in principle with Sergi Enrich|publisher=Real Zaragoza|language=es|date=19 July 2023|access-date=20 July 2023}}</ref> and [[SD Huesca]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realzaragoza.com/noticias/el-real-zaragoza-y-la-sd-huesca-acuerdan-la-cesion-de-sergi-enrich-por-una-temporada|title=El Real Zaragoza y la SD Huesca acuerdan la cesión de Sergi Enrich por una temporada|trans-title=Real Zaragoza and SD Huesca agree the loan of Sergi Enrich for one season|publisher=Real Zaragoza|language=es|date=15 August 2024|access-date=15 August 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sdhuesca.es/noticias/sergi-enrich-jugador-de-la-sd-huesca-dos-temporadas-mas|title=Sergi Enrich, jugador de la SD Huesca dos temporadas más|trans-title=Sergi Enrich, SD Huesca player two further seasons|publisher=SD Huesca|language=es|date=14 July 2025|access-date=17 July 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In October 2016, Enrich and teammate [[Antonio Luna (footballer)|Antonio Luna]] apologised when a [[Amateur pornography|sex tape]] involving them and a woman went [[Viral video|viral]] on the Internet.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/37581026|title=Antonio Luna and Sergi Enrich apologise after sex video appears|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=6 October 2016|access-date=17 December 2016}}</ref> Due to the woman's lack of consent to the filming, the pair were given two-year prison sentences in January 2021, [[Suspended sentence|suspended]] due to their lack of prior criminal records.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.abc.es/deportes/futbol/abci-enrich-luna-condena-pionera-contra-exhibicionismo-elite-202101200053_noticia.html|title=Enrich-Luna, condena pionera contra el exhibicionismo en la élite|trans-title=Enrich-Luna, landmark sentence against elite exhibitionism|newspaper=[[ABC (newspaper)|ABC]]|first=José Carlos|last=Carabias|language=es|date=20 January 2021|access-date=26 October 2021}}</ref>

'''Moussa Sow''' (born 19 January 1986) is a former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[forward (association football)|forward]]. Born in France, he represented [[Senegal national football team|Senegal]] at international level, scoring 18 goals in 50 appearances.

He was known for his [[bicycle kick]] goals<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Moussa Sow'un golü rekor kırdırdı!|url=https://www.hurriyet.com.tr/moussa-sowun-golu-rekor-kirdirdi-40267788|access-date=16 February 2021|website=www.hurriyet.com.tr|date=9 May 2017 |language=tr}}</ref> and emotional reactions such as crying when he failed to score, or when the team has lost.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Sporx|date=16 March 2014|title=Moussa Sow sahada ağladı! - Fenerbahçe|url=https://www.sporx.com/moussa-sow-sahada-agladi-SXHBQ374436SXQ|access-date=16 February 2021|website=Sporx|language=tr-TR}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Rennes===
He started his professional career at [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Stade Rennais]] in 2004 as an 18-year-old. In his first couple of seasons, Sow made his mark mostly in cup competitions, scoring a brace for [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]] against [[USC Corte|Corte]] on 6 January 2006 in the [[2005–06 Coupe de France|Coupe de France]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scoresway.com/index.php?sport=soccer&page=match&id=332391|title=CORTE 2–3 RENNES|publisher=Fenerbahce.org|date=7 January 2006|access-date=8 August 2012}}</ref> and one in an away game against [[Lille OSC|Lille]] in the [[Coupe de la Ligue]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.stade-rennais-online.com/Moussa-Sow.html|title=Moussa Sow : ses dernières actualités|publisher=Stade-rennais-online.com|date=18 November 2012|access-date=18 November 2012}}</ref>

====Sedan (loan)====
He was loaned out to [[CS Sedan Ardennes|Sedan]] in 2007, scoring six goals in 30 appearances for the club. Upon his return to Rennes, he was the club's first-choice striker for two seasons before joining [[Lille OSC|Lille]] on a free transfer In June 2010.

===Lille===
[[File:Moussa Sow 2011.jpg|thumbnail|left|Sow, whilst playing for [[Lille OSC|Lille]]]]
After his contract with [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]] came to an end, the 24-year–old forward signed a three-year deal with [[Lille OSC]] on 28 June 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.losc.fr/?r=0,0,1,9785|title=Moussa Sow au LOSC jusqu'en 2013|publisher=Losc.fr|date=18 November 2012|access-date=18 November 2012}}</ref> Sow scored on his debut for Lille in a 1–1 draw away to his former club Rennes.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/295059?cc=5739|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120716091142/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/295059?cc=5739|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 July 2012|title=Sow secures point for Lille|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=7 August 2010|access-date=18 November 2012}}</ref> But Moussa Sow did not score again in the league until a 90th-minute goal on 19 September gave Lille all three points in a tough home contest against [[AJ Auxerre|Auxerre]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=294914&cc=5739|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120717180526/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=294914&cc=5739|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 July 2012|title=Sow sinks Auxerre|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=19 September 2010|access-date=18 November 2012}}</ref>

Sow scored his first hat-trick for Lille on 13 November 2010, the goals came in a 5–2 away victory to [[Stade Malherbe Caen|Caen]], with both [[Gervinho]] and [[Franck Beria]] grabbing 90th-minute goals to seal the win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=294943&cc=5739|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120716000924/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=294943&cc=5739|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 July 2012|title=Caen 2–5 Lille|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=13 November 2010|access-date=18 November 2012}}</ref> Less than a month later on 5 December 2010, Sow netted another hat-trick this time against [[FC Lorient|Lorient]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-us/match/47010/lille-vs-fc-lorient/preview|title=Lille vs FC Lorient Preview|publisher=Goal.com|date=5 December 2010|access-date=18 November 2012}}</ref> His goals helped Lille to a 6–3 win and firmly placed his side into contention for the [[Ligue 1]] crown.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=295233&cc=5739|title=Lille show credentials|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=5 December 2010|access-date=18 November 2012|archive-date=12 January 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120112081427/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=295233&cc=5739|url-status=dead}}</ref> Lille went into the winter break in sole position of first place, as Sow fired in their only goal in a 1–1 draw with [[AS Saint-Étienne|Saint Étienne]] on 22 December 2010.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=295119&cc=5739|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120720024614/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=295119&cc=5739|url-status=dead|archive-date=20 July 2012|title=Lille 1–1 St Etienne|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=22 December 2010|access-date=18 November 2012}}</ref>

Sow scored his 22nd goal of the Ligue 1 campaign in a 2–2 draw with [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] on 21 May 2011. The result ensured that Lille would secure their first Ligue 1 title since 1954.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ligue1.com/ligue1/article/sow-good-as-lille-take-title.htm|title=SOW GOOD AS LILLE TAKE TITLE|publisher=Ligue1.com|date=21 May 2011|access-date=18 November 2012|archive-date=21 April 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190421080815/https://www.ligue1.com/ligue1/article/sow-good-as-lille-take-title.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> Sow scored his third hat-trick, on the final day of the season, as Lille tied the knot on their championship season with an emphatic 3–2 victory over former club Rennes.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/295131?cc=5739|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120717232112/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/295131?cc=5739|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 July 2012|title=Champions Lille celebrate in style|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=29 May 2011|access-date=18 November 2012}}</ref> Sow was the top scorer of the [[2010–11 Ligue 1|2010–11 season]] with 25 league goals and also contributed with three assists<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ligue1.com/ligue1/classementButeurs#sai=79&journee1=1&journee2=38&cat=G&poste=Tous|title=OFFICIAL TOP SCORER CHART|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=18 November 2012|access-date=18 November 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150710062621/http://www.ligue1.com/ligue1/classementButeurs#sai=79&journee1=1&journee2=38&cat=G&poste=Tous|archive-date=10 July 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> and been in the Team of the Year.

===Fenerbahçe===
[[File:Arsenal vs Fenerbahce (9611226325).jpg|thumbnail|left|Moussa Sow with [[Fenerbahçe S.K.|Fenerbahçe]] during a match against [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]]]]
[[File:Moussa Sow'14.JPG|thumbnail|right|Sow playing for [[Fenerbahçe S.K.|Fenerbahçe]] in 2014]]
On 27 January 2012, [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (football)|Fenerbahçe]] acquired Sow for €10 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://kap.gov.tr/yay/Bildirim/Bildirim.aspx?id=183566|title=Moussa Sow'un transferi konusunda taraflarla anlaşıldı|publisher=Kap.gov.tr|date=27 January 2012|access-date=18 November 2012}}</ref> He signed a 4.5-year contract which would have kept him at the club until the end of 2015–16 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.turkish-football.com/news_read.php?id=2333|title=Moussa Sow has signed a 4.5-year contract with Fenerbahçe|publisher=Turkish-football.com|date=27 January 2012|access-date=18 November 2012}}</ref> Sow made his debut against local rivals [[Beşiktaş J.K.|Beşiktaş]] on 5 February 2012, scoring a goal in the second minute of [[injury time]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fenerbahce.org/fb2008/detay.asp?ContentID=27853|title=Fenerbahçe 2–0 Beşiktaş|publisher=Fenerbahce.org|date=5 February 2012|access-date=18 November 2012}}</ref> On 18 March he scored the first goal of the [[Kıtalar Arası Derbi|derby match]] with a [[bicycle kick]] against [[Galatasaray S.K. (football team)|Galatasaray]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.zonalmarking.net/2012/03/18/fenerbahce-2-2-galatasaray-tactics/ |title=Fenerbahce 2-2 Galatasaray: Fenerbahce score two great goals, then go too defensive |publisher=Zonal Marking |date=18 March 2012 |access-date=22 May 2013 |archive-date=29 June 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170629063648/http://www.zonalmarking.net/2012/03/18/fenerbahce-2-2-galatasaray-tactics/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> He continued his good run of form by scoring a late equaliser against [[Kayserispor]] to earn a draw for his team in [[2011–12 Turkish Cup#Quarter-finals|quarter-finals]] of the [[Turkish Cup]] on 12 April 2012, helping his team to reach the semi-finals through a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]]. Sow also scored the second goal for his team against rivals [[Trabzonspor]] on 15 April 2012. Over the course of the [[2011–12 Süper Lig|2011–12 season]] Sow played 12 league matches and scored 7 goals. Sow earned his first trophy with Fener in the [[2012 Turkish Cup Final|Turkish Cup]] final on 16 May as the club ripped apart [[Bursaspor]] by a score of 4–0.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tff.org/default.aspx?pageID=267&ftxtID=15173 |title=50. Ziraat Türkiye Kupası Fenerbahçe'nin |publisher=TFF |date=16 May 2012 |access-date=22 May 2013 |language=tr }}</ref>

In the [[2012–13 Süper Lig|2012–13 season]] Sow scored 13 goals in 22 league matches and three goals in [[UEFA|European matches]]. On 3 March 2013, he scored twice against Beşiktaş followed by a goal each in the following league matches, a 4–1 victory against Bursaspor and a 2–1 win against. [[Antalyaspor]]. On 22 May 2013, he scored the solitary goal as Fenerbahçe defeated Trabzonspor to secure the club's second straight [[2012–13 Turkish Cup]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/soccer-fenerbahce-defeat-trabzonspor-1-0-win-turkish-195344118.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130630173631/http://sports.yahoo.com/news/soccer-fenerbahce-defeat-trabzonspor-1-0-win-turkish-195344118.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=30 June 2013 |title=Soccer-Fenerbahce defeat Trabzonspor 1-0 to win Turkish Cup |publisher=Yahoo Sports |date=22 May 2013 |access-date=22 May 2013 }}</ref> consolation for falling short to city rivals Galatasaray in the league campaign. On 21 September 2013, Fenerbahçe were victorious in a 4–0 win against [[Elazığspor]] while Sow completed his first hat-trick for the club during this match.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fenerbahce.org/detay.asp?ContentID=36314|title=Fenerbahçe 4–0 Elazığspor|date=21 September 2013|access-date=21 September 2013|publisher=fenerbahce.org}}</ref> Sow cried after leaving Fenerbahçe and stated that he will forever be only a Fenerbahçe fan.<ref>{{Citation|title=Sow Kadıköy'e gözyaşlarıyla veda etti... - tr.beinsports.com|date=31 August 2015 |url=https://tr.beinsports.com/haber/sow-kadikoye-gozyaslariyla-veda-etti|language=tr|access-date=14 April 2021}}</ref>

===Al Ahli===
On 29 August 2015, [[Al-Ahli Dubai F.C.|Al Ahli]] acquired Sow for €16 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/sport/al-ahli-set-to-beat-sunderland-to-signing-of-fenerbahce-striker-moussa-sow-1.38058/|title=Al Ahli set to beat Sunderland to signing of Fenerbahce striker Moussa Sow|publisher=thenational.ae|date=31 August 2015|access-date=31 August 2015}}</ref>

====Return to Fenerbahçe on loan====
On 31 August 2016, Sow wanted to return to Fenerbahçe and returned to Fenerbahçe on a season long loan deal from Al Ahli.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fenerbahce.org/detay.asp?ContentID=51904|title=Moussa Sow İstanbul'da|publisher=Fenerbahçe S.K.|date=31 August 2016|access-date=8 November 2016}}</ref> In November 2016, Fenerbahçe began selling shirts with Sow's name and number turned upside as tribute to his repeated times of his amazing bicycle kick goals, the latter of whom he scored a hat-trick against.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/row-zed/moussa-sow-good-overhead-kicks-9359065|title=Moussa Sow is so good at overhead kicks that Fenerbahce now sell UPSIDE DOWN versions of his shirt|publisher=Daily Mirror|date=29 November 2016|access-date=8 December 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fanatik.com.tr/2016/11/25/ozet-caykur-rizespor-fenerbahce-mac-sonucu-1-5-1264053|title=(ÖZET) Çaykur Rizespor Fenerbahçe maç sonucu: 1-5|publisher=Fanatik|date=28 November 2016|access-date=8 December 2016}}</ref> On 8 December 2016, Sow scored another bicycle kick, this time in the [[UEFA Europa League]] in a 1–0 away victory against [[Feyenoord]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportsjoe.ie/football/remember-moussa-sows-bicycle-kick-against-manchester-united-hes-only-gone-and-done-it-again/105589|title=Remember Moussa Sow's bicycle kick against Manchester United? He's only gone and done it again|publisher=[[sportsjoe.ie]]|date=8 December 2016|access-date=27 August 2020}}</ref>

====Bursaspor (loan)====
In January 2018, Sow joined [[Bursaspor]] on loan from Al Ahli until the end of 2017–18 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/moussa-sow-joins-turkish-super-lig-outfit-bursaspor-from/1v8jn05w94l2u1979ejyhyrodn|title=Moussa Sow joins Turkish Super Lig outfit Bursaspor from Shabab Al-Ahli|publisher=Goal|date=13 January 2018|access-date=27 March 2017}}</ref>

===Gazişehir Gaziantep===
On 28 January 2019, Sow signed for [[Gazişehir Gaziantep F.K.|Gazişehir Gaziantep]] on a one-and-a-half-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.hurriyet.com.tr/sporarena/moussa-sow-insanlar-sunu-bilsin-transferim-41097274|title= Moussa Sow: İnsanlar şunu bilsin, transferim...|date=28 January 2019|access-date=28 January 2019}}</ref>

==International career==
On 5 September 2010, Sow scored his first goal for [[Senegal national football team|Senegal]] in a 4–0 defeat of the [[DR Congo national football team|Democratic Republic of Congo]] during [[2012 Africa Cup of Nations qualification|qualifying]] for the [[2012 Africa Cup of Nations]]. He scored three more times in the qualifying phase as well as once in a 2–1 defeat to [[Equatorial Guinea national football team|Equatorial Guinea]] at the tournament finals.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/16734221|title=Africa Cup of Nations: Equatorial Guinea in quarters as Senegal crash out|access-date=24 January 2015|work=BBC}}</ref>

At the [[2015 Africa Cup of Nations]], Sow scored Senegal's winning goal as they defeated [[Ghana national football team|Ghana]] 2–1 in the team's opening match.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/30773499|title=Ghana 1-2 Senegal|date=19 January 2015|work=BBC}}</ref>

In May 2018 he was named in Senegal's 23-man squad for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]] in Russia.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Crawford |first1=Stephen |title=Revealed: Every World Cup 2018 squad - Final 23-man lists |url=https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/revealed-every-world-cup-2018-squad-23-man-preliminary-lists/oa0atsduflsv1nsf6oqk576rb |website=Goal |access-date=16 July 2019 |date=4 June 2018}}</ref>

He retired from international football in August 2018.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Okeleji |first1=Oluwashina |title=Senegal striker Moussa Sow announces his international retirement |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/45045613 |access-date=28 January 2019 |work=BBC Sport |date=2 August 2018}}</ref>
