'''Papiss Demba Cissé''' ({{IPA|fr|sise}}; born 3 June 1985) is a Senegalese former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays amateur football as a [[forward (association football)|forward]] for Cheshire Veterans Football League side Wythenshawe Vets Over-35s.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-10-21 |title=Meet the Sunday league team with 1,800 Premier League appearances |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/c2emr7per0mo |access-date=2026-01-15 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref>

Formerly of [[SC Freiburg]], he once held the record of most goals scored by an [[Ethnic groups of Africa|African]] player in a single [[Bundesliga]] campaign – 22 in the [[2010–11 Bundesliga|2010–11]] season. 

A full international for [[Senegal national football team|Senegal]] from 2009 to 2015, Cissé represented the country at the [[2012 Africa Cup of Nations|2012]] and [[2015 Africa Cup of Nations|2015]] [[Africa Cup of Nations]].

==Club career==
===Early career===
Cissé began his career with [[Génération Foot]] and [[AS Douanes (Dakar)|Douanes Dakar]] before transferring to the French side [[FC Metz|Metz]] in summer 2005.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bundesliga.de/de/liga/news/2009/index.php?f=0000143683.php |title=Cissé wechselt zum SC Freiburg |date=28 December 2009 |publisher=bundesliga.de |language=de |access-date=10 September 2011 |archive-date=6 April 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120406182215/http://www.bundesliga.de/de/liga/news/2009/index.php?f=0000143683.php |url-status=dead }}</ref> After only one month during the [[2005–06 Ligue 1|2005–06 season]], he left Metz and was loaned to French side [[AS Cherbourg Football|Cherbourg]]. During the season, Cissé played 26 matches and scored 11 goals for the [[Normandy]] club.<ref name=kicker_1>{{cite web |url=https://www.kicker.de/freiburg-holt-cissc3a9-518946/artikel |title=Freiburg holt Cissé |language=de |publisher=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] |date=28 December 2009 |access-date=10 September 2011}}</ref> After the season, Cissé returned to Metz for a further two years before being loaned again to [[LB Châteauroux|Châteauroux]] in January 2008<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.scfreiburg.com/teams/profis/meldungen/zweite-winter-neuverpflichtung |title=Zweite Winter Neuverpflichtung |language=de |publisher=SC Freiburg |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100107080046/http://www.scfreiburg.com/teams/profis/meldungen/zweite-winter-neuverpflichtung |archive-date=7 January 2010}}</ref> and before returning to Metz in July 2008 for a third stint.

===SC Freiburg===
Cissé signed for German [[Bundesliga]] side [[SC Freiburg]] on 28 December 2009 for a fee of €1.62 million. He initially became a transfer target for Freiburg in the summer of 2009 after he scored a goal and assisted on another in a 2–1 friendly win for Metz over the club. However, a transfer fee could not be agreed upon at the time. [[Hannover 96]] also expressed interest in the player.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.badische-zeitung.de/sport/scfreiburg/sc-neuzugang-ciss-sucht-die-herausforderung--25276843.html |title=SC-Neuzugang Cissé sucht die Herausforderung |language=de |publisher=badische-zeitung.de |date=7 January 2010 |access-date=10 September 2011}}</ref> In his first partial season at Freiburg, Cissé appeared in 16 matches, scoring six goals.

During the [[2010–11 Bundesliga]] season, which was his first full season with Freiburg, Cissé was ranked second in the league in terms of goals scored, only behind [[Mario Gómez]] of [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]], who scored 28. Cissé also set a club and league record; his 22 goals during the course of the season set the single-season goal record by a Freiburg player, as well as setting a new record for the most goals scored by an [[Africa]]n in a single Bundesliga season. The record was previously held by [[Tony Yeboah]], who scored 20 goals with [[Eintracht Frankfurt]] in [[1992–93 Fußball-Bundesliga|1992–93]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://bundesliga.de/en/liga/news/2010/index.php?f=0000183236.php |title=Discovery of the season: Papiss Demba Cisse |date=18 May 2011 |access-date=10 September 2011 |publisher=bundesliga.de |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120415174451/http://www.bundesliga.de/en/liga/news/2010/index.php?f=0000183236.php |archive-date=15 April 2012 }}</ref> That same season, Cissé won the EFFIFU award for being the most efficient striker in the league.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.scfreiburg.com/teams/profis/meldungen/ciss%C3%A9-effizientester-bundesliga-st%C3%BCrmer |title=Cissé effizientester-Bundesliga-Stürmer |language=de |access-date=10 September 2011 |publisher=SC Freiburg |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110716065150/http://www.scfreiburg.com/teams/profis/meldungen/ciss%C3%A9-effizientester-bundesliga-st%C3%BCrmer |archive-date=16 July 2011 }}</ref>

===Newcastle United===

====2011–12 season====
On 21 January 2012, Cissé signed for [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] on a five-and-a-half-year deal for an estimated fee in the region of £9.3 million, linking up with fellow [[Senegal national football team|Senegal]] striker [[Demba Ba]] in the process.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2012/jan/17/newcastle-freiburg-papiss-demba-cisse |title=Newcastle sign Papiss Demba Cissé |date=17 January 2012 |access-date=7 February 2012 |work=The Guardian}}</ref> He was subsequently handed the number 9 shirt, formerly worn by Newcastle legend Alan Shearer.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nufc.co.uk/articles/20120117/newcastle-sign-papiss-cisse_2281670_2580079 |title=Newcastle Sign Papiss Cisse |access-date=17 January 2012 |publisher=Newcastle United F.C. |archive-date=8 December 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151208180122/http://www.nufc.co.uk/articles/20120117/newcastle-sign-papiss-cisse_2281670_2580079 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On 5 February, Cissé made his debut for Newcastle in the 2–1 league win against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] at [[St James' Park]]. He replaced the injured [[Leon Best]] in the 14th minute before scoring the winning goal in the 71st minute with a breath-taking volley, chesting it before volleying with his left into the top left corner of the net.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16779054 |title=Newcastle 2–1 Aston Villa |date=5 February 2012 |access-date=5 February 2012 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 11 February, he made his first start for the club in the 5–0 away league defeat against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] at [[White Hart Lane]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16884811 |title=Tottenham Hotspur 5–0 Newcastle United |date=11 February 2012 |access-date=1 April 2012 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 25 February, he scored in the sixth minute in a 2–2 home draw against [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17093384 |title=Newcastle United 2–2 Wolves |date=25 February 2012 |access-date=25 February 2012 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 25 March, he scored two first-half goals in Newcastle's 1–3 league victory against [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] at [[The Hawthorns]], but he was denied a [[hat-trick]] early in the second half by a save by West Brom goalkeeper [[Ben Foster (footballer)|Ben Foster]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17419728 |title=West Bromwich Albion 1–3 Newcastle United |date=25 March 2012 |access-date=1 April 2012 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> Cissé's brace against West Brom made him the quickest player since [[Les Ferdinand]] to hit the five-goal mark for Newcastle.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/newcastle-united/nufc-news/2012/03/31/papiss-cisse-is-destined-for-great-things-72703-30663774/ |title=Papiss Cisse is destined for great things |date=31 March 2012 |access-date=1 April 2012 |work=Newcastle Chronicle}}</ref>

Cissé scored his sixth and seventh goals, against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], in a 2–0 home win.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17503293 |title=Newcastle 2–0 Liverpool |date=1 April 2012 |access-date=1 April 2012 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> He scored a third consecutive brace at [[Liberty Stadium]] in a 2–0 away win against [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]] on 6 April, bringing his tally to nine goals in eight matches.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17558919 |title=Swansea 0–2 Newcastle |date=6 April 2012 |access-date=6 April 2012 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> This made him Newcastle's most prolific goals per-game goalscorer of all-time, ahead of [[Hughie Gallacher]]. On 9 April, he scored his tenth goal in nine matches for Newcastle against [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] in a 2–0 home win.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17581414 |title=Newcastle 2–0 Bolton |date=9 April 2012 |access-date=9 April 2012 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 21 April, Cissé scored his 11th goal in ten matches during a 3–0 win against [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17711736 |title=Newcastle 3–0 Stoke |publisher=BBC Sport |date=21 April 2012 |access-date=14 June 2012}}</ref> He then managed to score his 12th and 13th Premier League goals in a 2–0 win against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]] on 2 May 2012, the second of which he curled the ball with the outside of his foot from 37 yards out, which looped over goalkeeper [[Petr Cech]]. Cissé described the goal as the best of his career, and was subsequently chosen as the BBC's [[BBC Goal of the Season|Goal of the Season]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.twitter.com/BBCSport/status/201809117105504256 |title=BBC Sport on Twitter: "Alan (the God) Hansen and Alan Shearer choose Papiss Cisse's goal for Newcastle against Chelsea as @BBCMOTD's goal of the season" |date=14 May 2012 |access-date=14 May 2012 |website=Twitter}}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=January 2018}} At the end of his first half season with Newcastle, he was known for his consistent goalscoring, with astonishing goals firing the North East club into a fifth place spot in the table.

====2012–13 season====
On 4 July 2012, it was reported that Newcastle had blocked an offer from the [[Senegalese Football Federation]] for Cissé to play for [[Senegal national football team|Senegal]] at [[Football at the 2012 Summer Olympics|2012 Summer Olympics]] in [[London]]. The reason behind the decision was that Newcastle wanted their key striker fit for a tough season ahead, playing European football.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/23231/7891861/Cisse-denied-Olympic-call-up |title=Cisse denied Olympic call-up |publisher=Sky Sports |date=12 July 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120720004449/http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/23231/7891861/Cisse-denied-Olympic-call-up |archive-date=20 July 2012}}</ref> Cissé scored his first goal in the [[2012–13 Newcastle United F.C. season|2012–13]] season with a header in the [[2012–13 Football League Cup|League Cup]] against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]. He scored Newcastle's third goal in their [[2012–13 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] defeat of [[Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]] on 4 October 2012, Newcastle's 100th match [[Newcastle United F.C. in European football|in European competition]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0202-0e9d7ad21834-b433219140bb-1000--newcastle-beat-bordeaux-to-reach-century-in-style/ |title=Newcastle beat Bordeaux to reach century in style |publisher=UEFA |date=4 October 2012 |access-date=6 April 2013 |first=Dan |last=Ross}}</ref> He scored his first [[2012–13 Premier League|Premier League]] goal of the season in a 2–1 win over [[West Bromich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] on 28 October 2012, as a shot taken by [[Sammy Ameobi]] deflected off Cissé and into the net. The striker's scoring was scarce throughout the opening four months of the season, only scoring his second league goal of the season on 28 November, a 2–1 away defeat to [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://espnfc.com/us/en/report/345725/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5901 |title=Stoke late-show stuns Newcastle |publisher=ESPNFC |date=28 November 2012 |access-date=6 April 2013}}</ref>

Cissé started against [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] alongside [[Shola Ameobi]] and scored a header in the second minute in a 2–1 defeat on 2 January 2013.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://espnfc.com/us/en/report/345665/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5901 |title=Anichebe worsens Magpies plight |publisher=ESPNFC |date=2 January 2013 |access-date=6 April 2013}}</ref> Cissé scored a spectacular 25-yard volley in Newcastle's 4–2 win over [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] on 24 February, helping the club come from behind to secure a crucial victory over fellow relegation strugglers.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21489679 |title=Newcastle 4–2 Southampton |publisher=BBC Sport |date=24 February 2013 |access-date=6 April 2013}}</ref> Cissé scored an injury time winner at home to Stoke City on 10 March, sending Newcastle into 13th place.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21646451 |title=Papiss Cisse scored a stoppage-time winner as Newcastle came from behind for the third straight home Premier League game to deservedly beat Stoke |publisher=BBC |date=10 March 2013 |access-date=10 January 2018 |first=David |last=Orstien}}</ref> On 14 March, in the second leg Europa League Round of 16 tie at home to [[FC Anzhi Makhachkala|Anzhi Makhachkala]], Cissé headed in a 94th-minute winner as Newcastle progressed to the quarter-finals with a 1–0 aggregate victory.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0207-0e83de726041-e61d998dd13a-1000--last-gasp-cisse-helps-newcastle-oust-ten-man-anji/ |title=Last-gasp Cissé helps Newcastle oust ten-man Anji |publisher=UEFA |date=14 March 2013}}</ref>

Cissé also scored the first goal in a 3–1 loss away to [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] in the first leg of Newcastle's Europa League quarter-final tie on 4 April.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/21963634 |title=Benfica 3–1 Newcastle |publisher=BBC Sport |date=4 April 2013 |access-date=20 September 2014}}</ref> Three days later, he scored an injury time winner in a 1–0 victory over [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]], causing him to jump into the crowd and sent manager Alan Pardew, in celebration, running in also.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/21986350 |title=Newcastle 1–0 Fulham |publisher=BBC Sport |date=7 April 2013 |access-date=20 September 2014}}</ref> Cissé scored his fourth goal of the [[2012–13 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]] campaign in a 1–1 home draw with Benfica, but it was not enough to see Newcastle into the semi-finals of the competition as they fell 4–2 on aggregate.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/025a-0ea9138d6c62-82cd392857cc-1000--jittery-benfica-rebuff-newcastle-comeback/ |title=Jittery Benfica rebuff Newcastle comeback |publisher=UEFA |date=11 April 2013 |access-date=20 September 2014}}</ref>

====2013–14 season====
On 25 September 2013, Cissé opened his account for the [[2013–14 Newcastle United F.C. season|2013–14]] season in a 2–0 win for Newcastle against [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] in the third round of the [[2013–14 Football League Cup|Football League Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/24140574 |title=Newcastle United 2–0 Leeds United |publisher=BBC Sport |date=25 September 2013 |access-date=20 September 2014}}</ref> Cissé scored his first Premier League goal of the season in a 5–1 home rout of [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] on Boxing Day, converting a late penalty.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/25442217 |title=Newcastle United 5–1 Stoke City |publisher=BBC Sport |date=26 December 2013 |access-date=20 September 2014}}</ref>

On 22 March 2014, he scored a last-minute winner to claim all three points for Newcastle in a 1–0 victory at home to Crystal Palace, only his second league goal of the season.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/mar/22/newcastle-united-crystal-palace-premier-league-match-report |title=Papiss Cissé's last-gasp strike sinks Crystal Palace at Newcastle United |work=The Guardian |date=22 March 2014 |access-date=20 September 2014}}</ref> Cissé's season finished on 19 April against [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]] as he limped off in the 21st minute.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/26999058 |title=Newcastle United 1–2 Swansea City |publisher=BBC Sport |date=19 April 2014 |access-date=20 September 2014}}</ref> It was revealed by Newcastle that Cissé had broken his [[kneecap]] and that he had undergone surgery on the injury.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/may/09/papiss-cisse-newcastle-united-injury |title=Newcastle United expect long layoff for injured Papiss Cissé |work=The Guardian |date=9 May 2014 |access-date=20 September 2014}}</ref>

====2014–15 season====
[[File:Newcastle United vs Watford, 19 September 2015 (08).JPG|thumb|upright|Cissé playing for [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] in 2015]]

After breaking his knee cap against Swansea in April 2014, Cissé returned to France to recover from his injury.<ref name=Injury>{{cite web |url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/papiss-cisse-way-ahead-schedule-7234855 |title=Papiss Cisse 'way ahead' of schedule after making good recovery from injury |work=Newcastle Chronicle |date=9 June 2014 |access-date=20 September 2014}}</ref> In June, it was revealed that Cissé would return from his injury earlier than expected and would return to Newcastle for pre-season training along with the rest of the first-team squad.<ref name=Injury /> On 10 September 2014, Newcastle manager [[Alan Pardew]] confirmed that Cissé would return to the Newcastle squad for their home match against [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] on 20 September.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/papiss-cisse-nearing-newcastle-united-7744544 |title=Papiss Cisse nearing a Newcastle United return as Alan Pardew ponders changes |work=Newcastle Chronicle |date=10 September 2014 |access-date=20 September 2014}}</ref>

Cissé made his return from injury against Hull on 20 September, replacing [[Emmanuel Rivière]] in the second half, and scoring both goals for Newcastle as they came back from two goals down to rescue a 2–2 draw.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/29187314 |title=Newcastle 2–2 Hull City |publisher=BBC Sport |date=20 September 2014 |access-date=20 September 2014}}</ref> Cissé celebrated both goals by lifting up his jersey to reveal a message dedicated to team-mate [[Jonás Gutiérrez]], who recently revealed that he had been diagnosed with [[testicular cancer]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2014/sep/20/newcastle-united-hull-city-premier-league-match-report |title=Newcastle grab draw with Hull as Papiss Cissé reprieves Alan Pardew |work=The Guardian |date=20 September 2014 |access-date=20 September 2014}}</ref> Two weeks later, another brace by Cissé earned Newcastle an identical result at [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Swansea 2–2 Newcastle |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29389679 |access-date=4 October 2014 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=4 October 2014}}</ref> On 5 December, he came on as a substitute for [[Rémy Cabella]] and scored both of Newcastle's goals as they defeated leaders Chelsea 2–1, inflicting on their opponents a first defeat of the season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Newcastle 2–1 Chelsea |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30257076 |access-date=6 December 2014 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=6 December 2014}}</ref> After scoring a penalty on [[Boxing Day]] in the 3–1 loss at Manchester United, Cissé scored again. In the next match, scoring the equaliser in a 3–2 victory over [[Everton F.C.|Everton]] on 28 December, taking his tally to nine league goals in just 14 matches. During the match, however, he intentionally thrust his elbow into [[Séamus Coleman]]'s face during a corner.<ref>{{cite web |title=Papiss Cisse deserves three match ban for 'really nasty' elbow, according to Graeme Souness |url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/papiss-cisse-deserves-three-match-8353855 |work=Newcastle Chronicle |date=28 December 2014 |access-date=29 December 2014}}</ref> Cissé was charged with dangerous conduct and banned for three matches by the [[The Football Association|FA]]. After returning from the [[2015 Africa Cup of Nations]], Cissé scored a header against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]], his tenth league goal of the season, on 11 February. On 28 February, he scored his 11th goal of the season against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] with a goal just outside the six-yard box.

On 7 March 2015, Cissé was handed a six-match ban by the FA after a spitting incident with [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] defender [[Jonny Evans]], and one more for elbowing Everton's Séamus Coleman. All together, it was a seven-match ban.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/31773054 |title=Jonny Evans banned for six matches, Papiss Cisse for seven |date=7 March 2015 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=8 March 2015}}</ref> Cissé returned to the team as a second-half substitute in Newcastle's 1–1 draw with West Brom on 9 May.

====2015–16 season====
Cissé started the first match of the season at home against [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]], scoring after chesting the ball in from close range to make the score 1–1. Despite scoring, however, he was substituted for new signing [[Aleksandar Mitrović]], who had recently joined from [[R.S.C. Anderlecht|Anderlecht]]. The match finished in a 2–2 draw.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33750572 |title=Newcastle United 2–2 Southampton |publisher=BBC Sport |date=9 August 2015 |access-date=11 July 2016}}</ref> On 28 November 2015, he opened the scoring in an eventual 5–1 loss to [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34887485 |title=Crystal Palace 5–1 Newcastle United |publisher=BBC Sport |date=28 November 2015 |access-date=11 July 2016}}</ref> Cissé's final goal for the club came in a 2–2 draw against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], on 23 April 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36061096 |title=Liverpool 2–2 Newcastle United |publisher=BBC Sport |date=23 April 2016 |access-date=11 July 2016}}</ref>

===Shandong Luneng===
On 9 July 2016, it was announced that Cissé had joined [[Chinese Super League]] club [[Shandong Luneng Taishan F.C.|Shandong Luneng]] for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nufc.co.uk/articles/20160709/cisse-joins-shandong-luneng_2281670_5715649 |title=Cisse Joins Shandong Luneng |publisher=Newcastle United F.C. |date=9 July 2016 |access-date=9 July 2016 |archive-date=11 August 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160811110957/http://www.nufc.co.uk/articles/20160709/cisse-joins-shandong-luneng_2281670_5715649 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He scored on his second appearance for the club, in an eventual 4–1 win over [[Hangzhou Greentown F.C.|Hangzhou Greentown]].

===Alanyaspor===
====2018–19 season====
On 31 August 2018, he signed with [[Alanyaspor]] of the Turkish [[Süper Lig]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.hurriyet.com.tr/sporarena/papiss-cisse-resmen-aytemiz-alanyasporda-40943180|title=Papiss Cisse resmen Aytemiz Alanyaspor'da|date=1 September 2018|publisher=Hürriyet|language=tr, fr|access-date=29 April 2019}}</ref> He made his debut against [[Göztepe S.K.|Göztepe]] on 1 September 2018 and he scored his first goal against [[Kasımpaşa S.K.|Kasımpaşa]] on 23 September 2018 and in the same game he scored one more goal and Alanyaspor won the game 2–1.

On 28 April 2019, Cissé was involved in a coach crash which killed Alanyaspor team mate [[Josef Šural]]. Cissé escaped with minor injuries.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/former-nufc-striker-papiss-cisse-16194871|title=Former NUFC striker Papiss Cisse 'injured' in Alanyaspor coach crash|last=Musgrove|first=Andrew|date=29 April 2019|website=nechronicle|access-date=30 May 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://metro.co.uk/2019/04/29/former-england-player-steven-caulker-ex-newcastle-striker-papiss-cisse-injured-crash-9334575/|title=Former England player and ex-Newcastle striker injured in Josef Sural crash|date=29 April 2019|website=Metro|language=en-US|access-date=30 May 2019}}</ref>

===Fenerbahçe===
On 1 October 2020, Fenerbahçe announced the signing of Cissé.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=Fenerbahce |number=1311643862922915847 |date=1 October 2020 |title=Ailemize hoş geldin! }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Papiss Cisse Fenerbahçemizde|trans-title=Papiss Cissé joins Fenerbahçe|access-date=1 October 2020|url=https://www.fenerbahce.org/haberler/futbol/2020/10/papiss-cisse-fenerbahcemizde|date=1 October 2020|language=tr|publisher=Fenerbahçe SK}}</ref>

===Amiens===
On 31 August 2022, Cissé signed with [[Ligue 2]] side [[Amiens SC]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Papiss Cissé est amiénois !|trans-title=Papiss Cissé is amienois!|access-date=10 September 2022|url=http://www.amiensfootball.com/blog/article/papiss-cisse-est-amienois-12752|date=31 August 2022|language=fr|publisher=Amiens SC}}</ref> On 1 July 2023, Cissé was released.

===Free agent===
In November 2023, Cissé began training with English club [[Macclesfield F.C.|Macclesfield]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=McGrath |first=Mike |date=2023-11-13 |title=Ex-Newcastle striker Papiss Cisse training with Robbie Savage's Macclesfield FC |language=en-GB |work=The Telegraph |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2023/11/13/newcastle-papiss-cisse-training-robbie-savage-macclesfield/ |access-date=2023-11-13 |issn=0307-1235}}</ref>
===Al Qabila FC===
In March 2025, Cissé returned to football to play for UAE side [[Al Qabila FC]], now known as [[FC Palm City]].

==International career==
Cissé made his international debut for [[Senegal national football team|Senegal]] on 12 August 2009, in a friendly away to [[Congo DR national football team|Congo DR]], scoring two goals as Senegal emerged victorious 2–1. Cissé scored a hat-trick in his fourth appearance for the national side, as Senegal ran away to a 7–0 victory over [[Mauritius national football team|Mauritius]] on 9 October 2010 in a [[2012 Africa Cup of Nations qualification|qualifying match]] for the [[2012 Africa Cup of Nations]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2010/10/09/africa/africa-cup-of-nations/senegal/mauritius/916406/ |title=Senegal 7–0 Mauritius |publisher=SoccerWay |date=9 October 2010 |access-date=6 April 2013}}</ref> Cissé also captained the Senegal team from 2012 to 2013. Cissé's most recent Senegalese goal was against Botswana in November 2014, his 16th international goal.

==Personal life==
Cissé is a practicing [[Muslim]], and when [[Goal celebration|celebrating a goal]] he often performs the [[Sujud]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.republika.co.id/berita/sepakbola/liga-inggris/12/05/08/m3pitx-dua-striker-muslim-newcastle-bantah-berseteru |title=Dua Striker Muslim Newcastle Bantah Berseteru |publisher=Republika Online |language=id |date=8 May 2012 |access-date=6 April 2013}}</ref> He along with other Muslim Newcastle players [[Cheick Tioté]], [[Demba Ba]] and [[Hatem Ben Arfa]] allegedly objected to Newcastle United's shirt-sponsorship deal with high-interest loans company [[Wonga.com|Wonga]] as Islam generally forbids promoting usury or financial exploitation.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23347131 |title=Papiss Cisse pulls out of Newcastle tour after sponsor row |publisher=BBC Sport |date=17 July 2013 |access-date=30 September 2013 |first=Ben |last=Smith}}</ref> Following the publication of a photograph showing Cissé at a gaming table at Aspers Casino in Newcastle,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-tyne-23424012 |title=Footballer Papiss Cisse 'let Muslims down' in casino visit |publisher=BBC News |date=23 July 2013 |access-date=5 June 2015}}</ref> it was announced that the matter had been resolved, with Cissé agreeing to wear the shirt featuring the logo of the loan company.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23455637 |title=Papiss Cisse and Newcastle resolve shirt sponsor dispute |publisher=BBC Sport |date=25 July 2013 |access-date=30 September 2013 |first=Ben |last=Smith}}</ref>

'''Jacob Matthew Decourcey Ramsey''' (born 28 May 2001) is an English professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]] for {{English football updater|AstonVil}} club [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]].

Ramsey is a product of the [[Aston Villa Under-23s and Academy|Aston Villa Academy]] and made his senior debut for the club in a [[EFL Championship]] match in February 2019. He represented [[England national football team|England]] at youth level and was a member of the [[England national under-21 football team|under-21]] squad in 2023.

==Club career==

=== Aston Villa ===
Ramsey joined the youth academy of [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] at the age of six.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/jacob-ramsey-aston-villa-wiki-15778812|title=Who is Jacob Ramsey? The wonderkid Villa are very excited about|first=Alex|last=Dicken|website=Birmingham Mail|date=16 February 2019|accessdate=19 April 2019}}</ref> He was often among the smallest players in his age group in youth football and would supplement his football training with boxing training with his father, an ex-professional boxer, to build muscle.<ref name=":1">{{cite web |last=Ramsey |first=Jacob |date=23 May 2022 |title=The Red Card that Changed My Life {{!}} By Jacob Ramsey |url=https://www.theplayerstribune.com/posts/jacob-ramsey-aston-villa-soccer-premier-league |access-date=25 May 2022 |website=The Players' Tribune}}</ref>

On 15 January 2019, Ramsey signed a professional contract with Aston Villa.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.avfc.co.uk/News/2019/01/15/jacob-ramsey-signs-new-contract|title=Ramsey signs Aston Villa deal|publisher=Aston Villa F.C|date=15 January 2019|access-date=19 April 2019}}</ref> Ramsey caught national attention playing for Aston Villa U18s in the 2018–19 [[FA Youth Cup]], scoring 2 goals in every round, until the Fifth Round. On 2 February 2019, Ramsey was given a straight red card less than ten minutes into Villa's Fifth Round defeat against [[AFC Bournemouth Under-21s and Academy|AFC Bournemouth U18s]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=McGroarty |first=Adam |date=2 February 2019 |title=Clinical Scrimshaw Scores Brace to See AFC Bournemouth Past Aston Villa in Youth Cup |url=https://www.thefa.com/news/2019/feb/02/fa-youth-cup-fifth-round-020219 |access-date=25 May 2022 |publisher=The Football Association}}</ref> While suspended for the youth team, Ramsey joined first team training to "make up the numbers" during a spate of injuries.<ref name=":1" /> After training with the first team, 17-year-old Ramsey was selected by manager [[Dean Smith (footballer, born 1971)|Dean Smith]] to be on the bench for a [[EFL Championship|Championship]] game against Brentford on 13 February 2019 in which he was an unused substitute and then made his professional debut with Aston Villa as a 61st minute substitute in a 2–0 loss to [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] three days later.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2019/02/16/england/championship/aston-villa-football-club/west-bromwich-albion-football-club/2802099/|title=Aston Villa vs. West Bromwich Albion – 16 February 2019|publisher=Soccerway|access-date=19 April 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/signs-promise-assessing-aston-villa-15842312|title='Signs of promise' – Assessing the Aston Villa debut of Jacob Ramsey|first=Gregg|last=Evans|date=16 February 2019|accessdate=29 August 2023|website=Birmingham Mail}}</ref>

On 1 May 2019, at the Aston Villa End-of-Season awards, Ramsey was named "2018–19 Academy Player of the Season".<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.avfc.co.uk/News/2019/05/01/aston-villa-end-of-season-award-winners|title=End-of-Season Awards: All the winners|date=1 May 2019|publisher=Aston Villa F.C.|access-date=2 May 2019}}</ref>

On 31 January 2020, Ramsey signed for [[Doncaster Rovers F.C.|Doncaster Rovers]] on loan for the remainder of the [[2019–20 Aston Villa F.C. season|2019–20 season]]. On the same day, he signed a new three-and-a-half-year contract with Aston Villa.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/51333331|title=Jacob Ramsey & Jason Lokilo: Doncaster sign Aston Villa midfielder and Crystal Palace winger|work=BBC Sport|date=31 January 2020|access-date=29 August 2023}}</ref> On 4 February 2020, Ramsey made his Doncaster debut, in a 3–0 away victory over [[Tranmere Rovers F.C.|Tranmere Rovers]], in which he scored his first two goals in senior football.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/sport/football/tranmere-rovers-0-doncaster-rovers-3-jacob-ramsey-celebrates-his-rovers-debut-in-style-1-10239313|title=Tranmere Rovers 0 Doncaster Rovers 3: Jacob Ramsey celebrates his Rovers debut in style|first=Leon|last=Wobschall|date=4 February 2020|accessdate=4 February 2020|website=The Yorkshire Post}}</ref> However, the [[EFL League One]] season was initially postponed and, on 9 June 2020, ended due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]<ref>{{Cite news|last=de Menezes|first=Jack|date=9 June 2020|title=League One and Two seasons ended due to coronavirus to confirm promotion and relegation|work=The Independent|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/football-league/league-1-2-season-cancelled-efl-promotion-relegation-a9556861.html|access-date=16 June 2020}}</ref> and Ramsey re-joined the Aston Villa squad ahead of the resumption of the Premier League.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Rushton|first=James|date=9 June 2020|title=Talented youngster sends five word message ahead of Aston Villa comeback|work=Birmingham Mail|url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/talented-youngster-sends-five-word-18392204|access-date=16 June 2020}}</ref>

On 15 September 2020, after making substitute appearances against [[Brighton and Hove Albion]] and [[Fulham]] in the third round of both the previous seasons' domestic cup competitions, Ramsey was given his first ever start for Aston Villa, in a 3–1 victory over [[Burton Albion F.C.|Burton Albion]] in the [[EFL Cup]].<ref>{{Cite news|last=Maher|first=Matt|date=15 September 2020|title=Carabao Cup: Burton 1 Aston Villa 3 – Report|work=Express & Star|url=https://www.expressandstar.com/sport/football/aston-villa/2020/09/15/carabao-cup-burton-1-aston-villa-3-report/|access-date=15 September 2020|archive-date=14 November 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221114204252/https://www.expressandstar.com/sport/football/aston-villa/2020/09/15/carabao-cup-burton-1-aston-villa-3-report/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 28 September, the 19-year-old made his Premier League debut as a second-half substitute in a 3–0 away win over [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]]. On 12 December, he made his first league start for Villa in a 1–0 away win over [[West Midlands (county)|West Midlands]] rivals [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Ben |last=Collins |title=Wolves 0–1 Aston Villa: Anwar El Ghazi penalty wins West Midlands derby |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/55197157|work=BBC Sport |date=12 December 2020 |accessdate=12 December 2020}}</ref>

On 9 February 2021, Ramsey signed a new four-and-a-half-year contract with the club.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.avfc.co.uk/news/2021/february/Jacob-Ramsey-pens-new-deal/ |title=Jacob Ramsey pens new deal |publisher=Aston Villa F.C. |date=9 February 2021 |access-date=9 February 2021}}</ref>
[[File:Jacob Ramsey 2021.jpg|thumb|Ramsey playing for [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] in 2021]]
On 22 October 2021, Ramsey scored his first goal for Aston Villa in the Premier League, a late consolation goal in a 3–1 defeat to [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]].<ref>{{cite news|date=23 October 2021|title=Ramsey pleased to break scoring duck with stunning strike|url=https://www.avfc.co.uk/news/2021/october/23/ramsey-pleased-to-break-pl-duck-with-stunning-strike/|access-date=24 October in a 2–0 victory over [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] which was also voted goal of the month.<ref>{{cite news|date=30 December 2021|title=Jacob Ramsey voted Villa Player of the Month|url=https://www.avfc.co.uk/news/2021/december/30/jacob-ramsey-avfc-player-of-the-month/|access-date=2 January 2022|publisher=Aston Villa F.C.}}</ref> On 15 January 2022, Ramsey scored his first goal at [[Villa Park]] against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.manutd.com/en/news/detail/match-report-aston-villa-vs-man-utd-15-january-2022|title=Aston Villa 2 Manchester United 2|first=Matthew|last=Holt|date=15 January 2022|accessdate=15 January 2022|publisher=Manchester United F.C.}}</ref> On 9 February, Ramsey scored two goals against [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]], marking his first Premier League brace.<ref>{{cite news |last=Lansley |first=Peter |date=9 February 2022 |title=Jacob Ramsey shines as Villa and Leeds share spoils after six-goal thriller |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/feb/09/aston-villa-leeds-premier-league-match-report |access-date=25 March 2022 |work=The Guardian }}</ref> On 26 April 2022, Ramsey signed a contract extension with Aston Villa, lasting until 2027.<ref>{{cite news |date=26 April 2022 |title=Jacob Ramsey pens new contract |url=https://www.avfc.co.uk/news/2022/april/26/ramsey-pens-new-contract/ |access-date=26 April 2022 |publisher=Aston Villa F.C.}}</ref> On 12 May, at Villa's [[2021–22 Aston Villa F.C. season|2021–22]] End Of Season awards, Ramsey was voted Young Player of the Season by supporters, and Player's Player of the Season by his teammates.<ref name=":3">{{cite web |date=12 May 2022 |title=🏆 Young Player of the Season 🏆 Players' Player of the Season Starboy. ✨ |url=https://twitter.com/avfcofficial/status/1524826113247264769 |access-date=12 May 2022 |work=@AVFCOfficial on Twitter}}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=June 2025}}

On 6 November 2022, Ramsey scored an own goal and for Villa in the same game, a 3–1 home victory over Manchester United.<ref>{{cite news |last=Rose |first=Gary |date=6 November 2022 |title='Special day' as Emery gives Villa fans hope |work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/63535339 |access-date=7 November 2022}}</ref> After a successful [[2022–23 Aston Villa F.C. season|2022–23]] season, Ramsey was recognised by the Premier League with the "2022/23 Premier League Academy Graduate" award.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=23 May 2023 |title=Jacob Ramsey wins Premier League Academy Graduate Award |url=https://www.avfc.co.uk/news/2023/may/23/ramsey-wins-premier-league-academy-graduate-award/ |access-date=2023-05-23 |website=Aston Villa Football Club}}</ref> At the Aston Villa end of season awards, Ramsey was named Young Player of the Season for the second season running.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |date=23 May 2023 |title=He's one of our own.✨@JacobRamsey41 is our Young Player of the Season for 2022/23! 🙌 |url=https://twitter.com/AVFCOfficial/status/1661078224112173056 |access-date=2023-05-23 |via=Twitter |language=en}}</ref>{{Primary source inline|date=June 2025}}

Ramsey missed much of the [[2023–24 Aston Villa F.C. season|2023–24 season]] for Villa, making only 16 appearances (half of which he started), due to a hamstring injury in January and two foot injuries; a metatarsal fracture in July while playing for England's U21's which reoccurred in October, and a toe injury in a match against [[Luton Town]] in March.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Tanswell |first=Jacob |title=Villa's Ramsey out for rest of season with foot injury |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5393690/2024/04/05/jacob-ramsey-aston-villa-injury-latest/ |access-date=2024-08-06 |work=The New York Times |date=5 April 2024 |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> On 1 August 2024, Ramsey was confirmed to be fit ahead of the new season, featuring in a pre-season tour of the United States.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Townley |first=John |date=31 July 2024 |title=Aston Villa team news vs RB Leipzig confirmed as Jacob Ramsey returns |url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/aston-villa-team-news-vs-29650696 |access-date=2024-08-06 |website=Birmingham Live |language=en}}</ref>

On 10 May 2025, Ramsey received the first red card of his senior career, for two bookable offences, in a 1–0 victory away at [[AFC Bournemouth|Bournemouth]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Clancy |first=Adam |date=10 May 2025 |title=Villa do Wat's needed to stay in UCL race |url=https://www.flashscore.co.uk/match/football/4Uh7Tp9a/#/report |access-date=2025-05-10 |website=flashscore.co.uk |language=en-GB}}</ref>

On 17 August 2025, Ramsey signed for [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] for an undisclosed fee,<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |title=Jacob Ramsey signs for Newcastle United - Newcastle United |url=https://www.newcastleunited.com/en/news/jacob-ramsey-signs-for-newcastle-united |access-date=2025-08-17 |website=www.newcastleunited.com |language=en}}</ref> reported to be in the range of £40 million.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-08-14 |title=Reports: Newcastle agree fee for Villa's Ramsey |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/45977853/newcastle-united-transfer-fee-aston-villa-jacob-ramsey |access-date=2025-08-17 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Sunday Ogochukwu Oliseh''' (born 14 September 1974) is a Nigerian [[Association football|football]] manager and former footballer who played as a [[defensive midfielder]]. Physical yet technically gifted, he played for top European clubs including [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]], [[Borussia Dortmund]] and [[Juventus FC|Juventus]].

==Playing career==
Oliseh played 55 international matches and scored 4 goals for [[Nigeria national football team|Nigeria]],<ref name="Oliseh stats"/> and played at the [[1994 FIFA World Cup|1994]] and [[1998 FIFA World Cup|1998]] [[FIFA World Cup|FIFA World Cups]]. Oliseh was also part of Nigeria's Olympic gold medal winning team of [[Football at the 1996 Summer Olympics|1996]].

Oliseh was voted Africa's third best footballer in 1998 by CAF.

He is mostly remembered for scoring the winning goal in the group stage match against [[Spain national football team|Spain]] in the [[1998 FIFA World Cup|1998 World Cup]], as Nigeria prevailed 3–2. A throw-in deep in the Spanish half was headed clear by [[Fernando Hierro]] – Oliseh ran and fired an explosive shot from 25 yards and took Spanish [[Goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]] [[Andoni Zubizarreta]] completely by surprise.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=69Eu8HMrG94 |title=Oliseh goal vs. Spain |website=[[YouTube]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110201195014/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=69Eu8HMrG94 |archive-date=1 February 2011 }}</ref> Despite captaining Nigeria during the [[2002 African Cup of Nations]], Oliseh was omitted from his country's [[2002 FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] squad later that year for disciplinary reasons. After missing out on World Cup selection, Oliseh retired from international football in June 2002, demanding unpaid allowances and dues owed to be paid.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/africa/2053413.stm | work=BBC News | first=Osasu | last=Obayiuwana | title=Sunday Oliseh quits | date=19 June 2002 | access-date = 14 October 2012}}</ref>

In March 2004, Oliseh was sacked by [[Borussia Dortmund]] after headbutting teammate [[Vahid Hashemian]] while on loan at [[VfL Bochum]] allegedly over racial remarks.<ref>{{cite news| url=http://edition.cnn.com/2004/SPORT/football/03/11/germany.oliseh/index.html | work=CNN | title=Oliseh shown door after punch-up | date=11 March 2004 | access-date = 14 October 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news| url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/africa/3505318.stm | work=BBC News | title=Oliseh not surprised | date=12 March 2004 | access-date = 14 October 2012}}</ref>

In January 2006, at the age of 31, Oliseh retired from professional football after playing a half season for [[Belgian First Division A]] top club [[K.R.C. Genk]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sport.be/fr/jupilerleague/0506/nieuws/article.html?Article_ID=116717&comp=2304 |title=Oliseh leaves Genk |language=fr |publisher=sport.be |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070926235324/http://www.sport.be/fr/jupilerleague/0506/nieuws/article.html?Article_ID=116717&comp=2304 |archive-date=26 September 2007 }}</ref>

==Managerial career==
Oliseh started his coaching career in Belgium with youth teams in the Belgian 3rd Division Verviers, notably the Under 19 team. He graduated to the first team as chief coach of Verviers in the 2008–09 season. During the 2014–15 season, he was appointed as the Chief Coach and Club Manager of RCS VISE in the Belgium 3rd Division.

In 2015–16, was appointed by the Nigerian Football Federation (NFF) the National Team Chief Coach of Nigeria (Super Eagles of Nigeria) where he made an impressive statistic of; 14 Games (Only 2 losses) 19 Goals scored, 6 conceded.

He qualified Nigeria to the CHAN tournament in Rwanda, qualified Nigeria to the Group phase of the 2018 world cup Qualifiers and on his first game as Chief Coach of Nigeria in an AFCON qualifier managed a draw in Tanzania.
He resigned as Nigeria's national coach at about 2:28am on 26 February 2016 exactly a month to the team's encounter with the Pharaohs of Egypt in the AFCON qualifiers. He was barely 8 months into his stay as manager due to contract violations, lack of support, unpaid wages and benefits to his players, Asst. Coaches and himself.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.360nobs.com/2016/02/sunday-oliseh-quits-super-eagles-former-captain-quits-as-head-coach/|title=Sunday Oliseh Quits Super Eagles: Coach Resigns Over Lack Of Suppor|website=www.360nobs.com|access-date=14 May 2018}}</ref>
On 27 December 2016, it was announced that Oliseh had been appointed as the new manager of [[Fortuna Sittard]].<ref>[http://nos.nl/artikel/2150260-fortuna-sittard-verrast-oliseh-is-de-nieuwe-trainer.html Fortuna Sittard verrast: Oliseh is de nieuwe trainer] (Dutch). NOS. 27 December 2016.</ref> He was fired on 14 February 2018,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fortunasittard.nl/nieuws/fortuna-sittard-stelt-sunday-oliseh-op-non-actief|title=FORTUNA SITTARD STELT SUNDAY OLISEH OP NON-ACTIEF|date=14 February 2018|publisher=[[Fortuna Sittard]]|language=nl|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180214194611/https://www.fortunasittard.nl/nieuws/fortuna-sittard-stelt-sunday-oliseh-op-non-actief|archive-date=14 February 2018}}</ref> and claimed the reason he was fired was because he refused to participate in illegal activities at the club.<ref>[https://twitter.com/SundayOOliseh/status/963804333618946049 Sunday Oliseh on Twitter] Sunday Oliseh. 14 February 2018.</ref> In January 2024, former Nigerian captain and Chelsea player [[Mikel John Obi|John Mikel Obi]], described Oliseh as easily the worst coach he ever played under because he had no clue what he was doing and ruined the unity of players within the [[Nigeria national football team|national team]] which led to [[Vincent Enyeama]] leaving the national team.

After two years without a club, in March 2020, Oliseh stated that he had turned down "two jobs from Belgian clubs", but that he waited for the right offer.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Titus |first1=Vincent |title=Sunday Oliseh reveals why he is yet to return to management |url=https://futaa.com/article/204265/n-a |publisher=Futaa |access-date=23 September 2020 |date=18 March 2020 |quote=As reported by Sports Extra, Oliseh says he is yet to receive the right offer having turned down two jobs from Belgian clubs. The 45-year-old has been without a club for the last two years since parting ways with Dutch club Fortuna Sittard in 2018.}}</ref>

In June 2022, he was appointed as the new head coach of German club [[SV 19 Straelen]].<ref>[https://www.goal.com/en-ng/news/nigeria-legend-oliseh-primed-for-coaching-return-with-german-club-sv-straelen/bltf5ff1e0df5b84db4 Nigeria legend Oliseh primed for coaching return with German club SV Straelen] Goal.com. 22 June 2022.</ref><ref>[https://www.thisdaylive.com/index.php/2022/06/22/oliseh-appointed-coach-in-germany/ Oliseh Appointed Coach in Germany
] Thisdaylive.com. 22 June 2022.</ref> In August 2022, after just two months in charge, he quit his position after the team suffered five losses in five games.<ref>[https://www.goal.com/en-ng/news/nigeria-legend-oliseh-resigns-from-german-side-sv-straelen-after-two-months/blta4a94c94c6bf5c7b Nigeria legend Oliseh resigns from German side SV Straelen after two months] Goal.com. 24 August 2022.</ref>

==Style of play==
Oliseh was a physical yet technically gifted midfielder.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/oliseh-to-liverpool-klopp-football-will-be-boring-if-we-all-played-same-way/blt482eb96199f119a6 |title=Oliseh to Liverpool's Klopp: 'Football will be boring if we all played same way' |publisher=www.goal.com |date=8 May 2022 |access-date=23 November 2023 }}</ref> Although he essentially played as a defensive midfielder throughout his career, [[Jonathan Wilson (writer)|Jonathan Wilson]] noted in a 2013 article for ''[[The Guardian]]'' that he was an early example of a more [[Midfielder#Deep-lying playmaker (Strolling 10)|creative]] interpreter of this role, who focussed more on ball retention and passing rather than solely looking to win back possession.<ref name="WilsonHolding13">{{Cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2013/dec/18/question-holding-midfielders-changing-role|title=The Question: what does the changing role of holding midfielders tell us?|last=Wilson|first=Jonathan|author-link=Jonathan Wilson (writer)|work=[[The Guardian]]|date=18 December 2013|access-date=31 October 2014}}</ref>

==Personal life==
His younger brothers, [[Azubuike Oliseh|Azubuike]] and [[Egutu Oliseh|Egutu]], were also professional footballers; another brother is [[Churchill Oliseh]] and his nephew is [[Sekou Oliseh]].

He was chosen as one of the Designated Players for Development by [[J.League]] and [[Japan Football Association|JFA]] in 2002 when he was a student of [[Hamana High School]]. Because of this status, Yano was able to register as a [[Júbilo Iwata]] player while he was still eligible to play for his high school club. However, he did not play any official match for Iwata. After graduating from his high school, he joined [[J1 League]] side [[Kashiwa Reysol]]. He played as substitute forward from first season. Although his opportunity to play increased late from summer 2005, Reysol was relegated to [[J2 League]] end of [[2005 J.League Division 1|2005 season]]. In 2006, Yano was transferred to [[Albirex Niigata]] with teammate [[Mitsuru Nagata]]. He quickly established himself as a first-choice forward. Although his play style was a tall center forward, he was converted to right winger of three forwards in 2009 because Niigata gain same style forward [[Hideo Oshima]]. In August 2010, Yano was transferred to [[Bundesliga]] club [[SC Freiburg]].{{cite web | url =http://www.badische-zeitung.de/sport/scfreiburg/kisho-yano-beim-sc-freiburg-debuet-geglueckt--35296656.html|language=de | title =SC Freiburg: Japaner in der Bundesliga: Kisho Yano beim SC Freiburg: Debüt geglückt| date = 7 January 2009 | access-date = 26 December 2012 | publisher =Badische Zeitung}} After an unsuccessful stint in Europe, he returned to Japan and signed for Niigata in February 2012.{{cite web | url = http://www.albirex.co.jp/tools/page_store/news_4513.html | title = ＳＣフライブルクから矢野貴章選手 移籍加入内定のお知らせ | publisher = Albirex Niigata | date = 8 February 2012 | access-date = 8 February 2012 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120210204216/http://www.albirex.co.jp/tools/page_store/news_4513.html | archive-date = 10 February 2012 | url-status = dead }} Although he initially played as regular forward, he lost his position and he played many matches as substitute forward from June.[https://data.j-league.or.jp/SS/jpn/team/2012010001_000130_W0707_J.html J.League] The club results were also sluggish and finished at the 15th place of 18 clubs in [[2012 J.League Division 1|2012 season]]. In 2013, Yano moved to [[Nagoya Grampus]]. Although he initially played as center forward instead [[Joshua Kennedy]] who was injured, Kennedy came back in May and Yano played many matches as substitute forward. In 2014, Yano was converted to right side back by new manager [[Akira Nishino (footballer)|Akira Nishino]] and became a regular player as right side back. Although he played as regular player every season, Nagoya finished at the 16th place of 18 clubs in [[2016 J1 League|2016 season]] and was relegated to J2 League. In 2017, Yano re-joined Albirex Niigata for the first time in four years. Although he played many matches as right side back, Niigata was relegated to J2 end of [[2017 J1 League|2017 season]]. He was returned to his original position forward by new manager [[Masakazu Suzuki]] in 2018. ==International career== Yano represented Japan at several underage levels and was a member of the [[Japan national under-17 football team|Japan U-17 team]] at the [[2001 FIFA U-17 World Championship|2001 U-17 World Championship]] finals where he scored one goal. He received his first cap for the [[Japan national football team|Japan national team]] when he came on as a substitute on 24 March 2007 in a friendly against [[Peru national football team|Peru]].[http://www.jfootball-db.com/en/players/yano_kisho.html Japan National Football Team Database] He was a member of the Japan team for the [[2007 AFC Asian Cup|2007 Asian Cup]] finals and played two games as a substitute. Yano's first international goal was an [[injury time]] winner against [[Switzerland national football team|Switzerland]] on 11 September 2007 in a friendly played in [[Hypo-Arena|Klagenfurt]].{{cite web | url = http://www.iht.com/articles/ap/2007/09/11/sports/EU-SPT-SOC-Switzerland-Japan.php | title = Japan beats Switzerland 4–3 to win Austrian four-nations tournament | publisher = [[International Herald Tribune]] | date = 11 September 2007 | access-date = 23 November 2008}} In May 2010, he was selected for the [[2010 FIFA World Cup|2010 World Cup]]. At the World Cup, he played once, coming on as a substitute against [[Cameroon national football team|Cameroon]].
