'''Pablo Gabriel García Pérez''' ({{IPA|es-419|ˈpaβlo ɣaˈβɾjel ɣaɾˈsi.a ˈpeɾes|lang}};{{efn|In isolation, ''Gabriel'' and ''García'' are pronounced {{IPA|es|ɡaˈβɾjel|}} and {{IPA|es|ɡaɾˈsi.a|}} respectively.}} born 11 May 1977) is a Uruguayan professional [[Association football|football]] [[Manager (association football)|manager]] and former player who played as a [[defensive midfielder]]. He is the manager of [[Cypriot First Division]] club [[APOEL FC|APOEL]].

A player of physical approach to the game (which earned him a reputation for being a dirty player), his nickname is ''Canario'' ([[Atlantic Canary|canary]]), referring to his birthplace.<ref name=Spunk>{{cite news|url=https://blogs.20minutos.es/quefuede/2015/03/05/que-fue-de-pablo-garcia-garra-uruguaya-en-grandes-de-espana/|title=Qué fue de… Pablo García: garra uruguaya en grandes de España|trans-title=What happened to… Pablo García: Uruguayan spunk in Spanish greats|newspaper=[[20 minutos]]|first=Edu|last=Casado|language=es|date=5 March 2015|access-date=12 October 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elobservador.com.uy/nota/pablo-garcia-el-futbol-griego-lleva-anos-podrido--20183138590|title=Pablo García: "El fútbol griego lleva años podrido"|trans-title=Pablo García: "Greek football has been rotten for years"|newspaper=[[El Observador (Uruguay)|El Observador]]|language=es|date=13 March 2018|access-date=12 October 2019}}</ref> He spent most of his professional career in [[La Liga]], making 135 appearances in six years in representation of four teams, but also played several seasons in Greece with [[PAOK FC|PAOK]].<ref name=PAOK>{{cite web|url=https://www.sport24.gr/Columns/longform/ton-gkarsia-den-tha-ton-prokaleis-ton-gkarsia.4335448.html|title=Τον Γκαρσία δεν θα τον προκαλείς. Τον Γκαρσία|trans-title=García will not be challenged. García|publisher=Sport 24|first=Niki|last=Bakoulis|language=el|date=25 October 2016|access-date=12 October 2019}}</ref>

A [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguayan international]] over one decade, García appeared for the nation at the [[2002 FIFA World Cup|2002 World Cup]] and two [[Copa América]] tournaments.

==Club career==
===Early career===
Born in [[Pando, Uruguay|Pando]], [[Canelones Department]], García started his career in [[Montevideo Wanderers F.C.|Montevideo Wanderers]]. After a six-month spell at [[Peñarol]], he signed for [[Atlético Madrid]], but would never make it past [[Atlético Madrid B|their reserves]], being transferred to Italian giants [[AC Milan]] two years later.<ref name=LG>{{cite web|url=https://www.lagalerna.com/hijos-decada-uruguayo/|title=Pablo García, el uruguayo|trans-title=Pablo García, the Uruguayan|publisher=La Galerna|first=Antonio|last=Valderrama|language=es|date=23 August 2015|access-date=25 May 2021}}</ref>

After just five [[Serie A]] appearances during the [[2000–01 Serie A|2000–01 season]], García was loaned to fellow top-division club [[Venezia FC|Venezia]] in January 2002. In spite of [[2001–02 Serie A|their relegation]], he had overall good performances.<ref name=LG/>

===Spain===
Moving to [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]] for the [[2002–03 La Liga|2002–03 campaign]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/0188-0f8e919fe567-958c0bb8992a-1000--osasuna-snap-up-uruguayan/|title=Osasuna snap up Uruguayan|publisher=UEFA|date=23 August 2002|access-date=21 March 2025}}</ref> García played intense football throughout three seasons in [[Navarre]]. In his first match, a 2–2 [[La Liga]] draw at [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] on 1 September 2002, he collected a [[Penalty card#Yellow card|booking]] and scored the match's final goal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espndeportes.espn.com/futbolespanol/noticias/villarrealosasuna010902.html|title=Se relajó y le empataron|trans-title=They relaxed and allowed draw|publisher=[[ESPN Deportes]]|language=es|date=1 September 2002|access-date=31 August 2018}}</ref>

In [[2004–05 Copa del Rey|the final]] of the 2005 [[Copa del Rey]], García, already an essential midfield element for Osasuna, received a straight [[Ejection (sports)|red card]] after a dangerous challenge on [[Real Betis]]' [[Joaquín (footballer, born 1981)|Joaquín]], in an eventual 2–1 [[Overtime (sports)|extra time]] loss.<ref name=CUP>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01aa-0ea7c2f1ec05-c09c10a9a459-1000--dani-delivers-for-betis/|title=Dani delivers for Betis|publisher=UEFA|date=11 June 2005|access-date=3 October 2015}}</ref> However, he had already caught the eye of [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] which signed the player to a three-year contract, with compatriot [[Carlos Diogo]] also being purchased.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/newsid=313446.html|title=Uruguayan pair make Madrid move|publisher=UEFA|date=1 July 2005|access-date=26 April 2010}}</ref>

Having totalled 17 yellow (season-most) and one red cards during [[2004–05 La Liga|2004–05]] (the Cup final notwithstanding),<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.noticiasdenavarra.com/2018/05/02/osasuna/las-amarillas-de-merida|title=Las amarillas de Mérida|trans-title=Mérida's yellows|newspaper=Noticias de Navarra|first1=Javi|last1=Gómez|first2=Javier|last2=Bergasa|language=es|date=2 May 2018|access-date=31 August 2018}}</ref> García made his Real Madrid official debut on 10 September 2005, playing 11 minutes in a 2–3 home defeat to [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/diario/2005/09/11/deportes/1126389603_850215.html|title=Un marciano con silbato|trans-title=A Marcian with a whistle|newspaper=[[El País]]|first=Santiago|last=Segurola|language=es|date=11 September 2005|access-date=31 August 2018}}</ref> Eventually, he won the battle for the team's first-choice holding midfielder over [[Thomas Gravesen]], although none were an undisputed starter.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2005/09/16/mas_futbol/1126852031_850215.html|title=Pablo García desplaza a Gravesen del cuadrado|trans-title=Pablo García takes Gravesen's place in square|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|first=Mikel|last=Recalde|language=es|date=16 September 2005|access-date=31 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2006/02/08/mas_futbol/1139383614_850215.html|title=Gravesen empieza a ser un problema en el Madrid|trans-title=Gravesen is starting to be a problem at Madrid|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Carmen|last=Colino|language=es|date=8 February 2006|access-date=31 August 2018}}</ref>

García helped Madrid to a runner-up place in the [[2005–06 La Liga|2005–06 season]], but was deemed surplus to requirements by new manager [[Fabio Capello]] and, on 29 August 2006, he agreed to a one-year loan at Celta.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/newsid=450117.html|title=Pablo García joins Celta expedition|publisher=UEFA|date=29 August 2006|access-date=26 April 2010}}</ref> After an uneventful personal [[2006–07 La Liga|campaign]] where he was injured for most of the year<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2006/09/10/futbol/1157920890.html|title=El Celta sentencia ante un Nàstic débil en defensa|trans-title=Celta finish it against defensively weak Nàstic|newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]|language=es|date=10 September 2006|access-date=31 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2006/12/23/mas_futbol/1166858841_850215.html|title=Pablo García podría dejar el Celta en el mes de enero|trans-title=Pablo García might leave Celta in the month of January|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Carlos|last=Jiménez|language=es|date=23 December 2006|access-date=31 August 2018}}</ref> and was also relegated, he returned to the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium]] in July 2007 to be loaned immediately again, this time to newly promoted [[Real Murcia CF|Real Murcia]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archivo.marca.com/edicion/marca/futbol/1a_division/real_madrid/es/desarrollo/1017433.html|title=El Real Madrid cede al uruguayo Pablo García al Murcia|trans-title=Real Madrid loan Uruguayan Pablo García to Murcia|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=17 July 2007|access-date=31 August 2018}}</ref>

===PAOK===
[[File:Pablogarcia.JPG|thumb|250px|García in action for PAOK in 2010]]
Following [[2007–08 La Liga|another relegation]], García was released by Real Madrid on 10 July 2008,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=824133.html|title=Real announce Garcia departure|publisher=FIFA|date=10 July 2008|access-date=24 May 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080711051701/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=824133.html|archive-date=11 July 2008}}</ref> and joined [[PAOK FC|PAOK]] later that month. He quickly became a fan favorite for his tenacity, being shown three red cards in his first six games and also starring in an incident with [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] player [[Diogo (footballer, born 1987)|Diogo]]; after being hit in the face by Diogo's elbow in a confrontation during a [[Set piece (football)|set piece]], García retaliated with a punch to the Brazilian's abdomen; both actions, surprisingly, eluded the referee's attention, but the Uruguayan eventually received a three-match ban.<ref name=PAOK/>

García's [[2009–10 Super League Greece|second season]] was much better overall, as PAOK only conceded 16 goals in 30 matches, finishing second in the table, with him forming a stable midfield partnership with Spaniard [[Vitolo (footballer, born 1983)|Vitolo]]. On 21 February 2010, he scored in a 2–1 home win over against [[Panathinaikos F.C.|Panathinaikos]], shortening the gap to that opposition to two points.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sportime.gr/podosfairo/paok/paok-panathinaikos-2-1-otan-o-gkarsia-ligize-meta-to-apithano-gkol-faoul-vid/|title=ΠΑΟΚ – Παναθηναϊκός 2–1: Όταν ο Γκαρσία "λύγιζε" μετά το απίθανο γκολ-φάουλ (vid)|trans-title=PAOK – Panathinaikos 2–1: When García "bent it" following an unlikely goal-foul (vid)|publisher=Sportime|first=Vassilis|last=Bandis|language=el|date=20 December 2020|access-date=6 December 2021}}</ref> Additionally, he renewed his link until 2012, even agreeing to a reduction in his salary in line with the club's stagnant finances.<ref name=Spunk/>

On 23 May 2012, it was announced that the 35-year-old García renewed his contract for one more year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://paokfc.gr/swift.jsp?CMRCode=16TSMNPJ8&extLang=|title=Επέκταση συμβολαίου με τον Pablo Garcia|publisher=PAOK FC|language=el|date=23 May 2012|access-date=23 May 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120526003604/http://www.paokfc.gr/swift.jsp?CMRCode=16TSMNPJ8&extLang=|archive-date=26 May 2012}}</ref> On 20 March of the following year, he was released by mutual consent after falling out with coach [[Georgios Donis]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gazzetta.gr/weekend-journal/article/1284870/paok-donis-mia-shesi|title=ΠΑΟΚ – Δώνης: Μια σχέση…|trans-title=PAOK – Donis: A relationship…|publisher=Gazzetta|first=Stavros|last=Sundoulidis|language=el|access-date=12 October 2019}}</ref>

García returned to PAOK on 4 June 2013 at the request of major shareholder [[Ivan Savvidis]], on a one-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.iefimerida.gr/news/108826/%CF%83%CE%B5-%CE%B3%CE%BD%CF%8E%CF%81%CE%B9%CE%BC%CE%B1-%CE%BB%CE%B7%CE%BC%CE%AD%CF%81%CE%B9%CE%B1-%CE%BF-%CF%80%CE%AC%CE%BC%CF%80%CE%BB%CE%BF-%CE%B3%CE%BA%CE%B1%CF%81%CF%83%CE%AF%CE%B1|title=Επιστρέφει στον ΠΑΟΚ ο Πάμπλο Γκαρσία|trans-title=Pablo García returns to PAOK|publisher=Iefimerida|language=el|date=4 June 2013|access-date=12 October 2019}}</ref> In the following winter [[transfer window]], however, he left for fellow [[Super League Greece]] side [[Xanthi F.C.|Skoda Xanthi]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sigmalive.com/sports/football/greece/90458/gkarsia-tha-timiso-ti-fanela-tis-ksanthis|title=Γκαρσία: Θα τιμήσω τη φανέλα της Ξάνθης!|trans-title=García: I will honour Xanthi's shirt!|publisher=[[Sigma TV|Sigma Live]]|language=el|date=10 January 2014|access-date=12 October 2019}}</ref> retiring after a couple of months at the age of 37 and settling in [[Thessaloniki]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/futbol-internacional/2018/03/13/5aa7a56e22601dd1338b458d.html|title=Pablo García, el ídolo del PAOK que se sintió un 'extraterrestre' en el Real {{sic|nolink=y|Madrd}}|trans-title=Pablo García, PAOK's idol who felt like an 'alien' in Real Madrid|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|first=Juan|last=Castro|language=es|date=13 March 2018|access-date=12 October 2019}}</ref>

==International career==
A full [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguayan international]] since 13 December 1997, in a [[King Fahd Cup]] match against [[United Arab Emirates national football team|United Arab Emirates]], García quickly developed into a mainstay for the national team, going on to earn a total of 66 [[Cap (sport)|caps]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/uru-recintlp.html|title=Uruguay – Record international players|publisher=[[RSSSF]]|first=Luis Fernando|last=Passo Alpuin|access-date=6 April 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/pggarcia-intl.html|title=Pablo Garcia – International Appearances|publisher=RSSSF|first=Luis Fernando|last=Passo Alpuin|access-date=6 April 2008}}</ref> He played all 270 minutes in the country's participation in the [[2002 FIFA World Cup]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport3/worldcup2002/hi/matches_wallchart/uruguay_v_denmark/default.stm|title=Tomasson double sinks Uruguay|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=1 June 2002|access-date=12 October 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport3/worldcup2002/hi/matches_wallchart/france_v_uruguay/default.stm|title=France face anxious wait|publisher=BBC Sport|date=6 June 2002|access-date=12 October 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport3/worldcup2002/hi/matches_wallchart/senegal_v_uruguay/default.stm|title=Senegal cling on to qualify|publisher=BBC Sport|date=11 June 2002|access-date=12 October 2019}}</ref> but was not able to help [[2006 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)|qualify]] for the [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006 edition]] after losing a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shootout]] to [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia]] on 16 November 2005.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nacion.com/puro-deporte/uruguay-un-mar-de-lagrimas/NA35JCINZFEHXFUNW64P5MG3UA/story/|title=Uruguay, un mar de lágrimas|trans-title=Uruguay, a sea of tears|newspaper=[[La Nación]]|language=es|date=17 November 2005|access-date=12 October 2019}}</ref>

García scored a powerful finesse shot from outside the box against [[Venezuela national football team|Venezuela]] in the [[2007 Copa América]] quarter-finals,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ovaciondigital.com.uy/copa-america-2015/uruguay-chile-copa-america.html|title=¿Otra vez a amargar al dueño de casa?|trans-title=Out to get hosts again?|publisher=Ovación Digital|language=es|date=21 June 2015|access-date=20 January 2017}}</ref> but also missed a decisive penalty against [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]] in the next round.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/internationals/6290410.stm|title=Brazil reach Copa America final|publisher=BBC Sport|date=11 July 2007|access-date=7 June 2017}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
On 24 May 2015, García returned to PAOK in an unspecified position.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.paokfc.gr/nea/20150524-kai-o-pamplo-gkarsia-stin-oikogeneia-tou-paok/|script-title=el:Και ο Πάμπλο Γκαρσία στην οικογένεια του ΠΑΟΚ!|trans-title=Pablo Garcia in PAOK's family!|publisher=PAOK FC|language=el|date=24 May 2015|access-date=26 June 2015}}</ref> The following month, the club's sporting director [[Frank Arnesen]] announced that the former would start his managerial career as an [[Manager (association football)|assistant]] in the under-17 team.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.paok24.com/podosfairo/46023/proponitis-o-pamplo|script-title=el:Προπονητής ο Πάμπλο|trans-title=Coach Pablo|publisher=PAOK 24|language=el|date=25 June 2015|access-date=26 June 2015}}</ref>

García was undefeated for 78 matches during his spell at the helm of the under-19 side, winning three national championships in the process.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.insidesport.com/betting-tips/panetolikos-paok/452|title=Panetolikos-PAOK|publisher=Inside Sport|first=Christophe|last=V.|date=1 November 2020|access-date=1 November 2020}}{{Dead link|date=July 2025|bot=InternetArchiveBot|fix-attempted=yes}}</ref> On 30 October 2020, he was appointed coach of the main squad following the dismissal of [[Abel Ferreira]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.infobae.com/america/agencias/2020/10/31/uruguayo-pablo-garcia-nuevo-entrenador-del-paok-de-salonica/|title=Uruguayo Pablo García nuevo entrenador del PAOK de Salónica|trans-title=Uruguay's Pablo García new manager of PAOK Thessaloniki|newspaper=[[Infobae]]|language=es|date=31 October 2020|access-date=1 November 2020}}</ref> taking them from sixth place to a [[2020–21 Super League Greece|final runner-up position]] 26 points behind champions Olympiacos.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.newsit.gr/athlitika/paok-telos-o-gkarsia-apo-ti-thesi-tou-proponiti/3292495/|title=ΠΑΟΚ: Τέλος ο Γκαρσία από τη θέση του προπονητή|trans-title=PAOK: García relieved of managerial duties|publisher=NewsIt|language=el|date=26 May 2021|access-date=8 March 2024}}</ref> The following 22 May, he won the [[Greek Football Cup|domestic cup]] with a 2–1 victory against the same opposition in [[2020–21 Greek Football Cup|the final]];<ref name=PAOKCUP>{{cite web|url=https://greekcitytimes.com/2021/05/23/paok-win-greek-cup-final-over-olympiakos/|title=Paok win Greek cup final over Olympiakos|publisher=Greek City Times|date=23 May 2021|access-date=24 May 2021}}</ref> he was fired shortly after, however, being offered a position at [[PAOK B|the reserves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.sport24.gr/football/telos-o-gkarsia-apo-ton-paok.9243359.html|title=Τέλος ο Γκαρσία από τον ΠΑΟΚ|trans-title=End of the road for García at PAOK|publisher=Sport 24|first=Savvas|last=Giombanoglou|language=el|date=26 May 2021|access-date=26 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://radar.gr/article/paok-xespasma-pablo-gkarsia-gia-tin-apolysi-tou|title=ΠΑΟΚ: «Ξέσπασμα» Πάμπλο Γκαρσία για την απόλυσή του|trans-title=PAOK: Pablo García "opens up" on dismissal|publisher=Radar|language=el|date=30 May 2021|access-date=25 February 2024}}</ref>

In summer 2023, García was appointed at [[Panserraikos F.C.|Panserraikos]] also from the Greek top tier.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://serressport.gr/me-igeti-pablo-gkarsia-stin-super-league-o-pans/|title=Με ηγέτη Πάμπλο Γκαρσία στην Super League o Πανσερραϊκός!|trans-title=Pablo García to manage Panserraikos in Super League!|publisher=Serres Sport|language=el|date=4 July 2023|access-date=25 February 2024}}</ref> In the [[2023–24 Greek Football Cup|cup quarter-finals]], they were eliminated by PAOK 9–0 on aggregate.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gazzetta.gr/football/kypello-elladas/2300526/ta-highlights-apo-paok-panserraikos-5-0-vid|title=Τα highlights από το ΠΑΟΚ-Πανσερραϊκός 5–0 (vid)|trans-title=PAOK-Panserraikos 5–0 highlights (vid)|publisher=Gazzetta|language=el|date=31 January 2024|access-date=25 February 2024}}</ref> 

On 11 May 2024, García announced he was leaving the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://capitano.gr/articles/pamplo-gkarsia-feygo-apo-ton-panserraiko|title=Πάμπλο Γκαρσία: «Φεύγω από τον Πανσερραϊκό»|trans-title=Pablo García: "I am leaving Panserraikos"|publisher=Capitano|language=el|date=11 May 2024|access-date=17 May 2024}}</ref> Later that month, he became the manager of [[Atromitos F.C.|Atromitos]] in the same league after signing a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://m.todomercadoweb.es/amp/europa/atromitos-pablo-garcia-firmo-su-contrato-485154|title=Atromitos, Pablo García firmó su contrato|trans-title=Atromitos, Pablo García signed his contract|publisher=Todo Mercado Web|language=es|date=31 May 2024|access-date=4 June 2024}}</ref>

'''Pascal Feindouno''' (born 27 February 1981) is a Guinean former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[winger (association football)|winger]]. He scored 30 goals in 85 appearances between 1998 and 2012 for the [[Guinea national football team|Guinea national team]].

==Club career==

===Early career===
Born in [[Conakry]], Feindouno began his career with [[Club Industriel de Kamsar]] where played for two years before signing with [[Hirondelles de Conakry]] in January 1998.

===Bordeaux, and Lorient loan===
Feindouno started his European career at [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux]] in July 1998, and scored the goal which gave the club the Ligue 1 Championship title in 1999. He spent the 2001–02 season on loan at [[FC Lorient|Lorient]]. Whilst at Lorient Feindouno played in the [[2002 Coupe de France Final]] in which they beat [[SC Bastia]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/match/86381|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120204145900/http://www.lequipe.fr/Football/match/86381|url-status=dead|archive-date=4 February 2012|title=Bastia 0-1 Lorient|publisher=lequipe.fr |date=11 May 2002 |access-date=28 July 2016}}</ref>

===Saint-Étienne===
Feindouno left Bordeaux to join [[AS Saint-Étienne|Saint-Étienne]] before the 2004–05 season. He missed Guinea's lost quarter final against the Ivory Coast in the 2008 African Nations due to suspension.

In summer 2007 he was linked with a move away from his club, with many sides from all over Europe interested in his services. Feindouno stated his desire to link up with close friend and former Lorient teammate [[Jean-Claude Darcheville]] at Scottish side [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] in May 2007 or in the January transfer window of 2008.<ref>[http://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/sport/display.var.1429932.0.0.php Guinea star in Gers plea]</ref> On 12 October 2007, it was reported that [[Premier League|Premiership]] club [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]]'s manager [[Rafael Benítez]] was to make a bid to sign him in the January transfer window.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Maniere |first1=Etienne |title=Liverpool : Benitez veut toujours Feindouno |url=https://www.footmercato.net/a4966035897077780223-liverpool-benitez-veut-toujours-feindouno |website=Foot Mercato |access-date=7 October 2020 |language=fr |date=8 October 2007}}</ref>

===Qatar and Saudi Arabia===
On 24 September 2008, Feindouno moved to [[Al Sadd SC]] of the [[Qatar National First Division]] for €7 million, signing a contract for four years.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.africanews.com/site/list_messages/20650 |title=AfricaNews - Feindouno file au Qatar - Subsites news |access-date=24 September 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110928063746/http://www.africanews.com/site/list_messages/20650 |archive-date=28 September 2011}}</ref> After one year at Al Sadd, he was transferred to [[Al-Rayyan SC|Al Rayyan Sports Club]] on a one-year loan. On 29 January 2010, he moved to [[Al-Nassr FC|Al-Nassr]] on a three-month loan.

In the summer 2010 transfer window, he reportedly attracted interest from [[Everton F.C.|Everton]], [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] and [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] but nothing came of it. [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] were reported to have offered him a contract worth £10,000 a week on 11 December 2010.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.express.co.uk/posts/view/216789/Pascal-s-one-of-the-BhoysPascal-s-one-of-the-BhoysPascal-s-one-of-the-BhoysPascal-s-one-of-the-BhoysPascal-s-one-of-the-BhoysPascal-s-one-of-the-BhoysPascal-s-one-of-the-Bhoys|title=Pascal's one of the Bhoys|newspaper=Daily Express|date=11 December 2010|access-date=11 January 2011|first=Scott|last=Burns}}</ref>

===Later career===
In February 2011, he confirmed that he had signed for [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] after trials with [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] and [[Wigan Athletic]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/90/france/2011/02/01/2332944/pascal-feindouno-i-have-signed-with-monaco|title=Pascal Feindouno: I Have Signed With Monaco {{!}} Goal.com|website=www.goal.com|language=en|access-date=26 March 2018}}</ref>

He left Monaco after their relegation and on 22 June joined [[Swiss Super League]] outfit [[FC Sion]], but left in January 2012 after the [[Swiss Football Association]] deducted 36 points for fielding ineligible players.

In July 2012, he signed for the Turkish club [[Elazığspor]] and his contract was terminated in February 2013, before the end of the 2012–13 season. In April 2013, he returned to Guinea, signing a four-month contract with [[AS Kaloum Star]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.afriquefoot-guinee.com/news-836.htm|title=Transferts : Pascal Feindouno se relance à l'AS Kaloum!|publisher=Guinée Afrique foot|date=21 April 2013|language=fr|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130430025148/http://www.afriquefoot-guinee.com/news-836.htm|archive-date=30 April 2013}}</ref>

On 30 August 2013, Swiss Super League team [[FC Lausanne-Sport|Lausanne-Sport]] announced that Feindouno had agreed to a short-term deal until Christmas Day, with an option to extend for a further year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lausanne-sport.ch/detailnews.php?id=580|title=Transferts|publisher=[[FC Lausanne-Sport]] official site|language=fr|date=30 August 2013|access-date=13 October 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131014172823/http://www.lausanne-sport.ch/detailnews.php?id=580|archive-date=14 October 2013}}</ref>

In September 2014, Feindouno signed a one-year contract with Moroccan club [[Hassania Agadir]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Feindouno au Maroc ! |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Feindouno-au-maroc/495933 |access-date=12 March 2019 |work=L'Équipe |date=2 September 2014 |language=fr}}</ref> In February 2015, he agreed the termination of his contract.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hattabi |first1=Dahbia |title=Pascal Feindouno est sans club ! |url=http://www.footmercato.net/flash-mercato/pascal-feindouno-est-sans-club_149071 |website=footmercato.net |date=27 February 2015 |access-date=12 March 2019 |language=fr}}</ref>

On 17 November 2015, Feindouno joined [[CS Sedan Ardennes]], along with his stepson [[Abdoul Karim Sylla (footballer, born 1992)|Abdoul Karim Sylla]].<ref name="sedan">{{cite news |title=Transfert : Pascal Feindouno signe à Sedan |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Transfert-pascal-feindouno-signe-a-sedan/608633 |access-date=12 March 2019 |work=L'Équipe |date=18 November 2015 |language=fr}}</ref> On 2 December, it was reported that the club's doctor had refused to grant him permission to play football after cardiac tests had shown "abnormalities" in the size of an [[artery]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Problèmes cardiaques pour Feindouno |url=http://www.leparisien.fr/espace-premium/sports/problemes-cardiaques-pour-feindouno-02-12-2015-5330949.php |access-date=12 March 2019 |work=Le Parisien |date=2 December 2015 |language=fr}}</ref> Two days later, he was linked with a move to Congolese side [[TP Mazembe]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Pascal Feindouno au TP Mazembe ? |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Pascal-feindouno-au-tp-mazembe/614053 |access-date=12 March 2019 |work=L'Équipe |date=6 December 2014 |language=fr}}</ref>

In May 2016, he moved to Lithuanian side [[FK Atlantas]], again with Abdoul Karim Sylla.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Crépin |first1=Timothé |title=Pascal Feindouno : "En Lituanie, les gens ont été surpris de me voir arriver" |url=https://www.francefootball.fr/news/Pascal-feindouno-en-lituanie-les-gens-ont-ete-surpris-de-me-voir-arriver/665851 |website=France Football |access-date=12 March 2019 |language=fr |date=2 May 2016}}</ref>

==International career==
Feindouno was a member of the [[Guinea national football team|Guinea national team]] that competed in the [[2004 African Nations Cup]], finishing second in their group in the first round of competition, before losing in the quarter finals to [[Mali national football team|Mali]]. He was the captain of Guinea.

==Personal life==
Feindouno acquired [[French nationality law|French nationality]] by [[naturalization]] on 21 October 2004.<ref>{{Cite web |title=JORF n° 0249 du 24 octobre 2004 - Légifrance |url=https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/jorf/jo/2004/10/24/0249 |access-date=2023-12-22 |website=legifrance.gouv.fr |page=17999 |language=fr |format=PDF}}</ref>

Pascal Feindouno's brother is midfielder [[Simon Feindouno]]. His other brother [[Benjamin Feindouno]] also played football but was found dead at his home in August 2025.<ref>{{cite web |last=Fleury |first=Valentin |title=L'ancien footballeur Benjamin Feindouno, le frère de Pascal, retrouvé mort avec son corps en état de décomposition |trans-title=Former footballer Benjamin Feindouno, Pascal's brother, found dead with his body in a state of decomposition |website=Le Figaro |date=2025-09-02 |url=https://www.lefigaro.fr/sports/football/l-ancien-footballeur-benjamin-feindouno-le-frere-de-pascal-feindouno-retrouve-mort-avec-son-corps-en-etat-de-decomposition-20250902 |language=fr |access-date=2025-09-04}}</ref> His stepson Abdoul Karim Sylla is a footballer as well.<ref name="sofooot">{{cite web |url=http://www.sofoot.com/feindouno-personne-ne-serait-venu-me-chercher-dans-mon-lit-212169.html |title=Personne ne serait venu me chercher dans mon lit |trans-title=No one would have come looking for me in my bed |publisher=www.sofoot.com |language=fr |first=Raphael |last=Gaftarnik |date=19 November 2015 |access-date=1 January 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201020180917/https://www.sofoot.com/feindouno-personne-ne-serait-venu-me-chercher-dans-mon-lit-212169.html |archive-date=2020-10-20 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

He represented the [[Ivory Coast national football team|Ivory Coast national team]] from 2000 to 2012. ==Club career== Keïta, also known as 'Popito', began his career at homeland club [[Africa Sports]], before moving on to Tunisian Club [[Etoile du Sahel]]. Following spells in United Arab Emirates with [[Al Ain]] and Qatar with [[Al Sadd SC|Al Sadd]], he moved to France with Ligue 1 club [[OSC Lille|Lille]] in 2005. ===Lyon=== On 31 May 2007, [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] chairman [[Jean-Michel Aulas]] revealed that the club had made bids for both Keïta and his teammate [[Mathieu Bodmer]].{{Cite web|url=http://eurosport.yahoo.com/31052007/58/ligue-1-lyon-chase-keita.html|title=Yahoo|website=Yahoo|language=en-US|access-date=26 March 2018}}{{Dead link|date=September 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} On 16 June 2007, Lyon confirmed the signing of Keïta from Lille for €18 million, with Bodmer also moving to Lyon.{{cite web |url=http://uk.reuters.com/article/soccer-france-lyon-idUKL16748220070616 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170712061018/http://uk.reuters.com/article/soccer-france-lyon-idUKL16748220070616 |url-status=dead |archive-date=12 July 2017 |title=Soccer – Lyon sign Lille players Bodmer and Keïta |publisher=[[Reuters]] |date=16 June 2007 |access-date=29 May 2013}} During his two seasons at the club, he made 52 appearances in all competitions, scoring 5 goals.{{cite web |url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/soccer/2009-07-02-2474878506_x.htm |title=Abdul Kader Keïta leaves Lyon for Galatasaray |publisher=USATODAY.com |date=2 July 2009 |access-date=29 May 2013 |archive-date=23 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220323132205/http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/soccer/2009-07-02-2474878506_x.htm |url-status=live }} ===Galatasaray=== On 2 July 2009, [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]] officially announced that Keïta joined the Turkish club and signed a three-year contract, for €8.5 million transfer fee plus €500,000 variable.{{Cite web |date=2009 |title=Reference Document 2008/09 |url=http://www.actusnewswire.com/documents/ACTUS-0-3288-OL-DDR-0809-GB.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200814043337/http://www.actusnewswire.com/documents/ACTUS-0-3288-OL-DDR-0809-GB.pdf |archive-date=14 August 2020 |publisher=[[Olympique Lyonnais]] |page=50}} He scored his first goal for Galatasaray in a [[UEFA Europa League]] qualification match against [[Maccabi Netanya F.C.|Maccabi Netanya]] in the 5th minute. On 12 December, Keïta scored for Galatasaray in a 3–2 victory over [[Antalyaspor]]. On 18 February 2010, Keïta scored a late equalizer to secure a 1–1 away draw for Galatasaray against [[Atlético Madrid]] in the UEFA Europa League. Later, in the second leg he equalized again to make it 1–1, but Galatasaray failed to qualify. On 28 February, he scored the second and fourth goals in a 4–1 victory over [[Kasımpaşa S.K.|Kasımpaşa]]. His first goal was a volley from just inside the penalty area. In Galatasaray's 3–0 victory over [[MKE Ankaragücü]] in March, Keïta scored the second goal as well as assisting the final goal. On 11 April 2010, he assisted two of [[Milan Baroš]]' goals in a 4–1 victory over [[Diyarbakırspor]]. A week later, he scored the first goal in a 1–2 victory over [[Manisaspor]]. ===Al Sadd=== Keïta rejoined his previous club [[Al Sadd SC|Al Sadd]] in July 2010, for €8.15 million.{{cite news|url=http://www.kap.gov.tr/yay/Bildirim/Bildirim.aspx?id=120980|title=Galatasaray Profesyonel Futbol Takımı oyuncumuz Abdul Kader Keïta'nin avro8.150.000 bedelle Katar AL SADD S.C. Kulübüne transfer olması.|date=6 July 2011|access-date=23 September 2011|work=Turkish Public Disclosure System (KAP)|language=tr|archive-date=31 March 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120331085232/http://www.kap.gov.tr/yay/Bildirim/Bildirim.aspx?id=120980|url-status=live}} Keïta was involved in a melee which ensued on 19 October in the [[2011 AFC Champions League]] semi final first-leg between [[Suwon Samsung Bluewings]] and Al Sadd. Suwon player [[Choi Sung-hwan (footballer)|Choi Sung-Hwan]] was inadvertently kicked in the head by an Al Sadd defender, and Suwon's Yeom Ki-hoon let the ball out after Choi Sung-hwan went down with a head injury inside Al Sadd's box. While Choi was being tended to by medics, Keïta took the free kick quickly, and passed it to teammate [[Mamadou Niang]] unknowingly to the Suwon defense who thought possession would be returned to them according to FIFA fair play rules. Niang sprinted down the center half past the goalkeeper to score a second goal for Al Sadd. The chaos was further elevated when a Suwon fan ran onto the pitch, causing a brawl to erupt between the two teams. Afterwards, Keïta received a red card, allegedly for running towards the fan, slapping him in the back of the head and grabbing him by his throat.{{Cite web |url=http://www.bernama.com/bernama/v5/newsworld.php?id=621375 |title=BERNAMA – Asian Football Body Investigating In-game Brawl In South Korea |access-date=20 October 2011 |archive-date=4 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304043425/http://www.bernama.com/bernama/v5/newsworld.php?id=621375 |url-status=live }} His teammate [[Lee Jung-Soo]] had told the press that Keïta had apologized for assisting Niang in scoring the goal, and admitted it was wrong. Al Sadd's coach, Jorge Fossati, suggested that Al Sadd was annoyed that Suwon had not immediately put the ball out of play, and decided to take actions into their own hands.{{Cite news|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/columns/story/_/id/971787/asia-shamed-by-showpiece-brawl?cc=4716|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111023001741/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/columns/story/_/id/971787/asia-shamed-by-showpiece-brawl?cc=4716|url-status=dead|archive-date=23 October 2011|title=Asia shamed by showpiece brawl|work=ESPNFC.com|access-date=26 March 2018}} Keïta was later suspended by AFC for the return leg. Keïta scored a goal in the [[2011 AFC Champions League Final|AFC Champions League Final]] on 5 November, as his side defeated [[Jeonbuk Hyundai Motors|Jeonbuk Motors]] on penalties after the match ended 2–2 and was named as [[Man of the Match]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/soccer/report?gameId=333495|title=Jeonbuk Motors vs. Al Sadd - Football Match Report - November 5, 2011 - ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=26 March 2018}} He left the team at the end of the 2011–12 season, and was linked with several teams in England and stated his interest of playing in the [[Premier League]].{{cite web |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11700/8307095/Ivory-Coast-winger-Abdul-Kader-Keita-is-keen-on-a-move-to-the-Premier-League |title=Ivory Coast winger Abdul Kader Keïta is keen on a move to the Premier League |publisher=[[Sky Sports]] |date=3 December 2012 |access-date=29 May 2013 |first=Giscard |last=Gourizo}} ==International career== Keïta had a distinguished international career with 72 [[Cap (football)|caps]] for the [[Ivory Coast national football team|Ivory Coast]], representing the team at the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]], [[2010 FIFA World Cup]] and at four [[Africa Cup of Nations]] in [[2002 Africa Cup of Nations|2002]], [[2008 Africa Cup of Nations|2008]], [[2010 Africa Cup of Nations|2010]], and [[2012 Africa Cup of Nations|2012]], helping them finish runner-up in 2012. Keïta was selected for [[2010 African Nations Cup]] and played three matches, scoring once against [[Algeria national football team|Algeria]] during the quarter-final match. ===2010 World Cup incident=== During the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]] in South Africa, Keïta was involved in an off-the-ball incident with [[Kaká]] during a group game against [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]]. Keïta ran into Kaká and fell onto the floor, clutching his face, as if in great pain. Kaká was shown a yellow card, his second of the match, and sent off. [[Australian Broadcasting Corporation|ABC]] wrote "Abdul Kader Keïta's embarrassing reaction to a love-tap in the midriff from the Brazilian playmaker was both laughable and disgraceful. Obviously hoping to get Kaka in further hot water after he had only just earlier been shown his first yellow card, Keïta fell to the ground and clutched his face as if he'd been shot from close range. He blatantly cheated to ensure the Brazilian was given his marching orders."{{cite '''Francisco Javier González Pérez''' ({{IPA|es|fɾanˈθisko xaˈβjeɾ ɣonˈθaleθ ˈpeɾeθ}}; born 14 July 1969), known as '''Fran''', is a Spanish former professional [[association football|footballer]].

He spent his entire career with [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo]] as a skilled [[left midfielder]] with [[Passing (association football)|passing]] ability, helping the club win the first [[La Liga]] title in its history.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lavozdegalicia.es/noticia/torremarathon/2019/03/28/heroes-superdepor/00031553776559527243756.htm|title=¿Qué fue de los héroes del Superdépor?|trans-title=What happened to the heroes of Superdépor?|newspaper=[[La Voz de Galicia]]|first=Iván|last=Antelo|language=es|date=28 March 2019|access-date=19 February 2025}}</ref>

Fran represented [[Spain national football team|Spain]] at [[UEFA Euro 2000|Euro 2000]].

==Club career==
Fran, one of the most notable players in [[Deportivo de La Coruña]]'s history, was born in [[Carreira (Ribeira)|Carreira]], [[Santa Uxía de Ribeira]], [[Galicia (Spain)|Galicia]], and was promoted to the first team in 1988, making his [[La Liga]] debut on 31 August 1991 in a 2–1 away loss against [[Valencia CF|Valencia]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1991/09/01/pagina-16/1440404/pdf.html|title=El Valencia reacciona a tiempo|trans-title=Valencia react on time|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|first=Luis|last=Urrutia|language=es|date=1 September 1991|access-date=5 November 2017}}</ref> Quickly established, he only missed eight league games in his first five seasons – also scoring on 24 occasions – while already being [[Captain (association football)|captain]].<ref name=SD>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2017/03/07/primera/1488900629_217206.html|title=¿Qué fue de Fran, el capitán del Superdepor?|trans-title=What happened to Fran, captain of Superdepor?|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|first=Alberto|last=Pérez Sierra|language=es|date=7 March 2017|access-date=5 November 2017}}</ref>

In the [[1995–96 La Liga|1995–96]] off-season, [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] almost signed Fran (previously, in early 1992 and unbeknownst to him, he had agreed to a pre-contract with that club after having already put pen to paper to a new deal at Deportivo),<ref>{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/diario/1992/02/07/deportes/697417203_850215.html|title=Fran firmó contratos con el Deportivo y el Madrid asesorado por un diputado socialista|trans-title=Fran signed contracts with Deportivo and Madrid aided by a socialist deputy|newspaper=[[El País]]|first=Juan José|last=Paradinas|language=es|date=7 February 1992|access-date=5 November 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.relevo.com/futbol/liga-primera/fichaje-rentable-historia-real-madrid-20230212130746-nt.html|title=La desconocida historia del fichaje (y la ruptura) de Fran por el Madrid: "Pero tú, chaval, ¿de qué guindo caíste?"|trans-title=The unknown story of the signing (and falling) of Fran for Madrid: "But you, my boy, what were you thinking?"|publisher=[[Relevo]]|first=Manuel|last=Amor|language=es|date=12 February 2023|access-date=2 January 2026}}</ref> but he regretted leaving and returned quickly. In [[1999–2000 La Liga|1999–2000]], as ''Depor'' claimed their first national championship, injuries limited him to only 22 matches, and he added a goal in a 2–0 home win over Valencia on 12 March 2000.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://elpais.com/diario/2000/03/13/deportes/952902015_850215.html|title=El líder renace cuando más lo necesita|trans-title=Leaders reborn when they needed it the most|newspaper=El País|first=Xosé|last=Hermida|language=es|date=13 March 2000|access-date=7 August 2016}}</ref>

Fran retired from football at the end of the [[2004–05 La Liga|2004–05 campaign]] after 17 years at the [[Estadio Riazor]], 14 in the first division, at the same time as [[Mauro Silva]], with both playing their last game on 22 May 2005 in a 3–0 home defeat to [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2005/05/23/mas_futbol/1116829635_850215.html|title=El Mallorca da un portazo al ciclo de Fran y Mauro Silva|trans-title=Mallorca slam door on Fran and Mauro Silva's cycle|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Fermín|last=De la Calle|language=es|date=23 May 2005|access-date=7 August 2016}}</ref> He made 700 competitive appearances.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2020/05/11/segunda/1589184669_657423.html|title=Fran, el último 'one club man' del Deportivo|trans-title=Fran, Deportivo's last one-club man|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Luis|last=De la Cruz|language=es|date=11 May 2020|access-date=11 May 2021}}</ref>

In 2008, Fran returned to Deportivo, joining its [[indoor soccer]] team alongside former teammates [[Djalminha]], [[Donato (footballer)|Donato]], [[Noureddine Naybet]] and [[Jacques Songo'o]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2009/03/13/mas_futbol/1236898853_850215.html|title=Deportivo 11 Valencia 11|newspaper=Diario AS|language=es|date=13 March 2009|access-date=7 August 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.defensacentral.com/madridismo/41534-ftbol-indoor-deportivo-djalminha-fran-amavisca-alfonso/|title=Djalminha y Fran destrozan al Madrid|trans-title=Djalminha and Fran destroy Madrid|publisher=Defensa Central|language=es|date=29 January 2010|access-date=7 August 2016}}</ref>

==International career==
Fran made his [[Spanish national football team|Spain national team]] debut on 27 January 1993, in a [[Exhibition game|friendly]] 1–1 draw against [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]] in [[Las Palmas]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1993/01/28/pagina-15/1264280/pdf.html|title=Más joven, pero igual de gris|trans-title=Younger, but just as grey|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Rogelio|last=Román|language=es|date=28 January 1993|access-date=7 August 2016}}</ref> He earned 16 [[Cap (sport)|caps]] in total,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lavozdegalicia.es/noticia/torremarathon/hemeroteca/2015/01/27/00031422303067208940444.htm|title=Fran cumple 20 años como internacional|trans-title=Fran celebrates 20 years as an international|newspaper=La Voz de Galicia|language=es|date=27 January 2015|access-date=2 January 2026}}</ref> participating at [[UEFA Euro 2000]] where he played his last international, a 4–3 group stage victory over [[Serbia national football team|Yugoslavia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/euro2000/800459.stm|title=Spain survive in seven-goal classic|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=21 June 2000|access-date=16 July 2013}}</ref>

In April 2016, Fran was appointed [[Galicia national football team|Galicia]]'s manager alongside [[Míchel Salgado]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.atlantico.net/articulo/deportes/riazor-escenario-galicia-venezuela-fran-y-michel-salgado-tecnicos/20160414114706525419.html|title=Riazor, escenario del Galicia-Venezuela con Fran y Míchel Salgado de técnicos|trans-title=Riazor, venue of Galicia-Venezuela with Fran and Míchel Salgado as managers|newspaper=[[Atlántico Diario]]|language=es|date=14 April 2016|access-date=15 June 2019}}</ref> He left the role eight years later.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.atlantico.net/deporte-local/vigues-diego-martinez-nuevo-seleccionador-gallego-futbol_1_20240410-1114933.html|title=El vigués Diego Martínez es el nuevo seleccionador gallego de fútbol|trans-title=Vigo-born Diego Martínez is the new Galician national football team manager|newspaper=Atlántico Diario|first=Marcos|last=Martín Reboredo|language=es|date=10 April 2024|access-date=2 January 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Fran's older brother, [[José Ramón (footballer, born 1968)|José Ramón]], was also a footballer (and a midfielder). He too spent several seasons with Deportivo, but with much less individual impact.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.laopinioncoruna.es/deportivo/2014/07/18/excapitan-deportivo-jose-ramon-incorpora/861411.html|title=El excapitán del Deportivo José Ramón se incorpora al fútbol base|trans-title=Former Deportivo captain José Ramón added to youth football|newspaper=La Opinión A Coruña|language=es|date=18 July 2014|access-date=7 August 2016}}</ref>

His son [[Nico González (footballer, born 2002)|Nicolás]] is also involved in the sport. Having been brought up at [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], he later played for [[FC Porto|Porto]]<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2021/04/15/primera/1618514859_788607.html|title=El Barça atará al hijo de Fran|trans-title=Barça will shield Fran's son|newspaper=Diario AS|language=es|date=15 April 2021|access-date=29 August 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lavozdegalicia.es/noticia/deportes/2021/12/23/fran-nico-gonzalez-saborean-2021/00031640286345708289324.htm|title=Fran y Nico González saborean el 2021|trans-title=Fran and Nico González taste 2021|newspaper=La Voz de Galicia|first1=A.|last1=Centeno|first2=Iván|last2=Antelo|language=es|date=23 December 2021|access-date=6 January 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lavozdegalicia.es/noticia/deportes/2024/10/07/nico-gonzalez-logra-mvp-oporto-regala-recogepelotas/00031728297129475662999.htm|title=Nico González logra el MVP del partido y se lo regala a un recogepelotas|trans-title=Nico González gets MVP of the match and gives it to a ballboy|newspaper=La Voz de Galicia|language=es|date=7 October 2024|access-date=4 December 2024}}</ref> and [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/nico-gonzalez-signs-63874209|title=Nico becomes City’s fourth winter signing|publisher=Manchester City F.C.|first=Rob|last=Pollard|date=3 February 2025|access-date=19 February 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.wandsworthguardian.co.uk/sport/national/24913473.nico-gonzalez-says-father-told-joining-manchester-city-the-best-thing/|title=Nico Gonzalez says his father told him joining Manchester City ‘the best thing’|newspaper=Wandsworth Times|date=5 February 2025|access-date=20 February 2025}}</ref>

'''Andrés Nicolás D'Alessandro''' (born 15 April 1981) is an Argentine former professional footballer who played as an [[Midfielder#Attacking midfielder|attacking midfielder]]. 

Known as ''El Cabezón'' ("Big Head") for how large his big head looks on his small frame rather than any ego connotations,<ref name="boba">{{cite web|last1=Brega|first1=Giordano|title=Si affloscia la "boba" di Andres D'Alessandro. Il cabezon torna in Argentina|trans-title=The "boba" of Andres D'Alessandro comes to an end. ''El cabezón'' returns to Argentina|url=http://www.affaritaliani.it/sport/andresdalessandroaddioeuropa060208.html?refresh_ce|publisher=Affari Italiani|access-date=1 March 2015|language=it|date=9 February 2008}}</ref> he won an Olympic gold medal with [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] in [[Football at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2004]] and also played at that year's [[2004 Copa América|Copa América]].

In 2020, he was awarded Brazilian citizenship.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Povo|first=Correio do|title=D'Alessandro é naturalizado brasileiro após 12 anos de Inter|url=https://www.correiodopovo.com.br/esportes/inter/d-alessandro-%C3%A9-naturalizado-brasileiro-ap%C3%B3s-12-anos-de-inter-1.482216|access-date=2021-07-10|website=Correio do Povo|date=17 September 2020 |language=pt-br}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-09-17|title=Andrés D'Alessandro se nacionalizó brasileño|url=https://www.espn.com.ar/futbol/brasil/nota/_/id/7446083/andres-dalessandro-se-nacionalizo-brasileno|access-date=2021-07-10|website=ESPN.com.ar|language=es}}</ref>

D'Alessandro is regarded as one of Internacional's most notable players, alongside figures such as [[Paulo Roberto Falcão|Falcão]], [[Valdomiro Vaz Franco|Valdomiro]], and [[Fernandão (footballer, born 1978)|Fernandão]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=D'Alessandro {{!}} Sport Club Internacional |url=https://internacional.com.br/clube/idolos/d-alessandro |access-date=2026-08-02 |website=internacional.com.br}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Early career===
D'Alessandro was born in the [[La Paternal, Buenos Aires|La Paternal]] section of [[Buenos Aires]], Argentina. He joined the labor force as a pizza delivery boy before becoming a professional footballer.<ref>Page 12 of [[News of the World]] sport section; 9 April 2006.</ref> He emerged through the [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]] [[youth system]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Player Profile: Andres D´Alessandro|url=http://www.southamericanfutbol.com/2010/04/player-profile-andres-d%C2%B4alessandro/ |publisher=Southamericanfutbol.com |access-date=17 February 2011}}</ref> that has produced much of Argentina's top talent over the years. He followed the likes of [[Santiago Solari]] and [[Pablo Aimar]] through the ranks, together with [[Javier Saviola]], with whom he shared the limelight in the 2001 [[Football World Youth Championship|Youth World Championship]].

His talent attracted attention from European clubs following his success and performances at the 2001 FIFA World Youth Championship. He subsequently spent time on trial at West Ham in 2001 but no deal was agreed, with the management considering [[Joe Cole]] too similar and fee too high.<ref name="WestHamRedknapp">{{cite web | last=Bailey | first=Graeme | title=HAMMERS TO FAIL WITH D`ALESSANDRO BID | website=Sky Sports | date=2001-02-09 | url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/2203690/hammers-to-fail-with-d-alessandro-bid | access-date=2026-05-13}}</ref><ref name="PortsmouthRedknapp">{{cite web | last=McMahon | first=Mark | title=The Pompey duo former West Ham and Spurs boss Harry Redknapp ranks as two of his greatest January signings | website=The News | date=2022-01-30 | url=https://www.portsmouth.co.uk/sport/football/portsmouth-fc/the-pompey-duo-harry-redknapp-ranks-as-two-of-his-greatest-january-signings-3547824 | access-date=2026-05-13}}</ref>

With the River Plate senior team, he won the [[2001–02 Primera Divisió|2001–02]] and [[2002–03 Primera Divisió|2002–03]] [[Argentine Primera División|Primera División]]; the 2002–03 season was one of his best, scoring 15 goals in 40 appearances. 

His 15 goals included several memorable performances, most notably River Plate's 5–2 victory over Rosario Central on 29 September 2002, when he scored twice and provided two assists.<ref>{{Cite web |title=River Plate 5-2 Rosario Central - Apertura 2002 |url=https://lahistoriariver.com/partidos/river-plate-vs-rosario-central-apertura-2002-29-09-2002 |access-date=2026-08-05 |website=La Historia River |language=es}}</ref> He also delivered an outstanding display on 8 June 2003, scoring once and grabbing two more assists in a 4–0 win against San Lorenzo.

In the 2003 Libertadores, he scored 4 goals, including a free kick in the round of 16 1st leg against [[SC Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]] to help his team win the match 2–1.<ref>{{Cite web |title=River 2-1 Corinthians {{!}} Libertadores 2003 |url=https://estadisticasriver.com/partido/river-plate-vs-corinthians-brasil-copa-libertadores-2003-01-05-2003/ |access-date=2026-08-05 |website=Estadísticas de River Plate |language=es-AR}}</ref> 

===Spell in Europe===
Following continuing impressive performances, D'Alessandro eventually transferred to German Bundesliga club Wolfsburg in July 2003 for a club record €9 million.<ref>{{cite news|title=Wolfsburg snap up D'Alessandro |url=http://www.uefa.com/competitions/intertotocup/news/kind=1/newsid=80971.html |work=[[UEFA]] |date=12 June 2003 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090528085909/http://www.uefa.com/competitions/intertotocup/news/kind%3D1/newsid%3D80971.html |archive-date=28 May 2009 |url-status=dead}}</ref> On 21 September 2005, D'Alessandro scored the [[Bundesliga]]'s 40,000th goal since its creation in 1963, netting the fourth goal in a 4–2 victory over [[Hannover 96]].

On 31 January 2006, to the surprise of most fans, D'Alessandro joined English [[Premier League]] club [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] on loan for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Portsmouth snap up d'Alessandro|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/p/portsmouth/4665826.stm|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|access-date=17 February 2011|date=31 January 2006}}</ref> His main objective with his new club was to blend in with new teammates and help his club to avoid relegation. On [[Easter Monday]], 17 April, he scored his first goal in English football – a contender for goal of the season – in Portsmouth's 2–1 defeat away to [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/4906468.stm |title= Charlton 2–1 Portsmouth |publisher=[[BBC]] |date=17 April 2006 |access-date=1 September 2009}}</ref>

Portsmouth survived and manager [[Harry Redknapp]] sought to sign D'Alessandro on a permanent basis, but on 17 June 2006, he completed a season-long loan switch to [[La Liga]] outfit [[Real Zaragoza]], citing his desire to play in Spain as a major factor in his decision. His club had a great season, finishing sixth in the league, qualifying for next years UEFA Cup, and narrowly being eliminated from the Copa del Rey quarter-finals to Barcelona on away goals. On 6 June 2007, he signed a contract at Zaragoza, keeping him at the club until 2011. However he suffered disciplinary problems in his second year at the club; he was involved in a heated altercation with teammate [[Pablo Aimar]] in training on 17 October 2007, and later stated that he felt coach [[Víctor Fernández]] was giving Aimar preferential treatment.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2007-10-17 |title=D'Alessandro y Aimar, a punto de llegar a las manos |url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2007/10/17/actualidad/1192605723_850215.html |access-date=2026-08-03 |work=El País |language=es |issn=1134-6582}}</ref>

===Return to South America===
In 2008, despite expressing his desire to join River Plate, the club and the player were unable to come to an agreement. Shortly after, he joined his former River Plate manager [[Ramón Díaz]] at Argentine club [[Club Atlético San Lorenzo de Almagro|San Lorenzo]]. Despite his short spell at the club, he became one of their most important players. One of his most memorable performances came on 8 May, in the second leg of the Copa Libertadores round of 16 match against River Plate; with San Lorenzo down 2–0 at the 60th minute, D'Alessandro was involved in both of his team's goals as they scored twice in 5 minutes to win 4–3 on aggregate.<ref>{{Cite web |date=8 May 2008 |title=River 2-2 San Lorenzo (3-4 agg) |url=https://www.espn.co.uk/football/commentary/_/gameId/235396 |access-date=2026-08-03 |website=www.espn.co.uk}}</ref> Shortly after the match, D'alessandro told reporters, "This victory is special because of the people directing the club, who made a mistake." He said this because of the failed attempt to return to River after leaving Wolfsburg.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2018-12-18 |title=River ya enfrentó a D'Alessandro |url=https://www.ole.com.ar/river-plate/river-enfrento-alessandro-libertadores-river-inter_0_2Qw_xtyk0.html |access-date=2026-08-03 |website=Olé |language=es-AR}}</ref> 

However, after Díaz left the club, D'Alesandro opted to move to Brazil to play for [[Sport Club Internacional|Internacional]] and joined on 1 August 2008.<ref>{{cite web |title=D'Alessandro Pens Four-Year Inter Deal |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/584/brazil/2008/08/01/799856/dalessandro-pens-four-year-inter-deal |publisher=Goal.com |date=1 August 2008 |access-date=17 February 2011}}</ref>

On 13 December 2008 it was reported on [[ESPN Deportes]] that the [[Los Angeles Galaxy]] had made a $10 million offer to for D'Alessandro but was declined.<ref>{{cite web|title=Internacional turn down Galaxy D'Alessandro bid|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=602275&sec=global&cc=5901|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081217110445/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=602275&sec=global&cc=5901|url-status=dead|archive-date=17 December 2008|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|access-date=17 February 2011 | date = 14 December 2008}}</ref>

He played an important role in Inter's 2008 Copa Sudamericana title, scoring 2 goals in the semifinal second leg against Chivas.  In 2009 Internacional finished in second place in both the [[2009 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|Brasileirão]] and [[2009 Copa do Brasil|Copa do Brasil]]. In 2010, D'Alessandro led Internacional to their second [[2010 Copa Libertadores|Libertadores Championship]], and was elected the [[South American Player of the Year|best player in South America for that year]];<ref>{{cite web|last1=Rinaldi|first1=Cesare|title=Calcio Sudamericano: Andres D'Alessandro è il Balon de Oro 2010|url=http://www.calcioblog.it/post/15487/calcio-sudamericano-andres-dalessandro-e-il-balon-de-oro-2010|website=calcioblog.it|access-date=1 March 2015|date=31 December 2010|archive-date=2 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402111027/http://www.calcioblog.it/post/15487/calcio-sudamericano-andres-dalessandro-e-il-balon-de-oro-2010|url-status=dead}}</ref> in the [[2010 FIFA Club World Cup]], he also helped Internacional to a third-place finish, and was awarded the [[FIFA Club World Cup#Awards|Bronze Ball]] as the tournament's third best player. In 2011 D'Alessadro had personally an even better year, but Internacional only managed to win the [[2011 Campeonato Gaúcho|State Championship]]. 2012 was a bad year for both Internacional and D'Alessandro. Furthermore, rumours of him leaving to play in China caused a major distraction; after long drawn out drama he stayed but soon was injured. In 2013 his game improved again, and while Inter only won the [[2013 Campeonato Gaúcho|State Championship]], he was praised as the only positive factor of the team that year. 2014 started well; D'Alessandro continued to play well and led Inter to their 4th straight [[2014 Campeonato Gaúcho|Gaucho Championship]].

On 3 February 2016, he returned to River Plate after {{frac|12|1|2}} years on a loan deal.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://espn.uol.com.br/noticia/575130_argentino-de-maior-sucesso-na-historia-do-brasil-dalessandro-deixa-inter-apos-8-anos|title = Argentino de maior sucesso na história do Brasil, d'Alessandro deixa Inter após 8 anos| work=ESPN }}</ref> He won his second Recopa Sudamericana and the Copa Argentina during his stay at the club. After that, he returned to Internacional de Porto Alegre for the 2017 season. 

He scored in his last match as a professional, a 2–1 victory for Inter on 16 April 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |date=16 April 2022 |title=O adeus de D'Alessandro, argentino que se tornou o gigante do Beira-Rio, do RS e do futebol brasileiro |url=https://www.terra.com.br/esportes/internacional/o-adeus-de-dalessandro-argentino-que-se-tornou-o-gigante-do-beira-rio-do-rs-e-do-futebol-brasileiro,4c2cce095a4729f4d6bdd12ae6d37310wb058clh.html |access-date=2026-08-05 |website=Terra |language=pt-BR}}</ref> 

==International career==
D'Alessandro won the [[2001 FIFA World Youth Championship|2001 Under-20 World Championship]] with the [[Argentina national under-20 football team|Argentine youth side]], held in Buenos Aires; due to his performances alongside his club teammate [[Javier Saviola]], he was awarded the [[FIFA World Youth Championship#Awards|Silver Ball]] as the tournament's second best player. D'Alessandro had originally started the tournament as a substitute, but injuries allowed him a place in the team in later matches. Argentina beat [[Ghana national football team|Ghana]] 3–0 in [[2001 FIFA World Youth Championship final|the final]].

D'Alessandro has represented [[Argentina national football team|Argentina's senior side]] on 28 occasions, scoring 4 times between 2001 and 2011. He also represented [[Argentina national under-23 football team|Argentina's under-23 side]] at the [[Football at the 2004 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2004 Olympic Games]] in Athens, where Argentina won a gold medal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Andres D ALESSANDRO|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/statisticsandrecords/players/player=180182/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080318224108/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/statisticsandrecords/players/player=180182/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=18 March 2008|publisher=FIFA|access-date=1 March 2015}}</ref>

D'Alessandro also took part in the [[2004 Copa América]] with Argentina. He scored his only goal of the tournament in the group stage, in Argentina's 6–1 victory over [[Ecuador national football team|Ecuador]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Saviola blows Ecuador away|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2004/jul/08/newsstory.sport4|work=The Guardian|access-date=28 February 2015|date=8 July 2004}}</ref> In the [[2004 Copa América final|final]], against rivals [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]], he missed Argentina's first penalty in the resulting shootout, following a 2–2 draw after extra time; Argentina were defeated 4–2 in the shootout.<ref>{{cite web|title=Brazil win Copa shoot-out|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/internationals/3922603.stm|work=BBC News|access-date=28 February 2015|date=25 July 2004}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=O'Connor|first1=Michael|title=Brazil snatch cup in late twist|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2004/jul/26/newsstory.sport5|work=The Guardian|access-date=28 February 2015|date=26 July 2004}}</ref>

On 20 August 2010, [[Sergio Batista]] recalled D'Alessandro to the national team for a friendly against [[Spain national football team|Spain]], which was played on 7 September 2010 at the Monumental Stadium River Plate.

==Style of play==
D'Alessandro was best known for his [[Dribbling#Association football|dribbling]] ability, creativity, and technical skill, and was adept at beating players with body [[Dummy (football)|feints]] and tricks, such as the dragback (''boba''), [[Nutmeg (football)|nutmeg]], or [[Pelé runaround move|the Blomqvist shuffle]];<ref>{{cite web|last1=Brega|first1=Giordano|title=Si affloscia la "boba" di Andres D'Alessandro. Il cabezon torna in Argentina|url=http://www.affaritaliani.it/sport/andresdalessandroaddioeuropa060208.html?refresh_ce|website=affaritaliani.it|access-date=1 March 2015|language=it |trans-title=The "boba" of Andres D'Alessandro comes to an end. El cabezon returns to Argentina|date=9 February 2008}}</ref><ref name="D' Alessandro, la maledizione del mancato Maradona">{{cite web|last1=Dotto|first1=Matteo|title=D' Alessandro, la maledizione del mancato Maradona|url=http://archiviostorico.corriere.it/2006/febbraio/07/Alessandro_maledizione_del_mancato_Maradona_co_9_060207120.shtml|website=archiviostorico.corriere.it|publisher=Il Corriere della Sera|access-date=1 March 2015|language=it |trans-title=D'Alessandro, the curse of the unfulfilled New Maradona |date=7 February 2006}}</ref> and was also an accurate [[Direct free kick|free-kick]] taker.<ref name="D' Alessandro, la maledizione del mancato Maradona"/> D'Alessandro is also known for his short passing ability, which makes him a capable [[Assist (football)|assist]] provider.<ref name="D' Alessandro, la maledizione del mancato Maradona"/>

In 2001, he was named one of the 100 best young footballers in the world by ''[[Don Balón]]'',<ref>{{cite web|title=Don Balon's list of the 100 best young players in the world|url=http://www.thespoiler.co.uk/2010/11/02/don-balons-list-of-the-100-best-young-players-in-the-world/|website=thespoiler.co.uk|date=2 November 2010|access-date=1 March 2015}}</ref> and he was also labelled one of [[Diego Armando Maradona|Maradona]]'s potential [[New Maradona|heirs]] by the media and by Maradona himself; despite his precocious talent however, he was not able to fully fulfill the potential he demonstrated in his youth.<ref name="D' Alessandro, la maledizione del mancato Maradona"/>

'''Joaquín Oscar Larrivey''' ({{IPA|es|xoaˈkin lariˈβej}}; born 20 August 1984) is an Argentine professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[centre forward]] for Chilean club [[Deportes Concepción (Chile)|Deportes Concepción]].

He is nicknamed ''el Bati'', for his physical resemblance to former footballer [[Gabriel Batistuta]]. Larrivey also holds a [[European Union]] passport as a second nationality.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2007/giugno/05/Fiorentina_Balzaretti_Cagliari_bloccato_Larrivey_ga_10_070605073.shtml|title=Fiorentina: c' è Balzaretti Cagliari, bloccato Larrivey Il Parma va su Di Natale|date=5 June 2007|access-date=25 December 2010|work=La Gazzetta dello Sport|language=it}}</ref>

==Biography==
Larrivey was born on 20 August 1984 in [[Gualeguay, Entre Ríos|Gualeguay]], Argentina.<ref>{{cite web |title=¡FELIZ CUMPLEAÑOS LARRIVEY! {{!}} Radio AzulChile |url=https://radioazulchile.cl/feliz-cumpleanos-larrivey/ |website=Radio AzulChile |access-date=26 July 2026 |language=es |date=20 August 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Concha |first1=Julián |title=Joaquín Larrivey renueva con 41 años: “Nadie me cuestiona porque con goles demuestro mi vigencia; en Conce estoy muy feliz” |url=https://www.latercera.com/el-deportivo/noticia/joaquin-larrivey-renueva-con-41-anos-nadie-me-cuestiona-porque-con-goles-demuestro-mi-vigencia-en-conce-estoy-muy-feliz/ |website=La Tercera |access-date=26 July 2026 |language=es |date=5 August 2025}}</ref> He began his career in Argentina with [[Club Atlético Huracán|Huracán]] and quickly became an important player for the side. Larrivey was signed by Italian [[Serie A]] side [[Cagliari Calcio|Cagliari]] in June 2007 on a 4-year contract.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cagliaricalcio.net/news/notizia.asp?idNotizia=3848&type=0&id_menu=2|title=Arriva Larrivey|date=15 June 2007|access-date=10 August 2010|work=Cagliari Calcio|language=it|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070928024206/http://www.cagliaricalcio.net/news/notizia.asp?idNotizia=3848&type=0&id_menu=2|archive-date=28 September 2007}}</ref> On 12 February 2009 [[Club Atlético Vélez Sársfield|Vélez Sársfield]] of [[Argentine Primera División]] signed him on loan until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cagliaricalcio.net/news/notizia.asp?idNotizia=6673&type=0&id_menu=2|title=Arrivederci Larry!|date=12 February 2009|access-date=10 August 2010|work=Cagliari Calcio|language=it|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090214165407/http://cagliaricalcio.net/news/notizia.asp?idNotizia=6673&type=0&id_menu=2|archive-date=14 February 2009}}</ref> He started successfully at Vélez scoring in his debut game against [[Club Atlético Tigre|Tigre]]. He also scored against [[Godoy Cruz Antonio Tomba|Godoy Cruz]] and [[Rosario Central]]. However, after this last one (which was in the 7th game of the Clausura tournament) he was held scoreless. On 1 July 2009, Larrivey returned to Cagliari. On 5 August 2010, he was loaned to [[Club Atlético Colón]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cagliaricalcio.net/news/notizia.asp?idNotizia=9003&type=0&id_menu=2|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120724173804/http://www.cagliaricalcio.net/news/notizia.asp?idNotizia=9003&type=0&id_menu=2|url-status=dead|archive-date=24 July 2012|title=Larrivey al Colòn|date=5 August 2010|access-date=10 August 2010|work=Cagliari Calcio|language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.clubcolon.com.ar/noticia.php?id=1180|title=El Bati Larrivey ya es uno más|date=8 August 2010|access-date=10 August 2010|work=Club Atlético Colón|language=es|archive-date=3 October 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111003065016/http://www.clubcolon.com.ar/noticia.php?id=1180|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2011, Joaquin Larrivey returned to Cagliari again, this time to take a first team place. After the departure of [[Alessandro Matri]] who was sold to [[Juventus FC]] and [[Robert Acquafresca]] who returned to [[Genoa C.F.C.|Genoa]] after his 1-year loan, Larrivey and [[Ânderson Miguel da Silva|Nenê]] became the first choice strikers. He was assigned the number 9 shirt before the beginning of the season.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cagliaricalcio.net/news/11744/il-cagliari-da-i-numeri.html|title=Il Cagliari dà i numeri|date=10 August 2011|access-date=25 August 2011|work=Cagliari Calcio|language=it|archive-date=3 May 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120503113750/http://www.cagliaricalcio.net/news/11744/il-cagliari-da-i-numeri.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 21 August 2011, Larrivey scored a hat-trick in a 5–1 win over [[U.C. AlbinoLeffe]] in the [[Coppa Italia]], becoming only the second player to do so in the history of Cagliari, together with legend [[Luigi Riva|"Gigi" Riva]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cagliaricalcio.net/news/11796/larrivey-eguaglia-riva.html|title=Larrivey eguaglia Riva|date=22 August 2011|access-date=25 August 2011|work=Cagliari Calcio|language=it|archive-date=3 May 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120503113817/http://www.cagliaricalcio.net/news/11796/larrivey-eguaglia-riva.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> On 28 November 2012 Larrivey left Cagliari .<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cagliaricalcio.net/news/13816/il-saluto-di-larrivey.html|title=Il saluto di Larrivey|date=28 November 2012|access-date=14 June 2015|publisher=Cagliari Calcio|language=it|archive-date=1 December 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121201034032/http://www.cagliaricalcio.net/news/13816/il-saluto-di-larrivey.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 17 December 2012 Larrivey was presented as a new player for Mexican club [[Club de Fútbol Atlante|Atlante]]. He was signed to form the attack with Chilean [[Esteban Paredes]]. On 27 January 2013 he scored his first goals with the club recording a brace against Chiapas in a 4–3 victory.

In January 2020, Larrivey moved to Chile and signed with [[Club Universidad de Chile|Universidad de Chile]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Miranda |first1=Gonzalo |title=Universidad de Chile oficializó el fichaje de Joaquín Larrivey |url=https://www.adnradio.cl/deportes/2020/01/09/universidad-de-chile-oficializo-el-fichaje-de-joaquin-larrivey-4000358.html |access-date=10 February 2025 |work=[[ADN Radio Chile|ADN Radio]] |date=9 January 2020 |language=es}}</ref>

On 3 February 2022, Larrivey joined [[Serie B]] side [[Cosenza Calcio|Cosenza]] on a deal until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ilcosenza.it/2022/02/03/joaquin-larrivey-e-il-nuovo-attaccante-del-cosenza/|title=JOAQUÍN LARRIVEY È IL NUOVO ATTACCANTE DEL COSENZA|publisher=[[Cosenza Calcio]]|date=3 February 2022|accessdate=3 February 2022|language=Italian}}</ref> On 31 January 2023, Larrivey's contract with Cosenza was terminated by mutual consent.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Cosenza Calcio|url=http://www.ilcosenza.it/2023/01/31/larrivey-risoluzione-contrattuale/|title=Risolto il contratto con Joaquin Larrivey|date=31 January 2023|access-date=31 January 2023|language=it}}</ref>

On 2 February 2023, Larrivey signed with [[F.C. Südtirol|Südtirol]], also in [[Serie B]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Südtirol|url=https://www.fc-suedtirol.com/it/news/joaqu%C3%ADn-larrivey-esperienza-in-attacco/24-2723.html|title=Joaquín Larrivey, esperienza in attacco|date=2 February 2023|access-date=3 February 2023|language=it}}</ref>

In June 2023, Larrivey returned to Chile and joined [[Deportes Magallanes|Magallanes]] in the [[Primera B de Chile|Primera B]] (second level).<ref>{{cite news |title=Regresa al fútbol chileno: Magallanes oficializó el fichaje de Joaquín Larrivey |url=https://onefootball.com/de/news/regresa-al-futbol-chileno-magallanes-oficializo-el-fichaje-de-joaquin-larrivey-37630102 |access-date=10 February 2025 |work=OneFootball |date=10 February 2025 |language=es}}</ref> In 2025, he switched to [[Deportes Concepción (Chile)|Deportes Concepción]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=González |first1=Christian |title=Deportes Concepción asegura goles para el retorno a la Primera B: ficha a Joaquín Larrivey |url=https://www.latercera.com/el-deportivo/noticia/deportes-concepcion-asegura-goles-para-el-retorno-a-la-primera-b-ficha-a-joaquin-larrivey/2PFBECXXJRBH5LHATMWJZXNXZI/ |access-date=10 February 2025 |work=[[La Tercera]] |date=28 January 2025 |language=es}}</ref>

==Personal life==
He is the son-in-law of [[Gerardo Reinoso]], an Argentine former professional football player.<ref>{{cite web |title="Corazón dividido": Larrivey y la apuesta con su suegro, un histórico de la UC |url=https://chile.as.com/chile/2020/10/02/futbol/1601637592_073887.html |publisher=[[Diario AS|AS Chile]] |access-date=13 March 2021 |language=es |date=2 October 2020}}</ref>

In July 2026, Larrivey got [[Chilean nationality law|Chilean nationality by residence]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Huerta |first1=Rodrigo |title=El nuevo paso de Larrivey en Chile: oficial |url=https://chile.as.com/futbol/el-nuevo-paso-de-larrivey-en-chile-oficial-f202607-n/ |access-date=24 July 2026 |work=[[Diario AS]] |date=24 July 2026 |language=es}}</ref>
