'''Walid Regragui''' (also spelled '''Hoalid''' or '''Oualid'''; {{Langx|ber|ⵡⴰⵍⵉⴷ ⵔⴻⴳⵔⴰⴳⵉ}}, {{langx|ar|وليد الركراكي}}; born 23 September 1975) is a French-Moroccan professional [[Association football|football]] manager and former player who played at [[right-back]]. He was most recently the head coach of the [[Morocco national football team|Morocco national team]].

Born in France, he represented the Morocco national team as a player. He spent most of his club career in France, with spells in Spain and Morocco. As a coach, he led [[Fath Union Sport|FUS Rabat]] and [[Wydad AC]], winning the [[CAF Champions League|African Champions League]] in 2022 and the [[Botola Pro|Moroccan league]] twice. He also managed [[Al Duhail SC|Al Duhail]] in Qatar, winning the league. With Morocco, he led them to the semi-finals of the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]], making history as the first team from [[Africa]] and the [[Arab world]] to reach this stage. He then led Morocco as they qualified for the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]] and won the [[2025 Africa Cup of Nations]] on home soil before resigning.

==Playing career==
Born in [[Corbeil-Essonnes]], Essonne,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/FootballFicheEntraineur4656.html |title=Walid Regragui |newspaper=L'Équipe |location=Paris |access-date=10 December 2022 |language=fr}}</ref> France, Regragui was a full international for Morocco. Clubs he played for include [[Toulouse FC|Toulouse]], [[AC Ajaccio]], [[Grenoble Foot 38|Grenoble]] and [[Racing de Santander|Racing Santander]]. In the summer of 2009, he moved from Grenoble to Moroccan club [[Moghreb Tétouan]].<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20131122190213/http://www.fifa.com/world-match-centre/nationalleagues/nationalleague=morocco-championnat-national-botola-2000000056/news/newsid/109/505/1/index.html Excitement building in Morocco]. FIFA. 27 August 2009.</ref>

Regragui played in the Moroccan squad that reached [[2004 Africa Cup of Nations final|the final]] of the [[2004 African Cup of Nations|2004 AFCON]], losing 1–2 to [[Tunisia national football team|Tunisia]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=AFCON 2025: Morocco "want to write history" after reaching first semi-final since 2004, says head coach Walid Regragui |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/news/afcon-2025-morocco-walid-regragui-write-history-first-semi-final-since-2004 |last=Fentuo |first=Fentuo Tahiru |date=2026-01-10 |access-date=2026-03-06}}</ref>

== Managerial career ==
=== Morocco ===
After retiring as a player, Regragui started his football coaching career as the assistant coach of Morocco's national team in September 2012.{{citation needed|date=December 2022}}

=== FUS ===
On 8 May 2014, he landed a head coaching job with [[Fath Union Sport]] for the 2014–15 season.<ref>[http://magharebia.com/en_GB/articles/awi/newsbriefs/sports/2014/05/09/newsbrief-02 FUS Rabat sign new coach] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304103410/http://magharebia.com/en_GB/articles/awi/newsbriefs/sports/2014/05/09/newsbrief-02 |date=4 March 2016 }} ''Magharebia''. 9 May 2014.</ref> Following his league performances and [[Moroccan Throne Cup]] victory in 2014, he was named Mars d'Or Coach of the Year in March 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=31 March 2015 |title=Et les gagnants sont Badr Hari, Walid Regragui, Mehdi Benatia et Adam Lamhamdi |url=https://lematin.ma/journal/2015/mars-d-or-2015_et-les-gagnants-sont-badr-hari-walid-regragui-mehdi-benatia-et-adam-lamhamdi/220884.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230314223359/https://lematin.ma/journal/2015/mars-d-or-2015_et-les-gagnants-sont-badr-hari-walid-regragui-mehdi-benatia-et-adam-lamhamdi/220884.html#federation=archive.wikiwix.com&tab=url |archive-date=14 March 2023 |access-date=14 March 2023 |website=Le Matin |language=fr |url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref><ref name=":1" />

On 22 January 2020, he left the club by mutual consent.<ref>{{cite web |title=COMMUNIQUE DU FATH UNION SPORT |date=22 January 2020 |url=http://fus.ma/fr/communique-du-fath-union-sport-7/ |language=fr |access-date=24 January 2020 |archive-date=23 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221123161305/http://fus.ma/fr/communique-du-fath-union-sport-7/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

=== Wydad AC ===
On 10 August 2021, Regragui was appointed as the head coach of [[Botola]] side [[Wydad AC]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=الركراكي يوقع عقود انضمامه للوداد الرياضي كمدرب للفريق الأوّل|trans-title=Regragui signs his contracts with Wydad as coach of the first team. |url=https://www.elbotola.com/article/2021-08-10-15-07-323.html|access-date=10 August 2021 |website=elbotola.com |language=ar}}</ref> The team went on to win the [[2021–22 Botola]] in his first season.{{citation needed|date=January 2025}} On 30 May 2022, he led Wydad AC to win its third [[CAF Champions League]] title, after beating defending champions [[Al Ahly SC|Al Ahly]] in the [[2022 CAF Champions League Final|final]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=El Moutaraji double delivers third TotalEnergies CAF Champions League title to Wydad |url=https://www.cafonline.com/total-caf-champions-league/news/el-moutaraji-double-delivers-third-totalenergies-caf-champions-league-title-to-w |access-date=13 June 2022 |website=CAFOnline.com}}</ref> He became only the second Moroccan manager to win the [[List of CAF club competition winning coaches|African Champions League]], after [[Hussein Ammouta]] with Wydad in [[2017 CAF Champions League Final|2017]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=الركراكي ثاني مدرب مغربي يتوج بلقب دوري أبطال أفريقيا |url=https://www.elbotola.com/article/2022-05-30-21-23-483.html |access-date=13 June 2022 |website=elbotola.com |language=ar}}</ref> In December 2022, Regragui was nominated for the 2022 [[IFFHS World's Best Club Coach]] for his performance in the year in review with Wydad before becoming head coach of the Moroccan national team.<ref>{{Cite web |date=24 December 2022 |title=IFFHS MEN'S WORLD BEST CLUB COACH 2022 - TOP 15 |url=https://iffhs.com/en/news/iffhs-awards-2022-the-candidates-2429 |access-date=12 January 2023 |website=IFFHS}}</ref> He was subsequently adjudged the third best behind [[Carlo Ancelotti]] and [[Pep Guardiola]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=9 January 2023 |title=IFFHS AWARDS 2022 - MEN'S WORLD BEST CLUB COACH |url=https://iffhs.com/en/news/iffhs-awards-2022-mens-world-best-club-coach-2461 |access-date=9 January 2023 |website=IFFHS}}</ref>

=== Return to Morocco ===
On 31 August 2022, Regragui was appointed as the new head coach for the [[Morocco national football team|Morocco national team]] after the dismissal of former head coach [[Vahid Halilhodžić]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=31 August 2022 |title=Walid Regragui confirmed as new Atlas Lions coach |url=https://en.hespress.com/48484-walid-regragui-confirmed-as-new-officially-atlas-lions-trainer.html |access-date=21 September 2022 |website=HESPRESS English – Morocco News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=1 September 2022 |title=Morocco appoint Walid Regragui as head coach |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/morocco-mar/story/4735154/morocco-appoint-walid-regragui-as-head-coach |access-date=21 September 2022 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref> On 21 September 2022, Regragui coached his first friendly game, which ended in a 1–0 victory against [[Madagascar national football team|Madagascar]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=21 September 2022 |title=الركراكي يحقق أول فوز مع منتخب المغرب |url=https://www.hespress.com/الركراكي-يحقق-أول-فوز-مع-منتخب-المغرب-1051187.html |access-date=22 September 2022 |website=Hespress – هسبريس جريدة إلكترونية مغربية |language=ar}}</ref>

In the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]], he led Morocco to the [[2022 FIFA World Cup knockout stage|knockout stage]] for the first time since 1986,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thenationalnews.com/fifa-world-cup-2022/2022/12/01/morocco-cruise-past-canada-to-make-world-cup-last-16-for-first-time-since-1986/ |title=Morocco cruise past Canada to make World Cup last 16 for first time since 1986 |website=The National News |date=1 December 2022}}</ref> and to the quarter finals after beating [[Spain national football team|Spain]] on penalties in the round of 16,<ref>{{cite news |title=Morocco beat Spain in penalties to reach Quarter finals |url=https://www.africanews.com/2022/12/06/world-cup-morocco-beat-spain-in-penalties-to-reach-quarter-finals/ |access-date=6 December 2022 |website=Africa News |date=6 December 2022}}</ref> making Morocco the fourth African nation and the first Arab nation to qualify for this stage in a World Cup competition.<ref>{{cite news |title=World Cup 2022: Morocco heads to quarter finals, eliminating Spain on penalties |url=https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/world-cup-morocco-qualifies-quarter-finals-after-eliminating-spain |access-date=6 December 2022 |work=Middle East Eye |date=6 December 2022}}</ref><ref name="Reuters 2022">{{Cite news |last=Amir |first=Shady |date=December 7, 2022 |title=Mr Avocado Head has Morocco daring to dream |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/mr-avocado-head-has-morocco-daring-dream-2022-12-07/ |access-date=December 10, 2022}}</ref> Regragui himself is the first African manager, and first Arab manager to reach this stage. Morocco would later beat favourite<ref>{{Cite web |title=Morocco vs Portugal - Betting Odds |url=http://www.oddschecker.com/football/world-cup/morocco-v-portugal/winner |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221210011057/https://www.oddschecker.com/football/world-cup/morocco-v-portugal/winner |archive-date=10 December 2022 |access-date=11 December 2022 |website=[[Oddschecker]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Khalil |first=Shaimaa |date=11 December 2022 |title=World Cup 2022: 'We witnessed history as Morocco won' |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-63930050 |access-date=14 December 2022 |website=[[BBC News]]}}</ref> [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]] 1–0 and move on to the semi-finals,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Morocco 1–0 Portugal |url=https://www.fifa.com/fifaplus/en/match-centre/match/17/255711/285074/400128140?competitionEntryId=17 |access-date=10 December 2022 '''Laurent Noël Bonnart''' (born 25 December 1979) is a French former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|full-back]].

==Career==
Born in [[Chambray-lès-Tours]], Indre-et-Loire,<ref name="Lequipe"/> Bonnart began his career with [[Le Mans UC72]], he became a regular in the team from the start of the 2001–02 season, having made his debut in [[Ligue 2]] in the season's first match.{{citation needed|date=April 2025}}

In 2007, he moved from [[Le Mans UC72|Le Mans]] to [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]].{{citation needed|date=April 2025}}

In 2010, he moved to [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] on a free transfer.{{citation needed|date=April 2025}}

'''Matuzalém Francelino da Silva''' (born 10 June 1980), commonly known as just '''Matuzalém''', is a Brazilian [[association football|football]] manager and former player, who played as a [[midfielder]]. ==Club career== ===Early career=== Matuzalém began his career at [[Salvador, Bahia|Salvador]]-based [[Esporte Clube Vitória|Vitória]] and quickly established his place in lower level of the [[Brazil national football team|Brazil national team]]. Described as a "goalscoring midfielder" by [[Eurosport]], he first emerged in the [[1997 FIFA World Youth Championship]] in Egypt. There, he scored three goals in six games, including a critical goal in the final match. ===Napoli=== In 1999, Matuzalém left Vitória to join [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]] in Italy, via [[Parma AC|Parma]], in a temporary deal,{{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/1999/giugno/17/Napoli_via_all_operazione_rilancio_ga_0_9906175520.shtml|title=Napoli: via all' operazione rilancio La difesa e' a posto, arriva Robbiati|date=17 June 1999|access-date=5 May 2010|work=La Gazzetta dello Sport|last=Malfitano|first=Mimmo|language=it}} where he remained for two seasons, the first was spent in [[Serie B]] – during which he helped the team win promotion to the Italian top flight – and the second season in [[Serie A]], in what would be Napoli's last in season in the Italian top flight for six years. The club signed Matuzalém in a [[co-ownership (football)|co-ownership deal]] for 5 billion [[Italian lira|lire]] in the summer of 2000.Parma AC SpA Report and Accounts on 30 June 2001 {{in lang|it}} Matuzalém was a regular starter at Napoli, but only scored twice in 52 appearances during his tenure in [[Naples]]. ===Piacenza and Brescia=== Following his Napoli spell, Matuzalém was bought back by Parma, subsequently reselling half of his rights to [[Piacenza Calcio|Piacenza]] in another [[co-ownership (football)|co-ownership]] deal in the summer of 2001, for 6 billion [[Italian lira|Lire]] (€3,098,741).Parma AC SpA Report and Accounts on 30 June 2002 {{in lang|it}}){{cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2002/maggio/20/Liverpool_caccia_Rui_Costa_ga_0_0205206421.shtml|title=Liverpool a caccia di Rui Costa|date=20 May 2002|access-date=1 September 2009|publisher=La Gazzetta dello Sport|language=it}} Matuzalém stayed at Piacenza alongside [[Amauri]], [[Nicola Mora]] and [[Matteo Guardalben]], all of which were also partly owned by Parma. With Piacenza during [[2001–02 Serie A|2001–02 season]], the team finished 14th in the league. In the opening round of the season, Matuzalém became the first foreigner to score for Piacenza in Serie A. In June 2002, Parma reacquired all of his rights again.{{Cite web|url=http://www.lega-calcio.it/ita/partecipazioni2002.pdf|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20071118213039/http://www.lega-calcio.it/ita/partecipazioni2002.pdf|archive-date = 18 November 2007|title = Home Page | Lega Serie A}} The second season of the loan spell saw Matuzalém switch to [[Brescia Calcio|Brescia]] on loan, where he had the opportunity to play alongside [[Roberto Baggio]]. He played nearly every match and the deal was made permanent at the end of the season. However, he only lasted one more year at the club, before [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] giants [[FC Shakhtar Donetsk|Shakhtar Donetsk]] signed him in 2004. ===Shakhtar Donetsk=== In June 2004, Shakhtar Donetsk signed Matuzalém from Brescia, paying Brescia €8,000,000, Matuzalém's agents €3,750,000 and €221,092 to Matuzalém's former clubs as [[Solidarity Contribution (football)|solidarity contribution]].{{cite news|url=http://www.tas-cas.org/d2wfiles/document/3229/5048/0/Award%201519-1520%20_internet_.pdf|title=CAS 2008/A/1519 – FC Shakhtar Donetsk (Ukraine) v/ Mr. Matuzalem Francelino da Silva (Brazil) & Real Zaragoza SAD (Spain) & FIFA
CAS 2008/A/1520 – Mr. Matuzalem Francelino da Silva (Brazil) & Real Zaragoza SAD (Spain) v/ FC Shakhtar Donetsk (Ukraine) & FIFA|date=19 May 2009|access-date=6 November 2009|publisher=Court of Arbitration for Sport|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090715045223/http://www.tas-cas.org/d2wfiles/document/3229/5048/0/Award%201519-1520%20_internet_.pdf|archive-date=15 July 2009}} It was a Ukrainian record at the time. After the transfer of [[Anatoliy Tymoschuk]] to [[FC Zenit St. Petersburg|Zenit Saint Petersburg]], he became the new [[Captain (association football)|captain]] of the club for the 2006–07 season and was voted the club's Player of the Year. During his three seasons with the club, he won two league titles and scored 25 goals in 68 appearances. On 1 July 2007, [[US Città di Palermo|Palermo]] made an offer of US$7,000,000 for Matuzalém, but it was rejected. ===Real Zaragoza and breach of contract saga=== On 2 July 2007, Matuzalém notified in writing Shakhtar of the fact that he unilaterally terminated their contractual relationship with immediate effect. On 5 July, Shakhtar replied Matuzalém and/or his new club should pay the sum in the release clause of €25 million, or Shakhtar would start legal action. The actual phrasing in the contract, however, stated that Shakhtar would be under an obligation to release him if the new club offered to pay that amount. It was not, strictly speaking, a penalty clause. On 18 July, however, he was presented as [[Real Zaragoza]]'s newest signing.{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/competitions/uefacup/news/kind=1/newsid=562072.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090416194809/http://www.uefa.com/competitions/uefacup/news/kind=1/newsid=562072.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 April 2009|title=Zaragoza get Pavón and Matuzalem|date=18 July 2007|access-date=21 February 2008|publisher=UEFA }} Shakhtar informed Zaragoza to request the club to pay the fee. After played four games and scoring once, Matuzalém was reported injured since September 2007{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/competitions/uefacup/news/kind=1/newsid=594172.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090416194814/http://www.uefa.com/competitions/uefacup/news/kind=1/newsid=594172.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 April 2009|title=Matuzalem signed off at Zaragoza|date=27 September 2007|access-date=21 February 2008|publisher=UEFA }} and returned in March 2008. During his only season with the club, he featured scarcely, due to a ligament injury he sustained in September 2007; in total, he obtained 14 appearances, scoring a single goal in La Liga. Zaragoza were relegated at the end of the season. Matuzalém's case was considered by FIFA Dispute Resolution Chamber (DRC) on 2 November 2007, which ruled Matuzalém and Zaragoza jointly and severally liable, ordering payment of €6,800,000 to Shakhtar.{{cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/mm/document/affederation/administration/117623_43278.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121107020431/http://www.fifa.com/mm/document/affederation/administration/117623_43278.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=7 November 2012|title=FIFA Dispute Resolution Chamber Decision (Labour Disputes 117623)|date=2 November 2007|access-date=6 November 2009|publisher=FIFA}} On 19 March 2008, however, Shakhtar appealed to the [[Court of Arbitration for Sport]] (CAS), as the club perceived the fee set by FIFA DRC as too low. On 20 March, Matuzalém and Zaragoza also made an appeal to CAS for the compensation. On 19 May 2009, the CAS ordered Matuzalém to pay €11,858,934 to Shakhtar for breach of contract.{{cite news|url=http://shakhtar.comn/en/news/9537|title=Shakhtar win "Matuzalem Case"|date=19 May 2009|access-date=9 May 2009|publisher=shakhtar.com}} {{dead link|date=January 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}{{cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/aboutfifa/federation/administration/news/newsid=1059709.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090523152705/http://www.fifa.com/aboutfifa/federation/administration/news/newsid=1059709.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=23 May 2009|title=FIFA takes note of Matuzalem decision|date=19 May 2009|access-date=20 May 2009|publisher=FIFA.com}} The decision was upheld by the [[Federal Supreme Court of Switzerland|Swiss Federal Tribunal]].Swiss Federal Tribunal 4A_320/2009 of 2 June 2010 Zaragoza also later paid €500,000 to Shakhtar on 1 September 2010. Neither Matuzalém or Zaragoza were able to pay the ordered compensation. For this reason, further sanctions, including banning Matuzalém from all football-related activities, were imposed by FIFA on 31 August 2010. This FIFA decision was appealed to the CAS but was rejected on 29 June 2011. The CAS decision was appealed to the Swiss Federal Tribunal. In its decision rendered on 27 March 2012, the Swiss Federal Tribunal annulled the CAS decision, as they found the ban on Matuzalém "a severe infringement of [his] right to privacy". The Tribunal also questioned whether the sanction was likely to lead to the payment of the compensation, which was the stated purpose of the ban. The compensation to be paid to Shakhtar was not affected by this case. This remains the only case where a CAS decision has been overturned based on the merits of the case.Roy Levy: [http://www.probst-law.ch/bilder/The-International-Sports-Law-Journal-2012.pdf Swiss Federal Tribunal overrules CAS award in a landmark decision: FIFA vs Matuzalem] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140325190508/http://www.probst-law.ch/bilder/The-International-Sports-Law-Journal-2012.pdf |date=25 March 2014 }} ===Lazio=== In July 2008, Matuzalém returned to Italy after four years, joining [[SS Lazio|Lazio]] on a season-long loan{{Cite web|url=http://www.corrieredellosport.it/Notizie/Calcio/36900/Ufficiale%2C+Matuzalem+alla+Lazio|title=Corriere dello Sport: Ufficiale – Matuzalem e' della Lazio|website=Corrieredellosport.it|access-date=11 December 2021}}{{Dead link|date=February 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} with an option to buy at the end of the season for €13 million (plus [[VAT]]). Injuries plagued his season, though when fit he established a place for himself in the centre of the Lazio midfield alongside [[Cristian Ledesma (footballer, born 1982)|Cristian Ledesma]]. He claimed some silverware as Lazio won their fifth [[Coppa Italia]], however a booking in the semi-final against [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] meant he missed the [[2009 Coppa Italia final|final]] victory against [[UC Sampdoria|Sampdoria]]. At the end of the season, Lazio exercised the option to keep him on a permanent basis, but for €5,310,000 on a five-year contract. In the [[2009 Supercoppa Italiana]], he scored the opening goal in an eventual 2–1 victory over [[Inter Milan|Inter]].{{cite web |url=https://www.football-italia.net/151905/matuzalem-addicted-mozzarella |title=Matuzalem: 'Addicted to mozzarella' |publisher=Football Italia |date=7 April 2020 |access-date=9 April 2020 }} On 14 March 2010, Matuzalém was injured{{cite news|url=http://www.sslazio.it/cms/view/home/news/archivio/elenco_news/infermeria/s152/c3553 |title=Infermeria |date=15 March 2010 |access-date=2 May 2010 |work=SS Lazio |language=it |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100323062101/http://www.sslazio.it/cms/view/home/news/archivio/elenco_news/infermeria/s152/c3553 |archive-date=23 March 2010 }} and missed the remainder of the season. He became a backup of Ledesma and [[Cristian Brocchi]] in next season. ===Genoa=== On 3 January 2013, Matuzalém was signed by [[Genoa CFC|Genoa]] on a temporary deal.{{cite news|url=http://www.sslazio.it/news/news/1-news/3541-comunicato.html|title=Comunicato|date=3 January 2013|access-date=14 March 2015|publisher=SS Lazio|language=it|archive-date=16 March 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150316124351/http://www.sslazio.it/news/news/1-news/3541-comunicato.html|url-status=dead}} On 24 August 2013 Matuzalém formally joined Genoa on free transfer{{cite web|url=http://www.sslazio.it/images/stories/documenti/pdf/investor_relator/Bilancio%20S.S.%20LAZIO%20SpA%2030-06-2014.pdf|title=Bilancio S.S. Risoluzione consensuale del contratto |work=La Gazzetta dello Sport |language=it |last1=De Pietro |first1=Alessandro |date=8 January 2016 |access-date=9 April 2020 }} ===Miami FC=== Matuzalém signed with [[Miami FC]] of the [[North American Soccer League (2011–2017)|North American Soccer League]] (NASL) on 20 January 2016.{{cite web|url=http://www.nasl.com/news/2016/01/20/serie-a-veteran-matuzalm-joins-miami-fc|title=Serie A Veteran MatuzalÃ©m Joins Miami FC|publisher=Nasl.com|date=20 January 2016|access-date=30 November 2017}} He was released on 12 May 2016.{{cite web|url=http://www.nasl.com/transactions|title=TRANSACTIONS|publisher=Nasl.com|access-date=30 November 2017}} ===Monterosi=== Following his spell in the United States, Matuzalém returned to Italy and was assigned by [[Nuova Monterosi]] in December 2016, a [[Serie D]] team based in Lazio, who were playing in group G at the time.{{cite web |url=http://www.monterosifc.com/monterosi-fc-benvenuto-francelino-matuzalem/ |title=Il Monterosi Fc dà il benvenuto a Francelino Matuzalem! |publisher=Monterosi FC |language=it |date=5 December 2015 |access-date=9 April 2020 }} He retired from professional football in June 2018 in order to pursue a coaching career.{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/it/notizie/viterbo-matuzalem-in-ospedale-ricoverato-in-stato/3i4dy6u0xzyj163h8j0hqclwx |title=Viterbo, Matuzalem in ospedale: ricoverato in stato confusionale |publisher=Goal.com |language=it |date=26 March 2019 |access-date=9 April 2020 }} On 27 September, he obtained his [[UEFA A Licence|UEFA A coaching licence]], which allows him to serve as a head coach of youth teams and [[Serie C]] teams, or as an assistant coach for Serie B and Serie A sides.{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/it/notizie/nuovi-allenatori-abilitati-ci-sono-pirlo-gilardino-e/1tu8gzr75cyuzz9estwkhffdw |title=Nuovi allenatori abilitati: ci sono Pirlo, Gilardino e Batistuta |publisher=Goal.com |language=it |date=27 September 2018 |access-date=9 April 2020 }} ==International career== Although he was never [[Cap (football)|capped]] for [[Brazil national football team|Brazil at senior level]], Matuzalém represented Brazil at youth level, playing alongside [[Ronaldinho]]. He was a member of the [[Brazil national under-17 football team|Brazil U17 team]] that won the [[1997 FIFA U-17 World Championship]] in Brazil, and also took part at the [[1999 FIFA World Youth Championship]] with the [[Brazil national under-20 football team|U20 side]]; in the former tournament, he played a key role in his team's success, scoring three goals in six games, including the decisive goal in the final victory.{{cite news |url=https://www.repubblica.it/speciale/2008/estate-del-calcio/scheda_giocatori/m.html |title=Gli Uomini – Mercato |work=La Repubblica |language=it |access-date=9 April 2020 }} ==Style of play== Described as a "classic [[playmaker]]" in the Italian media, Matuzalém is an energetic offensive–minded midfielder, known in particular for his passing, creativity, and technique, as well as his tactical intelligence, which earned him the nickname "The Professor". A diminutive and hard-working left–footed player, with a slender build and significant stamina, his usual position is that of a [[central midfielder]], although he is also capable of playing as an [[attacking midfielder]], due to his eye for goal from midfield, or as a [[winger (association football)|left–sided midfielder]]; he has also been deployed as a [[defensive midfielder]], a position in which he usually functioned as a [[deep-lying playmaker]]. Despite his ability, he also earned a reputation for being overly aggressive, due to his physical and tenacious playing style, and for lacking discipline on the pitch; during his time in Italy, he earned 11 red cards between Serie A and Serie B. He earned the name Matuzalém due to his maturity and precocious performances as a youngster.{{cite web |url=https://www.eurosport.co.uk/football/la-liga/2006-2007/zaragoza-sign-matuzalem_sto1250355/story.shtml |title=Zaragoza sign Matuzalem |publisher=Eurosport |date=18 July 2007 |access-date=20 March 2020 }}{{cite web|url=http://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/lazio/?action=read&idnet=bGFsYXppb3NpYW1vbm9pLml0LTE4NjQx|title="Doppio regista", Matuzalem prova a convincere Reja|publisher=TuttoMercatoWeb.com|language=it|access-date=14 January 2015}}{{cite web|url=http://www.storiapiacenza1919.it/rosa01.htm|title=Rosa Piacenza 2001-02|publisher=StoriaPiacenza1919.it|language=it|access-date=14 January 2015}}{{cite web|url=http://www.lalaziosiamonoi.it/esclusive/esclusiva-il-professor-matuzalem-sale-in-cattedra-lucescu-e-il-piu-forte-giocatore-che-ho-allenato-lo-shakhtar-la-fifa-intervenga-presto-ma-deve-pagar-14710|title=ESCLUSIVA - Il professor Matuzalem sale in cattedra, Lucescu: "E' il più forte giocatore che ho allenato... On 9 July 2016, he was loaned to [[Segunda División B]] side [[Real Unión]] for one year.{{cite web|url=https://www.realsociedad.eus/es/noticias/detalle/tena-y-gorosabel-cedidos-al-real-union|title=Tena y Gorosabel, cedidos al Real Unión|trans-title=Tena and Gorosabel, loaned to Real Unión|publisher=Real Sociedad|language=es|date=9 July 2016|accessdate=25 September 2017}} On 16 June 2017, Gorosabel renewed his Real Sociedad contract until 2019 and was promoted to [[Real Sociedad B|the reserves]], also competing in the third level.{{cite web|url=https://www.realsociedad.eus/es/noticias/detalle/renueva-con-la-real-5|title=Renueva con la Real|trans-title=Renews with Real|publisher=Real Sociedad|language=es|date=16 June 2017|accessdate=25 September 2017}} He made his first team – and [[La Liga]] – debut on 21 September, starting in a 3–0 away loss against [[Levante UD]].{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/2017/09/20/primera/1505937466_246319.html|title=Levante 3–0 Real Sociedad: Chema anota el gol de la jornada|trans-title=Levante 3–0 Real Sociedad: Chema scores the goal of the round|publisher=[[Diario AS]]|language=es|date=21 September 2017|accessdate=25 September 2017}} On 5 December 2017, Gorosabel renewed his contract until 2021,{{cite web|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/20171205/433441775468/la-real-sociedad-renueva-a-andoni-gorosabel-hasta-2021.html|title=La Real Sociedad renueva a Andoni Gorosabel hasta 2021|trans-title=Real Sociedad renew Andoni Gorosabel until 2021|publisher=Mundo Deportivo|language=es|date=5 December 2017|access-date=14 August 2018}} and spent the remainder of [[2017–18 La Liga|the campaign]] as a second-choice to [[Álvaro Odriozola]], overtaking longtime incumbent [[Carlos Martínez (footballer, born April 1986)|Carlos Martínez]]. web|url=https://real-sociedad.diariovasco.com/andoni-gorosabel-real-sociedad-20180716001109-ntvo.html|title=Gorosabel: "Soy lateral y lo primero es defender, aunque me gusta jugar al {{Medal|W|[[2000 AFC Asian Cup|2000 Lebanon]]|}} {{Medal|Competition|[[FIFA Confederations Cup]]}} {{Medal|RU|[[2001 FIFA Confederations Cup|2001 Korea/Japan]]|}} }} {{Nihongo|'''Shinji Ono'''|小野 伸二|Ono Shinji|born 27 September 1979}} is a Japanese former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[midfielder]]. He started his senior career with [[J1 League]] side Urawa Reds before moving Dutch side [[Feyenoord]] in 2001 where he won the [[UEFA Cup]] in 2002. He returned to Urawa Reds in 2006 where he won the [[2006 J.League Division 1|2006]] J League title in his first season back at the club and the [[2007 AFC Champions League|2007]] AFC Champions League in his second season. He moved to Bundesliga side Bochum in January 2008 but made limited appearances due to injuries. He signed for [[Shimizu S-Pulse]] in January 2010. He subsequently played for Western Sydney Wanderers, Hokkaido Consadole Sapporo and Ryukyu before retiring in 2023. He earned 56 caps for the Japan national team. He was part of the squads for the 1998, 2002 and 2006 World Cups. ==Career== ===Urawa Reds=== Ono grew up in the [[Shizuoka Prefecture]] and began his professional career with [[Urawa Reds]] in the [[J1 League]] in 1998. The same year, he became the youngest Japanese player to play at [[1998 FIFA World Cup|1998 World Cup]], at age 18.{{cite web |url=http://sofc.jp/captain/eng.html |title=About Shinji Captain |publisher=Ono Shinji Official Web Site |access-date=15 October 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121125020549/http://sofc.jp/captain/eng.html |archive-date=25 November 2012}} He caught the attention of foreign clubs with his performance at the [[1999 FIFA World Youth Championship|1999 World Youth Championship]] in Nigeria, where he captained the [[Japan national under-20 football team|Japanese Under-20]] side that reached the final. But later that year, he suffered a severe knee injury in a qualification match for the [[Football at the 2000 Summer Olympics|2000 Olympics]] with [[Japan national under-23 football team|Japan's Under-23 side]], forcing him to miss the rest of the season and Olympic qualifying.{{cite web |url=http://www.the-rising-sun-news.com/news/index.php/overseas-japanese/other-countries/shinji-ono |title=Shinji Ono |publisher=the-rising-sun-news.com |access-date=15 October 2012 }}{{Dead link|date=March 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} ===Feyenoord=== After a strong performance at the [[2001 FIFA Confederations Cup|2001 Confederations Cup]], Ono moved to [[Feyenoord]] of the Dutch [[Eredivisie]] in 2001. In his first season, he helped Feyenoord win the 2002 [[UEFA Cup]], making him the first Japanese in history to win a European trophy. However, a string of injuries kept him sidelined for long periods. After he missed the majority of 2004–05, the club sold him.{{cite web |url=http://thestar.com.my/sports/story.asp?file=/2006/1/15/sports/13119042&sec=sports |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130221175506/http://thestar.com.my/sports/story.asp?file=/2006/1/15/sports/13119042&sec=sports |url-status=dead |archive-date=21 February 2013 |title=Feyenoord midfielder Ono on his way home to join Urawa Reds |publisher=thestar.com.my |date=15 January 2006 |access-date=15 October 2012 }} His stint at the [[Rotterdam]] based club is highly rated and Dutch midfielder [[Wesley Sneijder]] said "Shinji Ono is the toughest opponent I've ever faced".{{cite web |url=http://netherlands.worldcupblog.org/world-cup-2010/wes-sneijder-analysis-of-world-class-player.html |title=Wes Sneijder: analysis of world class player |publisher=International Football News - World Cup Blog |date=31 October 2010 |access-date=18 February 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120714185657/http://netherlands.worldcupblog.org/world-cup-2010/wes-sneijder-analysis-of-world-class-player.html |archive-date=14 July 2012}} ===Urawa Reds return=== On 13 January 2006, Ono returned to the J1 League, signing a three-year deal with his former club [[Urawa Reds]].{{cite web |url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=352255&campaign=rss&source=soccernet&cc=3436 |title=Ono back to Japan from Feyenoord |publisher=ESPN Soccernet |date=15 December 2005 |access-date=15 October 2012 |archive-date=16 July 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120716181250/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/news/story?id=352255&campaign=rss&source=soccernet&cc=3436 |url-status=dead }} ===Bochum=== In the 2008 January transfer window, Ono returned to Europe, signing with [[Bundesliga]]'s [[VfL Bochum|Bochum]]. On 3 February 2008, Ono made his Bundesliga debut in an away game against [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]], and he had two assists that helped Bochum with their first ever win over Bremen at [[Weserstadion]]. Ono suffered injuries in the following two years in Bochum, and could only play 34 matches in which he gave four assists for the club. In the winter break of 2009–10, Ono requested a return to Japan for personal reasons. Different Japanese clubs were interested in the midfielder. Bochum allowed him to leave under the condition that they could find a successor.{{cite web | url = http://www.goal.com/de/news/968/transfermarkt/2010/01/08/1733144/exklusiv-wechsel-von-shinji-ono-h%C3%A4ngt-vom-nachfolger-ab | title = Exklusiv: Wechsel von Shinji Ono hängt vom Nachfolger ab | language = de | publisher = goal.com | date = 8 January 2010 | access-date = 15 October 2012}} ===Shimizu S-Pulse=== [[File:Shinji Ono Omiya Ardija vs Shimizu S-Pulse @ NACK5 Stadium.jpg|thumb|Shinji Ono playing for Shimizu S-Pulse in 2012.]] On 9 January 2010, Ono returned to his native [[Shizuoka Prefecture]] by signing for [[Shimizu S-Pulse]].{{cite web|url=http://www.s-pulse.co.jp/news/20100109-2078.html |title=Official press release |language=ja |publisher=s-pulse.co.jp |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100112094111/http://www.s-pulse.co.jp/news/20100109-2078.html |archive-date=12 January 2010 }} The transfer fee were rumored to be €300,000 for the midfielder whose contract in Bochum expired in the summer of 2010. In an interview he declared that the main reason for his transfer was his wish to reunite with his wife and children, who were still living in Japan.{{cite web | url = http://www.goal.com/de/news/1022/interview/2010/01/09/1734987/shinji-ono-im-exklusiven-abschiedsinterview-wegen-der | title = Shinji Ono im exklusiven Abschiedsinterview: Wegen der Familie zurück nach Japan | language = de | publisher = goal.com | date = 9 January 2010 | access-date = 15 October 2012}} ===Western Sydney Wanderers=== On 28 September 2012, it was announced that Shinji Ono had signed with new [[A-League]] club [[Western Sydney Wanderers FC|Western Sydney Wanderers]] on a two-year deal as the club's [[A-League#Marquee player|marquee player]]. The Wanderers were offered former German international [[Michael Ballack]]{{cite web|title=Western Sydney Wanderers chairman Lyall Gorman says club is considering options with Michael Ballack|url=http://www.foxsports.com.au/football/a-league/deal-to-bring-former-germany-captain-michael-ballack-to-western-sydney-wanderers-reportedly-imminent/story-e6frf4gl-1226478417827|website=Fox Sports Australia|access-date=17 June 2016}} but preferred to sign Ono.{{cite web |url=http://www.footballaustralia.com.au/news-display/wanderers-sign-shinji-ono/49461 |title=Wanderers sign Shinji Ono |publisher=footballaustralia.com.au |date=28 September 2012 |access-date=15 October 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121016234536/http://www.footballaustralia.com.au/news-display/wanderers-sign-shinji-ono/49461 |archive-date=16 October 2012}} He made his debut for the Wanderers on 6 October, in a scoreless draw against [[Central Coast Mariners]], in the first game of the season. Ono scored his first goal for the club with a penalty in round 10 against Brisbane Roar.{{cite web |url=http://localtoday.com.au/sport-news/49926-Ono-scores-as-Wanderers-beat-Roar-again.html |title=Ono off the mark as Wanderers beat Roar |publisher=Local Today |access-date=2 January 2013 }}{{Dead link|date=July 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} Ono scored two stunning goals to help the Wanderers beat Melbourne Victory 2–1 in round 14 on 1 January 2013.{{cite web|url=http://www.smh.com.au/sport/a-league/ono-aleague-double-lifts-wanderers-20130101-2c4cx.html |title=Ono A-League double lifts Wanderers |date=January 2013 |publisher=smh.com.au |access-date=2 January 2013}} On 16 January 2014, the club announced that Ono would return to Japan at the end of the A-League season. Ono will link up with [[J2 League]] club [[Hokkaido Consadole Sapporo|Consadole Sapporo]] to play out the remainder of the season in Japan as the club chases promotion to the J1 League. On 4 May 2014, Ono played his last A-League game for the Wanderers, in a 2–1 Grand Final loss to [[Brisbane Roar FC|Brisbane Roar]], in what was to be the Wanderers' second successive Grand Final defeat.{{cite web|url=http://www.smh.com.au/sport/soccer/soccer-match-report/brisbane-roars-extratime-victory-breaks-western-sydney-wanderers-hearts-20140504-zr46v.html | title=Brisbane Roar's extra-time victory breaks Western Sydney Wanderers' hearts | publisher=smh.com.au | date= 4 May 2014| access-date= 9 May 2014 | first =Dominic| last = Bossi}} ===Hokkaido Consadole Sapporo=== web|url=http://www.footballaustralia.com.au/news-display/Shinji-Ono-to-return-to-Japan-at-seasons-end/83310|title=Shinji Ono to return to Japan at season's end|publisher=[[Football Federation 2014}} ===FC Ryukyu=== On 5 August 2019, Ono signed with [[J2 League]] club [[FC Ryukyu]].{{cite web|url=http://fcryukyu.com/news/20343/|title=小野伸二 選手 FC琉球2019シーズン移籍加入のお知らせ|trans-title=Shinji Ono FC agreement.{{cite web|url=http://fcryukyu.com/news/26012/|title=小野伸二選手 退団のお知らせ|trans-title=Shinji Ono's departure notice|language=Japanese|publisher=[[FC Ryukyu]]|date=25 December 2020}} ===Return to Hokkaido Consadole Sapporo=== On 1 January 2021, it was announced that he would return to his former club, Hokkaido Consadole Sapporo, as a permanent transfer.{{cite web |url=https://www.consadole-sapporo.jp/news/2021/01/5690/|title=小野伸二選手 完全移籍加入のお知らせ|date=1 January 2021}} His uniform number is 44, the same as when he belonged to Sapporo last time. On 9 June of the same year, in the second round of the Emperor's Cup at Sony Sendai, he scored his first goal in an official match in four years with a direct free kick. This goal made him the oldest player to score in the Emperor's Cup (41 years and 255 days old). On 28 January 2022, it was announced that he had signed a lifetime contract with Hokkaido Consadole Sapporo.{{cite web |url=https://news.yahoo.co.jp/articles/62b92a2d80d3290fe00122721b34c95d6bce6b43|title=小野伸二、Ｊ１札幌と生涯契約…現役引退後も「経験を還元できたら」|work=Yahoo!ニュース |date=28 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220128190856/https://news.yahoo.co.jp/articles/62b92a2d80d3290fe00122721b34c95d6bce6b43 |archive-date=28 January 2022 }} Ono commented, "I consider Hokkaido to be my second home. I don't know how I will end my active career, but I hope to continue to give back to the club by sharing my experiences". In addition, Hokkaido Consadole Sapporo representative director and GM Daikatsu Mikami expressed his intention to prioritize Ono's wishes, saying, "I will let him decide whether he wants to be a coach or join the front desk". On 27 September 2023, the day he celebrated his 44th birthday, which is the same as his jersey number, he posted on his Instagram a message posted on the Hokkaido Consadole Sapporo official website:{{cite web |url=https://www.nikkansports.com/soccer/news/202309270000359.html|title=【札幌】「天才」小野伸二が引退発表「足がそろそろ休ませてくれ」44歳誕生日、Ｗ杯３大会連続|date=27 September 2023}}{{cite web |url=https://www.consadole-sapporo.jp/news/2023/09/9353/|title=小野伸二選手 現役引退のお知らせ|date=27 September 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230927110838/https://www.consadole-sapporo.jp/news/2023/09/9353/ |archive-date=27 September 2023 }} "I have a report to share with you all. 39th anniversary of my first encounter with soccer. My feet, which have been my companions for many years, are telling me it's time to give them a rest, so I've decided to end my career as a professional soccer player at the end of this season. There are still a few games left in the season. However, I will continue to prepare as well as possible so that I can be involved in the game as much as possible. I ask for your support until the end". Shinji Ono announced that he will retire as an active player after the 2023 season. On 3 December 2023, at the 2023 J1 league season final round, Ono played his last professional game against Urawa. He said goodbye to his colleague and every fan.{{cite web |url=https://www.soccerdigestweb.com/news/detail/id=143929|title=こんなに美しい場面があるだろうか――小野伸二、ラストダンスにファン感涙。浦和の選手たちも花道「何回見ても泣く」「やっぱり別格」|date=3 December 2023}} ==International career== When fit, Ono was an ever-present member of the [[Japan national football team|Japan national team]]. He made his full international debut on 1 April 1998 against [[South Korea national football team|South Korea]] in a friendly. After his appearance in the 1998 World Cup, he was a key member of the Japanese squad in the [[2002 FIFA World Cup]]. He has represented Japan at every age level starting with the U-16 team, and was one of three overage selections at the [[Football at the 2004 Summer Olympics|2004 Olympics]] in Athens. Injuries limited Ono to just one appearance in the final round of the [[2006 FIFA World Cup (qualification AFC)|qualification]] for the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]] and missed the Confederations Cup in 2003 and 2005. '''Pablo Andrés Contreras Fica''' ({{IPA|es|ˈpaβlo konˈtɾeɾas}}; born 11 September 1978) is a Chilean retired [[Association football|footballer]], who played as a [[centre back]] or even as a [[right back]].

Contreras began his career at [[Colo-Colo]]. He earned his first senior honours in 1997, winning the [[Chilean Primera División]] title. He also won an [[Chile at the 2000 Summer Olympics|Olympic bronze medal]] with [[Chile national football team|Chile]] in the [[2000 Summer Olympics|Sydney Games]]. Contreras moved to Europe in 1999, signing with French side [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]], where he won the [[Ligue 1]] in his first season.

After his spell in France, he was loaned to [[Argentine Primera División]] club [[Racing Club de Avellaneda|Racing Club]] in 2001, and the next season Contreras joined Spain's [[La Liga]] side [[Celta de Vigo]] in a €4.2 million transfer deal. He was immediately loaned to [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]] and then to [[Sporting Clube de Portugal|Sporting CP]], playing in the [[UEFA Champions League]], before returning after to Celta. He played over 100 matches with the [[Galicia (Spain)|Galician]] club until the [[2006–07 La Liga|2006–07 season]], after Celta's relegation to the [[Spanish Second Division|Segunda División]], after which he decided to leave the club. He signed a six-month contract with [[S.C. Braga|Braga]] in January 2008 before moving in June of that year to [[Super League Greece]] side [[PAOK FC|PAOK]]. In the middle of the [[2011–12 Super League Greece|2011–12 season]], Conteras left the club due to the [[Greek government-debt crisis|Greek government debt-crisis]] and opted to return to Colo-Colo, coached by [[Ivo Basay]] at the time.

A Chilean international on 66 occasions, Contreras was part of squad that earned the [[Olympic medal|bronze medal]] in the [[2000 Summer Olympics]] at [[Sydney]]. In his country, Pablo is nicknamed [[Esparta]]co by [[Chilevisión]] relator Paulo Flores specifically, referred him as the [[Sparta, Greece|Spartan]] hero of his national team during the matches, when Contreras was under the orders of [[Claudio Borghi (football manager)|Claudio Borghi]] in Chile.

==Club career==

===Colo-Colo===
Born in [[Santiago]], Contreras made his way through [[Colo-Colo]]'s youth ranks, alongside fellow stopper [[David Henríquez (footballer, born 1977)|David Henríquez]], as the club was then managed by former international – also a defender – [[Pedro Reyes (footballer)|Pedro Reyes]]. He made his professional debuts in 1997, helping the club to two [[Chilean Primera División|first division]] titles and appearing in 37 first-team matches in the next two seasons.

===Monaco===
Afterwards, Contreras made a move to [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] of France. At the young age of 21, he was an important element in Monaco's [[1999–2000 Division 1|league]] and [[Trophée des champions|Supercup]] victories of 2000. He also appeared for the club in both the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]] and [[UEFA Champions League]].

In January 2001, however, it was discovered that Contreras was using a fake Italian passport in order to gain European Union status. A [[Paris]] court fined the player [[Euro|€]]30,000, and he received a two-year ban.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/europe/1260808.stm |title=French Court bans South American footballers |publisher=BBC News |date=4 April 2001 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/newsid=1524.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121023105729/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/newsid=1524.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=23 October 2012 |title=Celta land banned Contreras |publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=24 August 2012 }}</ref>

Monaco was then forced to loan Contreras out to another team, and he moved to Argentina with [[Racing Club de Avellaneda|Racing Club]]. Shortly after, in July 2001, he was sold to [[Celta de Vigo]] for €4.2 million.

===Osasuna===
[[File:Pablo Contreras 001 037.jpg|thumb|right|212px|Pablo Contreras in 2010.]]
Contreras did not join Celta immediately, being loaned to fellow [[La Liga]] side [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]]. Immediately cast into the [[Navarre]]se's starting XI, he made 31 league appearances, but the club could only [[2001–02 La Liga|finish 17th]], narrowly avoiding relegation.

===Sporting CP===
For the following season, another loan ensued, now to Portugal with giants [[Sporting Clube de Portugal|Sporting CP]], where he once again started throughout [[2002–03 Primeira Liga|the season]], with the ''Lions'' winning no silverware at all; they were also eliminated in the [[2002–03 UEFA Champions League|Champions League qualifying rounds]] by [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]].

===Celta===
In the summer of 2003, 25-year old Contreras finally moved to Celta. He appeared rarely in [[2003–04 La Liga|his debut season]], as the [[Galicia (Spain)|Galicians]] were participating for the first time ever in the [[2003–04 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]]. He appeared in seven games as Celta eventually lost in the [[round of 16]] to [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], but also saw his team relegate to [[Segunda División]], after a 19th-place finish in the league. Contreras became first-choice for Celta in the following seasons but, after another relegation, in [[2006–07 La Liga|2006–07]], was deemed surplus to requirements by the coaching staff ([[Bulgaria]]n [[Hristo Stoichkov]] was one of four during the [[2007–08 Segunda División|unsuccessful campaign]] in division two), and left the club in January 2008, after being released from his contract.

===Braga===
Contreras returned to Portugal after four years, joining [[S.C. Braga|Braga]] on a six-month contract,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/01c9-0e6eecbc3e82-e9c2dabcee5a-1000--braga-seal-deal-for-contreras/ |title=Braga seal deal for Contreras |publisher=[[UEFA]] |date=16 January 2008 }}</ref> and was regularly used during his spell, helping his team [[2007–08 Primeira Liga|finish seventh]].

===PAOK===
[[File:Pablocontreras.JPG|thumb|right|250px|Pablo Contreras playing for [[PAOK FC|PAOK]] in 2010.]]
In June 2008, Contreras agreed to a two-year link with Greek club [[PAOK FC|PAOK]], citing his trust in former Celta teammate [[Zisis Vryzas]] – and the club's chairman [[Theodoros Zagorakis]] – as the main factors for his move,<ref>[https://peloteroschilenosenelmundo.blogspot.com/2009/12/paok-de-pablo-contreras-vence-ergotelis.html PAOK con Pablo Contreras presente vence a Ergotelis (PAOK defeats Ergotelis with Pablo Contreras in lineup)]; Peloteros Chilenos en el Mundo, 20 December 2009 {{in lang|es}}</ref> refusing also the opportunity of return to Colo-Colo, because the club offered him a very high salary.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cooperativa.cl/noticias/deportes/futbol/colo-colo/pablo-contreras-se-debate-entre-colo-colo-y-oferta-desde-grecia/2008-06-12/150136.html|title=Pablo Contreras se debate entre Colo Colo y oferta desde Grecia|website=Cooperativa.cl|accessdate=23 December 2022}}</ref> He made his official debut for the team on 30 August in a 2–0 away win over [[OFI Crete F.C.|OFI]] and his first goal came in an important 1–0 home victory in the [[Aris and PAOK rivalry|derby]] against [[Aris Thessaloniki F.C.|Aris]]. On 24 December, was reported that Contreras would join Italian [[Serie A]] club [[Reggina Calcio|Reggina]] during [[New Year's Eve]], though the move never materialized.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cooperativa.cl/noticias/deportes/futbol/chilenos-en-el-exterior/prensa-italiana-asegura-que-pablo-contreras-sera-nuevo-jugador-de-reggina/2008-12-24/121432.html|title=Prensa italiana asegura que Pablo Contreras será nuevo jugador de Reggina|website=Cooperativa.cl|accessdate=23 December 2022}}</ref> On 21 February, he scored his second official goal for PAOK against another traditional derby of the club, [[Iraklis F.C. (Thessaloniki)|Iraklis]], that PAOK won thanks to him. He was promoted to [[Captain (association football)|team captain]] in [[2009–10 Super League Greece|his second season]], alongside [[Sérgio Conceição]], who retired shortly after.<ref>[http://www.paok24.com/interviewsitem.asp?s=12&id=55 Πάμπλο Κοντρέρας : Η συνέντευξη]; PAOK 24, 18 January 2011 {{in lang|el}}</ref>

In late January 2011, shortly before a match against Aris, he was informed of the loss of his father, but opted to leave for his country only after the game.<ref>[http://www.contra.gr/Soccer/Hellas/Superleague/PAOK/307680.html Αναχωρεί για Χιλή ο Κοντρέρας, χάνει τον Ολυμπιακό]; Contra, 30 January 2011 {{in lang|el}}</ref> On 2 January 2012, Contreras mutually terminated his contract with PAOK.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www2.paok24.com/newsitem.asp?s=12&id=14889&t=1|script-title=el:Συμφωνία με Κοντρέρας για τη λύση|publisher=PAOK 24|language=el|date=2 January 2012|access-date=2 January 2012|archive-date=8 January 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120108035030/http://www2.paok24.com/newsitem.asp?s=12&id=14889&t=1|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Return to Colo-Colo===
On 7 January 2012, it was confirmed that Contreras was returning to [[Chilean Primera División|Chilean]] club Colo-Colo,<ref>{{cite news |url= http://www.emol.com/noticias/deportes/2012/01/07/520547/pablo-contreras-ya-arribo-a-chile-para-comenzar-los-trabajos-con-colo-colo.html |title= Pablo Contreras ya arribo a Chile para comenzar trabajos con Colo-Colo | work = Emol.com | publisher = Emol |date= 7 January 2012}}</ref> after several rumours of a possible move to [[Argentine Primera División|Argentina]]'s [[Club Atlético Colón|Colón]] and also other European and American clubs. On 19 January, he made his unofficial debut in an [[exhibition match]] against [[Unión Temuco]], where he played very well despite a 2–1 defeat.<ref>{{cite news |url= http://latercera.com/noticia/deportes/2012/01/656-425590-9-union-temuco-sorprendio-a-colo-colo-y-lo-elimino-de-cuadrangular-amistoso.shtml |title= Unión Temuco sorprendió a Colo Colo y lo eliminó de cuadrangular amistoso |publisher= [[La Tercera|La Tercera.cl]] |date= 19 January 2012 |archive-date= 28 April 2016 |access-date= 3 May 2012 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160428140406/http://www.latercera.com/noticia/deportes/2012/01/656-425590-9-union-temuco-sorprendio-a-colo-colo-y-lo-elimino-de-cuadrangular-amistoso.shtml |url-status= dead }}</ref> After the pre-season in [[Temuco, Chile|Temuco]], Contreras played well for his team, now in the [[Colo-Colo|Noche Alba]] against Peruvian side [[Alianza Lima]] at the [[Estadio Monumental David Arellano|Estadio Monumental]].<ref>{{cite news |url= http://www.elmostrador.cl/noticias/pais/2012/01/25/colo-colo-se-rehabilita-con-victoria-2-0-sobre-alianza-lima-en-la-noche-alba-2012/ |title= Fútbol: Colo Colo se rehabilita con victoria 2-0 sobre Alianza Lima en la 'Noche Alba 2012' | publisher = [[Terra Chile]] | date = 24 January 2012}}</ref> On 29 January, Contreras played his first competitive match of the season against [[Deportes Iquique]] in a 0–0 home draw, thus being his first competitive match for Colo-Colo since his return.<ref>{{cite news | url = http://www.colocolo.cl/2012/01/colo-colo-empato-con-iquique-en-opaco-partido/ | title = Colo Colo empató con Iquique en opaco partido | publisher = [[Colo-Colo|Colo-colo.cl]] | date = 29 January 2012}}</ref> He instantly became an irreplaceable player for coach [[Ivo Basay]], helping the team win important games during his tenure, for example against [[Cobreloa]] at [[Calama, Chile|Calama]] and [[O'Higgins F.C.|O'Higgins]] in the capital, thus becoming a mainstay [[centre back]] for Basay's team. On 14 April, his assist to [[Rodrigo Millar]] for the first goal in the derby against [[CDUC|Universidad Católica]], salvaged a 1–1 draw at the [[Estadio Monumental David Arellano|Estadio Monumental]] for the first match under new head coach [[Luis Pérez Muñoz|Luis Pérez]] after Basay's departure, who abandoned the club after a 4–2 away loss against [[Unión Española]]. After [[Esteban Paredes]] moved to [[Atlante F.C.|Atlante]], Pablo became Colo-Colo's captain due to his experience and tenure.

===Olympiacos===
On 16 August 2012, Contreras returned to Greece, signing a contract with [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]]. On 27 August, he made his debut with in an away win against [[Veria F.C.|Veria]]. On 27 January, he scored the only goal in a 1–0 away win against [[Panthrakikos F.C.|Panthrakikos]].

===Melbourne Victory===
On 22 September 2013, it was confirmed Contreras signed for Australian club [[Melbourne Victory FC|Melbourne Victory]]. Contreras made his debut in Round 1 against [[Melbourne City FC|Melbourne Heart]], playing the full 90 minutes.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.footballaustralia.com.au/news-display/Victory-gets-its-marquee-man/75478|title=Victory gets its marquee man|publisher=[[Football Federation Australia]]|date=22 September 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130927030102/http://www.footballaustralia.com.au/news-display/Victory-gets-its-marquee-man/75478|archive-date=27 September 2013}}</ref> He was, however, suspended after the match for two games due to an off-the-ball incident where he blocked an opponent in the derby match.

In January 2014, Contreras announced on Chilean radio that he would retire at the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.smh.com.au/sport/soccer/melbourne-victorys-chilean-international-pablo-contreras-to-retire-at-the-end-of-the-season-20140125-31foz.html|title = Melbourne Victory's Chilean international Pablo Contreras to retire at the end of the season|date = 25 January 2014}}</ref> Strong performances near the end of the season, however, prompted speculation that Contreras might play on with the Victory for the 2014–15 season, albeit on reduced wages. Shortly after Melbourne Victory's semi-loss against eventual [[A-League]] champions [[Brisbane Roar FC|Brisbane Roar]], however, he confirmed his retirement.<ref>[http://www.heraldsun.com.au/sport/football/chilean-defender-pablo-contreras-retires-jimmy-jeggo-leaves-victory-to-join-adelaide/story-fnk6pqhd-1226902473748 Chilean Defender Pablo Contreras Retires Jimmy Jeggo Leaves Victory To Join Adelaide]''Herald Sun'' {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140505095712/http://www.heraldsun.com.au/sport/football/chilean-defender-pablo-contreras-retires-jimmy-jeggo-leaves-victory-to-join-adelaide/story-fnk6pqhd-1226902473748 |date=5 May 2014 }}</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Pablo Contreras 2011.jpg|thumb|100px|Contreras playing for [[Chile national football team|Chile]] in 2011.]]
As a youth player, Contreras represented Chile at under-17 level in the {{ill|lt=1995 South American Championship|1995 South American U-17 Championship|es|Campeonato Sudamericano Sub-17 de 1995|vertical-align=sup}}<ref>{{cite web |title=Nóminas de Chile para Campeonatos Sudamericanos Sub-17 |url=https://www.partidosdelaroja.com/1970/01/nominas-de-chile-para-sudamericanos-sub17.html |website=Partidos de La Roja |access-date=30 September 2022 |language=es}}</ref> and at under-20 level in the [[1997 South American U-20 Championship|1997 South American Championship]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Nóminas de Chile para Campeonatos Sudamericanos Sub-20 |url=https://www.partidosdelaroja.com/1970/01/nominas-de-chile-para-sudamericanos-sub20.html |website=Partidos de La Roja |access-date=30 September 2022 |language=es}}</ref>

Contreras made his debut for [[Chile national football team|Chile]] team on 17 February 1999 against [[Guatemala national football team|Guatemala]]. He was then picked for [[1999 Copa América|that year]]'s [[Copa América]] in [[Paraguay]], helping the national side finish in fourth position.

In 2000, Contreras participated at the [[Football at the 2000 Summer Olympics|2000 Summer Olympics]], where Chile won the [[bronze medal]], and the player was named one of the best defenders in the tournament. He also featured prominently in qualification for the [[2002 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)|2002]] and [[2006 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)|2006]] [[FIFA World Cup]], with Chile failing to make the final stages on both occasions.

One of the darkest moments in Contreras' career happened during the [[2007 Copa América]]. Alongside [[Reinaldo Navia]], [[Jorge Valdivia]], [[Rodrigo Tello]], [[Jorge Francisco Vargas|Jorge Vargas]] and [[Álvaro Ormeño]], he was involved in an incident at the team's hotel involving the staff. The employees claimed the team players were celebrating drunk, throwing food, and destroying hotel property after qualifying for the second round of the tournament – Chile lost the next game 6–1 against [[Brazil national football team|Brazil]].

Afterwards, national coach [[Nelson Acosta]] resigned and all the players involved were suspended for 20 games by the [[Federación de Fútbol de Chile|ANFP]]. After serving ten games, Contreras, as well as the other players involved – with the exception of Ormeño – signed a letter admitting their involvement and apologizing for the incident, and the punishment was lifted. After being reinstated, Contreras became an important member under [[Marcelo Bielsa]], as Chile [[2010 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)|qualified]] for [[2010 FIFA World Cup|the World Cup]] in [[South Africa]], the nation's first in 12 years. Contreras became the second-captain, after goalkeeper [[Claudio Bravo]], when the team was managed by [[Claudio Borghi (football manager)|Claudio Borghi]].

'''Emerson da Conceição''' (born 23 February 1986), known as '''Emerson''', is a Brazilian former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|left back]].

==Club career==

===Lille===
In January 2007, aged only 20, [[São Paulo]]-born Emerson left his country and moved to [[Lille OSC]] in France. He appeared in only two [[Ligue 1]] games in [[2006–07 Ligue 1|his first season]], his debut coming on 8 April in a 1–4 away loss against [[Olympique de Marseille]].

Emerson became first-choice from the [[2008–09 Ligue 1|2008–09 campaign]] onwards, and contributed with 20 league matches in [[2010–11 Ligue 1|2010–11]] as ''[[Mastiff|Les Dogues]]'' won their first national championship in 57 years. He also helped the team [[2010–11 Coupe de France|win]] the [[Coupe de France]], but remained [[Substitute (association football)|on the bench]] during [[2011 Coupe de France Final|the final]] against [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain FC]].

===Benfica===
In late July 2011, Emerson signed for Portuguese club [[S.L. Benfica]], for an undisclosed fee.<ref>[http://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/2557/news/2011/07/21/2583879/benfica-formally-unveil-eduardo-emerson-ezequiel-garay Benfica formally unveil Eduardo, Emerson & Ezequiel Garay]; Goal.com, 21 July 2011</ref> In [[2011–12 Primeira Liga|his first and only season]], he beat competition from [[FIFA World Cup|World]] and [[UEFA European Championship|European]] champion [[Joan Capdevila]].

===Trabzonspor===
On 3 September 2012, Emerson joined [[Trabzonspor]] in Turkey for €1.6 million.<ref>[http://www.turkish-football.com/news_read.php?id=3463 Trabzonspor sign Brazilian Benfica left back Emerson Da Conceiçao]; Turkish Football, 3 September 2012</ref> One year later he signed for [[Stade Rennais F.C.]] in the French top flight, returning to his homeland in 2014 with [[Clube Atlético Mineiro]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.otempo.com.br/blogs/esportes-19.235882/atl%C3%A9tico-acerta-com-lateral-esquerdo-e-espera-apenas-a-libera%C3%A7%C3%A3o-do-rennes-19.236488|title=Atlético acerta com lateral-esquerdo e espera apenas a liberação do Rennes|trans-title=Atlético agrees with left-back and awaits only for Rennes release|publisher=O Tempo|language=Portuguese|date=24 February 2014|accessdate=18 July 2014|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140726160806/http://www.otempo.com.br/blogs/esportes-19.235882/atl%C3%A9tico-acerta-com-lateral-esquerdo-e-espera-apenas-a-libera%C3%A7%C3%A3o-do-rennes-19.236488|archivedate=26 July 2014}}</ref>

'''Pablo Orbaiz Lesaka''' (born 6 February 1979) is a Spanish former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[defensive midfielder]].

After starting out at [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]], he went on to play 11 years in [[La Liga]] with [[Athletic Bilbao]],<ref name=Dream>{{cite news|url=http://www.deia.com/2011/09/01/athletic/jugar-la-champions-es-un-sueno-para-mi|title=Orbaiz: "Jugar la Champions es un sueño para mí"|trans-title=Orbaiz: "To play in the Champions League is a dream for me"|newspaper=[[Deia (newspaper)|Deia]]|first=Marta|last=Hernández|language=Spanish|date=1 September 2011|accessdate=10 October 2011|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://archive.today/20120723210807/http://www.deia.com/2011/09/01/athletic/jugar-la-champions-es-un-sueno-para-mi|archivedate=23 July 2012}}</ref> appearing in 318 competitive matches and scoring 13 goals.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elcorreo.com/athletic/noticias/201603/06/orbaiz-para-trabajar-athletic-20160306112523.html|title=Orbaiz: «Para trabajar en el Athletic hay que estar preparado»|trans-title=Orbaiz: "To work at Athletic one has to be ready"|newspaper=[[El Correo]]|first=Robert|last=Basic|language=Spanish|date=6 March 2016|accessdate=29 April 2025}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Osasuna and Athletic===
Born in [[Pamplona]], Orbaiz began his career at his hometown club [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]],<ref name=Like/> exclusively playing in the [[Segunda División]] with the team. He contributed 29 appearances and one goal in his final season, [[1999–2000 Segunda División|1999–2000]], as the [[Navarre]]se returned to [[La Liga]] after a six-year absence.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cope.es/emisoras/navarra/navarra-provincia/pamplona/noticias/lotina-cruchaga-orbiaz-trzeciak-mateo-alfredo-reviven-ascenso-del-ano-2000-20200604_751841|title=Lotina, Cruchaga, Orbaiz, Trzeciak, Mateo y Alfredo reviven el ascenso del año 2000|trans-title=Lotina, Cruchaga, Orbaiz, Trzeciak, Mateo and Alfredo relive promotion of the year 2000|publisher=[[Cadena COPE]]|first=Alberto|last=Sanz|language=Spanish|date=4 June 2020|accessdate=29 April 2025}}</ref>

In the summer of 2000, Orbaiz signed for neighbours [[Athletic Bilbao]]; the transfer was originally agreed in 1999, but the clubs then agreed that he would stay for an extra season in exchange for a loan move for [[Tiko (footballer)|Tiko]] in the same direction.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2002/01/14/liga/1010998159.html |title=La sensación se llama Tiko|trans-title=The sensation is called Tiko|newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]|first=Jon|last=Rivas|language=Spanish|date=14 January 2002|accessdate=20 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/20140806/athletic-bilbao/el-cambio-de-cromos-orbaiz-tiko_54412805795.html|title=El cambio de cromos Orbaiz-Tiko|trans-title=Orbaiz-Tiko change of cards|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|first=Iñaki|last=Ugalde|language=Spanish|date=6 August 2014|accessdate=20 February 2026}}</ref> He was a very important midfield element from the start, playing 35 league matches and scoring three goals in the [[2004–05 La Liga|2004–05 campaign]] and adding eight [[2004–05 UEFA Cup|appearances]] in the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]]. He also suffered serious knee injuries in [[2002–03 La Liga|2002–03]] and [[2006–07 La Liga|2006–07]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11848/2254488|title=Orbaiz out for season|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|first=Francisco|last=Acedo|date=9 January 2003|accessdate=11 December 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11848/2393139/|title=Orbaiz blow for Bilbao|publisher=Sky Sports|first=Francisco|last=Acedo|date=19 October 2006|accessdate=11 December 2012}}</ref>

Orbaiz continued to be first-choice when healthy in the [[2009–10 La Liga|2009–10 season]]. However, from February to March 2010, he was [[Ejection (sports)|sent off]] twice for dangerous challenges – both of which resulted in two-match bans – at [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] (2–1 loss)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/275602?cc=5739|title=Drama as Villarreal defeat Bilbao|publisher=[[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]]|date=13 February 2010|accessdate=10 October 2011|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://archive.today/20120723184444/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/275602?cc=5739|archivedate=23 July 2012}}</ref> and at home against [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] (2–2, he also scored the opener in the latter game).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/275784?cc=5739|title=Leon strikes late|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=20 March 2010|accessdate=10 October 2011|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://archive.today/20120716074123/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/275784?cc=5739|archivedate=16 July 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2010/03/23/mas_futbol/1269298865_850215.html|title=Dos partidos a Orbaiz y uno a Miguel Torres|trans-title=Two games for Orbaiz and one for Miguel Torres|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|language=Spanish|date=23 March 2010|accessdate=29 April 2025}}</ref> 

For the [[2010–11 La Liga|following campaign]], Orbaiz was promoted to [[Captain (association football)|team captain]] after the departures of [[Joseba Etxeberria]] and [[Francisco Yeste]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://bilbao.theoffside.com/team-news/athletic-club-has-a-new-captain.html|title=Athletic Club has a new captain|publisher=The Offside|date=25 July 2010|accessdate=11 December 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714142826/http://bilbao.theoffside.com/team-news/athletic-club-has-a-new-captain.html|archive-date=14 July 2014}}</ref>

===Later career===
In late August 2011, after another [[2010–11 La Liga|season]] of regular use by manager [[Joaquín Caparrós]] – 26 games, 1,675 minutes – as Athletic once again [[2011–12 UEFA Europa League|qualified for the Europa League]], the 32-year-old Orbaiz was loaned to [[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiacos]] in Greece, joining a host of compatriots at the [[Piraeus]] side including manager [[Ernesto Valverde]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=1&d=1000&berria=11086&idi=2|title=Pablo Orbaiz loaned to Olympiacos|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=30 August 2011|accessdate=10 October 2011|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20111110042433/http://www.athletic-club.net/web/main.asp?a=0&b=1&c=1&d=1000&berria=11086&idi=2|archivedate=10 November 2011}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/025a-0ea6a95c334b-ab9bf22c1944-1000--olympiacos-injuries-no-excuse-for-valverde/|title=Olympiacos injuries no excuse for Valverde|publisher=UEFA|date=5 December 2011|accessdate=29 April 2025}}</ref> He won the domestic [[Double (association football)|double]]<ref name=Double>{{cite web|url=https://www.eldesmarque.com/futbol/athletic-club/20120615/el-olympiacos-le-tiende-la-mano-a-orbaiz-para-seguir_60031160.html|title=El Olympiacos le tiende la mano a Orbaiz para seguir|trans-title=Olympiacos hold out their hand to Orbaiz for him to continue|publisher=El Desmarque|language=Spanish|date=15 June 2012|accessdate=29 April 2025}}</ref> and was able to realise his ambition of playing in the [[UEFA Champions League]], making four [[2011–12 UEFA Champions League|group-stage appearances]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/champions-league/2018/09/19/5ba19398268e3e371b8b4594.html#google_vignette|title=La Champions League lejos de los focos|trans-title=The Champions League away from the spotlight|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=Spanish|date=19 September 2018|accessdate=29 April 2025}}</ref><ref name=Dream/> 

Orbaiz was subsequently released by Athletic Bilbao, signing a one-year contract with [[FC Rubin Kazan|Rubin Kazan]] and reuniting with countryman and former Olympiacos teammate [[Iván Marcano]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/01ff-0e7e8343b94c-962ead26b71b-1000--rubin-reel-in-midfielders-tore-and-orbaiz/|title=Rubin reel in midfielders Töre and Orbaiz|publisher=UEFA|date=26 July 2012|accessdate=29 April 2025}}</ref> He retired in June 2015 aged 36, following a spell with amateurs [[CD Valle de Egüés|Valle de Egüés]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elcorreo.com/deportes/futbol/pablo-orbaiz-jugar-20180826225648-nt.html|title=Pablo Orbaiz: «Jugar en Tercera es una de las cosas que más me ha llenado»|trans-title=Pablo Orbaiz: "Playing in ''Tercera'' is one of the things that filled me the most"|newspaper=El Correo|first=Javier|last=Ortiz de Lazcano|language=Spanish|date=26 August 2018|accessdate=29 April 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
Orbaiz made his debut with [[Spain national football team|Spain]] on 21 August 2002 in a [[testimonial match]] for [[Ferenc Puskás]] against [[Hungary national football team|Hungary]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://elpais.com/diario/2002/08/22/deportes/1029967201_850215.html|title=Poca luz para tanto estreno|trans-title=Too little light for so many premieres|newspaper=[[El País]]|first=Ramón|last=Besa|language=Spanish|date=22 August 2002|accessdate=12 November 2015}}</ref> representing the nation on a further three occasions.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elcorreo.com/deportes/futbol/grupo-jovenes-talentos-20190423192521-nt.html|title=Un grupo de jóvenes talentos que sería la base de la España campeona|trans-title=A group of young talents that could be the foundation of champions Spain|newspaper=El Correo|language=Spanish|date=23 April 2019|accessdate=29 April 2025}}</ref> Previously, he helped [[Spain national under-20 football team|the under-20s]] to win the [[1999 FIFA World Youth Championship]].<ref name=U20>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2009/04/17/futbol/seleccion/1239983100.html|title=Qué fue de los campeones del mundo sub20|trans-title=What happened to the under-20 world champions|newspaper=Marca|first=Miguel Ángel|last=García|language=Spanish|date=17 April 2009|accessdate=3 May 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cuadernosdefutbol.com/2014/05/campeonato-del-mundo-sub20-1999-iii-espana-se-corona-en-nigeria/|title=Campeonato del Mundo sub'20 1999 (III): España se corona en Nigeria|trans-title=1999 Under'20 World Cup (III): Spain crowned in Nigeria|publisher=Cuadernos de Fútbol|first=Óscar|last=Díez|language=Spanish|date=1 May 2014|accessdate=29 April 2025}}</ref>
