'''Nolberto Albino Solano Todco''' (born 12 December 1974) is a Peruvian professional [[Manager (association football)|football manager]] and former player who is the manager of the [[Pakistan national football team|Pakistan national team]].

Solano spent much of his career in the [[Premier League]], primarily with [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]], and also with [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] and [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]]. He became the first Peruvian to play in the Premier League, and appear in the [[FA Cup]] final. He is considered a cult hero at the Tyneside club, and was also noted for his [[trumpet]] playing and formed his own [[Salsa music|salsa]] band named The Geordie Latinos.<ref name="icNewcastle">{{cite web|url=http://icnewcastle.icnetwork.co.uk/chroniclelive/eveningchronicle/tm_headline=solano%2Ds-tune-army%26method=full%26objectid=18076147%26siteid=50081-name_page.html |access-date=27 May 2007 |title=Solano's tune army | publisher=icNewcastle}}</ref> He has described himself as an "adopted [[Geordie]]."<ref name="The Guardian">{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2004/jan/10/sport.comment2 |access-date=10 June 2007 |title=Solano blows his own trumpet | work=The Guardian | location=London | first=Michael | last=Walker | date=10 January 2004}}</ref>

Solano is a popular figure in his native Peru, where he is seen as one of the most famous Peruvians, appearing on telephone cards and having his wedding televised live.<ref name="Solano Tunes Of Glory">{{cite news| url=https://www.questia.com/read/1G1-60384954 |title=oalano Tunes Of Glory|last=Howey|first=Martin|date=21 May 1999| work=The Mirror (London)|access-date=4 August 2008}}</ref><ref name="Diego made me a star - ace Solano">{{cite news|title=Diego made me a star – ace Solano|last=Hill|first=Graham|date=1 February 2004 |work=Sunday Mercury (Birmingham)}} ''"Solano is a hero in Peru where his face appears in TV adverts. The 29-year-old winger is such a household name there that even his wedding was televised live."''</ref> He played 95 times for the [[Peru national football team|national team]] between 1994 and 2009, including at the [[1995 Copa América|1995]], [[1999 Copa América|1999]] and [[2004 Copa América]] and the [[2000 CONCACAF Gold Cup]].

Towards the end of his career, he went into coaching, and was first team coach at non-league side [[Newcastle Benfield F.C.|Newcastle Benfield]], while contracted to [[Hartlepool United F.C.|Hartlepool United]]. He had short spells at [[Universitario de Deportes|Universitario]] and [[José Gálvez FBC|José Gálvez]], and was manager of [[Internacional de Toronto]] for a few matches, before the club had its licensing agreement terminated. From 2015 to 2022, Solano was involved within the national team setup, as assistant manager to [[Ricardo Gareca]] and manager of the [[Peru Olympic football team|Olympic team]]. In 2023, he briefly led [[AFC Eskilstuna]] in the Swedish [[Superettan]], before another brief term as manager of [[Blyth Spartans A.F.C.|Blyth Spartans]] in 2024.

==Club career==

===Early career===
{{BLP unreferenced section|date=November 2023}}
Solano signed his first professional contract with the [[Peruvian Primera División]] side [[Sporting Cristal]] in 1992 at the age of 17. He made his league debut on 13 April 1992 in his team's 2–0 win against [[Asociación Deportiva San Agustín|San Agustín]]. Towards the end of his first season at Sporting Cristal, he signed a one-year contract with [[Club Centro Deportivo Municipal|Deportivo Municipal]], before returning to Cristal at the end of 1993. He was part of the Sporting Cristal squad of the 1990s during which the club won the Peru Primera División Championships (1994, 1995 and 1996) and reached the finals of the 1997 [[Copa Libertadores]]. Along with [[Roberto Palacios]], [[Flavio Maestri]], [[Julio César de Andrade Moura|Julinho]] and [[Jorge Soto (footballer)|Jorge Soto]], he was one of Sporting Cristal's most recognized players of the era.

===Boca Juniors===
In 1997, aged 22, he signed for Argentinian side [[Boca Juniors]] where he became a teammate of [[Diego Maradona]], who nicknamed Solano the 'Maestrito'.<ref name="The Guardian" /> Solano said in 2004 that he would like to play for Boca Juniors again, but admitted he was perhaps too old for the ambition to be realized.<ref>{{cite news|title=Solano's Boca dream|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11677/2311645/|publisher=Sky Sports|date=24 September 2004|access-date=20 May 2012}}</ref>

===Newcastle United===
[[File:1999 FA Cup Final Solano free kick.jpg|thumb|250px|Solano preparing to take a free kick in the 1999 FA Cup final]]
In June 1998, Solano was close to a £3.75 million transfer to [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] with a £16,000 weekly wage.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Nixon |first1=Alan |title=Football: Solano poised to sign for Arsenal |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-solano-poised-to-sign-for-arsenal-1163551.html |access-date=4 November 2023 |work=The Independent |date=7 June 1998}}</ref> In August, he signed for [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] for £2.5 million, as one of [[Kenny Dalglish]]'s final signings for the club.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Stewart |first1=Rob |last2=Ley |first2=John |title=Robson eyes Carr after Solano sale |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2372107/Robson-eyes-Carr-after-Solano-sale.html |access-date=4 November 2023 |work=The Daily Telegraph |date=30 January 2004}}</ref>

Solano's first team debut for Newcastle came in a Premier League match against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] on 22 August 1998, when he came on after 67 minutes as a substitute for goalscorer [[Andreas Andersson (footballer, born 1974)|Andreas Andersson]] in a 1–1 away draw.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ryder |first1=Lee |title=Blue feeling |url=https://www.thefreelibrary.com/Blue+feeling.-a0143471306 |access-date=4 November 2023 |work=Evening Chronicle |date=21 March 2006}}</ref> His first of six goals that season equalised in a 3–1 home win over [[Wimbledon F.C.|Wimbledon]] on 28 November,<ref>{{cite news |last1=Wilson |first1=Paul |title=Ferguson's double Scotch |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/1998/nov/28/match.sport8 |access-date=4 November 2023 |work=The Guardian |date=28 November 1998}}</ref> and the last one was the decider in a 4–3 victory at [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]] on 3 April 1999.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Collings |first1=Timothy |title=Speed's decisive deed settles goal feast |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/Observer_Match_Report/0,,-16033,00.html |access-date=4 November 2023 |work=The Guardian |date=3 April 1999}}</ref> On 22 May, he started in the [[1999 FA Cup final]], which his team lost 2–0 to [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] at [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Bennett |first1=George |title='Make history' – Nobby Solano urges Newcastle United to right the wrongs of 1999 FA Cup final defeat |url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/newcastle-manchester-united-nobby-solano-26329759 |access-date=4 November 2023 |work=Evening Chronicle |date=25 February 2023}}</ref>

On 2 January 2001, Solano scored the first goal of a 4–2 loss at [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]], but was sent off nine minutes later for handling the ball on the goal line; [[Darren Anderton]] missed the resulting penalty.<ref>{{cite news |title=Three off as Spurs hit Toon |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/1096260.stm |access-date=4 November 2023 |website=BBC Sport |date=2 January 2001}}</ref> He was given a red card again on 14 April in a loss at [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] for the same offence, conceding a penalty from which [[Marcus Stewart]] scored the only goal.<ref>{{cite news |title=Late Ipswich strike thwarts Magpies |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/1274587.stm |access-date=4 November 2023 |website=BBC Sport |date=14 April 2001}}</ref>

In June 2001, he signed a new five-year contract with the club.<ref>{{cite news |title=Solano commits to Newcastle |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/n/newcastle_united/1397201.stm |access-date=4 November 2023 |website=BBC Sport |date=19 June 2001}}</ref> A month later he scored what he later described as "the best goal of [his] career" with a solo effort against [[TSV 1860 München|1860 München]].<ref name="Sol bids farewell">{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071023060133/http://www.nufc.premiumtv.co.uk/page/NewsDetail/0,,10278~1103820,00.html |archive-date=23 October 2007 |title=Sol Bids Farewell To Toon | publisher=Newcastle United F.C. |date=1 September 2007|url=http://www.nufc.premiumtv.co.uk/page/NewsDetail/0,,10278~1103820,00.html }}</ref> On 22 December, he scored the last-minute winner in a 4–3 comeback win at [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]], putting Newcastle in first place at the hosts' expense.<ref>{{cite news |title=Toon rally denies Leeds |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/1722577.stm |access-date=4 November 2023 |website=BBC Sport |date=22 December 2001}}</ref>

On 26 April 2003, Solano's penalty was the only goal of the [[Tyne–Wear derby]] away to [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]]. He took the spot kick due to [[Alan Shearer]]'s injury earlier in the game.<ref>{{cite news |title=Magpies see off Sunderland |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/2960631.stm |access-date=4 November 2023 |website=BBC Sport |date=26 April 2003}}</ref> Six months later in another local derby away to [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]], he was not named in the starting line-up or on the substitutes' bench, prompting him to drive home.<ref>{{cite news |title=Solano storms out |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/n/newcastle_united/3206526.stm |access-date=4 November 2023 |website=BBC Sport |date=20 October 2003}}</ref>

===Aston Villa===
Solano joined [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] in January 2004 for a fee of £1.5 million and signed a two-and-a-half-year contract with the club.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/a/aston_villa/3445405.stm|title=Solano signs for Villa|date=30 January 2004|website=BBC Sport|access-date=6 June 2008}}</ref> He attributed his leaving Newcastle to a "strained relationship" with manager [[Bobby Robson]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Nobby blames Bobby for exit|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11677/2348173/|publisher=Sky Sports|date=11 September 2005|access-date=20 May 2012}}</ref> He made his debut in a 5–0 win over [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] on 31 January,<ref>{{cite news |title=Leicester 0–5 Aston Villa |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/3417881.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=31 January 2004 |access-date=23 January 2010}}</ref> and was sent off on 24 April in a 2–1 win at Middlesbrough for slapping [[George Boateng]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Turnbull |first1=Simon |title=Solano and Crouch give Boro a slap in the face |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/solano-and-crouch-give-boro-a-slap-in-the-face-561184.html |access-date=4 November 2023 |work=The Independent |date=25 April 2004}}</ref>

On 22 September 2004, Solano scored his first goal for Villa from a free kick in a 3–1 home win over [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] in the second round of the [[Football League Cup]], having earlier assisted a goal by [[Juan Pablo Ángel]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Aston Villa 3–1 QPR |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/league_cup/3656008.stm |access-date=4 November 2023 |website=BBC Sport |date=22 September 2004}}</ref> A first league goal followed a month later in a 2–0 win against [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]], also by a free kick at [[Villa Park]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Aston Villa 2–0 Fulham |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/3727532.stm |access-date=4 November 2023 |website=BBC Sport |date=23 October 2004}}</ref> He ended the [[2004–05 Aston Villa F.C. season|2004–05 season]] as top scorer,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.soccerbase.com/teams/team.sd?team_id=154&teamTabs=stats&season_id=134 |title=Aston Villa: 2004/05: Player Appearances |work=Soccerbase |publisher=Centurycomm |access-date=5 June 2012}}</ref> and was elected the club's Player of the Year by the supporters, his teammates,<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.birminghammail.net/birmingham-sport/aston-villa-fc/2005/05/10/nobby-rues-villa-gaffes-50002-15499636/ |title=Nobby rues Villa gaffes |first=Bill |last=Howell |newspaper=Birmingham Mail |date=10 May 2005 |access-date=5 June 2012}}</ref> and the local press.

In what was Solano's last appearance for Villa, on 23 August 2005, he was sent off for striking [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]]'s [[Richard Hughes (footballer)|Richard Hughes]] in the face in a 1–1 draw at [[Fratton Park]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Hughes: I'm no cheat|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11674/2346043/ |first=James |last=Pearson |publisher=Sky Sports|date=25 August 2005|access-date=5 June 2012}}</ref> On transfer deadline day, Solano rejected a late offer to join [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] and agreed to return to Newcastle.<ref>{{cite news|title=Solano shunned Reds|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11669/2347432/ |first=Mark |last=Buckingham |publisher=Sky Sports|date=2 September 2005|access-date=20 May 2012}}</ref>

===Return to Newcastle United===
Solano returned to Newcastle United on 31 August 2005 for a fee believed by the BBC to be £1.5 million. He signed a contract originally for two years, but with the option for Newcastle to extend it for another year. [[Midfielder]] [[James Milner (footballer)|James Milner]] went in the other direction, joining Aston Villa on a season-long loan.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/n/newcastle_united/4202864.stm|title=Solano makes return to Newcastle|date=31 August 2005 |website=BBC Sport|access-date=5 June 2012}}</ref> Solano revealed that [[Alan Shearer]] had played an influential role in arranging his return.<ref>{{cite news|title=Nobby: Al crucial in my return|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11678/2347952/ |first=Mark |last=Kendall |publisher=Sky Sports|date=4 September 2005|access-date=20 May 2012}}</ref>

The first game of Solano's second spell was a 3–2 home derby win over Sunderland on 23 October.<ref>{{cite news |title=Home support for Solano |url=https://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/news/7148110.home-support-solano/ |access-date=4 November 2023 |work=The Northern Echo |date=22 October 2005}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Morton |first1=David |title=Newcastle 3–2 Sunderland: Emre hits a winning free-kick on this day 10 years ago |url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/news/history/newcastle-3-2-sunderland-emre-10312024 |access-date=4 November 2023 |work=Evening Chronicle |date=22 October 2015}}</ref> The first goal of the spell, on his 31st birthday on 10 December, decided the game against Arsenal at [[St James' Park]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Morton |first1=David |title=Newcastle 1–0 Arsenal: Nobby Solano strike spikes the Gunners back in 2005 |url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/news/history/newcastle-1-0-arsenal-nobby-9948897 |access-date=4 November 2023 |work=Evening Chronicle |date=28 August 2005}}</ref>

In the 2006–07 season, injuries to right-back [[Stephen Carr]] and others caused manager [[Glenn Roeder]] to play Solano at right-back instead of his usual right-wing position. However it was not an unfamiliar playing position to Solano, as he had started his football career in defence and had featured at right-back for his country. With his contract due to expire at the end of the season, Solano said he would be "crazy" to move on at the age of 32,<ref>{{cite news|title=Solano fancies Magpies stay|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11678/2402277/|publisher=Sky Sports|date=14 January 2007|access-date=20 May 2012}}</ref> and duly signed a new one-year contract. However a few months later, he asked to leave the club to be closer to his family, who had moved to London.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/n/newcastle_united/6945496.stm|title=Solano linked to West Ham switch|date=14 August 2007 |website=BBC Sport|access-date=6 June 2008}}</ref> His one regret was that he had been unable to help the club win a trophy for the fans.<ref>{{cite news|title=Nobby's trophy regret|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11678/2708144/ |first=James |last=Dall |publisher=Sky Sports|date=4 September 2007|access-date=20 May 2012}}</ref>

===West Ham United===
[[File:Solano.png|thumb|left|upright|Solano playing for West Ham United]]
Solano signed a one-year contract with [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] in August 2007.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/w/west_ham_utd/6973578.stm|title=West Ham sign Solano and Camara|date=31 August 2007|website=BBC Sport|access-date=6 June 2008}}</ref> He made his debut for West Ham in October 2007, coming on as a second-half substitute in the 3–1 home win against [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]], and was instrumental in West Ham's second goal, his shot being deflected into the Sunderland goal by goalkeeper, [[Craig Gordon]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/7043009.stm|title=West Ham 3–1 Sunderland |last=Lillywhite|first=James|date=21 October 2007|website=BBC Sport|access-date=6 June 2008}}</ref> His first goal for West Ham was a free-kick and the fifth goal in West Ham's 5–0 away win against [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]] on 10 November 2007.<ref name="1st West Ham goal">{{cite web|url=http://www.whufc.com/page/News/0,,12562~1164492,00.html| access-date=10 November 2007 | title=Derby County 0–5 West Ham United| publisher=whufc.com}}</ref> In the last game of the season on 11 May 2008 Solano scored his second free-kick goal, against Aston Villa, the match ended 2–2. He was released by West Ham when his contract expired at the end of the [[2007–08 in English football|2007–08]] season having scored four goals in 23 appearances.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/w/west_ham_utd/7451377.stm|title=West Ham release veteran Solano |date=12 June 2008|website=BBC Sport|access-date=12 June 2008}}</ref>

===Larissa and Universitario===
Although Solano was rumoured to be interesting [[LA Galaxy]],<ref>{{cite news|title=Solano in Galaxy talks|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11685/3852494/|publisher=Sky Sports|date=22 July 2008|access-date=20 May 2012}}</ref> he became "one of the biggest signings in the club’s history" when he signed for [[Super League Greece]] club [[Athlitiki Enosi Larissa F.C.|AEL]] in August 2008.<ref>{{cite news|title=Solano Signs For Larissa|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/117/greece/2008/08/11/814528/solano-signs-for-larissa |first=Chris |last=Paraskevas |publisher=Goal.com|date=11 August 2008|access-date=20 May 2012}}</ref>

He then returned to Peru with [[Universitario de Deportes|Universitario]] for [[2009 Club Universitario de Deportes season|its 2009 season]], for whom he scored a crucial penalty against [[Alianza Lima]] in the play-off for the Peruvian Primera División title,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2009/dec/14/nolberto-solano-universitario-nacional-peru-paraguay |title=Nolberto Solano stars as titles are decided across South America |publisher=Guardian.co.uk |agency=Reuters |date=14 December 2009 |access-date=5 June 2012}}</ref> helping the team to a 2–0 aggregate victory to seal the club's 25th league title and win the national championship.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=29 December 2009 |title=Universitario confirms departure of Nolberto Solano to Colchester United |url=https://andina.pe/agencia/noticia.aspx?id=271815 |access-date=23 September 2024 |website=andina.pe |language=es}}</ref>

===Leicester City===
[[File:Nobby Solano.png|thumb|right|upright|Solano playing for Leicester City]]
Solano returned to England, where he trained with [[Colchester United F.C.|Colchester United]]<ref>{{cite news|title = Nolberto Solano trains with Colchester United| url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/c/colchester_united/8426171.stm|website = BBC Sport|date = 22 December 2009 |access-date=5 June 2012}}</ref> and with Newcastle,<ref>{{cite news|title = Solano training with Magpies|url = http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11688_5868368,00.html|publisher = Sky Sports|date = 18 January 2010 |access-date =23 January 2010 }}</ref> before, on 22 January 2010, signing for [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] until the end of the season. He was reunited with [[Nigel Pearson]], who had been assistant manager at Newcastle.<ref>{{cite news|title = Leicester sign former Newcastle winger Nolberto Solano|url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/l/leicester_city/8474599.stm|website = BBC Sport|date =22 January 2010 |access-date =5 June 2012}}</ref> He made his debut as an 84th-minute substitute in a goalless draw against Newcastle at the [[Walkers Stadium]] on 30 January.<ref>{{cite news|title = Leicester 0–0 Newcastle|url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_div_1/8483774.stm|website = BBC Sport|date =30 January 2010 |access-date =5 June 2012}}</ref> Solano played eleven league games, scoring in a 4–3 penalty shootout defeat to [[Cardiff City]] in the [[Football League Championship play-offs|Championship play-off]] semi-final second leg.<ref>{{cite news|title = Cardiff 2–3 Leicester (agg 3–3)|url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_div_1/8672579.stm|website = BBC Sport|date =12 May 2010 |access-date =13 May 2010 |first=Peter|last=Shuttleworth}}</ref> He was offered a contract for a further six months, but chose to leave the club,<ref>{{cite news |title =Defender Wayne Brown and midfielder Nolberto Solano quit Leicester City |url =http://www.thisisleicestershire.co.uk/Wayne-Brown-Nolberto-Solano-quit-Leicester-City/story-12073446-detail/story.html |archive-url =https://archive.today/20130505095750/http://www.thisisleicestershire.co.uk/Wayne-Brown-Nolberto-Solano-quit-Leicester-City/story-12073446-detail/story.html |url-status =dead |archive-date =5 May 2013 |publisher =This is Leicestershire |date =7 July 2010 |access-date =9 July 2010 }}</ref> preferring to follow Pearson to [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.thisishullandeastriding.co.uk/HULL-CITY-Solano-hails-perfect-boss-Pearson/story-11967732-detail/story.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130505080243/http://www.thisishullandeastriding.co.uk/HULL-CITY-Solano-hails-perfect-boss-Pearson/story-11967732-detail/story.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=5 May 2013 |title=HULL CITY: Solano hails 'perfect boss' – Peru star was happy to follow |publisher=This is Hull and East Riding |date=24 July 2010 |access-date=5 June 2012 }}</ref>

===Hull City===
Solano rejoined Pearson, who had recently taken over the manager's job at Hull City, signing a one-year deal.<ref>{{cite news| title       = HULL CITY: Solano and Harper agree deals|url=http://www.sporthull.co.uk/hullcity/news/HULL-CITY-Solano-Harper-agree-deals/article-2404959-detail/article.html| archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20100715083826/http://www.sporthull.co.uk/hullcity/news/HULL-CITY-Solano-Harper-agree-deals/article-2404959-detail/article.html|archive-date=15 July 2010|newspaper=Hull Daily Mail|date= 10 July 2010|access-date=10 July 2010 }}</ref> Despite initial expectations that Solano would be with Hull City for only a single season before retiring, Solano revealed in April 2011, that he hoped that he would be able to extend his stay with the Tigers beyond the 2010–11 season, by combining a playing and coaching role, as [[Nick Barmby]] had done.<ref>{{cite news|title= HULL CITY: Nobby looks for new role – and an extended stay with Tigers |url= http://www.thisishullandeastriding.co.uk/hullcityhome/hullcity/HULL-CITY-Nobby-looks-new-role/article-3425483-detail/article.html |archive-url = https://archive.today/20130505084718/http://www.thisishullandeastriding.co.uk/hullcityhome/hullcity/HULL-CITY-Nobby-looks-new-role/article-3425483-detail/article.html |url-status = dead |archive-date = 5 May 2013|newspaper= Hull Daily Mail |date= 9 April 2010|access-date = 9 April 2010}}</ref>

===Hartlepool United===
[[File:Nolberto Solano 30-07-11 1.png|thumb|200px|right|Solano with [[Hartlepool United F.C.|Hartlepool United]] in 2011]]
On 13 May 2011, Solano signed for [[Hartlepool United F.C.|Hartlepool United]], having previously worked with their manager [[Mick Wadsworth]] at Newcastle.<ref>{{cite news| title= Pools Make Sensational Swoop For Solano| url = http://www.hartlepoolunited.co.uk/page/NewsDetail/0,,10326~2359341,00.html| publisher = Hartlepool United F.C| date = 13 May 2011| access-date = 13 May 2010| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120417223012/http://www.hartlepoolunited.co.uk/page/NewsDetail/0,,10326~2359341,00.html| archive-date= 17 April 2012| url-status= dead}}</ref>

On 2 August, Solano scored in a friendly against [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.inthemadcrowd.co.uk/UI/Match.aspx?oid=5221 |title=Hartlepool 1–3 Sunderland |website=In The Mad Crowd |access-date=19 October 2023}}</ref> rivals of his former club Newcastle United, and scored his first league goal for Hartlepool on 17 September at home against [[Bury F.C.|Bury]].<ref>{{soccerbase season|15057|2011|access-date=19 October 2023}}</ref> The following week, Solano scored their first goal direct from a free-kick in a 2–1 away win at [[AFC Bournemouth]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14958266 |title=Bournemouth 1–2 Hartlepool |website=BBC Sport |date=24 September 2011 |access-date=19 October 2023}}</ref> Following Wadsworth's sacking, his successor, first-team coach [[Neale Cooper]], confirmed that Solano was not part of his plans, because he needed "players who will really graft, [and] that's not Nobby's game".<ref>{{cite news|title=Hartlepool boss Cooper has no place for Nolberto Solano|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16638298|website=BBC Sport|date=19 January 2012|access-date=19 January 2012}}</ref> In April 2012, the club confirmed Solano had been advised not to play for the remainder of the season because of recurring illness.<ref>{{cite news|title=Illness ends campaign for Hartlepool's Nolberto Solano|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17691346|website=BBC Sport|date=12 April 2012|access-date=20 May 2012}}</ref>

In February 2012, Solano became first-team coach at [[Northern League (football)|Northern League]] side [[Newcastle Benfield F.C.|Newcastle Benfield]] while remaining a member of Hartlepool's playing squad.<ref name="retirement" />

==International career==
Solano earned 95 caps and scored 20 goals for [[Peru national football team|Peru]]. His debut on 3 May 1994 was a 1–0 win over neighbours [[Colombia national football team|Colombia]] at the [[Miami Orange Bowl]], and his first goal on 25 June 1995 was the only one of a friendly win over visitors [[Slovakia national football team|Slovakia]]. He played at the [[Copa América]] in [[1995 Copa América|1995]] and [[1999 Copa América|1999]], scoring in a 3–3 quarter-final draw with [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]] and the subsequent penalty shootout defeat in the latter, as well as featuring at the [[2000 CONCACAF Gold Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Nolberto Solano – International Appearances |url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/solano-intl.html |access-date=4 November 2023 |publisher=RSSSF}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Barnard |first1=Mike |title=Surprises reign in Copa America |url=https://nypost.com/1999/07/13/surprises-reign-in-copa-america/ |access-date=4 November 2023 |work=New York Post |date=13 July 1999}}</ref>

At the [[2004 Copa América]] on home soil, Solano scored in group games against [[Venezuela national football team|Venezuela]] (win) and Colombia (draw) in a run to the quarter-finals.<ref>{{cite news |title=Colombia reach last eight |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/internationals/3882099.stm |access-date=4 November 2023 |website=BBC Sport |date=10 July 2004}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Solano on target for hosts |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/solano-on-target-for-hosts-6983370.html |access-date=4 November 2023 |work=Evening Standard}}</ref> He said in June 2005 that his international career was over,<ref>{{cite news |title=Peru appoint Uribe as coach again |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2007/SPORT/football/03/08/peru.coach/index.html |access-date=4 November 2023 |publisher=CNN |date=8 March 2007| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070317181456/https://edition.cnn.com/2007/SPORT/football/03/08/peru.coach/index.html| archive-date=17 March 2007}}</ref> but returned in September 2007.<ref>{{cite news |title=International Call-Ups For Toon Trio |url=https://www.nufc.co.uk/news/archive/international-call-ups-for-toon-trio/ |access-date=4 November 2023 |publisher=Newcastle United F.C. |date=28 August 2007}}</ref> He announced his international retirement in October 2009 with the team having not qualified for the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]], and said that he wanted to be a manager so he could finally take Peru to a World Cup.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,12010_5604221,00.html|title=Solano Ends Peru Career|publisher=Sky Sports|date=3 October 2009}}</ref>

==Managerial career==
Solano took the first step into coaching as the part-time first-team coach of [[Newcastle Benfield F.C.|Newcastle Benfield]] in 2012.<ref name="retirement">{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16856443|title=Nolberto Solano retires to coach Newcastle Benfield|date=2 February 2012|website=BBC Sport|access-date=2 February 2012}}</ref>

In June 2012, he was confirmed as manager of [[Peruvian Primera División]] club [[Universitario de Deportes|Universitario]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.clubuniversitario.org/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=965:nolberto-solano-qestoy-orgulloso-de-llegar-nuevamente-a-universitarioq&catid=66:noticias&Itemid=196 |title=Nolberto Solano: 'Estoy orgulloso de llegar nuevamente a Universitario' |publisher=Club Universitario de Deportes |date=4 June 2012 |access-date=5 June 2012 |language=es |trans-title=Nolberto Solano: 'I'm proud to be back at Universitario'}}</ref> On 12 December, Universitario confirmed that Solano had left the club, despite the fact he guided the club into the top half of the table after being in the relegation zone when he first took charge.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://tyneandwear.sky.com/sportsnews/article/50046|title=Nobby Solano's First Managerial Role At Universitario In Peru Comes to an End|date=12 December 2012|publisher=Sky|access-date=13 December 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121214121948/http://tyneandwear.sky.com/sportsnews/article/50046|archive-date=14 December 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

From three months from 23 April 2013, Solano was manager of [[José Gálvez FBC|José Gálvez]] of the same league. The team slipped from penultimate to last place in his brief spell.<ref>{{cite news |title=Nolberto Solano fue presentado como nuevo entrenador del José Gálvez|trans-title=Nolberto Solano was presented as new manager of José Gálvez |url=https://rpp.pe/futbol/descentralizado/nolberto-solano-fue-presentado-como-nuevo-entrenador-del-jose-galvez-noticia-588223 |access-date=4 November 2023 |publisher=RPP |date=23 April 2023 |language=Spanish}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Nolberto Solano fue cesado en José Gálvez|trans-title=Nolberto Solano was fired by José Gálvez |url=https://peru.com/futbol/descentralizado/nolberto-solano-fue-cesado-jose-galvez-noticia-153381/ |access-date=4 November 2023 |publisher=Peru.com |date=23 July 2013 |language=Spanish}}</ref>

In May 2014, Solano became the head coach of Canadian club [[Internacional de Toronto]] in [[League1 Ontario]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://rpp.pe/futbol/mas-futbol/nolberto-solano-fue-presentado-como-tecnico-del-internacional-toronto-noticia-689068|trans-title=Nolberto Solano was introduced as coach of the International Toronto|title=Nolberto Solano fue presentado como técnico del Internacional Toronto|language=es|date=2 May 2014|work=[[Radio Programas del Perú]]}}</ref> However, on 22 July, the club had its licensing agreement terminated<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.league1ontario.com/article/notification|title=Notification|publisher=League1 Ontario|access-date=24 July 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140809213053/http://www.league1ontario.com/article/notification|archive-date=9 August 2014}}</ref> due to issues regarding the payment of player salaries, ending his tenure.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://archivo.depor.com/futbol-internacional/equipo-que-dirigia-nolberto-solano-canada-fue-desafiliado-league-1-1022129|title=Equipo que dirigía Nolberto Solano en Canadá fue desafiliado de la League 1|trans-title=Team led by Nolberto Solano in Canada was disenrolled from League 1|date=5 August 2018|work=Depor}}</ref>

In May 2015, Solano was hired as a technical assistant to [[Ricardo Gareca]] on the Peru national team.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=30 July 2018 |title=Watch: Solano proud of Peru's performance at World Cup |url=https://timesofmalta.com/article/watch-solano-proud-with-perus-performance-at-world-cup.685659 |access-date=23 September 2024 |website=Times of Malta |language=en-gb}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Selección peruana: FPF confirma a Solano como asistente de Gareca|trans-title=Peruvian national team: FPF confirm Solano as Gareca's assistant |url=https://rpp.pe/futbol/mas-futbol/seleccion-peruana-fpf-confirma-a-solano-como-asistente-de-gareca-noticia-797708 |access-date=4 November 2023 |publisher=RPP |date=15 May 2015 |language=Spanish}}</ref> He also led the [[Peru Olympic football team|U-23 team]].<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.whufc.com/news/articles/2017/december/29-december/where-are-they-now-night-hammers-dethroned-champions| title=Where are they now? The night the Hammers dethroned the champions| publisher=West Ham United F.C.| date=29 December 2017| access-date=29 December 2017}}</ref> The team qualified for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]], their first for 36 years, but after a playoff defeat to [[Australia men's national soccer team|Australia]] on penalties in June 2022 denied them a second consecutive appearance, the entire coaching staff departed.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Jara |first1=Umberto |title=A pesar del adiós a Qatar 2022; inmensa gratitud a Ricardo Gareca y su equipo|trans-title=Despite the farewell to Qatar 2022; immense gratitude to Ricardo Gareca and his team |url=https://once.pe/a-pesar-del-adios-a-qatar-2022-inmensa-gratitud-a-ricardo-gareca-y-su-equipo/ |access-date=4 November 2023 |publisher=Once |date=13 June 2022 |language=Spanish}}</ref>

Solano was hired by [[AFC Eskilstuna]], second-last in the Swedish second-tier [[Superettan]], on 14 July 2023.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Closa |first1=Andrea |title=Se muda a Suecia: Nolberto Solano fue presentado como entrenador del AFC Eskilstuna|trans-title=He's moving to Sweden: Nolberto Solano was presented as manager of AFC Eskilstuna |url=https://rpp.pe/futbol/peruanos-en-el-mundo/se-muda-a-suecia-nolberto-solano-fue-presentado-como-entrenador-del-afc-eskilstuna-noticia-1495355 |access-date=4 November 2023 |publisher=RPP |date=14 July 2023 |language=Spanish}}</ref> He was dismissed on 10 October, with the team unmoved in the table.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Galiano |first1=Renzo |title=Nolberto Solano, despedido del AFC Eskilstuna por malos resultados en el ascenso de Suecia |trans-title=Nolberto Solano, dismissed from AFC Eskilstuna for bad results in Swedish second tier|url=https://www.infobae.com/peru/2023/10/09/nolberto-solano-despedido-del-afc-eskilstuna-por-malos-resultados-en-el-ascenso-de-suecia/ |access-date=4 November 2023 |publisher=Infobae |date=10 October 2023 |language=Spanish}}</ref>

On 3 May 2024, Solano returned to north–eastern England, when he was appointed as manager of [[Blyth Spartans A.F.C.|Blyth Spartans]] on a one-year contract. The team had dismissed [[Jon Shaw]] after relegation from the [[National League North]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Nolberto Solano: Blyth Spartans appoint Newcastle legend as manager | website=BBC Sport | date=3 May 2024 | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c6pygxgwwe2o | access-date=3 May 2024}}</ref> He would work with [[Steve Howard]], its sporting director.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Waugh |first=Chris |title=Ex-Newcastle winger Nolberto Solano appointed as Blyth Spartans manager |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5469152/2024/05/03/nolberto-solano-blyth-spartans/ |access-date=23 September 2024 |work=The New York Times |date=3 May 2024 |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> On 27 August 2024, Solano was sacked by Blyth Spartans following a winless start to the campaign in the [[Northern Premier League]] with his final game being a 4–1 loss to [[Morpeth Town A.F.C.|Morpeth Town]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.blythspartans.com/club-statement-nolberto-solano/ | title=Club Statement | Nolberto Solano | date=27 August 2024 }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Everitt |first=Natascha |date=28 August 2024 |title='I don't know what he's thinking' – Solano 'disappointed' by Blyth sacking |url=https://talksport.com/football/2024578/nolberto-solano-blyth-spartans-sacking-newcastle/ |access-date=23 September 2024 |website=talkSPORT |language=en-gb}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=28 August 2024 |title=Nolberto Solano: Blyth Spartans sack boss after winless start |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/articles/cvg3pr3p827o |access-date=23 September 2024 |website=BBC Sport |language=en-GB}}</ref> Solano said he was "very disappointed" noting that he had only ten players available to prepare during the pre-season.<ref name=":1" />

On 21 July 2025, Solano was appointed head coach of the [[Pakistan national under-23 football team|Pakistan national under-23 team]] ahead of the [[2026 AFC U-23 Asian Cup qualification|2026 AFC U-23 Asian Cup qualifiers]]. He was concurrently appointed as the head coach of the senior [[Pakistan national football team|Pakistan national team]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pakistan football team gets new head, assistant coaches |url=https://www.geo.tv/latest/615096-pakistan-football-team-gets-new-head-assistant-coaches |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=www.geo.tv |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Depor |first=Redacción |date=2025-07-21 |title=Nolberto Solano dirigirá a la Selección de Pakistán: ganaron un partido oficial en 7 años |url=https://depor.com/futbol-peruano/peruanos-en-el-mundo/nolberto-solano-a-seleccion-de-pakistan-sera-director-tecnico-de-absoluta-y-sub-23-ganaron-1-partido-en-7-anos-noticia/ |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=Depor |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Pagán |first=José Luis Blanco |date=2025-07-21 |title=¡Bombazo! Nolberto Solano será entrenador de la Selección Sub 23 de Pakistán |url=https://rpp.pe/futbol/peruanos-en-el-mundo/nolberto-solano-fue-anunciado-como-tecnico-de-la-seleccion-de-pakistan-noticia-1647267 |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=rpp.pe |language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Solano fue designado como nuevo DT de la selección absoluta y U23 de Pakistán |url=https://ovacion.pe/noticias/peruanos-mundo/solano-fue-designado-nuevo-dt-seleccion-absoluta-u23-pakistan |access-date=2025-07-21 |website=ovacion.pe |language=es}}</ref>

== Ambassador ==
Solano is an ambassador for [[Betsson]] in Latin America.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Partnerships |url=https://www.onebetsson.com/collaborations/ |access-date=23 September 2024 |website=One Betsson |language=en-US |archive-date=23 September 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240923201014/https://www.onebetsson.com/collaborations/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Solano qualified for a temporary [[Work permit (United Kingdom)|work permit in the United Kingdom]] when he signed for Newcastle, as he was an international regular for Peru. He later obtained a [[Greek passport]] through an ancestor, to bypass the need for a work permit as a citizen of the European Union. In 2001, the police and the Football Association investigated Solano's Greek passport as potentially fake. After a four-year investigation, he was cleared of any wrongdoing.<ref>{{cite news |title=Solano confident of clearing his Greek passport hurdle |url=https://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/news/7117323.solano-confident-clearing-greek-passport-hurdle/ |access-date=4 November 2023 |work=The Northern Echo |date=19 February 2001}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Solano in clear over passport |url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/solano-in-clear-over-passport-1581804 |access-date=4 November 2023 |work=Evening Chronicle |date=6 July 2005}}</ref>

'''Claudio Benoît Beauvue''' (born 16 April 1988) is a Guadeloupean professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Winger (association football)|winger]] and [[Forward (association football)|forward]].

Beauvais has spent the majority of his career in France, notably with [[ES Troyes AC|Troyes]], [[LB Châteauroux|Châteauroux]], [[En Avant Guingamp|Guingamp]], [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]], and [[Stade Malherbe Caen|Caen]]. He has also played for [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]], [[CD Leganés|Leganés]], and [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]] in Spain.

==Club career==
===Troyes===
Beauvue joined [[ES Troyes AC|Troyes]] from [[FC Nantes|Nantes]]' academy in 2006. He made his professional debut on 24 August 2007 against [[SC Bastia|Bastia]] in the [[2007–08 Ligue 2]] season. He signed his first professional contract with the club in the summer of 2008.

===Chateauroux===
On 23 March 2011, Beauvue was loaned (with an option to make deal permanent) for the [[2011–12 Ligue 2]] season to [[LB Châteauroux|Châteauroux]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Transfert : le Lyonnais Claudio Beauvue vendu au Celta Vigo pour 5 millions d'euros + 2,5 de bonus|trans-title=Transfer: Lyon's Claudio Beauvue sold to Celta Vigo for 5 million euros and 2.5 in bonuses|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Transfert-le-lyonnais-claudio-beauvue-vendu-au-celta-vigo-pour-5-millions-d-euros-2-5-de-bonus/625876|accessdate=26 January 2016|work=L'Equipe|date=19 January 2016|language=French}}</ref> He made his first start against [[En Avant de Guingamp|Guingamp]] and scored 10 goals in 37 matches during the [[Ligue 2]] campaign, with Châteauroux exercising their option to make the loan deal permanent.

On 19 October 2012, during the [[2012–13 Ligue 2|2012–13 season]], Beauvue scored a [[Hattrick (football)|hat-trick]] in a Ligue 2 match against [[Gazélec Ajaccio]] (3–1).

===Bastia===
On 29 January 2013, Beauvue was loaned – with an option to buy – to [[Ligue 1]] side Bastia. He made his first start for the [[Corsica]]n side against [[Evian Thonon Gaillard F.C.|Evian]] and scored his first and only goal for the side during the 36th matchday of the [[2012–13 Ligue 1|2012–13 Ligue 1 season]] against [[Montpellier HSC|Montpellier]]. At the end of the season, Bastia did not opt to purchase Beauvue.

===Guingamp===
On 30 June 2013, Beauvue signed for Guingamp. During his first season, he lifted the [[Coupe de France]] with his team after they beat [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]] 2–0 at the [[Stade de France]].

During the next season, Beauvue became a regular starter for the side during its [[2014–15 Ligue 1|Ligue 1]] and [[UEFA Europa League]] campaign. He scored five goals in the Europa League – one against [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]], one against [[FC Dinamo Minsk|Dinamo Minsk]], two against [[PAOK FC|PAOK]] and one against [[FC Dynamo Kyiv|Dynamo Kyiv]] – in a campaign in which Guingamp were able to qualify for the round of 16 of the Europa League for the first team in club history.

Beauvue finished the season with 22 goals in 46 games that season, fifth-most in Ligue 1 behind [[Alexandre Lacazette]], [[André-Pierre Gignac]], [[Zlatan Ibrahimović]] and [[Edinson Cavani]].

===Lyon===
On 27 June 2015, Beauvue joined [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] on a four-year contract. The transfer fee was estimated at €4.5 million, with €3 million bonus. He played his first match with the side against [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]], a 2–0 loss in the [[Trophée des Champions]] played in [[Montreal]]. He scored his first goal with the club in a 1–0 win against former club Guingamp at the [[Stade du Roudourou]]. He did not celebrate the goal, however, and opted to spend the night at the Panier des Salades, a bar frequented by Guingamp fans.

Despite his numerous first-team starts, Beauvue failed to fit in with the Lyon style of play, which is more focused on passing and possession. He scored his last goal for the club against another former side, Troyes.

===Celta Vigo===
On 16 January 2016, during the winter transfer window, Beauvue joined Spanish [[La Liga]] side [[RC Celta de Vigo|Celta Vigo]] on a €5 million transfer fee, along with a €2.5 million bonus. He signed a five-year contract.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Rodden|first1=Mark|title=Celta Vigo's Claudio Beauvue 'happy' after he 'suffered' at Lyon|url=http://www.espnfc.com/story/2789828/claudio-beauvue-happy-after-he-suffered-at-lyon|accessdate=23 August 2016|work=ESPNFC|date=19 January 2016}}</ref>

====Loan to Leganés====
On 29 August 2017, Beauvue was loaned to fellow top tier club [[CD Leganés|Leganés]], for one season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.deportivoleganes.com/noticia/el-frances-claudio-beauvue-refuerza-la-delantera-pepinera-para-esta-temporada|title=El francés Claudio Beauvue refuerza la delantera pepinera para esta temporada|trans-title=The French Claudio Beauvue bolsters the forward line ''pepinera'' for this season|publisher=CD Leganés|language=es|date=29 August 2017|accessdate=30 August 2017|archive-date=1 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170901025234/http://www.deportivoleganes.com/noticia/el-frances-claudio-beauvue-refuerza-la-delantera-pepinera-para-esta-temporada|url-status=dead}}</ref>

====Loan to Caen====
On 30 August 2018, Beauvue joined [[Stade Malherbe Caen|Caen]] on loan for the 2018–19 season. Caen secured an option to sign him permanently.<ref>{{cite news |title=Claudio Beauvue (Celta Vigo) prêté à Caen (officiel) |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Claudio-beauvue-celta-vigo-prete-a-caen-officiel/935345 |accessdate=31 August 2018 |work=L'Équipe |date=30 August 2018 |language=French}}</ref>

===Deportivo La Coruña===
On 18 January 2020, Beauvue signed a 18-month contract with [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rcdeportivo.es/noticia/claudio-beauvue-nuevo-jugador-del-deportivo-2019-2020|title=Claudio Beauvue, nuevo jugador del Deportivo 2019–2020|trans-title=Claudio Beauvue, new player of Deportivo 2019–2020|publisher=Deportivo La Coruña|language=es|date=18 January 2020|accessdate=17 February 2020}}</ref> He scored two goals in their final match of the season against Fuenlabrada (2-1). This game was postponed from the final matchday on 20 July. Beauvue (who was on holiday) travelled from the other side of the world to A Coruña for playing the match on 7 August as it was rescheduled very late. Despite the relegation of Deportivo to the Segunda B the striker decided to stay at the club.

===Boulogne===
In August 2021, Beauvue signed with [[US Boulogne|Boulogne]] in the [[Championnat National]], the third tier of French football.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=[[US Boulogne|Boulogne]]|url=http://www.usbco.com/claudio-beauvue-est-boulonnais-a5387.html|title=CLAUDIO BEAUVUE EST BOULONNAIS !|date=18 August 2021|accessdate=8 December 2021|language=fr}}</ref>

=== Ivry ===
In February 2023, Beauvue joined [[Championnat National 3]] club [[US Ivry|Ivry]] until the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Escaillet |first=Corentin |date=30 July 2023 |title=Football : Beauvue sous les couleurs du Racing Calais, c’est officiel |url=https://www.nordlittoral.fr/181069/article/2023-07-30/football-beauvue-sous-les-couleurs-du-racing-calais-c-est-officiel |access-date=20 November 2023 |website=www.nordlittoral.fr |language=fr}}</ref>

=== Calais ===
On 29 July 2023, Beauvue signed for [[Régional 1]] club [[RC Calais|Calais]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=sourice |first=frédéric |date=29 July 2023 |title=Foot (R1) - Claudio Beauvue à Calais, c’est fait ! |url=https://www.lavoixdunord.fr/1357399/article/2023-07-29/foot-r1-claudio-beauvue-calais-c-est-fait |access-date=20 November 2023 |website=La Voix du Nord |language=fr}}</ref> They achieved promotion to the [[Championnat National 3]] at the end of the season.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Bouchacourt |first=Jérome |date=23 June 2024 |title=Le Racing Club de Calais est promu en National 3 ! |url=https://footamateur.ouest-france.fr/le-racing-club-de-calais-est-promu-en-national-3/ |access-date=23 July 2024 |website=Foot Amateur |language=fr-FR}}</ref>

==International career==
Beauvue was born in Guadeloupe and moved to [[metropolitan France]] at a young age. He was called up to the [[Guadeloupe national football team|Guadeloupe team]] in 2008 and scored his first goal for them in 2016, against [[Suriname national football team|Suriname]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.concacaf.com/category/caribbean-cup-men/game-detail/266641 |title=Caribbean Cup – Men |archive-url=https://archive.today/20160814181411/http://www.concacaf.com/category/caribbean-cup-men/game-detail/266641 |archive-date=14 August 2016 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''Jason Grégory Denayer''' (born 28 June 1995) is a Belgian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who last played as a [[centre-back]] for [[Saudi Pro League]] club [[Al Fateh SC|Al Fateh]].

Denayer made his professional debut while on loan at Celtic, being named the [[PFA Scotland Young Player of the Year]] after helping them win the [[Scottish Premiership]] and [[Scottish League Cup]]. He then spent the following season on loan at [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]], helping them win the [[Turkish Cup]].

He played several times for Belgium at [[Belgium national under-19 football team|Under-19]] and [[Belgium national under-21 football team|Under-21]] levels, before making his full [[Belgium national football team|senior]] debut in March 2015. He was named in Belgium's 23-man squad for [[UEFA Euro 2016]] and made one appearance, playing in their quarter-final tie against [[Wales national football team|Wales]]. He also featured at [[UEFA Euro 2020]] and in the [[2021 UEFA Nations League Finals]] where he took fourth place.<ref>[https://www.uefa.com/uefananationsleague/match/2030760-- UEFA] italy-vs-belgium/lineups/ {{Dead link|date=November 2024}}</ref>

==Early life==
Denayer was born in [[Jette]], Brussels, Belgium, to a Congolese mother and Belgian father.<ref>{{cite web |title=First team: Jason Denayer |url=https://www.ol.fr/en/contents/players/j/jason-denayer |website=ol.fr |access-date=9 February 2021}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Early career===
Denayer started playing football at age six, where he started out at FC Ganshoren and then [[R.S.C. Anderlecht|Anderlecht]]. At the age of 13, he joined the [[JMG Academy]] in [[Lier, Belgium|Lier]]. It was there he was converted from playing as a striker to becoming a defender. Denayer credits his time at JMG for honing his football technique. Youths at the academy do not play normal competition football, instead taking part in small-sided games among each other, focusing on technique and education in a private school. They trained in bare feet to improve their touch; "It helps to develop your technical skills. Once you've reached a certain level, you're allowed to put on shoes. From then on the training is focused on technique and playing in small spaces" explained Denayer. He described the regime as "tough", adding "Your day started at 7 am and ended at 10:30 pm. In between you had 90 minutes – just before bedtime – to call your friends or family. It was playing football, studying, eat, sleep".<ref>{{cite news|last=Henderson|first=Mark|title=Jason Denayer hails the world-renowned Jean-Marc Guillou Academy|url=http://www.celticfc.net/news/6524|access-date=7 July 2015|work=Celtic FC|date=30 August 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=I've Got Striker's Instinct – Celtic Defender Jason Denayer|url=http://www.insidefutbol.com/2014/09/19/ive-got-strikers-instinct-celtic-defender-jason-denayer/161794/|access-date=7 July 2015|work=Inside Futbol|date=19 September 2014}}</ref><ref name="manc">{{cite news|title=A la rencontre de Jason Denayer, défenseur belge de Manchester City|url=http://www.rtbf.be/sport/football/etranger/angleterre/detail_a-la-rencontre-de-jason-denayer-defenseur-central-belge-de-manchester-city?id=8107196|publisher=RTBF Sport|language=fr|date=7 October 2013|access-date=21 August 2014}}</ref><ref name="bfoot">{{cite news|last=Terreur|first=Kristof|title=Jason Denayer: Belgium's barefoot warrior ready to be the new Kompany|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/jun/08/jason-denayer-belgium-euro-2016-manchester-city|access-date=13 June 2016|work=The Guardian|date=8 June 2016}}</ref>

In 2013, [[Lierse S.K. (1906)|Lierse]], who are in partnership with the JMG Academy, attempted to sign Denayer. However, he rejected their offer and instead moved abroad to England to try and find a club. He had a trial at [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], but club and player failed to reach an agreement. He then went for a trial at [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]].<ref name="bfoot" />

===Manchester City===
In July 2013 Denayer joined the [[Manchester City F.C. Reserves and Academy|Manchester City]] academy.<ref name="manc" /> In the summer transfer window, Denayer signed his first professional contract at Manchester City after a successful trial.<ref>{{cite news|title=Premier League: Jason Denayer wants to break into Man City's first-team squad|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11679/9011789/premier-league-jason-denayer-wants-to-break-into-man-citys-first-team-squad|publisher=Sky Sports|date=6 November 2013|access-date=21 August 2014}}</ref> Denayer was ever present for the club's campaign in the [[2013–14 UEFA Youth League|UEFA Youth League]], where he made eight appearances, scoring once in a 6–0 win over [[FC Bayern Munich Junior Team|Bayern Munich]].<ref>{{cite news|title=City kids thrash Bayern counterparts|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/manchester-city-6-0-bayern-munich-6128565|work=Manchester Evening News|date=2 October 2013|access-date=21 August 2014}}</ref> Denayer also played a huge role in domestic competitions where he helped the club finish fourth in the [[2013–14 Professional U21 Development League|Professional U21 Development League]], as well as reaching the final of the [[U21 Premier League Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|title=EDS Player of the Year Nominee: Jason Denayer|url=http://www.mcfc.co.uk/News/EDS-news/2014/EDS-Player-of-the-Year-Nominee-Jason-Denayer|publisher=Manchester City FC|date=9 July 2014|access-date=21 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140821194426/http://www.mcfc.co.uk/News/EDS-news/2014/EDS-Player-of-the-Year-Nominee-Jason-Denayer|archive-date=21 August 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In pre-season during July 2014, Denayer was included in the first team and started in a 2–0 friendly loss away against [[Dundee F.C.|Dundee]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Brennan |first1=Stuart |title=Dundee 2 City 0: Pre-season friendly report |url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/dundee-2-manchester-city-0-7416059 |access-date=17 September 2020 |work=Manchester Evening News |date=14 July 2014}}</ref>

On 10 July 2015, it was confirmed that he would be in the club's squad for their pre-season tour in Australia.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mcfc.co.uk/News/Tour-2015/2015/Official-Manchester-City-Tour-2015-squad-list/1436520345 |access-date=19 July 2015 |publisher=Manchester City FC |date=10 July 2015 |title=Official Tour 2015 squad list |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150715122441/http://www.mcfc.co.uk/News/Tour-2015/2015/Official-Manchester-City-Tour-2015-squad-list/1436520345 |archive-date=15 July 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Denayer signed a new five-year deal on 13 July 2015.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mcfc.co.uk/News/Team-news/2015/July/Denayer-pens-new-five-year-deal/1436789872 |access-date=19 July 2015 |publisher=Manchester City FC |title=Denayer pens new five-year deal |date=13 July 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150715164957/http://www.mcfc.co.uk/News/Team-news/2015/July/Denayer-pens-new-five-year-deal/1436789872 |archive-date=15 July 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

====Loan to Celtic====
On 12 August 2014, [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] signed Denayer on a season-long loan from [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], making him one of [[Ronny Deila]]'s first major signings as Celtic manager.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28754894 |title=Jason Denayer: Celtic sign Manchester City defender on loan |publisher=BBC Sport |date=12 August 2014 |access-date=12 August 2014}}</ref> Denayer revealed that [[Vincent Kompany]] and [[Patrick Vieira]] played a vital role for him in joining the club.<ref>{{cite news|title=I was sold on Celtic move by Vincent Kompany & Patrick Vieira, says Jason Denayer|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/sold-celtic-move-vincent-kompany-4042950|last=Parks|first=Gordon|date=13 August 2014|work=Daily Record |access-date=30 October 2014}}</ref>

He scored on his debut and was named [[man of the match]] in a 6–1 victory at home to [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] in the [[Scottish Premiership]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28716867 |title=Celtic 6–1 Dundee United |publisher=BBC Sport |date=16 August 2014 |access-date=16 August 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.celticfc.net/news/6463 |title=Six of the Best for Brilliant Bhoys |publisher=Celtic FC |date=16 August 2014 |access-date=16 August 2014}}</ref> Four days later, on 20 August 2014, Denayer made his Champions League debut, in a 1–1 draw against [[NK Maribor|Maribor]], where he was part of the starting line-up.<ref>{{cite news|title=Maribor 1–1 Celtic|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28784367|work=BBC Sport|date=20 August 2014|access-date=21 August 2014}}</ref> His second goal came in a 2–1 win over [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] on 13 September 2014.<ref>{{cite news|title=Scottish Premiership: Celtic beat Aberdeen 2–1 at Parkhead|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11787/9468046/three-points-for-celtic-as-jason-denayer-and-kris-commons-score-in-celtics-2-1-win-over-aberdeen|publisher=Sky Sports|date=13 September 2014|access-date=30 October 2014}}</ref> The defender scored again for Celtic on 18 October 2014, in a 5–0 win over [[Ross County F.C.|Ross County]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Ross County 0–5 Celtic|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29580112|work=BBC Sport|date=18 October 2014|access-date=30 October 2014}}</ref> By the end of December, Denayer had made 17 appearances for Celtic<ref>{{cite web|last1=Baillie|first1=Michael|title=Celtic plan to extend Jason Denayer loan deal|url=http://www.express.co.uk/sport/football/548868/Celtic-plan-to-extend-Jason-Denayer-loan-deal|work=Express.co.uk|access-date=9 February 2015|date=26 December 2014}}</ref> and formed a solid partnership with [[Virgil van Dijk]] in central defence.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jason Denayer hopes Virgil van Dijk will resist lure of big-bucks move until the end of the season|url=http://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/celtic/jason-denayer-hopes-virgil-van-dijk-will-resist-lure-of-big-bucks-move-194894n.116481643|work=Evening Times|access-date=9 February 2015|date=20 January 2015}}</ref><ref name="old">{{cite web|title=Jason Denayer hopes Old Firm form will not go unnoticed|url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/football/jason-denayer-hopes-old-firm-form-will-not-go-unnoticed.117729943|work=HeraldScotland|access-date=1 March 2015|date=5 February 2015}}</ref> Denayer commented about playing alongside Van Dijk: "We play well together and he is a very good player", adding "I am also learning from him as well. He has more experience than me and he knows what to say to me. I listen to him because I know he can help make me a better player."<ref name="old" />

Just months after arriving at Celtic, reports claimed that Celtic were keen to extend Denayer's loan spell by another year.<ref>{{cite news|title=Celtic keen to extend Denayer loan deal|url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/football/celtic-keen-to-extend-denayer-loan-deal.25509197|work=The Herald|location=Glasgow|date=3 October 2014|access-date=30 October 2014}}</ref> However, Denayer immediately ruled out joining Celtic on a permanent basis, insisting that he hoped to earn a first team place at Manchester City in the near future.<ref>{{cite news|title=Transfer news: Jason Denayer hoping his future lies at Manchester City|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11065/9530199/transfer-news-jason-denayer-hoping-his-future-lies-at-manchester-city|publisher=Sky Sports|date=23 October 2014|access-date=30 October 2014}}</ref> Manchester City kept an eye on Denayer's progress at Celtic, with [[Manchester City F.C. Reserves and Academy|Development Side]] coach Patrick Vieira stating "When I watch Jason playing for Celtic, or [[Rony Lopes|Marcos Lopes]] playing at Lille, it makes us really proud. The way they are performing lets me know we are doing things the right stuff {{sic}}", and adding "The object is to provide players for the first team, but we know the gap is massive from under-21 to the first team – but this is one way we can get them there."<ref>{{cite web|last=Brennan|first=Stuart|title=Vieira 'proud' of City loan rangers Denayer and Lopes|url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/vieira-proud-city-loan-rangers-8137116?|work=Manchester Evening News|access-date=9 February 2015|date=19 November 2014}}</ref>

Denayer won his first major trophy on 15 March 2015 when he played in Celtic's 2–0 win over Dundee United in the [[2015 Scottish League Cup Final|League Cup Final]] at [[Hampden Park]].<ref name="lcup15">{{cite web|last=McConnell|first=Alison|title=First cup medal ticks all the right boxes for on-loan Celtic star Jason Denayer...now for the Treble|url=http://www.eveningtimes.co.uk/celtic/celticcomment/first-cup-medal-ticks-all-the-right-boxes-for-on-loan-celtic-star-200312n.120705422|work=Evening Times|access-date=30 March 2015|date=15 March 2015}}</ref> He was described as being "strong in the tackle" and "comfortable with the ball".<ref>{{cite web|last=Gannon|first=Michael|title=Man by man ratings: Dundee United 0 Celtic 2, Scottish League Cup Final|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-match-reports/man-man-ratings-dundee-united-5341191|work=Daily Record|access-date=30 March 2015|date=15 March 2015}}</ref> Denayer himself stated that "It is the first cup final and first win of my career, so it was a very special day for me."<ref name="lcup15" /> He also praised Celtic manager [[Ronny Deila]]: "He has been a very good coach for me", adding "I think I have improved and got better at Celtic. He [Deila] has trusted me to play and I have learned so much from that."<ref name="lcup15" />

On 2 May, Celtic were confirmed as Premiership champions when Dundee United defeated nearest competitors [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Spence|first1=Jim|title=Dundee Utd 1–0 Aberdeen|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32447990|access-date=4 May 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=2 May 2015}}</ref> The next day, Denayer was voted the [[PFA Scotland Young Player of the Year]], with his teammate [[Stefan Johansen]] taking [[PFA Scotland Players' Player of the Year|the overall prize]]. After winning the prize, he said when asked if he would remain at Celtic: "I don't know. I need to wait until summer and see what is going to happen... When I came here I just wanted to play some games and take some experience, but now I win trophies and personal trophies so it has gone better than I expected".<ref name=young>{{cite news|title=Stefan Johansen: Celtic midfielder named Scottish PFA player of the year|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32578058|access-date=4 May 2015|work=BBC Sport|date=3 May 2015}}</ref>

====Loan to Galatasaray====
In August 2015, [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]] signed Denayer on a season-long loan from Manchester City.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.hln.be/hln/nl/1301/Premier-League/article/detail/2438987/2015/08/29/Denayer-naar-Galatasaray.dhtml |title=Denayer naar Galatasaray |work=Het Laatste Nieuws |language=nl |date=29 August 2015 |access-date=30 August 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Man City defender joins Galatasaray on loan |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/34112782 |publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=1 September 2015|date=1 September 2015}}</ref> Denayer played his first game for Galatasaray on 15 September 2015, in a [[UEFA Champions League]] tie against [[Atlético Madrid]].<ref name="lw09">{{cite web|title=Loan Watch: Byrne and Denayer make league debuts|url=http://www.mcfc.co.uk/news/team-news/2015/september/loan-watch-byrne-and-denayer-make-league-debuts/1442843565|publisher=Manchester City FC|date=21 September 2015|access-date=26 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151124100721/http://www.mcfc.co.uk/News/Team-news/2015/September/Loan-Watch-Byrne-and-Denayer-make-league-debuts/1442843565|archive-date=24 November 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> Despite a 2–0 defeat, the Belgium defender turned in an impressive performance. He then made his league debut on 19 September in match away against [[Trabzonspor]], playing on the right side of defence, helping his new side keep a clean sheet in a 1–0 victory.<ref>{{cite news|title=Trabzonspor 0–1 Galatasaray|url=http://www.hurriyet.com.tr/spor/futbol/30117675.asp|access-date=7 October 2015|work=Hürriyet Daily News|date=20 September 2015|language=tr}}</ref> Denayer continued to display his natural attributes of pace and power, whilst also improving his reading of the game. Two assists for goals against [[Eskişehirspor]] and [[Gaziantepspor]] also highlighted his ability to contribute to the attacking side of the game.<ref>{{cite web|last=Pollard|first=Rob|title=A Progress Report on Galatasaray's Manchester City Loanee Jason Denayer|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2596368-a-progress-report-on-galatasarays-manchester-city-loanee-jason-denayer|website=Bleacher Report|access-date=1 February 2016|date=7 December 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Galatasaray vs. Gaziantepspor 2–1|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2015/09/26/turkey/super-lig/galatasaray-sk/gaziantepspor/2074374/|website=Soccerway|access-date=1 February 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Galatasaray vs. Eskişehirspor 4–0|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2015/10/29/turkey/super-lig/galatasaray-sk/eskisehirspor/2074410/|website=Soccerway|access-date=1 February 2016}}</ref>

His last match for Galatasaray was in the Turkish Cup Final against [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (football)|Fenerbahçe]] on 26 May 2016. Denayer provided the assist for the only goal of the game on 30 minutes; a flick on from [[Emre Colak]]'s corner on to [[Lukas Podolski]] who headed in from close range.<ref name="tcup">{{cite news|title=Galatasaray: 1 Fenerbahçe: 0 / Kupa Galatasaray'ın... (Maç özeti)|url=http://www.hurriyet.com.tr/galatasaray1-0-fenerbahce-mac-ozeti-40109504|access-date=13 June 2016|work=Hürriyet Daily News|date=26 May 2016}}</ref>

====Loan to Sunderland====
On 31 August 2016, Denayer joined Premier League side [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] on a season-long loan deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.safc.com/news/team-news/2016/august/sunderland-sign-denayer|title=Sunderland sign Denayer|publisher=Sunderland AFC|date=31 August 2016|access-date=31 August 2016}}</ref> However, Sunderland were poor and ended up being relegated. Denayer struggled to perform consistently and was often fielded in midfield instead of his natural position as a defender.<ref>{{cite news|title=Manchester City and entourage of Jason Denayer make decision on his future|url=http://www.mcfcwatch.com/2017/04/26/manchester-city-and-entourage-of-jason-denayer-make-decision-on-his-future/|access-date=23 May 2017|work=City Watch|date=26 April 2017|archive-date=17 May 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170517011010/http://www.mcfcwatch.com/2017/04/26/manchester-city-and-entourage-of-jason-denayer-make-decision-on-his-future/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=David Moyes resigns: What went wrong for him at Sunderland?|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11695/10889147/david-moyes-resigns-what-went-wrong-for-him-at-sunderland|access-date=23 May 2017|work=Sky Sports|date=23 May 2017}}</ref> He was also hindered by a series of niggling injuries towards the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Mennear|first1=Richard|title=End of season player ratings: Who shone and who flopped for Sunderland |url=http://www.shieldsgazette.com/sport/football/sunderland-afc/end-of-season-player-ratings-who-shone-and-who-flopped-for-sunderland-1-8570348|access-date=5 June 2017|work=The Shields Gazette|date=31 May 2017}}</ref>

===Lyon===
On 21 August 2018, Denayer joined [[Ligue 1]] club [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]] for €6.5m, signing a four-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Oatway |first1=Caroline |title=Jason Denayer joins Lyon |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/first-team/first-team-news/2018/august/man-city-jason-denayer-lyon-transfer-news |publisher=Manchester City FC|access-date=21 August 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=News Release: Jason Denayer, 4 years at OL |url=https://www.ol.fr/fr-fr/contenus/articles/2018/08/20/communique-jason-denayer-sengage-avec-lol-pour-les-prochaines-saisons |publisher=Olympique Lyonnais |access-date=21 August 2018 |language=fr}}</ref> Denayer was a regular for the team, having 31 starts in the [[2018–19 Olympique Lyonnais season|2018–19 season]] and scoring two goals. He faced his former employers, Manchester City, in the [[2019–20 UEFA Champions League#Quarter-finals|Champions League quarter-finals]] on 15 August 2020, as Lyon won 3–1.{{Citation needed|date=June 2022}}

==International career==
[[File:Jason Denayer 2015.jpg|150px|thumb|Denayer playing for Belgium in 2015]]

From 2013 on, Denayer represented Belgium at different levels, such as [[Belgium national under-19 football team|Belgium U19]] and [[Belgium national under-21 football team|Belgium U21]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Manchester City Youth International Round Up|url=http://www.mcfc.co.uk/News/EDS-news/2014/Youth-international-round-up-5-March|publisher=Manchester City FC|date=5 March 2014|access-date=21 August 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141007025018/http://www.mcfc.co.uk/news/eds-news/2014/youth-international-round-up-5-march|archive-date=7 October 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 2 October 2014, national team manager [[Marc Wilmots]] called him for the first time to the Belgium national team for their [[UEFA Euro 2016 qualifying|Euro 2016 qualification match]] against [[Andorra national football team|Andorra]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.belgianfootball.be/nl/nieuws/24-rode-duivels-voor-andorra-en-bosni%C3%AB-en-herzegovina|title=24 Rode Duivels voor Andorra en Bosnië en Herzegovina|language=nl|publisher=Royal Belgian Football Association|date=2 October 2014 |access-date=2 October 2014}}</ref> Denayer was included in further international squads for Euro qualifier matches against [[Bosnia national football team|Bosnia]] and [[Wales national football team|Wales]] and for a friendly against [[Iceland national football team|Iceland]].<ref name="sw">{{cite web|title=J. Denayer|url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/jason-denayer/314033/|publisher=Peerform Group|work=Soccerway|access-date=7 July 2017}}</ref> However, he was an unused substitute in each of these four games.<ref name="sw"/>

Denayer made his senior international debut for [[Belgium national football team|Belgium]] on 31 March 2015 in a [[UEFA Euro 2016]] qualifier away to [[Israel national football team|Israel]] at the [[Teddy Stadium]] in [[Jerusalem]]. He replaced [[Aston Villa]] striker [[Christian Benteke]] in the 67th minute of a 1–0 win which put Belgium at the top of the group.<ref>{{cite web|title=Israel 0–1 Belgium|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32140200|work=BBC Sport|access-date=31 March 2015 |date=31 March 2015}}</ref> Denayer made his first start for the senior side on 7 June 2015, in a friendly match against [[France national football team|France]] in [[Paris]] which Belgium won 4–3.<ref name="rbjd">{{cite web|title=Jason Denayer|url=http://static.belgianfootball.be/project/publiek/jrinterfr/speler_PH_6411.htm#itop|publisher=Royal Belgian Football Association|access-date=9 June 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=France 3–4 Belgium, 7 June 2015|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2015/06/07/world/friendlies/france/belgium/1987008/|publisher=Perform Group|work=Soccerway|access-date=9 June 2015}}</ref> Manager Marc Wilmots substituted Denayer late on in the match for a minor knock sustained, and pointed out that it was after this that France scored twice to pull the game back to 4–3.<ref>{{cite news|title=Jason Denayer: Team mates told me to play the Celtic way as I prepared for first Belgium start|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/jason-denayer-team-mates-told-5849512|access-date=9 June 2015|work=Daily Record|date=9 June 2015}}</ref>

He was named in Belgium's 23-man squad for the [[UEFA Euro 2016|2016 European Championships]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Marc Wilmots unveils Belgium squad for Euro 2016|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/29908/10300579/marc-wilmots-unveils-belgium-squad-for-euro-2016|access-date=1 September 2016|work=Sky Sports|date=31 May 2016}}</ref> Denayer only played once, coming in to an injury depleted Belgian defence for their quarter-final tie against [[Wales national football team|Wales]]. Belgium, and Denayer in particular, were run ragged by Wales and lost 3–1.<ref>{{cite news|title=Belgium coach Marc Wilmots admits lapses by young makeshift defence costed match with Wales|url=http://www.foxsports.com.au/football/the-euros/belgium-coach-marc-wilmots-admits-lapses-by-young-makeshift-defence-costed-match-with-wales/news-story/819ff4fbf68cbbbf6bf57e680cc02595|access-date=1 September 2016|work=Fox Sports}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Phillips|first=Mitch|title=Analysis – Belgium floored by Denayer's defensive disaster|url=http://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-euro-wal-bel-analysis-idUKKCN0ZH631|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160914221543/http://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-euro-wal-bel-analysis-idUKKCN0ZH631|url-status=dead|archive-date=14 September 2016|access-date=1 September 2016|work=Reuters|date=1 July 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Who starred and who flopped as Wales stunned Belgium to reach Euro 2016 semi-finals?|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2016/07/01/wales-vs-belgium-euro-2016-quarter-final-player-ratings/jason-denayer/|access-date=1 September 2016|work=The Telegraph|date=1 July 2016}}</ref>

On 17 May 2021, Denayer was included in the final 26-man squad for the re-arranged [[UEFA Euro 2020]].<ref name="Red Devils Squad">{{cite news |url=https://www.rbfa.be/en/news/selection-red-devils-euro-2020-has-been-announced |title=Selection of the Red Devils for EURO 2020 has been announced |work=[[Royal Belgian Football Association]] |date=17 May 2021 |access-date=17 May 2021}}</ref>
