'''Jordi Gómez García-Penche''' (born 24 May 1985) is a Spanish former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[central midfielder]].

After playing for the [[reserve team]]s of [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] and [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]], he spent most of his career in England, mainly with [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]] with whom he won the [[FA Cup]] in [[2013 FA Cup final|2013]].

==Club career==
===Early career===
Born in [[Barcelona]], [[Catalonia]], Gómez emerged through [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]]'s youth ranks.<ref name=PFM/> He played once for the first team in competitive games, [[Substitute (association football)|coming on]] for [[Thiago Motta]] in the 68th minute of a [[2005–06 Copa del Rey|6–0 win]] against [[Zamora CF|Zamora]] in the [[Copa del Rey]] on 11 January 2006.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2006/01/11/futbol/1137019926.html|title=El Barça aumenta el récord por inercia|trans-title=Barça extend record through inertia|newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]|first=Carlos|last=Guisasola|language=es|date=11 January 2006|access-date=1 March 2016}}</ref> 

Gómez completed his development with neighbours [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]], making his official debut with the latter in a 4–0 away defeat to [[Real Murcia CF]] on 23 March 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=226638&cc=5739|title=Murcia 4–0 Espanyol|publisher=[[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]]|date=23 March 2008|access-date=17 February 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120716045558/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=226638&cc=5739|archive-date=16 July 2012}}</ref> He appeared in two more [[La Liga]] matches during his tenure, always as a second-half substitute.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/20121124/fc-barcelona/barca-wigan-messi-jordi-gomez_54355607398.html|title=Jordi Gómez, otra joya de la cosecha de Oporto|trans-title=Jordi Gómez, another gem of the Porto harvest|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|first=José Luis|last=Artús|language=es|date=24 November 2012|access-date=3 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://inglaterraencasa.com/jordi-gomez-unico-espanol-de-la-plantilla-del-sunderland-afc/|title=Jordi Gómez es el único español de la plantilla del Sunderland AFC|trans-title=Jordi Gómez is the only Spaniard in Sunderland AFC's squad|publisher=Inglaterra en Casa|language=es|date=15 July 2015|access-date=3 September 2025}}</ref>

===Swansea City===
On 6 June 2008, Gómez signed for [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]] of the [[Football League Championship]] on a [[2008–09 Football League Championship|season]]-long [[Loan (association football)|loan]], for a fee of £200,000;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/s/swansea_city/7436259.stm|title=Spanish duo complete Liberty move|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=6 June 2008|access-date=16 August 2009}}</ref> his teammate [[Albert Serrán]] also made the move, albeit in a permanent situation.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/20120531/futbol/internacional/jordi-gomez-wigan-swan-premier-league-messi-roberto-martinez_54301332632.html|title=Jordi Gómez: "Lo he tenido difícil con la afición del Wigan. Han hecho falta más resultados y goles"|trans-title=Jordi Gómez: "I had a tough time with Wigan's supporters. More results and goals was what we needed"|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Alexa|last=Botines|language=es|date=31 May 2012|access-date=3 September 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.swanseacity.com/news/record-signing-joins-list-spanish-swans|title=Record signing joins list of Spanish Swans|publisher=Swansea City A.F.C.|date=11 August 2016|access-date=3 September 2025}}</ref> He scored the winning goal with a deflected [[Free kick (association football)|free kick]] against rivals [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]] on 23 September, in the first [[South Wales derby]] for seven years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/league_cup/7626773.stm|title=Swansea 1–0 Cardiff|publisher=BBC Sport|date=23 September 2008|access-date=16 August 2009}}</ref>

Scouts describe Gómez as having "a lovely ability to receive the ball in space or if he is marked tightly, find space after his first touch."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/blog/2009/feb/24/swansea-jordi-gomez-scouting-report|title=Scouting report: Jordi Gómez, Swansea City|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|first=Steve|last=Claridge|date=24 February 2009|access-date=16 August 2009}}</ref> Whilst on loan, reports surfaced that Swansea wanted to sign him permanently<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11688/5098047/|title=Swans keen to keep Gomez|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|first=Chris|last=Burton|date=25 March 2009|access-date=19 December 2012}}</ref> and other teams were supposedly interested in acquiring his services,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11661/5353116/|title=Boro linked with Gomez|publisher=Sky Sports|first=Francisco|last=Acedo|date=28 May 2009|access-date=19 December 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.dailyrecord.co.uk/sport/other-sports/celtic-eye-2m-swoop-for-espanyol-1015745|title=Celtic eye £2m swoop for Espanyol star Jordi Gomez|newspaper=[[Daily Record (Scotland)|Daily Record]]|first=James|last=Traynor|date=26 March 2009|access-date=19 December 2012}}</ref> but nothing came of it, as manager [[Roberto Martínez]] eventually announced the club would not be able to retain the player due to his high price tag.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11688/5247411/|title=Swans – No bid for Gomez|publisher=Sky Sports|first=Chris|last=Galea|date=27 April 2009|access-date=19 December 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11688/5265102/|title=Gomez in dark over future|publisher=Sky Sports|date=1 May 2009|access-date=19 December 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11688/5341988/|title=Martinez doubts Gomez return|publisher=Sky Sports|date=22 May 2009|access-date=19 December 2012}}</ref>

===Wigan Athletic===
Gómez finished the season with 14 goals in all competitions and returned to Espanyol, being immediately sold to [[Premier League]] side [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]] on a three-year contract on 19 June 2009, with the transfer fee estimated to be in the region of £1.7 million – the move also meant he would be reunited with his former Swansea boss, compatriot Martínez.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/w/wigan_athletic/8109864.stm|title=Wigan capture Gomez from Espanyol|publisher=BBC Sport|date=19 June 2009|access-date=19 June 2009}}</ref> He debuted in a 2–0 victory over [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] on 15 August,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/8197493.stm|title=Aston Villa 0–2 Wigan|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Mandeep|last=Sanghera|date=15 August 2009|access-date=16 August 2009}}</ref> and netted his first goal for the club against [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] on 5 December, albeit in a 2–3 home loss.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/8388601.stm|title=Wigan 2–3 Birmingham|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Les|last=Roopanarine|date=5 December 2009|access-date=5 December 2009}}</ref>

Gómez scored his second league goal in a 2–0 defeat of [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] on 2 October 2010. However, during the match, he escaped suffering a [[Human leg|leg]] injury after a challenge from [[Karl Henry]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11095/6422105/|title=Martinez feared leg break|publisher=Sky Sports|first=James|last=Dall|date=2 October 2010|access-date=19 December 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.wigantoday.net/sport/wigan-athletic/patience-pays-off-for-jordi-1-1683822|title=Patience pays off for Jordi|newspaper=[[Wigan Evening Post]]|date=4 October 2010|access-date=2 January 2013}}</ref>

On 17 December 2011, Gómez scored the equaliser for the hosts in a 1–1 draw against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], his fourth goal in five league games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16124079|title=Wigan 1–1 Chelsea|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Sam|last=Sheringham|date=17 December 2011|access-date=16 February 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2011/dec/17/wigan-athletic-chelsea-premier-league|title=Jordi Gómez grabs late Wigan Athletic equaliser to foil Chelsea|newspaper=The Guardian|first=Paul|last=Wilson|date=17 December 2011|access-date=16 February 2012}}</ref> He netted the second goal at [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] in the eighth minute of an eventual 2–1 away win on 16 April 2012 at the [[Emirates Stadium]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/317956?cc=5739|title=Wigan shock misfiring Gunners|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=16 April 2012|access-date=16 April 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120419220718/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/317956?cc=5739|archive-date=19 April 2012}}</ref> and the Latics once again [[2011–12 Premier League|managed to avoid relegation]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17890899|title=Blackburn have been relegated to the Championship after losing at home to Wigan, whose Premier League status is secure for next season|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Phil|last=Dawkes|date=7 May 2012|access-date=24 November 2012}}</ref>

On 28 August 2012, Gómez scored once as Wigan defeated [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] 4–1 away to [[2012–13 Football League Cup|reach the third round]] of the [[Football League Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/match-reports/nottingham-forest-1-4-wigan-maynor-1283844|title=Nott'm Forest 1–4 Wigan: First-half blitz helps Latics dodge banana-skin|newspaper=[[Daily Mirror]]|location=London|date=28 August 2012|access-date=29 August 2012}}</ref> On 24 November, he netted a [[hat-trick]] to help his club win 3–2 at home against [[Reading F.C.|Reading]] at the [[DW Stadium]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20374799|title=Wigan 3–2 Reading|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Neil|last=Johnston|date=24 November 2012|access-date=28 November 2012}}</ref> becoming just the second Spaniard to achieve the feat in the Premier League after [[Fernando Torres]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11682/8285417/Jordi-Gomez-expresses-joy-at-scoring-a-hat-trick-against-Reading|title=Jordi Gomez expresses joy at scoring a hat-trick against Reading|publisher=Sky Sports|date=26 November 2012|access-date=19 December 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/2874/team-of-the-week/2012/11/26/3555792/premier-league-team-of-the-week-hat-trick-hero-gomez-joins|title=Premier League Team of the Week: Hat-trick hero Gomez joins Anderson & Reina|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|date=26 November 2012|access-date=19 December 2012}}</ref>

On 9 March 2013, Gómez provided the cross from which [[Maynor Figueroa]] opened the scoring at [[Everton F.C.|Everton]], and he added the final 3–0 for his team's third goal in as many minutes, in an eventual qualification to [[2012–13 FA Cup|the semi-finals]] of the [[FA Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21639357|title=Everton 0–3 Wigan|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Phil|last=McNulty|date=9 March 2013|access-date=17 March 2013}}</ref> He helped them [[2013 FA Cup Final|win the competition]], being replaced after 81 minutes by [[Ben Watson (footballer born July 1985)|Ben Watson]], who went on to score the winning goal;<ref name=FACUP>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22409634|title=FA Cup final: Manchester City 0–1 Wigan Athletic|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Phil|last=McNulty|date=11 May 2013|access-date=19 May 2013}}</ref> however, only three days later, with him on the pitch again, the side were relegated from the top division following a 1–4 away defeat to Arsenal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22430454|title=Arsenal 4–1 Wigan|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Chris|last=McKenna|date=14 May 2013|access-date=19 May 2013}}</ref>

Gómez remained at Wigan for [[2013–14 Football League Championship|their first season]] back in the Championship, and also participated in the club's [[2013–14 UEFA Europa League|inaugural campaign]] in the [[UEFA Europa League]]. On 12 December 2013, in the last group stage match, he scored a [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty kick]] to put his team ahead at [[NK Maribor|Maribor]], but the Slovene ultimately won 2–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25303137|title=NK Maribor 2–1 Wigan|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Gary|last=Rose|date=12 December 2013|access-date=3 November 2014}}</ref>

===Sunderland===
On 29 May 2014, Gómez signed a three-year deal with [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] on a [[Free transfer (association football)|free transfer]] after his contract at Wigan expired.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.safc.com/news/team-news/2014/may/gomez-agrees-move|title=Gomez agrees move|publisher=Sunderland A.F.C.|date=29 May 2014|access-date=29 May 2014}}</ref> He made his debut on 16 August, coming on as a 68th-minute substitute for [[Jack Rodwell]] in a 2–2 draw away to [[West Bromwich Albion F.C|West Bromwich Albion]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28718388|title=West Bromwich Albion 2–2 Sunderland|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Jamie|last=Strickland|date=16 August 2014|access-date=27 August 2014}}</ref> and scored his first goal 11 days later in a 3–0 [[2014–15 Football League Cup|League Cup]] second-round victory at Birmingham City.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/28862763|title=Birmingham City 0–3 Sunderland|publisher=BBC Sport|date=27 August 2014|access-date=27 August 2014}}</ref>

Gómez scored his first league goal for his new team on 3 November, the second in a 3–1 away win over [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29782372|title=Crystal Palace 1–3 Sunderland|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Marc|last=Higginson|date=3 November 2014|access-date=3 November 2014}}</ref> His third goal of [[2014–15 Premier League|the campaign]] came on 13 December, where he scored a penalty to open the scoring in a 1–1 draw at home to [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30357563|title=Sunderland 1–1 West Ham United|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Luke|last=Reddy|date=13 December 2014|access-date=15 May 2015}}</ref>

On 3 February 2015, Gómez netted another penalty in a 3–1 win at [[Fulham F.C|Fulham]] in an [[2014–15 FA Cup|FA Cup fourth round replay]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30991113|title=Fulham 1–3 Sunderland|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Michael|last=Emons|date=3 February 2015|access-date=15 May 2015}}</ref> On 2 May, again from 12 yards, he scored once in each half as the ''Black Cats'' defeated [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] 2–1 at the [[Stadium of Light]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32460246|title=Sunderland 2–1 Southampton|publisher=BBC Sport|date=2 May 2015|access-date=3 May 2015}}</ref> The following week, his shot was deflected in by [[Danny Graham (footballer)|Danny Graham]] to give the latter his first Sunderland goal, in a 2–0 away victory over [[Everton F.C.|Everton]];<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32561779|title=Everton 0–2 Sunderland|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Jamie|last=Strickland|date=9 May 2015|access-date=15 May 2015}}</ref> still in that month, he was ruled out for the last three games of the season with a fractured kneecap.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sunderlandecho.com/sport/sunderland-afc/dick-advocaat-backs-liam-bridcutt-for-sunderland-s-showdown-against-leicester-1-7263535|title=Dick Advocaat backs Liam Bridcutt for Sunderland's showdown against Leicester|newspaper=[[Sunderland Echo]]|date=15 May 2015|access-date=15 May 2015|archive-date=17 May 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150517080132/http://www.sunderlandecho.com/sport/sunderland-afc/dick-advocaat-backs-liam-bridcutt-for-sunderland-s-showdown-against-leicester-1-7263535|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In the 2016 winter [[transfer window]], after making only six appearances in the first half of [[2015–16 Premier League|the season]], Gómez was loaned to Championship club [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] until June.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35467269|title=Jordi Gomez: Blackburn sign Sunderland midfielder on loan|publisher=BBC Sport|date=1 February 2016|access-date=2 February 2016}}</ref> He scored in his debut on 6 February, helping to a 1–1 draw at [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2016/feb/06/middlesbrough-blackburn-rovers-championship-match-report|title=David Nugent earns Middlesbrough point against Blackburn Rovers|newspaper=The Guardian|first=Michael|last=Walker|date=6 February 2016|access-date=6 February 2016}}</ref> He netted twice three weeks later, including a last-minute winner from a 30-yard free kick in a 3–2 win against [[Milton Keynes Dons F.C.|Milton Keynes Dons]] at [[Ewood Park]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eurosport.co.uk/football/jordi-gomez-saves-the-best-for-last-as-blackburn-beat-mk-dons_sto5226198/story.shtml|title=Jordi Gomez saves the best for last as Blackburn beat MK Dons|publisher=[[Eurosport]]|date=27 February 2016|access-date=27 February 2016}}</ref>

===Three clubs in two years===
On 17 August 2016, Gómez rejoined Wigan Athletic on a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sunderlandecho.com/sport/football/sunderland-afc/sunderland-midfielder-re-joins-wigan-athletic-1-8073535|title=Sunderland midfielder re-joins Wigan Athletic|newspaper=Sunderland Echo|first=Richard|last=Mennear|date=17 August 2016|access-date=17 August 2016}}</ref> He returned to Spain after nearly nine years on 31 January 2017, signing with [[Rayo Vallecano]] of the [[Segunda División]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/12691/10749766/jordi-gomez-joins-rayo-vallecano-on-loan|title=Jordi Gomez joins Rayo Vallecano from Wigan Athletic|publisher=Sky Sports|date=31 January 2017|access-date=31 January 2017}}</ref>

Gómez moved to Bulgarian club [[PFC Levski Sofia|Levski Sofia]] on 6 July 2017, on a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://levski.bg/news/details/176221|title=Жорди Гомес подписа за две години с ПФК Левски|trans-title=Jordi Gómez signed for two years with PFC Levski|publisher=Levski Sofia|language=bg|date=6 July 2017|access-date=6 July 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618052337/https://levski.bg/news/details/176221|archive-date=18 June 2018}}</ref>

===Omonia===
On 16 August 2018, Gómez joined [[AC Omonia|Omonia]] of the [[Cypriot First Division]] on a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.omonoiafc.com.cy/%CE%BA%CE%B1%CF%84%CE%B1%CF%81%CF%87%CE%AE%CE%BD-%CF%83%CF%85%CE%BC%CF%86%CF%89%CE%BD%CE%AF%CE%B1-%CE%BC%CE%B5-jordi-gomez/|title=Καταρχήν συμφωνία με Jordi Gomez|trans-title=Agreement in principle with Jordi Gómez|publisher=AC Omonia|language=el|date=16 August 2018|access-date=31 January 2020}}</ref> Already as [[Captain (association football)|team captain]], he agreed to extensions until 2021 and 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.omonoiafc.com.cy/%ce%b5%cf%80%ce%ad%ce%ba%cf%84%ce%b1%cf%83%ce%b7-%cf%83%cf%85%ce%bd%ce%b5%cf%81%ce%b3%ce%b1%cf%83%ce%af%ce%b1%cf%82-%ce%bc%ce%b5-jordi-gomez/|title=Επέκταση συνεργασίας με Jordi Gomez!|trans-title=Extension of cooperation with Jordi Gómez!|publisher=AC Omonia|language=el|date=26 July 2019|access-date=28 June 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.omonoiafc.com.cy/%cf%83%cf%84%ce%b7%ce%bd-%ce%bf%ce%bc%ce%bf%ce%bd%ce%bf%ce%b9%ce%b1-%ce%ba%ce%b1%ce%b9-%cf%84%ce%b7-%ce%bd%ce%ad%ce%b1-%cf%83%ce%b5%ce%b6%cf%8c%ce%bd-%ce%bf-%cf%84%ce%b6%ce%b9%cf%8c%cf%81%ce%bd%cf%84/|title=Στην ΟΜΟΝΟΙΑ και τη νέα σεζόν ο Τζιόρντι Γκόμεθ!|trans-title=Jordi Gómez at OMONIA and the new season!|publisher=AC Omonia|language=el|date=12 May 2021|access-date=9 July 2022}}</ref>

Gómez's team was leading the [[2019–20 Cypriot First Division|2019–20 championship]] when the season was abandoned due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Cyprus|COVID-19 pandemic]]; although they were not awarded the title, they did secure a place in the [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League|qualifying rounds]] of the [[UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.financialmirror.com/2020/05/30/project-omonia-fc-expands-to-europe/|title=Project Omonia FC expands to Europe|newspaper=[[Financial Mirror]]|first=Kyriacos|last=Kiliaris|date=30 May 2020|access-date=31 August 2020}}</ref>

The [[2020–21 Cypriot First Division|following campaign]] proved successful for both team and player, as Gómez helped them qualify for the group stage of a European competition for the first time in history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-champions-omo-rsb-report-idUKKBN26735O|title=Omonoia knock out Red Star to reach Champions League playoff round|agency=[[Reuters]]|date=16 September 2020|access-date=28 June 2022}}</ref> On 29 October 2020, he scored a goal from inside his half in a 2–1 home loss against [[PSV Eindhoven|PSV]] in the [[2020–21 UEFA Europa League|Europa League]], breaking the record for the furthest distance for a goal ever scored in the competition.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/soccer/news/uefa-europa-league-produces-another-crazy-goal-from-halfway-line-this-time-from-jordi-gomez-vs-psv/|title=UEFA Europa League produces another crazy goal from halfway line -- this time from Jordi Gomez vs. PSV|publisher=[[CBS Sports]]|first=Gabriel|last=Fernandez|date=29 October 2020|access-date=29 October 2020}}</ref> He ended the domestic league as a champion, Omonia's first in 11 years.<ref name=CFD>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/futbol-internacional/2021/05/20/60a5a7c622601d013b8b4584.html|title=Jordi Gómez: de ganar la FA Cup con el Wigan a campeón de Liga en Chipre con Omonia|trans-title=Jordi Gómez: from winning the FA Cup with Wigan to being League champion in Cyprus with Omonia|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|first=Alberto|last=Rubio|language=es|date=20 May 2021|access-date=1 June 2021}}</ref>

On 25 November 2021, Gómez scored again from his half in the 89th minute of a 2–2 away draw at [[Qarabağ FK|Qarabağ]] in the [[2021–22 UEFA Europa Conference League|Europa Conference League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.24sports.com.cy/gr/sports/podosfairo/kypros/a-katigoria/omonoia/karampax-omonoia-11ades|title=Μαγεία Γκόμεθ… παλικαρίσιος βαθμός|trans-title=|publisher=24 Sports|language=el|date=25 November 2021|access-date=28 June 2022}}</ref> The following February, he suffered a ruptured knee ligament which kept him out of action for several months.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://goal.philenews.com/podosfero/kypros/a-katigoria/omonoia/terastio-pligma-me-gkometh-anammena-karvouna-stin-omonoia/|title=Τεράστιο πλήγμα με Γκόμεθ, σε αναμμένα "κάρβουνα" στην Ομόνοια|trans-title=|publisher=Phile News|first=Kostas|last=Kallis|language=el|date=5 February 2022|access-date=28 June 2022}}</ref> He scored his last goal for the club on 5 January in the 1–1 away draw against [[Pafos FC|Pafos]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://omada.reporter.com.cy/football-cyprus/article/536290/o-ggometh-pire-tin-boykia-apo-tin-pafo-kai-charise-ton-bathmo-stin-omonoia|title=Ο Γκόμεθ πήρε την μπουκιά από την Πάφο και χάρισε τον βαθμό στην Ομόνοια|trans-title=Gómez took a bite at Paphos and rescued point for Omonia|publisher=Omada|language=el|date=5 January 2022|access-date=28 June 2022}}</ref> and in May it was announced that the 37-year-old would not be retained.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.omonoiafc.com.cy/%ce%b1%cf%81%cf%87%ce%b7%ce%b3%ce%ad-%ce%ae%cf%81%ce%b8%ce%b5-%ce%b7-%cf%8e%cf%81%ce%b1-%ce%b3%ce%b9%ce%b1-%cf%84%ce%bf-%cf%80%ce%b9%ce%bf-%ce%bc%ce%b5%ce%b3%ce%ac%ce%bb%ce%bf-%ce%b5%cf%85%cf%87/|title=Αρχηγέ, ήρθε η ώρα για το πιο μεγάλο ευχαριστώ!|trans-title=Chief, it's time for the biggest thank you!|publisher=AC Omonia|language=el|date=31 May 2022|access-date=28 June 2022}}</ref>

===Later career===
Gómez signed a one-year deal with [[Cypriot Second Division]] side [[PAC Omonia 29M]] in November 2022, effective from 1 January 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://goal.philenews.com/podosfero/kypros/v-katigoria/omonoia-29is-maiou/episimo-o-tzornti-gkometh-stin-omonoia-29is-maiou/|title=Επίσημο: Ο Τζόρντι Γκόμεθ στην Ομόνοια 29ης Μαΐου!|trans-title=Official: Jordi Gómez to Omonia 29 May!|publisher=Phile News|language=el|date=29 November 2022|access-date=25 March 2023}}</ref>

'''Timothy Tarpeh Weah''' (born February 22, 2000) is an American professional [[association football|soccer]] player who plays as a [[winger (association football)|winger]], [[right-back]] or [[right wing-back]] for [[Ligue 1]] club [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]], whom he [[captain (association football)|captain]]s, and the [[United States men's national soccer team|United States national team]].

Weah made his professional debut for [[Ligue 1]] club [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]] in 2018, winning [[Ligue 1]] twice and the [[Trophée des Champions]] once. He won a [[Scottish Premiership]] and [[Scottish Cup]] [[Double (association football)|double]] on loan at [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] in 2019. He then joined [[Lille OSC|Lille]], winning another Ligue 1 title and Trophée des Champions in 2021. In July 2023 he joined [[Serie A]] club [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] and won the [[2023–24 Coppa Italia]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=May 15, 2024 |title=USMNT stars Weston McKennie and Tim Weah lift a trophy as Juventus claim Coppa Italia with victory over Atalanta {{!}} Goal.com US |url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/lists/weston-mckennie-tim-weah-usmnt-coppa-italia-juventus/blt5979575ec00f2bd1 |access-date=May 15, 2024 |website=goal.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

In March 2018, Weah earned his first senior international [[cap (association football)|cap]] for the United States. He was part of the squad that won the [[CONCACAF Nations League]] in [[2021 CONCACAF Nations League Finals|2021]], [[2023 CONCACAF Nations League Finals|2023]], and [[2024 CONCACAF Nations League Finals|2024]].

Weah is the son of [[George Weah]], the former [[President of Liberia]], who was previously also a professional soccer player, having won the [[Ballon d'Or]] in [[1995 Ballon d'Or|1995]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=December 2, 2022 |title=Timothy Weah – From stepping out of legendary father's shadow to being praised by Pele |work=The Times of India |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/fifa-world-cup-2022/fifa-world-cup-2022-timothy-weah-from-stepping-out-of-legendary-fathers-shadow-to-being-praised-by-pele/articleshow/95936933.cms |access-date=September 4, 2023 |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

==Early and personal life==
Weah was born on February 22, 2000, in [[Brooklyn]], New York, to Liberian [[George Weah]] (at the time a professional footballer) and his Jamaican wife [[Clar Weah|Clar]]. George Weah was elected as the [[President of Liberia|25th President of Liberia]] in 2018, after serving three years in the [[Senate of Liberia]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Udoh |first=Colin |date=June 8, 2021 |title=Liberia has 'loads of Tim Weahs' after USMNT striker becomes cap-tied |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/liberia/story/4403232/liberia-has-loads-of-tim-weahs-after-usmnt-striker-becomes-cap-tied |access-date=November 21, 2022 |website=ESPN|language=en}}</ref>

Weah has two older siblings, [[George Weah Jr.|George Jr.]] and Tita. He spent his early life in Brooklyn, [[Valley Stream, New York|Valley Stream]], New York, and [[Pembroke Pines, Florida|Pembroke Pines]], Florida. Weah is fluent in English and French and enjoys producing [[trap music|trap soul]] music.<ref name="USSF-Five">{{cite news |date=October 16, 2017 |title=Five Things to Know About U-17 MNT Striker Tim Weah |url=https://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2017/05/02/12/51/20170501-feat-u17mnt-five-things-to-know-about-tim-weah-son-of-george-weah |publisher=U.S. Soccer |access-date=March 3, 2018}}</ref> He is close friends with fellow soccer player [[Tyler Adams]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46851603 |title=Timothy Weah: USA teammate backs 'dynamic' PSG forward at Celtic |date=January 13, 2019 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> as well as former [[Lille OSC|Lille]] teammates [[Jonathan David]] and [[Angel Gomes]].<ref>{{cite news |language=fr |url=https://lepetitlillois.com/2021/10/31/timothy-weah-evoque-sa-relation-avec-jonathan-david-et-angel-gomes |title=Timothy Weah évoque sa relation avec Jonathan David et Angel Gomes |last=Bja |first=Rayan |date=October 31, 2021 |website=Le Petit Lillois |access-date=July 6, 2023}}</ref> His cousin, [[Kyle Duncan (soccer)|Kyle Duncan]], is also a professional soccer player for [[New York Red Bulls]] in [[Major League Soccer]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Showell|first=Alex|date=August 18, 2016|title=U.S. U-20 defender Kyle Duncan promoted to Valenciennes first team|url=https://www.starsandstripesfc.com/2016/8/18/12528468/u-s-u-20-defender-kyle-duncan-promoted-to-valenciennes-first-team|access-date=August 8, 2020|website=Stars and Stripes FC|language=en}}</ref> He is not related to Liberian-born footballer [[Patrick Weah]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://zonecoverage.com/2021/mn-united/wayward-weah-mnufcs-prodigy-is-carving-his-own-path/|title=Wayward Weah: MNUFC's Prodigy Is Carving His Own Path|first=Jacob|last=Schneider|date=May 9, 2021|website=Zone Coverage}}</ref>

==Club career==
=== Early career ===
Weah was taught soccer by his father and while in Florida played for West Pines United,<ref name="SA-2015">{{cite news|last=Woitalla|first=Mike|date=April 14, 2015|title=George Weah's son progresses in U.S. national team program|work=[[Soccer America]]|url=https://www.socceramerica.com/publications/article/63306/george-weahs-son-progresses-in-us-national-team.html|access-date=March 3, 2018}}</ref> before moving back to New York and joining the Rosedale Soccer Club in [[Queens]], New York, owned by his uncle.<ref name="USSF-Five"/> Weah played three seasons with BW Gottschee, a team in the [[U.S. Soccer Development Academy]] system, and transferred to the [[New York Red Bulls Academy]] in 2013.<ref name="USSF-Five"/> He had a trial with [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] at the age of 13.<ref>{{cite news|date=March 29, 2013|title=Son of Weah having Chelsea trial|publisher=ESPN|url=http://en.espn.co.uk/football/sport/story/199844.html|access-date=March 3, 2018}}</ref> Weah relocated to France in 2014 to join the [[Paris Saint-Germain Academy]]. In his first start with the academy team, he scored a hat-trick in an 8–1 victory for PSG over Bulgarian side [[PFC Ludogorets Razgrad|Ludogorets Razgrad]] in the [[UEFA Youth League]].<ref name="ESPN-Contract">{{cite news|last=Johnson|first=Jonathan|date=July 3, 2017|title=PSG sign Timothy Weah, son of former Ballon d'Or winner, to first pro contract|publisher=ESPN|url=http://www.espn.com/soccer/paris-saint-germain/story/3152626/psg-sign-timothy-weahson-of-former-ballon-dor-winnerto-first-pro-contract|access-date=March 3, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|date=September 28, 2016|title=Hat-trick for Weah as Paris score eight|publisher=[[UEFA]]|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefayouthleague/news/0253-0d04680ba70e-34fa1b8e2006-1000--hat-trick-for-weah-as-paris-score-eight/|access-date=March 3, 2018}}</ref>

===Paris Saint-Germain===
[[File:FC Salzburg gegen Paris St. Germain (UEFA Youth League-21. Februar 2017) 17.jpg|thumb|Weah (right) and [[Claudio Gomes]] with PSG at [[FC Red Bull Salzburg|Red Bull Salzburg]] in the [[UEFA Youth League]] in 2017]]
On July 3, 2017, Weah signed a three-year professional contract with [[Paris Saint-Germain F.C.|Paris Saint-Germain]], the club for whom his father had played in the 1990s.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Kay |first=Stanley |date=July 3, 2017 |title=USA U-17 forward Timothy Weah signs first professional contract with PSG |url=https://www.si.com/planet-futbol/2017/07/03/timothy-weah-george-psg-contract |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=March 3, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Johnson |first=Jonathan |date=July 3, 2017 |title=Big things expected of Weah at PSG and by the United States |url=http://www.espn.com/soccer/club/paris-saint-germain/160/blog/post/3152694/big-things-expected-of-timothy-weah-at-psg-and-by-the-united-states |publisher=ESPN |access-date=March 3, 2018}}</ref> He spent most of the season with the reserves in the [[Championnat National 2 (1993–2026)|Championnat National 2]] and the under-19 squad in the UEFA Youth League.<ref>{{cite news |date=March 3, 2018 |title=8312 jours après le dernier match de son père, Timothy Weah a débuté avec le PSG |trans-title=8,312 days after his father's last match, Timothy Weah starts for PSG |url=https://www.eurosport.fr/football/ligue-1/2017-2018/8312-jours-apres-le-dernier-match-de-son-pere-timothy-weah-a-debute-avec-le-psg_sto6662013/story.shtml |publisher=[[Eurosport]] |language=fr |agency=[[Agence France-Presse]] |access-date=March 3, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Kennedy |first=Paul |date=March 3, 2018 |title=U.S. Abroad Tracker (25 and younger): Tim Weah called up for French leader PSG's game at Troyes |url=https://www.socceramerica.com/publications/article/76980/us-abroad-tracker-25-and-younger-tim-weah-cal.html?edition=18710 |work=Soccer America |access-date=March 3, 2018}}</ref>

Weah was named to the first-team squad for a Ligue 1 fixture against [[Troyes AC|Troyes]] on March 3, 2018, while the club's starting forwards were rested for an upcoming Champions League match.<ref>{{cite news |last=Johnson |first=Jonathan |date=March 2, 2018 |title=PSG rest starters, name U.S.'s Timothy Weah in first-team squad |url=http://www.espn.com/soccer/paris-saint-germain/story/3403564/psg-name-uss-timothy-weah-in-first-team-squad-while-resting-starters |publisher=ESPN |access-date=March 3, 2018}}</ref> He came on as a substitute in the 79th minute of the match and had a goal-scoring opportunity in stoppage time that was saved by the Troyes goalkeeper.<ref name="ESPN-PSGdebut">{{cite news |date=March 3, 2018 |title=U.S.'s Timothy Weah, son of George, makes debut for PSG |url=http://www.espn.com/soccer/paris-saint-germain/story/3404724/us-youth-international-timothy-weah-son-of-george-makes-debut-for-psg?src=com |publisher=ESPN |access-date=March 3, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Valentine |first=Ben |date=March 5, 2018 |title=Americans Abroad: Weah's nearly perfect debut while Johannsson saves Bremen |url=http://www.goal.com/en-us/news/americans-abroad-johannssons-renaissance-continues-while/1a9qdmw7i5l7i1fw6ahzvbt40b |work=[[Goal.com]] |access-date=March 5, 2018}}</ref> Weah made his first start for Paris Saint-Germain in a 0–0 draw against [[Stade Malherbe Caen|Caen]] on the last day of the Ligue 1 season.<ref>{{cite news |last=Johnson |first=Jonathan |date=May 19, 2018 |title=Timothy Weah handed first Paris Saint-Germain senior team start |url=http://www.espn.com/soccer/paris-saint-germain/story/3504240/timothy-weah-earns-first-paris-saint-germain-senior-team-start |publisher=ESPN |access-date=May 29, 2018}}</ref> Weah scored his first competitive goal for PSG during a 4–0 win against [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] in the [[2018 Trophée des Champions|Trophée des Champions]] on August 4, 2018.<ref>{{cite news |last=Bushnell |first=Henry |date=August 4, 2018 |title=USMNT's Tim Weah scores first pro goal for PSG in French super cup |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/usmnts-tim-weah-scores-first-pro-goal-psg-french-super-cup-video-145121644.html |work=[[Yahoo! Sports]] |access-date=August 5, 2018}}</ref> He scored his first league goal a week later in the club's season opener, a 3–0 win over Caen.<ref>{{cite news |date=August 13, 2018 |title=Paris Saint Germain 3–0 Caen |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/45163002 |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |access-date=August 13, 2018}}</ref>

He joined [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] on a six-month loan on January 7, 2019,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Timothy Weah joins Celtic on loan from Paris Saint-Germain |publisher=Celtic F.C. |date=January 7, 2019 |access-date=January 7, 2019 |url=http://www.celticfc.net/news/15566}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46787977 |title=Timothy Weah: Celtic secure 'hungry' PSG forward [[Scottish Cup]] fourth round match at home to [[Airdrieonians F.C.|Airdrieonians]] and scored in a 3–0 win.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Southwick |first1=Andrew |title=Celtic 3–0 Airdrieonians |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46847909 |access-date=January 22, 2019 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=January 19, 2019}}</ref> Weah's second goal for Celtic, and his first in the league, came in a 4–0 victory over [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] on January 23.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/46887206 |title=Celtic 4-0 St Mirren: Oliver Burke, Scott Sinclair & Timothy Weah score |date=January 23, 2019 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> In February 2019 he was added to Celtic's Europa League squad.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47127623 |title=Celtic: No place for Vakoun Issouf Bayo in Europa League squad |date=February 5, 2019 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> With Celtic, he won the [[Scottish Premiership]] and the team advanced to the Scottish Cup final.<ref>{{cite news |last=Paulina Maupome |first=Ana |date=May 5, 2019 |title=Tim Weah wins Scottish Premiership with Celtic |url=https://en.as.com/en/2019/05/05/football/1557009719_940247.html |work=AS |access-date=May 11, 2019}}</ref> Weah's loan spell at Celtic was terminated early by the club in May after he was selected to the US squad for the Under-20 World Cup, causing him to miss the Scottish Cup final.<ref name = "U20WC"/><ref>{{cite news |last=McConnell |first=Alison |date=May 10, 2019 |title=Celtic 2019}}</ref>

===Lille===
[[File:RC Lens - Lille OSC (17-09-2021) 77.jpg|thumb|upright|Weah playing for [[Lille OSC|Lille]] in 2021]]

On June 29, 2019, Weah signed a five-year contract with [[Lille OSC|Lille]], starting on July 1. The undisclosed fee was reported by ''[[L'Équipe]]'' to be €10 million ($11.37 million).<ref>{{cite news |date=June 30, 2019 |title=Lille sign U.S. international winger Weah from PSG |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-soccer-france-lil-weah/lille-sign-u-s-international-winger-weah-from-psg-idUSKCN1TV0QC |publisher=Reuters |access-date=July 12, 2019}}</ref> He made his debut on August 11, starting in a 2–1 home win over [[FC Nantes|Nantes]]. He played 68 minutes before being substituted for [[Yusuf Yazıcı]].<ref>{{cite news |title=USMNT's Weah earns start in Ligue 1 opener for Lille |url=https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/usmnts-weah-earns-start-in-ligue-1-opener-for-lille/14hdfq7a88au51lhl05v5j3ctb |access-date=August 29, 2019 |publisher=Goal.com |date=August 11, 2019}}</ref> Weah made three appearances for Lille throughout the 2019–20 season,<ref name="soccerway" /> but he missed most of the season due to injury; Weah suffered two hamstring injuries that kept him out of the bulk of the [[Ligue 1]] season. The first injury occurred in a game against [[Amiens SC|Amiens]], keeping him out for six months, then the second occurred during his first match back with the team in a game against [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=Mendola|first=Nicholas|date=February 29, 2020|title=USMNT forward Weah undergoes season-ending hamstring surgery|url=https://soccer.nbcsports.com/2020/02/29/usmnt-lille-americans-abroad-timothy-weah-ligue-1/|access-date=August 8, 2020|website=ProSoccerTalk {{!}} NBC Sports|language=en-US}}</ref> His injury was successfully operated in March 2020 by surgeon Lasse Lempainen in [[Turku]], Finland.<ref>[https://www.iltalehti.fi/jalkapallo/a/3c1ef484-8d17-4eaf-adcf-e04bb0585880 Miksi supertähdet haluavat leikkaushoitoa Turussa? Lasse kertoo työstään huippufutarien luottomiehenä: "Ei heitä kukaan tänne pakota"], [[Iltalehti]], March 3, 2020</ref>

Weah made his return from injury during the [[2020–21 Ligue 1]] season, during Lille's second match of the season. He came on in the 79th minute of the game against [[Stade de Reims|Reims]] for [[Burak Yılmaz]] and played 16 minutes.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Stade de Reims vs. Lille - Football Match Commentary - August 30, 2020 - ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/commentary?gameId=573256|access-date=August 30, 2020|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref> On the next Europa League matchday, Weah started and scored his first goal for Lille in a 3–2 loss against his former club Celtic.<ref>{{Cite web|date=December 10, 2020|title=Tim Weah scores 1st goal for Lille in Europa loss at Celtic|url=https://apnews.com/article/international-soccer-yusuf-yazici-george-weah-tim-weah-ligue-1-1d1538093031e2da253b14c449de643a|access-date=December 17, 2020|website=AP NEWS}}</ref> On December 16, he came on as a substitute against [[Dijon FCO|Dijon]] and scored his first Ligue 1 goal for Lille, capping off a 2–0 victory.<ref>{{Cite magazine|last=Creditor|first=Avi|title=USMNT's Weah Scores Again for Lille|url=https://www.si.com/soccer/2020/12/16/tim-weah-goal-video-lille-dijon-usmnt|access-date=December 17, 2020|magazine=Sports Illustrated|date=December 16, 2020 |language=en-us}}</ref> He played 28 games and scored three goals as ''Les Dogues'' won their first league title for a decade.<ref>{{cite news |title=George Weah son wins French league title |url=https://nilepost.co.ug/2021/05/25/george-weah-son-wins-french-league-title/ |access-date=December 21, 2022 |work=Nile Post |date=May 25, 2021}}</ref> On August 1, the team won the [[2021 Trophée des Champions]] 1–0 against PSG in Israel, with Weah playing the last 14 minutes in place of [[Jonathan David]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Résultat et résumé : Lille - PSG|trans-title=Result and report: Lille - PSG |url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/match-direct/trophee-des-champions/2021/lille-psg-live/518295 |access-date=December 21, 2022 |work=[[L'Équipe]] |date=August 1, 2022 |language=French}}</ref>

On March 19, 2022, Weah was sent off in a 1–0 win at Nantes for a foul on [[Samuel Moutoussamy]], who required assistance to leave the field.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Holyman |first1=I. |title=Lille bounce back after European exit |url=https://www.ligue1.com/Articles/MATCH-REPORTS/2022/03/19/lille-bounce-back-nantes-onana-lens-clermont-clauss |access-date=December 21, 2022 |work=Ligue 1 |date=March 19, 2022}}</ref> He did not score until May 14 in the penultimate league fixture, a 3–1 win at [[OGC Nice|Nice]]<ref>{{cite news |last1=Henry Jr. |first1=Larry |title=Americans Abroad Player of the Week: Tim Weah |url=https://sbisoccer.com/2022/05/americans-abroad-player-of-the-week-tim-weah |access-date=December 21, 2022 |work=SBI Soccer |date=May 16, 2022}}</ref> and followed it a week later with both goals of a home 2–2 tie with [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Lejolivet |first1=Pierre |title=Stade Rennais. Après le nul à Lille, ce sera la Ligue Europa pour les Rouge et Noir|trans-title=Stade Rennais. After the tie at Lille, it will be the Europa League for the Red and Blacks|url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/sport/football/ligue-1/direct/direct-lille-rennes-suivez-le-match-de-la-38e-journee-de-ligue-1-en-live-2d710254-d844-11ec-b74d-895ee302236d |access-date=December 21, 2022 |work=[[Ouest-France]] |date=May 21, 2022 |language=French}}</ref>

===Juventus===
Following four seasons with the French side, Weah signed for [[Serie A]] club [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] on July 1, 2023, on a five-year contract running until June 30, 2028.<ref>{{cite news |language=fr |url=https://www.losc.fr/node/11190 |title=Bonne route, Timothy Weah |date=July 1, 2023 |publisher=[[Lille OSC|LOSC]] |access-date=July 6, 2023}}</ref><ref name="JuvePR">{{cite press release |title=Agreement with Lille for the definitive acquisition of the player Weah |url=https://www.juventus.com/images/image/private/fl_attachment/dev/gjivsbbtoukabnsshneh.pdf |publisher=[[Juventus FC|Juventus]] |date=July 1, 2023 |access-date=July 6, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230701133521/https://www.juventus.com/images/image/private/fl_attachment/dev/gjivsbbtoukabnsshneh.pdf |archive-date=July 1, 2023}}</ref> The financial details of the transfer include an initial and base fee of €10.3 million ($11.22 million) payable to Lille in two years, a maximum of €2.1 million ($2.29 million) add-ons depending on sporting conditions, and €1 million ($1.09 million) of incidental charges.<ref name="JuvePR"/>

On January 4, 2024, Weah scored his first goal for Juventus in a 6–1 win against [[US Salernitana 1919|Salernitana]] in the round of 16 stage of the [[2023–24 Coppa Italia|Coppa Italia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/soccer/news/usmnt-star-timothy-weah-unleashes-rocket-for-first-juventus-goal-video|title=USMNT star Timothy Weah scores first Juventus goal with rocket shot (video)|date=January 4, 2024|access-date=January 4, 2024|website=NBC Sports}}</ref> Juventus went on to win the Coppa Italia, beating [[Atalanta BC|Atalanta]] in the [[2024 Coppa Italia final|final]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 15, 2024 |title=USMNT stars Weston McKennie and Tim Weah lift a trophy as Juventus claim Coppa Italia with victory over Atalanta {{!}} Goal.com US |url=https://www.goal.com/en-us/lists/weston-mckennie-tim-weah-usmnt-coppa-italia-juventus/blt5979575ec00f2bd1 |access-date=May 18, 2024 |website=www.goal.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

====Marseille loan====
On August 6, 2025, Weah signed for [[Ligue 1]] club [[Olympique de Marseille|Olympique Marseille]] on loan, with an obligation to buy for a fee that could reach €18 million ($21 million).<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 6, 2025|title=Timothy Weah joins OM|url=https://www.om.fr/en/news/4803/1st-team/100251-timothy-weah-joins-om|access-date=August 7, 2025|website=Olympique de Marseille}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=August 6, 2025|title=USA's Tim Weah Joins Marseille After Two-Year Stint at Juventus|url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/soccer/us-winger-tim-weah-returns-to-french-soccer-with-move-from-juventus-to-marseille|access-date=August 7, 2025|website=[[Fox Sports]]}}</ref>

===Marseille===
On June 8, 2026, Weah joined Marseille on a permanent deal, signing a contract until 2030.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sbisoccer.com/2026/06/tim-weah-joins-marseille-after-french-club-exercises-purchase-option?amp=1|title=Tim Weah joins Marseille after French club exercises purchase option|website=sbisoccer.com|author=Larry Henry Jr.|date=June 8, 2026}}</ref> He was later made [[captain (association football)|captain]] on August 20, 2026.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://onefootball.com/en/news/why-timothy-weah-was-named-om-captain-43305432|title=Why Timothy Weah was named OM captain|work=OneFootball|date=August 20, 2026|access-date=August 20, 2026}}</ref>

==International career==
In addition to the United States, Weah was eligible to represent [[France national football team|France]], [[Jamaica national football team|Jamaica]], and [[Liberia national football team|Liberia]], through residency and his parents' citizenships.<ref>{{cite news |last=McMahon |first=Bobby |date=October 20, 2017 |title=As Tim Weah Prepares For World Cup Q-F, His Soccer-Legend Dad George Is Running For President |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/bobbymcmahon/2017/10/20/as-tim-weah-prepares-for-world-cup-q-f-his-soccer-legend-dad-george-is-running-for-president/#49a98307ecee |work=Forbes |access-date=March 3, 2018}}</ref> Weah stated that his decision to represent the United States "wasn't hard at all" and was based on his love of the country and his teammates.<ref>{{cite news |last=Sciaretta |first=Brian |date=May 12, 2017 |title=Soccer Success Runs in the Family for Timothy Weah |url=http://americansoccernow.com/articles/soccer-success-runs-in-the-family-for-timothy-weah |work=American Soccer Now |access-date=March 3, 2018}}</ref>

===Youth===
Weah has represented the United States on several youth national teams, beginning with a call-up to train with the under-14 team in 2012.<ref name=U14>{{cite news |date=August 1, 2012 |title=Under-14 Boys' National Team Head Coach Hugo Perez Selects 50 Players for August Training Camp |url=https://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2014/03/17/13/13/u14-bnt-head-coach-hugo-perez-selects-50-players-for-august-training-camp |publisher=U.S. Soccer |access-date=March 3, 2018}}</ref> Weah was selected to join the [[United States boys' national under-15 soccer team|under-15 team]] at the Tournament delle Nazioni in Italy, scoring the winning goal in the final against Austria.<ref name=U15>{{cite news |date=May 1, 2015 |title=U-15 BNT Wins Tournament delle Nazioni with 3-2 Victory over Austria |url=https://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2015/05/01/10/39/150501-u15-bnt-wins-tournament-delle-nazioni |publisher=U.S. Soccer |access-date=March 3, 2018}}</ref>

He was called up to the [[United States men's national under-17 soccer team|under-17 team]], under the management of former under-15 coach [[John Hackworth]], in December 2015 for a series of friendlies in Florida.<ref>{{cite news |date=November 30, 2015 |title=Ten players connected to MLS teams named to US roster for U-17 friendly tournament |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2015/11/30/players-connected-mls-teams-named-us-roster-u-17-tournament |publisher=MLSsoccer.com |access-date=March 3, 2018}}</ref> Weah joined the team for the [[Montaigu Tournament]], which the United States won after he scored in the final against hosts France.<ref>{{cite news |date=March 18, 2016 |title=U-17 MNT Heads to France for 44th International Montaigu Tournament |url=https://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2016/03/18/14/46/160318-u17mnt-heads-to-france-for-44th-international-montaigu-tournament |publisher=U.S. Soccer |access-date=March 3, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=March 28, 2016 |title=United States U17s top France for Montaigu Tournament title |url=http://www.espn.com/soccer/united-states/story/2838851/united-states-u17s-top-france-for-montaigu-tournament-title |publisher=ESPN |access-date=March 3, 2018}}</ref> At another set of friendlies in Florida, Weah made three substitute appearances and scored twice.<ref>{{cite news |last=Clark |first=Travis |date=December 7, 2016 |title=Scouting the Men's U-17s: 5 players with senior national team futures |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/us/features/usmnt-u-17s-scouting-senior-team-future-nike-friendlies |work=[[FourFourTwo]] |access-date=March 3, 2018 |archive-date=March 25, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190325115020/https://www.fourfourtwo.com/us/features/usmnt-u-17s-scouting-senior-team-future-nike-friendlies |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was part of the under-17 squad that finished second in the [[2017 CONCACAF U-17 Championship]], scoring two goals.<ref>{{cite news |date=May 5, 2017 |title=Tim Weah, son of George, helps US qualify for U17 World Cup |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/2017/05/05/tim-weah-son-of-george-helps-us-qualify-for-u17-world-cup/101356822/ |work=[[USA Today]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=March 3, 2018}}</ref>

He was selected to represent the United States at the [[2017 FIFA U-17 World Cup|2017 FIFA Under-17 World Cup]] in India.<ref>{{cite magazine |last=Creditor |first=Avi |date=September 21, 2017 |title=Sargent, Weah, Atlanta United Trio Headline USA U-17 World Cup Roster |url=https://www.si.com/soccer/2017/09/21/usa-u17-world-cup-roster-sargent-carleton-weah-india |magazine=Sports Illustrated |access-date=March 3, 2018}}</ref> In the team's first knockout stage match, Weah scored a [[hat-trick]] in a 5–0 victory over [[Paraguay men's national under-17 football team|Paraguay]].<ref name="ESPN-U17">{{cite news |last=Selvaraj |first=Jonathan |date=October 16, 2017 |title=U.S.' Timothy Weah makes a name for himself at the Under-17 World Cup |url=http://www.espn.com/soccer/united-states/story/3231287/usas-timothy-weah-makes-a-name-for-himself |publisher=ESPN |access-date=March 3, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=October 17, 2018 |title=George Weah's son Timothy scores hat-trick in Under-17 World Cup for US |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/41650115 |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |access-date=March 3, 2018}}</ref> The hat-trick was the first one recorded by a United States men's national team player at any level during the knockout stages of a World Cup and the fifth overall for any American male player at a World Cup.<ref>{{cite web |title=More on Tim Weah's Historic Hat Trick vs Paraguay at the FIFA U-17 World Cup |url=https://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2017/10/16/20/01/20171016-feat-u17mnt-tim-weah-scores-historic-hat-trick-vs-paraguay-u17-world-cup |publisher=U.S. Soccer |access-date=March 3, 2018}}</ref>

Weah was named in the United States squad for the [[2019 FIFA U-20 World Cup|2019 FIFA Under-20 World Cup]] in [[Poland]].<ref name = "U20WC">{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/48230367 |title=Celtic: Timothy Weah leaves club after being picked by US |date=May 10, 2019 |access-date=May 10, 2019 |publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref> He scored twice during the tournament, against [[Qatar national under-20 football team|Qatar]] in the group stage to qualify for the knockout stage<ref>{{cite news |last=Tannenwald |first=Jonathan |date=May 30, 2019 |title=Tim Weah goal sends U.S. to under-20 World Cup knockout rounds with 1-0 win over Qatar |url=https://www.inquirer.com/soccer/tim-weah-usmnt-under-20-world-cup-qatar-20190530.html |work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |access-date=July 12, 2019}}</ref> and against [[Ecuador national under-20 football team|Ecuador]] in their quarterfinal defeat.<ref>{{cite news |last=Gonzalez |first=Roger |date=June 8, 2019 |title=U.S. falls to Ecuador in U-20 World Cup quarterfinals, but makes history with run |url=https://www.cbssports.com/soccer/news/u-s-falls-to-ecuador-in-u-20-world-cup-quarterfinals-but-makes-history-with-run/ |work=[[CBS Sports]] |access-date=July 12, 2019}}</ref>

===Senior===
Weah made his full debut for the [[United States men's national soccer team|senior national team]] in a 1–0 friendly win against [[Paraguay national football team|Paraguay]] on March 27, 2018, entering the match as a substitute for fellow debutant [[Marky Delgado]] in the 86th minute. He was the first player born in the 2000s to earn a senior cap for the United States.<ref>{{cite news |last=Goff |first=Steven |date=March 27, 2018 |title=USMNT defeats Paraguay, 1–0, on Bobby Wood's goal |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/soccer-insider/wp/2018/03/27/usmnt-defeats-paraguay-1-0-on-bobby-woods-goal/ |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |access-date=March 27, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |date=March 27, 2018 |title=Weah Becomes First Player Born in 2000 to Earn MNT Cap |url=https://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2018/03/27/14/59/20180327-news-mnt-tim-weah-first-player-born-in-2000 |publisher=U.S. Soccer |access-date=March 27, 2018}}</ref> During a friendly against [[Bolivia national football team|Bolivia]] on May 28, 2018, his first international start, Weah scored his first international goal and became the fourth-youngest player to score for the United States, ahead of [[Josh Sargent]], who scored his first earlier in the match.<ref>{{cite news |last=Blum |first=Ronald |date=May 28, 2018 |title=Sargent & Weah, both 18, score as US beats Bolivia 3–0 |url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/article/Sargent-Weah-both-18-score-as-US-beats-12949557.php |work=[[San Francisco Chronicle]] |agency=Associated Press |access-date=May 28, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=May 28, 2018 |title=USA 3–0 Bolivia |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44287954 |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |access-date=May 29, 2018}}</ref>

On June 6, 2021, Weah came on as a 60th-minute substitute for [[Sergiño Dest]] in a 3–2 overtime win over [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]] in the [[2021 CONCACAF Nations League Final|CONCACAF Nations League Final]] at [[Empower Field at Mile High|Mile High Stadium]] in [[Denver]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Schepanskyi |first1=Dan |title=Sergino Dest helps USA to beat Mexico in CONCACAF Nations League final |url=https://tribuna.com/en/news/fcbarcelona-2021-06-07-sergino-dest-helps-usa-to-beat-mexico-in-concacaf-nations-league-final/ |access-date=December 21, 2022 |work=Tribuna |date=June 7, 2021}}</ref> He scored his first competitive international goal on November 16, opening a 1–1 tie away to [[Jamaica national football team|Jamaica]] in [[2022 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONCACAF)|2022 FIFA World Cup qualification]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Blum |first1=Ronald |title=Timothy Weah's goal earns US men bumpy 1–1 draw at Jamaica in World Cup qualifier |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2021/11/16/sports/timothy-weahs-goal-earns-us-men-bumpy-1-1-draw-jamaica-world-cup-qualifier/ |access-date=December 21, 2022 |work=[[The Boston Globe]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=June 16, 2021}}</ref> He was part of the squad that reached the last 16 of the [[2022 FIFA World Cup|final tournament]] in [[Qatar]], scoring against [[Wales national football team|Wales]] in the 1–1 tie in the first group game.<ref>{{cite news |last=Said |first=Nick |date=November 21, 2022 |title=Weah gives U.S. 1–0 halftime lead against Wales |url=https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/weah-gives-us-1-0-halftime-lead-against-wales-2022-11-21/ |work=[[Reuters]] |access-date=November 30, 2022}}</ref>
[[File:2022 FIFA World Cup United States 1–1 Wales - (17) (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|180px|Weah with the [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]] at the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]].]]
Weah was included in the American squad for the [[2024 Copa América]] hosted on home soil.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ussoccer.com/stories/2024/06/us-mens-national-soccer-team-roster-players-2024-copa-america|title=Berhalter Selects 26-Player Roster to Represent the United States in 2024 Copa América|publisher=[[United States Soccer Federation]]|date=June 14, 2024}}</ref> In their second group stage match against [[Panama national football team|Panama]], he was sent off with a straight red card (upgraded from a yellow card following a [[Video assistant referee|VAR]] review) after striking Panamanian defender [[Roderick Miller (footballer)|Roderick Miller]] in the head.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/story/_/id/40447615/copa-america-2024-usa-tim-weah-red-card-panama|title=USA's Tim Weah shown red card in loss to Panama at Copa América|publisher=ESPN|date=June 27, 2024}}</ref> The U.S. eventually lost the match 2–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/soccer/news/usa-soccer-vs-panama-score-sloppy-usmnt-stunned-at-copa-america-chances-of-advancing-take-huge-hit/live/|title=USA soccer vs. Panama score: Sloppy USMNT stunned at Copa America, chances of advancing take huge hit|work=CBS Sports|date=June 27, 2024}}</ref> Afterward, Weah along with teammates [[Folarin Balogun]], [[Chris Richards (soccer)|Chris Richards]] and [[Weston McKennie]] all suffered [[Racism in association football|racist abuse]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c844jrxewv8t|title=Copa America: USA 1–2 Panama - Timothy Weah suffers racist abuse after red card|publisher=BBC Sport|date=June 27, 2024}}</ref>

Ahead of the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]], Weah said he was "disappointed" in ticket prices at the tournament and that he believed that it would be "more of a show" and that "real fans will miss matches" due to the pricing.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.si.com/soccer/usmnt-star-tim-weah-slams-staggering-ticket-prices-for-2026-world-cup|title=USMNT Star Tim Weah Slams Staggering Ticket Prices for 2026 World Cup|last=Steiner|first=Ben|date=January 16, 2026|access-date=February 1, 2026|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]}}</ref> The comments prompted United States head coach [[Mauricio Pochettino]] to respond, saying it was not Weah's "duty to evaluate the price of the ticket" and praise FIFA, adding that it was not his or Weah's place "to provide our opinion" about FIFA's decisions.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/7008022/2026/01/29/mauricio-pochettino-tim-weah-world-cup-ticket-prices-fifa-usmnt/|title=Pochettino on Weah's critique of World Cup ticket prices: Players should keep focus on the field|last=Tenorio|first=Paul|date=January 29, 2026|access-date=February 1, 2026|work=[[The New York Times]]|department=[[The Athletic]]}}</ref>

On May 26, 2026, Weah was selected in the 26-man squad for the 2026 FIFA World Cup.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.fifa.com/en/tournaments/mens/worldcup/canadamexicousa2026/articles/usa-squad-announcement-mauricio-pochettino|title=Pulisic, McKennie spearhead USA squad |date=May 26, 2026|access-date=June 12, 2026|language=en}}</ref>

a former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[defender (association football)|defender]]. Born in France, he played for the [[Congo national football team|Congo national team]].{{cite web|title=Samba: No regrets choosing Congo|url=https://www.fifa.com/world-match-centre/news/newsid/144/945/8/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150921214855/http://www.fifa.com/world-match-centre/news/newsid/144/945/8/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=21 September 2015|access-date=20 September 2015}} Samba notably played in the [[Premier League]] for [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] where he played for five years, notching up 161 league appearances with 16 goals. He also played top flight football in [[England]] for [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] with a spell in the [[EFL Championship]] for [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]]. He also played for [[CS Sedan Ardennes|Sedan]], [[Hertha BSC]], [[FC Anzhi Makhachkala|Anzhi Makhachkala]], [[FC Dynamo Moscow|Dynamo Moscow]] and [[Panathinaikos F.C.|Panathinaikos]]. ==Club career== ===Early career=== Born in the [[Paris aire urbaine|Parisian]] suburb of [[Créteil]], Samba began his career with [[France|French]] [[Ligue 2]] club [[CS Sedan Ardennes|Sedan]], having previously played for D’Issy-les-Moulineaux and [[FC Rouen|Rouen]].{{cite news|title=Samba: I was close to quitting|url=https://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/1993881.samba-close-quitting/|publisher=The Lancashire Telegraph|date=25 January 2008|access-date=3 May 2020}}{{cite news|title=Christopher Samba: 'I came from nothing. I never want to be like that again'|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/profiles/christopher-samba-i-came-from-nothing-i-never-want-to-be-like-that-again-2076262.html|work=The Independent|date=11 September 2010|access-date=3 May 2020}} As a result, he left Créteil in his youth to move to Sedan.{{cite web|url=https://fcdynamo.ru/news/interview/?id_4=5205|title=География "Динамо". Кристофер Самба. Кретей|publisher=FC Dynamo Moscow|language=ru|date=23 October 2013|access-date=3 May 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200502193849/https://fcdynamo.ru/news/interview/?id_4=5205|archive-date=2 May 2020|url-status=live}} At one point, Samba played in a striker position before switching to a centre–back position.{{cite news|title=How have Blackburn Rovers ended up without a goal threat?|url=https://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/4305788.blackburn-rovers-ended-without-goal-threat/|publisher=The Lancashire Telegraph|date=21 April 2009|access-date=3 May 2020}} After progressing through the ranks of the Sedan's Academy, he made his debut for the club in the opening game of the season against [[FC Istres]], starting a match before being sent–off in the 57th minute, in a 2–0 loss.{{cite news|title=Istre-Sedan : Le groupe...|url=http://www.allezsedan.com/article492_Istre-Sedan_:_Le_groupe....html|publisher=Allez Sedan|language=fr|date=1 August 2003|access-date=3 May 2020}} However, after making two more appearances for the side, Samba suffered an adductors injury that kept him out for the rest of the 2003–04 season.{{cite news|title=Retour de Liri et dernières nouvelles|url=http://www.allezsedan.com/article669_Retour_de_Liri_et_dernieres_nouvelles.html|publisher=Allez Sedan|language=fr|date=21 January 2004|access-date=3 May 2020}} His injury cost him his chance of earning his professional contract at Sedan and was released by the club at the end of the 2003–04 season.{{cite news|title=J'AI ÉTÉ JETÉ COMME UNE CHAUSSETTE|url=https://sport24.lefigaro.fr/football/etranger/angleterre/actualites/j-ai-ete-jete-comme-une-chaussette-432654|publisher=Sport 24 La Figaro|language=fr|date=27 November 2010|access-date=3 May 2020}} ===Hertha BSC=== Following his release by Sedan, Samba revealed that he "had lots of trials with clubs during that time, but none of them came off". He also said: "I had no club and I had to train by myself for a long period of time. I was 19 years old. I had to recover from the injury myself without a physio, no money. For six months I did not have a club and I was just training. I went to small teams like Rouen who did not even want to let me train with them." Eventually, Samba was signed by [[Berlin]]-based club [[Hertha BSC]] of the [[Germany|German]] [[Bundesliga]] after being scouted while on international duty at Congo. Immediately after signing for Hertha BSC, Samba was assigned to [[Hertha BSC II]]. After making his Hertha BSC II debut, he then scored his first goal for the reserve side, in a 5–2 win against [[SC Preußen Münster|Preußen Münster]] on 27 March 2005.{{cite news|title=Union Verliert Hertha Berlin Verlaesst Abstiegsraenge|url=https://www.morgenpost.de/printarchiv/sport/article104212521/Union-verliert-Hertha-verlaesst-Abstiegsraenge.html|publisher=Berliner Morgenpost|language=de|date=29 March 2005|access-date=3 May 2020}} Samba later scored two more goals in the 2004–05 season, scoring against [[Borussia Dortmund II]] and [[Wuppertaler SV]].{{cite news|title=Nachrichten|url=https://www.morgenpost.de/printarchiv/sport/article104445159/Nachrichten.html|publisher=Berliner Morgenpost|language=de|date=21 April 2005|access-date=3 May 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Fussball Nachrichten|url=https://www.morgenpost.de/printarchiv/sport/article104449234/Fussball-Nachrichten.html|publisher=Berliner Morgenpost|language=de|date=1 May 2005|access-date=3 May 2020}} At the end of the 2004–05 season, he went on to make sixteen appearances and scoring three times in all competitions. {{cite news|title=Junge Spieler im Kader Goetz Foedert Talente|url=https://www.morgenpost.de/printarchiv/sport/article104483643/Junge-Spieler-im-Kader-Goetz-foerdert-Talente.html|publisher=Berliner Morgenpost|language=de|date=5 August 2005|access-date=3 May 2020}} He made his first team debut for Hertha BSC, coming on in the 86th minute and played for the rest of the game, as they beat [[TuS Koblenz]] in the first round of the DFB Cup.{{cite news|title=Keita schockt die Hertha - doch Kovac kontert|url=https://www.kicker.de/koblenz-gegen-hertha-2005-dfb-pokal-722977/spielbericht|publisher=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]]|language=de|date=19 August 2005|access-date=3 May 2020}} Seven days later on 26 August 2005, Samba made his league debut for the club, coming on as a 70th-minute substitute, in a 3–0 loss against [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]].{{cite news|title=Scholl sorgt für die Entscheidung|url=https://www.kicker.de/bayern-gegen-hertha-2005-bundesliga-723030/analyse|publisher=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]]|language=de|date=26 August 2005|access-date=3 May 2020}} Since making his debut for the club, Samba appeared in the first team, mostly coming from the substitute bench.{{cite news|title=Spaeter Schock Fuer Hertha|url=https://www.morgenpost.de/printarchiv/sport/article104506195/Spaeter-Schock-fuer-Hertha.html|publisher=Berliner Morgenpost|language=de|date=2 October 2005|access-date=3 May 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Malik Fathi Als Vorbild|url=https://www.morgenpost.de/printarchiv/sport/article104520252/Malik-Fathi-als-Vorbild.html|publisher=Berliner Morgenpost|language=de|date=12 November 2005|access-date=3 May 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Christopher Samba Zahlt Lehrgeld Bei Seinem Debuet In Der Startelf|url=https://www.morgenpost.de/printarchiv/sport/article104532271/Christopher-Samba-zahlt-Lehrgeld-bei-seinem-Debuet-in-der-Startelf.html|publisher=Berliner Morgenpost|language=de|date=19 December 2005|access-date=3 May 2020}} But Samba often returned to play for the Hertha BSC II and scored once in twelve appearances.{{cite news|title=Hertha Amateure Trennen Sich Torlos Vom FC St Pauli|url=https://www.morgenpost.de/printarchiv/sport/article104500450/Hertha-Amateure-trennen-sich-torlos-vom-FC-St-Pauli.html|publisher=Berliner Morgenpost|language=de|date=18 September 2005|access-date=3 May 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Fussball Nachrichten|url=https://www.morgenpost.de/printarchiv/sport/article104511579/Fussball-Nachrichten.html|publisher=Berliner Morgenpost|language=de|date=16 October 2005|access-date=3 May 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Hoch Hoeher Madlung|url=https://www.morgenpost.de/printarchiv/sport/article104532301/Hoch-hoeher-Madlung.html|publisher=Berliner Morgenpost|language=de|date=19 December 2005|access-date=3 May 2020}} It was announced on 18 March 2006 that he signed a contract extension with the club, keeping him until 2008.{{cite news|title="Герта" продлила контракты с молодыми игроками|url=https://www.sport-express.ru/football/rfpl/news/124051/|publisher=Sport Express|language=ru|date=18 March 2006|access-date=3 May 2020}} However, as the 2005–06 season progressed, Samba suffered a hamstring injury that kept him out for the rest of the season.{{cite news|title=Fathi und Samba Bleiben Bis 2008 bei Hertha BSC Friedrich Verletzt|url=https://www.morgenpost.de/printarchiv/sport/article104561124/Fathi-und-Samba-bleiben-bis-2008-bei-Hertha-BSC-Friedrich-verletzt.html|publisher=Berliner Morgenpost|language=de|date=18 March 2006|access-date=3 May 2020}} Despite this, he went on to make twelve appearances for the senior team in all competitions. In the 2006–07 season, Samba continued to appear in the first team, mostly coming from the substitute bench.{{cite news|title=Alternativen Sind Da Fehlen Noch|url=https://www.morgenpost.de/printarchiv/sport/article104609818/Alternativen-sind-da-Tore-fehlen-noch.html|publisher=Berliner Morgenpost|language=de|date=15 August 2006|access-date=3 May 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Unnoetige Einlage Von Marko Pantelic|url=https://www.morgenpost.de/printarchiv/sport/article104614257/Unnoetige-Einlage-von-Marko-Pantelic.html|publisher=Berliner Morgenpost|language=de|date=28 August 2006|access-date=3 May 2020}}

{{cite news|title=Hoeness Gibt Den Kampf Um Bastuerk Noch Nicht Verloren|url=https://www.morgenpost.de/printarchiv/sport/article103028891/Hoeness-gibt-den-Kampf-um-Bastuerk-noch-nicht-verloren.html|publisher=Berliner Morgenpost|language=de|date=18 December 2006|access-date=3 May 2020}} However throughout his time at Hertha BSC, he struggled to break into the Hertha first team and desired a move elsewhere in the January [[transfer window]].{{cite web|title=Hertha Berlin Tactical Formations|publisher=Football-Lineups|url=http://www.football-lineups.com/players/player.php?route=722|access-date=7 February 2007|archive-url=https://archive.today/20121206014022/http://www.football-lineups.com/players/player.php?route=722|archive-date=6 December 2012|url-status=dead}} ===Blackburn Rovers=== Having desire to move elsewhere, Samba was invited by [[Mark Hughes]] to undertake a five-day trial at [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]].{{cite news|title=Samba Zum Probetraining Nach Blackburn Rovers|url=https://www.morgenpost.de/printarchiv/sport/article103040028/Samba-zum-Probetraining-nach-Blackburn.html|publisher=Berliner Morgenpost|language=de|date=12 January 2007|access-date=3 May 2020}} He quickly made an impression at the trial that Hughes wanted to sign him.{{cite news|title=Hughes set for Samba move|url=https://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/1140225.hughes-set-samba-move/|publisher=The Lancashire Telegraph|date=23 January 2007|access-date=3 May 2020}} Two days later on 25 January 2007, he completed a transfer to Blackburn Rovers of the [[Premier League]], signing a three-and-a-half-year deal for £450,000 and taking the number 21 shirt.{{cite news|title=Samba signs for Rovers|url=https://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/1149607.samba-signs-rovers/|publisher=The Lancashire Telegraph|date=26 January 2007|access-date=3 May 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Blackburn bring in defender Samba|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/b/blackburn_rovers/6300359.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|date=26 January 2007|access-date=3 May 2020}} Samba made his Blackburn Rovers debut against [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]] in the [[2006–07 FA Cup|FA Cup]] Fourth Round as a 69th-minute substitute for [[Ryan Nelsen]], as they won 4–0.{{cite news|title=Luton Town 0 Blackburn Rovers 4|url=https://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/1153996.luton-town-0-blackburn-rovers-4/|publisher=The Lancashire Telegraph|date=29 January 2007|access-date=3 May 2020}} Two days later on 31 January 2007, he made his Premiership debut on 31 January against [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]] in a 3–0 defeat.{{cite news|title=Chelsea 3–0 Blackburn Rovers|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/6309645.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|date=31 January 2007|access-date=3 May 2020}}
{{cite web|title=Chelsea Blackburn Rovers|publisher=Football-Lineups|url=http://www.football-lineups.com/wiki/_match3674.php| access-date=7 February 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070305132610/http://www.football-lineups.com/wiki/_match3674.php|archive-date=5 March 2007|url-status=live}} Since making his debut for the club, Samba quickly became a first team regular for the side.{{cite news|title= Samba: We can shock Gunners|url=https://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/1202172.samba-can-shock-gunners/|publisher=The Lancashire Telegraph|date=19 February 2007|access-date=3 May 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Samba 'buy of Premiership'|url=https://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/1231389.samba-buy-premiership/|publisher=The Lancashire Telegraph|date=2 March 2007|access-date=3 May 2020}}
{{cite news|title=No pain, no gain for Nelsen|url=https://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/1257645.no-pain-no-gain-nelsen/|publisher=The Lancashire Telegraph|date=14 March 2007|access-date=3 May 2020}} On 17 March 2007, he scored his first goal for Blackburn Rovers against [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] with a header in the 47th minute, coming in the 1–2 defeat at [[Ewood Park]].{{cite news|title=Blackburn Rovers 1 West Ham United 2|url=https://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/1267617.blackburn-rovers-1-west-ham-united-2/|publisher=The Lancashire Telegraph|date=17 March 2007|access-date=3 May 2020}} Samba then scored his second goal for the club in a 3–1 victory over [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] at Ewood Park on 18 April 2007, playing the full 90 minutes with [[Ryan Nelsen]] at the centre of defence.{{cite news|title=Rovers 3 Watford 1: Benni hits the 20 mark|url=https://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/1339708.rovers-3-watford-1-benni-hits-20-mark/|publisher=The Lancashire Telegraph|date=19 April 2007|access-date=3 May 2020}} Since making his debut for Blackburn Rovers, he quickly became a fan favourite among supporters and was named Newcomer of the Year Awards at the club's award ceremony.{{cite news|title=We've got to use technology|url=https://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/football/1272173.got-use-technology/|publisher=The Lancashire Telegraph|date=20 March 2007|access-date=3 May 2020}}

{{cite news|title=Rovers v Bolton: The curse of the home side|url=https://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/2067026.rovers-v-bolton-curse-home-side/|publisher=The Lancashire Telegraph|date=23 February 2008|access-date=3 May 2020}}
{{cite news|title=Chris Samba: I'm not scared of facing big guns|url=https://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/2179228.chris-samba-not-scared-facing-big-guns/|publisher=The Lancashire Telegraph|date=8 April 2008|access-date=3 May 2020}} At one point during a 2–1 loss against West Ham United, he was involved in altercation with teammate [[David Dunn]] after conceding the equalising and the argument carried on in the dressing room at half-time.{{cite news|title=Samba calls for a killer instinct|url=https://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/2132492.samba-calls-killer-instinct/|publisher=The Lancashire Telegraph|date=19 March 2008|access-date=3 May 2020}} After the match, Manager Hughes commented about the argument, acknowledging the frustration taking place in a game.{{cite news|title=Samba spat is dunn and dusted|url=https://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/2138653.samba-spat-dunn-dusted/|publisher=The Lancashire Telegraph|date=21 March 2008|access-date=3 May 2020}} At the end of the 2007–08 season, Samba made a total of forty–one appearances and scoring three goals in all competitions.
