===Genoa===
In June 2010, ''[[La Gazzetta dello Sport]]'' reported that Inter Milan agreed a deal with [[Genoa C.F.C.|Genoa]] to sign centre-back [[Andrea Ranocchia]] and that Destro was part of the exchange deal.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2010/giugno/22/Maicon_sono_solo_due_milioni_ga_10_100622049.shtml|title=Maicon, ci sono solo due milioni fra l' Inter e il Real|date=22 June 2010|access-date=20 July 2010|last=Graziano|first=Mirko|work=La Gazzetta dello Sport|language=it}}</ref> The transfer became official on 20 July 2010, when Genoa purchased a preferential option to sign Destro in a [[co-ownership (football)|co-ownership]] deal in June 2010.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.inter.it/aas/news/reader?N=34163&L=en|title=Mattia Destro on loan to Genoa|date=20 July 2010|access-date=12 September 2010|work=FC Internazionale Milano|publisher=inter.it|archive-date=25 July 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100725112734/http://www.inter.it/aas/news/reader?N=34163&L=en|url-status=dead}}</ref>

After the injury of [[Luca Toni]], Destro started his first match in [[Serie A]], against [[A.C. ChievoVerona|Chievo]], on 12 September 2010 as the only central forward in the 3–4–3 formation chosen for the match, and scored a goal in the sixth minute of the match. However, Genoa lost the match 1–3.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.legaseriea.it/c/document_library/get_file?uuid=91912f03-14d0-4c3f-9184-8def8409da7e&groupId=10192|title=Match Report: Genoa 1–3 Chievo|date=12 September 2010|access-date=12 September 2010|work=Panini Digital|publisher=Published by Lega Calcio Serie A|format=PDF|language=it|archive-date=16 September 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100916010202/http://www.legaseriea.it/c/document_library/get_file?uuid=91912f03-14d0-4c3f-9184-8def8409da7e&groupId=10192|url-status=dead}}</ref>

As another 50% registration rights of Ranocchia were sold to Inter in January 2011 for €12.5 million,<ref name=Inter2011bilancio/> Destro was sold to Genoa in June for €4.5 million.<ref name=Inter2011bilancio/> That month, Genoa also signed his Inter teammate [[Samuele Longo]] in a co-ownership deal.<ref name=Inter2011bilancio>FC Internazionale Milano Report and Accounts on 30 June 2011 {{in lang|it}}</ref> The two strikers became part of the exchange that led to Inter's signing of Ranocchia.

===Siena===
In 2011, Destro left for Serie A newcomers [[S.S. Robur Siena|Siena]] on loan for €1.5 million<ref>AC Siena Report and Accounts on 30 June 2011 {{in lang|it}}</ref> with an option for a co-ownership deal.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.acsiena.it/2011/07/04/destro-in-bianconerodomani-le-visite-mediche/ |title=Destro in bianconero Domani le visite mediche |access-date=23 May 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141031100958/http://www.acsiena.it/2011/07/04/destro-in-bianconerodomani-le-visite-mediche/ |archive-date=31 October 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Destro became the team's top goalscorer with 12 goals, followed by [[Emanuele Calaiò]]'s 11 goals. On 20 June 2012, Siena purchased half of Destro's registration rights from Genoa for €1.3 million.<ref name="ReferenceA">AC Siena SpA Report and Accounts on 30 June 2012 {{in lang|it}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://luckmar.blogspot.it/2013/01/il-peso-del-monte-paschi-nel-bilancio.html|title=Appunti di Luca Marotta|author=Luca Marotta|access-date=13 July 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.acsiena.it/2012/06/20/destro-esercitato-il-diritto-di-riscatto-per-la-meta-del-cartellino/|title=Destro, esercitato il diritto di riscatto per la metà del cartellino|date=20 June 2012|access-date=21 June 2012|publisher=AC Siena|language=it|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141031100349/http://www.acsiena.it/2012/06/20/destro-esercitato-il-diritto-di-riscatto-per-la-meta-del-cartellino/|archive-date=31 October 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> However, after [[A.S. Roma|Roma]] formed an agreement with both Genoa and Siena, Genoa bought back Destro from Siena for €7.5 million million (€6 million cash plus half of [[Eugenio Lamanna]])<ref name="ReferenceA"/><ref>Genoa CFC SpA Report and Accounts on 31 December 2012 {{in lang|it}}</ref> in order to complete the deal.

===Roma===
On 30 July 2012, Roma announced they had signed Destro from Genoa in a loan deal for €11.5 million (€8.5 million cash plus half of the rights to both [[Giammario Piscitella]] and [[Valerio Verre]]) with the option to purchase him outright for an additional €4.5 million (which meant Destro would cost Roma €16 million in total if the purchase was completed). Destro would replace the [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]]-bound striker [[Fabio Borini]], whom Roma just sold for €13.3 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.asroma.it/pdf/corporate/operazioni_di_mercato/2012-07-30_Destro-Piscitella-Verre.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120813040132/http://www.asroma.it/pdf/corporate/operazioni_di_mercato/2012-07-30_Destro-Piscitella-Verre.pdf |archive-date=13 August 2012 |title=MATTIA DESTRO – GIAMMARIO PISCITELLA – VALERIO VERRE Operazioni di mercato |date=30 July 2012 |access-date=1 February 2017 |publisher=A.S. Roma |language=it |url-status=dead }}</ref> Destro made his Roma debut on 2 September 2012 in a 3–1 [[2012–13 Serie A|Serie A]] win away against Inter.<ref name="sway">{{cite web|title=M. Destro|url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/mattia-destro/85503/|publisher=Soccerway|access-date=27 August 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Internazionale 1 - 3 Roma|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2012/09/02/italy/serie-a/fc-internazionale-milano/as-roma/1351265/|publisher=Soccerway|access-date=27 August 2014}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the ''Giallorossi'' in a 4–1 home match against [[U.S. Città di Palermo|Palermo]] on 4 November.<ref name="sway" /><ref name="1rg">{{cite web|title=Roma 4 - 1 Palermo 1|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2012/11/04/italy/serie-a/as-roma/us-citta-di-palermo/1351349/|publisher=Soccerway|access-date=27 August 2014}}</ref> He also received his first red card with the club in the same match after receiving two bookings from the referee, the second of which was for taking off his shirt when celebrating his goal.<ref name="1rg" /><ref>{{cite web|title=Roma-Palermo 4-1/ Zeman respira Totti, Osvaldo, Lamela e Destro|url=http://sport.ilmessaggero.it/asroma/roma-palermo-4-1/229612.shtml|publisher=ilmessaggero.it|access-date=27 August 2014|archive-date=31 October 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141031095455/http://sport.ilmessaggero.it/asroma/roma-palermo-4-1/229612.shtml|url-status=dead}}</ref> Destro played 21 Serie A matches for Roma in his first season, many in which he came on as a substitute, and scored six goals.<ref name="sway" /> Roma finished a distant sixth in Serie A,<ref>{{cite web|title=Italy 2012/13|website=[[RSSSF]]|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesi/ital2013.html|access-date=27 August 2014}}</ref> but did reach the final of [[2012–13 Coppa Italia|Coppa Italia]].<ref name="cup13" /> Destro scored five goals en route, making him top-scorer for the tournament.<ref name="cup13a" /> However, [[S.S. Lazio|Lazio]] edged a 1–0 win over Roma in the [[2013 Coppa Italia Final|final]].<ref name="cup13" />

Destro had struggled with injury during his first season at Roma, and these problems continued into the [[2013–14 A.S. Roma season|2013–14 season]].<ref name="injury">{{cite web|title=motional Destro ends injury misery with Roma winner|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/soccer-emotional-destro-ends-injury-misery-roma-winner-173531259--sow.html|publisher=Reuters|access-date=27 August 2014|date=8 December 2013}}</ref> He did not make his first appearance until 8 November 2013, when he came on as a substitute early in the second half against [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]].<ref name="rtn">{{cite web|title=Roma 2 - 1 Fiorentina|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2013/12/08/italy/serie-a/as-roma/acf-fiorentina/1552124/|publisher=Soccerway|access-date=27 August 2014}}</ref> He made an immediate impact, scoring the winning goal in the 67th minute in a 2–1 victory.<ref name="injury" /><ref name="rtn" />
<ref>{{cite web|last1=Bandini|first1=Nicky|title=Roma's Mattia Destro rides again as Francesco Totti lifts the fans|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2013/dec/09/roma-mattio-destro-francesco-totti-fiorentina-serie-a|work=The Guardian|access-date=27 August 2014|date=9 December 2013}}</ref> Destro then started playing regularly,<ref name="sway" /> showing the goalscoring form from earlier in his career. As the season progressed, he scored twice in a 3–0 win over [[U.C. Sampdoria|Sampdoria]] in February and a hat-trick in a 3–1 win over [[Cagliari Calcio|Cagliari]] in April 2014.<ref name="sway" /> Controversy followed the Cagliari game, during which Destro had punched defender [[Davide Astori]] but was not punished at the time by the referee. However, the league authorities later imposed a three-match ban on Destro (which became four matches for accumulated yellow cards).<ref>{{cite web|last1=Bonn|first1=Kyle|title=Roma dealt double blow with Destro banned, Benatia injured|url=http://prosoccertalk.nbcsports.com/2014/04/11/roma-dealt-double-blow-with-destro-banned-benatia-injured/|publisher=ProSoccerTalk|access-date=27 August 2014|date=11 April 2014}}</ref> Despite this, Destro scored 13 league goals for Roma, finishing the season as the club's top scorer and helping his side to a second-place finish in [[2013–14 Serie A|Serie A]], behind [[Juventus FC|Juventus]].<ref name="roma2014">{{cite web|title=Fernando Torres and Mattia Destro will not be in Chelsea and Roma swap deal, says agent|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/chelsea/11048383/Fernando-Torres-and-Mattia-Destro-will-not-be-in-Chelsea-and-Roma-swap-deal-says-agent.html|publisher=The Telegraph|access-date=26 August 2014|date=21 August 2014}}</ref> He was ranked as one of the best strikers in Serie A.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2190804-ranking-the-top-10-strikers-in-serie-a-after-the-2014-transfer-window#slide0|publisher=Bleacherreport|date=8 September 2014|title=Ranking the Top 10 Strikers in Serie A After the 2014 Transfer Window}}</ref> Only [[Sergio Aguero]] and [[Lionel Messi]] had a better goal-per-minute ratio than Destro across [[Big Five (association football)|Europe's top five leagues]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2358852-everything-ac-milan-fans-need-to-know-about-new-signing-mattia-destro|publisher=Bleacherreport|date=9 February 2015|title=Everything AC Milan Fans Need to Know About New Signing Mattia Destro}}</ref>

Destro was the subject of intense transfer speculation during the summer of 2014, being heavily linked by the media with moves to [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] and [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Vargas|first1=Ivan|title=Mattia Destro, una opción italiana para la delantera del Real Madrid|url=http://www.fichajes.com/liga/mattia-destro-una-opcion-italiana-para-la-delantera-del-real-madrid_77673|publisher=Fichajes.com|access-date=28 August 2014|date=28 August 2014}}</ref> [[VFL Wolfsburg]] offered €30 million, which was rejected by Roma choosing to keep him.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2343771-arsenal-transfer-news-morgan-schneiderlin-rumours-revived-mattia-destro-latest |publisher=Bleacherreport|date=27 January 2015|title= Arsenal Transfer News: Morgan Schneiderlin Rumours Revived, Mattia Destro Latest}}</ref> He scored his first goal of the [[2014–15 Serie A|2014–15 Serie A season]] on 20 September as Roma won 2–0 against Cagliari.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29277844|title=BBC Sport - Roma 2-0 Cagliari|work=BBC Sport|access-date=13 July 2015}}</ref> He scored his second of the season in the 2–0 victory over [[Hellas Verona F.C.|Hellas Verona]], a 40-yard half volley to seal the victory after [[Alessandro Florenzi]]'s earlier strike.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29311904|title=BBC Sport - Roma 2-0 Verona|work=BBC Sport|access-date=13 July 2015}}</ref>

===AC Milan===
On 30 January 2015, Destro moved to [[A.C. Milan|AC Milan]] on loan from Roma.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/31051923|title=BBC Sport - Mattia Destro: Roma striker joins AC Milan on loan|work=BBC Sport|access-date=13 July 2015}}</ref> He scored his first Milan goal in a 1–1 draw with [[Empoli F.C.|Empoli]] on 15 February.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Serie-A/15-02-2015/milan-empoli-1-1-primo-gol-destro-pari-maccarone-san-siro-fischia-100897942010.shtml | title=Milan-Empoli 1-1: primo gol di Destro, pari di Maccarone. E San Siro fischia | date=15 February 2015 | publisher=www.gazzetta.it | access-date=13 July 2015 | language=it}}</ref> He left the club at the end of the 2014–15 season, having scored 3 goals in 15 matches.

===Bologna===
On 20 August 2015, [[Bologna F.C. 1909|Bologna]] signed Destro from Roma for €8.5 million plus bonuses up to €3 million, on a five-year deal.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.asroma.it/en/news/destro_completes_move_to_bologna/ | title=DESTRO COMPLETES MOVE TO BOLOGNA | publisher=A.S. Roma Official Website | access-date=20 August 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150909090529/http://www.asroma.it/en/news/destro_completes_move_to_bologna/|archive-date=9 September 2015}}</ref> Destro was the highest earning player of Bologna that season with a net salary of €1.6 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Calciomercato/storie/07-09-2015/tutti-ingaggi-serie-a-juve-leader-milan-oltre-100-inter-24/bologna-27-milioni.shtml|title= Tutti gli ingaggi della Serie A: Juve leader, Milan oltre i 100, Inter +24 |date=7 September 2015|access-date=6 September 2016|work=La Gazzetta dello Sport|publisher=RCSMedia Group|language=it}}</ref> He made his debut on 22 August 2015, coming on as a substitute in the 2–1 defeat to Lazio.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2015/08/22/italy/serie-a/ss-lazio-roma/bologna-fc-1909/2120382/?ICID=PL_MS_02 | title=Lazio vs. Bologna - 22 August 2015 - Soccerway }}</ref> He scored his first goal in a 3–0 win over [[Atalanta B.C.|Atalanta]] on 1 November. Destro signed a new contract worth €2 million per year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.panorama.it/sport/calcio/stipendi-calciatori-serie-a-squadre/%3famp=true|language=it|title=Tutti gli stipendi dei calciatori di serie A|publisher=Panorama.it}}{{Dead link|date=February 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>

===Genoa return===
On 4 January 2020, Destro agreed a return to [[Genoa C.F.C.|Genoa]], on loan until the end of the [[2019–20 Genoa C.F.C. season|season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tuttomercatoweb.com/serie-a/ufficiale-mattia-destro-e-un-nuovo-attaccante-del-genoa-1332847|publisher=tuttomercatoweb.com|date=4 January 2020|access-date=5 January 2020|title=UFFICIALE: Mattia Destro è un nuovo attaccante del Genoa|trans-title=Official: Mattia Destro is the new Genoa striker|language=it}}</ref> On 7 September 2020, he signed a permanent contract with the club on a [[Free transfer (association football)|free transfer]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/serie-a/ufficiale-genoa-destro-resta-nuovo-accordo-firmato-col-grifone-1429704|publisher=tuttomercatoweb.com|date=7 September 2020|access-date=8 September 2020|title=Genoa, Destro resta: nuovo accordo firmato col Grifone|trans-title=Genoa, Destro stays: new agreement reached with the Grifone|language=it}}</ref>

===Empoli===
On 28 June 2022, Destro signed with Serie A club [[Empoli F.C.|Empoli]] on a free transfer.<ref>{{Cite web |date=28 June 2022 |title=Mattia Destro è un nuovo calciatore azzurro |url=https://empolifc.com/mattia-destro-e-un-nuovo-calciatore-azzurro/ |access-date=28 June 2022 |website=empolifc.com |publisher=[[Empoli FC]] |language=it |archive-date=29 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220629095020/https://empolifc.com/mattia-destro-e-un-nuovo-calciatore-azzurro/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://m.tuttomercatoweb.com/serie-a/ufficiale-mattia-destro-e-un-nuovo-centravanti-dell-empoli-1699514|title=UFFICIALE: Mattia Destro è un nuovo centravanti dell'Empoli}}</ref> After leaving Empoli as a free agent at the end of the 2022–23 season, he re-joined the club on 29 August 2023.<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Empoli|url=https://empolifc.com/mattia-destro-e-di-nuovo-un-calciatore-azzurro/|title=Mattia Destro è di nuovo un calciatore azzurro|trans-title=Mattia Destro is once again a blue footballer|date=29 August 2023|access-date=29 August 2023|language=it}}</ref>

===Reggiana===
After 8 months as a free agent, on 31 March 2025 Destro finally signed for a new club, dropping out of Serie A after 15 years to join Serie B club [[A.C. Reggiana 1919|Reggiana]] until the end of the season.

==International career==
===Youth teams===
Destro has been capped for the ''Azzurrini'' at almost every level, from under-16 to under-21, except the under-20 team. Destro received his first call-up in 2005 Christmas to a training camp.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.figc.it/Assets/contentresources_2/ContenutoGenerico/65.$plit/C_2_ContenutoGenerico_5878_upfDownload.pdf|title=Comunicato Stampa|date=22 December 2005|access-date=14 November 2011|work=FIGC|language=it}}</ref> Destro scored more than one goal in average for the Italian U19 team, and scored 10 out of his first 11 games. He failed to score, in any of the [[2010 UEFA European Under-19 Championship|final tournament]]'s matches.

Destro made his debut for the Italy under-16 team in the international [[Val-de-Marne]] tournament.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.figc.it/Assets/contentresources_2/ContenutoGenerico/10.$plit/C_2_ContenutoGenerico_6243_upfDownload.pdf|title=COMUNICATO STAMPA|date=27 October 2006|access-date=12 September 2010|work=FIGC|language=it}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.inter.it/aas/news/reader?N=24364&L=en|title=SEVEN INTERNATIONAL CALL-UPS|date=24 October 2006|access-date=12 September 2010|work=FC Internazionale Milano|publisher=inter.it|archive-date=10 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121010193743/http://www.inter.it/aas/news/reader?N=24364&L=en|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was the member of under-17 team in [[2008 UEFA European Under-17 Championship qualifying round|2008 Euro qualification]] along with then-Inter teammates [[Davide Santon]], [[Luca Caldirola]], and [[Michele Rigione]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.figc.it/en/204/783/2007/09/News.shtml|title=THREE DAYS OF TRAINING FOR THE EUROPEAN QUALIFICATIONS |date=24 September 2007|access-date=12 September 2010|work=FIGC}}</ref>) scoring one goal in two appearances. Destro started all three matches of [[2008 UEFA European Under-17 Championship elite round|the elite qualification]] and scored one goal.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.figc.it/en/204/106/2007/10/News.shtml|title=UNDER 17 DEBUTS WITH A WIN TEAM BEATS ARMENIA THURSDAY AGAINST CYPRUS |date=2 October 2007|access-date=12 September 2010|work=FIGC}}</ref> He was also called up to the 2008 Minsk under-17 International Tournament<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.figc.it/en/204/3664/2008/01/News.shtml|title=International tournament: team plays against Moldova, Belarus and Russia |date=7 January 2008|access-date=4 September 2010|work=FIGC}}</ref> where he scored a goal in a 1–1 draw with Moldova<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.figc.it/it/204/3676/2008/01/News.shtml|title=Torneo di Minsk: pareggio degli Azzurrini contro la Moldova |date=8 January 2008|access-date=4 September 2010|work=FIGC|language=it}}</ref> and a goal in the 3–0 win against Belarus.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.figc.it/it/204/3685/2008/01/News.shtml|title=Torneo di Minsk: battuta la Bielorussia. Oggi Russia-Italia|date=9 January 2008|access-date=4 September 2010|work=FIGC|language=it}}</ref> Eventually the ''Azzurrini'' lost 0–1 to Russia (line-up unavailable) and finished third after winning 1–0 against [[Belgium national under-17 football team|Belgium]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.figc.it/en/204/3722/2008/01/News.shtml|title=Minsk Tournament: Italy beats Belgium and finishes third |date=14 January 2008|access-date=4 September 2010|work=FIGC}}</ref> (line-up unavailable).

On 17 December 2008, Destro scored a goal in his [[Italy national under-19 football team|under-19]] debut, a 3–1 win against [[Romania national under-19 football team|Romania]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://sport.repubblica.it/news/sport/calcio-amichevole-under-19-italia-romania/3460354|title=CALCIO, AMICHEVOLE UNDER 19: ITALIA-ROMANIA 3–1|date=17 December 2008|access-date=13 September 2010|work=la Repubblica|language=it|archive-date=22 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180822214731/http://sport.repubblica.it/news/sport/calcio-amichevole-under-19-italia-romania/3460354|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://archiviostorico.gazzetta.it/2008/dicembre/18/taccuino_ga_10_081218028.shtml|title=taccuino|date=18 December 2008|access-date=12 September 2010|work=La Gazzetta dello Sport|language=it}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.inter.it/aas/news/reader?N=30446&L=en|title=Under-19 call-ups for 4 Primavera players|date=11 December 2008|access-date=12 September 2010|work=FC Internazionale Milano|publisher=inter.it|archive-date=10 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121010193823/http://www.inter.it/aas/news/reader?N=30446&L=en|url-status=dead}}</ref> Destro scored the only goal in the following match in March 2009, a 1–0 defeat of [[Norway national under-19 football team|Norway]]. under-19 football team|Turkey]] in January 2010,<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.figc.it/en/204/23267/2010/01/News.shtml|title=ITALY WINS 3–0 AGAINST TURKEY: IN RUSSIA IN MAY FOR EURO |date=20 January web|url=https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=504292&spielid=141&action=schema&teama=Italien&teamb=Deutschland |title=Match report: Italy 1–1 Germany |date=17 March 2010 |access-date=12 September 2010 |work=DFB |language=de |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100421054612/https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=504292&spielid=141&action=schema&teama=Italien&teamb=Deutschland |archive-date=21 April 2010 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.figc.it/en/204/23899/2010/03/News.shtml|title=Italy and Germany. Piscedda: "The team is growing" |date=17 March 2010|access-date=12 September 2010|work=FIGC}}</ref> and three goals in two appearances at [[2010 UEFA European Under-19 Football Championship elite qualification|the elite round]] in May 2010. Only in the friendly match against [[Switzerland national under-19 football team|Switzerland]] in April 2010 did Destro not score.

He played all three matches of [[2010 UEFA European Under-19 Championship]] for Italy's U19 team. The team failed to score any goal and finished at the bottom of Group B (equal 7th).

When striker [[Alberto Paloschi]] was about to miss the final qualification match of [[2011 UEFA European Under-21 Championship qualification]] due to injury, Destro received his first under-21 call-up<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.football-italia.net/sep05f.html|title=U-21: Destro added to squad|date=5 September 2010|access-date=12 September 2010|work=Football Italia}}</ref> and substituted [[Stefano Okaka]] in the 80th minute. That ''Azzurrini'' won against [[Wales national under-21 football team|Wales]] 1–0 and went on ahead of Wales as the group champions by winning the head-to-head record. On 8 October 2010, he started the play-off match and partnered with Okaka up front in a 4–4–2 formation, scoring the opening goal by converting a [[Diego Fabbrini]] pass with a left-foot shot.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.uefa.com/under21/match/2003237--italy-vs-belarus/|title=Destro and Okaka put Italy in control|date=8 October 2010|access-date=10 October 2010|publisher=UEFA }}</ref> He was substituted by [[Luca Marrone]] in the 53rd minute as the coach changed to a 4–3–3 formation. The ''Azzurrini'' eventually defeated [[Belarus national under-21 football team|Belarus]] 2–0. However, after losing winger [[Ezequiel Schelotto]] and fullback [[Lorenzo De Silvestri]], Italy lost 0–3 to Belarus in [[Barysaw|Borisov]]. Destro was substituted by winger [[Guido Marilungo]] at half-time.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.corrieredellosport.it/calcio/azzurri/2010/10/12-133222/Incredibile%3A+Under+fuori+da+Europei+e+Olimpiadi|title=Incredibile: Under fuori da Europei e Olimpiadi|date=12 October 2010|access-date=13 October 2010|work=Corriere dello Sport – Stadio|language=it|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141031185444/http://www.corrieredellosport.it/calcio/azzurri/2010/10/12-133222/Incredibile:+Under+fuori+da+Europei+e+Olimpiadi|archive-date=31 October 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref> He scored against Turkey in a 1–0 win for the under-21 Championship qualifier.

===Senior team===
[[File:Mattia Destro.jpg|thumb|Destro with [[Italy national football team|Italy]] in 2012]]
Destro was included by head coach [[Cesare Prandelli]] in the 32-man preliminary squad for [[UEFA Euro 2012]] in Poland and Ukraine, but was not included in the final squad for the tournament.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/prandelli-names-final-team-for-italy-ahead-of-euro-2012-1.1196893|title=Prandelli names final team for Italy ahead of Euro 2012|publisher=CBC Sports|date=29 May 2012|access-date=7 September 2016}}</ref>

On 15 August 2012, he made his debut with the [[Italy national football team|Italy national team]], starting in a 1–2 friendly loss to [[England national football team|England]] at [[Wembley Stadium]]. He was substituted off for fellow debutant [[Diego Fabbrini]] in the 84th minute.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19238374|title=England 2-1 Italy|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=15 August 2012|access-date=3 June 2014}}</ref> In Destro's third appearance, on 11 September, he scored his first international goal in the first five minutes of Italy's 2–0 win against [[Malta national football team|Malta]] at the [[Stadio Alberto Braglia]] in [[Modena]], in Italy's second [[2014 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|2014 FIFA World Cup qualifying match]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/worldcup/season=2014/matches/round=2000294/match=2008568/postmatch/report/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120914174550/http://www.uefa.com/worldcup/season=2014/matches/round=2000294/match=2008568/postmatch/report/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=14 September 2012|title=Italy off the mark with minimum fuss|publisher=[[UEFA]]|date=11 September 2012|access-date=7 September 2016}}</ref>

Destro was named in the provisional 30-man squad for the [[2014 FIFA World Cup|2014 World Cup]], but was one of seven players cut from the final squad.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/27402363|title=World Cup 2014: Italy omit Giuseppe Rossi from final squad|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=1 June 2014|access-date=3 June 2014}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Destro is a quick striker with good technique and an ability to play off of his teammates, which enables him to participate in the build-up of plays. He is an accurate finisher, known for his anticipation, as well as his ability to make attacking runs into the area and subsequently shoot first time.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportmediaset.mediaset.it/mercato/articoli/articolo19276.shtml?frommobile|title=Febbre da '90: i talenti italiani|publisher=Sport Mediaset|language=it|date=29 December 2008|access-date=1 February 2017|archive-date=7 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107012115/http://www.sportmediaset.mediaset.it/mercato/articoli/articolo19276.shtml?frommobile|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/serie-a/esclusiva-tmw-carlo-regno-il-primo-mattia-destro-tra-i-grandi-371426|title=ESCLUSIVA TMW - Carlo Regno: "Il primo Mattia Destro tra i grandi..."|publisher=tuttomercatoweb.com|language=it|author1=Alessio Alaimo|date=24 July 2012|access-date=2 February 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.goal.com/it/news/809/z/2010/10/13/2160443/generazione-di-fenomeni-mattia-destro-lultimo-gioiello-della|title=Mattia Destro, l'ultimo gioiello della scuola dei bomber all'italiana|publisher=goal.com|language=it|date=13 October 2010|access-date=14 November 2014}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Destro is the son of former Italian footballer [[Flavio Destro]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Sky Sports Scout - Mattia Destro|work=Sky Sports |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/15198/7666028/sky-sports-scout-mattia-destro|access-date=30 January 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.gazzetta.it/Calcio/Giovani/Campionato_Primavera/25-01-2009/primavera-inter-c--50259167771.shtml|title=Primavera, l'Inter c'è Destro, magie "alla Ibra"|last=Della Valle|first=Fabiana|date=25 January 2009|work=La Gazzetta dello Sport|language=it|access-date=12 September 2010}}</ref> On 1 September 2014, he married model girlfriend [[Ludovica Caramis]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Mattia Destro sposa Ludovica Caramis: matrimonio da favola. E lei è super sexy|date=2 September 2014 |url=http://www.oggi.it/gossip/amori/2014/09/02/mattia-destro-sposa-ludovica-caramis-matrimonio-da-favola-e-lei-e-super-sexy/|publisher=Oggi|access-date=30 January 2015}}</ref>

In September 2020 he tested positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Genoa, anche Destro è positivo al Covid|url=https://www.ilmessaggero.it/sport/calcio/genoa_covid_giocatori_positivi_destro_asl_allenamenti_rinvio_torino-5497164.html|access-date=1 October 2020|website=www.ilmessaggero.it|date=October 2020 |language=it}}</ref><ref>{{Cite press release|title=Nota della società|url=https://genoacfc.it/nota-della-societa-4/|publisher=Genoa|date=1 October 2020|access-date=2 October 2020|language=it}}</ref>

'''Francisco Javier Muñoz Llompart''' (born 5 September 1980), known as '''Xisco''', is a Spanish [[Association football|football]] [[Manager (association football)|manager]] and former player who played mainly as a [[winger (association football)|left winger]]. He is the head coach of [[Malaysia Super League]] club [[Johor Darul Ta'zim F.C.|Johor Darul Ta'zim]].

He played 194 matches and scored 20 goals over nine seasons in [[La Liga]], spending four years at [[Real Betis|Betis]], also representing [[Valencia CF|Valencia]], [[CD Tenerife|Tenerife]], [[Recreativo de Huelva|Recreativo]] and [[Levante UD|Levante]] and winning the [[2004 UEFA Cup final|2004 UEFA Cup]] with Valencia. Starting in 2011, he played four seasons in Georgia with [[FC Dinamo Tbilisi|Dinamo Tbilisi]].

In 2019, Xisco rejoined Dinamo Tbilisi as part of the technical team, and in 2020 became their head coach. In December 2020, he was appointed at [[Watford F.C.|Watford]], achieving promotion to the [[Premier League]] in his first season but being sacked in October 2021 despite the club sitting 15th. That same month, he became manager of [[SD Huesca|Huesca]], before being replaced in June 2022. He signed for [[Anorthosis Famagusta FC|Anorthosis]] in October that year, but left three months later. In July 2023, he joined [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]] as head coach before being dismissed in October after failing to win any matches in charge.

==Playing career==
===Valencia===
Xisco was born in [[Manacor]], [[Balearic Islands]]. He began in the youth ranks of local [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]], making ten senior appearances for the [[RCD Mallorca B|B team]] in the [[Segunda División B]] in 1998. After two years with [[Valencia CF|Valencia]]'s [[Valencia CF Mestalla|equivalent]], he moved on loan to [[Recreativo de Huelva]] of [[Segunda División]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2002/07/31/mas_futbol/1028066426_850215.html|title=El Valencia cede a Xisco al Recreativo de Huelva|trans-title=Valencia loan Xisco to Recreativo de Huelva|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|language=es|date=31 July 2002|access-date=4 January 2021}}</ref> scoring ten goals in his [[2000–01 Segunda División|first season]]. He then joined [[CD Tenerife|Tenerife]] for [[2001–02 La Liga|2001–02]], before returning (always on loan) to his previous club for the [[2002–03 La Liga|2002–03 campaign]], still in [[La Liga]].<ref name=LEVANTE>{{cite web|url=https://www.levanteud.com/es/info/el-levante-ud-cierra-su-plantilla-con-el-fichaje-de-xisco-munoz|title=El Levante UD cierra su plantilla con el fichaje de Xisco Muñoz|trans-title=Levante UD complete their squad with signing of Xisco Muñoz|publisher=Levante UD|language=es|date=1 September 2009|access-date=21 January 2021}}</ref>

Xisco returned to Valencia in summer 2003 for two additional seasons, making 22 appearances as the ''Che'' conquered the [[2003–04 La Liga|2004 league title]]; he scored once as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] on 2 November 2003 to conclude a 5–0 away win against Mallorca.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/diario/2003/11/03/deportes/1067814007_850215.html|first=Cayetano|last=Ros|title=Oliveira se destapa en Son Moix|trans-title=Oliveira runs wild at ''Son Moix''|newspaper=[[El País]]|language=es|date=3 November 2003|access-date=4 January 2021}}</ref> He added eight matches in their [[2003–04 UEFA Cup|victorious run]] in the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]] also in that year, but remained on the bench in [[2004 UEFA Cup final|the final]] against [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/3724215.stm|title=Valencia 2–0 Marseille|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=19 May 2004|access-date=4 January 2021}}</ref>

===Betis===
Xisco signed with [[Real Betis]] in 2005 on a six-year deal,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/025a-0eaa0c5064f6-9a751475cb72-1000--xisco-the-kid-for-betis/|title=Xisco the kid for Betis|publisher=UEFA|date=4 July 2005|access-date=6 March 2013}}</ref> often delivering in various attacking positions and displaying all-around teamwork. He netted three times in [[2006–07 La Liga|2006–07]], including a couple of late goals against [[Racing de Santander]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=203953&cc=5739|title=Real Betis 1–1 Racing Santander|publisher=[[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]]|date=21 January 2007|access-date=6 March 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121026013943/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=203953&cc=5739|archive-date=26 October 2012}}</ref> and [[Gimnàstic de Tarragona]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=204957&cc=5739|title=Real Betis 1–1 Gimnastic de Tarragona|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=19 May 2007|access-date=6 March 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121026013948/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=204957&cc=5739|archive-date=26 October 2012}}</ref> as the [[Andalusia]]ns only avoided top-flight relegation in the last matchday.

In a rocky [[2008–09 La Liga|2008–09 season]], which ended in relegation,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.diariodesevilla.es/realbetis/plantilla-Betis_0_265173693.html|title=La plantilla del Betis, uno a uno|trans-title=The Betis squad, one by one|newspaper=[[Diario de Sevilla]]|first=Javier|last=Mérida|language=es|date=3 June 2009|access-date=21 January 2021}}</ref> Xisco only featured in nine games, scoring once.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.20minutos.es/deportes/noticia/valladolid-betis-liga-444014/0/|title=El Betis revive de la mano de Sergio García ante un Valladolid impreciso (1–3)|trans-title=Betis come to life courtesy of Sergio García against iffy Valladolid (1–3)|newspaper=[[20 minutos]]|language=es|date=18 January 2009|access-date=21 January 2021}}</ref> Dark spots included being replaced after having himself been used as a substitute in a 2–1 home defeat to [[Málaga CF|Málaga]], on 11 January 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=253063&cc=5739|title=Real Betis 1–2 Málaga|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=11 January 2009|access-date=6 March 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120715123334/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=253063&cc=5739|archive-date=15 July 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://sevilla.eldesmarque.com/real-betis/27394--sp-1544613525|title=Xisco, Babic y Juanlu, apartados; el caso llega a Jabugo|trans-title=Xisco, Babic and Juanlu, ousted; affair reaches Jabugo|publisher=El Desmarque|first=Álvaro|last=Moscoso|language=es|date=12 January 2009|access-date=2 January 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304083146/http://sevilla.eldesmarque.com/real-betis/27394--sp-1544613525|archive-date=4 March 2016}}</ref>

===Levante and later career===
In the dying minutes of the August 2009 [[transfer window]], Xisco rescinded his Betis contract and joined [[Levante UD|Levante]] also in the second division, for two seasons.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/es/news/21/fichajes/2009/09/01/1474420/mercado-el-levante-ficha-al-b%C3%A9tico-xisco|title=Mercado: El Levante ficha al bético Xisco|trans-title=Market: Levante sign ''bético'' Xisco|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|language=es|date=1 September 2009|access-date=2 January 2016}}</ref> In [[2009–10 Segunda División|his first]], he played the most he had in years, also scoring eight goals<ref>{{cite web|url=https://eldesmarque.com/valencia/levante-ud/noticias-2/14631-xisco-munoz-se-retira-y-sera-entrenador-ayudante-en-el-nastic-de-tarragona|title=Xisco Muñoz: se retira el cañón del último ascenso|trans-title=Xisco Muñoz: top gun in last promotion retires|publisher=El Desmarque|language=es|date=17 June 2016|access-date=21 January 2021}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026|bot=InternetArchiveBot}}</ref> as the [[Valencian Community]] side returned to the top flight after a two-year absence.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2010/06/13/futbol/2adivision/1276451701.html|title=El Levante celebra el centenario con un ascenso|trans-title=Levante celebrate century with promotion|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=13 June 2010|access-date=2 January 2016}}</ref>

Xisco contributed 26 matches – 18 starts – in [[2010–11 La Liga|2010–11]], as Levante finally managed to stay afloat. On 22 January 2011, he scored his only goal of the campaign in a 4–1 away loss against [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=302183&cc=5739|title=Fabiano treble sinks Levante|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=22 January 2011|access-date=6 March 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121026013958/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=302183&cc=5739|archive-date=26 October 2012}}</ref> and was released in May.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.superdeporte.es/levante/2011/05/26/xisco-munoz-marcha-triste-agradecido/128881.html|title=Xisco Muñoz se marcha "muy triste y agradecido"|trans-title=Xisco Muñoz leaves "with great sadness and appreciation"|newspaper=[[Super Deporte]]|first=Ismael|last=Algarra|language=es|date=26 May 2011|access-date=21 January 2021}}</ref>

Already aged 30, Xisco moved abroad for the first time, signing with [[FC Dinamo Tbilisi|Dinamo Tbilisi]] in [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]] and sharing teams with several compatriots.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.terra.es/deportes/futbol/articulo/dinamo-tblisi-ficha-xisco-coto-919519.htm|title=El Dinamo Tbilisi georgiano ficha a 'Xisco' Muñoz, Coto y Yagüe|trans-title=Georgia's Dinamo Tbilisi sign 'Xisco' Muñoz, Coto and Yagüe|publisher=[[Terra (company)|Terra]]|language=es|date=28 June 2011|access-date=3 July 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140226215132/http://www.terra.es/deportes/futbol/articulo/dinamo-tblisi-ficha-xisco-coto-919519.htm|archive-date=26 February 2014}}</ref> In [[2012–13 Umaglesi Liga|2012–13]], he won the [[Erovnuli Liga]] and also scored a career-best 22 goals, best in the competition.<ref name=TOPSCORER>{{cite web|url=http://sombalears.es/2013/05/xisco-munoz-campeon-de-liga-y-maximo-goleador-en-la-liga-de-georgia/|title=Xisco Muñoz, campeón de liga y máximo goleador en Georgia|trans-title=Xisco Muñoz, league champion and top scorer in Georgia|publisher=Som Balears|first=Luc|last=Alemany|language=es|date=6 May 2013|access-date=3 July 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130703224432/http://sombalears.es/2013/05/xisco-munoz-campeon-de-liga-y-maximo-goleador-en-la-liga-de-georgia/|archive-date=3 July 2013}}</ref> The player and the team retained their titles [[2013–14 Umaglesi Liga|a year later]], and his goal concluded the 3–0 win at [[FC Sioni Bolnisi|Sioni Bolnisi]] that confirmed it.<ref name=UEFA>{{cite web|url=https://es.uefa.com/insideuefa/member-associations/GEO/news/0215-0f8a56e19131-66f52f7993f4-1000--el-dinamo-retiene-el-titulo/?referrer=%2Fmemberassociations%2Fassociation%3Dgeo%2Fnews%2Fnewsid%3D2104407|title=El Dínamo retiene el título|trans-title=Dinamo retain title|publisher=UEFA|language=es|date=11 May 2014|access-date=4 January 2021}}{{dead link|date=March 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

On 14 December 2014, Xisco returned to his homeland after agreeing to an 18-month deal with third-tier Gimnàstic.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gimnasticdetarragona.com/cat2/es/act-noticia.php?id=6261|title=Xisco Muñoz, nuevo fichaje grana|trans-title=Xisco Muñoz, new ''grana'' signing|publisher=Gimnàstic Tarragona|language=es|date=14 December 2014|access-date=15 December 2014}}</ref> On 18 June 2016, he announced his retirement and became [[Vicente Moreno]]'s assistant.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gimnasticdetarragona.cat/es/xisco-munoz-penja-les-botes-i-formara-part-del-cos-tecnic-grana/|title=Xisco Muñoz cuelga las botas y formará parte del cuerpo técnico grana|trans-title=Xisco Muñoz hangs up boots and will be a part of the ''grana'' staff|publisher=Gimnàstic Tarragona|language=es|date=18 June 2016|access-date=18 June 2016}}</ref> In September of the following year, he stood in as manager of [[farm team]] [[CF Pobla de Mafumet|Pobla de Mafumet]] in the [[Tercera División]], after the promotion of [[Rodri (footballer, born 1971)|Rodri]] to the ''Nàstic'' job.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://futbolcatalunya.com/xisco-munoz-i-manel-cazorla-substitueixen-a-rodri-a-la-pobla/|title=Xisco Muñoz i Manel Cazorla substitueixen a Rodri a La Pobla|trans-title=Xisco Muñoz and Manel Cazorla replace Rodri at La Pobla|publisher=Futbol Catalunya|language=ca|date=12 September 2017|access-date=3 October 2021}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
===Dinamo Tbilisi===
Xisco returned to Dinamo Tbilisi in January 2019, as part of [[Zaur Svanadze]]'s staff.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://es.besoccer.com/noticia/xisco-munoz-regresa-al-dinamo-tiflis-566283|title=Xisco Muñoz regresa al Dinamo Tiflis|trans-title=Xisco Muñoz returns to Dinamo Tbilisi|publisher=Be Soccer|language=es|date=13 January 2019|access-date=1 May 2020|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191203152620/https://es.besoccer.com/noticia/xisco-munoz-regresa-al-dinamo-tiflis-566283|archive-date=3 December 2019}}</ref> He left at the end of the year, after the team had [[2019 Erovnuli Liga|claimed the national championship]] following a three-year absence.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2019/12/20/internacional/1576854995_717246.html|title=Vicente y Xisco dejan el Dinamo Tiflis tras ganar la liga georgiana|trans-title=Vicente and Xisco leave Dinamo Tbilisi after winning the Georgian league|newspaper=Diario AS|language=es|date=20 December 2019|access-date=1 May 2020}}</ref>

In August 2020, Xisco again returned to Dinamo, now as head coach of the club.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2020/08/31/migrantes_del_balon/1598895890_570195.html|title=Xisco Muñoz regresa al Dinamo Tbilisi, su segunda casa|trans-title=Xisco returns to Dinamo Tbilisi, his second home|newspaper=Diario AS|first=Martín|last=Manchón|language=es|date=31 August 2020|access-date=13 September 2020}}</ref> With several compatriots on the pitch and the bench, they [[2020 Erovnuli Liga|won the league]] in December.<ref name=COACH>{{cite news|url=https://www.ultimahora.es/deportes/futbol/2020/12/10/1221711/xisco-munoz-gana-liga-georgiana.html|title=Xisco Muñoz hace campeón al Dinamo de Tiflis|trans-title=Xisco Muñoz makes Dinamo Tbilisi into champions|newspaper=[[Última Hora (Spain)|Última Hora]]|language=es|date=10 December 2020|access-date=4 January 2021}}</ref>

===Watford===
Xisco was appointed as manager of [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] on 21 December 2020, after the dismissal of [[Vladimir Ivić]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.watfordfc.com/news/club/official-xisco-munoz-appointed-head-coach|title=Official: Xisco Muñoz appointed head coach|publisher=Watford F.C.|date=21 December 2020|access-date=21 December 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11686/12168816/xisco-munoz-watford-appoint-spaniard-as-new-head-coach-following-sacking-of-vladimir-ivic|title=Xisco Munoz: Watford appoint Spaniard as new head coach following sacking of Vladimir Ivic|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|date=21 December 2020|access-date=11 February 2021}}</ref> His debut in the [[EFL Championship]] was five days later, a 1–0 home victory over leaders [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.watfordobserver.co.uk/sport/18971214.xisco-munoz-delighted-watford-win-norwich-city/|title=Xisco Munoz delighted by Watford win over Norwich City|newspaper=[[Watford Observer]]|first=Ryan|last=Gray|date=26 December 2020|access-date=4 January 2021}}</ref>

After a run of five straight wins, Xisco was awarded the [[EFL Championship Manager of the Month|Championship Manager of the Month]] award for March 2021.<ref name=MOTM>{{cite web|url=https://www.watfordfc.com/news/munoz-wins-manager-of-the-month-its-for-everyone|title=Muñoz wins Manager Of The Month: "It's for everyone"|publisher=Watford F.C.|first=Kevin|last=Affleck|date=9 April 2021|access-date=9 April 2021}}</ref> On 24 April, his team [[2020–21 EFL Championship|achieved promotion]] to the [[Premier League]] with two games remaining, after a 1–0 win against [[Millwall F.C.|Millwall]] at [[Vicarage Road]].<ref name=EFL>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/56781828|title=Watford 1–0 Millwall|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Rob|last=Stevens|date=24 April 2021|access-date=25 April 2021}}</ref>

Xisco was sacked on 3 October 2021, with the side being 15th after seven matches; it was the 13th change in the club's hotseat since the arrival of owner [[Gino Pozzo]] in 2012.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/58778752|title=Xisco Munoz: Watford sack manager after poor spell|publisher=BBC Sport|date=3 October 2021|access-date=3 October 2021}}</ref> In an official statement, Watford wrote that the coach had been presiding over a "negative trend at a time when team cohesion should be visibly improving".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.watfordfc.com/news/club-statement-xisco-munoz|title=Club statement: Xisco Muñoz|publisher=Watford F.C.|date=3 October 2021|access-date=3 October 2021}}</ref>

===Huesca===
On 26 October 2021, Xisco signed as coach of [[SD Huesca|Huesca]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.superdeporte.es/futbol/2021/10/26/xisco-munoz-nuevo-entrenador-huesca-58838880.html|title=Xisco Muñoz, nuevo entrenador del Huesca|trans-title=Xisco Muñoz, new Huesca manager|newspaper=Super Deporte|first=Javier|last=Bengoa|language=es|date=26 October 2021|access-date=17 November 2021}}</ref> Having finished in 13th in his [[2021–22 Segunda División|only season]] with nine wins out of 30,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.heraldo.es/noticias/deportes/futbol/sd-huesca/2022/05/29/xisco-sd-huesca-no-objetivo-disculpas-reflexionar-1577966.html|title=Xisco Muñoz: "No se ha logrado el objetivo, hay que pedir disculpas y reflexionar"|trans-title=Xisco Muñoz: "The objective hasn't been achieved, we have to apologise and reflect"|newspaper=[[Heraldo de Aragón]]|first=Miguel|last=Barluenga|language=es|date=29 May 2022|access-date=16 June 2022}}</ref> he was replaced in June by [[José Ángel Ziganda]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.heraldo.es/noticias/deportes/futbol/sd-huesca/2022/06/13/cuco-ziganda-sd-huesca-si-quiero-1581272.html|title=Cuco Ziganda da el "sí, quiero" a la SD Huesca|trans-title=Cuco Ziganda gives the "yes, I do" to SD Huesca"|newspaper=Heraldo de Aragón|first=Miguel|last=Barluenga|language=es|date=13 June 2022|access-date=16 June 2022}}</ref>

===Anorthosis===
On 4 October 2022, Xisco was appointed manager of [[Cypriot First Division]] club [[Anorthosis Famagusta FC|Anorthosis]] until the end of [[2022–23 Cypriot First Division|the season]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.watfordobserver.co.uk/sport/23017661.ex-watford-boss-munoz-takes-anorthosis-famagusta-cyprus/|title=Ex-Watford boss Munoz takes over at Anorthosis Famagusta in Cyprus|newspaper=Watford Observer|first=Anthony|last=Matthews|date=4 October 2022|access-date=4 October 2022}}</ref> Three months later, after a series of five winless games, he was replaced by [[Vesko Mihajlović]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://protathlima.cyprustimes.com/podosfairo-kyprou/a-katigoria/anorthosi/me-vesko-kontra-se-aek/|title=Με Βέσκο κόντρα σε ΑΕΚ|trans-title=With Vesko against AEK|publisher=Protathlima|language=el|date=5 January 2023|access-date=6 March 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://huelva24.com/art/168308/gorka-santamaria-ya-tiene-nuevo-equipo-y-xisco-munoz-es-cesado-en-chipre|title=Gorka Santamaría ya tiene nuevo equipo y Xisco Muñoz es cesado en Chipre|trans-title=Gorka Santamaría already has a new team and Xisco Muñoz is sacked in Cyprus|publisher=Huelva 24|language=es|date=13 January 2023|access-date=6 March 2023}}</ref>

===Sheffield Wednesday===
On 4 July 2023, Xisco joined [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]] as head coach;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.swfc.co.uk/news/2023/july/owls-appoint-xisco-munoz-as-first-team-manager/|title=Owls appoint Xisco Muñoz as first team manager|publisher=Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|date=4 July 2023|access-date=4 July 2023}}</ref> he brought in his brother Miguel as assistant, Roberto Cuesta as first-team coach and Antonello Brambilla as goalkeeper coach, all of whom he had worked with at Watford.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.swfc.co.uk/news/2023/july/xisco-adds-to-coaching-team/|title=Xisco adds to coaching team|publisher=Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|date=14 July 2023|access-date=14 July 2023}}</ref> His first competitive game in charge was at home to newly relegated [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]], a 2–1 defeat,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.examinerlive.co.uk/sport/football/news/highlights-sheffield-wednesday-southampton-updates-27459346|title=Sheffield Wednesday 1 Southampton 2 highlights as ex-Blades striker Che Adams bags later winner|newspaper=Yorkshire Examiner|first=Ricky|last=Charlesworth|date=4 August 2023|access-date=6 August 2023}}</ref> and culminated in a 1–0 away loss to [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] on 3 October. He had led the Owls to their worst ever start to a season, with just two points from the first ten matches.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.yorkshirepost.co.uk/sport/football/sheffield-wednesday/xisco-munoz-has-now-led-sheffield-wednesday-to-worst-start-in-their-history-after-loss-to-west-brom-4358615|title=Xisco Munoz has now led Sheffield Wednesday to worst start in their history after loss to West Brom|newspaper=[[The Yorkshire Post]]|date=3 October 2023|access-date=4 October 2023}}</ref> A day later, he was dismissed.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.swfc.co.uk/news/2023/october/club-statement/|title=Club statement|publisher=Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|date=4 October 2023|access-date=4 October 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/66852888|title=Xisco Munoz: Sheffield Wednesday sack boss after winless start in Championship|publisher=BBC Sport|date=4 October 2023|access-date=5 October 2023}}</ref>

===DAC Dunajská Streda===
On 19 November 2023, Xisco signed as manager of [[FC DAC 1904 Dunajská Streda|DAC Dunajská Streda]] until the end of [[2023–24 Slovak First Football League|the campaign]], with the option of another year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://fcdac.sk/sk/clanek.asp?id=Novym-trenerom-DAC-u-Xisco-Munoz-9622|title=Novým trénerom DAC-u Xisco Muňoz|trans-title=Xisco Muñoz is the new manager of DAC|publisher=DAC Dunajská Streda|first=Nagy|last=Krisztián|language=sk|date=19 November 2023|access-date=1 December 2023|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250123210350/https://fcdac.sk/sk/clanek.asp?id=Novym-trenerom-DAC-u-Xisco-Munoz-9622|archive-date=23 January 2025}}</ref> He was relieved of his duties on 27 November 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://fcdac.sk//sk/clanek.asp?id=Xisco-Munoz-konci-na-lavicke-DAC-u-10723|title=Xisco Muňoz končí na lavičke DAC-u|trans-title=Xisco Muňoz ends up on the DAC bench|publisher=DAC Dunajská Streda|first=Nagy|last=Krisztián|language=sk|date=27 November 2024|access-date=29 November 2024|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241207133349/https://fcdac.sk/sk/clanek.asp?id=Xisco-Munoz-konci-na-lavicke-DAC-u-10723|archive-date=7 December 2024}}</ref>

===Johor Darul Ta'zim===
Xisco became coach of [[Johor Darul Ta'zim F.C.|Johor Darul Ta'zim]] on 6 June 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the-afc.com/en/club/afc_champions_league_elite.html/news/munoz-takes-charge-of-johor-darul-tazim|title=Munoz takes charge of Johor Darul Ta'zim|publisher=[[Asian Football Confederation]]|date=7 June 2025|access-date=12 August 2026}}</ref> During his [[2025–26 Malaysia Super League|first season]] in charge, he led the team to a fourth consecutive [[Treble (association football)#Domestic trebles|domestic treble]], winning the [[Malaysia Super League]], [[Malaysia FA Cup]] and [[Malaysia Cup]]. Additionally, he guided them to the [[2025–26 AFC Champions League Elite|quarter-finals]] of the [[AFC Champions League Elite]], where they lost 2–1 to defending champions [[Al-Ahli Saudi FC|Al-Ahli]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.the-afc.com/en/club/afc_champions_league_elite.html/news/munoz-proud-of-jdt-despite-heartbreaking-exit|title=Munoz proud of JDT despite heartbreaking exit|publisher=Asian Football Confederation|date=18 April 2026|access-date=12 August 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nst.com.my/sports/football/2026/05/1450314/munoz-finds-asian-football-his-toughest-challenge-yet|title=Munoz finds Asian football his toughest challenge yet|newspaper=[[New Straits Times]]|first=Farah|last=Azharie|date=28 May 2026|access-date=12 August 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Xisco is the older brother of another footballer, [[Toni Muñoz (footballer, born 1982)|Toni Muñoz]]. He appeared once for Mallorca's first team, but spent the vast majority of his career in the lower leagues of his country.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://archivo.marca.com/edicion/marca/futbol/1a_division/murcia/es/desarrollo/1027157.html|title=El Murcia derrota al Larissa en la presentación ante su público|trans-title=Murcia defeat Larissa in presentation to home crowd|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=18 August 2007|access-date=6 March 2013}}</ref>

'''Sascha Riether''' ({{IPA|de|ˈzaʃa ˈʁiːtɐ}}; born 23 March 1983) is a German former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Defender (association football)|right back]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kicker.de/sascha-riether/spieler/bundesliga/2011-12/1-fc-koeln|title=Riether, Sascha|language=de|publisher=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]]|access-date =9 July 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190308201640/http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/bundesliga/vereine/1-bundesliga/2011-12/1-fc-koeln-16/28296/spieler_sascha-riether.html |archive-date=8 March 2019|url-status=live}}</ref> In addition to playing in the right-back position, Riether has also played in defensive midfield, center back and right midfield positions throughout his whole career.<ref>{{cite news|title=Felix Magaths Härtefälle: Von Simunek bis Dejagah|url=https://www.kicker.de/felix-magaths-haertefaelle_von-simunek-bis-dejagah-217225/artikel|publisher=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]]|language=de|date=4 August 2009|access-date =25 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180318113932/http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/bundesliga/startseite/217225/artikel_felix-magaths-haertefaelle_von-simunek-bis-dejagah.html|archive-date=18 March 2018|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fulhamfc.com/kids-zone/ffc-news/2013/march/08/riethers-tips|title=Riether's Right-Back Tips|publisher=Fulham F.C.|date=8 March 2013|access-date =25 March 2018|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180324193020/http://www.fulhamfc.com/kids-zone/ffc-news/2013/march/08/riethers-tips|archivedate=24 March 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

His then U19 manager [[Uli Stielike]] described him in his early career as "very disciplined, versatile player, strong on the right side."<ref>{{cite news|title="Lehmann - der Durchstarter der EM"|url=https://www.kicker.de/lehmann---der-durchstarter-der-em-269474/artikel|publisher=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]]|language=de|date=2 August 2002|access-date =25 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180703064956/http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/junioren/startseite/269474/artikel_lehmann---der-durchstarter-der-em.html|archive-date=3 July 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> During his playing career, Riether was known for his high commitment during the match and was considered a player who was more inclined to horizontal passes instead of creating chances with long passes.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://spielverlagerung.de/2011/12/20/adventskalender-turchen-20-sascha-riether/|title=Adventskalender, Türchen 20: Sascha Born in [[Lahr]], [[West Germany]], Riether came from a football family in which his father and older brother and started playing football when he was four years old.<ref name="Riether Four Years Old">{{cite web|url=https://www.badische-zeitung.de/natuerlich-bin-ich-aufgeregt--191760974.html|title="Natürlich bin ich aufgeregt"|publisher=Badische Zeitung|language=de|date=12 May 2007|access-date=7 March 2021|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210305160636/https://www.badische-zeitung.de/natuerlich-bin-ich-aufgeregt--191760974.html|archive-date=5 March 2021|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Riether Interview 2013">{{cite web|url=https://www.badische-zeitung.de/mein-spitzname-ist-maschine--73299617.html|title="Mein Spitzname ist Maschine"|publisher=Badische Zeitung|language=de|date=5 July 2013|access-date=7 March 2021|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210305161356/https://www.badische-zeitung.de/mein-spitzname-ist-maschine--73299617.html|archive-date=5 March 2021|url-status=live}}</ref> Riether then started his football career at B-youth of SC Freiburg before he joined the side in July 1998.<ref name="Riether1"/><ref name="Riether Four Years Old"/><ref name="Riether Interview 2013"/> Riether previously was at the youth teams of FV Kuhbach (now SC Kuhbach-Reichenbach) and Offenburger FV.<ref name="Riether1"/><ref name="Riether Interview 2013"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.scfreiburg.com/node/8559|title=Sascha Riether kehrt zum SC zurück|publisher=SC Freiburg|language=de|date=27 June 2014|access-date =25 March 2018|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180325114338/https://www.scfreiburg.com/node/8559|archivedate=25 March 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Fulham===
On 6 July 2012, Riether moved to [[Premier League]] side [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]] on a season-long loan deal from parent club 1. FC Köln, after they were relegated to the [[2012–13 2. Bundesliga|2. Bundesliga]], reuniting with his former Wolfsburg teammate [[Ashkan Dejagah]].<ref name="Riether The Guardian 2012"/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/18742678|title=Fulham sign Cologne defender Sascha Riether on loan|publisher=BBC Sport|date=6 July 2012|access-date =6 July 2012}}</ref> The move also had an option to acquire the player at the end of the loan period.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fulhamfc.com/news/2012/july/06/fulham-sign-riether|title=Fulham Sign Riether|publisher=Fulham F.C.|date=6 July 2012|access-date =25 March 2018|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180323231103/http://www.fulhamfc.com/news/2012/july/06/fulham-sign-riether|archivedate=23 March 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> After securing the move to his new club, Riether spoke of his delight for being able to suit up at [[Craven Cottage]], "I remember Craven Cottage being a great stadium with great fans, and I hope I can go on to have a great season here."<ref>{{cite web|title=Fulham secure Riether on loan|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=1660859.html|publisher=FIFA Official Website|date=6 July 2012|access-date =6 July 2012|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120707205155/https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=1660859.html|archivedate=7 July 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Riether made his Fulham debut on the first day of the season against [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]], a 5–0 thumping of the Canaries at Craven Cottage.<ref>{{cite news|title=Fulham 5 Norwich City 0: Fulham score five to beat sorry Norwich City|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/fulham-5-norwich-0-fulham-score-five-to-beat-sorry-norwich-8059889.html|work=London Evening Standard|date=18 August 2012|access-date =25 March 2018}}</ref> Since making his debut, he quickly established himself in the starting eleven for the side, beating out [[Stephen Kelly (Irish footballer)|Stephen Kelly]] over the right–back position.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fulhamfc.com/news/2012/august/17/riether-preview|title=Riether Preview|publisher=Fulham F.C.|date=17 August 2012|access-date =25 March 2018|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180323233341/http://www.fulhamfc.com/news/2012/august/17/riether-preview|archivedate=23 March 2018|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fulhamfc.com/news/2012/september/17/rietherreaction|title=So Much Fun|publisher=Fulham F.C.|date=17 September 2012|access-date =25 March 2018|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180323233358/http://www.fulhamfc.com/news/2012/september/17/rietherreaction|archivedate=23 March 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> On 10 November, Riether was adjudged to have handled the ball inside the area and referee [[Phil Dowd]] awarded a 93rd-minute penalty to [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] with the game tied 3–3; [[Mikel Arteta]]'s spot-kick was saved by [[Mark Schwarzer]] and Fulham escaped the [[Emirates Stadium|Emirates]] with a point.<ref>{{cite news|title=Mikel Arteta's late penalty was saved as Arsenal and Fulham drew 3-3|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/arsenal-vs-fulham/report/261661|publisher=Sky Sports|date=11 November 2012|access-date =25 March 2018}}</ref> Riether scored his first goal in the Premier League for Fulham in a 2–2 draw at [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] on 2 March 2013.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21556900|title=Sunderland rallied from two goals down to draw with Fulham and end a three-match losing run|publisher=BBC Sport|date=2 March 2013|access-date =2 March 2013}}</ref> Despite missing out three matches during the 2012–13 season,<ref>{{cite news|title=Fulham defender suffers injury blow|url=https://www.getwestlondon.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/fulham-defender-suffers-injury-blow-5971307|publisher=Get West London|date=9 December 2012|access-date =25 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Fulham handed boost ahead of Stoke City clash|url=https://www.getwestlondon.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/fulham-handed-boost-ahead-stoke-5969814|publisher=Get West London|date=22 February 2013|access-date =25 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Fulham handed boost ahead of Everton trip|url=https://www.getwestlondon.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/fulham-handed-boost-ahead-everton-5968323|publisher=Get West London|date=25 April 2013|access-date =25 March 2018}}</ref> he went on to make 39 appearances and scoring once in all competitions. Following a successful debut season in [[2012–13 Premier League|England]], Riether was voted as the club's Player of the Season by his fellow players, beating out the likes of top scorer [[Dimitar Berbatov]] and [[Greece national football team|Greek]] midfielder [[Giorgos Karagounis]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Premier League report card: 11th to 20th|url=http://www.espnfc.com/story/1454703/premier-league-2012-13-club-by-club-review-11th-20th|publisher=ESPN FC|date=20 May 2013|access-date =20 May 2013|first1=Roger|last1=Bennett|first2=Iain|last2=Macintosh}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fulhamfc.com/news/2013/may/07/player-of-the-season|title=Player of the Season|publisher=Fulham F.C.|date=7 May 2013|access-date =25 March 2018|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180324203058/http://www.fulhamfc.com/news/2013/may/07/player-of-the-season|archivedate=24 March 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 16 May 2013, Riether agreed a permanent deal with Fulham for an undisclosed fee. He said "I am pleased after a first season in England and am focused on my other tasks in Fulham."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11681/8716534/premier-league-sascha-riether-agrees-permanent-deal-with-fulham|title=Premier League: Sascha Riether agrees Permanent Deal with =25 March 2018}}</ref> Riether continued to regain his first team place, in the right–back position despite facing competition from new signing, [[Elsad Zverotić]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Jol eyes defensive boost ahead of deadline|url=https://www.getwestlondon.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/jol-eyes-defensive-boost-ahead-5965140|publisher=Get West London|date=29 August 2013|access-date =25 ===Senior career===
Due to his good performance at Wolfsburg, Riether was considered to be called up by the national team.<ref>{{cite news|title=Sascha Riether: Bald wieder für Deutschland|url=https://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/bald-wieder-fuer-deutschland-10157410.bild.html|publisher=Bild.de|language=de|date=20 October 2009|access-date =25 March 2018}}</ref> However, in May 2010, he was cut from being short–listed for the [[2010 FIFA World Cup|FIFA World Cup]] squad for the side.<ref>{{cite news|title=Raus! Meister-Absturz reißt Schäfer und Gentner mit|url=https://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/reisst-schaefer-und-gentner-mit-12459256.bild.html|publisher=Bild.de|language=de|date=7 May 2010|access-date =25 March 2018}}</ref> Three months later, he was finally called up by the senior team.<ref>{{cite news|title=Debütantenball für Riether und Reus|url=https://www.kicker.de/debuetantenball-fuer-riether-und-reus-540781/artikel|publisher=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]]|language=de|date=6 August 2010|access-date =25 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180703065312/http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/nationalelf/startseite/540781/artikel_debuetantenball-fuer-riether-und-reus.html|archive-date=3 July 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

Riether made his debut with the [[Germany national football team|Germany national team]] on 11 August 2010, in a friendly against [[Denmark national football team|Denmark]] and played 34 minutes coming on as substitute for [[Andreas Beck (footballer)|Andreas Beck]], as the match finished in a 2–2 draw.<ref>{{cite web|url =https://www.uefa.com/european-qualifiers/teams/players/53639--sascha-riether/|title=Sascha Riether|publisher=UEFA|access-date =6 July 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Löw-Schützlinge mit Licht und Schatten|url=https://www.kicker.de/daenemark-gegen-deutschland-2010-nationalteams-freundschaftsspiele-995258/analyse|publisher=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]]|language=de|date=11 August 2010|access-date =25 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180624084510/http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/nationalelf/startseite/fussball-nationalteams-freundschaftsspiele/2010/5/995258/spielanalyse_daenemark_deutschland.html|archive-date=24 June 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> After the match, he said about his debut, quoting: "It was very special for me, the first international match, but unfortunately we did not win, but I'm really happy to get a taste of it."<ref>{{cite news|title=Löw: "Gute Ansätze"|url=https://www.kicker.de/loew_gute-ansaetze-541031/artikel|publisher=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]]|language=de|date=11 August 2010|access-date =25 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180703065309/http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/nationalelf/startseite/541031/artikel_loew_gute-ansaetze.html|archive-date=3 July 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

To date, Riether's only other appearance with the national side was on 7 September 2010, playing the full 90 minutes of a 6–1 thumping of [[Azerbaijan national football team|Azerbaijan]] in a [[UEFA Euro 2012 qualifying Group A|UEFA Euro 2012]] qualifying match.<ref>{{cite news|title=Klose trifft doppelt|url=https://www.kicker.de/deutschland-gegen-aserbaidschan-2010-em-qualifikation-999626/analyse|publisher=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]]|language=de|date=7 September 2010|access-date =25 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180703112307/http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/em/qualifikation/em-qualifikation/2010-11/2/999626/spielanalyse_deutschland_aserbaidschan.html|archive-date=3 July 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> Since then, he has been called up by the national team on two occasions.<ref>{{cite news|title=Klärung der "K-Frage" vor dem 2018|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Löw gibt Großkreutz eine Chance|url=https://www.kicker.de/loew-gibt-grosskreutz-eine-chance-543102/artikel|publisher=[[Kicker ==Personal life==
Born in [[Lahr]], [[West Germany]], Riether grew up in [[Kühbach]] and excelled in wrestling.<ref name="Riether1">{{cite news|title=Der kleinste macht die größten Schritte|url=https://www.kicker.de/der-kleinste-macht-die-groessten-schritte-277479/artikel|publisher=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]]|language=de|date=9 January 2003|access-date =25 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180317143225/http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/2bundesliga/startseite/277479/artikel_der-kleinste-macht-die-groessten-schritte.html|archive-date=17 March 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> However, he had no interest in freestyle or Greco-Roman, leading him to change his interests to football.<ref name="Riether1"/><ref name="Riether Interview 2013"/> His interest in endurance racing earned him the nickname "Herbie".<ref>{{cite news|title=Calmund schnappt sich Sascha Riether|url=https://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/berater-vertrag-mit-reiner-calmund-6526356.bild.html|publisher=Bild.de|language=de|date=21 November 2008|access-date =25 March 2018}}</ref> Growing up, he supported Borussia Dortmund and idolised [[Matthias Sammer]].<ref name="Riether Four Years Old"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fulhamfc.com/kids-zone/ffc-news/my-hero-riether|title=Riether: My Hero|publisher=Fulham F.C.|date=13 December 2012|access-date =25 March 2018|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180324191106/http://www.fulhamfc.com/kids-zone/ffc-news/my-hero-riether|archivedate=24 March 2018|url-status=live}}</ref>

In his early football career, Riether developed a reputation as "a good schoolboy, who always does his work without corners and edges, never attracts attention and therefore sometimes receives too little attention."<ref>{{cite news|title=Riether: Weg mit dem braven Image|url=https://www.kicker.de/riether_weg-mit-dem-braven-image-309004/artikel|publisher=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]]|language=de|date=3 January 2005|access-date =25 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180317174836/http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/bundesliga/startseite/309004/artikel_riether_weg-mit-dem-braven-image.html|archive-date=17 March 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> He left school "at least 2-Abi" in 2002.<ref name="Riether Four Years Old"/><ref>{{cite news|title=So schlau sind unsere Fußball-Stars|url=https://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/manuel-neuer/schlaue-fussball-spieler-21092650.bild.html|publisher=Bild.de|language=de|date=18 November 2011|access-date =25 March 2018}}</ref> In addition to speaking German, Riether speaks Spanish, French, English and some Portuguese.<ref>{{cite news|title=Riether: Darum verzichte ich für Köln auf Geld|url=https://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/sascha-riether/darum-verzichte-ich-fuer-koeln-auf-geld-18782810.bild.html|publisher=Bild.de|language=de|date=10 July 2011|access-date =25 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.fulhamfc.com/news/2012/july/14/a-fluent-approach|title=A Fluent Approach|publisher=Fulham F.C.|date=14 July 2012|access-date =25 March 2018|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180323231119/http://www.fulhamfc.com/news/2012/july/14/a-fluent-approach|archivedate=23 March 2018|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://schalke04.de/interview/sascha-riether-wir-sind-eine-mannschaft/|title=Sascha Riether: Wir sind eine Mannschaft!|date=11 August 2016 |publisher=FC Schalke 04|language=de|access-date =25 March 2018|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180325155438/https://schalke04.de/interview/sascha-riether-wir-sind-eine-mannschaft/|archivedate=25 March 2018|url-status=live}}</ref> During his time at Wolfsburg, Riether developed a friendship with his then teammates, Gentner and [[Marcel Schäfer]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Das brutale Kumpel-Duell|url=https://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/vfl-wolfsburg/das-brutale-kumpel-duell-16891320.bild.html|publisher=Bild.de|language=de|date=18 March 2011|access-date =25 March 2018}}</ref>

Riether is married to his wife Susana, a law student.<ref>{{cite news|title=Sascha Riether: Den Uefa-Cup im Blick und die Heimat im Herzen|url=https://www.bo.de/sport/lokalsport/sascha-riether-den-uefa-cup-im-blick-und-die-heimat-im-herzen|publisher=Baden Line|language=de|date=8 April 2009|access-date =25 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Schalkes Neuer Sascha Riether ist Meister ohne Meisterprämie|url=https://www.derwesten.de/sport/fussball/s04/schalkes-neuer-sascha-riether-ist-meister-ohne-meisterpraemie-id11012896.html|publisher=Der Westen|language=de|date=23 August 2015|access-date=7 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=FC Schalke 04: So schön feiern die Schalke-Stars Weihnachten|url=https://www.derwesten.de/sport/fussball/s04/fc-schalke-04-so-schoen-feiern-die-schalke-stars-weihnachten-id209083791.html|publisher=Der Westen|language=de|date=25 December 2016|access-date=7 March 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://schalke04.de/inside/neu-der-schalke-04-podcast-folge-1-mit-sascha-riether/|title=Neu: Der Schalke 04 Podcast – Folge 1 mit Sascha Riether|publisher=FC Schalke 04|language=de|date=9 August 2019|access-date=7 March 2021|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200813075655/https://schalke04.de/inside/neu-der-schalke-04-podcast-folge-1-mit-sascha-riether/|archive-date=13 August 2020|url-status=live}}</ref> In June 2020, he became a first time father when his wife gave birth to a baby girl, Sarah.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://schalke04.de/bundesliga/sascha-riether-ueber-babyglueck-berlin-und-bayer-04/|title=Sascha Riether über Babyglück, Berlin und Bayer 04|publisher=FC Schalke 04|language=de|date=10 June 2020|access-date=7 March 2021|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20200918200807/https://schalke04.de/bundesliga/sascha-riether-ueber-babyglueck-berlin-und-bayer-04/|archive-date=18 September 2020|url-status=live}}</ref>
