'''Daniel Omoya Braaten''' (born 25 May 1982) is a Norwegian former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[winger (association football)|winger]]. He has previously played for [[Skeid Fotball|Skeid]], [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]], [[Bolton Wanderers]], [[Toulouse FC|Toulouse]], [[SK Brann|Brann]] and [[Stabæk Fotball|Stabæk]]. Of Nigerian descent, he was capped 52 times for the [[Norway national football team|Norway national team]], scoring 4 goals.

==Club career==
===Early career===
[[File:Daniel Braaten.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Braaten playing for [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]]]]

Braaten was born in [[Oslo]], Norway.<ref>{{Hugman|22380|access-date=19 April 2022}}</ref> He started his career in the [[Skeid Fotball|Skeid]] youth academy at the age of six. He later won the Norwegian Junior Cup with the team in 1999, aged 17. The following year he was promoted to the first team, where he played for four years before joining giants [[Rosenborg BK]] in 2004, after 102 caps and 22 goals for Skeid. Before signing for Rosenborg, Braaten had attracted interest from various clubs in Norway and abroad, and had a trial with French side [[RC Lens]] in late 2003 with [[Daniel Fredheim Holm]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.vg.no/pub/vgart.hbs?artid=208436 |title=Lens vil ha Daniel Braaten - 1. divisjon - VG |website=Vg.no |date=5 January 2004 |access-date=1 October 2016}}</ref> Braaten had however trained with Rosenborg as early as autumn 2002, but was still in contract with Skeid, before signing in 2004 for approximately £250,000.

Braaten had become one of the most profiled players of the [[Norwegian Premier League]], through his colourful, untraditional and artistic playing style. He had become known especially for his individual technical skills and physical strength, and as a player who did unexpected things on the field, surprising both opposing players and the audience. He was famous not only for his pace, but also for his mastery of the [[seal dribble]], an incredibly difficult trick involving running while bouncing (and controlling) the ball on top of the head.

===European career===
[[File:Daniel Braaten'13.JPG|thumb|upright|Braaten playing for [[F.C. Copenhagen|Copenhagen]] in 2013]]

On 3 August 2007, Braaten signed for [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] for a reported fee of £450,000. He scored his first goal in English football just over three weeks later, netting the final goal in Bolton's 3–0 win over [[Reading F.C.|Reading]].<ref>{{cite news| url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/6952878.stm | work=BBC News | first=Caroline | last=Cheese | title=Bolton 3–0 Reading | date=25 August 2007}}</ref> He failed to secure a permanent spot on the team, however, and after a tough season in England, Braaten signed a three-year contract with French side Toulouse on 25 June 2008.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://fotball.adressa.no/internasjonal/article111145.ece |title=Hareide glad for Braaten-overgang | adressa.no |access-date=25 June 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080628173843/http://fotball.adressa.no/internasjonal/article111145.ece |archive-date=28 June 2008}}</ref> He was included as part of the deal which saw [[Johan Elmander]] move to Bolton. He scored his first league goal in Toulouse's 4–1 victory over [[Paris Saint-Germain FC|Paris Saint-Germain]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuilleMatch.asp?saison%3D2008%2F2009%26code_evt%3DD1%26code_jr_tr%3DJ29%26num_ordre%3D10 |title=Ligue 1 : Toulouse FC / Paris Saint-Germain - 29ème Journée - Feuille de match |access-date=22 March 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090324134017/http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuilleMatch.asp?saison=2008%2F2009&code_evt=D1&code_jr_tr=J29&num_ordre=10 |archive-date=24 March 2009}}</ref> He performed a unique celebration by spinning on his back while spinning upwards at the same time after scoring his first goal for the club. He was released from his contract in July 2013.

Two months later, in September, Braaten signed a one-year-long deal with Danish side [[F.C. Copenhagen|Copenhagen]], where he was given shirt no. 22. During his time in the Danish capital, he scored one goal in the league and a back-heel goal in the [[UEFA Champions League]] to secure a 1–0 victory over [[Galatasaray S.K. (football)|Galatasaray]]. At the end of the season Braaten left Copenhagen without a new contract and returned to Norway.

===Return to Norway===
On 9 February 2015, Braaten signed a one-year deal with [[Kjetil Rekdal]] and [[Vålerenga]] in the Norwegian [[Tippeliga]] after almost eight months as a free agent. He scored his first, and only, goal for his new club away versus [[Sandefjord Fotball|Sandefjord]] on his birthday, 25 May. On 3 December 2015, it was announced that his contract would not be renewed, something that surprised many critics as he had performed well in the previous season.<ref>{{cite web|author=Joachim Baardsen joachim.baardsen@dagbladet.no |url=http://www.dagbladet.no/2015/12/03/sport/fotball/valerenga/daniel_braaten/42222440/ |title=Braaten ferdig i Vålerenga - sport |website=Dagbladet.no |date=3 December 2015 |access-date=1 October 2016}}</ref> After training with [[SK Brann]] during the winter, he signed a one-year contract with the club on 21 February 2016, his fourth club in just as many years.<ref name="brann1">{{cite web |author=Tekst: Gorm Natlandsmyr, Brann.no |url=http://www.brann.no/news/article/rtex0qi4yk8l1jf8a6vs5k2t3/title/na-har-braaten-signert-for-brann |title=Nyheter | Brann |website=Brann.no |access-date=1 October 2016 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160224084141/http://www.brann.no/news/article/rtex0qi4yk8l1jf8a6vs5k2t3/title/na-har-braaten-signert-for-brann |archive-date=24 February 2016}}</ref> After 55 games for Brann, he left the club at the end of the 2018 season.<ref>[https://www.tv2.no/a/10218390/ Daniel Braaten (36) er ferdig i Brann], tv2.no, 15 November 2018</ref>

==International career==
[[File:Daniel Braaten defended by Stewart Downing Norway-England.jpg|thumb|upright|Braaten (right) playing for Norway in 2012]]

After playing four matches for Norway U18 in 2000, and two matches for [[Norway national under-21 football team|Norway U21]] in 2003,<ref name="nff">{{cite web|url=http://www.fotball.no/Community/Profil/?fiksId=1999268 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120509144507/http://www.fotball.no/Community/Profil/?fiksId=1999268 |url-status=dead |archive-date=9 May 2012 |language=no |title=Daniel Omoya Braaten's profil |work=fotball.no |publisher=[[Football Association of Norway]] |access-date=31 October 2012 }}</ref> Braaten made his debut for [[Norway national football team|Norway]] on 22 January 2004 in a [[exhibition game|friendly match]] against [[Sweden men's national football team|Sweden]], when playing for Skeid in [[Adeccoligaen]], the [[Norwegian football league system|second-tier]] league in Norway. His first international goal came against [[Estonia national football team|Estonia]], in a [[Exhibition game|Friendly]] match on 20 April 2005, a game Norway won 2–1. As of May 2018, he has been [[cap (football)|capped]] 52 times for [[Norway national football team|Norway]], scoring four goals.<ref name="Søfting">{{cite web|url=http://www.home.no/greenriver/players/braaten.html |language=no |title=Daniel Braaten |access-date=12 November 2011 |first=Thomas |last=Søfting |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120612180533/http://www.home.no/greenriver/players/braaten.html |archive-date=12 June 2012}}</ref>

'''Walter Gerardo Pandiani Urquiza''' (born 27 April 1976) is a Uruguayan [[Association football|football]] [[Manager (association football)|manager]] and former player who played as a [[Forward (association football)#Striker|striker]]. He is the current [[Manager (association football)|manager]] of [[Tercera Federación]] club [[Palencia CF|Palencia]].

He started his career at [[Peñarol]] in Uruguay, before moving to Spain in 2000, where he would spend the next 12 out of 13 seasons, playing 279 games in [[La Liga]], scoring 82 goals, and winning the [[Copa del Rey]] three times. He first moved to [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo]], where he would spend five years, including loan spells with [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]], and also [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] in England who he then joined permanently in 2005. He then joined [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] and helped them reach the [[2007 UEFA Cup final]], before joining [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]]. After four years, he returned to Espanyol, and also had short spells with [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] and a  few other teams, before retiring from professional football in 2016. He also played four times for the [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay national team]] between 2001 and 2004.

==Playing career==
===Early years and Deportivo===
Born in [[Montevideo]], Pandiani started his career with hometown club [[C.A. Progreso|Progreso]], moving on to [[Basáñez]] and [[Peñarol]], the latter also in the country's capital. In December 1999 he agreed terms to join [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]] as a replacement for his compatriot [[Sergio Daniel Martínez|Sergio Martínez]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rcdeportivo.es/noticia/manteca-martinez-por-pandiani|title=Manteca Martínez por Pandiani|trans-title=Manteca Martínez for Pandiani|publisher=Deportivo La Coruña|language=es|date=23 December 1999|access-date=4 October 2017}}</ref> and the move was officially completed the following January when he signed a five-and-a-half-year deal for an undisclosed fee, still remaining with Peñarol until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lr21.com.uy/deportes/520-walter-pandiani-jugara-hasta-junio-en-penarol|title=Walter Pandiani jugará hasta junio en Peñarol|trans-title=Walter Pandiani will play in Peñarol until June|publisher=La Red 21|language=es|date=18 January 2000|access-date=4 October 2017}}</ref>

Pandiani made his debut for the Spaniards on 27 August 2000, coming [[Substitute (association football)|from the bench]] for [[Diego Tristán]] in a [[2000 Supercopa de España|2–0 win]] over [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] at [[Estadio Riazor]] in the [[Supercopa de España]] return match.<ref name=SC>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundo/2000/08/27/deportes/967412498.html|title=El Deportivo se impone al Espanyol (2–0) y gana su segunda Supercopa|trans-title=Deportivo best Espanyol (2–0) and win their second Supercup|newspaper=El Mundo|language=es|date=28 August 2000|access-date=18 October 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://theworldgame.sbs.com.au/article/2000/08/29/deportivo-win-spanish-super-cup|title=Deportivo win Spanish Super Cup|publisher=[[Special Broadcasting Service]]|date=29 August 2000|access-date=4 October 2017}}</ref> Despite never being an undisputed starter for the [[Galicia (Spain)|Galician]] team he was one of their most important attacking elements, often scoring as a substitute, netting 13 goals during the [[2003–04 La Liga|2003–04 season]].<ref name=LEÓN/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lr21.com.uy/deportes/142424-pandiani-llego-a-trece|title=Pandiani llegó a trece|trans-title=Pandiani made it to thirteen|publisher=La Red 21|language=es|date=24 May 2004|access-date=9 January 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vavel.com/es/futbol/segunda-division/recreativodehuelva/338638-joselu-estoy-contento-por-los-goles-pero-frustrado-por-el-partido.html|title=El Dépor presume de suplentes goleadores|trans-title=Dépor boast of scoring substitutes|publisher=Vavel|first=Fernando|last=Martínez Duarte|language=es|date=15 April 2014|access-date=12 September 2012}}</ref>

Pandiani, who had a successful loan stint at [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] while still at Depor,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/025a-0eaad6d7906f-4afd5a2596b8-1000--pandiani-seeks-magic-seven/|title=Pandiani seeks magic seven|publisher=UEFA|first=Andy|last=Hall|date=7 October 2003|access-date=7 May 2016}}</ref> moved to [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] in the [[Premier League]], also on loan, in January 2005, after a series of run-ins with coach [[Javier Irureta]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2005/01/18/liga/1106078368.html|title=Pandiani: "Cuando todo va mal Irureta se lava las manos"|trans-title=Pandiani: "When everything goes wrong Irureta washes his hands"|newspaper=El Mundo|language=es|date=18 January 2005|access-date=9 January 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11843_2324255,00.html|title=Depor boss blasts Pandiani|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|first=Mark|last=Kendall|date=19 January 2005|access-date=26 October 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/b/birmingham_city/4225423.stm|title=Birmingham complete Pandiani loan|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=1 February 2005|access-date=26 October 2008}}</ref> He scored a goal on his debut against [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] in a 2–1 home win,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/4221115.stm|title=Birmingham 2–1 Southampton|publisher=BBC Sport|date=2 February 2005|access-date=26 October 2008}}</ref> and went on to score three more in [[2004–05 FA Premier League|the season]], prompting manager [[Steve Bruce]] to sign him on a permanent contract for a reported fee of [[Pound sterling|£]]3 million.<ref name="Espanyol">{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/b/birmingham_city/4608030.stm|title=Pandiani completes Espanyol move|publisher=BBC Sport|date=13 January 2006|access-date=26 October 2008}}</ref>

During his time at Deportivo, Pandiani bought a big red truck which he drove to training, a type of vehicle that he is a fan of, which he kept while at Deportivo, Espanyol and Osasuna. He personalised it with his nickname "El Rifle", a Uruguayan flag, and the emblems of his club and Uruguayan club [[Peñarol]].<ref name=lorry>{{Cite news |title=Can any professional footballers drive a heavy goods vehicle? |author=The Knowledge, Football |work=The Guardian |date=13 October 2021 |url= https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/oct/13/can-any-professional-footballers-drive-a-heavy-goods-vehicle}}</ref>

===Espanyol===
Having failed to continue to display his previous form, Pandiani returned to Spain on 13 January 2006, after completing a move to Espanyol for £1 million.<ref name="Espanyol"/>

In [[2006–07 La Liga|his first full season]] he scored only seven [[La Liga]] goals,<ref name=0607UEFA>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/0254-0d7b9f8b46c3-d7a7d5ea9cd0-1000--pandiani-picks-up-scoring-prize/|title=Pandiani picks up scoring prize|publisher=UEFA|date=17 May 2007|access-date=9 April 2013}}</ref> including a first-half [[hat-trick]] against eventual champions [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/05/13/sports/13iht-CUP.1.5684696.html?_r=0 |title=Soccer: Real Madrid rallies against Espanyol and rises to top of Spanish League|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=13 May 2007|access-date=9 April 2013}}</ref> but was top scorer in the [[2006–07 UEFA Cup]] with eleven as his club reached [[2007 UEFA Cup Final|the final]], which they lost [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|on penalties]] to [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]].<ref name=0607UEFA/>

During his time at Espanyol, Pandiani, and Barcelona's [[José Manuel Pinto]], drove in the 2011 Barcelona "[[Monster Jam]]" [[monster truck]] event.<ref>{{Cite web |title=La Monster Jam 2011 llega a Barcelona con Pinto y Pandiani |trans-title=Monster Jam 2011 arrives at Barcelona with Pinto and Pandiani |last=Serrano |first=Alejandro |website=AutoBild.es |date=12 November 2011 |url= https://www.autobild.es/reportajes/monster-jam-2011-barcelona-174157 |language=es}}</ref>

===Osasuna===
For [[2007–08 La Liga|2007–08]], Pandiani joined [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11827_2621913,00.html|title=Osasuna swoop for Rifle|publisher=Sky Sports|first=Mark|last=Kendall|date=29 July 2007|access-date=26 October 2008}}</ref> Scarcely used in his first year, he was instrumental for the [[Navarre]]se in [[2008–09 La Liga|the following campaign]], especially after the arrival in mid-October of coach [[José Antonio Camacho]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://espndeportes.espn.com/news/story?id=765126&s=esp&type=story|title=Mi sueño es jugar en Peñarol con mi hijo |trans-title=I dream of playing in Peñarol with my son|publisher=[[ESPN Deportes]]|language=es|date=14 January 2009|access-date=12 September 2012}}</ref> finishing as the club's top scorer.

Osasuna's first goal of the [[2010–11 La Liga|2010–11 season]] only came in the fourth matchday, and the 34-year-old Pandiani scored it through a header as the team came from behind to win it 3–1 against [[Real Sociedad]], at home.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/story/825495/la-liga-real-win-fiery-encounter-osasuna-win|title=Real win fiery encounter, Osasuna win|publisher=[[ESPN FC]]|date=21 September 2010|access-date=19 January 2016}}</ref> On 30 January 2011, during [[half-time]] of a 1–0 home win against Real Madrid, he was involved in a "verbal spat" with [[Cristiano Ronaldo]], suggesting afterwards that "As a footballer he is a phenomenon but to do the things he does, maybe he has a screw loose."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/story/875252/walter-pandiani-cocky-cristiano-ronaldo-has-a-screw-loose|title=Pandiani: Ronaldo has 'screw loose'|publisher=ESPN FC|date=3 February 2011|access-date=19 January 2016}}</ref>

===Later career===
The 35-year-old Pandiani returned to Espanyol for [[2011–12 La Liga|2011–12]], signing a one-year contract<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11095/7144487/|title=Pandiani pens Espanyol deal|publisher=Sky Sports|date=2 September 2011|access-date=13 November 2011}}</ref> and acting mainly as backup to youth graduate [[Álvaro Vázquez]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2011/10/27/futbol/1adivision/1319745408.html|title=Pandiani siempre se guarda una bala|trans-title=Pandiani always has one bullet left|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|first=Ramiro|last=Aldunate|date=27 October 2011|access-date=12 September 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ligabbva.com/news/2012/01/18/pandiani-y-albin-a-salvar-al-espanyol.html|title=Pandiani y Albín, a salvar al Espanyol|trans-title=Pandiani and Albín, to Espanyol's rescue|publisher=Liga BBVA|language=es|date=18 January 2012|access-date=12 September 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120122001657/http://www.ligabbva.com/news/2012/01/18/pandiani-y-albin-a-salvar-al-espanyol.html|archive-date=22 January 2012}}</ref> On 22 September he came from the bench to score the game's only goal at home against [[Getafe CF|Getafe]], in stoppage time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=1514976.html |title=Late Pandiani strike sinks Getafe|publisher=FIFA|date=22 September 2011|access-date=9 September 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110926024516/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid%3D1514976.html|archive-date=26 September 2011}}</ref> On 27 October he repeated the feat, albeit not so late in the game, with a powerful header at home to [[Real Betis]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://asia.eurosport.com/football/la-liga/2009-2010/espanyol-beat-betis_sto3002950/story.shtml|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160225110352/http://asia.eurosport.com/football/la-liga/2009-2010/espanyol-beat-betis_sto3002950/story.shtml|url-status=dead|archive-date=25 February 2016|title=Espanyol extend Betis losing streak|publisher=[[Eurosport]]|date=28 October 2011|access-date=19 January 2016}}</ref>

In late August 2012, Pandiani signed a one-year contract with [[Segunda División]] club [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]], where his 18-year-old son [[Nico Pandiani|Nico]] was a [[Villarreal CF C|C-team]] player.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.com/story/1144947/pandiani-family-happy-with-villarreal-move|title=Pandianis happy with Villarreal move|publisher=ESPN FC|first=Dermot|last=Corrigan|date=28 August 2012|access-date=19 January 2016}}</ref> On his debut, at home to [[CD Guadalajara (Spain)|Guadalajara]] on 2 September, he entered the game as a second-half substitute and scored the winning goal,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.villarrealcf.es/en/news/item/3026-another-comeback-in-el-madrigal-2-1|title=Another comeback in El Madrigal (2–1)|publisher=Villarreal CF|date=2 September 2012|access-date=19 January 2016}}</ref> and did the same the following week in another narrow win, at [[SD Ponferradina|Ponferradina]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2012/09/08/futbol/2adivision/1347127995.html|title=Pandiani acaba con las ilusiones de la Ponferradina|trans-title=Pandiani destroys Ponferradina's illusions|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=8 September 2012|access-date=9 September 2012}}</ref>

In late January 2013, Pandiani and Nico left Villarreal and joined [[CD Atlético Baleares|Atlético Baleares]] of the [[Segunda División B]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cdatleticobaleares.com/noticias/1067/presentacion-de-nico-y-walter-pandiani/|title=Presentación de Nico y Walter Pandiani|trans-title=Introducing Nico and Walter Pandiani|publisher=CD Atlético Baleares|language=es|date=31 January 2013|access-date=24 February 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130216025035/http://cdatleticobaleares.com/noticias/1067/presentacion-de-nico-y-walter-pandiani/|archive-date=16 February 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.abc.es/deportes/futbol/20130202/abci-pandiani-hijo-baleares-201302012137.html|title=El Atlético Baleares une a los Pandiani|trans-title=Atlético Baleares unite the Pandianis|newspaper=[[ABC (newspaper)|ABC]]|first=Jorge A.|last=Moreno|language=es|date=2 February 2013|access-date=17 February 2013}}</ref> They both started in Nico's second senior match, and Pandiani scored in the 2–1 defeat away to [[UE Sant Andreu|Sant Andreu]] on 12 May.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.futbolbalear.es/2013/05/12/cronica-2a-division-b-ue-sant-andreu-2-1-at-baleares/|title=Crónica 2ª División B: UE Sant Andreu 2–1 At Baleares|trans-title=2ª División B report: UE Sant Andreu 2–1 At Baleares|publisher=Fútbol Balear|language=es|date=12 May 2013|access-date=5 February 2014}}</ref>

In October 2013, the pair returned to Uruguay and signed for [[Uruguayan Primera División|Primera División]] club [[Miramar Misiones]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://diariouruguay.com.uy/los-pandiani-en-sociedad-vuelven-al-futbol-uruguayo/|title=Walter Pandiani volverá al fútbol uruguayo para defender a Miramar Misiones|trans-title=Walter Pandiani returns to Uruguayan football to play for Miramar Misiones|newspaper=El Diario|first=Gonzalo|last=Basal|language=es|date=29 October 2013|access-date=5 February 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140221220601/http://diariouruguay.com.uy/los-pandiani-en-sociedad-vuelven-al-futbol-uruguayo/|archive-date=21 February 2014}}</ref> Pandiani scored three times in the six remaining matches of the [[2013–14 Uruguayan Primera División season|2013–14 Apertura]], as his team finished next to bottom, and played regularly during the Clausura but scored only twice as they repeated their previous finish, which contributed to relegation.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesu/uru2014.html|title=Uruguay 2013/14|first=Francisco|last=Fernández|date=26 February 2015|website=[[RSSSF]]|access-date=2 June 2015}}</ref>

Pandiani returned to the Barcelona area where he spent the 2014–15 season coaching junior teams at [[CD Masnou|Masnou]], where two of his sons played. He said that although he had always wanted to coach, he still thought of himself as a player and was open to offers;<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sport.es/es/noticias/futbol-catala/futbol-base-del-masnou-manos-del-rifle-pandiani-3739106|title=El fútbol base del Masnou, en manos del 'Rifle' Pandiani|trans-title=The youth setup at Masnou, in the hands of 'Rifle' Pandiani|newspaper=[[Sport (Spanish newspaper)|Sport]]|first=Sergi|last=Capdevila|language=es|date=2 December 2014|access-date=2 June 2015}}</ref> in June 2015, he signed for [[FC Lausanne-Sport|Lausanne-Sport]] of the [[Swiss Challenge League]], with the remit of supervising and teaching the tricks of the trade to the 15-year-old striker [[Andi Zeqiri]], who had already made his first-team debut.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lausanne-sport.ch/detailnews.php?id=1068|title=Communiqué de presse|trans-title=Press release|publisher=FC Lausanne-Sport|language=fr|date=2 June 2015|access-date=2 June 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150712201008/http://www.lausanne-sport.ch/detailnews.php?id=1068|archive-date=12 July 2015}}</ref> The club won promotion to the [[Swiss Super League|Super League]] as champions in his [[2015–16 Swiss Challenge League|only season]]; his one goal was an equaliser in a 1–1 home draw with [[FC Aarau|Aarau]] on 4 April, taking [[Walter Samuel]]'s record as oldest person to score in either of the [[Swiss football league system|top two divisions]] of Swiss football, though the Argentine played for [[FC Basel|Basel]] in the top flight.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lematin.ch/story/pandiani-est-devenu-le-plus-vieux-buteur-de-la-ligue-267798765106|title=Pandiani est devenu le plus vieux buteur de la Ligue|trans-title=Pandiani became the oldest goalscorer in the League|newspaper=[[Le Matin (Switzerland)|Le Matin]]|first=Sergi|last=Capdevila|language=es|date=2 December 2014|access-date=2 June 2015}}</ref>

Pandiani announced his retirement on 16 June 2016 after a 23-year professional career, at the age of 40.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sport.es/es/noticias/futbol/pandiani-anuncia-retirada-5210227|title=Pandiani anuncia su retirada|trans-title=Pandiani announces his retirement|newspaper=Sport|language=es|date=16 June 2016|access-date=16 June 2016}}</ref> After he retired, his truck was auctioned in Barcelona with 518,000 miles on the clock.<ref name=lorry/>

==International career==
Despite his relatively successful career in Spain, Pandiani only received four [[Cap (sport)|caps]] for [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.navarrasport.com/noticias/pandiani-no-va-con-uruguay|title=Pandiani no va con Uruguay|trans-title=Pandiani does not go with Uruguay|publisher=Navarra Sport|language=es|date=30 October 2009|access-date=19 January 2016}}</ref> the first coming on 28 March 2001 in a 1–0 home defeat against [[Paraguay national football team|Paraguay]] in the [[2002 FIFA World Cup qualification (CONMEBOL)|2002 World Cup qualifiers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesu/uru-intres2005.html|title=Uruguay – International Matches 2001–2005|first=Martín|last=Tabeira|date=31 October 2006|website=[[RSSSF]]|access-date=19 January 2016}}</ref>

==Managerial career==
Pandiani returned to Masnou after retiring, now as a first-team manager. Sacked on 2 November 2016,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/futbol-catala/20161102/411521312252/walter-pandiani-deja-de-entrenar-al-masnou.html|title=Walter Pandiani deja de entrenar al Masnou|trans-title=Walter Pandiani no longer in charge of Masnou|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|language=es|date=2 November 2016|access-date=14 June 2018}}</ref> he was appointed at the helm of [[CE Europa|Europa]]'s ''Juvenil A'' squad on 13 December.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.diariolagrada.com/noticias/espanyol/pandiani-dirigira-juvenil-europa_21016.html|title=Pandiani dirigirá al Juvenil A del Europa|trans-title=Pandiani will manage the ''Juvenil A'' of Europa|publisher=Diario La Grada|language=es|date=13 December 2016|access-date=14 June 2018}}</ref>

On 27 June 2017, Pandiani was named manager of [[CE L'Hospitalet|Hospitalet]]'s youth squad.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/futbol-catalan/pandiani-dirigira-juvenil-lhospitalet-6132119|title=Pandiani dirigirá al juvenil de L'Hospitalet|trans-title=Pandiani will manage the ''juvenil'' of L'Hospitalet|newspaper=Sport|language=es|date=27 June 2017|access-date=14 June 2018}}</ref> Two years later, he was given his first senior managerial job at [[Lorca FC|Lorca]] in the [[Tercera División]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2019/07/05/mas_futbol/1562322985_906856.html|title=Walter Pandiani vuelve a España para entrenar al Lorca en Tercera|trans-title=Walter Pandiani returns to Spain to manage Lorca in ''Tercera''|newspaper=Diario AS|language=es|first=Javi|last=González V.|date=5 July 2019|access-date=31 October 2022}}</ref> He left on 30 December 2019, with the team in seventh place.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://murciaplaza.com/ElinternacionaluruguayoPandianidejaelbanquillodelLorcaFCseismesesdespusdellegar|title=El internacional uruguayo Pandiani deja el banquillo del Lorca FC seis meses después de llegar|trans-title=Uruguayan international Pandiani leaves the Lorca FC dugout six months after arriving|publisher=Murcia Plaza|language=es|first=M. G.|last=Tallón|date=30 December 2019|access-date=31 October 2022}}</ref>

Following a spell at [[Dibba Al-Hisn Sports Club|Dibba Al-Hisn]] in the United Arab Emirates, where he signed his son Axel,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/internacional/20210125/491748754253/axel-pandiani-se-une-a-su-padre-walter-en-el-dibba-al-hisn-arabe.html|title=Axel Pandiani se une a su padre Walter en el Dibba Al-Hisn árabe|trans-title=Axel Pandiani joins his father Walter at Arab Dibba Al-Hisn|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|language=es|first=Javier|last=Alfaro|date=25 January 2021|access-date=31 October 2022}}</ref> Pandiani was hired at [[C.A. Cerro|Cerro]] in the [[Uruguayan Segunda División]] in June 2021. He lost in the promotion playoffs to [[Defensor Sporting|Defensor]] in his [[2021 Uruguayan Primera División season|first season]] and was sacked in July 2022 with the team in fourth.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elpais.com.uy/ovacion/futbol/cerro-quedo-entrenador-walter-pandiani-continua-club.html|title=Walter Pandiani no sigue en Cerro y ya tiene nuevo entrenador|trans-title=Walter Pandiani does not continue in Cerro and they now have a new manager|newspaper=El País|language=es|date=6 July 2022|access-date=31 October 2022}}</ref> 

On 27 July 2022, Pandiani signed for [[Club Sportivo Cerrito|Cerrito]], in last place in the top flight.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elpais.com.uy/ovacion/futbol/cerrito-arranca-torneo-clausura-nuevo-tecnico-asumio-walter-rifle-pandiani.html|title=Cerrito arranca el Torneo Clausura con nuevo técnico: asumió Walter "Rifle" Pandiani|trans-title=Cerrito begin the Torneo Clausura with new manager: Walter "Rifle" Pandiani signed|newspaper=El País|language=es|date=27 July 2022|access-date=31 October 2022}}</ref> He was fired on 30 August after taking two points from five games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com.pa/futbol/uruguay/nota/_/id/10846870/pandiani-salida-cerrito-vuelve-marcenaro|title=Pandiani se fue de Cerrito tras un mes en el cargo y vuelve Marcenaro
|trans-title=Pandiani left Cerrito after a month in the role and Marcenaro returns|publisher=ESPN|language=es|date=30 August 2022|access-date=31 October 2022}}</ref>

Pandiani was announced as the new manager of [[Albion F.C.|Albion]] on 20 December 2022, ahead of the [[2023 Uruguayan Segunda División season|2023 season]] in the second division.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://albionfc.uy/bienvenido-rifle/|title=Bienvenido, ¡Rifle!|trans-title=Welcome, Rifle!|publisher=Albion F.C.|language=es|date=20 December 2022|accessdate=8 January 2023}}</ref> He left the club at the end of the campaign, and took over [[Miramar Misiones]] in the top tier on 27 May 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.montevideo.com.uy/Deportes/Walter-Rifle-Pandiani-fue-anunciado-como-nuevo-director-tecnico-de-Miramar-Misiones-uc889554|title=Walter "Rifle" Pandiani fue anunciado como nuevo director técnico de Miramar Misiones|trans-title=Walter ''Rifle'' Pandiani was announced as new manager of Miramar Misiones|publisher=Fútbol.uy|language=es|date=27 May 2024|access-date=27 May 2024}}</ref>

==Style of play==

דודו אוואט | image = DuduAouate.jpg | caption = Aouate playing with [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] in 2012 | fullname = David Aouate | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1977|10|17|df=yes}} | birth_place = [[Nazareth Illit]], Israel | height = 1.88 m | position = [[Goalkeeper (association football)|Goalkeeper]] | currentclub = | youthyears1 = | youthclubs1 = [[Maccabi Haifa F.C.|Maccabi Haifa]] | years1 = 1995–1997 | clubs1 = [[Maccabi Haifa F.C.|Maccabi Haifa]] | caps1 = 0 | goals1 = 0 | years2 = 1995–1996 | clubs2 = → [[Hapoel Nazareth Illit F.C.|Hapoel Nazareth Illit]] (loan) | caps2 = 3 | goals2 = 0 | years3 = 1997–1998 | clubs3 = [[Maccabi Tel Aviv F.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] | caps3 = 1 | goals3 = 0 | years4 = 1998–2001 | clubs4 = [[Hapoel Haifa F.C.|Hapoel Haifa]] | caps4 = 104 | goals4 = 0 | years5 = 2001–2003 | clubs5 = [[Maccabi Haifa F.C.|Maccabi Haifa]] | caps5 = 60 | goals5 = 0 | years6 = 2003–2006 | clubs6 = [[Racing de Santander|Racing Santander]] | caps6 = 78 | goals6 = 0 | years7 = 2006–2008 | clubs7 = [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]] | caps7 = 66 | goals7 = 0 | years8 = 2009–2014 | clubs8 = [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] | caps8 = 167 | goals8 = 0 | totalcaps = 479 | totalgoals = 0 | nationalyears1 = 1998–1999 | nationalteam1 = [[Israel national under-21 football team|Israel U21]] | nationalcaps1 = 12 | nationalgoals1 = 0 | nationalyears2 = 1999–2014 | nationalteam2 = [[Israel national football team|Israel]] | nationalcaps2 = 78 | nationalgoals2 = 0 }} '''David "Dudu" Aouate''' (or Awat,{{cite web |title=Dudu Awat International Games and Goals |url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/isra-intlp-awat.html |website=[[RSSSF]] |access-date=4 September 2021}} {{langx|he|דוד "דודו" אוואט}}, ''pronounced Dūdū Ahwaht''; born 17 October 1977) is an Israeli retired professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]]. After playing for several clubs in his country, most notably [[Maccabi Haifa F.C.|Maccabi Haifa]], he moved to Spain in 2003, going on to represent [[Racing de Santander]], [[Deportivo de La Coruña|Deportivo La Coruña]] and [[RCD Mallorca|Mallorca]] for a total of 303 [[La Liga]] matches. Aouate won 78 [[Cap (sport)|caps]] for [[Israel national football team|Israel]], during 14 years.[https://www.uefa.com/european-qualifiers/news/0253-0d7f791cee6e-7b6195a61906-1000--israel-goalkeeper-aouate-announces-retirement/ Israel goalkeeper Aouate announces retirement]; UEFA, 8 August 2014 ==Club career== ===Israel=== David Aouate was born in [[Nazareth Illit]], [[Israel]] (now [[Nof HaGalil]], Israel), to a family of [[Sephardic Jewish]] descent. He began his career at [[Maccabi Haifa F.C.]] where he had also played youth football, as an understudy to [[Nir Davidovich]]. Wanting first-team action, he was loaned to [[Hapoel Nazareth Illit F.C.]] but never got a real chance until he transferred to [[Hapoel Haifa F.C.|Hapoel Haifa FC]], having been assured that he would be the club's first-choice, but he again found himself struggling to establish himself as such. Early in the [[1998–99 Liga Leumit|1998–99 season]], however, the team's regular, [[Avi Peretz (football player)|Avi Peretz]], was injured, and Aouate took his place. Hapoel eventually won the championship that year and he was praised for his performances; by the time Peretz recovered, Aouate was irreplaceable. Aouate's performances for Hapoel saw him get called up to the [[Israel national football team|Israel national team]] in 1999. In the [[2001–02 Israeli Premier League|2001–02 campaign]] he returned to Maccabi Haifa as a cover for Davidovich, who was seriously injured, and the team went on to win the [[Israeli Premier League|Premier League]] as he established himself as the undisputed starter. In [[2002–03 Israeli Premier League|2002–03]], Aouate was the starter as Maccabi [[2002–03 UEFA Champions League|played]] in the [[UEFA Champions League]], the first time an Israeli side made it to the group stage of the competition. Haifa finished in third place in their group following a historic victory over powerhouse [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]],[https://web.archive.org/web/20121203233953/http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/season=2002/matches/round=1636/match=1036505/postmatch/report/index.html Maccabi celebrate famous victory]; UEFA, 29 October 2002 finishing runners-up in the league to Maccabi Tel Aviv; his solid performances earned him a transfer to European football, with Spanish club [[Racing de Santander]] signing him on 17 July 2003.[https://web.archive.org/web/20141006154137/http://www.uefa.com/news/newsid=82756.html Awat races to Racing]; UEFA, 18 July 2003 ===Spain=== Aouate's move to Spain was made easier by the fact that he obtained a [[French nationality law|French passport]], thus not counting as a foreigner. After forcing his way into the starting line-up in [[2004–05 La Liga|2004–05]] due to [[Ricardo (footballer, born 1971)|Ricardo]]'s loan return to Manchester United – going on to play 74 games out of 76 in his final two years – he signed a four-year contract with fellow [[La Liga]] side [[Deportivo de La Coruña]] in August 2006,[https://web.archive.org/web/20141007010643/http://www.uefa.com/news/newsid=443609.html Awate joy, Diané despair]; UEFA, 9 August 2006 in a swap deal involving three players plus [[Euro|€]]1.5 million. He quickly paid back the confidence of his new club with an excellent [[2006–07 La Liga|season]], appearing in all 38 matches; ''[[Don Balón]]'', a Spanish football magazine, placed him eighth on their list of La Liga's Footballer of the Year in 2007. In [[2007–08 La Liga|2007–08]]'s January winter [[transfer window]], after losing first-choice status to [[Gustavo Munúa]], both goalkeepers were involved in a post-training punching session that resulted in both being suspended for the match against [[Villarreal CF]], as well as subsequent league games.[http://www.cnn.com/2008/SPORT/football/01/11/spain.deportivo/index.html Deportivo keepers axed after fight]; [[CNN]], 11 January 2008 In February, due to [[Deportivo de La Coruña B|B-team]] keeper [[Fabricio Agosto|Fabri]]'s inexperience, both players were reinstated in the squad, with the Israeli regaining starting duties. In late December, as he had been training separately with Munúa, not being part of ''Depor'' manager [[Miguel Ángel Lotina]]'s plans, Aouate signed with [[RCD Mallorca]] for approximately €1 million until June 2011,[http://www.marca.com/edicion/marca/futbol/1a_division/mallorca/es/desarrollo/1195012.html El Mallorca cierra con el Depor la compra de Aouate (Mallorca agree to Aouate purchase with Depor)]; [[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]], 28 December 2008 {{in lang|es}} as the [[Balearic Islands]] club was struggling in [[2008–09 La Liga|the league]] and dealing with an injury to first-choice [[Miguel Ángel Moyá]]. He made his debut on 8 January 2009, in a 3–1 win over [[UD Almería]] for [[2008–09 Copa del Rey|the campaign]]'s [[Copa del Rey]];{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/diario/2009/01/09/deportes/1231455604_850215.html|title=El Mallorca aparca su crisis|trans-title=Mallorca park crisis|publisher=[[El País]]|language=Spanish|date=9 January 2009|accessdate=12 November 2017}} four days later, with Moyà still injured, he appeared in a 0–3 league loss at [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]].{{cite news|url=http://archivo.marca.com/edicion/marca/futbol/1a_division/cronica/es/desarrollo/1197486.html|title=El Real Madrid flota sobre un náufrago|trans-title=Real Madrid float over a shipwreck|publisher=Marca|language=Spanish|date=11 January 2009|accessdate=12 November 2017}} In June 2009, Moyà left for [[Valencia CF]] and Aouate became the automatic first-choice. In February 2013, he tied Mallorca's record for most appearances for a goalkeeper,{{cite web|url=http://rcdm.es/sabias-que-aouate-es-el-portero-con-mas-partidos-disputados-en-primera-con-el-mallorca/|title=¿Sabías que Aouate es el portero con más partidos disputados en Primera con el Mallorca?|trans-title=Did you know Aouate is the goalkeeper with the most matches played in ''Primera'' with Mallorca?|publisher=RCDM|language=Spanish|date=11 March 2013|accessdate=12 November 2017}} and announced his retirement on 8 August 2014 at the age of 36. After his retirement he became the club's major shareholder, after buying Biel Cerdà and [[Lorenzo Serra Ferrer]]'s shares,[http://ultimahora.es/mallorca/deportes/real-mallorca/2014/130448/cerda-pacta-venta-acciones-dudu-aouate.html Aouate se hace con el control del Mallorca (Aouate takes control of Mallorca)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140812224913/http://ultimahora.es/mallorca/deportes/real-mallorca/2014/130448/cerda-pacta-venta-acciones-dudu-aouate.html |date=12 August 2014 }}; [[Última Hora (Spain)|Última Hora]], 7 August 2014 {{in lang|es}} and was named [[general manager]] on 11 August.[http://www.marca.com/2014/08/11/futbol/equipos/mallorca/1407756306.html Aouate consensuará con Nadal el proyecto deportivo del Mallorca (Aouate to team with Nadal in Mallorca's sporting project)]; Marca, 11 August 2014 {{in lang|es}} ====Yom Kippur controversy==== In an interview with Spain's ''[[Diario AS]]'', Aouate was asked about the significance of [[Yom Kippur]] and some general questions about the prohibitions of the holiday. He added that he understood that playing football in this holiday was not allowed, but stated that if forced to play against [[Real Sociedad]], in a September 2006 match, he would; his comments swirled a huge controversy in Israel with even a member of the [[Shas]] party calling for the player to be removed from the national team.[https://web.archive.org/web/20070426021114/http://www.haaretz.com/hasen/spages/766078.html Awat sparks storm with decision to play on Yom Kippur]; [[Haaretz]], 25 September 2006 In September 2010, Aouate decided not to play against [[CA Osasuna]] because the game was supposed to start 18 minutes before the end of the Jewish fast day, and Mallorca accepted his rationale.{{cite web|url=http://www.breakingfootballnews.com/la-liga/athletic-bilbao-vs-mallorca-live-online-basques-look-to-return-to-home-dominance/9829|title=Basques look to return to home dominance|publisher=Breaking Football News|date=21 September 2010|accessdate=5 January 2011}}{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_6TCg8TsJDY |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/_6TCg8TsJDY |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live|title=Israeli goalkeeper says no to playing on Yom Kippur|date=5 October 2010 |via=[[YouTube]]|accessdate=5 January 2011}}{{cbignore}} ====Antisemitism==== In December 2009, during a match between Osasuna and Mallorca, Aouate was subjected to antisemitic chants coming from the [[Navarre]]se supporters – additionally, they waved [[Palestinian flag]]s and called him "a murderer". The [[Royal Spanish Football Federation]] set up an inquiry into the incident, this being already the second time the player faced such abuse (the previous occurrence also being against Osasuna in 2006, while he was with Deportivo).{{cite news|url=https://www.haaretz.com/hasen/spages/1135179.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091216220457/http://www.haaretz.com/hasen/spages/1135179.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 December 2009|title=Spanish soccer fans chant anti-Semitic slogans at Israeli goalkeeper|publisher=Haaretz|date=15 December 2009|accessdate=15 December 2009}} ==International career== Aouate's strong domestic form earned him his first [[Israel national football team|Israel]] call-ups, and his debut occurred on 10 October 1999 in a 0–3 away loss against [[Spain national football team|Spain]] for the [[UEFA Euro 2000]] [[UEFA Euro 2000 qualifying|qualifiers]].{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundo/1999/octubre/10/deportes/futbol.html|title=España cierra la fase de clasificación ganando a Israel y con 40 goles en ocho partidos|trans-title=Spain close qualifying stage defeating Israel and with 40 goals in eight matches|publisher=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]|language=Spanish|date=10 October 1999|accessdate=12 November 2017}} Since then, he became an integral member of the national team set-up. On 24 March 2007, Aouate kept a [[Shutout#Association football|clean sheet]] in the 0–0 home draw to [[England national football team|England]] in the [[UEFA Euro 2008 qualifying|Euro 2008 qualifying campaign]], saving several shots from the opposition.{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0254-0d7b9fdba71b-410b499df849-1000--england-find-no-way-past-israel/|title=England find '''Hans Adu Sarpei''' (born 28 June 1976) is a Ghanaian former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[full-back (association football)|full-back]].

He also was a long time regular for the [[Ghana national football team|Ghana national team]]. Sarpei most recently played for his country at the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]] in South Africa.

==Club career==
Sarpei was born in [[Tema, Ghana|Tema]]. He was with [[VfL Wolfsburg]] for six seasons, where he extended his contract until 30 June 2007 in February 2004. He joined Wolfsburg in 2001 and made over 130 appearances for the Wolves. At the end of the [[2006–07 Bundesliga]] season, then Wolfsburg manager [[Klaus Augenthaler]] decided not to renew Sarpei's contract.

On 18 May 2007, Sarpei moved to [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] on a free transfer signing a two-year deal.<ref>{{cite news | date=18 May 2007 | url=https://www.kicker.de/bayer-holt-sarpei-365808/artikel | title= Bayer holt Sarpei | publisher=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] | access-date = 18 May 2007 | language = de}}</ref><ref>{{cite news | date=19 May 2007 | url=http://www.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/SportsArchive/artikel.php?ID=124303 | title= Sarpei heads to Leverkusen | publisher=ghanaweb.com | access-date=19 May 2007}}</ref>

==International career==
Sarpei was a member of the [[Ghana national football team|Ghana national team]]. As such, he participated at the [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006 World Cup]] and the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]]. He also received call-ups for the [[2006 African Cup of Nations]] and the [[2010 African Cup of Nations]] squads.{{cn|date=July 2023}}

==Media career==
In 2016, it was announced that Sarpei would be a host on the [[Netflix]] [[reality show]] ''[[Ultimate Beastmaster]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://variety.com/2016/digital/news/ultimate-beastmaster-netflix-competition-series-sylvester-stallone-dave-broome-1201769095/|title=Netflix Orders Global Competition Series 'Ultimate Beastmaster' from Sylvester Stallone, Dave Broome|last=Prudon|first=Laura|work=Variety|date=9 May 2016|access-date=5 October 2016}}</ref>

He portrayed Balthasar in the 2015 film ''[[3 Türken und ein Baby]]''.

==Personal life==
Sarpei, who also has a German passport, moved to Germany from Ghana with his parents, when he was a child.<ref>{{cite news | date=1 January 2005 | url=http://www.hanssarpei.de/menu/laufbahn.asp | title=Hans Sarpei: Meine Laufbahn | publisher=www.hanssarpei.de | access-date=1 January 2005 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20041217221427/http://www.hanssarpei.de/menu/laufbahn.asp | archive-date=17 December 2004 | df=dmy-all }}</ref> His older brother, Edward, is a former Bundesliga player for [[1. FC Köln]], currently playing for BP Worringen.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.ghanaweb.com/GhanaHomePage/soccer//player.php?ID=44 | title = Ghanaweb Profile – Edward Sarpei | publisher = ghanaweb.com | access-date = 28 December 2009}}</ref>
Sarpei enjoys his large Facebook followership which recoined various [[Chuck Norris facts]] on him.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://fussball.zdf.de/ZDFsport/inhalt/14/0,5676,8349358,00.html?dr=1/ | title = Warum Hans Sarpei auf Facebook Kult ist ... | language = de | publisher = ZDF.de | access-date = 10 March 2012 }}{{Dead link|date=January 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

Mariano Pernía:
{{short description|Spanish footballer (born 1977)}} {{family name hatnote|Pernía|Molina|lang=Spanish}} {{Use dmy dates|date=October 2022}} {{Infobox football biography | name = Mariano Pernía | image = Mariano Pernía.jpg | image_size = | alt = | caption = Pernía playing for [[Atlético Madrid]] in 2007 | fullname = Mariano Andrés Pernía Molina{{cite web |title=2006 FIFA World Cup Germany List of Players |url=https://www.fifadata.com/document/fwc/2006/PDF/FWC_2006_SquadLists.pdf |publisher=FIFA |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190610174527/https://www.fifadata.com/document/fwc/2006/PDF/FWC_2006_SquadLists.pdf |archive-date=10 June 2019 |page=25}} | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1977|5|4|df=y}} | birth_place = [[Buenos Aires]], Argentina | height = 1.77 m | position = [[Left back]] | currentclub = | youthyears1 = | youthclubs1 = [[San Lorenzo de Almagro|San Lorenzo]] | years1 = 1997–1999 | clubs1 = [[San Lorenzo de Almagro|San Lorenzo]] | caps1 = 0 | goals1 = 0 | years2 = 1999–2002 | clubs2 = [[Club Atlético Independiente|Independiente]] | caps2 = 46 | goals2 = 2 | years3 = 2003–2004 | clubs3 = [[Recreativo de Huelva|Recreativo]] | caps3 = 59 | goals3 = 3 | years4 = 2004–2006 | clubs4 = [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] | caps4 = 72 | goals4 = 13 | years5 = 2006–2010 | clubs5 = [[Atlético Madrid]] | caps5 = 80 | goals5 = 1 | years6 = 2010 | clubs6 = [[Club Nacional de Football|Nacional]] | caps6 = 7 | goals6 = 0 | years7 = 2011–2012 | clubs7 = [[Club Atlético Tigre|Tigre]] | caps7 = 9 | goals7 = 1 | totalcaps = 273 | totalgoals = 20 | nationalyears1 = 2006–2007 | nationalteam1 = [[Spain national football team|Spain]] | nationalcaps1 = 11 | nationalgoals1 = 1 }} '''Mariano Andrés Pernía Molina''' (born 4 May 1977) is a retired [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[left back]] and current [[Auto racing|race car]] driver. Born in Argentina, he represented the [[Spain national football team|Spain national team]] in the [[2006 FIFA World Cup|2006 World Cup]]. After starting professionally with [[Club Atlético Independiente|Independiente]], he moved to Spain in the early 2000s, going on to represent three teams in the country – most notably [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] and [[Atlético Madrid]], scoring ten [[La Liga]] goals in one sole season with the former – amassing Spanish top flight totals of 171 matches and 16 goals over seven seasons. == Club career == Born in [[Buenos Aires]], [[Argentina]], Pernía came through the ranks at [[San Lorenzo de Almagro]], but never achieved a first-team presence. He got his first chance of professional football when he moved to [[Club Atlético Independiente]], but found himself moving in and out of the main squad; he made a total of 57 appearances for the club in all competitions, scoring two goals. In January 2003, Pernía moved to [[La Liga]] with [[Recreativo de Huelva]] He started in the [[Copa del Rey]] [[2002–03 Copa del Rey|final loss]] to [[RCD Mallorca]],{{cite news|url=http://elpais.com/diario/2003/06/29/deportes/1056837603_850215.html|title=Eto'o pone Mallorca a brindar|trans-title=Eto'o has Mallorca toasting|publisher=[[El País]]|language=es|date=29 June 2003|access-date=5 April 2016}} but the [[Andalusia]]ns were also [[2002–03 La Liga|relegated that season]]; he played 40 league matches during [[2003–04 Segunda División|the following campaign]]'s [[Segunda División|second division]]. Although Pernía was 26 and yet to break into regular top flight football, he made the most of his opportunity when he moved to newly promoted [[Getafe CF]] in 2004. He made an immediate impact in the [[Madrid]] side as an attacking defender with a killer left foot, scoring three goals in his debut season including a 40-metre effort against [[Real Betis]];[http://elpais.com/diario/2005/11/06/deportes/1131231611_850215.html El cañonero infatigable (The tireless gunner)]; El País, 6 November 2005 {{in lang|es}} he was a major part of an underrated team that survived [[2004–05 La Liga|their first season in the top division]]. [[2005–06 La Liga|2005–06]] saw Pernía start 35 out of 38 games for Getafe, and he amazingly finished the season with ten goals and two assists, becoming the highest scoring defender in a season for 20 years. With such good form, his future was the source of much speculation and, despite a bid from [[Valencia CF]], he signed a four-year contract with [[Atlético Madrid]] in February 2006 starting in [[2006–07 La Liga|the following campaign]],[http://www.20minutos.es/noticia/92514/0/pernia/atletico/madrid/ Pernía ficha por el Atlético de Madrid (Pernía signs for Atlético de Madrid)]; [[20 minutos]], 20 February 2006 {{in lang|es}} going on to battle with [[Antonio López (footballer, born 1981)|Antonio López]] for the left-back position[http://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2006/07/18/futbol/1153249736.html Aguirre duda entre Antonio López y Pernía (Aguirre doubts between Antonio López and Pernía)]; [[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]], 18 July 2006 {{in lang|es}}– he was [[Ejection (sports)|sent off]] in his final appearance for Getafe, a 0–1 away loss to [[RC Celta de Vigo]].{{cite news|url=https://www.20minutos.es/deportes/noticia/118630/0/|title=El Espanyol se salva en tiempo de descuento y manda al Alavés a Segunda División|trans-title=Espanyol save themselves in injury time and send Alavés to ''Segunda División''|publisher=20 minutos|last=R. Vega|first=Raúl|language=es|date=13 May 2006|access-date=20 June 2018}} During his first year with his new club, Pernía played second-fiddle to López under manager [[Javier Aguirre]]. Subsequently, at the season's end, speculation was rife that he would return to Getafe following the departure of former teammate [[Javier Paredes]] to [[Real Zaragoza]], but he committed himself to Atlético.{{cn|date=June 2025}} However, in [[2007–08 La Liga|2007–08]], the tables turned, and Pernía gained positional battle with López, featuring in 29 league contests as the ''Colchoneros'' finished fourth, with the subsequent [[2008–09 UEFA Champions League|qualification]] to the [[UEFA Champions League]]. Throughout [[2008–09 La Liga|the following campaign]] he remained first-choice for most of the games, and also saw the birth of his own official fanclub – "Peña Pernía", which was Atlético's fastest growing ''peña'' of 2008. However, in early July 2009, he and his family were involved in a serious car accident, in the player's native Argentina. Both his daughter and nephew were unharmed, but he suffered a broken [[clavicle]] and minor [[lung]] injuries. He went on to fully recover, but the vehicle was practically and totally destroyed;[https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01db-0e72634eae22-668d2b4a2f4b-1000--pernia-stable-following-car-crash/ Pernía stable following car crash]; UEFA, 8 July 2009 [[2009–10 La Liga|his season]] consisted of only two appearances: against [[UD Marbella]] for the [[2009–10 Copa del Rey|domestic cup]], and in the league against [[Xerez CD]] (a 1–2 home loss).{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2010/05/18/mas_futbol/1274133604_850215.html|title=La expedición del Atlético ya está en Barcelona|trans-title=Atlético's expedition is already in Barcelona|publisher=[[Diario AS]]|last=Díaz|first=F. J.|language=es|date=18 May 2010|access-date=20 June 2018}} Aged 33, Pernía was released by Atlético in July 2010, signing with [[Montevideo]]'s [[Club Nacional de Football]] two months later. In the following [[transfer window]], however, he returned to his nation of birth, joining [[Argentine Primera División|Primera División]]'s [[Club Atlético Tigre]].{{cite news|url=http://www.larazon.com.ar/deportes/Pernia-lateral-izquierdo-Tigre_0_203100019.html|title=Pernía para el lateral izquierdo de Tigre|trans-title=Pernía for Tigre left-back|publisher=[[La Razón (Buenos Aires)|La Razón]]|language=es|date=10 January 2011|access-date=23 January 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303230834/http://www.larazon.com.ar/deportes/Pernia-lateral-izquierdo-Tigre_0_203100019.html|archive-date=3 March 2016|url-status=dead}} == International career == Pernía's excellent form throughout 2005–06 made him a contender for international selection with both [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] and [[Spain national football team|Spain]]. Although born in Argentina, he was granted Spanish citizenship in May 2006.{{cn|date=June 2025}} Initially, national team boss [[Luis Aragonés]] opted not to pick Pernía for Spain's team in the [[2006 FIFA World Cup]] – his reasoning was entirely legal and explained under current [[FIFA]] rules on squad selection. [[Asier del Horno]] was supposed to be first-choice leftback for the competition, but an ankle injury sustained in the build-up to the tournament saw Pernía controversially called up as his last-minute replacement after a personal call from the coach.[http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/world_cup_2006/teams/spain/5037052.stm Pernia replaces injured Del Horno]; [[BBC Sport]], 1 June 2006{{cite news|url=http://deportes.elpais.com/deportes/2013/10/08/actualidad/1381258813_336530.html|title=El fútbol y la 'españolía'|trans-title=Football and 'Spanishness'|publisher=El País|language=es|date=29 October 2013|access-date=5 April 2017}} In the last [[Exhibition game|friendly]] before the tournament in Germany he made his debut against [[Croatia national football team|Croatia]], and scored from a [[Direct free kick|free-kick]] on 7 June 2006 in a match played in [[Geneva]].[https://web.archive.org/web/20140715030845/http://es.uefa.com/worldcup/news/newsid=428123.html Debut de Pernía con gol (Pernía debut with goal)]; UEFA, 8 June 2006 {{in lang|es}} Surprisingly, Pernía came from third-choice to starter, and appeared in the final stages in group wins against [[Ukraine national football team|Ukraine]] and [[Tunisia national football team|Tunisia]], and also in their [[Single-elimination tournament|round-of-16]] loss to [[France national football team|France]]. ===International goals=== {| class="wikitable" ! # !! Date !! Venue !! Opponent !! Score !! Result !! Competition |- | 1. || 7 June 2006 || [[Stade de Genève]], Geneva, Switzerland || {{fb|CRO}} || '''1'''–1 || 2–1 || [[Exhibition game|Friendly]] |} == Motorsport career == After retiring from football, like his father and brother [[Leonel Pernía|Leonel]], Mariano began to compete in motorsports. He has competed mainly in [[Turismo Nacional]] but also in [[TC2000 Championship|TC2000]] and [[Super TC2000]].{{Cite web |title=Mariano Pernía {{!}} Racing career profile {{!}} Driver Database |url=https://www.driverdb.com/drivers/mariano-pernia/ |access-date=2023-05-05 |website=www.driverdb.com}} ==Personal life== Pernía had football in his family. He was the son of a famous Argentine player, [[Vicente Pernía]] (who was ironically left controversially out of the [[Argentina national football team|Argentine squad]] for the [[1978 FIFA World Cup]]), to whom he dedicated his World Cup call-up to.{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/mundial/2006/2006/06/01/grupo_h/1149161289.html|title=Pernía jugará el Mundial que su 'papá' no pudo|trans-title=Pernía will play the World Cup his 'daddy' could not|publisher=El Mundo|last=Saiz|first=Alba|language=es|date=1 June 2006|access-date=20 June 2018}} Pernía's mother was Olga, and he also had four brothers and a sister: his eldest brother, Gastón, played for the [[Orlando Sharks]] in the [[Major Indoor Soccer League (2001–08)|Major Indoor Soccer League]]. Another brother, [[Leonel Pernía|Leonel]], played for the Chicago Storm in the same competition and also raced cars in his country, competing in the [[World Touring Car Championship]];{{cite news|url=http://edant.ole.com.ar/notas/2007/04/23/01405526.html|title="Dejo la pelota por los autos"|trans-title=I quit football for cars|publisher=[[Olé (sports newspaper)|Olé]]|last=Feito|first=Mauro|language=es|date=23 April 2007|access-date=20 June 2018}}{{cite news|url=http://www.elgrafico.com.ar/2010/09/14/C-3069-sigo-pensando-que-11-pernias-le-ganan-a-11-maradonas.php|title="Sigo pensando que 11 Pernías le ganan a 11 Maradonas"|trans-title=I still think 11 Pernías beat 11 Maradonas|publisher=[[El Gráfico (Argentina)|El Gráfico]]|last=Borinsky|first=Diego|language=es|date=14 September 2010|access-date=20 June 2018}} his great-grandparents were also Spanish.{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2006/01/25/mas_futbol/1138174057_850215.html|title=Vicente Pernía: "Ver a mi hijo con España sería un orgullo"|trans-title=Vicente Pernía: "It would be an honour to see my son with Spain"|publisher=Diario AS|last=Gabilondo|first=Aritz|language=es|date=25 January 2006|access-date=20 June 2018}} Pernía's daughter was already born in Spain. He was on holiday in [[Tandil]] with his family upon getting the call from Aragonés, and subsequently had to delay his 20 June wedding in order to play in the World Cup. He said of the call-up:
"My wife's happy for me although a bit disappointed about having to postpone the wedding".[https://fifaworldcupgermany2006.blogspot.com/2006_05_28_archive.html Pernía goes to the World Cup for Spain]; FIFA World Cup Germany, 2 June 2006

'''Martin Stoll''' (born 9 February 1983) is a retired German [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|centre-back]]. He is currently the U16 manager of [[Karlsruher SC]].

==Career==
Stoll's first club was VfB Breitenbronn, but as Breitenbronn had no youth teams, Stoll had to play for SV Aglasterhausen's youth team, while still belonging to the club Breitenbronn.<ref>[http://www.fcaarau.ch/cont/news/2009/06/16/4343.php Martin Stoll wechselt für drei Jahre zum FC Aarau] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090619210720/http://www.fcaarau.ch/cont/news/2009/06/16/4343.php |date=19 June 2009 }}</ref> In the summer of 1995, Stoll moved for three years to [[SV Sandhausen]].

In July 1998, Stoll joined [[Karlsruher SC II]]. After two years with Karlsruher SC II, in July 2000, he signed a contract with [[VfB Stuttgart II]], before he returned to [[Karlsruher SC|KSC]] in the summer of 2002.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080818171016/http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/bundesliga/vereine/spielersteckbrief/object/29744/saison/2008-09 Kicker Profile]</ref> On 16 June 2009, he left Karlsruher SC and signed a three-year contract with [[Axpo Super League]] club [[FC Aarau]]. After just one season in Switzerland, Stoll returned to Germany with [[3. Liga]] club [[Hansa Rostock]], who he helped into second place and promotion come the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.3-liga.com/tabelle1011.php|title=3. Liga Tabelle 10/11}}</ref> At the start of the [[2011–12 2. Bundesliga|2011–12 season]] he moved to also newly promoted club [[Dynamo Dresden]]. Dynamo came ninth in the league that season, and previous clubs [[F.C. Hansa Rostock|Hansa Rostock]] and Karlsruher SC were both relegated.

Despite this, he chose to move back to the [[3. Liga]] and KSC at the end of the season, with whom he remained.

==International career==
Stoll is a youth international for Germany, and also was called up to the [[Germany national football B team|Germany Team 2006]] in 2005.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://datencenter.dfb.de/profil/16476|title = Martin Stoll Personenprofil}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
Stoll retired at the end of the 2018–19 season and became U16 manager for [[Karlsruher SC]].<ref>[https://www.ksc.de/akademie/mannschaften/news/show/article/martin-stoll-wird-neuer-u16-trainer/ MARTIN STOLL WIRD NEUER U16-TRAINER], ksc.de, 26 May 2019</ref>
