'''Robert Kenedy Nunes do Nascimento''' (born 8 February 1996), known as '''Kenedy''', is a Brazilian professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[winger (association football)|left winger]] for [[Liga MX]] club [[C.F. Pachuca|Pachuca]].

Kenedy made his professional debut aged 17 for [[Fluminense FC|Fluminense]], scoring five goals in 40 official games before a £6.3 million move to Chelsea in 2015. Kenedy has represented Brazil at [[Brazil national under-17 football team|under-17]] and [[Brazil national under-20 football team|under-20]] levels.

==Club career==
===Early career===
Born in [[Santa Rita do Sapucaí]], [[Minas Gerais]], Kenedy is named after [[Robert F. Kennedy]].<ref name="nick">{{cite news |last=Dorrington |first=Nick |date=30 June 2015 |title=Chelsea signing Kenedy is comparable to fellow Brazilian Hulk |url=https://www.espn.com/football/story/_/id/37425287 |access-date=31 December 2024 |work=ESPN}}</ref> He began his career at local club Santarritense before moving to [[Friburguense Atlético Clube|Friburguense]] in [[Rio de Janeiro state]] at the age of 11, going on to [[Clube de Regatas Vasco da Gama|Vasco da Gama]] and [[Atlético Mineiro]] before arriving at [[Fluminense FC|Fluminense]].<ref name=nick/>

===Fluminense===
Kenedy made his professional debut on 28 July 2013 in a 2–0 [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|Série A]] defeat at [[Grêmio Foot-Ball Porto Alegrense|Grêmio]], replacing [[Wágner (footballer, born 1985)|Wágner]] for the final nine minutes. On 24 May 2014, he scored his first professional goal, the only one in an away win over [[Esporte Clube Bahia]].<ref>{{cite news|title=FLU SEGURA PRESSÃO, VENCE O BAHIA E DORME NA LIDERANÇA DO BRASILEIRO|trans-title=''FLU'' KEEP UP THE PRESSURE, DEFEAT BAHIA AND STAY AT THE TOP OF THE BRASILEIRO|url=http://globoesporte.globo.com/jogo/brasileirao2014/24-05-2014/bahia-fluminense.html|access-date=23 August 2015|publisher=Globo|date=24 May 2014|language=pt}}</ref> He netted his second goal for the club in September, a late equaliser against [[Cruzeiro Esporte Clube|Cruzeiro]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=Transfer Spotlight: The 'new Neymar' who could be on his way to Manchester United |url=http://talksport.com/football/transfer-spotlight-new-neymar-who-could-be-his-way-manchester-united-150306138785 |publisher=TalkSport |date=6 March 2015 |archive-date=30 June 2015 |access-date=27 June 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150630062311/http://talksport.com/football/transfer-spotlight-new-neymar-who-could-be-his-way-manchester-united-150306138785 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

In March 2015, Kenedy scored in three home victories for ''Flu'' in [[2015 Campeonato Carioca|that year]]'s [[Campeonato Carioca]]. On 18 April, in the tournament's semi-final, he missed their first attempt as they lost 9–8 in a [[penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shootout]] to [[Botafogo de Futebol e Regatas|Botafogo]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Ribeiro |first=Ronaldo Júnior |date=18 April 2015 |title=Botafogo 2 x 1 Fluminense: Após infinidade de pênaltis, goleiro marca e põe Fogão na final |trans-title=After an infinity of penalties, goalkeeper scores and puts ''Fogão '' in the final |url=http://www.goal.com/br/match/botafogo-vs-fluminense/2027645/report?ICID=MP_MS_5 |access-date=12 December 2015 |publisher=Goal.com |language=pt}}</ref>

===Chelsea===
====2015–16 season====
[[File:Kenedy 2016-03-12.jpg|thumb|upright|Kenedy playing for [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] in 2016]]

On 26 June 2015, Fluminense announced that Kenedy had been sold to an unnamed club<ref>{{Cite news |title=DEAL! Chelsea beat Manchester United to signing of Brazilian star Kenedy |url=http://www.express.co.uk/sport/football/587228/Chelsea-Manchester-United-Kenedy-Transfer-Gossip-Confirmed-Done-Deal |publisher=Daily Express |date=26 June 2015}}</ref> for a fee around the region of £6.3 million.<ref>{{cite news |last=O'Rourke |first=Peter |date=30 June 2015 |title=Kenedy set to sign for Chelsea from Fluminense |url=https://www.espn.com/football/story/_/id/37422861 |access-date=31 December 2024 |work=ESPN}}</ref> It was later confirmed that Kenedy was on trial at [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], where he played in a pre-season match against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]], after Kenedy was given permission from Fluminense to play in the game as he had not yet been formally signed. On 22 August 2015, Chelsea completed the transfer.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kenedy signs|url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2015/08/kenedy-signs.html|publisher=Chelsea FC|access-date=22 August 2015}}</ref>

A week later, Kenedy made his debut against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]], coming on as a 68th-minute substitute for [[César Azpilicueta]] in a 2–1 home defeat.<ref>{{cite news|last=Rose|first=Gary|title=Chelsea 1–2 Crystal Palace|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34025310|access-date=29 August 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=29 August 2015}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club on 23 September in the third round of the [[Football League Cup|League Cup]] at [[Walsall F.C.|Walsall]], also assisting compatriot [[Ramires]] in the 4–1 victory;<ref>{{cite news|title=Walsall 1–4 Chelsea|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/34265632|access-date=23 September 2015|publisher=BBC Sport|date=23 September 2015}}</ref> his first league goal was the following 1 March, a 39th-second effort in a 2–1 win at [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] that was the fastest goal of the season.<ref>{{cite news|last=Reddy|first=Luke|title=Norwich City 1–2 Chelsea|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/35637648|access-date=2 March 2016|publisher=BBC Sport|date=1 March 2016}}</ref>

====Loan to Watford====
On 30 August 2016, Kenedy joined [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] on a season-long [[loan (sports)|loan]] after having a bid accepted from Chelsea.<ref>{{Cite press release|title=Watford loan for Kenedy|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2016/08/30/watford-switch-for-kenedy|publisher=Chelsea F.C.|date=30 August 2016|access-date=8 September 2020}}</ref> On 26 September, he made his only appearance for the Hornets in a 2–0 away defeat against [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]], replacing [[Roberto Pereyra]] with 15 minutes remaining.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Burnley 2–0 Watford |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/37404133 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=26 September 2016 |access-date=26 September 2016}}</ref> After struggling with injuries, manager [[Walter Mazzarri]], confirmed that Kenedy had returned to Chelsea on 12 December after a disappointing loan spell.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Kenedy has returned to Chelsea from underwhelming loan spell at Watford, confirms Walter Mazzarri |url=http://metro.co.uk/2016/12/12/kenedy-has-returned-to-chelsea-from-underwhelming-loan-spell-at-watford-walter-mazzarri-6318553 |publisher=Metro |date=12 December 2016 |access-date=18 December 2016}}/</ref>

====2016–17 season====
After being recalled by Chelsea from his loan spell with Watford, Kenedy made his return for the Blues in their 4–0 home victory over [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] in their [[FA Cup]] fourth round tie. Retaining his number 16 jersey, Kenedy replaced [[César Azpilicueta]] with just under twenty minutes remaining.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Chelsea 4–0 Brentford |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/38700669 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=28 January 2017 |access-date=1 February 2017}}</ref> He made his first start under Conte against Watford on 15 May 2017.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.goal.com/en-gh/news/4349/main/2017/05/15/35547882/chelsea-team-news-terry-leads-experimental-champions|title=Chelsea team news: Terry leads experimental champions - Goal.com|date=15 May 2017|work=Goal.com|access-date=15 May 2017|language=en-GH}}</ref>

====2017–18 season====
During a pre-season tour of China, Kenedy caused controversy by posting two inflammatory videos on social media, one captioned "Porra china", roughly translating to "Fuck China", and the other of a sleeping Chinese security guard captioned "Acorda china. Vacilão", translating to "Wake up China. You idiot".<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=25 July 2017|title=Chelsea's Kenedy sent home from China tour after offensive social media posts|url=http://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/jul/25/chelsea-kenedy-china-tour-sent-home|access-date=29 April 2021|website=the Guardian|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Wheaton|first=Oliver|date=26 July 2017|title=What did Chelsea's Kenedy say about China and what does 'porra' mean?|url=https://metro.co.uk/2017/07/26/what-did-chelseas-kenedy-say-about-china-and-what-does-porra-mean-6806402/|access-date=29 April 2021|website=Metro|language=en}}</ref> The incident was met with uproar by Chinese fans and media.<ref name=":0"/> As a result, Kenedy was sent back to England for damaging relationships with the Asian fan base.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Murphy |first=Paul |date=25 July 2017 |title=Chelsea send Kenedy home after China comments on social media |url=https://www.espn.com/football/story/_/id/37527699 |access-date=31 December 2024 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref> Both Kenedy and Chelsea later issued apologies over the incident and the club stated that the player had been "strongly reprimanded and disciplined". Following the incident, Chinese media outlets were ordered to withdraw stories related to Chelsea from homepages and apps and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs confirmed that there was a remote possibility of a ban for the club.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hu |first=Zhicheng |date=24 July 2017 |title=Chelsea 'persona non grata' in China over Kenedy's offensive posts |url=http://m.goal.com/s/en-ng/news/4071/premier-league/2017/07/24/37283542/chelsea-persona-non-grata-in-china-over-kenedys-offensive |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170801135807/http://m.goal.com/s/en-ng/news/4071/premier-league/2017/07/24/37283542/chelsea-persona-non-grata-in-china-over-kenedys-offensive |archive-date=1 August 2017 |access-date=24 July 2017 |publisher=GOAL.com}}</ref>

In August, a loan to [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] fell through on transfer deadline day.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/football/2017/09/19/kenedy-primed-surprise-chelsea-reprieve-first-appearance-since/| title=Kenedy primed for surprise Chelsea reprieve with first appearance since being sent home from China tour |date=19 September 2017 |publisher=Telegraph}}</ref> On 20 September 2017, Kenedy made his first appearance since the incident during pre-season when he started against [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] in the League Cup. He scored the opener in a 5–1 victory.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/41249727|title=Chelsea 5–1 Nottingham|publisher=BBC Sport|date=20 September 2017|access-date=20 September 2017}}</ref>

====Loans to Newcastle United====
On 23 January 2018, Kenedy joined Newcastle United on loan for the remainder of the [[2017–18 in English football|2017–18 season]].<ref>{{cite press release|title=Newcastle sign Kenedy on loan|url=https://www.nufc.co.uk/news/latest-news/newcastle-sign-kenedy-on-loan|access-date=23 January 2018|publisher=[[Newcastle United F.C.]] Official Site|date=23 January 2018}}</ref> Kenedy impressed on his Newcastle debut, creating [[Jamaal Lascelles]] opener from a corner kick in a 1–1 draw with [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Newcastle United 1–1 Burnley. Premier League|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/42799047|access-date=3 February 2018|agency=BBC Sport}}</ref> On 10 March, Kenedy won the Man of the Match award after scoring a brace in Newcastle's 3–0 win against [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Newcastle United 3–0 Southampton. Premier League|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/43267239|access-date=21 March 2018|agency=BBC Sport}}</ref>
Kenedy provided an assist for [[Ayoze Perez]]'s 80th-minute winner in Newcastle's 1–0 victory against [[Huddersfield Town F.C|Huddersfield]] on 31 March.<ref>{{cite news|title=Newcastle United 1–0 Huddersfield Town. Premier League|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/43524304|access-date=7 April 2018|work=BBC Sport}}</ref>

He returned to [[Tyneside]] on loan for the [[2018–19 in English football|2018–19 season]].<ref name="NBC">{{cite news |last=Mendola |first=Nicholas |date=12 July 2018 |title=Newcastle gets 2nd Kenedy loan, sells Merino to La Liga |url=https://soccer.nbcsports.com/2018/07/12/newcastle-gets-2nd-kenedy-loan-sells-merino-to-la-liga/ |access-date=12 July 2018 |publisher=NBC Sports}}</ref> Kenedy had a particularly poor match in a goalless draw at [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]] on 18 August, he avoided a red card for a kick at [[Víctor Camarasa]], became the first player since 2010 to play a full Premier League first half without completing a pass and his penalty in added time to win the game was saved by [[Neil Etheridge]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Chowdhury |first=Saj |title=Kenedy: Newcastle midfielder's display to forget at Cardiff City Stadium |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45234934 |access-date=18 August 2018 |work=BBC Sport |date=18 August 2018}}</ref> On 6 October, Kenedy scored his first goal of the season in a 3–2 loss at [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Manchester United 3-2 Newcastle United: Fightback relieves pressure on Mourinho|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45689298|date=6 October 2018|access-date=28 March 2019|publisher=BBC Sport}}</ref>

====Loan to Getafe====
On 2 September 2019, Kenedy was loaned to [[La Liga]] side [[Getafe CF]] for the [[2019–20 La Liga|2019–20 season]].<ref>{{cite press release|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2019/09/02/spanish-loan-for-kenedy|title=Spanish loan for Kenedy|publisher=Chelsea FC|date=2 September 2019|access-date=3 September 2019}}</ref> On 3 November 2019, he scored his first league goal of the season in a 1–0 win over [[Celta Vigo]].<ref>{{cite web|date=3 November 2019|title=LIVE Commentary Celta Vigo-Getafe 0-1|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/celta-vigo-vs-getafe/415742|access-date=3 November 2019|publisher=Sky Sports}}</ref>

====Loan to Granada====
On 8 September 2020, Kenedy returned to Spain with [[Granada CF|Granada]] on loan until the end of [[2020–21 Granada CF season|2020–21 season]].<ref>{{Cite press release|title=El Granada CF acuerda con el Chelsea FC la cesión de Kenedy por una temporada|url=https://www.granadacf.es/noticia/el-granada-cf-acuerda-con-el-chelsea-fc-la-cesion-de-kenedy-por-una-temporada|publisher=Granada C.F.|date=8 September 2020|access-date=8 September 2020|language=es}}</ref> He made his club debut as a substitute on 12 September 2020, in a 2–0 win against [[Athletic Bilbao]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Granada 2-0 Athletic|url=https://as.com/futbol/2020/09/12/primera/1599924328_449465.amp.html|website=as.com|date=12 September 2020|access-date=13 September 2020|language=es}}</ref>

====Loan to Flamengo====
On 18 August 2021, Kenedy extended his contract with Chelsea and returned to Brazil on loan with [[Clube de Regatas do Flamengo|Flamengo]] until July 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Kenedy extends contract and heads out on loan |url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2021/08/18/kenedy-extends-contract-and-heads-out-on-loan |publisher=Chelsea F.C. |access-date=18 August 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://ge.globo.com/futebol/times/flamengo/noticia/reforco-acertado-flamengo-paga-r-3-mi-e-tem-kenedy-por-emprestimo-de-um-ano.ghtml|title=Flamengo paga R$ 3 milhões e acerta empréstimo de Kenedy por uma temporada|publisher=Globoesporte.com|language=pt-BR|date=15 August 2021|access-date=15 August 2021}}</ref> He was recalled by Chelsea in January 2022 due to an injury to [[Ben Chilwell]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chelseafc.com/en/news/2022/01/14/tuchel-press-conference-ahead-of-manchester-city|title=Tuchel rules defender out with Covid-19, discusses his plans for Kenedy and looking into the transfer market|publisher=[[Chelsea F.C.]]|date=14 January 2022|access-date=14 January 2022}}</ref>

====2021–22 season====
Kenedy made his first Chelsea appearance in over four years when he started in a 3–2 win over [[Luton Town F.C.|Luton Town]] in the [[FA Cup]] on 2 March 2022. He also played in the next round against [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] later that month. On the final day of the season, he made his first league appearance for the Blues in five years, starting in a 2–1 win over [[Watford F.C.|Watford]].

===Valladolid===
In September 2022, Kenedy joined [[La Liga]] club [[Real Valladolid]] for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kenedy, pólvora ofensiva {{!}} Real Valladolid - Web Oficial |url=https://www.realvalladolid.es/noticia/kenedy-polvora-ofensiva |access-date=1 September 2022 |website=Kenedy, pólvora ofensiva {{!}} Real Valladolid - Web Oficial |language=es}}</ref>

=== Pachuca ===
In May 2025, Kenedy joined Mexican club [[C.F. Pachuca|Pachuca]] on a one-year loan.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realvalladolid.es/noticias/kenedy-cedido-al-cf-pachuca|title=Kenedy, cedido al CF Pachuca|publisher=Real Valladolid|language=es|date=20 May 2025}}</ref> A year later, the move became permanent.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kenedy, traspasado al CF Pachuca |url=https://www.realvalladolid.es/noticias/kenedy-traspasado-al-cf-pachuca |access-date=2026-07-10 |website=www.realvalladolid.es |language=es}}</ref>

==International career==
Kenedy scored six goals in eight games for [[Brazil national under-17 football team|Brazil under-17s]] as they came third at the [[2013 South American Under-17 Football Championship|2013 South American Championship]] in Argentina.

Kenedy originally named as part of the [[Brazil national under-20 football team|Brazil under-20]] squad for the [[2015 FIFA U-20 World Cup|2015 World Cup]] in New Zealand, but missed the tournament with [[appendicitis]], being replaced by [[Malcom (footballer)|Malcom]] as the team ended as runners-up.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://selecao.cbf.com.br/noticias/selecao-base-masculina/kenedy-esta-desconvocado-malcom-sera-seu-substituto#.VVlPAUPOrzx|title=Kenedy está desconvocado da Sub-20. Malcom será seu substituto|trans-title=Kenedy is left out of the U-20. Malcom will be his substitute|language=pt|publisher=selecao.cbf.com.br|author=Assessoria CBF|date=17 May 2015|access-date=17 May 2015}}</ref>

==Style of play==
An [[NBC Sports]] article by Nicholas Mendola in 2018 credited Kenedy's versatility, stating "The Brazilian left-sided man can play virtually any field position besides [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|center back]]".<ref name="NBC"/>

'''Lewis Edward Buxton''' (born 10 December 1983) is an English former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]].

Buxton began his career with [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] where he progressed through the youth ranks at the club. He gained [[Glossary of association football terms#F|first team]] experience with loan spells at [[Exeter City F.C.|Exeter City]] and [[AFC Bournemouth]]. He joined [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] in January 2005 in order to find first team football. His time at the [[Britannia Stadium]] was hampered by injury and he left for [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]] in October 2008. With the Owls, Buxton established himself as a regular member of the team and spent seven years, making 207 appearances.

==Career==
===Portsmouth===
A promising young defender, after working his way up through the [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] youth ranks, Buxton made his first team debut at the beginning of the 2001–02 season, aged 17, in a 1–0 win at Stockport County. He was soon a regular in [[Graham Rix]]'s squad.

However, following [[Harry Redknapp]]'s appointment as manager at the club, and the subsequent influx of new players, Buxton found games harder to come by. He was loaned out to [[Exeter City F.C.|Exeter City]] for October 2002, but upon his return to Fratton Park still found the competition too great. In January he was loaned to [[AFC Bournemouth]] for the remainder of the season. He played 18 games whilst at Bournemouth, and helped them achieve promotion.

He returned to Portsmouth for the 2003–04 season, but by October he was again not in the first team picture, and so returned to Bournemouth for the season, this time playing 28 games for the Cherries. It was a similar story during the 2004–05 season when Buxton failed to break into the team on a regular basis.

===Stoke City===
After turning down several loan offers he decided to call time on his Portsmouth career and transferred to [[Football League Championship]] club [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] in January 2005.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/s/stoke_city/4123345.stm|title=Stoke swoop for young Pompey duo|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=24 December 2004|access-date=11 July 2007}}</ref> He scored his first senior goal in Stoke's 3–1 defeat to [[Wolverhampton Wanderers]] in September 2005.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_div_1/4255426.stm|title=Stoke 1–3 Wolves|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=24 September 2005}}</ref>

He was sidelined for the first 2 months of the season due to a back injury, but he made his first start of the season in Stoke City's 1–0 win at [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] as a centre-half. However, he required an operation on his back, which kept him out for the remainder of the [[2006–07 in English football|2006–07 season]]. He since recovered and was ready for pre-season training, prior to the start of the [[2007–08 in English football|2007–08 season]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/s/stoke_city/6763465.stm|title=Buxton back from injury nightmare|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=18 June 2007|access-date=11 July 2007}}</ref> He made his comeback as a substitute for [[Stephen Wright (English footballer)|Stephen Wright]] in the 33rd minute of Stoke's 2–1 win over [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] on 18 August 2007.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_div_1/6941751.stm|title=Stoke 2–1 Charlton|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=19 August 2007|date=18 August 2007}}</ref> Buxton only appeared fleetingly in the 2007–08 season.

===Sheffield Wednesday===
On 17 October 2008 Buxton moved to [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]] on an initial one-month loan deal.<ref>{{cite web |title=Owls land Stoke defender on loan |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=17 October 2008 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/s/sheff_wed/7675720.stm |access-date=17 October 2008}}</ref> This was made a full deal on 26 January 2009 after Buxton expressed his desire to leave Stoke and move to Wednesday. He signed a {{frac|2|1|2}}-year contract. On 31 January 2009, Buxton scored his first goal for Wednesday against [[Birmingham City F.C|Birmingham City]]. He has played in many different positions at Hillsborough. These are Right Back, Left Back, Centre Back, Right Wing and Centre Midfield. He achieved promotion to the [[EFL Championship|Championship]] with Wednesday in May 2012.

In 2012–13, Buxton was voted player of the year by the [[Sheffield Wednesday]] supporters. This was following a consistency across over 40 games in a regularly changed Wednesday defensive unit. Buxton was released by Wednesday at the end of the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Sheffield Wednesday release 11 players including Lewis Buxton|publisher=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/32596487|access-date=8 May 2015}}</ref>

===Rotherham United===
In June 2015 Buxton signed for [[Rotherham United F.C.|Rotherham United]] on a one-year contract with the option of a further year.<ref>{{cite news|title=Lewis Buxton: Rotherham United sign ex-Owls defender|publisher=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33278305|access-date=25 June 2015}}</ref> After Rotherham had succeeded in surviving from relegation in the Championship, finishing one place above the drop in 21st,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.soccerstats.com/latest.asp?league=england2|title=Championship table, stats, form and results|website=SoccerSTATS.com}}</ref> the club decided to opt in not keeping Buxton for a further season, and instead let his contract run out, releasing him.

===Bolton Wanderers===
On 5 August 2016, following a successful trial with [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]], Buxton turned down a one-year contract signing in favour of a one-year contract to join [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Lewis Buxton joins Bolton Wanderers|url=http://www.bwfc.co.uk/news/article/2016-17/bolton-wanderers-lewis-buxton-sky-bet-league-one-2016-17-3227094.aspx|website=Bolton Wanderers FC|access-date=5 August 2016}}</ref> On 11 May 2017 the club confirmed that Buxton would be leaving at the end of his contract on 30 June.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.bwfc.co.uk/news/article/2016-17/bolton-wanderers-player-departures-2016-17-3713022.aspx|title=Wanderers confirm player departures|publisher=Bolton Wanderers Official Site|access-date=2017-05-11|language=en|archive-date=11 May 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170511181912/http://www.bwfc.co.uk/news/article/2016-17/bolton-wanderers-player-departures-2016-17-3713022.aspx|url-status=dead}}</ref> Buxton retired from playing football after leaving the Trotters.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bolton's 2017 summer released list: Where are they now? |url=https://lionofviennasuite.sbnation.com/2018/6/11/17446998/boltons-2017-summer-released-list |website=lionofviennasuite.sbnation.com |date=11 June 2018 |access-date=4 December 2019}}</ref>

==Post-retirement==
After retiring Buxton co-founded Human Experience Coaching, working with players in the [[Premier League]], [[EFL Championship|Championship]], and [[Major League Soccer]] and also wrote a book named ''The Athlete's Bible''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.portsmouth.co.uk/sport/football/portsmouth-fc/ex-sheffield-wednesday-and-stoke-man-lewis-buxton-i-was-a-teenage-portsmouth-regular-tracked-by-england-but-brilliant-blues-kicked-on-quicker-than-me-3162657|title=Ex-Sheffield Wednesday and Stoke man Lewis Buxton: I was a teenage Portsmouth regular tracked by England - but brilliant Blues kicked on quicker than me}}</ref>

'''Stig Inge Bjørnebye''' (born 11 December 1969) is a Norwegian former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played in Norway, England and Denmark, most notably for [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], and is currently the performance director of the Scottish football club [[Glasgow Rangers|Rangers]]. His preferred position was [[Defender (association football)#Left back|left back]], which he occupied for domestic clubs and the national team. Bjørnebye was appointed assistant manager of Norway in 2003, relinquishing the role three years later to succeed [[Tom Nordlie]] as manager of [[IK Start|Start]]. He was the sports director of [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]] from March 2015 until November 2019.

For club and country, Bjørnebye was noted for his precise deliveries from the flanks. Described as a "solid, no-nonsense full-back",<ref name="Who">{{cite book |title=Who's Who of Liverpool |last=Matthews |first=Tony |author-link=Tony Matthews |year=2006 |publisher=[[Mainstream Publishing]] |location=Edinburgh |isbn=1-84596-140-4 |page=31 }}</ref> Bjørnebye played competitive football for 16 years, and appeared in 194 [[Premier League]] matches, until injury compelled retirement in March 2003. He played for the [[Norway national football team|Norwegian national team]] in the [[1994 FIFA World Cup|1994]] and [[1998 FIFA World Cup]] and the [[UEFA Euro 2000|Euro 2000]] and was capped 75 times, scoring once.

== Club career ==
Stig Inge Bjørnebye was born in [[Elverum Municipality]], the son of skier [[Jo Inge Bjørnebye]], who competed in the [[1968 Winter Olympics|1968]] and [[1972 Winter Olympics]]. As a child, Bjørnebye exhibited an interest in emulating his father by becoming a [[Ski jumping|ski jumper]].<ref name="NRK">{{cite web |url=http://www.nrk.no/programmer/radio/stjerneklart/1.3367272 |title=Stig Inge Bjørnebye |date=3 September 2007 |publisher=[[Norwegian Broadcasting Corporation|NRK]] |language=no |access-date=3 February 2008 }}</ref>

His footballing career began as a youth player with home club [[Elverum Fotball|Elverum]], before joining [[Strømmen IF|Strømmen]] in the late 1980s.<ref name="stats">{{NFT player|id=14059|name=Bjørnebye, Stig Inge|access-date=21 January 2008}}</ref> He moved to [[KIL Toppfotball|Kongsvinger]] in 1989, establishing himself as a first-team regular in the [[Norwegian top division]]. After three seasons with Kongsvinger, he transferred to [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]] in 1992, where he in his inaugural season won the Norwegian top division and the [[Norwegian Cup]],<ref name="NRK"/> in the final of which he scored the deciding goal against [[Lillestrøm SK|Lillestrøm]].<ref name="LFCH">{{cite web |url=http://www.lfchistory.net/Players/Player/Profile/268 |title=Stig Inge Bjørnebye |publisher=LFChistory |access-date=10 January 2011 }}</ref>

His performances merited inclusion in the national team and attracted the attention of Liverpool's manager [[Graeme Souness]], who bought Bjørnebye for [[Pound Sterling|£]]600,000 less than one year after moving to Rosenborg.<ref name="LFCH"/> Signed as a replacement for [[David Burrows (footballer)|David Burrows]], Bjørnebye debuted inauspiciously on 19 December 1992 in a 5–1 defeat to [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Football: Coventry shatter Liverpool illusions |first=Jasper |last=Rees |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-coventry-shatter-liverpool-illusions-1564560.html |newspaper=The Independent |date=20 December 1992 |access-date=14 January 2011 |location=London |archive-date=29 September 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170929183943/http://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-coventry-shatter-liverpool-illusions-1564560.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Initial difficulties adapting to the Premier League caused many fans to question his displays on the pitch and he returned to Norway on loan to Rosenborg in 1994.<ref name="Who"/><ref name="LFCTV">{{cite web |url=http://www.liverpoolfc.tv/history/past-players/stig-inge-bjrnebye |title=Stig Inge Bjørnebye |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |access-date=10 January 2011 }}</ref>

Bjørnebye's experiences as a Reds' player in the [[1994–95 in English football|1994–95]] season, under the management of [[Roy Evans]], were markedly more successful than that of previous campaigns.<ref name="LFCTV"/> He gained a regular place in the senior team, supplanting the left back position from [[Julian Dicks]], and featured in the 2–1 win against [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] in the final of the [[1995 Football League Cup Final|1995 League Cup Final]] on 2 April 1995.<ref name="LFCTV"/><ref>{{cite news |title=Liverpool prevail in cup final to savour |first=Glenn |last=Moore |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/liverpool-prevail-in-cup-final-to-savour-1614114.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220525/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/liverpool-prevail-in-cup-final-to-savour-1614114.html |archive-date=25 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |newspaper=The Independent |date=3 April 1995 |access-date=10 January 2011 |location=London}}</ref> Subsequent injury, a broken leg sustained on 5 April 1995 in a 3–1 win match against [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Bjrnebye's despair |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/bjrnebyes-despair-1614656.html |newspaper=The Independent |date=7 April 1995 |access-date=14 January 2011 |location=London |archive-date=27 April 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190427064556/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/bjrnebyes-despair-1614656.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> terminated his season and he was replaced by [[Steve Harkness]].<ref name="Who"/>

{| class="toccolours" style="float: left; margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 2em; font-size: 85%; background:#c6dbf7; color:black; width:30em; max-width: 40%;" cellspacing="5"
| style="text-align: left;" |

"I am not very good at [remembering what my fondest footballing memories are] but if I had to pick, I would say my time with Rosenborg, the World Cup game against Mexico in 1994 and my three cup finals – at Ullevaal, Wembley and the Millennium Stadium,"
|-
| style="text-align: left;" | UEFA.com, 11 March 2003.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bjørnebye succumbs to eye injury |url=http://www.uefa.com/news/newsid=58045,print.htmx |work=UEFA |date=11 March 2003 |access-date=10 January 2011 }}{{dead link|date=March 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>
 |}

Unavailable for several months, Bjørnebye appeared just twice for Liverpool in the [[1995–96 in English football|1995–96]] season.<ref name="LFCTV"/> Recovery and injuries to other left back candidates enabled Bjørnebye to reclaim his place the [[1996–97 in English football|following season]], in which he scored his first goal for Liverpool on 17 August 1996 in a 3–3 draw against [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Absolutely Fabrizio for Boro |first=Simon |last=Turnbull |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/absolutely-fabrizio-for-boro-1310336.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220525/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/absolutely-fabrizio-for-boro-1310336.html |archive-date=25 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |newspaper=The Independent |date=18 August 1996 |access-date=10 January 2011 |location=London}}</ref> He contributed to the club's most convincing title challenge since the inception of the Premier League by supplying club strikers [[Stan Collymore]] and [[Robbie Fowler]] with precise crosses.<ref name="LFCH"/> He was ultimately included in the [[Professional Footballers' Association|PFA]] Team of the Year with [[Steve McManaman]] and [[Mark Wright (footballer born 1963)|Mark Wright]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Pick of the Premiership |url=http://www.thefa.com/England/news/2005/pfa_teamofseason |work=[[The Football Association]] |date=26 April 2005|access-date=10 January 2011 }}</ref> The acquisition of [[Steve Staunton]] and arrival of [[Gérard Houllier]] in the [[1998–99 in English football|1998–99]] season, limited Bjørnebye's first-team opportunities, leading to his effective marginalisation.<ref name="LFCTV"/><ref name="Peo">{{cite news |title=Bjornebye growls a goodbye |url=https://www.questia.com/read/1G1-60639508 |newspaper=[[The Sunday People|The People]]  |date=20 September 1998 }}{{dead link|date=July 2021}}</ref> Bjørnebye affirmed his recurring determination to stay at Liverpool that season, remarking "If I didn't have any fight in my stomach I'd have left Liverpool at least three times before".<ref name="Peo"/>

Unable to displace Staunton and [[Dominic Matteo]], Bjørnebye agreed to a loan move to Danish side [[Brøndby IF|Brøndby]] in 2000,<ref name="LFCTV"/> who finished second in the [[Danish Superliga]] with Bjørnebye on the team.<ref name="NRK"/> He decided to permanently leave Liverpool after returning from the [[UEFA Euro 2000|European Championship]], accepting a £300,000 transfer to [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] that reunited him with former manager Graeme Souness.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bjornebye seals Rovers deal |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/euro2000/teams/norway/806980.stm |work=[[BBC Sport]] |publisher=[[BBC]] |date=26 June 2000 |access-date=5 February 2008 }}</ref> Promotion to the Premier League was achieved in his first year with Rovers, in the process, Bjørnebye scored his only goal for the club on 11 November 2000, in a 2–2 draw against Portsmouth.<ref>{{cite news |title=Portsmouth 2–2 Blackburn |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_div_1/1016615.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=11 November 2000 |access-date=15 September 2009 }}</ref> His final trophy was gained when Blackburn defeated [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] 2–1 in the [[2002 Football League Cup Final|2002 League Cup Final]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Cole strike stuns Spurs |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/worthington_cup/1834988.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=24 February 2002 |access-date=10 January 2011 }}</ref> Successive injuries after the cup victory disrupted and eventually ended his career as a footballer. While preparing for the [[2002–03 in English football|2002–03]] season, Bjørnebye fractured his eye socket in a training accident. He complained of double vision, underwent surgery, and was rendered unavailable for seven months. Further injury inflicted during a League Cup match on 17 December 2002, in a 2–0 win against [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]] escalated, while Bjørnebye was recovering in Norway, necessitating emergency surgery to avert the possibility of foot amputation.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bjornebye in foot fear |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/b/blackburn_rovers/2667631.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=17 January 2003 |access-date=6 February 2008 }}</ref> Bjørnebye announced his retirement on 11 March 2003. Blackburn manager Graeme Souness reacted to the decision with a statement:

{{Blockquote|It's a very sad day. As far as I am concerned it could hardly be worse for Stig is the consummate dedicated professional. He is as good a professional as any I have worked with, I couldn’t name anybody better and he is [a] fine role model and a proper, proper human being. Stig has had a wonderful career, it's a great shame that it has to end with a freak training-ground accident as he felt, quite rightly, that he could have played longer.<ref>{{cite news |title=Retiring Bjornebye says bye-bye |url=http://www.breakingnews.ie/sport/retiring-bjornebye-says-bye-bye-91233.html |work=Breaking News |date=11 March 2003 |access-date=10 January 2011 }}</ref>}}

== International career ==
Bjørnebye was [[Cap (sport)#Association football|capped]] 75 times by [[Norway national football team|Norway]], scoring once – an [[olympic goal]] in a 1–0 friendly against the [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]] on 8 September 1993. Having represented his country at youth, [[Norway national under-21 football team|under-21]], and "B" level,<ref name="Who"/> Bjørnebye debuted for the senior team on 31 May 1989 against [[Austria national football team|Austria]].<ref name="RSSSF">{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/noo-recintlp.html |title=Norway – Record International Players |work=RSSSF |access-date=6 February 2008 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130504194906/http://www.rsssf.com/miscellaneous/noo-recintlp.html |archive-date=4 May 2013 }}</ref> The majority of his caps were collected during [[Egil Olsen]]'s eight-year tenure as manager of Norway. Under Olsen's guidance, Norway employed a "long ball" policy that was contingent on the height of Olsen's squad.<ref name="CNN">{{cite news |title=Norway's style won't change without Olsen |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/soccer/world/events/1998/worldcup/news/1998/06/28/norway_reaction |work=[[CNN Sports Illustrated]] |publisher=[[CNN]] |date=28 June 1998 |access-date=7 February 2008 |archive-date=18 February 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080218035509/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/soccer/world/events/1998/worldcup/news/1998/06/28/norway_reaction/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> The tactic of directing long passes to the tall winger [[Jostein Flo]], principally delivered by Bjørnebye, became popularly referred to in Norway as the "[[Flo Pass]]" (Flo-pasningen).<ref name="NRK"/> Although criticised for employing the long-ball approach and maintaining a defensively-orientated mentality, Olsen secured qualification for the World Cups of [[1994 FIFA World Cup|1994]] and [[1998 FIFA World Cup|1998]].<ref name="CNN"/> Bjørnebye participated in both tournaments – seven matches in total.<ref>{{cite news |title=Stig BJORNEBYE |url=https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/statisticsandrecords/players/player=46646/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081011000729/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/statisticsandrecords/players/player=46646/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=11 October 2008 |work=[[FIFA]] |access-date=7 February 2008 }}</ref>

He decided to retire from international football after the 1998 World Cup, intending to focus on his domestic career and family. Bjørnebye unexpectedly reversed his decision after [[Nils Johan Semb]] persuaded him to return to the squad for [[UEFA Euro 2000|Euro 2000]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Premiership stars in Norway squad |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/euro2000/teams/norway/768295.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=29 May 2000 |access-date=10 January 2011 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/euro2000/teams/norway/squad/768636.stm |title=Stig Inge Bjornebye |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |access-date=6 February 2008 |date=29 May 2000}}</ref> Unused in Norway's 1–0 win against Spain on 13 June 2000, Bjørnebye was first introduced to the competition in the second match of the group stage, in a 0–1 loss on 18 June 2000 against [[Yugoslavia national football team|Yugoslavia]], as a 35-minute substitute for his Liverpool colleague [[Vegard Heggem]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Yugoslavs ease past Norway |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/euro2000/796484.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=18 June 2000 |access-date=10 January 2011 }}</ref> He retained his place, featuring in the goalless draw against [[Slovenia national football team|Slovenia]] on 21 June 2000, which eliminated Norway from the tournament.<ref>{{cite news |title=Norway crash out after Slovenia draw |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/euro2000/800614.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=21 June 2000 |access-date=10 January 2011 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Norway crash out after Slovenia draw |archive-date=26 November 2007 |work=FIFA |access-date=10 January 2011 }}</ref> placing him ninth in the overall record of appearances for Norway as of 2007.<ref name="RSSSF"/>

== Managerial career ==
Bjørnebye returned to football in a non-playing capacity when he was selected by the [[Football Association of Norway|Norwegian Football Association]] to replace [[Harald Aabrekk]] as Norway's assistant manager, subordinate to the newly appointed [[Åge Hareide]]. Prior to the announcement, the media in England had reported that Bjørnebye was considering maintaining a relationship with Blackburn by becoming a scout for the club.<ref>{{cite news |title=New Role Stig |url=http://www.burnleycitizen.co.uk/archive/2003/12/10/Lancashire+Archive/5867525.New_role_Stig/ |newspaper=[[Lancashire Evening Telegraph]] |date=10 December 2003 |access-date=10 January 2011 }}</ref> He vacated his position in 2006 to succeed Tom Nordlie as manager of [[IK Start|Start]]. Success was forthcoming in his first season; the club competed in Europe and Bjørnebye was the highest earning coach of the season, ahead of his predecessor Nordlie, with an income of almost seven million [[Norwegian krone|krone]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Bjørnebye best betalte trener |first=Kristian |last=Elster |url=http://www.nrksport.no/fotball/eliteserien/1.3728706 |work=NRK Sport |publisher=NRK |language=no |date=12 October 2007 |access-date=7 February 2008 }}</ref> His appointment lasted two seasons, ending with dismissal in September 2007, after a series of poor results that placed the club in serious danger of being relegated from the [[Tippeligaen]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Det er mitt ansvar |first1=Jamel |last1=Rake |first2=Anders |last2=K. Christiansen |url=http://www.vg.no/pub/vgart.hbs?artid=161732 |newspaper=[[Verdens Gang]] |language=no |date=5 September 2007 |access-date=7 February 2008 }}</ref> He was replaced by [[Benny Lennartsson]], who was unable to preserve the club's premier league status; Start were relegated to Norway's [[Adeccoligaen|second tier]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Torrid finish for Start |first=Elvind |last=Aarre |url=http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/news/newsid=613796.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121026070643/http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/news/newsid=613796.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=26 October 2012 |work=UEFA |date=4 November 2007 |access-date=10 January 2011 }}</ref>

On 15 March 2015, Stig Inge Bjørnebye succeeded [[Erik Hoftun]] as the sports director of [[Eliteserien (football)|Eliteserien]] club [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.rbk.no/lag/stig-inge-bjornebye|title=Stig Inge Bjørnebye|work=Rosenborg|access-date=31 March 2017|language=nb-NO|archive-date=31 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170331210306/http://www.rbk.no/lag/stig-inge-bjornebye|url-status=dead}}</ref> He since has won [[Double (association football)|the double]] with [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]] two seasons (2015 and 2016). [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]] is the first club in the history of [[Football in Norway|Norwegian football]] to do so two consecutive seasons.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.t-a.no/sport/tronderball/2016/11/20/Rosenborg-tok-en-historisk-dobbel-etter-kalasseier-i-cupfinalen-13816314.ece|title=Rosenborg tok en historisk dobbel etter kalasseier i cupfinalen|last=Holberg|first=Jonas A.|date=20 November 2016|work=www.t-a.no|access-date=31 March 2017|language=nb-NO|archive-date=31 March 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170331211009/http://www.t-a.no/sport/tronderball/2016/11/20/Rosenborg-tok-en-historisk-dobbel-etter-kalasseier-i-cupfinalen-13816314.ece|url-status=dead}}</ref> As the sports director of Rosenborg Ballklub he has many responsibilities, among many others signing on new players and renewing contracts with existing players. The most notable signing came on 6 March 2017: [[Nicklas Bendtner]] signed on for a three-year contract with the Norwegian side. This was the most surprising and most notable signing in the history of [[Football in Norway|Norwegian football]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11727/10793112/nicklas-bendtner-seals-transfer-from-nottingham-forest-to-rosenborg|title=Nicklas Bendtner seals transfer from Nottingham Forest to Rosenborg|work=Sky Sports|access-date=31 March 2017|language=en}}</ref> Teammate [[Pål André Helland]] commented: "It shouldn't come as a surprise if he becomes the top scorer and we win the [[Eliteserien (football)|league]]."<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.tv2.no/a/8976736/|title=Bendtner på plass hos RBK: - Det bør ikke komme som en overraskelse om han blir toppscorer og vi tar gull|last=AS|first=TV 2|work=TV 2|access-date=31 March 2017|language=no-nb}}</ref>

In 2021, Bjørnebye succeeded [[Peter Christiansen (footballer, born 1975)|Peter Christiansen]] as the sports director of the [[Superligaen]] club [[AGF Aarhus|AGF]] in Denmark. In January 2025, AGF hired a new sports director. So Stig's contract was not renewed and he left Aarhus.

In December 2025, he become interim football consultant and adviser at [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Rangers appoint Bjornebye as interim advisor |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/articles/c79xjq3g7yeo |website=[[BBC Sport]] |access-date=7 January 2026 |date=17 December 2025}}</ref> On 18 June 2026 it was confirmed that he had been appointed on a permanent contract as Rangers' Performance Director. His role continues to focus on first team recruitment as well as overseeing the performance department and youth academy.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bjornebye lands permanent Rangers job as new role explained |url=https://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/football/26205988.bjornebye-lands-permanent-rangers-job-new-role-explained/ |website=[[The Herald (Glasgow)]] |access-date=19 June 2026 |date=18 June 2026}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Bjørnebye is married to the former [[Byåsen IL|Byåsen]] [[Team handball|handball]] player [[Hege Frøseth]], with whom he has three children.<ref name="NRK"/>

'''Rasmus Jönsson''' ({{IPA|sv|ˈrǎsːmɵs ˈjœ̌nːsɔn}}; born 27 January 1990) is a Swedish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who is normally deployed as a [[second striker]].

==Career==

=== Helsingborgs IF ===
He plays as a striker and got his breakthrough in 2008, scoring four goals in [[Allsvenskan]] alongside [[Henrik Larsson]] in [[Helsingborgs IF]]. Jönsson is commonly called "Sugröret", meaning ''the drinking straw'', among his teammates.{{citation needed|date=May 2022}} During the season 2010 in Allsvenskan, Helsingborgs IF Finished in second place just two points short of [[Malmö FF]]. Helsingborg however didn't allow this to let them down after a good season and finished it off on a high winning the [[Svenska Cupen]] in a final against [[Hammarby Fotboll|Hammarby IF]] with Rasmus scoring the only goal in the game late on. On 29 August 2011, Helsingborgs IF confirmed that a deal had been agreed for Jönsson to join [[Bundesliga]] side [[VfL Wolfsburg]] on a four-year deal. Jönsson said that he was sad to leave Helsingborg but happy to take an important step forward in his career.{{citation needed|date=May 2022}}

=== VfL Wolfsburg ===
On 11 September 2011, Rasmus Jönsson made his Bundesliga debut from start against [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]] and he assisted for [[Mario Mandžukić]]'s second goal. Jönsson played 90 minutes before being substituted.

==== Loan to FSV Frankfurt ====
On 29 January 2013, it was announced that Jönsson would join [[FSV Frankfurt]] on loan for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.neuepresse.de/Sport/Regional/Wolfsburg-verleiht-Joensson-und-Schulze | title = Wolfsburg verleiht Jönsson und Schulze | language = de | publisher = Neue Presse | date = 9 January 2013 | access-date = 30 June 2013 | archive-date = 10 August 2020 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20200810103319/https://www.neuepresse.de/Sportbuzzer/Sport-Regional/Wolfsburg-verleiht-Joensson-und-Schulze | url-status = dead }}</ref>

=== AaB ===
On 9 August 2013, it was announced that Jönsson would join the Danish Superliga club [[AaB Fodbold|AaB]] on a loan spell for the 2013/2014 season. On Sunday 6 October he scored twice against Viborg. On 21 July 2014, it was announced that Jönsson joined [[AaB Fodbold|AaB]] on a permanent two-year basis. Jönsson got shirt number 10.

=== OB ===
In the Summer of 2016, Jönsson signed with the Danish club [[Odense Boldklub|OB]]. In OB he was reunited with head coach [[Kent Nielsen]]. Nielsen was head coach in [[AaB Fodbold|AaB]] when Jönsson joined the club before the 2013-14 season.

=== Buriram United ===
On 2 July 2019 it was announced he had signed a deal with [[Buriram United]] in [[Thai League 1]] until 30 November 2022. On the same day he traveled with his new teammates to their away fixture against [[JL Chiangmai United F.C.]] in the [[Thai League Cup]]. His team won 2–1 and Jönsson provided an assist.

'''Eduard "Edu" Oriol Gràcia''' (born 5 November 1986) is a Spanish former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]].

==Club career==
Born in [[Cambrils]], [[Province of Tarragona|Tarragona]], [[Catalonia]], Oriol started playing with amateurs [[CF Pobla de Mafumet]], having a loan spell with [[CF Reus Deportiu]] whilst on contract with the former. In the [[2008–09 Segunda División B|2008–09 season]], still in his native region, he competed in the [[Segunda División B]] with [[UE Sant Andreu]].<ref name=FCB>{{cite web|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.es/es/noticias/1189060/edu-oriol-y-abraham-minero-vidas-paralelas-con-pasado-azulgrana|title=Edu Oriol y Abraham Minero, vidas paralelas con pasado azulgrana|trans-title=Edu Oriol and Abraham Minero, parallel lives with an ''azulgrana'' past|publisher=FC Barcelona|language=es|date=14 November 2011|access-date=23 June 2025}}</ref>

Oriol moved to [[FC Barcelona]] in the summer of 2009, helping [[FC Barcelona Atlètic|the reserves]] to [[2009–10 Segunda División B|return]] to [[Segunda División]] by appearing in 29 games and scoring three goals.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/2010/06/20/futbol/mas_futbol/1277060846.html|title=El filial del Barcelona vuelve a Segunda doce años después|trans-title=Barcelona reserves return to ''Segunda'' twelve years later|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=20 June 2010|access-date=22 June 2025}}</ref> After once again featuring heavily for ''Barça B'' in the [[2010–11 Segunda División|2010–11 campaign]],<ref name=FCB/> as the team finished in third position – being however ineligible for [[2011 Segunda División play-offs|playoff promotion]] – he signed for [[La Liga]] club [[Real Zaragoza]] for three years.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.heraldo.es/noticias/deportes/el_real_zaragoza_ficha_dos_jugadores_cantera_del_barcelona.html|title=El Real Zaragoza ficha a dos jugadores de la cantera del F.C. Barcelona|trans-title=Real Zaragoza sign two players from F.C. Barcelona's youth system|newspaper=[[Heraldo de Aragón]]|language=es|date=2 July 2011|access-date=12 November 2013}}</ref>

Oriol made his debut in the top flight on 28 August 2011, coming on as a second-half [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] in a 0–6 home loss against [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/324018?cc=5739|title=Ronaldo gets Madrid show underway|publisher=[[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]]|date=28 August 2011|access-date=12 November 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121102065146/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/324018?cc=5739|archive-date=2 November 2012}}</ref> He scored the first of his two goals in the competition on 29 April 2012, opening the 2–0 win over [[Athletic Bilbao]] also at the [[La Romareda]];<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elperiodicodearagon.com/deportes/2012/04/29/real-zaragoza-juega-equipo-primera-47541423.html|title=El Real Zaragoza juega como un equipo de Primera|trans-title=Real Zaragoza play like a ''Primera'' team|newspaper=[[El Periódico de Aragón]]|first=Alfonso|last=Hernández|language=es|date=29 April 2012|access-date=22 June 2025}}</ref> the other came one week later, the only as the hosts defeated [[Levante UD]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rtve.es/deportes/20120502/zaragoza-sigue-vivo-tras-vencer-levante/521057.shtml|title=El Zaragoza sigue vivo tras vencer al Levante|trans-title=Zaragoza remain alive after beating Levante|publisher=[[RTVE]]|language=es|date=2 May 2012|access-date=23 June 2025}}</ref>

Oriol joined [[Azerbaijan Premier League]]'s [[Khazar Lankaran FK]] in late August 2013 on a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://lankaranfc.com/news/2013/08/Edu-Oriol-signed-for-Khazar-Lankaran/2917|title=Edu Oriol "Xəzər Lənkəran"da!|trans-title=Edu Oriol to Khazar Lankaran!|publisher=FK Khazar|language=az|date=August 2013|access-date=2 January 2014|url-status=usurped|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140102194735/http://lankaranfc.com/news/2013/08/Edu-Oriol-signed-for-Khazar-Lankaran/2917|archive-date=2 January 2014}}</ref> following the [[Aragon]]ese's [[2012–13 La Liga|relegation]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.azerisport.com/az/futbol/20130826071458770.html|title=Barcelonanın sabiq üzvü rəsmən Xəzər Lənkəranda! (foto)|trans-title=Khazar Lankaran sign former Barcelona player! (photo)|publisher=Azeri Sport|language=az|date=27 August 2013|access-date=23 October 2013}}</ref> He won his first piece of silverware on 23 October, helping his new team to defeat [[Neftçi PFK]] in [[2013 Azerbaijan Supercup|that year]]'s [[Azerbaijan Supercup]].<ref name=MVP>{{cite web|url=https://www.europasur.es/balona/Balona-Linense-sanluqueno-Edu-Oriol-MVP-novena-jornada_0_1623439031.html|title=El Sanluqueño trae a La Línea al MVP de la última jornada: Edu Oriol|trans-title=Sanluqueño bring last round's MVP to La Línea: Edu Oriol|publisher=Europa Sur|first=Rubén|last=Almagro|language=es|date=26 October 2021|access-date=6 July 2022}}</ref>

On 13 January 2014, Oriol's contract with Khazar was cancelled by mutual consent, after he failed to settle in [[Azerbaijan]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.azerifootball.com/ru/17/news/23138.html|script-title=ru:Испанец расторг контракт с Хазаром|trans-title=|publisher=Azeri Football|language=ru|date=13 January 2014|access-date=13 January 2014}}</ref> The following day, he penned a two-year deal with [[AEL Limassol]] in the [[Cypriot First Division]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fichajes.com/a1146631374658928964-edu-oriol-cambia-azerbaiyan-por-chipre|title=Edu Oriol cambia Azerbaiyán por Chipre|trans-title=Edu Oriol swaps Azerbaijan for Cyprus|publisher=Fichajes|first=Rafael|last=Castro|language=es|date=14 January 2014|access-date=6 July 2022}}</ref>

On 18 August 2014, Oriol agreed to a one-year contract with the option of a further year with [[EFL Championship|Football League Championship]] side [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]], linking up with his twin brother [[Joan Oriol|Joan]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.blackpoolfc.co.uk/news/article/another-oriol-arrives-1836151.aspx|title=Another Oriol arrives|publisher=Blackpool F.C.|date=18 August 2014|access-date=18 August 2014}}</ref> His contract was terminated by mutual consent on 12 January 2015,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.blackpoolgazette.co.uk/sport/football/blackpool-fc/oriol-twins-head-out-of-pool-1-7047151|title=Oriol twins head out of Pool|newspaper=[[Blackpool Gazette]]|date=13 January 2015|access-date=3 December 2017}}</ref> and he moved to the Romanian [[Liga I]] with [[FC Rapid București]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.digisport.ro/fotbal/liga-1/joan-oriol-se-desparte-de-rapid-dar-promite-nu-as-putea-juca-in-romania-la-alta-echipa-ce-oferte-are-170160|title=Joan Oriol se desparte de Rapid, dar promite: "Nu aș putea juca în România la altă echipă". Ce oferte are|trans-title=Joan Oriol cuts ties with Rapid, but promises: "I could not play with another team in Romania." What offers are there?|publisher=[[Digi Sport (Romania)|Digi Sport]]|language=ro|date=24 May 2015|access-date=24 July 2018}}</ref>

Oriol subsequently returned to his homeland and its second tier, featuring rarely for [[Som Maresme FC|UE Llagostera]]<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.marca.com/futbol/llagostera/2016/01/13/5696a589ca4741f8638b4631.html|title=El Llagostera ficha a Edu Oriol y rescinde el contrato de Ortuño|trans-title=Llagostera sign Edu Oriol and terminate Ortuño's contract|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=13 January 2016|access-date=24 July 2018}}</ref> and [[CD Tenerife]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elperiodicodearagon.com/noticias/deportes/edu-oriol-deja-llagostera-ficha-tenerife_1121778.html|title=Edu Oriol deja el Llagostera y ficha por el Tenerife|trans-title=Edu Oriol leaves Llagostera and signs for Tenerife|newspaper=El Periódico de Aragón|language=es|date=26 June 2016|access-date=24 July 2018}}</ref> In late November 2017, the 31-year-old signed with amateurs [[UD Ibiza]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.futbolbalear.es/2017/11/29/edu-oriol-nuevo-jugador-de-la-ud-ibiza/|title=Edu Oriol nuevo jugador de la UD Ibiza|trans-title=Edu Oriol new UD Ibiza player|publisher=Fútbol Balear|language=es|date=29 November 2017|access-date=24 July 2018}}</ref> leaving at the end of [[2017–18 Tercera División|the season]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://periodicodeibiza.es/deportes/deporte-ibiza/2018/02/16/883751/edu-oriol-continua-ibiza.html|title=Edu Oriol no continúa en la UD Ibiza|trans-title=Edu Oriol does not remain at UD Ibiza|newspaper=Periódico de Ibiza|language=es|date=16 February 2018|access-date=22 February 2018}}</ref>

In August 2018, Oriol joined third-division club [[Atlético Sanluqueño CF]]; upon arriving, he labelled his former Blackpool manager [[Lee Clark (footballer)|Lee Clark]] a "racist".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fichajes.com/a4368560714425049161-info-fichajes-com-joan-y-edu-la-aventura-inglesa-de-los-hermanos-oriol|title=Info Fichajes.com: Joan y Edu, la aventura inglesa de los hermanos Oriol|trans-title=Fichajes.com Info: Joan and Edu, the English adventure of the Oriol brothers|publisher=Fichajes|first=Iván|last=Vargas|language=es|date=5 November 2014|access-date=23 June 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.diariodejerez.es/deportes/Edu-Oriol-habla-claro-Sanlucar_0_1271272893.html|title=Edu Oriol, habla alto y claro en Sanlúcar|trans-title=Edu Oriol, he speaks loud and clear in Sanlúcar|newspaper=Diario de Jerez|first=Paco|last=Bernal|language=es|date=9 August 2018|access-date=23 June 2025}}</ref> He equalled a career-best six goals in his [[2018–19 Segunda División B|debut campaign]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.diaridetarragona.com/deportes/128319/sanlucar-hace-renacer-a-edu-oriol-20200620-0029-nhdt202006200029.html|title=Sanlúcar hace renacer a Edu Oriol|trans-title=Sanlúcar brings Edu Oriol back to life|newspaper=[[Diari de Tarragona]]|first=Marc|last=Libiano|language=es|date=20 June 2020|access-date=23 June 2025}}</ref> and was eventually named [[Captain (association football)|captain]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://atleticosanluquenocf.com/debut-de-edu-oriol-con-el-brazalete-de-capitan/|title=Debut de Edu Oriol con el brazalete de capitán|trans-title=Debut of Edu Oriol with the captain's armband|publisher=Atlético Sanluqueño CF|language=es|date=27 July 2021|access-date=23 June 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Oriol's [[twin]] brother, [[Joan Oriol|Joan]], was also a footballer. A [[Defender (association football)|defender]], he shared teams with his sibling on several occasions.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/20101229/edu-y-joan-oriol-tu-al-barca-yo-al-villarreal_54095651111.html|title=Edu y Joan Oriol: tú al Barça, yo al Villarreal|trans-title=Edu and Joan Oriol: you go to Barça, i go to Villarreal|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|language=es|date=29 December 2010|access-date=1 March 2014}}</ref>
