'''André Stéphane Bikey-Amougou''' (born 8 January 1985) is a Cameroonian former [[association football|footballer]] who is an [[Coach (sport)|assistant manager]] of Egyptian club [[Zamalek SC|Zamalek]]. Primarily a [[defender (association football)|defender]], he could also play in [[midfielder|midfield]] and was known for his physical presence. He is generally known by his first surname '''Bikey''' except between 2011 and 2012 while playing for Burnley when he decided to use his second surname '''Amougou'''.

He moved to Spain at the age of 15 to train with [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] before finding the opportunity of first-team football in Portugal with [[F.C. Marco|Marco]] in the 2002–03 season. He went on to have brief spells with [[F.C. Paços de Ferreira|Paços de Ferreira]], [[C.D. Aves|Aves]], and [[U.D. Leiria|União de Leiria]], before joining Russian club [[FC Shinnik Yaroslavl|Shinnik Yaroslavl]] in 2005. He switched to [[FC Lokomotiv Moscow|Lokomotiv Moscow]] the following year. He joined English [[Premier League]] side [[Reading F.C.|Reading]] on a season-long loan in August 2006 before joining the club permanently for a £1 million fee in April 2007. He was sold to [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] for £2.8 million in August 2009. He joined [[Bristol City F.C.|Bristol City]] on loan in March 2012 before joining [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] on a [[Free transfer (association football)|free transfer]] in August 2012. He moved on to Greek club [[Panetolikos F.C.|Panetolikos]] in September 2013 before returning to England in July 2014 to play for [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]]. He moved to India in October 2015 after being recruited by [[NorthEast United FC|NorthEast United]] and moved on to [[FC Pune City|Pune City]] in July 2016. He returned to England to join [[Port Vale F.C.|Port Vale]] in March 2017 before going back to India five months later to play for a new club [[Jamshedpur FC|Jamshedpur]]. He switched to [[ATK (football club)|ATK]] in August 2018 and played for Spanish club [[CF Igualada]] in 2020.

He won a total of 25 [[Cap (sport)|cap]]s for [[Cameroon national football team|Cameroon]], scoring one international goal. He was a squad member in three [[Africa Cup of Nations]] tournaments: [[2006 Africa Cup of Nations|2006]], [[2008 Africa Cup of Nations|2008]], and [[2010 Africa Cup of Nations|2010]]. Cameroon finished as runners-up in 2008, though he missed [[2008 Africa Cup of Nations final|the final]] after being [[Ejection (sports)|sent off]] in the semi-finals for pushing over a stretcher bearer. He also represented the [[Cameroon national under-23 football team|Cameroon Olympic]] team at the [[2008 Summer Olympics]].

==Club career==
===Spain and Portugal===
Bikey left his native Cameroon to start his footballing career at [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]] in [[Spain]] when he was 15. Still, he failed to make the grade at the [[Estadi Olímpic Lluís Companys]] and left without making a first-team appearance.<ref>{{cite news|title=Make ISL a longer league, says Andre Bikey|url=https://www.deccanchronicle.com/sports/football/140916/make-isl-a-longer-league-andre-bikey.html|access-date=19 March 2017|work=Deccan Chronicle|date=14 September 2016|language=en}}</ref> He signed with [[Portugal|Portuguese]] [[LigaPro|Segunda Liga]] side [[F.C. Marco|Marco]], and made his debut in professional football in a 6–1 home win over [[A.D. Ovarense|Ovarense]] on 29 September 2002.<ref>{{cite web|title=ForaDeJogo.net – Marco 6 – 1 Ovarense // Liga de Honra|url=https://www.foradejogo.net/match.php?match=200315400110508|website=ForaDeJogo|access-date=19 March 2017}}</ref> He scored his first senior goal in a 3–0 home win over [[F.C. Felgueiras|Felgueiras]] on 19 April.<ref>{{cite web|title=ForaDeJogo.net – Marco 3 – 0 Felgueiras // Liga de Honra|url=https://www.foradejogo.net/match.php?match=200315400112807|website=ForaDeJogo|access-date=19 March 2017}}</ref> He played a total of 13 games during the [[2002–03 Segunda Liga|2002–03]] season and was [[Ejection (sports)|sent off]] for two bookable offences on the penultimate match of the campaign, in a 4–0 defeat by [[S.C. Farense|Farense]] at the [[Estádio de São Luís]] on 25 May.<ref>{{cite web|title=ForaDeJogo.net – Farense 4 – 0 Marco // Liga de Honra|url=https://www.foradejogo.net/match.php?match=200315400113305|website=ForaDeJogo|access-date=19 March 2017}}</ref>

He then joined [[Primeira Liga]] club [[F.C. Paços de Ferreira|Paços de Ferreira]]. He made his debut in the top flight in a 1–0 defeat by [[C.S. Marítimo|Marítimo]] at the [[Estádio da Mata Real]] on 13 September 2003.<ref>{{cite web|title=ForaDeJogo.net – Paços de Ferreira 0 – 1 Marítimo // Superliga Galp Energia|url=https://www.foradejogo.net/match.php?match=200415400010403|website=ForaDeJogo|access-date=19 March 2017}}</ref> He played one further game for the "Beavers" before he followed [[Manager (association football)|manager]] [[José Manuel Gomes]] to return to the Segunda Liga to play for [[C.D. Aves|Aves]]. He played 14 games for Aves in the second half of the [[2003–04 Segunda Liga|2003–04]] season and was sent off on the final day of the campaign after being shown two yellow cards in a 3–0 loss to [[S.C. Covilhã|Sporting Covilhã]] at the [[Estádio do CD Aves]] on 9 May.<ref>{{cite web|title=ForaDeJogo.net – Aves 0 – 3 Sp. Covilhã // Liga de Honra|url=https://www.foradejogo.net/match.php?match=200415400113407|website=ForaDeJogo|access-date=19 March 2017}}</ref> He went on to train with Primeira Liga side [[U.D. Leiria|União de Leiria]], though did not make a competitive appearance for the club.<ref>{{cite news|title=Lokomotiv contrata Bikey – UEFA.com|url=https://pt.uefa.com/news-media/news/01aa-0e6cd282374a-576d0ee53592-1000--lokomotiv-contrata-bikey/|access-date=19 March 2017|work=[[UEFA]]|date=20 June 2005|language=pt}}</ref>

===Russia===
Bikey moved to [[Russia]] to join [[Russian Premier League|Premier League]] club [[FC Shinnik Yaroslavl|Shinnik Yaroslavl]]. He scored one goal in 11 league games for [[Oleg Dolmatov]]'s "Black-Blues". His performances attracted the attention of [[FC Lokomotiv Moscow|Lokomotiv Moscow]] [[head coach]] [[Vladimir Eshtrekov]], who signed him in July 2005. Lokomotiv ended the [[2005 Russian Premier League|2005]] season in third place after finishing behind runners-up [[FC Spartak Moscow|Spartak Moscow]] on matches won. He played for the club in the qualification stages of the [[UEFA Champions League]], and was sent off in the competition as they were knocked out by [[Austria]]n side [[SK Rapid Wien|Rapid Wien]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Rapid Wien vs. Lokomotiv Moskva – 10 August 2005 – Soccerway|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2005/08/10/europe/uefa-champions-league/sk-rapid-wien/fk-lokomotiv-moscow/306372/|website=au.soccerway.com|access-date=19 March 2017|language=en}}</ref> Lokomotiv dropped into the [[UEFA Europa League]], and Bikey played for the club as they were knocked out by Spanish side [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] in the Round of 32.<ref>{{cite web|title=Sevilla vs. Lokomotiv Moskva – 23 February 2006 – Soccerway|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2006/02/23/europe/uefa-cup/sevilla-futbol-club/fk-lokomotiv-moscow/330941/?ICID=PL_MS_06|website=au.soccerway.com|access-date=19 March 2017|language=en}}</ref> Bikey featured in five league games in the early part of the [[2006 Russian Premier League|2006]] season. He was popular with supporters yet struggled to find a common ground with most of the teammates, and perceived himself as [[Racism in Russia|targeted for racist abuse]] to the extent that he felt it necessary to carry a gun whilst out in [[Moscow]] to protect himself from racist gangs.<ref>{{cite news|last1=White|first1=Duncan|title=Andrey Bikey: Why I carried a gun in Moscow|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/2300751/Andrey-Bikey-Why-I-carried-a-gun-in-Moscow.html|access-date=18 March 2017|work=The Telegraph|date=18 May 2008|language=en}}</ref> He was allowed to leave by head coach [[Slavoljub Muslin]] in August 2006, who said "he is a good player, he just doesn’t fit into our team".<ref>{{cite news|title=Royals give trial to Cameroon defender|url=http://www.getreading.co.uk/sport/other-sport/royals-give-trial-cameroon-defender-4261330|access-date=21 March 2017|work=getreading|date=2 August 2006}}</ref>

[[File:André Bikey.png|thumb|left|150px|Bikey playing for [[Reading F.C.|Reading]] in 2008]]

===Reading===
Bikey joined English [[Premier League]] club [[Reading F.C.|Reading]] for an initial trial period during their pre-season trip to [[Sweden]] in 2006, where he impressed manager [[Steve Coppell]] despite being sent off in his final trial match for head-butting an [[Örgryte IS]] player.<ref>{{cite news|title=Bikey sent off in headbutt shame|url=http://www.getreading.co.uk/sport/other-sport/bikey-sent-headbutt-shame-4261355|access-date=19 March 2017|work=getreading|date=8 August 2006}}</ref> After much negotiation with Lokomotiv, a season-long loan deal was agreed on 26 August 2006, giving Reading the option to purchase the player at the end of the loan.<ref>{{cite news|title=Reading make Bikey loan capture|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/r/reading/5241928.stm|access-date=18 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=11 August 2006}}</ref> He was sent off for receiving two yellow cards in only his second Premier League appearance, after pulling [[Didier Drogba]]'s shirt in a 1–0 defeat to [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] at the [[Madejski Stadium]] on 14 October.<ref>{{cite news|title=Reading 0–1 Chelsea|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/5415980.stm|access-date=19 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=14 October 2006}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club in his return to action 11 days later, as Reading were knocked out of the [[EFL Cup|League Cup]] after being beaten 4–3 by [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] at [[Anfield]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Liverpool 4–3 Reading|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/league_cup/6072612.stm|access-date=19 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=25 October 2006}}</ref> He expressed a desire to obtain a permanent deal,<ref>{{cite news|title=Bikey targets new deal with Royals |url=http://www.getreading.co.uk/sport/readingfc/2007/2007972/bikey_targets_new_deal_with_royals |work=[[Reading Evening Post]] |date=22 February 2007 |access-date=25 February 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070302083435/http://www.getreading.co.uk/sport/readingfc/2007/2007972/bikey_targets_new_deal_with_royals |archive-date=2 March 2007 |url-status=live}}</ref> and following improving performances, it was announced on 24 April 2007 that Bikey had signed a three-year [[Association football contracts|contract]] with Reading for a [[Transfer (association football)|transfer]] fee in excess of £1 million.<ref>{{cite news|title=Bikey impresses at Reading|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/africa/6368685.stm|access-date=18 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=16 February 2007}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Bikey pens permanent Reading deal|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/r/reading/6587145.stm|access-date=18 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=24 April 2007}}</ref>

Bikey scored his first league goal for Reading in a 2–1 home defeat to Chelsea on 15 August 2007, which he celebrated with a triple somersault.<ref>{{cite news | title=Reading 1–2 Chelsea | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/6941811.stm | work=[[BBC Sport]] | date=15 August 2007 | access-date=22 March 2008}}</ref> He scored two more goals in a 2–1 home win over [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] on 22 March.<ref>{{cite news | title=Reading 2–1 Birmingham | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/7298218.stm | work=BBC Sport | date=22 March 2008 | access-date=22 March 2008| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080325005515/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/7298218.stm| archive-date= 25 March 2008 | url-status=live}}</ref> He ended the [[2007–08 Reading F.C. season|2007–08]] season with 24 appearances to his name. Still, he was unable to prevent the "Royals" from being [[promotion and relegation|relegated]]. Speaking in September 2008, Coppell bemoaned the fact that Bikey's international commitments had left him only able to train with the club for six days within three months.<ref>{{cite news|title=Coppell reveals Bikey frustration|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/r/reading/7616391.stm|access-date=18 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=15 September 2008}}</ref> He scored three goals in 25 [[EFL Championship|Championship]] games during the [[2008–09 Reading F.C. season|2008–09]] campaign as Reading qualified for the [[English Football League play-offs|play-offs]]. However, he was sent off for stamping on [[Robbie Blake]] during the play-off semi-final first leg at [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] on 9 May, having earlier conceded the winning [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty]] taken by [[Graham Alexander]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Defender Bikey sorry for red card|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/r/reading/8044259.stm|access-date=18 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=11 May 2009}}</ref> He aggravated the situation by ripping off his shirt and stamping around the [[Football pitch|pitch]], resulting in the extension of his ban to five games and a charge for improper conduct.<ref>{{cite news|title=FA hits Bikey with conduct charge|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/r/reading/8047869.stm|access-date=18 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=13 May 2009}}</ref>

===Burnley===
Having beaten Reading in the play-offs, Burnley went on to win [[Promotion and relegation|promotion]] into the Premier League, and manager [[Owen Coyle]] signed Bikey to a three-year deal on 18 August 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/b/burnley/8206870.stm|title=Bikey completes move to Burnley |date=18 August 2009|work=BBC Sport|access-date=18 August 2009| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20090818101456/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/b/burnley/8206870.stm| archive-date= 18 August 2009 | url-status=live}}</ref> The fee was undisclosed, but was reported as being around £2.8 million.<ref>{{cite news|title=Burnley sign Bikey from Reading|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/burnley-sign-bikey-from-reading-1773610.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220507/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/burnley-sign-bikey-from-reading-1773610.html |archive-date=7 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|access-date=19 March 2017|work=The Independent|date=18 August 2009}}{{cbignore}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the "Clarets" in a 2–1 win over Birmingham City at [[Turf Moor]] on 3 October.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Sanghera|first1=Mandeep|title=Burnley 2–1 Birmingham|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/8281481.stm|access-date=19 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=3 October 2009}}</ref> He ended the [[2009–10 Burnley F.C. season|2009–10]] season with 31 appearances to his name, playing mostly in midfield, as Burnley were relegated to the Championship. Speaking in August 2010, manager [[Brian Laws]] said that Bikey would be played at centre-half as he was more comfortable there and "could be one of outstanding centre halves in the division".<ref>{{cite news|last1=Geldard|first1=Suzanne|title=Bikey is a giant, says Burnley boss Laws|url=http://www.lancashiretelegraph.co.uk/sport/8345279.display/|access-date=19 March 2017|work=Lancashire Telegraph|date=21 August 2010|language=en}}</ref> Laws reportedly turned down an approach for Bikey from "a major European club" on transfer deadline day.<ref>{{cite news|title=Laws turned down Bikey bid|url=http://www.skysports.com/football/news/11708/6356019/laws-turned-down-bikey-bid|access-date=19 March 2017|work=Sky Sports|date=3 September 2010|language=en}}</ref> Bikey went on to score two goals in 30 appearances across the [[2010–11 Burnley F.C. season|2010–11]] campaign.

He was dropped by manager [[Eddie Howe]] at the start of the [[2011–12 Burnley F.C. season|2011–12]] season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Andre Amougou pleased with Burnley first team return|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14999565|access-date=19 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=21 September 2011}}</ref> On 22 March, he secured a loan move to Championship rivals [[Bristol City F.C.|Bristol City]] until the end of [[2011–12 Bristol City F.C. season|the season]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Bristol City sign Hogan Ephraim, Andre Amougou & Dekel Keinan|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17480345|access-date=19 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=22 March 2012}}</ref> Manager [[Derek McInnes]] said he was "delighted" with his performances, and Bikey played in seven of the "Robins" last eight fixtures, in which City remained unbeaten, to help the club retain their Championship status.<ref>{{cite news|title=Bristol City manager Derek McInnes pleased with the impact made by loan signings|url=http://www.bristolpost.co.uk/bristol-city-manager-derek-mcinnes-pleased-impact/story-15634037-detail/story.html|access-date=19 March 2017|work=Bristol Post|date=27 March 2012|language=en}}</ref> However, after returning from [[Ashton Gate (stadium)|Ashton Gate]] to Burnley he learned that he would be released upon the expiry of his contract.<ref>{{cite news|title=Burnley release defender Clarke Carlisle|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/18120327|access-date=19 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=18 May 2012}}</ref>

===Middlesbrough===
On 11 September 2012, Bikey signed for Middlesbrough on a [[Free transfer (association football)|free transfer]] after impressing manager [[Tony Mowbray]] on trial, who wanted cover for injured [[Captain (association football)|captain]] [[Rhys Williams (soccer, born 1988)|Rhys Williams]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Cameroon defender Andre Bikey joins Middlesbrough|url=http://www.gazettelive.co.uk/news/local-news/cameroon-defender-andre-bikey-joins-3670441|access-date=18 March 2017|work=Gazette Live|date=12 September 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Middlesbrough captain Rhys Williams undergoes ankle surgery|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19573896|access-date=18 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=12 September 2012}}</ref> He made his debut in a 2–0 home win over [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]] four days later. Mowbray praised him after the match.<ref>{{cite news|title=Middlesbrough: Andre Bikey debut impresses Tony Mowbray|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19624343|access-date=18 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=17 September 2012}}</ref> He scored his first goal for "Boro" with a [[Header (association football)|header]] in a 4–1 defeat away to [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19554081|title=Blackpool 4 – 1 Middlesbrough|publisher=[[BBC]]|date=18 September 2012 |access-date=16 September 2013}}</ref> He made 37 appearances throughout the [[2012–13 Middlesbrough F.C. season|2012–13]] season, but left the [[Riverside Stadium]] after he was released in the summer.<ref>{{cite news|title=Middlesbrough consider Dean Whitehead contract offer|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23005235|access-date=18 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=21 June 2013}}</ref>

===Later career===
In July 2013, he trained with the Spanish [[Segunda División]] team [[CE Sabadell FC|Sabadell]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Sanchez|first1=Jordi|title=Salamero sigue interesado en André Bikey|url=http://www.mundodeportivo.com/20130728/futbol/liga-segunda-division/sabadell-quiere-fichar-camerunes-andre-bikey_54378172335.html|access-date=19 March 2017|work=Mundo Deportivo|date=28 July 2013}}</ref> On 16 September 2013, Bikey signed a one-year contract with [[Greece|Greek]] [[Super League Greece|Super League]] side [[Panetolikos F.C.|Panetolikos]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Cameroonian defender Andre Bikey joins Greek side Panetolikos|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/24110007|access-date=18 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=16 September 2013}}</ref> On 10 November, he scored both goals in the "Canaries" 2–1 win over [[Levadiakos F.C.|Levadiakos]] at [[Panetolikos Stadium]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Panaitolikos vs. Levadiakos – 10 November 2013 – Soccerway|url=https://int.soccerway.com/matches/2013/11/10/greece/super-league/panaitolikos-agrinio/levadiakos-fc/1523748/|website=uk.soccerway.com|access-date=19 March 2017|language=en}}</ref> He made a total of 26 appearances for Panetolikos over the course of the [[2013–14 Super League Greece|2013–14]] season.

In July 2014, Bikey returned to England to sign for Championship side [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] on a two-year contract after impressing manager [[Bob Peeters]] on trial.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Charlton complete signing of André Bikey |url=http://www.cafc.co.uk/news/article/20140709-andre-bikey-1731260.aspx |work=Charlton Athletic FC |date=9 July 2014 |access-date=9 July 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140712000921/http://www.cafc.co.uk/news/article/20140709-andre-bikey-1731260.aspx |archive-date=12 July 2014 |url-status=dead}}</ref> He scored his first and only goal for Charlton in a 1–1 draw with [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] at [[The Valley (London)|The Valley]] on 16 September.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/29120664| title=Charlton 1–1 Wolves | work=BBC Sport | date=15 September 2014 | publisher=BBC| access-date=2 September 2015}}</ref> He featured 34 times for the "Addicks" in the [[2014–15 Charlton Athletic F.C. season|2014–15]] season. Still, he was a peripheral figure after [[Guy Luzon]] took charge in January.<ref>{{cite news|title=Andre Bikey and Loic Nego leave Charlton Athletic|url=http://www.skysports.com/app/transfer/news/12691/9973691/andre-bikey-and-loic-nego-leave-charlton-athletic|access-date=21 March 2017|work=Sky Sports|date=31 August 2015|language=en}}</ref> On 31 August 2015, Bikey's contract was cancelled by mutual consent.<ref>{{Cite news |title=André Bikey-Amougou leaves Charlton |url=http://www.cafc.co.uk/news/article/charlton-athletic-cancel-contract-of-andre-bikey-amougou-2658632.aspx? |publisher=Charlton Athletic FC |date=31 August 2015 |access-date=31 August 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150831211537/http://www.cafc.co.uk/news/article/charlton-athletic-cancel-contract-of-andre-bikey-amougou-2658632.aspx |archive-date=31 August 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

In October 2015, Bikey signed for [[Indian Super League]] team [[NorthEast United FC|NorthEast United]] as a replacement for the injured [[Miguel Garcia (Portuguese footballer)|Miguel Garcia]].<ref name="man m">{{cite news|last1=Vickers|first1=Anthony|title=Watch man mountain Andre Bikey's somersault goal celebration|url=http://www.gazettelive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/watch-andre-bikey-celebration-prompted-11172883|access-date=18 March 2017|work=Gazette Live|date=12 April 2016}}</ref> He featured nine times during the [[2015 Indian Super League|2015]] season, scoring one goal, as [[César Farías]]'s "Highlanders" posted a fifth-place finish.<ref name="man m"/> In July 2016, Bikey signed for fellow Indian Super League side [[FC Pune City]] after being signed by [[Antonio López Habas]].<ref>{{cite web|title=FC Pune City rope in Bruno Arias and Andre Bikey|url=http://indianexpress.com/article/sports/football/fc-pune-city-rope-in-bruno-arias-and-andre-bikey-2936969/|work=The Indian Express|access-date=27 July 2016|date=26 July 2016}}</ref> However, he was unable to feature for the club due to injury.<ref>{{cite news|title=ISL 2016: FC Pune City coach Antonio Lopez Habas focuses on the future after disappointing season - Goal.com|url=http://www.goal.com/en-india/news/7083/isl/2016/12/01/30055102/isl-2016-fc-pune-city-coach-antonio-lopez-habas-focuses-on|access-date=19 March 2017|work=Goal.com|date=1 December 2016|language=en-IN}}</ref>

On 17 March 2017, Bikey once again returned to England and signed for [[EFL League One]] side [[Port Vale F.C.|Port Vale]] on a deal until the end of the [[2016–17 Port Vale F.C. season|2016–17]] season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Andre Bikey: Former Reading defender signs for Port Vale|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39309840|access-date=18 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=17 March 2017}}</ref> He was signed by [[caretaker manager]] [[Michael Brown (footballer, born 1977)|Michael Brown]] to provide cover for his only two fit centre-halves.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Baggaley|first1=Mike|title=Port Vale sign defender Andre Bikey|url=http://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/port-vale-sign-defender-andre-bikey/story-30211582-detail/story.html|access-date=19 March 2017|work=Stoke Sentinel|date=17 March 2017|language=en}}</ref> Brown emphasized that Bikey was still recovering fitness from a quadriceps injury and that there was no timescale on how soon he would be able to play for the first-team.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Baggaley|first1=Mike|title=Port Vale boss Brown explains Andre Bikey deal and fitness|url=http://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/port-vale-boss-michael-brown-explains-andre-bikey-deal/story-30215897-detail/story.html|access-date=20 March 2017|work=Stoke Sentinel|date=20 March 2017|language=en}}</ref> However, injury trouble with [[Remie Streete]] meant Bikey was forced to play despite struggling with fitness and hamstring problems of his own, and Bikey was in fact one of the "Valiants" better players towards the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Baggaley|first1=Mike|title=Port Vale: Michael Brown so impressed with Andre Bikey|url=http://www.stokesentinel.co.uk/oxford-v-port-vale-brown-so-impressed-with-bikey/story-30274351-detail/story.html|access-date=17 April 2017|work=Stoke Sentinel|date=17 April 2017|language=en}}</ref>

On 29 August 2017, Bikey signed with newly formed Indian Super League side [[Jamshedpur FC|Jamshedpur]] after being recruited by former Reading manager Steve Coppell.<ref>{{cite news|title=Jamshedpur FC sign Cameroonian defender Bikey – Times of India|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/indian-super-league/top-stories/jamshedpur-fc-sign-cameroonian-defender-bikey/articleshow/60279242.cms|access-date=29 August 2017|work=The Times of India|date=29 August 2017}}</ref> On 18 August 2018, he joined Steve Coppell at Indian Super League rivals [[ATK (football club)|ATK]].<ref>{{cite web |title=ATK rope in Cameroon defender Andre Bikey |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/indian-super-league/top-stories/atk-rope-in-cameroon-defender-andre-bikey/articleshow/65451719.cms |work=The Times of India|access-date=18 August 2018 |date=18 August 2018}}</ref> He played two [[Tercera División]] games for [[CF Igualada]] in the [[Tercera División|2019–20]] season.<ref name="Soccerway"/>

==International career==
Bikey was named by head coach [[Artur Jorge (footballer, born 1946)|Artur Jorge]] in the [[Cameroon national football team|Cameroon]] squad for the [[2006 Africa Cup of Nations]] in [[Egypt]], and won his first [[Cap (sport)|cap]] after coming on as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for [[Raymond Kalla]] in a 2–0 win over [[Togo national football team|Togo]] in a group stage game at [[Cairo]]'s [[Cairo Military Academy Stadium|Military Academy Stadium]] on 25 January.<ref>{{cite news|title=Atouba makes Nations Cup U-turn|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/africa/4599510.stm|access-date=21 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=10 January 2006}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Clockwatch: Cameroon 2–0 Togo|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/africa/4646726.stm|access-date=19 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=25 January 2006}}</ref> He went on to play in the quarter-finals, and converted his penalty in the shoot-out defeat to the [[Ivory Coast national football team|Ivory Coast]] on 4 February.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Copnall|first1=James|title=Cameroon 1–1 Ivory Coast|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/africa/4675316.stm|access-date=19 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=4 February 2006}}</ref> He was dropped by new coach [[Arie Haan]] after the tournament, and then turned down a call-up under [[Jules Nyongha]] in March 2007.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Etonge|first1=Martin|title=Cameroon recall Wome|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/africa/5370370.stm|access-date=21 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=22 September 2006}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Duo turn down Cameroon call-up|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/africa/6454959.stm|access-date=21 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=15 March 2007}}</ref>

He was named by [[Otto Pfister]] in Cameroon's squad for the [[2008 Africa Cup of Nations]] in [[Ghana]].<ref>{{cite news | date=31 December 2007 | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/africa/7166292.stm|first=Martin|last= Etonge | title=Cameroon cancel Kenya camp | work=BBC Sport | access-date=1 January 2008| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080103101307/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/africa/7166292.stm| archive-date= 3 January 2008|url-status=live}}</ref> On 31 February, he was sent off in the semi-final win over [[Ghana national football team|Ghana]] after a bizarre incident where he pushed a Ghanaian stretcher bearer in the dying seconds of the match.<ref>{{cite news | date=8 February 2008 | url=http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/sport/football/article3334382.ece | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604181252/http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/sport/football/article3334382.ece | url-status=dead | archive-date=4 June 2011 | title=André Bikey to miss final after shove | work=[[The Times]] | access-date=8 February 2008 | location=London}}</ref> The medic in question, Samuel Ashia, said that "It was very forceful, and I landed badly. It didn’t hurt at the time but the next day my head ached and the area around my waist did, too... he hasn't apologised and I will be happy when he does, because no player should do that."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/africa/7237636.stm|title=Bikey yet to say sorry, says medic|work=BBC Sport|date=10 February 2008|first=Piers|last=Edwards}}</ref> Bikey was banned from [[2008 Africa Cup of Nations final|the final]] and Cameroon were fined US$5,000 by the [[Confederation of African Football|CAF]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccerlens.com/andre-bikey-acn-08-red-card/5747/|title=André Bikey Attacks Medic And Misses ACN 08 final – Was He Provoked Or Did He Lose His Head?|publisher=SoccerLens|date=10 February 2008|first=Steve|last=Amoia}}</ref> [[Egypt national football team|Egypt]] went on to beat Cameroon in the final.{{citation needed|date=July 2025}}

He scored his first and only international goal in a 3–0 victory over [[Mauritius national football team|Mauritius]] in a [[2010 FIFA World Cup qualification (CAF)|World Cup qualification]] match in [[Curepipe]] on 8 June 2008.<ref>{{cite news|title=Cameroon extend lead in Group 1|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/africa/7441766.stm|access-date=19 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=8 June 2008}}</ref> He was named in [[Football at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's team squads|Cameroon's squad]] for the [[Football at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2008 Summer Olympics]] in [[Beijing]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Olympic sides in Hong Kong invite|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/africa/7472090.stm|access-date=18 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=24 June 2008}}</ref> He played in all three group games as well as the quarter-final, where Cameroon were beaten 2–0 by [[Brazil national under-23 football team|Brazil]] in [[Overtime (sports)|extra time]] at the [[Shenyang Olympic Sports Center Stadium]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Olympic Football Tournaments Beijing 2008 – Brazil 2:0 a.e.t. Cameroon – Report |url=https://www.fifa.com/tournaments/archive/mensolympic/beijing2008/matches/round=250022/match=300051811/report.html|access-date=19 March 2017|work=FIFA.com}}</ref>

He was named in the squad for the [[2010 Africa Cup of Nations]] in [[Angola]], and played in Cameroon's 3–1 extra-time defeat to Egypt at the [[Estádio Nacional de Ombaka]] in the quarter-finals on 25 January.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Steinberg|first1=Jacob|title=Ahmed Hassan's controversial strike helps Egypt past sloppy Cameroon|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2010/jan/25/egypt-cameroon-africa-cup-of-nations|access-date=19 March 2017|work=The Guardian|date=25 January 2010}}</ref> However, he was benched for much of the tournament by [[Paul Le Guen]] and was not named in the squad for the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite news|title=BBC Sport – Football – Cameroon coach Paul Le Guen sends warning to players|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/africa/8481085.stm|access-date=21 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=26 January 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=BBC Sport – Football – Cameroon set to appoint new coach|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/africa/8882127.stm|access-date=18 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=3 August 2010}}</ref> He was recalled by new head coach [[Javier Clemente]] and won the last of his 25 caps in a 3–0 [[Exhibition game|friendly]] victory over [[Poland national football team|Poland]] on 11 August 2010.<ref>{{cite news|title=Andrew Bikey in the form of his life for Burnley FC|url=http://www.burnleyexpress.net/sport/football/clarets/andrew-bikey-in-the-form-of-his-life-for-burnley-fc-1-2226437|access-date=21 March 2017|work=Burnley Express|date=13 September 2010|language=en}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
On 27 July 2020, Bikey was named [[José Manuel Gomes|José Gomes]]' assistant at Spanish [[Segunda División]] side [[UD Almería]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.getreading.co.uk/sport/football/transfer-news/ex-reading-fc-boss-jose-18676450|title=Ex Reading FC boss Jose Gomes lands third job in nine months|publisher=Berkshire Live|date=28 July 2020|access-date=29 July 2020}}</ref> He joined Gomes again in 2022 to be his assistant at rival Segunda División side [[SD Ponferradina]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Ilusión renovada, pocas caras nuevas y un par de ausencias para empeza |url=https://www.lanuevacronica.com/ilusion-renovada-pocas-caras-nuevas-y-un-par-de-ausencias-para-empezar-a-trabajar |access-date=26 July 2022 |work=La Nueva Crónica: Diario leonés de información general |date=7 July 2022 |language=es}}</ref> He joined Egyptian club [[Zamalek SC|Zamalek]] as a coach in 2024, three months before they lifted the [[CAF Confederations Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Ngwa |first1=Lesley |title=André Bikey wins first trophy as Zamalek coach |url=https://kick442.com/andre-bikey-wins-first-trophy-as-zamalek-coach/ |access-date=10 June 2024 |work=KICK442 Sport News |date=20 May 2024}}</ref>

==Style of play==
Primarily a [[Defender (association football)|defender]], he could also play in [[midfielder|midfield]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Bikey pleased with new position|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/b/burnley/8288829.stm|access-date=18 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=3 October 2009}}</ref> He had great strength and athleticism, as well as good technical ability.<ref>{{cite news|title=Middlesbrough sign Cameroon defender Andre Bikey|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19561652|access-date=18 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=11 September 2012}}</ref> He was described by the ''Middlesbrough Gazette'' as an "absolute monster, a physically imposing hulk with a massive turning circle who did a solid if sometimes erratic job at Boro but was always worth at least one heart-stopping moment of madness per game".<ref name="man m"/> He [[Goal celebration|celebrated his goals]] with a [[hat-trick]] of [[somersault]]s.<ref>{{cite web|title=Andre Bikey|url=http://www.readingfc.co.uk/stats/madejski-men/andre-bikey/|website=www.readingfc.co.uk|access-date=19 March 2017|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170320053347/http://www.readingfc.co.uk/stats/madejski-men/andre-bikey/|archive-date=20 March 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In April 2007, it was reported that Bikey had a Portuguese wife and was a fan of British food and comedy, particularly [[Mr. Bean]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Bikey embraces English culture|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/africa/6567053.stm|access-date=18 March 2017|work=BBC Sport|date=18 April 2007}}</ref>

'''Andrei Agius''' (born 12 August 1986) is a Maltese [[association football|footballer]] who is currently employed as head coach at [[Hibernians F.C.|Hibernians]].

==Club career==
===Early career===
Agius began his career with [[St. Lucia F.C.|Santa Lucija]], his hometown club, before joining the youth nursery of [[Sliema Wanderers F.C.|Sliema Wanderers]], the most decorated club in Maltese football.

In July 2003, Agius was part of the Sliema Wanderers under-16 squad that participated in the Nikola Kotkov Tournament, organised by the Academy Lokomotiv 101.

On 19 December 2003, aged only 17, Agius, who started out as a midfielder, made his senior debut for Sliema Wanderers in a Premier League match against [[Floriana F.C.|Floriana]] but his determination to pursue a professional career meant that, just weeks after his first senior appearance, the then teenage defender left for his first overseas challenge.

=== Serbia and Montenegro ===
Agius headed to Serbia and Montenegro to join first-division club [[FK Zemun|Zemun]] on an initial six-month contract but played mostly for Zemun's youth team, scoring two goals in the process.

=== Italy ===
In the summer of 2004, Agius moved to Italy after catching the eye of Sicilian club [[Sporting Mascalucia]] who offered him a contract. In his first season with Sport Club Mascalucia, Agius scored three goals and was voted as the most promising midfielder in the Italy's regional championship.

Following another positive season with Mascalucia, Agius secured a contract with then [[Serie A]] club [[F.C. Messina Peloro|Messina]], where he became a regular in the reserve squad. In his first season with Messina, Agius switched from midfield to defence.

In February 2006, Agius featured in the Torneo Mondiale di Calcio Coppa Carnevale and scored two goals, one against [[U.S. Pistoiese 1921|Pistoiese]] and the other against [[Torino F.C.|Torino]]. In May 2006, Agius was among the Messina substitutes for the Serie A match against [[Empoli F.C.|Empoli]].

After his initial one-year spell with Messina, Agius was loaned to Serie C side [[A.C. Martina|Martina]] during the August transfer window in 2006. In season 2006–07, Agius faced intense competition for first-team places from experienced and seasoned players but still managed to make some appearances for Martina in the [[2006–07 Coppa Italia|Coppa Italia]].

In season 2007–08, Agius moved to [[F.C. Igea Virtus Barcellona|Igea Virtus]], regarded as the second team of Messina Calcio. In his first season with Igea Virtus, Agius played 34 league matches and one in the Coppa Italia. His performances with Virtus earned him a four-year contract with Messina in March 2008 but the following summer, financial difficulties forced the Serie B club to file for bankruptcy. Agius was freed from his contractual obligations with the club and rejoined Igea Virtus where he was an automatic choice in their first team.

Later on in the 2009–10 season, Agius signed for Serie C team [[A.S.D. Nuova Cassino 1924|Cassino]] in a co-ownership deal with [[U.S. Salernitana 1919|Salernitana]]. In January 2010, Agius was loaned to [[A.S. Melfi|Melfi]], and eventually signed a two-year contract with the club. A year later, it looked as though Agius was going to sign for Serie B side [[U.S. Triestina Calcio 1918|Triestina]], and also played for the team in a triangular tournament, but nothing came of it.

In January 2011, Agius joined Maltese Premier League club [[Birkirkara F.C.|Birkirkara]] on a short-term loan deal. On 31 August 2011, Agius signed for Italian side [[U.S. Latina Calcio|Latina]], and was part of the squad that won promotion to Serie B as well as winning the [[2012–13 Coppa Italia Lega Pro]]. US Latina's promotion to the second division of Italian football led to a squad overhaul in the summer of 2013 and Agius opted to join Sardinian club [[S.E.F. Torres 1903|Torres]].

=== Return to Malta ===
In the summer of 2014, Agius returned to Malta to join [[Hibernians F.C.|Hibernians]], his hometown club. With his current club he won two [[Maltese Premier League]] titles (in [[2014–15 Maltese Premier League|2014–15]] and [[2016–17 Maltese Premier League|2016–17]]).

Agius was also in the Hibs team that caused a shock by beating Israel's [[Maccabi Tel Aviv F.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] 2–1 in the first leg of their [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League]] second qualifying round tie at the [[Hibernians Stadium]] on 14 July 2015. In 2019, he won the award as [[Maltese Player of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.mfa.com.mt/en/news/news/3922/hibs-defender-agius-named-mfa-footballer-of-the-year.htm|title= Hibs defender Agius named MFA Footballer of the Year|author=<!--Not stated--> |date= 25 May 2019|website= |publisher= Maltese Football Association|access-date= 25 May 2019}}</ref>

== International career ==
Agius earned his first call-up to [[Malta national under-21 football team|Malta's under-21]] squad, then coached by [[Mark Miller (footballer)|Mark Miller]], in August 2003 for a friendly match against [[Italy national under-21 football team|Italy under-21]]. Agius has represented Malta 37 times at under-21 level. In 2005, he formed part of the Malta under-21 team that participated in the [[Football at the 2005 Mediterranean Games|Mediterranean Games]], held in [[Almería]], Spain.

In February 2006, Agius, then aged 19, was named in Malta's senior squad for the biennial Malta International football tournament. The other participating nations were [[Georgia national football team|Georgia]] and [[Moldova national football team|Moldova]].

On 4 June 2021, he played his 100th match for Malta in a 2–1 loss in a friendly match against [[Kosovo national football team|Kosovo]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.independent.com.mt/articles/2021-06-05/football/Friendly-match-Late-defensive-slip-again-lets-Malta-down-6736234074 |title=Friendly match: Late defensive slip again lets Malta down |website=independent.com.mt |date=5 June 2021 }}</ref>

Born in France, he represents the [[DR Congo national football team|DR Congo national team]]. ==Club career== ===Monaco=== Born in [[Meaux]], France, Tisserand began his career at [[INF Clairefontaine]] before leaving for [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]] when he was thirteen.{{cite news|title=Le joueur de Monaco fait rêver les ados de Meaux|url=http://www.leparisien.fr/espace-premium/seine-et-marne-77/le-joueur-de-monaco-fait-rever-les-ados-de-meaux-25-12-2013-3437805.php|publisher=Le Parisien|date=25 December 2013|accessdate=16 April 2017}} In June 2013, he signed his first professional contract with Monaco, having spent four years at the reserve side.{{cite news|title=Monaco : premier contrat professionnel pour M. Tisserand|url=http://www.afrik-foot.com/monaco-premier-contrat-professionnel-pour-m-tisserand|publisher=Afrik-Foot|language=French|date=13 June 2013|accessdate=16 April 2017}} Following this, he was called up by the first team for the pre-season tour with Monaco by manager [[Claudio Ranieri]].{{cite news|title=23 joueurs de l'AS Monaco à la reprise de l'entraînement en Italie|url=http://archives.monacomatin.mc/derniere-minute/23-joueurs-de-las-monaco-a-la-reprise-de-lentrainement-en-italie.1327080.html|publisher=Monaco Matin|language=French|date=1 July 2013|accessdate=16 April 2017}} Ranieri was impressed with his ability in training and took him to the pre-season with the club.{{cite news|title=Nom : Tisserand, prénom : Marcel|url=http://www.football365.fr/nom-tisserand-prenom-marcel-1314561.html|publisher=Football 365|language=French|date=29 July 2013|accessdate=16 April 2017}} Tisserand made his professional debut at 10 August 2013 against [[Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]] in the first [[Ligue 1]] game for AS Monaco in the 2013–14 season.{{cite news|title=Ligue 1 - Falcao a rugi|url=http://www.goal.com/fr/match/bordeaux-vs-monaco/1479048/report?ICID=MP_MS_5|publisher=Goal.com|language=French|date=10 August 2013|accessdate=16 April 2017}} On 5 October 2013, he made his first Monaco start, playing in the [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|left–back]] position, in a 2–1 win over [[AS Saint-Étienne|Saint-Étienne]].{{cite news|title=Ils ont dit...|url=http://www.sport24.com/football/ligue-1/actualites/ils-ont-dit-656590|publisher=Le Figaro|language=French|date=5 October 2013|accessdate=16 April 2017}} On 19 December 2013, he signed a contract extension with the club, keeping him until 2018.{{cite news|title=Marcel Tisserand jusqu'en 2018|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Tisserand-jusqu-en-2018/426456|publisher=L’Equipe|language=French|date=19 December 2013|accessdate=16 April 2017}} However, he struggled in the first team, being relegated to the substitutes bench due to competition from [[Layvin Kurzawa]] and making six appearances in the 2013–14 season. After ending his two–year loan spell at Toulouse, Tisserand returned to Monaco and expressed desire to play in the Monaco's first team in the 2016–17 season.{{cite news|title= Ligue 1 Marcel Tisserand : «M'imposer à Monaco|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Marcel-tisserand-toulouse-la-causerie-de-dupraz-j-en-avais-les-larmes-aux-yeux/682704|publisher=L’Equipe|language=French|date=26 May 2016|accessdate=16 April 2017}} In the 2016–17 season, he only made one appearance for the club, in a 1–0 win over [[FC Nantes|Nantes]] on 20 August 2016.{{cite news|title=L1 (J2) : MÊME AVEC UNE ÉQUIPE B, MONACO ÉTAIT TROP COSTAUD POUR NANTES|url=http://www.football365.fr/l1-j2-meme-equipe-b-monaco-etait-costaud-nantes-2669789.html|publisher=Football 365|language=French|date=20 August 2016|accessdate=16 April 2017}} ====Loan to Lens==== After being told by the club's management that he was allowed to leave the club in the winter transfer window,{{cite news|title=Monaco dégraisse|url=http://sport24.lefigaro.fr/football/transferts/fil-info/monaco-degraisse-673852|publisher=Le Figaro|language=French|date=19 January 2014|accessdate=16 April 2017}} Tisserand joined [[Ligue 2]] side [[RC Lens|Lens]] on loan for the rest of the season on 20 January 2014.{{cite web |url=http://www.rclens.fr/infos_2014/01/20_arrivee_tisserand/index.php |title=Officiel : Marcel Tisserand rejoint le Racing ! |publisher=RC Lens |language=French |date=20 January 2014 |accessdate=16 April 2017 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304040229/http://www.rclens.fr/infos_2014/01/20_arrivee_tisserand/index.php |archivedate=4 March 2016 |url-status=dead }} Upon joining Lens, he expressed hope the move would help him earn a first-team chance at Monaco next season.{{cite news|title=Marcel Tisserand : " Lens, c'est le bon choix "|url=http://www.madeinlens.com/actualite-rclens-football/rc-lens-actualite/16129-marcel-tisserand-lens-c-est-le-bon-choix.html|publisher=Made in Lens|language=French|date=29 January 2014|accessdate=16 April 2017}} Tisserand made his Lens debut on 27 January 2014, playing the full 90 minutes in a 2–1 win over [[AJ Auxerre|Auxerre]].{{cite news|title=Lens en profite, pas Angers|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Lens-en-profite-pas-angers/435855|publisher=L’Equipe|language=French|date=27 January 2014|accessdate=16 April 2017}} On 8 March 2014, he scored his first professional goal in a 1–0 win over [[FC Metz|Metz]].{{cite news|title=Metz 0 – 1 Lens|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Le-choc-pour-lens/447546|publisher=L’Equipe|language=French|date=8 March 2014|accessdate=16 April 2017}} From that moment on, he became a first-team regular under Manager [[Antoine Kombouaré]] for the rest of the season going on to help the club achieve promotion to [[Ligue 2]] (which was later invalidated). Despite setbacks from injury and suspension, Tisserand made a total of twelve appearances for the club, all of which were starts.{{cite news|title=RC Lens - Laval : confirmer malgré les blessés|url=http://www.madeinlens.com/actualite-rclens-football/made-in-lens-actualite-articles/16199-rc-lens-laval-confirmer-malgre-les-blesses.html|publisher=Made in Lens|language=French|date=1 February 2014|accessdate=16 April 2017}}
{{cite news|title=RC Lens - Niort : le RC Lens au révélateur niortais|url=http://www.madeinlens.com/actualite-rclens-football/made-in-lens-actualite-articles/17245-rc-lens-niort-le-rc-lens-au-revelateur-niortais.html|publisher=Made in Lens|language=French|date=12 April 2014|accessdate=16 April 2017}} At the end of the 2013–14 season, the club was keen on signing him on loan for a second time.{{cite news|title=Lens : Tisserand revient en prêt|url=http://www.afrik-foot.com/lens-tisserand-revient-en-pret|publisher=Afrik-Foot|language=French|date=27 June 2014|accessdate=16 April 2017}} However, they did not succeed in re-signing him citing financial problems.{{cite news|title=Areola et Tisserand restent à Lens|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Areola-et-tisserand-restent-a-lens/479841|publisher=L’Equipe|language=French|date=4 July 2014|accessdate=16 April 2017}} ====Loan to Toulouse==== Expecting to be loaned out again,{{cite news|title=Tisserand poursuit à Lens|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Tisserand-poursuit-a-lens/477513|publisher=L’Equipe|language=French|date=26 June 2014|accessdate=16 April 2017}} Tisserand was loaned once again to fellow [[Ligue 1]] side [[Toulouse FC|Toulouse]] in July 2014.{{cite news|title=Officiel: Marcel Tisserand toulousain pour une saison ! |url=http://www.tfc.info/news/1190700/officiel-marcel-tisserand-toulousain-une-saison |work=[[Toulouse FC|tfc.info]] |date=25 July 2014 |accessdate=25 July 2014 |language=fr |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160409073109/http://tfc.info/officiel-marcel-tisserand-toulousain-pour-une-saison |archivedate=9 April 2016 |url-status=live }} At the start of the season, he suffered an injury that ruled him out for several matches.{{cite news|title=Toulouse : Quatre absents contre Nice|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Quatre-absents-contre-nice/488366|publisher=L’Equipe|language=French|date=7 August 2014|accessdate=16 April 2017}} In September, he returned to first-team training{{cite news|title=TFC Retour de Tisserand|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Retour-de-tisserand/501135|publisher=L’Equipe|language=French|date=22 September 2014|accessdate=16 April 2017}} and made his Toulouse debut on 23 September 2014, starting in a 3–0 win over [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]].{{cite news|title= Foot - L1 - 7e j. Toulouse la tient enfin|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Toulouse-la-tient-enfin/501405|publisher=L’Equipe|language=French|date=23 September 2014|accessdate=16 April 2017}} At end of 2014, he suffered a further injury setback{{cite news|title=Ligue 1 TFC Cascade de forfaits|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Cascade-de-forfaits/507773|publisher=L’Equipe|language=French|date=18 October 2014|accessdate=16 April 2017}} and at one point, was ineligible to play against his parent club, Monaco, despite request from Toulouse.{{cite news|title=Toulouse : Tisserand ne jouera pas contre Monaco|url=http://www.football365.fr/toulouse-tisserand-ne-jouera-pas-contre-monaco-2062615.html|publisher=Football 365|language=French|date=4 December 2014|accessdate=16 April 2017}} After returning to the first team, Tisserand provided an assist for [[Aleksandar Pešić]] to score the only goal in 1–0 win against [[Stade de Reims|Reims]] on 31 January 2015.{{cite news|title=Toulouse l'attendait depuis longtemps|url=http://www.football365.fr/toulouse-lattendait-depuis-longtemps-1053971.html|publisher=Football 365|language=French|date=31 January 2015|accessdate=16 April 2017}} In a 3–2 loss against Metz on 4 April 2015, he was sent off for a second bookable offence and served one-match suspension as a result.{{cite news|title=Metz revit, le TFC sombre|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Metz-revit-le-tfc-sombre/548452|publisher=L’Equipe|language=French|date=4 April 2015|accessdate=16 April 2017}} Despite suffering setbacks towards the end of the season,{{cite news|title=Ligue 1 TFC Avec Trejo, sans Ahamada contre Saint-Etienne|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Avec-trejo-sans-ahamada-contre-l-asse/539499|publisher=L’Equipe|language=French|date=27 February 2015|accessdate=16 April 2017}}
{{cite news|title=Ligue 1 TFC Le TFC avec Kana-Biyik et Pesic|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Le-tfc-avec-kana-biyik-et-pesic/555490|publisher=L’Equipe|language=French|date=2 May 2015|accessdate=16 April 2017}} Tisserand went on to make 22 appearances in all competitions in the 2014–15 season. In the 2015–16 season, Monaco manager [[Leonardo Jardim]] stated he was keen on using Tisserand in the first team this season, due to his good performance in the previous season.{{cite news|title=Ligue 1 ASM Leonardo Jardim veut voir Marcel Tisserand|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Leonardo-jardim-veut-voir-marcel-tisserand/570224|publisher=L’Equipe|language=French|date=29 June 2015|accessdate=16 April 2017}} On 21 July 2015, however, Tisserand was loaned out to Toulouse again for the season.{{cite news|title=Foot –Transfert Tisserand de retour à Toulouse|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Marcel-tisserand-de-retour-a-toulouse/575773|publisher=L’Equipe|language=French|date=21 July 2015|accessdate=16 April 2017}} He made his season debut in the opening game of the season, playing as a right–back in a 2–1 win over [[AS Saint-Étienne|Saint-Étienne]].{{cite news|title=Football - Ligue 1 - 1re journée - Toulouse-Saint-Étienne, 17 heures Toulouse voit-il trop grand ?|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Article/Toulouse-voit-il-trop-grand-nbsp/55340|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170416221715/http://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Article/Toulouse-voit-il-trop-grand-nbsp/55340|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 April 2017|publisher=L’Equipe|language=French|date=9 August 2015|accessdate=16 April 2017}} He was sent off for a second bookable offence in the second half of a 3–0 win over [[Troyes AC|Troyes]] on 2 December 2015, and was suspended for two matches.{{cite news|title=Michel Der Zakarian (Nantes) et Betrand Desplat (Guingamp) convoqués devant la commission de discipline|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Stephane-darbion-troyes-et-marcel-tisserand-toulouse-suspendu-deux-matches-ferme/615382/|publisher=L’Equipe|language=French|date=10 December 2015|accessdate=16 April 2017}} On 24 January 2016, Tisserand started against his parent club, Monaco, where he played for 67 minutes, in a 4–0 loss.{{cite news|title=Toulouse avec Machach à Monaco mais sans Kana-Biyik|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Toulouse-avec-machach-a-monaco-mais-sans-kana-biyik/627455/|publisher=L’Equipe|language=French|date=23 January 2016|accessdate=16 April 2017}} He scored his first Toulouse goal on 23 April 2016, in a 3–2 loss against [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]].{{cite news|title= Lyon domine Toulouse (3-2) au terme d'un match fou et prend la 2e place|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Lyon-domine-toulouse-3-2-au-terme-d-un-match-fou-et-prend-la-2e-place/655055|publisher=L’Equipe|language=French|date=23 April 2016|accessdate=16 April 2017}} Having become a first team regular in his second season at the club, Tisserand went on to make 36 appearances scoring once in all competitions. Reflecting on his time at Toulouse, Tisserand credited Manager [[Pascal Dupraz]] for helping the side avoid relegation, where they finished 17th place.{{cite news|title=Marcel Tisserand (Toulouse): "La causerie de Dupraz ? J'en avais les larmes aux yeux"|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Marcel-tisserand-toulouse-la-causerie-de-dupraz-j-en-avais-les-larmes-aux-yeux/682704|publisher=L’Equipe|language=French|date=26 May web|url=http://www.fcingolstadt.de/news/6158-schanzer-machen-das-rennen-marcel-tisserand-wechselt-zum-fci/|title=Schanzer machen das rennen: Marcel Tisserand wechselt zum FCI|language=de|publisher=FC {{cite news|title=Tisserand: Walpurgis im Zwiespalt|url=https://www.kicker.de/tisserand_walpurgis-im-zwiespalt-669743/artikel|publisher=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]]|language=German|date=27 January 2017|access-date=16 April 2017}} Following DR Congo's elimination in the Africa Cup of Nation, he returned to the first team on 11 February 2017, in a 2–0 loss against [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]].{{cite news|title=Bayern zieht den Kopf spät aus der Schlinge|url=https://www.kicker.de/ingolstadt-gegen-bayern-2017-bundesliga-3317429/analyse|publisher=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]]|language=German|date=11 February 2017|access-date=16 April 2017}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.fcingolstadt.de/news/6717-schanzer-unterliegen-bayern-in-letzter-minute/|title=SCHANZER UNTERLIEGEN BAYERN IN LETZTER MINUTE|publisher=FC Ingolstadt 04|language=German|date=11 February 2017|accessdate=22 November 2019|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20191120193720/https://www.fcingolstadt.de/news/6717-schanzer-unterliegen-bayern-in-letzter-minute/|archivedate=20 November 2019|url-status=live}} Following this, Tisserand continued to regain his first team place for the rest of the season.{{cite news|title=Tisserand: Starkes Comeback|url=https://www.donaukurier.de/sport/fussball/fcingolstadt04/fc04-berichte/Rund-Tisserand-Starkes-Comeback;art19158,3324836|publisher=Donaukurier|language=German|date=12 February 2017|accessdate=22 November 2019}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.fcingolstadt.de/news/6895-kittel-und-cohen-schiessen-fci-zum-derbysieg/|title=KITTEL UND COHEN SCHIESSEN FCI ZUM DERBYSIEG|publisher=FC Ingolstadt 04|language=German|date=5 April 2017|accessdate=22 November 2019|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20191120193210/https://www.fcingolstadt.de/news/6895-kittel-und-cohen-schiessen-fci-zum-derbysieg/|archivedate=20 November 2019|url-status=live}} However, FC Ingolstadt 04 was relegated to 2.Bundesliga after drawing 1–1 against [[SC Freiburg]] on 13 May 2017, which he set up a goal for [[Maximilian Philipp]] to score the opener in the game.{{cite web|url=https://www.fcingolstadt.de/news/7053-remis-reicht-nicht-schanzer-verlieren-den-kampf-um-den-klassenerhalt/|title=REMIS REICHT NICHT: SCHANZER VERLIEREN DEN KAMPF UM DEN KLASSENERHALT|publisher=FC Ingolstadt 04|language=German|date=13 May 2017|accessdate=22 November 2019|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20191120193134/https://www.fcingolstadt.de/news/7053-remis-reicht-nicht-schanzer-verlieren-den-kampf-um-den-klassenerhalt/|archivedate=20 November 2019|url-status=live}}
{{cite news|title=Ein Trio sticht heraus|url=https://www.donaukurier.de/sport/fussball/fcingolstadt04/fc04-berichte/Ingolstadt-DKmobil-wochennl212017-Ein-Trio-sticht-heraus;art19158,3394996|publisher=Donaukurier|language=German|date=23 May 2017|accessdate=22 November 2019}} At the end of the 2016–17 season, Tisserand went on to make twenty–nine appearances in all competitions. ===Wolfsburg=== It was announced on 22 August 2017 that [[VfL Wolfsburg|Wolfsburg]] signed Tisserland on a season–long loan deal for the rest of the 2017–18 season.{{cite news|title=Fix: Wolfsburg holt Tisserand als Brooks-Ersatz|url=https://www.kicker.de/fix_wolfsburg-holt-tisserand-als-brooks-ersatz-704441/artikel|publisher=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]]|language=German|date=22 August 2017|access-date=22 November 2019}} It came after when FC Ingolstadt 04 dropped both him and [[Florent Hadergjonaj]] from the first team until the end of August.{{cite web|url=https://www.fcingolstadt.de/news/7305-tisserand-und-hadergjonaj-bis-31-august-2017-freigestellt/|title=TISSERAND UND HADERGJONAJ BIS 31. AUGUST 2017 FREIGESTELLT|publisher=FC Ingolstadt 04|language=German|date=13 August 2017|accessdate=22 November 2019|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20191120192716/https://www.fcingolstadt.de/news/7305-tisserand-und-hadergjonaj-bis-31-august-2017-freigestellt/|archivedate=20 November 2019|url-status=live}} Tisserand made his VfL Wolfsburg debut, starting the whole game, in a 1–0 win over [[Eintracht Frankfurt]] on 26 August 2017.{{cite news|title=Wolfsburg siegt dank Didavi in Frankfurt|url=https://www.kicker.de/frankfurt-gegen-wolfsburg-2017-bundesliga-3827601/analyse|publisher=[[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]]|language=German|date=26 August 2017|access-date=22 November 2019}} However, he suffered a thigh injury that kept him out for two matches and didn't return until on 22 September 2017, starting the whole game, in a 2–2 draw against [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]].{{cite news|title=VfL Wolfsburg: Tisserand und Camacho angeschlagen - Abwehrnot wird noch größer|url=https://www.sportbuzzer.de/artikel/vfl-wolfsburg-tisserand-und-camacho-angeschlagen-abwehrnot-wird-noch-grosser/|publisher=Sport Buzzer|language=German|date=7 September 2017|accessdate=22 November 2019}}

{{in lang|fr}} In March 2016, he was called up to the provisional squad of the senior [[DR Congo national football team|DR Congo national team]]{{cite news|title=RD Congo : Afobe et Tisserand appelés|url=http://www.football365.fr/rd-congo-afobe-et-tisserand-appeles-2423625.html|publisher=Football 365|language=French|date=10 March 2016|accessdate=16 April 2017}} before being dropped due to '''Jean-Louis Leca''' (born 21 September 1985) is a French former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[goalkeeper (association football)|goalkeeper]]. He played for the [[Corsica national football team|Corsica national team]].

==Club career==
Jean-Louis Leca was trained in Corsica. He played his first [[Ligue 1]] game with [[SC Bastia|Bastia]] in the [[2004–05 Ligue 1|2004-05 season]].{{citation needed|date=October 2023}}

He joined [[Valenciennes FC|Valenciennes]] in 2008. He then went back to his former club Bastia. He joined [[AC Ajaccio|Ajaccio]] in 2017, after Bastia filled for bankruptcy.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-10-18 |title=Jean-Louis Leca, gardien du RC Lens, raconte ses identités corse et ch'ti |url=https://www.20minutes.fr/lille/3147363-20211018-ligue-1-si-corse-construit-nord-fait-devenir-homme-raconte-gardien-lensois-jean-louis-leca |access-date=2023-03-02 |website=www.20minutes.fr |language=fr}}</ref>

In July 2018, Leca joined French club [[RC Lens|Lens]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Lens-officialise-le-recrutement-de-jean-louis-leca-et-de-trois-autres-joueurs/908111|title=Lens officialise le recrutement de Jean-Louis Leca et de trois autres joueurs|last=Rédaction|work=L'ÉQUIPE|access-date=23 July 2018|language=fr-FR}}</ref> He played his first game on 27 July 2018 against [[Ligue 2]] club [[US Orléans|Orléans]]. In December 2022, he extended his contract with Lens until 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2022-12-16 |title=RC Lens : Jean-Louis Leca prolonge d’un an |url=https://www.lavoixdunord.fr/1267671/article/2022-12-16/rc-lens-jean-louis-leca-prolonge-d-un |access-date=2023-03-02 |website=La Voix du Nord |language=fr}}</ref> In May 2024, he announced his retirement at the end of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Guilbaud |first=Philippe |date=2024-05-17 |title=RC Lens : Jean-Louis Leca arrête sa carrière |url=https://www.lavoixdunord.fr/1462955/article/2024-05-17/rc-lens-jean-louis-leca-arrete-sa-carriere |access-date=2024-05-22 |website=La Voix du Nord |language=fr}}</ref>

When Leca played for Bastia, he followed a tradition of displaying the [[Flag and coat of arms of Corsica|Corsican flag]] after the final whistle whenever the team won.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2014-10-19 |title=SC Bastia release statement following violent incidents at the Allianz Riviera last night - Get French Football News |url=https://www.getfootballnewsfrance.com/2014/sc-bastia-release-statement-following-violent-incidents-at-the-allianz-riviera-last-night/ |access-date=2026-05-15 |language=en-US}}</ref>
