'''Tamás Kádár''' (born 14 March 1990)<ref name="SW">{{Soccerway|tamas-kadar/87806}}</ref> is a Hungarian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays for [[Nemzeti Bajnokság I]] club [[MTK Budapest FC|MTK Budapest]]. He is a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] and is equally capable at centre-back or left-back. He made his debut for [[Zalaegerszegi TE]] at the age of 16 and has since gone on to win Hungary U-21 honours.

==Club career==

===Zalaegerszeg===
Kádár made his debut for [[Zalaegerszegi TE]] in 2006.<ref name="Kadar on Premier radar">{{cite news | title = Kadar on Premier radar | url = http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11661_2949706,00.html
| publisher = Sky Sports | date = 6 December 2007 | access-date =15 December 2007}}</ref> He was offered trials by [[Premier League]] clubs [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] and [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] in December 2007.<ref name="Kadar on Premier radar"/><ref name="Big Sam eyes Hungarian starlet">{{cite news |title=Big Sam eyes Hungarian starlet
| url = http://www.skysports.com/story/0,19528,11678_2988126,00.html
|publisher=Sky Sports |date = 17 December 2007 |access-date=17 December 2007}}</ref> He made 14 league appearances, four domestic cup appearances and two [[Intertoto Cup]] appearances for Zalaegerszegi TE.

===Newcastle United===
[[File:Kádár Tamás.JPG|thumb|left|150px|Kádár at Zalaegerszeg]]
Kádár's transfer was allowed due to Hungary being within the [[European Union]]. Normally a player must be 18 years old at minimum, but within the European Union players could be transferred at the age of 16.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/mm/document/affederation/administration/status%5ftransfer%5fen%5f25.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070922234650/http://fifa.com/mm/document/affederation/administration/status%5ftransfer%5fen%5f25.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=22 September 2007 |title=FIFA Regulations for the Status and Transfer of Players: Article 19 Protection of Minors |access-date=11 January 2008 |date=18 December 2004 |publisher=FIFA}}</ref>

Local news reports in [[Newcastle upon Tyne|Newcastle]] stated that Kádár had attended a reserve match at Newcastle on 8 January 2008, and would sign for the club in the coming days. Kádár became the 3rd youngster to sign for Newcastle in the January transfer window following the signings of [[Ben Tozer]] and [[Wesley Ngo Baheng]]. After some hold-ups as a result of [[Sam Allardyce]]'s sacking, the deal was confirmed on 18 January, the same day that [[Kevin Keegan]] was unveiled to the press for his second stint as manager.

During the [[Premier League 2008–09|2008–09 season]], Kádár was mostly plying his trade in the reserves but appeared on the bench as an unused substitute for Newcastle's home league match with [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] and the FA Cup 3rd round game with [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]].

On 21 January 2009, he suffered a broken leg in a reserve match against [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]], ruling him out for six months.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://icnewcastle.icnetwork.co.uk/newcastleunited/sundaysun//tm_headline=tamas-kadar-out-for-months-after-leg-break&method=full&objectid=22752955&siteid=72703-name_page.html |title=Tamas Kadar out for months after leg break |date=22 January 2009 |access-date=22 January 2009 |publisher=Newcastle.co.uk}}</ref>

On 11 July 2009, he returned to action for Newcastle United, helping in their victory 3–0 over [[Shamrock Rovers F.C.|Shamrock Rovers]]. This was Newcastle's first pre-season match of the 2009–10 season. He made his full first team debut in the 4–3 victory over [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]] in the [[Football League Cup|League Cup]] in August, before making his league debut on 31 August as part of a 1–0 home win against [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]]. Although behind [[Steven Taylor (footballer)|Steven Taylor]] and [[Fabricio Coloccini]] in the pecking order, he has turned in some strong performances whenever new manager [[Chris Hughton]] played him, especially when Taylor and Coloccini were out injured during various times of the season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Impressive Kadar is very happy with life on Tyneside|url=http://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/sport/4829620.Impressive_Kadar_is_very_happy_with_life_on_Tyneside/|publisher=[[Northern Echo]]|date=4 January 2010}}</ref> In the 2010–2011 season, he was given a chance in the opening rounds of the [[Football League Cup|League Cup]] playing in central defence for their round two clash with minnows [[Accrington Stanley]]. Newcastle won 3-2 thanks to goals from [[Peter Lovenkrands]], [[Shola Ameobi]] and [[Ryan Taylor (footballer born 1984)|Ryan Taylor]]. In the [[2011–12 Premier League|2011–12]] season of the [[Premier League]] Kádár became close to the first squad after the injuries of Fabricio Coloccini and Steven Taylor.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tynetime.com/2011/12/04/tamas-kadar-has-a-huge-chance-to-revive-his-newcastle-united-career/|title=Tamás Kádár has a huge chance to revive his Newcastle United career|date=4 December 2011 |access-date=7 December 2011 |publisher=tynetime.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/newcastle-united/nufc-news//tm_headline=tamas-kadar-in-chance-to-save-nufc-career%26method=full%26objectid=29909000%26siteid=72703-name_page.html|title=Tamas Kadar in chance to save NUFC career|date=5 December 2011 |access-date=7 December 2011 |publisher=chroniclelive.co.uk}}</ref>

He was released by Newcastle United on 1 June 2012.<ref name="Magpies Announce Retained List">{{cite web | url=http://www.nufc.co.uk/articles/20120601/magpies-announce-retained-list_2281670_2795339 | title=Magpies Announce Retained List | date=1 June 2012 | publisher=Newcastle United | access-date=1 June 2012}}</ref>

====Huddersfield Town (loan)====
On 10 January 2011, Kádár signed on loan at [[Football League One]] side [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]], managed by [[Lee Clark (footballer)|Lee Clark]], who was a coach at Newcastle, when he originally signed for the Magpies.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nufc.co.uk/articles/20110111/terriers-for-tamas_2281670_2263151 |title=Terriers For Tamas |date=11 January 2011 |access-date=11 January 2011 |publisher=nufc.co.uk |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110128164110/http://www.nufc.co.uk/articles/20110111/terriers-for-tamas_2281670_2263151 |archive-date=28 January 2011 |df=dmy-all }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/h/huddersfield_town/9357067.stm|title=Huddersfield Town sign Newcastle defender Tamas Kadar|date=11 January 2011 |access-date=11 January 2011 |publisher=bbc.co.uk }}</ref> He made his debut in the 3–2 win over [[Plymouth Argyle F.C.|Plymouth Argyle]] at the [[Galpharm Stadium]], the following day.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_div_2/9354110.stm|title=Huddersfield 3-2 Plymouth|date=5 November 2017|access-date=5 November 2017|via=news.bbc.co.uk}}</ref> Following an injury picked up in the game at [[Walsall F.C.|Walsall]], he returned to Newcastle.

===Roda JC Kerkrade===
After a successful trial period, Kádár was officially signed by Dutch [[Eredivisie]] club [[Roda JC Kerkrade]] on 7 August 2012.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=1677028.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120811092853/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=1677028.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=11 August 2012|title=Roda sign up Kadar|date=7 August 2012|access-date=7 August 2012|publisher=FIFA}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tribalfootball.com/articles/roda-jc-sign-newcastle-defender-kadar-3437181|title=Roda JC sign Newcastle defender Kadar|date=8 August 2012|access-date=8 August 2012|publisher=Tribal Football}}</ref> Although in the [[2012–13 Eredivisie|2012–13]] season of the Eredivisie Kádár played 11 matches, he wanted to get more possibilities to play, therefore Roda loaned him to the Hungarian club Diósgyőr for the rest of the 2012–13 season.

===Diósgyőr===
[[File:Kadar2015.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Kádár at Lech Poznan]]
On 3 June 2013, Kádár was signed by [[Hungarian League]] club [[Diósgyőri VTK]] after playing 13 matches and scoring 1 goal in the [[2012–13 Nemzeti Bajnokság I|2012–13]] season of the Hungarian League on loan from Roda JC Kerkade.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nemzetisport.hu/labdarugo_nb_i/dvtk-kadart-vegleg-megszereztek-a-diosgyoriek-hivatalos-2250671|title=Kádárt végleg megszerezte a klub - hivatalos|date=3 June 2013|publisher=Nemzeti Sport}}</ref>

===Lech Poznań===
On 29 January 2015, Kádár was signed by [[Ekstraklasa]] club [[Lech Poznań]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nemzetisport.hu/legiosok/legiosok-kadar-tamas-alairt-a-lech-poznanhoz-hivatalos-2391525|title=Légiósok: Kádár Tamás aláírt a Lech Poznanhoz - hivatalos|date=30 January 2015|publisher=[[Nemzeti Sport]]}}</ref> He signed a three-and-a-half-year contract with the [[Polish people|Polish]] club.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nemzetisport.hu/labdarugo_nb_i/dvtk-megegyeztek-a-kerovel-kadar-tamas-atigazolasa-ugyeben-2390677|title=DVTK: megegyeztek a kérővel Kádár átigazolása ügyében|date=26 January 2015|publisher=[[Nemzeti Sport]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nemzetisport.hu/labdarugo_nb_i/dvtk-kadar-tamas-megegyezett-a-lech-poznannal-sajtohir-2391177|title=DVTK: Kádár 3 és fél évre a Lech Poznané lesz - hivatalos|date=28 January 2015|publisher=[[Nemzeti Sport]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lechpoznan.pl/news/tamas,kadar,przejdzie,testy#.VMn4L9LF_To|title=Tamas Kadar przejdzie testy|date=28 January 2015|publisher=Official Lech Poznań Website}}</ref>

In the [[2015–16 Ekstraklasa]] season Kádár made 29, and 4 [[2015–16 Polish Cup]] appearances.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://int.soccerway.com/players/tamas-kadar/87806/|title=Tamas Kadar - Soccerway|date=11 June 2016|publisher=Soccerway.com}}</ref>

===Dynamo Kyiv===
On 10 February 2017, Kádár signed a four-year contract with the Ukrainian champions [[FC Dynamo Kyiv|Dynamo Kyiv]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://fcdynamo.kiev.ua/en/allnews/news/tamash_kadar_gravets_fk_dinamo_kiiv/|title=Tamas KADAR – FC Dynamo Kyiv player!|website=fcdynamo.kiev.ua|access-date=2019-06-21}}</ref>

===Újpest===
On 10 February 2022, Kádár returned to Hungary and signed with [[Újpest FC|Újpest]].<ref>{{cite press release|publisher=Újpest|url=https://ujpestfc.hu/article?id=20111|title=Another reinforcement has arrived!|date=10 February 2022|access-date=3 May 2022|archive-date=23 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220923062810/https://ujpestfc.hu/article?id=20111|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Paks===
On 14 July 2022, Kádár signed with [[Paksi FC|Paks]].<ref>{{cite web|publisher=Paks|url=https://paksifc.hu/news.php?extend.10259.12|title=Kádár Tamás is nálunk folytatja!|trans-title=Tamás Kádár also continues with us!|date=14 July 2022|access-date=15 March 2023|language=hu}}</ref>

===MTK Budapest===
On 15 June 2023, it was announced that Kádár had signed a contract with [[MTK Budapest FC|MTK Budapest]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mtkbudapest.hu/hu/hirek/57-szeres-valogatott-vedovel-erositettunk|title=57-SZERES VÁLOGATOTT VÉDŐVEL ERŐSÍTETTÜNK|trans-title=WE ARE REINFORCED WITH 57 TIMES SELECTED PROTECTION|publisher=mtkbudapest.hu|language=hu|date=15 June 2023|accessdate=9 August 2023}}</ref> On 15 May 2026, he played his lats match in a 2-2 draw against [[Puskás Akadémia FC]] at the [[Pancho Aréna]], in [[Felcsút]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-05-15 |title=Videó: Kádár Tamás visszavonul, a Pancho Arénában búcsúzott a futballtól |url=https://www.nemzetisport.hu/labdarugo-nb-i/2026/05/video-kadar-tamas-visszavonul-a-pancho-arenaban-bucsuzott-a-futballtol |access-date=2026-05-16 |website=Nemzeti Sport |language=hu}}</ref>

==International career==
On 12 May 2008, Kádár received his first call up to the [[Hungary national football team|Hungary senior squad]], though he did not make an appearance.<ref>{{cite news|title=Hungary vs Greece |url=http://www.skysports.com/football/hungary-vs-greece/teams/103115|access-date=20 October 2016|publisher=Sky Sports|date=24 May 2008 }}</ref> He was recalled to the U21 side for several [[2011 UEFA European Under-21 Football Championship qualification Group 3|2011 European Championship]] qualifiers. On 17 November 2010 Kádár played his first match for the national team against [[Lithuania national football team|Lithuania]] at the [[Stadion Sóstói]] in [[Székesfehérvár]], Hungary. The final result was 2-0 to Hungary. He also played in the match that resulted in the 5–0 victory over [[Liechtenstein national football team|Liechtenstein]] at the [[Puskás Ferenc Stadium]] in Hungary.

Kádár gained a reputation of a defender who, while moving up on the left side from defense, could successfully spot and assist a quick attack: on 16 October 2012 against [[Turkey national football team|Turkey]] he gave an assist to [[Ádám Szalai|Szalai]] which resulted in the second Hungarian goal,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/worldcup/season=2014/matches/round=2000294/match=2008618/postmatch/report/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121019231319/http://www.uefa.com/worldcup/season=2014/matches/round=2000294/match=2008618/postmatch/report/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=19 October 2012|title=Hungary battle back to beat Turkey|publisher=UEFA|date=16 October 2012|access-date=16 October 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/preliminaries/news/newsid=1785772/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121018201159/http://www.fifa.com/worldcup/preliminaries/news/newsid=1785772/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=18 October 2012|title=Turkish hopes dented after Hungary defeat|publisher=FIFA|date=16 October 2012|access-date=16 October 2012}}</ref> he provided an assist to [[Dániel Böde]] against the Faroe Islands, and to [[Tamás Priskin]] against Norway.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://index.hu/sport/futball/2016/eb/jatekosok/tamas_kadar|title=Index - Európa-bajnokság 2016 - adatlap -}}</ref>

Kádár was selected for Hungary's [[UEFA Euro 2016|Euro 2016]] squad.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/history/news/0253-0d813fac0b2c-04ea0dbfc8e5-1000--hungary-on-the-offensive-with-euro-squad/|title=Hungary on the offensive with EURO squad|publisher=[[UEFA]]|date=31 May 2016|access-date=31 May 2016}}</ref>

On 14 June 2016, Kádár played in the first group match in a 2–0 victory over [[Austria national football team|Austria]] at the [[UEFA Euro 2016 Group F]] match at [[Nouveau Stade de Bordeaux]], [[Bordeaux]], France.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/match/2017960--austria-vs-hungary/|title=UEFA Euro 2016: Austria 0-2 Hungary|publisher=[[UEFA.com]]}}</ref> Three days later, on 18 June 2016, he played in a 1–1 draw against [[Iceland national football team|Iceland]] at the [[Stade Vélodrome]], [[Marseille]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/match/2017962--iceland-vs-hungary/|title=UEFA Euro 2016: Iceland 1–1 Hungary|publisher=[[UEFA.com]]}}</ref>

==Image==
Upon his arrival to the [[Ekstraklasa]] club [[Lech Poznań]], he was nicknamed Bad boy by the fans of the club for resembling [[Jesse Pinkman]] from the [[AMC (TV channel)|AMC]] TV series [[Breaking Bad]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nemzetisport.hu/legiosok/lech-remelem-meg-ma-alairhatok-kadar-becenevet-is-kapott-2391433|title=Lech: Kádár pénteken ír alá, már becenevet is kapott|date=29 January 2015|publisher=[[Nemzeti Sport]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lech.tv/video-id-15947-kadar_na_testach_w_lechu|title=Kadar na testach w Lechu|date=29 January 2015|publisher=Official Lech Poznan Website}}</ref> He is known for his multitude of [[tattoo]]s, which he started collecting as a hobby after his club banned him from riding a motorcycle.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.blikk.hu/sport/magyar-foci/egy-ev-alatt-30-tetkot-varratott-magara-a-valogatott-focista/vgb2wvf|title=Egy év alatt 30 tetkót varratott magára a válogatott focista|date=19 February 2016}}</ref>

'''Leon Aderemi Balogun'''{{Audio|Leon_Aderemi_Balogun.wav|listen}} (born 28 June 1988) is a German-born Nigerian professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[centre-back]] or [[right-back]] for [[Nemzeti Bajnokság I]] club [[Győri ETO FC|ETO Győr]].<ref name="ETO">{{cite news |url=https://eto.hu/hu/article/korabbi-premier-league--es-bundesliga-jatekos-az-eto-fc-uj-szerzemenye |title=Korábbi Premier League- és Bundesliga-játékos az ETO FC új szerzeménye |trans-title=Former Premier League and Bundesliga player is new signing for ETO FC |date=6 August 2026 |publisher=[[Győri ETO FC|ETO Győr]] Official Website |website=eto.hu |language=hu}}</ref>

==Club career==
===Early career===
He made his [[Bundesliga]] debut on 19 April 2009 for [[Hannover 96]] in a game against [[Hamburger SV]].<ref name=firstgame>{{cite web | url = http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/bundesliga/spieltag/spielpaarungsbericht/object/863662/saison/2008-09/naviindex/1 | title = Petric als Blitzarbeiter | publisher = [[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] | access-date = 3 April 2010 | language = de | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20090611072438/http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/bundesliga/spieltag/spielpaarungsbericht/object/863662/saison/2008-09/naviindex/1 | archive-date = 11 June 2009 }}</ref>

After his contract with [[2. Bundesliga]] side [[Fortuna Düsseldorf]] expired in summer 2014, he was without a club for three months until he joined fellow leaguer [[SV Darmstadt 98|Darmstadt 98]]. He signed a contract until the end of the 2014–15 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sv98.de/news/1_mannschaft/details/datum/2014/10/02/lilien-verstaerken-sich-mit-leon-balogun.htm|title=Lilien verstärken sich mit Leon Balogun|trans-title=Lilien strengthens with Leon Balogun|date=2 October 2014|access-date=12 March 2015|language=de|publisher=SV Darmstadt 98|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141004075233/http://www.sv98.de/news/1_mannschaft/details/datum/2014/10/02/lilien-verstaerken-sich-mit-leon-balogun.htm|archive-date=4 October 2014}}</ref>

===Brighton & Hove Albion===
On 22 May 2018, Balogun signed a two-year deal with [[Premier League]] club [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44217096|title=Leon Balogun: Brighton sign Nigeria international on free transfer|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=22 May 2018|access-date=16 June 2018|archive-date=5 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180805132317/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/44217096|url-status=live}}</ref>

Balogun made his competitive debut for the Sussex club coming on as an early substitute against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] replacing injured [[Lewis Dunk]]. The Seagulls went on to beat United 3–2 at [[Falmer Stadium]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45159603|title=Brighton 3–2 Man Utd: Brighton score three first-half goals to stun visitors – BBC Sport|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=19 August 2018|access-date=31 August 2018|archive-date=10 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190510075922/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45159603|url-status=live}}</ref>

He scored his first goal for the Albion to make it 2–0 against bitter rivals [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] at Falmer Stadium where he scored in 25 seconds after being subbed on replacing [[Pascal Groß]] as a result of a [[Shane Duffy]] red card for head butting. The game finished 3–1 to the Albion to claim the boasting rights in the [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.–Crystal Palace F.C. rivalry|M23 derby]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46353455|title=Brighton 3–1 Crystal Palace: Ten-man Seagulls sweep Eagles aside – BBC Sport|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=4 December 2018|access-date=5 December 2018|archive-date=30 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330164436/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46353455|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 27 August 2019, Balogun played in his first ever [[2019–20 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]] match in a 2–1 away win over [[Bristol Rovers F.C.|Bristol Rovers]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49402996 |title=Bristol Rovers v Brighton & Hove Albion - BBC Sport |publisher=BBC Sport |date=27 August 2019 |access-date=27 August 2019 |archive-date=27 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190827203722/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/49402996 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Wigan Athletic===
Balogun signed for [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]] on 31 January 2020 on a six-month loan deal.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://wiganathletic.com/news/2020/january/Latics-complete-loan-signing-of-Brighton-Hove-Albion-defender-Leon-Balogun/ |title=LATICS COMPLETE LOAN SIGNING OF BRIGHTON & HOVE ALBION DEFENDER LEON BALOGUN |publisher=Wigan Athletic FC |date=31 January 2020 |access-date=31 January 2020 |archive-date=31 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200131235159/https://wiganathletic.com/news/2020/january/Latics-complete-loan-signing-of-Brighton-Hove-Albion-defender-Leon-Balogun/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On 25 June 2020, he signed a short term permanent contract with the Latics until the end of the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Update | Wigan Athletic Player Contracts |date=26 June 2020 |url=https://wiganathletic.com/news/2020/june/Update-Wigan-Athletic-Player-Contracts/ |publisher=Wigan Athletic |access-date=28 June 2020 |archive-date=28 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200628010034/https://wiganathletic.com/news/2020/june/Update-Wigan-Athletic-Player-Contracts/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Rangers===
Balogun signed for [[Scottish Premiership]] club [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]] on 24 July 2020 on a one-year contract, with an option in the club's favour to extend for a further year.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/rangers-sign-leon-balogun/4dgSPcsFODzzFSopsYeTJP |title=Rangers sign Leon Balogun |publisher=Rangers F.C. |date=24 July 2020 |access-date=25 July 2020 |archive-date=24 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200724173538/https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/rangers-sign-leon-balogun/4dgSPcsFODzzFSopsYeTJP |url-status=live }}</ref> He made his debut for Rangers a week later, on 1 August, in a [[Scottish Premiership]] match against [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] where he impressed during a 1–0 win.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53535016 | title=Aberdeen 0-1 Rangers | publisher=BBC | work=BBC Sport | date=1 August 2020 | first=Clive | last=Lindsay | access-date=23 February 2021 | archive-date=12 April 2021 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210412020937/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/53535016 | url-status=live }}</ref> During February 2021, he deputised at right back after an injury to club captain [[James Tavernier]] and the suspension of reserve player [[Nathan Patterson (footballer)|Nathan Patterson]]. Balogun previously played at right back earlier in his career when in Germany.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/leon-balogun-prepared-to-park-his-ego-to-play-at-right-back-332gf30zp | title=Leon Balogun prepared to park his ego to play at right back | work=The Times | first=Paul | last=Forsyth | date=20 February 2021 | access-date=23 February 2021 | archive-date=21 February 2021 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210221061124/https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/leon-balogun-prepared-to-park-his-ego-to-play-at-right-back-332gf30zp | url-status=live }}</ref>

On 9 April 2021, Balogun signed a new one-year contract with [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/leon-balogun-extends-his-rangers-contract/4kavOaT3NmmrTRSVs6m5PE|title=LEON BALOGUN EXTENDS HIS RANGERS CONTRACT|publisher=Rangers FC|date=9 April 2021|access-date=9 April 2021|archive-date=28 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220128091008/https://www.rangers.co.uk/Article/leon-balogun-extends-his-rangers-contract/4kavOaT3NmmrTRSVs6m5PE|url-status=live}}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club on 27 October 2021, in a [[Europa League]] group stage match against [[Brøndby IF]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12440476/rangers-2-0-brondby-leon-balogun-and-kemar-roofe-on-target-at-ibrox|title=Rangers 2-0 Brondby: Leon Balogun and Kemar Roofe on target at Ibrox|publisher=Sky Sports News|date=22 October 2021|access-date=8 November 2021|archive-date=9 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211109014717/https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/12440476/rangers-2-0-brondby-leon-balogun-and-kemar-roofe-on-target-at-ibrox|url-status=live}}</ref> Balogun left Rangers in June 2022 after his contract expired, with his final appearance coming in their [[2022 Scottish Cup Final]] victory.<ref name = mccoist/><ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61685938 | title=Rangers: Leon Balogun exits at end of contract along with Andy Firth | work=BBC Sport | publisher=BBC | date=3 June 2022 | access-date=3 June 2022 | archive-date=3 June 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220603185240/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61685938 | url-status=live }}</ref> Rangers legend [[Ally McCoist]] commented two months later that he had been "surprised" by Balogun's departure, and suggested that the club should re-sign him.<ref name = mccoist>{{cite web |url=https://news.stv.tv/sport/ally-mccoist-and-kenny-miller-urge-rangers-to-re-sign-leon-balogun-following-psv-eindhoven-draw |title=Ally McCoist and Kenny Miller urge Rangers to re-sign Leon Balogun following PSV Eindhoven draw |website=STV News |first=Peter |last=Cassidy |date=17 August 2022 |accessdate=21 August 2022 |archive-date=17 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220817093844/https://news.stv.tv/sport/ally-mccoist-and-kenny-miller-urge-rangers-to-re-sign-leon-balogun-following-psv-eindhoven-draw |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Queens Park Rangers===
Balogun signed a one-year contract with [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] on 26 August 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62694637 |title=Leon Balogun: QPR sign ex-Rangers defender on one-year deal |website=BBC Sport |date=26 August 2022 |accessdate=26 August 2022 |archive-date=26 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220826174234/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/62694637 |url-status=live }}</ref> He scored his first goal for the club on 22 October 2022, which proved to be the winner, against his former club Wigan Athletic.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/63266866 | title=QPR hold off Wigan pressure to stay top | work=BBC Sport | access-date=22 October 2022 | archive-date=22 October 2022 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221022173117/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/63266866 | url-status=live }}</ref>

===Return to Rangers===
He returned to Rangers on 12 July 2023, a year after departing from the club as a free agent. His return was one celebrated by the club and its fans, as well as Balogun himself, who felt as though he had “come home”.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/leon-balogun-it-feels-like-coming-home/5aVGph43dCQMdZwmTlWmil|title=Leon Balogun: It Feels Like Coming Home|website=Rangers F.C.|date=12 July 2023|accessdate=17 December 2023|archive-date=17 December 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231217214829/https://www.rangers.co.uk/article/leon-balogun-it-feels-like-coming-home/5aVGph43dCQMdZwmTlWmil|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Aris Limassol===
On 20 June 2025, Balogun signed a one-year contract with [[Cypriot First Division]] club [[Aris Limassol FC|Aris Limassol]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://arisfc.com/en/news/leon-balogun-is-green-2025-06-20/ |title=Leon Balogun is Green! |website=Aris Limassol FC |date=20 June 2025 |accessdate=20 June 2025}}</ref>

===ETO Győr===
On 6 August 2026, Balogun signed a contract with [[Nemzeti Bajnokság I|Hungarian]] club [[Győri ETO FC|ETO Győr]].<ref name="ETO" />

==International career==
[[File:FWC 2018 - Group D - NGA v ISL - Photo 21.jpg|thumb|left|Balogun with Nigeria against [[Iceland national football team|Iceland]] at the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]]]]

Born to a Nigerian father and German mother, Balogun was called up by [[Nigeria national football team|Nigeria]] for a March 2014 friendly against Mexico as a replacement for [[Joseph Yobo]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/26433716|title=Joseph Yobo ruled out of Nigeria friendly against Mexico|date=4 March 2014|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=14 May 2018|archive-date=24 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924202541/http://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/26433716|url-status=live}}</ref> Balogun entered at half-time, but was injured after 20 minutes in a collision with signage on the touchline. He fractured his foot and was set to miss 2–3 months after surgery. However, he later confirmed to news media that his injury did not require surgery.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mtnfootball.com/international/fifa-world-cup-2014/news/2014/mar/07-new-eagles-star-balogun-out-for-2-months.html |title=New Eagles star Balogun out for 2 months |access-date=7 March 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140307153416/http://www.mtnfootball.com/international/fifa-world-cup-2014/news/2014/mar/07-new-eagles-star-balogun-out-for-2-months.html| work=MTNFootball.com|archive-date=7 March 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.supersport.com/football/super-eagles/news/140314/Eagles_Balogun_on_the_mend|title=Eagles' Balogun on the mend|first=Sammy|last=Wejinya|publisher=SuperSport|date=14 March 2014|access-date=5 June 2018|language=en-ZA|archive-date=22 November 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171122061639/https://www.supersport.com/football/super-eagles/news/140314/eagles_balogun_on_the_mend|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 25 March 2015, he played his second game for Nigeria in a 1–0 loss against Uganda.
He played his third game for the country on 13 June 2015 when he featured in a 2–0 win over Chad in the opening game of qualifying for the 2017 African Nations Cup.

In June 2018, he was named in Nigeria's final 23-man [[2018 FIFA World Cup squads#Nigeria|squad]] for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]] in Russia.<ref>{{cite news |last=Udoh |first=Colin |url=http://www.espn.com/soccer/nigeria/story/3516588/nigeria-super-eagles-drop-ola-ainamikel-agu-from-world-cup-squad |title=Super Eagles drop Aina, Agu from World Cup squad |publisher=ESPN |date=3 June 2018 |access-date=5 June 2018 |archive-date=12 June 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612143440/http://www.espn.com/soccer/nigeria/story/3516588/nigeria-super-eagles-drop-ola-ainamikel-agu-from-world-cup-squad |url-status=live }}</ref> Balogun played in every minute of the three games Nigeria played in, including a 2–0 win over [[Iceland national football team|Iceland]], but were eliminated after finishing 3rd in their group.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/world-cup|publisher=BBC Sport|title=World Cup - Football - BBC Sport|access-date=26 June 2019|archive-date=2 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190702035250/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/world-cup|url-status=live}}</ref>

Balogun was included in Nigeria's squad for the [[2019 Africa Cup of Nations]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/teams/nigeria|publisher=BBC Sport|title=Nigeria - Football - BBC Sport|access-date=26 June 2019|archive-date=23 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190623092341/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/teams/nigeria|url-status=live}}</ref> His first appearance in the competition came in Nigeria's second group game against [[Guinean national football team|Guinea]] in which Nigeria won 1–0 to seal qualification into the knockouts.<ref>{{cite news |url= https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/live/football/48775948 |title= Africa Cup of Nations: Nigeria 1-0 Guinea - Omeruo header seals qualification |work= BBC Sport |date= 26 June 2019 |publisher= Sport |access-date= 26 June 2019 |archive-date= 26 June 2019 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20190626143535/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/live/football/48775948 |url-status= live }}</ref> Balogun made four appearances in the competition where The Super Eagles finished as bronze medallists.<ref name="BBC Sport">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/live/football/49022063|title=Africa Cup of Nations third-place play-off - Tunisia 0–1 Nigeria - Live - BBC Sport|publisher=BBC Sport|date=17 July 2019|access-date=20 July 2019|archive-date=17 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190717234341/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/live/football/49022063|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Balogun was born in [[Berlin]], West Germany<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/person/pe14542/leon-balogun/ |title=Leon Balogun: Profile |website=worldfootball.net |publisher=HEIM:SPIEL |access-date=25 July 2020 |archive-date=25 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200725175821/https://www.worldfootball.net/player_summary/leon-balogun/ |url-status=live }}</ref> to a Nigerian-Yoruba father and a German mother.<ref name=":0" /> Balogun was raised [[Roman Catholicism|Roman Catholic]] and attended a Catholic [[primary school]], but was not religious as a child.<ref name=":1" /> However, during the hardships of his early footballing career he became more devout.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|title=Bologun said he found strength in religion when he was struggling to make the grade as a teenager.|url=https://www.pulse.ng/sports/football/leon-balogun-reveals-how-he-found-god-id7296174.html|newspaper=[[Pulse Nigeria]]|first=Steve|last=Dede|date=11 September 2017|access-date=25 August 2018|archive-date=26 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180826080739/https://www.pulse.ng/sports/football/leon-balogun-reveals-how-he-found-god-id7296174.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/us/soccer/news/leon-balogun-what-can-premier-league-fans-expect-from-nigeria-star/18c388mesyslg1nlmkntu7waba|title=Leon Balogun: What can Premier League fans expect from Nigeria star?|first=Patrick|last=Gleeson|date=16 June 2018|access-date=25 August 2018|publisher=Sporting News|archive-date=26 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180826113458/http://www.sportingnews.com/us/soccer/news/leon-balogun-what-can-premier-league-fans-expect-from-nigeria-star/18c388mesyslg1nlmkntu7waba|url-status=live}}</ref> Balogun speaks fluent [[English language|English]] and [[German language|German]], but does not speak [[Yoruba language|Yoruba]], as his parents tried to assimilate him into German culture.<ref name=":0">{{cite web|title=Why I did not learn Yoruba — Leon Balogun|url=http://www.nigeriavillagesquare.com/sports/why-i-did-not-learn-yoruba-%E2%80%94-leon-balogun.html|date=23 March 2014|access-date=25 August 2018|work=Nigeria Village Square|archive-date=26 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180826114826/http://www.nigeriavillagesquare.com/sports/why-i-did-not-learn-yoruba-%E2%80%94-leon-balogun.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In November 2019 Balogun said there needed to be a collective response from players to [[Racism in association football|racism in football]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50658573|title=Nigeria's Leon Balogun says fight against racism is a collective responsibility|work=BBC Sport|date=5 December 2019|access-date=5 December 2019|archive-date=5 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191205140009/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50658573|url-status=live}}</ref>

'''Iván Iglesias Corteguera''' (born 16 December 1971) is a Spanish former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[midfielder]].

==Club career==
Born in [[Gijón]], [[Asturias]], Iglesias started playing professionally with local [[Sporting de Gijón]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sport.jotdown.es/2025/03/04/ivan-iglesias/|title=Iván Iglesias: «Cuando fiché por el Oviedo, siempre había alguien que me insultaba, yo tragaba saliva y miraba para otro lado»|trans-title=Iván Iglesias: "When I signed for Oviedo, there was always someone insulting me, I got my shit together and looked the other way"|publisher=[[Jot Down]]|first=Pablo|last=Batalla|language=Spanish|date=4 March 2025|accessdate=5 March 2025}}</ref> After just two seasons – and only appearing regularly in [[1992–93 La Liga|1992–93]] – he was signed by [[La Liga]] club [[FC Barcelona]] in summer 1993, after agreeing to a five-year contract.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1993/07/11/pagina-16/1276489/pdf.html|title=Iván, con todas las de la ley|trans-title=Iván, as it should|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|first=Jaume|last=Miserachs|language=Spanish|date=11 July 1993|accessdate=18 May 2015}}</ref>

Never an undisputed starter at the [[Camp Nou]], Iglesias did make 71 competitive appearances in his two-year spell.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.sport.es/es/noticias/barca/ivan-iglesias-trabajar-cruyff-master-continuo-7223694|title=Iván Iglesias: "Trabajar con Cruyff fue un master continuo"|trans-title=Iván Iglesias: "Working with Cruyff was a neverending clinic"|newspaper=[[Sport (Spanish newspaper)|Sport]]|first=David|last=Salinas|language=Spanish|date=30 December 2018|accessdate=5 March 2025}}</ref> On 8 January 1994, he closed the scoring for [[Johan Cruyff]]'s side against [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in a 5–0 home rout;<ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1994/01/09/pagina-2/1288708/pdf.html|title=El Barça se apunta otro 5–0 histórico|trans-title=Barça clinch another historic 5–0|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Andrés|last=Astruells|language=Spanish|date=9 January 1994|accessdate=18 May 2015}}</ref> Barcelona eventually clinched the [[1993–94 La Liga|league title]].<ref name=MD>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/1994/05/15/pagina-2/1290293/pdf.html|title=Apoteosis en la cuarta|trans-title=Exhilaration in fourth|newspaper=Mundo Deportivo|first=Francesc|last=Perearnau|language=Spanish|date=15 May 1994|accessdate=18 May 2015}}</ref>

Shortly after suffering an [[anterior cruciate ligament injury]], Iglesias returned to Sporting for the [[1995–96 La Liga|1995–96 campaign]] (on loan), after which he switched to neighbouring [[Real Oviedo]] where he would stay for four years, always in the top flight. He retired in June 2002 aged 30 while at [[Rayo Vallecano]] in the same league, totalling 230 games and 21 goals over 11 seasons.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lavozdeasturias.es/noticia/sporting1905/2018/12/31/ivan-iglesias/00031546271261273142427.htm|title=Ex Sporting: ¿Qué fue de Iván Iglesias?|trans-title=Ex Sporting: What happened to Iván Iglesias?|newspaper=[[La Voz de Asturias]]|first=Estefanía|last=Domingo Carruébano|language=Spanish|date=31 December 2018|accessdate=5 March 2025}}</ref>

Iglesias later opened a football school with his former Sporting teammate [[Juanele]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://blogs.20minutos.es/quefuede/2009/08/07/quao-fue-de-ivaan-iglesias/|title=Qué fue de… Iván Iglesias|trans-title=What happened to… Iván Iglesias|newspaper=[[20 minutos]]|first=Edu|last=Casado|language=Spanish|date=7 August 2009|accessdate=18 May 2015}}</ref>

'''Rohan Anthony Ricketts''' (born 22 December 1982) is an English former professional [[association football|footballer]].

==Club career==

===Arsenal===
Ricketts started out with [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], with whom he won the [[FA Youth Cup]] in 2000 and 2001.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.arsenal.com/history/profiles/567/rohan-ricketts |title=Rohan Ricketts – Arsenal Player Database |work=arsenal.com |publisher=[[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] |accessdate=29 April 2009 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120404131535/http://www.arsenal.com/history/profiles/567/rohan-ricketts |archivedate=4 April 2012 |df=dmy-all }}</ref> He made one appearance for them, in the [[Football League Cup|League Cup]], against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/worthington_cup/1637817.stm |title=Arsenal win battle of the reserves |work=[[BBC Sport]] |publisher=[[BBC|British Broadcasting Corporation]] |date=5 November 2001 |access-date=29 April 2009}}</ref>

===Tottenham Hotspur===
In 2002, he made the unusual step of joining Arsenal's rivals [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]],<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/t/tottenham_hotspur/2126671.stm |title=Spurs sign Arsenal midfielder |work=[[BBC Sport]] |publisher=[[BBC|British Broadcasting Corporation]] |date=13 July 2002 |access-date=29 April 2009}}</ref> and became just the fourth player to make the switch from Arsenal to [[Tottenham Hotspur]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.mehstg.com/arsefacts.htm |title=Spurs v Arsenal facts |publisher=mehstg |accessdate=29 April 2009}}</ref> and only the twelfth to appear for both sides since their formation.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fifa.com/classicfootball/news/newsid=107971.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090213120551/http://www.fifa.com/classicfootball/news/newsid=107971.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=13 February 2009 |title=The Classic: Arsenal – Tottenham Hotspur |publisher=[[FIFA]] |date=29 November 2006 |accessdate=29 April 2009 }}</ref>

Ricketts did not play a single game in his first season, but was a first-team regular in [[2003–04 in English football|2003–04]] and his form saw him agree a one-year contract extension with the club in December 2003.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/t/tottenham_hotspur/3324937.stm |title=Ricketts extends Spurs deal |work=BBC News |publisher=British Broadcasting Corporation |date=16 December 2003 |access-date=29 April 2009}}</ref> [[Tord Grip]] was impressed with his ability and there was talk of him being called up to the senior [[England national football team|England]] squad {{Citation needed|date=March 2017}}, but following on from [[Glenn Hoddle]]'s sacking as Tottenham manager, Ricketts found his first team opportunities limited, despite being named Player of the Month in August and September for Tottenham{{Citation needed|date=March 2017}}. He scored one league goal during his time at Spurs, in a 2–1 win over [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] in November 2003.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/keane-takes-advantage-of-villas-shortcomings-736733.html |title=Keane takes advantage of Villa's shortcomings |work=[[The Independent]] |date=24 November 2003 |accessdate=25 August 2009 | location=London | first=Mike | last=Rowbottom}}{{dead link|date=August 2021|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> He also scored once in the League Cup for Spurs, in a game against Coventry City.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/league_cup/3125076.stm |title=Coventry 0–3 Spurs |publisher=BBC |date=24 September 2003 |access-date=7 November 2009}}</ref>

====Loan spells====
The following season, under [[Jacques Santini]] and then [[Martin Jol]], he found appearances harder to come by and had two loan spells, first at [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]], and then [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]], linking up with his former manager, Glenn Hoddle. He scored once for Wolves, in a 2–1 win over Reading on 30 April 2005.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_div_1/4475911.stm |title=Reading 1–2 Wolves |publisher=BBC |date=30 April 2005 |access-date=7 November 2009}}</ref>

===Wolves & Barnsley===
In the summer of 2005 he moved to [[Molineux stadium|Molineux]] on a permanent basis. He had a loan spell at [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] in 2007 and was released by Wolves in May of the same year.

Ricketts signed a two-year deal with [[Football League Championship|Championship]] side [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]] in July 2007 but was released on 11 April 2008.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.barnsleyfc.premiumtv.co.uk/page/NewsDetail/0,,10309~1287516,00.html |title=RICKETTS DEPARTS |publisher=barnsleyfc.co.uk |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20080413121318/http://www.barnsleyfc.premiumtv.co.uk/page/NewsDetail/0%2C%2C10309~1287516%2C00.html |archivedate=13 April 2008 }}</ref> That same day he was signed by [[Toronto FC]] of [[Major League Soccer]].

===Toronto FC===
Rohan Ricketts scored his first two goals for [[Toronto FC]] against the [[Colorado Rapids]] on 14 June 2008. In 2008 Ricketts made 26 starts (27 total appearances) and scored four goals in the regular season; he added two more goals in the [[Canadian Championship]].

[[File:Rohan-ricketts-2009-06-02.jpg|thumb|200px|Ricketts with [[Toronto FC]] in 2009]]
In 2009, Ricketts was pushed down Toronto FC's depth chart due to the arrivals of Canadian international [[Dwayne DeRosario]] and young American [[Sam Cronin]]; in June, Toronto released Ricketts, clearing the salary cap space necessary for the club to sign Canadian international [[Ali Gerba]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/soccer/toronto-fc-release-ricketts-1.786270 |title=Toronto FC release Ricketts |work=[[CBC.ca]] |publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation]] |date=17 June 2009}}</ref>

Following his release from Toronto, Ricketts reportedly spurned interest from several English clubs to go on trial with [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] in August 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.eveningexpress.co.uk/Article.aspx/1346771?UserKey= |title=I'll reject Championship for Aberdeen FC |publisher=[[Evening Express (Scotland)|Evening Express]] |date=11 August 2009 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110726214518/http://www.eveningexpress.co.uk/Article.aspx/1346771?UserKey= |archivedate=26 July 2011 }}</ref> Ricketts reportedly impressed during his trial{{emdash}}in particular in Aberdeen's 1–0 win over [[Hull City A.F.C.|Hull City]] in a preseason friendly match{{emdash}}but budgetary constraints reportedly complicated the potential signing, and Ricketts ultimately did not remain with the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://lesrosbifs.wordpress.com/2009/08/12/latest-ex-toronto-man-ricketts-edges-closer-to-aberdeen-move-west-ham-united-and-manchester-united-old-boy-in-south-africa/ |title=Latest: Ex-Toronto man Ricketts edges closer to Aberdeen move; West Ham United and Manchester United old boy in South Africa |publisher=Les Rosbifs |date=12 August 2009 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090816220610/http://lesrosbifs.wordpress.com/2009/08/12/latest-ex-toronto-man-ricketts-edges-closer-to-aberdeen-move-west-ham-united-and-manchester-united-old-boy-in-south-africa/ |archivedate=16 August 2009 }}</ref>

===Later career===
In early 2010 during the winter transfer market in Europe, Ricketts signed for Hungarian club [[Diósgyőri VTK]]. He made one first-team appearance as the club were relegated from Hungary's top professional league to the [[NB2]]. In August 2010 Ricketts signed for [[FC Dacia Chişinău]] of the [[Moldovan National Division]]. He made his debut the same month in a 0–0 draw against [[FC Academia UTM Chişinău]].He left the club three months later, claiming he had not been paid.<ref name="intldebut">{{cite web |url=http://www.talksport.co.uk/radio/hawksbee-and-jacobs/blog/2010-11-10/ricketts-i-dont-want-play-championship-im-football-purist |title=Ricketts: 'I don't want to play in the Championship – I'm a football purist' |publisher=talksport.co.uk |date=10 November 2010 |accessdate=11 November 2010 |archive-date=19 November 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101119101231/http://www.talksport.co.uk/radio/hawksbee-and-jacobs/blog/2010-11-10/ricketts-i-dont-want-play-championship-im-football-purist |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Ricketts signed for German club [[SV Wilhelmshaven]] in January 2011, but left the club at the end of the 2010–11 season.<ref name="Rohan Ricketts 'hopeful' over Southend United deal">{{cite news | title = Rohan Ricketts 'hopeful' over Southend United deal | url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14135573 | publisher = BBC Sport | date = 14 July 2011 | access-date = 24 July 2011}}</ref> He went on trial at two English clubs,  [[Southend United F.C.|Southend United]] and Stevenage,<ref name="Rohan Ricketts 'hopeful' over Southend United deal" /><ref name="Southend boss Sturrock considers Ricketts & Leonard deals">{{cite news | title = Southend boss Sturrock considers Ricketts & Leonard deals | url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14197997 | publisher = BBC Sport | date = 19 July 2011 | access-date = 24 July 2011}}</ref><ref name="Rohan Ricketts wants 'fair' Southend United deal">{{cite news | title = Rohan Ricketts wants 'fair' Southend United deal | url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14231310 | publisher = BBC Sport | date = 21 July 2011 | access-date = 24 July 2011}}</ref><ref name="Rohan Ricketts open to Stevenage chance">{{cite news | title = Rohan Ricketts open to Stevenage chance | url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14278214 | publisher = BBC Sport | date = 25 July 2011 | access-date = 25 July 2011}}</ref><ref name="Stevenage 0–1 Arsenal XI">{{cite news |title=Stevenage 0–1 Arsenal XI |url=http://www.stevenagefc.com/page/LatestNewsDetail/0,,10839~2400176,00.html |publisher=Stevenage F.C. |date=23 July 2011 |accessdate=24 July 2011 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120609121117/http://www.stevenagefc.com/page/LatestNewsDetail/0%2C%2C10839~2400176%2C00.html |archivedate=9 June 2012}}</ref> but did not sign for either. Instead  Ricketts signed for [[League of Ireland]] champions [[Shamrock Rovers F.C.|Shamrock Rovers]] in August 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rte.ie/sport/soccer/2011/0831/shamrockrovers_rickettsr_patersonj.html|title=Ricketts & Paterson sign for Rovers|date=31 August 2011|work=RTÉ Sport |accessdate=14 September 2011}}</ref> He made his first team debut away to [[Dundalk F.C.|Dundalk]] on 3 September and was involved in both goals, providing the cross for the first goal and the pass to win a penalty for the second goal in a 2–1 win. Ricketts played in the [[UEFA Europa League]] in a 3–1 defeat against former club Tottenham Hotspur. He was released from Shamrock Rovers in December 2011, after not being offered a new contract.

In March 2012, Ricketts sign a one-season contract with [[Football League One|League One]] side [[Exeter City F.C.|Exeter City]], but left the club before the end of the season after just one substitute appearance. |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20131005040551/http://lesrosbifs.org/confirmed-former-spurs-man-rohan-ricketts-to-leave-ecuador/ |archivedate=5 October 2013 }}</ref>

Ricketts signed for [[PTT Rayong F.C.|PTT Rayong]] of the [[Thai Premier League]] in January 2014,<ref>{{cite web|title=ปตท.เซ็น ทีมชาติเฮติ กับ ริกเกต ก่อนตลาดแข้งนอกปิดเที่ยงคืน |url=http://tl.smmonline.net/news/113720.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141010015501/http://tl.smmonline.net/news/113720.html|url-status=usurped|archive-date=10 October 2014|work=smmonline.com|accessdate=25 February 2014}}</ref> but his contract was terminated by mutual agreement nine months later. In January 2015 he signed for [[Hong Kong Premier League]] side [[Eastern Sports Club]].<ref>{{cite web|title=新加盟球員 |url=http://www.eastern-sportsclub.com/news.php |website=eastern-sportsclub.com |publisher=[[Eastern Sports Club]] |accessdate=8 January 2015 |language=Chinese |date=8 January 2015 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150107151905/http://www.eastern-sportsclub.com/news.php |archivedate=7 January 2015 }}</ref> He then joined [[Bangladesh Premier League (football)|Bangladesh Premier League]] club [[Abahani Limited (Dhaka)|Abahani Limited Dhaka]] in March 2016,<ref>{{cite web|title=First English League player to play in Bangladesh!|url=http://www.observerbd.com/2016/03/24/143138.php|website=observerbd.com|publisher=The Daily Observer|accessdate=13 April 2016|date=24 March 2016}}</ref> returned to England to play for  [[Leatherhead F.C.|Leatherhead]] in November 2016,<ref>{{cite web|title=Squad News ahead of FA Trophy tie vs Chesham United|url=http://www.leatherheadfootballclub.co.uk/news/squad-news-ahead-of-fa-trophy-tie-vs-chesham-unite-1714480.html|website=leatherheadfootballclub.co.uk|publisher=Leatherhead F.C.|accessdate=9 December 2016|date=3 November 2016|archive-date=20 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220104110/http://www.leatherheadfootballclub.co.uk/news/squad-news-ahead-of-fa-trophy-tie-vs-chesham-unite-1714480.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> before leaving the club a month later .<ref>{{cite web|title=Squad News Update|url=http://www.leatherheadfootballclub.co.uk/news/squad-news-update-1731275.html|website=leatherheadfootballclub.co.uk|publisher=Leathered F.C.|accessdate=9 December 2016|date=9 December 2016|archive-date=20 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161220104107/http://www.leatherheadfootballclub.co.uk/news/squad-news-update-1731275.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Ahead of the [[2018 League1 Ontario season]], it was announced that Ricketts had returned to Canada to play for [[Master's Futbol]].<ref>{{cite news|title=League 1 Ontario 2018 Preview|url=http://www.northernstartingeleven.com/league-1-ontario-2018-preview/|accessdate=28 April 2018|work=Northern Starting Eleven|date=27 April 2018|archive-date=29 April 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180429210603/http://www.northernstartingeleven.com/league-1-ontario-2018-preview/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He did not return for the 2019 season.

In 2024, Ricketts returned to [[Ontario Premier League|League1 Ontario]] to play for [[Unionville Milliken SC|Unionville Milliken]]. He made 4 appearances across the [[2024 League1 Ontario season]].

==International career==
Ricketts was capped by [[England national football team|England]] at [[England national under-18 football team|under-18]] and [[England national under-20 football team|under-20]] level.

==Personal life==
During the [[2010 FIFA World Cup]], he co-hosted ''The Hardcore Footy Show: South Africa 2010'' with [[Brendan Dunlop]], on Hardcore Sports Radio, Sirius 98 and was a regular on [[The Sports Network|TSN]] for football. On 24 August 2010, Rohan joined the team of Canada's largest sports radio network, [[CJCL]] (Fan 590). He is currently a sports columnist with them. He also signed to write for online magazine, the Sabotage Times, on 29 August.
<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.flickr.com/photos/27365656@N06/2607792105/ |title=50 on Flickr – Photo Sharing! |publisher=Flickr.com |date=24 June 2008}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web| title=Ricketts | url=http://i25.tinypic.com/24fa8hy.jpg | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110521191516/http://i25.tinypic.com/24fa8hy.jpg | archive-date=2011-05-21}}</ref>{{bcn|date=August 2026}}

In May 2011, Ricketts launched his own (now defunct) online-only magazine, ''Column 10''. The magazine, which includes a host of features on sport, music, film, fashion and more, has included exclusive interviews with football journalist [[Henry Winter]], official FIFA Agent Charles Collymore and [[DJ Spoony]]. The magazine closed in 2015.{{cn|date=December 2024}}

'''Kizito Musampa''' (born 20 July 1977) is a former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[winger (association football)|left winger]].

Musampa had a journeyman career, playing for [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]], [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]], [[Malaga CF|Málaga]], [[Atlético Madrid]] and [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]].<ref>[https://www.vice.com/nl/article/kiki-musampa-geluk-paard/ Kiki Musampa en zijn intense geluk op een paard] vice.com</ref><ref>[https://www.vice.com/nl/article/kiki-musampa-degradatiekraker-derde-klasse/ We volgden Kiki Musampa bij zijn degradatiekraker in de derde klasse] vice.com</ref> Born [[Zaire]], he earned 28 caps representing the Netherlands at under-20 and under-21 levels. He was known for his pace and [[Direct free kick|free-kicks]].<ref name=Korea/>

==Club career==

===Ajax and Bordeaux===
Born in [[Kinshasa]], [[Zaire]], now the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]], Musampa first started off in the [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] youth academy, where he played a total of 31 games in two seasons and scored six goals including a winner scored against [[NAC Breda]], which was the first Ajax goal in the new current stadium, the [[Johan Cruyff Arena]]. He also scored in the quarter-final of the Champions League against Borussia Dortmund in 1996; Ajax went on to win the game 2–0, and went on to the final. 
He subsequently signed for [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]] in 1997 to further his experience and with the intention of being selected for the [[Netherlands national football team|Netherlands national team]] to compete in the [[1998 FIFA World Cup]], although he was ultimately overlooked by then coach [[Guus Hiddink]].

===Málaga and Atlético===
After spending two seasons at the French club, he decided to move on to Spanish club [[Málaga CF|Málaga]], where he played 94 games and scored a total of 22 goals in four seasons. In 2003, he was transferred to [[Atlético Madrid]] for €3 million on a five-year contract, a year before his Málaga contract was due to expire,<ref>{{cite web |title=Atletico capture Musampa |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11838/2267257/atletico-capture-musampa |date=5 June 2003 |access-date=7 January 2014 |publisher=Sky Sports}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Musampa signs contract with Atletico |url=http://espnfc.com/news/story?id=269123 |date=5 June 2003 |access-date=7 January 2014 |publisher=UEFA Official Website}}</ref> in what he viewed as a potentially good career move.<ref>{{cite web |title=Musampa earns Atlético move |url=http://www.uefa.com/footballeurope/news/kind=2/newsid=73220.html |date=5 June 2003 |access-date=17 March 2008 |publisher=UEFA Official Website}}{{dead link|date=March 2025|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> In his first season with the club, he played 26 matches and scored two goals; although, in the following season, he was relegated to the substitutes' bench and only scraped together eight games in 2004.

===Manchester City===
In January 2005, Musampa moved to [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] of the [[Premier League]] on loan after becoming a fringe player at Atlético.<ref>{{cite web |title=Man City seal Musampa loan deal |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/m/man_city/4207751.stm |date=27 January 2005 |access-date=7 January 2014 |publisher=BBC}}</ref> In his first six months, he scored three goals in 14 games; his first City goal was a "spectacular volley" in the last-minute which was the winner against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] and gave [[Stuart Pearce]] his first win as City [[Manager (association football)|manager]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Man City 1-0 Liverpool |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/4403613.stm |date=9 April 2005 |access-date=7 January 2014 |publisher=BBC}}</ref> while he also scored goals against [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]] in a 2–1 victory,<ref>{{cite web |title=Aston Villa 1-2 Man City |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/4501113.stm |date=7 May 2005 |access-date=7 January 2014 |publisher=BBC}}</ref> and an equaliser against [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] which wasn't enough to help City qualify for the [[2005–06 UEFA Cup]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Man City 1-1 Middlesbrough |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/4525109.stm |date=15 May 2005 |access-date=7 January 2014 |publisher=BBC}}</ref>

In June 2005, Musampa agreed up to stay at Manchester City for a second season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Musampa stays at Man City on loan |url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/m/man_city/4611941.stm |date=5 June 2005 |access-date=7 January 2014 |publisher=BBC}}</ref> He started the new season as a regular first team player, but lost his first team place in December, after which he played irregularly, with the majority of his appearances being in central midfield. At the end of the 2005–06 season, he returned to Atlético.

===Trabzonspor and AZ===
On 30 August 2006, Musampa signed a three-year contract for Turkish club [[Trabzonspor]] on a free transfer.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/competitions/uefacup/news/kind=1/newsid=451130.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080309013653/http://www.uefa.com/competitions/uefacup/news/kind=1/newsid=451130.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=9 March 2008|title=Musampa touches down in Trabzon|date=30 August 2006|access-date=17 March 2008|publisher=[[UEFA]]}}</ref>

After being released from Trabzonspor, Musampa trained with [[Premier League|English Premiership]] side [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]]<ref>[http://www.safc.com/index.php?page_id=13285 Kiki hopes for run-out /<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> for a period but ultimately was not signed by the club.<ref>[http://www.safc.com/index.php?page_id=13343 No Musampa deal /<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> After returning to the Netherlands, Musampa trained with [[Eredivisie]] outfit [[AZ (football club)|AZ]]. In November 2007, he signed a contract at the club for the rest of the season, but he was released from his contract on 1 January 2008.

===FC Seoul===
After an unsuccessful trial with [[Toronto FC]] of [[Major League Soccer]] he signed a two-year contract with [[K-League]] side [[FC Seoul]] in March 2008.<ref name=Korea>{{Cite web|url=https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/www/news/special/2008/03/136_21448.html|title = FC Seoul Acquires Musampa|date = 26 March 2008}}</ref> His stay in South Korea was brief, as he made just three league appearances and two [[Hauzen Cup|League Cup]] appearances for the club before the two parties agreed to mutually terminate his contract in June 2008.

===Willem II===
On 14 March 2009, Musampa returned to professional football signing for [[Willem II Tilburg|Willem II]] in the Netherlands.<ref>[http://www.imscouting.com/global_news_item.aspx?id=1545 Willem II sign Kiki Musampa] {{dead link|date=January 2018|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

===Metz===
In September 2009, the winger went on trial with French side [[FC Metz|Metz]] and scored one goal in a friendly match, but the club did not sign him in the end.<ref>[http://www.sofoot.com/kiki-musampa-a-l-essai-a-metz-116314-news.html Kiki Musampa à l’essai à Metz] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090906091707/http://www.sofoot.com/kiki-musampa-a-l-essai-a-metz-116314-news.html |date=6 September 2009 }}</ref>

He eventually{{when|date=June 2026}} announced his retirement from professional football.

==International career==
Musampa was a member of the Netherlands U20 team at the [[1995 FIFA World Youth Championship]], playing all three group matches, the team did not proceed past the group stage. Musampa went on to be a key player for the [[Netherlands national under-21 football team|Netherlands Under-21s]] and achieved 25 caps, scoring 8 goals, he is currently in the [[Netherlands national under-21 football team#Most capped players|top 10 players]] for both caps and goals at that level. His form whilst on loan at Manchester City earned him a call-up to the [[Netherlands national football team|Netherlands]] squad to play [[Romania national football team|Romania]] and [[Finland national football team|Finland]] but he played in neither game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Musampa named by Oranje |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11667/2335677/ |access-date=7 January 2014 |publisher=Sky Sports}}</ref>
