{{cite news|title=L'OM PUISSANCE 6|url=https://sport24.lefigaro.fr/football/ligue-1/Homes-Clubs/marseille/actualites/l-om-puissance-6-116994|publisher=Le Figaro|language=fr|date=8 February 2008|access-date=29 May 2021}} Grandin's debut for Marseille came on 9 February 2008 against [[OGC Nice|Nice]] and started the match, playing 89 minutes before being substituted, in a 2–0 win.{{cite news|title=Nice 0-2 OM : comme des guerriers|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/2982/nice-0-2-om-comme-des-guerriers.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=10 February 2008|access-date=29 May 2021}}Mbr>{{cite news|title=PREMIÈRE RÉUSSIE POUR GRANDIN|url=https://sport24.lefigaro.fr/football/coupe-de-france/actualites/premiere-reussie-pour-grandin-115589|publisher=Le Figaro|language=fr|date=11 February 2008|access-date=29 May 2021}} On 17 May 2008, the last day of the season against [[RC Strasbourg Alsace|Strasbourg]], he came on as a substitute after an injury to striker [[Mamadou Niang]], and sent his pass set up to Nasri to score as Marseille won 4–3 and so qualified for the preliminary round of the Champions League.{{cite news|title=OM 4-3 Strasbourg : la tactique et les joueurs|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/3148/om-4-3-strasbourg-la-tactique-et-les-joueurs.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=17 May 2008|access-date=29 May 2021}} At the end of the 2007–08 season, Grandin made eight league appearances, most of them as a substitute.{{cite news|title=OM 2-1 PSG : la tactique et les joueurs|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/2994/om-2-1-psg-la-tactique-et-les-joueurs.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=18 February 2008|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=OM-Auxerre : discussion tactique|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/news-3896/om-auxerre-discussion-tactique.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=1 March 2008|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=Bilan de l'OM version 2007-08 : les joueurs (3/3)|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/3184/bilan-de-l-om-version-2007-08-les-joueurs33.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=1 June 2008|access-date=29 May 2021}} In the [[2008–09 Ligue 1|2008–09 season]], Grandin was in the starting line-up in the first game of the season at [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]], scoring Marseille's fourth goal in stoppage time, in a 4–4 draw.{{cite news|title=Rennes 4-4 OM : la tactique et les joueurs|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/3310/rennes-4-4-om-la-tactique-et-les-joueurs.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=11 August 2008|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=Grandin : "pour le moral, c'est bien, mais..."|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/news-4777/grandin-pour-le-moral-c-est-bien-mais.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=11 August 2008|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=LES PARADOXES DE L'OM|url=https://sport24.lefigaro.fr/football/ligue-1/Homes-Clubs/marseille/actualites/les-paradoxes-de-l-om-180894|publisher=Le Figaro|language=fr|date=11 August 2008|access-date=29 May 2021}} On 13 August 2008, he made his European debut in the [[2008–09 UEFA Champions League qualifying rounds|third qualifying round]] of the [[2008–09 UEFA Champions League|Champions League]], in a single-goal victory at Norwegian side [[SK Brann|Brann]].{{cite web|title=UEFA – Grandin|url=http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/clubs/player=98520/index.html|publisher=[[UEFA]]|access-date=12 August 2010|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100827222645/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/clubs/player=98520/index.html|archive-date=27 August 2010|url-status=dead}}{{cite news|title=L'OM SUR LA BONNE VOIE|url=https://sport24.lefigaro.fr/football/ligue-des-champions/actualites/l-om-sur-la-bonne-voie-181414|publisher=Le Figaro|language=fr|date=13 August 2008|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=Brann Bergen 0-1 OM : la tactique et les joueurs|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/3314/brann-bergen-0-1-om-la-tactique-et-les-joueurs.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=15 August 2008|access-date=29 May 2021}} Four days later on 17 August 2008, Grandin scored his second goal for the club, in a 4–0 win against [[AJ Auxerre|Auxerre]].{{cite news|title=Le message de l'OM|url=https://www.lefigaro.fr/football/2008/08/17/02003-20080817ARTSPO00221-live-marseille-auxerre.php|publisher=Le Figaro|language=fr|date=17 August 2008|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=Ligue 1 (2 e journée). Marseille - Auxerre : 4-0 OM : huit buts en deux matchs!|url=https://www.letelegramme.fr/ar/viewarticle1024.php?aaaammjj=20080818&article=3642767&type=ar|publisher=Le Telegramme|language=fr|date=17 August 2008|access-date=29 May 2021}} In the return leg against Brann, he helped Marseille win 2–1 to advance to the next round of the UEFA Cup tournament.{{cite news|title=DANS LA COUR DES GRANDS|url=https://sport24.lefigaro.fr/football/ligue-des-champions/actualites/dans-la-cour-des-grands-186958|publisher=Le Figaro|language=fr|date=28 August 2008|access-date=29 May 2021}} However, Grandin then fell out of favour into the plans of [[Eric Gerets]] and lack of playing time in Marseille.{{cite news|title=Le Havre 0-1 OM : la tactique et les joueurs|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/3330/le-havre-0-1-om-la-tactique-et-les-joueurs.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=26 August 2008|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=Plusieurs incertains pour Le Mans|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/news-5113/plusieurs-incertains-pour-le-mans.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=26 September 2008|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=Grandin ne pense qu'à l'OM|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/news-5228/grandin-ne-pense-qu-a-l-om.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=10 October 2008|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=Elliot Grandin : "je me sens bien" - Source: Footmarseille.com|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/news-5236/elliot-grandin-je-me-sens-bien.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=11 October 2008|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=Bilan à la mi-saison : les joueurs|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/3548/bilan-a-la-mi-saison-les-joueurs.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=2 January 2009|access-date=29 May 2021}} As a result, he was linked a move away from the club in the January [[transfer window]], with clubs, such as, [[Grenoble Foot 38|Grenoble]], [[Le Havre AC|Le Havre]] and Strasbourg were interested in signing him.{{cite news|title=Grandin vers Grenoble|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/3515/grandin-vers-grenoble.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=20 December 2008|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=Grandin vers Le Havre?|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/3525/grandin-vers-le-havre.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=23 December 2008|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=Grandin : le HAC, le RCS ou l'OM?|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/news-6065/grandin-le-hac-le-rcs-ou-l-om.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=23 December 2008|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=Grandin et Samassa surpris?|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/news-6088/grandin-et-samassa-surpris.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=30 December 2008|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=Grandin priorité du club doyen?|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/news-6215/grandin-priorite-du-club-doyen.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=14 January 2009|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=Grandin prêté mais où?|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/news-6373/grandin-prete-mais-ou.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=29 January 2009|access-date=29 May 2021}} By the time Grandin departed from Marseille, he made a further eight appearances, scoring twice. Grandin joined fellow Ligue 1 side [[Grenoble Foot 38|Grenoble]] on loan for five months on 30 January 2009.{{cite web|title=GF38 The Attack|url=http://www.gf38.fr/fr/toute-l-actualite-du-gf38-le-gf38-d-attaque.2.0.ida.704.html#actu_704|publisher=[[Grenoble Foot 38]]|access-date=12 August 2010|language=French|date=30 January 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090203160712/http://www.gf38.fr/fr/toute-l-actualite-du-gf38-le-gf38-d-attaque.2.0.ida.704.html#actu_704|archive-date=3 February 2009}}{{cite news|title=Grandin prêté à Grenoble|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/3609/grandin-prete-a-grenoble.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=30 January 2009|access-date=29 May 2021}} He made his debut on 7 February 2009, starting the whole game, in a goalless home draw with Valenciennes.{{cite news|title=A chacun son point|url=https://www.lefigaro.fr/football/2009/02/08/02003-20090208ARTSPO00148-suivez-le-multiplex.php|publisher=Le Figaro|language=fr|date=8 February 2009|access-date=29 May 2021}} Grandin became a first team regular for the club, rotating in playing either midfield and striker positions.{{cite news|title= Grandin veut s'imposer au GF38|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/news-6487/grandin-veut-s-imposer-au-gf38.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=8 February 2009|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=Grandin souhaite revenir à l'OM|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/news-7007/grandin-souhaite-revenir-a-l-om.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=30 March 2009|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=OM - Grenoble : pas de Grandin|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/news-7126/om-grenoble-pas-de-grandin.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=11 April 2009|access-date=29 May 2021}} He made a total of eight appearances before returning to Marseille at the end of the season.{{cite news|title=Grenoble renvoie Grandin à la maison|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/news-7708/grenoble-renvoie-grandin-a-la-maison.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=6 June 2009|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=Bilan des prêtés : Elliot Grandin|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/news-7717/bilan-des-pretes-elliot-grandin.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=7 June 2009|access-date=29 May 2021}} Having been told by new manager [[Didier Deschamps]] of being in a new plan ahead of the [[2009–10 Ligue 1|new season]], Grandin was linked a move away from Marseille, with [[Standard Liège]], [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]] and [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] interested in signing him in the summer transfer window.{{cite news|title=GRANDIN POUSSÉ DEHORS|url=https://sport24.lefigaro.fr/football/transferts/fil-info/grandin-pousse-dehors-280403|publisher=Le Figaro|language=fr|date=15 July 2009|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=Grandin à Sheffield Wednesday?|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/3873/grandin-a-sheffield-wednesday.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=22 July 2009|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=Birmingham City: Two new names in the frame for moves to Blues|url=https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/birmingham-city-two-new-names-98774|publisher=Birmingham Mail|date=26 July 2009|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=LE STANDARD VEUT GRANDIN|url=https://sport24.lefigaro.fr/football/transferts/fil-info/le-standard-veut-grandin-277396|publisher=La Figaro|language=fr|date=24 July 2009|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=Христо Янев: Бардон, Нифлор и Барт са по-добри от Гранден|url=https://football24.bg/novina/31984-hristo-yanev-bardon-niflor-i-bart-sa-po-dobri-ot-granden|publisher=Football 24.bg|language=bg|date=23 January 2010|access-date=29 May 2021|archive-date=26 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210526200920/https://football24.bg/novina/31984-hristo-yanev-bardon-niflor-i-bart-sa-po-dobri-ot-granden|url-status=dead}} On 18 August 2009, it was reported by ''[[L'Équipe]]'' that he would go on trial in England with [[Premier League]] club [[Stoke City F.C.|Stoke City]] five days later and that Stoke had first option on the player for around €1 million.{{cite news|title=Marseille winger Elliot Grandin to undergo trial at Stoke City|url=http://www.imscouting.com/global-news-article/marseille-winger-elliot-grandin-to-undergo-trial-a/2865/|publisher=IM Scouting|date=18 August 2009|access-date=2 May 2012}}
{{cite news|title=STOKE ESSAYE GRANDIN|url=https://sport24.lefigaro.fr/football/transferts/fil-info/stoke-essaye-grandin-291151|publisher=Le Figaro|language=fr|date=24 August 2009|access-date=29 May 2021}} After returning to France, Marseille released Grandin from his contract on 2 September.{{cite web|title=Elliot Grandin quitte l'OM|url=http://www.om.net/fr/Saison/101005/Actualites/41757/Elliot_Grandin_quitte_l_OM|publisher=[[Olympique de Marseille]]|language=French|access-date=12 August 2010|date=2 September 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140221190912/http://www.om.net/fr/Saison/101005/Actualites/41757/Elliot_Grandin_quitte_l_OM|archive-date=21 February 2014|url-status=dead}} The club later called him as one of the worst signings.{{cite news|title=Mercato hivernal : les pires recrues de l'OM|url=http://www.footmarseille.com/news-40322/mercato-hivernal-les-pires-recrues-de-l-om.html|publisher=Foot Marseille|language=fr|date=30 December 2017|access-date=29 May 2021}} ===CSKA Sofia=== On 5 January 2010, Grandin was reportedly in negotiations with Romanian [[Liga I]] club [[FC Rapid București|Rapid Bucharest]], and was believed to be about to sign for the club;{{cite web|title=Exclusiv / Grandin, primul transfer al Rapidului|url=http://rapidisti.gsp.ro/stiri/18317/exclusiv--grandin-primul-transfer-al-rapidului.htm|publisher=rapidisti.ro|access-date=12 August 2010|language=Romanian|date=6 January 2010|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100108083229/http://rapidisti.gsp.ro/stiri/18317/exclusiv--grandin-primul-transfer-al-rapidului.htm|archive-date=8 January 2010|url-status=dead}}{{cite news|title=Ţinta Rapidului: Grandin = Boya|url=https://www.gsp.ro/fotbal/liga-1/inta-rapidului-grandin-boya-170208.html|publisher=Gazeta Sporturilor|language=ro|date=8 January 2010|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=Francezul Grandin anunţă Rapidul că vrea mai mult!|url=https://www.gsp.ro/fotbal/liga-1/francezul-grandin-anunta-rapidul-ca-vrea-mai-mult-170726.html|publisher=Gazeta Sporturilor|language=ro|date=11 January 2010|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=Гранден: Не искам и да чувам за Румъния|url=https://football24.bg/novina/31781-granden-ne-iskam-i-da-chuvam-za-rumyniya|publisher=Football 24.bg|language=bg|date=17 January 2010|access-date=29 May 2021|archive-date=26 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210526200845/https://football24.bg/novina/31781-granden-ne-iskam-i-da-chuvam-za-rumyniya|url-status=dead}} however, on 20 January he signed an 18-month contract with Bulgarian [[Bulgarian A Professional Football Group|A PFG]] club [[PFC CSKA Sofia|CSKA Sofia]], after they gave him an improved offer that gave him 30% of any future sale proceeds.{{cite news|title=EXCLUSIV / Grandin: "Nu vreau să vin în România!"|url=https://www.gsp.ro/fotbal/liga-1/exclusiv-grandin-nu-vreau-sa-vin-in-romania-171870.html|publisher=Gazeta Sporturilor|language=ro|date=17 January 2010|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=Скандалджията Гранден подписа за 6000 евро|url=https://football24.bg/novina/31874-skandaldzhiyata-granden-podpisa-za-6000-evro|publisher=Football 24.bg|language=bg|date=20 January 2010|access-date=29 May 2021|archive-date=26 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210526200845/https://football24.bg/novina/31874-skandaldzhiyata-granden-podpisa-za-6000-evro|url-status=dead}}
{{cite news|title=Гранден - момчето на шефа|url=https://football24.bg/novina/32100-granden-momcheto-na-shefa|publisher=Football 24.bg|language=bg|date=26 January 2010|access-date=29 May 2021|archive-date=26 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210526201014/https://football24.bg/novina/32100-granden-momcheto-na-shefa|url-status=dead}} However, Grandin suffered a setback with an injury during the winter break and was sidelined for a month.{{cite news|title=Травмата на Гранден не е сериозна|url=https://football24.bg/novina/32467-travmata-na-granden-ne-e-seriozna|publisher=Football 24.bg|language=bg|date=2 February 2010|access-date=29 May 2021|archive-date=26 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210526201125/https://football24.bg/novina/32467-travmata-na-granden-ne-e-seriozna|url-status=dead}}
{{cite news|title=Гранден отново контузен|url=https://football24.bg/novina/33128-granden-otnovo-kontuze|publisher=Football 24.bg|language=bg|date=18 February 2010|access-date=29 May 2021}}{{Dead link|date=October 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}
{{cite news|title=Гранден бил скатавка и единак|url=https://football24.bg/novina/33174-granden-bil-skatavka-i-edinak|publisher=Football 24.bg|language=bg|date=20 February 2010|access-date=29 May 2021|archive-date=26 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210526200634/https://football24.bg/novina/33174-granden-bil-skatavka-i-edinak|url-status=dead}} He made his competitive debut for the club on 13 March 2010 against [[FC Sportist Svoge|Sportist Svoge]], scoring the opening goal and providing an assist in a 4–1 win.{{cite news|title=Гранден дебютира - ясна е групата на ЦСКА за Спортист|url=https://football24.bg/novina/34009-granden-debiutira-yasna-e-grupata-na-cska-za-sportist|publisher=Football 24.bg|language=bg|date=13 March 2010|access-date=29 May 2021|archive-date=26 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210526200532/https://football24.bg/novina/34009-granden-debiutira-yasna-e-grupata-na-cska-za-sportist|url-status=dead}}
{{cite news|title=ЦСКА мачка Своге, страхотен Гранден (ВИДЕО)|url=https://football24.bg/novina/34039-cska-machka-svoge-strahoten-granden-video|publisher=Football 24.bg|language=bg|date=13 March 2010|access-date=29 May 2021|archive-date=26 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210526200530/https://football24.bg/novina/34039-cska-machka-svoge-strahoten-granden-video|url-status=dead}} Grandin then scored his second goal for CSKA Sofia, in a 4–2 win against [[OFC Sliven 2000|OFC Sliven]] on 10 April 2010.{{cite news|title=ЦСКА най-после би, Про. Бг скри мача от зрителите|url=https://football24.bg/novina/35227-cska-naj-posle-bi-pro-bg-skri-macha-ot-zritelite|publisher=Football 24.bg|language=bg|date=10 April 2010|access-date=29 May 2021|archive-date=26 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210526200101/https://football24.bg/novina/35227-cska-naj-posle-bi-pro-bg-skri-macha-ot-zritelite|url-status=dead}} He scored two goals in two matches between 24 April 2010 and 2 May 2010 against [[PFC Slavia Sofia|Slavia Sofia]] and [[FC Lokomotiv 1929 Sofia|Lokomotiv Sofia]].{{cite news|title=Ренесансът в "червено" продължава|url=https://football24.bg/novina/35969-renesansyt-v-cherveno-prodylzhava|publisher=Football 24.bg|language=bg|date=24 April 2010|access-date=29 May 2021|archive-date=26 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210526201520/https://football24.bg/novina/35969-renesansyt-v-cherveno-prodylzhava|url-status=dead}}
{{cite news|title=ЦСКА в Лига Европа след разгром над Локо (София)|url=https://football24.bg/novina/36334-cska-v-liga-evropa-sled-razgrom-nad-loko-sofiya|publisher=Football 24.bg|language=bg|date=2 May 2010|access-date=29 May 2021|archive-date=26 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210526204559/https://football24.bg/novina/36334-cska-v-liga-evropa-sled-razgrom-nad-loko-sofiya|url-status=dead}} Grandin became a first team regular for the club, and helped CSKA Sofia finish second.{{cite news|title=Левски - ЦСКА: куците срещу сакатите|url=https://football24.bg/novina/34513-levski-cska-kucite-sreshtu-sakatite|publisher=Football 24.bg|language=bg|date=26 March 2010|access-date=29 May 2021|archive-date=26 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210526200712/https://football24.bg/novina/34513-levski-cska-kucite-sreshtu-sakatite|url-status=dead}}

{{cite news|title=ЦСКА позлатява Гранден при титла|url=https://football24.bg/novina/34595-cska-pozlatyava-granden-pri-titla|publisher=Football 24.bg|language=bg|date=28 March 2010|access-date=29 May 2021|archive-date=26 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210526200255/https://football24.bg/novina/34595-cska-pozlatyava-granden-pri-titla|url-status=dead}}

|url=http://www.blackpoolfc.co.uk/page/NewsDetail/0,,10432~2118202,00.html |title=Four New Faces At Bloomfield Road |date=11 August 2010 |publisher=[[Blackpool F.C.]] |access-date=11 August 2010 web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/b/blackpool/8904013.stm|title= Blackpool sign quartet ahead of Premier League debut |publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=11 August 2010|access-date=11 August 2010}} Three days after signing for the club, he made his debut as Blackpool made their bow in the Premier League and set up a goal for [[Marlon Harewood]], who scored twice in a 4–0 win over [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]] at the [[DW Stadium]].{{cite news|title=Wigan Athletic 0–4 Blackpool|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/8904972.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|date=14 August 2010|access-date=29 May 2021}} Since joining the club, Grandin was involved in the first team, playing in the midfield position and spoke positively of manager [[Ian Holloway]]'s lead|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/liverpool-0-2-blackpool-charlie-adam-3348276|publisher=Daily Mirror|date=3 October 2010|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=West Ham 0-0 Blackpool - Hammers denied two penalties in goalless draw|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/west-ham-0-0-blackpool---3347006|publisher=Daily Mirror|date=13 November 2010|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=Elliot Grandin: 'Holloway's mad, he likes to joke around – but he's been very important for me'|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/profiles/elliot-grandin-holloways-mad-he-likes-to-joke-around-ndash-but-hes-been-very-important-for-me-2201259.html|work=The Independent|date=2 February 2011|access-date=2 May 2012}} He then played a role in two separate matches against [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] on 1 November 2010 and then against [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] on 27 November 2010 by assisting both matches that saw Blackpool earn a draw and win respectively.{{cite news|title=Blackpool 2–1 West Bromwich Albion|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/9136516.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|date=1 November 2010|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=Bolton Wanderers 2–2 Blackpool|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/9221083.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|date=27 November 2010|access-date=29 May 2021}} However, Grandin suffered a hamstring injury during a match against [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] on 28 December 2010 and was substituted in the 19th minute, as the club lost 2–0.{{cite news|title=Sunderland 0–2 Blackpool|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/9317216.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|date=28 December 2010|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=GRANDIN OUT DEUX SEMAINES|url=https://sport24.lefigaro.fr/football/etranger/angleterre/fil-info/grandin-out-deux-semaines-440663|publisher=Le Figaro|language=fr|date=31 December 2010|access-date=29 May 2021}} But he made his return to the starting line–up against [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] on 12 January 2011 and played 64 minutes before being substituted, in a 2–1 win.{{cite news|title=Blackpool 2–1 Liverpool|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/9345343.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|date=12 January 2011|access-date=29 May 2021}} On 12 February 2011, Grandin scored his first goal for the club in a 1–1 home draw with [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]].[http://www.blackpoolfc.co.uk/page/NewsDetail/0,10432~2291955,00.html "GRANDIN HAPPY WITH FIRST STRIKE"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110216055717/http://www.blackpoolfc.co.uk/page/NewsDetail/0%2C%2C10432~2291955%2C00.html |date=16 February 2011 }} - Blackpool F.C.'s official website, 12 February 2011. Shortly after, Grandin suffered a hamstring injury that saw him miss two matches.{{cite news|title=Ian Holloway relieved to end Blackpool's run of five straight defeats with point against Aston Villa|url=https://www.goal.com/en-gb/news/2896/premier-league/2011/02/12/2349710/ian-holloway-relieved-to-end-blackpools-run-of-five-straight|publisher=Goal.com|date=12 February 2011|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|title=Blackpool star men out of Chelsea clash|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/blackpool-chelsea-team-news-top-3331158|publisher=Daily Mirror|date=4 March 2011|access-date=29 May 2021}} He then made his return to the starting line–up against [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] on 19 March 2011 and played 66 minutes before being substituted, in a 2–2 draw.{{cite news|title=Blackburn Rovers 2–2 Blackpool|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_prem/9426550.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|date=19 March 2011|access-date=29 May 2021}} However, Blackpool were relegated to the [[EFL Championship|Championship]] after losing 4–2 against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] in the last game of the season.{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/13444164|title=Manchester United 4–2 Blackpool|publisher=BBC Sport|date=22 May 2011|access-date=29 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110523075914/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/13444164.stm|archive-date=23 May 2011|url-status=live}} At the end of the 2010–11 season, Grandin made twenty–four appearances and scoring once in all competitions. In the 2011–12 season, Grandin made three starts for Blackpool, as the club earned six points in the first two league matches of the season.{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14337494|title=Hull City 0–1 Blackpool|publisher=BBC Sport|date=6 August 2011|access-date=29 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110806051036/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/14337494.stm|archive-date=6 August 2011|url-status=live}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/14435081|title=Blackpool 2–1 Peterborough United|publisher=BBC Sport|date=14 August 2011|access-date=29 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110815160645/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/14435081.stm|archive-date=15 August 2011|url-status=live}}
{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_div_1/14471691.stm|title=Blackpool 0–1 Derby County|publisher=BBC Sport|date=18 August 2011|access-date=29 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110817035559/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_div_1/14471691.stm|archive-date=17 August 2011|url-status=live}} However, he suffered an injury on his toe that kept him out for four weeks.{{cite news|title=Grandin suffers toe setback|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11095/7214078/|publisher=Sky Sport|date=30 September 2011|access-date=30 September 2011|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141110175017/http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11095/7214078|archive-date=10 November 2014|url-status=dead}} After missing 17 games through injury, Grandin made his return to the first team against [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]] on 26 December 2011, coming on as a 63rd-minute substitute, in a 3–1 win.{{cite news|title=Grandin set for Blackpool return|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11728/7358061/grandin-set-for-blackpool-return|publisher=Sky Sports|date=7 December 2011|access-date=29 May 2021}}
{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_div_1/16240508.stm|title=Barnsley 1–3 Blackpool|publisher=BBC Sport|date=26 December 2011|access-date=29 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111229202706/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_div_1/16240508.stm|archive-date=29 December 2011|url-status=live}} Two weeks later on 14 January 2012, he scored his first goal of the season and later set up Blackpool's second goal of the game, in a 2–2 draw against [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]].{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16453658|title=Ispwich Town 2–2 Blackpool|publisher=BBC Sport|date=14 January 2012|access-date=29 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120117162718/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/16453658.stm|archive-date=17 January 2012|url-status=live}} In a follow–up match against Crystal Palace, Grandin scored his second goal of the season, in a 2–1 win.{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16559765|title=Blackpool 2–1 Crystal Palace|publisher=BBC Sport|date=21 January 2012|access-date=29 May 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120124135027/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/16559765.stm|archive-date=24 January 2012|url-status=live}} By the time he was loaned out to OGC Nice, Grandin went on to make seven appearances and scoring two times in all competitions. books|url=http://www.blackpoolgazette.co.uk/sport/blackpool-fc/grandin-still-on-blackpool-s-books-1-4577164|publisher=Blackpool Gazette|date=23 May 2012|access-date=9 August web|url=https://www.blackpoolfc.co.uk/news/2012/august/report-blackpool-1-morecambe-2/|title=Report: Blackpool 1 Morecambe 2|publisher=Blackpool F.C.|date=12 August 2012|access-date=29 May Middlesbrough|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/19554081|publisher=BBC Sport|date=18 September 2012|access-date=9 August 2013}} Shortly after, Grandin was not included for the next five news|title=Midfielder could have future, says Holloway|url=http://www.blackpoolgazette.co.uk/sport/blackpool-fc/midfielder-could-have-future-says-holloway-1-5013108|publisher=Blackpool Gazette|date=11 2013|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141019195936/http://www.blackpoolgazette.co.uk/sport/blackpool-fc/midfielder-could-have-future-says-holloway-1-5013108|archive-date=19 October {{cite web|url=https://www.blackpoolfc.co.uk/news/2012/october/grandin-determined-to-build-on-draw/|title=Grandin Determined To Build On Draw|publisher=Blackpool F.C.|date=23 October 2012|access-date=29 May 2021|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210527200457/https://www.blackpoolfc.co.uk/news/2012/october/grandin-determined-to-build-on-draw/|archive-date=27 May 2021|url-status=live}} This was followed up by scoring his third goal of the game, in a 1–1 draw against [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]].{{cite news|title=Blackpool 1-1 Brighton|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20014351|publisher=BBC Sport|date=27 October 2012|access-date=9 August 2013}} However, the departure of Holloway led to the player's first team opportunities being reduced and appeared an unused substitute for the remainder of the matches played.{{cite web|url=https://www.efl.com/news/2012/november/appleton-reveals-grandin-omission/|title=Appleton reveals Grandin omission|publisher=The Football League|date=29 November 2012|access-date=29 May 2021|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210527204004/https://www.efl.com/news/2012/november/appleton-reveals-grandin-omission/|archive-date=27 May 2021|url-status=live}}
{{cite web|url=https://www.blackpoolfc.co.uk/news/2013/february/team-news-two-changes/|title=Team News: Two Changes|publisher=Blackpool F.C.|date=23 February 2013|access-date=29 May 2021|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210527195604/https://www.blackpoolfc.co.uk/news/2013/february/team-news-two-changes/|archive-date=27 May 2021|url-status=live}} At the end of the 2012–13 season, he went on to make thirteen appearances and scoring three times in all competitions. Following this, Grandin was released by the club.{{cite news|title=Thomas Ince & Matt Phillips: Blackpool take up one-year options|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22465800|publisher=BBC Sport|date=9 May 2013|access-date=31 July 2013}} ====Loan to Nice==== Grandin returned to his native country by signing a season-long loan deal with [[OGC Nice]] on 28 January 2012.{{cite web|url=https://www.ogcnice.com/fr/actualite/7380/elliot-grandin-s-engage-avec-l-ogc-nice|title=ELLIOT GRANDIN S'ENGAGE AVEC L'OGC NICE|publisher=OGC Nice|language=fr|date=28 January 2012|access-date=29 May 2021|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210526191001/https://www.ogcnice.com/fr/actualite/7380/elliot-grandin-s-engage-avec-l-ogc-nice|archive-date=26 May 2021|url-status=dead}}
[https://web.archive.org/web/20220607104347/https://www.blackpoolfc.co.uk/page/NewsDetail/0,10432~2591696,00.html "GRANDIN JOINS NICE ON LOAN"] - Blackpool F.C.'s official website, 28 January 2012. Upon joining the club, he said: "I have had great experiences abroad, in Bulgaria and in England, but I really wanted to come back to France. I felt like I didn't finish the job here. So when the Nice opportunity presented itself, I did everything to make it happen. It is a real challenge for me, I really want to help the club."{{cite web|url=https://www.ogcnice.com/fr/actualite/7390/elliot-grandin-un-vrai-challenge|title=ELLIOT GRANDIN : " UN VRAI CHALLENGE "|publisher=OGC Nice|language=fr|date=30 January 2012|access-date=29 May 2021|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210526191251/https://www.ogcnice.com/fr/actualite/7390/elliot-grandin-un-vrai-challenge|archive-date=26 May 2021|url-status=dead}} It was later revealed that a family factor was the reason Grandin returned to his native country to resolve his problem there.{{cite web|url=https://www.blackpoolfc.co.uk/news/2012/july/grandin-happy-at-blackpool/|title=Grandin Happy At Blackpool|publisher=Blackpool F.C.|date=9 July 2012|access-date=29 May 2021|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20210527195834/https://www.blackpoolfc.co.uk/news/2012/july/grandin-happy-at-blackpool/|archive-date=27 May 2021|url-status=live}} Grandin made his debut for OGC Nice, starting the whole game, in a 2–1 loss against his former club, Marseille on 1 February 2012.{{cite web|url=https://www.ogcnice.com/fr/actualite/7393/marseille-2-1-nice|title=MARSEILLE 2-1 NICE|publisher=OGC Nice|language=fr|date=1 February 2012|access-date=29 May Blackpool=== On 6 February 2014, Grandin returned to Blackpool on a deal until the end of the [[2013–14 Football League Championship|2013–14]] season after leaving Crystal Palace at the end of Following his return, he said moving back to the club felt like home and revealed that interim manager [[Barry Ferguson]] played a role of giving him a chance.{{cite web|url=http://www.blackpoolfc.co.uk/news/article/grandin-im-back-home-1343869.aspx|title=Grandin: I'm Back Home|publisher=Blackpool FC|access-date=13 August 2014|date=6 February Town|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/26796261|publisher=BBC Sport|date=5 April 2014|access-date=13 August 2014}} However, he found his first team opportunities limited and found his playing Following this, Blackpool opted not to offer him a new contract.{{cite web|url=http://www.blackpoolfc.co.uk/news/article/retained-list-201314-1554900.aspx|title=Retained List|publisher=[[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]]|access-date=13 August 2014|date=16 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140811194952/http://www.blackpoolfc.co.uk/news/article/retained-list-201314-1554900.aspx |archive-date=11 August 2014|url-status=unfit}} Following his departure from Blackpool, he was linked with a move to Championship clubs, including a return to Blackpool.{{cite news|title=Transfer news: Elliot Grandin wanted by three Championship clubs|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11065/9381973/transfer-news-elliot-grandin-wanted-by-three-championship-clubs|publisher=Sky Sports|date=21 July 2014|access-date=13 August 2014}} ===Later career=== After leaving Blackpool, Grandin moved to Romania, where he joined [[FC Astra Giurgiu|Astra Giurgiu]] on 15 August 2014.{{cite news|title=VIDEO Astra a transferat un jucător dorit de Rapid » Fotbalistul a jucat în Premier League şi în Ligue 1|url=http://www.gsp.ro/fotbal/liga-1/video-astra-a-transferat-un-jucator-dorit-de-rapid-fotbalistul-a-jucat-in-premier-league-si-in-ligue-1-432238.html|publisher=Gazeta Sporturilor|language=ro|date=15 August 2014|access-date=29 May 2021}} Grandin made his debut for the club against Rapid Bucharest on 24 August 2014, coming on as a 74th-minute substitute and scored his first goal for Astra Giurgiu, in a 2–0 win.{{cite news|title=VIDEO Rapid - Astra 0-2. Calificare istorică în grupele UEFA Europa League!|url=https://www.digisport.ro/live-text/video-astra-lyon-0-1-calificare-istorica-in-grupele-uefa-europa-league-290425|publisher=Digi Sport|language=ro|date=28 August 2014|access-date=29 May 2021}}

{{cite news|title=Επιστροφή στις νίκες|url=https://dialogos.com.cy/epistrofi-stis-nikes/|publisher=Haravgi|language=el|date=15 January 2017|access-date=29 May 2021}} A month later on 18 February 2017, he scored his first goal for Ermis Aradippou, having come on as an 83rd-minute substitute, in a 4–0 win.{{cite news|title=Τεσσάρα με Μασίνουα|url=https://dialogos.com.cy/tessara-me-masinoua/|publisher=Haravgi|language=el|date=18 February 2017|access-date=29 May 2021}} In a follow–up match against [[AEK Larnaca FC|AEK Larnaca]], Grandin set up two goals for the club, as they lost 3–2.{{cite news|title=Τα χρειάστηκε|url=https://dialogos.com.cy/ta-chriastike/|publisher=Haravgi|language=el|date=26 February 2017|access-date=29 May 2021}} He later scored two more goals for Ermis Aradippou, coming against [[Doxa Katokopias FC|Doxa Katokopias]] and [[Ethnikos Achna FC|Ethnikos Achna]].{{cite news|title=Έριξε πεντάρα η Δόξα|url=https://dialogos.com.cy/erixe-pentara-i-doxa/|publisher=Haravgi|language=el|date=22 April 2017|access-date=29 May 2021}}

Martigues perd du terrain, le quatuor de tête assure|url=https://www.footamateur.fr/national-2-martigues-perd-terrain-quatuor-de-tete-assure/|publisher=Foot Amateur|language=fr|date=3 February 2018|access-date=29 May 2021}} At the end of the 2017–18 season, Grandin went on to make nine appearances in all competitions for Étoile Fréjus Saint-Raphaël. '''Gaizka Larrazabal Goikoetxea''' (born 17 December 1997) is a Spanish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Defender (association football)#Wing-back|right wing-back]] or [[Midfielder#Winger|right winger]] for {{English football updater|BoltonWa}} club [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]]..

==Club career==
Born in [[Bilbao]], [[Biscay]], [[Basque Country (autonomous community)|Basque Country]], Larrazabal started his career with Lauro Ikastola, the team affiliated to his school in the town of [[Loiu]]. In 2015, he had a successful trial with Bilbao-based youth club [[Danok Bat CF|Danok Bat]];<ref name=reno>{{cite web |url=https://www.elcorreo.com/deportes/futbol/liga-segunda-b/bilbao-athletic/athletic-negocia-gaizka-20190410144054-nt.html |title=El Athletic negocia con Gaizka Larrazabal para su renovación |trans-title=Athletic negotiates with Gaizka Larrazabal for his renewal |language=es |work=[[El Correo]] |date=10 April 2019 |accessdate=25 August 2019}}</ref> it took until the latter part of his season there to establish himself in the team in the [[División de Honor Juvenil de Fútbol|'Juvenil' league]], but by its end he had drawn interest from senior clubs.<ref name=reno/>

On 3 June 2016, after finishing his formation, Larrazabal signed for newly promoted [[Segunda División B]] side [[Zamudio SD|Zamudio]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://eldesmarque.com/bizkaia/kirolak/53535-el-zamudio-sigue-con-su-apuesta-por-juveniles-de-calidad|title=El Zamudio sigue con su apuesta por juveniles de calidad|trans-title=Zamudio keep with their bet on quality youngsters|publisher=El Desmarque|language=es|date=3 June 2016|accessdate=16 August 2019}}</ref> He made his senior debut on 27 August 2016, playing the entire second half in a 1–3 home loss to [[Bilbao Athletic]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lacanteradelezama.com/dos-de-dos-para-el-bilbao-athletic/|title=Dos de dos para el Bilbao Athletic|trans-title=Two out of two for Bilbao Athletic|publisher=La Cantera de Lezama|language=es|date=27 August 2016|accessdate=16 August 2019}}</ref> and scored his first goal on 10 December by netting the last in a 3–1 home defeat of [[CD Toledo|Toledo]]. He finished [[2016–17 Segunda División B|the campaign]] with three goals in 29 appearances, although Zamudio finished bottom of the table and were relegated.

On 5 April 2017, Larrazabal agreed to a two-year contract with [[Athletic Bilbao]], effective as of 1 July;<ref name=MD>{{cite web|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/futbol/athletic-bilbao/20170405/421463670086/aitor-larrazabal-gaizka-larrazabal-athletic.html|title=El Athletic se hace con los servicios de Gaizka Larrazabal|trans-title=Athletic get the services of Gaizka Larrazabal|publisher=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|language=es|date=5 April 2017|accessdate=16 August 2019}}</ref> upon arriving, he was assigned to the B-team. He spent two seasons with Bilbao Athletic in the third tier, playing regularly for the team and scoring nine goals in [[2018–19 Segunda División B|2018–19]].<ref name=sacrificio>{{cite web |url=https://as.com/futbol/2019/07/23/primera/1563902679_160282.html |title=Larrazabal convence a Garitano a base de sacrificio |trans-title=Larrazabal convinces Garitano on the basis of sacrifice |language=es |work=[[Diario AS]] |date=23 July 2019|accessdate=26 August 2019}}</ref>

On 14 May 2019, Larrazabal agreed to a new two-year deal with the ''Lions'', being definitely promoted to the main squad.<ref name=AB>{{cite web|url=https://www.athletic-club.eus/en/news/2019/05/14/gaizka-larrazabal-pasara-a-formar-parte-de-la-primera-plantilla|title=Gaizka Larrazabal will become part of the first team|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=14 May 2019|accessdate=16 August 2019}}</ref> He made his first team – and [[La Liga]] – debut on 24 August, coming on as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for [[Óscar de Marcos]] in a 1–1 draw away to [[Getafe CF|Getafe]].<ref name=justo>{{cite web |url=https://elpais.com/deportes/2019/08/24/actualidad/1566653765_737427.html |title=Empate justo entre Getafe y Athletic |trans-title=Fair draw between Getafe and Athletic |language=es |work=[[El País]] |date=25 August 2019 |accessdate=25 August 2019}}</ref>

On 2 October 2020, Larrazabal terminated his contract with the ''Lions'',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.athletic-club.eus/en/news/2020/10/02/gaizka-larrazabal-released-from-contract|title=Gaizka Larrazabal released from contract|publisher=Athletic Bilbao|date=2 October 2020|accessdate=2 October 2020}}</ref> and agreed to a three-year deal with [[Segunda División]] side [[Real Zaragoza]] just hours later;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realzaragoza.com/noticias/el-real-zaragoza-cierra-la-incorporaci-n-de-gaizka-larrazabal|title=El Real Zaragoza cierra la incorporación de Gaizka Larrazabal|trans-title=Real Zaragoza sign Gaizka Larrazabal|publisher=Real Zaragoza|language=es|date=2 October 2020|accessdate=2 October 2020}}</ref> Athletic also retained a two-year buyback clause. On 24 August of the following year, he moved to fellow second division side [[SD Amorebieta|Amorebieta]] on loan for [[2021–22 Segunda División|the season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.realzaragoza.com/noticias/acuerdo-para-la-cesi-n-de-gaizka-larrazabal-al-amorebieta|title=Acuerdo para la cesión de Gaizka Larrazabal al Amorebieta|trans-title=Agreement for the loan of Gaizka Larrazabal to Amorebieta|publisher=SD Amorebieta|language=es|date=24 August 2021|accessdate=25 August 2021}}</ref>

While on loan at Amorebieta, Larrazabal was converted into a [[Defender (association football)#Wing-back|right wing-back]], being an undisputed starter for the side.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/2021/11/04/segunda/1636032965_376882.html|title=Larra, el cachorro reconvertido en carrilero de élite en Lezama|trans-title=Larra, the puppy reconverted into a top tier wing-back in Lezama|work=Diario AS|language=es|date=5 November 2021|accessdate=14 January 2022}}</ref>

On 3 July 2023, [[Primeira Liga]] side [[Casa Pia A.C.|Casa Pia]] announced the free signing of Larrazabal.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=3 July 2023 |title=Extremo espanhol Gaizka Larrazabal chega ao Casa Pia oriundo do Real Zaragoza |trans-title=Spanish winger Gaizka Larrazabal arrives at Casa Pia from Real Zaragoza |url=https://observador.pt/2023/07/03/extremo-espanhol-gaizka-larrazabal-chega-ao-casa-pia-oriundo-do-real-zaragoza/ |access-date=11 August 2023 |website=Observador |language=pt-PT}}</ref>

==International career==
Larrazabal made his debut for the unofficial [[Basque Country national football team|Basque Country national team]] in May 2019, in a 0–0 draw away to [[Panama national football team|Panama]] for which a small, youthful and inexperienced squad was selected.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://as.com/futbol/2019/05/30/mas_futbol/1559206252_926357.html |title=Empate sin goles de la Euskal Selekzioa ante Panamá |trans-title=Basque Selection goalless draw against Panama |language=es |work=Diario AS |date=30 May 2019 |accessdate=26 August 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.eitb.eus/es/deportes/futbol/detalle/6442714/resultado-fotos-partido-euskal-selekzioa-panama-00/ |title=Empate entre la Euskal Selekzioa y Panamá (0-0) |trans-title=Draw between Basque Selection and Panama (0-0) |language=es |work=[[EITB]] |date=30 May 2019 |accessdate=26 August 2019}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Larrazabal's father is [[Aitor Larrazábal]], who made over 400 appearances for Athletic Bilbao as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] between 1990 and 2004 and later became a manager,<ref name=MD/><ref name=AB/> and whose goal celebrations included producing a [[pacifier]] from his shorts to represent his baby sons.<ref name=sacrificio/><ref name=nohijo>{{cite web |url=https://www.deia.eus/2019/05/24/deportes/futbol/gaizka-tiene-que-ser-gaizka-y-no-el-hijo-de-aitor-larrazabal |title="Gaizka tiene que ser Gaizka y no el hijo de Aitor Larrazabal" |trans-title=Gaizka has to be Gaizka and not the son of Aitor Larrazabal |language=es |work=Deia |date=24 May 2019 |accessdate=26 August 2019 |archive-date=21 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190721121639/https://www.deia.eus/2019/05/24/deportes/futbol/gaizka-tiene-que-ser-gaizka-y-no-el-hijo-de-aitor-larrazabal |url-status=dead }}</ref> They met as opponents when Gaizka was playing for Zamudio and Aitor was in charge of [[SD Amorebieta|Amorebieta]],<ref name=MD/> and again when Bilbao Athletic faced [[Barakaldo CF|Barakaldo]].

In 2002,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.athletic-club.eus/en/teams/athletic-club/2002-03/matches/1_2298 |title=Amurrio 1 - 2 Athletic Club |publisher=Athletic Bilbao |date=11 September 2002 |accessdate=25 August 2019}}</ref> Aitor lined up in the same Athletic Bilbao team as [[Aritz Aduriz]], who was also on the field for Gaizka's debut for the club nearly 17 years later.<ref name=sacrificio/><ref name=justo/> The Larrazabals were the first father and son to play for Athletic since goalkeepers [[Carmelo Cedrún|Carmelo]] and [[Andoni Cedrún]],<ref name=AB/><ref name=nohijo/> and the first to both feature for the Basque Country team since [[Periko Alonso|'Periko']] and [[Xabi Alonso]].

== Career ==

'''Thievy Guivane Bifouma Koulossa''' (born 13 May 1992) is a professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[Forward (association football)|forward]] for [[Persian Gulf Pro League]] club [[Persepolis F.C.|Persepolis]].

He spent most of his early career in Spain, totalling 68 [[La Liga]] games and eight goals for [[RCD Espanyol|Espanyol]], [[UD Almería|Almería]] and [[Granada CF|Granada]] in addition to a season on loan at [[UD Las Palmas|Las Palmas]] in the [[Segunda División]]. As well as brief spells in England with [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] and France with [[Stade de Reims|Reims]] and [[SC Bastia|Bastia]], he represented four clubs in Turkey's [[Süper Lig]].

Formerly a [[France national youth football team|youth international for France]], where he was born, Bifouma made his senior debut for the [[Congo national football team|Congo]] in 2014. He competed at the [[2015 Africa Cup of Nations]], where he was joint top scorer.

==Club career==
===Espanyol===
Bifouma was born in [[Saint-Denis, Seine-Saint-Denis]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.leparisien.fr/archives/il-ne-faut-pas-avoir-peur-10-12-2014-4361361.php|title="Il ne faut pas avoir peur"|trans-title="There's no need to be afraid"|newspaper=[[Le Parisien]]|language=fr|date=10 December 2014|access-date=4 April 2020}}</ref> He joined [[RCD Espanyol]] in Spain in early 2010, not yet aged 18, signing from [[RC Strasbourg Alsace]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rtl.be/art/sport/football/football-etranger/thierry-bifouma-l-homme-qui-a-mis-un-triple-au-barca-video--546551.aspx|title=Thierry Bifouma, l'homme qui a mis un triplé au Barça! (vidéo)|trans-title=Thierry Bifouma, the man who put three past Barça! (video)|publisher=[[RTL Group]]|language=fr|date=11 August 2011|access-date=9 April 2025}}</ref> On 13 March 2011, he made his debut with the [[Catalonia|Catalans]]' first team, after coming on as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for [[Joan Verdú (footballer)|Joan Verdú]] in the dying minutes of a 2–0 [[La Liga]] home win against [[Deportivo de La Coruña]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/302188?cc=5739|title=Alonso and Verdu fire Espanyol|publisher=[[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]]|date=13 March 2011|access-date=23 May 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121026133553/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/302188?cc=5739|archive-date=26 October 2012}}</ref>

On 10 August 2011, in the [[Copa Catalunya]] final, Bifouma netted a [[hat-trick]] in a 3–0 victory over a [[FC Barcelona]] team that was filled with reserve and youth players.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2011/08/10/futbol/1adivision/1312927358.html|title=El Espanyol se da un festín en el derbi de la mano de Thievy|trans-title=Espanyol indulge themselves in derby courtesy of Thievy|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=10 August 2011|access-date=12 August 2011}}</ref> On 17 December, he scored his first goal with the main squad, opening an eventual 2–1 away defeat of [[Sporting de Gijón]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/323877?cc=5739|title=Sporting Gijón 1–2 Espanyol|publisher=ESPN Soccernet|date=17 December 2011|access-date=29 December 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120713164745/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/323877?cc=5739|archive-date=13 July 2012}}</ref>

In September 2012, Bifouma was loaned to [[UD Las Palmas]] of [[Segunda División]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.laprovincia.es/deportes/2012/09/01/ud-refuerza-cesion-delantero-galo-10510699.html|title=La UD se refuerza con la cesión del delantero galo Thievy Bifouma|trans-title=UD bolster with loan of Gaul forward Thievy Bifouma|newspaper=[[La Provincia (Canary Islands)|La Provincia]]|first=Paco|last=Cabrera|language=es|date=1 September 2012|access-date=9 April 2025}}</ref> After [[2012–13 Segunda División|a successful spell]], he extended his contract with Espanyol until 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.tintaamarilla.es/noticia.php?id=7815|title=Thievy, españolista hasta el 2017|trans-title=Thievy, ''españolista'' until 2017|publisher=Tinta Amarilla|language=es|date=12 July 2013|access-date=28 August 2013}}</ref>

On 31 January 2014, Bifouma signed for [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] on a loan deal with a view to a permanent transfer, being awarded the number 50 shirt.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rcdespanyol.com/principal.php?modulo=detalleNoticia&idnoticia=17210&idseccion=28&idlinkchk=0&idmenu=9&idsubmenu=108|title=Thievy jugarà al West Bromwich Albion|trans-title=Thievy will play in West Bromwich Albion|publisher=RCD Espanyol|language=ca|date=31 January 2014|access-date=31 January 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wba.co.uk/news/article/albion-sign-thievy-bifouma-1332504.aspx|title=Albion sign Thievy Bifouna|publisher=West Bromwich Albion F.C.|date=31 January 2014|access-date=31 January 2014}}</ref> He made his debut in the [[Premier League]] eight days later, playing the second half and scoring within 36 seconds of taking the pitch in a 3–1 away loss against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25995046|title=Crystal Palace 3–1 West Bromwich Albion|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|first=Graham|last=Chase|date=8 February 2014|access-date=8 February 2014}}</ref>

Bifouma moved to fellow top-division club [[UD Almería]] on 13 August 2014, in a [[2014–15 La Liga|season]]-long loan.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.udalmeriasad.com/-/el-almeria-refuerza-su-ataque-con-el-fichaje-de-thievy|title=El Almería refuerza su ataque con el fichaje de Thievy|trans-title=Almería bolster attack with the signing of Thievy|publisher=UD Almería|language=es|date=13 August 2014|access-date=13 August 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140814025546/http://www.udalmeriasad.com/-/el-almeria-refuerza-su-ataque-con-el-fichaje-de-thievy|archive-date=14 August 2014}}</ref> On 19 March of the following year, he was suspended for one month due to allegations of breach of contract with his former agent;<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2015/03/19/futbol/equipos/almeria/1426778183.html|title=Thievy, sancionado con un mes por una denuncia de su exagente|trans-title=Thievy, suspended for a month due to a complaint from his ex-agent|newspaper=Marca|language=es|date=19 March 2015|access-date=19 March 2015}}</ref> the ban was lifted days later, and he continued to appear regularly for the [[Andalusia]]ns, which suffered relegation.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.diariodealmeria.es/deportes/Descenso-claro-responsable_0_919108167.html|title=Descenso con un claro responsable (2–3)|trans-title=Relegation has a clear guilty party (2–3)|newspaper=[[Diario de Almería]]|first=Paco|last=Gregorio|language=es|date=23 May 2015|access-date=4 April 2020}}</ref>

On 19 August 2015, Bifouma was loaned to [[Granada CF]] of the same league for one year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://granadacf.es/es/el-club/noticias-club/1534-thievy-ya-esta-aqui|title=¡Thievy ya está aquí!|trans-title=Thievy is already here!|publisher=Granada CF|language=es|date=19 August 2015|access-date=19 August 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924023511/http://www.granadacf.es/es/el-club/noticias-club/1534-thievy-ya-esta-aqui|archive-date=24 September 2015}}</ref> He finished the season with [[Stade de Reims]], also owned by Espanyol.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://france3-regions.francetvinfo.fr/champagne-ardenne/marne/reims/l-attaquant-thievy-bifouma-rejoint-l-effectif-du-stade-de-reims-915561.html|title=L'attaquant Thievy Bifouma rejoint l'effectif du Stade de Reims|trans-title=Forward Thievy Bifouma joins Stade de Reims roster|publisher=[[France 3]]|first=Lionel|last=Gonzalez|language=fr|date=28 January 2016|access-date=29 July 2016}}</ref>

===Turkey===
On 28 July 2016, Bifouma signed for fellow French [[Ligue 1]] club [[SC Bastia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sc-bastia.corsica/?p=121786|title=4 arrivées et 3 départs au Sporting|trans-title=4 arrivals and 3 departures at Sporting|publisher=SC Bastia|language=fr|date=28 July 2016|access-date=28 July 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rcdespanyol.com/ca/actualitat/thievy-traspassat-al-sc-bastia/_n:3265/|title=Thievy, traspassat al SC Bastia|trans-title=Thievy, transferred to SC Bastia|publisher=RCD Espanyol|language=ca|date=28 July 2016|access-date=28 July 2016}}</ref> He was on the move again in the following [[transfer window]], joining [[Süper Lig]]'s [[Osmanlıspor]] on a three-and-a-half-year deal.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.yenisafak.com/osmanlispor-transfer-haberi---thievy-bifouma-osmanlisporda-h-2598356|title=Osmanlıspor transfer haberi – Thievy Bifouma Osmanlıspor'da|trans-title=Osmanlıspor transfer news – Thievy Bifouma to Osmanlıspor|newspaper=[[Yeni Şafak]]|language=tr|date=17 January 2017|access-date=17 January 2017}}</ref> He scored just one goal in 22 total games for the team from [[Ankara]], in their 5–1 win at [[Adanaspor]] in the [[Süper Lig]] on 19 February 2017.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://skor.sozcu.com.tr/2017/02/19/adanaspor-osmanlispor-canli-anlatim-591781/|title=Adanaspor 1–5 Osmanlıspor / Maç özeti|trans-title=Adanaspor 1–5 Osmanlıspor / Match highlights|publisher=Skor|language=tr|date=19 February 2017|access-date=1 July 2020}}</ref>

Remaining in the same league, Bifouma signed a one-year contract with [[Sivasspor]] on 9 September 2017.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Thievy-bifouma-signe-pour-un-an-a-sivasspor/833446|title=Thievy Bifouma signe pour un an à Sivasspor|trans-title=Thievy Bifouma signs for one year at Sivasspor|newspaper=L'Équipe|language=fr|date=11 September 2017|access-date=1 July 2020}}</ref> Only eight days later, he netted twice in a 4–2 victory on his return to the [[Osmanlı Stadium]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/futbol/demir-grup-sivasspor-osmanlisporu-4-2-yendi-/912598|title=Demir Grup Sivasspor, Osmanlıspor'u 4–2 yendi|trans-title=Demir Grup Sivasspor, Osmanlıspor beat 4–2|publisher=[[Anadolu Agency]]|language=tr|date=17 September 2017|access-date=1 July 2020}}</ref>

Bifouma went back to the Turkish capital in June 2018, agreeing to a three-year deal at [[MKE Ankaragücü]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kingfut.com/2018/06/20/thievy-bifouma-ankaragucu/|title=Congolese Thievy Bifouma joins MKE Ankaragücü|publisher=[[KingFut]]|first=Youssef|last=Waell|date=20 June 2018|access-date=1 July 2020}}</ref> He scored once during his brief tenure, a late consolation in a 2–1 home defeat to [[Kasımpaşa S.K.]] on 2 September,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kingfut.com/2018/09/02/trezeguet-scores-winner-for-kasimpasa/|title=Trezeguet scores winner for Kasimpasa|publisher=KingFut|first=Luke|last=McBride|date=2 September 2018|access-date=1 July 2020}}</ref> and moved on again on 22 January 2019 when he signed with third-placed [[Yeni Malatyaspor]] for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.football365.fr/thievy-bifouma-ex-reims-rejoint-malatyaspor-officiel-8847094.html|title=Thievy Bifouma (ex-Reims) rejoint Malatyaspor (officiel)|trans-title=Thievy Bifouma (ex-Reims) joins Malatyaspor (official)|publisher=Football 365|language=fr|date=22 January 2019|access-date=1 July 2020}}</ref> On 15 December that year, he scored in a 2–0 win at [[Beşiktaş J.K.]] which broke the [[Istanbul]] club's six-match winning streak.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aa.com.tr/en/sports/football-besiktas-lose-to-yeni-malatyaspor-2-0-at-home/1674567|title=Football: Besiktas lose to Yeni Malatyaspor 2–0 at home|publisher=Anadolu Agency|first=Emre|last=Aşıkçı|date=15 December 2019|access-date=14 December 2021}}</ref>

On 17 July 2020, Bifouma moved to the [[Chinese Super League]]'s [[Shenzhen F.C.]] on an undisclosed contract for a fee of around €3 million.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rfi.fr/fr/afrique-foot/20200718-le-congolais-thievy-bifouma-quitte-la-turquie-shenzhen-en-chine|title=Le Congolais Thievy Bifouma quitte la Turquie pour Shenzhen en Chine|trans-title=Congolese Thievy Bifouma leaves Turkey for Shenzhen in China|publisher=[[Radio France Internationale]]|language=fr|date=18 July 2020|access-date=14 December 2021}}</ref> The following 19 April, he was released by mutual accord and signed for [[Jiangxi Dingnan United F.C.|Heilongjiang Ice City F.C.]] in the [[China League One|country's second tier]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://africafootunited.com/mercato-thievy-bifouma-quitte-shenzhen-pour-la-d2-chinoise/|title=Mercato: Thievy Bifouma quitte Shenzhen pour la D2 chinoise|trans-title=Transfer market: Thievy Bifouma leaves Shenzhen for the Chinese second division|publisher=Africa Foot United|first=Ange|last=M'Poli M'Toama|language=fr|date=19 April 2021|access-date=14 December 2021}}</ref>

Ten months after leaving China with no goals and one [[Assist (association football)|assist]] to his name from nine appearances, Bifouma returned to Turkey in February 2022, signing for a [[Bursaspor]] side fighting to remain in the [[TFF First League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.adiac-congo.com/content/transferts-thievy-bifouma-bursaspor-la-derniere-chance-de-relance-134851|title=Transferts: Thievy Bifouma à Bursaspor, la dernière chance de relance?|trans-title=Transfers: Thievy Bifouma to Bursaspor, last chance of a comeback?|publisher=[[Agence d'Information d'Afrique Centrale]]|first=Camille|last=Delourme|language=fr|date=9 February 2022|access-date=27 July 2022}}</ref> He was one of 17 players to leave following [[2021–22 TFF First League|their relegation]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bursaspordabugun.com/tr/haberler/detay/bursaspor-eriyor-bakin-kimler-gitti-48419|title=Bursaspor eriyor! Bakın kimler gitti|trans-title=Bursaspor are melting! Look who left!|newspaper=Bursasporda Bugün|language=tr|date=4 July 2022|access-date=27 July 2022}}</ref>

===Greece===
On 16 September 2022, Bifouma joined [[OFI Crete F.C.]] on a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sport24.gr/football/ofi-metagrafes-anakoinose-ton-mpifoyma-gia-dyo-chronia.9760947.html|title=ΟΦΗ μεταγραφές: Ανακοίνωσε τον Μπιφουμά για δύο χρόνια|trans-title=OFI transfers: Bifouma announced for two years|publisher=Sport 24|first=Thomas|last=Tsouvaras|language=el|date=16 September 2022|access-date=12 June 2023}}</ref> The [[2023–24 Super League Greece|following season]], he moved to fellow [[Super League Greece]] side [[A.E. Kifisia F.C.|A.E. Kifisia FC]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.adiac-congo.com/content/transferts-lae-kifisia-mise-sur-thievy-bifouma-151160|title=Transferts: l’AE Kifisia mise sur Thievy Bifouma|trans-title=Transfers: AE Kifisia bet on Thievy Bifouma|publisher=Agence d'Information d'Afrique Centrale|language=fr|date=1 September 2023|access-date=9 April 2025}}</ref>

===Iran===
In August 2024, Bifouma signed for [[Esteghlal Khuzestan F.C.]] in the [[Persian Gulf Pro League]]; he agreed to the deal with the express intention of facing [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] of [[Al Nassr FC]] in the [[AFC Champions League Elite]], thinking he was joining [[Esteghlal F.C.]] instead.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://metro.co.uk/2024/12/24/i-moved-iran-face-cristiano-ronaldo-one-mistake-ruined-everything-22162375/|title=‘I moved to Iran to face Cristiano Ronaldo – but one mistake ruined everything’|newspaper=[[Metro (British newspaper)|Metro]]|first=Ben|last=Fleming|date=24 December 2024|access-date=9 April 2025}}</ref>

Bifouma remained in the country and division for the [[2025–26 Persian Gulf Pro League|2025–26 campaign]], joining [[Persepolis F.C.]] on a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.mehrnews.com/news/231001/Thievy-Bifouma-joins-Persepolis/|title=Thievy Bifouma joins Persepolis|publisher=[[Mehr News Agency]]|date=25 April 2025|access-date=15 May 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.iranintl.com/202505158606|title=اولین خرید فصل رسمی شد؛ تیوی بیفوما به پرسپولیس پیوست|trans-title=The first signing of the season is official; Thievy Bifouma joins Persepolis|publisher=[[Iran International]]|language=fa|date=15 May 2025|access-date=15 May 2025}}</ref>

==International career==
A [[France national youth football team|French youth international]], Bifouma opted to represent [[Congo national football team|Congo]] at the senior level, receiving a [[FIFA]] clearance on 1 August 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.africatopsports.com/2014/08/01/congo-fifa-donne-feu-vert-thievy-bifouma/|title=Congo: La FIFA donne feu vert à Thievy Bifouma|trans-title=Congo: FIFA gives green light to Thievy Bifouma|publisher=Africa Top Sports|first=Franck|last=Orocoti|language=fr|date=1 August 2014|access-date=20 September 2014}}</ref> He made his full debut a day later, replacing [[Julsy Boukama-Kaya]] in the 68th minute of a 2–0 away loss against [[Rwanda national football team|Rwanda]] in the second leg of the [[2015 Africa Cup of Nations qualification|2015 Africa Cup of Nations second qualification round]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.afrik-foot.com/can-2015-le-benin-et-le-congo-renverses-et-elimines-aux-tirs-au-but|title=CAN 2015: Le Bénin et le Congo renversés et éliminés aux tirs au but!|trans-title=CAN 2015: Benin and Congo beaten and eliminated on penalties!|publisher=Afrik Foot|first=Romain|last=Lantheaume|language=fr|date=2 August 2014|access-date=9 April 2025}}</ref>

On 6 September 2014, in the same competition, Bifouma scored a brace in a 3–2 win in [[Nigeria national football team|Nigeria]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/29060222|title=Nigeria suffer shock Afcon defeat to Congo Brazzaville|publisher=BBC Sport|date=6 September 2014|access-date=9 April 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.taipeitimes.com/News/sport/archives/2014/09/08/2003599261|title=Congo stun defending African champs Nigeria|newspaper=[[Taipei Times]]|date=8 September 2014|access-date=9 April 2025}}</ref> At the [[2015 Africa Cup of Nations]] finals, he netted Congo's first goal of the tournament in a 1–1 draw with hosts [[Equatorial Guinea national football team|Equatorial Guinea]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/30758380|title=Equatorial Guinea 1–1 Congo|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Ian|last=Hughes|date=17 January 2015|access-date=24 January 2015}}</ref> He also scored the opener in their 2–1 group phase victory over [[Burkina Faso national football team|Burkina Faso]], a result which qualified the nation to the quarter-finals for the first time since 1992,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30868924|title=Congo 2–1 Burkina Faso|publisher=BBC Sport|date=25 January 2015|access-date=25 January 2015}}</ref> where he grabbed his final goal against the [[DR Congo national football team|DR Congo]], putting his team ahead 2–0 but in an eventual 4–2 defeat;<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/30963458|title=Congo 2–4 DR Congo|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Ian|last=Hughes|date=31 January 2015|access-date=31 January 2015}}</ref> with three goals, he was one of five joint top scorers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://kawowo.com/2017/01/15/afcon-top-scorers-look-previous-tournament-net-busters/|title=AFCON Top Scorers: A look at the previous tournament net busters|publisher=Kawowo Sports|first=David|last=Isabirye|date=15 January 2017|access-date=1 July 2020}}</ref>

Having missed over two years of games for reasons including travel restrictions in China during the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], Bifouma was recalled to the Congolese squad in September 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.afrik-foot.com/congo-bifouma-de-retour-dans-la-liste-contre-la-gambie|title=Congo: Bifouma de retour dans la liste contre la Gambie!|trans-title=Congo: Bifouma back in the list against the Gambia!|publisher=Afrik Foot|language=fr|date=25 September 2020|access-date=14 December 2021}}</ref> He finally played again the following 26 March, in a goalless draw at home to [[Senegal national football team|Senegal]] in [[2021 Africa Cup of Nations]] [[2021 Africa Cup of Nations qualification|qualification]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.adiac-congo.com/node/125585|title=Congo-Sénégal: Thievy Bifouma promet d’être à la hauteur|trans-title=Congo-Senegal: Thievy Bifouma promises to be up to the task|publisher=Agence d'Information d'Afrique Centrale|first=James|last=Golden Eloué|language=fr|date=25 March 2021|access-date=14 December 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rfi.fr/fr/afrique-foot/20210326-can-2021-le-congo-b-tient-t%C3%AAte-au-s%C3%A9n%C3%A9gal-et-garde-ses-chances-de-qualification|title=CAN 2021: le Congo-B tient tête au Sénégal et garde ses chances de qualification|trans-title=2021 ACN: Republic of Congo stand up to Senegal and maintain their chances of qualification|publisher=Radio France International|first=Ndiasse|last=Sambe|language=fr|date=16 March 2021|access-date=14 December 2021}}</ref>

'''Sándor Torghelle''' ({{IPA|hu|ˈʃaːndor ˈtorɡɛllɛ|lang}}; born 5 May 1982) is a Hungarian former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[forward (association football)|forward]]. During his career, he played for [[Budapest Honvéd FC|Honvéd]], [[Marcali]], [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]], [[Panathinaikos F.C.|Panathinaikos]], [[PAOK FC|PAOK]], [[FC Carl Zeiss Jena|Carl Zeiss Jena]], [[FC Augsburg]], [[Fortuna Düsseldorf]], [[Videoton FC|Videoton]], and [[Vasas SC|Vasas]]. He played 42 games for the [[Hungary national football team|Hungary national team]] between 2004 and 2010.

==Club career==

===Crystal Palace===
After developing in Hungary and playing for [[Budapest Honvéd FC|Budapest Honvéd]], Marcali VFC and [[MTK Hungária FC|MTK Hungária]], Torghelle signed for [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]], in August 2004 for a fee of roughly £750,000. He caught their eyes after scoring both goals for [[Hungary national football team|Hungary national team]] in their shock international friendly 2–0 victory over [[Germany national football team|Germany]] in [[Kaiserslautern]] before [[UEFA Euro 2004]].<ref name="Hungary shock Germany">{{cite news |title=Hungary shock Germany |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/euro_2004/germany/3781939.stm |website=BBC Sport |date=6 June 2004 |access-date=2 September 2018}}</ref> He wore the number 10 shirt, that of a first-choice striker, but found it hard to gain a regular place in the Crystal Palace starting eleven with [[Andy Johnson (English footballer)|Andy Johnson]] often playing as a lone striker. He scored only one goal in a League Cup match against Charlton, but the referee sent him off late in the game for diving.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/league_cup/3947053.stm | title = Charlton 1-2 Crystal Palace | publisher = [[BBC]] | date = 27 October 2004 |access-date=12 November 2009}}</ref>

After 12 months at Palace, Torghelle was first stripped of his first-team squad number (given number 30, while 10 went to new signing [[Jon Macken]]), and shortly after was loaned out to [[Panathinaikos F.C.|Panathinaikos]] in Greece for the 2005–06 season. In the deal, there was no clause for re-calling him, so he spent the whole season in Greece.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.origo.hu/sport/magyarfoci/20050803torghelle.html | publisher = origo.hu | title = Torghelle a Panathinaikoszhoz szerződikt | date = 3 August 2005 | language = Hungarian | accessdate = 9 August 2011}}</ref> However, he failed to impress, and Panathinaikos chose not to make the deal permanent.

===PAOK===
Torghelle was transferred to [[PAOK FC|PAOK]] in Greece and handed a three-year contract, being one of the three players that were traded for the transfer of striker [[Dimitris Salpingidis]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.origo.hu/sport/magyarfoci/20060818torghelle.html | publisher = origo.hu | title = Torghelle a PAOK-hoz igazolt | date = 18 August 2006 | language = Hungarian | accessdate = 9 August 2011}}</ref>

He was also famous for his failure to score even a single goal since he was transferred from Crystal Palace, yet this "curse" was lifted when he scored in a PAOK-[[Olympiacos F.C.|Olympiakos]] derby in early 2007. He left PAOK at the end of the 2006–07 season for [[2. Bundesliga]] team [[FC Carl Zeiss Jena|Carl Zeiss Jena]]. There, he finally met the expectations, scoring eight goals over the course of the [[2007–08 2. Bundesliga]] season. Carl Zeiss Jena finished in last place and was relegated to the new [[3. Liga]].

===FC Augsburg===
Torghelle transferred to [[2. Bundesliga]] team [[FC Augsburg]] before the start of the 2008–09 season.  He played two seasons for the largest team in [[Swabia (Bavaria)|Swabian Bavaria]].

===Fortuna Düsseldorf===
On 17 May 2010, Torghelle left FC Augsburg and signed with another [[2. Bundesliga]] team [[Fortuna Düsseldorf]].

===Budapest Honvéd===
Torghelle signed with former club [[Budapest Honvéd FC|Honvéd]] in August 2011.<ref>{{cite web |title=Torghelle's contract was terminated in Düsseldorf (in Hungarian) |url=http://hvg.hu/sport/20110817_torghelle_sandor_foci |website=hvg.com |date=17 August 2011 |accessdate=3 September 2018}}</ref> That reunion was short-lived and he signed for fellow Hungarian [[Nemzeti Bajnokság I|National Championship]] team [[MOL Vidi FC|Videoton FC]] in January 2012.

==International career==
Torghelle made 42 appearances for the [[Hungary national football team|Hungary national team]].<ref>{{cite web|author=Mamrud, Roberto|title=Hungary - Record International Players|website=[[RSSSF]]|url=https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/hong-recintlp.html|date= 11 December 2009}}</ref> He scored several decisive ones during the 2010 World Cup Qualification campaign, such as against Albania and Malta. He came to prominence after scoring both goals in a 2–0 victory over [[Germany national football team|Germany]] in a friendly match in 2004.<ref name="Hungary shock Germany"/>

'''Igor Alexandre Lolo''' (born 22 July 1982) is an Ivorian former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]].

==Club career==
Born in [[Adzopé]], Ivory Coast, Lolo started his career with [[ASEC Mimosas]] where he was spotted by [[K.S.K. Beveren]] who signed  him a contract to play in Belgium. He stayed there one season before leaving for [[FC Metalurh Donetsk]]. After one season in [[Donetsk]], he chose to come back to Belgium and was signed by [[K.F.C. Germinal Beerschot]]. After two seasons with Beerschot, he went to [[KRC Genk]]. Lolo moved to [[FC Dnipro Dnipropetrovsk]] in September 2008 for €4 million, before signing a two-and-a-half-year deal with [[AS Monaco FC|AS Monaco]] on 28 January 2009.<ref>[http://www.asm-fc.com/uk/article.aspx?id=7348 Igor Lolo signed for AS Monaco FC]{{dead link|date=November 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

In the summer of 2013, Lolo signed a two-year contract with [[FC Rostov]]. Previously, he played for fellow [[Russian Premier League]] side [[FC Kuban Krasnodar|Kuban Krasnodar]], but had his contract with them terminated in April 2013.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ivorian Defender Lolo Joins FC Rostov|url=http://en.rsport.ru/football/20130612/667391537.html|publisher=en.rsport.ru/|access-date=21 June 2013}}</ref>

In 2016, he joined [[K.V.C. Westerlo|Westerlo]].<ref>[http://www.kvcwesterlo.be/a-kern/nieuws/item/2170-contract-igor-lolo-ontbonden CONTRACT IGOR LOLO ONTBONDEN]‚ kvcwesterlo.be, 8 December 2016</ref>

==International career==
Lolo received his first cap in the friendly match against [[Paraguay national football team|Paraguay]] at [[Kirin Cup]] on 22 May 2008.

'''Nicolò Cherubin''' (born 2 December 1986) is an Italian [[association football|football]] coach and former player, who played as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]]. He is the current assistant coach of [[Serie D]] club [[Luparense F.C. (football)|Luparense]].

==Playing career==
===Early career===
{{expand section|date=September 2017}}

===Bologna===
Cherubin joined Bologna in July 2010 for €1.5 million fee.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://corrieredibologna.corriere.it/media/pdf/bologna_bilancio/nota-integrativa-parte-1.pdf|title=Bilancio intermedio al 31 dicembre 2010: Nota integrativa: parte 1|date=4 April 2011|accessdate=14 June 2011|work=Bologna F.C. 1909|publisher=re-published by Corriere di Bologna|language=Italian}}</ref> Cherubin spent two seasons on loan at [[Atalanta B.C.]] from 2014 to 2016. He returned to Bologna on 1 July 2016, receiving a call-up from the coach.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bolognafc.it/torinobfc-i-convocati-2/|title=#TorinoBFC: i convocati|date=27 August 2016|access-date=4 September 2016|publisher=Bologna F.C. 1909|language=Italian}}</ref> However, he only appeared as an unused substitute in that match.

===Verona===
On 31 August 2016, Cherubin joined [[Hellas Verona F.C.|Verona]] on a season-long loan deal, with an obligation to make the deal permanent. As part of the deal, [[Filip Helander]] moved to Bologna.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bolognafc.it/en/helander-signs-for-bologna-cherubin-moves-to-verona/|title=Helander signs for Bologna, Cherubin moves to Verona|publisher=Bologna F.C. 1909|date=31 August 2016|access-date=2 September 2016}}</ref>

On 12 June 2017, Cherubin joined Verona on a definitive basis.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.hellasverona.it/2017/06/12/ufficiale_cherubin_e_gialloblu_helander_al_bologna|title=Ufficiale: Cherubin è gialloblù, Helander al Bologna|date=12 June 2017|access-date=25 June 2017|publisher=Hellas Verona F.C.|language=Italian|archive-date=31 October 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191031121240/https://www.hellasverona.it/2017/06/12/ufficiale_cherubin_e_gialloblu_helander_al_bologna|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Padova===
On 9 January 2019, Cherubin joined [[Calcio Padova|Padova]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://m.tuttomercatoweb.com/serie-b/ufficiale-padova-acquistato-a-titolo-definitivo-cherubin-dal-verona-1200008|access-date=10 January 2019|title=UFFICIALE: Padova, acquistato a titolo definitivo Cherubin dal Verona|language=Italian}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
On 11 June 2022, Cherubin was formally appointed as the new assistant coach of [[Serie D]] club [[Luparense F.C. (football)|Luparense]], after having served as a player and then as a technical collaborator for previous head coach [[Nicola Zanini]] during the 2021–22 season.<ref>{{cite web |language=it |url=https://www.tuttocampo.it/Veneto/PD/News/1495940/luparense-l-ex-difensore-del-bologna-cherubin-e-il-nuovo-vice-allenatore-dei-lupi |publisher=Tuttocampo |accessdate=19 December 2022 |date=11 July 2022 |title=Luparense, l'ex difensore del Bologna Cherubin è il nuovo Vice Allenatore dei Lupi}}</ref>

On 19 December 2022, Cherubin was promoted as head coach of Luparense, replacing [[Mauro Zironelli]] in charge of the first team,<ref>{{cite web |language=it |url=https://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/serie-d/ufficiale-l-ex-bari-e-juve-ng-zironelli-esonerato-dalla-luparense-squadra-a-cherubin-1769774 |publisher=TuttoMercatoWeb |accessdate=19 December 2022 |date=19 December 2022 |title=L'ex Bari e Juve NG Zironelli esonerato dalla Luparense. Squadra a Cherubin}}</ref> but was then moved back to his assistant job eight days later as Zironelli was reappointed in charge.<ref>{{cite web |language=it |url=https://www.tuttomercatoweb.com/serie-d/ufficiale-dietrofront-della-luparense-richiamato-in-panchina-mister-zironelli-1772097 |publisher=TuttoMercatoWeb |accessdate=27 December 2022 |date=27 December 2022 |title=Dietrofront della Luparense. Richiamato in panchina mister Zironelli}}</ref>
