'''Robert James Blake''' (born 4 March 1976) is an English former professional [[association football|footballer]] who is a first-team coach at [[National League South]] club [[Eastbourne Borough F.C.|Eastbourne Borough]]. He began his career as a [[striker (association football)|striker]] but was increasingly used as [[midfielder]] in the latter part of his career. He began his professional career with [[Darlington F.C.|Darlington]] in 1994 and went on to make more than 500 appearances in [[the Football League]] and [[Premier League]] playing for [[Bradford City A.F.C.|Bradford City]], [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]], Burnley, [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]], [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]], [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] and [[Doncaster Rovers F.C.|Doncaster Rovers]]. Blake was the subject of many [[transfer (football)|transfers]] throughout his career, with career total transfer fees reaching £3.6 million.{{cite web |url=https://www.soccerbase.com/players/player.sd?player_id=736 |title=Robbie Blake |access-date=24 February 2008 |work=Soccerbase |publisher=Centurycomm}} ==Playing career== ===Darlington=== Born in [[Middlesbrough]], England, Blake began his professional football career at [[Division Three]] side [[Darlington F.C.|Darlington]] in the [[1994-95 in English football|1994–95]] season after signing on from the [[youth team|youth academy]]. He spent the first few seasons of his career playing at [[Feethams]], and also was loaned out to [[Waterford United]] during the 1995–96 season, making some 68 league appearances and scoring 21 goals before the club received an offer, from then [[Football League First Division|Division One]] side, [[Bradford City A.F.C.|Bradford City]] in March 1997. Bradford made a [[Pound sterling|£]]300,000 offer for the player which Darlington accepted.{{cite web |url = http://www.burnleyfootballclub.premiumtv.co.uk/page/ProfilesDetail/0,,10413~5548,00.html |title = Robbie Blake |access-date = 24 February 2008 |publisher = Burnley official website |url-status = dead |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080307123116/http://www.burnleyfootballclub.premiumtv.co.uk/page/ProfilesDetail/0%2C%2C10413~5548%2C00.html |archive-date = 7 March 2008 |df = dmy-all }} ===Bradford City=== Blake quickly settled into the Bradford side and he scored eight goals in his first full season, first under [[Chris Kamara]] and then [[Paul Jewell]]. He was sent off in the final game of the [[1997-98 in English football|1997–98]] season against [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] meaning he was suspended for the start of the following season. But he forced his way back into the team and scored in his first game back in a 2–2 draw with [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]]. He and new signing [[Lee Mills]] forged a lethal partnership in attack sharing 40 goals. Blake scored 16 goals{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/n/nottm_forest/891660.stm |title=Blake agrees Forest stay |access-date=24 February 2008 |date=22 August 2000 |publisher=BBC Sport}} as City won promotion to the [[Premier League|Premiership]]. Blake scored the winning goal in the final game against [[Wolverhampton Wanderers F.C.|Wolverhampton Wanderers]] of the [[1998-99 in English football|1998–99]] season to see his side finish the season as league runners-up. However the following season was harder for Blake and he struggled to make an impact in the [[Premier League|Premiership]], starting just 15 games for Bradford, with a further 12 played as a substitute. The next season at [[Valley Parade]] began much differently for Blake after being sent on loan to Division One side [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] for two months, scoring once against Barnsley.{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_div_1/970411.stm |title=Barnsley 3–4 Forest |publisher=[[BBC]] |date=14 October 2000 |access-date=6 January 2010}} Following his 2-month loan spell at Forest he returned to Bradford where he finished the season with four goals from his 14 starts in the [[2000-01 in English football|2000–01]] season with Bradford ultimately being relegated to Division One. During the summer of 2001 former loan club Nottingham Forest made an undisclosed bid for the player which was rejected. Following the failed transfer bid Forest manager [[David Platt (footballer)|David Platt]] said;
"The offer was turned down, and as no further finance is available, we must assume the deal is dead" – ''David Platt''{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/n/nottm_forest/1033894.stm |title=Forest bid for Blake rejected |access-date=24 February 2008 |date=21 November 2000 |publisher=BBC Sport}}
This was not the last transfer offer Bradford would receive as just a few months later on 25 January 2002 the club received a £1 million transfer bid from fellow Division One side [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] and, due to Bradford's poor financial status, the club had no option but to sell the player. ===Burnley=== Blake signed a three-year contract with the Clarets but did not feature much in the remaining six months of the season due to a [[hernia]] injury. In his second season at Burnley Blake was the club's top scorer with 22 goals in all competitions from 46 games. That summer, long time Burnley manager [[Stan Ternent]] left the club and was replaced by [[Steve Cotterill]] and under the new manager Blake continued his prolific goal scoring with 13 goals in the run up to the January transfer window. When the transfer window opened Blake was subject of multiple bids by Premiership clubs, all of which were rejected (at first). Several bids were made by [[Wigan Athletic F.C.|Wigan Athletic]] who had offers of £500,000 and £600,000 rejected. Following the failed bids Wigan manager [[Paul Jewell]] said;
"The position is that we made an offer for him and it's been turned down, it's as simple as that" – ''Paul Jewell''{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/w/wigan_athletic/4076645.stm |title=Jewell still keen to sign Blake |access-date=24 February 2008 |date=7 December 2004 |publisher=BBC Sport}}
Wigan later made a third for the player, a revised figure of £700,000. Again the Burnley board turned down this offer and no further bids were made by the Latics.{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/b/burnley/4057809.stm |title=Burnley snub third bid for Blake |access-date=24 February 2008 |date=9 December 2004 |publisher=BBC Sport}} In his final game of his first spell at Burnley he scored what is possibly the best goal of his Burnley career leathering in a stunning free kick from 35 yards in a local derby against Preston North End. Eventually a successful bid of £1.25 million was made by [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] and Blake once again had a chance to prove himself in the top league.{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/b/birmingham_city/4161059.stm |title=Blake confident over Blues place |access-date=24 February 2008 |date=10 January 2005 |publisher=BBC Sport}} ===Birmingham City=== Blake made his debut for Birmingham in the [[FA Cup]] against [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] on 8 January 2005 as a second-half substitute. Blake was confident that he could push for a starting place at Birmingham saying:
"[[Clinton Morrison]] and [[Emile Heskey]] have done fantastically well, but hopefully I can push them for a place. I can play in a few positions, behind the strikers or dropping deep, and that gives the gaffer some selections to think about. I thought if anything a bottom four team in the Premiership would come in for me but Birmingham, with the quality of players they have, was an even bigger bonus." – ''Robbie Blake''
In an interview with [[BBC Sport]]. Blake's hopes did not materialise, he went on to play just 11 games for the club and only scored two goals.{{cite news |url = http://www.football.co.uk/leeds_united/whites_chase_blake_deal_195835.shtml |title = Whites chase Blake deal |access-date = 24 February 2008 |date = 29 September 2005 |publisher = Football.co.uk |url-status = dead |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080706193231/http://www.football.co.uk/leeds_united/whites_chase_blake_deal_195835.shtml |archive-date = 6 July 2008 |df = dmy-all }} During the summer of that year Birmingham confirmed that they had received an offer from Leeds United for Blake:
"We have had an offer from Leeds for Robbie Blake. We are considering it and talks are ongoing. Robbie has done very well for us, but he feels he wants to play more and at Leeds he would probably play every week" – ''[[Steve Bruce]]''
Blake did not travel with his teammates on the pre-season tour as he was still in negotiations with Leeds{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/l/leeds_united/4676313.stm |title=Blake not joining Birmingham tour |access-date=24 February 2008 |date=12 July 2005 |publisher=BBC Sport}} and he was eventually signed for £800,000.{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/l/leeds_united/4664143.stm |title=Striker Blake seals Leeds switch |access-date=24 February 2008 |date=18 July 2005 |publisher=BBC Sport}}{{cite news |url = http://www.burnleyfootballclub.premiumtv.co.uk/page/LatestHeadlines/0,,10413~1072650,00.html |title = Robbie's Turf Return |access-date = 24 February 2008 |date = 13 July 2007 |publisher = Burnley official website |url-status = dead |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070916100607/http://www.burnleyfootballclub.premiumtv.co.uk/page/LatestHeadlines/0%2C%2C10413~1072650%2C00.html |archive-date = 16 September 2007 |df = dmy-all }} ===Leeds United=== Blake signed a three-year deal at [[Elland Road]] and commented that although moving to Leeds was stepping back a division he was looking forward to winning promotion with his new club;
"It's a step back in terms of divisions but hopefully I can get back into the Premier League with Leeds. With the quality of players we have got, I'm sure there will be no end of goals going in." – ''Robbie Blake''
He made his debut for the club alongside Northern Ireland striker [[David Healy (footballer)|David Healy]] in the first match of the [[2005-06 in English football|2005–06]] season against [[Millwall F.C.|Millwall]] and scored his first goal just two days later in the Championship match against [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]] at [[Ninian Park]].{{cite web |url = http://www.leedsutd365.co.uk/pages/players/singleplayers/robbieblakestriker.shtml |title = Former Leeds United Player Robbie Blake Striker |access-date = 24 February 2008 |date = 9 September 2005 |publisher = Leeds United 365 |url-status = usurped |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080226002425/http://www.leedsutd365.co.uk/pages/players/singleplayers/robbieblakestriker.shtml |archive-date = 26 February 2008 |df = dmy-all }} He went on to make 31 starts for Leeds and finished the season with 11 goals. Blake was one of six strikers at Leeds and was not a first team regular until the second season when [[Dennis Wise]] was appointed manager following [[Kevin Blackwell]]'s departure. Blake did manage eight goals in the [[2006-07 in English football|2006–07]] season but this was not enough to save Leeds from [[relegation]] after the club filed for [[Administration (law)|administration]] and suffered a 10-point deduction.{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/l/leeds_united/6625751.stm |title=Relegated Leeds in administration |access-date=24 February 2008 |date=4 May 2007 |publisher=BBC Sport}} Following their relegation to the [[Football League One]] Leeds struggled to hang on to their players with the likes of [[David Healy (footballer)|David Healy]], [[Richard Cresswell]], [[Neil Sullivan]] and [[Kevin Nicholls]] all leaving the club.{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_div_2/6229520.stm |title=League One form guide |access-date=24 February 2008 |date=6 August 2007 |publisher=BBC Sport}} Blake soon followed when he was re-signed by Burnley for a fee of £250,000 on 13 July 2007 and signed a three-year deal.{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/b/burnley/6898095.stm |title=Burnley sign Leeds striker Blake |access-date=24 February 2008 |date=13 July 2007 |publisher=BBC Sport}} A number of clauses on the sale meant the total transfer fee would rise to £350,000 after 40 games and also included a further payment if Burnley were to be promoted. ===Return to Burnley=== With Blake back at his old club, manager [[Steve Cotterill]] revealed that Blake felt he had "unfinished business" with the club and that the player needed no persuasion to sign the deal.{{cite news |url = http://www.burnleyfootballclub.premiumtv.co.uk/page/LatestHeadlines/0,,10413~1073190,00.html |title = Blake's "Unfinished Business" |access-date = 24 February 2008 |date = 14 July 2007 |publisher = Burnley official website |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070917172335/http://www.burnleyfootballclub.premiumtv.co.uk/page/LatestHeadlines/0,,10413~1073190,00.html |archive-date = 17 September 2007 |url-status = dead |df = dmy-all }} Burnley director Brendan Flood also revealed that Burnley had been working on a deal for a couple of weeks prior to the announcement:
"With strikers, once it gets mooted that they may be on the move, it invites others to join the hunt. Being able to keep it under wraps is therefore vital, otherwise you get competitive bids coming and the price spirals. Robbie is a proven entertainer and one of the top strikers in the Championship and we know he is always going to score goals. But the really important factor is that he is happy and keen to play for Burnley."{{cite news |url = http://www.burnleyfootballclub.premiumtv.co.uk/page/LatestHeadlines/0,,10413~1072935,00.html |title = Flood Salutes Gaffer |access-date = 24 February 2008 |date = 13 July 2007 |publisher = Burnley official website |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070916101429/http://www.burnleyfootballclub.premiumtv.co.uk/page/LatestHeadlines/0,,10413~1072935,00.html |archive-date = 16 September 2007 |url-status = dead |df = dmy-all }} – ''Brendan Flood''
Blake made his return debut for the club on 11 August 2007 in the opening fixture of the [[2007-08 in English football|2007–08]] Football League Championship season against [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] which Burnley won 2–1.{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_div_1/6931078.stm |title=Burnley 2–1 West Brom |access-date=24 February 2008 |date=11 August 2007 |publisher=BBC Sport}} He then scored the first goal of his second spell with the Clarets against in the [[Football League Cup|League Cup]] game against [[Oldham Athletic A.F.C.|Oldham Athletic]].{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/league_cup/6963488.stm |title=Burnley 3–0 Oldham |access-date=24 February 2008 |date=28 August 2007 |publisher=BBC Sport}} He was heavily praised by both his{{cite web |url = http://www.burnleyfootballclub.premiumtv.co.uk/page/TheGaffer/0,,10413~1123722,00.html |title = Gaffer: Robbie Was Faultless |access-date = 24 February 2008 |publisher = Burnley official website }}{{Dead link|date=September 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} and other managers{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_div_1/7008061.stm |title=Burnley 1–1 Crystal Palace |access-date=24 February 2008 |date=29 September 2007 |publisher=BBC Sport}} as well as the press for his excellent form at the start of the 2007–2008 season, most notably for his performance in the 1–1 draw against [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] just days after the birth of his daughter Mia.{{cite news |url = http://www.burnleycitizen.co.uk/display.var.1725218.0..php |title = Cotterill's tribute to 'majestic' Blake |access-date = 24 February 2008 |date = 1 October 2007 |publisher = Burnley & Pendle Citizen |first = Jason |last = Kayley}}{{dead link|date=January 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} Blake finished the season with 10 goals and 14 assists in 43 matches. Blake came close to helping Burnley into the [[2009 Football League Cup Final|2009 League Cup final]] by scoring one goal and making two more in the second leg of the side's semi-final against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]]. The goals put Burnley just two minutes away from the final, before Tottenham scored twice in the final two minutes to reach the final on aggregate.{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/league_cup/7824257.stm |title=Burnley 3–2 Tottenham (agg 4–6) |date=21 January 2009 |access-date=21 January 2009 |publisher=BBC Sport |first=Ian |last=Hughes}} Blake returned to the top flight once again in May 2009, this time with Burnley after Burnley beat Sheffield United 1–0 in the play-off final at Wembley. A match which Blake played in, directly against a young [[Kyle Walker]]. Blake scored his first [[Premier League]] goal since 2005 on 19 August 2009 against the defending Premier League champions [[Manchester United]], in a 1–0 win. This was Burnley's first home game in the top flight of English football for 33 years.{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/eng_prem/8202360.stm|title=Burnley 1 – 0 Man Utd|date=19 August 2009|work=BBC Sport|access-date=20 August 2009}} ===Bolton Wanderers=== On 30 June 2010, it was announced that he had signed for [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] on a free transfer and would officially join the club a day later.{{cite web|url=http://www.theboltonnews.co.uk/sport/wanderers/wanderersnews/8246286.Wanderers_snap_up_Burnley_star/|title=Wanderers snap up Burnley star|date=30 June 2010|work=The Bolton News|access-date=30 June 2010}} He made his debut for Wanderers in their 3–1 win over [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] at Upton Park on 21 August and scored his first goal for the club eight days later in the home game against former employers [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] with a free kick that earned Bolton a 2–2 draw. As the season drew on, Blake became less and less involved in the first team and several clubs showed interest in signing him on loan, but the player decided to stay and fight for his first team place.{{cite web|url=http://www.theboltonnews.co.uk/sport/wanderers/wanderersnews/8880574.Striker_turns_down_move_to_Norwich_City/|title=Striker turns down move to Norwich City|date=1 March 2011|work=The Bolton News|access-date=1 March 2011}} At the end of the season, the club decided to take up the option on extending his contract for another year.{{cite web|url=http://www.theboltonnews.co.uk/sport/wanderers/wanderersnews/9045783.New_deal_for_Blake/?|title=New deal for Blake|date=24 May 2011|work=The Bolton News|access-date=24 May 2011}} However, at the end of the following season, following Bolton's relegation from the Premier League, Blake was released.[https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/18091522 "Bolton Wanderers allow 15 players to leave after relegation"] BBC Sport 18 May 2012 Retrieved 21 May 2012 He made only three appearances in his second season with only one of them in the league, on the opening day of the season. ===Doncaster Rovers=== On 27 June 2012, it was announced that Blake had signed a one-year deal for [[Doncaster Rovers F.C.|Doncaster Rovers]] on a free transfer.{{cite web|url=http://www.doncasterroversfc.co.uk/page/NewsHome/0,,10329,00.html|title=Striker Blake Joins Rovers|date=27 June 2012|work=doncasterroversfc.co.uk|access-date=27 June 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120624141714/http://www.doncasterroversfc.co.uk/page/NewsHome/0,,10329,00.html|archive-date=24 June 2012|url-status=dead}} After two League Cup starts and several appearances from the bench, he scored his first goal for Rovers on 1 December 2012 in an FA Cup game at [[Oldham Athletic A.F.C.|Oldham Athletic]].{{cite news|title=Oldham v Doncaster|work=BBC Sport |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20474460|access-date=1 December 2012}} With no appearances since January, Blake's contract was terminated by mutual consent on 25 March 2013, with him having scored once in 14 appearances for the club.{{cite news|title=Doncaster Rovers release forward Robbie Blake|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21930082|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=26 March 2013}} ===Team Northumbria=== On 2 November 2013, it was announced that Blake had signed for [[Team Northumbria F.C.|Team Northumbria]] who are in the Division One of the [[Northern Football League|Northern League]] on a free transfer.{{cite web|url=http://www.thenorthernecho.co.uk/sport/10782087.Blake_signs_for_TN|title=Blake signs for TN|date=4 November '''Carlos Javier Grossmüller''' (born 4 May 1983) is a Uruguayan [[association football|football]] [[Manager (association football)|manager]] and former player who played as a [[midfielder]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.kicker.de/regionalligen/44199/vereinsspieler_carlos-grossmueller.html | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20121019004212/http://www.kicker.de/regionalligen/44199/vereinsspieler_carlos-grossmueller.html | url-status = dead | archive-date = October 19, 2012 | title = Grossmüller, Carlos | language = German | publisher = [[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] | access-date =June 1, 2011}}</ref>

==Career==
Born in [[Montevideo]], Uruguay, Grossmüller began his footballing career in 1988, at the age of five, as a youth player with his local team, Ombu.

In 2002, he made his professional debut for [[Primera División Uruguaya]] side [[Danubio F.C.|Danubio]], making mostly substitute appearances for the next two seasons, but being part of the 2004 championship team.

In 2004, he was sent on loan to [[Centro Atlético Fénix]] to gain experience, where he made six appearances in the [[Segunda División Uruguay]] before going back to Danubio. During the next two seasons at Danubio, he went on to play 52 league games, netted 13 goals, and won two more titles, (2006 Apertura, 2007 Clausura) which prompted interest from German side [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]]. Schalke later signed him in the summer of 2007 on a four-year contract.

His first goal in the [[Bundesliga]], a free kick against [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]], went on to be nominated as "Goal of the Month" in German television.<ref>{{Cite web |date=27 October 2007 |title=FC Schalke 04 - Werder Bremen 1:1 (Bundesliga 2007/2008, 11. Round) |url=https://www.worldfootball.net/match-report/ma48457/lineup/ |access-date=2024-04-08 |website=worldfootball.net |language=en}}</ref> On 31 August 2009, he returned to his former club Danubio on loan until 30 June 2010. On 30 July 2010, he was signed by newly promoted [[Serie A]] side [[U.S. Lecce|Lecce]]. After Lecce were relegated at the end of the 2011–12 season, he returned to Uruguay and joined [[C.A. Peñarol|Peñarol]] on 22 August 2012.<ref>{{cite news |date=August 24, 2012 |title=Carlos Grossmuller llegó para reforzar a Peñarol |url=http://www.xn--pearol-xwa.org/uc_1064_1.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130416101110/http://www.xn--pearol-xwa.org/uc_1064_1.html |archive-date=April 16, 2013 |accessdate=August 22, 2012 |publisher=capeñarol.org |language=Spanish}}</ref>

In 2013, he joined [[C.A. Cerro|Cerro]] and played with them until 2014.

He made another return to Danubio in 2018 and left the club in 2020. 

==International career==
He made his début with the [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay national team]] against [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]] in 2003.

'''Alain Caveglia''' (born 28 March 1968) is a French former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[striker (association football)|striker]].

==Career==
Caveglia was born in [[Vénissieux]], Rhône. A prolific goalscorer, he started at [[FC Gueugnon|Guegnon]], making his [[Ligue 1]] debuts on 21 August 1990 with [[FC Sochaux-Montbéliard|Sochaux]], against [[Stade Brestois 29|Brest]]. After two more top division seasons at [[Le Havre AC|Le Havre]] he moved to [[Olympique Lyonnais|Lyon]], being eventually named [[captain (association football)|captain]] on both teams and being affectionately nicknamed ''Cavégol'' in the latter.<ref name=LHAC>[http://www.hac-foot.com/actualite/fin-de-carriere-d-alain-caveglia-retour-sur-son-parcours.html Fin de carrière d'Alain Cavéglia: retour sur son parcours (End of career for Alain Cavéglia: a summary)]; Le Havre AC, 20 April 2002 (in French)</ref>

In January 2000, Caveglia joined [[FC Nantes|Nantes]], going on to win his only professional silverware in his six-month stint, [[1999–2000 Coupe de France|the season]]'s [[Coupe de France]], gaining a [[Penalty kick (association football)|penalty]] in the [[Last-minute goal|last minute]] of a 2–1 [[2000 Coupe de France Final|final win]] over amateurs [[Calais RUFC]] which was converted by [[Antoine Sibierski]].<ref name=BBC>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/sport/football/740136.stm|title=Calais robbed by cruel blow|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=8 May 2000|access-date=2 August 2016}}</ref> In July of that year he returned to Le Havre, going on to amass a further 30 [[Ligue 2]] goals (in [[2001–02 French Division 2|2001–02]], his 14 helped the side return to the top flight) and subsequently retiring in June 2002, aged 34.<ref name=LHAC/>

On 19 August 2011, Caveglia was appointed [[director of football]] at [[Stade Malherbe Caen|Caen]].<ref>[http://www.smcaen.fr/liste-saisons/saison-2011-2012/actualites/depeches/depeche.2011-08-19.7076004023 Alain Caveglia rejoint le SM Caen (Alain Caveglia joins SM Caen)] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110920212544/http://www.smcaen.fr/liste-saisons/saison-2011-2012/actualites/depeches/depeche.2011-08-19.7076004023 |date=20 September 2011 }}; SM Caen, 19 August 2011 (in French)</ref> He left the club at the end of April 2019, and one month later, he was appointed, still as sporting director, at AS Villers Houlgate Côte Fleurie (ASVH).<ref>[https://asvh.fr/2019/05/20/alain-caveglia-nouveau-conseiller-sportif/ Alain CAVEGLIA nouveau Conseiller Sportif], asvh.fr, 20 May 2019</ref>

'''Michele Ferri''' (born 28 May 1981) is an Italian former [[association football]] [[defender (football)|defender]] who last played for Italian club [[Varese Calcio S.S.D.|Varese]].

==Career==
===Milan===
He grew up within the [[A.C. Milan]] youth system, but never played a full senior game for the ''rossoneri'', instead being sent to lower league teams, namely [[A.C. Cesena|Cesena]] and [[U.S. Triestina Calcio|Triestina]].

===Triestina ===
Ferri was sold to Triestina in a [[co-ownership (football)|co-ownership deal]] for 400 million [[Italian lira|lire]] (€206,583) along with [[Eder Baù]] (200 million lire) and [[Alessandro Budel]] (400 million lire) in June 2002.<ref>A.C. Milan S.p.A. ''bilancio'' (financial report and accounts) on 30 June 2002, PDF purchased from Italian [[Camera di Commercio, Industria, Agricoltura e Artigianato|C.C.I.A.A.]] (in Italian)</ref> On 11 June 2003 Triestina acquired the remain half of the contract from Milan for €2 million (with Budel returned to Milan also for €2 million fee).<ref>A.C. Milan S.p.A. ''bilancio'' (financial report and accounts) on 30 June 2003, PDF purchased from Italian [[Camera di Commercio, Industria, Agricoltura e Artigianato|C.C.I.A.A.]] (in Italian)</ref><ref>U.S. Triestina Calcio S.p.A. ''bilancio'' (financial report and accounts) on 30 June 2003, PDF purchased from Italian [[Camera di Commercio, Industria, Agricoltura e Artigianato|C.C.I.A.A.]] (in Italian)</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.lega-calcio.it/ita/partecipazioni2003.pdf|title=Partecipazioni 2003|trans-title=Co-ownership 2003|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20071118213220/http://www.lega-calcio.it/ita/partecipazioni2003.pdf|archivedate=18 November 2007|date=26 June 2003|access-date=21 June 2017|publisher=Lega Nazionale Professionisti|language=Italian}}</ref>

===Palermo===
On 19 July 2003, Ferri was acquired by [[Serie B]] club [[U.S. Città di Palermo|Palermo]] for a fee of €1 million and a 5-year contract,<ref>U.S. Città di Palermo S.p.A. ''bilancio'' (financial report and accounts) on 30 June 2005, PDF purchased from Italian [[Camera di Commercio, Industria, Agricoltura e Artigianato|C.C.I.A.A.]] (in Italian)</ref><ref>{{cite press release|url=http://palermocalcio.it/it/0304/news/scheda.php?id=137|title=PRESO MICHELE FERRI DALLA TRIESTINA|date=19 July 2003|access-date=21 June 2017|publisher=U.S. Città di Palermo|language=Italian}}</ref> which then became league champions in 2004. But after Palermo won promotion to Serie A, his first team appearances were limited to 15 games. Ferri made his Serie A debut on 6 January 2005 for Palermo, against [[Reggina Calcio|Reggina]].

On 31 January 2006 he was sold to [[Cagliari Calcio|Cagliari]] for €1 million fee, in another co-ownership deal.<ref>U.S. Città di Palermo S.p.A. ''bilancio'' (financial report and accounts) on 30 June 2006, PDF purchased from Italian [[Camera di Commercio, Industria, Agricoltura e Artigianato|C.C.I.A.A.]] (in Italian)</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.uefa.com/competitions/uefacup/news/kind=1/newsid=390822.html|title=Palermo call Tedesco home|date=2006-01-31|access-date=2009-01-30|publisher=[[UEFA]]|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060519031131/http://www.uefa.com/competitions/UEFACup/news/Kind%3D1/newsId%3D390822.html|archive-date=2006-05-19}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://palermocalcio.it/it/0506/news/scheda.php?id=4732|title=Ferri ceduto al Cagliari|date=31 January 2006|access-date=21 June 2017|publisher=U.S. Città di Palermo|language=Italian}}</ref>

===Cagliari===
Ferri was signed by [[Cagliari Calcio|Cagliari]] on 31 January 2006, re-joining Budel. In June 2007 Cagliari bought the remaining half of the registration rights of Ferri, for an additional €600,000 fee.<ref>U.S. Città di Palermo S.p.A. ''bilancio'' (financial report and accounts) on 30 June 2007, PDF purchased from Italian [[Camera di Commercio, Industria, Agricoltura e Artigianato|C.C.I.A.A.]] (in Italian)</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cagliaricalcio.net/news/6080/ferri-e-per-intero-del-cagliari.html|title=Ferri è per intero del Cagliari|date=20 June 2007|accessdate=28 March 2013|publisher=Cagliari Calcio|language=Italian}}</ref><ref>{{cite press release|url=http://palermocalcio.it/it/0607/news/scheda.php?id=7247|title=Ceduti Codrea, Ferri, D'Aiello e Di Franco, alle buste Makinwa e Matteini|date=20 June 2007|access-date=21 June 2017|publisher=U.S. Città di Palermo|language=Italian}}</ref>

===Sampdoria===
He joined [[U.C. Sampdoria|Sampdoria]] in January 2009 for a peppercorn fee of €1,000.<ref>U.C. Sampdoria S.p.A. ''bilancio'' (financial report and accounts) on 31 December 2009, PDF purchased from Italian [[Camera di Commercio, Industria, Agricoltura e Artigianato|C.C.I.A.A.]] (in Italian)</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.sampdoria.it/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=4318&Itemid=73|title=Dal Cagliari arriva a titolo definitivo Michele Ferri|date=2009-01-29|accessdate=2009-08-11|publisher=Sampdoria|language=Italian}}</ref> He just played twice in [[2008–09 Serie A]] season for Cagliari in September against [[A.C. Siena]] and November against [[Calcio Catania]] before joined Sampdoria. He successively left the club on a free transfer and joined Serie B outfit [[Vicenza Calcio|Vicenza]] later in September 2009.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.vicenza.com/mx_op-nwminiportal_id-1643_opt-1522796_cat-3049001001.shtml |title=Michele Ferri in biancorosso |date=2009-09-17 |accessdate=2009-10-17 |publisher=Vicenza Calcio |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090923151257/http://www.vicenza.com/mx_op-nwminiportal_id-1643_opt-1522796_cat-3049001001.shtml |archivedate=September 23, 2009 }}</ref>

In November 2010, Ferri joined [[Atalanta B.C.|Atalanta]] in another free transfer.

On 31 January 2014, Ferri joined [[Serie B]] side [[Trapani Calcio|Trapani]], signing a deal until the end of the 2013–14 season.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.trapanicalcio.it/trapanicalcio/notizie/750-arriva-il-difensore-michele-ferri.html|title=Arriva il difensore Michele Ferri|date=2014-01-31|accessdate=2014-02-03|publisher=Trapani Calcio|language=Italian|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160808073726/http://www.trapanicalcio.it/trapanicalcio/notizie/750-arriva-il-difensore-michele-ferri.html|archive-date=2016-08-08|url-status=dead}}</ref> He successively left Trapani to join fellow Serie B club [[F.C. Pro Vercelli 1892|Pro Vercelli]]. He then played the 2015–2016 season with hometown club [[Aurora Pro Patria 1919|Pro Patria]], which he then left to join [[Serie D]] club [[Varese Calcio S.S.D.|Varese]] during the summer of 2016.

'''Claudio Bonomi''' (born 28 December 1972), is an Italian former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[midfielder]].

==Playing career==
Having started his career at [[ASD Fanfulla]], Bonomi played during the 1990s for several of the main teams in Italian football, such as [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]], [[Empoli FC|Empoli]], Lecce and [[UC Sampdoria|Sampdoria]]. In 2002–03, he was part of the champion squad for Fiorentina in Serie C2. He played in the last years of his career in the [[Eccellenza]] and [[Promozione]] categories.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.teleaesse.it/sport/calcio-scontrone-claudio-bonomi-riparte-dallatletico-sanniti/ |title=Scontrone, Claudio Bonomi riparte dall'Atletico Sanniti |website=teleaesse.it |date=10 August 2014 |access-date=29 October 2024 |language=it}}</ref><ref name="Castello 2000">{{cite web|url=https://calciopeligno.blogspot.com/2015/06/castello-2000-torna-claudio-bonomi.html |title=Castello 2000: torna Claudio Bonomi. |website=Calcio Peligno |date=18 July 2015 |access-date=29 October 2024 |language=it}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://ilcalcio.net/carriera-claudio-bonomi |title=Carriera di Claudio Bonomi |website=ilcalcio.net |access-date=29 October 2024 |language=it}}</ref>

==Managerial career==

Bonomi became a coach soon after retiring, managing Castello 2000 in the [[Prima Categoria]]. His most recent work was at Barisardo, which competes in Eccellenza.<ref name="Castello 2000" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://sardegna.diariosportivo.it/articoli/bonomi-disegna-il-suo-barisardo-paura-di-nessuno-e-pronti-fare-il-nostro-gioco-casa-e |title=Bonomi disegna il suo Barisardo: "Paura di nessuno e pronti a fare il nostro gioco in casa e fuori" |website=sardegna.diariosportivo.it |date=5 September 2023 |access-date=29 October 2024 |language=it}}</ref>

'''Joel Joshua Frederick Melvin "Jobi" McAnuff''' (born 9 November 1981) is a former [[Association football|footballer]]. He was predominantly a [[Midfielder#Winger|winger]] but he has also played as an occasional [[Midfielder#Central midfielder|central midfielder]]. Since his retirement he has worked as a pundit.

McAnuff began his career at [[Wimbledon F.C.|Wimbledon]], making over 100 appearances for the club before brief spells at [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] and [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]]. McAnuff joined [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] in 2005, spending two years there before moving again, this time to [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] before joining [[Reading F.C.|Reading]] in 2009. He was appointed captain in 2011 and went on to make over 200 appearances in all competition for the Royals. Prior to Reading's promotion to the Premier League in [[2011–12 Football League Championship|2011–12]] he had spent his entire career playing in England's second tier, amassing over 400 league appearances. He joined Leyton Orient in 2014.

Born in London, McAnuff has represented [[Jamaica national football team|Jamaica]], his father's country of birth, at international level. He made his debut in May 2002 although his next appearance did not come until nearly eleven years later in February 2013. He was part of their squads which won the [[2014 Caribbean Cup]] and competed at the [[2015 Copa América]].

==Club career==
===Early career===
Born in [[Edmonton, London|Edmonton]], London, McAnuff made his professional debut in the [[2001–02 in English football|2001–02]] season with [[Football League First Division|First Division]] side [[Wimbledon F.C.|Wimbledon]].<ref name="PFA 385"/> He played 104 games and scored 15 goals for the club, staying until Wimbledon's last season, [[2003–04 in English football|2003–04]]. In March 2003, [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] manager [[Harry Redknapp]] agreed a deal to bring McAnuff and teammate [[Nigel Reo-Coker]] to the south coast club in preparation for their first Premiership season.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/p/portsmouth/2995190.stm|title=Pompey agree Reo-Coker fee|date=16 June 2003|publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=3 June 2007}}</ref> Financial problems resulted in the player remaining at Wimbledon despite having already signed contracts with Portsmouth.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/p/portsmouth/3135805.stm|title=Pompey concede Dons duo defeat|date=8 August 2003|publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=3 June 2007}}</ref>

In the January 2004 transfer window, with Wimbledon now in [[Administration (British football)|administration]], West Ham manager [[Alan Pardew]] signed McAnuff for [[West Ham United F.C.|West Ham United]] joining fellow former Wimbledon players, [[Nigel Reo-Coker]] and [[Adam Nowland]].<ref>{{cite news
|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/w/west_ham_utd/3456533.stm
|title=West Ham sign McAnuff
|publisher=BBC Sport
|date=2 March 2004 |access-date=17 May 2011}}</ref> He played only 14 games for the club, scoring one goal against Crewe.<ref>{{cite news
|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_div_1/3507704.stm
|title=West Ham 4–2 Crewe
|publisher=BBC Sport
|date=16 March 2004 |access-date=26 October 2009}}</ref> To generate funds for future transfers Pardew was forced to sell McAnuff<ref>{{cite web
|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/pardew-haunted-by-mcanuff-6973497.html
|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130114071255/http://www.thisislondon.co.uk/sport/article-14444857-pardew-haunted-by-mcanuff.do
|url-status=live
|archive-date=14 January 2013
|title=Pardew haunted by McAnuff
|publisher=thisislondon.co.uk
|access-date=17 May 2011}}</ref> and on 12 August 2004, he joined [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]] for a fee of £250,000 and was virtually ever-present in his first year at the club. He made his debut against [[Ipswich Town F.C.|Ipswich Town]], scoring his first goal against his former side West Ham United during a 4–1 win.<ref>{{cite news
|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_div_1/3967405.stm
|title=Cardiff 4–1 West Ham
|publisher=BBC Sport
|date=3 November 2004 |access-date=26 October 2009}}</ref> He played 48 games and scored 3 goals and picked up numerous player of the month awards.{{Citation needed|date=July 2008}}  With Cardiff in financial difficulty, McAnuff left the club at the end of the [[2004–05 in English football|2004–05]] season to join [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] for a fee of around £600,000.<ref name="McAnuff completes Palace switch">{{cite news | title=McAnuff completes Palace switch | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/c/crystal_palace/4586531.stm| publisher=[[BBC Sport]] | date=31 May 2005 | access-date=5 September 2008}}</ref>

===Crystal Palace===
In his first season at Selhurst Park, McAnuff played 43 games and scored eight goals. His performances in the Championship understandably led to interest from a number of clubs and in the summer of 2006 being linked with moves to [[Watford F.C.|Watford]], [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] and [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]], the latter managed by his former boss at Palace [[Iain Dowie]].{{Citation needed|date=July 2008}}  However, it was announced during the summer 2006 transfer window that he would stay at Crystal Palace, and play for the Eagles under new boss [[Peter Taylor (footballer, born 1953)|Peter Taylor]].

===Watford===
After a less successful [[2006–07 in English football|2006–07]] campaign, McAnuff moved to Watford in June 2007 in a deal worth an initial £1.75 million.<ref name="Winger McAnuff signs for Watford">{{cite news | title=Winger McAnuff signs for Watford | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/w/watford/6724031.stm | publisher=[[BBC Sport]] | date=5 June 2007 | access-date=5 June 2007}}</ref>
[[File:Jobi McAnuff (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|upright|McAnuff playing for [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] in 2008]]

===Reading===
[[File:Jobi McAnuff - reading (cropped).jpg|thumb|200px|McAnuff playing for [[Reading F.C.|Reading]] in 2010]]
McAnuff joined [[Reading F.C.|Reading]] on 27 August 2009, then managed by former [[Watford F.C.|Watford]] boss [[Brendan Rodgers]], on a three-year contract for an undisclosed fee.<ref>{{cite news|title=Reading sign McAnuff and Rasiak |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/r/reading/8225581.stm |publisher=[[BBC Sport]] |date=27 August 2009 |access-date=28 August 2009}}</ref> He made his debut against his former club Watford on 26 September 2009 with his first goal coming a month later in a 3–1 win over [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]] on 31 October.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_div_1/8326123.stm |title=Coventry 1 – 3 Reading |publisher=BBC |date=31 October 2009 |access-date=20 November 2009}}</ref>

He scored the third goal against [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]] in the [[2011 Football League Championship play-off final#second legs|2011 play-off]] semi-final with a storming run, sealing a 3–0 victory and sending Reading to [[Wembley Stadium|Wembley]] for the final against [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.getreading.co.uk/sport/football/readingfc/s/2092806_twogoal_long_ends_reading_fcs_wembley_wait |title=Two-goal Long ends Reading FC's Wembley wait |date=17 May 2011 |publisher=Get Reading |access-date=28 January 2013}}</ref> McAnuff started in the final and provided assists for both Reading goals but was unable to prevent them losing the game 4 – 2.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_div_1/13497817.stm |title=Reading 2 – 4 Swansea |publisher=BBC |access-date=28 January 2013}}</ref> [[Ívar Ingimarsson|Ivar Ingimarsson]] and [[Matt Mills]] both left the club in the months following the play-off final defeat and on 13 July 2011, days after extending his contract until 2014, McAnuff was named as the new Reading captain.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.getreading.co.uk/sport/football/readingfc/s/2096065_mcanuff_picked_as_new_reading_fc_captain |title=McAnuff picked as new Reading FC captain |date=12 July 2011 |publisher=Get Reading |access-date=28 January 2013}}</ref> On being named captain he paid tribute to his predecessors and described it as a "massive honour".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.getreading.co.uk/sport/football/readingfc/s/2096500_mcanuff_honoured_to_be_named_reading_fc_captain |title=McAnuff honoured to be named Reading FC captain |date=18 July 2011 |publisher=Get Reading |access-date=28 January 2013}}</ref>

The 2012–13 season saw McAnuff playing in the [[Premier League]] for the first time in his twelve-year career. By 27 November, he had laid on four goals for his teammates, lying joint third in the league assists table.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.readingfc.co.uk/news/article/our-assists-king-271112-512024.aspx |title=Our Assists King |publisher=Reading FC |access-date=26 January 2013}}</ref> He had to wait until February for his first goal of the season, scoring in Reading's 2–1 [[FA Cup]] fifth round defeat to [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] at Old Trafford.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21449426 |title=Man Utd 2–1 Reading |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=21 February 2013}}</ref>

He left the club at the end of the 2013–14 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jobi, Mikele & Kaspars to move on|url=http://www.readingfc.co.uk/news/article/mcanuff-leigertwood-gorkss-leave-060514-1539505.aspx|publisher=Reading F.C.}}</ref> McAnuff gave an exclusive interview to Get Reading saying he is fine over not getting a renewed contract, though he went on to say: "My time at Reading has been fantastic. It's been a thoroughly enjoyable chapter of my life, a stable one as well. Five seasons is a large chunk of my career. I've captained the club with massive amounts of pride and enjoyment. I've had many great times, the Championship win obviously, and also some bad ones as well. But it's been a fantastic experience. It's a time of my career I'll never forget."<ref>{{cite news|title=McAnuff: I'll never forget my five 'fantastic' years at Reading FC|url=http://www.getreading.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/mcanuff-ill-never-forget-five-7080787|publisher=Get Reading|date=6 May 2014|access-date=11 May 2014}}</ref>

===Leyton Orient===
On 25 July 2014, McAnuff signed a two-year deal with [[Football League One|League One]] side [[Leyton Orient F.C.|Leyton Orient]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=NEWS: Jobi McAnuff Signs |url=http://www.leytonorient.com/news/article/mcanuff-signs-250714-1782911.aspx |publisher=Leyton Orient F.C |date=25 July 2014 |access-date=25 July 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150710085240/http://www.leytonorient.com/news/article/mcanuff-signs-250714-1782911.aspx |archive-date=10 July 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In May 2016, he was released from Leyton Orient when it was announced that he would not be retained when his contract expired.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36314548|title=Leyton Orient: Mathieu Baudry among eight players to leave League Two club|publisher=BBC Sport|date=17 May 2016|access-date=24 May 2016}}</ref>

McAnuff began trialing with [[Minnesota United FC|Minnesota United]] of the [[North American Soccer League (2011–2017)|North American Soccer League]] in June 2016.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Burdine|first1=Wes|title=Minnesota United Want-Ad: "Some F*cking Barn-Burners"|url=http://fiftyfive.one/2016/06/loons-look-reinforcements-season-break/|access-date=28 June 2016|publisher=FiftyFive.One|date=23 June 2016}}</ref> McAnuff made an appearance for Minnesota United in an international friendly against [[Liga MX]] side [[Club León]] on 25 June 2016 in the first ever football match at [[Target Field]].<ref>{{cite news|title=LOONS AND LEÓN BATTLE IN FRONT OF 18,505 AT TARGET FIELD|url=http://www.mnunitedfc.com/news/2016/06/25/loons-and-len-battle-in-front-of-18505-at-target-field|access-date=28 June 2016|publisher=Minnesota United FC|date=25 June 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160629152131/http://www.mnunitedfc.com/news/2016/06/25/loons-and-leon-battle-in-front-of-18505-at-target-field|archive-date=29 June 2016}}</ref>

===Stevenage===
On 19 July 2016 McAnuff signed for [[Football League Two|League Two]] team [[Stevenage F.C.|Stevenage]] on a free transfer.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/36833587 | title=Jobi McAnuff: Stevenage sign Jamaica winger on free transfer | publisher=BBC Sport | date=19 July 2016 | access-date=20 July 2016}}</ref>

===Return to Leyton Orient===
On 20 July 2017, it was announced that McAnuff would return to Leyton Orient. He captained the side in the 2018–19 season and went on to win the league title. He later signed a further contract extension and moved into a player/coach role.

He was made [[Manager (association football)|interim manager]] of Leyton Orient on 28 February 2021 following the sacking of [[Ross Embleton]].<ref>{{cite web | url= https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11742/12231995/jobi-mcanuff-named-interim-boss-of-leyton-orient-following-ross-embletons-departure | title=McAnuff named Interim Manager of Leyton Orient | publisher=Sky Sports | date=28 February 2021| access-date=28 February 2021}}</ref> He retired from playing at the end of the [[2020–21 Leyton Orient F.C. season|2020–21]] season. He was released from his management duties and left the club on 8 May 2021.<ref>{{cite web | url= https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/57042794 | title= Jobi McAnuff: Leyton Orient will not offer interim manager permanent job  | publisher=BBC Sport | date=8 May 2021| access-date=8 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url= https://www.leytonorient.com/2021/05/09/jobi-mcanuff-retires-from-playing-a-look-back-at-a-wonderful-career/ | title= JOBI MCANUFF RETIRES FROM PLAYING: A LOOK BACK AT A WONDERFUL CAREER  | publisher=Leyton Orient | date=9 May 2021| access-date=9 May 2021}}</ref>

'''Frederik Hillersborg Sørensen''' (born 14 April 1992) is a Danish professional [[association football|footballer]] who plays for Italian {{Italian football updater|UnionBrescia}} club [[Union Brescia]].<ref name=autogenerated1 /> His primary position is [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|centre back]] but he can also play as a [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|right back]].

==Club career==
===Early career===
Born in [[Copenhagen]], Sørensen began playing football with hometown clubs [[KFUM Roskilde]] and [[FC Roskilde]] before joining [[Lyngby Boldklub|Lyngby]] in 2007. After breaking into the first team, he was under contract until 2013.<ref name=Juve/>

===Juventus===
Sørensen officially signed for [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] on 27 August 2010<ref name="Juve">{{Cite web|url=http://www.bold.dk/fodbold/nyheder/Lyngby-udlejer-forsvarstalent-til-Juventus/|title=Lyngby udlejer forsvarstalent til Juventus|date=27 August 2010|website=Bold.dk}}</ref> after a trial with the Turin-based club in July of the same year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://lyngby-boldklub.dk/Nyheder/U19_nyt/Lyngby_udlejer_Frederik_S%F8rensen_til_Juventus/ |title=Lyngby udlejer Frederik Sørensen til Juventus|website=Lyngby Boldklub|date=27 August 2010 |language=da|url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120712071649/http://lyngby-boldklub.dk/Nyheder/U19_nyt/Lyngby_udlejer_Frederik_S%F8rensen_til_Juventus/ |archive-date=12 July 2012 }}</ref> After injuries to [[Leandro Rinaudo]] and [[Zdeněk Grygera]] that would rule them out for several months, Sørensen was called up to the first team for the first time against [[Bologna F.C. 1909|Bologna]] on 23 October 2010,<ref>{{closed access}}{{cite news|url=http://www.juventus.com/site/ita/NEWS_newsseriea_2D1D3804FFF5471AB461570EB6ED4037.asp|title=I 21 bianconeri disponibili per il Bologna|website=Juventus|date=23 October 2010|access-date=8 November 2010|language=it|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101026011924/http://www.juventus.com/site/ita/NEWS_newsseriea_2D1D3804FFF5471AB461570EB6ED4037.asp|archive-date=26 October 2010}} {{password-protected}}</ref> and against [[A.C. Milan|Milan]].<ref>{{closed access}}{{Cite news|title=Rientra Amauri, 20 convocati per il big match|trans-title=Amauri Returned, 20 call-up for a big match|url=http://www.juventus.com/site/ita/NEWS_newsseriea_E47247636598447F8FFED9426126ABE5.asp|website=Juventus|date=29 October 2010|access-date=8 November 2010|language=it|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101107073845/http://www.juventus.com/site/ita/NEWS_newsseriea_E47247636598447F8FFED9426126ABE5.asp|archive-date=7 November 2010}} {{password-protected}}</ref>

===Bologna===
On 17 January 2012, Sørensen was officially sent to Bologna in a [[co-ownership (football)|co-ownership deal]] for €2.5 million (initially in a cash-plus-player deal, for [[Saphir Taïder]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.juventus.com/wps/wcm/connect/c74c784c-da0f-4894-acff-36a25db908cb/Relazione+finanziara+semestrale+DEFINITIVA+ENG.pdf?MOD=AJPERES&CACHEID=c74c784c-da0f-4894-acff-36a25db908cb|title=Half-yearly financial report at 31 December 2011|date=29 March 2012|access-date=18 June 2012|publisher=Juventus FC|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150119124148/http://www.juventus.com/wps/wcm/connect/c74c784c-da0f-4894-acff-36a25db908cb/Relazione+finanziara+semestrale+DEFINITIVA+ENG.pdf?MOD=AJPERES&CACHEID=c74c784c-da0f-4894-acff-36a25db908cb|archive-date=19 January 2015}}</ref> Despite making just three league appearances for his new club during the remainder of the 2011–12 Serie A campaign, the young defender became an integral part of his club's first team throughout the [[2012–13 Serie A]] season, after they had renewed the co-ownership agreement with Juventus.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Sørensen: "Orgoglioso di essere qui"|url=http://www.bolognafc.it/news.asp?id=2628|website=Bologna FC 1909|date=19 January 2012|access-date=18 June 2012|language=it|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120126022210/http://www.bolognafc.it/news.asp?id=2628|url-status=dead|archive-date=26 January 2012}}</ref>

===Return to Juventus===
On 20 June 2014, Sørensen was re-signed on a permanent basis by Juventus for €800,000.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.juventus.com/juve/en/news/co-ownership-of-gabbiadini-and-sorensen|title = Juventus News: Latest news & highlights}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Annual Financial Report 30 June 2014|url=http://www.juventus.com/media/native/investor-relations-docs/english/financial-statemet-and-reports/2013-2014/Relazione+finanziaria+annuale+30_06_2014+eng.pdf|url-status=dead|website=Juventus|date=21 November 2014|access-date=13 October 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181004231922/http://www.juventus.com/media/native/investor-relations-docs/english/financial-statemet-and-reports/2013-2014/Relazione+finanziaria+annuale+30_06_2014+eng.pdf|archive-date=4 October 2018}}</ref> In August 2014, Sørensen started training with English side [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]] ahead of completing a loan move to the club, but the move collapsed after a disagreement between the player's agent and Leeds owner [[Massimo Cellino]], resulting him in returning to Juventus.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.yorkshireeveningpost.co.uk/sport/leeds-united/latest-whites-news/leeds-united-agent-blamed-as-sorensen-loan-deal-collapses-1-6776850|title=Leeds United: Agent blamed as Sorensen loan deal collapses|date=8 August 2014|work=Yorkshire Evening Post|access-date=8 August 2014}}</ref>

===Hellas Verona (loan)===
Sørensen officially signed for [[Hellas Verona F.C.|Hellas Verona]] on 29 August 2014 on a one-year loan deal for €300,000.<ref name=Verona>{{cite news|title=Sorensen joins Hellas Verona, Rosseti moves to Atalanta|url=http://www.juventus.com/juve/en/news/sorensen-rosseti-loans|website=Juventus|date=29 August 2014|access-date=31 August 2014}}</ref><ref name=Juventus2015bilancio>{{Cite web|title=Relazione finanziaria annuale al 30 giugno 2015|url=http://www.juventus.com/media/native/investor-relations-docs/italiano/bilanci/1415/Relazione%20finanziaria%20annuale%20al%2030%20giugno%202015%20definitiva_bassa.pdf|website=Juventus F.C.|date=1 October 2015|access-date=11 October 2015|language=it|format=PDF (1.24MB)|archive-date=24 November 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151124082256/http://www.juventus.com/media/native/investor-relations-docs/italiano/bilanci/1415/Relazione%20finanziaria%20annuale%20al%2030%20giugno%202015%20definitiva_bassa.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===1. FC Köln===
In July 2015, German [[Bundesliga]] side [[1. FC Köln]] signed Sørensen for €1.6 million.<ref name=Juventus2015bilancio/><ref>{{Cite web|title=Frederik Sørensen joins 1. FC Köln|url=https://www.fc-koeln.de/en/fc-info/news/detailpage/details/frederik-soerensen-joins-1-fc-koeln/|website=1. FC Köln|date=11 July 2015|access-date=11 July 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150712155032/https://www.fc-koeln.de/en/fc-info/news/detailpage/details/frederik-soerensen-joins-1-fc-koeln/|archive-date=12 July 2015}}</ref> He quickly established himself as a starter in the centre of Köln's defence and, in January 2017, signed a contract extension until 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Lehmann, Risse, und Sørensen {{!}} Verlängert mit Leistungsträgern|url=https://fc.de/fc-info/news/detailseite/details/fc-verlaengert-mit-leistungstraegern/|url-status=dead|website=1. FC Köln|date=11 January 2017|access-date=24 May 2018|language=de|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201111192606/https://fc.de/fc-info/news/detailseite/details/fc-verlaengert-mit-leistungstraegern/|archive-date=11 November 2020}}</ref> The team qualified for the [[2017–18 UEFA Europa League]] but suffered relegation just one season later.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Kölns Abstieg ist besiegelt|url=https://www.spiegel.de/sport/fussball/1-fc-koeln-bundesliga-abstieg-ist-besiegelt-a-1205358.html|website=[[Der Spiegel]]|date=28 April 2018|access-date=24 May 2018|language=de}}</ref> On 16 January 2021, it was reported that the club had released Sørensen from his contract.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kicker.de/soerensen-loest-vertrag-in-koeln-offenbar-auf-4000000036410/transfermeldung|title=Sörensen löst Vertrag in Köln offenbar auf|access-date=16 January 2021|language=de}}</ref>

====Loan to BSC Young Boys====
On 18 August 2019, Sørensen was loaned out to Swiss club [[BSC Young Boys]] for the 2019–20 season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Frederik Sørensen Leihweise zu YB|url=https://www.bscyb.ch/news?nID=11582|website=BSC Young Boys|date=18 August 2019|language=de}}</ref>

===Delfino Pescara 1936===
Having been released by 1.FC Köln, Sørensen joined [[Serie B]] club [[Delfino Pescara 1936|Pescara]] on a free transfer.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Frederik Sorensen è un nuovo giocatore #BiancAzzurro|url=https://www.pescaracalcio.com/frederik-sorensen-e-un-nuovo-giocatore-biancazzurro/|access-date=21 January 2021|website=Delfino Pescara 1936|date=20 January 2021}}</ref>

==International career==
Sørensen has been capped four times for the [[Denmark national under-17 football team|Danish U17 team]], twice against [[Portugal national under-17 football team|Portugal]],<ref>{{Cite news|title=U/17 landsholdet slog til igen mod Portugal.|url=http://www.dbu.dk/news/newsShow.aspx?id=250288|website=Danish Football Association|date=5 December 2008|access-date=8 November 2010|language=da|archive-date=9 December 2008|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081209023517/http://www.dbu.dk/news/newsShow.aspx?id=250288|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.dbu.dk/Nyheder/2008/December/endnu_en_sejr_i_portugal.aspx|title=Endnu en sejr i Portugal|website=Danish Football Association|date=5 December 2008|access-date=8 November 2010|language=da}}</ref> and twice against Greece.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.dbu.dk/news/newsShow.aspx?id=250619|title=Sjældent nederlag til U/17|website=Danish Football Association|date=10 February 2009|access-date=8 November 2010|language=da|archive-date=16 June 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110616200146/http://www.dbu.dk/news/newsShow.aspx?id=250619|url-status=dead}}</ref> He also played once for the U18 team in an unofficial friendly matches against Bavaria and Romania U18 as an unused substitute.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.dbu.dk/news/newsShow.aspx?id=251856|title=U/18 tog 3. pladsen i Tjekkiet|website=Danish Football Association|date=20 August 2009|access-date=8 November 2010|language=da|archive-date=16 June 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110616200218/http://www.dbu.dk/news/newsShow.aspx?id=251856|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was a part of the Danish squad for the [[UEFA European Under-21 Championship]], but he only played the first match and got injured as Denmark were eliminated after the group phase.

In June 2015, Sørensen was called up to the [[Denmark national football team|Danish senior squad]] for a friendly match against [[Montenegro national football team|Montenegro]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Olsen plyndrer U21-landshold for otte spillere|url=https://ekstrabladet.dk/sport/fodbold/landsholdsfodbold/olsen-plyndrer-u21-landshold-for-otte-spillere/5590486|website=[[Ekstra Bladet]]|date=2 June 2015|language=da}}</ref> In 2017, he debuted against [[Germany national football team|Germany]] during the [[2018 FIFA World Cup qualification]] that ended in a 1–1 draw.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Dansker tager til schweizisk mesterklub|url=https://sport.tv2.dk/fodbold/2019-08-18-dansker-tager-til-schweizisk-mesterklub|website=[[TV 2 (Denmark)|TV 2 Denmark]]|date=18 August 2019|language=da}}</ref>

'''Adriano Fabiano Rossato''' (born 27 August 1977 in [[Vila Velha]], [[Espírito Santo]]) is a Brazilian former [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[left back]], and is a [[manager (association football)|manager]].

==Football career==
During his Brazilian career, [[direct free kick|free kick]] specialist Rossato represented [[Botafogo de Futebol e Regatas|Botafogo]], [[Rio Branco Atlético Clube|Rio Branco-ES]], [[Criciúma Esporte Clube|Criciúma]], [[Associação Atlética Portuguesa (RJ)|Portuguesa-RJ]], [[União Agrícola Barbarense Futebol Clube|União Barbarense]] and [[Marília Atlético Clube|Marília]], moving to Portugal in July 2002 with [[Madeira]]'s [[C.D. Nacional|Nacional]]. During two seasons he scored an impressive 17 [[Primeira Liga]] goals, including a [[hat-trick]] against [[S.C. Beira-Mar|Beira-Mar]] on 25 April 2004 (3–0 home win).<ref>[http://www.record.xl.pt/Futebol/Nacional/1a_liga/interior.aspx?content_id=195309 Nacional-Beira-Mar, 3–0: "Bombas" de Rossato carimbam ida à Europa (Nacional-Beira-Mar, 3–0: Rossato "bombs" stamp trip to Europe)]; [[Record (Portuguese newspaper)|Record]], 26 April 2004 (in Portuguese)</ref>

Bought by [[FC Porto|Porto]] in July 2004, Rossato never played an official game for the northerners. He then joined [[La Liga]] side [[Real Sociedad]],<ref>[https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/01a0-0ea6f4362d9d-7f1c17d1d2f7-1000--nuno-valente-stays-on/ Nuno Valente stays on]; UEFA, 31 August 2004</ref> scoring – from a free kick – in only his second [[2004–05 La Liga|season]] appearance, a 1–2 loss to [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]],<ref>[http://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2004/09/26/liga/1096235210.html La Real se hunde en Sevilla (Real hit bottom in Seville)]; [[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]], 26 September 2004 {{in lang|es}}</ref> finishing with 22 matches.

For [[2005–06 Primeira Liga|2005–06]], Rossato was loaned back to Portugal, signing with [[S.C. Braga|Braga]] on a one-year deal.<ref>[https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/news/01ac-0e6cfdc65d74-36edfeb18ec5-1000--braga-right-for-rossato/ Braga right for Rossato]; UEFA, 30 August 2005</ref> Having returned to Sociedad for the following campaign, he returned - again on loan - to the [[Iberian Peninsula|Iberian]] neighbours, moving to [[U.D. Leiria|União Leiria]] in January 2007.<ref>[https://www.futebol365.pt/artigo/15272-u-leiria-rossato-por-emprestimo-ate-final-da-epoca/ U. Leiria: Rossato por empréstimo até final da época (U. Leiria: Rossato on loan until end of season)]; Futebol 365, 30 January 2007 (in Portuguese)</ref>

Released in the summer of 2007, Rossato joined [[Segunda División|second division]] team [[Málaga CF|Málaga]], being instrumental in the [[Andalusia]]ns' [[2007–08 Segunda División|2008 top flight return]] after a two-year absence. He would miss, however, the vast majority of [[2008–09 La Liga|the next season]] due to injury;<ref>[http://www.malagacf.com/es/noticia/primer-equipo/fabiano-rossato-evoluciona-bien-su-lesion/241/311 Fabiano Rossato evoluciona bien de su lesión (Fabiano Rossato recovering well from his injury)]; Málaga CF, 28 October 2008 {{in lang|es}}</ref><ref>[http://malagacf.diariosur.es/noticias/2008-12-12/rossato-sufre-recaida-aunque-20081212.html Rossato sufre una recaída, aunque se descarta una lesión grave (Rossato suffers relapse, but serious injury ruled out)]; [[Diario Sur]], 12 December 2008 {{in lang|es}}</ref> his first match took place only on 17 May 2009, as he played the second half of a 1–2 away loss to [[Sporting de Gijón|Sporting Gijón]] (12 minutes played).<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20120714113306/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/253053?cc=5739|title=Sporting Gijón 2–1 Málaga}}; [[ESPN FC|ESPN Soccernet]], 17 May 2009</ref>

Because of his injuries, Málaga announced in July 2009 it would not renew Rossato's contract, so the player was released. Late in the following month the 32-year-old signed for another club in the country, second level's [[UD Salamanca|Salamanca]].<ref>[http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2009/08/21/mas_futbol/1250836059_850215.html Rossato ficha por la Unión (Rossato signs for Unión)]; [[Diario AS]], 21 August 2009 {{in lang|es}}</ref><ref>[http://www.marca.com/2009/11/07/futbol/2adivision/1257627964.html El Salamanca tira de remontada ante el Levante (Salamanca display comeback ways against Levante)]; [[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]], 7 November 2009 {{in lang|es}}</ref>

'''Juan Manuel Falcón Jiménez''' (born 24 February 1989) is a Venezuelan retired professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Forward (association football)#Striker|striker]].

==Club career==
=== Portuguesa FC ===
His first steps in professional football were in [[Portuguesa FC]], where he started playing as a [[midfielder]]. Later on, he passed over several field positions until reaching the forward spot.<ref>[http://www.liderendeportes.com/noticias/futbol/juan-falcon--delantero-por--cosas-del-destino-.aspx Juan Falcón, delantero por “cosas del destino” (Juan Falcón: Forward for "a matter of fate")] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304192703/http://www.liderendeportes.com/noticias/futbol/juan-falcon--delantero-por--cosas-del-destino-.aspx |date=4 March 2016 }}; Líder en Deportes, 27 April 2014 {{in lang|es}}</ref>

Falcón scored his first professional goal in a [[Copa Venezuela]] match against [[Zamora FC]], which eventually would be his last destination in the local league after a small period in [[Trujillanos FC]].

=== Zamora ===
With Zamora, he won the league two times in a row and he became the top goalscorer in the league with 19 goals.

===FC Metz===
In mid 2014, he signed a three-year contract with French team [[FC Metz]], in a transfer reported to be around €800,000.<ref>[http://www.eluniversal.com/deportes/torneo-clausura-2014/140418/juan-falcon-llevara-sus-goles-a-francia Juan Falcón llevará sus goles a Francia (Juan Falcón will bring his goals to France)]; [[El Universal (Caracas)|El Universal]], 18 April 2014 {{in lang|es}}</ref> He left the club in 2016.

===Retirement===
After two years without a club, Falcón confirmed on 17 January 2020, that he had retired at the age of 30 due to a knee injury.<ref>[https://solovenex.com/tuit-juan-falcon-se-retira-del-futbol-a-los-30-anos/ (+TUIT) Juan Falcón se retira del fútbol a los 30 años], solovenex.com, 17 January 2020</ref>

==International career==
He made his debut on 23 March 2008, coming as a substitute against [[El Salvador national football team|El Salvador]].

'''Domingo José Larrainzar Santamaría''' ('''Txomin Larrainzar''' in [[Basque language|Basque]]; born 8 September 1969) is a Spanish former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played mainly as a [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|central defender]].

His younger brother [[Iñigo Larrainzar|Iñigo]], often referred to as ''Larrainzar II'', was also a footballer, and both played at [[CA Osasuna|Osasuna]].<ref>[https://blogs.20minutos.es/quefuede/tag/inigo-larrainzar/ Qué fue de… Iñigo Larrainzar: otro canterano osasunista en Bilbao (What happened to… Iñigo Larrainzar: another Osasuna youth player in Bilbao)]; [[20 minutos]], 10 July 2014 (in Spanish)</ref>

==Club career==
Larrainzar was born in [[Pamplona]]. A product of hometown [[CA Osasuna]]'s youth ranks, he totalled seven [[La Liga]] appearances from 1988 to 1990. In his [[1990–91 La Liga|third season]] he helped with 14 games and one goal to help the [[Navarre]]se club to finish fourth and [[1991–92 UEFA Cup|qualify]] for the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]]<ref>[http://www.diariodenavarra.es/noticias/deportes/futbol/osasuna/aquella_uefa_hace_anos_42792_1027.html Aquella UEFA de hace 20 años (That UEFA from 20 years ago)]; [[Diario de Navarra]], 4 October 2011 (in Spanish)</ref>– although younger, his brother [[Iñigo Larrainzar|Iñigo]] was already an essential member of the squad.

With Osasuna in the [[Segunda División]], Larrainzar dropped down to [[Segunda División B]] and signed for [[Málaga CF]], helping the side to return to the top flight in just two years. Although never an undisputed starter, he featured regularly.<ref>[https://www.laliga.com/noticias/que-fue-de-txomin-larrainzar Qué fue de... Txomin Larrainzar (What happened to... Txomin Larrainzar)]; [[La Liga]], 11 March 2015 (in Spanish)</ref>

In [[2002–03 Segunda División|2002–03]], prior to Málaga's [[2002 UEFA Intertoto Cup|victory]] in the [[UEFA Intertoto Cup]], Larrainzar returned to the second tier with [[Levante UD]],<ref>[https://as.com/futbol/2002/08/07/mas_futbol/1028671206_850215.html Aizpurúa y Larrainzar, nuevos jugadores del Levante (Aizpurúa and Larrainzar, new Levante players)]; [[Diario AS]], 7 August 2002 (in Spanish)</ref> but retired at the end of the campaign at the age of 33.

'''José Fernando Marqués Martínez''' (born 4 December 1984) is a Spanish former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[midfielder]].

==Club career==
Born in [[Madrid]], Marqués first appeared professionally for hometown's [[Rayo Vallecano]], playing ten games in [[La Liga]] then 25 in [[Segunda División]]. In the [[2004–05 La Liga|2004–05 season]] he signed with [[Racing de Santander]], but several bouts of indiscipline made him fall out of favour with the management,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.eldiariomontanes.es/pg060115/prensa/noticias/Deportes/200601/15/DMO-DEP-203.html|title=Marqués, detenido a las 5 de la mañana tras un accidente en el Ayuntamiento|trans-title=Marqués, arrested at 5 A.M. after accident in City Hall|newspaper=[[El Diario Montañés]]|language=es|date=15 January 2006|accessdate=1 April 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.eldiariomontanes.es/prensa/20060716/deportes/marques-paradero-desconocido_200607160028.html|title=Marqués, en paradero desconocido|trans-title=Marqués, unknown whereabouts|newspaper=El Diario Montañés|language=es|date=16 July 2006|accessdate=1 April 2014}}</ref> and he joined [[Atlético Madrid]] on loan in the January [[transfer window]]; he spent his first months with the capital side's [[Atlético Madrid B|B-team]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.notasdefutbol.com/racing-de-santander/fernando-marques-ejemplo-de-indisciplina|title=Fernando Marqués, ejemplo de indisciplina|trans-title=Fernando Marqués, example of indiscipline|publisher=Notas de Fútbol|language=es|date=29 September 2005|accessdate=27 August 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090905113303/http://www.notasdefutbol.com/racing-de-santander/fernando-marques-ejemplo-de-indisciplina|archive-date=5 September 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://hemeroteca.mundodeportivo.com/preview/2007/04/06/pagina-9/872184/pdf.html|title=La curiosa historia de Fernando Marqués|trans-title=The curious story of Fernando Marqués|newspaper=[[Mundo Deportivo]]|language=es|date=6 April 2007|accessdate=1 April 2014}}</ref>

Eventually Marqués failed to settle with both clubs, with which he still had another spell.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2006/12/22/mas_futbol/1166742010_850215.html|title=Fernando Marqués llega con la carta de libertad hasta final de temporada|trans-title=Fernando Marqués arrives as a free agent until the end of the season|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|language=es|date=22 December 2006|accessdate=1 April 2014}}</ref> After less than one month with [[CD Castellón]]<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.eldiariomontanes.es/prensa/20060819/deportes/marques-castellon_20060819.html|title=Marqués se va al Castellón|trans-title=Marqués goes to Castellón|newspaper=El Diario Montañés|language=es|date=19 August 2006|accessdate=1 April 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elperiodicomediterraneo.com/noticias/castellon/club-medita-rescindir-contrato-fernando-marques_245685.html|title=El club medita rescindir el contrato a Fernando Marqués|trans-title=Club thinking about terminating contract to Fernando Marqués|newspaper=El Periódico Mediterráneo|language=es|date=31 August 2006|accessdate=1 April 2014}}</ref> he joined [[Greece|Greek]] club [[Iraklis F.C. (Thessaloniki)|Iraklis]], remaining in the country until the end of his contract on 16 June 2009.

On 26 June 2009, Marqués was linked with a move to [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dailyexpress.co.uk/posts/view/110129|title=Celts agree £3.8M Fortune fee|newspaper=[[Daily Express]]|date=26 June 2009|accessdate=26 June 2009}}</ref> Following the initial link with the player the [[Scottish Premier League]] club offered him a trial on 14 July, and the player's agent, Manuel Ferrer, was quoted: "Celtic have made a proposal for Fernando to go on trial for a few days. However, this is unsure." He continued: "It's normal in the UK for players to go on trial. In Spain and Europe they do not do this kind of thing. So we are speaking and I hope he will accept"; eventually, nothing came of it.

During the month of August, Marqués went on a week-long trial with [[RCD Espanyol]]. On the 25th, after convincing manager [[Mauricio Pochettino]], he secured a contract for the [[2009–10 La Liga|2009–10 campaign]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rcdespanyol.com/principal.php?modulo=detalleNoticia&idnoticia=7387&idioma=1&idmenu=9&idsubmenu=108|title=Marqués será el siguiente fichaje|trans-title=Marqués will be next signing|publisher=RCD Espanyol|language=es|date=25 August 2009|access-date=26 August 2009|archive-date=28 September 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110928175316/http://www.rcdespanyol.com/principal.php?modulo=detalleNoticia&idnoticia=7387&idioma=1&idmenu=9&idsubmenu=108|url-status=dead}}</ref> He scored his first and only goal for the [[Catalonia|Catalans]] on 10 January 2010, coming on as a second-half [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] in a 2–1 home win against [[Real Zaragoza]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/uk/en/report/275896/report.html?soccernet=true&cc=5739|title=Marques eases pressure on Espanyol|publisher=[[ESPN Soccernet]]|date=10 January 2010|accessdate=10 December 2012}}</ref>

Marques was signed by [[Parma F.C.]] on 14 July 2010<ref>{{cite news|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101009032559/http://fcparma.com/stagione/archivio-news/7079-arriva-marques-presentazione-al-tardini-ore-18-e-diretta-sulla-web-tv.html|archive-date=9 October 2010|url=http://www.fcparma.com/stagione/archivio-news/7079-arriva-marques-presentazione-al-tardini-ore-18-e-diretta-sulla-web-tv.html|title=Arriva Marques: presentazione al Tardini ore 18 e diretta sulla web tv|trans-title=Marques arrives: presentation at the Tardini 18:00 live on web tv|publisher=Parma FC|language=it|date=14 July 2010|url-status=usurped|accessdate=25 August 2011}}</ref> on loan from [[Terrassa FC]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.legaseriea.it/it/serie-a-tim/calcio-mercato?p_p_id=BDC_calciomercato_WAR_LegaCalcioBDC&p_p_lifecycle=0&p_p_state=normal&p_p_mode=view&p_p_col_id=column-1&p_p_col_pos=1&p_p_col_count=2&_BDC_calciomercato_WAR_LegaCalcioBDC_flagEstivo=true|title=Calcio mercato|trans-title=Football market|publisher=Lega Serie A|language=it|date=1 September 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101007100740/http://www.legaseriea.it/it/serie-a-tim/calcio-mercato?p_p_id=BDC_calciomercato_WAR_LegaCalcioBDC&p_p_lifecycle=0&p_p_state=normal&p_p_mode=view&p_p_col_id=column-1&p_p_col_pos=1&p_p_col_count=2&_BDC_calciomercato_WAR_LegaCalcioBDC_flagEstivo=true|archive-date=7 October 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref> for €200,000,<ref>Parma F.C. S.p.A. ''bilancio'' (financial report and accounts) on 30 June 2011 (in Italian) [http://www.registroimprese.it/ Require purchase in CCIAA]</ref> but injury disrupted [[2010–11 Serie A|his first year]] at the club and he did not take to the pitch once in the second half of the [[Serie A]] season. Nevertheless, the former signed him outright.

Marqués was released in the summer of 2012, but he appealed to the [[Italian Football Federation]] as he did not agree to the early termination. The governing body restored the contract,<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.figc.it/Assets/contentresources_2/ContenutoGenerico/47.$plit/C_2_ContenutoGenerico_35740_StrilloComunicatoUfficiale_lstAllegati_Allegato_0_upfAllegato.pdf|title=Comunicato ufficiale N°233/CGF (2012–13)|trans-title=Official announcement N°233/CGF (2012–13)|publisher=[[Italian Football Federation]]|language=it|date=5 April 2013|accessdate=6 March 2014}}</ref> but Parma appealed to both the Italian Federation's Federal Court of Justice and the ''Tribunale Nazionale di Arbitrato per lo Sport'' (TNAS) of the [[Italian National Olympic Committee]]. The club later withdrew its appeal to the latter, after the contract was finally terminated by mutual consent.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.coni.it/images/TNAS/709_A.pdf|title=Tribunale nazionale di arbitrato per lo sport|trans-title=National court for sport arbitrations|publisher=Coni|language=it|accessdate=6 March 2014}}</ref>
