'''Jacques Abardonado''' (born 27 May 1978) is a French football manager and former player, currently assistant coach of [[Ligue 1]] club [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]].

== Career ==
Abardonado joined [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] as a player in 1996, coming from [[US Marseille Endoume|Marseille Endoume]]. He ended his professional playing career at OM in 2014 to pursue coaching. Between 2014 and 2023, he held several roles within the club: assistant coach for the reserve team, head coach for the youth squads, assistant for the U19s, assistant for the first team, and served as interim head coach between [[Marcelino García Toral|Marcelino]]'s departure and [[Gennaro Gattuso]]'s arrival.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fayet |first=Mathias |date=2024-04-06 |title=OM : très belle nouvelle pour un enfant du club |url=https://www.onzemondial.com/ligue-1/om-tres-belle-nouvelle-pour-un-enfant-du-club-880812 |access-date=2025-05-28 |website=Onze Mondial |language=fr}}</ref> In February 2026, he was appointed caretaker manager again after the exit of [[Roberto De Zerbi]].<ref>{{cite news |title=OM. « Les joueurs sont atteints psychologiquement » estime Abardonado après le nul concédé face à Strasbourg |url=https://www.ouest-france.fr/sport/football/olympique-de-marseille/om-les-joueurs-sont-atteints-psychologiquement-estime-abardonado-apres-le-match-face-a-strasbourg-7e1ac622-09dc-11f1-8f27-f38523081a88 |access-date=18 February 2026 |work=[[Ouest-France]] |date=14 February 2026 |language=French}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Abardonado is of [[Gitanos|Spanish Romani]] descent through his father.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sofoot.com/mon-pere-voulait-que-je-sois-musicien-ou-footballeur-220811.html|title=" Mon père voulait que je sois musicien ou footballeur "|date=19 April 2016 }}</ref> His cousin is the French footballer [[André-Pierre Gignac]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2009/mar/24/ben-lyttleton-ligue-gignac-toulouse |work=[[The Guardian]] |location=London |title=Gignac's rocky road takes a turn for the better with call for national service |first=Ben |last=Lyttleton |date=24 March 2009 |access-date=1 September 2022}}</ref> He grew up in [[La Castellane]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=OM : gitan, cousin de Gignac, né comme Zidane et volcanique... Qui est Jacques "Pancho" Abardonado, entraîneur intérimaire de Marseille |url=https://www.ladepeche.fr/2023/09/21/om-gitan-cousin-de-gignac-ne-comme-zidane-et-volcanique-qui-est-jacques-pancho-abardonado-entraineur-interimaire-de-marseille-11468530.php |access-date=8 January 2024 |website=ladepeche.fr |language=fr}}</ref>

'''Iñaki Bea Jauregi''' (born 27 June 1978) is a Spanish former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|central defender]], currently [[Manager (association football)|manager]] of [[Segunda Federación]] club [[Gimnástica Segoviana CF|Gimnástica Segoviana]].

==Playing career==
Bea was born in [[Amurrio]], [[Álava]]. After starting out with modest clubs in his native [[Basque Country (autonomous community)|Basque Country]], and having a stint in the [[Segunda División B]] with [[Ciudad de Murcia]], he had his first taste of professional football at [[Lorca Deportiva CF]] in the [[2005–06 Segunda División|2005–06 season]], helping the side retain their [[Segunda División]] status under [[Unai Emery]].<ref>[https://www.marca.com/futbol/eibar/2017/03/04/58bab2cd468aeb46098b460c.html Iñaki Bea: fontanero, ferretero, futbolista, ojeador... y entrenador contra el Madrid (Iñaki Bea: plumber, ironmonger, footballer, scout... and manager against Madrid)]; [[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]], 4 March 2017 (in Spanish)</ref>

Subsequently, Bea joined [[Real Valladolid]], scoring three goals in 35 games as the [[Castile and León]] team [[2006–07 Segunda División|returned]] to [[La Liga]] in 2007 after a three-year absence<ref>[https://www.canarias7.es/hemeroteca/el_valladolid_aprovecha_la_debilidad_defensiva_canaria-HJCSN33859 El Valladolid aprovecha la debilidad defensiva canaria (Valladolid take advantage of Canarian defensive weakness)]; [[Canarias7]], 3 September 2006 (in Spanish)</ref><ref>[https://www.abc.es/deportes/sevi-valladolid-eficaz-gana-numancia-y-dispara-200701220300-1631044148315_noticia.html Un Valladolid eficaz gana al Numancia y se dispara (Effective Valladolid beat Numancia and take off)]; [[ABC (newspaper)|ABC]], 22 January 2007 (in Spanish)</ref><ref>[https://www.20minutos.es/deportes/noticia/lorca-valladolid-arrollador-210979/0/ El Lorca se estrella ante un Valladolid arrollador (Lorca crash into crushing Valladolid)]; [[20 minutos]], 12 March 2007 (in Spanish)</ref><ref name=Job>[https://www.marca.com/futbol/valladolid/2018/11/09/5be55157e5fdea2b0d8b4683.html Iñaki Bea: "El trabajo de Sergio es bestial" (Iñaki Bea: "Sergio is doing one hell of a job")]; Marca, 9 November 2018 (in Spanish)</ref> but being less used in the following years – only seven matches in the [[2007–08 La Liga|2007–08 campaign]] and 17 in [[2008–09 La Liga|2008–09]].<ref>[https://as.com/futbol/mas_futbol/inaki-bea-se-convierte-en-el-nuevo-entrenador-del-numancia-n/ Iñaki Bea se convierte en el nuevo entrenador del Numancia (Iñaki Bea becomes the new manager of Numancia)]; [[Diario AS]], 11 November 2022 (in Spanish)</ref> He made his debut in the [[Spanish football league system|Spanish top flight]] on 28 October 2007, featuring 45 minutes in the 2–2 away draw against [[CA Osasuna]].<ref>[http://www.marca.com/marcador/futbol/2007_08/primera/jornada_9/osa_vad/indexCronica.html Angustioso empate en el Reyno (Anxious draw at the Reyno)]; Marca, 28 October 2007 (in Spanish)</ref>

Bea left in June 2009,<ref>[https://www.elnortedecastilla.es/20090604/deportes/real_valladolid/futbolista-hizo-querer-zorrilla-20090604.html El futbolista que se hizo querer en Zorrilla (The footballer who earned people's love at Zorrilla)]; [[El Norte de Castilla]], 4 June 2009 (in Spanish)</ref> moving to the second tier with [[Real Murcia CF]].<ref>[https://www.marca.com/2009/07/03/futbol/equipos/murcia/1246638593.html El Real Murcia se refuerza de tres en tres (Real Murcia strengthen in groups of three)]; Marca, 3 July 2009 (in Spanish)</ref> He was [[2009–10 Segunda División|relegated in his only season]], being subsequently released.<ref>[https://www.laverdad.es/murcia/20100707/deportes/real-murcia/inaki-octavo-jugador-abandona-201007071749.html Iñaki Bea, octava baja del Real Murcia tras el descenso (Iñaki Bea, eighth out at Real Murcia after relegation)]; [[La Verdad (Murcia)|La Verdad]], 7 July 2010 (in Spanish)</ref> 

Aged 32, Bea had his first experience abroad, signing a 1+1 contract with [[Austria]]n club [[FC Wacker Innsbruck (2002)|FC Wacker Innsbruck]].<ref>[http://fc-wacker-innsbruck.at/news/kampfmannschaft/2310-inaki-bea-jauregi-wechselt-zu-wacker-innsbruck Iñaki Bea Jauregi wechselt zu Wacker Innsbruck (Iñaki Bea Jauregi moves to Wacker Innsbruck)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100701073444/http://www.fc-wacker-innsbruck.at/news/kampfmannschaft/2310-inaki-bea-jauregi-wechselt-zu-wacker-innsbruck|date=1 July 2010}}; Wacker Innsbruck, 28 June 2010 (in German)</ref> He made his [[Austrian Football Bundesliga|Bundesliga]] debut on 18 July 2010, playing the entire 4–0 home win over [[SK Rapid Wien]].<ref>[http://sportv1.orf.at/100718-3905/?href=http%3A%2F%2Fsportv1.orf.at%2F100718-3905%2F3906bigstory_txt.html Sensation am Tivoli (Show at Tivoli)]; [[ORF (broadcaster)|ORF]], 18 July 2010 (in German)</ref> His only goal in the competition arrived on 22 September of that year, when he helped to a 4–2 away defeat of [[Kapfenberger SV]].<ref>[https://www.news.at/a/drei-tore-minuten-innsbruck-kapfenberg-4-2-278079 Drei Tore innerhalb von nur zehn Minuten: Innsbruck schlägt Kapfenberg souverän 4:2 (Three goals in just ten minutes: Innsbruck have no problem beating Kapfenberg 4:2)]; [[NEWS (Austrian magazine)|NEWS]], 22 September 2010 (in German)</ref>

==Coaching career==
After retiring, Bea worked as assistant manager at [[Levante UD]] and [[SD Eibar]] under [[José Luis Mendilibar]], his former coach at Valladolid.<ref>[https://www.elcorreo.com/alava/deportes/futbol/liga-primera/201406/04/inaki-ayudante-tecnico-mendilibar-20140603205421.html Iñaki Bea, ayudante técnico de Mendilibar (Iñaki Bea, Mendilibar's technical assistant)]; [[El Correo]], 4 June 2014 (in Spanish)</ref><ref>[https://elpais.com/deportes/2017/01/21/actualidad/1485020363_420190.html Iñaki Bea, un segundo con historia (Iñaki Bea, this sidekick has quite a past)]; [[El País]], 22 January 2017 (in Spanish)</ref><ref name=Job/> On 24 February 2022, he was appointed head coach of the [[Dominican Republic national football team|Dominican Republic national side]].<ref>[https://www.cope.es/deportes/futbol/futbol-internacional/noticias/inaki-bea-convierte-nuevo-seleccionador-futbol-republica-dominicana-20220224_1912206 Iñaki Bea se convierte en el nuevo seleccionador de fútbol de República Dominicana (Iñaki Bea becomes the new Dominican Republic national team football manager)]; [[Cadena COPE]], 24 February 2022 (in Spanish)</ref>

Bea signed with [[CD Numancia]] in the same capacity in November 2022.<ref>[https://as.com/futbol/mas_futbol/inaki-bea-presentado-como-nuevo-entrenador-del-numancia-n/ Iñaki Bea, presentado como nuevo entrenador del Numancia (Iñaki Bea, presented as new manager of Numancia)]; Diario AS, 14 November 2022 (in Spanish)</ref> The following 1 May, he was dismissed.<ref>[https://as.com/futbol/mas_futbol/inaki-bea-destituido-como-entrenador-del-numancia-n/ Iñaki Bea destituido como entrenador del Numancia (Iñaki Bea dismissed as manager of Numancia)]; Diario AS, 1 May 2023 (in Spanish)</ref>

Subsequently, Bea was in charge of [[Segunda Federación]] clubs [[Águilas FC]]<ref>[https://www.laopiniondemurcia.es/deportes/2024/02/19/aguilas-fc-ficha-inaki-bea-98378912.html El Águilas FC ficha a Iñaki Bea como entrenador (Águilas FC sign Iñaki Bea as manager)]; La Opinión de Murcia, 19 February 2024 (in Spanish)</ref> and [[Gimnástica Segoviana CF]].<ref>[https://www.eldiasegovia.es/noticia/zc63ebc14-3d00-45a3-97cf632abc480e47/202507/inaki-bea-tecnico-de-la-sego-me-gusta-el-futbol-de-vertigo Iñaki Bea, técnico de la Sego: "Me gusta el fútbol de vértigo" (Iñaki Bea, manager of Sego: "I like football in the fast lane")]; El Día de Segovia, 23 July 2025 (in Spanish)</ref>

'''Danny Galm''' (born 17 March 1986) is a German professional [[Manager (association football)|football manager]] and former [[football player|player]] who played as a [[striker (association football)|striker]]. He currently manages [[FC Liefering]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/regionalliga/rlwest/regionalliga-west/2009-10/1-fc-kaiserslautern-ii-130/36144/spieler_danny-galm.html | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20090813000404/http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/regionalliga/rlwest/regionalliga-west/2009-10/1-fc-kaiserslautern-ii-130/36144/spieler_danny-galm.html | url-status = dead | archive-date = 13 August 2009 | title = Galm, Danny | language = German | publisher = [[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] | access-date = 20 February 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.fussballdaten.de/spieler/galmdanny/ | title = Danny Galm | language = German | publisher = fussballdaten.de | accessdate = 20 February 2010}}</ref>

==Career==
Having previously played for [[VfB Stuttgart II]], [[Eintracht Frankfurt II]], and [[FC Energie Cottbus|Energie Cottbus]], he joined  [[Stuttgarter Kickers]] in February 2009, but transferred to [[1. FC Kaiserslautern II]] after Stuttgarter Kickers were relegated from the [[3. Liga]]. He spent four-and-a-half seasons with [[SpVgg Neckarelz]]. After a half-season with [[Viktoria Aschaffenburg]], he ended his playing career. In June 2023, he took over the head coaching role at [[SV Sandhausen]] at the start of the 2023–24 season.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.dfb.de/news/detail/sv-sandhausen-danny-galm-wird-cheftrainer-252702/|website=dfb.de|title=SV Sandhausen: Danny Galm wird Cheftrainer|date=19 June 2023|accessdate=19 June 2023}}</ref> He was sacked in October 2023.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dfb.de/news/detail/sandhausen-stellt-trainer-galm-frei-256052/|title=Sandhausen stellt Trainer Galm frei|website=dfb.de |date=22 October 2023|access-date=22 October 2023|language=de}}</ref>

In February 2026, he succeeded [[Daniel Beichler]] as manager of Austrian club [[FC Liefering]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.fc-liefering.at/de/aktuelles/news/danny-galm-neuer-cheftrainer|title=Danny Galm neuer Cheftrainer des FC Liefering|website=FC Liefering |date=18 February 2026|access-date=22 March 2026|language=de}}</ref>

'''Levin Mete Öztunalı''' (born 15 March 1996) is a German professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as a [[midfielder]].<ref name="soccerway">{{Soccerway|258664}}</ref>

Following seven years in the academy of [[Hamburger SV]], Öztunalı made his senior debut with [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] in 2013. He made 15 league appearances for the club before joining [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]] on a season-and-a-half loan deal two years later. Following the expiration of the loan in 2016, Öztunalı joined [[1. FSV Mainz 05|Mainz]], where he spent 5 years before joining [[1. FC Union Berlin|Union Berlin]] in 2021. After two years there, he returned to Hamburg in 2023.

He has also represented [[Germany national football team|Germany]] at various youth levels and was part of the squads which won the [[2014 UEFA European Under-19 Championship|UEFA European Under-19 Championship]] in 2014 and the [[2017 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|UEFA European Under-21 Championship]] in 2017. He gained 30 caps and scored 7 goals until 2019.

==Club career==
===Bayer Leverkusen===
[[file:Levin-Oeztunali.jpg|thumb|upright=0.7|left|Öztunalı with Leverkusen in 2014]]
On 2 February 2013, [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] announced the signing of Öztunalı from Bundesliga rivals [[Hamburger SV|Hamburg]] on a five-year deal, with the transfer to be completed at the end of the season.<ref name="Bayer04">{{cite web | date = 2 February 2013 |url=http://www.bayer04.de/b04-ENG/en/_md_aktuell-dt.aspx?aktuell=aktuell-4134|title=Bayer 04 sign Levin Öztunalı| website = Bayer Leverkusen |access-date=19 January 2016}}</ref> He made his debut on 10 August, coming on as a late substitute for [[Gonzalo Castro]] in a 3-1 win over [[SC Freiburg|Freiburg]].<ref name="SBNation">{{cite news |last= McCauley|first= Kevin | date = 10 August 2013 |url=https://www.sbnation.com/soccer/2013/8/10/4608766/bayer-vs-freiburg-final-score-result-2013-bundesliga|title=Bayer 04 sign Levin Öztunalı| website = SB Nation|access-date=19 January 2016}}</ref> At 17 years and 146 days old, Öztunalı became the youngest player to ever play for Leverkusen in the Bundesliga and the 11th youngest player in the history of the competition.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.bild.de/sport/fussball/levin-oeztunali/seeler-enkel-schreibt-geschichte-31787340.bild.html|title=Seeler grandson writes history|website=Bild|date=12 August 2013|access-date=3 May 2016 | language = de}}</ref> On 26 August 2014, Öztunalı was voted the second-best u-18 player in Germany behind teammate [[Julian Brandt]], and in doing so, he was awarded the silver [[Fritz Walter Medal]].<ref name="Leverkusen">{{cite web | date = 26 August 2014 |url=http://www.bayer04.de/b04-ENG/en/_md_aktuell-dt.aspx?aktuell=aktuell-5202|title=Brandt awarded gold Fritz Walter medal| website = Bayer Leverkusen|access-date=19 January 2016}}</ref>

====Loan spell at Werder Bremen====
On 21 December 2014, Öztunalı joined [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]] on an 18-month loan deal, running until the end of the 2015–16 campaign.<ref name="WerderBremen">{{cite web | date = 21 December 2014 | url = https://www.werder.de/de/profis/news/52949.php | title = Levin Öztunalı amplifies the SV Werder | website = Werder Bremen | access-date = 19 January 2016 | language = de | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160124133206/http://www.werder.de/de/profis/news/52949.php | archive-date = 24 January 2016 | url-status = dead }}</ref> Upon his arrival in Bremen, Chief Executive [[Thomas Eichin]] described Öztunalı as "one of the most sought-after talents in the Bundesliga."<ref name="Vavel">{{cite web |last= Killen|first= Stephen | date = 21 December 2014 |url=http://www.vavel.com/en/international-football/germany-bundesliga/428341-german-u-20-national-team-levin-oztunali-joins-werder-bremen-on-loan-till-2016.html|title=German U-20 Levin Öztunalı joins Werder Bremen on loan 'til 2016| website = Vavel|access-date=19 January 2016}}</ref> His first goal for ''Die Grün-Weißen'' came on the final day of the [[2014–15 Bundesliga|2014–15 season]] when he netted in a 3–2 loss to [[Borussia Dortmund]].<ref name="Goal">{{cite web |last= Thompson|first= Peter | date = 23 May 2015 |url=http://www.goal.com/en-us/match/borussia-dortmund-vs-werder-bremen/1713981/report|title=Borussia Dortmund 3–2 Werder Bremen: Dortmund seals European spot as Klopp says farewell| website = Goal.com |access-date=19 January 2016}}</ref> Öztunalı had to wait until May of the following season to score his next goal for the club, netting one and assisting another in a 6–2 drubbing of [[VfB Stuttgart|Stuttgart]]. The result saw Bremen climb out of the relegation zone at the expense of their opponents.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.espnfc.com/german-bundesliga/match/426844/werder-bremen-vfb-stuttgart/report|title=Werder Bremen go clear of relegation zone with rout of Stuttgart|website=ESPN|date=2 May 2016|access-date=3 May 2016}}</ref> He made his final appearance for the club on 14 May, playing for 77 minutes as Bremen beat [[Eintracht Frankfurt]] 1–0 to avoid relegation.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://talksport.com/football/bundesliga-results-werder-bremen-avoid-relegation-thanks-djilobodji-goal-and-amazing|title=Bundesliga results: Werder Bremen avoid relegation thanks to Djilobodji goal and amazing support |website=talkSPORT|date=14 May 2016|access-date=4 June 2016}}</ref>

On 2 June 2016, amid speculation that Öztunalı would remain at Werder Bremen, Bayer Leverkusen director of football [[Rudi Völler]] confirmed that he would be returning to Leverkusen and would be part of the squad for the following season.<ref>{{cite web |last=Lußem|first=Frank | date = 2 June 2016|url=https://www.kicker.de/oeztunali_voeller-schiebt-den-riegel-vor-653153/artikel|title=Öztunalı: Völler schiebt den Riegel vor|website=kicker|access-date=4 June 2016 }}</ref> Öztunalı amassed a total of 46 appearances across all competitions during his 18-month spell with Werder Bremen.

===Mainz 05===
On 25 August 2016, Leverkusen's Bundesliga rivals [[1. FSV Mainz 05|Mainz 05]] announced the signing of Öztunalı on a five-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mainz05.de/mainz05/en/aktuell/news/news-detail/article/oeztunali-wird-05er.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160826142244/http://www.mainz05.de/mainz05/en/aktuell/news/news-detail/article/oeztunali-wird-05er.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=26 August 2016|title=Öztunalı is a Zerofiver|website=Mainz 05|date=25 August 2016|access-date=25 August 2016}}</ref> He made his debut against [[Borussia Dortmund]] on 27 August, coming on as a second half substitute for [[Suat Serdar]], and scored his first goal for the club in the following match-week in a 4–4 draw with [[TSG 1899 Hoffenheim|Hoffenheim]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.espnfc.com/german-bundesliga/story/2948254/werder-bremen-held-down-by-augsburg;-hoffenheim-storm-back-in-mainz-draw|title=Augsburg keep down Werder Bremen; Hoffenheim storm back in Mainz draw|website=ESPN|date=11 September 2016|access-date=11 September 2016}}</ref> He scored his first-ever European goal on 29 September, netting the winner in a 3–2 [[UEFA Europa League]] victory over Azerbaijani side [[FK Qabala|Qabala]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.espnfc.com/uefa-europa-league/story/2962180/inter-milan-lose-second-straight-in-europa-league-as-southampton-draw|title=Zlatan Ibrahimovic lifts Man United as Inter lose again in Europa League|website=ESPN|date=29 September 2016|access-date=30 September 2016}}</ref> He ultimately made 36 appearances in the season across all competitions, including 23 starts and five goals in the league as Mainz narrowly avoided the relegation play-offs.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://kwese.espn.com/football/blog/espn-fc-united/68/post/3220261/scouting-spotlight-jorginho-mikel-oyarzabal-levin-oztunali|title=Scouting Spotlight: Jorginho, Mikel Oyarzabal, Levin Oztunali|website=ESPN|last=Stanger|first=Matthew|date=7 October 2017|access-date=8 February 2018}}</ref>

===Hamburger SV===
On 27 June 2023, Öztunalı joined [[Hamburger SV]] on a free transfer, on a contract until 2026.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.hsv.de/en/hsv-sign-levin-oeztunali|title=HSV sign Levin Öztunalı|website=www.hsv.de|date=4 July 2023| language = English}}</ref>

==International career==
He has represented various German youth teams, however, as he is not capped at senior international level, he is eligible to represent for [[Germany national football team|Germany]] or [[Turkey national football team|Turkey]].

===German national youth teams===
[[File:2017083211455 2017-03-24 Fussball U21 Deutschland vs England - Sven - 1D X II - 0335 - AK8I3148 mod.jpg|thumb|Öztunalı (left) in action for [[Germany national youth football team|Germany]] against [[England national under-21 football team|England U21]] in 2017]]
Öztunalı has represented Germany at various youth levels since his debut for the [[Germany national youth football team|U15 side]] in 2010.<ref name="Vavel"/> In 2014, he was part of the squad which took part in the [[2014 UEFA European Under-19 Championship|UEFA European Under-19 Championship]] in Hungary. He scored the third goal in a semi-final victory over Austria and started in the final as Germany claimed the title with a 1–0 win over Portugal.<ref name=19EC>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/under19/news/0257-0ded26790c91-d928d49378e0-1000--germany-planning-pays-off-for-oztunali/|title=Germany planning pays off for Öztunalı|website=UEFA|last=Haslam|first=Andrew|date=29 July 2014|access-date=3 May 2017}}</ref> His form throughout the competition saw him named in the Team of the Tournament alongside top scorer [[Davie Selke]] and four other countrymen.<ref name=TOTT>{{cite web|url=http://www.uefa.com/under19/season=2014/technical-report/uefa-technical-team/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140914012505/http://www.uefa.com/under19/season=2014/technical-report/uefa-technical-team/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=14 September 2014|title=The UEFA Technical Team Team of the Tournament|website=UEFA|access-date=3 May 2017}}</ref>

In 2017, Öztunalı was one of 23 players selected in [[Stefan Kuntz]]'s squad for the [[2017 UEFA European Under-21 Championship]] in Poland.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/under21/history/teams/200047--germany/|title=Under-21 - Germany|website=UEFA|access-date=22 June 2017}}</ref> Germany were ultimately crowned champions, beating [[Spain national under-21 football team|Spain]] 1–0 in the final to claim the title.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/40451698|title=Germany won their second European Under-21 Championship with victory over four-time champions Spain in Poland|website=BBC|date=30 June 2017|access-date=1 July 2017}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Öztunalı is the grandson of former German international footballer and [[FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] finalist [[Uwe Seeler]].<ref name="DieWelt">{{cite web |last= Bogena|first= Kai Niels | date = 7 November 2015 |url=https://www.welt.de/sport/fussball/bundesliga/werder-bremen/article148507944/Der-Karriere-Knick-des-Uwe-Seeler-Enkels.html|title=Die Karriere-Knick des Uwe-Seeler-Enkels | website = Die Welt |access-date=19 January 2016}}{{in lang|de}}</ref> His father is [[Turkish people|Turkish]] and previously served as a scout for [[Hamburger SV]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.rp-online.de/sport/seeler-wuetet-nach-wechsel-seines-enkels-zu-bayer-04-aid-1.3166201|title=Seeler wütet nach Wechsel seines Enkels zu Bayer 04|website=RD Online|date=4 February 2013|access-date=3 May 2016 | language = de}}</ref>

'''Laurent Delorge''' (born 21 July 1979) is a [[Belgium|Belgian]] former [[Football (soccer)|footballer]]. He formerly served [[K.A.A. Gent|AA Gent]], [[Coventry City]], [[Lierse S.K. (1906)|Lierse SK]], [[RSC Anderlecht]], [[ADO Den Haag]], [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] and [[Roda JC Kerkrade]].

== Career ==
After scoring five goals in ten appearances in his [[Belgian First Division A|Jupiler League]] debut season for [[K.A.A. Gent|AA Gent]] he was transferred to [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]] who at the time were playing in the [[FA Premier League]].

Delorge signed for Coventry midway through the 1998/99 season, however he didn't make his first appearance for the club until 29 January 2000, when he came on as a substitute in Coventry's defeat to [[Charlton Athletic]] in the [[FA Cup]].<ref>{{cite news 
|url=http://www.sportinglife.com/football/premiership/charlton/reports/story_get.cgi?STORY_NAME=soccer/00/01/29/SOCCER_Coventry_Nightlead.html&TEAMHD=charlton&DIV=prem&TEAM=CHARLTON--ATHLETIC&RH=Charlton--Athletic&PREV_SEASON=1998&BID=
|title=Coventry 2 Charlton 3
|publisher=Sporting Life
|date=29 January 2000 |accessdate=11 March 2012}}</ref> His next appearance didn't come until 15 September 2001. However, in this game he made an instant impact; coming off the bench to score the winner against [[Sheffield United]] with practically his first touch of the game.<ref>{{cite news 
|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/competitions/championship/4777570/Nilssons-bench-mark.html
|title=Nilsson's bench mark
|publisher=The Daily Telegraph
|date=16 September 2001 |accessdate=9 March 2012}}</ref> He fell out with manager [[Gordon Strachan]] but was recalled when [[Roland Nilsson]] took over. He ultimately failed in his bid to become a first team regular but in 2001/02 he made 28 starts, scoring 4 goals.

When [[Lierse S.K. (1906)|Lierse SK]] offered him a contract to return to the Jupiler League in his home country he ended his foreign career straight away and soon became one of their key players. Eventually this led to a transfer to [[RSC Anderlecht]] for the 2005/06 season.

At Anderlecht he was fired on 17 February 2006 for alleged 'wrongdoing' with former club Lierse SK in conjunction with the match-fixing investigation in Belgian football. Not much later he signed a 3-year contract deal with [[Netherlands|Dutch]] [[Eredivisie]] side [[ADO Den Haag]]. In a disappointing season ADO was unable to remain in the Eredivisie and were relegated to the [[Eerste Divisie]]. Delorge however was offered a contract at [[AFC Ajax|Ajax]] and signed a 2-year contract on 10 May 2007.

In his first year in [[Amsterdam]] he played four matches, but in his second year he did not play once. In the winter of 2009, [[Roda JC]] contracted the disappointed Delorge, who became a first team regular at the [[Eredivisie]] club before his retirement in July 2013.

'''Hans-Jürgen Stefan Schwarz''' ({{IPA|de|ˈʃteːfan ˈʃvaʁts}}; {{IPA|sv|ˈsteːfan ˈɧʋaʈs}}; born 18 April 1969) is a Swedish former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[midfielder]]. Schwarz started off his career with [[Malmö FF]] in 1987 before moving on to represent [[Benfica]], [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], [[Fiorentina]] and [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] until he retired at [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] in 2003. Schwarz won 69 [[Cap (sport)|caps]] for the [[Sweden men's national football team|Sweden national team]], scoring six goals. He represented his country at the [[1990 FIFA World Cup]], [[UEFA Euro 1992]] and most notably the [[1994 FIFA World Cup]] where Sweden finished third.

== Club career ==
Born to a German father (who played football in lower leagues in Germany) and a Swedish mother in the city of [[Malmö]], Schwarz started his playing career as a midfielder with Kulladals FF's academy. Between 1985 and 1987, he spent two seasons with [[Bayer Leverkusen]]'s youth team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://wwwc.aftonbladet.se/sport/0001/08/stefan.html|title = Aftonbladet sport: Erik Haag möter Stefan Schwarz}}</ref> He made his debut as a professional footballer with his hometown club [[Malmö FF]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://sydsvenskan.se/sport/fotboll/mff/article442740/Har-spelat-i-sex-lander.html |title=Har spelat i sex länder – Sport – Sydsvenskan-Nyheter Dygnet Runt |publisher=Sydsvenskan.se |date=18 April 1969 |access-date=12 June 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110810181840/http://www.sydsvenskan.se/sport/fotboll/mff/article442740/Har-spelat-i-sex-lander.html |archive-date=10 August 2011 }}</ref> He then moved to [[S.L. Benfica|Benfica]] for the [[1990–91 S.L. Benfica season|1990–91 season]] to play under manager [[Sven-Göran Eriksson]]. Schwarz became a regular starter for Benfica, winning the [[Primeira Liga]] twice, and playing in the side that knocked [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] out of the [[1991–92 European Cup second round|European Cup]] in 1991.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-08-01 |title=uefa.com|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/match/4667--arsenal-vs-benfica/lineups/}}</ref>

He subsequently moved to [[London]] to play for Arsenal in the summer of 1994 for £1.8 million but grew frustrated with [[George Graham (footballer, born 1944)|George Graham]]'s defensive tactics.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Spurling |first=Jon |title=Top Guns |publisher=Aureus |year=2001 |pages=95–96}}</ref> The defeat to Real Zaragoza in the [[1995 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup final]] was Schwarz's last game for Arsenal. He left [[Arsenal Stadium|Highbury]] after just one season at the club.<ref name="Arsenal" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-01-20 |title=that-match-is-still-iconic-in-sweden-stefan-schwarz-on-knocking-england-out-of-the-euros |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/that-match-is-still-iconic-in-sweden-stefan-schwarz-on-knocking-england-out-of-the-euros}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Schwarz |first=Stefan |title=De kallade mig Gud |publisher=Lava forlag |year=2016 |location=Sweden}}</ref>

Schwarz then completed a £2.5 million transfer to [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]]. He spent three seasons in Italy, lifting the [[1996 Coppa Italia Final|Coppa Italia]] and [[1996 Supercoppa Italiana|Super Cup]]. In the summer 1998 he reunited with [[Claudio Ranieri]], moving to Spain to join [[Valencia CF|Valencia]]. After one season he joined English side [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] on 29 July 1999 for a then-club record fee of £3.75 million.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-01 |title=Posts Sunderland official FB. |website=[[Facebook]] |url=https://www.facebook.com/118389841508479/posts/1120977181249735/}}</ref> Because of Schwarz's publicly-expressed desire to become a space tourist, the club inserted a "Space Clause" into his contract, stating that if he were to travel beyond Earth's atmosphere his contract would become wholly invalid.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-03-01 |title=the-joy-of-six-strange-sports-contract-clauses |newspaper=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/blog/2015/jun/24/the-joy-of-six-strange-sports-contract-clauses|last1=Carpenter |first1=Les }}</ref>

He was bestowed with the [[Guldbollen]] in November 1999, Sweden's award for footballer of the year.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-01 |title=guldbollen-1999/ |url=https://fogis.se/arkiv/tidigare/2001/11/guldbollen-1999/}}</ref> Schwarz eventually fell out with manager [[Peter Reid]] and was transfer listed in summer 2002.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2023-01-20 |title=Laslandes and Schwarz in Sunderland clear-out |newspaper=The Guardian |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2002/may/22/newsstory.sport5}}</ref> He made his last appearance for the club coming off the bench for the final 25 minutes of the League Cup tie at [[Sheffield United F.C.|Sheffield United]] 3 December 2002. Schwarz retired from playing in March 2003.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chroniclelive.co.uk/sport/football/football-news/sunderland-old-boy-stefan-schwarz-10570212.amp|title=Sunderland old boy Stefan Schwarz backs the Black Cats to beat the drop|website=Chronicle Live.co.uk|date=8 December 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/sport/football/fa_carling_premiership/410156.stm |title=FA Carling Premiership | Footballer banned from space |publisher=BBC News |date=2 August 1999 |access-date=12 June 2013}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-03-01 |title=i-love-sunderland-roker-report-meets-stefan-schwarz |url=https://rokerreport.sbnation.com/2016/11/14/13598240/i-love-sunderland-roker-report-meets-stefan-schwarz}}</ref>

==International career==
After having represented the [[Sweden men's national under-17 football team|Sweden U17]], [[Sweden men's national under-19 football team|U19]], and [[Sweden national under-21 football team|U21]] teams, Schwarz made his full international debut for [[Sweden men's national football team|Sweden]] on 14 February 1990 as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] in a [[friendly game]] against the [[United Arab Emirates national football team results|United Arab Emirates]] where he replaced [[Pontus Kåmark]] in the 80th minute before also scoring his first international goal in a 1–1 draw.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Stefan Schwarz – Spelarstatistik – Svensk fotboll|url=https://www.svenskfotboll.se/spelarfakta/stefan-schwarz/91ed8e08-8692-4b4f-a9ac-17e406c88931|access-date=2020-11-04|website=svenskfotboll.se.|language=sv}}</ref><ref name=":1" /> A few months later he appeared in his first major tournament for Sweden as he played in all three games at left back as Sweden was eliminated from the [[1990 FIFA World Cup]] after the group stage.<ref name=":0" />

In 1992, Schwarz appeared in three games as Sweden progressed to the semi-finals of [[UEFA Euro 1992]] before being eliminated by [[West Germany national football team|West Germany]].<ref name=":0" /> In 1994, he played in [[centre midfield]] alongside [[Jonas Thern]] as Sweden finished third at the [[1994 FIFA World Cup]].<ref name=":0" /> An injury to his [[Achilles tendon]] kept him out of the squad for [[Euro 2000|UEFA Euro 2000]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2000-03-30|title=Österrike-Sverige: Schwarz skadad – missar EM. Fotboll. 1-1 på usel plan. Sunderlandproffset slet av hälsenan. Även Fredrik Ljungberg och Patrik Andersson skadade|url=https://www.dn.se/arkiv/sport/osterrike-sverige-schwarz-skadad-missar-em-fotboll-1-1-pa-usel-plan-sunderlandproffset-slet-av/|access-date=2020-11-04|website=[[Dagens Nyheter]]|language=sv}}</ref>

He declared his international retirement in August 2001 to focus on his club team after a series of injuries while with the national team.<ref>{{Cite web|title="Aldrig mera landslaget"|url=https://www.aftonbladet.se/a/ka3nWQ|access-date=2020-11-04|website=Aftonbladet|date=23 August 2001 |language=sv}}</ref> His last international appearance came in a [[2002 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|2002 FIFA World Cup qualifier]] against [[Moldova national football team|Moldova]] on 28 March 2001.<ref name=":0" />

Schwarz won a total of 69 [[Cap (sport)|caps]] during his career, scoring six goals.<ref name=":0" />

'''Emeka Ifejiagwa''' ({{IPAc-en||audio=Ig-Emeka Ifejiagwa.ogg}}; born 30 October 1977) is a Nigerian retired [[Association football|footballer]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/bundesliga/vereine/1-bundesliga/2011-12/vfl-wolfsburg-24/26097/spieler_emeka-ifejiagwa.html | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160304205217/http://www.kicker.de/news/fussball/bundesliga/vereine/1-bundesliga/2011-12/vfl-wolfsburg-24/26097/spieler_emeka-ifejiagwa.html | url-status = dead | archive-date = 4 March 2016 | title = Ifejiagwa, Emeka | language = German | publisher = [[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] | access-date = 11 February 2012}}</ref>

==Career==
Ifejiagwa played for [[Udoji United]], [[Iwuanyanwo Nationale]] and [[Bendel Insurance F.C.|Bendel Insurance]] in Nigeria, for [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]] and [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]] in England, for [[CA Osasuna]] in Spain, and for [[VfL Wolfsburg]] and [[SV Waldhof Mannheim|Waldhof Mannheim]] in Germany.

After retiring as a player due to injury, Ifejiagwa began to work for Globalsports Advertisement in [[Barcelona]], Spain.

'''Pape Amodou "Modou" Sougou''' (born 18 December 1984) is a Senegalese former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Midfielder#Winger|right winger]].

==Club career==
===Early years and Portugal===
Born in the village of Fissel in the [[M'bour department]], Sougou started his career with [[Dakar]]-based [[AS Douanes (Senegal)|AS Douanes]]. He moved to Portugal in 2004 at the age of 19, signing a four-year contract with [[U.D. Leiria]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.record.xl.pt/Futebol/Nacional/1a_liga/uniao_leiria/interior.aspx?content_id=208742|title=Sougou reforça ataque|trans-title=Sougou bolsters offense|newspaper=[[Record (Portuguese newspaper)|Record]]|language=Portuguese|date=1 September 2004|accessdate=28 August 2015}}</ref> He made his [[Primeira Liga]] debut on 29 November, coming on as a late [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] in a 1–0 home win against [[S.L. Benfica]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.record.pt/futebol/futebol-nacional/liga-bwin/benfica/detalhe/u-leiria-benfica-1-0-mais-uma-ingenuidade-e-tres-pontos-a-voar|title=U. Leiria-Benfica, 1–0: Mais uma ingenuidade e três pontos a voar|trans-title=U. Leiria-Benfica, 1–0: Naïve once again and three points out the window|newspaper=Record|language=Portuguese|date=29 November 2004|accessdate=3 February 2022}}</ref>

Sougou continued to compete in the Portuguese top flight the following six seasons, representing [[Vitória F.C.|Vitória de Setúbal]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.record.xl.pt/Futebol/Nacional/1a_liga/vitoria_setubal/interior.aspx?content_id=270730|title=Senegalês Sougou de partida|trans-title=Senegalese Sougou on the move|newspaper=Record|first=Manuel|last=Varela|language=Portuguese|date=24 May 2006|accessdate=28 August 2015|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924143837/http://www.record.xl.pt/Futebol/Nacional/1a_liga/vitoria_setubal/interior.aspx?content_id=270730|archivedate=24 September 2015}}</ref> Leiria<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.record.xl.pt/Futebol/Nacional/1a_liga/uniao_leiria/interior.aspx?content_id=271738|title=Sougou vai assinar por duas épocas|trans-title=Sougou to sign for two seasons|newspaper=Record|language=Portuguese|date=2 June 2006|accessdate=28 August 2015}}</ref> and [[Académica de Coimbra (football)|Académica de Coimbra]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.record.xl.pt/futebol/nacional/interior.aspx?content_id=348360|title=Sougou por três temporadas|trans-title=Sougou for three seasons|newspaper=Record|language=Portuguese|date=29 June 2008|accessdate=28 August 2015}}</ref> In [[2009–10 Primeira Liga|2009–10]], whilst at the service of the latter club, he scored a career-best in the country nine goals in 29 matches, helping it to the 11th position; additionally, in early 2013, he revealed that he came close to signing with [[FC Porto]] when [[André Villas-Boas]] was the manager, but a potential deal fell through due to injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://maisfutebol.iol.pt/sougou-estive-quase-a-assinar-pelo-f-c-porto|title=Sougou: "Estive quase a assinar pelo F.C. Porto"|trans-title=Sougou: "I came close to signing for F.C. Porto"|publisher=Mais Futebol|language=Portuguese|date=24 January 2013|accessdate=7 December 2018}}</ref>

===CFR Cluj===
In late May 2011, Sougou joined [[Liga I]] side [[CFR Cluj]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://maisfutebol.iol.pt/cluj-confirma-sougou-renan-e-lionn|title=Cluj confirma Sougou, Renan e Lionn|trans-title=Cluj confirm Sougou, Renan and Lionn|publisher=Mais Futebol|language=Portuguese|date=23 May 2011|accessdate=3 February 2022}}</ref> having previously signed a pre-contract agreement.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://cfrmania.gsp.ro/stiri/10129/cfr-a-semnat-azi-cu-senegalezul-modou-sougou.htm|title=CFR a semnat azi cu senegalezul Modou Sougou|trans-title=CFR signed today with Senegalese Modou Sougou|newspaper=[[Gazeta Sporturilor]]|language=Romanian|date=1 February 2011|accessdate=19 March 2013|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140907162252/http://cfrmania.gsp.ro/stiri/10129/cfr-a-semnat-azi-cu-senegalezul-modou-sougou.htm|archive-date=7 September 2014}}</ref> The move was put on hold because his previous club, Académica, wanted [[Euro|€]]300,000 in compensation,<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.gsp.ro/fotbal/liga-1/cfr-negociaza-inca-transferul-senegalezului-modou-sougou-academica-cere-300-000-de-euro-227238.html|title=CFR negociază încă transferul senegalezului Modou Sougou. Academica cere 300.000 de euro|trans-title=CFR still in negotiations for transfer of Senegalese Modou Sougou. Académica demand 300,000 euros|newspaper=Gazeta Sporturilor|language=Romanian|date=4 February 2011|accessdate=19 March 2013}}</ref> but the transfer was eventually completed whilst the player stated one of the main reasons to sign was rejoining former manager [[Jorge Costa]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.gsp.ro/fotbal/liga-1/sougou-spune-ca-a-ales-cfr-ul-pentru-a-si-trece-in-palmares-primele-trofee-o-carte-cistigatoare-244730.html|title=Sougou spune că a ales CFR-ul pentru a-şi trece în palmares primele trofee: "O carte cîştigătoare!"|trans-title=Sougou says he chose CFR and has won the first trophy: "A winning book!"|newspaper=Gazeta Sporturilor|language=Romanian|date=21 June 2011|accessdate=19 March 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.gsp.ro/fotbal/liga-1/moudou-sougou-filosoful-golgeter-de-la-cfr-249030.html|title=Moudou Sougou, filosoful golgeter de la CFR|trans-title=Moudou Sougou, CFR's philosopher goal-getter|newspaper=Gazeta Sporturilor|language=Romanian|date=26 July 2011|accessdate=19 March 2013}}</ref>

Sougou finished his [[2011–12 Liga I|first year]] in Romania as joint-ninth top scorer with ten goals, adding several [[Assist (association football)|assists]]<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.gsp.ro/fotbal/liga-1/mm-esti-atent-sougou-a-devenit-cel-mai-bun-pasator-din-liga-1-324175.html|title=MM, eşti atent? Sougou a devenit cel mai bun pasator din Liga 1|trans-title=MM, are you paying attention? Sougou has become the best passer in League 1|newspaper=Gazeta Sporturilor|first=Liviu|last=Manolache|language=Romanian|date=14 April 2012|accessdate=19 March 2013}}</ref> to help his team win the national championship for the third time in five years. In January 2012, chairman Julius Muresan revealed that the player had been given a release clause of €11 million.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.gsp.ro/fotbal/liga-1/intangibil-contractul-lui-sougou-are-o-clauza-de-reziliere-de-11-milioane-de-euro-296823.html|title=Intangibil » Contractul lui Sougou are o clauză de reziliere de 11 milioane de euro|trans-title=Untouchable » Sougou's contract has a termination clause of 11 million euros|newspaper=Gazeta Sporturilor|language=Romanian|date=13 January 2012|accessdate=19 March 2013}}</ref>

On 20 November 2012, Sougou provided two passes for two goals of teammate [[Rui Pedro (footballer, born 1988)|Rui Pedro]]'s [[hat-trick]] in a 3–1 away victory over [[S.C. Braga]] in the [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League|group stage]] of [[UEFA Champions League]];<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0203-0e81181e050e-86f8f71cfc8d-1000--rui-pedro-hat-trick-ends-braga-s-hopes-at-cfr/|title=Rui Pedro hat-trick ends Braga's hopes at CFR|publisher=UEFA|first=Paul-Daniel|last=Zaharia|date=20 November 2012|accessdate=19 March 2013}}</ref> he himself scored twice in two 2–1 wins in the qualifying rounds, at [[FC Slovan Liberec]] and [[FC Basel]]. Later that year, he was named by ''[[Gazeta Sporturilor]]'' as the second best foreign player in the country behind [[Wesley (footballer, born 1980)|Wesley]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.gsp.ro/gsp-special/anchetele-gazetei/sougou-nu-a-fost-surprins-de-faptul-ca-wesley-a-fost-desemnat-cel-mai-bun-stranier-din-2012-e-un-jucator-extraordinar-379986.html|title=Sougou nu a fost surprins de faptul că Wesley a fost desemnat cel mai bun stranier din 2012: "E un jucător extraordinar"|trans-title=Sougou was not surprised Wesley was named best foreign player in 2012: "He's a great player"|newspaper=Gazeta Sporturilor|language=Romanian|date=20 December 2012|accessdate=19 March 2013}}</ref>

===Marseille===
On 24 January 2013, Sougou agreed to a three-year deal with [[Olympique de Marseille]] for €4.5 million and a €600,000 annual salary.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.om.net/fr/Saison/101002/Actualites/64940/Sougou_est_Olympien|title=Sougou est Olympien!|trans-title=Sougou is an Olympian!|publisher=Olympique Marseille|language=French|date=24 January 2013|accessdate=24 January 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130127005520/http://www.om.net/fr/Saison/101002/Actualites/64940/Sougou_est_Olympien|archive-date=27 January 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.gsp.ro/fotbal/liga-1/detaliile-afacerii-sougou-suma-totala-de-transfer-si-ce-beneficii-vor-avea-cei-de-la-cfr-cluj-386898.html|title=Detaliile "afacerii Sougou" » Suma totală de transfer şi ce beneficii vor avea cei de la CFR Cluj|trans-title="Sougou affair" details » Total amount of transfer and its benefits for CFR Cluj|newspaper=Gazeta Sporturilor|language=French|date=24 January 2013|accessdate=24 January 2013}}</ref> Upon his arrival, manager [[Élie Baup]] stated: ''"We saw that we were missing an accelerator against Montpellier [...]. Sougou has all of these qualities."''<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sofoot.com/sougou-debarque-a-l-om-166086.html|title=Sougou débarque à l'OM|trans-title=Sougou lands in Marseille|publisher=So Foot|language=French|date=23 January 2013|accessdate=19 March 2013}}</ref>

Sougou scored his first goal on 30 January 2013, in a 2–1 away defeat of [[FC Rouen]] in the [[2012–13 Coupe de France|round of 32]] of the [[Coupe de France]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.gsp.ro/international/campionate/gol-la-debut-pentru-sougou-senegalezul-a-inscris-in-meciul-din-cupa-cu-rouen-388430.html|title=Gol la debut pentru Sougou » Senegalezul a înscris în meciul din Cupă cu Rouen|trans-title=First goal for Sougou » Senegalese scored in cup match with Rouen|newspaper=Gazeta Sporturilor|language=Romanian|date=30 January 2013|accessdate=19 March 2013}}</ref> His first appearance in [[Ligue 1]] took place on 3 February, when he featured 13 minutes of the 0–1 home loss to [[AS Nancy Lorraine]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rtl.fr/sport/l1-23eme-journee-battu-par-nancy-l-om-decroche-7757631298|title=L1 – 23ème journée: battu par Nancy, l'OM décroche|trans-title=L1 – 23rd matchday: beaten by Nancy, OM lose ground|publisher=[[RTL (French radio)|RTL]]|language=French|date=3 February 2013|accessdate=7 December 2018}}</ref>

Subsequently, Sougou served two consecutive loan spells at fellow league club [[Thonon Evian Grand Genève FC|Thonon Évian FC]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.20minutes.fr/sport/1207901-20130807-20130807-transfert-saber-khlifa-rejoint-lom|title=Transfert: Saber Khlifa rejoint l'OM|trans-title=Transfer: Saber Khlifa rejoins OM|newspaper=[[20 minutes (France)|20 minutes]]|language=French|date=7 August 2013|accessdate=7 August 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/Sougou-prete-a-evian/495462|title=Sougou prêté à Evian|trans-title=Sougou loaned to Evian|newspaper=[[L'Équipe]]|language=French|date=1 September 2014|accessdate=7 August 2015}}</ref> He was fairly played during his two-year tenure, scoring seven times in all competitions and helping his team avoid relegation.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lavoixdunord.fr/art/sports/footl1-marseille-libere-sougou-ia0b0n2976529|title=Foot/L1 – Marseille libère Sougou|trans-title=Foot/L1 – Marseille release Sougou|newspaper=[[La Voix du Nord (daily)|La Voix du Nord]]|language=French|date=4 August 2015|accessdate=3 February 2022}}</ref>

After returning to ''l'OM'', Sougou was left out of the pre-season tour by coach [[Marcelo Bielsa]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.lequipe.fr/Football/Actualites/L-om-sans-modou-sougou-en-turquie/575849|title=L'OM sans Modou Sougou en Turquie|trans-title=OM without Modou Sougou in Turquie|newspaper=L'Équipe|language=French|date=21 July 2015|accessdate=7 August 2015}}</ref> He left by mutual consent on 4 August 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.maxifoot.fr/football/article-25944.htm|title=Transfert: pendant que l'OM libère Sougou et cherche à recaser Doria, Bielsa discute avec le Mexique...|trans-title=Transfer: whilst OM release Sougou and look to place Doria, Bielsa in talks with Mexico...|publisher=Maxi Foot|first=Pierre-Damien|last=Lacourte|language=French|date=4 August 2015|accessdate=7 August 2015}}</ref>

===Sheffield Wednesday===
On 5 August 2015, Sougou signed for [[Football League Championship|Championship]] side [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]] on a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.swfc.co.uk/news/article/sougou-seals-wednesday-switch-2596208.aspx|title=Sougou seals Wednesday switch|publisher=Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|date=5 August 2015|accessdate=7 August 2015|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150807163148/http://www.swfc.co.uk/news/article/sougou-seals-wednesday-switch-2596208.aspx|archivedate=7 August 2015}}</ref> He scored on his debut for his new team six days later, in a [[2015–16 Football League Cup|4–1 win]] against [[Mansfield Town F.C.|Mansfield Town]] in the [[EFL Cup|League Cup]] at the [[Hillsborough Stadium]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/33769201|title=Sheffield Wednesday 4–1 Mansfield Town|publisher=[[BBC Sport]]|date=11 August 2015|accessdate=11 August 2015}}</ref>

On 31 January 2017, Sougou returned to Portugal and its top division when he joined [[Moreirense F.C.]] until the end of [[2016–17 Primeira Liga|the season]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11703/10749763/modou-sougou-makes-loan-switch-from-sheffield-wednesday|title=Modou Sougou makes loan switch from Sheffield Wednesday|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|date=31 January 2017|accessdate=31 January 2017}}</ref>

===Mumbai City===
Sougou joined [[Mumbai City FC]] of the [[Indian Super League]] on 3 September 2018, ahead of the [[2018–19 Indian Super League|upcoming campaign]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.business-standard.com/article/news-ians/mumbai-city-sign-senegalese-winger-sougou-118090301098_1.html|title=Mumbai City sign Senegalese winger Sougou|newspaper=[[Business Standard]]|date=3 September 2018|accessdate=3 April 2020}}</ref> He scored a career-best 12 goals in his first year, helping his team to the third position and only trailing [[FC Goa]]'s [[Coro (footballer)|Coro]] in the individual chart.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://scroll.in/field/930794/isl-striker-modou-sougou-extends-stay-with-mumbai-city-for-another-year|title=ISL: Striker Modou Sougou extends stay with Mumbai City for another year|publisher=[[Scroll.in]]|date=16 July 2019|accessdate=3 April 2020}}</ref>

==International career==
Sougou made his debut for [[Senegal national football team|Senegal]] on 21 August 2007, playing the first half of a 1–1 [[Exhibition game|friendly]] draw against [[Ghana national football team|Ghana]] in [[London]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/soccer-africa-senegal-idUKL1948690720070819|title=Senegal's Diouf back for Ghana friendly|publisher=[[Reuters]]|date=19 August 2007|accessdate=3 February 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://fr.allafrica.com/stories/200708220840.html|title=Ghana/Sénégal: Football – Match amical international joué hier à Londres / Sénégal-Ghana 1–1 – Les "lions" rassurants|trans-title=Ghana/Senegal: Football – International friendly played yesterday in London / Senegal-Ghana 1–1 – Collected "lions"|publisher=[[AllAfrica]]|first=B.|last=Khalifa Ndiaye|language=French|date=22 August 2007|accessdate=3 February 2022}}</ref> He was selected for the [[2008 Africa Cup of Nations]] tournament,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/africa/7151646.stm|title=Senegal choose 38-man squad|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Piers|last=Edwards|date=19 December 2007|accessdate=3 February 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/30472561|title=Sougou pessimistic over chances of a Nations Cup recall|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Oluwashina|last=Okeleji|date=14 December 2014|accessdate=3 February 2022}}</ref> appearing in two games an eventual group-stage exit.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://maisfutebol.iol.pt/can-2008-angola-bate-senegal-3-1-com-manucho-em-destaque|title=CAN 2008: Angola bate Senegal (3–1) com Manucho em destaque|trans-title=CAN 2008: Angola beat Senegal (3–1) with Manucho as the star|publisher=Mais Futebol|language=Portuguese|date=27 January 2008|accessdate=3 February 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/africa/7218811.stm|title=Group D results|publisher=BBC Sport|first=Alistair|last=Magowan|date=31 January 2008|accessdate=3 February 2022}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Sougou is a practising Muslim, and observed fasting during the Islamic month of [[Ramadan]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.gsp.ro/fotbal/liga-1/sougou-a-slabit-trei-kilograme-in-perioada-ramadanului-credinta-imi-da-forta-262594.html|title=Sougou a slăbit trei kilograme în perioada Ramadanului » "Credinţa îmi dă forţă"|trans-title=Sougou lost three kilograms during the Ramadan » "Faith gives me strength"|newspaper=Gazeta Sporturilor|language=Romanian|date=15 September 2011|accessdate=19 March 2013}}</ref>

'''Rudolf Skácel''' ({{IPA|cs|ˈskaːtsɛl|lang}}; born 17 July 1979) is a retired professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[midfielder]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.edinburghlive.co.uk/sport/football/hearts-legend-rudi-skacel-calls-16369855|title=Hearts legend speaks on his decision to retire from football|last=Pilcher|first=Ross|date=3 June 2019|website=edinburghlive|access-date=3 June 2019}}</ref> He was capped at international level by the [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic]]. He was generally deployed as a left sided [[midfield]] player but proved himself to be versatile, having also played as a central [[attacking midfielder]] and a [[Left back#Full back|left back]] at Southampton.

Skácel began his career with [[FC Hradec Králové]] before joining [[Gambrinus liga]] side [[Slavia Prague]], where he caught the attention of [[France|French]] giants [[Olympique de Marseille]]. However, he struggled to establish himself in the first-team during his time with ''L'OM'' and was loaned out to [[Panathinaikos F.C.|Panathinaikos]] and [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]]. The latter loan spell saw him establish himself as a fan favourite, culminating in him scoring in the [[2006 Scottish Cup Final]] as the ''Jambos'' emerged victorious. He then went on to [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] where he spent three years, including a six-month loan spell with [[Hertha BSC]]. before being released. A brief return to [[SK Slavia Prague|Slavia Prague]] and a short spell with [[Athlitiki Enosi Larissa F.C.|AEL]] followed, before he returned to Hearts. His second spell at the Edinburgh club proved to be just as successful as he ended both seasons as the club's top scorer and scored two goals in the [[2012 Scottish Cup Final]] against [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]]' biggest rivals [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] en route to another cup victory.

He received infrequent call-ups to the [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic national team]], amassing seven caps over a period of seven years.

==Club career==

===Czech Republic===
Skácel was born in [[Trutnov]] and began his career with Czech club [[FC Hradec Králové]], making his senior debut in 1999 and helping his team to gain promotion back to the Czech top flight. In February 2002 he was signed by [[SK Slavia Prague|Slavia Prague]], for a fee of 14 million [[Czech koruna]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://fotbal.idnes.cz/slavia-koupila-juniorskeho-reprezentanta-fjm-/fotbal.aspx?c=A020221_092030_fotbal_min|title=Slavia koupila juniorského reprezentanta|language=cs|work=idnes.cz|date=21 February 2002|access-date=31 March 2013}}</ref> In May 2002 he won the [[Czech Cup]] with Slavia, beating their fierce rivals [[Sparta Prague]] in the final. He also won gold with the [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic]] in the [[UEFA European Under-21 Championship|European Under-21 Football Championship]].

His [[UEFA Cup]] and [[Gambrinus liga|Czech league]] performances in the 2002–03 season were noticed by [[France|French]] club [[Olympique de Marseille]] manager [[Alain Perrin]].

===Marseille===
In August 2003 Marseille concluded a deal<ref>{{cite web | url = http://quickstart.clari.net/qs_se/webnews/wed/bq/Qfbl-fra-cze-skacel.R62-_DaV.html | title = Marseille sign Skacel | date = 31 August 2003 | publisher = clari.net | access-date = 13 March 2008 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20071012120614/http://quickstart.clari.net/qs_se/webnews/wed/bq/Qfbl-fra-cze-skacel.R62-_DaV.html/ | archive-date = 12 October 2007 | df = dmy-all }}</ref> to sign Skácel for a fee of 2.5 million Euros. He made his debut on 13 September 2003, playing the entire match in a 5–0 victory over [[Le Mans FC|Le Mans]] at [[Stade Vélodrome]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=103643&cc=5739 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20031130094535/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=103643&cc=5739 | url-status = dead | archive-date = 30 November 2003 | title = Report: Marseille 5–0 Le Mans | publisher = ESPN Soccernet | date = 13 September 2003 | access-date = 26 October 2012}}</ref> His first and only goal for ''L'OM'' came in a 3–1 home victory over [[SC Bastia|Bastia]] on 5 October 2003.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/126071?cc=5739 | archive-url = https://archive.today/20120715154612/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/126071?cc=5739 | url-status = dead | archive-date = 15 July 2012 | title = Report: Marseille 3–1 Bastia | publisher =  ESPN Soccernet| date = 5 October 2003 | access-date = 26 October 2012}}</ref>

After his first season at Marseille, Skácel found himself out of favour after [[Alain Perrin]] was sacked. This led to Skácel being loaned out to Greek club [[Panathinaikos F.C.|Panathinaikos]] with an option of a permanent deal. He scored twice on his debut in a 3–2 cup victory over [[Atsalenios F.C.|Atsalenios]]. Skácel played in the [[UEFA Champions League]] for the first time in his career for Panathinaikos, playing in five of the six group and scoring in a 2–2 away draw with [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]] as the Greek club finished third in Group E to earn the consolation of a place in the [[UEFA Cup]]. During his time with Panathinaikos he scored five goals in all competitions.

===Heart of Midlothian===
After [[Panathinaikos F.C.|Panathinaikos]] did not take up their option to buy Skácel, [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Heart of Midlothian]] manager [[George Burley]] stepped in with an offer to take him on a season's loan from Marseille. In July 2005, the deal was concluded to take Skácel to Hearts on loan with the option of a permanent deal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/h/heart_of_midlothian/4694147.stm |title=Hearts complete capture of Skacel |date=19 July 2005 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=13 March 2008}}</ref>

Skacel made his Hearts debut on 30 July 2005 in the season opener, a match in which he scored his first goal for the club, in a 4-2 victory over Kilmarnock.<ref name="First Hearts Goal">{{cite web | title=Kilmarnock 2-4 Hearts | website=BBC SPORT | date=30 July 2005 | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/4729377.stm | access-date=22 August 2025}}</ref>

At the start of the 2005–06 season, Hearts won the first seven league games with Skácel scoring in each of them to set a [[Scottish Premier League]] record. Skacel became only the second player in SPL history to score in seven consecutive games, tying [[Mark Viduka]]'s record.<ref name="Record">{{cite web | title=Inverness CT 0-1 Hearts | website=BBC SPORT | date=17 September 2005 | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/4251202.stm | access-date=22 August 2025}}</ref>

Skácel's home debut was a 4–0 victory over [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]]' city rivals [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] at [[Tynecastle Stadium|Tynecastle]] in which he opened the scoring.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/scot_prem/4748451.stm |title=Hearts 4–0 Hibernian |date=7 August 2005 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=13 March 2008}}</ref> This was to be a common sight for the Hearts fans as Skácel went on to score 16 goals over the season and also scored the Hearts goal in the [[Scottish Cup]] final victory over Gretna.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/scot_cups/4764967.stm |title=Hearts 1–1 Gretna (4–2 on pens) |date=13 May 2006 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=13 March 2008}}</ref> He was shortlisted for the [[PFA Scotland Players' Player of the Year|Scottish PFA Players' Player award]], but lost out to [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] winger [[Shaun Maloney]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/c/celtic/4951722.stm | title=Maloney in historic awards double | publisher=[[BBC]] | date=1 May 2006 | access-date=13 May 2019}}</ref>

Despite announcing that the club had signed Skácel on a permanent deal,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/h/heart_of_midlothian/4960778.stm |title=Hearts say Skacel is staying on |date=2 May 2006 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=13 March 2008}}</ref> Skácel's celebration and post match comments after the Cup Final suggested that he had played his last game for the club.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/h/heart_of_midlothian/4770601.stm |title=Skacel bids farewell |date=14 May 2006 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=13 March 2008}}</ref> On 3 July 2006, it was revealed that Skácel and [[Andy Webster (footballer, born 1982)|Andy Webster]] had failed to join up with the squad for pre-season training prompting rumours of Skácel's departure.<ref>{{cite web | title=Hearts get tough with absent pair | website=BBC SPORT | date=3 July 2006 | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/h/heart_of_midlothian/5140482.stm | access-date=22 August 2025}}</ref>

Opposition fans point to accusations of [[Diving (association football)|diving]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/h/heart_of_midlothian/4861978.stm |title=Skacel ready to alter behaviour |date=30 March 2006 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=13 March 2008}}</ref> and that he spat at [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] captain [[Neil Lennon]];<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/h/heart_of_midlothian/4962096.stm |title=Lennon and Skacel row over spit |date=1 May 2006 |publisher=BBC Sport |access-date=13 March 2008}}</ref> although these accusations were reported to the [[Scottish Football Association]] they were not pursued.

===Southampton and Hertha Berlin===
On 29 July 2006, Skácel joined [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] for £1.6 million<ref>{{cite web|title=Saints land Skacel in £1.6m deal |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/s/southampton/5227082.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=25 October 2010|date=29 July 2006}}</ref> and linked up again with former Hearts manager [[George Burley]]. Although Skácel plays in midfield he found himself playing the majority of games at left back after the departure of [[Gareth Bale]] to [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] in May 2007. He scored from 25 yards in the 3–2 victory of [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] on 6 October 2007.

On 31 January 2008, Skácel moved to [[Hertha BSC]] on loan until the end of the season. Skácel had requested the move to boost his chances of representing his country on the international scene. Southampton acting chief executive Lee Hoos was quoted as saying: "The Czech national manager views the Championship very much as a second tier league – even though it is the fifth most popular in Europe. Skácel felt he would not get a look in unless he was playing in a top division".<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11688/3097562/skacel-departs-southampton|title=Skacel departs Southampton|date= 1 February 2008|work=Sky Sports|access-date=24 October 2014}}</ref> Skácel succeeded in making the [[UEFA Euro 2008]] squad, due to injury to [[Daniel Pudil]], but was an unused substitute in all three of their games as the Czechs crashed out at the group stages.

Skácel returned to Southampton for the start of the [[2008–09 in English football|2008–09 season]]. He was released from his contract on 2 May 2009, after Southampton were relegated to League One.

===Return to Slavia Prague===
Skácel returned to former club [[SK Slavia Prague|Slavia Prague]] in October 2009, six years after leaving to join [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.transfermarketweb.com/?action=read&idsel=45930 | title = Skacel returns to Slavia | publisher = FOOTBALLpress.net | date = 13 October 2009 | access-date = 26 October 2012}}</ref> He made his first appearance since returning in a 2–1 league defeat to [[Sigma Olomouc]] at the [[Synot Tip Arena]].<ref>[http://www.slavia.cz/novinka.asp?id=16111&typ=clanek Slavia 1–2 Sigma] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100206025321/http://www.slavia.cz/novinka.asp?id=16111 |date=6 February 2010 }}, Slavia.cz, 26 October 2009.</ref> He made his fifth and final league appearance of his second spell with the club on 29 November 2009, scoring a hat-trick against [[FC Brno]] in a 3–1 victory.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=1141563.html | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20091203152537/http://www.fifa.com/worldfootball/clubfootball/news/newsid=1141563.html | url-status = dead | archive-date = 3 December 2009 | title = Skacel treble downs Brno | publisher =  FIFA.com | date = 29 November 2009 | access-date =24 January 2011}}</ref>

===Larissa===
In January 2010, Skácel signed for Larissa on a free transfer until June 2010 with the option of a further year.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.soccerbase.gr/news.aspx?lang=en&id=2010-01-25 | title = Larissa signed Skacel | publisher = soccerbase.gr | access-date =27 January 2010 | date = 25 January 2010}}</ref>

===Return to Heart of Midlothian===
On 16 September 2010, Skácel returned to Hearts on a one-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rudi returns to Hearts|url=http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20100916/rudi-returns-to-hearts_2241384_2141199|publisher=Heart of Midlothian FC|access-date=16 September 2010|date=16 September 2010|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100918210335/http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20100916/rudi-returns-to-hearts_2241384_2141199|archive-date=18 September 2010}}</ref> He marked his first start and home debut in his second spell at Hearts with a goal against [[Rangers F.C.|Rangers]].

On 23 October 2010, he bagged a hat-trick in Hearts' 3–0 win over [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jim Jefferies delighted by Hearts display |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/h/heart_of_midlothian/9121349.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=25 October 2010|date=23 October 2010}}</ref> Skácel continued his superb form with a 32nd-minute 30-yard volley against [[Hamilton Academical F.C.|Hamilton Academical]] on 20 November 2010. Hearts went on to win the match 2–0.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hearts boss Jim Jefferies hails clinical finishing|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/h/heart_of_midlothian/9213071.stm|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=22 November 2010|date=20 November 2010}}</ref> On 11 December 2010 he played a key role as the Jambos' recorded their biggest win of the season, scoring twice in a 5–0 victory over [[Aberdeen F.C.|Aberdeen]] at Tynecastle.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/9274624.stm | title = Hearts 5 – 0 Aberdeen | publisher =  BBC Sport | date = 11 December 2010 | access-date =16 December 2010}}</ref> On 19 March 2011 Skácel scored his 10th and 11th goals of the season in a dramatic 3–2 victory over [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]]; his 93rd-minute strike proving the winner. Skácel ended the [[2010–11 Scottish Premier League|2010–11 season]] as the ''Jambos''' top scorer with 13 goals.

Despite joining the Hearts squad for their pre-season preparations Skácel's involvement was severely limited due to injury.
