January 2012 | access-date = 26 October 2012}}</ref> He continued his impressive start to 2012 with his second Hearts hat-trick against St. Mirren at Tynecastle on 14 January. Following [[Marius Žaliūkas]]' [[Misconduct (association football)#Sending-off offences red card|sending-off]] the ''Jambos'' trailed 2–1 but Skácel's hat-trick inspired the ten men to an incredible 5–2 victory.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/scot_prem/16453455.stm | title = Hearts 5–2 St. Mirren | publisher = BBC Sport | date = 14 January 2011 | access-date = 26 October 2012}}</ref> After the match Skácel, voiced his desire to extend his contract and spend the remainder of the season with Hearts.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/16563619 | title = Hearts' Rudi Skacel wants to stay until the summer | publisher = BBC Sport | date = 14 January 2012 | access-date = 26 October 2012}}</ref> On 31 January 2012, Hearts announced that he had signed a contract extension and would be staying on until the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20120131/rudi-staying-on_2241384_2591147 | title = Rudi staying on! | publisher = Heartsfc.co.uk | date = 31 January 2012 | access-date = 26 October 2012 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120203052506/http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20120131/rudi-staying-on_2241384_2591147 | archive-date = 3 February 2012 | df = dmy-all }}</ref> His 100th competitive appearance for Hearts came in a 2–0 [[Edinburgh derby]] win on 18 April 2012.  He continued his impressive goal scoring record against St. Mirren in the [[2011–12 Scottish Cup|Scottish Cup]], scoring in the quarter-finals in a 2–2 draw at Tynecastle,<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17243643 | title = Hearts 2–2 St. Mirren | publisher = BBC Sport | date = 10 March 2012 | access-date = 26 October 2012}}</ref> as well as in a 2–0 victory at [[St Mirren Park]] in the resultant replay.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17363148 | title = St. Mirren 0–2 Hearts | publisher = BBC Sport | date = 21 March 2012 | access-date = 26 October 2012}}</ref> He also scored the opener in the [[2011–12 Scottish Cup#Semi-finals|semi-final]] victory over [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] at [[Hampden Park|Hampden]] as Hearts progressed to the final.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17649430 | title = Celtic 1–2 Hearts | publisher = BBC Sport | date = 15 April 2012 | access-date = 26 October 2012}}</ref> He scored the second and fifth goals and earned the [[man of the match]] award<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.scottishfa.co.uk/scottish_fa_news.cfm?page=1957&newsCategoryID=7&newsID=9890 | title = Skacel named man of the match | publisher = Scottish FA | date = 19 May 2012 | access-date = 26 October 2012}}</ref> as Hearts routed rivals [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibs]] 5–1 in a historic [[2012 Scottish Cup Final|final]], taking his goal tally in the competition to five in just seven games and 18 in all competitions for the season, his best return in his three seasons as a Hearts player. He said after the match that the final would probably be his last match for Hearts and that it was ''"the best way to say goodbye with the cup in my hands"'',<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/18134313 | title = Scottish Cup hero Rudi Skacel 'likely to exit Hearts' | publisher = BBC Sport | date =  19 May 2012| access-date = 26 October 2012}}</ref> meaning that he would once again depart following a Scottish Cup triumph.

On 9 October 2012, Hearts announced that Skácel had returned to train with the club.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20121009/rudi-offered-training-facilities_2241384_2943993 | title = Rudi offered training facilities | publisher = Heartsfc.co.uk | date = 9 October 2012 | access-date = 27 October 2012 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20121125061731/http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20121009/rudi-offered-training-facilities_2241384_2943993 | archive-date = 25 November 2012 | df = dmy-all }}</ref> However, a permanent return was made impossible by a transfer embargo imposed on the club by the SPL due to recurring late payments of the wages of players and staff.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.espn.co.uk/football/sport/story/176087.html | title = SPL confirm Hearts transfer embargo | publisher = ESPN | date =  24 October 2012| access-date = 27 October 2012}}</ref>

===Dundee United===
Skacel joined [[Dundee United F.C.|Dundee United]] on 26 October 2012 contracted until 30 January 2013.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.dundeeunitedfc.co.uk/index.asp?tm=2&nid=4346&cd=2012 | title = United Sign Skacel | publisher = Dundee United | date = 26 October 2012 | access-date = 26 October 2012}}</ref> He instantly caused controversy by, as he had previously hinted on his [[Twitter]] account, selecting the number 51 shirt at his new club in reference to Hearts' victory over rivals Hibernian in the [[2012 Scottish Cup Final|Scottish Cup Final]]. Manager [[Peter Houston]] apologised to Hibs fans saying he was unaware of the significance of the number and would not have allowed Skácel to wear 51 had he known his reasons for selecting it.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11794/8199664/Dundee-United-boss-sorry-for-Rudi-Skacel-s-Hibs-wind-up | title = Dundee United boss sorry for Rudi Skacel's Hibs wind-up | publisher = Sky Sports | date = 27 October 2012 | access-date = 27 October 2012}}</ref> Skácel made his debut a day after signing, as a second-half substitute in a 1–0 victory over [[St Mirren F.C.|St Mirren]] at [[St Mirren Park]]. He faced his former club, Hearts, four days later on 31 October in a [[2011-12 Scottish League Cup#Quarter-finals|Scottish League Cup quarter-final]] at [[Tannadice]] and received a warm reception from the travelling Hearts support when he appeared as a substitute in [[extra time#Association football|extra time]] as United were eventually defeated 5–4 on [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20053644 | title = Dundee Utd 1–1 Hearts (4–5 pens) | publisher = BBC Sport | date = 31 October 2012 | access-date = 2 December 2012}}</ref> His first seven appearances for Dundee United were as a substitute, before making his first start on 27 November 2012 in a 2–1 home defeat to [[Motherwell F.C.|Motherwell]] in the league. This match also marked his 100th appearance in the [[Scottish Premier League]]. He scored his first goal for the ''Terrors'' on 15 December 2012, in a thrilling 4–4 league draw with [[Inverness Caledonian Thistle F.C.|Inverness Caledonian Thistle]] at Tannadice.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/20650417 | title = Dundee Utd 4–4 Inverness CT | publisher = BBC Sport | date = 15 December 2012 | access-date = 17 December 2012}}</ref> He made a total of 16 appearances for United, scoring once as he was utilized primarily as a second-half substitute with ten of his appearances coming from the bench.

On 25 January 2013, Dundee United confirmed that they would not be extending Skácel's contract beyond January.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rudi Skacel set for Dundee United departure|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/21200303|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=1 March 2013|date=25 January 2013}}</ref> Skacel left the club when his contract expired on 30 January.

===Second return to Slavia Prague===
On 6 March 2013, [[SK Slavia Prague|Slavia Prague]] announced that Skácel had returned for a third spell and signed a contract until the end of the season as the club battled against relegation.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://sport.stv.tv/football/216579-rudi-skacel-rejoins-slavia-prague-until-the-end-of-the-season/ | title = Rudolf Skácel returns to Slavia Prague | publisher = STV | date = 6 March 2013 | access-date = 6 March 2013}}</ref> He made the first appearance of his return on 16 March 2013 in a 3–1 [[2012–13 Gambrinus liga|league]] win over [[Slovan Liberec]] at [[Stadion Eden]], receiving a warm reception from the home fans as he came on as a substitute in the 69th minute. He replaced [[Captain (association football)|captain]] [[Karol Kisel]] and was given the captain's armband for the remainder of the game.

He departed upon the expiration of his contract at the end of the season having made a total of five appearances.

===Later career===
In January 2014 Skácel was linked with a move to [[Scottish Championship]] side [[Alloa Athletic F.C.|Alloa Athletic]] where former Hearts teammate [[Paul Hartley]] was manager.<ref>{{cite web|title=Alloa eye Rudi Skacel after landing Hibs' Ross Caldwell |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25683935|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=6 February 2014|date=10 January 2014}}</ref>
However The Wasps tentative interest went no further and days later it was revealed Skácel was once again training with Hearts with a view to signing for the administration hit club should the [[Scottish Professional Football League|SPFL]] allow for players made redundant in the summer to be replaced despite the club's transfer embargo.<ref>{{cite web|title=No immediate new faces at Hearts but Skacel in training|url=http://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/no-immediate-new-faces-at-hearts-but-skacel-in-training-1-3267417|publisher=Edinburgh Evening News|access-date=6 February 2014|date=14 January 2014}}</ref> Hearts cancelled the playing contract of goalkeeping coach [[Alan Combe]], in keeping with the one-in, one-out policy of their transfer embargo, to make space for Skácel<ref>{{cite web|title=Hearts seek under-21 recruit after Adam King's Swansea move|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/25914429|publisher=BBC Sport|access-date=6 February 2014|date=28 January 2014}}</ref> only for the SPFL to reject the move stating that it was not viable to replace a 39-year-old goalkeeping coach/player who has never appeared in a match day squad with a midfielder.<ref>{{cite web|title=Gary snaps up striker|url=http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20140130/gary-snaps-up-striker_2241384_3645612|publisher=Heartsfc.co.uk|access-date=6 February 2014|date=30 January 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140202150935/http://www.heartsfc.co.uk/articles/20140130/gary-snaps-up-striker_2241384_3645612|archive-date=2 February 2014}}</ref> Skácel expressed his bitter disappointment at the refusal and stated that the decision had left him without motivation and considering retirement.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rudi Skacel: SPFL decision to block my Hearts move stinks |url=http://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/rudi-skacel-spfl-decision-to-block-my-hearts-move-stinks-1-3294669|publisher=Edinburgh Evening News|access-date=6 February 2014|date=5 February 2014}}</ref>

===Raith Rovers===
After a spell in his native Czech Republic, Skácel was linked with a return to [[Scotland]], after [[Raith Rovers F.C.|Raith Rovers]] manager [[Gary Locke (Scottish footballer)|Gary Locke]] expressed an interest in the former [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech international]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.thecourier.co.uk/fp/sport/football/scottish-championship/223601/raith-boss-gary-locke-makes-bid-to-bring-rudi-skacel-to-starks-park/ |title=Raith boss Gary Locke makes bid to bring Rudi Skacel to Stark's Park |first=Neil |last=Robertson |work=The Courier |publisher=DC Thomson Co Ltd |date=15 July 2016 |access-date=21 July 2016}}</ref> On 21 July 2016, Skácel signed with the [[Scottish Championship]] side.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.raithrovers.net/25903/major-signing-news-skacel-and-mcmanus-join-lockes-rovers.htm |title=Major signing news: Skacel and McManus join Locke's Rovers |publisher=Raith Rovers F.C. |date=21 July 2016 |access-date=21 July 2016}}</ref>

=== 1. FK Příbram ===
Following his release from Raith Rovers, Skacel returned to the Czech Republic and signed for [[1. FK Příbram]] in the Czech National Football League. In his first season with Příbram he helped the club achieve promotion to the Czech First League. In his final playing season, Skacel made 16 appearances and scored one goal as Příbram escaped relegation <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fkpribram.cz/clanek.asp?id=Rudolf-Skacel-v-nedeli-ukonci-karieru-5708|title=Rudolf Skácel v neděli ukončí kariéru|website=1.FK PŘÍBRAM - Fotbalový klub|access-date=3 June 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fkpribram.cz/clanek.asp?id=Tohle-je-posledni-sezona-5475|title=Tohle je poslední sezona|website=1.FK PŘÍBRAM - Fotbalový klub|access-date=3 June 2019}}</ref>

Skacel retired following Příbram's relegation playoff victory over [[FC Zbrojovka Brno]] on 2 June 2019.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.fnliga.cz/clanek/4671-brno-v-pribrami-neskorovalo-a-po-bezbrankove-remize-se-udrzeli-stredocesi|title=Brno v Příbrami neskórovalo a po bezbrankové remíze se udrželi Středočeši|website=FORTUNA:NÁRODNÍ LIGA|access-date=3 June 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com/sport/football/hearts/latest-hearts-news/rudi-skacel-hearts-legend-to-bring-curtain-down-on-career-this-weekend-1-4939346|title=Rudi Skacel, Hearts legend, to bring curtain down on career this weekend|website=www.edinburghnews.scotsman.com|language=en|access-date=3 June 2019}}</ref>

==International career==
Skácel made his [[Czech Republic national under-21 football team|Czech Republic under-21]] debut against [[Bulgaria national under-21 football team|Bulgaria]] on 5 October 2001 in [[Teplice]], scoring the third goal in an 8–0 victory.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.fotbal.cz/c/nat/21/2001/match10.asp | title = Zápis o utkání č. 74 | language = cs | publisher = fotbal.cz | access-date = 16 October 2011 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20110811115329/http://www.fotbal.cz/c/nat/21/2001/match10.asp | archive-date = 11 August 2011 | df = dmy-all }}</ref> He was part of the [[Czech Republic national under-21 football team|Czech Republic under-21]] [[2002 UEFA European Under-21 Football Championship squads#Czech Republic|squad]] at the [[2002 UEFA European Under-21 Football Championship]] in [[Switzerland]], along with his future [[Heart of Midlothian F.C.|Hearts]] teammate [[Michal Pospíšil]]. Both players converted in a penalty shoot-out as the Czechs emerged victorious in the [[2002 UEFA European Under-21 Football Championship#Final|final]] against [[France under-21 national football team|France]].

Skácel made his [[Czech Republic national football team|Czech Republic national team]] debut on 12 November 2003 against [[Canada men's national soccer team|Canada]]. He once again got off to a scoring start as he replaced [[Jan Koller]] after 73 minutes and scored eight minutes later in a 5–1 victory.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.fotbal.cz/c/nat/AM/2003/match9.asp | title = Zápis o utkání č. 620/112 | language = cs | publisher = fotbal.cz | access-date = 16 October 2011 | url-status = dead | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20120503194426/http://www.fotbal.cz/c/nat/AM/2003/match9.asp | archive-date = 3 May 2012 | df = dmy-all }}</ref> He was named in the Czech squad for [[UEFA Euro 2008|Euro 2008]] as a replacement for the injured [[Daniel Pudil]] but did not leave the bench as the Czechs exited at the group stage. Skácel amassed seven caps for his country, scoring once.

'''Daniel Halfar''' (born 7 January 1988) is a German former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[midfielder]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.kicker.de/daniel-halfar/spieler/2-bundesliga/2011-12/1860-muenchen | title = Halfar, Daniel| language = German | publisher = [[Kicker (magazine)|Kicker]] | access-date = 30 July 2011}}</ref>

==Career==
Born in [[Mannheim]], Halfar began his career at MFC Phönix Mannheim 02.

In 1997, he joined [[1. FC Kaiserslautern]]. He made his debut on 11 December 2005 against [[FC Bayern Munich|Bayern Munich]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Kahn sichert die Herbstmeisterschaft|url=https://www.kicker.de/bayern-gegen-klautern-2005-bundesliga-723147/analyse|access-date=14 January 2018|work=kicker Online|date=11 December 2005|language=German}}</ref> Ten days later, with Halfar having made three substitute appearances in the [[Bundesliga]], it was announced his first professional contract had been agreed, which would run from 1 January 2006 to 30 June 2010.<ref>{{cite news|title=FCK-Talent Daniel Halfar wird Profi|url=http://www.rp-online.de/sport/fussball/fck-talent-daniel-halfar-wird-profi-aid-1.2481457|accessdate=14 January 2018|work=Rheinische Post|date=21 December 2005|language=German}}</ref> He scored his first two goals in a match against [[MSV Duisburg]] on 4 February 2006.<ref>{{cite news|title=Halfar wird Held des Tages|url=https://www.kicker.de/duisburg-gegen-klautern-2006-bundesliga-723172/analyse|access-date=14 January 2018|work=kicker Online|date=4 February 2006|language=German}}</ref> making him the youngest Kaiserslautern player to score (18 years, 28 days). Following his first season, Halfar was seen as a very big talent.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Müller|first1=Jan Christian|title=Gelobt, gefallen, auferstanden|url=http://www.fr.de/sport/volltreffer-gelobt-gefallen-auferstanden-a-1152794|accessdate=14 January 2018|work=Frankfurter Rundschau|date=24 November 2008|language=German}}</ref>

In August 2007 he moved to [[Arminia Bielefeld]]. He scored his first goal for his new club on 22 November 2008 against [[VfB Stuttgart]]. After three seasons with Arminia Bielefeld and scoring only one goal for the club, he was sold on a free transfer to [[TSV 1860 Munich|1860 Munich]]. In the summer of 2013 he transferred to [[1. FC Köln]], signing a three-year contract.

After having played for [[1. FC Kaiserslautern]] between 2015 and 2018, Halfar retired from football in November 2018 due to a hip injury.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Arndt |first1=Maurice |title=Halfar: "Kleine Schritte gehen und mit den Aufgaben wachsen" |url=https://www.fupa.net/berichte/fc-rot-weiss-kirchlengern-halfar-kleine-schritte-gehen-und-m-2238042.html |website=fupa.net |publisher=Fußball Passau |accessdate=5 July 2020 |date=2 November 2018}}</ref>

==International career==
Halfar played for the [[Germany national under-21 football team|Germany U21 national team]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=500109&no_cache=1&action=showPlayer&player=halfar_daniel&lang=D&cHash=e9147e7d37 |title=Nationalspieler Daniel Halfar |language=German |publisher=dfb.de |accessdate=15 August 2010 |date=10 February 2009 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110424180156/http://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=500109&no_cache=1&action=showPlayer&player=halfar_daniel&lang=D&cHash=e9147e7d37 |archivedate=24 April 2011}}</ref>

'''Dean Dwight Gordon''' (born 10 February 1973) is an English former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[left-back]] between 1991 and 2009 in his native England as well as Cyprus and New Zealand.

He notably played [[Premier League]] football for [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]] and [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]], having also had spells as a professional with [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]], [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]], [[Reading F.C.|Reading]], [[Grimsby Town F.C.|Grimsby Town]], [[APOEL Nicosia]], [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]], [[Albany United]], [[New Zealand Knights]], [[Auckland City FC|Auckland City]] and [[Torquay United F.C.|Torquay United]]. Gordon also spent time playing in the English Non-League system with [[Worksop Town F.C.|Worksop Town]], [[Crook Town F.C.|Crook Town]], [[Lewes F.C.|Lewes]], [[Whitby Town F.C.|Whitby Town]], [[Ilkeston Town F.C. (1945)|Ilkeston Town]], [[Glapwell F.C.|Glapwell]], [[Workington A.F.C.|Workington]] and [[Thornaby F.C.|Thornaby]].

Gordon, who was born in [[Croydon]], South London, is an example of a journeyman footballer having represented 20 different clubs during an 18-year career, but despite this he had only played for two clubs in his first ten years in the game but spent his latter years playing for numerous clubs.

==Club career==

===Crystal Palace===
Gordon began his career as a trainee with [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]], turning professional in July 1991. He went on to make over 200 appearances for the Eagles and was known to be a strong in the tackle and impressive going forward down the left flank. His speedy forays often resulted in spectacular goals as he let fly from the edge of the box.

===Middlesbrough===
Gordon joined fellow [[Premier League]] club [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] for a fee of £900,000 on 6 July 1998. In his first season at the [[Riverside Stadium|Riverside]] he played in every league game. In November 2001 Gordon went on loan to [[Cardiff City F.C.|Cardiff City]],<ref>[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/c/cardiff_city/1669831.stm Gordon signs for Bluebirds]</ref> scoring once against Blackpool,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_div_2/1699201.stm |title=Blackpool 1–1 Cardiff |publisher=[[BBC]] |date=15 December 2001 |access-date=19 January 2010}}</ref> and was released by Middlesbrough at the end of that season.

===Coventry City===
Gordon joined [[Coventry City F.C.|Coventry City]] in July 2002<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20040825123211/http://www.bbc.co.uk/coventry/sport/stories/2002/08/09/hyldgaard-in-the-frame.shtml Pressure's on as McAllister era starts for real]</ref> and was a regular in his first season at [[Highfield Road]], scoring once against Ipswich Town.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/eng_div_1/2917751.stm |title=Coventry 2–4 Ipswich |publisher=[[BBC]] |date=12 April 2003 |access-date=19 January 2010}}</ref> However, he lost his place and joined [[Reading F.C.|Reading]] on loan in March 2004,<ref>[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/teams/r/reading/3560691.stm Reading swoop for Gordon]</ref>
and eventually went on trial with [[Hibernian F.C.|Hibernian]] in July 2004.<ref>[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/h/hibernian/3894123.stm Hibs look to Gordon]</ref>

===Grimsby Town===
Gordon signed with [[Football League Two]] side [[Grimsby Town F.C.|Grimsby Town]] on a free transfer in August 2004, his first club outside of the top two tiers of English football, but despite holding down a regular place in the team he was released in March 2005 by [[Russell Slade]].

===APOEL Nicosia===
On 2005 Gordon moved to Cyprus to play for [[APOEL F.C.|APOEL Nicosia]], but he was released from the club a few months later.

===Later career===
In November 2005, Gordon joined non-league [[Crook Town F.C.|Crook Town]], where he could rebuild his English football career, which had been delayed due problems with gaining international clearance,<ref>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20070930035211/http://www.nonleaguedaily.com/news/index.php?newsmode=FULL&nid=32230 Crook lose star recruit]}}</ref> while being near to his business in [[Darlington]].<ref>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20070930030806/http://www.nonleaguedaily.com/news/index.php?newsmode=FULL&nid=30793 Dean Gordon joins Crook]}}</ref> He subsequently had an unsuccessful trial with [[Barnsley F.C.|Barnsley]] before joining [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]] in January 2006,<ref>[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/b/blackpool/4596286.stm Defender Gordon joins Blackpool]</ref> but was released after playing just once.<ref>[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/b/blackpool/4689038.stm Blackpool release defender Gordon]</ref> A proposed move to [[Chester City F.C.|Chester City]] was blocked as Gordon was not allowed to sign for two clubs inside the transfer window. As a result, he moved to [[Lewes F.C.|Lewes]] in February 2006,<ref>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20070930040755/http://www.nonleaguedaily.com/news/index.php?newsmode=FULL&nid=33272 Gordon coup for Lewis]}}</ref> before the following month rejoining Crook Town.<ref>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20070930033414/http://www.nonleaguedaily.com/news/index.php?newsmode=FULL&nid=33490 Gordon's back at Crook]}}</ref> Later that month he joined [[Worksop Town F.C.|Worksop Town]],<ref>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20070927201025/http://www.nonleaguedaily.com/news/index.php?newsmode=FULL&nid=33567 Now Gordon joins Tigers]}}</ref> where he played until the end of the season.

Gordon then moved to New Zealand and signed for [[Auckland]] North Shore team [[Albany United]] in June 2006.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.albanyunited.org/dean%20gordon.htm |title=Dean Gordon signs for Albany Utd |access-date=31 August 2006 |archive-date=4 October 2006 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061004234207/http://www.albanyunited.org/dean%20gordon.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref> He subsequently moved to [[Auckland City FC|Auckland City]] in September the same year,<ref name="NZ_Herald_10401631">{{cite web |url=http://www.nzherald.co.nz/section/4/story.cfm?c_id=4&objectid=10401631 |title=Soccer: Auckland City strengthen squad before title defence |author=Brown, Michael |date=17 September 2006 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |accessdate=27 September 2011}}</ref> scoring twice in five games.<ref>[http://www.aucklandcityfc.com/cgi-bin/control.pl?Function=Display&Item=mh_playapp.txt Auckland City 2006-7 player appearances] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071013100242/http://www.aucklandcityfc.com/cgi-bin/control.pl?Function=Display&Item=mh_playapp.txt |date=13 October 2007 }}</ref>

In December 2006, Gordon left City to join [[A-League]] team [[New Zealand Knights]] in a surprise move,<ref>[http://knightsfc.com/default.aspx?s=newsdisplay&id=6149 Gordon takes on Knights opportunity]{{Dead link|date=March 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> forgoing the chance to play for City against [[FC Barcelona|Barcelona]] in the [[FIFA Club World Cup]] in Japan.<ref name="TVNZ_908432">{{cite web |url=http://tvnz.co.nz/view/page/411317/908432 |title=Gordon joins Knights |work=[[Television New Zealand]] |accessdate=27 September 2011}}</ref>

He played six times for the Knights in the A-League,<ref>[http://www.socceraust.co.uk/2006/ALGE/player00185.html Hyundai A-League 2006/07 Player Details – Dean Gordon] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927030701/http://www.socceraust.co.uk/2006/ALGE/player00185.html |date=27 September 2007 }}</ref> before returning to England where he rejoined Lewes in February 2007.<ref>{{usurped|1=[https://web.archive.org/web/20070930031439/http://www.nonleaguedaily.com/news/index.php?newsmode=FULL&nid=40200 Dean Gordon back with Rooks]}}</ref>

He began training with English club [[Torquay United F.C.|Torquay United]]<ref>[https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/teams/t/torquay_united/6360825.stm Torquay capture Blades' teenager]</ref> and signed for the Gulls on non-contract terms on 16 February 2007. He made his debut the following day in a 1–0 defeat at home to [[Hartlepool United F.C.|Hartlepool United]]. He played eight times as Torquay were relegated to the [[Conference National]] and was released at the end of the season.

After playing seven games in late 2007 for [[Whitby Town F.C.|Whitby Town]] on a match-to-match basis, he then signed for another [[Northern Premier League]] side, [[Ilkeston Town F.C. (1945)|Ilkeston Town]] in August 2008.<ref>http://www.ilkestonadvertiser.co.uk/sport/Another-joins-up-as-Robins.4430547.jp {{Dead link|date=February 2022}}</ref> Gordon also had a short but successful spell at local teesside based club [[Thornaby F.C.|Thornaby]].

In March 2009, Gordon signed for [[Conference North]] side [[Workington A.F.C.|Workington]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Now Gordon joins Reds |publisher=NonLeagueDaily.com |date=17 March 2009 |accessdate=18 March 2009 |url=http://www.nonleaguedaily.com/news/index.php?&newsmode=FULL&nid=56410 |url-status=usurped |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120908232605/http://www.nonleaguedaily.com/news/index.php?&newsmode=FULL&nid=56410 |archivedate=8 September 2012}}</ref>

==International career==
Gordon appeared 13 times for the [[England national under-21 football team|England Under-21s]] in the mid-1990s.

==Personal life==
Following his retirement, Gordon lived in [[City of Sunderland|Sunderland]] and began coaching and teaching for the 'Show Racism The Red Card' group and now goes around schools in the North East to teach them about racism. Dean runs Futsal Sunderland in the city, providing competitions and other Futsal events for all ages.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sundaysun.co.uk/news/north-east-news/2010/06/13/ex-boro-player-dean-gordon-target-of-racist-abuse-79310-26640178/|title = Sunday Sun - North East news, sport and what's on | date=29 April 2025 }}</ref>

He is the father of [[Southampton FC]] player [[Nathan Wood-Gordon]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://football-wonderkids.co.uk/player/nathan-wood-gordon/|title=Nathan Wood-Gordon|access-date=31 July 2018|archive-date=31 July 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180731062256/http://football-wonderkids.co.uk/player/nathan-wood-gordon/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''Raúl Goni Bayo''' (born 12 October 1988) is a Spanish former professional [[Association football|footballer]] who played as a [[Defender (association football)#Centre-back|central defender]].

==Club career==
Goni was born in [[Zaragoza]], [[Aragon]]. A product of [[Real Zaragoza]]'s youth ranks, he made his first-team – and [[La Liga]] – debut on 31 October 2007 in a 1–0 away win against [[UD Almería]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://elpais.com/diario/2007/11/01/deportes/1193871611_850215.html|title=El Zaragoza se despierta a tiempo|trans-title=Zaragoza wake up in time|newspaper=[[El País]]|first=Juan José|last=Mateo Ruiz-Gálvez|language=es|date=1 November 2007|access-date=21 June 2016}}</ref> but spent his first two professional seasons, however, mainly registered with [[Deportivo Aragón|the reserves]].

In the [[2010–11 Segunda División B|2010–11 campaign]], Goni played with [[Real Madrid Castilla]] of [[Segunda División B]] on loan, being regularly used during his spell (20 games in the regular season plus one in [[2010–11 Segunda División Play-Off|the playoffs]]) and subsequently returning to Zaragoza.

==International career==
Goni won his only [[Cap (sport)|cap]] for the [[Spain national under-21 football team|Spain under-21 side]] on 10 February 2009, featuring 21 minutes as a starter in a 1–1 [[Exhibition game|friendly]] draw with [[Norway national under-21 football team|Norway]] held in [[Cartagena, Spain|Cartagena]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2009/02/10/futbol/seleccion/1234301874.html|title=La Sub-21 no pasa del empate con Noruega|trans-title=The Under-21s can only draw with Norway|newspaper=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]]|language=es|date=10 February 2009|access-date=17 August 2018}}</ref>

{{Short description|Spanish footballer (born 1979)}}
'''Javier Garrido Ramirez''' (born 1 July 1979) is a Spanish former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played as a [[defender (association football)|defender]] or [[winger (association football)|winger]].

==Early life==

Garrido is a native of [[Valencia]], Spain, and joined the youth academy of Spanish side [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] as a youth player.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/2003/01/14/mas_futbol/1042498804_850215.html|title=Garrido: "En el Camp Nou trataré de dar lo máximo, sin miedo"|publisher=as.com}}</ref>

==Club career==

Garrido started his senior career with [[La Liga]] side [[Valencia CF|Valencia]], and initially mainly played when defender [[Curro Torres]] was unable to play or was rested.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/2002/12/27/polideportivo/1040966152_850215.html|title=Garrido: "Yo me mantengo al margen"|publisher=as.com}}</ref>
During the 2002–03 season, despite being described as playing at a "good level" for [[Valencia CF|Valencia]], the winter signing of French defender [[Anthony Réveillère]] caused him to be sent on loan.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://as.com/masdeporte/2002/12/28/polideportivo/1041052586_850215.html|title=Garrido será el gran perjudicado|publisher=as.com}}</ref> He helped Valencia win the [[2003–04 UEFA Cup]], the [[2003–04 Copa del Rey]], and two league titles.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.superdeporte.es/valencia-cf/2008/07/02/ex-valencianista-garrido-incorpora-secretaria-53746119.html|title=El ex valencianista Garrido se incorpora a la secretaria técnica|publisher=superdeporte.es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.diariocordoba.com/deportes/2004/05/17/valencia-busca-doblete-torneo-multiples-38877617.html|title=El Valencia busca el doblete en el torneo de sus múltiples rotaciones|publisher=diariocordoba.com}}</ref> In 2002, he was sent on loan to Spanish second tier side [[Córdoba CF|Córdoba]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.diariocordoba.com/deportes/2003/08/19/garrido-dice-contento-38941607.html|title=Garrido dice que está contento de su estado|publisher=diariocordoba.com}}</ref> However, he suffered an ankle injury while playing for the club.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.diariocordoba.com/deportes/2003/03/27/cordoba-valencia-acortar-lesion-garrido-38999377.html|title=Córdoba y Valencia trabajan para acortar la lesión de Garrido|publisher=diariocordoba.com}}</ref>

In 2004, he was sent on loan to [[Ligue 1]] side [[AS Saint-Etienne|Saint-Etienne]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurosport.es/futbol/copa-de-la-uefa/2008-2009/garrido-y-saint-etienne_sto1720431/story.shtml|title=Javier Garrido - Eurosport article|access-date=2023-09-12|archive-date=2023-04-19|archive-url=https://archive.today/20230419210042/https://www.eurosport.es/futbol/copa-de-la-uefa/2008-2009/garrido-y-saint-etienne_sto1720431/story.shtml|url-status=bot: unknown}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lasprovincias.es/valencia/20081008/deportes/mas-futbol/caldera-frios-alpes-20081008.html|title=Una caldera en los fríos Alpes|publisher=lasprovincias.es}}</ref> However, while playing for the club, he failed to adapt and was known for his poor performances and marking ability.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.poteaux-carres.com/article-C5220060626202642-1er-juillet-1979-Naissance-de-Javier-Garrido.html|title=Naissance de Javier Garrido}}</ref> That winter, without the club's permission, he played for a Spanish regional representative team and broke a ligament.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.butfootballclub.fr/photo/a,21079,asse-les-5-plus-grands-flops-de-lhistoire-du-club.html|title=ASSE : les 5 plus grands flops de l'histoire du club|publisher=butfootballclub.fr}}</ref>
In 2006, he almost signed for Spanish side Lorca, but the transfer never happened.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://hemeroteca-paginas.mundodeportivo.com/EMD02/PUB/2006/08/13/EMD20060813025MDA.pdf|title=Garrido por el Lorca está en el aire|publisher=mundodeportivo.com}}</ref>

At the age of 27-seven, he retired from professional football due to a knee injury.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.levante-emv.com/deportes/2006/08/31/garrido-ex-valencia-retira-futbol-13671228.html|title=Garrido, ex del Valencia, se retira del fútbol|publisher=levante-emv.com}}</ref>
In total, he made 22 appearances in the [[La Liga]] and ten appearances in the Ligue 1.<ref>{{BDFutbol|1199}}</ref>

==International career==

Garrido played for the [[Valencian Community autonomous football team]].

==Style of play==

Garrido mainly operated as a full-back or winger.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://hemeroteca-paginas.mundodeportivo.com/EMD02/PUB/2006/07/23/EMD20060723019MDA.pdf|title=Javier Garrido - Mundo Deportivo article}}</ref>

==Post-playing career==

After retiring from professional football, Garrido worked as a football agent.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://plazadeportiva.valenciaplaza.com/garrido-agente-de-kang-in-lee-queda-mucho-por-hablar|title=Garrido: "Queda mucho por hablar"|publisher=plazadeportiva.com}}</ref>

'''Bruno Akrapović''' (born 26 September 1967) is a Bosnian professional [[Manager (association football)|football manager]] and former [[Football player|player]].

==Club career==
Starting his career in his native [[Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina|Bosnia and Herzegovina]], at the time part of [[Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia|Yugoslavia]], Akrapović spent the majority of his career playing for various clubs in the [[Bundesliga]] and [[2. Bundesliga]], among others [[VfL Wolfsburg]], [[1. FSV Mainz 05|Mainz 05]] and [[FC Energie Cottbus|Energie Cottbus]]. He played alongside [[Jürgen Klopp]] at Mainz between 1994 and 1997.<ref>[https://www.augsburger-allgemeine.de/sport/fc-augsburg/Die-kuriose-Karriere-des-Bruno-Akrapovic-id34506892.html Die kuriose Karriere des Bruno Akrapovic] - Augsburger Allgemeine {{in lang|de}}</ref>

==International career==
Akrapović made his senior debut for [[Bosnia and Herzegovina national football team|Bosnia and Herzegovina]] in a March 2000 [[Exhibition game|friendly match]] against [[North Macedonia national football team|Macedonia]] and has earned a total of 14 caps, scoring one goal.<ref>[https://www.rsssf.org/miscellaneous/bih-recintlp.html Appearances for Bosnia and Herzegovina National Team] - RSSSF</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://sportsport.ba/bh_fudbal/akrapovic-volio-bih-da-aaron-igra-za-bih/50476|title=Akrapović Volio BIH da Aaron Igra za BIH|work=sportsport.ba|date=23 January 2011|access-date=4 June 2011|language=bs}}</ref> His final international was a September 2002 [[UEFA Euro 2004 qualifying|European Championship qualification]] match against [[Romania national football team|Romania]].<ref name="RSSSF_INTL">{{cite web|url=https://eu-football.info/_player.php?id=208|title=Player Database|website=eu-football.info|access-date=10 January 2021}}</ref>

==Managerial career==
On 16 January 2010, Akrapović received his [[UEFA Pro Licence]] in the [[Football Association of Bosnia and Herzegovina]]'s educational facility in [[Jablanica, Bosnia and Herzegovina|Jablanica]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sarajevo-x.com/sport/nogomet/clanak/110105084|title=Profesionalne licence Barbarezu, Piplici i kolegama|date=5 January 2011|access-date=4 June 2011|work=sarajevo-x.com|language=bs}}</ref>

Akrapović managed [[KF Shkëndija|Shkëndija]] in the [[Macedonian First Football League|Macedonian First League]] and [[RNK Split]] in Croatia,<ref>[https://www.index.hr/sport/clanak/preokret-u-splitu-scoria-odbio-sjesti-na-klupu-kluba-koji-ne-placa-igrace/950071.aspx Scoria odbio sjesti na klupu: "Bilo bi nepošteno da klub plaća mene, a ne igrače"] - Index {{in lang|hr}}</ref> before relocating to Bulgaria in 2017 to become the manager of [[PFC Lokomotiv Plovdiv|Lokomotiv Plovdiv]] where he won the [[Bulgarian Cup]] twice in a row in the seasons [[2018–19 Bulgarian Cup|2018–19]] and [[2019–20 Bulgarian Cup|2019–20]], as well as the [[Bulgarian Supercup]] in [[2020 Bulgarian Supercup|2020]].

On 14 June 2022, Akrapović was appointed as manager of [[Saudi Pro League]] club [[Al Wehda FC|Al-Wehda]].<ref>{{cite web |title=الوحدة يعلن عن تعاقده مع الإيطالي "برونو أكرابوفيتش" لتدريب الفريق الكروي الأول |url=https://sabq.org/sports/%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%88%D8%AD%D8%AF%D8%A9-%D9%8A%D8%B9%D9%84%D9%86-%D8%B9%D9%86-%D8%AA%D8%B9%D8%A7%D9%82%D8%AF%D9%87-%D9%85%D8%B9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A5%D9%8A%D8%B7%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%8A-%D8%A8%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86%D9%88-%D8%A3%D9%83%D8%B1%D8%A7%D8%A8%D9%88%D9%81%D9%8A%D8%AA%D8%B4-%D9%84%D8%AA%D8%AF%D8%B1%D9%8A%D8%A8-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%81%D8%B1%D9%8A%D9%82-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%83%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%8A-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A3%D9%88%D9%84}}</ref> On 20 October 2022, he was sacked after only two wins in eight matches.<ref name="20 Oct">{{cite web |title=الوحدة يقيل أكرابوفيتش.. والبديل سييرا |url=https://arriyadiyah.com/785348}}</ref> On 30 December 2022, Akrapović was appointed as manager of Cypriot side [[Akritas Chlorakas]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Bruno Akrapović pronašao novi angažman|url=https://sportsport.ba/fudbal/bruno-akrapovic-akritas-chlor/441451|date=30 December 2022|access-date=1 January 2023|language=bs}}</ref> On 27 February 2023, he was sacked after only two months.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bruno Akrapović je danas shvatio da je odlazak na Kipar bio pogrešan potez|url=https://sportsport.ba/fudbal/bruno-akrapovic-otkaz/445277|date=28 February 2023|access-date=1 March 2023|language=bs}}</ref>

On 8 January 2024, Akrapović became the manager of his native [[Premier League of Bosnia and Herzegovina|Bosnian Premier League]] club [[FK Željezničar Sarajevo|Željezničar]], signing a one-and-a-half-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.klix.ba/sport/nogomet/iznenadjenje-s-grbavice-bruno-akrapovic-je-novi-trener-zeljeznicara/240108165|title=Iznenađenje s Grbavice: Bruno Akrapović je novi trener Željezničara|date=8 January 2024|access-date=8 January 2024|language=bs|author=H.H.|publisher=Klix.ba}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.klix.ba/sport/nogomet/akrapovic-o-svom-novom-zeljeznicaru-imamo-dogovor-za-pojacanja-navijaci-su-impresivni/240110109|title=Akrapović o svom "novom" Željezničaru: Imamo dogovor za pojačanja, navijači su impresivni|date=10 January 2024|access-date=10 January 2024|language=bs|interviewer=Dino Pajo|publisher=Klix.ba}}</ref> His first game in charge of Željezničar was a 0–0 home draw against [[HŠK Zrinjski Mostar|Zrinjski Mostar]] on 17 February 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportsport.ba/fudbal/fk-zeljeznicar-hsk-zrinjski/468768|title=Igrači i navijači Željezničara na visini zadatka, ali na Grbavici žale za propuštenim šansama|date=17 February 2024|access-date=17 February 2024|language=bs|author=E. Škorić|publisher=sportsport.ba}}</ref> He suffered his first defeat as Željezničar manager on 26 February, losing 2–0 away to [[NK Široki Brijeg|Široki Brijeg]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sport1.oslobodjenje.ba/s1/fudbal/premijer-liga-bih/kupresak-i-misic-donijeli-radost-sirokom-brijegu-protiv-zeljeznicara-934000|title=Kuprešak i Mišić donijeli radost Širokom Brijegu protiv Željezničara|date=26 February 2024|access-date=26 February 2024|language=bs|author=S.P.|publisher=Sport1.ba}}</ref> He was victorious in his first [[Sarajevo derby]], beating rivals [[FK Sarajevo|Sarajevo]] 3–0 at home on 3 March 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportsport.ba/fudbal/fk-zeljeznicar-fk-sarajevo/469833|title=Sarajevo poniženo na Grbavici, Galić junak Plavih!|date=3 March 2024|access-date=3 March 2024|language=bs|author=E. Škorić|publisher=sportsport.ba}}</ref> Following a series of poor results, and with Željezničar sitting in the relegation zone with four points from their previous six games, Akrapović and the club mutually terminated his contract on 20 April 2024.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sport1.oslobodjenje.ba/s1/fudbal/premijer-liga-bih/pamti-se-pobjeda-u-derbiju-protiv-sarajeva-bruno-akrapovic-klupu-napusta-bez-veceg-uspjeha-948083|title=Pamti se pobjeda u derbiju protiv Sarajeva: Bruno Akrapović klupu napušta bez većeg uspjeha|date=20 April 2024|access-date=20 April 2024|language=bs|author=S.P.|publisher=Sport1.ba}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Akrapović's wife is Italian, and their son Aaron Akrapović used to represent the [[Italy national under-17 football team|Italy U17 national team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportsport.ba/fudbal/spreman-sam-promijeniti-nacionalni-dres/44670|title="Spreman sam promijeniti nacionalni dres"|date=11 October 2010|access-date=8 January 2024|language=bs|publisher=sportsport.ba}}</ref>

'''Jorge Wagner Goés Conceição''', or simply '''Jorge Wagner''' (born 17 November 1978), is a Brazilian former [[Association football|footballer]].

Mainly an [[Midfielder#Attacking midfielder|attacking midfielder]], but could also play as a [[Midfielder#Wide midfielder|left midfielder]], [[Defender (association football)#Wing-back|left wing-back]], [[Forward (association football)#Winger|left winger]], [[Midfielder#Central midfielder|central midfielder]] and [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|left back]], Jorge Wagner was known for his versatility, creativity and fierce shot.

==Career==

===Bahia===
Wágner played for [[Esporte Clube Bahia]] during the 2000/2001 season, scoring 7 goals in 23 appearances.

===Cruzeiro===
He then moved to [[Cruzeiro Esporte Clube]] where he made 33 league appearances, scoring 4 goals.

===Lokomotiv Moscow===
Wágner then moved to [[FC Lokomotiv Moscow]] in 2003. He made only 7 league appearances before being loaned to [[Sport Club Corinthians Paulista|Corinthians]] where he made 18 league appearances. He returned to [[FC Lokomotiv Moscow]] where he made only 6 more league appearances.

===Internacional===
Wágner then moved to [[Sport Club Internacional|Internacional]] in 2005 where he made 13 first team appearances, scoring 4 goals. In 2006, during his second season with [[Sport Club Internacional|Internacional]] he won the [[Copa Libertadores]] beating rivals [[São Paulo Futebol Clube]].

===Real Betis===
Wágner moved to [[Real Betis|Betis]] in August 2006. He was purchased for €200,000. Wágner made his [[Real Betis|Betis]] debut against [[Athletic Bilbao]] on 10 September 2006 at the [[Manuel Ruiz de Lopera]] stadium, which [[Real Betis|Betis]] won 3–0. He came on as a second-half substitute.

===São Paulo===
Wágner was then loaned to São Paulo from Betis for 2007 season where he missed the early rounds of the season through injury. However, after regaining full fitness he enjoyed 1st team football and went on to win the [[Campeonato Brasileiro Série A|Campeonato Brasileiro]] in 2007 and was voted the best left midfielder by the [[Brazilian Football Confederation|CBF]]. São Paulo have since agreed a permanent deal with [[Real Betis|Betis]] and Wágner has signed a 3-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.saopaulofc.com.br/news.php?cod=25065|archive-url=https://archive.today/20071019230410/http://www.saopaulofc.com.br/news.php?cod=25065|url-status=dead|archive-date=19 October 2007|title=São Paulo diz que está tudo certo para ter Jorge Wagner por 3 anos|publisher=saopaulofc.com.br|access-date=4 January 2008|date=3 January 2008}}</ref>

===In Japan===
On 7 July 2010, Jorge Wagner sign a contract to 2011 with Japanese club [[Kashiwa Reysol]]. He was one of the key players in Reysol's first ever [[J1 League]] winning campaign, recording 11 goals in 31 appearances. He was also named as one of the players in the [[J. League Best Eleven]] after the season.

===Vitória===

On 20 January 2015 Jorge Wágner was signed by Brazilian club [[Esporte Clube Vitória|Vitória]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Vitória anuncia contratação do meia Jorge Wagner, ex-São Paulo, Corinthians e Inter [Vitória announced the signing of former São Paulo, Corinthians and Inter midfielder Jorge Wágner]|url=http://espn.uol.com.br/noticia/476584_vitoria-anuncia-contratacao-do-meia-jorge-wagner-ex-sao-paulo-corinthians-e-inter|publisher=ESPN Brasil|access-date=20 January 2015|language=pt}}</ref>

==Brazilian team==

In 2008, Jorge Wagner, still uncapped for the national team at any level, according to [[O Globo]], was in a list of 74 players who could be called up by coach [[Dunga]] to play [[2008 Summer Olympics]] for Brazilian team. However, Jorge Wagner was not called up to play that competition.<ref>[http://olimpiadas.uol.com.br/ultimas/2008/05/17/ult5584u1672.jhtm Digão entra em pré-lista olímpica de Dunga, diz jornal]</ref>

'''Miguel Albiol Tortajada''' ({{IPA|es|miˈɣel alˈβjol|lang}}; born 2 September 1981) is a Spanish former professional [[association football|footballer]] who played mainly as a [[right midfielder]].

In a 16-year career, he amassed [[Segunda División]] totals of 178 matches and two goals over seven seasons, in representation of three clubs. In [[La Liga]], he appeared for [[Valencia CF|Valencia]].

==Club career==
Born in [[Vilamarxant]], [[Valencian Community]], Albiol was a product of hometown [[Valencia CF|Valencia]]'s youth ranks as younger brother [[Raúl Albiol|Raúl]] after him, and played once with its first team, during [[2002–03 La Liga|2002–03]]'s [[La Liga]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.elmundo.es/elmundodeporte/2002/12/13/liga/1039798967.html|title=El Valencia gana un 'derby' sin rival|trans-title=Valencia win opposition-free derby|newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]|first=Fernando|last=Llamas|language=es|date=14 December 2002|access-date=2 May 2016}}</ref> He finished [[2002–03 Segunda División|that season]] in the [[Segunda División]] with [[Real Murcia CF|Real Murcia]], featuring regularly ''[[wikt:en route|en route]]'' to the club's promotion.<ref name=PROMOTIONS>{{cite news|url=https://as.com/futbol/2008/12/28/mas_futbol/1230449272_850215.html|title="El ascenso del Murcia fue bonito, el del Rayo especial"|trans-title="The promotion with Murcia was beautiful, the one with Rayo special"|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|first=Maite|last=Martín|language=es|date=28 December 2008|access-date=22 November 2021}}</ref>

Released by the ''Che'', Albiol spent a further year with [[Recreativo de Huelva]] (also second tier), then had a steady period with [[Rayo Vallecano]]. He was instrumental in the latter side's [[2007–08 Segunda División B|2008 promotion to division two]], after four consecutive playoff failures.<ref name=PROMOTIONS/>

In July 2009, apparently after having everything arranged with [[Hércules CF|Hércules]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.informacion.es/deportes/2009/07/03/albiol-anos-7313070.html|title=Albiol, dos años|trans-title=Albiol, two years|newspaper=Diario Información|language=es|date=3 July 2009|access-date=1 April 2021}}</ref> Albiol agreed on a return move to Murcia, signing for three years.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/es/news/21/fichajes/2009/07/07/1368900/mercado-miguel-albiol-vuelve-al-murcia|title=Mercado: Miguel Albiol vuelve al Murcia|trans-title=Market: Miguel Albiol returns to Murcia|publisher=[[Goal (website)|Goal]]|language=es|date=7 July 2009|access-date=13 November 2009}}</ref> He appeared in 30 games in his [[2009–10 Segunda División|first season]] – 22 starts – which ended in second-division relegation.

==Personal life==
Albiol's younger brother, [[Raúl Albiol|Raúl]], was also a footballer. He represented with success Valencia, [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]], [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]], [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]] and the [[Spain national football team|Spain national team]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2010/10/26/mas_futbol/1288074418_850215.html|title=Los hermanos Albiol frente a frente|trans-title=The Albiol brothers face to face|newspaper=Diario AS|language=es|date=26 October 2010|access-date=2 May 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/cs/Satellite/es/Actualidad_Primer_Equipo/1330072821710/noticia/Entrevista/1330072821710.htm?idEsp=1330065768332|title=RealAlbiol: "Mourinho nos ha dado carácter.
